The Twelve Heroes Lide had knighted had become legends in Dawn City, and countless young people took pride in them with his encouragement.
“I will try my hardest,” a hint of excitement and longing appeared on Little Jones’s face.
“Good,” Lide nodded, his gaze shifting to the second generation Bloodline who had immediately come upon hearing the news, all present except for Emi and the guardian Frey of the sacred land.
Due to weather conditions, he had already ordered a halt to the plundering of populations, and all Bloodline on the border had returned to Dawn City.
It’s worth mentioning that aside from Audis, Ivy, Lucy, and Dylan, four of the second generation Bloodline had broken through to level 10, and Frey, the guardian of the sacred land, had also broken through to level 10 last night, becoming a true Advanced Mage.
Five Advanced Mages at level 10, one level 15 blasphemer, plus him, the level 11 Ancestor.
To say the Bloodline had doubled in strength compared to three months ago would be no exaggeration.
Especially in high-level combat power, they completely overpowered what the Bloodline was before.
Give him some more time to develop, and he believed even if facing his teacher Spark’s White Tower, they could easily be crushed.
“Audis, Ivy, Lucy, Dylan, you four come with me, along with 100 Bloodline and 200 Magic Language Bats.
Also, call Emi.
The dignity of the Bloodline cannot be provoked!”
The One-eyed Giants were usually gregarious creatures, and solitary One-eyed Giants were rare, so this time they would inevitably encounter a One-eyed Giant Tribe.
Except for Frey, he took all the high-level forces with him.
Though the One-eyed Giants were powerful, he harbored no fear, and instead, his heart was filled with murderous intent.
No one could infringe upon the Bloodline he ruled, no one had that right.
Moreover, though the One-eyed Giants were formidable, they had a fatal weakness.
They couldn’t fly.
The Bloodline, holding aerial dominance, had absolute initiative.
If Hena hadn’t been protecting Jones, he wouldn’t have been so severely injured.
In just ten minutes, all the Bloodline and Magic Language Bats were assembled.
Above Dawn City, the shapes of Magic Language Bats covered half the city.
The shadows they cast on the ground as they flew past were like the Abyss Demons that hunt giant dragons.
Every low pass stirred the crowds in the square into exclamations of awe and admiration.
The sky was now nearing dusk.
Although the condition of the Bloodline was still somewhat affected, it wasn’t as severe as at midday.
This was Lide’s very first time leading the Bloodline into battle, his blood boiling with excitement.
Every man dreams of commanding armies at war, and Lide was no exception; on Earth, he never had the opportunity.
But in Glory World, he was the king of a race, the master of a city.
He could launch a war wagering lives at any moment.
His blood was seething.
Without further ado, the expeditionary Bloodline assembled on the plaza of Dawn City.
Amid the curious gazes of the surrounding crowd, the Bloodline, arrayed in neat formation, radiated a powerful presence.
Residents spontaneously ceased their chatter amidst the solemn atmosphere and unconsciously stood up straight.
“Holy Light Bloodline, follow me to battle for the sake of Dawn City!”
Liderson’s chilling tone spread across the entire plaza.
“Yes, Ancestor Crown.”
After the uniform response, a hundred Bloodline members mounted the giant Magic Language Bats.
Whoosh~
The Magic Language Bats flapped their enormous wings, whipping up a gust of wind.
Under the astonished gaze of the crowd, all the Magic Language Bats took flight, reducing to tiny black dots in the blink of an eye.
The humans present felt an inexplicable surge of pride, as if the might of this army somehow reflected glory upon themselves.
The reason for this sudden event quickly spread among the people after the departure of the Bloodline.
The mining team dispatched by Lord Kachar had after over a month of arduous searching, finally located an iron mine, but right beside it was a One-eyed Giant Tribe.
The ferocious One-eyed Giants had ambushed the young Prospectors without any warning, during which a member of the Holy Light Bloodline was gravely injured while protecting the young Prospectors, and two blacksmiths were also killed.
Upon hearing the news, Lord Kachar was incensed. The dignity of the Holy Light Bloodline was not to be challenged, and the lives of Dawn City’s residents could not be lost in vain.
In his anger, Lord Kachar decided to take matters into his own hands, to seize that iron mine for Dawn City and exterminate the One-eyed Giants who had killed its inhabitants.
The polished message spread to everyone’s ears from a department called Propaganda in City Hall in a very short time.
Propaganda had always been a high ground to seize, and this secretly established department was small in size, did not recruit outsiders, and was personally overseen by Harrison.
It was a department Liderson paid close attention to.
Upon hearing the news, the residents of Dawn City were filled with righteous indignation, full of anger toward the One-eyed Giants, and silently prayed for the safe return of the Holy Light Bloodline.
This was a war of vengeance waged on behalf of the residents of Dawn City, uniting all with a common enemy.
External conflicts are one of the best ways to resolve internal strife. Faced with a formidable enemy, the entire Dawn City instantly united.
Liderson and Jones rode on the same Magic Language Bat.
With a wingspan between 10 and 12 blades, the Magic Language Bats could be considered the rulers of the sky, their size not conceding to any other lifeform of the same level.
The iron mine Jones had found was not too far from Dawn City.
After half a Sunshine Hour of high-speed flight, under the guidance of Jones, Liderson sighted the attacked location.
It was a hidden area not easy to discover.
To get there, one had to pass through two towering mountains, and the passageway was only 30 blades wide, with a curving aerial path stretching a thousand blades in length.
Liderson believed that if it weren’t for the search for the iron mine, no one would pass through this place.
The Far Mountain Range was no mere hillock, lofty peaks abounded, so there was also no curiosity about such a place.
After traveling through the winding passage, an expansive space suddenly opened up before them.
A vast valley, surrounded by towering mountains, appeared, resembling the shape of a bowl.
Jones stretched out his hand towards the entrance of the valley.
Hundreds of blades above the sky, Liderson looked down upon the land.
Before him was a mountain range uncovered by snow, and the bare rocks showed a grayish brown entirely different from the surrounding peaks.
This had to be the iron mine.
To the right of the mountainside was a forest of uniform height reaching 15 blades, stretching endlessly.
Pale gray leaves were blanketed with thick snow, only a few tips reached out; the grayish bark was like stone pillars, exuding a tenacious and ancient aura.
At the edge of the deep forest and the mine, there were conspicuous signs of battle.
The ground was pockmarked, and there were several enormous footprints clearly left by One-eyed Giants.
Around these were scattered bloodstains, and there was a carcass of a Magic Language Bat that had been eaten, leaving only bones which bore the marks of sharp teeth—indisputably the handiwork of One-eyed Giants.
Liderson’s gaze was icy; this was the Bloodline’s first loss in such a long time.
He did not let the Bloodline land, instead with a wave of his hand, his voice, carried by magic power, reached everyone’s ears.
“Audis, take people to explore the range of this valley, confirm if there are any other passages leading outside.”
“Emi, you may go alone to search for that damned One-eyed Giant Tribe.”
“All other Bloodline, ascend to 1000 blades, and wait for nightfall.”
Rashness will only result in a passive situation; before war, one must ascertain the exact details of the enemy.
This wasn’t a fight between one or two individuals, but a war between one race and another, where even the smallest mistake could result in innumerable casualties.
Bloodline who received the order acted immediately according to the instructions.
As the Shadow High Priest, a Level 15 blasphemer, Emi, was undoubtedly the most powerful being present, especially after being transformed into a Bloodline and having learned Liderson’s Small Fireball Skill.
Even when facing a One-eyed Giant Tribe, Emi feared nothing, thus Liderson confidently allowed it to scout alone.
As for the other Bloodline, Liderson decided to act after dark.
The night was the Bloodline’s most formidable weapon.
Emi immediately used its race’s talent in the sky, transforming into a bat.
Thump~
Hundreds of bats flew towards the ground, disappearing from Liderson’s sight in an instant.
The ascended Bloodline now maintained a silent stance, waiting for Audis and Emi to bring back information, and for the arrival of the Night Goddess.
The snowstorm that had just ceased picked up again as the already dim daylight near dusk grew even darker.
Jones sat on the Magic Language Bat, looking at Liderson’s tall and straight figure, and then at the solemn Bloodline beside him, feeling an inexplicable tension.
A great battle was imminent.

chapters.title: Chapter 130: The One-eyed Giant Will Never Be Enslaved (Combined)
chapters.content:
Chapter 130: Chapter 130: The One-eyed Giant Will Never Be Enslaved (Combined)
The howling wind and snow continued, and seconds and minutes passed by.
Lide was not in a hurry, sitting calmly behind the Magic Language Bat.
Because nightfall was imminent.
Other creatures might become a significant threat after nightfall, but the Bloodline was different.
The Bloodline truly became complete in the darkness, and the night was their most powerful weapon.
An hour after the last ray of sunlight faded, Audis brought back news.
“Ancestor Crown, this valley is completely enclosed by high mountains; we haven’t found another way out. The place we entered from is the only passageway in and out.
Because of the forest, we haven’t spotted the One-eyed Giant…”
Lide nodded; he didn’t blame Audis. The valley was vast, stretching tens of kilometers in length and width. Finding an uncertain number of enemies in such a broad and dense forest was indeed no simple task.
“Now that it has turned dark, you four lead teams of twenty Bloodline members each.
Spread out in this forest and search thoroughly. Once you discover a One-eyed Giant, immediately send a signal to alert us.”
Feeling the surging power within him, Lide gave the command directly. He had waited this long just for night to fall.
At this moment, the time of the Bloodline had come.
“Yes, Ancestor Crown.”
The Bloodline members quickly formed teams and, led by a few second generation Bloodline, entered the forest.
As bats, the Bloodline flew quickly. Despite the vastness of the forest, he was confident it wouldn’t take long to find the other party.
“Jones, I’ll have someone take you back to Dawn City first, and then you can return after daylight tomorrow,”
Lide turned and looked at the already tired Jones behind him, revealing a smile.
For a twelve-year-old child, having gone through such a lengthy period was indeed tiring.
Jones glanced at Lide and was about to express his desire to stay when he looked around and, feeling somewhat disheartened, hung his head.
“Lord Kachar… am I… am I useless?”
Hearing this, Lide couldn’t help but chuckle, patting his shoulder.
“Jones, you are still very young. Not everyone is useful all the time. Work hard, and I hope that in the future, you can help Dawn City find more ore veins.
I believe in you.”
The instant Words of Encouragement King Lide fully revived Jones, who looked up at him with admiration on his face.
“Lord Kachar, you truly are great…”
Indeed, greatness, to speak with him in such a high regard, Jones felt warmed inside.
“Go back.”
After the Bloodline had escorted Jones away, Lide’s expression gradually became serious.
This land held the iron ore he desperately needed, and no matter how powerful the One-eyed Giants were, he had to conquer this land.
Nothing could stop him.
The Bloodline… would never back down.
“Leave ten of our people to watch the Magic Language Bats and wait for my command; the rest will join me in the forest,”
Lide no longer waited for news from Audis and the others. After nightfall, the surging magic power within him filled him with immense confidence.
“Yes, Ancestor Crown.”
Bang~
High in the sky above the forest, behind the colossal bat, under the newly emerging chilly moonlight.
Lide, clad in a deep blue Mage’s robe, stood up and, stepping off the back of the bat, leaped directly toward the ground.
In the moonlit sky, the flapping of the Magic Language Bat’s wings became the backdrop in this moment.
Whoosh whoosh whoosh~
The wild wind roared.
His high-speed descent made Lide’s velocity reach its zenith within seconds, and the resistance from the air brought an impact that caused a buzzing in his ears.
Descending from above.
A kilometer’s distance flashed by in a blink of an eye, and right as he was about to crash into the earth, bang~
Lide’s figure disappeared, and a flock of bats appeared in the sky.
A swarm of exactly 100 bats sped into the forest, a racial talent to transform into bats.
The moment Lide entered the deep forest, a furious roar burst forth from afar as if some ancient creature had awakened.
The whole forest trembled at that instant.
Lide, now a bat, quickly adjusted his direction and dashed towards the source of the noise.
Everything around him turned into twisted lines of light.
Elsewhere,
Emi stood outside a cave, looking at the seven-blade tall One-eyed Giant before him with an extremely ugly expression.
He had not expected to encounter a Level 15 One-eyed Giant lord here.
Miscalculated.
That wasn’t the key issue, however. The key was that this One-eyed Giant lord possessed intelligence far surpassing that of an ordinary One-eyed Giant, making him even more troublesome to deal with.
“Damn Vampire!! You must die!!”
The enraged voice was like the muffled thunder within dark clouds.
Ancient giant language.
This language, a high-level language passed down from ancient giants, was understandable even to those who had never learned giant language, as it was a form of direct mental communication.
The face of the One-eyed Giant lord was filled with immeasurable rage. This despicable human had dared to ambush him just now!!
The huge Wolf Fang Club in his hand swung down furiously.
Emi’s face changed again, as he quickly slid into the shadows and escaped at a high speed.
Having evolved into a Bloodline, and now a Shadow High Priest, his abilities were once again enhanced, and his combat power in the shadow at night was almost terrifyingly strong.
But no matter how much he strengthened himself, it was extremely foolish to engage in close combat with a One-eyed Giant and to compete in strength.
To keep a distance and attack with magic was what a Mage should do.
Boom~
A fireball as large as a millstone erupted from underneath the shadow of the trees.
The One-eyed Giant lord, caught off guard, instinctively used his hand to shield his face.
Boom~
A terrifying heatwave erupted, and the violent energy set the surrounding forest on fire, which was then extinguished by the melting snow.
However, the One-eyed Giant lord’s grey skin, wrinkled like the bark of ancient trees, was merely slightly scorched by the Fireball Technique and didn’t really affect him.
But the intense heat brought excruciating pain, making the One-eyed Giant lord even more furious.
“Vampire, I will let you taste death!!”
His legs, like mountains, powered up, and his body charged towards the shadows with a burst of speed, sweeping through the area with his gigantic Wolf Fang Club, imposing unparalleled force.
Pen~
The ground shook as if moved by a landslide; several large trees that required three men to wrap their arms around were directly smashed apart.
The broken branches crashed to the ground, kicking up a flurry of snowflakes.
And Emi, hiding in the shadows, had already shifted his position.
When Lide arrived, he saw the One-eyed Giant lord plowing through the surrounding forest like a giant bulldozer.
Tall trees lay toppled on the ground, piling up into a mountain of wood.
The body of the One-eyed Giant lord was covered in black scorch marks from the magic, and to Lide’s surprise, there was a scar slashing nearly across his entire body with thick blood oozing, clearly from a great battle before his engagement with Emi.
“Damn Vampire!! I will find you, I will crush your head!!”
The insane roar traveled far in the quiet night sky.
“Ancestor Crown, this monster is a One-eyed Giant lord. It has reached Level 15, and its skin is immune to magic below the Three Circle.”
Lide had transformed back into human form and, flapping his bat wings, hovered above in the sky as Emi quietly appeared behind him.
In the short term, he was unable to deal with the One-eyed Giant lord of the same level, but the flexibility of the Bloodline meant the lord could not deal with him either.
Lide nodded slightly as he regarded the One-eyed Giant lord still rampaging unabatedly.
“Did you cause the scar on the One-eyed Giant lord’s body?”
“No, he already had it when I encountered him. This One-eyed Giant lord has very high Magic Resistance; it’s very difficult for me to harm him in a short time!”
Emi hurriedly explained, the skin of the One-eyed Giant lord, immune to Second Circle magic, had caused him no small amount of trouble.
Lide’s eyes flickered with contemplation. Could there be creatures here capable of injuring a One-eyed Giant Lord?
“Do you have any other creatures?”
“Ancestor Crown, there are only One-eyed Giants here; there should be a tribe of One-eyed Giants in the caverns beyond,”
Lide nodded.
“What are the weaknesses of the One-eyed Giants?”
“Weaknesses?” Emi recalled, “Although One-eyed Giants possess great strength, they are extremely cumbersome units, which we can exploit.
Moreover, One-eyed Giants are exceedingly protective of their young. If their offspring are attacked during battle, the One-eyed Giants often rage, and they will even sacrifice their lives to protect their young.”
Lide’s eyes lit up at this information.
“I understand, now have all of the Bloodlines come over.
We take them one-on-one.”
Emi blinked, puzzled, “One-on-one?”
“Of course, we, the Bloodline, take on the One-eyed Giant Lords one-on-one. Any questions?”
Emi nodded her head in sudden realization, as if it were obvious.
“Of course, no questions. Ancestor Crown, do we need to call all from the Bloodline in Dawn City to duel with them?”
Lide looked deeply at Emi, his face filled with emotion.
“Indeed, you understand me well, but let’s not this time. Perhaps next time.”
In fact, without Lide’s summons, the Bloodlines who heard the commotion had already started rapidly converging as backup.
When the sky became shrouded with the figures of Magic Language Bats, when hundreds of Bloodlines appeared around,
The One-eyed Giant Lord sensed something amiss and suddenly looked up, roaring at the Bloodlines fluttering in the sky.
“Filthy vampires, are you declaring war on the great Thunder Tribe?!”
The ancient giant language bellowed.
Despite being confronted by an overwhelming number of Bloodlines, the One-eyed Giant Lord showed no signs of weakness, his face filled with fury.
Cosso Thunder
Title: Wisdom (Intelligence increased by 50%)
Age: 289
Level: 15 (Severely starving state)
Profession: Giant Heavy Armored Warrior
Ancient Giant Bloodline: Activated, strength increased by 300%, skin immune to Second Circle and below spells.
Introduction: An outstanding One-eyed Giant Lord who not only possesses great strength but also remarkable wisdom.
After reviewing the opponent’s information, Lide raised his eyebrows.
A 15-level giant lord, not only possessing Ancient Giant Bloodline but also holding the title of a Wisdom.
No wonder this One-eyed Giant Lord was able to compete with Emi, the Shadow High Priest, for so long without a scratch, his Bloodline Talent was indeed formidable.
“Cosso Thunder, leader of the One-eyed Giant Tribe, I am the Ancestor of the Holy Light Bloodline—Kachar.
You have trespassed onto Holy Light Bloodline territory, harming our Magic Language Bats”
“I, on behalf of the Holy Light Bloodline, declare war on the One-eyed Giant Tribe until one side submits or is annihilated!”
Lide’s voice, amplified by magic power, boomed through the sky like thunder.
Although the One-eyed Giant Lord in front of him could not understand the common language of the mainland, the message Lide sent directly with his spiritual power still made the meaning clear to him.
The One-eyed Giant Lord, seeing the giant bats that covered the sky, felt his anger slowly subside.
A flicker of apprehension crossed his eyes, and his intelligence made him aware of the difficulty of his adversary.
He let out a fierce roar towards the vast twenty-blade-high cavern behind him.
Boom~
Under everyone’s gaze, One-eyed Giants began to emerge one after another from the cavern, stepping heavily in front of the Bloodline.
One, two, three, up to the 21st.
The entire One-eyed Giant Tribe was all present.
Seven male One-eyed Giants, eight female One-eyed Giants, plus six who were only three blades high, not yet mature younglings.
And among them, five of the One-eyed Giants had reached the staggering level of 10, with as many as ten One-eyed Giants at level 9.
This was a power that could be called formidable, and Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly.
After brief observation, an interesting discovery made his heart stir.
Among these One-eyed Giants, except for the few young ones, all bore numerous scars on their bodies.
Though none were as conspicuous as the ferocious scar on Cosso Thunder’s belly, they had all sustained serious injuries, clearly having gone through a great battle.
This One-eyed Giant Tribe must have undergone something to have fallen to this state.
Moreover, the critical point was that each One-eyed Giant’s attribute panel contained a particular attribute.
The Hunger State.
This discovery instantly led him to many associations.
Apart from humans, the Bloodline could not turn other humanoid creatures into vampires, so the concept of a vampiric One-eyed Giant did not exist.
But what if they were to enslave the other party?
Looking at a group of One-eyed Giants who vigilantly watched the Bloodline in the sky but dared not initiate an attack and could only emit angry roars, Lide stroked his chin, revealing a contemplative look in his eyes.
The Bloodline were flying three to four hundred blades high in the air, where the One-eyed Giants could only throw stones, but at such a distance, the agile Bloodline could easily dodge, rendering even the greatest anger ineffective against them.
Lide maintained an oppressive but non-attacking stance, simply hovering in mid-air.
This posture exerted immense pressure on the One-eyed Giants below. Not to mention the Bloodline themselves, merely the ten-plus blades wingspan of the Magic Language Bats posed a fatal sense of threat to these massive creatures.
Too many of them, a full two hundred Magic Language Bats; even without attacking and just patrolling, they could cause great unease in the hearts of these One-eyed Giants.
After ten minutes, a few small bats flew out from the cave behind the One-eyed Giants under the cover of night.
With a flap of their wings, they quickly arrived in front of Lide. He stretched out his hand to catch the small bats and closed his eyes slightly.
A moment later, a cold smile appeared on his lips.
The specially trained small bats had not found any new enemies in the cave.
Which meant that here, this was everything they had.
Knowing the enemy and knowing oneself ensures victory in every battle. He had not waited this long just to watch a show.
Now, it was time to begin this racial war.
Lide’s voice was chillingly cold, “All Bloodline, prepare to cast spells and ride the Magic Language Bats for a dive bombing.”
The Bloodline, who had air superiority, now had absolute initiative. Even if the One-eyed Giants on the ground were boss-level beings capable of toppling city walls, it was to no avail.
Without countermeasures, even the powerful One-eyed Giants must kneel and submit in his hands.
“Cosso Thunder.
I am the Lord of Dawn City, Clan Leader of the Holy Light Bloodline. I will launch an extermination attack on you,
The Bloodline will kill every member of your One-eyed Giant Tribe!”
Lide continued to exert pressure on the One-eyed Giant chieftain with his words during the spellcasting interval of the Bloodline.
Yelling before a battle might seem foolish, but it often imposed even greater psychological pressure on those at a disadvantage.
If he were facing a group of ordinary One-eyed Giants, he would not have bothered with them and would have simply fought first.
But now, this intelligent One-eyed Giant evoked different thoughts in him.
These damned vampires!!
Cosso Thunder bellowed angrily at the sky, but faced with that sky-covering number, a flicker of unease that even he could not detect flashed in his eyes.
The enemy was too numerous, too powerful.
Unless he could gain the support of the Thunder Tribe, he had no confidence in facing such a number of vampires.
But now he was just a loser who had failed to compete for the throne, and the Thunder Tribe was out of reach.
Inevitably, a surge of fear rose in his heart.
His three wives and six children were still behind him, and with his newfound intelligence, he did not wish to die like this.
But the dignity of a One-eyed Giant chieftain made it impossible for him to admit defeat before the battle had even begun, let alone surrender to a bunch of damned vampires!!
Cosso Thunder would never admit defeat!!
One-eyed Giants never enslave themselves!!
Just then, over a hundred Bloodline mounted on giant bats dove down, each Bloodline gripping a Second Circle magic.
The dense magical fluctuations made the very sky tremble.
The bombardment from the dive began.

chapters.title: Chapter 131 - 131 Kneeling Submission
chapters.content:
Chapter 131: Chapter 131 Kneeling Submission
No one had ever thought that war could be fought this way.
The Bloodline members sat on Magic Language Bats, and after casting spells, the bats dived down, releasing large fireballs from a hundred blades’ height above the One-eyed Giants.
The Magic Language Bats then ascended again, never entering the low-altitude area below a hundred blades.
If it were just one or two Bloodline members, the effect would undoubtedly be weak, but hundreds of Bloodline members formed a continuous bombing network.
This was a dive-bombing operation only seen in modern warfare.
After the first wave of bombing, the ascending Bloodline members released a second spell, then began a new round of casting after one cycle.
Boom, boom, boom~
Terrifying Big Fireball Skills fell from the sky, each explosion far exceeding the Small Fireball Skill by more than five times, easily demolishing half a building.
Even more powerful than TNT.
A sea of fire.
The horrifying heat turned all the surrounding ice and snow into water.
In the central area of intense bombing, the One-eyed Giants endured wave after wave of assaults.
The young of the One-eyed Giants were protected underneath the bodies of female giants, but the scorching temperature still inevitably caused them to let out piercing screams.
Seeing their offspring being viciously attacked, those One-eyed Giants initially trying to flee turned back to protect the six still immature youngsters.
Though they possessed high magic resistance, fear spread inevitably under the overwhelming assault of the Bloodline.
After all, they were intelligent beings. Even with low IQs, they were still capable of feeling fear.
What was crucial was the Bloodline’s agility. Though the underground One-eyed Giants could toss boulders high into the air, the agile bodies of the Bloodline allowed them to easily dodge.
Even if a Magic Language Bat was hit by chance, its robust physical fitness could still endure the attack from the One-eyed Giants.
Even if a Magic Language Bat was injured, the Bloodline riding it could simply switch to another bat and continue fighting.
The war reached a fever pitch from the start.
After casting spells at high altitudes, the Bloodline rode their bats in dives, bombing the ground, while the One-eyed Giants on the ground, in a fury, hurled various giant rocks and trees at the Bloodline.
One fireball after another, carrying the hottest and most explosive magic energy, exploded on the ground, forming a huge circle of flames around the One-eyed Giants.
Unable to flee immediately to protect their young, the surrounded One-eyed Giants could not escape anymore. The raging flames around them, with their green scorching light, could melt rocks.
A battle without air control was undoubtedly a futile and brutal resistance, and under the Bloodline’s magical bombardment, the ground had turned into a sea of fire.
If any One-eyed Giant attempted to escape, Emi hidden in the shadows would teach them a lesson with a Three Circle Magic spell, preventing the One-eyed Giant Tribe from even raising their heads under the intense bombing.
Lide had still not taken action; he merely commanded from the outside, adjusting the Bloodline’s bombing frequency and altitude. This was the first time he had applied his concepts to warfare involving the Bloodline.
In the memories of the Blood Clan Ancestor, Bloodline battles were always direct confrontations with the enemy, with air superiority often not yielding a suppressive effect.
He blended modern warfare strategies when facing ground races without air control, maximizing the advantages of the Bloodline.
Of course, this strategy only worked against races that could not challenge the Bloodline’s air control, like the Beastmen’s Double-legged Flying Dragons, where it would fail.
Even so, Lide was continuously amazed by the potential shown by the Bloodline each time.
This was a true Upper Race, powerful and domineering.
In the nighttime, the Bloodline’s fighting abilities were undoubtedly elevated to their highest, each Bloodline being able to cast the Second Circle Big Fireball Skill about 15 times, and after drinking Magic Blood, this number more than doubled, with the speed of magic recovery skyrocketing, and no one cared about the depletion of magic energy.
After enduring 25 rounds of bombardment, the resilient One-eyed Giants were finally nearing collapse.
The One-eyed Giants possessed the Ancient Giant Bloodline; their skin had extremely high magic resistance, with a One-eyed Giant chieftain immune to damage from spells below Three Circles, and adult One-eyed Giants immune to spells below Two Circles.
But no matter how strong the immunity, there was a threshold that could be exceeded, just like Lide could use a First Circle spell to melt stones resistant to Four Circle spells.
After continuous fireball bombardments, the ground had turned into a sea of fire.
The still-exploding fireballs raised the temperature to an unimaginable level.
Apart from Cosso Thunder, the One-eyed Giant chieftain, the other One-eyed Giants could not hold out any longer.
The scorching flames rapidly thinned the air, and each breath they took felt like it was searing their throats.
Thump, thump, thump~
One by one, the weakened One-eyed Giants collapsed into the sea of fire.
Barely alive.
Despair filled Cosso Thunder’s eyes as he turned to look behind him at the One-eyed Giant Tribe, with no one left standing, swallowed by fear.
If he had died valorously on the battlefield, he would not have felt fear, but being trapped and slowly burned alive, unable to fight back and waiting for death, that torment was indescribable.
“Cosso Thunder.
I am Kachar, the Ancestor of the Holy Light Bloodline. Unless one side chooses to submit, the war will continue until the One-eyed Giant Tribe is exterminated.
Your children, your women, everything you hold dear will turn to ash under the magic of the Bloodline!”
What seemed like a powerless—even somewhat childish—shout had now become unbearably heavy.
The suffocating pressure made Cosso Thunder’s defenses crumble bit by bit.
Lide’s gaze was cold as he slowly conjured a gigantic fireball in his hand, its explosive magical energy several times that of the Big Fireball Skill.
He hurled it toward the ground.
Boom~
The fireball exploded in front of Thunder.
A terrifying shockwave erupted.
The searing energy of the elements swept through the heavens and the earth again.
Flames, ten blades high, seemed poised to devour the One-eyed Giant chieftain.
This completely shattered Cosso Thunder’s resolve.
He turned his head to look at the One-eyed Giants who had all fallen, still coughing violently in unconsciousness, nearly at death’s door.
He knelt on one knee.
His massive one eye showed despair.
Already severely injured in the fight for the chieftain’s position, he no longer had the strength to resist.
“I am willing to submit to you, Ancestor of the Holy Light Bloodline.”
Hearing this, a slight smile curled the corners of Lide’s mouth.
There are no races that cannot be conquered, only forces that are not strong enough.
“Stop the attack.”
Lide prevented the Bloodline from launching another attack.
Hundreds of Bloodline members held giant fireballs, their cold gaze fixed on the ground, ready to make the One-eyed Giants taste magic once again at just a command.
The dark night sky was lit up bright red.
Alone, he descended from the sky with his huge bat wings flapping.
Amidst the vast flames, Lide with his bat wings seemed like a Great Demon bursting out of a lava-filled Hell.
Filled with awe-inspiring power.
The weakened Cosso, upon seeing Lide, flashed a deep fear in his eyes. This vampire had decimated their tribe without even making contact.
Strength commanded respect.
The power of the Bloodline instilled fear, commanded respect, and garnered reverence in him.
“Cosso Thunder, submission is not disgraceful. I will make your tribe stronger.
Swear it.”
Thunder’s large one eye regarded Lide, a struggle flickering within, but eventually, it settled into calmness.
He couldn’t afford to gamble anymore.
“Oi…pf…nq…Great deity who controls death and souls, I am your loyal servant, I am your most devout believer, I am willing to use your power to sign a Soul Contract with my master.
If the contract is ever broken, I will offer my soul, to serve you for all eternity, great Death God.”
As soon as Lide sensed the flicker of a soul in his Spiritual Sea, he immediately felt relieved.
The Soul Contract, devised by the Death God, deals with the fundamental rule forces of Glory; even the Death God himself cannot void this contract.
Moreover, after signing the Soul Contract, the secondary contractor would gradually develop a fondness for the primary contractor, eventually reaching the ultimate loyalty.
This is also why the Soul Contract has spread throughout the Glory World.
“Ding~ You have gained the loyalty of the One-eyed Giant Tribe. The power of Dawn City has grown, gaining character experience—1000”
“Ding, your strength has earned Cosso Thunder’s awe, increasing your Legend Level in the Underworld by 1 point.”
The system’s update caused Lide’s eyes to snap open.
Legend Level in the Underworld???

chapters.title: Chapter 132 - 132 Unexpected Discovery
chapters.content:
Chapter 132: Chapter 132 Unexpected Discovery
Underworld Legend Level??
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly at the prompt, his thoughts turning, but he didn’t rush to investigate.
After Cosso Thunder swore his oath, he gained a considerable 1000 experience points.
His experience now reached—LV11 (5061/6000), just 1000 points shy of levelling up again.
This was an unexpected gain.
The key was that a powerful One-eyed Giant Tribe would now belong to Dawn City, to his private assets.
That was what mattered most.
Although in this war these one-eyed giants were powerless against the Bloodline, these warriors, known for their strength on the surface, were not so weak.
Had the Bloodline confronted them head-on, Lide was certain that even if they could claim victory, at least one-third of the Bloodline would fall.
Unfortunately for the giants, they had encountered him, the Bloodline with absolute control of the skies.
This battle was much like Earth’s US forces attacking Kosovo, with hundreds of thousands of ground troops stationed in Kosovo, bombarded and obliterated by the air superiority of the US forces, rendering the formidable ground army utterly defenceless.
Were Kosovo’s ground forces not strong?
No, it was an imbalance of advantages.
One-eyed Giants were adept at close-range, positional warfare; the Bloodline excelled at flexible raids.
Using their strength against the enemy’s weakness, these heavy warriors adept at siege warfare could only submit under the magic of the Bloodline.
After a while, the flames slowly dissipated.
Below, the scene unfolded before Lide’s eyes.
Ghastly.
Twenty one-eyed giants lay on the scorched earth, their grey, wrinkled skin now charred black, like overcooked baked potatoes.
The acrid smell of trees yet to burn completely filled the air, accompanied by the crackling and bursting of branches.
A few whelps emitted unconscious wails—weak, pained groans that made the scene even more sorrowful.
“Master… I beseech you to save my kin…”
Cosso, weak, was propping himself up, his voice thick with anxiety as he spoke breathlessly, his scars made more fearsome by the flames’ searing.
His three women and six children had all fainted, with the Death God ready to take their souls; he needed help.
“Audis, take these one-eyed giants back to Dawn City.”
Lide nodded; these one-eyed giants were now his property, with great use for the future—no need to lose them here.
Audis looked strangely, eyeing the one-eyed giants’ towering six-blade-tall stature, slightly vexed.
The Magic Language Bat could carry about 1000 pounds, and an adult one-eyed giant weighed a hefty 2000 pounds—not even two bats could carry one away.
“Use Mage’s Hand,”
Lide said irritably, seeing that Audis remained silent.
“One Mage’s Hand has a strength of 700-800 pounds; 4 Bloodline should be enough to move a one-eyed giant.”
Reminded by Lide, Audis revealed an admiring expression.
That kind of slick operation was possible?
He immediately turned to arrange for the personnel to carry the dying one-eyed giants back to Dawn City.
After giving his instructions, Lide turned solemnly to Cosso, who stood three to four times his height beside him.
“Cosso, from now on, the One-eyed Giant Tribe is a thing of the past, and you are now residents of Dawn City.
I will heal their wounds, no need to worry.
Now tell me, why did you appear here?”
Curious about the system prompt he had just seen, Lide wondered.
One-eyed giants were not common creatures; these beings of great strength often lived in places rarely tread by man.
Although the Far Mountain Range was a place few humans dared to enter, it was still beneath the eyes of the Bloodline.
In the two hundred years of memory from the Blood Clan Ancestor, there had never been any mention of one-eyed giants in the Far Mountain Range.
Even though the terrain was remote, it was improbable that they had gone undiscovered for centuries, especially when they were so close to Dawn City.
After receiving Lide’s promise, Cosso relaxed considerably, glancing at his still unconscious kin before turning and speaking respectfully to Lide.
“Master, we came to the surface from the Thunder Tribe in the Underworld. I lost the contest for the tribal chief position against my brother.
The defeated have no right to stay in the tribe, I was exiled by the new chief.”
“I had originally planned to take my warriors and my woman to another habitat, but we accidentally discovered a route to the surface world. In our exploration, we came here…”
Underworld?
Lide’s eyes opened wide, filled with intense curiosity.
In Glory World, it wasn’t just the surface that hosted life; there was a magnificent world beneath the ground, where the strength and diversity of the subterranean creatures were in no way inferior to those on the surface.
One-eyed Giants, Gray Dwarfs, Half-Elves, Cave Dwellers, Dark Night Elves, Snake Race, and so on, as well as the legendary Underground Cities where jewels piled in warehouses, and Gold Pucks clogged the moats.
The Underworld has always been synonymous with both wealth and danger.
In human legends, countless times have adventurers ventured deep into the Underworld. They killed Evil Dragons, plundered wealthy Underground Cities, and seized Divine Artifacts and gold. These people were heroes revered and worshipped by humankind.
But because, apart from a few well-known passages, there are no numerous channels connecting the Underworld and the surface world, it’s quite difficult to enter the Underworld.
Mystery, wealth, threat, Underground City, Evil Dragons… these are all synonymous with the Underworld.
The One-eyed Giants actually came from the Underworld.
This is a major event.
If One-eyed Giants can come up, that means they can go down, and with the One-eyed Giants’ size, the passage must be quite large.
Logically, if the Bloodline didn’t need to feed on human blood, the Underworld would be a better destination… There’s no sunshine in the Underworld.
A flash of excitement crossed his eyes.
“The Underworld? Is that the cave behind you?”
“Yes, Master.
Inside the cave is a dark hole, leading directly to the Underworld; it’s only a day’s journey away.”
After pondering for a moment, Cosso Thunder replied with a voice as resonant as thunder.
A day’s journey?
Lide pondered; the distance wasn’t too far.
“Are there any strong creatures near the passage to the Underworld?” He had to ask clearly, as the dangers in the Underworld were incomparable to those on the surface.
The Underworld was a three-dimensional existence, with evil and powerful creatures potentially appearing below the feet or overhead.
“No, aside from a group of Kobolds, there are no strong creatures.”
“What’s your experience of living in the Underworld like? Tell me about it.”
“Yes, Master,”
Cosso nodded, unable to defy Lide’s command. After a brief contemplation, the big fellow began recounting his past in a very dry and uninteresting monotone.
Cosso lived in a very powerful One-eyed Giant Tribe — the Thunder Tribe, and he was the son of the previous chieftain.
The Thunder Tribe lived in a swamp, home to fearsome creatures such as Dire Wolves, goblins, Cave Spiders, and Ogres, all dwelling within the Underworld.
But the One-eyed Giants were the most powerful entities in the swamp; all evil creatures were their hunting targets.
However, good times didn’t last long. Cosso’s father, the One-eyed Giant chieftain who was close to reaching Extraordinary Rank, encountered a Black Dragon in the depths of the swamp.
The might of the Black Dragon was not something the not-yet-Extraordinary chieftain could withstand; his father lost his life.
After the Thunder Tribe lost its powerful Protector, it gradually lost its say in the swamp.
The Thunder Tribe prepared to relocate, but the decision to move required the chieftain’s order.
Cosso fought his brother to contest the chieftain’s position, and the result was clear; the wisdom-titled Cosso did not gain much in terms of combat ability.
He was defeated. Although not killed, he lost the right to remain in the Thunder Tribe. A tribe could only have one king, and Cosso was exiled.
After more than half a Sunshine Hour, Cosso drily finished recounting his experiences.
Even though he had awakened wisdom, this big fellow’s storytelling skills were evidently nonexistent.
Despite Cosso’s disjointed narrative, Lide gleaned several key pieces of information.
The Underworld where the One-eyed Giants resided was vast, and even the Thunder Tribe couldn’t explore the swamp to its borders.
Not far from the Thunder Tribe, there was a city built by Half-Elves. The Thunder Tribe had even traded Demon Beast carcasses for weapons in that city.
The city was inhabited by many intelligent Races, including Dark Elves, Gray Dwarfs, Dark Knights, and Undead Mages, among others.
Although Cosso’s introduction was very dry and not quite accurate, Lide could feel a huge and exciting world unfolding before him.
A wholly different Underworld compared to the surface world.
Cosso was like opening a window for Lide, beyond which lay a world rich in color and splendor.

chapters.title: Chapter 133: 133: Huge Harvest, Sensational Dawn City
chapters.content:
Chapter 133: Chapter 133: Huge Harvest, Sensational Dawn City
Although Lide was very interested in the splendid Underworld, he wisely chose not to explore it immediately after hearing Kachar’s words.
Currently, Dawn City did not have the resources to develop a new map, lacking both manpower and material resources.
Especially since there were creatures like the Black Dragon in this Underworld, recklessly heading there was not something to be praised.
He couldn’t even handle the affairs within Dawn City yet.
However, this could also be reserved as an opportunity; once Dawn City became more powerful, they could send people to explore the Underworld.
Although the Underworld did not have the material wealth of the surface world, its ores were enough to make any surface creature envious.
...
Be it gold mines or others.
“Kachar, do not mention anything about the Underworld to anyone else, remember!”
“Yes, Master,” seeing Lide’s stern gaze, Kachar immediately nodded in agreement.
“Let’s head back to Dawn City.”
Lide took a deep look at the large, dark cave not far away and took off into the sky.
The matter here was temporarily concluded; what came next was not to think of those potentials but to first extract the iron ore next to the One-eyed Giant.
Eight Bloodlines lifted Kachar into the sky using Mage’s Hand. This 7-blade tall, One-eyed Giant lord weighed over 3,000 pounds, truly a small land tank.
Eight Mage’s Hands dragged Kachar, who was 7-blades tall, from head to toe.
A rather comical scene indeed.
And Kachar, this cumbersome One-eyed Giant, experienced flying for the first time in his life.
The only difference was the experience wasn’t all that great.
Carrying the One-eyed Giant, the Bloodlines’ speed inevitably decreased by half.
Finally, after nearly a Sunshine Hour, the bat flock flew back over Dawn City.
When 22 horrifically large One-eyed Giants were brought back to Dawn City by the Bloodlines riding Magic Language Bats using Mage’s Hand.
The entire city was astounded.
Aside from the Hero Selection Contest, there had never been such an outcry of joy.
Nearly everyone was rushing to spread the news.
Kachar City Lord had achieved a victory in the war!!
When Lide had just left with the Bloodlines, the propaganda department had already gloriously publicized his campaign against the One-eyed Giants widely.
Everyone knew Lide had waged war against the evil One-eyed Giants for Dawn City.
Now that he had returned victorious, it was a great boost to morale.
Especially when the One-eyed Giants appeared exceptionally powerful, it amplified the jubilation.
The terrifying height of the One-eyed Giants, displayed in the square of Dawn City, made the crowd shudder with fear.
They were enormous!!
The One-eyed Giants were beyond everyone’s imagination.
They dared not imagine what destruction such powerful creatures could cause if they attacked.
It was simply indescribable.
What excited the crowd even more was that, even such powerful One-eyed Giants had been captured by the great Holy Light Bloodline.
The victors belonged to Dawn City, to the Holy Light Bloodline, and also to every single resident!
External conflicts were always the best way to shift internal conflicts, and a war waged against the One-eyed Giants had caused the morale in Dawn City to soar tremendously.
“Life Goddess above!! Is this the legendary giant? He’s really too tall, his hand is taller than me!!”
“It’s unbelievable, that such a powerful creature like the One-eyed Giant could be defeated!! Praise Kachar City Lord!! Praise Holy Light Bloodline!”
“Hahaha, we’ve won the victory!! These damned One-eyed Giants dared to injure the great ones of the Holy Light Bloodline, they truly deserve to be hanged one by one!!”
“…”
The boost to morale was immense, the influence brought about by the victory of our troops had the most direct demonstration.
And among the crowd, the civilians with ulterior motives vanished completely in the presence of the One-eyed Giants.
Such powerful creatures were defeated by the Holy Light Bloodline; who else could be their opponent?!!
Hearing the news, residents flocked to the square, the crowd growing larger and larger.
Eventually, all the residents of Dawn City gathered in the square, the excitement rivaling that of the Hero Selection Contest.
In the midst of the excited discussions of the crowd, Kachar, the strongest One-eyed Giant lord, made his appearance.
Thud~
From mid-air, ten blades high off the ground, Kachar leaped down amidst the crowd’s screams.
Boom~
The entire ground shook.
The moment Koso appeared in front of the crowd, the previously lively atmosphere abruptly turned cold, and the air fell into silence.
Fear that could not be suppressed emerged in everyone’s eyes.
His huge figure, explosive muscles, terrifying one-eyed face, ferocious appearance, and his gray-black wrinkled skin—all of it exuded a daunting presence.
Fierce and terrifying, powerful and shocking.
After seeing Koso, instead of fainting, the crowd screamed in panic and began retreating frantically.
Screaming, shouting, children crying, women scolding—the scene instantly became chaotic.
Damn it, one of those One-eyed Giants has already awakened!!
It was terrifying, how could such a powerful creature be dealt with?!
Even lying on the ground, a One-eyed Giant could bring immense psychological pressure to the crowd. Standing up, the even taller One-eyed Giant lord made the people feel the most direct and intense shock.
It was too fierce. Once such a creature attacked them, it would be as simple as stepping on ants.
Their height only reached the knees of the One-eyed Giant; the intense oppression brought tremendous panic to the crowd, fearing that this powerful creature would attack.
Just as the frantic turmoil spread, a familiar figure in the sky made everyone halt abruptly.
Kachar City Lord!!
Lide rode atop the huge Magic Language Bat, circling in the sky, its wings stirring up huge gusts.
Looking up at the figure riding the giant bat in the sky, the crowd inexplicably lost their fear at that moment.
It seemed that the figure, many times smaller than the One-eyed Giant, appeared even larger in their hearts, instilling boundless confidence in the crowd without even speaking.
Lide controlled the Magic Language Bat to slowly descend; when he flipped off its back, the originally chaotic crowd had regained calm, no longer retreating under the oppression of Koso’s huge figure.
An inexplicable and strong trust.
Step by step~
Walking slowly to the center of the square, under the warm yellow glow of the Magic Lamp, his handsome face was filled with an indescribable aura.
Flawless perfection.
At that moment, he seemed to be the stabilizing force amidst the tempest; standing there, even next to a giant, he appeared the tallest of all.
Then, a scene that shocked all humanity unfolded.
The One-eyed Giant that they feared bowed suddenly upon seeing Lide, its huge gray-black one-eyed head firmly touching the ground.
Submitting in the most humble manner.
Thud~
The sound of his forehead colliding with the bluestone floor echoed through the hearts of everyone.
Seeing this scene, something inside the crowd seemed to erupt.
A burst of unspeakable excitement, pride, and arrogance exploded in an instant.
“Long live the Kachar City Lord!!!”
As the first voice rose, all of Dawn City boiled over.
“Long live the Kachar City Lord!!”
“Long live the Kachar City Lord!!”
“Kachar…”
Such a powerful creature, nearly unrivaled, had submitted at the feet of their City Lord—intense pride nearly bursting from the crowd.
They shared in the glory.
The most powerful beings must submit before the Kachar City Lord, before the Holy Light Bloodline, before Dawn City!
A strong sense of confidence and honor now converged in everyone’s hearts.
Outsiders would hardly be able to imagine the massive shift happening within the hearts of the crowd.
Victory is often the best way to garner support, and Lide once again showcased the immense power of the Holy Light Bloodline.
“My people, I am your City Lord, Kachar.”
“Today, we have achieved another victory!!
These powerful One-eyed Giants, legendary creatures that can battle with giant dragons, have submitted under the magic of the Holy Light Bloodline!!”
“In the future, we will have the One-eyed Giants working for Dawn City!!
You have witnessed this historic moment, you are the participants and witnesses of the rise of Dawn City!!”
“Cheer, my people, as I will lead Dawn City to conquer all enemies!!”
Lide’s resonant voice completely plunged Dawn City into a frenzy.
Tonight was destined to be sleepless.
Because all the residents were frantically discussing their City Lord, discussing the Holy Light Bloodline, and envisioning their future.

chapters.title: Chapter 134: 134 Giants Will Never Be Slaves, Unless Room and Board are Included
chapters.content:
Chapter 134: Chapter 134 Giants Will Never Be Slaves, Unless Room and Board are Included
It had been three days since the conquest of the One-eyed Giant Tribe.
In fact, Lide had been monitoring the injuries of the One-eyed Giants, but the speed of healing these big fellows had exceeded Lide’s expectations.
It took a full three days to barely heal them.
And the appetite of the One-eyed Giants also opened Lide’s eyes.
One One-eyed Giant could eat the rations of twenty people each day, and providing food for 22 One-eyed Giants required provisions for 400 people.
It was literally a bottomless pit.
...
What made him both laugh and cry was that, after getting enough food, the One-eyed Giants, who were initially indifferent to him even with a Soul Contract, became extremely respectful whenever they saw him.
Originally, those One-eyed Giants forced into joining Dawn City were somewhat reluctant, but after being well-fed, they had become very proactive.
One-eyed Giants would never serve as slaves, unless room and board were included??
After a thorough discussion with Cosso, Lide also came to a realization. Although the Underworld was teeming with creatures and rich in ores, it was severely lacking in food.
Added to the huge appetite of the One-eyed Giants, even extensive hunting was not enough to fill their stomachs, so they were always in a state of hunger.
In the Underworld, a One-eyed Giant might never get the chance to eat their fill from birth to death; this group, used to being starved, suddenly relished being well-fed.
That was almost too good for them.
Thus, their initial reluctance was quickly cast aside by the group of One-eyed Giants.
Lide didn’t know whether to laugh or cry upon learning this news. He wondered why he had even bothered with fighting if they were so easily swayed.
No wonder, initially, the attribute panel of these One-eyed Giants all showed an extremely hungry negative status.
He had thought it was due to some other reason, but it turned out they were truly just starved.
It was both laughable and pitiful.
What slightly consoled Lide was that the strength of the One-eyed Giants was indeed formidable… at least against ground troops.
There were a total of 22 One-eyed Giants, including one Level 15 One-eyed Giant Lord—Cosso Thunder.
There were 5 Level 10 One-eyed Giant warriors, 10 Level 8-9 adult One-eyed Giants, and 6 Level 4 juvenile cubs.
All of these One-eyed Giants had signed a Soul Contract and belonged to him as private property.
The disposition of the One-eyed Giants was more inclined towards that of heavy-armored warriors. When facing cavalry or infantry, One-eyed Giants were nearly invincible.
Their large size gave them a massive advantage against smaller creatures.
This was a unique racial advantage.
It seemed in Glory, there were hardly any perfect creatures, almost every race had its strengths and weaknesses.
Mighty as giant dragons and Elves, their disadvantage was a low birth rate; it might take hundreds or even thousands of years for them to reproduce.
Conversely, humans with lesser innate talent might have already spawned a kingdom.
The strength of One-eyed Giants lay in their powerful bodies.
At the same level, humans might not be able to withstand a punch from a One-eyed Giant, but correspondingly, their intelligence was not high, which was the shortcoming of One-eyed Giants.
However, now that the Bloodline was there to compensate for their deficiencies, One-eyed Giants could be considered powerful.
One had control of the skies, and the other had control of the ground.
And with Bloodline directing the battles, their low intelligence was not an issue.
But now, Lide was not contemplating matters of war, but something more important and urgent that he wanted to start.
Iron mining.
After the One-eyed Giants were conquered, Lide truly owned a mine at home.
Yearning for the iron mine, he once again sent Jones, the young prospector, with a few blacksmiths to Giant Valley.
Of course, that name was something he had come up with temporarily.
The results were very encouraging. According to Jones’s inference, the iron mine in Giant Valley was a rich vein with a vast reserve.
Lide was very relieved.
Ore was a fundamental necessity for the development of a city. Without its own mines, operation was simply impossible; unlike other cities, Dawn City couldn’t just purchase ore.
Thus, the most crucial thing was to immediately develop this iron mine and get it operational as soon as possible. Dawn City was in desperate need of ore.
“Harry, how many people know how to mine ore?”
Lide, massaging his temples with some headache, asked this on the third floor of the City Hall.
The mine was there, but mining it was another issue.
Mining wasn’t as simple as digging sand.
“Clan Leader, three blacksmiths know, and there are about 20 humans who have worked in the mines.”
“Then gather these people together and send 100 from the Bloodline to accompany them. Build the mine as quickly as possible.”
Harrison looked somewhat hesitant.
“Lord Lide, the weather is too cold now. If we don’t use Mages to mine, humans will find it difficult to work.”
The warm fireplace stirred up flames, and the warmth inside the room made Lide almost forget the harsh weather outside.
He turned to look out the window. Feather-like heavy snow was still falling, and outside roofs were covered with a thick layer of snowflakes.
A world of silver.
The cold was the greatest enemy. Digging holes while wrapped in thick cotton coats was a bit too much to ask of these ordinary humans.
Suddenly, a gigantic figure appeared in the window.
A One-eyed Giant.
These past few days, the One-eyed Giant had been living comfortably in Dawn City, not only having its injuries treated but also eating its fill every day.
One-eyed Giants were not inherently evil or bloodthirsty, and Lide had strictly ordered that no one could harm humans or damage houses and streets in Dawn City.
With the control of the Soul Contract, this group of One-eyed Giants dared not violate the command.
So, these few days, the One-eyed Giants had familiarized themselves with the humans in Dawn City.
Humans also realized that these One-eyed Giants weren’t as temperamental as they had imagined, and they were even happy to help with chores as long as they were given something to eat.
These giants, with the intelligence of a twelve or thirteen-year-old human child, were soon coaxed thoroughly by humans and developed a fondness for this place.
It was somewhat like humans jointly raising a few pets.
Lide found it amusing upon hearing this news; it seemed a magical power had emerged in the city he had built by hand.
Humans no longer feared other unusual races.
Yet, this was a good thing. An inclusive city was indeed a more attractive city.
“These big guys, loafing around eating for free isn’t right.
Let Cosso lead their people to mine the ore, hmm, set a fair amount, they can get enough food to be full as long as they complete the work each day.
And the more they complete, the more food they get.”
For these big guys, Lide believed there was nothing more tempting than the prospect of a full stomach.
“As for Cosso, we can give him some extra tasks, after all, this bastard has three wives and six children to feed.”
Speaking of this, Lide chuckled a bit; a One-eyed Giant with three wives and six children was really something.
These immensely strong individuals were definitely good at mining ore; Lide believed they wouldn’t be slower than machines.
He had seen Cosso himself swinging a Wolf Fang Club, shattering the ground.
That strength, if used in mining, would surely be effective.

chapters.title: Chapter 135: 135 I Want the Nine Dragons Chariot
chapters.content:
Chapter 135: Chapter 135 I Want the Nine Dragons Chariot
“`
However, to get the One-eyed Giants to mine ore, the key now was to prepare suitable tools for these big guys.
Despite their astonishing strength stemming from their Ancient Giant Bloodline, they couldn’t possibly mine with their bare hands.
And human-sized pickaxes and sledgehammers looked like chopsticks in the hands of a One-eyed Giant, utterly useless.
So right now, what we needed was to custom-make a batch of fitting weapons for these big fellows.
“Harrison, bring Biso to the blacksmith shop.”
...
“Do you want to make mining tools for the One-eyed Giants?”
He then had a somewhat odd expression on his face.
“Clan Leader, although the One-eyed Giants may be rather clumsy, they are incredibly powerful creatures. To use them for mining, might we not…”
He didn’t finish his sentence, but the implication was clear.
Harrison might not like wars, but he had a soft spot for such honest creatures like the One-eyed Giants.
If we could equip these big guys with heavy armor and weapons, they would certainly become an incredibly formidable fighting force.
For the Bloodline, who lacked ground troops, this was considered a significant supplement.
Lide shook his head, “No, Dawn City does not need to wage war externally for now. We want to use these big fellows for production.
Take them to the blacksmith shop, forge a batch of suitable pickaxes and sledgehammers for them to mine with. I believe there’s nothing more urgent than this.”
Harrison shrugged, looking somewhat regretfully at the One-eyed Giants playing and roughhousing outside the window.
It seemed that the sight of One-eyed Giants in heavy armor charging through an enemy’s army was not something we would witness anytime soon.
The blacksmith shop was established in the northern part of the central area, not far from the city walls. For a long time to come, ironware would remain a controlled item in Dawn City.
During World War II on Earth, steel production was an important indicator of a country’s strength. Although Glory was a Magic World, the role of steel here wasn’t any less significant than on Earth.
By the time Lide arrived at the blacksmith shop, Harrison had already brought Biso and another One-eyed Giant there.
The two huge figures, like small mountains, completely blocked the entrance to the blacksmith shop.
“Master~”
“Master~”
Upon seeing Lide’s figure, the two One-eyed Giants greeted him respectfully.
Their voices rumbled like muffled thunder, sounding sincere and naive.
They had great respect for this master who could feed them.
Koso was doing fine; his intelligence was already comparable to that of humans, although he was still very naive, having not been exposed to human society for long.
But the other One-eyed Giants were different, they only had the intelligence of a twelve or thirteen-year-old human. Although not dumb, their thinking was rather immature, the sort that could be easily tricked with some coaxing.
Just the fact that they could be well-fed in Dawn City was enough to make them incredibly happy.
“Koso, Dawn City will no longer provide free food to you in the future.”
Ah?
Koso panicked at Lide’s words. These past few days, they had eaten well and lived comfortably in Dawn City. Now, if there were no food, would they have to return to those hungry days?
Who would want to go hungry when they could eat their fill? Capitalism’s sugar-coated bullets had already corrupted Koso to the point where he could never go back to that simple era where a mouthful to fill the stomach was satisfying.
“Master, Koso is willing to fight for you, as long as you continue to provide food. Even at the cost of life, the One-eyed Giants will not fear!”
Koso patted his chest firmly, giving a spirited promise.
Lide couldn’t help but laugh and cry at this fellow who was willing to humble himself for a mouthful of food. If he had known this would happen, why would he have ever bothered?
“Koso, you will have to earn your own food in the future. I will provide an excellent job for you—mining ore.
The blacksmith shop will forge tools that are right for you; the iron mines in Giant Valley will be yours to mine.
In the future, I will employ you in exchange for food and Gold Puck. The more ore you mine, the more food and Gold Puck you will receive. You and the other One-eyed Giants won’t go hungry.”
Upon hearing this, Koso’s eyes instantly lit up.
He knew about mining. The Thunder Tribe in the Underworld had a mine, and they would trade the ores they mined with the Half-Elves’ cities in exchange for food and weapons.
The job was simple and well-suited for them.
“Master, I am willing.”
Koso’s voice was full of joy; not having to go hungry was the greatest happiness for a One-eyed Giant.
These strong creatures, accustomed to hunger, had no idea how low their demands were.
Lide nodded in satisfaction. These big guys might not be the brightest, but they were obedient and did not create any trouble; well-fed, they were as docile as puppies.
“`
“Very well.
Harrison, go call the head of the blacksmith shop over here.”
Soon enough, Harrison was leading a white-haired old man with a face full of gray beard, short in stature but extremely sturdy, before Lide.
“Good day, honorable Kachar City Lord. I’m the person in charge of the blacksmith shop, Gold Mining. It is an honor to heed your command.”
Lide looked at Gold Mining, who only reached his chest in height but whose muscles couldn’t be concealed even by his clothes, with some curiosity.
“Mr. Gold Mining, are you part of the Human Clan?”
Gold Mining laughed heartily.
“Kachar City Lord, I am half-human, half-dwarf. My veins carry half of the dwarf bloodline.”
Lide then realized, dwarves had quite a reputation in the Glory World.
Although they were short, their bodies were incredibly strong, and dwarves loved forging weapons the most. Weapons crafted by dwarves were absolutely top quality, a fact unanimously recognized in the Glory World.
“Mr. Gold Mining, can you help forge mining tools suitable for the One-eyed Giant?
As you might have heard, we found an extremely rich iron mine outside Dawn City, in Giant Valley. We need workers to mine the ore, and One-eyed Giants are undoubtedly the best choice, but the lack of tools has troubled me.”
Lide’s words filled Gold Mining with admiration, “Kachar City Lord, your far-sighted vision is worthy of praise from the Forge God.
If it were those shortsighted, vile human nobles, the first thing they would think of would be using One-eyed Giants to draw their carriages.”
Hearing this, Lide was momentarily taken aback.
One-eyed Giants pulling carriages?
Sounds quite ostentatious?
Imagine Koso, the One-eyed Giant with gray wrinkled skin immune to the powers of a Three Circle Mage, seven blades tall, of level 15, muscles exploding with raw strength, his intimidating presence nothing short of terrifying, pulling his carriage.
That seems quite a sensation.
He was tempted.
But after contemplating it, Lide still suppressed this alluring idea.
In the future, when Dawn City flourishes, not only One-eyed Giants, but he would enslave two giant dragons to pull the carriage, no, nine.
Lide gritted his teeth in determination.
Nine Dragons Chariot, it’s just that imposing.
“But that’s for the future. Can you forge tools that large?”
Crafting ordinary tools and making large-scale equipment are not on the same level of difficulty; the larger they are, the harder it is to make, especially in this world lacking modern machinery.
Gold Mining’s dark face showed a hint of difficulty, even with the forging talent from his dwarf bloodline, he felt troubled.
“Kachar City Lord, with the current manufacturing technology of the blacksmith shop, it’s very hard,”
he said before turning to look at the empty blacksmith shop. Even the most brilliant blacksmith couldn’t create a Divine Artifact without tools and materials.
“Is there anything challenging?” Lide asked directly.
“If you could get the assistance of 100 members of the Holy Light Bloodline, no, maybe 50 would be enough. I have confidence to give it a try.
But the steel needed for forging…”
“I will have 100 Bloodline members assist you. I can’t find more steel right now.
But the blacksmith shop should still have thousands of farming tools not yet distributed, right? Melt down these iron tools for me to recast.”
Hearing this decisive statement, Gold Mining nodded without hesitation.
“As you command, Kachar City Lord, I will forge mining tools that will satisfy you.”
“Hmm, good, let me know if there are any more difficulties. Koso, you stay here to assist Gold Mining with the testing.”
After giving his instructions, Lide turned and left.
But as he walked away, he was still thinking about what Gold Mining, the man with half dwarf bloodline, had said.
One-eyed Giants pulling carriages…
Why does that have such a visual impact?
Why is it so appealing?
As the Lord of Dawn, the Blood Clan Ancestor, the master of the Crimson Mage Tower, using a One-eyed Giant to pull a carriage wouldn’t be excessive, right?
At least it should be giant dragons pulling the carriage to match his status…

chapters.title: Chapter 136: 136 This Time We're Going to Make a Fortune
chapters.content:
Chapter 136: Chapter 136 This Time We’re Going to Make a Fortune
The idea of using a giant dragon to pull a cart greatly excited Lide Kachar, but thinking about the various legends surrounding the giant dragon, he suppressed the fervor in his heart.
Enslaving a giant dragon, though fascinating, would require a level of strength that would strain even Green City, a metropolis overseen by an Extraordinary Mage.
To achieve this one day, more effort was needed.
When the number of the Bloodline surpassed ten thousand, it might become feasible.
Koso, the One-eyed Giant, knew where to find a Black Dragon, and he hadn’t forgotten the affairs of the underworld; once he became more powerful…
After Lide left, the half-blood smith named Gold Mining, who had a distinctly Dwarven-style name, gathered all the blacksmiths to discuss.
...
Helping a One-eyed Giant, standing six or seven blades tall, to forge mining weapons was no easy task, considering the sheer size was enough to perplex the current rudimentary blacksmithing facilities.
The simple-minded appearance of Koso gave Gold Mining a headache.
He couldn’t help but frown in distress.
Lide was unaware of the great challenge he had posed to the blacksmiths as he turned his attention to another matter when they were worried.
The Dawn Church had been completed.
Driven by her fervent study of divinity, Emi, nearly without sleep, constantly supervised the construction site and repeatedly urged the workers to accelerate the construction of the church.
Under Emi’s strong insistence, the church, originally converted from an abandoned manor, was built in just a few days.
Although it lacked the luxury and refinement of the grand churches in Green City, it was more than sufficient for the needs of Dawn City, which lacked everything.
The most critical aspect was that Emi could now preach openly.
The Dawn Sect, a sect that had just been named a few days ago, was ready to make a significant impact.
In Emi’s view, divine beings were just a group of stronger creatures and weren’t worthy of worship.
Possessing the title of “blasphemer,” he had never held divinities in high regard; while he respected their power, he felt no fear towards them.
But now, the Ancestor of the Bloodline, the great Kachar Crown, possessed the key to becoming one of these powerful beings.
To Emi, an individual obsessed with power, this was a divine gift from the Goddess of Luck.
He could hardly wait.
In the eyes of the common people, divine beings were omnipotent; they were powerful, possessed eternal life, and could arbitrarily decide the life and death of commoners—all of which commanded their reverence.
The spread of faith was often due to powerful and mysterious unknown forces, and Emi, having spent decades as a priest in the Knight Temple, fully understood this.
Thus, he was confident that he could quickly establish the Dawn Sect as the sole and universally revered sect in Dawn City.
He was filled with confidence.
Lide attended the inauguration of the church, or rather, he unveiled a new era.
From this day forward, Dawn City would witness the rise of a new, singular sect.
Outside the Dawn Church, ten girls clad in pristine white priest robes and holding bouquets of flowers stood against the wind, their robes fluttering and the fragrance of the flowers filling the air.
In the chilling winter season, this was a strikingly vibrant sight.
“Ancestor Crown, the Dawn Church is grand because of your arrival.”
“Welcome, great Kachar Crown.”
After Emi led the bow, the row of girls behind him bowed deeply in unison, their eyes filled with profound admiration.
These were the Temple Saintesses that Emi had personally selected, each girl possessing innate Casting Talent, destined to become priests in the future.
With nearly ten thousand people in Dawn City, finding a few beautiful and appropriate-aged girls was not difficult.
Lide slightly nodded, gazing at the church that now belonged to him.
Since it was a renovation, the reliefs and color murals still bore a distinct Bloodline style.
The church, twelve blades high with four levels, was built from white boulders; under the evening light, it exuded a unique sandblasted texture of the rocks.
Entering through the white door carved with a relief of a Bloodline spreading its wings, he stepped into the first-floor hall.
The church hall housed over 500 wooden seats, surrounded by pristine white walls that emanated an indescribable sanctity.
Directly opposite in the center of the church was a vibrant, four-blade-high colored relief of a majestic figure.
The figure in the relief seemed as if standing right before them, monumental and imposing.
Behind him spread large, striking bat wings, as if he had just returned from annihilating worlds in the abyss.
The fangs visible on his lips marked his identity as a Bloodline.
Behind him, powerful creatures—giants, Titans, Elves, giant dragons, Great Demons, Six-winged Angels, and others—were all kneeling in submission.
This varicolored relief instantly awed all who saw it, undoubtedly carved by a master skilled in the craft.
Watching the relief, which bore his exact likeness, Lide’s lips twitched slightly.
Being sculpted on a wall like this… it truly was an indescribable feeling.
“Ancestor Crown, it was I who personally carved this.”
Emi’s eyes also held deep satisfaction, having carved religious murals for decades at the Knight Temple, but this one was his most satisfying.
“Enough said about that.
Do you have any thoughts on the proselytizing plan?”
Lide stared intently at Emi.
A beautiful building was nice, but ultimately, the Dawn Church had to engage in proselytizing—the goal was to harness the power of faith, not just to construct a pretty structure.
He only had Oli as a believer and could only acquire one point of the power of faith each day, which was hardly enough for research.
Lide’s understanding of the power of faith was still very basic. He knew it was a form of very advanced energy, but how to use it remained a complete mystery.
His knowledge of the power of faith had been imparted by Emi, a Level 15 Shadow High Priest, who also had only a Level 15 understanding and whose knowledge benefited from an incursion into the Knight God’s Divine Country.
Thus, both were quite confused.
Lide felt like he had been given the key ingredients to build nuclear weapons but had no idea how to actually create them.
Establishing the Dawn Sect was meant to build the metaphorical nuclear weapons of this world.
Regarding the power of faith, Lide felt it wasn’t even comparable to magic power in terms of energy fluctuation, but he was aware of his limited understanding. Were nuclear weapons even on the same level as TNT in equivalent mass?
He needed a key to unlock this puzzle, and the Dawn Sect was that key.
“Ancestor Crown, leave the preaching of the Dawn Sect to me. After the Frost Month, you will see a completely different Dawn Sect.
If there’s any change in your power of faith during this period, I hope you can inform me immediately.”
For Emi, who had spent decades as a priest in the Knight Temple, preaching was not a significant issue, especially in Dawn City, where he had the absolute home-ground advantage.
There weren’t any external sects competing for believers here; if he couldn’t develop in such an environment, he truly might as well commit suicide out of guilt.
“Good, what do you need me to do for the church now?”
Emi smiled slightly, respectfully gesturing toward the high platform in front of the colorful relief.
“You need to stand there and announce the establishment of the Dawn Sect, including your divine position.”
Was this like an opening ceremony?
Lide looked at Emi’s serious expression and couldn’t help but smile a little.
The Dawn Church had just opened its doors, and few wanted to venture out in the cold winter, so besides the 10 young girls, only he and Emi remained inside the church.
Well, let’s start off on the right foot.
Under everyone’s gaze, Lide stepped forward to the high platform of the church, his penetrating gaze sweeping over the pristine white walls, a solemn feeling rising inexplicably within him.
He straightened his expression.
“I, Kachar, here declare the establishment of the Dawn Sect, whose doctrine shall be…”
Suddenly, a phrase from the news popped into Lide’s mind.
“To continually become stronger, fight tenaciously, remain united, be fearless, love family and country.”
That seemed alright, didn’t it?
Lide glanced down at Emi’s somewhat baffled look, cleared his throat, disregarded his reaction, and continued,
“As a deity of the Holy Light Bloodline and Blood, in the name of the Blood Clan Ancestor and the master of the dawn, I announce”
“The official establishment of the Dawn Sect!”
After the last sentence, a sudden system notification in his mind left him stunned.
This works???
“Ding, Lide Kachar declares the establishment of the Dawn Sect, divine positions: Bloodline and Blood, doctrine: Keep constantly striving to become stronger, fight tenaciously, remain united, be fearless, love family and country.
Detection of Lide Kachar possessing the city—Dawn City, possessing the race—Holy Light Bloodline, possessing one fanatic believer.
Minimum requirements for the establishment of the sect met, Dawn Sect established.”
