Stanley cursed, and his magic power instantly gathered, ready to cast the Three Circle Magic – a Dark Magic Ball held in his hand in just a second.
But at that moment, rumble~
The ground shook.
Unnoticed by all, the One-eyed Giant Cosso, who had been scorched at thousands of degrees for minutes and thought by everyone to be near death, suddenly opened his huge one-eye.
His mountain-like sturdy arm propped against the scorched earth as he heaved himself up.
The air was instantly filled with a suffocating feeling, and the ambiance around him visibly darkened.
The giant one-eye, fierce and ferocious, his nostrils flaring with hot breath, and his slightly opened mouth revealed tusks sharper than razors.
His enormous body, with grey-white wrinkled skin, shimmered with a metallic luster, standing seven blades tall, his muscles as if cast from steel.
Cosso, now revived with the Ancient Giant Bloodline, was filled with an indescribable sense of power.
The Bronze One-eyed Giant—Cosso Thunder.
Had awakened.
Stanley’s pupils shrank suddenly, releasing both Three Circle Magic Spells at once.
Bang bang~
The Dark Magic Ball devoured all surrounding energy.
The grievously injured Lide had no chance to dodge.
Seeing this, Cosso’s one-eye glared fiercely, and with two steps forward, he swung his palm through the air,
Splat~
The huge palm collided with the Dark Magic Ball, but to Stanley’s shock, the Three Circle Magic was extinguished by Cosso with a single slap.
Extinguished as if swatting a fly!
The two Three Circle Magic Spells didn’t even have the privilege to leave a mark on this One-eyed Giant.
“How is this possible?! Although One-eyed Giants have high Magic Resistance, they couldn’t possibly ignore the damage from Three Circle Magic so easily!”
Stanley watched in disbelief.
The formidable level of the One-eyed Giant was beyond his expectations.
And he had watched from the shadows as Vampire spells scorched this One-eyed Giant for minutes.
Even if undead, it couldn’t possibly return to normal in just a few minutes, right? His mind was filled with confusion and amazement.
But Lide paid no heed to that, his gaze cold with killing intent flaring up.
“Cosso, kill them.”
“Cosso obeys your command.”
The echoing, booming voice, like distant thunder, in Ancient Giant language, pierced directly to the soul.
Stanley’s face held a trace of gravity as, behind him, Kolong was also fraught with surprise. The One-eyed Giant, whom Kolong thought had lost its combat effectiveness, had unexpectedly regained its full strength.
Even more powerful than before, it seemed.
What was this all about? Could Magic Attacks now differentiate between friend and foe?
Kolong, the Level 17 Dark Bishop, was filled with bafflement and confusion.
Flap-flap~
Simultaneously, the Magic Language Bats previously driven away by Groot once again enveloped the sky.
The heavily injured Bloodline members took this opportunity to transform into bats and scatter in flight, and the One-eyed Giants, in worse shape due to their size, also dragged their battered bodies backwards.
After Stanley’s twisted sense of bravado led him to make a few extra remarks, the situation on the ground shifted immediately.
It seemed villains always died because they talked too much.
“Attack!”
Although severely injured, Lide did not retreat a single step.
Even though the Bloodline and One-eyed Giants were exhausted and their condition greatly worsened, they couldn’t afford to lose this fight – losing this time would be a hundred times worse than losing to Groot.
If they lost, all the Bloodline and One-eyed Giants here would be killed.
No one could accept that outcome.
The Magic Language Bats in the sky, under the command of the Bloodline, began a frenzied dive attacking the two believers of the Evil God.
The Bloodline members who still hadn’t lost their combat capabilities quickly regrouped.
They began to provide intermittent magical support.
On receiving the command, Cosso charged at the two believers of the Evil God first.
After becoming a Bronze One-eyed Giant, he felt a significant increase in strength—he needed a battle to test his new power.
For Dawn City!
Boom-boom-boom~
The earth shook with Cosso’s charge.
The moment Lide had given the command, Stanley and Cosso were immediately entangled by the fearless Magic Language Bats.
Even if they wanted to ignore these massive bats, attacking Lide and the other Bloodline members was impossible.
Though of lower level, the giant size of the Magic Language Bats was there for all to see.
In this world, there were no fictional concepts like health bars; even a Level 7 Magic Language Bat might deliver a fatal blow if it hit a Level 15 Dark Priest’s neck.
Though entangled, the two believers of the Evil God were, after all, top combatants, and their strength was far beyond that of the Magic Language Bats.
And unlike ordinary spellcasters, their spells had very short casting times, even the Three Circle Magic could be cast in a second or two, effectively turning them into magic machine guns.
Every few seconds, a Magic Language Bat would fall, the ground’s trembling never stopped.
The Magic Language Bats suffered heavy casualties in the brief encounter.
Seeing this, Lide felt no pity; Magic Language Bats were not an irreproducible resource—they could be created again given time.
But now, if they couldn’t finish off these two believers of the Evil God, it would be their end.
Mercy does not command an army.
Emi, witnessing this scene, had a bitter expression. As a fellow spellcaster, these protected priests exhibited far greater destructive power.
Simultaneously, he vowed inwardly that after this, he must learn more spells to boost his strength, so he wouldn’t need the Vampire Ancestor’s help in the future.
The battle turned intense immediately following Lide’s command.
The desperate Bloodline disregarded all costs.
The Magic Language Bats risked their lives to fiercely restrict their two opponents’ movements, while Cosso, the Bronze One-eyed Giant, took on the role of main attacker.
Holding a Wolf Fang Club from another One-eyed Giant, his monstrous form could shatter the earth with a single swing.
Numerous huge pits formed during the combat.
Furthermore, after his advancement, Cosso’s magic resistance was absurdly high; Stanley and Kolong’s dark magic could not harm Cosso at all.
The bloodline of the Bronze One-eyed Giant was directly immune to Four Circle Magic, and the strongest spells the two had were merely Four Circle.
Thus, the previously fierce Stanley and Kolong were immediately overwhelmed by Cosso with the aid of the Magic Language Bats.
Boom~
Magic power burst forth, a frightful tide of energy sweeping across the surroundings.
Four Circle Magic, Void Devour.
Stanley fought desperately to hold Cosso back, buying the Dark Bishop Kolong a precious bit of time.
After a brief casting, Kolong deployed his most powerful spell—Void Devour.
Void Devour: Creates a void that devours the enemy, banishing them to a different plane.
Suddenly, the space in front of Cosso fractured, a massive black hole engulfing the risen Cosso.
Numerous Magic Language Bats, unable to react in time, were torn to pieces by the closing space.
Relieved at this sight, Stanley breathed a sigh of relief, for the One-eyed Giant had been too fierce, overpowering him alone.
Void Devour was a spatial banishing spell, not a direct effect spell, hence high magic resistance was ineffective against it.
“Kill that damned Vampire Ancestor!”
Dark Bishop Kolong’s voice was filled with rage. What was supposed to be an easy hunting trip turned out to be so humiliating due to one One-eyed Giant.
With a fierce grin, Stanley advanced, casting a Dark Sphere at the spellcasting Bloodline member ahead.
Clash~
A massive burst of energy erupted, and over ten Bloodline members who couldn’t dodge in time were instantly blasted into corpses.
The other Bloodline members began to retreat as the number of those able to fight had fallen below fifty, with the majority of them having sustained severe injuries.
Stanley swept his gaze around and immediately spotted Lide commanding from the Bloodline’s back lines.
“Perhaps you should be thankful, to die at the hands of the faithful of the great God of Tyranny.”
Stanley shouted across a distance of dozens of blades.
Joy unspeakable filled his eyes.
Once again, he formed a Dark Magic Ball in his hand.
Just then—bang!
Crack!
The sound of a heavy weapon hitting a wall rang out, and the space recently devoured by Cosso shattered like glass.
A gigantic hand reached out from the void, slamming into Stanley.
The fragile Mage Shield burst instantly.
Blood spewed out as he was thrown backward.
Crack!
The space shattered completely, and Cosso’s robust body reappeared unscathed; the Void Devour had no effect.
Stanley and Kolong’s expressions turned ugly.
“This damned One-eyed Giant, his Magic Resistance is too high, we can’t inflict any damage on him.”
Rage filled Stanley’s eyes, for spellcasters feared nothing more than encountering creatures with extremely high Magic Resistance.
Because powerful magic was ineffective against them, even the strongest spellcasters would feel powerless.
Moreover, the opponent’s strength was significantly high, and one could easily be killed in an instant.
“We can’t go on like this. The glory of the God of Tyranny must not be challenged!”
Then, Kolong did something that stunned everyone.
“Great God of Tyranny, your most loyal believer begs you to grant him power.”
The Level-17 Dark Bishop Kolong raised both hands above his head and then knelt fiercely to the ground, reciting this prayer in the Abyssal Blasphemy language.
Moments later.
A gaze of indescribable authority passed through countless planes and fixed on this spot, and under everyone’s shocked looks, Kolong’s body began to rise, inch by inch, with yellow and blue flames erupting all around him.
Bang, bang, bang!
Little by little, he transformed.
Two blades, three blades, five blades… At last, Kolong, the Level-17 Dark Bishop, had grown to a height of ten blades, and his body was no longer made of flesh and blood but had become a demonic form composed entirely of rock.
The true creature from the abyss—Molten Demon.
Cosso was now entirely made of rock, with yellow and blue intertwined flames exuding from him, the horrifying heat distorting the space around him.
Each step he took left a fiery red footprint on the ground; even the rocks nearby would melt into magma in less than ten seconds if they were within his vicinity.
Molten Demon (Transformation)
Level: 19
???
???
Lide could see the attributes which were very simple, yet their simplicity made him gasp in awe.
After transforming, Dark Bishop Kolong had reached Level 19, while his opponent Cosso was only Level 16.
He didn’t have much time to think, as after transforming into the Molten Demon, Kolong charged towards the bronze One-eyed Giant.
Cosso was not to be outdone. His huge one eye radiating a ferocious glare, he emitted a stunning roar and charged.
Bang!
Cosso’s massive Wolf Fang Club smashed violently towards the Molten Demon’s head, but the Molten Demon blocked with his right hand, the heavyweight club causing no damage whatsoever.
The Molten Demon punched Cosso’s chest, which made his pain increase and his glare all the more ferocious.
This was a battle between giants.
The sky shattered, and the sea roared; the entire valley seemed to be in the midst of an earthquake.
The battle between the Molten Demon and the One-eyed Giant suddenly quieted the scene.
Everyone stayed far from the battlefield because no one wanted to be accidentally crushed by them.
The ground crumbled under the battle of the two giants.
Rumble, rumble—
Unexpectedly, something occurred again that surprised everyone.
“Great God of Tyranny, your most loyal believer begs you to grant him power,” Stanley called upon the Evil God once more, now that Cosso was no longer entangling him.
As expected, that malevolent and potent aura appeared once again.
God of Tyranny Bain.
Even separated by countless planes, the power of the Evil God left everyone breathless.
Initially matching the Molten Demon blow for blow, Cosso’s soul suddenly trembled, a wave of excruciating pain rushed through him, and his massive body fell to his knees.
Five Circle Magic: Soul Shock.
The Evil God Bain had personally cast the spell across countless planes.
Even Cosso, who had high magic resistance, had suffered a heavy blow in the face of Five Circle Magic, because it was a spell cast by a deity.
Stanley’s face showed intense pleasure, Divine Descent was the most powerful Divine Art of the Late Bell Church, usable only once every three months.
Its sole purpose was to briefly summon the will of a deity to attack the enemy.
That was a deity, after all, even if it couldn’t affect the Main Plane too much, but just casting it once could determine the outcome of a war.
The Molten Demon, seizing the opportunity, grabbed Cosso’s two legs, swung him around like a sack a few times, and then slammed him onto the ground.
Bang~
The head of the One-eyed Giant fiercely smashed into the ground, causing a burst of spiderweb cracks, and debris of mud and rocks flew everywhere.
Cosso, having been struck by the Five Circle Magic attack, had no strength left to counterattack.
The outcome was decided.
The scene fell into a death-like silence, even the fearless Bloodline couldn’t help but fall quiet.
They no longer had the ability to defeat a Level 19 Molten Demon.
The strongest fighters, Cosso and Emi, had both been heavily injured, who else could fight?
Lide raised his head and looked around.
A bitter smile flickered in his eyes, the battle had reached a point where they were out of options.
Then a hint of coldness flashed through his eyes.
“Entire Bloodline, assemble, prepare to attack.”
Northern warriors, fearless, undaunted.
The Bloodline had never retreated even half a step!
Seeing this scene, Stanley couldn’t hold back his inner sneer, his brutal face thick with scorn.
“Weak vampires, kneel and accept your fate.”
The Molten Demon also uttered a chilling voice.
“Death, destruction.”
The Abyss’s blasphemous language was terrifying and cold.
The air was filled with an aura of desolation, and the Bloodline, regardless of their severe injuries, silently assembled.
Even faced with an almost insurmountable enemy, not one of them backed down.
Just a second before Lide ordered the attack,
A scornful, crisp voice echoed through the valley.
“So weak indeed.”
“A demon who has power but knows not how to use it can boast of its strength.”
“What a dull battle.”
Lide abruptly turned his head, and a lady with a wild beauty, wearing a leather skirt and short boots appeared in his sight.
The atmosphere changed instantly, everyone confusedly looked towards the newcomer.
Tat-tat-tat~
The wild-eyed lady stepped forward under everyone’s gaze, slowly pulled out a giant sword that was stuck in the ground, and effortlessly lifted it.
Her tall, slender figure holding the giant sword strangely provided a sense of harmony, as if this lady was meant to wield this weapon that should belong to an armored warrior.
Seeing this, the two Evil God believers frowned, not taking this abruptly appearing woman seriously.
“Foolish woman, kill her!”
The voice of the Molten Demon boomed like thunder.
Stanley, hearing this, his lips curled into a wicked smile, and he cast a spell with both hands.
Two Dark Magic Balls carrying lethal intent flew towards the wild lady holding the giant sword.
Death descends.
Stanley even imagined the scene of the opponent being blasted to pieces.
Under everyone’s gaze, the fair-skinned lady with wild eyes raised her eyebrow, showed no sign of retreat, and directly moved forward with her sword,
Striking directly down at the two Dark Magic Balls.
“Idiot!” Stanley’s smile just began to form, but in the next second, it abruptly stopped.
“How, how is this possible!?”
The two Dark Magic Balls were cleaved into quarters by the giant sword and then dissipated into magical elements vanishing in the air.
Unscathed.
Seeing the faint glow on the giant sword, Stanley was hugely shocked.
“Fearless! Extreme!! You, you are a Northern Warrior, no, you are from the Northern Royal Family!!”
Stanley’s eyes widened to their fullest.
His voice sharp with astonishment.
“How is this possible, don’t you need the blood of the Golden Race to recover?
How is this possible?? Could there be a giant dragon here??”

chapters.title: Chapter 181: 182: Wild, Sexy, Powerful Woman (2-in-1)
chapters.content:
Chapter 181: Chapter 182: Wild, Sexy, Powerful Woman (2-in-1)
Hearing this, Lide’s head jerked up.
Because the Northern Land Valkyrie’s body was originally covered with bark-like scars, although she hadn’t changed her attire, the scars had vanished for some unknown reason.
Thus, he did not recognize her as the Northern Land Valkyrie immediately.
After he did, alarm shot through his heart. What about Isa??
He hastily opened the attribute panel and breathed a sigh of relief when he saw Isa was unharmed.
Isa was fine, but how had the Northern Land Valkyrie recovered??
...
Lide’s eyes were full of confusion as he opened the attribute panel of the other party.
Betty Smollett
Title:
Northern Pearl (The most dazzling gem of the Northern Plateau, dearly loved and respected by the Northern people, with a constant reputation of respect in the Northern Plateau)
Northern Land Valkyrie (The strongest female warrior of the Northern lands, boasting flawless skills and formidable bloodline, with constant mastery in various weapons and combat skills elevated to legendary)
Age: 27
Level: 16
Profession: Northern Warrior
Bloodline: Northern Royal Bloodline, possessing extraordinary traits: Fearless.
Bloodline activation grants immunity to pain, immunity to mental spells, triple strengthening of the extraordinary trait: Fearless, strength increases by 100%, stamina and life recovery speed increase by 1000%, and can mobilize the power of the bloodline to heal bodily injuries, duration: one Sunshine Hour.
Introduction: The youngest Valkyrie of the Northern lands, the brilliant Northern Pearl, with an infinite future for the Northern Royal Family.
Bond: Isa…?, both parties in the bond can acquire one bloodline talent from each other, bonds divided into primary and sub-bonds, the sub-bond must unconditionally obey the commands of the primary bond.
After reading through the attributes of the Northern Land Valkyrie, Lide’s eyes gleamed with deep surprise.
Such a powerful talent, worthy of the Northern Royal Bloodline, this strength.
Too strong.
Even Lide felt that the Northern Royal Bloodline might not be inferior to the talents of the Golden Race.
Too strong, Lide couldn’t help but exclaim a few more times.
And by looking at the attribute explanation, Isa was indeed involved in the revival of the Northern Land Valkyrie.
However, what relieved him was that he also saw a note about the bond on Isa’s panel; differently, Isa was the primary bond.
This eased his worries considerably.
He didn’t have time to think more about the implications as a fierce battle erupted before him.
The bloodline of the Northern Royal Family, the Northern Pearl, the youngest Valkyrie, with various titles, Betty’s combat strength was a whole level higher than this LVL 16 Northern Warrior Grotte.
Clang~
The tall and feral Betty took a step, her body speed surged.
The air seemed to be torn apart at that moment, a huge wave erupted.
Stanley’s face drastically changed, his hands casting another spell.
Bang Bang~
Two Bursting Fireballs were hurled out~
Crack~
Just like before, the Bursting Fireballs couldn’t get close to Betty and were sliced apart by her greatsword.
Legendary level combat skills were intimidatingly powerful.
Stanley, a follower of the Evil God, was raging with anger but had no choice but to retreat swiftly.
At this moment, Kolong, transformed into a LVL 19 Molten Demon, suddenly turned his head, his enormous arm smashing towards Betty.
The blue and yellow Abyss Demon Flame, with a temperature that could melt steel, came surging.
At this critical moment, when Betty could no longer dodge and everyone was holding their breath for her,
Her already strong aura soared.
Northern Royal Bloodline, activated.
The glow of the greatsword she wielded flared.
Fearless of anything, excitement flickered in Betty’s wild eyes as her strength exploded.
She struck at the arm of the Molten Demon, which was thrice thicker than her body.
Before everyone’s eyes, the ten-blade-tall Molten Demon’s fist, like a siege hammer imbued with Abyss Demon Flame, collided with the greatsword whose brilliance of the Northern light flared.
Crack~
The ground burst with a wave, the Abyss Demon Flame splashing, the searing air turning the debris that flew from the ground instantly red.
The scene was incredibly beautiful.
Countless stones and dirt splashed around the two combatants, scorched red by the heat, bursting like fireworks.
Wild Dance.
But an even more shocking scene ensued.
Betty’s longsword, after being briefly halted by the Molten Demon, swung again.
Crack, crack, crack~
Like cleaving through a massive boulder, Betty sliced through the arm of the Molten Demon right from its fist.
Countless rocks imbued with yellow and blue magic flames shattered, spilling onto the ground and melting into pools and holes of varying sizes of molten lava.
Ants shaking a tree.
Despite such a vast disparity in size, this member of the Northern Royal Family managed to sever half the arm of a Molten Demon with a single sword strike.
Then an even more astonishing scene occurred.
A sharp gleam flashed through Betty’s eyes, her warrior’s intuition pinpointing the behemoth’s weakness.
Her legs compressed like springs, unleashing powerful energy, and she leapt up.
After two steps up the Molten Demon’s arm, she appeared right in front of its eyes.
The Molten Demon, infuriated by such brazen provocation, let out a furious roar, its demon flames rapidly swelling, and at the same time, its right hand viciously hammered down toward Betty.
If she were hit, the Northern Pearl, strong as she was, would suffer grave injuries.
Betty’s wild eyes narrowed slightly, the glow on her greatsword intensifying to three blades.
Ignoring the arm about to smash into her, she held her sword with both hands through heat that could melt steel and, with all her might, slashed at the neck of the Molten Demon.
Her sword strike was like the Creator God splitting heaven and earth.
Crack~
The Molten Demon’s arm, on the verge of hitting Betty, came to a futile halt, and Betty’s body in the air also descended at that moment.
Thud~ On one knee, she planted the greatsword before her.
Around the pair in battle, yellow-blue Abyss Demon Flames flickered, and in the fiery red holes on the ground, lava flowed.
Behind her, the Molten Demon at that moment
Boom~
Its massive head soared into the air, finally carving a parabola before smashing into the ground beside Betty, kicking up a cloud of dust.
The large body of the Molten Demon behind her started to collapse slowly.
Boom~
Like a mountain collapsing, the ground shook violently.
The Bloodline observing this became enveloped in an indescribable atmosphere.
Their expressions turned vividly diverse as they watched the silhouette of Betty.
The Northern Royal Bloodline? Is this the true might of the Northern Royal Bloodline?!!
Immeasurably powerful, it was simply beyond description.
That was a Level 19 Molten Demon, even the bronze One-eyed Giant Kosoh was getting suppressed, but just like that, in two moves, it was annihilated??
Lide was no less shocked than the other Bloodline,
At this moment, he couldn’t help but recall the dense, more exaggerated than old tree bark, scars he had seen on Betty’s body.
What kind of battles had this wild lady endured to possess such formidable strength?
Were Legendary Level combat skills truly this powerful?
Compared to Betty, Grot, that exceedingly troublesome Level 16 Northern Warrior, was child’s play.
Was this the true potential of the first among the Glorious Three Warriors, the Northern Warrior?
No wonder she had earned this extreme honor among numerous powerful races.
Truly deserved.
The Molten Demon she faced, a Transformed Creature at Level 19, wasn’t truly a Level 19; Kolong could never express the Molten Demon’s power, not even half of it, so the combat strength was not on par with a full-fledged Level 19.
If it were a true Molten Demon, the outcome would surely have been different.
But, the victor is king, and no one cared about the reasons behind it—all they knew was that Betty had vanquished a Level 19 Molten Demon.
After the Molten Demon was beheaded, the spell summoning the demon disappeared, and the demon’s body on the spot slowly disintegrated, revealing Kolong, the Late Bell Church’s Level 17 Dark bishop, dead where he lay.
Summoning transformation spells, while granting immense strength, also meant that defeat would spell one’s own death.
Stanley, witnessing this, felt his brain consumed by fear.
If a Level 19 Molten Demon had been slain, could he escape??
Determined, amid everyone’s gaze, he pulled out a magic scroll thick with dark energy from his pocket.
Rip~
He tore it open directly.
Immediately following, an aura more potent and more sinister than Kolong’s Divine Descent emerged within the valley.
“Great God of Tyranny, your believer begs for your descent!!”
“Divine Descent had just been used, and the space that had been torn open was created by a magic scroll that Stanley had obtained by sacrificing a great deal of life.”
It served more or less the same purpose as Divine Descent, able to briefly open a space passage and allow the tyrannical god a short visit.
Though the strength of this arrival was diminished by countless times, it might not even reach the Transcendent level, but it was enough to deal with ordinary enemies.
This was Stanley’s final trump card. He couldn’t believe that a member of the Northern Royal Family would be so forceful in the face of divine power.
The great God of Tyranny was an eternal deity, no one could desecrate the deity’s dignity, no one!
The scene just now, where Kolong had transformed into a Molten Demon only to have his head severed by Betty’s sword, truly frightened him.
That scene was too exaggerated and horrific.
So Stanley was now reckless.
He no longer thought about how much prey or spoils of war he could obtain, but how he could survive.
Upon seeing the space gate slowly forming in the void above, Betty’s face showed a mocking smile.
Her eyes wild and untamed.
“A garbage Divine Descent? Really lacking in skill.”
The crisp tone carried a warrior’s unique pride.
She turned her head to look at a half-human-high stone on the ground and violently kicked it, sending the rock forcefully flying off the ground.
After running forward with ten or so strides, Betty exerted her strength from her legs, leaping nearly ten strides high into the air.
She landed perfectly on the rock, her body soaring even higher.
The technique was similar to Grott borrowing the Magic Language Bat’s body to step into the sky, the only difference was that this time the Northern Land Valkyrie faced the pressure of a divine entity.
Watching that damned Northern Royal Family storm towards the space gate twenty strides high, a hint of indescribable scorn appeared in Stanley’s eyes.
That was the power of a great deity. Did a damned Northern dare to shake a deity?
But before the smile on his face dissipated, a shocking scene unfolded.
Betty held her sword with both hands, the blade shining brightly for several strides with ultimate intent.
Without the slightest hesitation, she slashed directly at the newly formed space gate.
And at that moment, a black eye appeared within the space gate, its presence far more intense than that of a demon by a thousand times.”
“Wretched humans, submit to me, and I shall grant you eternal life and mighty power…”
Before the voice from within the space gate could finish, there was a crack—
The great sword fell.
As the newly formed space gate was struck by the sword augmented with ultimate intent, it burst apart instantly.
And the eyeball inside the gate was chopped into oblivion.
The God of Tyranny, Bain, in the bottomless abyss, didn’t even have a chance to react before losing the touch of the Main Plane.
Stanley’s face, previously full of confidence, turned ashen, disbelieving the sight before him.
These damned blasphemers!! How dare she, how dare she strike at a deity?!
“Next time I will surely punish you damned heretics, blasphemers, for my god!!”
After speaking, he immediately cast a Light Body and Concealing Skill on himself and without any hesitation, began to retreat.
But it was all in vain.
In the eyes of Betty, who had killed a level 19 Molten Demon in one blow and disregarded divine pressure, there were few who could slip away from under her watch.
Her Legendary Level combat skills were too formidable for words.
As Stanley stepped into the shadows, the greatsword flew out from behind him and knocked him down.
If it hadn’t been for the flat of the blade striking him, he would have likely been slain with a single blow.
Betty, dragging Stanley, who was now like a dead dog unable to move, tossed him in front of Lide.
“He’s yours.”
Then, this wild lady who belonged to the Northern Royal Family, capable of treating a level 19 Molten Demon like a dog and who brushed aside the pressure of a deity, did something that left Lide utterly astonished.
“Oi…pf…nq… Great deity of death and souls, I am your loyal servant, I am your most devout follower, I wish to use your power to sign a Soul Contract with my master. If the contract is broken, I will offer my soul, to serve you for all eternity, the great Death God.”
Lide was completely baffled by the operation of this combat powerhouse Valkyrie. What was going on?
After winning the fight, she wanted to sign a Soul Contract with me?
Betty straightened up, seeing the puzzlement in Lide’s eyes, and gave him a casual smile, winking at him.
“Isa told me to do this, my master. You handle things here yourself,” she said before turning to leave without giving Lide any face.
I…
Lide watched Betty leave, twisting her tall and spirited figure, his expression complex.
Although he had gained a Valkyrie with off-the-chart combat ability, why didn’t he feel as happy as he should?
He turned his head irritably to look at Stanley, who had been beaten by Betty into a state resembling a dead dog.
“Break his limbs and imprison him.”
After speaking, he turned his head to gaze at the surroundings, his expression slightly heavy.
“Take stock of the battle damage, treat the injured, and in addition, bring back the bodies of all the warriors who sacrificed themselves for Dawn City.
I want to hold a hero’s funeral for them.”
The landscape was desolate.
The valley, once filled with green trees and lush grass, had now become a wasteland.
The scorched trees, the holes left by the battles, the traces of explosions from the magic bombardments, and even many places were still emitting a pungent smoke.
It was like the aftermath of a giant dragon’s breath, everything had turned to ash and smoke.
Most of the bodies of the Northern Warriors that had littered the ground were now charred, and even the number of Magic Language Bats that had fallen exceeded two hundred.
Their giant bodies lay scattered across the valley like small hills.
The scene was tragic.
Lide looked at this scene and remained silent for a long time without speaking.
This was Dawn City’s first hard-fought battle.
In the previous fight against the One-eyed Giant Tribe, they had had enough advantage, completely pressing the enemy, but this time was different. The enemy was too strong.
Whether Groot, the Level 16 Northern Warrior, or Stanley and Kolong, the two Evil God believers, their strength was first-rate.
The top combat power of Dawn City was completely under pressure.
In the end, if it hadn’t been for Betty, the Northern Land Valkyrie being revived by Isa and making a strong move,
Even if they could win today, of the hundreds of Bloodline and the several hundred Magic Language Bats fluttering in the skies, perhaps fewer than ten would have remained.
It was too tragic; the casualties of this battle could truly be described as devastating.
“Ancestor Crown, the count is in,”
Half a Sunshine Hour later, Emi came to Lide, her tone respectful.
“Speak.”
Lide’s expression was not relaxed, and his gaze intensely fixed on the Shadow High Priest.
“One One-eyed Giant dead, forty-three Bloodline dead, seventy-eight seriously injured, and the rest with minor injuries. Two hundred and thirty-four Magic Language Bats dead, one hundred and ten seriously injured, with the rest having minor injuries.”
“Furthermore, all second-generation Bloodline are seriously wounded; Koso is seriously injured.”
Even though he had been prepared mentally, hearing these numbers still silenced Lide for a good while.
This battle had truly been fought to the limits, using every bit of strength available.
Emi looked at Lide’s eyes, conveying a hint of guilt. “Ancestor Crown, it is my lack of strength…”
Of course, the sight of Groot, the Northern Warrior, overwhelming her was still a sore point for this Level 15 blasphemer.
Lide shook his head, “How long have you been at Level 15? If you could defeat Groot, then the Northern Warriors would no longer hold the honor of being the strongest fighters among countless races.”
Lide was very clear about this; he knew the gap between them.
A fighting race known for its combat prowess pitted against a priest vastly weaker than himself; their strengths were not even on the same scale.
Emi’s strength lay in her functionality; if someone could cooperate with her, the various Shadow Skills of the Shadow Priest could have a powerful, amplifying effect.
Unfortunately, Koso, the One-eyed Giant, just couldn’t coordinate with Emi. Their ways of fighting were not even in the same concept.
“What about the spoils of war?”
“Twenty-three surviving Northern Warriors, including five Level 10 warriors.
The Level 16 Northern Warrior Groot, the Level 15 bishop of the Late Bell Church Stanley, plus, the Northern Royal Family….”
For other races, enemy captives who refuse to surrender are merely prisoners without much value.
But for the Bloodline, these captured enemies are far more precious trophies.
As long as they’re not dead, the Bloodline can turn the enemies into their own.
This is the most powerful and perverse aspect of the Bloodline; other races might see their numbers dwindle with war, but only the Bloodline and the Undead grow more numerous with conflict.
As long as casualties remain within a certain range in each battle, the power of the Bloodline will grow stronger with each fight.
This battle had many sacrifices, but as for gains, three Level 15 combatants could easily balance out these losses.
Even if they had only gained one Level 15 combatant, it would have been a profit.
Lide took a deep breath, his thoughts shifting to the Dark Contract.
Finally, they had the capital to contend with them.
He turned to glance at the bodies of Bloodline warriors lined up beside him, a glint of coldness flashing in his eyes.
These sacrifices would ultimately become nourishment, allowing Dawn City to grow stronger.
And you, will taste the fury of the Bloodline.
Dark Contract!!

chapters.title: Chapter 182: 183 When the Northern Warrior Becomes a Bloodline...
chapters.content:
Chapter 182: Chapter 183 When the Northern Warrior Becomes a Bloodline…
The Bloodline was still organizing the battlefield, and Lide watched the surroundings with sharp eyes.
A contemplative look flashed through his eyes.
The battle had been won… no matter the cost in lives.
And the spoils were the existence of three advanced warriors above Level 15.
These three top combat powers were dozens of times more valuable than the sacrificed Bloodline and Magic Language Bats combined.
It was a huge fortune.
...
This battle made Lide even more aware of what the Bloodline currently lacked—top combat power.
If he had started with Betty, the Northern Land Valkyrie, as a trump card in his hand, Lide was even confident that he could have ended this battle with zero casualties.
Thus, the Bloodline’s weaknesses must be compensated for; even with Betty’s addition, it was still not enough, the Bloodline needed greater strength.
Therefore, Lide was now urgently choosing between Stanley and Grote to transform one into a Bloodline.
Betty, with her Northern Royal Bloodline, would logically be the best choice, but now she had become Isa’s restraint and had also signed a Soul Contract with him.
She was already part of their camp, so Betty was excluded, leaving Grote and Stanley.
Logically, Lide should not be hesitating between Grote and Stanley, as Grote completely overpowered Stanley in terms of combat power.
However, there was a significant issue—the Late Bell Church had a vast influence within Green City.
This power hidden in the shadows was somewhat tempting to Lide.
If he transformed Stanley into a Bloodline, he could immediately possess the influence that the Late Bell Church had cultivated in Green City for decades.
In combating the Dark Contract, they could directly utilize the power of the Late Bell Church to fight them.
But conversely, although Stanley’s subordinates were just the Northern Warriors who had been killed or captured, having nearly no influence within Green City, his high combat power was enough to offset all of that.
If they gained Grote, a Northern Warrior capable of dominating Kosso and Emi in combat, in addition to having Betty, the high-end combat power of Dawn City would further increase.
Because of the Bloodline issues, Lide could only perform the initial embrace once a month, and the battle would commence in three days.
Therefore, he could only choose one between the two.
Ordinary Bloodline could only undergo the initial embrace once a year, and all the Bloodline had already gone through it during the Frost Month.
Moreover, even if some Bloodline had their initial embrace saved up, Lide could not afford to let them squander resources; in case the Bloodline Power was insufficient, causing a level decrease, the loss would be substantial.
Having steadied himself, Lide laughed a bit as he slapped his head; actually, the answer had always been clear, he was just coveting Stanley.
Grote’s role was currently much more significant than Stanley’s.
Without further hesitation, he decided on Grote in his heart.
The performance of high-end combat power had just been sufficient to explain everything; had Betty not appeared, whether the Bloodline could have survived at all was still debatable.
Even Emi and Kosso, two Level 15 beings, might not have survived.
This was the effect of high-end combat power—against lower-level professionals, it could display an overwhelming state.
“The Clan Leader, we are ready.”
Frey, a second-generation Bloodline who guarded the sacred land and had experienced the Battle of Green City a century ago, came forward to report to Lide.
Lide turned to look at Frey, whose originally blue Mage robe was no longer recognizable, covered in soot and dirt, with even a huge gash from a longsword across the chest.
The scene was dire.
He patted Frey on the shoulder, remaining silent.
In the recent battle, this second generation Bloodline had killed at least 7 Northern Warriors, including some 10th Level Advanced Professionals.
“We’re going home,” the tone carrying an inexplicable meaning.
“Yes,” Frey listened and was momentarily stunned, seeing Lide’s encouraging look made his eyes inexplicably well up. To hide his inner softness, he suddenly lowered his head and turned around quickly to leave.
Lide watched Frey’s retreating figure for a long time without speaking.
When the fate of a race was in his hands, it was great power but also great pressure.
Isa also came down from the mountain at this time, her face showing excitement as she approached Lide.
“Teacher~”
Looking at the happy-faced girl, and then looking back at Betty who was continuously giving Isa an indulgent smile, Lide felt somewhat emotional.
This little girl truly was a treasure given to him by the Goddess of Luck.
Isa, seeing Lide not speaking, felt a bit uneasy, cautiously glanced at him, then quickly explained.
“Teacher, I just awakened a special ability two days ago and hadn’t had the chance to tell you, just when Sister Betty—”
Lide smiled looking at those slightly anxious crimson eyes, and reached out to touch the girl’s head.
“Isa, don’t be nervous. You did very well. Most of the time, when unexpected things happen, you need to make decisions on your own.
In the future, it will be the same. When the teacher is not around, you need to learn to make decisions on your own.
As long as you seriously consider your own safety, the consequences of the issue, and you can bear the consequences, then boldly go ahead with it.”
At that moment, Lide was like an elder brother, teaching his younger sister to grow up.
With Lide’s encouragement, Isa’s crimson eyes shone with joy.
“Mhm~” The little girl felt very satisfied, thrilled to have helped her teacher~~
Betty quietly watched this scene from behind, feeling somewhat complex in her heart.
She suddenly recalled what she was doing at the age of fourteen or fifteen. Was she hunting snow wolves alone on the snowy mountains, or was she wrestling with giant water pythons in the ice river? It was a bit unclear…
Half a day later, seeing that the Bloodline preparations were about complete, Lide said with a hint of mystery,
“Today I will take you to a new city; that place will also be our new home.”
Betty, who hadn’t spoken until then, expressed her interest upon hearing this, “A Vampire’s ancient castle? I have been in the North for so many years but have never seen a Vampire’s lair.
Is it like the legends describe, built within dark caves, airtight, with bats hanging all around the ceiling, cold springs seeping through the rocks…”
Lide slightly twitched his mouth, “You’ll see when we get there.”
He finished speaking and no longer paid attention to this wild Northern Land Valkyrie.
Suddenly, he inexplicably remembered the female Elf he had met in front of Elvis Tavern—Ariel, the 17th level Master Archer.
Like Betty, Ariel also carried a wildness, but there was a clear distinction; Elves were renowned for their wealth and grandeur, whereas beneath Betty’s leather armor, there was nothing remarkable.
It might look better if the two switched places.
Lide looked amused.
He wondered who would win in a fight—the well-known talented Elf, or Betty with her Northern Royal Bloodline, capable of killing a 19th level Molten Demon in seconds?
It was a pity he wasn’t familiar with that Elf, otherwise having those two fight would have been spectacular.
Soon, the scene was set, all the Bloodline and Magic Language Bats awaited Lide’s command to take off.
Without delay, Lide mounted the leading bat and ordered them to fly.
Isa, with Betty’s support, also climbed onto the saddle-backed bat, hiding shyly in Lide’s arms as she looked up with anticipation at the Magic Language Bat sitting below.
It was Isa’s first flight on a Demon Beast, and the little girl felt both excited and frightened, clutching tightly at Lide’s robe.
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh~
The huge bat wings flapped, raising a choking black dust from the scorched earth beneath the valley.
The massive body of the Magic Language Bat slowly ascended, with the ground gradually shrinking below.
At that moment, the moon, which had been hidden behind the clouds, finally revealed itself, pouring down cold moonlight like mercury.
The landscape unfolded before everyone’s eyes.
The forests and mountains below were draped in a silver cloak, and among the howling mountain winds, swaying gracefully, every scene was adorned with a unique beauty by the moonlight.
The gloom in everyone’s hearts nearly disappeared under such a beautiful scene.
Isa leaned back slightly, feeling that firm chest and an indescribable sense of safety emerged, her eyes narrowing into crescents.
Betty, however, sat rather bored behind Lide. For her, as a member of the Northern Royal Family with her own Griffin, the flight rides in the Northern Plateau were nothing novel.
She was more looking forward to the ancient Vampire castle.
In human legends, Vampires often represent mystery and gore, and their lairs are considered terrifying.
As Bloodline did not exist in the North, naturally there would be no such mysterious buildings like Vampire castles in their legends.
Four Sunshine Hours later, the large group of bats returned to Dawn City.
Betty sat behind Lide, the three of them riding a single Magic Language Bat.
After crossing a valley, Betty saw from afar the city nestled among thousands of towering peaks.
Majestic and spectacular.
Admiration flickered in her eyes.
“Truly, this is fitting of a Vampire’s castle, beyond all expectations.”
Upon seeing his city, Lide immediately showed deep joy.
At this moment, he felt very much like a returning wanderer, filled with excitement and an inexplicable thrill.
After a grand battle, all of the Bloodline were exhausted, but upon seeing Dawn City from above, everyone cried out in excitement.
The sounds carried far into the empty night sky.
Without experiencing a life-and-death battle, without feeling the complex emotions of walking alive out from under the Death God’s scythe, one would hardly understand the Bloodline’s feelings at this moment.
When the Bloodline, filled with excitement, landed the Magic Language Bats in Dawn City, the patrolling Security Team members quickly spotted them.
Having redeployed most of the Bloodline for the past two days, the patrols of the Security Team had been significantly increased
The sight of countless injured Bloodline and Magic Language Bats astonished the security team members.
Especially when rows of bodies were laid out on the square, the atmosphere amongst the Security Team grew heavy.
“Quick, go report to Lord Harrison.”
“Where are the medical staff? Quick, fetch someone…”
“Hiss, so many bodies, what exactly did the Bloodline endure?!”
Upon receiving the news, Harrison, who was stationed in Dawn City, arrived immediately.
“Goodnight, Clan Leader,” Harrison said with a heavy expression, observing the Bloodline around him in disarray.
“Clan Leader, did we win this battle?”
Lide remained silent for a moment before nodding, his tone solemn.
“We won, though at a great cost. But all the heroes who sacrificed themselves will not be forgotten; Dawn City will grow stronger because of them.”
“Harrison, immediately arrange for the injured Bloodline members to be treated at the blood pool. Also, inform the breeding farm to prepare the pigs and heal the Magic Language Bats, which have also suffered significant damage.”
“I need them to recover completely within two days, not three.”
“Additionally, gather the remains of the heroes who died for Dawn City. I want to hold a public funeral for them in ten days.”
Lide issued several commands in quick succession, and finally, pointing to Grot, who was being guarded by the second-generation Bloodline and was still unconscious, he spoke with a resolute tone.
“Take him to the City Hall. After tonight, the Bloodline will have gained a powerful new Bloodline member.”
After finishing, Lide glanced at Betty, but she showed no reaction, as if Grot, the Northern Warrior, had nothing to do with her.
“Yes, Clan Leader,” Harrison, undisturbed by minor details, immediately went to prepare upon receiving the order.
After issuing his commands, Lide turned to look at Isa yawning and Betty, who was curiously observing Dawn City.
“Isa, Betty, you’ll rest at my estate tonight; I still have important matters to deal with today.”
Isa, looking a bit sleepy, obediently nodded. “Yes, Teacher.” She never argued with Lide’s words.
Betty, on the other hand, simply shrugged indifferently. Rather than resting, she was more interested in exploring this legendary vampire castle.
Curiosity indeed.
After Isa and Betty left with the Bloodline members, Lide immediately returned to his office in the City Hall.
At the same time, all the injured Bloodline members were taken to the blood pool.
As long as they weren’t dead on the battlefield, Lide wasn’t worried; the Bloodline’s innate talents guaranteed their robust life force.
Regardless of the severity of their wounds, they could quickly recover to normal with fresh blood—the talents of the Upper Race were unreasonably formidable.
“Prepare ten bottles of Magic Blood for me.”
“Yes, Clan Leader,”
After instructing Harrison, Lide walked to where Grot lay on the carpet.
Without any hesitation, he leaned down, picked up Grot’s wrist, and bit into it.
The mysterious power hidden within his bloodline began to infuse into Grot’s body.
Blood Clan Ancestor: You are the Ancestor of the Bloodline, possessing a powerful bloodline, immune to sunlight. You can develop one Bloodline member per month; all Bloodline members and their descendants will have unwavering loyalty to you, providing you with 1 character Experience point per month.
He had only first embraced Emi before, so the power uniquely belonging to the Bloodline was now intensely potent in his bloodline.
Grot had suffered severe injuries under the spells of nearly two hundred Bloodline members; had it not been for the robust constitution of the Northern Warrior, he would have already met with Death God.
Now, he could only lie on the ground and let Lide infuse the Bloodline power into him.
This formidable Northern Warrior began to transform as his surface skin, charred black, cracked open and regrew new skin, as if emerging from a cocoon into a butterfly.
The originally weak aura slowly steadied, and his life force grew from a flickering candle to a blazing torch.
The path of transformation and evolution had begun.
What fascinating reactions would occur after the Northern Warrior became part of the Bloodline?
Lide looked forward to it immensely.

chapters.title: Chapter 183: 184 Betty's Wonderful Journey in Dawn City
chapters.content:
Chapter 183: Chapter 184 Betty’s Wonderful Journey in Dawn City
The next morning, as dawn was just beginning to break, Betty, who was sound asleep on the large bed draped with a grey-white soft blanket, suddenly opened her eyes.
Something was amiss. This wasn’t the place she knew.
Those pitch-black eyes, sharp as a hawk’s, swiftly scanned the unfamiliar surroundings as she rolled over and grabbed the giant sword by the bed.
Her body slightly bent, she surveyed the room with the wariness of a cheetah.
But then, as if remembering something, the tension in her face eased, and she dropped the giant sword back onto the floor, listlessly lying down on the bed again.
Her long legs, visible below the leather shorts, were particularly enticing against the grey-white blanket.
...
The only pity was that the flat landscape beneath her upper body’s armor lessened the allure considerably.
“Sister Betty, what’s wrong?”
Betty turned to see Isa, curled up on the other side of the bed, her sleepy eyes blurry as she looked at her, and a hint of embarrassment crossed Betty’s face.
“Isa, I’m fine. You keep sleeping; I’m just going for a walk.”
“Oh~,” Isa pouted and dozed off again.
Betty sighed with relief.
How embarrassing. Thankfully, no outsider had seen it.
She stood up, straightened her clothes, and was about to walk out when she paused at the threshold.
Glancing back at the luxurious carpet, her gaze fell on the weapon lying askew.
After a moment of thought, she turned back to pick up the giant sword from the ground.
For a Northern Warrior, having no weapon at hand could make her feel even more vulnerable than being without clothes.
Tap tap tap~
Betty cautiously stepped out of the room, her footsteps emitting a distinct crisp sound on the wooden floor.
The two Bloodline guards in the hallway showed a respectful demeanor upon seeing Betty, bowing with a hand to their chest.
“Good day, Lady Betty. Would you like us to take you to see Ancestor Crown?”
These two Bloodlines had participated in the battle the previous night and had witnessed Betty slaughtering the Molten Demon and cutting down the Divine oppression in mere seconds.
Out of respect for the strong, even the proud Bloodline still maintained sufficient reverence.
Betty waved her hand nonchalantly.
“No need, I just want to have a look around.”
Betty’s feelings toward the Bloodline were neutral. She neither disliked nor particularly favored them.
In the bitterly cold Northern Plateau, the mere struggle to survive consumed much of the Northern people’s energy.
As for the rest, they simply didn’t care.
Furthermore, due to the desolate and harsh living conditions of the Northern Plateau, combined with the overpowering strength of the Northern Warriors,
there had never been traces of the Bloodline; given this backdrop, the people had no particular sentiment toward the demons spoken of by humans.
To the Northern people, survival was the sole priority. Nothing else mattered.
“As you wish. Shall we accompany you…”
Before they could finish, Betty gestured with her hand.
“No need, you guys stay here to protect Isa.”
“Yes, Lady Betty.”
Betty nodded, reassured, and turned to leave.
She was so trusting of the Bloodline entirely because when she formed a bond with Isa, they came to understand each other’s memories.
Isa’s tragic past made Betty see a reflection of her younger self, evoking a sense of compassion, while the warmth in everything Lide had done for Isa was something Betty had never felt before.
That’s why she agreed so readily to Isa’s request to sign a Soul Contract with Lide.
Nothing happened without a reason; all seemingly beautiful outcomes were just the fruits of seeds previously sown.
If Lide’s intentions toward Isa, the girl with the Golden Bloodline, were purely exploitative, he might have been met not with Betty’s pledge but with the sharp blade of the Northern Land Valkyrie.
Betty knew that the Blood Clan Ancestor valued Isa highly, and on his territory, nothing would harm Isa, so Betty left the house with peace of mind.
Wearing a leather jacket, short leather pants, and leather boots on her feet.
Tall and sexy, her black eyes were filled with wildness, and her slightly tied-back hair softened her sensuality and wildness slightly.
Yet this aura became even more captivating.
Betty walked down the stairs and everything in Lide Manor astonished her.
Exquisite Vampire statues, giant dragon bas-reliefs on the walls, colorful oil paintings, colored glass windows around the corridor corners, semi-circular white arches…
All sorts of aesthetically pleasing designs gave Betty, accustomed to the rugged architecture of the North, a breath of different air.
Yet she didn’t dislike the refined; in fact, she quite liked it.
Stepping on the cobblestoned ground, Betty left the manor which she found indescribably luxurious.
After greeting the two Bloodline guards, she pushed open the gates of the manor.
Outside lay wide, clean streets.
She had arrived at Dawn City late last night when most of its inhabitants were already asleep.
Now it was different; dawn had broken, and the residents were beginning to rise and prepare for the day’s work.
At the moment the gates opened, the scene on the street came into Betty’s view.
Lide’s manor was located in the central district, so it was a commercial hub, bustling and vibrant.
Early risers greeted each other in groups, some holding steaming bread or wheat porridge.
Everyone’s face wore a smile, their expressions relaxed.
Clean and tidy clothes adorned their bodies, their faces were lively, and she couldn’t find a single shabbily dressed person among the passersby.
What surprised Betty the most was how clean the streets were, and the absence of foul-smelling beggars on the sidewalks.
She found this scene astonishing.
In an instant, Betty developed a deep interest in this Vampire-run city.
According to legend, shouldn’t Vampire castles be gloomy and terrifying, filled with dead men’s bones everywhere?
How come here, not only are there humans, but each one seems so free.
In the eyes of the crowd, Betty could not see fear or dread; she could even distinctly feel that the vigor of these people was completely different from that of humans she had seen in the cities of the North.
If one word could describe it, it would be vitality.
Yes, she could see vitality in these people’s eyes, whereas in other human cities, even the better-dressed common folk had a tentative heaviness in their gaze, lacking that relaxed and carefree air.
Curiosity piqued, Lide’s handsome face inexplicably emerged in her mind.
“It seems this Vampire has some skills,”
She walked on down the street.
Because it was early, most of the shops on both sides of the street weren’t open yet, save for a couple of breakfast vendors already doing business.
The street was paved with bluestone, and most of the buildings on either side were three-story buildings adorned with bas-reliefs celebrating the Divine.
Betty’s eyes hardly knew where to look, her excitement palpable as she carried her giant sword and gazed around curiously.
Even the residents, witnessing Betty carrying her giant sword and strolling around the streets early in the morning, were somewhat curious. A few even boldly approached her to say hello.
“I’m Aunt Mary from the bakery. Miss, are you heading out hunting so early with that weapon?” Aunt Mary’s expression was somewhat wistful; such a young girl already up to hunt must have a tough life.
Her own niece, after all, couldn’t be persuaded to get out of bed before noon.
After saying this, Aunt Mary looked at Betty’s slender waist with even more pity. So skinny—what a pitiable girl.
“Would you like to stop by my bakery and try a couple of freshly baked, steaming honey bread?”
Betty’s expression turned incredibly odd upon hearing Aunt Mary’s words.
She was a Northern Land Valkyrie, after all. Even if these civilians did not know her true identity, she was still carrying a giant sword.
Weren’t these ordinary folks afraid?
Glory wasn’t a world where everyone was equal, the common people were nowhere near the same societal class as those with powerful Professions.
“No, I… I don’t need it, thank you,” Betty suddenly realized she hardly knew how to make conversation anymore.
“Ha ha ha, don’t be shy, Aunt Mary’s honey bread is the best in Dawn City, and don’t worry, today I won’t accept any copper pucks from you.”
“If you like, I can introduce you to a good job, so you won’t have to go hunting so early every day…”
Aunt Mary said, smiling broadly as she reached for Betty’s hand and pulled her along.
Betty, who wouldn’t be afraid even when fighting a giant dragon, felt somewhat at a loss in the face of the enthusiastic Aunt Mary.
But deep down, she strangely didn’t resent Aunt Mary, instead somewhat relishing the warmth of being treated with such enthusiasm.
Just then, a patrol team clad in armor and wearing red armbands on their shoulders approached from the opposite direction.
However, to Betty’s surprise, the one leading the team was a Vampire with bat wings outstretched behind him and Tusks visible in his mouth.
Could it be that these Vampires weren’t concealing their identities?
What shocked her even more was that the residents greeted the patrolling Vampire with a smile instead of fear.
The Vampire showed no offence at being approached by civilians, nodding back at times, even the children seeing this didn’t cry or fuss.
This scene, completely contrary to Betty’s expectations, shattered her worldview.
First, civilians daring to ignore the identity of those with Professions, and now, Vampires who were said to be more terrifying than Demons could coexist peacefully with humans…
Was this city really managed by Vampires?
Betty felt bewildered.
“Madam, please present your identification.”
As the Security Team passed by, one of them, with a keen eye, spotted Betty, who clearly stood out from the surrounding residents, and immediately came forward to check.
“Identification? What’s that? I don’t have any.”
Betty shrugged her shoulders, planting the giant sword lightly on the ground, and the clanging sound of metal hitting the earth rang out.
The threat implied by the scene was unmistakable.
Aunt Mary hurriedly came forward to mediate.
“Jie Ke, this lady is my guest. Such a young girl has to get up early every day to go hunting, there’s no need to make things difficult for her…”
The young man named Jie Ke looked somewhat stunned.
“Go hunting??”
Betty gazed at Aunt Mary standing in front of her, her eyes clouding with complexity. As the Northern Land Valkyrie, this was the first time in her life that a commoner had protected her.
“Are you Lady Betty??” The Bloodline member, who hadn’t paid much attention to this place, was drawn over by their conversation. Seeing Betty, he immediately approached with a look of pleasure and greeted her.
“Good day, respected Lady Betty, thank you for your contributions to Dawn City, Dawn City welcomes your arrival!”
After speaking, the leader of the Bloodline turned to loudly address the patrolling members and the surrounding crowd,
“This lady is the hero of Dawn City. Last night, the Kachar City Lord personally led the Holy Light Bloodline in a just war for Dawn City.
Lady Betty here helped the Holy Light Bloodline defeat the formidable enemy!! Her bravery earned praise from the Kachar City Lord himself!
The Kachar City Lord specifically instructed the Security Team that any place in Dawn City is open to Lady Betty.”
After the graceful Bloodline member finished speaking, he bowed once more to Betty, his hand on his chest,
“Dawn City welcomes your arrival, respected Lady Betty.”
Upon witnessing this, the surrounding crowd immediately burst into cheers, clapping in unison.
Aunt Mary looked on with a face full of surprise and joy,
“So it was you who helped us win the war!!
That’s wonderful, Miss Betty, from now on, you won’t need to spend a single copper puck for bread at Aunt Mary’s bakery! I’ll cover all the costs!”
Betty’s face turned red with the praise.
The news that the great Kachar City Lord had deployed the Holy Light Bloodline to participate in battle over the past couple of days had been disseminated to all the residents by the Publicity Department.
In the Publicity Department’s announcements, powerful enemies were said to want to destroy the influence that Dawn City had established in the outside human world.
The great Kachar City Lord, in order to protect the interests of Dawn City and the future benefits of all residents, decided to launch a proactive attack.
It was a war launched for the future of Dawn City.
Therefore, after hearing the Bloodline leader’s words, the residents immediately felt a surge of goodwill towards the woman wielding the giant sword.
“Lady Betty, thank you.”
“Welcome to our city…”
“You truly are an admirable and great figure…”
“You’ve earned the praise of the Ancestor Crown, it’s really incredible…”
Betty, who had thought a confrontation was inevitable, looked around at the crowd’s sincere cheering and admiration, suddenly feeling shy.
Even as the Northern Land Valkyrie, while she had heard countless praises, this was the first time she had received such pure, enthusiastic praise devoid of any other interests.
Her face beamed with a thick smile.
She suddenly found that she was quite fond of this city.

chapters.title: Chapter 184: 185 Post-War Loot, Hunting Dark Contract (Major Chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 184: Chapter 185 Post-War Loot, Hunting Dark Contract (Major Chapter)
As the first ray of sunlight rose in the sky,, Lide, sitting behind his desk on the third floor of City Hall, suddenly opened his eyes.
He turned his head to look at the burly figure lying unconscious on the floor.
He felt a powerful aura awakening.
Thump, thump~
Thump, thump~
Grot Kachar, who had been injected with the Bloodline’s blood, now had a heart that burst with vitality like a water pump. Though it beat slowly, it was strong and robust.
...
At this moment, the thick, mercury-like blood in Grot’s body was driven by his heart to flow throughout his veins, with each heartbeat, his inner strength grew.
The heart of the Bloodline was more like a source of energy; it was no longer a weakness and even a stab to the heart could not cause a fatal injury.
Lide and the other second-generation Bloodline descendants in the room watched with sparkling eyes as Grot’s aura slowly underwent a metamorphosis, filled with anticipation.
The might of Grot was evident to all; he alone could suppress Emi and Kolong, compelling hundreds of Bloodline members not to gather in the sky.
If Lide had not decisively adopted a one-for-one brutal tactic in the end, they might have had to pay a much higher price to defeat the opponent.
This was a powerful warrior who commanded respect from his foes, a pure warrior.
Next to Grot at this moment were nine empty, semi-transparent glass bottles, the remnants of magical fluctuations at the mouth of the bottles indicating what had been inside — Magic Blood.
A single glass bottle could hold three liters of liquid, and just these nine bottles of Magic Blood had caused Lide great distress.
After several battles, Lide had used up about one-fifth of the Magic Blood in the blood pool, regardless of the cost.
It didn’t seem like much, but this pool of Magic Blood had been accumulated over a hundred years.
It was a non-renewable resource in the short term.
Use a little, lose a little.
But at this moment, Lide did not have time to consider so much, as his gaze was firmly fixed on the increasingly powerful Grot.
This Northern Warrior was like a young dragon breaking out of its shell, filled with a breathtaking presence.
Swoosh~
Grot, lying on the grey velvet carpet, abruptly opened his eyes, his sharp gaze like that of a hawk ready to hunt, and he sat up straight.
Startled by the sight of the Bloodline members surrounding him, he was about to react, but upon seeing Lide out of the corner of his eye, he immediately froze.
Familiarity, dependence, trust—the powerful Bloodline power dissolved any hostility in Grot like water escaping.
At the same time, a stream of information passed through Grot’s bloodline, and after receiving it, his eyes gradually softened.
Moments later, the robust burly man rose to his feet, and his head, which had never bowed even in the face of death, lowered in Lide’s presence as he clasped his chest in salute.
“Good day, Ancestor Crown.”
Lide’s eyes showed a hint of satisfaction, and he said with a solemn tone, “Grot, as the Blood Clan Ancestor, I bestow upon you a new surname — Kachar.”
Upon hearing this, something stirred in Grot’s heart, a mysterious force surged through his bloodline, and it seemed as though his soul was sublimated at that moment, with some missing piece in his bloodline being filled by Lide’s words.
Once again, he clasped his chest and bowed his head.
“Grot Kachar, at your command.”
Thus, this mighty Northern Warrior became a part of the honored Upper Race — the Bloodline.
Dawn City’s high-end combat strength had increased by one.
At the same time, a system notification also sounded in Lide’s ear.
“Ding, Grot Kachar Bloodline transformation successful, Bloodline strength increased, awarded character experience — 2000.”
2000 experience points weren’t bad, much better than the 1000 experience he earned from the battle outside of Green City.
Indeed, after defeating Grot, Stanley, and Kolong, all formidable level 15 entities, Lide only gained 1000 character experience points, so little that he hardly considered mentioning it.
Lide eagerly began to check Grot’s attributes.
He was keen to know what sort of being would emerge from the combination of a Northern Warrior and the Bloodline.
Northern Bloodline?? Quite exciting indeed.
Grot Kachar
Title: Child of the North (Cold Resistance +50%, Body Recovery Speed +30%, Strength +30%)
Age: 67
Level: 16
Profession: Northern Warrior
Bloodline: Blood of Fearlessness, a new bloodline formed from the fusion of the Northern Warrior’s and the Bloodline’s bloodlines.
Blood of Fearlessness: During activation, immune to pain, immune to mind-affecting spells,
physical recovery speed and life recovery speed increased by 500%,
Magic Resistance increased by 200%,
strength increased by 60%,
body recovery speed increased by 1000% at night, able to harness the bloodline’s power to heal bodily wounds, duration: 30 minutes.
Gains the Extraordinary Trait: Fearlessness during bloodline activation.
Introduction: Son of the North, once hailed as the most likely warrior to break through and become Legendary.
Northern people have lifespans of up to 150 years, which increase to 200 after breaking through level 15, so the 67-year-old Grot was still in his prime.
Awesome.
After reading Grot’s attributes, Lide’s face showed a huge surprise.
Too powerful.
The original Grot was already able to suppress Emi and Kolong in combat; now, the fusion of his Northern Bloodline with the Bloodline had become the new Bloodline — Blood of Fearlessness.
His strength directly rose two levels.
Although the fused Blood of Fearlessness wasn’t as strong as Lady Betty’s Royal Bloodline,
Lide knew full well that beings like Betty, who had a Golden Bloodline like Isa, were extremely rare and scarce, so he never harbored any unrealistic fantasies.
By comparison, Grot had given him plenty of surprises.
It could be said that Lide now held an absolute trump card in his hand; no, with Betty, he had a pair of jokers, the big and little ghost, ready to explode.
Adding to this, with Emi and Kolong, who had just awakened his Ancient Giant Bloodline and evolved into a Bronze Giant, as well as Stanley, the level 15 Dark Priest who would rejoin them in no more than a month.
Though Lide suffered huge losses in this war, the gains were tenfold, a hundredfold larger.
Dawn City now boasted 4 top-level combatants with 3 at level 16 and 1 at level 15.
Even if he faced the Dark Contract head-on at this moment, he would no longer feel the slightest unease.
As the balance shifted, the strength of the Dark Contract had greatly diminished.
In just one day, we lost three of our top fighters; now only four remained.
The Eight-Armed Snake Demon Roy from the Abyss, the Undead Mage Withered Bone with his Bone Dragon, plus a mysterious person, Nelson, who had not shown his true face, and lastly, Viscount Bernard who was close to Transcendent.
Lide held onto the combat forces, the 15th Level Shadow High Priest Emi, 15th Level Bronze One-eyed Giant Koso, the Child of the North Grot Kachar at Level 16, and Lady Betty of the Northern Royal Family at Level 16—who could instantaneously slay 19th Level Molten Demons and extinguish the Dignity of the Divine.
When bayonets clash and draw blood, only then can we know who will win and who will lose.
Such a great price had been paid, but now we had finally gathered enough strength to fight the opposition.
Moreover, there was very good news now: The Dark Contract was unaware of everything that had happened.
The Crimson Mage Tower was still hidden in the shadows.
This asymmetric information could determine the final outcome of this game.
“Very well, no matter what has happened before, from now on, you are a member of the Holy Light Bloodline.
Grot, the Blood Clan welcomes you,” Lide said as he patted the shoulder of Grot, who was twice his height, with a smile that came from within.
No matter how hostile we were before, he was one of us now.
Humans still retained their original memories and personalities after evolving into the Bloodline,
and their temperaments wouldn’t suddenly change from warm and exuberant to cold and introverted because they became a Bloodline.
However, the powerful blood of the Bloodline would subtly transform new members, slowly deepening their identification with their Bloodline identity, but this process was lengthy and might take years.
The good point was that this sense of identity was permanent, imprinted into the soul and blood.
Thus, most new members of the Bloodline showed little change at the beginning; only after a long time would their daily habits gradually align with those of the Bloodline.
Of course, there was no harm in this, but rather over time, the power of the blood would strengthen.
Grot’s gaze was somewhat complicated as he looked at the second-generation Bloodline beside him, and he nodded.
Just moments before, they were enemies, and now they were comrades—this feeling was indeed strange.
However, he did not give it much thought; in battle, one could not hold back against an enemy, and as a Northern Warrior who had fought half his life, he was quite open-minded about these matters.
“Ancestor Crown, the blood of the Northern Royal Family…”
Lide looked at Grot, who seemed to have more to say but hesitated, and smiled slightly.
“Don’t worry, Betty is fine. She hasn’t become a Bloodline; she is still a Northern person.”
Of course, whether Betty became a Bloodline or not didn’t matter anymore, with Isa’s bonds in front and his Soul Contract behind.
This Northern Royal Bloodline had been firmly tethered to the chariot of Dawn City, becoming a Sharp Blade in his hands.
Grot breathed a sigh of relief. Although he had become a Bloodline, he still didn’t wish for the blood of the Northern Royal Family to be extinguished.
In human countries, royalty might be just a title, but in the Northern lands, it was different.
The Talent held by the royal blood was far beyond what an ordinary Northern Warrior could compare to, and Grot was even confident that no matter when he fought Betty, the victor would always be Betty alone.
No one understood the Talent inherent in the royal blood better than this Child of the North; only a powerful Northern Royal Family could lead the Northern people.
This was the sole reason he paid a huge price to save the dying Betty; the North could not be without a royal family.
“Clan Leader, Lady Betty requests an audience,”
While the two were conversing, a Bloodline from outside entered the room to report.
“Bring her in,”
“Yes.”
Soon, the slender and tall Betty, with a giant sword completely disproportionate to her size, stepped into the office, her eyes carrying a wild aura.
It was only then that Lide could clearly see Betty’s face.
Unlike any other girl, Betty’s features were very three-dimensional, with a kind of indescribable heroic beauty, and those black eyes held a wildness that seemed impossible to suppress.
This sort of woman would certainly be queen-like on Earth, capable of making countless men submit at her feet.
Upon seeing an unharmed Betty, Grot Kachar showed a broad smile on his face and took two steps forward, placing his right fist over his heart.
“Good day, Princess Betty, of the Morlon Tribe of the North, Grot Kachar greets you.”
Betty’s eyes brightened upon hearing Grot’s words, “Grot?” A touch of affection flashed in her eyes, “Child of the North, I have heard your name.”
After finishing her statement, a shadow seemed to pass over her eyes as if recalling some past events, “What a pity, the Morlon Tribe is no more, otherwise we might have had the chance to fight side by side in the North.”
Betty gave Lide a profound look, “However, you are now one of the Bloodline.”
Grot was slightly startled, and looking into Betty’s eyes, he felt a pang of discomfort, “Princess Betty, is it true that only you are left of the Northern Royal Family?”
Betty looked at Grot with some curiosity, “Who told you that?”
“Ah, is it not so? The Nolan Empire and the Radiant Empire broke through the Northern Plateau, the Nolan Empire has occupied our land, and the Radiant Empire is hunting our royal family, even legends have taken action…”
Betty nodded, her voice growing heavier, “The general information is correct, but as strong as the legends of the Radiant Empire are, our Northern legends are not weak.
After the North was breached, the royal family led three hundred thousand Northern people away from the Northern Plateau through the Space Gate.
They are now in a plane discovered by the royal family many years ago, and the living conditions there are much better than on the Northern Plateau.”
Upon hearing this, Grot immediately showed great joy,
“So, it means our North has not lost its heritage!!”
Betty shook her head, “No, Northern warriors could never lose their heritage. In fact, if the royal family had not already considered relocating, it would have been impossible for the Nolan Empire and the Radiant Empire to take the Northern Plateau no matter how strong they were,” Betty declared, lifting her head proudly.
As the leader of Glory’s three great warriors, the Northern Warrior was not as weak and vulnerable as the outside world imagined.
Although the Northern people were few in number, they were all soldiers, and each Northerner was a powerful warrior.
No one could insult the North.
Grot felt a great weight lift from his chest upon hearing this, his voice filled with exuberance.
“The Glory of the North shall light our path ahead.”
A look of longing appeared in Betty’s eyes as she echoed, “The Glory of the North shall light our path ahead.”
Lide watched the two reminisce without interjecting.
Understanding more after Betty’s words, he figured out why Betty had no reaction to him turning Grot into a member of the Bloodline.
The heritage of the North was still unbroken; a warrior who had already left the North was not so important.
After waiting for the two to finish their topic, Lide went straight to the main topic.
He turned his head and swept a gaze over all the second-generation Bloodline members in the room, his eyes burning as he stared at Grot.
“Grot, the Crimson Mage Tower is my territory, no one can recklessly make my property their hunting target.
I need you to master all the information about the Dark Contract.”
His eyes flashed with a hint of chill, his tone carrying an unquestionable resolve and an indomitable determination.
“This time, we are going to hunt the Dark Contract.”

chapters.title: Chapter 185: 186 The Abyss Gate Opens, Wind Rises in Green City (Major Chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 185: Chapter 186 The Abyss Gate Opens, Wind Rises in Green City (Major Chapter)
May 14th.
The largest city in the southern part of the Nolan Empire, Green City, was nearing dusk, with the orange sun slowly sinking behind the mountains.
The weather, stepping into summer, was extremely hot, and a restless atmosphere enveloped the entire city.
The sewers on both sides of the streets bubbled and emitted a foul stench under the high temperatures, and although there were fewer beggars on the streets than during the Frost Month, quite a few were still kneeling in shaded areas begging from pedestrians.
Civilians dressed in gray sackcloth robes, sweaty in the scorching air, were unloading sacks of wheat from the carts for the grain shop at Cross Street, their neck skin ashen like charcoal.
Next to the grain shop, a fat fruit vendor look worriedly at the sparse clientele in his shop, idly fanning to drive away flies buzzing around the fruits.
...
To the right of the fruit shop, on a broad wall, an image of the Life Goddess was painted with colorful dyes. Above the painted wall, a pointed spire adorned with stained glass swung from side to side, ticking the time away, providing entertainment for both the shopkeeper and the civilians hauling grain.
The city seemed no different from usual, with the nobles enjoying themselves in manors, and the civilians working hard.
But right after the sun fell into the valley, about fifty miles north of Green City, a piercing loud crack sounded.
Like glass shattering.
