Right afterward, the originally golden sky instantly turned gray-black, and an indescribable presence emerged.
Terrifying, bloody, brutal.
All the negative adjectives could aptly describe this presence.
It was as if a demon that had once devoured humanity had broken its seal and descended upon the world.
Inside Green City, whether civilians or professionals, a tremendous fear arose in their hearts, as if venomous snakes lurking in the dark were staring at them.
Within a modest courtyard in the City Lord’s manor of Green City,
An old man was sitting under a broad-leaved maple tree, flipping through a yellowed magic book, appearing to be in his early sixties, wearing a white mage robe, thin, and seemingly ordinary, having little distinction from an average civilian of Green City.
When that dark presence appeared over Green City, the old man suddenly turned his head.
His deep eyes filled with uncontrollable fury.
“The breath of the Abyss! Damn it, who opened the gate to the space of the Abyss??”
Right after speaking, he abruptly stood up, his originally ordinary aura suddenly transforming.
An exaggerated magic power condensed around him, causing a magic tide within a hundred blades’ range.
The white robe he wore also emitted strong magic fluctuations, and it seemed like space itself fluctuated with his breath.
In all of Green City, the only one who possessed such power was—an Extraordinary Mage: Rock Hart.
This Protector of Green City, the only Extraordinary Existence, had reached the Extraordinary Rank over a century ago.
The next second, Rock’s body disappeared from the spot.
When he reappeared, he was already outside Green City, a staggering ten kilometers away from the City Lord’s manor where he had vanished.
As Rock’s body appeared outside Green City and disappeared again in the next moment, even some civilians passing by had not managed to catch a clear glimpse of him.
In less than 10 seconds, this incredibly powerful Extraordinary Mage had already reached the Space Gate that connected to the bottomless Abyss.
Where the Space Gate opened had originally been a lush forest, but now, the area was completely corrupted by the Abyssal breath.
Green leaves turned gray and cold upon contact with the dark and chilly breath of the Abyss, dropping within seconds, and even before hitting the ground were already completely corroded.
At that moment, at the Space Gate which was a thousand blades long in the sky, thousands of small demons with long tails and flapping wings emerged.
Rock’s expression grew exceedingly grim as he looked back at Green City momentarily before stepping into the Space Gate.
“We must close the Space Gate, otherwise the whole Green City will be overwhelmed by demons.”
“The aura of the Main Plane is too enticing for the Abyss, and right now it’s just minor demons. Once the more powerful demons react, everything will be beyond redemption.”
“Even Green City, no matter how strong, cannot withstand the power of the Abyss.”
“Not only did this Extraordinary Existence notice this scene, but all high-level professionals within Green City sensed the anomaly as well.”
“Countless high-level professionals who usually lay hidden, surged towards the outskirts of the city.”
“The arrival of Abyss Demons signifies the onset of a life-and-death war between races.”
“No one can remain unscathed in this war.”
“At this moment, Lide was about three hundred blades away from the Crimson Mage Tower.”
“This was the spot Lide picked for today after Viscount Bernard had agreed to plunder the Crimson Mage Tower.”
“Viscount Bernard’s plan was not complex; in fact, it was quite simple.”
“When the Abyss Gate opened and drew the attention of the entire Green City, as soon as Viscount Bernard gave the attack command, everyone from the Dark Contract would assault the Crimson Mage Tower.”
“They would plunder everything they saw, whether it was Divine Artifacts or people, or anything else.”
“Lide had been wanting to get close to this powerful and mysterious chairman these past few days,”
“Unfortunately, since the last meeting, Viscount Bernard had not gathered the people of the Dark Contract again; everything was commanded through covert orders.”
“Because of this, Lide felt quite helpless. Although he had the power to counteract the opponent, he could not find his adversary.”
“He also thought about taking out other top combat strengths of the Dark Contract from the city to repeat the action of attacking Grout.”
“Unfortunately, the remaining few were craftier than each other, and he hadn’t even seen their faces these past few days.”
“Here they come.”
“After feeling the rich Abyss aura spreading from the north of Green City, Lide’s eyes narrowed.”
“He did not want to make the Crimson Mage Tower the main battlefield, as it would result in tremendous losses whether they win or lose.”
“Even though he had made many arrangements these past two days, such losses were unavoidable.”
“This was not something he could control. Viscount Bernard was very cautious, and Lide couldn’t find more opportunities, so he had to confront the enemy at the Crimson Mage Tower.”
“Fortunately, the enemy did not know that their prey, the Crimson Mage Tower, was hunting them.”
“For this, he had made adequate preparations.”
“The Space Transmission Scroll is ready; Coso will enter the field at the very first necessity.”
“Emi’s face was solemn. These past few days, after being suppressed by Grout, the Shadow High Priest was not beaten down; instead, he continually sought to redeem himself.”
“Only by achieving military feats can one wash away the disgrace on them.”
“So, it was Emi who was most eager for the Dark Contract to go to war.”
“In a small two-story room, Grout silently watched outside the window while Betty lay nonchalantly on a wooden chair.”
“Wait, I need the enemy to appear before launching an attack.”
“Because of Viscount Bernard’s caution, Lide had to restrain his emotions and patiently wait for the prey to take the bait.”
“Dark Contract saw the Crimson Mage Tower as prey, but the Crimson Mage Tower also saw the enemy as prey.”
“The Bloodline was never a kind or weak race.”
“Furthermore, with the racial characteristics of the Bloodline, as long as the casualty ratio was maintained within a certain range, they would only grow stronger the more they fought.”
As time ticked away by the second, the abyssal presence in the northern area grew increasingly intense, to the point that even from dozens of leagues away, the city of Green City could feel the dark, brutal, and bloody aura.
Livestock kept by the city’s residents scream frantically, and rats in the sewers began to emerge from the ground en masse, creating a scene reminiscent of the apocalypse.
Due to the flood of demons from the abyss, Green City’s military had been dispatched to patrol the northern district, yet many abyss demons still appeared within Green City.
This city of a million humans began to descend into chaos.
Some malevolent underground forces, upon seeing this scene, did not join in killing the demons; instead, they took advantage of the chaos to rob and plunder, blatantly displaying mankind’s worst instincts.
For a moment, Green City’s military were running all over the place, plunging the entire city into an atmosphere of panic.
An hour after the abyssal aura intensified and Green City descended into chaos,
a splendid firework burst in the sky.
Bang~
Light radiated in all directions.
Bright as the starry sky.
“It’s coming,” Lide’s eyes hardened, this was the signal for the Dark Contract to attack the Crimson Mage Tower.
The few people inside the room immediately perked up, the always listless Betty suddenly stood up. At this moment, the Northern Land Valkyrie resembled a hunting falcon, her eyes filled with wild sharpness, a stark contrast to her previous languid demeanor.
Lifting the giant sword she had not yet returned to Grot, her face revealed an eager expression.
Battle is the ultimate destiny of the Northern people.
Fearless, undaunted!
At that moment, to the north of the Crimson Mage Tower, an indescribably terrifying aura appeared.
A skeleton dragon with a wingspan of fifteen blades and a body length of ten blades, its body composed of bones flashing metallic luster, and soulfires of eerie blue hue flickered within its skull.
Level 18 Undead Life—Bone Dragon!
The bone dragon’s damaged wings looked like dark objects unearthed after millennia of decay, the fierce barbs on the wings capable of piercing a warrior’s shield, the powerful limbs below adorned with dangerously sharp claws.
A powerful and terrifying undead creature.
And above the bone dragon, a figure cloaked in a cape was particularly striking.
This was the master of the bone dragon—Undead Mage Lord Withered Bones.
This age-old Undead Mage, finally released his bone dragon under everyone’s gaze.
Under Withered Bones’ control, the bone dragon sharply dove towards the ground, spurting~
A chilly, dark energy erupted from its massive bone jaws.
Undead Breath.
Even the lifeless giant dragons had not lost their innate talents; the bone dragon’s undead breath carried a dense energy of death.
The moment the buildings on the ground were touched by the Undead Breath, they rapidly decayed and turned to ashes within seconds.
With its massive broken wings flapping, the bone dragon didn’t shy away from a tall bell tower at the street corner, smashing straight into it.
Crack~ The wooden and stone bell tower shattered into pieces.
Wood chunks collapsed in heaps.
Huge blocks of bluestone tumbled from the bell tower, smashing into the street below, springing two blades high and rolling several more blades before fiercely overturning an angel statue.
Debris scattered everywhere.
The Crimson Mage Tower seemed to have sensed the threat as well, and with the towering Mage Tower at its core, a semi-transparent Magic Shield rose, enveloping the entire area of the Mage Tower within.
After toppling the bell tower, the Bone Dragon flew directly towards the Crimson Mage Tower, with Lord Withered Bones behind it showing a hint of excitement.
“Gah gah gah~ embrace Death!!”
“The great Lord Withered Bones will escort you to the Death God!!”
The Bone Dragon seated below spewed Dragon Breath again.
Gray, cold Death Energy erupted, crackling~
The massive corrosive energy barely leaked out a bit, causing the surrounding houses unprotected by the Magic Shield to decay and collapse immediately.
However, the Undead Breath did not break through the Magic Shield directly, but rather stirred up ripples upon it one after the other.
Clearly, the strong protective power blocked the lethal Death Breath.
Lide watched this scene intently from within a cottage, not taking action even though Lord Withered Bones had already directed the Bone Dragon to attack the Crimson Mage Tower.
His sharp gaze continually surveyed the surroundings, sensing an eerie atmosphere.
So far, only Lord Withered Bones had acted alone, which was odd, very odd.
After all, neither the Abyss Eight-Armed Snake Demon Roy nor Viscount Bernard could possibly be absent.
The battle had already begun; were they really playing some trashy trick of holding back their power?
Despite his confusion, Lide did not rush to make a decision, his gaze still surveying the surroundings, hoping to quickly identify the main enemy he was facing.
This was a battle destined for a life-and-death struggle, and war never involved luck or mercy.
One wrong decision could cause the entire Crimson Mage Tower and Dawn City to suffer tremendous loss.
This was the power of a superior, but also a responsibility.
The Lord Withered Bones who directed the Bone Dragon to attack the Crimson Mage Tower was ignored by him.
Acting rashly before the enemy appeared would undoubtedly be very foolish.
But continuing like this was not a solution either.
Lide watched as the Mage Shield gradually thinned, his breathing growing rapid.
The Magic Shield of the Crimson Mage Tower might only last another minute.
Once the Magic Shield shattered, the Crimson Mage Tower he had spent half a year and over a hundred thousand Gold Puck to build might turn to ash under the Dragon Breath in a matter of minutes.
As the Magic Shield of the Crimson Mage Tower weakened further, and Lide’s aura grew icier, a rumbling sound emerged~
A loud noise came from the central area of Green City, followed by a surge of powerful momentum.
Lide’s expression suddenly changed.
He abruptly turned his head, a look of disbelief appearing in his eyes.
For he vaguely sensed that this aura was all too familiar.
Emi and Grot also turned their heads towards Lide.
“Ancestor Crown, that’s Viscount Bernard,” both spoke in unison.
Lide’s brow furrowed sharply.
A bad premonition rose in his heart.

chapters.title: Chapter 186: 187: On the Cultivation of Old Coins (Long Chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 186: Chapter 187: On the Cultivation of Old Coins (Long Chapter)
Lide felt a familiar presence emanating from the direction of the City Lord’s Manor, and his heart skipped a beat.
Especially when he sensed that the Magic Shield over the City Lord’s Manor shattered in just a few seconds, his premonition grew even stronger.
“Is that Viscount Bernard’s presence?” he asked Emi and Grote with some uncertainty.
“Ancestor Crown, it is Viscount Bernard’s presence, no one knows him better than we do,” Emi nodded. After twenty years in the Dark Contract, although she hadn’t gained Viscount Bernard’s absolute trust, it wasn’t difficult to identify him.
Grote also gave a definitive reply.
“My Lord, it is indeed Viscount Bernard.”
...
Lide glanced at the two of them, his gaze inexplicably complex.
It was likely that Viscount Bernard’s target was not the Crimson Mage Tower at all, but the City Lord’s Manor.
All the previous doubts threaded together at this moment.
No wonder Viscount Bernard, despite having the power to easily crush the Crimson Mage Tower, still put so much effort into preparation.
First, he used the power of the Late Bell Church to create a mysterious weapon that could restrict a Divine Artifact,
and then spent months plotting to open a Space Gate to the Abyss, attracting Green City’s advanced professionals.
Originally, Lide thought the other party was just being cautious, but now it seemed that the Crimson Mage Tower, constantly mentioned by Viscount Bernard, was nothing but a decoy.
His real goal was only one—the City Lord’s Manor.
But why didn’t he directly target the City Lord’s Manor; why go through such a big detour?
Lide then sensed something and suddenly turned his head. Through the half-open window, he saw five strong presences with levels exceeding fifteen surrounding the Crimson Mage Tower.
Five advanced professionals directly encircled Withered Bones, who was commanding the Bone Dragon to attack the Crimson Mage Tower.
This scene made him instantly enlightened.
“This play of attacking east and striking west is quite slick.”
At this moment, Lide had deep sentiments, Viscount Bernard truly deserved to be the boss behind the enormous underground force, the Dark Contract.
If he didn’t have Emi as an insider, infiltrating the Dark Contract and capturing three top-tier fighters above level fifteen,
now everyone in the Dark Contract would be used as pawns by Viscount Bernard.
Just Withered Bones, Emi, Grote, Stanley, and the deceased Kolong, these five top-tier fighters attacking the Crimson Mage Tower,
would surely attract most of the advanced professionals staying in Green City during this sensitive period of the Abyss Demon’s emergence.
At that time, Viscount Bernard would perfectly achieve his goal.
Lide took a deep look at the Bone Dragon still flying in the sky, shaking his head.
First was the Abyss Gate, then the attack on the Crimson Mage Tower, these two feints would surely draw out most of the defense forces from the City Lord’s residence, even if their guard was strong.
It seemed that Viscount Bernard’s real purpose in ordering the Dark Contract to plunder the Crimson Mage Tower was to draw away the defensive forces and create an opportunity for himself.
The more people attacking the Crimson Mage Tower, the more top-tier fighting forces would be attracted to Green City.
Moreover, once the battle started, those involved in the fight were unlikely to leave and support the City Lord’s Manor. And if a battle broke out, few would have the energy to attend to Viscount Bernard at the City Lord’s Manor.
It was dark, damnably dark.
Lide spat resentfully at this big boss who was close to becoming an Extraordinary Existence.
It wasn’t scary for someone to be powerful, but it was frightening for a powerful person to be a sly old coin; that was utterly disgusting.
Viscount Bernard had been planning for such a long time, orchestrating everything so complexly that apart from a few people in the Dark Contract, most had been played by him.
What was his true purpose? What was there in the City Lord’s Manor that attracted this boss??
A glint of contemplation flashed through his eyes, something that would compel an Extraordinary Existence to go to such lengths must be a treasure of unimaginable value.
Unfortunately, Lide took one last deep look at the distant City Lord’s Manor.
Even the most precious treasure was beyond his current reach.
Because the City Lord’s Manor was the only place in Green City inhabited by an Extraordinary Existence. Although it was very likely that the Extraordinary Mage had been lured away by the scent of the Abyss, no one dared to be sure when he would return.
The power he held was not weak, but it was still nothing compared to an Extraordinary Being.
He had initially thought that today would bring about a fierce battle, but now it seemed that the fight clearly wasn’t going to happen.
Turning his head, he glanced at the Bone Dragon in the sky, confronting five level fifteen beings in Green City’s military uniforms on the ground, with a flicker of cold light in his eyes.
“Keep an eye on that damned Undead Mage, I don’t believe he will be killed so easily.”
Facing the hunt of five top-tier level fifteen fighters, even Grote, Child of the North, had to be careful and vigilant. But the Undead Mage Withered Bones showed no fear at all, instead letting out piercing shrieks in the air.
“Gaga gaga~ Foolish mortals, the great Withered Bone is not something you can withstand!”
“Meeting the Death God is your best destiny.”
“Rage, my darlings, I want you to taste the flavor of the Undead Breath~!”
Among the five advanced professionals who came to the Crimson Mage Tower to hunt the Undead Mage Withered Bone, there were two warriors, a thief, plus a priest, and an archer.
They formed the classic trinity of warrior, mage, and priest, and naturally, they did not shrink back when facing a level 14 Undead Mage like Withered Bone.
Even if this Undead Mage had an 18-level Bone Dragon at his command.
The massive Bone Dragon suddenly turned and flew toward the middle-aged man in priestly robes on the ground.
Despite the distance of several dozen blades, the breath bearing the aura of death, the Undead Breath, spewed forth.
The 18-level Bone Dragon’s breath, had the power to destroy the sky and earth.
Any building that came into contact with the Undead Breath would instantly decay and collapse, reducing half a street to ash under the dragon’s breath.
At this moment, the priest standing in the street did not panic. At the critical moment, he blinked, and his figure instantly left the range of the dragon’s breath.
Meanwhile, the nearby thief had also gone invisible, and the two warriors were protecting the archer, who kept drawing her bow and shooting arrows while also looking for opportunities to attack.
Lide was witnessing the combat style of human advanced professionals for the first time.
Apparently, these humans were often in sync with one another, forming an unspoken understanding. Each knew what to do and when to do it.
So, even when faced with an 18-level Bone Dragon, there was no panic amongst them.
The warriors always stood in front of the archer and the priest, and although the thief remained invisible, the occasional strange noise from the rooftops still indicated that he was always looking for an opportunity.
Unfortunately, the Bone Dragon was too sensitive, and there was never a good moment.
The stalemate continued in this way.
The Bone Dragon had the advantage in the air, but due to its large size it lacked agility within the city, unable to deal with the five people.
The five people on the ground, although numerically superior, didn’t have air superiority. They could only helplessly watch as the Bone Dragon dominated the skies above.
Lide, witnessing this scene, was not too surprised. Both sides were tough, and after watching the lackluster battle for a moment, as if remembering something important, he suddenly turned his head to Emi and said,
“Emi, could you leave a space imprint on the Bone Dragon?”
Emi was startled and, after pondering for a moment, nodded decisively.
“The Bone Dragon’s body is very large; leaving a space imprint won’t be a problem. Moreover, since the Bone Dragon isn’t very intelligent, it won’t detect it.
The only problem is that due to the immense power within the Bone Dragon’s body, the space imprint can only last for half a Sunshine Hour before dissipating.”
Lide nodded, his eyes flashing with meaning.
“That will be enough. This Undead Mage won’t stay in Green City for long. Once the human Griffins and Pegasuses arrive, the Bone Dragon won’t have it so easy.
Once you leave the space imprint, will you be able to track this Undead Mage?”
Upon hearing the question, Emi thought for a moment before nodding firmly.
“As long as there is a space imprint and it’s within my casting distance, there will be absolutely no problem.”
As a Shadow High Priest, Emi had a strong grasp of spatial magic, or more precisely, the Shadow Side’s spatial magic.
Tracking through location was a simple operation, not a troublesome task for him.
Lide’s eyes brightened.
“Go leave a space imprint on the Bone Dragon, and be careful not to let the Undead Mage notice.
Since the people from the Dark Contract haven’t come, we should at least collect some other spoils of war.”
Emi, as the Shadow High Priest, was someone Lide did not worry about accomplishing the task of leaving an imprint on the Bone Dragon.
If he couldn’t do even that, then there wouldn’t be much use keeping this Shadow High Priest around.
Originally, he thought today would be a tough battle, but now the situation had drastically changed, and plans could not keep up with changes.
Although there was no need to confront Viscount Bernard, a being close to transcendent existence, head-on anymore, Lide was not content to let it go. He had prepared for so long, so without taking back some spoils of war, wouldn’t that be letting down his own planning today?
At this time, the Undead Mage Withered Bone, who was showing off on the Bone Dragon, naturally caught his eye. He had an enduring impression of this talkative fellow.
Furthermore, the hunting of an Undead Mage and an 18-level Bone Dragon seemed quite sweet.
Bang~
Just then, a more intense explosion sounded from the city center.
A terrifying presence, like the emergence of an abyssal demon out to destroy the world, filled the air with a heart-thumping fluctuation.
The aura of divinity.
Lide suddenly turned his head, his eyes narrowing.
Although he did not know what kind of battle the city center was undergoing at this moment, he was certain it was a hundred times more intense than at the Crimson Mage Tower.
Viscount Bernard opened the most central cabinet in the City Lord’s secret chamber with magic and took out a grey Magic Scroll made of unnamed Magic Materials, two palm-widths wide and half a blade long, his face showing a thick smile.
“The dense evil aura is no wonder that Transcendent didn’t carry it on him, this power can only be controlled by us from the Abyss.
Roy, let’s go, the Twelve Magic Scrolls are in hand…”
If Lide were here, he would be shocked by Viscount Bernard’s words, as the ultimate goal of the boss of the Dark Contract was actually the Legendary Divine Artifact crafted by the Creator God himself—the Twelve Magic Scrolls.
The Twelve Magic Scrolls, as the legend goes, were divided into twelve parts, each sealing a powerful and mysterious energy.
Most crucially, the Twelve Magic Scrolls could bestow unimaginable powers upon the Spellcasters,
and thus, the Twelve Magic Scrolls had always been regarded as the supreme Divine Artifact among mages; however, there had never been any reports of anyone acquiring it, so most Spellcasters considered it just an ancient myth.
The figure of the Eight-Armed Snake Demon, Roy, appeared in the secret chamber, its narrow green eyes taking a deep look at Viscount Bernard.
The gaze remained cold and brutal, and his body emitted a chilling aura.
“Viscount Bernard, don’t forget our agreement.”
Viscount Bernard smiled faintly, “I received the information about that young dragon last year, I swear by my soul, I have not deceived you.”
Roy nodded in satisfaction; the eight arms behind him carried eight long sabers, and the enormous grey-patterned snake tail writhed on the ground, appearing both resilient and terribly frightening.
“Pleasure doing business with you.”
The two exchanged a smile, but in their eyes, each held a meaning unknown to the other.
This was cooperation among Abyss Demons.
“Viscount Bernard, the people from the City Lord’s mansion have arrived, we need to withdraw.”
At that moment, an urgent figure came from outside the secret chamber. Hearing the report from the newcomer, Viscount Bernard nodded.
He left the secret chamber with Roy.
Now that he had obtained what he wanted, there was no need to stay any longer; the Gold Puck and various treasures in the secret chamber couldn’t even make Viscount Bernard take a second glance.
Quickly following his subordinates to the courtyard of the City Lord’s estate, Viscount Bernard was preparing to lead the subordinates of the Dark Contract to retreat when suddenly space rippled, crackling—
Like glass shattering, space violently shook and then collapsed.
A white-robed, short-statured old mage, his expression full of rage, appeared about thirty blades away from Viscount Bernard.
Magic Energy madly converged around the old man, even stirring up a Magic Tide within a few seconds.
The person was none other than Rock Hart, the only Extraordinary Mage from Green City who had entered the Abyss during Sunshine Hour.
“Lord Rock”
The guards, clad in Dwarf-forged full armor, hurriedly arrived upon seeing the old man, with unrestrained joy on their faces.
The moment Rock appeared, the crowd thought they were assured victory, as no one doubted how powerful a Transcendent could be.
“How is this possible, didn’t Lord Barro stop you from coming back?” Viscount Bernard’s eyes flickered with deep wariness and confusion upon seeing Rock, the Transcendent.
He had arranged for an Extraordinary Level Abyss Flame Demon to ambush Rock in the Abyss, even if the Flame Demon couldn’t kill Rock, he shouldn’t have let Rock escape the Abyss so quickly.
Hearing this, Rock’s wrinkled face showed a trace of disdain as he waved his hand and the space in front of him shattered.
Then, under everyone’s gaze, a giant skull, half the height of a person, fell out of the shattered space.
The skull bore enormous horns and exuded an extremely evil aura, chilling the ordinary guards even in death.
Drops of burning hot blood fell from the neck onto the ground, and the bluestone immediately corroded, creating pockmarks in a grotesquely horrifying scene.
An Abyss Demon.
“This weak Flame Demon is your ally??”
Viscount Bernard’s eyes widened in shock at the sight and he instinctively took a step back.
Looking back at Rock, his heart was filled with awe.
Too strong, this Transcendent was too strong!!
He guessed that the other might already be nearing Legendary status.
Even the Flame Demon, who was also of Transcendent-level, couldn’t withstand a single Sunshine Hour, too strong.
“Hand over the Twelve Magic Scrolls, Abyss Devil, these are not for you to touch.”
Rock’s tone was calm, but the presence of the Transcendent-level Flame Demon’s skull exerted tremendous pressure on Viscount Bernard and Roy, the Eight-Armed Snake Demon.
No one dared to ignore the will of a Transcendent, unless they wanted to meet Death right away.
Viscount Bernard’s face changed again and again, his previously graceful demeanor was nowhere to be found, his eyes filled with tension.
He gritted his teeth and fiercely pulled out a Magic Scroll from his bosom that emitted a heart-palpitating aura, tearing it open directly without giving anyone time to react.
An indescribable, terrifying presence appeared.
Brutal, cold, and at the same time—unparalleled in strength.
Divine Power!
Upon sensing that aura, Lord Rock’s eyes widened sharply and his hands instantly conjured two Four Circle Magics, but just as he was about to cast them, half a second before, the abundant Magic Energy in the air disappeared without a trace as if it had been drained.
The Spell that the Extraordinary Mage had just gathered shattered instantly.
“Magic Prohibition Domain?!!”
Lord Rock’s gaze narrowed, unable to contain the fury in his heart.
Damn it, this Abyss Demon was too prepared, actually borrowing the power of the Divine to create a Magic Prohibition Domain.
After seeing this scene, Viscount Bernard finally showed a smile, his blue eyes taking a deep look at Lord Rock.
“Lord Rock, I hope the next time we meet, we can have a real confrontation,” he said, then lifted the gray-white Divine Artifact in his hand, the Legendary Twelve Magic Scrolls emitting an extremely chaotic and evil aura, irresistibly eye-catching.
Then, under the gaze of everyone around, Viscount Bernard took out another Magic Scroll and tore it open.
A Teleportation Array immediately appeared under their feet, also infused with Divine Power.
“I’ve borrowed your Divine Artifact.” After saying these words, whoosh—the Teleportation Scroll activated, and Viscount Bernard and Roy vanished on the spot.
Lord Rock watched this scene, his wrinkled face turning ashen.
Deep anger filled his eyes.
A mere Abyss Demon who hadn’t reached the Transcendent realm dared to play him like this!! The damn bastard!!
With a wave of his hand, explosive Magic Energy surged, and the Magic Prohibition Domain created from Divine Power shattered like exploding glass.
A Magic Prohibition Domain made with Divine Power lasted only a mere ten or so seconds before this Extraordinary Being. If Viscount Bernard had delayed even a little longer, he would likely have been taught a lesson in Magic by this Extraordinary Existence.
After Viscount Bernard left, Lord Rock did not give up. After sensing briefly, he waved his hand, and the space in front of him fractured, and he stepped into it.
“The Space Gate outside of the city has been sealed by me. Deploy the troops to clear out the Demons in the city,” he said, then turned to look at Viscount Bernard’s subordinates, “And these evil Underground Forces, don’t let a single one escape.
“You don’t need to come for me. No matter where that damned Devil flees to, I will retrieve what belongs to me, Lord Rock.”
After his voice fell, the space healed, and the place that was bustling just moments ago was now empty.
The crowd outside the scene looked at each other, somewhat at a loss.
From Viscount Bernard’s surprise attack on the City Lord’s residence that broke the Magic Shield, to Lord Rock’s return, followed by the disappearance of the three, the entire process took only a few minutes.
Most people were still dazed.
But when they saw the people of the Dark Contract scattering and fleeing, they quickly came to their senses, following Lord Rock’s instructions to cleanse the damnable Underground Forces.
After Viscount Bernard used the power of the Divine to trap Lord Rock, the Transcendent, and escape, the Withered Bones who were fighting around the Crimson Mage Tower also withdrew the Bone Dragon after their last clash with the subterranean five-man squad, and with a flash, entered the Space Gate.
Because in the not-too-distant sky appeared thousands of Griffins and Pegasuses, if he delayed any longer, even with a Level 18 Bone Dragon, he would undoubtedly perish.
“Cackle cackle cackle~ Despicable humans, the great Lord Withered Bones is not someone you can resist. Today I’m graciously granting you the privilege to live a little longer.
Until our next meeting, I’ll send you to meet Death.”
The mocking blue gaze beneath the black headgear vanished behind the Space Gate after finishing these words.
On the ground, the five Advanced-Level Professionals did not have a Spellcaster skilled in Space Magic, and the only Spellcaster Priest was not familiar with Space Magic.
The group exchanged glances, only able to shake their heads and stop in their tracks.
This damned Undead Mage!
With that, the sudden attack that occurred within Green City came to an end.
Many civilians were still utterly confused, unaware of what had happened. Only a few high-ranked Professionals faintly understood the truth but dared not speak of it.
Because, the wrath of Lord Rock was not something that just anyone could bear.
Lide narrowed his eyes slightly after Withered Bones entered the Space Gate.
His sharp gaze fixed on where Withered Bones had left.
“Emi, pinpoint his space, and follow him,”
This prey, he was determined to capture!

chapters.title: Chapter 187: 188: From Now On, There's a Chatty Little Skeleton on Dawn City's Square
chapters.content:
Chapter 187: Chapter 188: From Now On, There’s a Chatty Little Skeleton on Dawn City’s Square
Lord Withered Bones stepped through the Space Gate and appeared just outside Green City in the blink of an eye.
Beneath his cloak, those deep blue eyes took a lingering look at the city behind him, sprawled like a gigantic beast.
“Viscount Bernard, truly impressive, who would have thought you’d dare target an Extraordinary Existence.”
“How surprising.”
“Gah gah gah, I hope you can escape the pursuit of the Transcendent.”
Lord Withered Bones’s tone did not betray an ounce of frustration at being used as a pawn; instead, it was laced with barely concealed schadenfreude.
...
When he sensed Viscount Bernard’s presence in the City Lord’s Manor, he understood the reason behind it all. Being an Undead Life that had lived for countless years, he had seen through such conspiracies and schemes long ago.
He had felt something amiss about this operation from the start, suspecting that Viscount Bernard had other plans. He hadn’t expected the other party to be so bold as to attack the City Lord’s Manor and plunder the wealth of an Extraordinary Existence.
“The Dark Contract shall be destroyed from today,” Lord Withered Bones declared, floating in the air, his voice tinged with reluctance.
Having offended the Transcendent, the Dark Contract had lost its foothold in Green City.
“Losing a toy like this is truly boring. I heard the Royal Capital of Nolan Empire is rife with underground forces; perhaps I can take a look there.”
The Undead Mage, Lord Withered Bones, who possessed an endless lifespan, enjoyed joining various dark forces. Regrettably, the groups he joined often did not last as long as he did, so he had witnessed the destruction of countless underground forces.
Yet, he never tired of it.
It seemed only among humans could he find a sense of living, for he had lived far too long; time had long since lost its meaning to him.
“Lord Withered Bones, please wait. I think the Dark Contract will not be destroyed just like that.”
As Lord Withered Bones prepared to leave, a voice from below halted his actions.
Turning slightly, a tall, incredibly handsome figure emerged from the woods.
That elegant nobility was like a bright moon in the darkness, admirable.
“Are you the Vampire servant by Emi’s side?” Lord Withered Bones’s somber gaze flickered upon seeing Lide, his tone slightly annoyed.
“A level 13 Vampire? Who gave you the courage to speak to the great Lord Withered Bones like this?
“Don’t you know the great Lord Withered Bones is the Vice President of the Dark Contract, a being of higher stature than your master, Emi?
“You lowly servant, now kneel and beg for mercy from the great Lord Withered Bones, otherwise, I won’t mind grinding your skull into powder for alchemy materials.”
Lide couldn’t get a word in edgeways, his face expressing his speechlessness. Will this chatterbox ever let me speak?
“I…”
“Hmph, lowly Vampire, it’s too late now. I will make you understand never to offend the great Lord Withered Bones.”
“You…”
“Stop thinking about begging for mercy. Let me bestow upon you death and destruction.”
Unable to stand it anymore, Lide looked at the arrogant Lord Withered Bones floating mid-air and turned to look behind him.
“Are you ready? Strike now!”
Lord Withered Bones was caught off guard, still not reacting when a figure moving at a blade-speed of a hundred per second soared towards the sky.
Just as he instinctively tried to use Space Magic, the surrounding space instantly solidified.
Space Dimensional Anchor, the surrounding space was locked tight.
Lord Withered Bones, standing no more than a hundred blades away, saw the figure approach in just a second.
Only then did he see clearly, a woman, wearing a short skirt, her eyes filled with wildness.
Mage Shield, Mage Shield.
Though Lord Withered Bones was only level 14, he used a unique Talent only available to level 15 Spellcasters—Dual Casting—to instantly cover himself with two shields.
But it was too late.
The giant sword aglow with a faint light swung down, and the level 14 Lord Withered Bones stood no chance against the level 16 Betty.
Zzeerraa~
The two layers of the Mage Shield shattered like nothing, and with a slight tilt of the sword, Betty smashed the blade’s body onto Lord Withered Bones, sending him plummeting from the sky like a baseball.
At that moment, a burly figure surged from the ground.
Child of the North, Grot.
This burly warrior flapped his huge bat wings and launched right at the point where Lord Withered Bones was falling, smashing his giant sword onto Lord Withered Bones’s waist.
Bang—home run.
The body of Lord Withered Bones, cloaked in black, was smashed once more, soaring back into the sky.
Just then, as Betty’s figure descended, she came face to face with the ascending Lord Withered Bones, her eyes flashing wildly as she smashed down with the sword again.
Bang—
Lord Withered Bones’s body was batted around by Grot and Betty several times within a few seconds using their giant swords.
Finally, after Betty fell from the sky, the game ended.
Lord Withered Bones’s body quickly plunged, the fierce wind making his large black cloak rustle loudly.
Boom~
From hundreds of blades away, Lide could hear the final sound of Withered Bones crashing onto the ground.
At that moment, Emi, hiding in the shadows, had already made her move and appeared beside him within two seconds of his fall.
The handcuffs forged from magic-resistant stones firmly grasped Withered Bones’s hands, at the same time dispersing the magic power around him; her hands moved swiftly, and in the blink of an eye, she stripped him of all his possessions.
By the time Lide reached Emi’s side, he saw the true form of this Undead Mage for the first time.
Withered Bones, true Withered Bones.
On the grass, a skeleton entirely composed of white bones was very conspicuous; the soul fire within its skull flickered a ghostly blue, seemingly undulating continuously due to severe damage it had sustained.
Betty and Groot, two well-coordinated Northern Warriors, also reached Lide’s side and looked curiously at the Undead Mage on the ground.
It was also their first time seeing an Undead Mage.
“Legend has it that Undead Mages are transformed from corpses, and as long as their soul fire does not extinguish, they will never die,” Emi said somewhat wistfully. “These beings have no concept of time; Withered Bones existed even before I joined the Dark Contract, and no one knows how long he has lived.”
Lide stroked his chin, a level 14 Undead Life with a Bone Dragon undoubtedly a very valuable trophy.
However, as an Undead Mage was not a human, he couldn’t turn him into a Bloodline; hence, a very important question now was how to deal with this trophy.
“Emi, do you know how to handle an Undead Mage? Or, is there a way to control him?”
Emi pondered for a moment before giving a bitter smile,
“Ancestor Crown, Undead Mages are extremely peculiar and bizarre; no one knows what lies hidden within their soul fire.
Therefore, common control techniques like Soul Contracts are useless on them because they can abandon their detached soul fire anytime.”
Lide glanced at the two Northern Warriors; Betty shrugged and gestured helplessly with her hands. Combat she could handle, but researching how to control an Undead Mage was clearly beyond her scope.
Groot also decisively shook his head; this former Child of the North was obviously clueless about these matters.
“Is there a way to get his Bone Dragon?”
Withered Bones didn’t matter to Lide; he was after the powerful Bone Dragon, the real treasure he desired.
A level 14 Undead Mage, capable of overpowering five level 15 top combatants with his Bone Dragon.
“Cackle, foolish vampire, thinking of getting my little treasure, such an ignorant idea.”
The restrained Withered Bones on the ground suddenly spoke.
Lide looked curiously at Withered Bones; his white skull opened and closed between speaking, producing sounds that seemed to be made by vibrating the air directly, not by vibrating vocal cords like humans.
“Oh,” Lide nodded but did not speak.
Withered Bones was firmly locked on the ground by chains made of magic-resistant stone, completely unable to mobilize magic power.
Withered Bones’s skull turned towards him, a pale blue light flashing across his empty eye sockets, and Lide’s lack of inquiry seemed to irritate him.
“Hmph, ignorant vampire, my little treasure has already fused with my soul fire; as long as I die, you won’t get the powerful Bone Dragon,” Withered Bones taunted.
Lide nodded.
“Oh.”
Withered Bones raged upon hearing this.
“Do not disbelieve, vampire, do not use your ignorant mind to speculate about the great Lord Withered Bones. I…”
“Oh, I believe,” Lide cut him off.
Withered Bones’s soul fire fluctuated wildly with anger, making Emi wonder if it might ignite his skull.
“Bring him back to Dawn City and lock him up, better yet, display him on the Square so all citizens can view our trophy; perhaps our citizens would be interested in this little skeleton,” Lide said, not uttering such foolish words as asking for the Bone Dragon.
To threaten an Undead Life was absolutely the most stupid action; these beings, having lived who knows how long, simply do not care about death.
Even in the belief system of Undead Life, the concept of death does not exist; to them, death is merely a form of sleep.
This was a very peculiar creature, no longer even considered ‘alive’.
So, Lide preferred to have his Mages research how to forcibly take the Bone Dragon from the Undead Mage, rather than making threats.
Hearing this, Withered Bones burst into rage.
“Damn vampire, I am a great Undead Mage, not a little skeleton, no!”
“Great Lord Withered Bones will let you taste being scorched by Dragon’s Breath, I swear…”
Lide paid no attention to the verbose Undead Mage; though he had captured him, he still needed to figure out how to transform his captive into something useful for Dawn City.
“Emi, after the Dawn Mage Tower is built, establish a branch for researching Undead Magic; I want to thoroughly study these Undead Creatures.”
After finishing, he glanced at the still chattering Withered Bones, “As for this guy, display him on Dawn Square until we figure it out; let the residents witness what Undead Life is like.”
Capturing the prey but not finding a use for it was truly frustrating.
However, because of Lide’s decision, from that day forward, Dawn City’s Square had one more curiosity—a chatty little skeleton that boasted all day about having a powerful Bone Dragon.
The residents of Dawn City scoffed at this, mocking him and finding much amusement in their otherwise peaceful lives.

chapters.title: Chapter 188: 189: Leaving After the Deed is Done
chapters.content:
Chapter 188: Chapter 189: Leaving After the Deed is Done
After Emi personally brought back the Withered Bone to Dawn City.
The turmoil caused by the Dark Contract finally settled down.
The event, from its sudden onset to its conclusion, had caused a great shock to Lide within just a few days.
At the same time, this was the most labor-intensive war that Dawn City had fought, although the final battle was not fought due to Viscount Bernard’s change of target, yet the impact on Lide was profound.
For the first time, he directly experienced the role that high-end combatants like Grot and Betty played in war.
This greatly inspired and transformed his strategic thinking on warfare, and also gave him new ideas on how to develop Dawn City in the future.
...
It was not a glorious battle, but it was sufficient to influence the future.
After a few people left, Lide returned alone to the Crimson Mage Tower. Although the Mage Tower did not suffer much damage, the necessary follow-up work still needed to be done.
As for Grot, Betty, and the always absent Koso, they followed Emi back to Dawn City.
Grot returned because there were still 23 Northern Warriors imprisoned in the dungeons of Dawn City, so he had to go back, and Lide also arranged for Grot to learn the “True History” of the Bloodline to avoid future mishaps.
As for Betty, the explosively powerful Northern Land Valkyrie, it was because Isa was still in Dawn City, and this wildly spirited valkyrie also loved the atmosphere of Dawn City.
She was already eager to return and continue experiencing this unique city.
Crimson Mage Tower, third-floor study.
Lide’s tall and handsome figure sat behind a desk.
“Good day, Lord Lide”
Dressed in a black mage robe, the short-statured Carlo, respectfully bowed before Lide.
“Carlo, how much damage did the Crimson Mage Tower sustain yesterday?”
For safety, Vena had already been arranged by him to go out and purchase Magic Materials earlier.
Therefore, Carlo, now the first head of the Magic Factory, temporarily held the highest position here, responsible for the work of the Crimson Mage Tower.
The Crimson Mage Tower had now gotten on the right track, Vena had formed a management team beforehand, even if both main managers, Lide and Vena, were not there, the Crimson Mage Tower could still operate normally.
Carlo’s role was merely to supervise the normal operation of this team.
This plan was also given to Vena by Lide, a powerful force cannot be managed by a single manager alone,
Rather, a well-structured, efficient team should be established to handle issues, where the main leaders only need to set the general direction.
The girl completely trusted what Lide said, so she implemented this matter decisively.
“Lord Lide, the Crimson Mage Tower didn’t suffer much damage, because the Bone Dragon didn’t breach our Magic Shield.
However, due to the suddenness of the event, over thirty Mage Apprentices were seriously injured due to Magic Rebound from fright, and five of them died directly because of it…”
Uh… Lide was also left somewhat speechless upon hearing this. The enemy hadn’t even broken in, yet they had been scared to death.
It really was filled with dark humor.
However, he didn’t say much, although the Bone Dragon was Undead Life, its Dragon Power was no laughing matter.
The impact on the souls from the level 18 Dragon Power faced by ordinary level 1 Mage Apprentices was unimaginable.
It was a pressure from the soul, an instinctive suppression of life.
It was no wonder the apprentices, who were quietly engraving Magic Arrays inside the factory, were enveloped in Dragon Power and were frightened.
“Besides, because the Magic Shield required a large amount of Demon Crystal Stones to maintain, withstanding the attack of the Bone Dragon cost us at least ten thousand Gold Pucks worth of Demon Crystal Stones.”
Lide nodded slightly, war was fought with economics, and when the Crimson Mage Tower lacked high-end power, they could only pile up defense with money.
But it was still okay, for now, the Crimson Mage Tower wasn’t lacking money.
Just now, the Withered Bone had continuously attacked the Crimson Mage Tower for two minutes.
To withstand two minutes under the Dragon Breath of a level 18 Bone Dragon, these ten thousand Gold Pucks were well spent, even a bargain.
“When was this Magic Shield built?”
Carlo looked a bit puzzled at this question.
“Lord Lide, this is a masterpiece of Lord Spark, just completed the final steps four days ago, for which we also paid two thousand Gold Puck’s worth of Magic Materials.
You were not in the Crimson Mage Tower at that time.”
Twenty thousand Gold Pucks, Carlo, the interim person in charge, still felt the pain when he recalled it, constructing Magic Arrays was too expensive.
Lide nodded knowingly, a thoughtful glance flashing in his eyes.
From the effects of the Magic Array, Spark hadn’t exaggerated its use, the money invested was worthwhile.
He also developed a higher interest in the Ancient Alchemy Magic Array that Spark had mentioned.
If it wasn’t for the Magic Array that Spark had arranged costing hundreds of thousands of Gold Pucks, the Crimson Mage Tower would have likely been broken through by the Bone Dragon, and his losses would have been even greater.
Maybe in the future, he could increase the building of Ancient Alchemy Magic Arrays, his base couldn’t afford to have accidents.
“Make arrangements for the families of the deceased Mage Apprentices, compensate them with three times the amount of Gold Pucks.
Also, don’t stop the production of the Magic Factory, we won’t be attacked again.”
“Yes, Lord Lide”
“What’s the inventory of Magic Scrolls currently?”
“Due to issues with Magic Materials, the production at the Magic Factory hasn’t increased recently, so the inventory of Magic Scrolls has maintained a fairly stable state, currently totaling six thousand.”
Lide nodded again, Magic Scrolls, being the most important source of Gold Pucks for the Crimson Mage Tower at present, but constrained by the scarcity of Magic Materials, had not been able to increase production efficiency.
“Good, the Crimson Mage Tower is now in your hands, I hope you can do better than Vena.”
Carlo’s face lit up with excitement at these words.
“I dare not compare myself to Miss Vena, but Lord Lide, I will not let you down.”
“Good, you may leave.”
When Carlo had just left the house, an anxious voice came from outside the study.
“Kachar, Kachar! Did you hear that the Crimson Mage Tower was attacked by an Undead Mage and a Bone Dragon?”
Spark, dressed in a white robe, appeared inside the study, his disheveled white hair looking as if it hadn’t been washed for three days, reeking of a strong smell of alcohol, his eyes slightly intoxicated.
“Teacher, I’m fine.”
Feeling Spark’s concern, Lide felt a warmth in his heart,
“The city guard came and blocked the Bone Dragon, and that Undead Mage did not break through the Magic Shield of the Crimson Mage Tower.
I also have to thank you for the Magic Array you constructed, it’s really solid, it even blocked the breath of the Bone Dragon.”
Spark was immensely happy upon hearing this, a broad smile appeared on his face, and he lifted his head proudly.
“This is a Magic Array personally set up by Master Spark, the kid from the Kachar family, now you know its efficacy,”
The tone paused for a moment, a flicker of annoyance in his eyes.
“Hmph, these damn Undead Creatures daring to come to Green City!!
If I hadn’t drunk a few more cups of wine from the Storm Sea Domain and failed to notice this bastard, I would’ve definitely pulled out its Soul Fire for a roast.”
After saying this, he looked around somewhat nervously.
“Where is Isa?”
Lide shook his head with a wry smile upon hearing this.
This old man really was helpless, no wonder Lide hadn’t sensed his presence yesterday, he thought he had gone to explore the Abyss Gate but turned out, he just got drunk at home and didn’t notice the danger.
“Isa has been sent to a safe place, she won’t be back for a few days.
After all, the Crimson Mage Tower was attacked by the Bone Dragon, the City Lord’s manor was attacked by unknown enemies, and even an Abyss Gate appeared outside Green City, who knows what more deadly events might occur…”
Whether such events would occur in the future, Lide didn’t know, but definitely not in the short term, Viscount Bernard had offended a Transcendent being, and the Dark Contract would not have an easy time in the coming days.
Listening to Lide’s explanation, Spark furrowed his brow,
Indeed, the scene that appeared yesterday was too weird: the Abyss Gate, the Bone Dragon roaming, the City Lord’s manor being attacked.
There must be someone behind all these events, manipulating everything.
“That’s good, are you sure the place where Isa is staying is safe??”
Lide nodded with a resolute tone.
“There’s no safer place than that.”
The secluded Dawn City saw not even a dog around, aside from some wild Demon Beasts, who would venture hundreds of kilometers into the Far Mountain Range without reason.
The Far Mountain Range lacked attractions for adventurers; not only were there few Demon Beasts, but the terrain was also rugged and difficult to navigate, without the drive of profit, basically no one would adventure there.
Spark nodded assuredly, this old man really treasured Isa, if Lide had not previously taken her as his apprentice, he would have definitely taken her in.
But even so, Spark now considered this girl of the Golden Bloodline as his successor.
Smart, understanding, obedient, and her Talent in Magic was irrationally strong – all these traits made this Level 19 Great Mage extremely satisfied.
Suddenly, as if remembering something, Spark said with some hesitation.
“About the Ancient Alchemy Magic Array, you…”
“Every month from now on, I’ll give you 50,000 Gold Pucks to build the Magic Array, I hope it can be completed as soon as possible,” Lide said generously.
Spark’s slightly intoxicated eyes brightened, and he stepped forward to slap him hard on the shoulder.
“Hahaha, Kachar family kid, this is the best decision you’ve made in your life…”
The strong smell of alcohol made Lide frown, “Teacher, you should go downstairs and rest first.”
“Yes, my wine hasn’t… My Magic is not researched well enough yet.” Spark smacked his head delightedly and turned around to leave, not even giving Lide another glance.
Watching Spark hurriedly turn and leave, Lide couldn’t help but smile wryly; this self-indulgent old man really was whimsical.
Standing up, he walked to the transparent glass window, looking down at the Mage Apprentices busily coming and going below, a trace of satisfaction in his eyes.
The matter with the Dark Contract sorted, he could finally focus on development for a while.
Suddenly, as if thinking of something, his eyes revealed a bit of contemplation.
“The Crimson Mage Tower now lacks a high-level combat power to serve as a deterrent, if I transfer Betty…”
Although the Crimson Mage Tower had Spark as a supporter, in Green City no Noble dared to offend the unfathomable Spark.
But after all, that was his teacher, and there were many things Lide couldn’t let him handle.
Could he command Spark to eliminate a rival one day? That would be wishful thinking; the scruffy, arrogant old man wouldn’t even consider it.
If the Crimson Mage Tower had a top-tier combat power that he could completely control, it would only benefit the Tower.
Many covert matters would then be conveniently handled.
Moreover, Betty wasn’t a Bloodline, so he needn’t worry that she would be discovered by Spark or any other powerful Profession workers.
The major reason he hadn’t dispatched any ordinary Bloodline to the Crimson Mage Tower was that ordinary Bloodline lacked his potent ability to conceal the essence of a Bloodline.
It would be manageable short-term, but prolonged presence could easily reveal issues.
Most crucially, he didn’t want to keep Isa in Dawn City forever; after all, studying Magic with Spark was much better than learning from Emi or any other Bloodline.
With Betty’s return, she could also protect Isa, killing two birds with one stone.
After finalizing his plan, Lide called for Carlo, who had just left, instructing him to summon Miss Vena back and, in the meantime, temporarily hand over the management of the Crimson Mage Tower to him.
After sorting out these trivial matters, Lide returned alone to Dawn City.
Though the war had ended, he could not overlook the postwar tasks.
He still had to conduct funerals for the heroes who died in battle.

chapters.title: Chapter 189: 190 The Greatness of Dawn City
chapters.content:
Chapter 189: Chapter 190 The Greatness of Dawn City
Dawn City had once again achieved victory in war, and this news sent the entire city into a frenzy of excitement.
Public opinion has always been high ground that must be seized.
The propaganda department, which Lide had heavily supported, had now become the mouthpiece of Dawn City, swaying the opinions of all its citizens.
The commoners, who had not experienced the baptism of an explosion of knowledge, were completely unable to resist the wash of modern warfare propaganda.
Though the propaganda department did not provide detailed explanations about the related military actions, it still launched promotions every time the troops were deployed.
They would inform the civilians who the enemy of the Holy Light Bloodline was now, why our army was fighting, what would happen if we did not fight, what would happen if we lost, and what we could gain if we won.
...
Therefore, although the residents of Dawn City had not directly participated in the war, under the efforts of the propaganda department, every person felt as though they were personally involved.
In the past, most commoners in Glory would not be touched by the deaths or injuries of nobles or the army.
Because in the eyes of the commoners, the nobles and the army had always had a strained relationship with them; these nobles and the military were not fighting for them.
But Dawn City was different; the Holy Light Bloodline was fighting for them, sacrificing for them.
Therefore, every resident would mourn for the heroes who died for Dawn City and rejoice for the victories in war.
Because the great protectors of Dawn City, the Holy Light Bloodline, stood together with them, the interests of everyone were aligned.
The benefits of doing this were obvious, the cohesion of Dawn City would become stronger and stronger, and the residents’ support for the Holy Light Bloodline also increased significantly.
As a standard dictator boss, Lide, who controlled the fate of everyone, focused on both military and ideological fronts, ensuring strength in both aspects.
This war, which had sacrificed many of the Bloodline, brought quite a few changes to Dawn City.
Among them was Betty, who could be called a hero who saved the Bloodline; she received a warm welcome in Dawn City.
Especially since this hero was a tall, extremely attractive woman.
In the propaganda of the department, Betty had already become a super-hero-like figure, respected and loved by all.
This wild Valkyrie, amid the enthusiasm of the residents, rapidly grew fond of this city ruled by the Bloodline.
She even began to harbor the idea of not wanting to leave the city.
The bitter cold of the North made everyone fight desperately for living space, and as a member of the royal bloodline, Betty was no exception; she even gave more than the ordinary people because only through more battles could the royal bloodline within her body be activated.
Thus, for twenty years, from the day she learned to wield a weapon, she had been fighting.
Never had she felt the warmth of a home amidst the endless battles and killings, but here, she experienced a passion that was enough to console the heart, and the charm of the city deeply attracted her.
Isa felt the same way; this girl with ruby-like eyes did not face any discrimination in Dawn City.
In Green City, although she had Lide and Spark as her backing, no commoner dared to mistreat her with vile words.
However, Talent could directly sense whether others harbored malice or goodwill towards her. Those commoners who saw her red eyes might not have spoken out, but deep down, most were shocked, panicked, and even afraid and disgusted.
Even among the apprentices of the Crimson Mage Tower, a portion of them felt fear towards her, so she did not feel much warmth in the city of Green City.
But within Dawn City, it was different. Most civilians were kind and friendly to her, never showing malice because of her crimson eyes.
Living with vampires and one-eyed giants every day, the residents of Dawn City had long developed strong hearts.
What were Isa’s red eyes compared to that? They had even witnessed the birth of the Bloodline, and they went to the supposedly evil act of blood donation every month.
So no one cared whether Isa’s eyes were red or not; rather, the aunties liked this lovely girl very much.
An inclusive and open city is undoubtedly the most charming because there would be no discrimination, something unimaginable in Glory.
This charm was the reason Betty and Isa were deeply attracted.
By the time Lide returned to Dawn City, it was May 17th, three days after Viscount Bernard had attacked Green City and captured the Undead Mage, Withered Bone.
During these days, Dawn City was immersed in a mix of sorrow and excitement.
The sorrow lay in the dozens of coffins of the Holy Light Bloodline members displayed in the square, these were the heroes who died fighting for Dawn City.
Among them was one that was particularly conspicuous—the One-eyed Giant, whose large body had no suitable coffin and was only covered with a white cloth over the head.
Unable to cover the entire body, the numerous scars on the body were displayed in front of everyone, showing in the most direct way what kind of battle this One-eyed Giant, who died fighting for Dawn City, had suffered.
It was a shocking sight.
Many residents were deeply saddened by this because many of them knew the One-eyed Giant. These big fellows, equivalent to human teenagers, were a source of joy for many residents.
But now, the big pal who greeted them every day, who they could see every day, had gone forever.
Sorrow was unstoppable.
But there was also excitement, because even though a massive price was paid, Dawn City had won the final victory in this war.
“That must be Sir Kori, alas, just a few days ago he was patrolling with me…” a member of the patrol team said, his eyes dim as he looked at the name on the coffin in front of him.
“Goddess above, these are heroes who sacrificed for us…” an ordinary auntie’s eyes reddened a bit.
“This big fellow, he was just eating bread in my bakery last week, never thought I’d never see him again,” a businessman with a big belly sighed with emotion.
“Waaaah~ Mama, when I grow up I definitely want to be a hero, like Uncle Kobi, waaaah~”
A seven or eight-year-old boy looked at the portrait drawn with magic on the Bloodline’s coffin, his sobs and sniffs unceasing as he recognized the Bloodline who often gave him snacks.
Even though the death rate in Glory was incredibly high, death after all is the parting that people find hardest to let go of, especially in the always safe and peaceful Dawn City.
Many residents only now realized that, just as the City Hall had said, Dawn City was not actually safe. It was only because the Holy Light Bloodline blocked all threats for everyone that they had such a peaceful living environment.
There is never a time of peace and tranquility in the world, merely some who carry the weight for others.
Compared to before, and now, here is simply the Worry-free Divine Country they’ve all dreamt of.
Also, because of the coffins on the square, the number of Believers in the Dawn Sect increased greatly over the past few days, reaching a little over 6,000.
The entire Dawn City has only less than 3,000 residents still believing in other Divines, which for a newly born Sect, is already considered a great achievement.
The shift in faith is often the most difficult, because the first step is to make the original Believers abandon the faith they’ve held for the past ten or even several decades.
Many people have turned this matter into a lifestyle with their long-standing faith, and changing a lifestyle of several decades can indeed be very difficult.
“Good day, Clan Leader.” In the City Hall office, Harrison respectfully gave a salute to Lide who had just returned.
“Harrison, report on the current work.”
Although the confrontation with the Dark Contract wasn’t long, and even before and after the victory of the war it was barely a matter of ten days,
Lide always felt like he had spent a lot of time and energy on this.
“Yes, Clan Leader.”
“Currently, all the work in Dawn City is progressing smoothly,
First, the breeding farm has fully launched, and the workers recruited have exceeded 200, it is expected that in August it can operate at full capacity.
The aqueduct system you designed has provided a great convenience for the breeding farms, increasing the overall efficiency by at least thirty percent.”
“The expansion of the Magic Language Bats is also underway, it is estimated that by September the total number will reach 1,000, Dylan is already working on increasing the expansion of the Magic Language Bats,” Harrison paused in his speech.
Lide nodded but said nothing.
This time, the loss of more than two hundred Magic Language Bats constituted a huge casualty, dealing a significant blow to the already not well-off Magic Language Bat Clan.
And since the Magic Language Bats are an important labor force for Dawn City, this has also made the progress of many projects slow down.
Therefore, increasing the number of Magic Language Bats is a very important matter.
“Second, the Dawn Mage Tower has entered the final phase, because this battle has delayed the final process, it is estimated that construction will be completed by early June.”
“Third, agriculture, at present, excluding the elderly and children, a total of 8,300 people have been allocated land.
About 70% of these lands are planted with wheat, and the remaining lands have planted other fruits and vegetables.
The Moonlight Plain is fertile and the climate of Dawn City is very suitable for growing food, the wheat currently planted is doing well, it is expected that the harvest in July will yield around 350 to 450 pounds per acre.”
Upon hearing about agriculture, Lide immediately became interested because agriculture is undeniably the lifeline for Dawn City at this stage.
“Can you ensure a wheat yield of 350 pounds per acre?” Glory is not Earth; the seeds on Earth have been cultivated with the effort of countless people, and yields have increased by several times. Here, producing 350 pounds of wheat per acre is already considered high yield.
That meant that one acre of land could feed two people.
Based on the current cultivated land area in Dawn City, achieving a wheat yield of 350 pounds per acre, Dawn City could support a hundred thousand people next year.
This was undoubtedly news worth celebrating.
“Since it is the first planting, although the Agriculture Department organized a large number of experienced farmers to guide the cultivation, the specific outcome can’t be guaranteed,” Harrison did not directly answer.
Lide nodded, realizing he was a bit anxious.
But helplessly, if the lifeline of the Bloodline is blood, then the lifeline of humanity is undoubtedly food.
Now, the sustainability plan had already put the Bloodline’s lifeline in his own hands, and what remains is humanity. If this year’s harvest achieves the expected results, it would undoubtedly provide the strongest support for snatching population in the Frost Month.
He could then freely move forward with his subsequent plans.
Suddenly, as if remembering something, Lide continued to ask, “What about the construction of the school? Has City Hall planned for that?”
The two carriages driving Dawn City forward, the school, and the Mage Tower.
In Lide’s plan, these two buildings would be the most important channels for cultivating high-end talent in the future.

chapters.title: Chapter 190: 191: Funeral of a Hero, Carrying the Coffin
chapters.content:
Chapter 190: Chapter 191: Funeral of a Hero, Carrying the Coffin
“School?” Harrison paused briefly, then shook his head.
“Clan Leader, schools are not a necessity for Dawn City at the moment.
There are many tasks more important than school. I have already asked the City Hall to initiate evening classes in the square, where civilians can learn to read twice a week.”
Lide shook his head.
“Schools are a necessity, and they must be established in the future.
Education is a massive undertaking, and Dawn City must acquire more cutting-edge talents in the future.
...
However, it does indeed need to be prioritized later.”
Educational empowerment is an unchanging truth—most of Dawn City’s population are lower-class civilians, many of whom cannot even recognize their own names.
Only with a foundation of highly qualified people can more top talents emerge, a truth everyone must acknowledge.
A farmer who cannot read producing talents is certainly less likely than a level 15 Great Mage producing talents.
But for now, it is indeed too early to build schools since much work still needs to be done in various areas.
At the very least, people need to have enough food and clothing before they can think about education.
“The war has ended, and Dawn City now needs to return to its developmental path.
We cannot allow a single war to halt our progress.”
A heavy look flashed through Lide’s eyes.
“Tomorrow, we’ll hold a funeral for the heroes—to honor all those who died for Dawn City with the utmost respect.”
As the topic shifted, Harrison’s gaze dimmed slightly.
“Yes, Clan Leader.” He was the only second-generation Bloodline who hadn’t participated in the battle; all others had died on the frontline while he could only await news from the rear.
At that moment, Harrison couldn’t help but wonder if he had made a mistake. Was it really right not to study offensive magic?
If one day enemies reached Dawn City, would his role be limited to casting supportive magic from behind the Bloodline?
Harrison felt somewhat lost.
Lide, noticing Harrison’s dimmed gaze, seemed to understand his thoughts and shook his head slightly, “Harrison, not everyone needs to charge into battle.
I am very confident about the management skills Dawn City has taught you; you are as valuable as three level 15 Great Mages here.”
The fact was indeed true; without Harrison handling the tedious political affairs continuously, Lide wouldn’t have had the energy to do anything else.
Talents are diverse; they can be business prodigies, management experts, builders, or even blacksmiths forging weapons.
If a city only possesses powerful combat abilities, it is undoubtedly imbalanced—unless it is strong enough to disregard all enemies; otherwise, it is merely limping along.
Harrison nodded, and the dimness in his eyes gradually cleared, regaining their brightness.
“Clan Leader…I think I understand.”
…
Waging war always revolves around obtaining more living space, a theme that has never changed.
And the soldiers who fall in battle often bring the most heartache.
As the residents of Dawn City and the Holy Light Bloodline integrated, the initial fear and wariness had long vanished, replaced by a harmonious relationship.
But after this war, many residents found that the Bloodline members, who had been talking and laughing with them just days before, were now wrapped in white shrouds, encased in black coffins, forever leaving them.
Such sudden departures are often difficult to accept.
There are no wars without death.
With the efforts of the propaganda department,
The next day’s evening,
As the dusk deepened, the residents of Dawn City spontaneously gathered in Dawn Square.
These residents were dressed in black or dark clothes, wearing a white flower on their chest, standing solemnly on the square, their gazes complex as they looked at the neatly arranged coffins.
Above each coffin, magic-rendered paintings depicted faces with smiles, now eternal.
In the center of the dozens of coffins lay a one-eyed giant, vast as a hill, resting peacefully.
A white cloth covered its head, and its body was covered with dense scars, indicating the giant’s bravery.
Twenty members of the Bloodline continuously used magic to protect the body to prevent damage from high temperatures.
Beneath the twilight, pale golden light twinkled in the sky.
Below was a crowd filled with sorrow.
The atmosphere could easily infect others, and even those who did not personally know the deceased Bloodline members could not remain indifferent under such conditions.
“The City Lord of Kachar has arrived,”
A whisper ran through the crowd, and they turned their heads in unison.
Seeing him in a black mage robe, also adorned with a white flower, the crowd showed excited expressions.
“Good day, Your Excellency Kachar…”
“City Lord of Kachar…”
For a moment, even the air seemed less filled with sadness.
This was their king, the master of Dawn, beneath the great Divine, and their savior.
Lide, under the crowd’s gaze, solemnly stepped on the cobblestone ground, not turning as he walked directly through the gaps between the coffins, step by step.
In black attire, wearing a conspicuous white flower, the crowd’s gaze followed Lide as he moved forward.
The black coffins, the gigantic figure of the one-eyed giant, everything exuded a heavy air of mourning.
Lide’s gaze swept over each smiling image on the coffins, and his heart grew heavy.
These were the undisputed heroes of Dawn City, their deeds destined to be recorded in the annals of the city’s history.
Step-step—step-step—
The sound of stepping on the stone was very deep, step by step up to the high platform.
With a deep and piercing gaze, Lide looked down at the silent crowd below, taking a deep breath after feeling the heavy atmosphere in the air.
“My fellow citizens, I am your city lord, Kachar.”
A standard opening, but unlike before, Lide’s tone was very deep and serious.
Betty had brought Isa to the gathering as well, and both girls were dressed in black robes tailored for them by the tailor shop today.
Upon seeing Lide, Isa’s eyes immediately lit up, her small hand grasping Betty’s tightly.
And Betty, the Northern Land Valkyrie, looked around with curiosity. Although she had a favorable impression of this city, having seen death often, she did not feel much sadness towards it.
People from the Northern, never fearing death, especially not the warriors dying on the battlefield, which was an honor.
What interested her was that these commoners were so saddened by the sacrifice of vampires.
This was unimaginable anywhere else.
“Today, we are to hold a grand funeral for our heroes,”
“The Holy Light Bloodline are the protectors of Dawn City, the guardians of every resident.”
“Each member of the Holy Light Bloodline peacefully lying in their coffins has sacrificed for Dawn City.”
“They are heroes, undoubtedly heroes, heroes that every resident of Dawn City should hold in reverence.”
Lide’s tone was filled with sorrow.
“No one wishes to give up their life, yet for the sake of family and friends left behind, for the land beneath their feet, for the lovers in their arms.”
“Every member of the Holy Light Bloodline stood unwaveringly, sacrificing their lives for the prosperous future of Dawn City.”
“We are all beneficiaries,”
“Today, we gather here to mourn these heroes who sacrificed themselves for Dawn City, this honor belongs to them!”
Lide’s voice had an irresistible force of incitement, increasingly vehement.
“As the Patriarch of the Holy Light Bloodline and the City Lord of Dawn City, I swear to my people,”
“From now on, any resident who sacrifices themselves for Dawn City, whether commoners or the Holy Light Bloodline, shall be entitled to be buried in the Heroic Cemetery and will be eulogized by all of Dawn City.”
“To commemorate these heroes who died for Dawn City, I will erect the Dawn Heroes Memorial in the city,”
“Every hero who gave their life for Dawn City must be remembered!”
These words stirred the crowd below, everyone who sacrificed for Dawn City receiving such an honor was almost beyond belief.
Who wouldn’t want to be celebrated and revered after their death? The commoners were too insignificant in the past, insignificant to the point that no one cared about them, but now they felt recognized and valued once more.
And the Security Team and other City Hall employees were extremely excited, feeling a sense of purpose in the words of the City Lord of Kachar.
The people who contributed to Dawn City shall not be forgotten.
“Long live Lord Kachar!”
“Long live the City Lord of Kachar!”
“…”
As the commoners shouted loudly, the sorrowful atmosphere diminished significantly.
Watching the handsome figure on the platform, numerous residents felt genuinely grateful in their hearts.
Lide took a deep look at the crowd; the sacrifice of heroes was a sad affair, but it could also transform this sadness into a unifying and uplifting occasion.
Once the crowd quieted down, he continued.
“I hope every resident remembers this day.”
“To commemorate the fallen heroes, I’ve decided to declare their day of sacrifice—May 10th—as Hero Memorial Day.”
“Every May 10th, we shall hold a remembrance ceremony for the passed heroes.”
Lide paused, looking at the eager crowd below.
He spoke loudly.
“Now, to proceed with the hero’s funeral,”
“Offer flowers,”
At that moment, outside the square on the streets, the Holy Divine Priest, Nero, clad in a pure white priest’s robe, followed by twenty nuns holding pristine white flowers, stepped forward.
Nero’s eyes, glowing with a faint golden light, held indescribable dignity and sanctity, causing the surrounding crowd to unconsciously adopt a solemn expression.
No one dared to profane the Divine dignity.
Step by step.
The nuns behind her quietly chanted hymns, filling the scene with a strong religious atmosphere.
Under everyone’s gaze, Nero gently placed her flowers on the central coffin.
The white flowers contrasted sharply with the black coffin.
After offering the flowers, Nero bowed deeply to the coffin, then turned around and rejoined the nuns, chanting hymns softly.
The crowd began to step forward spontaneously, placing the white flowers they held or wore on the coffin.
The whole scene was solemn yet immensely sacred.
Everyone felt an inexplicable sense of honor in such a setting; being a part of it seemed like a matter of fortune for everyone.
For a full Sunshine Hour, the crowd finished offering flowers.
By then, the coffin was covered with a thick layer of fresh flowers.
Lide’s tone remained heavy.
“Enter the Heroic Cemetery,”
Upon hearing the command, the nearby Security Team members stepped forward to carry the coffins.
And the enormous corpse of the One-eyed Giant was lifted by twenty Bloodline members using Mage’s Hand.
The scene was striking.
Dozens of coffins, plus the body of a One-eyed Giant, began their procession down the streets of Dawn City.
All residents followed the funeral procession.
At this moment, the crowd was undivided by rank or familiarity; they all stood together.
They were all seeing off their heroes.
The fresh flowers from the coffins gradually fell onto the stone ground with each step forward, rendering the scene profoundly poignant.
