A path paved with flowers formed along the streets of Dawn City as the coffins progressed, lending an unspeakable sanctity to the flowers that fell.
Lide led the funeral procession at the very front.
Among the crowd, countless gazes watched this spectacle, all filled with emotion.
Even Betty, the Northern Land Valkyrie, accustomed to countless life-and-death situations, could not help but wear a solemn expression upon seeing such a scene.
To receive such an honorable funeral was almost every warrior’s dream; never had she seen such a grand funeral in the Northern lands, and the surprises in Dawn City grew increasingly profound for her.
She was also astounded by Lide’s actions.
As a sovereign of a city, a king of a race, witnessing such dedication to fallen warriors was unimaginable.
In Human Country, when had high-flung nobles ever cared about the life and death of their soldiers?
Glancing at the poignant eyes in the crowd, she suddenly understood something.
The city’s vibrancy and charm were not without reason.
Because they had such an exceptional City Lord, a king that even she envied.

chapters.title: Chapter 191: 192 The Eve of the Birth of a Dark Boss in Green City
chapters.content:
Chapter 191: Chapter 192 The Eve of the Birth of a Dark Boss in Green City
Lide had specifically designated an area as the Heroic Cemetery, where only those heroes who had sacrificed themselves for Dawn City were qualified to be buried. This place was not for ordinary people.
The burial process proceeded, soil filling the graves.
After the final gravestone was erected, Lide gazed across the over forty graves on the empty land and remained silent for a long while.
None of the residents of Dawn City who came to mourn made a sound either.
But at this moment, silence was more profound than sound.
Hearts quietly united.
...
The greatest purpose of the Heroic Cemetery was just that: to bond people’s hearts and boost morale to the maximum.
Anyone who sacrificed for Dawn City, once deceased, was entitled to be buried there and revered by others.
Such a practice was quite normal on Earth.
But in Glory World, it was exceptionally rare.
The world here was not a safe place, death wasn’t a big deal.
Only those with distinguished contributions were worthy of remembrance, while ordinary warriors and civilians who died in battle hardly enjoyed such elaborate funerals.
Yet, people always yearned for beauty. Which warrior wouldn’t want his name sung after a heroic death?
The Heroic Cemetery of Dawn City compensated for that, one could imagine the intense battle strength these respected warriors would unleash in future battles.
Lide didn’t deliver another speech. After spotting Isa among the crowd, he silently left with the little girl, leaving the residents to continue honoring the deceased heroes.
Among the crowd, many even gazed at the fresh gravestones with longing eyes.
If one day they could receive such an elaborate funeral upon their death, what regrets could they possibly have?
Ultimately, the funeral of heroes concluded successfully.
The cohesion of Dawn City was enhanced once again, and Lide, the initiator, held an indescribable status in the eyes of the residents.
Even those who did not follow the Dawn Sect nearly idolized Lide as a divine figure.
Only a great Divine could achieve such acts. Meeting the great Kachar City Lord was the greatest fortune of their lives, praise the Goddess of Luck!
The dead had passed away, but life must go on.
After the funeral, Lide returned to the City Hall and summoned all the top executives of Dawn City for a truly significant meeting.
He wanted to plan the key developmental focuses of Dawn City in the coming months.
His experiences in the battle against the Dark Contract had altered many of his views, urging him to modify the previous development directions.
This time, all the heavyweight figures of Dawn City attended.
The second-generation Bloodlines,
Frey, guardian of the sacred lands,
City Hall Chairman Harrison,
Dylan, the breeder of Magic Language Bats,
The two female Bloodlines, Ivy and Lucy,
Archer Augustine along with Audis who was in charge of plundering populations,
All seven Bloodlines who had followed Lide for a hundred years were present.
The remaining top combatants of Dawn City—Emi, Grote, and Betty—were also impressively present.
As for Koso, who had evolved into a bronze One-eyed Giant, due to his size, he could only listen to the meeting from the courtyard of the City Hall.
The huge head by the window was Koso; by leaning out of the third floor window, one could see his agile moving eye.
Lide was quite satisfied seeing this scene.
Now, Dawn City could be described as brimming with talents, a world apart from the meagerness when he first arrived among the Bloodline.
Even his mentor Spark, a 19th level Great Mage who oversaw the White Tower, Lide felt confident defeating the White Tower if it came to conflict.
This was the team he had painstakingly built.
“Grote, report on the matter concerning the Dark Contract and Viscount Bernard,”
In the large office, everyone sat around a long, oval, gray table, intricately carved chairs surrounding it, and Grote was directly named by Lide, who was seated at the head.
Although the Dark Contract had somewhat concluded, Lide’s interest had spiked elsewhere.
This former Child of the North stood up, his towering frame imposing, under everyone’s watchful eyes.
“Ancestor Crown, I arrived in Green City twenty-two years ago after leaving the North,” Grote began recounting his past.
“On the journey, I encountered a terrifying Demon Beast tide. The companions with me suffered horrendous losses; even I nearly perished.
Maybe it was the Goddess of Luck’s favor, it was during the most dangerous moment that Viscount Bernard saved me and all the Northern warriors.”
His tone paused, seemingly reflective as the memories still seemed to move him.
“Having no place to go after leaving the North, at Viscount Bernard’s invitation, I joined the Dark Contract, becoming his Guard Commander.”
Lide nodded, his eyes flickering with keenness.
“How much do you know about Viscount Bernard?”
He had always been wary of the elegant Viscount Bernard.
Although his final goal wasn’t the Crimson Mage Tower, and angering a Transcendent meant inevitably facing the wrath of Transcendents, survival was uncertain.
But for some reason, he didn’t believe Viscount Bernard would be killed by Extraordinary Hunting, his vigilance never waned.
And now, his plans were to snatch from Viscount Bernard’s mouth – it was essential to know more about his enemy.
Unexpectedly, Grote shook his head.
“Ancestor Crown, I don’t know much about Viscount Bernard.”
This response was beyond Lide’s expectations.
“How so?”
“I might be the Guard Commander for Viscount Bernard, but Viscount Bernard has never trusted me. He only valued me for my battle prowess as a Northern Warrior.
For over twenty years by his side, I never knew his true identity, not even his race or profession.”
Grot’s tone carried an unmistakable sense of astonishment, “Viscount Bernard is the most cautious person I have ever met.
He has never mentioned anything to me besides the Dark Contract, so as for him, perhaps I don’t know any more than anyone else.”
Everyone in the room exchanged glances.
It was unexpected for Grot to respond this way, being a Guard Commander who had served by his side for over twenty years and yet knew nothing of his real identity.
It was truly astonishing.
After hearing this, Lide fell silent for a long while, aware that Viscount Bernard was difficult to handle, but not to such an extent.
But once he made a decision about something he intended to do, he never entertained any thoughts of retreating.
A trace of a cold light flashed in his eyes.
“I don’t care about his real origins; I just want to know if Viscount Bernard doesn’t return soon,
do we have a chance to swallow up the Dark Contract!”
Hiss~
Emi and Grot exchanged glances upon hearing this, both showing some surprise. Swallow the Dark Contract?
This plan had never crossed their minds before, and although their top combat strength was not inferior to the Dark Contract, was it not too risky to act while the whereabouts of Viscount Bernard were unknown?
“Ancestor Crown, now is not a good time to swallow the Dark Contract.”
Lide’s gaze was piercing as he looked at Emi, who had just spoken.
“How so?”
Emi stood up and after a moment of contemplation said, “Although the Dark Contract is loosely managed, it has always been controlled by Viscount Bernard.
No one else knows the secrets hidden within the Dark Contract.
The true identities of those few masked figures in black robes who attend meetings are also known only to Viscount Bernard.
Even the various forces operated by the Dark Contract can only be mobilized by Viscount Bernard.”
Emi took a deep breath, “So it’s not an exaggeration to say that the Dark Contract is a force established by Viscount Bernard alone.
We vice presidents are merely pulled in randomly by him.
No one knows what purpose Viscount Bernard had in establishing the Dark Contract. I’ve once incidentally studied the origin of the Dark Contract.
Its emergence in Green City forty years ago was sudden and it wasn’t a local power,
so at a time when Viscount Bernard’s whereabouts are unknown, I believe it’s not a good time to strike at the Dark Contract.”
Lide understood the unspoken implications in Emi’s words—there were too many uncertainties.
But he did not back down, shaking his head with a determined tone.
“That’s not an issue. It doesn’t matter how Viscount Bernard controls the Dark Contract.
I don’t even plan to completely inherit the power of the Dark Contract.
I need a Dark Contract that I can fully control, even if it’s weaker than before.”
A resolute unshakeable determination shone in his deep dark eyes on that handsome face; once he was set on something, he was committed to accomplishing it without any excuses or rationale.
The time was right now, with the heavens, the terrain, and the people all on his side.
The timing, as Viscount Bernard had provoked an Extraordinary Existence for some reason and was now untraceable, but being marked by an Extraordinary, it could be imagined that he would not have an easy time soon.
The terrain, Green City was right under his eyes and the Dark Contract was within his reach.
The human element, the most crucial part, the Dark Contract’s Vice President Emi was his Bloodline, Viscount Bernard’s Guard Commander Grot was also his Bloodline,
an important member of the Dark Contract, the bishop of the Late Bell Church—Stanley, would become his Bloodline in a month.
Additionally, the Undead Mage Withered Bone had been captured by him; the current power of the Dark Contract was unprecedentedly weak without Viscount Bernard.
If he did not seize this opportunity to swallow the Dark Contract, then he would not be Lide.
And regardless of how powerful the Dark Contract had been before and how many forces it had hidden, those belonged to Viscount Bernard, not him.
He sought a force that was absolutely obedient; if those hidden forces couldn’t be attained, he would let them go.
It was no big deal.
Even just having the facade was enough for Lide to reap immense benefits.
Although previously loosely managed in Green City, the Dark Contract’s status and influence among the underground forces were absolutely top-ranking.
Without an owner, the Dark Contract was like a piece of honey-smeared bread to him, oozing an alluring sweet scent.
For all these reasons, after careful thought, Lide decided to make the move.
“Ancestor Crown, the Dark Contract is probably being besieged by the military of Green City at this moment. If we act now, will it be…?” Grot voiced his doubt with some hesitation.
Lide shook his head.
“No, I want to act while the Dark Contract is in chaos. If it weren’t for a crisis within the Dark Contract, how could we subdue them?”
A glimmer of deep meaning flashed in his eyes.
“A crisis for the Dark Contract might just be an opportunity for us.”
“Grot, Emi, secretly return to Green City and go undercover. Remember, during this time some Extraordinary might intervene to cleanse Green City, so be sure to prioritize your safety first.”
“While ensuring safety, secretly take control of the forces of the Dark Contract.”
“I want to see a new Dark Contract emerge in a month.”
“By then, the Dark Contract will have a new master.”

chapters.title: Chapter 192: 193: Planning the Future
chapters.content:
Chapter 192: Chapter 193: Planning the Future
After discussing it over, Lide decided to let Grote and Betty head back to Green City first, while Emi would return half a month later.
Because the Dawn Mage Tower was about to be completed.
This Mage Tower, which had taken half a year and had been under continuous construction day and night by hundreds of ordinary civilians, seven or eight One-eyed Giants, and over a hundred of the Bloodline, was finally about to be completed.
As the chief architect of the Mage Tower, Emi, of course, would not be absent.
Furthermore, the affairs of the Dark Contract were not something that could be settled in just a day or two.
Letting Grote return first to test the waters, and Betty because of Isa, Isa couldn’t possibly always stay in Dawn City, Spark, the Great Mage, could better assist Isa’s growth.
...
Moreover, the key thing was that Lide now had to find a powerful deterrent for the Crimson Mage Tower openly, though Spark had always been sheltering the Crimson Mage Tower, he couldn’t mobilize this “inexpensive teacher.”
And to subdue the Dark Contract was certainly not so simple; Grote’s combat capability was extraordinary, but compared to Betty, there was still a gap.
Both of them, plus the subsequent arrival of Emi, would inevitably create a formidable trident in Green City.
Now, Dawn City, which had entered a period of development, didn’t need that much high-end combat power. In terms of production, Betty’s role might not even be as significant as a single ordinary One-eyed Giant.
“Harry, keep developing Dawn City. I will provide all the resources needed. I hope that within the next few months, Dawn City will undergo even greater changes.”
At this point, the geographical advantage of Dawn City became evident.
Battle and strife outside, Dawn City would remain unaffected, and development would continue.
This advantage of being distant from external disturbances is one of the biggest strengths of Dawn City,
a dream for all the forces in Glory.
“Agriculture is the most critical project in all development and must be given top priority. Any matter related to agriculture must be dealt with as a matter of urgency,” Lide told everyone, “Agriculture relates to the raiding of the population during the Frost Month, and we must not be careless before the crops are harvested.”
“Yes, Clan Leader.”
The second generation Bloodline members uniformly responded, and under Lide’s repeated emphasis, everyone fully recognized the importance of the matter.
Lide, satisfied with the Bloodline members’ attitude, nodded and continued with the next arrangement.
“The mining operations cannot stop, either. Iron ore is our basic resource and indispensable for both civilian life and military needs. The role iron ore plays in the future will only grow.
The exploration teams must continue searching for veins; we cannot stop at just one, as it’s not enough to satisfy the development needs of Dawn City.
Harry, note this especially, to avoid a shortage of One-eyed Giants leading to a halt in mining operations.
It’s essential for humans to also engage in vein mining; I don’t want to see the mining sites come to a standstill again after the One-eyed Giants are pulled away.”
Due to the One-eyed Giants’ race advantage, they had almost single-handedly completed all the mining operations.
One One-eyed Giant’s work efficiency could match that of fifty or sixty normal people, creating a disparity in efficiency and thus a compelling reason for the mining sites’ disdain for ordinary humans and extreme reliance on One-eyed Giants.
This time, after the One-eyed Giants were reassigned by Lide into the combat sequence, the entire mining site came to a halt, severely affecting the iron mining.
The saying goes, “Don’t put all your eggs in one basket.” As the numbers of One-eyed Giants couldn’t be significantly increased, the role of humans also couldn’t be overlooked.
“Yes, Clan Leader, I’ll inform the construction department right away.”
Harry nodded with a serious expression, realizing the gravity of the situation after Lide pointed it out.
There were too few One-eyed Giants, and there was no alternative source for this non-renewable, rare labor force.
Yet, he couldn’t help but become dependent on these highly efficient production tools.
There was nothing wrong with that, but Harry had overlooked that the One-eyed Giants were not merely production tools but also powerful warriors. In the event of a war, these strong giants would have to join the battlefield.
Lide nodded without saying anything.
After getting used to the high efficiency of the One-eyed Giants, it was indeed hard to feel good about the work efficiency of ordinary humans.
But production resources were limited, and as the One-eyed Giants were even more effective than modern machinery, they played a significant role in Dawn City; therefore, it was impossible to use them all in one place.
Unless he could find more One-eyed Giants, he would have no choice but to involve humans in the mining industries; otherwise, the next time a battle broke out, the mines would face the same predicament as before.
Thinking of this, Lide turned his head to glance outside the window and sighed softly as he looked at Koso’s huge head.
“If only we could get our hands on a batch of One-eyed Giants,” he mused.
Moments later, he shook his head to dismiss the thought; now was not the time for such considerations.
The One-eyed Giants existed, but they were all in the Underworld of Giant Valley, and Dawn City currently lacked the resources to explore the vast Underworld.
He moved on to the next agenda item.
“Dylan must pay close attention to the breeding farms and the Magic Language Bat expansion. I want to see a large-scale participation of Magic Language Bats in the production of Dawn City as soon as possible.”
The recent significant reduction in the number of Magic Language Bats had impacted the construction progress of Dawn City greatly, and Lide attached great importance to this.
“Yes, Clan Leader,” Dylan, a towering figure, stood up and bowed with his hand on his chest.
“Audis and Lucy, you two will work with Harrison’s arrangements, deploying Bloodline where needed.
Ivy and Augustine, assist Harrison in managing Dawn City at the City Hall; I hope you can play an even greater role.”
“Frey, the responsibility of the holy land and the ordinary residents’ blood donations is yours to handle. You must ensure the safety of the blood pools, and the blood donations must not be neglected. I hope the two newly built blood pools can be filled within the next two years.
In addition, no one shall use the Magic Blood of the central blood pool without my orders.”
Lide issued a series of commands in rapid succession.
The second-generation Bloodline immediately rose and saluted.
“Yes, Clan Leader.”
Lide scanned the room, observing the spirited expressions on everyone’s faces and felt an inexplicable surge of boldness.
These were the subordinates he had built up bit by bit, the pillars of Dawn City’s future.
Every one of them was a person he absolutely trusted.
“The future of Dawn City lies in our hands; its development requires the efforts of us all.
I hope that each one of you can contribute even more to Dawn City.”
Lide’s deep gaze carried boundless boldness, and the corners of his mouth curled up high.
“For Dawn City!”
Everyone below was taken aback for a moment, then feeling moved, they looked at each other and stood up simultaneously, bowing to Lide with hands on their chests.
“For Dawn City!”
Their voices were in unison, filled with soaring fighting spirit.
Especially the seven second-generation Bloodline who had always followed Lide; they were particularly enthusiastic, firm in their belief that under Lide’s leadership, the Bloodline would seize the future.
All the Bloodline bowed to Lide, while Betty, the Northern Land Valkyrie, somewhat adorably and confusedly sat on her stool watching the sudden scene unfold.
She was still somewhat puzzled by the situation.
Feeling slightly out of place, she thought of saying something but, looking at Lide’s handsome, elegant, and powerful posture, she closed her mouth again.
At that moment, she felt as if she was in the presence of a king of a race, a sovereign with great deterring power.
Not to be challenged.
This wild Valkyrie of noble Bloodline quietly subdued some of her wildness before Lide.

chapters.title: Chapter 193: 194 The Dawn Mage Tower Opens...
chapters.content:
Chapter 193: Chapter 194 The Dawn Mage Tower Opens…
June 2nd.
A piece of news had the Dawn City boiling over.
The Crimson Mage Tower was completed and opened today.
The Great Kachar City Lord was to personally attend the completion ceremony.
To the common people of Glory, the three words “Mage Tower” were absolutely sacred and inviolable.
In the eyes of many, the status of the Mage Tower was comparable to a temple possessing the Divine.
...
Mysterious, powerful, dignified, magical, wealthy, influential, and so forth
These adjectives represented the truest thoughts of the commoners towards the Mage Tower.
If one were to debate which profession was the most powerful in Glory, opinions might differ—Dragon Knight, Mage, Temple Knight, Bloodline Warrior, and others could all potentially be ranked first.
But if one were to ask what profession the commoners of Glory most aspired to become,
There was no doubt, there was only one: Mage.
In a world of magic, the status of a Mage was equivalent to that of the Nobles, and yet a Mage possessed far greater power than any noble.
Everyone yearned to be an elegant gentleman, a debonair Mage Lord capable of casting magic at will.
Hence, when the Crimson Mage Tower was completed, all the residents of Dawn City were stirred.
For the Kachar City Lord had promised them that their children would have the opportunity to become apprentices in the Mage Tower and ascend to the lofty status of Mage Lords.
And the Great Kachar City Lord had never deceived them, never!!!
People hurried to spread the news, hope filling everyone’s eyes.
Although it didn’t mean their children necessarily possessed the Talent to be selected, it represented hope.
Whether or not one could be selected was one matter; having a choice was another.
Over the next few days, the spirits of the believers within the Dawn Sect surged once more.
For His Excellency Kachar had fulfilled his promises time and again, distributing houses, allocating land, constructing the Mage Tower—all of these accomplishments filled the residents with immense satisfaction and pride.
Lide was naturally pleased with this since everything in Dawn City was his private property… whether they were Bloodline or humans.
Hence, he would continue to implement more policies to develop and expand his private properties. Who would mind if the sheep in the pen were fed until plump?
Approaching dusk, on the outskirts of the southern district of Dawn City—the newly established Moonlight District, built upon the Moonlight Plain was mostly grassland, but this did not diminish its status in the hearts of Dawn City’s residents.
For here stood a monumental construction—the Crimson Mage Tower.
The construction of the Crimson Mage Tower from inception to completion involved over 500 human construction workers and more than a hundred Bloodline workers daily, even reaching a peak when 2,000 civilians, along with six or seven One-eyed Giants, worked on the site simultaneously.
Such costly efforts spent over half a year and used up 60,000 Gold Pucks to be finally completed.
A massive building had come into existence.
Lide stood in front of the main entrance of the Crimson Mage Tower; even having seen the grandeur of the White Tower, he couldn’t help but marvel at his own Mage Tower.
Magnificent and spectacular.
The Crimson Mage Tower consisted of one Main Tower and eight auxiliary towers.
The Main Tower stood twenty-seven blades high, comprising seven levels, with a square spire top and a circular body, covering an area Lide estimated to be ten times that of another famous Mage Tower.
It was even rounder by three circles when compared to Spark’s White Tower, belonging to the 19th level Great Mage.
The exterior walls of the round tower were smeared with black alchemy paint, a recipe Emi had obtained from inside the Knight Temple. These exterior wall coatings alone had cost Lide 20,000 Gold Pucks.
Of course, the effects were quite apparent as the concentration and activity of Magic Power within the Mage Tower were more than five times that of the outside world, making meditation and Magic Power training in the Mage Tower countless times stronger than outside.
The remaining eight subsidiary towers each stood 15 blades tall, with five levels, and covered twice the ground area of the Crimson Mage Tower, albeit slightly shorter in height.
The subsidiary towers were about three hundred blades away from the Main Tower, encircling it in the center from eight directions like stars around the moon.
Surprisingly, the eight subsidiary towers were not coated with the black alchemy paint but were other colors instead.
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet—like a rainbow, they presented seven different colors, with only the subsidiary tower in the center of the Mage Tower’s main gate matching the Main Tower’s black color.
The Mage Tower cluster, resembling a rainbow, carried a mysterious yet somewhat ethereal beauty, very much to Lide’s taste.
The Dawn Mage Tower cluster was isolated by towering blue walls, constructed from blue stones that the One-eyed Giant had transported from nearby mountains, some of which were as tall as three blades and weighed more than ten tons.
The walls stood five blades tall and, it was said, involved all of the Magic Language Bats, One-eyed Giants, and the Bloodline, taking a whole half month to complete.
The engineering effort was no less significant than that of the Mage Tower’s subsidiary towers.
The ground was paved with blue stones, and, thanks to the presence of magic, processing the blue stones was not very difficult, resulting in a smooth and even surface.
To enter the inside of the Mage Tower, one could only go through the black subsidiary tower at the front, with the towering walls enclosing the entire Mage Tower, only the middle recessed part connecting to the black subsidiary tower.
The black subsidiary gate was nine blades wide and six blades tall, allowing even a One-eyed Giant to enter.
From a distance, as one approached the black subsidiary tower, the towering Main Tower could no longer be seen, but from the magnificence of the subsidiary tower alone, it was evident just how vast the Dawn Mage Tower cluster really was.
Lide stepped up onto the stage early prepared, as residents always looked forward to his speeches on significant occasions.
All the residents had gathered today, curiously surveying the Mage Tower, and upon seeing Lide step onto the stage, immediately burst into fervent cheers.
“My people, I am your City Lord, Kachar.”
Each time he started his speech, Lide could stir up the crowd below.
“I promised you all, on the day you arrived in Dawn City,
that in the future, Dawn City would build a Mage Tower, would establish a school,
and every resident of Dawn City would one day have the opportunity to send your children to learn in the Mage Tower and the school.”
“Today, the Dawn Mage Tower has been completed!
My people, cheer~
I have built the future for all of you!!”
The crowd below could no longer contain their inner excitement and began clapping and cheering frantically.
“Long live His Majesty Kachar…”
“Long live the Kachar City Lord…”
“…”
All eyes were filled with deep respect, especially the believers of the Dawn Sect, who were brimming with fanaticism.
He was their great Majesty, a walking True God on earth, guiding them from the darkness into the light!
“The Dawn Mage Tower will be open for visits for three days, after which we will officially start recruiting Mage Apprentices.
Any youth of the appropriate age can be brought to the Dawn Mage Tower for talent assessment, and once qualified, they can enroll for free to become apprentices of the Dawn Mage Tower!”
With a grand gesture, Lide heralded a new chapter for Dawn City.

chapters.title: Chapter 194: 195: Emi is Shocked, Lide Actually Wants to Take a Mage to Farm? (Added More)
chapters.content:
Chapter 194: Chapter 195: Emi is Shocked, Lide Actually Wants to Take a Mage to Farm? (Added More)
The construction of the Mage Tower injected unimaginable vitality into Dawn City.
During the three days it was open, residents even set aside all their work to visit the Dawn Mage Tower.
Even though the Dawn Mage Tower was still an empty shell and most of the buildings were still in their initial state, this did not hinder the residents’ enthusiasm at all.
For it was their first time being in such close contact with a Mage Tower, the mysterious Mage Tower.
Only the high and mighty mage lords were qualified to reside within it.
The Holy Light Bloodline didn’t do much to stop them, apart from the core areas, the public areas were open for them to tour.
...
Many families with children of the appropriate age had exceptionally radiant smiles these past few days.
Although not all could meet the qualifications to enter the Mage Tower, there was still hope, wasn’t there?
On the seventh floor of the main tower of Dawn Mage Tower, Lide looked out through the transparent windows over the entire Mage Tower area.
In the distance was a barren grassland, devoid of people, and even further were the twinkling lights of Dawn City, which, entering the night, resembled a giant beast sprawled under the moonlight.
His gaze returned to his immediate surroundings, the seven-colored Mage Towers under the moonlight looked exceptionally charming, and he was very satisfied with the Magic Arrays with flowing Magic Fluctuations above the Mage Towers.
Although constructing the Mage Tower cost more than twenty times that of the Crimson Mage Tower, the infrastructure of Dawn Mage Tower was incomparable to that of the Crimson Mage Tower.
This was designed referencing an Extraordinary Level Mage Tower, not just any ordinary one.
One main tower, eight subsidiary towers, these nine spacious Mage Towers could accommodate nearly a thousand people at the same time.
Once the residential buildings within the range of the Mage Tower were completed, the number of people it could accommodate would surpass three thousand.
And such a scale of Dawn Mage Tower still had room for expansion.
If the population continues to increase in the future, new residential circles would be built outside the current walls of Dawn Mage Tower, and then the number of people it could accommodate could reach between eight thousand to ten thousand.
This was already comparable to the current population of Dawn City.
Of course, that was a plan for the future. For now, Dawn Mage Tower would suffice for at least the next five years.
“Ancestor Crown, Dawn Mage Tower was built using the blueprints of an Extraordinary Mage Tower, and it completely satisfies our current needs.
If further expansion is needed, the current building thickness of Dawn Mage Tower can easily allow the main tower to be expanded to the height of a hundred blades, and all subsidiary towers could also be upgraded to fifty blades,”
Emi reported confidently from behind Lide.
“And the main and subsidiary towers can also form a powerful Magic Array…”
Hearing this, Lide became somewhat interested. The construction of Dawn Mage Tower was under Emi’s control, and apart from occasionally reporting the progress, he had not deeply understood this Mage Tower that belonged to him.
He had many issues to handle and not enough time to pay attention to everything.
“Explain in detail.”
After the Bone Dragon’s attack on the Crimson Mage Tower was blocked by a Magic Shield, he had become very interested in Magic Arrays.
Although he had no plans to learn this vast discipline, he still maintained enough interest.
“Yes, Your Highness.
The blueprint of Dawn Mage Tower was obtained from a Transcendent at the Knight Temple. When we acquired this blueprint, I recorded it in detail just in case.
And this blueprint was originally preserved by a Transcendent of the Knight Temple.
This Transcendent provided a detailed explanation for this blueprint and also enhanced a powerful Magic Array from the Knight Temple and added it to it.
After thorough research, I confirmed that the Magic Array could be constructed, so I reserved space for building it during the construction of Dawn Mage Tower.
The functions of this Magic Array are very powerful, including detection, lie detection, tracking, defense, and more. If built, it would greatly assist Dawn City.”
After speaking, a hint of regret appeared in Emi’s eyes.
“However, the only pity is that we do not have enough Magic Crystal Stones, and building this Magic Array would cost no less than five hundred thousand Gold Pucks.”
I…
Upon hearing this, Lide felt overwhelmed.
It always involved money, why is building a Magic Array so expensive?
The Ancient Alchemy Magic Array for the Crimson Mage Tower hadn’t even reached its limit yet, and now here was another gold-consuming behemoth. It was really too much.
He had thought that establishing a Magic Factory would lead to a wealthy life, but now it was still necessary to be meticulous in budgeting.
He was earning a lot, true, but even more was needed for spending.
“Let’s put the construction of the Magic Array on hold for now, Dawn City won’t need it for a while.”
After considering it, Lide still shook his head and refused. Although the Magic Array was good, it wasn’t a high priority, and Dawn Mage Tower wasn’t the Crimson Mage Tower.
This place was safe enough, and establishing a Magic Array now wouldn’t be very useful.
On the other hand, the Crimson Mage Tower was a real necessity, as anything could happen in the outside world.
Although Emi felt somewhat regretful, he dared not say more because there was no room for discussion in the decisions Lide made.
“Yes, Ancestor Crown.”
“Furthermore, organize the residents to undergo Magic Talent tests as soon as possible, and any teenager under twenty who meets the basic requirements can be recruited into the Mage Tower for training.”
A gleam of determination flashed through Lide’s eyes, “In the future, Dawn City must have not only Combat Mages but also Production Mages.
Emi, from now on, divide Mage Apprentices into two types for assessment,
the first is Talent, those with high Mage Talent are to be prioritized for inclusion in the ranks of Combat Mages and should be first considered when developing the Bloodline.
The second is Character, Mage Apprentices who dare to take risks and are not afraid of combat should be developed into Combat Mages.
Others with lower talent and a gentler character should only be taught supportive Spells to become part of Dawn City’s productivity.”
Lide’s strategy was very clear. Mages, as a powerful group with command over forces, were undeniably strong in combat.
However, using them solely for combat would undoubtedly waste resources, and to him, the role of Mages in production was no less significant compared to their combat capabilities.
Regrettably, due to the entrenched influences of this world, no one would think of using Magic to farm.
To use Magic in production within Glory was an unconventional thought.
The idea that Mage equals Nobility had long been ingrained; having Nobility gentry engage in menial production? That’s likely the work of a mind eaten by Demons.
As a soul from the modern world, Lide obviously didn’t subscribe to these nonsensical notions. To him, the power possessed by Mages was akin to modern machinery capable of accomplishing many tasks that ordinary people could not.
His experiences during this period of construction had also validated his ideas.
Thus, he planned to develop Dawn Mage Tower into two parts.
The first part would undoubtedly be the combat section, where all mages would receive top-notch training to learn the most powerful spells,
while the second part would be the Ministry of Civil Affairs, where these Mages would be trained to become producers for Dawn City, learning supportive spells,
such as Mage’s Hand, Cleansing Skill, Driving Away Wild Beasts, Healing Skill, Physical Healing, and others that can be used for productive purposes.
Of course, this was just a rough plan of Lide’s; although promising, it still had many flaws that needed perfecting.
Building a city was about developing through exploration, and not making mistakes was not Lide’s way.
“Emi, you can take this opportunity to classify all the Bloodline’s Spells,
separating combat spells from supportive spells.
Especially list those that can be used in production, and later establish a dedicated research department within Dawn Mage Tower.
Specifically to study how to apply Spells to agricultural cultivation or other production construction.”
After hearing this, Emi opened his mouth to speak but then closed it and could only nod.
If he hadn’t become one of the Bloodline, this Shadow High Priest would surely have cursed Lide as a heretic; for dignified Spellcasters, to think all day about using Spells in agricultural production—preposterous.
Noble Spellcasters farming??
I….
But seeing Lide’s earnest gaze, Emi had to sincerely agree, clearly understanding Lide’s ideas.
He also knew how high a Mage’s productivity could be.
Understanding was one thing, acceptance another.
Lide noticed Emi’s frustrated expression and was indifferent, well aware of the deeply rooted notions of this world, unconcerned about who was right or wrong, but seeing it as a mere difference in perspective.
To him, as long as it was useful, what was wrong with Mages farming?
Even Dylan, the noble and elegant member of the Bloodline, he had made him raise pigs.
“Additionally, research on faith must not fall behind. In the future, there will be much for Dawn Mage Tower to research, and I hope you can get the Mage Tower up and running soon.”
Lide’s eyes were full of encouragement. Dawn Mage Tower’s future role was more than just a simple Mage Tower.
In fact, Lide preferred to think of it as a talent development base and research institution that would specialize in solving some problems he couldn’t solve on his own.
Upon hearing this, Emi immediately perked up.
“Ancestor Crown, Emi will follow your dispatch.”

chapters.title: Chapter 195: 196 The First Step to Absorbing the Dark Contract
chapters.content:
Chapter 195: Chapter 196 The First Step to Absorbing the Dark Contract
Dark Contract was in chaos.
When Viscount Bernard was being pursued by the Transcendents and had been missing for almost half a month, while the army of Green City was fervently hunting the members of Dark Contract, the leaderless Dark Contract plunged into unprecedented turbulence and chaos.
Every day, a large number of Dark Contract’s members were captured, and every day, strongholds were destroyed.
Even Grot, who had returned to Green City, did not know how powerful the Dark Contract, which Viscount Bernard had operated for decades, had been.
But now Dark Contract had become a scattered force, with no one stepping forward to lead this giant entity, turning this dark force into sheep to the slaughter.
The power composition of Dark Contract was very disparate, including Late Bell Church, Abyss Demons, Undead Mages, and the Shadow High Priest Emi, plus Grot, a Northern Warrior, and a mysterious person who had never revealed their true identity.
...
So, when Grot returned to Green City and wanted to consolidate the remaining forces of Dark Contract, he also felt somewhat at a loss as to where to begin.
Fortunately, he found an old stronghold and met a few of his old subordinates.
In the western district of Green City, an old civilian residence.
Grot looked at the five figures before him with a slightly grim expression.
After scanning the group, he spoke to the middle figure with a full beard and a large, burly figure, a Level 12 Advanced Warrior.
“Gary, what’s the situation with Dark Contract now? And what about Viscount Bernard?”
Dressed in gray warrior armor, with a dim look in his eyes, Gary shook his head, his voice very coarse.
“Lord Grot, Dark Contract has suffered heavy casualties these past days under the attacks from Green City’s army, our underground strongholds have already been mostly destroyed.
Currently, we might have fewer than 500 members left,” Gary said in a low tone, “The chairman has been without news, may the Life Goddess protect us, I hope Viscount Bernard returns safely.”
After speaking, he looked a bit blankly at Grot. Dark Contract had rescued him from the slums and nurtured him.
His life had been given by Dark Contract.
But now with Viscount Bernard missing, and Dark Contract nearly facing destruction, his faith for which he fought was about to collapse; he now felt directionless.
A contemplative look flashed in Grot’s eyes as he recalled the instructions from Lide. After pondering for a moment, he slowly spoke.
“Gary, although Viscount Bernard is being hunted by an Extraordinary Mage, we must believe that Viscount Bernard can escape.”
After finishing, he changed the subject, “But what I’m curious about is, why did Viscount Bernard suddenly attack the City Lord’s manor? Does he not know about the existence of the Transcendents?”
Gary shook his head, “I cannot fathom the wisdom of Viscount Bernard, I think, perhaps there was a deeper consideration.”
Though he said this, the Advanced Warrior’s eyes were still very confused.
Everyone knew that Extraordinary Beings were not to be provoked, yet under these circumstances, their boss still offended a Transcendent, which deeply puzzled him.
Grot slightly shook his head, his tone growing heavy.
“Yet, Viscount Bernard could have easily informed the members of Dark Contract beforehand, allowing our comrades to take cover to avoid Green City’s military encirclement.
But why would Viscount Bernard go about a pre-planned action and yet keep it hidden from our comrades?”
Ah? This…
Gary and the other four in the room were also full of confusion, and couldn’t help but widen their eyes to listen for Grot’s explanation.
“One would think that for such an important event, even if the chairman did not wish to reveal the secret, would it have been difficult to arrange for someone to notify Dark Contract’s members to take cover after the attack?
By the Goddess, our respected chairman, did he ever think about us? Did he really care about our lives?”
His harsh words, like a dagger, struck the hearts of others in the room, making everyone’s expression unsightly as wild thoughts tangled in their minds like weeds.
No matter how much they thought about it, the conclusion they reached was that Viscount Bernard had perhaps never cared about the lives of the other members of Dark Contract.
Although everyone knew that the lower-tier members weren’t valued, upon serious reflection, it was still hard to accept.
No one wanted to be considered expendable, or treated as a worthless piece to be discarded.
Grot shook his head, his tone seeming pained, “I’ve been Bernard’s Guard Commander, following Viscount Bernard for over twenty years,
but I’ve always felt that Dark Contract was nothing more than a tool for the chairman, a tool that’s discarded once its use is fulfilled.”
With a hint of lamentation on his face.
“Although I don’t want to admit it, I must say that perhaps Viscount Bernard has never cared about Dark Contract, nor has he ever cared about us who are willing to give our lives for him…”
These words, as Dark Contract was caught in encirclement and the ordinary members fell into panic, pierced like a sharp knife into their hearts.
Gary’s complexion turned pale as he shook his head, his beliefs seemingly crumbling slowly.
Although he didn’t want to acknowledge Grot’s words, the reality was right before him; he couldn’t not acknowledge it.
“No, that can’t be, perhaps Viscount Bernard is just entangled with the Extraordinary Mage, he definitely won’t abandon us,”
Another member of Dark Contract painfully refused to accept this reality.
Grot watched their vacant expressions and continued to pressure them.
“Give up? Yes, in fact, when Viscount Bernard chose not to make any arrangements before leaving Green City, we were already abandoned.
Didn’t everyone know our original target was the Crimson Mage Tower?
Everyone had prepared for months, but in the end, Viscount Bernard chose to attack the City Lord’s manor. Did he really not have time to arrange for the others in the Dark Contract?”
The voice grew colder.
“No, he had time, he just didn’t care about the lives of us all in the Dark Contract. How many of us died because of Viscount Bernard’s actions? Two thousand or three thousand?”
In fact, Viscount Bernard hadn’t involved ordinary gang members in this operation. Although it wasn’t exactly caring, he indeed hadn’t sent them to their deaths on purpose.
But the fact remained that, whether intentionally or not, the Dark Contract was now on the verge of collapse under the siege of Green City’s army.
Especially at this critical time, when all the higher-ups of the Dark Contract were absent.
Emi, Grot, along with the captured Stanley and Undead Mage Withered Bone, and the dead Kolong.
These five were the bulk of the Dark Contract’s top combat strength, while the Eight-Armed Snake Demon Roy and Viscount Bernard had left Green City, their whereabouts unknown.
The remaining mysterious person seemed to care nothing for the Dark Contract, even now when the Dark Contract was facing collapse, no one appeared.
So, the situation now was that the Dark Contract had no one to lead, all the influential members were gone, it would be strange if it weren’t collapsing under the siege.
“Lord Grot, what are your thoughts?”
Gary asked with a trembling tone, and the rest turned their gazes towards Grot, their eyes filled with hope.
Not many who had survived in the Underground Forces for so many years were fools, now with the other high-ranking members gone, the only one who could carry the weight of the Dark Contract was this formidable Northern Warrior.
Grot’s reputation in the Dark Contract wasn’t weak, on the contrary, due to the Northern people’s straightforward personality and powerful strength, he was highly respected.
So after he pointed out the current predicament of the Dark Contract, several middle-ranking members of the Dark Contract immediately shifted their hopes to him.
A Level 16 Northern Warrior, a powerful professional, could definitely carve out a living space for the Dark Contract.
Relying on the strong is human nature, even the nature of all life.
Grot, with a sharp gaze like that of an eagle, stared at the several people.
He uttered a sentence that instantly changed the color in their faces.
“Although Viscount Bernard has abandoned us, I will not abandon those who have fought alongside me.
I will take control of the Dark Contract, securing a path of survival for everyone!”
His tone was sonorous and firm, carrying an unshakeable determination.
None present were fools; they understood the intentions of this formidable Northern Warrior from the gleam in Grot’s eyes.
People exchanged looks, and for a moment, their hearts were in disarray.
Seeing this, Grot’s lips curved with an indifferent arc.
“If anyone doesn’t wish to become a part of the new Dark Contract, you can leave on your own.”
This statement caused some stir among the others in the room, but no one dared to stand up first; those who lived in the dark world were not without brains.
After glancing around at the others, Grot spoke solemnly, “If you wish to join the new Dark Contract, I, as a Northern Warrior, guarantee you.
We will become the new power in the Underworld of Green City, and together, we will govern the order of the Underworld.”
After finishing, he paused in his speech, looking at Gary and said word by word, “And, I never abandon any of my comrades unless my head is chopped off by the enemy!”
The room instantly fell silent upon this declaration, a strange emotion brewing in the eyes of those watching Grot.
Finally, Gary, the burly warrior, gritted his teeth and stood up, a fierce look flashed through his eyes as he knelt on one knee towards Grot.
“Lord Grot, Gary is willing to serve you!”
The others, seeing this, changed expressions and after exchanging looks, they too knelt down without further hesitation.
“Lord Grot, we are willing to serve you.”
The promise of the Northern Warrior moved them; in the underworld, they were nothing but expendables, their lives and wealth never truly valued.
But the Northern Warrior’s tradition of never abandoning a comrade inspired their trust, and Grot’s esteemed reputation in the Dark Contract gave them enough confidence.
Grot’s expression slightly relaxed, a depth appearing on his face.
The first step was finally taken.
Next, it was to swallow the entirety of the Dark Contract.
His eyes narrowed slightly, his sharp gaze like the blade of a warrior.
Ancestor Crown, from now on, I will control the Dark Contract for you.

chapters.title: Chapter 196 - 197: Sexy Undead Mage Claps Back Online...
chapters.content:
Chapter 196: Chapter 197: Sexy Undead Mage Claps Back Online…
“Emi, what about that Undead Mage?? How’s the research going? Have you found a way to control his Bone Dragon?”
It was during the Mage Tower’s initiation of talent tests for the residents that Lide suddenly remembered the captured Undead Mage, Withered Bone.
Knowing well the characteristics of Undead creatures, Lide didn’t even consider the thought of demanding surrender or threatening him.
These life forms with completely different thought patterns from normal creatures couldn’t be judged by conventional logic.
Emi looked rather distressed.
“Lord Lide, this damn Undead Mage is simply insane”
...
Lide raised his eyebrows, slightly amused, “What happened??”
It was the first time he had seen such an expression on Emi.
Emi couldn’t help but curse again.
“Damn Undead Mages, all these creatures are lunatics.
Ancestor Crown, Withered Bone has already fused his Soul Fire with the Bone Dragon’s Soul Fire”
Lide’s eyes were somewhat puzzled, and he said in confusion,
Source: , updated on ƝονǤᴑ.ᴄο
“It seems that the Undead Mage mentioned this before, but what does it matter?”
His understanding of the characters of Undead creatures came because the Blood Clan Ancestor had captured several Undead lives over a hundred years ago, leaving a deep impression in the memory of the Blood Clan Ancestor with their completely different thought patterns from humans.
But he had no clear idea beyond a deeper understanding, only knowing that these Undead lives were incredibly peculiar.
Emi said, exasperated, “Soul Fire is the most fundamental and original thing of Undead life,
and Withered Bone’s fusion of his Soul Fire with the Bone Dragon is not fusion in the usual sense, but a true fusion.”
Lide was baffled by Emi’s talk about fusion and non-fusion.
Emi slapped his forehead, beginning to explain, “Ancestor Crown, to put it another way, my Soul Fire is now completely that of the Bone Dragon,
In other words, the current Undead Mage Withered Bone is no longer a normal Undead creature.
He is now a Bone Dragon.
As long as you replace his body with that of a Bone Dragon, he can still breathe Dragon Breath!!”
Cough cough, Lide almost choked.
There was such a cunning operation??
“So we can’t snatch his Bone Dragon anymore??”
Emi spread his hands, his face the picture of helplessness.
“No way, that Bone Dragon might not seem closely related to him, but it’s essentially a part of him, even the Bone Dragon is himself.
If we kill him now, he will not die immediately; instead, he would use the body of the Bone Dragon to escape…”
Lide was left speechless.
These Undead lives really don’t play by human norms. Why would any sane Undead creature fuse their Soul Fire with their mount’s?
And to make matters worse, it made him so difficult to deal with.
“Where is Withered Bone now??”
“Dawn Square. Didn’t you say to put him on display in Dawn Square for the residents to witness an Undead life after the research was done?”
Lide nodded, a hint of resignation in his eyes, an 18th level Bone Dragon, truly desirable.
But for now, it seemed the only thing to do was to throw this Undead Mage in Dawn Square and see if a way could be found in the future to control this Undead Mage and make his Bone Dragon part of Dawn City.
Dawn Square is the only square in Dawn City, with a very large area, accommodating three or four tens of thousands of people for a gathering.
And at this moment on the eastern side of Dawn Square, next to a gallows with a hung mummy.
A humanoid skeleton made up of white bones, with Soul Fire flickering inside its skull, was bound with chains infused with antimagic stone, tightly secured against a wall engraved with the relief of a giant dragon.
Arm-thick iron nails were hammered into the relief wall, firmly securing the chains.
Looking at the white bone skeleton, its ankles, arms, neck, and even skull were all bound by the chains.
The corpse hanging beside this Undead creature on the gallows is Porter from the Wild Wolf Gang, whom Lide had once hanged, now turned into a mummy.
This corner had become a place of both curiosity and fear for the children of Dawn City.
At this moment, the addition of an Undead Creature to this corner of death instantly aroused the curiosity of countless people.
“Lord Raymond, what is this? Could it be the legendary undead??”
A freckle-faced young man full of curiosity asked Raymond, who was standing guard nearby.
Raymond had since risen to become a platoon leader in the Security Team, overseeing three squads, each with no fewer than ten people.
His status within Dawn City was no lesser than that of his cousin, Recker.
Upon hearing the questions from the crowd around him, Raymond spoke with a hint of pride,
“Indeed, this is the legendary Undead Mage, captured by Kachar City Lord in battle.
Just a few days ago, Kachar City Lord encountered a powerful Undead with a Bone Dragon and defeated him.
This skeleton is one of the Undead Creatures from that battle, now our spoil of war.”
His words instantly shocked the onlooking crowd.
“An Undead Mage?! Kachar City Lord is truly great!!”
“Hisss, the legendary Undead Mages are said to love robbing human graves, extremely evil and powerful; I never thought I’d see one in my lifetime!”
“Do you see the blue flame inside his head? I’d bet that’s the evil Soul Fire…”
“Lord Raymond, is the Undead Mage as powerful as the legends say??”
The pride in Raymond’s eyes intensified as he listened to the crowd’s discussions. As a member of the Security Team, what could make him prouder than the might of Dawn City?
From the moment he joined the Security Team and swore his loyalty to the statue of Kachar City Lord, he was branded with the mark of Dawn City and Kachar.
“No, I don’t know if this Undead Mage is powerful,
but Lord Emi said that Kachar City Lord personally ordered these foreign lives to be placed in Dawn Square, to let everyone know what kind of enemy our army faces.”
Raymond shook his head honestly; in fact, Emi had not told him about the origins of Lord Withered Bones, only commanded him to put the other party on display in Dawn Square.
Raymond didn’t think this little skeleton was particularly strong; otherwise, Lord Emi certainly wouldn’t have brazenly displayed it in Dawn Square.
At the same time, he felt a bit of regret. Imagine if the Undead Mage that Lord Bloodline mentioned, the one able to control the Bone Dragon, were on display in Dawn Square—that would be spectacular!
At this moment, the unconscious soul fire of Withered Bones flickered and slowly came to life.
The hollow white bone eye sockets revealed a ghastly blue flame, and the dry skull turned slightly. Upon seeing the crowd, it let out a harsh roar.
“Damn vampires, how dare you treat the great Lord Withered Bones this way! Lord Withered Bones will surely make you regret it!!!”
“Aaah, you dispelled my Magic Power! Curse you, I swear I’ll have my Bone Dragon breath its Dragon Breath onto your heads!!”
This shrill cry startled the surrounding residents.
Even Raymond was momentarily stupefied but quickly regained his composure, as Emi had already warned him that as long as the chains held, the Undead Mage was not dangerous.
“Everyone, do not panic; this damned Undead Mage has been bound by Lord Emi with iron chains. I swear to Kachar City Lord, he cannot harm us!”
The crowd, having heard this, and observing that the skeleton merely roared without taking any further action, immediately calmed down. Their eyes filled with tension and curiosity as they watched this legendary Undead Creature.
“It’s truly amazing. He can talk without flesh and blood…”
“I wonder if this Undead still needs to eat? If not, will it starve to death?”
“I really want to see if the fire in his skull is scorching hot…”
Lord Withered Bones, feeling uncomfortable all over as countless eyes filled with curiosity observed it, thought that what Lide said about being bound in Dawn City for the residents to gawk at was just a threat.
But unexpectedly, after Emi discovered its real connection to the Bone Dragon, they actually did chain it up in the square.
Lord Withered Bones felt a vast humiliation. It was, after all, the great Undead Mage, a powerful being with a Bone Dragon!!
Its heart was filled with rage.
“You damned vampire, once the great Lord Withered Bones gets out, I’ll make you taste the Dragon Breath!!”
“And you, you damned humans, what are you looking at, have you never seen such a powerful and majestic Undead Mage??”
“Hmph, the Soul Fire of the great Lord Withered Bones is not something you lowly, base commoners can peek at. Believe it or not, I’ll let the Bone Dragon out and have it burn off your heads with its Dragon Breath!”
“Foolish humans, stay away from me…”
Even though he was restrained, Lord Withered Bones showed no intention of admitting defeat, cursing at the residents who were pointing and whispering. His talkative nature was undeniably apparent.
From this day forward, the residents of Dawn City would have much more entertainment in their lives; a rambling, boastful little skeleton had officially entered Dawn City.

chapters.title: Chapter 197 - 198 Announcement: The Untold Story of the Northern Land Valkyrie and the Crimson Mage Tower
chapters.content:
Chapter 197: Chapter 198 Announcement: The Untold Story of the Northern Land Valkyrie and the Crimson Mage Tower
In fact, Dawn City had many matters to handle, whether it was the recruitment of Mage Apprentices at Dawn Mage Tower, city construction, the expansion of the Magic Language Bats, agriculture, and many more.
Handling all these would require several months of time that wouldn’t be free.
But Lide could not wait that long. Once the Mage Tower began testing the residents’ aptitude, he returned to Green City with Emi, Betty, and Isa.
Dawn Mage Tower had already entered the right track, and Emi, who was in charge, had become available.
Compared to the endless minor tasks in the short term, he had a more important matter to attend to.
The Dark Contract.
...
He was determined to have this massive underground force.
How could one aim for Crimson Mage Tower without paying a price?
Emi and Betty’s arrival was undoubtedly the greatest support to Groth, who lay lurking in Green City.
The combat power of this trident was enough to make one’s heart skip a beat.
After entering Green City, Emi soon left on his own. This former Knight Temple Priest, a local snake, couldn’t be more familiar with the city he had lived in for decades.
Moreover, the Bloodline had a unique way of communicating, and Lide was not worried about Emi not finding Groth.
Source: , updated on ƝονǤ0.с0
Crimson Mage Tower, third floor study.
Back in his own domain, Lide felt much more relaxed.
Betty, visiting the Mage Tower for the first time, was very curious and wandered around the study, occasionally pulling out a couple of thick books to flip through.
Little Isa sat obediently beside Lide, holding a volume of Glory’s general history and reading intently.
This little loli with the Golden Bloodline never changed despite the absolute doting from Lide and Spark; she remained endearing as ever.
Vina, who had just rushed back from afar, wore a long blue Mage robe that day, her delicate face covered with a bright smile.
The girl stood in front of the natural wood-colored desk with her hands clasped in front of her, shyly looking at Lide behind the desk, her face filled with joy and excitement.
It had been so long since she last saw Lord Lide.
Seeing the dependence and happiness in his little maid’s eyes, Lide’s mood also improved.
“Vina, how have things been for you outside recently?”
Vina had been sent to nearby cities to purchase magic materials on the eve of the Dark Contract’s attack on Crimson Mage Tower, and he had gone to White Tower to hire an Advanced Mage to protect the girl’s safety.
“Mr. Lide, thanks to Lord Spark’s reputation, everything went smoothly,”
Vina revealed a sincere smile, “During this time, we visited three cities and reached cooperation agreements with twenty-three merchant guilds.
We expect that magic materials worth more than 50,000 Gold Pucks will be transported to Green City in half a month.
Moreover, the amount of magic materials we receive every month will not be less than 50,000 Gold Pucks.”
Lide’s eyes immediately lit up.
Magic materials valued at 50,000 Gold Pucks were about the monthly output of Green City.
Of course, that referred to the magic materials suitable for Crimson Mage Tower to make magic scrolls.
Now, Vina had only been out for just over half a month, and she brought back enough to double that number.
This was a pleasant surprise for him.
Now, Crimson Mage Tower’s Magic Factory, whether it was the number of Mage Apprentices or other facilities, was adequate to produce more magic scrolls.
But the current situation was that production could not increase, maintaining only at a very ordinary level, and all because the lack of magic raw materials limited the Magic Factory’s production speed.
If the problem with magic raw materials was resolved, it was imaginable that there would be a surge in production from the Magic Factory in the near future.
“You did a great job, Vina. Thank you for your efforts.”
Lide grew more and more satisfied with his little maid.
Having Vina in charge of Crimson Mage Tower saved him an immeasurable amount of worry.
“Once you’re back, take over the operations of the Mage Tower fully, and by no means let the development momentum of the Mage Tower stop,”
“Yes, Lord Lide,”
Vina obediently nodded her head. To him, the girl remained that same unassuming little maid of the past.
In front of Lide, the girl was always that innocent little maid.
Suddenly, as if remembering something, Lide gestured to Betty.
“Betty,”
Hearing Lide’s voice, Betty who was browsing through books in the study put the age-yellowed book back on the oak bookshelf, and slowly made her way to the desk through the narrow aisle.
The bright light from outside shone through the glass windows into the study, and the yet-to-be-turned-off Magic Lamp also cast a warm yellow glow.
Both lights shone on Betty’s face with distinct features and clear contours, enhancing the exotic charm of her half-blood face.
Betty wore a gray leather torso armor and leather shorts that showed off her long legs, with a pair of black leather boots on her feet.
The distinctive temperament of a warrior, combined with a tall figure and wild eyes, gave this member of the Northern Royal Family an indescribable spice and wildness.
Betty gave Lide a slight nod but did not speak.
In fact, if it hadn’t been for the days she had spent in Dawn City witnessing various wonders, which had quietly increased her respect for the mysterious Blood Clan Ancestor, this wild-hearted Northern Land Valkyrie would not have been so obedient.
Even though Lide was the one she had signed a Soul Contract with.
As a Northern Land Valkyrie, only the absolute strongest could earn her respect and recognition.
Although Lide was not weak, there was still a gap before he could truly conquer this wild Valkyrie,
Perhaps, in the future, he might make this member of the Northern Royal Family kneel and sing of “conquest,” but that was definitely not now.
Vina had naturally noticed Betty rummaging around in the study earlier, and her eyes lit up with curiosity upon seeing her.
Betty also looked over and, seeing that the Level 3 little Mage beside her possessed such exceptional temperament and beauty, felt slightly annoyed and lifted her head high.
“Mr. Lide, is there something you need?”
“Let me introduce you. This is Betty, a member of the Crimson Mage Tower starting today,”
Lide, seemingly ignoring the undercurrent between the two, directly said, “Also, Betty is a Level 16 Northern Warrior and Isa’s Guardian.”
Level 16 Northern Warrior? Vina was taken aback, then her face showed a degree of respect.
“Respected Betty, Vina greets you.” Respect must be maintained towards the strong; this was the iron law of Glory.
Betty’s originally proud expression faded upon seeing the admiration in Vina’s eyes, and she glanced unsurely at Lide. Shouldn’t she be retaliating against an enemy’s provocation?
Watching this small interaction, Lide couldn’t help but be amused and frustrated. Betty, due to being constantly on the front lines of battle, was a strong fighter but rarely interacted with others.
She was superb when it came to wielding strength, but her communication skills were hardly better than Isa’s.
“Betty, this is Vina. When I’m not around, the Crimson Mage Tower is fully managed by Vina, whose managerial talent is no less impressive than your combat talent.
To put it plainly, Vina has been of greater help to me at times than any three Level 15 Advanced Professionals.”
Hearing this, Betty’s gaze softened slightly, and she gave Vina a small nod.
“Hello, Vina.”
Vina responded politely, “Greetings, Lady Betty, it’s an honor to meet you.”
Lide waved his hand to interrupt the awkward conversation.
“Vina, let the news of Betty’s inclusion in the Crimson Mage Tower spread secretly among the Underground Forces. I want everyone to know that the Crimson Mage Tower now has a Level 15 Northern Warrior as a member.”
“Yes, Lord Lide.”
Having the protection of a Level 15 and above Great Mage is one thing, but having full control of a Level 15 combat deterrent is quite another.
Betty shrugged her shoulders, not voicing any concern; she was uninterested in these matters.
That day, the underground forces of Green City spread rumors.
A Level 15 Northern Warrior who had wandered to Green City had joined the Crimson Mage Tower upon the invitation of its owner, Lide Kachar, becoming a member of the Crimson Mage Tower.
This news immediately caused quite a stir among the Nobles of Green City.
The Crimson Mage Tower had been gripping everyone’s attention lately.
With its terrifing efficiency in producing Magic Scrolls, the tower’s status in Green City was growing day by day, and more merchants and Nobles were keen to collaborate.
Though many dared not act because of Spark’s deterrence, the seemingly not-so-strong Crimson Mage Tower was still watched by certain Nobles, looking for opportunities in secret.
The ability to mass-produce Magic Scrolls was just too tempting.
The occasional capture of thieves trying to sneak into the Crimson Mage Tower was telling.
But now, the Crimson Mage Tower had its own Level 15 Professional, and it was a Northern Warrior known for strong combat skills.
This news quietly dismissed the small schemes of many Nobles.
Extraordinary Existences were too scarce; Green City, with its population of over a million, only had one.
Therefore, in the absence of an Extraordinary Existence, Professionals of Level 15 and above were the pinnacle of combat power.
To possess such a combatant meant undoubtedly being able to hold significant ground within Green City.
Moreover, the Crimson Mage Tower had the backing of Spark, an established Great Mage.
In an instant, the status of the Crimson Mage Tower rose once more within Green City, and its owner, Lide, was again the center of attention among the Nobles.
Indeed, many major Nobles were already considering the possibility of marriage alliances.
A mentor who was a Level 19 Great Mage, powerful, renowned as the youngest talent among Mages, and, critically, with the coveted technology to mass-produce Magic Scrolls.
It was, by all accounts, a prime resource.
Not long after the news of Betty joining the Crimson Mage Tower had spread, the tower received numerous overtures from major Nobles in the succeeding days.
Most of these overtures expressed a central theme.
My daughter is quite lovely; would you like to meet her?

chapters.title: Chapter 198 - 199 Fooled Again, Another One Lamed (Long Chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 198: Chapter 199 Fooled Again, Another One Lamed (Long Chapter)
June 17th.
Green City, West District.
Inside the main hall of a luxurious manor, an oval-shaped wooden long table was placed in the centre, surrounded by a circle of armchairs, which were currently filled with humans.
The 15th-level Shadow High Priest Emi sat at the secondary seat of the long table, while the main seat was occupied by the burly Grot, a 16th-level Bloodline and a former Northern Warrior.
This originally rugged Northern Warrior had become increasingly handsome after becoming a Bloodline.
However, the forthrightness typical of a Northern Warrior hadn’t disappeared from Grot; on the contrary, it had transformed into a kind of noble vigor full of charm.
...
His male charisma was off the charts.
Apart from the two of them, there were as many as 15 imposing figures seated around the long table. One could sense that each was an Advanced professional of at least 10th level upon concentrating on their aura.
A 15th-level Shadow Priest and a 16th-level Northern Warrior, together with a full 15 Advanced professionals of 10th level, constituted a force not to be underestimated.
However, Emi and Grot’s faces bore little semblance of a smile.
They were in big trouble—to be precise, the Dark Contract was in big trouble.
Emi’s expression was rather grim, and under the warm glow of the Magic Lamp, he appeared more stern.
Source: , updated on ƝᴑνǤο.сο
“After more than half a month of gathering, we’ve managed to assemble 15 Advanced professionals of 10th level for the Dark Contract, as well as 104 Intermediate professionals of levels 5 to 9. This force is not weak, but it’s still far from what we anticipated…”
Emi’s voice was somewhat low, clearly dissatisfied with this figure.
He then turned his head and looked at the people seated, his gaze heavy.
The Dark Contract managed by Viscount Bernard for decades was once incredibly powerful. At its peak, it had as many as 40 Advanced professionals above 10th level and over two thousand Intermediate professionals ranging from levels 5 to 9.
It was the foremost among the three major Dark Forces of Green City.
But now, following the disappearance of Viscount Bernard and the Eight-Armed Snake Demon Roy, the Dark Contract was being ruthlessly hunted by the Green City military forces, nearly on the brink of collapse in just over a month.
The once prominent Dark Giant had now lost its luster.
It could be said that if not for his and Grot’s intervention to gather these remnants, the Dark Contract might have been wiped out entirely.
Even if those forces hidden in the shadows, personally controlled by Viscount Bernard, hadn’t been struck by Green City’s military, decades of the Dark Contract’s operations would have gone up in flames.
“Those damned Green City military forces, as if cursed by an Undead Mage, have gone insane, hunting down the members of the Dark Contract relentlessly.
That we still have this many people is a blessing from the Goddess of Luck.
Moreover, we have the disgusting Heart-eating Demon competing with us for people! This bastard—I will chop off his filthy head with my sword one day!”
Grot shook his head, his face also looking rather pale.
It was the first time Ancestor Crown had entrusted him with such an important mission, but it had turned out to be incredibly challenging, which he undoubtedly found hard to accept.
However, with Green City’s military relentless in their pursuit, the leaderless Dark Contract was already weakened, and there was nothing he could do to change that fact.
Emi’s eyes flashed with contemplation as he turned to look at a warrior clad in silver armor below him.
“Gary, are you sure that half of the Dark Contract’s people have surrendered to Wales?”
Gary, seated to the right of Emi, flashed a look of anger.
“Yes, Lord Emi. I’ve contacted some of our former companions, but at least half of them have defected to that damned Heart-eating Demon!”
The Heart-eating Demon Wales, one of the three Dark Giants of Green City’s Underworld, as infamous as Viscount Bernard.
This evil and terrifying being controlled one-fifth of the territory in the West District.
Hearing the name Heart-eating Demon, Emi’s face showed a hint of wariness.
“This damned lunatic!!”
Originally human, the Heart-eating Demon Wales was one who had an extreme adoration for evil and idolized Demons. He had even performed certain legendary dark ceremonies and acquired a half-Demon Bloodline.
What the Dark Boss enjoyed most was to devour the steaming hot heart, rich with blood, of his defeated enemies.
The Heart-eating Demon Wales was an evil existence in the West District that could make even the most resolute warriors falter.
To have this much of their rightful power snatched away from their mouths by such a strong boss was infuriating and worrisome for both Emi and Grot.
“Wales is not alone; his Demon Heart controls one-fifth of the West District—a formidable enemy…” Emi took a deep breath.
“Viscount Bernard has been missing for more than a month and has not appeared yet. This evil Heart-eating Demon is probably unable to restrain its inner desires anymore.
This time, it’s normal for the opposition to make a move, even if the Heart-eating Demon doesn’t take action, there will be other forces that would devour the power of the Dark Contract.”
Grot spoke in a deep tone; the Underworld was by no means a benevolent existence.
Here, to gain power and wealth, some even sold their souls to the devil.
The Dark Contract formerly relied on the deterrent of Viscount Bernard and several other top fighters to become one of the three giants in the western district.
But now, Viscount Bernard has been subject to Extraordinary Hunting, and his whereabouts are unknown.
Most of the other top fighters have also been killed by Lide, directly resulting in a power vacuum.
If it weren’t for the earlier deterrent strength of Viscount Bernard, the power of the Dark Contract would have been disdained, and this vast force would have been devoured by the shadowy wolves long ago.
“Gary, what about the Fallen Knight Philip?” Emi took a deep breath and continued to ask.
“The Fallen Knight did not take action and seems to have little interest in fighting for territory and devouring the Dark Contract,” said Gary, shaking his head with a somewhat relieved tone.
Green City’s powerful Dark Forces are entrenched in the populous and complex western district; among countless Underground Forces in the western district, there are three major Dark Forces that make all Underground Forces tremble.
The Dark Contract led by Viscount Bernard, the Demon Heart headed by the Heart-eating Demon Wales, and the Sinking Fog led by the Fallen Knight Philip.
These three forces, in the crushing of countless small Underground Forces, have become giants with their terrifying strength – each giant hiding unimaginable power.
Plus, the backers of the three giants are entangled with Green City’s high-ranking Nobles, with significant influence not only in the Underworld but also in the areas bathed in light.
Therefore, the three major forces have always been the benchmark of Green City’s dark realm.
Due to the disappearance of Viscount Bernard, the deterrent power of the Dark Contract has dropped dramatically, and now it’s been targeted by its peer Dark Force, the Demon Heart. Thus, the pressure that Emi and Grot are facing at this time is imaginable.
According to their estimates, the Dark Contract has been devoured by the opponent by at least one-third of its personnel.
Emi dared to swear to the divine, that if they don’t take immediate action, most of the remaining people of the Dark Contract will also be eaten by the Demon Heart.
By then, the Dark Contract will transform from a giant capable of influencing Green City’s Underworld into a trivial small force.
This is something he and Grot can’t bear.
The Dark Contract is a force that Lide intends to claim, and no faults can be tolerated.
If most of its power is devoured by the Demon Heart, it won’t make sense to take down the Dark Contract.
“We must find a way to turn this around,” Grot said with a hint of severity in his voice. “If that damned Heart-eating Demon doesn’t withdraw from the Dark Contract’s territory,
then we’ll break his neck and send him to meet the damned Abyss Demon!!”
Northern Warriors, fearless, undaunted!!
Even as a Bloodline, the soul of fearlessness forged in the North does not care about any Heart-eating Demon.
Violence is the most direct way to solve problems.
Strength is truth, which is not only the mantra of the God of Justice but also the faith of every Northern Warrior.
Emi shook his head, “The Heart-eating Demon is an existence on the same level as Viscount Bernard, and for many years, nobody has known how powerful this half-demon is.
Moreover, the Demon Heart has a full 4 top professionals of level 15 and above.
Just with you and me, we can’t compete with them…”
Emi was very clear about this. In the Underworld, rashness without absolute certainty would only hasten one’s demise.
He then looked at Grot with eyes filled with hesitation.
“Unless, Lady Betty could take action.”
The Northern Royal Family, capable of instantly killing a level 19 Molten Demon, is their real trump card. If they had the Northern Land Valkyrie with them, they would certainly have the power to fight.
Betty’s strength is enough to fill anyone with confidence.
Grot hesitated too, “If we seek help from Lady Betty, the Ancestor Crown…”
This was Lide’s first mission for him, not completing it perfectly was undoubtedly a disappointment for him.
Before Emi could speak, a knock came from outside the door.
“Lord Emi, Lord Grot, Lord Wales from the Demon Heart has sent us an invitation…”
Emi and Grot exchanged glances, their expressions changing dramatically.
“How did this damned Heart-eating Demon know they were in this manor??”
“Come in!”
Without time to think further, an armored guard pushed open the doors of the great hall and entered the room with a black oak box.
“Open it.”
Following Emi’s order, the guard opened the oak box.
Clang~
A heart dripping with blood fell out and thumped a few times on the ground.
