“The people of the Dark Contract, meet me at Drucker Tavern tomorrow night at 9 PM, hahaha, I hope you can give me some surprises. It’s so boring without Viscount Bernard.
I despise those who are late. If I don’t see you, after tomorrow, the Dark Contract will become a part of the Heart of the Demon, and you rebels, your hearts will be plucked by me.”
A sinister and bizarre voice emanated from the heart, chilling to the bone.
After the last syllable dropped, the bloodied heart stopped beating, and the bloodstains on it quickly turned black.
Evil and terrifying Abyss Magic.
The room fell into a dead silence, an indescribable atmosphere brewing.
Both Emi and Grot had uncontrollable fury in their eyes.
This damned Heart-eating Demon!!
…
…
…
The next day, at 8:30 PM, in the West District.
The West District, watched over by the Night Goddess, is the true West District.
This land, forgotten by sin, is far from a desolate desert; instead, every inch of land oozes with the essence of Gold Puck.
Violence, murder, and crime often bring windfalls.
Without Green City’s complex laws to contend with, any line of business can be pursued here.
Human trafficking, arms smuggling, slave trade, hiring assassins, offering sacrifices to the Evil God, and so much more.
Whatever sin one can imagine in this world, it can happen here.
Green City, the largest city in the south, attracts countless adventurers and, concurrently, countless evils.
And these evils all conglomerate in the West District.
Hence, no matter how many people die here each year, the population of the West District always grows, never diminishing.
Drucker Tavern, located in the middle of the West District, is the busiest and most bustling place, directly under the control of the Heart of the Demon.
There are numerous, large and small, Underground Forces in the West District, the exact number of which is unknown.
The Heart of the Demon, the Dark Contract, and the Lost Fog—the three Dark Giants—are just one of many.
Though the three Dark Forces are powerful, even at their peak combined they cannot control the West District, not even half of it.
Because the waters of the West District are too deep, no one knows if the fruit shop owner at Cross Street Corner is a human or an Abyss Demon.
No one knows if the beggar on the street will flap wings to hunt passersby after nightfall.
The hidden evils here are beyond even the clean-up capability of Green City’s Extraordinary Existence.
On the second floor of Drucker Tavern, the Heart-eating Demon Wales, dressed in luxurious black noble attire with a cream-white napkin, sat elegantly at a round table covered with a white tablecloth, a picture of nobility as he held knife and fork.
In a room adorned in Central European Noble style, four mysterious beings, hidden under cloaks, stood in the shadows. Their presence was evil and fearsome.
Beneath the cloaks, their cold eyes seemed like venomous snakes lurking in the dark, causing hearts to race.
“Master, your food…”
A cart was pushed through the door, and a pale-faced maid served the food onto the round table.
After slightly adjusting the position, she respectfully lifted the semi-circular silver dish cover at the top of the plate.
Wales nodded in satisfaction and waved his hand, beginning to cut the food with utmost gentlemanly demeanor.
In conjunction with the surroundings that were elegantly decorated, the drastic contrast was enough to make any ordinary person’s legs buckle.
“Have the people from the Dark Covenant arrived yet?”
Four young maids dressed in simple servant clothes immediately came forward to clear the table.
In the room lit by pale red magic lamps, a tall bald man at the door immediately entered upon hearing the question, “Lord Wales, the people from the Dark Covenant haven’t arrived yet.”
Wales slightly lifted his head and looked at the bald man before him, a trace of cruelty flashing in his crimson eyes.
“Viscount Bernard dares to infuriate the Extraordinary, I think he must have been blinded by the Goddess of Calamity.
The Dark Covenant has stood off against the Demon Heart for decades; it’s time to put an end to it.
Pause the action of passing the news of the Dark Covenant’s base to the Green City army, a shattered Dark Covenant now suits the interests of the Demon Heart more.
Next, after dealing with Grot and Emi, these two rats, I will devour the entire Dark Covenant.”
“Hahaha, what a pleasant night, praise the Abyss!”
The expression on Wales’s face carried a hint of savage pleasure and in the light of the pale red magic lamps, looked particularly eerie and bizarre.
This being, with half a demon bloodline, could no longer be considered human.
The bald man in a black dress suit bowed deeply, clutching his chest,
“Your greatness is enough to catch the Extraordinary’s attention, the Dark Covenant is destined to be your prey… Praise you, my master”
Thud, thud, thud~
At this moment, a series of footsteps was heard from outside the room.
“My lord, the people from the Dark Covenant, have come.”
Excitement flashed through Wales’s eyes as he waved to the fully armored guard, “Let them in.”
After speaking, he glanced around, and the four maids in pure white servant attire immediately came forward to tidy up, then retreated backwards out of the room after cleaning.
Only the bald man in the black suit and four mysterious figures hidden beneath their cloaks remained inside.
Wales didn’t speak, his eyes showing a hint of intoxication.
After several minutes…
Bang~ The door opened.
The atmosphere in the room immediately grew tense.
The bald man in the black suit looked around with eyes filled with vigilance and malice, while the mysterious figures beneath the shadows turned their gaze towards the door.
At that moment, Grot, wearing full-body armor crafted by dwarves, entered the room.
Cradling a broadsword three palms wide that flickered with sharp brilliance, no one doubted the lethality of the weapon.
There was no attempt to hide the hostility in this Northern warrior’s eyes.
After looking around to ensure there was no threat, he stood to the left, resting his hands on the hilt of his sword, the point plunged into the ground like a sculpture of a man drawing a blade from the earth.
Once Grot had taken his position, Emi, wearing black priestly robes, appeared in the room, and Wales immediately recognized the two.
He was not unfamiliar with these two vice presidents of the Dark Covenant.
A trace of coldness flashed through his eyes. After dealing with these two filthy rats tonight, he could devour the Dark Covenant without any reservations.
But an unexpected situation arose as another figure stepped in from outside.
The newcomer, dressed in temple priest robes with an average build, captivated his attention with a scar slashing down diagonally from his forehead, nearly splitting half of his face.
Stanley, Wales recognized this Shadow Priest from the Late Bell Church; in fact, the Demon Heart had many dealings with the Late Bell Church, which had previously turned to the Demon Heart to purchase many offerings.
But it was not over yet; a woman appeared behind Stanley, her upper body clad in a black leather jacket, her lower body in leather pants, her face covered with a pure black mask, holding a greatsword just slightly smaller than Grot’s.
A wild aura hit them squarely.
Wales looked at the masked lady intently, he felt an indescribable danger emanating from this female warrior he had never seen before.
To his surprise, he had thought that with Viscount Bernard’s Dark Contract gone and the hunting of Green City’s army, there wouldn’t be so many top-level professionals showing up. But unexpectedly, four had come today.
And one of them posed a fatal threat to him.
Wales straightened his clothes, preparing to stand up.
But then, a surprising scene unfolded.
The masked lady, just like the others, went to the door and stood as if she were a servant awaiting the arrival of her master.
Wales felt a measure of unease.
Could it be that Viscount Bernard had already returned to Green City? His thoughts raced wildly.
Tap, tap—
He appeared.
An attractive figure appeared before Wales, illuminated by the pale red magic lamp.
Tall, with impeccable beauty and handsomeness, elegant and noble manners, every movement carried a strong air of nobility,
But that wasn’t the key point; what attracted Wales was the sharp fang at the corner of this figure’s mouth.
This was a Vampire, not Viscount Bernard.
Tap, tap, stepping into the room.
Just as Wales was about to speak, a scene occurred that made his gaze grow heavy—the first four to enter the room bowed in unison to the last Vampire to enter.
As if the most humble subjects were welcoming their king.
Wales sniffed slightly, his spiritual power spreading out wildly. He wanted to see just what level of existence this Vampire was, considering that even for Viscount Bernard, he had never seen these top-level professionals show him such respect.
A strange Vampire, on what basis?
But moments later, Wales’s eyes filled with shock; he couldn’t sense any aura from this Vampire at all.
This Vampire seemed like an ordinary human—yes, an ordinary human!!
But could it be possible? A mysterious existence who could be greeted by four top-level professionals was a powerless ordinary human??
In a moment, a layer of extreme mystery veiled this last Vampire to enter the room in Wales’s mind.
After Lide entered the room, he looked directly at the room’s master and unhesitatingly took his seat opposite Wales.
His gaze was piercing as he looked at the legendary Heart-eating Demon, the master of the Demon Heart, a Dark Boss on par with Viscount Bernard—Wales.
Knowing the seriousness of the issue after receiving a message from Emi overnight, he immediately contemplated a response.
A month had passed since he had first embraced Grot, and to maximally enhance his strength, he returned to Dawn City at the quickest pace to transform Stanley, the Late Bell Church’s Dark Priest, into a Bloodline.
Once Stanley had awakened, he immediately returned to Green City with him and Betty to confront Wales, the powerful Heart-eating Demon.
Subduing the Dark Contract was his new idea, but it was also a crucial part of his future plans, where there was no room for failure.
He had to win this victory.
Wales’s expression was immensely complex at this moment; he had initially thought that the most imposing Betty would be tonight’s true host.
But unexpectedly, this Vampire, whose aura could not be discerned in the slightest, sat in the position of honor amidst the respectful gazes of all.
This strange Vampire was the master of this group of people!!
This was too surprising, even Viscount Bernard couldn’t make these top-level professionals show such reverence.
Wales’s eyes flashed with intense confusion, but no matter how he sensed, this Vampire before him was just an ordinary person, without the slightest trace of magical fluctuation.
He was half a Demon, and demons’ sensitivity to energy was dozens of times greater than that of humans.
Yet even so, he could detect nothing.
Even when sensing with all his might, he faintly detected a holy power contained within this Vampire’s body, akin to the power of the Light Gods.
Yes, the Light Gods!!
By the demons above, he must be mad!
He actually sensed the power that only believers who worship the Divine Gods possess in a vampire!
Is it his demon bloodline that’s causing turmoil within him?
Wales, who had originally treated tonight’s meeting with contempt and carelessness, now became somber at this moment.
The heart-eating demon, infamous alongside Viscount Bernard and possessing a half-demon bloodline, treated Lide as a formidable enemy after he entered the room.
Wales wouldn’t be so agitated if it were merely the inability to sense Lide’s presence, but he could tell that Grot and the others respected this vampire from the bottom of their hearts.
In the dark world, only strength could command respect.
This once again proved his guess; this vampire must be a powerful being whose presence he couldn’t fathom!
And if he couldn’t sense his presence, there was only one possibility… Extraordinary.
The word that came to mind made him hold his breath for a moment.
In the few seconds after Lide took his seat, some cold sweat silently trickled down Wales’ forehead.
Lide’s expression did not change in the slightest, with Grot Betty standing on his left and right, and Stanley and Emi standing behind him.
He had long concealed his aura; possessing the power of faith, Lide was absolutely confident in hiding his presence if he chose not to be found, even from the Extraordinary.
After all, he was worshipped by thousands, and under his command were Holy Divine Priests and zealots. Though before this god, the term “pseudo” should be prefixed.
But the power of faith was of a higher level, indistinguishable to those who had not touched that tier.
Even the favored child of nature, a level 17 elf, couldn’t detect it, so how could a human with only a half-demon bloodline notice his anomaly?
Taking this moment, Lide opened Wales’ attribute panel.
Wales Ronal (half-demon)
Level: 19
???
???
A simple attribute panel, all question marks.
But as expected, this legendary heart-eating demon was on par with Viscount Bernard and Spark.
Lide took a deep breath. As the Crimson Mage Tower and Dawn City progressed, the strength of the enemies he had to face was increasing.
Now he had to directly confront one of the top figures in the city, a level 19 heart-eating demon, a Dark Giant with demon bloodline.
Lide was certain that even if you counted everyone in Green City, there were probably only about a dozen or so who reached level 19.
These were the real Dark Giants of Green City, like Spark, the level 19 who was the Vice President of the Mage Association, and Viscount Bernard, who was the President of the Dark Contract with six top level 15 professionals.
This heart-eating demon Wales was the master of one of the three major powers in the western district, “Demon Heart,” and also a powerful being with half-demon bloodline.
The higher the level he stood on, the stronger the enemies he faced; this was unavoidable.
Lide was not one to shy away; rather, he was eager to test his mettle against a level 19 being, a thrill akin to facing an entity nearly transcendent.
“Wales, I am the new master of the Dark Contract—Lord Ilo.”
Lide spoke with a calm tone. If Viscount Bernard were here, this name would certainly have felt familiar to him. In a gathering of the Dark Contract, Bernard had stopped Emi and Lide; on that occasion, Lide had introduced himself as Ilo.
“Master of ‘Demon Heart,’ state your intentions clearly. Your actions are now infringing upon the interests of the Dark Contract.”
His sharp gaze was like that of a hunting falcon.
“Otherwise, the Dark Contract will consider you enemies and will launch indiscriminate attacks.”
After Lide finished speaking, his aura became even more sanctified, with the power of faith nearly saturating his entire being, his eyes displaying intense dignity—the dignity of a god.
Yet paired with the vampire fangs that peeked out of his mouth, under the pale red light, it appeared so bizarre and eerie.
Wales, caught in that majestic gaze, felt an urge to look away, especially sensing the sanctified aura from Lide that filled him with instinctive disgust and an inescapable sense of dread.
Just how powerful was this being who could assimilate the Light Gods’ faith within his own body?!!
Could it be that this entity was about to break through from Extraordinary to Legendary, preparing to ascend to demigod status?
The power of the Light Gods was lethally effective against dark life, a fact that even the Dark Gods had to acknowledge, as well as a fundamental understanding handed down through the epochs in Glory.
“`
Yet now, an astonishing presence of power that only the Light Gods were known to possess was manifesting on the Vampire before him, complemented by the reverent expressions of the four top-tier professionals of level 15 and above at his side.
Wales was frantically imagining and deducing at this moment, and the conclusion he eventually reached nearly made him want to flee this place.
This one must certainly be laying the foundation for his future ascension to demigod status!
To harbor the Power of Faith of the Light Gods within his body, what a formidable being he must be.
He had once heard some dubious rumors among high-level demons, claiming that dark creatures, especially demons and vampires, these evil beings, found it difficult to possess faith.
They could not ascend to divinity through the power of faith.
Yet, to break through to higher realms, certain evil and mighty beings would forcibly occupy the temples of divinities, stealing the Power of Faith within to decipher the laws of faith, thus ascending to demigod status.
He had always thought these legends were false, but upon seeing the vampire before him, redolent of the aura of the Light Gods, he immediately began to waver.
“Respected Lord Ilo, the Heart of the Demon holds no ill will towards the Dark Contract…”
Upon hearing Wales’s words, Lide’s heart stirred, especially upon seeing the other party’s face which barely concealed its panic, he immediately sensed something.
This is quite interesting.
Lide’s gaze narrowed slightly.
“No ill will??”
Wales felt a shiver in his heart upon meeting Lide’s chilly gaze.
The one opposite him was very likely an existence about to transcend and enter the Legendary realm.
For the mighty, one must maintain sufficient reverence; this is the rule of survival in Glory.
“Yes, Lord Ilo, Viscount Bernard was once a comrade of the Heart of the Demon,
but now he is being hunted by the Transcendent, and the Dark Contract is thrown into disarray. If the Heart of the Demon does not act, perhaps the Dark Contract will not survive the encircling of Green City’s military until the return of Viscount Bernard…”
Wales’s face was full of righteousness, as if signaling to Green City’s military about the Dark Contract’s hideout was not his doing.
“So the Heart of the Demon is to assist the Dark Contract.
Lord Ilo, that Extraordinary Mage from Green City thoroughly detests the Dark Contract. Perhaps you need to take the Dark Contract into hiding with you to avoid trouble.
I have several estates in the west district that I could offer to you…”
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly upon hearing this, Wales’s expression just then was different compared to now, a test??
His tone was righteous, with a hint of authority and dominance.
“Wales, after I arrived, the Dark Contract no longer has to worry about that Extraordinary Mage.
Hiding?
Heh, I have never taken a single step back even when facing a mature Black Dragon.
Wales, you are already level 19; without a steadfast heart, how could you break through to higher ranks, let alone achieve eternity…”
His tone carried a faint hint of melancholy, exuding a sense of lonely grandeur from the high perch.
Become eternal??
Wales’s lips twitched fiercely, his eyes filled with undisguisable panic. What in this world could be eternal??
Gods!
Feeling the genuinely Holy Power emanating from Lide, not something external forces could mask, the respect in his eyes intensified
“Whether human or demon, the mighty never retreat at will, even if known for their schemes like the Snake Race, they too will be fearless at the crucial moment…”
Lide’s tone subtly suggested deeper meanings, causing Wales to pause, then his face revealed an excitement incomprehensible to outsiders, and he impulsively asked.
“Lord Ilo, how did you break through the Transcendent level in the beginning?”
After speaking, he instantly felt a tinge of regret, watching Lide carefully, fearful of offending this powerful being.
But he had been trapped at level 19 for far too long; he was already level 19 before he had even obtained the Demon Bloodline.
He transformed himself into a half-demon lifeform, hoping to use the power of demons to become Transcendent.
But transcending is too difficult, even with the strong bloodline of demons, it could not offer him greater assistance.
“`
So even with the slightest chance, Wales didn’t want to give up.
Lide was somewhat bewildered by these words. How had it suddenly turned into a request for advice on a Transcendent breakthrough?
They were just negotiating moments ago.
How would I know how to achieve a Transcendent breakthrough? I haven’t even reached level 15.
Maybe I’ve oversold it…
But looking into Wales’s passionate eyes, Lide cleared his throat.
“Wales,” Lide began, “do you know the difference between Transcendent and those below it?”
Difference? Wales had thought Lide wouldn’t bother with him, but unexpectedly, the other man responded.
Containing his joy, Wales pondered deeply.
After a long while, he answered with some hesitation, “The control of power?”
Those red eyes were filled with intense hope. He was so desperate to ascend to Transcendence. Now, to receive guidance from a powerful being who could command the faith of the Light Gods was like being favored by the Goddess of Luck.
Lide shook his head.
“No, power control is important, but it’s not everything.”
Wales furrowed his brow, reflecting deeply before speaking cautiously.
“Is it the accumulation of energy in the body?”
Lide continued to shake his head.
“No, a One-eyed Giant’s internal energy is far more abundant than a human’s, but they are still mere mortals.”
“Lord Ilo, please guide me. I am willing to give everything you desire.”
Wales could no longer hold back. He stood up, and before everyone’s eyes, he gave Lide a deep bow.
Grot and Betty exchanged glances, all somewhat confused.
How was this different than what they had imagined?
This level 19 Heart-eating Demon was asking their level 13 boss how to become Transcendent?
This…
Lide, of course, didn’t know their complicated thoughts and nodded with satisfaction, giving advice like someone who had been through it all.
“Your sincerity has moved me, Wales. The Goddess of Luck has favored you tonight. I’ll make an exception and give you some guidance.”
This statement made Emi and the others twitch at the corners of their mouths.
Lide’s tone became increasingly solemn, as if he were recalling his own glorious past.
“To break through to level 15, what’s needed is an accumulation of strength and skillful use.
But to become Transcendent, what’s required is a heart brave and fearless.”
“A heart that does not shrink back even before the gods.”
“A heart that knows no taboos, invincible in this world.”
“A heart that shatters eternity, ahem, that overcomes time, without fear or trepidation.”
“A heart…”
As Wales listened, he became entranced, feeling as if these were whispers from the Divine, a blessing from the Abyss.
Suddenly, as if struck by endless revelation, he realized that he had been on the wrong path all along.
Lord Ilo was truly powerful beyond belief, to share such vital secrets with him.
Wales was filled with indescribable excitement at this moment.
Praise the Demon, praise Lord Ilo!
Just as Lide was puffing himself up, Wales’s demeanor suddenly shifted.
A terrifying and savage aura filled the room, as if a giant dragon lurked within.
Lide was shocked. Could this bastard really be on the verge of a Transcendent breakthrough??

chapters.title: Chapter 199: 200 I hope you can become the Vice President of Demon Heart
chapters.content:
Chapter 199: Chapter 200 I hope you can become the Vice President of Demon Heart
Under Lide’s somewhat nervous gaze, Wales’s aura became increasingly powerful.
Even within the room, a tide of energy began to rise.
The cloaked figures in the shadows had now become alert, their gazes fixed intensely on Lide and his companions.
The moment any of them made a move, they would launch a brutal attack.
Lide watched as Wales, who had now closed his eyes, underwent a surge in power, and he took a deep breath.
He turned his head and slowly shook it at Betty, who was gripping her sword tightly, ready to unleash a monumental blow at any moment.
...
He stopped her from making any move on behalf of the Northern Royal Family.
Although Wales seemed defenseless standing before him, Lide had a feeling that even if everyone attacked together, they wouldn’t be able to harm this powerful being who possessed half a demon bloodline.
It was an instinct from the Ancestor’s bloodline, and it wouldn’t deceive him.
Wales was not like a Level 19 Molten Demon that Kedel had transformed into, which had only the appearance of strength but not even half of a Level 19’s power. This was a true Level 19 Dark Giant—Betty, despite her strength, would have a difficult time winning against him, a being who was on the brink of transcendence, and whose true strength was unknown to all.
After a full ten minutes, the tide of energy within the room finally receded.
Lide had been closely watching Wales’s attribute panel the entire time, and seeing that the level was still 19, he greatly relieved.
Fortunately, Wales hadn’t broken through to transcendence.
At the same time, Lide felt somewhat embarrassed; the lesson had been too profound. He thought to himself that he should brag less in the future, as he almost aided their enemy.
Swish—
Wales’s crimson eyes opened, their cruel and bloodthirsty look immediately chilling the atmosphere in the room.
Lide felt a soul shock coming towards him and quickly used the Power of Faith to protect his soul.
Only then did the cold and brutal aura disappear.
The Crimson Eye, a Bloodline Talent unique to Abyss Demons, performs a will check when gazing at an enemy. Failing the check results in fear, causing mental chaos and significantly reducing combat capability.
After Wales awoke, not only did the tense atmosphere in the room not ease, but it became even more oppressive due to the extraordinary actions of this Heart-eating Demon.
Wales, dressed in a luxurious suit, suddenly stood up and, under everyone’s watchful eyes and with a solemn expression, began walking step by step towards Lide.
The atmosphere in the room seemed to freeze as everyone’s eyes followed Wales’s movements.
The mysterious figures in the shadows had already drawn their longswords from the scabbards, ready to attack outsiders following their master’s lead.
The bald man in black suit had his magic gathering in his hands, emitting waves of magic fluctuations that radiated an extremely dangerous aura.
Behind Lide, Grotte’s muscles had suddenly tensed like a spring compressed to its limit, ready to unleash a world-splitting blow at any moment.
Betty’s legs were slightly bent like a hunting cheetah, her wild eyes fixed on Wales under her mask. The closer he got, the more intense the fighting spirit in her eyes became, with a faint yet significant holy gleam beginning to emanate from the giant sword by her side.
The Northern Land Valkyrie under the mask seemed wild and irascible.
Lide, upon seeing Wales’s actions, remained immovable, his gaze sharply fixed on the approaching figure.
At the same time, he had activated the Shadow Jump spell he had learned from Emi, ready to react immediately if this Heart-eating Demon made a move, assisting his subordinates in hunting down this dark boss.
In a moment where everyone was tense, as taut as a drawn bowstring,
as Wales approached Lide, under the astonished gaze of everyone—this Level 19 Heart-eating Demon, master of the Demon Heart, with half a demon bloodline—the Dark Giant… bowed deeply at the chest to Lide.
“Lord Ilo, Wales offers you the highest respect…”
The scene fell into a strange pause.
Everyone looked at this sight unsure what to say.
Lord?
The bald man in the black suit, with magic in his hand, stared in disbelief at the unyielding Lide.
To be addressed so respectfully as “Lord” by Mr. Wales… could it be—
And this vampire had just guided Mr. Wales, making him stronger in just a moment.
To achieve such a feat, there’s only one explanation—Transcendence!
Thinking this, the bald man’s eyes widened. Although he had suspected that this vampire was not simple, possibly even on the same level as his master,
now Wales’s actions confirmed everything. This vampire, whose aura seemed even more ordinary than a normal human’s, was a powerful being who surpassed Master Wales.
Never in his life had he seen his master bow to anyone like this.
After much contemplation, the bald man’s face became extremely animated, and his proud head followed its owner, bowing in support of Lide’s chest.
To deal with the powerful, one must maintain sufficient respect.
Moreover, the other party was Transcendent…
Transcendent! With just one move, they would all die here, except perhaps Sir Wales might have a chance to escape.
Facing a formidable existence that could not be resisted and might kill him at any moment, any level of respect was necessary.
At that moment, the few others hidden under cloaks and standing in the shadows were also shocked, quickly following Wales and the bald man in bowing deeply with their chests supported.
No one was a fool, for fools did not live long in the Underworld.
In just those few short seconds, the atmosphere shifted from tense to one that possibly erupted in battle to another extreme.
Betty and Groot exchanged glances, their hearts surging as well.
They had come with their weapons sharpened, wearing the sturdiest armor produced by dwarves, and even brought equipment and magic scrolls they usually hesitated to use.
They had thought a fierce battle would occur today.
But now…
The great boss of their opponent, an entity whose mere presence could shake the entire Underworld in Green City, had almost… almost submitted to their own level 13 boss.
This…
Gazing at Lide’s indifferent figure, they did not know how to describe it, but all shared the same thought.
Goddess of Life above, maybe the Ancestor Crown truly is blessed by the Creator God, a Son of the Creator God.
Even Emi was confused at this moment, wondering if the Ancestor Crown really was a god of dawn who had left the Divine Country to walk the Main Plane?
Otherwise, how could he achieve this extent?
Lide, watching the respectful Wales, breathed a sigh of relief. Thankfully he hadn’t gotten carried away.
His profound gaze fixated on this dark boss, his tone significant.
“Wales, have you realized it?”
Wales stood up straight, his face filled with excitement, “Lord Ilo, thank you for your guidance, your mercy, and generosity are enough to make the Creator God sing your praises. Under your guidance, I have now sensed the power of Transcendence.
It will take just ten years, no, five years! In just five years I will be able to step into Transcendence!!”
Wales’s tone grew increasingly excited, “Great Lord Ilo, from today onwards, you are the most honored guest of the Heart of Demon.”
Lide felt a wave of relief. It was not immediate transcendence, but five years… giving him five more years to grow, he did not believe he couldn’t handle a being who had just stepped into Transcendence.
“Indeed, although your talent is not high, your desire for power is among the top I have seen.
To touch Transcendence is truly not simple…”
Wales was overjoyed; being praised by a great existence capable of harboring the Power of Faith of the Light Gods was an immense honor.
“Lord Ilo, it’s an honor to receive your recognition.”
Just under Lide’s “guidance,” his stagnant strength had soared, even touching the threshold of Transcendence he hadn’t reached in over a hundred years.
At this moment, Wales held not the slightest doubt towards Lide, only respect and reverence.
This was definitely an existence whose power exceeded his imagination. To be taught by such a great being was as if favored by the Goddess of Luck, blessed by the Abyss.
Even if someone told him now that the person before him was just a level 13 vampire, he would not believe it and might even dig out the heart of the rumor spreader.
How could such a grand figure not be an existence above Transcendence?
People always believe what they want to believe, and the truth, many times, is not that important.
Lide looked at the bamboozled Wales, greatly satisfied in his heart. The longest road you’ll ever walk is your own scheming, for schemes are indeed a remedy to win people’s hearts.
His expression was incomparably holy.
“Even though you’ve touched Transcendence, remember, Wales, Transcendence is just the starting point.
The eternity ahead is what we chase.
Never forget why you started; having a beginning and an end is the correct path in the pursuit of power.”
Transcendence is just the starting point?
Never forget why you started, having a beginning and an end?
Wales’s heart trembled, and he felt as though he was receiving guidance from the God of Wisdom. Many of the problems that had troubled him were fading away, and he understood the path to transcendence much more clearly.
The realm of Lord Ilo was exceedingly high, with profound yet comprehensible verses that only someone as fearless of the Holy Light and powerful beyond imagination like Lord Ilo could comprehend.
“Lord Ilo, your wisdom, your strength, your power, and your magnanimity fill me with sincere admiration.”
Wales suppressed his inner joy and uttered a sentence that almost made Lide spit out his drink.
“I beseech Lord Ilo to become the vice president of the Demon Heart…”
Wales saw no issue with his decision.
This was a being above the transcendent, likely about to break through to become legendary.
The other’s realm, wisdom, and strength were already powerful beyond his understanding; even casual advice could clearly show him the future path to transcendence.
If he could frequently follow by his side, not needing much, even being guided once or twice a year, how many detours could he avoid, how much time could he save?
Could he possibly follow in Lord Ilo’s footsteps in the future, occupy a temple of the Light Gods, steal the faith within, become legendary, or even strive for ascension to demigod?
The beauty of it all, even just thinking about it in his mind, excited Wales beyond control.
Compared to that, what was being a vice president of Demon Heart? As long as he could step into a higher level, he could always establish another Demon Heart, one far stronger than the current one.
Lide’s appearance gave Wales, who had been stuck at level 19 for nearly a century, a rare glimmer of hope. This level 19 Heart-eating Demon, the undisputed super boss of the Underworld, had already been charmed by his own beautiful musings.
He could hardly wait.
To seek ascension beyond the extraordinary, he had paid unimaginable prices, even replacing half of his bloodline with that of a demon.
Yet, under such circumstances, he still couldn’t find the way forward; the difficulties he encountered seemed insurmountable but broke through with the other’s casual guidance.
After this event, he truly understood how important it was to have a powerful teacher guiding the way.
Even if Lord Ilo would not take him as a disciple, just receiving some guidance was worth any price he might pay.
Determination filled Wales’s face.
“I…” Lide opened his mouth, wanting to say something but not knowing how to say it.
Could this be a classic case of being conned into selling himself and helping others count the money?
Had he inadvertently become the enemy’s boss?
Betty and Emi were also deeply shaken by Wales’s words; wasn’t there supposed to be a negotiation, even to the point of conflict?
How had they almost become one family now?
This….
They exchanged glances, wisely staying silent.
Leaving everything to the wise judgment of the great Ancestor Crown.
“Lord Ilo, you need not worry, I believe you control the Dark Contract also to collect some uncommon alchemy materials and other items. Becoming the vice president of Demon Heart doesn’t require your involvement in management; any items you need, I shall collect for you…”
Wales, thinking the powerful crowned one worried about the trouble, quickly explained.
“And I will also have Demon Heart help you reorganize the Dark Contract; this won’t affect your role as vice president of Demon Heart…”
Watching Wales’s sincere gaze, Lide couldn’t help but twitch his mouth.
The age-old tricks really do win people’s hearts…
And becoming the vice president of Demon Heart really didn’t sound too bad.
Being one of the three great giants of the Underworld alone sounded quite prestigious.
“Wales, you are right. I control the Dark Contract merely to gather some magic materials and alchemy materials I need. Your sincerity has moved me; I agree to become the vice president of Demon Heart.”
After saying this, Lide’s face showed an expression that suggested Wales had clinched a great bargain.
“But don’t disturb me over trivial matters; what I command, you must handle with utmost speed.”
Hearing Lide’s response, Wales’s face could no longer hold back, a thick smile emerging as if he had gained a tremendous advantage.
This was a being beyond the extraordinary, approaching legendary!
Hahaha, truly marvelous…
“Indeed, Lord Ilo, Wales welcomes your joining; from now on, Demon Heart will always be at your command.”
A being close to Legendary had actually become a member of the Demon Heart.
Wales was filled with joy, feeling this was the most correct decision he had made in his life, and encountering Lord Ilo this year was definitely the Goddess of Luck winking at him.
Praise the demons, praise the Goddess of Luck, praise Lord Ilo!
“Kedel, notify all the underground forces in Green City that the Demon Heart will have a new Vice President—the great Lord Ilo.
Furthermore, Lord Ilo will reorganize the Dark Contract, and the Demon Heart will unconditionally assist in the formation of the Dark Contract. During this period, anyone who opposes the Dark Contract is opposing the Demon Heart.”
After Wales had received Lide’s agreement, he suppressed the surprise in his heart and continued to bet on him, not caring about these minor expenditures, to win favor from this unimaginably powerful being.
He even dared to bet that if others knew he had secured a nearly Legendary being to his chariot at such a small cost, they would definitely be envious.
What a clever decision, Wales was very satisfied with his actions, especially when he saw the smile on Lide’s face, his heart filled with joy.
Indeed, Lord Ilo is very pleased with my decision.
“Wales, you are a smart man. The Dark Contract has been severely damaged by the encirclement of the Green City military forces; I need to bring the Dark Contract back to a subversive state in the shortest time.
Stanley will coordinate with you on this.”
Lide said meaningfully as he patted Wales on the shoulder.
“Believe me, you will be surprised by what you did today.”
A brighter smile appeared on Wales’s face, seeing it as Lide’s appreciation of his actions.
Winning the favor of such a powerful existence, the future is bright.
It seemed he could already see himself becoming Extraordinary, even Legendary.
Lord Wales, haha, what an intoxicating title.
“As you wish, Lord Ilo…”
After the major issues were settled, the atmosphere became much more harmonious.
“Lord Ilo, the black market in the west district is currently co-managed by the Demon Heart and those Fallen Knights of the Sinking Mist.
You might be interested in the black market…”
After chatting for a while, Wales suddenly remembered something and boasted,
“The black market in the west area is the largest underground trading place in all of Green City, even the nobles of Green City have traded there.”
“As long as you have Gold Puck, you can buy anything you want here”
“The ritual to obtain the Demon Bloodline was acquired through the black market”
The black market?
Hearing this name, interest clearly sparked on Lide’s face.
Although the previous Dark Contract was strong, compared to the Demon Heart and the Sinking Mist, it was relatively new, so it had never managed to get a share of the most enticing black market in the west district.
Grotto had reported these detailed conditions of the Dark Contract a few days ago.
“What do you mean?”
“If you are interested in the black market, the Demon Heart can relinquish part of the management rights to let the Dark Contract participate as well,” spoke Wales, seemingly discussing a minor matter, completely nonchalant about the huge profits the black market generated annually.
However, other faces in the room subtly changed.
The man in the black suit next to Wales showed a pained expression, clearly indicating that Wales’s offer was significant for the Demon Heart.
Lide, sensing this, nodded slightly.
“Let Stanley handle these minor matters, Wales. Your actions and performance have won my friendship.
I believe the Demon Heart and the Dark Contract will become good partners.
And you, you will have an even more glorious future…”
Hearing Lide’s words, Wales instantly showed a radiant smile.
“It is my honor, Lord Ilo.”
Emi, standing behind, slightly bowed her head, with a deep sense of reflection in her eyes.
It was her first time seeing someone sell themselves and still be so excited.
Lord of Ancestor, truly worthy of being the Lord of Ancestor.

chapters.title: Chapter 200: 201: Beyond Imaginary Gains
chapters.content:
Chapter 200: Chapter 201: Beyond Imaginary Gains
Three Sunshine Hours later, Lide left Drucker Tavern with a beaming smile.
The Great Demon, Heart-eating Demon Wales of Demon Heart, humbly bade him farewell.
What was expected to be a fierce battle of a meeting ended in such a beautiful and harmonious situation.
When Lide returned to the temporary manor of Dark Contract, he couldn’t contain his inner joy and started to check the system notifications he had just received.
“Ding~ You have become the master of Dark Contract and have earned the recognition of Sovereign—Heart-eating Demon Wales of Demon Heart; your secondary identity, Ilo, in the Underworld of Green City—Legend Level +5.”
“Ding, you have become the Vice President of Demon Heart and are widely recognized and revered by the forces of the Underworld in Green City; your secondary identity, Ilo, in the Underworld of Green City—Legend Level +5.”
...
“Ding, your secondary identity—Ilo, has reached a Legend Level of 10 in the Underworld of Green City, activating the title: ‘Dark Legend’.”
“Dark Legend, attributes: 1, when facing Dark Race, your intimidation increases, and in front of creatures with a Legend Level five points below yours, you gain the Dignity Effect (enemies will fear you, and all attributes decrease by 30%), 2, a very high probability that Dark Creatures with a lower level than yours will join you, 3, you will be antagonized by creatures of the Good Camp and natural life.”
“Ding, because your secondary identity, Ilo, has a special intimidation effect on Heart-eating Demon Wales, your Legend Level increases by +10 when facing Wales.”
“Ding~ You have become the President of Dark Contract and have earned recognition from the Underworld forces of Green City, granting you character Experience—2000.”
What a massive gain.
Absolutely massive.
Lide never expected that the secondary identity he made up—Ilo, would be recognized by the system.
And it’s exaggerated that he now has 10 Legend Level points in the Underworld of Green City, even activating a powerful title: ‘Dark Legend’.
From now, in Green City, if life belongs to the Dark Race and doesn’t exceed five Legend Level points, facing him will decrease 30 attributes.
This is too awesome.
It’s just like cheating.
Unable to contain his inner happiness, Lide’s lips curved into a wide smile.
Moreover, it was key that his identity as the President of Dark Contract was recognized by the system and coupled with recognition from the Underworld of Green City.
This was equivalent to official certification.
Even though he had previously taken over Dark Contract, in the Underworld, Viscount Bernard was still recognized, and the nominal owner of Dark Contract would always be him as long as Bernard appeared.
But now it was different, these forces recognized the new master of Dark Contract—Ilo. No matter when Viscount Bernard appeared, there would only be one President of Dark Contract—unless Bernard managed to kill Ilo.
Gaining recognition often takes the most time, and Lide had been prepared for a long battle, but now he had reached the goal in one step.
There couldn’t be a more surprising event for him.
The single driving factor behind all this was none other than Heart-eating Demon Wales, the master of Demon Heart, who drove everything.
As one of the top three powerhouses of the Underworld in Green City, his recognition of Lide’s status meant that this powerhouse recognized Lide at least as a peer.
With the prestige of Wales, the identity of Ilo immediately gained recognition in the Underworld.
What amused Lide more was that he would also gain an additional 10 points of Legend Level when facing Wales.
This clearly signified that his status in the heart of Wales was immeasurably high.
“This Heart-eating Demon is not scary at all, praise the goddess~”
Lide looked at the information on the attribute panel, laughing very happily.
This wasn’t just a big win; it was an enormous, special windfall.
Not only did he resolve the issue with Dark Contract, but he even managed to bring the even more powerful Demon Heart into the same camp.
He had resolved his pressing concerns in a short period of time.
It could be said that he perfectly completed his plan.
However, there wasn’t without risks. If Heart-eating Demon Wales found out he had been deceived, then this half-demon Dark Great Boss might recklessly overturn Dark Contract.
One should never underestimate the power of a giant.
But Lide was naturally confident, the king of schemes having logged on, it wasn’t easy to see through him.
And as long as he had some time to develop, what was a Heart-eating Demon to him, when the potential of Dawn City hadn’t even been fully unleashed yet?
Within just half a year, he had advanced from abject poverty to being able to confront his opponent directly, what level could he reach by the time this Heart-eating Demon becomes Transcendent?
“Lord Ancestor Crown, your wisdom is truly worthy of the Creator God’s admiration.”
Emi, having returned to the manor of Dark Contract, immediately offered his heartfelt praise to Lide.
He had watched step by step as Lide developed to this level.
From initially being the top combat force to now where Betty, Groot, and even Stanley had stronger combat abilities than him, the strength of Dawn City had grown too quickly.
And the maneuvers Lide had shown during the development of Dawn City, along with his decisiveness in dealing with various difficulties, had earned him immense respect from this blasphemer.
Lide gently shook his head.
“No, this was purely accidental. If it wasn’t that this Heart-eating Demon overthought it, we wouldn’t have had such good results.”
Lide was clear about this. If the master of Demon Heart had been a fool, tonight wouldn’t have been so easy.
The half-demon, Wales, inherited the demon’s suspicion.
Such coincidences were too many, and it would be hard for a second occasion like this to occur.
“From now on in Dark Contract, everyone should address me by my ‘real name’—Ilo, regardless of whether there are outsiders present or not.”
He was somewhat uneasy, so he specifically reminded them again.
“Yes, Lord Ilo,” everyone smartly shouted in unison.
Only Betty sat in the chair, bored, watching the others sing in chorus.
She was only a hired thug temped over by Lide, appearing in the Dark Contract only when something important was at stake, so this wild Northern Land Valkyrie couldn’t be bothered to participate.
Lide didn’t mind, being the top combat strength of his side and having established great merits, naturally had some privileges. It was enough that she obeyed in crucial times.
“Stanley, from today, you and Groth will manage the Dark Contract together, with Emi assisting.
Currently, there are three main tasks you need to accomplish.
First, stabilize the interests of the Dark Contract,
The attacks by the Green City army have already caused the Dark Contract to lose many long-managed strongholds. With the addition of the Demon Heart, our power will become stable.
So, in the short term, I need you to gather as many of the Dark Contract members as possible to stabilize the original interests.”
Lide didn’t ramble, moving straight to the point and beginning to assign tasks.
The Dark Contract was his, officially recognized by the system.
A loose force was something he truly disliked seeing.
What he wanted was a force like the Crimson Mage Tower and Dawn City, which could become the sharp blade in his hand and strike at the enemy’s throat upon his command.
So, organizing the already half-ruined Dark Contract was a matter of utmost importance.
“Secondly, ascertain the intersecting interests with the Demon Heart.
For now, the Demon Heart will be an important ally to the Dark Contract for a long time, and you need to learn to utilize this ally.
I will secretly supply you with a batch of magic scrolls, which the Dark Contract can use to exchange for some interests with the Demon Heart.”
Lide understood the Demon Heart deeper. One should never casually trust these Dark Life beings’ promises.
Their promises aren’t absolute insurance; they can tear the contract if it benefits them.
This isn’t a world blanketed in light; in the Underworld, trust and betrayal are often equivalent.
The Dark Contract needing to return to the power of Viscount Bernard’s era would require substantial input of strength and also aid from the Demon Heart.
With the presence of the Heart-eating Demon, Ilo Wales, this would be much facilitated.
But if the Dark Contract and Demon Heart could form an alliance of interest, more effective support could undoubtedly be gained.
The magic scrolls were sharp weapons in Lide’s hands.
No one could resist the temptation of magic scrolls.
“Thirdly, expand the intelligence network of the Dark Contract.
I need the Dark Contract to be my eyes and ears; when I need information, the Dark Contract should be able to provide it to me promptly.”
The role of the Crimson Mage Tower meant that Lide couldn’t expect much useful information.
After all, partners of the Mage Tower were chambers of commerce and nobles, not likely to divulge valuable information.
Even if information could be obtained, it might not match what he needed.
However, the Dark Contract was different; this Underground Force had countless avenues to explore.
Casinos, taverns, brothels, and inns — these lower industries often served as hubs of information.
This sector was a blank stage in Green City for the Crimson Mage Tower. If not for this incident involving Emi, they might have been robbed blind without ever knowing how it happened.
This incident also made him much more vigilant about controlling the Dark Contract; that was a significant part of the reason for this plan.
“Yes, Lord Ilo.”
Stanley and others immediately nodded in agreement; as Bloodlines, they couldn’t possibly refuse a command from the Ancestor.
Lide, satisfied, looked approvingly at Stanley. Although previously an enemy, after converting this dark priest of the Late Bell Church to his side, he found him pleasant to the eye.
“You also need to reorganize the original division of power and business fields, eliminating some overly evil practices.
I only need the Dark Contract to operate—normal industries like taverns, brothels, inns, casinos.”
True, engaging in prostitution and gambling in the western district’s land of sin was merely the most ordinary of businesses.
“Later on, I will provide a specific magic scroll for the Dark Contract to operate.
I need you to extend your reach as swiftly as possible.”
Lide’s profound gaze rested on them, filled with deep meaning.
The Crimson Mage Tower visible in light, the Dark Contract hidden in shadow, plus the main base Dawn City as supportive backbone.
The development system he desired was finally in place.
A three-core development, truly flourishing on all fronts.
Regardless of the threat from any direction, he would have ample power to cope.
It could be said that the presence of the Dark Contract greatly compensated for the shortcomings of the Crimson Mage Tower, providing a strong and powerful protection for Lide’s financial resources.
The Crimson Mage Tower was protected by Spark overtly, deterred by Betty, shielded covertly by the Dark Contract, and supported by the potential ally Demon Heart.
Yet at this moment, no one knew that the master of the Crimson Mage Tower, Spark’s disciple Lide Kachar, a mere Advanced Mage with the title of a genius mage, had already silently become a significant power player in Green City.
The hidden strength beneath the iceberg of the Crimson Mage Tower was enough to shock everyone, this deep-water leviathan was lurking, just waiting for the enemy to appear.
The super boss who dominated both the dark and light scenes of Green City had officially stepped onto the stage today.

chapters.title: Chapter 201: 202: Game Beta Testing? Players? (Long Chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 201: Chapter 202: Game Beta Testing? Players? (Long Chapter)
After resolving the issue with the Dark Covenant, Lide finally got a chance to catch his breath.
From the moment he found out that the Dark Covenant was going to attack the Crimson Mage Tower, it had been over a month of effort to resolve the situation.
Although the gains were significant, the effort he had put in was undoubtedly substantial.
Even the highly energetic Lide began to feel a bit of fatigue from the high-intensity operation.
At present, with the support of the Demon Heart, the Dark Covenant had nothing to fear from any forces lurking in the shadows. They could still slaughter their way through and get back on track for development.
With the hidden support of the Dark Covenant beneath the surface, his openly known force—the Crimson Mage Tower—also had a broader space for further development.
...
Lide’s move in this chess game of power was quite impressive; it was definitely a forceful stroke for the grand scheme of things.
Not to mention the strategic positioning of two forces, one in the light and one in the dark, as well as having a safe base at the rear, this setup was incredibly satisfying.
Time flew, and once the business with the Dark Covenant was settled, Lide poured his efforts into the development of the Crimson Mage Tower.
Vina had already secured a trade partnership externally and had transported magic resources to the Crimson Mage Tower.
With sufficient supply of raw materials, the production at the Magic Factory was at full throttle, unleashing its full productive capacity, and the efficiency of producing magic scrolls had once again improved.
The market for magic scrolls in Green City was completely overwhelmed by the epoch-making production of the Magic Factory.
The Crimson Mage Tower had directly devoured ninety percent of the magic scroll market share, effectively monopolizing the market for low-end magic scrolls.
As for the earning power of such a monopoly, it could be said to be unsurpassed.
The influx of Gold Pucks began to swell the coffers of the Crimson Mage Tower, fattening up what had once been a withered purse.
Yet, with the Ancient Alchemy Magic Array, a gold-devouring beast, Lide was still not living the life of a landlord.
By mid-July, the Dark Covenant, with the support of the Demon Heart and magic scroll reinforcements from the Crimson Mage Tower, had regained its footing, allowing the once-dominant Dark Giant to bare its ferocious tusks again.
It was during this time the intel department started its strategic preparations.
Lide took Emi back to Dawn City at this juncture.
After a month of stabilization, the Dark Covenant had calmed down, and there was no longer a need for Emi to stay there.
Currently, with the presence of Stanley and Grot, two top-level professionals above level 15, as deterrents in terms of strategic strength, in addition to seventeen high-level professionals above level 10,
and adding the previous members of the Dark Covenant, there were a total of 600 intermediate professionals between levels 5 and 9.
This force could even be considered formidable in the West… although it still couldn’t compare to the Dark Covenant during its revolutionary days.
Yet the Dark Covenant’s reputation now was by no means less than when Viscount Bernard was in charge,
because the new Clan Leader of the Dark Covenant—Lord Ilo, this powerful being recognized by the Heart-eating Demon Wales, was very likely Transcendent.
This was a statement directly from Wales himself.
This news made many forces raise their highest vigilance and respect towards the Dark Covenant as it stood.
Transcendent, that was Transcendent! Who would dare provoke someone able to face the Death God?
The Dark Covenant also stabilized its foundation relying on this so-called Transcendent patron and became an entity no one dared to underestimate.
Lide didn’t pay much attention to this, as Stanley and Grot’s combination was enough to handle matters concerning the Dark Covenant; he brought Emi back for this reason.
Compared to the Dark Covenant, Dawn City was in greater need of Emi.
Dawn City, City Hall, third-floor office.
Lide looked at the spirited Harrison with a hint of confusion in his eyes.
“Harrison, why the urgency to have me return?”
Harrison, who had a somewhat scholarly temperament, couldn’t hide the joy on his face.
“Clan Leader, the first wheat harvest in Dawn City is ready for reaping…”
Lide was momentarily stunned, then promptly stood up, his eyes filled with surprise.
“Really? Has the Agriculture Department arranged a harvesting plan?”
The fact that the crop was ready for harvest was just as important to Lide as taking control of the Dark Covenant.
With food, the biggest quandary facing Dawn City would be solved.
The residents of Dawn City were about to break free from the iron chains around their necks.
Whether it be this year’s population plundering plan or the development plan for next year, food was the most crucial element, bar none.
Food was the foundation for everything; without enough to eat, there was no talking about development.
And now that the first harvest of food was ready, the significance this represented was tremendous.
“Your Highness, the Agriculture Department has been organizing residents to harvest since yesterday, expecting that all the wheat will be reaped within half a month.”
“That’s good, very good. How many pounds per acre can we expect?”
“The land in Moonlight Plain varies from fertile to barren, and each farmer has different levels of farming skills, so it’s hard to generalize.
But based on the Agriculture Department’s estimate, the average yield should be between 370 to 430 pounds per acre,” said Harrison, offering Lide a reassurance.
Even if the yield was only 370 pounds per acre, the crops currently cultivated on Moonlight Plain could feed 100,000 people for a year.
The policy of distributing land for free had finally taken effect.
The successful harvest of crops was a strategic victory for Lide, and it was extremely important.
And this was just the beginning. With the arrival of the second Frost Month, the issue of food in Dawn City would no longer trouble them.
The more the population grew, the more land they could cultivate, and they would only have more food. This was a virtuous cycle of development.
“Are the granaries built?”
“They were all completed half a month ago. Currently, there are four granaries, each located at a corner of Dawn City, and each is guarded by Bloodline and Security Team members.
The four granaries are estimated to store enough food for 300,000 people for a year.”
Harrison replied not with specific data but with a very clear visual response.
Lide nodded in satisfaction.
Currently, Dawn City’s grain policy was managed by the City Hall; private buying and selling on the market was prohibited, and farmers were required to sell their harvested food to the City Hall.
No matter the era or background, food was vital to life.
City Hall’s intervention directly guaranteed the stability of the food supply. Everything else could be unstable, but issues related to the livelihood of the people had to be stable.
Lide had severely admonished this: City Hall must directly control basic materials such as iron ore, food, cotton fabrics, etc. Other items that did not affect people’s livelihoods could be left to the market to regulate.
In fact, even on modern Earth, these industries critical to the livelihood of the people are mostly directly controlled by the state, so his decision was not inappropriate.
“Good, you organize this personally, and make sure to do the work well. Harvesting, drying, storage—every step must be taken seriously.”
Harrison, of course, knew the importance Lide placed on food, and he nodded solemnly.
“Yes, Clan Leader.”
After Harrison left, Lide couldn’t contain his excitement and left City Hall directly to rush to the outskirts of the city.
He wanted to see the farmland for himself.
The production of grain can be said to owe much credit to Lide; without his policies, these commoners probably couldn’t even touch the soil.
Stepping out of City Hall, an expansive view opened up before him, and his mood immediately lifted.
Dawn City had undergone massive construction and had greatly changed compared to before.
Whether it was the streets or the houses, most areas had been renovated.
On the cobblestone-paved streets, plants and flowers arranged in neat purple and red hues about half a person’s height flourished on both sides of the road, making for a lush and comfortable sight.
The surrounding houses were two to three stories tall, with white round archways on the ground floor and semi-circular windows on the second floor with translucent glass embedded.
Shops along the street opened their doors wide, selling all kinds of goods such as fruit, flowers, bread, tailor shops, and grocery stores, among others.
At the corner of a cross street stood a white marble statue clad in armor—if one looked closely, they could see it was none other than Lide himself.
Beautifully colored murals depicting religious stories of the Dawn Sect leading residents towards the light were painted on the blank walls along the streets.
Bustling and lively.
And what stood out the most was the exceptionally clean and tidy environment on the streets, with no trash or animal droppings to be seen.
This stemmed from Lide’s obsession with a clean city, and his heartfelt disgust for Green City, a city that reeked constantly.
He therefore ordered City Hall to resolve the environmental issues of Dawn City and to ensure that the terrible conditions of Green City would not occur.
Consequently, part of the logistics team had become full-time sanitation workers, and anyone who failed to throw trash in the bin would immediately be punished by the red-armband-wearing managers.
The punishments were severe; if caught, offenders had to work for a month mining in the mines for free.
Such strict measures meant nobody dared to litter or even spit on the ground.
So the pervasive stench that filled Green City was completely absent in Dawn City. Clean and tidy, it was not an exaggeration to say that it was cleaner than cities on Earth.
Under the strict regulations of City Hall, residents had developed good habits. If someone littered, they were immediately scorned by those around them and even directly reported.
Under such pressure, these commoners living at the bottom had actually developed good living habits.
The residents of Dawn City were not very concerned at first, but after being punished, they regulated their behavior and could clearly feel the improvement in their living environment. Eventually, they began to cherish and carefully maintain everything.
Walking through the city, Lide felt an immense sense of accomplishment as he observed the prosperous and lively scenes.
He had handcrafted all of it; without him, Dawn City would not exist. The feeling was indescribably wonderful.
Amidst the hustle and bustle, every resident wore a cheerful smile, their eyes filled with hope.
The citizens on the streets were dressed in clean and neat clothes; not a patch in sight, and not even old clothes were to be seen.
In just half a year, these refugees who had lost their homes had undergone a transformation from deep within.
And the one who brought them all of this change, of course, was the master of this city, the great Kachar City Lord.
“Good day, Lord Kachar.”
“Good day, respected Kachar City Lord…”
“Great Lord Kachar…”
Walking on the street, Lide was immediately recognized by the residents, although very few dared to approach and disturb him.
Every resident by his side would place their hand on their chest and bow reverently, their faces filled with awe and worship from the bottom of their hearts.
Each passing resident would stop in their tracks and bend at the waist to pay their respects upon seeing Lide, only straightening up after he had walked a fair distance away.
This is what respect looks like.
In this city, his prestige had long since been on par with the divine.
The scene where Lide passed was truly spectacular.
No matter who it was on the street, upon seeing him, everyone would immediately stop, place their hand on their chest, and bow, as lowly citizens worshiping their king.
Loyal believers were seeing their one and only faith, their great divine entity.
Like a touch on the mimosa pudica, everyone’s heads bowed in unison.
No one dared to make eye contact with Lide.
Even the patrolling security team would place a hand on their chest and bow, pledging their highest respect to the City Lord, their lord and master.
Lide initially found this scene quite satisfactory, but it began to feel rather dull when everyone did the same thing.
The heights were cold indeed; it was impossible to stroll through the city like an ordinary person anymore.
He did not linger, walking step by step along the main road and heading out of the city.
And wherever he passed, all residents looked on with reverence and worship.
This was the ruler of a city, the king of all its people.
With his actions, Lide had conquered everyone in this city.
It was his first time strolling alone in Dawn City during the day, at a time when people came and went.
Looking at everything around him, the sense of accomplishment that rose in his heart was indescribable.
This was his city; everything in this city belonged to him.
Here, he could decide the fate of anyone, including their life or death.
He was the sole ruler of this city, and as long as he wished, he could implement any mandate he wanted in the city.
Fairness, justice, kindness, evil—all were judged by him alone.
No one could defy his commands, nor did anyone have the right to refuse his will.
The feeling of holding absolute power was truly unforgettable.
Dressed in a black mage’s robe, the perfect demeanor of Lide, with the air of a noble, walked out of the city that belonged to him under the watchful eyes of the crowd.
Exiting the city from the Southern District, he walked on the wide road towards the agricultural area.
The Southern District’s range has now been expanded by nearly a third.
Under the construction department, the war ruins originally created from the battle with Emi had long been rebuilt, and the new houses were neatly arranged, which made the already sizable Southern District appear even more spacious.
This was to prepare for this year’s Frost Month population raid.
Dawn City’s population base was too small, and it was unrealistic to rely on childbirth for growth in the short term.
Moreover, due to the geographical constraints, the only way for fast development here was to plunder population from the outside world.
It could be said that the most important thing for Dawn City at present was population development; planting crops was for population growth, building the city was for the population, and expanding the Magic Language Bats was to plunder population more quickly.
The keynote of the sustainable development strategy he had set must have a large population as a premise.
Humans played the role of the foundation in Dawn City, the basis for the city’s development, while the Bloodline was the upper structure built upon this foundation.
Only when the foundation was solid could the Bloodline build a more perfect structure atop it.
And to ensure this foundation was solid, Lide estimated that only when the future population of Dawn City reached 300,000, or even 500,000 or a million, would it be truly stable.
By that time, even if faced with Green City which had tens of thousands of troops, Dawn City would not feel the slightest fear.
Outside the South District, the road leading to Moonlight Plain was named Moonlight Lane by Harrison.
Lide’s face was quite priceless when he heard that this road, which could simultaneously accommodate eighteen carriages, was named Moonlight Lane.
However, the name had already been decided, and he couldn’t be bothered to overturn it.
In the harvest season, the crowd on Moonlight Lane was very busy, with cattle and horses pulling carts on the road without pause.
The carts were loaded with freshly harvested wheat, the golden grains piled up in the grey hemp sacks.
Thanks to Dylan, a second-generation Bloodline’s efforts, almost every household in Dawn City now had cattle or horses to plow the fields, so these carts were also developed in keeping with the times.
This greatly reduced manual labor.
It might not yet be as convenient as modern machinery, but it was far more so than the previous methods involving carrying loads on backs and shoulders.
The Western District was still bordered by unopened grassland, the future site of Moonlight New City.
Looking in the distance, the end of the mountain on the left was faintly marked by a row of towering furnaces emitting black smoke—that was the working Steel Refining Furnace of the blacksmith’s shop.
Now the mining vein development in Giant Valley had entered the right track, delivering dozens of tons of ore to Dawn City for processing each day.
Steel was the lifeblood of industry, the wheelbarrow for a city’s development; having iron mines meant that Dawn City also received solid support for its development.
Dawn City’s good development was inseparable from the iron mines of Giant Valley.
Turning his head to view the front, nine towering cylindrical towers also appeared in Lide’s sight,
The Dawn Mage Tower, the residents of Dawn City now preferred to call it the Rainbow Mage Tower.
Among the nine Mage Towers, aside from the main tower and the auxiliary tower at the front gate which were black, the other auxiliary towers were the colors of a rainbow.
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.
Mysterious yet exuding a certain aesthetic beauty, it greatly suited the tastes of the residents.
During this period, all of Dawn City’s eligible youth had undergone Magic Talent testing.
Among these youths, 132 were found to possess Magic Talent, of course, by normal selection standards, it would be considerable if 30 were recruited by the Dawn Mage Tower.
But due to Lide’s life-based Mage program, even youths with average talent were recruited as alternate Mages.
Of course, these apprentices would not receive training in advanced combat Magic, but merely ordinary auxiliary Magic to prepare for future production and livelihood.
In addition, 200 new members of the Bloodline also joined the Mage Tower, becoming among its students.
The original intention of establishing the Dawn Mage Tower was to train Mages quickly; these novices, who had just become Bloodline during the Frost Month, were painfully lacking in their proficiency with Magic.
Although the Bloodline was an Upper Race possessing inherent Casting Talent, all of these required time to unfold.
The role of the Dawn Mage Tower was to focus on training and to shorten the time needed for their growth as quickly as possible.
Moreover, all the high-level Bloodline members had also taken up residence in the Mage Tower, with Harrison even serving as an auxiliary Tower Master.
The Bloodline only needed to rest for two to three Sunshine Hours each day, so they had plenty of time.
After finishing their work and then attending Magic lessons or lecturing other apprentices, they felt no pressure whatsoever.
The establishment of the Dawn Mage Tower truly marked a significant growth point for the Bloodline’s power, its impact could not be simply described in a few words.
Of course, to achieve the effect Lide desired for the Mage Tower, substantial investment and adequate time would still be needed.
However, these were not problems; everything would be resolved satisfactorily.
Lide gazed at the long Moonlight Path, unfurled his ferocious bat wings, and in the gaze of the crowd, flapped them to fly into the sky.
The road was too long, and hurrying along like this was quite a waste of time.
After ascending, his view slowly elevated, and the world before him suddenly became clear.
All things between heaven and earth could be seen at a glance.
The ability to fly was something all humans yearned for; the former Lide was no exception, so even now, he felt genuinely happy every time he flew.
While flying along the main road to the area above the Dawn Mage Tower, the farming region of Moonlight Plain came into view.
A golden glow.
The mature wheat under the sun’s rays stretched as far as the eye could see, the fields like they were sprinkled with Gold Puck.
A gentle breeze blew, causing waves of wheat to ripple, a feast for the eyes full of enchanting beauty.
The scorching air did nothing to dampen the residents’ enthusiasm below, each one wielding sickles hastily made by the smithy, harvesting the wheat in the fields.
This scene was very comforting to Lide; although the Bloodline did not need human food, possessing the soul of Huaxia, he was naturally inclined toward farming, so every time he saw this scene, he felt deeply satisfied.
After observing for a while from midair, Lide landed at the entrance of the Dawn Mage Tower.
Upon seeing Lide’s figure, the guarding Bloodline at the doorway immediately saluted with hand on chest.
“Good day, Clan Leader.”
Due to it being daytime, even though there were sun-shielding measures at the gate of the Mage Tower, the few Bloodline members still had a somewhat pale complexion.
Daytime was not friendly to the Bloodline.
“Where is Emi?”
Upon returning, Emi had come straight to the Mage Tower and had now become its dedicated administrator.
For the moment, since the Dawn Sect had the Holy Divine Priest, Nilo, Emi did not have much involvement with the Dawn Sect anymore.
Nilo was no less competent, and in terms of proselytizing, this girl with a faint golden hue in her eyes and a Divine-like dignity was even more persuasive to the residents—Nilo was the biggest contributor to the recent growth in apprentices within the Dawn Sect.
Now Lide had no time to manage the Dawn Sect; he had too many other matters to attend to, so he let Nilo take over the management.
“Marquis Emi is in the Black Tower…”
The Black Tower was the main tower of the Dawn Mage Tower, the 27-blade high Mage Tower was currently the most majestic building in Dawn City.
“Good.”
Lide nodded and stepped into the 15-blade high auxiliary Mage Tower in front of him.
The Dawn Mage Tower was protected by a circle of walls standing five blades high, only by entering through the black auxiliary tower at the front gate could one access the interior.
But just as he entered the Mage Tower, his figure abruptly halted, a system notification took him by surprise, scarcely concealing the amazement in his eyes.
“Ding~ ‘Glory’ beta test begins, the number of beta testers—100,000.”
“The game’s public test is 756 game days away.”
Game beta test, players??

chapters.title: Chapter 202 - 203: The Player's First Arrival (Major Chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 202: Chapter 203: The Player’s First Arrival (Major Chapter)
Green City Life Temple.
The Life Goddess, as the only great being in Glory that is simultaneously worshipped by the evil, neutral, and good camps, has temples that are the most numerous and commonly seen in Glory.
Even in the Bottomless Abyss, a place of Extreme Evil, one can find the presence of the Life Temple, a divine being who reigns above both good and evil.
In Glory, the most common phrase humans say—”Praise the Goddess”—is in reverence to this revered Life Goddess.
At this moment, inside the Life Temple of Green City, on an altar that was seldom used.
Swoosh~
...
A faint light flickered.
Then a young figure dressed in sackcloth appeared inside the temple.
The female priests and priests around saw this figure and their faces immediately displayed wide smiles.
An adventurer from an Otherworld had arrived.
Glory Light slowly opened his somewhat murky eyes, and what he saw was the snow-white ceiling above him, carved with bas-reliefs praising the Life Goddess, filled with a uniquely religious flavor.
His gaze slowly settled, and a look of surprise appeared on his face.
“This environment is so realistic, it’s hardly any different from what ‘Glory’ advertised…”
His heart stirred, he slightly propped himself up to a sitting position, and the touch of the cool stone altar beneath his palm surprised him even more.
This sensation was fantastic.
Glory Light was the ID he often used in games, and being selected as a beta tester this time was also by chance; he had never even experienced this legendary virtual game with extreme realism offline before.
Now, entering “Glory” and just a few details had given him a shock; this real feeling was incomparable to other trash games.
A virtual game achieving this level was an absolute piece of high-tech.
With a curious gaze, he turned his head to look around.
This medium-sized chapel with hundreds of fixed wooden seats on the floor and carvings on the snow-white walls around celebrating the divine.
All the decorations bore no significant difference from Medieval European chapels.
At this time, around him were more than a dozen priests in priestly robes, both men and women, looking at him curiously.
Among them, an elderly priest with snow-white hair and a kind and amiable face stepped forward, seemingly having something to say to him.
In Glory Light’s eyes, all these priests had a faint glow about them, especially the old priest in front of him, who looked like he was wearing clothes made of fluorescent lights.
It was suffused with an indescribable sanctity.
“Young man, are you the adventurer from an Otherworld?”
Priest Mite looked at the seventeen or eighteen-year-old boy with a bit of curiosity. He had received a divine revelation from the Life Goddess last night that today an adventurer from an Otherworld would be born in the Life Temple. All the clergy had to be ready to receive him.
The Life Goddess’s temple in Green City was extremely vast, and this smaller side hall was his responsibility, so he was already waiting.
Glory Light didn’t seem to hear Priest Mite’s question, his nose slightly twitched as he caught a whiff of the faint scent of jasmine.
Looking at the old man in front of him with curious eyes, the wrinkles on his face, the vicissitudes in his eyes, were laid bare before him.
He could even feel every breath they took and the dust in the air that floated with it; this was simply not something a game could do.
“This game is incredible; I haven’t actually traveled through time, have I?!”
Priest Mite’s frown deepened, and his forehead wrinkled more.
Because he couldn’t understand what the other was saying.
“Young man, are you the adventurer from an Otherworld?” With no other choice, the old priest repeated his question.
