Glory Light only then heard the old priest’s question clearly, but it was no use because he found he couldn’t understand at all.
“Elder, what are you saying?”
“&*%%￥￥##&*?”
“Elder, can you speak Chinese?”
“**%…*##@!&*HOY*UG?”
“What the fuck, what is this crap, we can’t even understand each other??”
Glory Light’s mouth twitched viciously; he very much felt the urge to curse.
Did it need to be so realistic?
Different languages too; what was he supposed to do now?
Glory Light and the old priest stared at each other, both speaking words neither could comprehend.
“Young man, don’t you know the common language of Glory?”
“**…*…%￥#%??”
“Young man, where are you from?”
“*￥%###￥%#…”
Finally, the old priest, with an expression of speechlessness, cradled his forehead and stretched out his hand to place it on Glory Light’s head.
Glory Light watched as the old man placed his hand on top of his head and immediately felt a chill down his spine. This NPC couldn’t possibly be wanting to silence him for good, could he??
Then he saw a faint glow appear in the hands of the old priest, and his head felt cool as if he understood something.
“Young man from another world, can you understand me now?” The old priest spoke again, and Glory Light almost burst into tears.
I’ve got a Husky… Does this game have to be so hardcore that I have to go through all this just to understand?
“Old man, I can understand now. I can understand, thank you for your help.”
The old priest looked pleased, “Young man, you’re welcome. It is the blessed command of the Goddess to help you.” He then added with some regret.
“However, I just used a Second Circle Spell, Language Comprehension, which only lasts for three Sunshine Hours. After the time passes, you will still be unable to understand me.
Young man from another world, if you want to live in the Main Plane of Glory, you still need to learn our language.”
Glory Light’s face changed, mmp, now I have to learn a language?
I can barely recognize all 21, uh, 22 letters of the English alphabet, and now you want me to learn the language of the game?
“Old man, I…”
“Young man, you may call me Priest Mite, I am an Intermediate Priest of the Life Temple.”
Mi Te interrupted Glory Light’s words, with unmistakable pride on his face.
Intermediate Priest of the Life Temple?
Glory Light immediately remembered the information released on the official website; the Life Goddess was one of the most powerful Deities in Glory, on the same level as the Death God.
She is revered and worshipped by all living things, even Undead Life holds respect for the Life Goddess.
“Priest Mite, you can call me Glory Light.”
“Glory Light? That’s a strange name. Only those of you from another world would use such a name as a moniker.
Young man, can you tell me about the Otherworld you come from?”
Mi Te was especially curious about this because, due to his power, he might never be able to step into another Plane in his lifetime, but that didn’t mean he didn’t yearn for other Planes.
“The world I come from is called Earth…” Glory Light didn’t think much of the other party’s question and directly answered.
But what he didn’t know was that as soon as he opened his mouth, the air fell silent, and no matter what he said, his voice couldn’t be heard by others.
However, in Mi Te’s ears, he heard something different.
“The world I come from is from the Lost Plane…”
But Glory Light was unaware that what he said was different from what Mi Te heard. After babbling on about how hard it was to win the internal test on the official website and how lucky he was, he concluded with “… and then I arrived in Glory.”
Mi Te looked touched. “Young man, I didn’t expect you would be from the Lost Plane; I understand your origin now.
The ancient wars caused many Planes to separate from the Main Plane of Glory. Perhaps the great Life Goddess sensed you needed help, which is why she allowed you to descend into the Main Plane again.”
Glory Light was dumbfounded. What lost plane? I was talking about Earth.
“Priest Mite, I said I’m from Earth.”
Mi Te looked puzzled.
“I know you’re from the Lost Plane.”
“I mean Earth, Earth!!”
“Why so worked up? There’s no shame in coming from the Lost Plane.”
“I…”
Glory Light suddenly came back to his senses, mmp, this must be some trick of the game system.
Even Earth is censored by the game, how extreme.
Well, Lost Plane or not, it doesn’t make a difference.
“Priest Emi, I’m really not interested in learning a new language. Could you teach me how to use this, uh…”
“Second Circle Spell: Language Comprehension.”
“Yes, yes, that’s the one. Can you teach me Language Comprehension?”
Hearing this request, Priest Emi looked somewhat disdainful.
“You need to be a Level 5 Spellcaster to learn Second Circle Spells, Glory Light, you’re just a commoner now and not eligible to learn spells.”
Glory Light’s face looked somewhat displeased.
“Do not worry, when your spell expires, you can come to me,” smiled Priest Mi Te, his expression clean and pure, “Under the Goddess’s crown, the oracle has commanded us to help you as much as possible.”
“And what about after that month?” Glory Light sharply caught the time frame mentioned.
“After one month, each casting will require a silver puck.”
Glory Light was stunned for a moment. The official website provided an explanation of the exchange rates for gold pucks, silver pucks, and copper pucks, but he didn’t know whether the value of a silver puck was considered high or low.
“Lord Mi Te, may I ask what I can do to assist you?”
After understanding the other party’s words, Glory Light immediately slipped into player mode.
For a player who wishes to level up, grow stronger and earn money, what could be faster than taking on a mission?
Mi Te shook his head, “Glory Light, you are too weak, even weaker than an ordinary citizen. Come back when you have become a professional.”
Mi Te’s merciless words left Glory Light slightly embarrassed, but as a player, how could he afford to lose face?
“Lord Mi Te, please help me transform into a Priest. I am willing to become a follower of the Life Goddess…”
However, Mi Te’s words once again made Glory Light feel the hardness of this world.
“No, Glory Light, becoming a Priest requires a talent that I sense you possess for casting spells, but it doesn’t meet the requirements of the Life Temple. You cannot become a Priest.
Perhaps you should look outside, a warrior’s profession may suit you better.”
Upon mentioning the word ‘warrior’, Emi’s face showed a disdain that Glory Light failed to notice.
Those brutish barbarians have always been looked down upon by spellcasters.
I need a talent to become a Priest?? Glory Light deeply felt the malice of this world.
Isn’t Priest a starting profession?
Mage, Priest, Archer, Thief, Warrior… those were the five, weren’t they? Why don’t I qualify??
He wanted to make a retort, but the calmness in Mi Te’s eyes made him abandon the thought.
“Could you give me some advice?”
“Young man, you can find a job outside to support yourself; maybe then, consider becoming a professional.”
Mi Te had not asked for any more valuable information, and by now he had lost interest in this adventurer from the Lost World, waving his hand to shoo him away.
The Lost World is a plane that lost contact with the Main Plane in the ancient wars; though they are called planes, most are weak entities, rarely holding anything of value.
Over the years, many Lost Planes were found, but most were barren. Emi mistook Glory Light’s lack of knowledge as coming from an insignificant plane.
And since Glory Light’s casting talent was poor, it naturally extinguished Mi Te’s interest in further entertaining him.
On hearing Emi’s tone, Glory Light walked out of the church with a sulky expression, and he glanced over his attributes.
Glory Light
Level: 1
Profession: Civilian
Reputation: 0
Skills: None
Status: (Understands Language)
A blank slate in all attributes, whiter than the test papers he handed in during exams.
“That’s it? Not even a tutorial for beginners?”
Stepping out of the splendid Life Temple church, Glory Light wore a blank expression on his face.
Standing in this city, he didn’t even know what to do next.
“MMP, isn’t this too hardcore? Who am I? What am I doing? Where am I going?”
By the time Glory Light stood on the main streets of Green City, the bustling scene made him instantly forget what he was supposed to do next, staring greedily at everything around him.
The city in front of him had a standard Medieval European style, with steeples adorning most buildings, and statues of giant dragons or angels above rooftops, circular stained glass windows below.
The walls lining the streets were mostly painted with colorful, vibrant murals.
It was rich in cultural flavor, something that could only be accumulated over time.
Glory Light’s eyes radiated with intense delight, feeling as if his eyes weren’t enough to take it all in.
On the spacious cobblestone streets, citizens dressed in grey linen moved cautiously, their eyes numb and lifeless, only showing emotion in the presence of Nobles and weapon-laden mercenaries, though it was merely fear.
Warriors decked in grey leather armor swaggered by street corners, heads held high with pride, drawing sidelong glances from the small traders in the shops and passing civilians.
Nobles riding tall horses wore luxurious attire, patterned with various gold and silver threads, partly open sleeves, and cultured neckties exemplifying the depth of Noble heritage.
Each scene was brimming with the charm of the Otherworld.
Under the sun’s radiance, my skin felt a burning sensation, while the distinct sour stench of a sewer pervaded the surroundings…
All these sensations left Glory Light’s expression indescribably thrilled.
“Holy shit, this is what a real virtual game is like! The previous ones were crap, no, this is an entire world!”
After looking around for a good while, Glory Light reluctantly withdrew his gaze, but in a blink of an eye, his complexion soured.
He suddenly remembered that he had no idea what to do now…
This was a completely open-world, and it left him feeling lost, accustomed as he was to games where you’d be bombarded with endless tasks upon logging in.
Just then, the chatter of two civilians in grey tunics, their skin darkened from the sun, reached him.
“Did you hear? The Crimson Mage Tower is recruiting Mage Apprentices again. You thinking of letting your kid try out?”
“Man, I’m jealous. They say you get 20 silver pucks every month just for being a Mage Apprentice…”
The bewildered Glory Light saw a glimmer of hope and approached with a wide smile, interrupting their conversation.
“Excuse me, do you guys know where the Crimson Mage Tower is?”
The two, initially startled by the sudden appearance of Glory Light, quickly wore a smug expression upon seeing that he was just another commoner like themselves.
“A new refugee?”
A refugee? As handsome as I am? Glory Light was furious on the spot, but upon seeing the two, each with arms thicker than his thighs, he decided to let bygones be bygones.
“No, I am an adventurer from another world. Do you two know where to find the Crimson Mage Tower that’s recruiting Mage Apprentices?”
An adventurer from another world?
The two gave a look of disdain.
Doesn’t even know the Crimson Mage Tower? These refugees are getting dumber.
“By the Goddess above, now even refugees dare to call themselves adventurers?
A Level 1 commoner adventurer? Hahaha, that’s really surprising…”
Glory Light, watching the scorn in the two NPCs’ eyes, felt as though he had received a fatal blow.
Believe it or not, on my first day in the game, I was actually mocked by two commoner NPCs!!
“MMP, if I don’t show you the power of a player today, you won’t know how many eyes Lord Ma has!”
In anger, Glory Light charged at the two civilians with a holy assault.
Three minutes later…
“I’m wrong, sirs, please not the face, ah, ah ah, not the face…”
“Stop, stop, I give up, I give up!”
“Dad, I was wrong…”
After being dragged into an alleyway and roughened up, Glory Light finally escaped with his life from the hands of the two bystander NPCs.
Feeling the aches all over his body, Glory Light was overwhelmed with sorrow.
What the hell kind of shitty game is this? I, a noble player, can’t even beat a random NPC.
“Do you see that tower? That’s the Crimson Mage Tower, tsk tsk tsk, lots of Mage Apprentices being recruited there these days, you could let your son try”
“Heh, Jie Li, you don’t know yet, do you? My son was chosen by the Crimson Mage Tower just yesterday…”
“Praise the Goddess, you are really lucky”
Just after crawling out of the alley, Glory Light’s spirit immediately lifted upon hearing the conversation between the two passers-by.
“I must have revenge!! You two damn bastards, I will show you how formidable I am.”
Glory Light suddenly turned his head toward the tower some three blocks away, with crimson walls and a twenty-plus blade tall, pointed-top round tower.
So this is the Crimson Mage Tower that recruits Mage Apprentices?
Priest Emi once said that I have a talent for casting…
Moreover, on the official Glory website, Mage is ranked as the number one profession.
“I will become a mage, I will have my revenge…”
The furious Glory Light, with two panda eyes and wearing tattered linen clothes, headed towards the crimson tower.
Lide had no idea at the time that the arrival of players was not as he had imagined…
The beginning for these dumbasses could be called Hell difficulty.

chapters.title: Chapter 203 - 204: This game is really fun, you can fight NPCs~ (Long Chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 203: Chapter 204: This game is really fun, you can fight NPCs~ (Long Chapter)
“Bro, this is the virtual game we’re talking about? It’s way too realistic, isn’t it??”
“Dude, check out that chick—those legs, that butt, those boobs, I can’t even handle it, hurry, help me get to bed….”
“Skank, get lost, what’s there to see in a bean sprout? Have you seen that noblewoman getting on the carriage? Do you get it??
That’s what I call a real beauty!!”
“Pfft, you know nothing, bro, flat-chested lolis are my true love.”
“Little bro, you’re still young, it’s the mature ladies who are……”
...
On a street near the western edge of Green City, three men, freshly emerged from the Life Goddess’ temple and dressed in grey burlap, lecherously eyed the passing crowd, especially at the sight of young, beautiful women, their eyes practically glowing.
One of them, with a cold expression like a facial paralysis, showed no interest in the others’ conversation.
The one called “Third Brother,” with short hair, spoke arrogantly,
“To think that we, the Hun Yuan Thunderclap Hand Cheng Kun brothers, have ruled the game world for years, and now we have finally experienced such a virtual game in our lifetime.”
After saying this, he stretched out his hand and turned to the other two.
“Shout our slogan!”
The two other players placed their hands over his.
The man with the cold face started, “I, Hun Yuan,”
The second, Third Brother, who liked mature ladies, quickly followed, “I, Thunderclap Hand,”
And the last one, fond of lolis, hurriedly added, “I, Cheng Kun.”
Finally, all three shouted together.
“We, the three brothers—Hun Yuan Thunderclap Hand Cheng Kun, will become the masters of this world, hurrah~”
After that, they looked at each other and smiled, very pleased with their slogan.
“What’s all the noise about? You filthy lowlife refugees, don’t spread your disgusting stench in front of my shop. Get lost!!”
Right after the players shouted their slogan, a fat merchant in a golden robe with a big belly and a long hooked nose burst out from a nearby fruit shop, his chest heaving with anger as he glared at Hun Yuan Thunderclap Hand Cheng Kun.
“You’ve disturbed my business ten times in half a day already, Green City is getting filthier by the day because of refugees like you. I really hope the Death God takes you away soon!”
His roaring voice was like that of a giant dragon, startling the three players.
But the trio quickly got angry.
“Motherfucker, that scared the hell out of me. How dare a petty merchant yell at your dad Hun Yuan?”
“Your grandpa Thunderclap Hand is going to teach you why the flower is so red today~”
“Your ancestor Cheng Kun will teach you a lesson!”
The trio had just come out from the Life Temple, and the effects of the Priest’s language comprehension hadn’t worn off yet.
So although they spoke in Huaxia, outsiders could understand them too, but this immediately ignited the merchant’s rage.
“You damn thieves, filthy robbers, I swear I will have the City Lord’s army throw you in jail!”
How dare a bunch of fleeing refugees shout at him like this? It’s outrageous!!
A sneer appeared on Hun Yuan’s face, “An NPC dares to show off against your gamer daddy?? Even if I get killed today, I’ll let you taste the gamer’s fist of justice.”
Gamers were fearless beings, and as such, they wouldn’t be cowed by an NPC in a game.
Thunderclap Hand and Cheng Kun weren’t about to stand down either, hearing Hun Yuan’s words, they immediately prepared to attack. Especially after seeing on the attribute panel that the merchant in front was just a plain merchant, they were reassured.
Swinging the fist of justice, they charged forward.
The fat merchant’s face changed.
These damned refugees really dared to strike him??
“Stop, you bastards, the Goddess will definitely punish you!”
Hun Yuan Thunderclap Hand Cheng Kun brothers were much more imposing than the previous Glory Light.
With their numbers and the fat merchant’s lack of combat prowess, he was instantly knocked to the ground.
“Watch grandpa perform the Monkey Steals The Peach!”
“Awoo~”
“The Millennium Kill!”
“AAAAAH!”
“Catch… ptooey, Dragon Claw Hand!”
“Wooo~~”
The severely beaten fat merchant experienced a bizarre array of techniques that made him start questioning his life.
After dealing with the merchant, the siblings looked at the unguarded shop and smirked.
“Second Brother, this jerk is so unreasonable; as messengers of justice, shouldn’t we rob from the rich to give to the poor?”
“Of course, how else can we showcase our strength…”
“Can NPC shops be robbed?”
“Hehe, let’s find out…”
Then, the street-side shop was plundered by the three of them.
For players, it’s just a game, there’s no psychological burden with murder or robbery, would they feel guilty about beating up an NPC?
Don’t even think about it.
So the trio robbed without any pressure, and the chubby merchant could only watch the scene with a face full of mournfulness, cursing these despicable refugees a thousand times in his heart.
Unfortunately, perhaps by coincidence or luck, there were a lot of pedestrians on the surrounding streets at the time, but no matter how much the chubby merchant yelled, no one paid him any attention; even the civilians who saw the scene quickened their pace and left.
Joking aside, this place is right next to the west district.
Daring to rob in broad daylight in front of everyone, this group was clearly not to be trifled with, if they got involved, someone might get killed.
These civilians had long found their own way of survival in the chaotic security environment, and those who were bold and reckless had already met the Death God.
In other areas, there might be people with a sense of justice who would take action, but being close to the west district meant that aside from the Green City patrol army, it was hard to encounter so-called righteous people.
Even believers of the Light God and the God of Justice had no thoughts about this forsaken land of sin, let alone other professionals.
“Is it done? This game is really too realistic, not only can you hit NPCs, you can even rob them just like that.
Hahaha, awesome~”
Thunderclap Hand was completely satisfied, the hardcore level of this game was beyond expectation.
What other game lets you beat up an NPC you dislike and rob them too?
This is the real deal virtual game, explosively realistic.
Turning his head to look at the belly-bloated merchant still wailing at the entrance of the fruit shop, Thunderclap Hand, annoyed, stepped forward and gave him another beating.
“Hmph, fatso, let me tell you, today, me, your second brother, and fourth brother robbing you is something you should accept. What we’re doing is robbing the rich to help the poor, doing good deeds, understand??
And some puny merchant NPC daring to scare us, you probably have no idea how renowned Hun Yuan Thunderclap Hand Cheng Kun really is!”
“You damned bastards, are you from an underground force? This place is protected by the Sinking Fog!! You will surely be killed!!”
The belly-bloated merchant, lying on the ground with two panda eyes, shouted furiously.
These three damned refugees, he must have these three jerks hanged, definitely!
What is the Sinking Fog? The three exchanged glances, intrigued by the name.
“Sinking Fog?? What is that, some kind of gang??
Hun Yuan bent down, questioning the swollen-faced, pig-headed merchant.
Hearing this, the chubby merchant grew even angrier.
“You damned refugees, you dare to rob without even knowing the Sinking Fog?!! This is the west district’s strongest of the three major forces, a protected area of the Sinking Fog.
No one can offend the Sinking Fog, you will surely be hanged at the gallows, I swear!!”
Seeing him still daring to threaten them at this moment, Hun Yuan immediately got angry.
“Fuck, what the hell is Sinking Fog, what three major forces!! Brothers, beat him up”
Bang bang bang~
Two players stepped forward and gave him another beating.
As players, although newly arrived, what were they afraid of? Wasn’t it just a robbery, just offending some underground force?
What is there to be afraid of?
After enjoying the beating, the trio immediately took a liking to this feeling.
Fourth brother Cheng Kun hesitantly said, “Second brother, third brother, are we still going to find NPCs to change professions or do quests? I feel… joining an underground gang and doing some robbery seems more thrilling.”
Players basically have no psychological burden, these guys are just here to play, whatever is fun is the way to go, as for good or evil, these rookie players who just arrived in Glory are not aware of it yet.
Hun Yuan showed approval on his face, “Not bad, definitely possible”
After finishing his words, he touched a large number of copper pucks in his pocket, still fixated on the chubby merchant.
Robbing is much faster than doing quests to make money.
Thunderclap Hand nodded vehemently, “I agree with this”
“So which gang shall we join?”
After Cheng Kun spoke, the three simultaneously turned their heads toward the chubby merchant.
“Tell us!!”
At this moment, the big-bellied merchant wanted to cry but had no tears, he really wanted to stand up and curse.
You beat me up that’s fine, you rob me, that’s fine, but now you even want me to guide you in the direction of your future development.
Isn’t this bullying too much?
But after being beaten up by the players’ iron fists, the chubby merchant also came to a realization.
These lowly refugees, though despicable, the merchant needed to measure the timing, knowing when to retreat and when to ruthlessly fleece the customers, this was the divine revelation taught by the great Goddess of Wealth.
He immediately spoke.
“Underworld of Green City has three major forces, Dark Contract, Demon Heart, Sinking Fog”
The chubby merchant’s eyes roamed wildly, quickly regaining his mercantile demeanor, “Three handsome and great dragon slayer heroes, perhaps you could join the Sinking Mist. Here, you can receive the best training.”
Upon finishing, he looked at the three eagerly, thinking that once they joined the Sinking Mist, he would definitely have fun with these damned refugees!!
He had paid the shelter fee to Sinking Mist for so many years and knew quite a few “big shots”; getting rid of two newcomers would be easy.
Naturally, the three were not so easily fooled.
Their expressions remained calm, “Tell us in detail about these three forces.”
There was some disappointment in the fat merchant’s eyes; however, having adjusted his attitude, he seemed unconcerned about the encounter just now and began to patiently explain.
“Sinking Mist is the most powerful existence among the three forces, commanded by the great fallen knight, Gavin. It’s an unrivaled power.”
The chubby merchant still didn’t give up, continuing to boast, “So joining the Sinking Mist is really the best choice.
The other two powers are many times weaker compared to the Sinking Mist.
Especially the Dark Contract—its president, Viscount Bernard, offended the Protector of Green City, the extraordinary Mage, Lord Rock, and has now vanished without a trace.
Moreover, because of offending Lord Rock, the Dark Contract has been ferociously besieged by the army of Green City in recent times and has suffered substantial losses.
What’s key now is that the Dark Contract has changed to a new president whose strength is unknown—Lord Ilo, who is very mysterious and seems to be a vampire. You might end up as vampire food if you joined…”
All three completely ignored the hidden meaning in the fat merchant’s words, exchanged glances, and felt very excited.
Listen to these titles—
Transcendent, Viscount Bernard, Vampire; very high-end.
They hadn’t expected to encounter such high-level information on their first day in the game, definitely a pleasant surprise.
They were even considering how they were going to boast on the ‘Glory’ forum.
“What about the Dark Contract now? What kind of existence is a Transcendent? And who is this Viscount Bernard?”
Hun Yuan continued to ask with a cold face.
The chubby merchant was frustrated, thinking, Am I supposed to be the boss of the Sinking Mist? How would I know this kind of information?
But seeing the three players with fists as big as sandsacks, he honestly continued.
“The Dark Contract has now become the weakest of the three forces, significantly inferior to the Demon Heart and Sinking Mist.
As for the Transcendent, I can only say that the extraordinary Mage, Lord Rock, is the Protector of our Green City, the only Transcendent existence here. His power is beyond what words can describe.”
“Viscount Bernard was the former president of the Dark Contract. His power is unclear, and since he has offended Lord Rock, he has disappeared without a trace.”
Hearing the fat merchant’s explanation, the three exchanged looks, their faces revealing uncontrollable excitement.
This information was fantastic for them, knowing so much secret intelligence on their first day was exhilarating.
“Second brother, we have to make a few posts when we get out, let that bunch of losers see just how awesome we, the Kun brothers of Hun Yuan Thunderclap Hand, are…”
Hun Yuan nodded, fully agreeing, “Perfect.”
“So, which force do we join? Just like this fatty said, join the Sinking Mist?” Thunderclap Hand hesitated a bit, “I always feel this jerk is up to no good.”
Cheng Kun sneered, “Do we even need to feel it? It’s obvious. Let’s ask about another one, what about Demon Heart? Just its name sounds powerful.”
After discussing, they turned to look at the chubby merchant who had barely managed to sit up.
“What about the Demon Heart?”
Hearing this name, the chubby merchant showed a hint of fear, “Controlled by the Heart-eating Demon, Wales, Demon Heart is the most evil of the three major forces.
It’s because the Heart-eating Demon, Wales, has a half demon bloodline. His favorite thing to do is to dig out the hearts of his defeated enemies and eat them fresh with blood…”
Seeing the panic on the chubby merchant’s face, they felt a bit creeped out too.
“Damn, this game is so real, look at this dead fatty, that kind of fear coming from the heart is really unsettling.”
Cheng Kun, who was the most cowardly among them, felt a chill upon hearing about the deeds of the Heart-eating Demon.
At that moment, Hun Yuan’s eyes sparkled with a hint of coldness as he stared at the chubby merchant, “You’re lying!”
The chubby merchant shook his head crazily, “No, I am not lying, the legend of the Heart-eating Demon, Wales, is well-known throughout the underground world of Green City; you can ask anyone in the western district.”
Hun Yuan shook his head, “No, I’m not talking about the Heart-eating Demon. I mean about the Dark Contract.”
“Dark Contract?” The merchant seemed puzzled, “I swear by the Goddess of Wealth, I haven’t deceived you…”
Thunderclap Hand and Cheng Kun also looked confusedly at Hun Yuan, “Second brother, what’s wrong?”
Hun Yuan scoffed, “According to what this bastard said, the Dark Contract offended the most powerful existence in this city. Logically, it shouldn’t have survived,
but now, the original president of the Dark Contract has disappeared, and this underground force still exists. Doesn’t that strike you as odd?
Normally, in the underworld, once a gang loses a powerful backing, it would be devoured by other forces in no time.
But this one hasn’t, don’t you find that strange?”
Thunderclap Hand and Cheng Kun looked at Hun Yuan with admiration, “Second Brother, are you the legendary domestic 007? Brilliant, truly brilliant!”
The chubby merchant couldn’t understand what the two were talking about, but seeing Hun Yuan’s mocking gaze, he suddenly felt more pain in his body.
“No, I’m not lying, the Dark Contract really lost their president, but during this time, because of the new president’s emergence, the master of Demon Heart, the Heart-eating Demon Wales, acknowledged the status of Dark Contract…
So although the Dark Contract has weakened a lot, it still remains one of the three great forces…”
Hun Yuan’s eyes showed a hint of interest, “So you mean, the problem lies with this new president?”
“Yes, the new president of the Dark Contract, Lord Ilo, is the legendary Vampire, whose strength is immeasurable,” the chubby merchant said with undisguised amazement in his eyes,
“The shocking part is, this Vampire isn’t just the president of the Dark Contract, but also has been invited by Heart-eating Demon Wales to become the vice president of Demon Heart.”
“It’s simply unbelievable, the Dark Contract and the previous Demon Heart were completely enemies; now, Demon Heart is actually letting the president of the Dark Contract serve as their vice president…”
Hearing this, Hun Yuan immediately understood that this new president was even more powerful.
“Second brother, have you figured it out? Which force shall we join?” Thunderclap Hand and Cheng Kun didn’t overthink it, urging Hun Yuan to make a decision.
For them, joining an Underground Force was merely for the convenience of engaging in exciting games like robbery; they didn’t consider much.
After all, in a game, what truly matters is having fun.
“Of course, the Dark Contract,” Hun Yuan was quite rational about this, “Just think about it, the president of Demon Heart is so formidable, holding two positions among the three major forces,
he’s both the president of the Dark Contract and the vice president of Demon Heart, compared to the disgusting Heart-eating Demon Wales, Vampires are much more acceptable.
If we latch onto such a big leg, won’t we be able to fly high in the future?
Let alone robbing an ordinary NPC merchant, wouldn’t we be able to rob anyone we want in this city?
We, Hun Yuan, Thunderclap Hand, and Cheng Kun, will become the new tycoons of the Green City’s Underworld…”
Hun Yuan’s words made Thunderclap Hand and Cheng Kun itch for action; they were college students, and aspiring to be gang leaders in real life would probably be suicidal, even the old lady from the building next door could take care of them.
But it’s different in the game, who hasn’t fantasized about leading underlings to pick up girls and slashing people in the streets, walking down the street majestically with hundreds of underlings?
This game even allows robbing in broad daylight, it’s so realistic; they can certainly live out their fantasies here.
“Let’s go, Hongxing Club opens today~”
“Fatso, do you know how to join the Dark Contract?”
Hearing this, the chubby merchant, with his big belly and wearing a golden robe, cursed these damned jerks in his heart, thinking what they took him for.
“I’m sorry, I…” Just as he was about to refuse, thump~ a sandbag-sized fist slammed down.
Hun Yuan sneered, “What were you saying?”
The merchant’s face trembled, and he quickly spoke, “Great dragon-slaying warriors, I swear to the Goddess of Wealth,
you just need to enter the western district and declare your origin in a crowded tavern, and you might meet someone from the Dark Contract.
I, I am just a merchant, I don’t know much, I really am just a merchant… sob sob… I’m a merchant… sob sob.”
By the end of it, the chubby merchant felt greatly wronged and couldn’t help bursting into loud crying, his voice filled with tears and his appearance sad; even the crowd pretending not to see couldn’t help but sneak a few peeks.
He swore, he only wanted to drive away those noisy guys next to his shop, but unexpectedly… sob sob, he was so miserable.
Hun Yuan, Thunderclap Hand, and Cheng Kun exchanged awkward glances.
Sweating internally.
MMP, you might not believe it if we didn’t say, but on our first day in the game, we robbed a roadside NPC merchant and even made him cry…
This game is just too damn fun…
“Alright, alright, we’ll let you go this time. Stop crying.”
Cheng Kun threatened awkwardly, and under the imposing presence of the three, the chubby merchant immediately choked back his tears, looking at them with red eyes, pitifully helpless.
“You’re an adult, acting like a child, isn’t this embarrassing?
It’s just a beating, right? You’re an NPC, what are you crying for? No more crying in the future.”
Thunderclap Hand stood up and intervened, speaking earnestly to the merchant,
“You need to be stronger, life is tough, but the future is bright, promising, and splendid. We have to believe in the college entrance examination… ah, I mean, we have to believe it’s possible…”
The merchant looked confused, “Possible what?”
Thunderclap Hand’s face stiffened, “Hmm, possible, possible, just possible, what does it matter?”
The merchant ended up swallowing his words, “Oh.”
Seeing this, Thunderclap Hand turned to Hun Yuan, looking smug, “Second brother, I’ve educated him, I believe he won’t dare next time, right, fatty?”
The chubby merchant almost cried again, now only praying for these jerks to leave his shop, he could only nod fiercely.
“See that, second brother?! That’s the power of knowledge.”
Hun Yuan ignored him, turning to glance at the street where people continually passed but nobody ever stopped or came in to help the merchant; his eyes reflected thoughtfulness.
“It seems the public order in the west side of Green City is even worse than I thought. We’ve been robbing for so long and no one has come to stop us, and there’s not even a patrolling officer… this is really shocking.”,
Cheng Kun asked curiously, “What does this indicate?”
Hun Yuan’s expression remained as stoic as ever, “It indicates chaos, it shows that this kind of thing is very common, it indicates that the patrolling force in Green City is very weak,
and it also indicates that we don’t need to worry too much about robbing other places in the future. This will be our paradise.
Let’s go join the Dark Contract and become professionals.
We, Hun Yuan, Thunderclap Hand, and Cheng Kun, will definitely become the gang leaders, ruling the entire Underground Force of Green City…”
He turned around after speaking, taking the dozen silver pucks and hundreds of copper pucks they had robbed from the chubby merchant and headed toward the western district.
The arrival of players melds into Glory gradually and silently, some choosing light, others darkness.
What happens next, remains a mystery.

chapters.title: Chapter 204 - 205: Hardcore Game, Players Making a Scene
chapters.content:
Chapter 204: Chapter 205: Hardcore Game, Players Making a Scene
Lide, after hearing the system prompt, didn’t return to Earth immediately; instead, he sorted out the affairs of the Mage Tower before declaring his seclusion.
His calm and composed approach was a stark contrast to the worries players had when he first entered “Glory.”
People do grow over time.
Now, Lide had transformed from a newbie vampire into a dark boss who spanned both legal and illegal spheres, commanding five top-tier level 15 combat forces, controlling a city, and ruling over an Upper Race.
His policies could change countless people’s fates, and his will was enough to make the dark giants who intimidated half of Green City shudder.
His strength provided him ample confidence to face future crises.
...
Moreover, the arrival of players might not be a bad thing for Lide, who was already accustomed to the workings of this world.
In the world of “Glory,” no one understood better that players were creatures who cause trouble—if there’s nothing to cause, they’ll find something.
Dealing with these guys wasn’t difficult at all; a little temptation, and they were more active than anyone else.
Even something as absurd as vampires coexisting peacefully with humans had occurred, so what couldn’t happen?
Lide’s lips curved into a smile, seemingly visualizing the scene where players, eager to learn the Small Fireball Technique, hustled to gather magic materials for the Crimson Mage Tower.
After the closed beta, the Crimson Mage Tower might not avoid players.
However, as his position rose higher and he accessed more information, Lide grew more confident.
In the future, it might not be impossible to make players an affiliate force of the Crimson Mage Tower—only if he dared, even the goddess would have to take maternity leave.
As for Dawn City, his true foundation, he had no immediate plans of opening it, and he wouldn’t allow players into this personally-owned city for a long time to come.
Having briefed Emi and Harrison about certain matters, Lide returned to Earth.
When the handsome, elegant, and nobly classic Lide opened his eyes from his bed,
the super handsome guy had returned.
Standing up, his deep dark gaze seemed like a sea of stars floating and sinking, and the aura of a superior cultivated over many months exuded a scent that quickened the opposite sex’s breath.
Anyone arriving at that moment would be amazed by the handsome young man’s aura.
Unfortunately, no one could appreciate this scene.
Sitting at his computer desk, Lide opened the official forum of “Glory” and saw the bustling activity.
The forum on the official website was nearly boiling over, with players frantically posting after the closed beta.
At this moment, dozens of posts were being refreshed every second, an enthusiasm hard to imagine in a game that had just undergone closed beta.
However, the reality was just as such, with the online closed beta causing an unimaginable stir following offline previews.
Moreover, “Glory” surprised everyone; many players were captivated at first sight by the vast, spectacular world.
No one expected the game to feel this real, every flower and brick,
the fresh air and the foul stench of the sewers, each NPC’s expressions and reactions—it seemed just like a real world.
Few players could resist such an authentic otherworldly journey.
Of course, along with the praise came countless complaints because the hardcore level of “Glory” also exceeded everyone’s expectations.
During the offline experience, players only enjoyed the fun of the game, but now they were deeply psychologically struck.
On the official forum, a post with up to 100,000 replies was pinned at the top, and the title of the post was,
“Everyone Has a Duty to Kill the Dog Planner.”
Lide clicked in with some curiosity and almost spluttered with laughter.
Don’t worry, no one’s saying, “What kind of trash game is this? I want to protest; I want to report; how could this game even launch???
First, let me talk about my experience. I was born in a city called Corner City in the Storm Sea Domain, and then—here comes the main point—I couldn’t understand what the NPCs were saying??
What the heck?? As a gamer, I couldn’t understand the game NPCs’ speech?
I thought there would be a solution to this issue, but no, there truly wasn’t.
That NPC priest somehow let me know one piece of information, that communication required the “Language Comprehension” magic… then the critical part, I thought the priest would give me its use, but he actually said he didn’t know it!!
You heard right, the priest didn’t know it! He said his talent wasn’t enough, and he couldn’t learn the spell!!
That really shocked my neighbor’s little goldfish!
What then? Then I damn just wandered around Corner City not understanding anything.
In such a big city, I was alone and utterly isolated…
I swear, this was the most helpless moment of my life.
No newbie guide, no quest pointers, no newbie village, no acquaintances, not even a common language.
Standing in the middle of the street, I had no idea what to do…
I wanted to take quests, but I couldn’t understand a word, and it was a completely unfamiliar language system. I had no idea what they were saying.
But that’s not even the main point; the key point is still to come.
At that time, two NPCs approached me, and although I couldn’t understand what they were saying, their expressions made me think I had come across some nice people with a mission, so I followed them.
But to my surprise, these damn NPCs were slave merchants! Yes, slave traders who buy and sell people!!
I, a player, a proud player, was actually kidnapped by two NPCs!! Ahhh, damn the planners!!
What’s even more infuriating is that less than an hour after being kidnapped, I was sold to a fat noble old woman.
Yes, just as you imagined, that old noblewoman wanted to do something to me… and right in front of the slave merchants.
If I hadn’t reacted quickly and smashed my head into a pillar, I might have already…
And then, when I died and tried to log back into the game to get my revenge, I found out I had to wait 24 hours before I could log in again!!
Damn it, I can’t contain my raging fury anymore.
Damn game planners, do you dare to come out?? If I don’t beat you up today and make you call me grandpa, I’d be living in vain.
How does this kind of game even qualify to be online? I demand immediate rectification, to give us players a clear sky!”
This accusation indeed makes the viewers weep and the listeners feel heartbroken.
Lide recalled when he became the Ancestor of the Bloodline, and fortunately, he had inherited the memory of the Blood Clan Ancestor, otherwise, the language barrier alone would have been a huge headache for him.
But what he didn’t expect was that the “Glory” game mechanic hadn’t been changed, and these players felt the harshness of the real world right from their first step.
As for being tricked by slave merchants, and nearly being subjected to that, he couldn’t help but laugh, what a rare gem.
However, such incidents seem not to be unusual in “Glory.” If he dared to go to the west area of Green City, the chances of being offered as a sacrifice at the Evil God Altar are not slim.
These NPCs don’t care if you’re a player or not, encountering the evil camp, anything could happen.
And the comments below were all complaints and jokes.
“I thought I was the only one experiencing this? Damn, the language barrier is insane, I don’t even know how to start conversing with a noble young lady…”
“Hahaha, the original poster is ruthless,”
“After reading about the original poster’s experiences, I actually feel a bit envious…”
“Strongly demanding to sacrifice the damn planners to the heavens, a good game is being ruined by these lousy planners.”
“I offer 5000RMB to buy a beta access account, if the original poster doesn’t want to play anymore, contact me.”
“Internal game guide, teaching you how to change professions to a hidden profession, if interested, contact me, qq34…”
“Seeking guides, I can’t do it anymore, I want to be kidnapped by slave merchants, I want to enjoy the abuse by a noble rich widow…”
Lide found these remarks quite entertaining; foolish players are always a source of joy.
However, in other posts, Lide also discovered many interesting things.
Especially a post titled “Discussing the Various Professions in Glory” caught Lide’s attention.
Broken Sword the Knight: Hello everyone, the handsome and dashing me is back~
I happened to draw a trial spot, and today I officially joined “Glory.”
For those who didn’t get the spot, I know you are very curious about the real world of “Glory,” let me briefly explain it to you.
Honestly, without exaggeration or bias, “Glory” is a masterpiece among virtual games, currently, there’s no other virtual MMO that can compare to “Glory.”
None!!
This isn’t bragging, but a practical inference by yours truly.
First, let’s talk about the realism in “Glory,” which is the lifeline of all virtual MMOs.
Some claim to be virtual games, but their idea of a virtual game is only limited to visuals and sensations; they have no clue what a real world is like.
But Glory is different. In “Glory,” I can smell the fragrance of flowers in the air, the stench from sewers, feel the warmth of the sun on my skin, and so much more.
In “Glory,” the level of realism I experienced is indistinguishable from reality.
This is something other so-called virtual games cannot match.
Of course, what I want to talk about today are not just these, but the professions in “Glory.”
Everyone knows that “Glory” is set in a medieval world with divine beings and countless races.
Currently, only the human race has been made available, and it is yet unknown whether a second race will be opened later.
Players can currently choose from five initial professions: Mage, Archer, Priest, Rogue, warrior.
Among these, the Mage has the highest difficulty, and the warrior has the lowest.
I was born in the Royal Capital of the Nolan Empire, one of the twelve human kingdoms and met a very powerful Priest in the Life Temple of the Royal Capital.
He was so powerful that I couldn’t even discern his level.
As for which profession I would change to, I had already made up my mind, but still, I asked the old priest if I could change my profession to be a Priest of the Life Temple.
The Priest surprised me with his words.
He said although I have a kind heart, I lack the Casting Talent to become a Priest; however, seeing my kindness, he could introduce me to become a Knight of the Life Temple.
He said Knight, but according to my deduction, it also falls under the category of the warrior profession.
This conversation provided me with a new hypothesis about “Glory.”
The initial professions weren’t something every player could choose.
It seemed players were born with hidden attribute points, which determined whether they could switch into a specific profession.
For example, in the game “Glory” as described on the official website, mages were the most powerful but also the most difficult; I predicted they would have the smallest number.
That’s why there were cases where players couldn’t switch professions, although this might be due to my low level; perhaps there were more opportunities later, but this would need verification.
And after reading many player posts, I confirmed this point.
Most people who wanted to become priests were declined, and probably only three to five in a hundred could succeed. The odds were incredibly low.
Warriors, on the other hand, because of the lower difficulty and talent requirements, most players who couldn’t become spellcasters were recommended to switch to warriors.
Hence, I inferred that future career switches would be the same. Becoming a mage would be incredibly hard, whereas becoming a warrior would be quite simple.
So here’s a piece of advice for everyone—if you can switch to a magic profession, do so, as the rarer something is, the more precious it should be.
Regarding archers and thieves, I haven’t delved deep, but based on the information from the official site, though easier than spellcasters, it’s definitely harder than warriors.
So, players considering these two professions need to think carefully.
Especially for archers, given the realism of this game, it’s quite possible you would actually have to practice archery, so if you don’t have the talent, perhaps steer clear.
That is my shallow view on the professions in “Glory,” which can serve as a preliminary reference for everyone, to be updated as we discover more.
The comments below too were quite animated.
“Knight, you’re seriously divine, a real tech wizard. I always love reading your guides.”
“Incredible, how can you deduce so much from so little information? Why is it only you using your brain so effectively?”
“Knight, have you switched professions yet? How can you switch?”
“Too real, my friend and I entered the game together, I became a priest but that guy was kicked out, saying he didn’t have the talent to be a spellcaster.”
“…”
Lide thought the ID ‘Broken Sword Knight’ looked familiar; it appeared this same guy had earlier posted about the divine rights and royal powers, noting how naturally priests belonged to the divine camp, which had caught his eye.
He silently followed Broken Sword Knight.
Although the words of Broken Sword Knight made sense, Lide keenly felt that perhaps the truth wasn’t so simple.
Spellcasters were recognized as rare in Glory, and thus held a far higher status than their equivalent-level professionals.
In Green City, there might be seven or eight hundred advanced level warriors and thieves.
But there were only about twenty advanced mages, even counting those hidden within the underground forces, no more than forty.
The numbers simply were not comparable.
The reason was due to the high talent requirements for spellcasters.
Players might not be unable to become spellcasters due to hidden system attributes, but rather because these players inherently lacked the casting talent.
Although this was just an uncertain deduction, Lide felt it was highly likely to be the case.
This caused him to change some of his views and secretly, he breathed a sigh of relief.
It seemed like players could not escape the rules of Glory; if they wanted to rampage and conquer as in other games, they could only dream of doing so in the foreseeable future.
Lide wasn’t clear about how extensive the world of Glory was, he only knew there were twelve human empires, and these empires managed only half of the land on the main plane of Glory, the rest occupied by obscure small nations, races, and unknown forces.
Thus, the 100,000 players in beta testing were merely a drop in this vast ocean, hardly causing a ripple.
Although players’ ability to continually respawn guaranteed they would eventually grow stronger, there wasn’t an immediate concern.
Lide browsed the forum a while longer before losing interest.
At this stage, players were still exploring the entirety of Glory, making it hard to encounter any useful information.
However, the overly hardcore nature of “Glory” directly sparked a massive protest among the players, even causing quite a stir online.
It reached the trending headlines across major media.
Countless players who didn’t draw beta test slots demanded that “Glory” open up test slots, and the ones who had gotten slots demanded the official platform add beginner missions and eliminate the hardcore language barrier.
If not changed, they threatened to cease playing.
Some even organized a boycott alliance to force the official website to alter the game mode.
For a time, the fighting spirit erupting from players was astonishing.
But to everyone’s frustration, the “Glory” official site simply ignored these issues, not even bothering to reply to the statements.
Despite the clamor and many posts by players, nobody took notice.
It was not until later that a brief announcement was randomly made on the official site, the content as hardcore as the game itself.
Glory is an extremely realistic world, please do not attempt to apply behaviors from other games to this world.
Here you can experience complete realism.
If you do not want to continue the game experience, please contact us to delete your account, and we will distribute it to other players who need it.
This official statement literally made a group of protesting players furious to the point of vomiting blood, and indeed, thousands of players, out of anger, chose to delete their accounts.
However, these cancelled accounts were snapped up by other players vying for spots within a matter of seconds.
It hardly had any impact on the game.
For a moment, those who cancelled their accounts cursed “Glory” officials as overbearing and unreasonable, while those who managed to snatch the accounts praised the officials as wise. The official website forum witnessed a fierce battle.
However, due to Glory’s firm stance, players truly recognized the uniqueness of this game, and as their experience deepened, they began to immerse themselves in this vast world.
A game can eventually become tiresome, but a world with hundreds of millions of years of history and enthralling content offers a charm that ordinary players cannot resist.
Especially when players discovered that they could really do anything in “Glory,” they went crazy.
The posts on the forum were constantly erupting.
“Is there anyone who wants to team up to learn the common language of Glory? Let’s form a Glory language study group.”
“The shocking historical depth, I actually found ancient Elf books in the church from millions of years ago, and the text truly recorded a real epic story, this game is freaking awesome.”
“Holy shit, I actually saw racy knight novels inside, it was quite an eye-opener, the officials of ‘Glory’ actually indulged in explicit content.”
“Help, I was sold to a tavern, and today I have to serve customers involuntarily, what should I do, who can save me.”
“I’m a fan of Yong Chun and Baji Fist. Surprisingly, I was taken as a disciple by a Level 10 warrior because of this. Here’s a secret, martial arts from the real world can also be used in ‘Glory.’ I need to go learn the warrior’s secret skills from my teacher now.”
Players initially found the game incredibly challenging, couldn’t communicate due to the language barrier, didn’t know what tasks to perform, and didn’t know what to do.
But as time went by, players gradually became familiar with their birth environments and immediately started integrating, relying on their shameless audacity and fearlessness, and slowly became a part of Glory.
This vast and exciting world immediately addicted the players.
However, what was most criticized were a few points, with the top one being the language barrier.
This was just too hardcore; it made countless players jump and curse, as players all started from the Life Temple, where some could be spellcasted for free, yet some priests still didn’t master this Second Circle Magic of language understanding.
This made many players extremely angry.
But the “Glory” officials simply didn’t care, too lazy to respond to the player’s criticisms.
Ultimately, players stumbled along for a long time and finally managed to learn some basic conversation, many felt they hadn’t been this serious and hardworking even during their college entrance exams.
Second, the death penalties were extremely harsh, with each death resulting in a loss of 20% of total experience, and a 24-hour cooldown was required before re-entering the game.
Moreover, one could not die more than five times within a month; otherwise, each death would incur a 72-hour death penalty, necessitating a three-day wait before re-entering the game.
It could be said that this death penalty in “Glory” directly hit the players’ Achilles’ heel, immediately making the players, who originally thought they could respawn infinitely, become extremely cautious.
This measure also provoked a unanimous outcry from all players.
Losing 20% of total experience per death was just too excessive. If the level was high, one death could cause a downgrade, which was unbearable.
Moreover, the cooldown time for death was also terribly long, having to wait until the next day to re-enter, which was just preposterous.
But “Glory,” as always, remained firm, indicating that because “Glory” is an extremely realistic world, too many and too frequent deaths could cause physical harm, so to avoid injury, it was necessary to limit the number of player deaths.
They wanted players to treasure their lives in “Glory” and not waste them frivolously.
Players were very dissatisfied with this explanation, but “Glory” didn’t bargain with them. They simply announced that if players were dissatisfied, they could delete their accounts.
As a result, a group of players were gnashing their teeth in irritation yet also exclaimed how irresistibly good the game was as they immersed themselves in “Glory.”
“Glory” had a great deterrent effect initially, but once familiar, it made people helpless to do anything but become addicted.
So although the call for boycott was loud, very few actually quit.
Not only that, but as players delved deeper into understanding “Glory,” more and more game screenshots were leaked,
“Glory’s” vibrant and vast worldview, extremely realistic characters and environment, and various unrestricted behavioral patterns, even hardcore ones like unrestricted sexual content.
This made the entire gaming community boil over.
Everyone who had offline experiences felt that this game was extraordinary, but no one could have imagined “Glory” would be so intense that it drove players crazy.
However, the pathetic 100,000 beta test slots, in the face of numerous players, were like drops in the ocean, barely making a ripple.
The beta test qualifications were also heatedly speculated upon, with wealthy tycoons even offering up to one hundred thousand for one.
Lide stayed on Earth for two days and even specifically went to an offline experience spot to ask some game-related questions to the girl who had added him on WeChat before.
But he didn’t get much news about “Glory”; instead, the girl, who was both attractive in figure and appearance, was utterly captivated as she looked at his handsome, charming face.
Especially his noble demeanor left the girl almost mesmerized, she even wanted to come to his house at eleven o’clock at night to see if the plain water he boiled tasted better.
Lide naturally refused righteously, saying, “I just wanted to inquire about the game, and you wanted to sleep with me.”
Only leaving a disappointed girl, who watched his impressive figure disappear into the distance, and even secretly sighed in her heart at the end,
“No wonder he’s the god I’ve chosen, even his silhouette is so handsome…”
Although “Glory” opened the beta testing channel, it did not disclose more useful news.
Disappointed, Lide returned to Dawn City.
By then, two days had elapsed since he had left Dawn City, which was already a week ago.

chapters.title: Chapter 205: 206: The Powerful Life Undergoing Transformation (Long Chapter, Extra Update)
chapters.content:
Chapter 205: Chapter 206: The Powerful Life Undergoing Transformation (Long Chapter, Extra Update)
A week passed, and Dawn City had not undergone many changes.
The waves of Earth players had not impacted the city hidden deep within the Far Mountain Range.
In the Dawn Mage Tower, as soon as Lide stepped out of his room, Emi immediately received news and rushed over.
First-floor hall.
“Good morning, Ancestor Crown,” Lide said with a nod after glancing at the bright window.
“Good morning, Emi.
...
How has Dawn City been these past few days, anything special happened?
Have there been any strangers speaking incomprehensible languages arriving in Dawn City?”
Although he had learned from forums that the player’s birthplace was at the Life Temple, Lide could not guarantee everyone was the same.
Dawn City also had temples, and although the Dawn Sect was his own sect, the appearance of players was not an impossibility.
Emi shook her head with a somewhat puzzled expression.
“Ancestor Crown, situated deep within the Far Mountain Range, it’s impossible for strangers to suddenly appear without our notice.
Moreover, we’ve already mobilized all citizens so if any strangers or criminal acts occur they will immediately report them.”
Lide smiled slightly upon hearing this.
Great people had said to surround the enemy with a vast ocean of people, and Lide highly approved of this powerful strategic thought, getting Harrison to implement this idea.
The City Hall had a rule, once something resembling the former Wolf Gang, or any other form of crime was reported to the Security Team, a gold puck reward could be obtained.
If the merits were significant, one might even obtain the most precious credits of Dawn City.
Therefore, it was nearly impossible for a stranger or a criminal to hide in Dawn City, unless they were unseen.
Otherwise, once anything was amiss, the citizens would be more than willing to report to the City Hall in exchange for precious credits.
“Mm, closely monitor this matter during this period, whether it’s the Mage Tower or elsewhere, as soon as someone speaking strange words or with behavior that doesn’t fit with the ordinary citizens appears, immediately notify the Security Team and report to me.”
Although Emi found Lide’s order somewhat strange, she still immediately nodded respectfully upon seeing his stern gaze.
“Yes, Your Crown.”
Whether Lide’s decision was justifiable or not, everyone must execute it unconditionally with no excuses.
After chatting for a while more, Harrison, who had been working in the Dawn Mage Tower for the past few days, also arrived.
“Good morning, Clan Leader.”
“Harrison, how is the harvest going?” The grain harvest had already begun when he left Dawn City.
In Lide’s heart, the issue of food was absolutely more critical at this point in time than the players.
“Clan Leader, we have harvested eighty percent of the grain in these few days, and after magical processing, it has all been placed into the granary,” Harrison reported.
Lide nodded with satisfaction. Grain represented the future development foundation of Dawn City, and hearing this news, he could not help but feel delighted.
“Has all the grain been taken to the storeroom? Have any residents kept the grain for themselves?”
Harrison shook his head, “According to City Hall regulations, besides the thirty percent tax owed, residents can also keep twenty percent of the grain. The rest must be sold to City Hall.”
Lide nodded, curious.
“Has anyone objected to this?”
Harrison’s expression turned odd as he shook his head, “Clan Leader, the land itself is provided to them for cultivation at no cost, so what could these commoners possibly object to?
Moreover, all the grain is purchased at four copper pucks per pound, and we only sell it for three copper pucks per pound.”
For the stability of the current phase, Lide had also subsidized the price of grain, which is why the selling price was lower than the purchase price.
For him, who now owned the Magic Factory — a gold puck generating machine, these little sums of money were no longer of any concern.
And as the old saying goes, take from the people to use for the people. Once these lambs have been fattened, skimming off the top was just a word away for him.
“Very good, ensure all the grain is controlled by City Hall, strictly forbid anyone from trading grain in the market.”
Lide reiterated, considering grain as strategic material, he would not allow free trading of grain among residents without sufficient reserves.
“Notify the Security Team, if any outsiders or strange faces not belonging to Dawn City are discovered, they must inform me immediately.”
He repeated the instructions given to Emi to Harrison; the matter of the players could not be taken lightly.
“Yes, Clan Leader.”
Harrison nodded solemnly, then as if recalling something, he hesitated.
“Clan Leader, the Magic Language Bats have recently shown some different changes…”
Lide’s heart skipped a beat upon hearing this, “Explain in detail.”
The Magic Language Bats were currently the most important productivity force of Dawn City and irreplaceable in the short term.
Should there be issues with this key point, it would be a huge setback for his plans.
Harrison shook his head, “Clan Leader, it’s not that the entire clan has problems; it’s one specific group — to be precise… one Magic Bat seems to be undergoing a transformation.”
Lide was startled, “Undergoing a transformation??”
Magic Language Bats were a unique Demon Beast of the Bloodline, only the Bloodline race, and no other, could breed them.
The entire Magic Language Bat Clan was bred from ordinary small bats, only after activating their hidden bloodline with the Bloodline’s blood could they become Magic Language Bats.
But this was the first time Lide had heard of the possibility of a Magic Language Bat undergoing a transformation.
Magic Language Bats have an initial Level of 5, a Mature Body at Level 7, an Elite Body at Level 9, and the most exceptional might break through Level 10, but that would be their limit.
Transformation is not a term to be used lightly; it isn’t simply about progressing from Level 9 to Level 10 — that’s just a normal upgrade.
Judging by Harrison’s expression, Lide keenly felt that this was no simple matter.
“Explain in detail.”
“Yes, Clan Leader.
Five days ago, as usual, the Giant Valley was mining ore veins when Lord Kolong was excavating a new tunnel.
At that time, the Magic Language Bat responsible for transporting the ore was carrying the ore Kolong had mined.”
Just when it happened, the newly opened mining tunnel collapsed for some unknown reason.
Lord Kachar couldn’t escape in time; a sharp stalactite pierced through his arm, and at the same time, a Magic Language Bat behind him was also pierced by the stalactite.”
Lide frowned, collapses in the mine had happened many times before.
One-eyed Giants had extremely large bodies; ordinary mining tunnels simply couldn’t accommodate them. Moreover, these big guys mined violently, rarely taking other factors into account, so collapses were common.
However, this group, possessing the Ancient Bloodline, was tough and hardy; even when the tunnels collapsed, it was difficult for them to get injured.
Harrison had reported to Lide a few times before. Initially, Lide was somewhat anxious, but after learning about the One-eyed Giants’ strength, he stopped holding regular meetings.
“And then?” Lide asked.
Harrison had a very strange expression.
“Magic Language Bats can recover from their injuries by consuming the fresh blood of other creatures.
The injured Kachar’s blood gushed out. Coincidentally, the Magic Language Bat behind him was also severely injured. Drenched in Kachar’s blood, at the same time…”
Lide nodded in realization, without needing to say it, he knew what had happened; not only had the Magic Language Bat bathed in the blood of the Bronze One-eyed Giant Kachar while seriously wounded, but it had also gorged itself on his blood.
The blood of high-level beings contained tremendous energy, and Kachar, who activated the Ancient Giant Bloodline and evolved into a Bronze One-eyed Giant, Lide estimated that even if there was a gap with giant dragons, it couldn’t be too much.
Especially since Kachar’s wounds from the recent trauma had already recovered, and the Bronze One-eyed Giant Bloodline was being tapped for greater potential.
For a low-level Magic Language Bat to undergo transformation after consuming such ancient lifeblood, it wasn’t inexplicable.
“How is that Magic Language Bat doing now?”
“Clan Leader, for the past five days the Magic Language Bat has been in a deep slumber, transforming, but the process is extremely slow. It seems to lack the crucial power. The Magic Language Bat’s transformation has now stalled…
According to Dylan’s speculation, if it cannot complete the transformation within three days, it’s highly likely that the Magic Language Bat will succumb to death.”
Lide looked somewhat displeased, “Has Magic Blood been fed to the Magic Language Bat?”
“It has been fed, and in no small amount.
While it did ease the Magic Language Bat’s condition to some extent, it still wasn’t much help. It seems that the problem isn’t a lack of energy.”
Lide was puzzled; normally, an unsuccessful transformation indicated a lack of energy. In the past, Emi and Grotto were like this, but they were fine after receiving a substantial amount of Magic Blood.
So why isn’t it working on the Magic Language Bat now?
“Take me to see it.”
Into what kind of creature could the Magic Language Bat, tainted with the blood of a Bronze One-eyed Giant, transform?
A One-eyed Bat? Giant Bat? Bat Giant?
Now that’s interesting, Lide thought to himself, amusingly, it seemed the gamers had influenced him too.
“Yes, Clan Leader.”
Harrison and Emi led the way, with Lide following the two out of the Mage Tower.
At the same time, his curiosity about this Bronze One-eyed Giant-blood imbued Magic Language Bat grew tremendously.
He had a vague feeling that this Magic Language Bat’s transformation was no simple matter.
The Magic Language Bat Cave was located on the mountainside east of Dawn City, very close to the holy land where Holy Spirits were kept.
On a prominent green stone platform with a length and width of two hundred blades, covered with claw marks, Lide looked at the Magic Language Bat curled up in the middle of the platform, frowning deeply.
Emi, Harrison, and Dylan were all following behind him.
“Clan Leader, this is the Magic Language Bat that sucked the blood of Koso,” Dylan’s burly figure seemed very oppressive.
“We have not been able to wake it since we transported it back from Giant Valley.”
Lide nodded, “Is Koso alright?”
“Koso recovered the second day and is now back mining in the valley.”
Lide couldn’t help but laugh and cry; the One-eyed Giants were already tough and enduring, but after evolving into a Bronze One-eyed Giant, Koso’s physique became even more monstrous.
To sustain such severe injuries and be able to mine the next day, these One-eyed Giants truly were an excellent labor force.
He then opened the Magic Language Bat’s attribute panel with some anticipation.
Magic Language Bat (In Transformation)
Transformation Species: Unknown, Current Transformation Degree: 32%
Current Status: In Transformation.
Success Rate: 1%
Seeing this status, Lide could not help but frown and turned to glance at another Magic Language Bat not far away, opening its attribute panel.
Magic Language Bat
Level: 7
Talent Skills:
[Frenzy: Will become enraged when injured, significantly increasing strength and becoming fearless of pain]
[Blood Rebirth: Devouring blood will quickly heal wounds on the body.]
[Super Strong Physique: Giant bats specially trained have extremely strong bodies]
[Sonic Wave: Giant bats can emit unique sound waves to locate positions and can also be converted into Spirit Magic – Constantly at Three Circle Magic: Spirit Shock]
Explanation: Giant bats bred by the Bloodline using special methods, possessing immense strength and extremely fast flying speed, can release spirit attacks, exclusive Demon Beasts of the Bloodline.
The attributes of the Magic Language Bat were very outstanding, although it was suppressed during the previous sniping of Stanley, Kolong, and Grote from the Late Bell Church.
That was because the power of the opponents was entirely beyond what the Magic Language Bat could handle, but among equals, the Magic Language Bat was not inferior to ordinary combatants.
Now the Magic Language Bat in transformation made Lide feel somewhat thorny; there was no indication in the bat’s status of why it had not successfully transformed.
Moreover, the rate of successful transformation was only 1%, which meant there was a 99% chance of failure.
Wasn’t this basically declaring the Magic Language Bat’s failure?
“Emi, do you have any ideas?”
Unable to detect the problem, Lide turned his gaze to Emi the blasphemer.
Among the many Level 15 top combatants, although Emi was not the most superior in combat, her experience from many years at the Knight Temple was definitely the broadest.
Emi pondered for a moment before responding with a wry smile,
“Ancestor Crown, I haven’t done much research in this area…”
After a pause, she added, “But I think the transformation of the Magic Language Bat must be due to the lack of some key factors.
And the most likely factor is energy.”
Harrison shook his head, “Marquis Emi, we have already fed them Magic Blood, but no matter how much we feed, the Magic Language Bats show no reaction.
I think what the Magic Language Bats lack is not energy, or rather, even if it is energy, it’s not ordinary energy…”
These words illuminated a spark in Emi’s eyes as she looked eagerly at Lide.
“Ancestor Crown, I once inadvertently entered the Divine Country of the Knight God and saw a few uses of the Power of Faith there.
The Power of Faith was once used by the Knight God to nurture his steeds…
And isn’t the Power of Faith a kind of higher-level energy?”
Their conversation immediately stirred Lide’s interest.
Emi, the blasphemer, was no simpleton; initially, he wanted to research how to become a god!
However, with the establishment of the Dawn Sect, although the Power of Faith grew more abundant, Emi also came to realize how difficult it was to understand the Power of Faith that even researching Legendary Strongmen at level 15 might not grasp.
So he temporarily extinguished the fervent idea of researching how to become a god in his heart.
But he had not forgotten about the Power of Faith; although he no longer fantasized about finding a quick way to divinity, it was still in his mind.
Lide trusted this blasphemer who had once set foot in the Divine Country of the Knight God.
“How did the Knight God do it? Did he directly infuse the Power of Faith into others?”
Emi nodded, “The information I got wasn’t very clear, whether the Knight God used Divine Arts in conjunction, I couldn’t tell.”
He finished with a bitter smile; getting a portion of information about the Divine was already incredibly lucky.
Lide nodded, understandingly, not pressing further.
Looking at the coiled Magic Language Bat before him, he approached directly after a moment’s contemplation.
Without trying, this Magic Language Bat was certainly going to die, what’s the difference between a 99% and 100% failure rate, both result in death.
Plus, the current state of this Magic Language Bat was caused by Koso’s blood, which, to him, were both renewable resources.
Even if this one died, he could let Koso donate some blood and create another one.
To him, as long as it wasn’t non-renewable, it wasn’t a concern.
As the lord of Dawn, the resources he could mobilize were beyond outsiders’ imaginations.
Just as he was about to take action, Lide suddenly remembered that as the Blood Clan Ancestor, the power of his Bloodline was no less than any creature; what if he used his own Bloodline Power on the Magic Language Bat?
Thinking this, excitement flashed in Lide’s eyes; he felt like a child filled with curiosity during a chemistry class.
He stepped forward. The body of the Magic Language Bat was massive, even when coiled on the ground with its wings folded, it still resembled a grey hill.
The Magic Language Bat’s skin lacked fur; under the grey surface, blue veins were visible.
Only on the head did the Magic Language Bat have very short fuzz, with elongated pointed ears, like enlarged Elf Ears.
Being a warm-blooded creature, its body was warm.
The vast wings folded like a cloak, shielding its body, while the sharp barbs on the wings, gleaming with a cold light, could pierce a warrior’s shield.
The grey body exuded a sense of oppression; although Lide had grown accustomed to the size of the Magic Language Bat, standing in front of such a gigantic creature still made him feel exceedingly small.
Shaking his head without further thought, he circled around to the front of the Magic Language Bat’s head.
At the moment, the Magic Language Bat’s head was resting on the ground, with its greyish-white nostrils continuously exhaling hot air.
The beast, which usually resembled a Demon, now seemed almost endearingly clumsy.
Lide reached out, bit his finger to draw blood, then used Mage’s Hand to pry open a gap in the tightly shut mouth of the Magic Language Bat and inserted his finger dripping with dark red blood.
Blood Clan Ancestor: You are the ancestor of the Bloodline, possessing a powerful Bloodline, immune to sunlight. You can develop one Bloodline each month, all Bloodline members and their descendants are eternally loyal to you, each Bloodline member can provide you with 1 character experience point per month.
It had been over a month since he transformed Stanley, the level 15 Dark Priest of the Late Bell Church, and his Bloodline Power had long been replenished.
Although the Bloodline Power usually didn’t significantly affect the Magic Language Bat, at this critical moment of transformation, Lide was curious whether his power as the Blood Clan Ancestor could help the Magic Language Bat.
As he summoned his power, the enigmatic force hidden deep in his bloodline slowly flowed and faded with the blood; Lide could distinctly feel the potent force entering the body of the Magic Language Bat before him.
After the last wisp of power was transferred, Lide’s body swayed.
His face turned pale, and with the disappearance of the Bloodline Power, his legs felt weak.
“Feels like I’ve done it seven times in one night; this kind of weakness is really something…”
He grumbled to himself, then opened the attribute panel of the Magic Language Bat.
Magic Language Bat (Transforming)
Transformation Species: Unknown, Current Transformation Degree 33%
Current State: Transforming.
Success Rate: 5%
“The transformation degree increased from 32% to 33%, and the success rate from 1% to 5%, it only increased this much??”
Lide’s expression grew frustrated, ‘My kidneys are spent, and you tell me you haven’t even started?’
Shaking his head, he put aside the sudden plan he had thought of and turned his attention instead to the Power of Faith.
Dawn Sect: The God of Dawn—Lide Kachar (Fake God)
Divine Arts: 0
Divine Position: Bloodline, Blood
Doctrines: Persevere relentlessly, fight tenaciously, unite as one, be Fearless, love family, love country.
Number of temples owned: 1
Number of Believers: Zealots 1, Devout Believers 363, Believers 1189, Sympathizers 5767
Power of Faith: 3530 points
“`
The currently available profession to switch to—Dawn Priest (requires the use of 200 Power of Faith points)
Personnel of the Divine Position at the Dawn Temple: Bishop Priest—Emi Kachar
Lide had not had the time to manage the affairs of the Dawn Sect for a while, so the accumulated Power of Faith had reached more than 3500 points by now, which, compared to before, was an enormous quantity.
This was the high-end power obtained from thousands of Believers praying non-stop for several months.
Utilizing the Power of Faith was simple; all the Power of Faith was condensed within his Spiritual Sea, and it could be directed with spiritual power to operate as he wished.
However, this kind of utilization was merely akin to moving goods; it couldn’t inspire the latent might of the Power of Faith.
Calming his mind, under the watchful eyes of second-generation Bloodline members, Lide’s hands slowly began to emit a holy light.
The Bloodline was highly sensitive to anything with a Divine Attribute, and even more so, Dark Creatures generally harbored fear and loathing towards the Divine.
It was an innate aversion, similar to how humans detest Undead and evil auras.
However, the holy power emanating from Lide at this moment didn’t seem to make the second-generation Bloodline members uncomfortable, which was quite miraculous.
