Lide didn’t continue after speaking, and was about to leave immediately when the stunningly beautiful figures of sisters Nilo and Nicole appeared before him.
“Your Highness~”
“Kachar City Lord~”
Lide shook his head with a slightly amused smile; these fellows – like nesting dolls, one after another.
“I will be in seclusion for a while; you all assist Harrison well.
Nilo, although the dwarves and beastmen each have their own Divine to worship, you can try to preach. The strongest power of the Dawn Sect is its inclusivity; be sure to make good use of our advantage.
Nicole, dealing with the dwarves and beastmen is quite challenging; stay close to Harrison to learn and ponder more.”
“Yes, Your Highness,” Nilo nodded, her stunningly beautiful face breaking into a soft smile.
Those pale golden eyes, filled with dignity, gave this girl, dressed in a pure white priest robe, an unspeakably holy aura.
And Nicole blinked her big, lively eyes, a slightly mischievous expression on her intelligent face. “Understood~ Kachar City Lord, I’ll help my sister,
and those little dwarves are actually quite easy to handle; don’t worry~”
Lide looked at the eager expression of the little girl and smiled broadly, ruffling her small head.
“If you do well with this matter, I will reward you when you return,”
“Really?” Nicole’s delicate face lit up with surprise.
“Of course, you can have whatever you want, provided that you satisfy me,”
The little girl patted her yet-to-develop chest, brimming with confidence.
“Just you wait and see; Nicole won’t disappoint you.”
Lide smiled faintly, said no more, and after giving a few more instructions to Nilo, he turned and returned to his manor.
He logged off.
He might stay on Earth for a while this time.
Stanley had reported to him, wanting to use the Undead from the Otherworld to establish a branch of the Dark Contract in the Lost World.
An NPC wanting to establish its own power on Earth.
This wildly imaginative idea had given Lide much inspiration.
Perhaps…

chapters.title: Chapter 234 - 235 Earth, Dawn City Branch (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 234: Chapter 235 Earth, Dawn City Branch (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)
Shanghai, Earth.
Lying in bed, Lide opened his eyes.
The familiar surroundings of his home once again appeared before him.
Each return gave him an unreal feeling, as if his life in Glory was just a long dream.
But looking at the handsome guy in the mirror still reminded him that this was more real than gold.
Standing up to adjust to his body for a moment, he felt a sense of loss.
In Glory, he was too powerful.
Although quite ordinary compared to those top-level combatants under him, as a Level 14 Advanced Mage, a single spell could easily demolish a building. He wouldn’t flinch in the face of a Mechanical Group from Earth—it was like being a human tank.
Having the strength to dismantle mechs with his bare hands felt so different compared to merely having a handsome face on Earth.
But even though he was weaker on Earth, the sense of safety was something Glory could never give.
At least here, he didn’t have to worry about a top-level Demon Beast suddenly turning up and taking him out—the most dangerous creatures on this planet were women.
Luckily, as a single man, Lide didn’t have to face a challenge more fearsome than Transcendents.
Turning on his computer, he logged onto the official website of “Glory” and began browsing the latest game news.
Stanley’s idea of opening a Dark Contract subsidiary on Earth had given Lide a lot of enlightenment.
He had been somewhat neglecting Earth’s role; because there’s no Magic Power on Earth, it was impossible to leverage the planet’s power for magic or even the more advanced Power of Faith.
He couldn’t possibly let a bunch of silly players suggest how to research magic, right?
Damn it, their outrageous ideas were certainly plentiful, but trying to put those fanciful ideas into practice would be disastrous—even with his strong affinity for Magic Power.
Improving magic was a very rigorous process that required exploring the function of each Magic Node, the speed and intensity of Magic Power flow,
And only after fully understanding the nature of all the Magic Nodes could one proceed with improvements.
Moreover, each spell’s Magic Nodes were completely different, which increased the difficulty of improving spells.
He had failed countless times before finally improving two spells.
This subtle sensation, only felt through personal experience, was not something players could solve by guessing or giving advice.
The Power of Faith was the same—a higher-tier force shrouded in mystery.
Although many novels and films on Earth mentioned the role of the Power of Faith.
But could he trust them?
Reading a hundred novels, each novel has a different description of the Power of Faith; which one should he believe?
Watching a hundred films, each film gives a different explanation of this power and its application; how should he operate?
Try them all one by one?
That would be insane. Even as the Vampire Ancestor with formidable Life Force, he wouldn’t dare to experiment like that.
He hadn’t paid much attention to Earth because it was incapable of providing what he wanted.
In a world without even a trace of uranium, how could he research atomic bombs? This was a joke.
But after Stanley’s hint, he suddenly understood, he got it.
Although Earth’s force couldn’t directly research Magic Power or the Power of Faith,
There was no need to be fixated on those aspects; there was plenty of room for maneuver. The official website of “Glory” was on Earth, and all player information also converged there.
He could absolutely set up a branch of Dawn City on Earth, using Earth’s power to help collect information from within “Glory.”
If he were alone, even if he spent 24 hours a day on the official Glory forum, he couldn’t collect information from half the players.
Or his mind would be filled with useless information.
After the game’s beta test, the 100,000 beta players had already started exploring “Glory.” Although slow and the beginning could be described as hellish difficulty,
After all, there were 100,000 people, and undoubtedly, players would explore many useful pieces of information.
For instance, hidden characters that appear, discovered Ancient Ruins, mysterious NPCs, powerful Demon Beast caves, buried giant dragon treasures, etc.
Players certainly wouldn’t be able to take on these quests right now and given players’ mischievous nature, they definitely wouldn’t be able to resist sharing them.
That’s when he could just pick the fruits, right?
What players couldn’t do, he could.
Right now, all 100,000 beta players combined weren’t as powerful as any one force in his hands.
If anything truly worthwhile was discovered, the power he could wield now was beyond any player’s comparison.
And the most crucial part was.
He wielded a powerful native force in “Glory”, capable of recruiting on Earth and cultivating his own players in the game.
By then, he’d truly be a force to be reckoned with on both fronts.
So, he planned to return to Earth and establish a force to support his development in “Glory”.
The Earth division of Dawn City, even the thought of it felt thrilling.
Lide’s smile curved up at the thought.
Moments later, he fell into deep contemplation again.
How to establish a force, he still needed to mull over.
The Li De of today was no longer the fresh resignee from a year ago.
After nearly a year of battling in Glory, he had experienced numerous battles, big and small, and in the fight against the Beastmen, he even personally slaughtered dozens of them.
The fates of tens of thousands of people under his command, in Dawn City, the Crimson Mage Tower, and the Dark Contract, were held in his hands.
The Lion Tribe, a Beastman tribe with an army of thousands, was forcefully defeated by him, and even the terrifying, Level 18 Beastman King, who could go toe to toe with a Bone Dragon, was captured by him.
If he wanted, he could even launch a large-scale war in Glory.
Experience is the best nutrient for growth.
Now, he had fundamentally transformed.
Not only had he become more handsome physically, but spiritually, he’d truly metamorphosed into a big boss in control of countless fates.
An elegant noble, an unequivocal superior.
“To establish a force in Glory, the most basic requirement is—strength. Without great strength, you’re just a sheep waiting for slaughter.
But Earth isn’t that dangerous; here, all you need is enough money.”
Thinking of this, Li De’s brow furrowed slightly.
In Glory, he was a super tycoon, earning hundreds of thousands of Gold Pucks a month with Magic Scrolls, able to buy anything he wanted… as long as it was for sale.
But on Earth, he was just an ordinary person. Though his parents left him this house, it was his lair and not for sale.
As for his savings, the mere thought of the 300,000 or so left in his account made the corner of his mouth twitch.
Before, he felt pretty good – after all, he owned a house and just needed a car to surpass 90% of people in Shanghai.
But compared to his wealth in “Glory”, he was less than a beggar.
“To establish a force that meets my requirements is actually quite simple…”
“First, I need enough Gold Pucks, no, RMB.”
“At least tens of millions.”
Li De’s eyes flickered with thought. Tens of millions in funds were astronomical for him a year ago when he just lost his job.
But now, it seemed to be not so difficult, only a matter of time.
This year’s experiences had allowed him to grow tremendously.
“How can I make money the fastest?” Li De murmured to himself, then suddenly burst out laughing.
“In Glory, the combined wealth of 100,000 players might not even be a tenth of mine.”
“Making money? Easy. I’m the biggest game merchant in Glory. Pay me RMB and I could even get Valen to forge you Extraordinary Equipment.”
Sitting atop three forces, the undisputed super big boss, and still needing to think about making money—that was the real joke.
Li De chuckled at his own slow-wittedness.
Opening the player forum for “Glory”, he casually searched and saw a multitude of posts buying Gold Pucks.
“Buying Gold Pucks, Silver Pucks, Copper Pucks in Bulk”
Game merchant here, professional Gold Puck buy-back, currently the highest exchange rate in the forum, 1 Copper Puck: 4.5 RMB, 1 Silver Puck: 470 RMB, 1 Gold Puck: 50,000 RMB, interested parties DM me.
“Twilight Studio Seeking Beta Players, Also Buying Game Coins in Bulk, DM for Price”
“Highest Exchange Rate Ever: 1 Gold Puck for 51,000.00 RMB, willing to pay more for large quantities, urgently seeking 20 pieces”
“Corner City Buying Rare Warrior Equipment, DM if available, Also Selling 10 Silver Pucks”
After browsing a few posts, to Li De’s surprise, the selling price of Gold Pucks was so high.
But then it made sense; a virtual gaming capsule sold for 200,000 RMB, and Glory was using private gaming capsules,
Aside from internet cafes that purchased a batch of equipment, most players who won the beta test had their gaming pods.
At the very least, most players weren’t poor.
With the hardcore nature of Glory, it has only been a little over a month since its release and players are just barely figuring out how to survive in the game.
Don’t even talk about living well, many times they can hardly manage to get a full meal.
How could those wealthy players stand for this?
I’m spending money to enjoy myself, I even bought a 200,000 RMB gaming capsule, f**k, and now you’re telling me my enjoyment of the game is moving bricks at the dock?
Under these circumstances, it’s no wonder players are pouring money into the game.
But money is hard to earn, ah, it’s too difficult to make money in Glory without the right connections.
Most players are still newbies, just wandering around at level 1 apprentice rank, without even stepping into the level 2 official profession stage.
Now, aside from doing some menial labor, their only option to make money is to join a mercenary corps and do some dangerous jobs.
Typically, it’s a fight to the death, where they die before even completing the mission.
While the reward might be lucrative, it further suppresses their level advancement.
Overall, players have found a way to survive in Glory that suits them.
But it’s still tough.
This hellish difficulty level has sparked countless protests on the forums over time.
But the official website remains unmoved, even thoughtfully asking players if they need to cancel their accounts.
This has enraged players to the point of cursing out the planners’ entire families a hundred times over.
If the official Glory game operations team’s address were on the website, angry players would’ve already shown up at their doorstep with a 40-meter-long machete to discuss the philosophy of life.
So at this stage, it’s common for players to be broke, and even with such high prices, it’s very hard to get your hands on silver pucks.
Lide casually clicked on a somewhat reliable post and started a private chat with a game coin merchant.
“Still buying Gold Pucks?”
At that moment, in a suburban area of Shanghai, Zhao Xinming looked at the notification on his phone, paused, and then with growing impatience, clicked to enter.
F**k, this idiot. Every time he asks if I’m buying Gold Pucks, he’s actually thought someone could sell them.
By the end of the conversation, the previously boastful folks would offer a couple of silver pucks at best, and the most ridiculous one sold only 10 copper pucks.
F**k, this is like screwing a husky.
“Buying, I’ll take as many as you have!!”
Zhao Xinming sent this message with a trace of impatience, seemingly already anticipating what the other person was about to say.
I have two silver pucks, can you give me a little extra…?
“Really taking as many as I have?”
Sh*t, Zhao Xinming felt his anger rise instantly upon seeing this skepticism.
“That’s right, I’ll take as many as you have! You can ask around about my nickname, the ‘Game Coin Little Prince’!!”
“ThumbsUp.jpg, then let’s start by selling a thousand Gold Pucks, I’m in Green City of the Nolan Empire, how do we trade?”
The mocking look on Zhao Xinming’s face froze when he saw this message.
“A thousand Gold Pucks? Not a thousand copper pucks??”
“Yep, if that’s too few I can add more, up to ten thousand isn’t a problem.”
Zhao Xinming felt breathless at those numbers, ten, ten thousand??
“Um, can we start with a trade for 10 pucks, no, 15 pucks??”
“…”
“Boss, boss, if you just agree to contact the seller for me, it’s guaranteed to be inside Green City!!”
“…”
“Boss, don’t stop talking, I assure you, it’s cash on delivery, what’s your address…”
“Ding~ The other party has left the chat”
Lide shook his head with a wry smile and closed the Glory forum.
If he had to sell them 10 or 15 at a time, he’d exhaust himself to death.
He didn’t have time to waste on their nonsense.
“Thought limitations, still stuck in the old ways.
Empiricism just won’t do.”
He actually went to the official forum to negotiate deals worth tens of millions with game coin merchants. Those who could handle transactions over a million were already considered strong.
Real power brokers wouldn’t be posting acquisition ads on forums, would they?
After a moment of contemplation, Lide’s eyes slowly brightened.
Selling Gold Pucks by himself was undoubtedly a foolish thing to do; even posting a message and waiting for others to inquire was annoying enough. How much he earned was one thing, but more importantly, it wasted his time.
In Dawn City, there was a heap of matters awaiting his attention.
The superior commands brains, the mediocre commands hands.
As the big boss, personally selling low-end things like Gold Pucks was beneath him.
What he needed was to find a group of capable people.
To establish a force, people were necessary; selling Gold Pucks was not the most pressing issue.
After clarifying his thoughts, Lide’s deep gaze regained the indifference and confidence from his days in Glory.
He opened his computer and searched for headhunters.
In the highly developed online sphere of 2051, the information he sought was easily found.
Sky Moon Headhunting, the top headhunting firm in Shanghai, specializes in elite recruitment for multinational corporations and Fortune 500 companies.
Of course, this huge headhunting firm also provides professional corporate acquisition services.
In other words, as long as he had the money, he could get these elites to do anything for him.
After registering his information on Sky Moon’s official website, it took less than three minutes for their service staff to call him to ask for details.
“I need to acquire a well-established gaming club that includes a professional gaming data analysis team, professional gaming merchandise sales team, professional gamer team, and a professional and mature management team…”
Lide unapologetically had the other party record everything he needed.
He had previously not shifted his mindset, always thinking about gradually cultivating his own force with money.
But there was no need for such trouble; a direct acquisition was sufficient.
As for where the money would come from… he naturally had a plan.
Due to the specialization of the gaming industry, a gaming club was undoubtedly the best acquisition target for him at the moment, more useful than buying a few companies.
Once he acquired a well-established gaming club, he wouldn’t have to worry about something as simple as selling Gold Pucks.
Just like with Dawn City, he only needed to plan and establish the farm; as for how long it took to be built, what materials to use, how to build, and how to plan production, these issues would naturally be handled by his subordinates.
He only needed to manage the overall direction.
This is how a superior delegates.
If this had been a year ago, even if he’d had the funds, he wouldn’t have dared to say he’d directly acquire a mature company, as his management skills were insufficient.
But things were different now; breadth of vision, observations, and tact had all been honed in the year that passed.
Whether it was acquiring a company or headhunting from other companies, the services offered by headhunting firms were essentially information services, exploiting information gaps to earn hefty service fees.
So, whether it was headhunting or helping clients acquire companies, although there was a considerable difference, the essence was still within this scope.
Thus, Lide’s request was not excessive, and even to a professional firm like Sky Moon Headhunting, it was quite straightforward.
“Mr. Li, have you made an assessment of your acquisition budget?”
The caller on the other end was a girl with a pleasant voice. After a brief consideration, Lide spoke slowly.
“I can accept a ceiling of 50 million to 100 million.”
Upon hearing this price, the tone of the person on the other end of the phone clearly became more animated, laced with a trace of excitement.
“Received, Sky Moon Headhunting will definitely provide you with the most professional services. Are you aware of the company acquisition fees?”
“Go ahead and tell me.”
“At present, Sky Moon Headhunting offers three tiers of service charges: the first tier, for small companies valued at two million or less, incurs a 20% service fee; the second tier, for companies valued within 20 million, charges an 18% service fee; and the third tier, for companies valued above 20 million, charges a 15% service fee. We’ll provide you with the first batch of candidate options in a week…”
15%? For 100 million, they’d be charging a service fee of 15 million.
Lide wasn’t sure if this price was high or low at the moment; he had casually learned that headhunting firms charged service fees ranging from 15 to 30% of a talent’s annual salary.
Meaning for a talent earning a million a year, the headhunting firm would charge a service fee of 150,000 to 300,000.
The cost of acquiring a company was often high; auditing accounts, checking the company’s profitability, verifying core businesses, investigating liabilities, and so on.
All of this required the most professional personnel.
So Lide wasn’t sure if the price was high or low, but naturally, he wouldn’t reveal any weaknesses during the negotiation, maintaining a nonchalant tone.
“No, I need you to provide the first batch of no fewer than five candidate lists within three days, and I will also be inquiring with other headhunting firms. I hope you can be swift,”
Hearing this, the other party clearly became much more nervous.
“Mr. Li, I assure you, Tianyue Headhunting is absolutely the most professional in Shanghai. We are fully capable of providing you with the best choices.
If you sign an exclusive headhunting service contract with us, we can lower the charge by three percentage points…”
Lide grinned slightly, “No, I don’t care about the money; I care about speed. I need the fastest speed to get the results I’m satisfied with.”
With only 350,000 in his card, Lide spoke in a calm and confident manner as if casually whipping out thirty or fifty billion was a trivial matter.
Hearing these strong financial words, the girl from Tianyue Headhunting was clearly silent for a moment, then decisively said,
“No problem, we will use all our resources to serve you.
Mr. Li, if you agree, we can sign the service contract right now. After signing the contract, you just need to pay a 10% service fee deposit, and we can immediately start searching for suitable companies for you.
Currently, based on the lowest acquisition amount—200 million—the service fee is 15%, which is 30 million. You just need to pay us 10% of that, which is 3 million, as the deposit.”
A 10% service fee as a deposit?
Lide decisively shook his head; if he gave out 3 million, how could he continue playing this game when he only had 350,000 in his account?
“Impossible, the initial search service does not require you to use too many resources.
I can only give you a 5% deposit. If you don’t agree, I will switch to another headhunting firm immediately,”
he finished, then impatiently added, “I believe in Tianyue Headhunting’s professionalism, which is why I approached you. Now, give me an answer immediately; if not, we can perhaps collaborate another time.”
His tone seemed ready to hang up the phone at any moment.
The other party’s breathing immediately quickened.
“Yes, Mr. Li, but we won’t be offering any further discounts on the service fee.”
Lide showed a smile, “As I said, as long as you can provide me with the best service, I don’t care about the service fee.
Pleasure doing business.”
The other party clearly breathed a sigh of relief, sounding very excited.
“Pleasure doing business.”
Before long, Tianyue Headhunting sent over the service contract, and the two parties even met in person via a virtual video call. During a fully recorded video and audio call, they amicably signed the contract.
Initially, Tianyue Headhunting had some doubts about the transaction, considering only a 5% fee was provided as a deposit; they even sent a senior executive to supervise.
Earning a profit of several million for the company was not considered a huge deal, but worth an extra look.
However, as soon as the deputy director saw the noble air Lide carried with his every move—a quality that could not be concealed—he immediately cast his doubts aside.
Two things in this world can’t be hidden: poverty and love.
The deputy from Tianyue Headhunting was used to seeing all kinds of people; he dealt with individuals with annual salaries of tens or even hundreds of millions or with fortunes in the billions. The difference between someone superior and an ordinary person was immediately apparent. This was unmistakably a super-wealthy second-generation from a high position with great power.
Such ease and irrefutable quality couldn’t possibly be cultivated in an ordinary household.
Of course, Lide was unaware of the other party’s thoughts. After thoroughly checking all information and qualifications of Tianyue Headhunting and ensuring everything was correct,
and after spending 50,000 yuan to have a renowned law firm verify the contract online, he signed the agreement and transferred the first installment, 1.5 million, into their account.
350,000 yuan leveraged the first step of a multimillion-acquisition deal.
As for inquiring other headhunting firms, Lide asked for a few quotes and proposals before not paying much attention to it.
The prices from Tianyue Headhunting were still quite reasonable.
————
————
————
————
The first batch of candidate lists took Lide by surprise, coming out on just the second day.
A total of seven large gaming clubs’ names lay on his desk, and the owners of these clubs were all thinking of selling.
With technological advancement, the gaming industry’s growth was healthier than ever, and its size was increasing.
Now, with a yearly output nearing 20 trillion RMB, many entertainment industries have already been overtaken by virtual games. The gaming industry has become the absolute mainstream of entertainment.
Such a huge market naturally attracted countless pursuers; everyone wanted to claim the sweetest slice of the pie.
Yet not every company or gaming club could survive; many closed their doors each year.
The Sword and Shield Club was one of them.
“Mr. Chen, Tian Yue headhunting and that buyer will be at the company at three o’clock…”
Mr. Chen slightly raised his head upon hearing this and looked towards the somewhat somber and graceful figure outside his office desk.
He let out a slight sigh.
“Little Zhao, you’ve been with me for such a long time now. If I sold the club, would you hate me?”
Zhao Yue shook her head, “Mr. Chen, you built the Sword and Shield Club from the ground up. I believe no one feels a deeper connection to it than you do.”
After a moment of silence, Mr. Chen slowly said, “If the company’s cash flow hadn’t hit a snag, I wouldn’t want to sell, either. This place represents our shared youth.”
Mr. Chen’s voice was very low. He had founded the Sword and Shield Club ten years ago, and he had gone from a 25-year-old young man to a 35-year-old uncle.
Life always seems to want to bring people to their knees. Some are still gritting their teeth and holding on, while others have long since been tamed.
With growing maturity, everyone has to give up many things they hold dear. The game he once loved so much hadn’t been played by him for three years now.
A hint of nostalgia appeared on Zhao Yue’s captivating face, “Yes, I joined the company at the age of twenty-two and have been here for ten years.”
Mr. Chen shook his head and laughed, “Enough of that, finding a good buyer for the Sword and Shield Club is also not a bad choice.
I hope the renowned Tian Yue headhunting won’t bring someone who disappoints me.”
Zhao Yue nodded slightly, “If they can’t satisfy us, Sword and Shield Club must not be sold.”
Mr. Chen very much agreed with this and nodded. Though he was in urgent need of money, this was, after all, his effort and toil. He didn’t want it to be wasted.
When Lide walked into the building with the huge logo of the Sword and Shield Club hanging above the entrance, his expression was somewhat playful.
The Sword and Shield Club had quite a reputation in the gaming world.
This club maintained professional player teams for nearly a dozen games, and Lide had even watched their competitions.
However, with the rapid pace of technological development, a popular virtual game might lose its popularity the following year.
Many teams had slowly faded from memory like that.
But for this well-known club, Lide still had quite a favorable impression. He needed such a professional club to provide him with data support.
Leading the way in front of him were 10 Tian Yue headhunting staff members dressed in professional business attire.
Six gentlemen and four ladies, among them, the youngest and most attractive woman was the one who had previously discussed the cooperation with Lide.
“Mr. Li, Sword and Shield Club is a very famous club, and it’s definitely a top contender in the gaming industry. I believe you’ve already gone through their information.
Three months ago, a buyer wanted to purchase the Sword and Shield Club and even offered 80 million.
Although the buyer didn’t reach a purchase agreement with the Sword and Shield Club in the end,
we have conducted a detailed investigation of the Sword and Shield Club for this purpose.
Debts, operation status, revenue, and so on are all included in the documents provided to you.
I believe that everything you need can be found in this club.”
Lide nodded with undeniable satisfaction; he trusted the professionalism of Tian Yue headhunting and had meticulously reviewed those documents the previous night.
The Sword and Shield Club indeed met his criteria.
The club was not only mature but also possessed many of the resources he needed.
A professional data analysis team, a professional player team, and even a professional game equipment sales team—this all corresponded perfectly with his requirements.
He needed a team that could provide him with sufficient information and had a group of players with considerable combat capability.
The Sword and Shield Club undoubtedly met his expectations perfectly.
Now the only question was, how much money would it take for them to sell?
His current card balance wouldn’t even cover the one-time appearance fee for Tian Yue headhunting’s 10 elite members.
That’s how poor a spender he was.
When Mr. Chen saw the people from Tian Yue headhunting in the meeting room, he immediately noticed the infuriatingly handsome figure in the crowd.
Dressed in a classic Versace suit that showcased Lide’s tall and majestic build and the unmistakable air of elegance and noble demeanor that couldn’t be concealed, it was truly eye-catching.
Anyone would recognize his distinction at first glance.
Mr. Chen immediately knew who today’s buyer was.
When he saw Lide’s young face, he let out a small sigh of relief.
He feared most that a man in his forties or fifties would come to purchase the club because people of that age were almost no longer interested in gaming.
For such a person to run a gaming club would be a disaster.
The reason he had rejected the previous 80 million offer was precisely because of this.
That buyer simply wanted to take the Sword and Shield Club to rake in profits and had no intention of actually managing it.
Young people are different; gaming is their nature, and there are hardly any young people who don’t play games, although not all of them necessarily manage it well, at least they won’t mess around.
“Hello, Mr. Chen…. and this is Mr. Li…”
After a round of polite handshakes and introductions, everyone took their seats.
Lide sat opposite Chen Feng and Zhao Yue.
The team from Sky Moon headhunters divided to sit to his left and right; he was undeniably the star of the day.
Although his pockets weren’t full, just by the way he carried himself seated there, no one dared to overlook him.
Lide looked at the two people opposite him with a somewhat playful look in his eyes. Chen Feng was okay, but Zhao Yue, a beautiful woman in her early thirties, made him unconsciously take a few more glances.
Dressed in a red professional suit, her voluptuous figure was like a ripe peach emitting an enticing fragrance,
with a delicate face that had a light beauty mark at the corner of her lips, which inexplicably added a few more touches of charm and seduction to her otherwise pure visage.
A perfect ten of a beautiful mature woman, the ripe kind.
“The first moment I saw Mr. Li, I was astonished; I feel fortunate to meet such a talented young man like Mr. Li.
Hahaha, where has Mr. Li been employed before? So young and yet so accomplished…”
Chen Feng had just settled in his seat and started with a hearty smile complimenting Lide.
Lide didn’t take it seriously; he was an old hand at this, nobody took those words to heart.
“Mr. Chen is quite the expert himself, to be able to manage a small unknown club to its current status, truly a model for our generation.
I heard Mr. Chen also runs a not-so-small chain of restaurants? Mr. Chen is truly the one I should be learning from…”
“Mr. Li flatters me; everyone says it’s impressive to be young and successful, but someone like Mr. Li sets the standard…”
“Mr. Chen is joking, Mr. Chen is the one who…”
After a round of insincere mutual flattery that got everyone from Sky Moon headhunters tired, all admired the unchanged expressions on their faces.
No wonder these people are bosses; with that thick skin, it would be a surprise if they didn’t do well.
Eventually, it was Chen Feng who couldn’t endure the pointless talk anymore and took the initiative to discuss the matter at hand.
“Mr. Li, I believe you’ve come this time because you’re very interested in Sword and Shield. Why do you want to acquire a game club?”
Lide’s expression didn’t change at all, as if the nonsense they had just been talking about had nothing to do with him.
Negotiations are like walking face-to-face on a log bridge, whoever steps back first loses.
“Mr. Chen, what do you think it’s for?” Lide slightly picked up the coffee on the table and took a slow sip.
After a brief pause, he didn’t wait for the slightly frowning Chen Feng to speak up and slowly said,
“Sword and Shield Club has a glorious history.
But now, Sword and Shield needs a better opportunity. I like games, and I’m confident I can make Sword and Shield Club do even better.”
“Do you know why I haven’t sold it even when someone offered 80 million RMB, Mr. Li?” Chen Feng didn’t directly respond to Lide but instead spoke his mind.
“To be honest, it doesn’t matter to whom I sell, the 80 million offer for Sword and Shield Club, though not low, is completely fair.
But what I can’t stand is to let someone who doesn’t love games take over Sword and Shield; that would be a disaster, and I don’t want to see Sword and Shield get trashed.”
Chen Feng looked at Lide and said word by word, “Does Mr. Li understand what I mean?”
Lide lightly smiled, “Mr. Chen doesn’t want to see Sword and Shield Club become purely commercial, right?”
After saying that, his eyes were ablaze as he looked at Chen Feng, “Mr. Chen, trust me, Sword and Shield is very important in my domain.
In fact, I won’t use Sword and Shield Club for profit in the short term. On the contrary, I will continuously invest funds to make Sword and Shield Club the leading presence in the country.
In my plan, Sword and Shield Club will be one of the top ten clubs in Huaxia, no, the first among the top ten.”
Although the promise was big, Chen Feng clearly wasn’t impressed, and just as he was about to speak, Zhao Yue interrupted.
“Then please tell me, Mr. Li, what arrangements or plans do you have?
Do you know how much it costs to build a top-tier club?”
Her captivating eyes fixed on Lide, as if trying to discern the truth from his expression.
Lide looked at the charming woman and smiled faintly.
“Money? I will invest one billion in operating funds each year for the next five years to support the club’s expansion, and I do not expect the club to be profitable for the next five years.”
Invest one billion per year??
Now, Sword and Shield Club’s total value was just between 70 and 80 million.
That was the result of Chen Feng’s 10 years of management. If what Lide said was true, then the strength of Sword and Shield Club would certainly grow rapidly.
Perhaps they wouldn’t reach the top ten in Huaxia, but reaching the top thirty, or even top twenty, was not impossible.
Lide’s lips curled slightly as he watched the subtle expressions on their faces, and he continued.
“This is not all. A hundred million in capital per year is just the baseline. If necessary, I’ll increase the investment.
I plan to invest 2 billion into the Sword and Shield Club over the next five years, truly making it the leading game club in Huaxia.”
Penniless Lide spoke of 2 billion as though it were a mere two hundred, casual and understated.
Even the people from Tian Yue Headhunting couldn’t help but be surprised by Lide’s boldness.
They’ve handled many acquisition cases worth billions, but they’ve never seen anyone willing to pour billions into a club worth only tens of millions.
This damn tycoon—why doesn’t he just buy a large game club outright?
While Sword and Shield Club wasn’t small, compared to giant ones, it was still just a little brother.
“Mr. Li, are you serious??”
Zhao Yue looked at Lide’s calm demeanor, very excited.
If this were true, then all the hard work they had slowly built up wouldn’t be in vain.
Lide shrugged, his face unchanged.
“Of course, this can be included in the acquisition contract.
Guaranteeing to invest at least a hundred million per year to develop the club, with a minimum of 2 billion over five years.
If this investment target is not met, after five years, you have the option to buy it back at market price.”
Lide’s tone was even, but the undeniable certainty and confidence affected everyone.
This is what a real tycoon would do.
Chen Feng was moved by Lide’s sincerity and immediately stood up, his eyes unexpectedly welling up.
“Mr. Li, the Sword and Shield Club is like my child. I designed every part of it, and every employee was personally recruited by me. I hope you will take good care of my child…”
Some people scorn their own startups, while others treasure them—human nature is complicated.
At this point, the people from Tian Yue Headhunting were looking at Lide with glowing eyes.
The negotiation had reached this point; the acquisition was half complete.
All they had done was provide some materials they had previously investigated, and before they even entered the scene, the negotiation was already nearing its end.
Their commission of tens of millions this time was too easily earned.
But just when everyone thought this would be a very successful collaboration, Lide shook his head.
“No, Mr. Chen, I’m not certain yet…”
Huh??
Everyone looked at Lide with questioning faces, somewhat puzzled.
You’ve promised so much, what more could there be now?
Chen Feng’s expression stiffened, and he immediately pressed for an answer.
“Mr. Li, do you have any doubts? I can answer any questions you have about Sword and Shield Club.”
Lide shook his head, his tone laced with a hint of mirth that outsiders couldn’t detect.
“I need to test the true strength of Sword and Shield Club. Only if it meets my requirements will I proceed with the acquisition.”
“Oh, what do you mean by that?” Chen Feng’s brow raised, not quite following Lide’s train of thought.
Lide smiled playfully.
“I also had a private studio. After ‘Glory’ launched, I got some beta testing qualifications through some channels.”
Everyone turned their heads towards him, curious.
Everyone knew ‘Glory’, the game that was currently the hottest topic, but what does that have to do with today’s acquisition?
“As it happens, my studio completed several major tasks, earning a considerable amount of ‘Glory’ game coins—Gold Pucks.”
As he said this, a playful smile flashed in Lide’s eyes.
“I need to test the strength of Sword and Shield Club, and the best way to do that is:
I have 3,000 Gold Pucks. You need to exchange these 3,000 Gold Pucks into RMB within one week, without causing market turmoil.
If you manage that, this deal will be valid.
If Sword and Shield Club can’t do it, the deal is off and I will find another suitable club.”
Lide·The Ultimate Schemer·Kachar logged in.

chapters.title: Chapter 235 - 236: Crimson Moon, Forging the Trident (10,000-word Mega Chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 235: Chapter 236: Crimson Moon, Forging the Trident (10,000-word Mega Chapter)
What is called a strategy? This is the real deal.
And it’s as open and noble as a strategy could be.
Lide wanted these people to earn their own indenture money.
The essence of negotiation is to use information asymmetry to obtain benefits.
Now, Lide had all the information, but no one knew his bottom line; the initiative was in his hands, and he controlled the entire situation.
Everyone who heard Lide’s words was taken aback, looking at this young man with an impressive demeanor somewhat peculiarly.
Clearly, his words surprised them all.
Why all of a sudden is there a test? And why the method of exchanging Game Coins for RMB??
Lide’s profound gaze bore into Chen Feng, his right hand’s slender fingers reaching out, gently tapping on the table’s surface, his face betraying not the slightest fluctuation.
Solid as a rock.
No one knew that the capital in his pocket couldn’t even afford the appearance fee for a headhunter from Crimson Moon; these 3,000 Gold Pucks were the source of funding for this acquisition.
If he went to exchange the Gold Pucks for RMB alone, it would take way too long.
On the forums, those gold coin merchants who could take down more than a dozen were considered decent, and large-scale outflows of Gold Pucks would undoubtedly have a significant impact on the market.
He couldn’t be bothered with such a time-consuming and effortful method that required no skill, so he simply handed it over to the Sword and Shield Club to handle.
With the popularity of “Glory,” he didn’t believe that the 100,000 players in the closed beta, amidst such robust demand, wouldn’t be able to absorb 3,000 Gold Pucks.
He had no channels to communicate with the large clubs that needed them.
But the Sword and Shield Club did.
Without causing market turbulence, with the Sword and Shield Club’s ten years of networking in the gaming industry, Lide believed they could execute the task perfectly.
Plus, it was a real test; if such a large company couldn’t mobilize hundreds of millions in capital, then this club, valued at 80 million, was just junk, unworthy of acquisition.
Even if the information provided by the headhunters from Crimson Moon was good, it wasn’t worth considering.
Watching Lide’s calm face, the room fell into a slight silence, everyone contemplating the deeper meaning behind his actions.
These elites believed that the ultra-rich second-generation heir certainly had some unknown deeper reason for his actions, surely it wasn’t as simple as it seemed…
But they all couldn’t possibly foresee that the seemingly well-off super-rich second-generation heir, who was discussing the investment of tens of billions, was in fact engaging in getting something for nothing.
It couldn’t really be called getting something for nothing.
It was just making them earn their own indenture money.
Chen Feng couldn’t imagine that the money from the sale of the club hadn’t surfaced yet, and he would only get it after the sale of the Gold Pucks.
This layered strategy was something he couldn’t detect, already stepping into the trap Lide had set.
The true King of Strategy.
“This task should not be difficult for you to complete with your connections; if you can’t, then our acquisition plan will come to an end.
I’ll look for a more suitable club.”
Lide’s tone carried an undeniable force.
Chen Feng naturally wouldn’t suspect Lide of lacking funds.
The mere fact that Crimson Moon headhunters sought him out was a symbol of strength.
Moreover, with Lide’s dazzling noble demeanor, even if he was told that Lide only had a few thousand in savings, he wouldn’t believe it.
How could an ordinary person possess such a remarkable demeanor? It’s not something that can be feigned; it’s ingrained.
Lide had merged with the memories of the Blood Clan Ancestor spanning two hundred years, inheriting that nobility that seeped into the soul.
Now, his every action carried an elegance he wasn’t even aware of.
This kind of demeanor, only attainable through good breeding and extensive cultivation, shone brighter than the Versace suit he wore, which had cost him all his savings before arriving.
That was the reason why no one doubted him.
Chen Feng nodded; he didn’t think Lide’s demands were unreasonable.
“No problem, ‘Glory’ is a game that our Sword and Shield Club plans to focus on next. It’s just that since it’s not yet public, we can’t participate.
But given our status in the gaming world, selling some game currency won’t be an issue.”
Beside him, Zhao Yue spoke up with a peculiar expression, interrupting the overconfident Chen Feng.
“Mr. Chen, 3000 Gold Pucks is quite a lot…”
Zhao Yue happened to have a beta test spot for “Glory,” playing it every day, and she certainly knew the current value of the “Glory” Gold Puck.
3000 Gold Pucks, now at the exchange rate of 50,000 RMB for one Gold Puck, amounts to 1.5 billion RMB.
It is no simple task to handle such a large sum, especially during a beta test limited to 100,000 players, without affecting the market.
Chen Feng had never played “Glory” and was therefore unaware of the market fluctuations; he hadn’t played games for a long time.
He only kept running the Sword and Shield Club because he couldn’t let go of the efforts he had put into it, so he wasn’t very clear about what 3000 Gold Pucks represented.
The surrounding staff from Tianyue Headhunting were similar to Chen Feng, not being fervent gamers and therefore not inclined to understand the exchange rates between a game’s currency and RMB.
Then, Zhao Yue leaned in and whispered a few words into Chen Feng’s ear.
“What, 3000 Gold Pucks are worth 150 million RMB???”
Chen Feng’s exclamation of surprise made everyone pause before they all turned to look at Lide, who was leisurely sipping from a white coffee cup.
The headhunters could only imagine the words “filthy rich” stamped in gold across Lide’s forehead.
A casual gesture involved hundreds of millions in capital – that was a true big shot.
Reality was not a movie; there weren’t that many wealthy people around.
The elites of Tianyue Headhunting present at the meeting didn’t make more than six to seven hundred thousand RMB a year, and that was already considered a high income.
Here was a young man who could afford what they couldn’t earn in a lifetime – such a big spender.
At the same time, the people from Tianyue Headhunting looked at Lide with an even more intense gaze.
This was a truly high-quality client; this deal alone could land their small team several hundred thousand in commission.
Chen Feng took a deep breath to calm his excitement and turned to look at Lide, speaking solemnly,
“Mr. Li, regarding your request for us to sell 3000 Gold Pucks, we accept.
However, the related service fees and commissions will still be collected by the Sword and Shield Club, after all, we have not completed the acquisition yet…”
Lide nodded nonchalantly, “No problem, but I’ll give you only one week.
These 3000 Gold Pucks were earned by my private studio in Green City, Nolan Empire, after completing a few large tasks.
You can discuss a plan and present it to me, this is my first collaboration with Sword and Shield.
I hope you won’t let me down.”
Whether the acquisition succeeded or not, Lide had already become a major client of the Sword and Shield Club.
The transactions they were involved in warranted a service fee of 3%.
With Gold Pucks valued at 1.5 billion, that was nearly 5 million RMB in fees alone, almost pure profit with just the use of some social resources.
The money was so easily earned that Chen Feng almost wanted to cling tightly to the thighs of this wealthy big shot.
“No problem at all, the Sword and Shield Club will live up to Mr. Li’s trust,” Chen Feng said with a brilliant smile.
Although Sword and Shield Club was a major business with an annual turnover of at least 50 million, their expenses were frightening, and their earning capacity was not particularly strong; last year’s net profit was only a little over 8 million.
Now Lide was offering them half a year’s profit with the flick of his finger.
Absolutely unconscionable wealth.
The negotiation had progressed to a preliminary agreement, and once Lide’s collaboration with Sword and Shield Club was completed, the real acquisition would follow.
Chen Feng happily began to introduce the Sword and Shield Club in more detail, and Lide, with patience and the assistance of Tianyue Headhunting, got a complete understanding of the club’s structure.
Their operational models, profit points, spending points, management team, and the games they were currently active in, among other things.
Although tedious, he gained a more profound understanding of the club he was about to acquire.
——————
——————
——————
The next morning,
Lide received a call from Chen Feng,
“Mr. Li, we have already contacted the buyers; a total of twenty-three game clubs are interested in the Gold Pucks you have.
However, due to the large quantity, they can only offer a ratio of 45,000 to 1 for the purchase.”
Lide wasn’t the least bit surprised by Chen Feng’s words; in fact, this was precisely the reason he had always emphasized not affecting market stability when trading Gold Pucks.
Currently, “Glory” was indeed popular, but it only had 100,000 beta testers.
This pond was too small to accommodate a giant crocodile like him.
In his calculations, 3,000 Gold Pucks was just the right amount that the market could absorb.
If he were to release 30,000 Gold Pucks into this market, the price of Gold Pucks would plummet wildly, and then not to mention 45,000 for 1 Gold Puck, even 10,000 RMB for 1 Gold Puck would be doubtful.
The current high price of Gold Pucks was caused by an imbalance in supply and demand; as time goes by, the price of Gold Pucks will inevitably drop slowly.
“Alright, what’s the plan for the trade?”
“Mr. Li, we have already reached out to seven gaming clubs in Green City, after you give them the Gold Pucks, they will deliver the Gold Pucks into the hands of other game guilds,
Players’ backpack storage is undroppable, so death won’t affect it.”
“Glory,” despite being to the extreme in terms of hardcore, was still quite considerate toward the players.
For example, each player has a backpack with 10 slots, and stored currency cannot be dropped.
“No problem. The game doesn’t have a chat system; how will they contact my people?”
“There’s a huge Angel statue in the center of Green City; they will be waiting in the game at three o’clock tomorrow afternoon, by then you just need to notify your subordinates to log in ahead of time tomorrow afternoon.
The code for the meeting has already been sent to your phone.
Each code corresponds to a different player guild, and the amount of Gold Pucks needed for each is different…”
Lide couldn’t help but shake his head with a wry smile. Meeting codes?
“My subordinates are now trapped in a major quest and can’t get out in a short time.
But they have subdued two NPCs to be their subordinates; I’ll have the NPCs meet with the players. Communicate with those player guilds again.”
“NPCs meeting up?” Chen Feng’s tone was a bit startled, but he didn’t care too much, “No problem.”
After in-depth research on the game yesterday, he also knew the game’s power; the NPCs’ intelligence wasn’t necessarily worse than the players’.
After discussing some details, Lide looked at the information on his phone with a very odd expression.
This code. If it were for the original residents of “Glory” to guess, they might never figure it out, even to their death.
“Mount Akina is rarely tread by foot; missing are the veteran drivers of years past.”
“Baotazhen river demon, Chicken stewed with mushrooms”
“Chang Wei, you still claim you know no martial arts; cousin, I heard you have a handwritten copy of the Avatamsaka Sutra, may I borrow it to look at?”
“…”
But is all this trouble necessary? Just log off and call to confirm once you meet… Lide was deeply doubtful whether these people’s intelligence needed an update.
—
—
—
Three days later.
A purchase operation that could be called rapid-fire was completed in full, from the moment Lide called Tianyue Headhunting to the completion of the entire acquisition, the total time used — 6 days.
Lide spent 80 million RMB to acquire the Sword and Shield Club, which had over 300 employees and had been deeply involved in the gaming industry for ten years.
At the same time, he paid Tianyue Headhunting a service fee of 12 million, becoming the fastest-earning and most worry-free service fee since the establishment of this top headhunting firm.
As a result, Lide also became the most esteemed customer of this top headhunting company.
The lady with the very sweet voice was arranged to be Lide’s 24-hour service assistant; whenever he needed Tianyue Headhunting, no matter the time or place, the other party would provide the most professional service for him at the first instance.
This policy fully demonstrated what it meant to be wealthy and powerful.
And those 3,000 Gold Pucks Lide owned were snapped up by the game guilds desperate for them, with a net income of 135 million.
He became a top-tier wealthy elite overnight.
After experiencing the reality and charm of “Glory”, all the game guilds realized the potential here, each almost frantically waving checkbooks to purchase.
The most generous guild spent a full 30 million in funds to buy Gold Pucks; an early investment to secure a certain advantage was not excessive, as they believed they could later earn back ten or a hundred times the profit.
After deducting 80 million for the acquisition of Sword and Shield Club, 12 million in service fees for Tianyue Headhunting, and the 3% handling fee of 4 million for the 3,000 Gold Pucks handled by the Sword and Shield Club,
Lide currently had a remaining fund of 39 million.
He didn’t hesitate and directly injected 34 million into the Sword and Shield Club, which had only a few hundred thousand left in its account, leaving an extra 5 million just in case.
The Sword and Shield Club, which had been unsettled by the acquisition, immediately quieted down after Lide of Finance University confidently announced a 30% pay raise for all core personnel.
Their initial resistance to the new owner immediately turned into a warm welcome.
Because of Chen Feng’s financial difficulties, they hadn’t seen a raise in a very long time, and no amount of nice words could compare to actual money. Clearly, Lide wasn’t planning to deal in mere promises.
The Sword and Shield Club was located in a high-tech park in Shanghai, just half an hour’s drive from Lide’s home.
After all the procedures were completed, on his first day taking charge of the Sword and Shield Club, Lide immediately called a senior management meeting.
He wanted to build a force that operated according to his will, and the current Sword and Shield Club was undoubtedly not up to par.
“Mr. Li, currently the Sword and Shield Club has established 12 professional teams, with a total of 150 people, competing in 8 virtual games.
Among these, two games achieve top three results annually and are the main sources of our club’s income.
There are 60 analysts and coaching staff, 70 team members for data collection, quest mining and so on, and 50 members of the game commerce organization responsible for game merchandise sales, plus a 20-person logistics support team…”
On his way to the meeting room, Assistant Zhao Yue, who he had hired as the new CEO’s assistant, took this opportunity to give him some basic information about the company.
Zhao Yue had had a discussion with the buxom woman after the acquisition was complete, and her perspectives and insights had garnered his approval, proving to be a competent subordinate.
And Zhao Yue didn’t want to leave the club she had worked at for ten years, so she stayed at Lide’s invitation.
Elite talents are always in demand; someone like Zhao Yue would be highly sought after anywhere, and even the headhunters from Angel and Moon had already offered her positions at other companies.
After getting to know the Sword and Shield Club in detail over the past few days, Lide couldn’t help but shake his head.
The foundation of the Sword and Shield Club wasn’t bad, but its profitability was. It relied only on two virtual games for revenue every year.
If their rankings fell, the club could potentially make a loss—such a business model was very small-scale.
Furthermore, due to the previous owner, Chen Feng’s insufficient funds, the growth momentum of the Sword and Shield Club was also very slow.
One could say that without his stepping in, the Sword and Shield Club would still fail to make any significant waves.
“Let’s talk about it in the meeting room.”
Lide, looking toward the nearby meeting room, cut off Zhao Yue’s report.
“Yes, Mr. Li.”
Although they had not been working together for long, Zhao Yue had basically figured out Lide’s character.
Once he has spoken, the matter is decided, without room for doubt. His manner is swift and decisive; the tasks he assigns can only be completed, without any room for negotiation.
This kind of resolute character is both easy and challenging to work with.
It’s easy in that as long as you complete the task, there will be no problems, but challenging because if you fail to complete the task or if the task is compromised, it will certainly be very uncomfortable.
And Lide’s behavior often made Zhao Yue feel very strange.
It’s like he’s, well, a real noble, not a modern castrated one who simply carries an honorary title.
But rather a noble from the old days who controlled the fate of everyone within his territory.
Sometimes, the cold, harsh look that Lide inadvertently displayed could terrify her, and Zhao Yue often wondered if he had been a mercenary involved in war, otherwise why would his presence be so frightening.
Lide didn’t know what Zhao Yue was thinking; otherwise, he could only sigh at how keen a woman’s intuition really was.
He wasn’t just a noble but also the master of a city, a king of a race, holding power in his hands that could launch a major war at any time.
Bang~
At the doorway of the meeting room, two young, beautiful girls helped open the door, and Lide gave them a slight nod before striding into the meeting room.
The spacious, well-lit conference room was filled to capacity, with enough seating for three hundred people, but there was not a single empty seat.
Tap tap~
Tap tap~
His boots made a crisp sound against the floor as Lide’s figure appeared in front of all the members of the Sword and Shield Club.
Today, Lide was dressed in a black Armani suit with dark patterns, the top-tier clothing accentuating his naturally heroic build and making him look even more handsome,
especially the unmistakable aristocratic aura that he naturally had, which made his entire being seem all the more elevated.
The ultimate super hottie.
Suddenly, the room buzzed with complicated murmurs.
Particularly the young girls, who now seemed to have their eyes wide open. Not only do boys like pretty females, girls also pay special attention to handsome and young wealthy men of merit.
Aspiring to beautiful things is human nature, and this applies to both men and women.
Clearly, the appearance of the stunningly handsome Lide, who could capture anyone’s attention, touched the hearts of those young girls.
“Our boss is this handsome guy??? Impossible, I don’t believe it, I already have a boyfriend, why did this domineering CEO appear now…”
“He’s too handsome, ahhh, how can he be so good-looking???”
“To have acquired such a big company at such a young age, and what’s key is that he’s really this handsome, he’s totally my type.”
“….”
Many of the young and self-proclaimed handsome guys felt crushed upon seeing Lide; compared to him, they felt they could scarcely show their faces outside.
Naturally, Lide was unaware of the flurry of thoughts the short walk had provoked below, as he confidently ascended to the chairman’s stage to take his seat.
The office gradually quieted down.
“My…” Lide nearly blurted out the habitual slogan from Dawn City as he began to speak.
He cleared his throat and then spoke composedly.
“My employees, my name is Lide, and I’m delighted to meet all of you.”
A round of polite applause ensued.
“As I believe you all know, the Sword and Shield Club has been entirely acquired by me.
I will not let down the hard work that Mr. Chen has invested over the past ten years.
The Sword and Shield Club will become a true sword that cuts through brambles and an invincible shield in our hands.”
Lide’s eyes shone as he looked at the employees below, announcing what everyone was most concerned about.
“All employees who remain at the club, to honor your past contributions to Sword and Shield, I declare that everyone will receive a 30% raise.”
Clap, clap, clap~
His words truly struck a chord, and everyone welcomed their new boss with the warmest applause, heartfelt and sincere.
“Besides that, I also have several new decisions to announce.”
Lide waited for the crowd’s cheers to subside before formally commencing today’s agenda.
Now that the company was his, he naturally wanted to imprint it with his own brand.
“Sword and Shield Club represents former glory, and I will lead everyone into a new era of success.
Starting tomorrow, Sword and Shield Club will officially be renamed—Crimson Moon.”
Everyone below had a bit of a wistful look, knowing that this day would come, but not so soon.
Zhao Yue’s expression was also complex, but seeing Lide’s resolute look, she refrained from voicing any objections.
A new kingdom needs a new name and flag; Sword and Shield Club belonged to Chen Feng, but now, this place belongs to the new king.
Crimson Moon.
It sounded quite good, Zhao Yue could only comfort herself silently.
Lide didn’t give the crowd a chance to respond and continued confidently.
“Currently, we have set up professional teams in 8 different games, and two games have been achieving satisfactory results.
This is the outcome of everyone’s hard work.
But at the moment, the virtual games on the market are a mixed bag, many of which can’t keep up with the times.
I have excellent professional players, but they aren’t matched with the right games.
I have insider information that ‘Glory’ is a game with immense potential, which I have personally tried out.
This game deserves our full commitment at Crimson Moon…”
At this point, a young man with long hair and a somewhat defiant expression raised his hand, interrupting Lide directly.
“Sorry, Mr. Li, why is this unreleased game worth our full commitment?
Could it be that Mr. Li is considering cutting other departments’ professional teams to partake in a game that hasn’t even been publicly tested yet??”
Lide frowned, this kind of confrontation with the boss in public—
This young man had something about him, not yet tempered by the harshness of society, right?
“Yes, you heard correctly. In the next half a month, I will be shutting down all other games, except for the two that are currently profitable.”
Swoosh~
A single stone stirred up a thousand waves, and everyone in the meeting room went insane.
The decision was tantamount to directly announcing that the majority of them were now unemployed.
Those two games couldn’t accommodate so many professional players.
And how could a game that hasn’t even been released be guaranteed to have potential?
This decision dealt a fatal blow to the good image Lide had just begun to establish.
“Mr. Li, I object!!”
“Mr. Li, this isn’t fair, you’ve only been here one day and have no clue how much effort we’ve put into these games!!”
“Impossible, if they shut down, I’ll resign immediately!!”
“Mr. Li, please reconsider…”
“….”
The meeting room was as noisy as a vegetable market.
Everyone was frantically protesting because this concerned the jobs of the majority here.
If it were shut down, what could they do? Play a game that wasn’t even in open beta yet??
Lide watched everything with an indifferent expression, his heart undisturbed.
As if the uproar in the meeting room had nothing to do with him at all.
After the crowd had been noisy for a few minutes, Lide finally began to speak slowly.
“Are you done??”
His indifferent voice quelled the scene, and although there was still dissatisfaction, calm was restored.
“Finished, now it’s my turn.”
Lide’s gaze slowly sharpened.
“What I say, I never change, all games are to be shut down, except for the two that are profitable.
This isn’t a discussion with you, it’s my decision.”
After saying this, he swept his gaze over the excited crowd and continued.
“There’s no need to worry about unemployment, I’ll arrange new jobs for you.
For the games that are shut down, all related personnel will enjoy the same benefits as before until ‘Glory’ goes into open beta.
I need you to focus on studying ‘Glory.’
This is the future.
I’ll repeat it once more, the teams of the shut-down games will become part of ‘Glory.’
Those who have never played ‘Glory’ can experience it offline over the weekend, and after that, you’ll understand my decision.”
After saying this, his tone became more solemn.
“Those who have objections to my decisions, those who are dissatisfied, can leave now.
The finance department staff is waiting outside for you; the resignation process will be completed within half an hour.”
At these words, swish swish swish, more than twenty figures stood up, each giving Lide a defiant look before turning to leave.
Many others were tempted but never took that step.
Lide watched this scene with an unchanged expression.
After these people left, he slowly said.
“Good, those who stay will have their year-end bonuses doubled. You will not regret today’s choice.” With a single sentence, he soothed the mood of the crowd.
After finishing, Lide turned his head to look at Zhao Yue, “Additionally, go to the esports school and recruit a group of young people with exceptional talent to fill these positions.
I need to cultivate a batch of talents for ‘Glory’ in advance.”
“Yes, Mr. Li,” Zhao Yue recorded Lide’s instructions with a serious expression.
This clever woman also knew that Lide was establishing his authority, so she did everything according to his will.
In this setting, she was certain that if she questioned him, she would definitely be rebuffed mercilessly.
Looking at the crowd below regaining their composure, Lide continued to boldly reform this power entirely his own.
Already accustomed to holding great power, with a single word determining the fate of the forces in his hands, he never wavered on major issues.
The art of governing lies in a combination of grace and strictness.
Simply put, it’s the carrot and stick policy, reprimand or even dismissal for those who disobey, and rewards, promotions, and raises for the compliant.
A slap followed by a sweet.
Earth is not Glory, where in Glory his will dictates the direction for all, with no one daring to contradict, but on Earth, every individual is independent, thus a certain degree of skill is needed for control.
“Starting today, the Crimson Moon will establish a new department—Glory Strategy Department.
Apart from the two games that have not been shut down, everyone else, whether coaching teams, data analysis teams, or professional players, will be merged into the Glory Strategy Department.
The relevant restructuring plans will be published by Assistant Zhao Yue before noon tomorrow.
Moreover, from next month on, a professional salary system will be implemented within the club.
M—for management, M1, M2, up to M12 presidential level, each level will have different salary treatments.
Z—for professional players, Z1 to Z12, divided into 12 levels, each professional player will enjoy treatments according to their level.
P—for professional technicians, P1 to P12, analysts, equipment sales team, logistics staff, all fall within the P level…”
Lide can be said to have completely changed the previous structure of the Sword and Shield Club.
Personnel and salary, these are the two most basic and important components of a company, and now both have changed.
There’s no need to elaborate on personnel; his main purpose in acquiring the Sword and Shield Club was to boost his operations in “Glory.”
And he needed to cultivate a group of high-quality professional players who could be his subordinates at his beck and call in the game.
His power in “Glory” was immense, but it had a fatal flaw: the natives couldn’t be resurrected.
Therefore, when faced with danger, he often hesitated to take action.
But players are different, he could outright command them to risk their lives to probe, and it wouldn’t incur a significant loss.
Therefore, personnel changes were a must and absolute, with no room for negotiation.
As for the salary treatment, it was a reference to the practices of major corporations, ensuring professionals engaged in professional work.
Let the managers handle managerial tasks, and the professional players do what they’re meant to do, without worrying about lacking promotion channels and being forced into management.
Many professional technical talents aren’t cut out for management—in small companies, they’re coerced into management due to no advancement paths, but in big companies, technical talents can stick to their field without worrying that sticking to tech will result in lower pay.
That’s the difference between big and small companies.
Lide’s restructuring was also aimed at allowing everyone to develop in their own professional direction, rather than contemplating other things.
Even the name change was decisive, and other games were cut without hesitation, so naturally, no one would stand up and irrationally oppose the issues Lide raised.
“These changes will materialize within three days.
To all staff, trust me, change is for a better tomorrow, and I wouldn’t spend hundreds of millions merely to leave you with nothing to do.
The future is in our hands.”
The response from the audience was rather tepid, but Lide was indifferent; gaining the recognition of everyone as a newly appointed boss is not that simple.
However, he would make these people understand who truly ruled here.
The rest of the meeting didn’t offer much substance, and after carrying on for over half an hour, listening to reports and statements from several executives, Lide announced the adjournment.
He didn’t expect to fully rally the club, with over 300 employees, to act at his command in just one day.
A power needed to be nurtured, and with the foundation Crimson Moon had now, he was confident that following the restructuring, these professionals would provide him with ample support.
A team of hundreds gathering and analyzing data for him—this efficiency was much greater than working alone.
He seemed to already envision the scene of various treasures and ancient ruins entering his pocket.
After the meeting dispersed,
in the President’s office,
Lide sat behind his desk, looking at Zhao Yue with a playful expression.
“Assistant Zhao, the pay plan, Glory Strategy Department, and the matter of recruiting talent from esports schools—all are in your hands.”
Hearing Lide’s direct words left Zhao Yue with a somewhat peculiar expression, wondering if her boss was a bit too impersonal.
“There’s a lot of work recently, you can hire an assistant team of no more than 10 people to help you handle these matters…”
Lide revealed a knowing smile after he had spoken.
“If your performance satisfies me, we might not need to bother with recruiters for our vacant deputy general manager position.”
Despite knowing that Lide was dishing out empty promises, Zhao Yue couldn’t help but have her heart flutter with excitement.
As a career woman, stepping into the role of deputy general manager meant reaching a new height in her career.
In the future, when headhunters sought to poach her, her salary would not be less than a million annual pay.
Right now, she was only at four hundred thousand.
“Thank you, Mr. Li. I will work hard. I will submit all these proposals to you within three days.”
Her tone was firm; becoming the deputy general manager was not just about salary and benefits increase for her.
She would also gain more autonomy and be able to better protect the club that she had devoted ten years of her youth to.
“Very well, you’ve been working hard these days.
If there is a shortage of management talent, feel free to contact Tianyue headhunters directly. We have enough funds on our accounts.”
Having money means having confidence. With the support of the Crimson Mage Tower Magic Scroll Factory, he could easily convert Gold Puck into a hefty sum of RMB at any time, giving weight to his words.
For three consecutive days, the Crimson Moon underwent a reorganization.
All the disorganized departments were consolidated.
Under Lide’s will, the current Crimson Moon had only three major departments.
First, the Professional Player Department. Excluding those who had left in the past few days, there were still 120 professional players. These were seasoned professionals, who had a good understanding of and ability in games.
Due to the rapid development of the gaming industry, being a professional player had become a recognised career. Although Crimson Moon didn’t have a professional player with more star power,
these players were skilled and belonged to the elite class of professional players; otherwise, the previous Sword and Shield Club would not have grown to such an extent.
Apart from the two profit-making games, all other players had been transferred by Lide to become reserve players for “Glory,” now fully diving into learning about “Glory” in preparation for its official launch.
Those two games that hadn’t been shut down were just a temporary measure by Lide to placate people. Once “Glory” launched, these individuals would also become part of “Glory.”
The second department was the Data Analysis Team.
This was a department Lide paid great attention to. It combined the previous coaching team, data collection team, analysis team, and so on, making it the largest department at Crimson Moon with a total of 130 people.
Apart from the twenty-plus people still collecting data on the two profit-making virtual worlds, everyone else had started researching “Glory.”
For this purpose, Lide planned to invest tens of millions in establishing a professional data analysis center. It was still in the planning stage, but it was certain to be operational before the launch of “Glory.”
This department would later be Lide’s vital source of intelligence, extraordinarily significant.
The third department was the Equipment Trading Department.
This would be Crimson Moon’s primary money-making tool in the future.
Lide’s advantage in “Glory” was too significant.
But to further expand this advantage, he needed to use game merchants.
He could exchange outdated equipment, weapons, and even Gold Puck with players for various precious materials, leveraging information asymmetry to shear the players as sheep.
This department was also one Lide was very optimistic about, currently with 45 people.
In the future, Lide planned to expand to a hundred-person team, though it was sufficient for now.
Finally was the Logistical Support Department, not much to say about it. Twenty-something people were dedicated solely to serving the others.
Thus, the scheme for the three major departments at Crimson Moon was formed.
Player Department, Data Analysis Department, Equipment Trading Department—this trident would be Lide’s crucial weapon for his future battles.
Players were the force, data analysis the intelligence, and equipment trading the funding.
Having money, people, and information, he naturally wouldn’t shy away from a fight.
Unfortunately, “Glory” had yet to launch, so his carefully assembled trident was still lying in wait.
However, Lide believed that as soon as “Glory” became available, it would be time for the trident to shine.
Afterward, Lide spent some more time on Earth handling various post-acquisition matters. Once Crimson Moon began to stabilize, Lide re-entered “Glory.”
By then, he had already spent 11 days on Earth, while a whole month had passed in Glory.
Yet, the growth of Dawn City had not halted in his absence… And Lide had plenty of new ideas to implement back in Dawn City.

chapters.title: Chapter 236 - 237: Powerful Divine Arts, Rebuilding the Mighty Lion (9800-word mega chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 236: Chapter 237: Powerful Divine Arts, Rebuilding the Mighty Lion (9800-word mega chapter)
Lide returned to Glory and felt an explosive power within his body, as well as a calling from the surrounding magical power with each movement. A hint of sentiment flashed in his eyes.
The feeling of controlling power was wonderful.
He shook his head, changed his clothes, and then left his manor to head to City Hall.
After spending 10 days on Earth, a month had passed in Glory, and he needed to hurry up.
During this month, apart from sending a message to Vina to have his maid, Gold Puck, transferred to a player, he periodically checked in to see if anything significant had happened.
He was pleased that the administrative system he had established in City Hall, although not yet perfect, could still operate normally in his absence.
That was what he wanted. A person’s ability and energy are always limited; it is impossible to manage everything, especially when the power in his hands grew increasingly vast.
A perfected system, however, could exert infinite energy.
He didn’t have the energy to monitor every task in Dawn City himself. After establishing the City Hall system, he just needed to ensure its normal operation to have control over the entire city.
On the third floor of City Hall, as soon as Lide stepped into his office, Harrison followed closely behind.
“Good day, Clan Leader.”
“Good day, Harrison.”
Lide looked at his top general with satisfaction. The rapid development of Dawn City was inseparable from Harrison’s abilities; in his view, Harrison’s value might even surpass that of a level 18 Bone Dragon.
Top-level combat power was hard to find, but top-level administrative talent was even rarer.
“How have the dwarfs and beastmen been settled?”
Harrison responded with a slightly strange expression.
“Clan Leader, both the dwarfs and beastmen have been… well arranged by Nicole. They have already started to integrate into Dawn City.”
Lide was somewhat surprised by this response and intrigued.
“How did this girl handle the dwarfs and beastmen?”
Harrison looked admiringly, “Clan Leader, your vision is truly far-sighted. I dare say even the Dark Goddess would be surprised by your wisdom…”
As Harrison unabashedly praised him, he went on to detail how Nicole had dealt with the dwarfs and beastmen over this time.
“Although Nicole is young, her talent in management is definitely much higher than mine.”
“In our original plan, the beastmen were to be treated as slaves, and Giant Valley would have been their best destination…”
Lide listened intently, and through Harrison’s narration, he grew even more admiring of Nicole’s ingenuity; he indeed hadn’t misjudged her.
Nicole hadn’t simply relegated the beastmen to slaves as Lide initially envisioned.
Instead, she created a new hierarchy — third-class residents, second-class residents, and first-class residents.
Third-class residents were a step above slaves, possessing slight rights but must bow and give way to official residents, making them the lowest tier.
Second-class residents had a higher status than third-class, and first-class residents stood above the second-class, with official residents at the top.
Those beastmen willing to join Dawn City received the status of third-class residents, the most active among them were given second-class status, and if they passed certain tests, they could even be granted the status of first-class residents.
Life for the beastmen in the barren wastelands was much harsher than for humans on the borders.
During this time in Dawn City, these beastmen experienced what true living was like for the first time.
Food – they had sweet white bread daily, never having to worry about hunger; even as captives, they were well-fed every day.
In the barren wastelands, hunger was something nearly every beastman experienced frequently.
To be truly fed, one had to be a clan leader; otherwise, even a warrior of level 10 or higher might not be assured of a full belly daily.
