﻿Chapter 279: Chapter 281: The Arrival of the Little Girl, and Again the Story of Isa’s Origins (8200 words) Chapter 279: Chapter 281: The Arrival of the Little Girl, and Again the Story of Isa’s Origins (8200 words) March 16th, Lide returned to Dawn City at the break of dawn.
Returning to the city victorious, Lide had very little time to rest. He immediately entered City Hall upon his return.
Harrison, who had been waiting there, could not contain his joy upon seeing Lide, and a radiant smile spread across his face.
He began to lavish praise on Lide without stinginess.
“Clan Leader, your strength is both admirable and astonishing, praise be to you!
The Dwarf Hill Ridges will now provide us with a steady stream of resources… Such a genius strategy.”
After defeating the Black Wind Tribe, Lide had the news sent back to Dawn City. He had already shared his thoughts on the development of the Dwarf Hill Ridges with Harrison, and this chairman of the City Council was well aware of Lide’s plans.
Now that the first step was successful, the future looked promising.
“Alright, it’s not like you’re hearing this for the first time.
Frey will be stationed at the Dwarf Hill Ridges from now on. I want you to have the construction department send a few elite master builders right away to help the Centaur build the market.”
Lide got straight to work assigning tasks, “We must set the rules for this trading market, and the Iron Hoof Tribe will cooperate fully.
Discuss this with Frey. He will be our representative in the Dwarf Hill Ridges from now on.”
Frey, as a once most powerful second-generation Bloodline, had always been valued highly by Lide.
Although his Level no longer kept up with the first-tier, Frey was meticulous and keeping him within the sanctuary seemed a waste of talent.
Therefore, Lide directly tasked Frey with taking charge of the Dwarf Hill Ridges.
The Dwarf Hill Ridges would become a significant resource point for Dawn City and would play a vital role.
It wasn’t enough to just have a local spokesperson like the Iron Hoof Tribe; one of their own was needed, and Frey was the best choice.
As for the vacancy left in the sanctuary, Lide was somewhat troubled.
Another reason to deploy Frey was that even though he had changed his Profession to Crimson Hunter and reached Level 12, it was still not sufficient.
This most secretive and crucial place was no longer suitable to be managed by a Bloodline who hadn’t reached Level 15.
With Dawn City growing more robust, they would face increasingly stronger enemies, and the Bloodline’s ultimate trump card had to be guarded by someone of sufficient influence and power.
Therefore, the sanctuary needed a new Guardian, and the minimum requirement was to reach Level 15—the higher, the better.
Because the sanctuary didn’t just house the Blood Pool; it also held what could be called the rare treasure of the Holy Spirit Relics.
That was a Divine corpse, of which there must be no loss.
The Bloodline’s current sustainable development strategy’s core was this Holy Spirit. Without it, Dawn City’s current growth momentum would be severely impaired.
Yet, deciding who to appoint as the guardian of the sanctuary proved difficult for him.
All of his top combatants already had compelling reasons to be stationed where they were.
Stanley, at Level 15, now managed the intelligence hub and bore responsibilities nearly as significant as Harrison’s. His crucial role ensured Stanley would no longer participate in other missions.
Emi, the Level 15 Shadow High Priest, was peculiarly missing in Risier City alongside Craig at Level 16. And even if Emi returned to Dawn City, he needed to control the vital Dawn Mage Tower—not a suitable candidate either.
Grot, at Level 17, managed the Dark Contract in Green City, securing a vast treasure trove of rare items for Dawn City.
In Stanley’s absence, this major figure in Green City’s Underworld, recognized as one of the three major leaders, had to be collaborated with a sufficiently influential person.
Even less suitable were those who were not of the Bloodline. Betty, the Level 16 Northern Land Valkyrie, guarded the Crimson Mage Tower and couldn’t leave the increasingly strong, ever-growing Crimson Mage Tower.
Level 18 Beastman King Kapp was currently in the Lion Tribe, and he couldn’t possibly divert him away to suppress the Mithril Vein, an incredibly precious ore vein, especially given the current unrest among the beastmen.
Level 15 Castro, Level 16 Koso, and Level 18 Withered Bone, these three colossal figures were not at all close to the holy land, and they might not even be able to enter the few caves leading to the Blood Pool.
After some thought, Lide realized that although he hadn’t found a suitable candidate, he discovered something that pleased him immensely.
He now possessed nine individuals with combat strength above Level 15, and adding himself, a level 15 Blood Clan Ancestor, that made exactly ten.
Ten top combatants, Withered Bone and Kapp at Level 18, were in the first tier,
Betty at Level 16 and Grot at Level 17, Castro at Level 15, comprised the second tier of combatants,
Craig at Level 16, Emi at Level 15, Stanley at Level 15, and Koso at Level 15, were the third tier.
Lide estimated that he should be the strongest within the second tier and the weakest within the first tier, his combat strength falling just a bit short of Level 18 Kapp.
After Level 15, each level up would result in an enormous increase in combat strength.
Although Lide’s Bloodline was powerful enough, Level 15 was still 3 levels behind Level 18.
But, he anticipated that once he reached Level 16, he would be able to manipulate all of his subordinates at will, even Kapp with his Level 18 combat strength.
Now, the absolute fighting force in Lide’s hands was enough to astonish anyone.
The Dark Contract, once led by Viscount Bernard and one of the three giants that dominated Green City, had a peak strength of only seven top fighters.
Now, after more than a year of development, Dawn City had unbeknownst become a behemoth that no one could ignore.
Moreover, he had now captured a Level 17 half-centaur who had awakened the Gale Bloodline and in just three months, his forces would gain yet another second-tier fighter.
“Clan Leader…”
Harrison’s call snapped Lide, who had drifted into deep contemplation, back to reality.
“What were we discussing just now?”
Hearing Lide’s question, Harrison wasn’t bothered, having long been exposed to the extent to which Lide’s thoughts could wander.
“Regarding the low hills, City Hall will specifically establish a department—Trade Department, to handle trade relations with the outside.
And Frey will take charge as the head of the Trade Department, fully responsible for matters concerning the low hills.”
Lide heard this increasingly familiar term and shook his head with a hint of amusement.
When he had taught Harrison about various advanced knowledge from Earth, he used modern management systems as examples, so inevitably, after Harrison’s adoption, City Hall’s various departments were marked by this influence.
“Alright, you take care of the preliminary responsibilities. Once it’s on track, hand it over to Frey for management.
This line is very important to us; put in a bit of extra effort, and it will yield a greater return.”
Lide’s deep gaze fell on Harrison. The low hills were a grand strategy he had laid out, which would provide Dawn City with a powerful resource supply in the future.
This seemingly barren land was filled with gold beneath its surface. The potential had already been hinted at by the profit of a million Gold Pucks from the recent trade with the Centaur Tribe.
Just dig deeper in the future, and Dawn City will gain even more.
“As you wish.” Harrison nodded in response, jotting the matter down in his notebook.
Having resolved this issue, Lide shifted the topic.
“How far has the crafting of the Extraordinary Equipment progressed now?”
During the three months of his slumber, the Mithril had been steadily accumulating. Without his orders, no one dared to tamper with these strategic reserve materials.
Upon awakening, Lide had ordered the Dwarf Forging Master, Master Valen, to craft armor and weapons for Kapp, Betty, and Grot, the three powerful warriors.
“But due to his excessive use of Demon Crystal Stones, he nearly wiped out all the gold pucks in Dawn City, lacking the funds to purchase the raw materials required for forging Extraordinary Equipment, so the process was delayed.
After that, he managed to alleviate his financial troubles only after trading with the Iron Hoof Tribe.
“The materials are all ready, but Master Valen has requested that they come back in person for a test.
After all, weapons are meant to be used by people, especially when it comes to Extraordinary Level equipment. Merely forging it based on a fixed data template doesn’t guarantee that the weapon will be suitable.”
Lide nodded thoughtfully. Extraordinary Equipment possesses all sorts of unimaginable magical powers, and given its high cost, the importance placed on it could never be overstated.
Castro’s strength had increased by more than five times after donning the Extraordinary Equipment. This was the boost to combat power that high-end equipment provided. Of course, the gold pucks it consumed were also enough to make this wealthy tycoon’s heart ache.
“Let them come back then, for it’s Extraordinary Equipment after all.”
“I’ve already sent out the message last night; they should be able to return before evening.”
Lide looked at Harrison appreciatively. This guy always made him feel at ease with how he handled things.
Sure enough, as dusk approached, Kapp and Grote were the first to arrive. These two eager beavers hurried into the smithy after greeting Lide, which left him both amused and exasperated.
Following closely behind them was the endlessly powerful Northern Land Valkyrie.
Betty was dressed in a black, skin-tight leather armor today, with a three-palm-wide silver greatsword in her hand, which, coupled with her slender body, seemed even more massive.
She wore leather trousers on her lower half, with two slender legs exuding an inviting charm.
With slightly disheveled long hair draped behind her, her pitch-black eyes vigilant and frosty, she was like a wild beast ready to hunt its prey, every move filled with an untamed essence.
And the one following this Northern Land Valkyrie was a petite figure, dressed in a pristine white Mage Robe, with eyes as gorgeous as rubies.
Her demeanor was sweet and demure, and upon seeing Lide, a heartwarming smile spread across the girl’s face.
When Lide saw Betty leading Isa towards him, a radiant smile instantly spread across his lips.
My little Isa is so endearing.
“Teacher~”
Upon seeing Lide, little Isa, contrary to her previous quiet and shy nature, excitedly ran toward him across the grass in the City Hall’s garden, clad in her pure white Mage Robe.
Eventually, Lide opened his arms wide and embraced the exuberant little girl, giving her a big hug.
He even lifted her up and spun her around twice, greatly satisfying Isa’s inner joy.
Moments later, Lide gently released her under Isa’s lingering gaze, and looking at her delicate face, he playfully pinched the girl’s nose.
“Isa, have you been obedient these days?”
Isa nodded dutifully, her eyes curving into crescent moons, radiating sheer delight untainted by any impurity.
“Mm… Isa has been good.”
After speaking, her small hands tightly clung to Lide’s right hand, eyes brimming with dependence.
“Teacher… Isa missed you…”
She spoke softly, her tone tinged with the unique shyness of a little girl, yet couldn’t contain surges of unrestrained exuberance.
Lide had been asleep for more than three months, and then returned to Dawn City with the arrival of Frost Month.
For Isa, this most important figure in her life had not been seen for half a year.
Longing for Lide had been her most frequent activity during this time.
When Lide was in his deep slumber, Isa had come to Dawn City with Betty, hoping to visit him. But at that time, Lide was asleep in the blood pool, and the Bloodline, in the interest of safety, didn’t allow anyone who was not of the Bloodline to enter, so Isa, who had come to Dawn City at the time, did not get to see Lide.
Seeing this figure, more important to him than his own life, the excitement and exhilaration in his heart overflowed beyond words.
Lide looked at the girl’s pure trust and dependence with great pleasure, such genuine expressions he had only seen in Isa, Venna, and Nyro’s eyes.
“Good girl,”
Lide couldn’t help but rub the girl’s little head again, his eyes filled with indulgence.
At that moment, Betty also arrived, the somewhat haughty heart of this female warrior flickered with joy upon seeing Lide.
Inside, she silently breathed a sigh of relief when no one else noticed.
For the Northern Land’s Valkyrie, the fact that Lide was unharmed was the greatest assurance.
She knew that whether it was Dawn City, the Dark Contract, the Crimson Mage Tower, or Isa, this guy was the most important person; if something happened to him, she couldn’t fathom the consequences.
Even Isa, this sweet and innocent girl, would probably change into someone else.
“Your Bloodline Power??”
After standing by Lide’s side for a while, Betty’s face showed surprise, even a hint of shock as she looked at him.
“What’s wrong?” Lide blinked, somewhat puzzled.
“It’s strong,” said Betty, her black eyes fixating on Lide. After making the serious statement, she felt the need to add more emphasis, “Very strong, very strong.”
Lide looked amused by Betty’s astonished expression, as if the powerful members of the Northern Royal Family were like people who had never seen the world.
Too strong.
Others might not feel it, but Betty, a female warrior who had been fighting since she learned to wield a weapon, had extremely keen senses.
Although Lide did not exude any aura, every pore on her body warned her of the danger when she was near Lide.
Danger, extreme danger.
In Lide’s slender body, there seemed to be an Ancient Giant Dragon hidden, ready to unleash power that could rip space and time.
After a deep look at this increasingly mysterious man, Betty did not say any more.
Yet a touch of eagerness quietly arose in her eyes as her fighting spirit slowly elevated.
The terrifying power hidden within Lide stirred her combat desire.
Feeling the atmosphere gradually rising around Betty, the corners of Lide’s mouth twitched slightly. Did this woman really want to fight him?
Damn, true to the Northern people.
I’m your master, can’t you grasp reality?
He took Little Yisha by the hand and decisively walked away.
He had no interest in battling with Betty at this time.
Betty watched Lide walk away without paying attention to her. In a very girlish manner, she pouted her lips, which looked surprisingly cute—too bad no one noticed. A moment later, Betty regained her somewhat haughty demeanor.
Back in his office, he took his seat.
Looking at Isa sitting beside him with her hands placed on her skirt, her posture ladylike and demure, Lide was very pleased.
He reached out to tousle her flaxen hair, and Isa slightly lifted her head, her eyes narrowing comfortably as she gazed at Lide.
“Teacher~”
Lide’s affection delighted the young girl, and months of longing were satisfied in the best way possible.
Lide gave a slight smile and casually opened Isa’s attribute panel.
Isa ??
Level: 8
Age: 16
Golden Bloodline: Awakening Level (15%)
Description: Possessing a Golden Bloodline of the Golden Race, the innate Talent of the Golden Race is enough to astonish the Divine.
Restricted Talent: Bonding – Bonded to Betty Smollett. The bonded parties can mutually gain one Bloodline Talent from each other. Bonding is categorized as primary and secondary, where the secondary must unconditionally obey the commands of the primary.
Level 8??
Lide’s eyes revealed a touch of astonishment. Isn’t this level advancement a bit exaggerated?
Over a year ago, little Isa hadn’t even reached Level 1.
Indeed, it is no wonder, given she is of the Golden Race. He had to rely on the system cheating upgrades to surpass the other by a head.
And her Golden Bloodline’s Awakening Level had increased from the last 10% to 15%.
Seeing this, Lide revealed an interested gaze. When Isa’s Bloodline Awakening reached 10%, she awakened the Bonding Talent and formed a bond with Betty during the most critical battle, saving the Bloodline from the Dark Bishop, Kolong of the Late Bell Church.
Betty’s legend of beheading the Level 19 Molten Demon after its Transformation with two sword strikes is still being circulated within the Bloodline to this day.
Therefore, it is highly possible that Isa’s Bloodline Awakening to 20% would grant her a new Talent.
Lide was quite interested in this.
The Talent of the Golden Race—little Isa was his treasure; naturally, the stronger, the better.
“Isa, has your Bloodline been slowly Awakening recently? Do you feel anything?”
Hearing Lide’s question, Isa’s eyes showed a touch of admiration. She hadn’t even had a chance to tell Lide about this yet.
“Yes, there’s a force awakening inside my body, but I can’t control this power at the moment, it seems it’s not yet fully formed…”
Not fully formed?
Lide nodded, “Can you feel how to control that energy? Do you need any help from your teacher? For example, do you need Magic Crystal Stones or Magic Potions?”
Betty, standing beside them at the moment, shook her head and interjected, “Master…”
The title seemed extremely awkward to say, and Betty’s face showed a subtlety. This fearless Valkyrie was always somewhat unnatural in front of Lide.
“Isa’s Bloodline will naturally awaken slowly with age, without the need for extra stimulation. Simply ensuring Isa’s growth is safe will suffice…”
Lide heard this and was quite envious.
This is the strong racial Talent of the Golden Life. As time passes, they naturally grow stronger.
The most famous of these are the giant dragons of the Longevity Species, who, as long as they live long, their strength will continue to grow. Moreover, the growth limit of dragons is extremely exaggerated. Eventually, they can even ascend to godhood and become part of the Dragon Clan Divine System.
Although the specific race of Isa is currently unknown, a Golden Race that can be compared to dragons surely won’t be inferior.
“Alright, Betty, Isa is our most important person. We must ensure her safety.”
Looking at the docile and cute Isa, Lide couldn’t help but feel a surge of affection. Too adorable.
Not to mention her cute appearance and high values, her Talent was explosively powerful, and her personality was very well-behaved. She was simply perfect.
Isa held Lide’s hand tightly, her eyes slightly squinting with content as she gazed at him.
“Teacher… Isa is very powerful. I can protect myself…”
Lide laughed heartily, “Yes, Isa is very powerful, but that’s for later.”
After teasing the little lass, Lide turned his gaze to Betty, “Betty, how is the situation at the Crimson Mage Tower now?”
Although the Crimson Mage Tower sent information to Dawn City every one or two days, after a long absence, it was necessary to hear the news from Betty.
But what Betty said shocked Lide.
“Master Spark has sustained a serious injury…”
“Master Spark is injured? When did this happen, and for what reason did he get injured?”
Lide couldn’t help but ask. Spark was a Level 19 Great Mage, a being near the Extraordinary Level.
In Green City, he is a true dominator that can rely on his strength to act without constraint.
Such a big figure had been seriously injured, which was incredible.
Betty shook her head.
“It happened just as we were on our way back, and the White Tower only just sent the news that Master Spark seems to have followed the Extraordinary Mage, Lord Rock, to the north.”
North?
Lide’s eyes flashed with a hint of gravity.
“Undead?”
Betty nodded, her tone also became a few degrees colder.
“Yes, Undead. After the Undead announced the establishment of the Undead Empire a few months ago, they temporarily declared a truce and returned the lands they had invaded to other empires. However, due to the large scale of their invasion, although the main force of the Undead has retreated, a large number of undead remnants have remained within the territory of the Nolan Empire. The Extraordinary Mage from Green City gathered all the top professionals to eliminate these residual Undead.”
Lide raised his eyebrows. In theory, in such a scenario, Spark’s strength would not likely suffer too much danger since the main forces of the opposition had retreated.
So why…
Seeing Lide’s confusion, Isa next to him spoke up to supplement Betty’s explanation.
“Grandfather Spark discovered a Death Cemetery that was being used to create high-level Undead, and the cemetery was causing severe damage to the surrounding areas. If we don’t destroy that Death Cemetery, it would affect hundreds of kilometers around it with the aura of Undead, turning humans and other life forms into undead, posing a huge hidden danger. Grandfather Spark was severely injured after entering the Death Cemetery and was afflicted by the power of Undead.”
Isa showed a bit of undeniable concern in her eyes. Apart from Lide, the slovenly and unkempt Spark had been the best to her.
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly, and his mood suddenly worsened. “How is Master Spark’s condition now?”
“For now, he’s okay. Lord Rock has sealed the aura of Undead in his body, which can’t harm him physically for a year or two. However, this is probably not the final solution.”
Betty shook her head. Although she didn’t have much fondness for that untidy Great Mage, he was unconditionally kind to Isa. She had to accept that favor.
Lide nodded. It seemed necessary to make a trip back soon.
Spark’s support for the Crimson Mage Tower was unimaginably significant to outsiders.
Without Spark’s influence, the Crimson Mage Tower could never have developed so quickly.
How lucrative are magic scrolls? The profits are enough to drive any family mad with desire.
It was indeed Spark’s forceful leverage, as a major figure in Green City, that safeguarded the Crimson Mage Tower; otherwise, the Crimson Mage Tower, which could bring in over a hundred thousand gold pucks each month, would have long been swallowed up by those high nobles.
Even the rapid development of Dawn City relied heavily on Spark’s influence in Green City.
His main source of revenue in the early days—the technology to manufacture magic scrolls—was given to him by Spark for free.
Although somewhat unserious at times, Spark genuinely took good care of his disciple.
“After the armor is forged, I’ll join you in returning.”
A few moments of deep thought flashed in Lide’s dark and profound eyes.
An eventful autumn indeed.
The beastmen of Risier City had yet to make a move, and a few days ago, he had tried to contact the Level 16 werewolf, Craig, using the power of faith, but his efforts were blocked by another force, preventing him from sensing any information from Craig.
It was the same with Emi; the Bloodline Ancestor’s blood could not relay messages to this second-generation Bloodline.
As the deity of Dawn City, he wielded the power of faith but was still blocked, indicating clearly who was behind this—the Divine.
The beastmen were even borrowing the strength of their gods, indicating a vast scheme.
Now add to this the Undead intent on founding an Undead Empire, and even Spark, a powerful Level 19 Great Mage, had been severely injured by a Death Cemetery left behind by the Undead.
The wind was shifting in an unwelcome direction.
The situation in the southern parts of the Nolan Empire had undergone a massive transformation compared to just a year ago.
Lide sensed the oppressive feeling of a storm on the horizon.
If he wanted to continue farming comfortably as he did a year ago, just managing his current domain, it seemed it would only become more challenging in the future.
This was also why he had continually taken the initiative to strike; in times of great change, if he didn’t enhance his own power as rapidly as possible, he might not even have the option to act in case of an emergency.
Becoming stronger was an eternal truth.
Although Dawn City was currently hidden deep within the Far Mountain Range, with little chance of being discovered in the short term,
being prepared for the worst was always what a ruler should do. As the helmsman of the giant ship that was Dawn City, he needed to chart the course for the future.
“Is there anything else?”
Lide had asked casually, but Betty, indeed, had more to report.
“Today, I heard from our merchants who returned from the Blue Sea Province that the Fishman Clan has blockaded the maritime area and has even launched attacks on over ten coastal cities in the Blue Sea Province.
Our trade missions could not procure the magic materials they set out to get.”
Lide’s brow furrowed further.
The sea housed a variety of demon beasts, making it an important source of resources. Many of the magic materials used by the Crimson Mage Tower come from marine sources.
The Fishman Empire, immense and neighboring the coastal waters of the Nolan Empire’s Blue Sea Province, had previously co-existed with humans with minimal interference.
It was rare to hear of the Fishman conducting large-scale invasions of port cities; after all, occupying human cities wasn’t of much use to them, given their critical weakness of needing to live near the water prevented them from expanding land-based power.
But such an incident happening now was highly unusual.
The eve of a storm’s arrival.
“And most crucially, many of the magic materials commonly used in the manufacture of magic scrolls cannot be substituted by any other materials.
For example, the tears of a magic fish, the deep sea squid, and even the deep sea cold iron essential for forging top-tier equipment, can only be produced by the ocean.”
Betty spoke with a profound familiarity; this wild valkyrie had not been idle during Lide’s absence, helping Vena manage the Crimson Mage Tower, so she was quite sensitive to these matters.
Once war broke out, the most direct impact would be the shortage of various supplies.
And even though these wars were thousands of miles away, their impact on the Crimson Mage Tower and even Dawn City was particularly evident.
The lack of raw materials for the production of magic scrolls alone was enough to cause a headache.
The Beastmen invasion of Risier City, the Undead severing the northern border, and now the invasion of the coastal Blue Sea Province by the Fishman Country.
It seemed that the south of the Nolan Empire had fallen into a strange and dangerous situation.
“Alright, I’ll handle these matters when I return.”
Lide couldn’t help but feel a headache; the wars, except for the one in Risier City which he was involved in, had nothing to do with him, but they were still a discomfort to him.
Shaking his head without dwelling on it much, he thought that once he got back to Green City, he could resolve these matters; fretting now was useless.
Without further delay, Lide stood up, “Come on, let’s go to the blacksmith shop; I had you return this time to forge extraordinary equipment for you.
As for the matters of the Crimson Mage Tower, I’ll solve them when I go back to Green City. The sky won’t fall as long as I am here.”
The strong confidence in his voice instantly infected Betty, her dark eyes slightly quivered, she admired Lide’s calm and confident demeanor in facing any significant issues most.
It reminded her of those legendary heroes destined to rule the Northern Lands from the northern myths—the very existence she aspired to and revered.
And Lide’s image seemed to be increasingly aligning with that direction.
A faint blush arose, unbidden, on Betty’s face, then she quickly shook her head to refocus her attention on the extraordinary equipment.
Extraordinary equipment, for the impoverished Northern Plateau, the entire royal family did not possess many pieces.
Although Betty was a valkyrie, she was not a child of the reigning Northern King in the Northern Royal Family, so the armor and weapons of the extraordinary level had always been beyond her reach.
The great sword in her hands had been obtained from Grot.
Having a set of extraordinary equipment was enough to make her happy, for a warrior’s weapon was their second life.
Lide watched Betty’s somewhat excited expression and smiled softly, taking Yisha by the hand to head out.
Soon after, they arrived at the blacksmith shop that had not yet been relocated to the weapons factory park.
In Lide’s plan, in the future, all factories would move to Moonlight Plain and form clusters of specific industries by type.
The blacksmith shop would naturally be for weapon manufacturing, alchemy bombs for the alchemy factory, and in the future, the magic factory would be established near the mage tower.
The city zones of Dawn City would eventually be purely residential areas, and these large factories would all be relocated.
Of course, a small portion of shops for everyday needs, such as forging kitchen knives and agricultural tools, would be retained.
“Good day, Your Lordship.”
Upon seeing Lide, Master Valen immediately bowed respectfully but then caught sight of Yisha from the corner of his eye.
The ruby-like eyes of the girl caused an indescribable shock to appear on the face of the dwarf forging master.
Pointing at Yisha, he stammered.
“Your Lordship, is that, that, that not the species from the Storm Sea Domain?”

﻿Chapter 280: Chapter 282: The Foodie Female Warrior, Returning to Green City (A 10,000-word mega chapter, added for Alliance Hierarch Jiu Yue) Chapter 280: Chapter 282: The Foodie Female Warrior, Returning to Green City (A 10,000-word mega chapter, added for Alliance Hierarch Jiu Yue) “The race from the Storm Sea Domain??”
Lide narrowed his eyes slightly, his gaze electric as he stared intently at Valen.
Spark had mentioned before that in his youth, he had encountered the red-eyed race in the Storm Sea Domain hunting two extraordinary dragons, but he was not clear about the ultimate fate of that dragon-hunting lady.
Now, Valen was also saying the same thing; it certainly could not be a coincidence.
“Valen, what race is it? Do you know about the Isa Race?”
Valen, sensing Lide’s pressing mood, couldn’t help but glance at Little Yisha again. Those red eyes were exactly the same as those of the race he had seen in the Storm Sea Domain when he was young.
He nodded gravely.
“Your Highness, when I was younger, I spent decades traveling across the glorious Main Plane. Although I stepped foot in less than one percent of it, I went to many dangerous or unique places.”
In the eyes of this three-hundred-year-old Dwarf, a hint of reminiscence showed.
“I have seen countless lives that are either magical or powerful, and among them, besides dragons and Abyss Demons, what shocked me the most was that powerful race with crimson eyes.”
Little Yisha’s expression was very tense at this time. Did she really still have kinfolk?
The words she had heard from Spark had given her hope, and now hearing the same news made her even more nervous.
Those clear and pure eyes stared tightly at Valen, anticipating his next words.
“It was an accidental encounter. At that time, I was aboard a large ship heading to a region prolific with magic treasure pearls.
But along the way, we encountered the very lifeform that all sailors in the Storm Sea Domain dread to meet—the Deep Sea Giant Beast!
Those bloodthirsty hunters are the most terrifying natural disasters in the Storm Sea Domain.
The one that attacked us was a beast two hundred blades in length; it considered our one hundred and fifty blade-long ship as prey.
To flee was our only hope; there was no chance of defeating it, and that Deep Sea Giant Beast had even reached an extraordinary level…
At that time, the seven Great Mages on our ship used magic frantically to accelerate the ship, and to avoid the Deep Sea Giant Beast, we greatly deviated from our original safe course.
A greater accident occurred.
Storm, a fierce storm struck us.
For the Storm Sea Domain, encountering a storm is nothing out of the ordinary.
But to adventurers, every storm is lethal, and that particular storm was a horrific natural disaster that the ship’s crew had never seen before.
The indescribably powerful storm made heaven and earth seem to lose their meaning…”
At this point, Valen’s eyes flashed with a hint of terror, as if that encounter a hundred years ago still made his heart palpitate.
“Even the Deep Sea Giant Beast, which was two hundred blades long in the deep sea, was blown up into the sky by the wind.
The seven Great Mages on our ship exhausted all their magic power to barely keep the big ship from capsizing.
But as time ticked by, the Demon Crystals ran out, the magic power ran out, and after everything was exhausted, we inevitably couldn’t hold on.
Just when our large ship was blown directly up into the sky by the storm, along with the Deep Sea Giant Beast floating in the air.
That lady of nobility appeared.”
Valen’s eyes shone with light at this moment.
“She wore a long red Mage robe, her face was as perfect as an angel’s.
With a wave of her hand, the storm that could lift the extraordinary Deep Sea Giant Beast into the sky stopped within a thousand blades range around her.
The two hundred blade-long Deep Sea Giant Beast, sensing something unusual and trying to resist, was easily burned to ash by her simple magic. Yes, right before all of us, the level twenty Deep Sea Giant Beast was incinerated to ash by a crimson Small Fireball.
Afterwards, the lady of nobility glanced at us, said no words, waved her hand, and we were transported along with the big ship directly out of the storm’s center.
The storm, capable of tearing space, couldn’t affect the lady of nobility at all.
When we came to our senses and checked, we found we had already appeared in a calm sea area hundreds of kilometers away.”
Speaking to this point, a fervent and unstoppable worship rose in Valen’s eyes.
“Later, after discussions among the seven Great Mages on our ship, we unanimously believed that the lady of nobility might very well have reached the limit of the legendary, a true Demigod.”
After finishing, Valen turned his head and stared intently at Yisha. “The lady of nobility’s eyes are identical to yours, and the aura emanating from your eyes is so similar—unmistakable like bright moonlight that cannot be covered up.
Kachar Your Highness, this honorable young lady, her origins must be far beyond our imagination.”
After listening to all this, Lide deeply sighed. This Dwarf’s experiences were truly full of twists and turns; if it weren’t for Valen’s integration into Dawn City, he would have surely thought the fellow was bluffing him.
Turning his head, he looked at Little Yisha with a slightly complex expression, who was full of longing on her face.
What’s the difference between saying that and saying nothing??
“Where did you encounter that lady? Can you find her again?”
Valen unexpectedly nodded, “That place is the most famous Death Sea Eye in the Storm Sea Domain. The magic energy there is extremely dense, and various Demon Beast resources are distributed. Many powerful races own their own islands there, and even giant dragons are often seen.
It’s very likely that the lady in question resides there.
So the best way to find them is to head to the Death Sea Eye.”
After saying this, Valen added a little more.
“Of course, to enter the Death Sea Eye, you must be at least Transcendent level, because that is the most dangerous place in the Storm Sea Domain.
Because the magic energy is too dense, terrifying storms frequently occur there, which are the nightmares of countless people.”
After hearing this, Lide looked at Little Yisha who turned her head and seemed somewhat nervous, smiled faintly, and reached out to pat the girl’s head.
“Don’t worry, your teacher won’t be rash. When Yisha grows up, I’ll take you there.”
Upon hearing this, Yisha immediately let out a sigh of relief and then revealed a radiant smile.
She nodded vigorously.
“Mm…”
Storm Sea Domain, Death Sea Eye.
Lide silently memorized this name, softened by the longing and anticipation in Little Yisha’s eyes.
Getting information about Yisha’s origin was an unexpected joy, but this was not a map to be explored in the short term. They would wait until Dawn City had enough Transcendent power to give it a try.
Just hearing the name Death Sea Eye suggests a map of sufficiently high level, possibly concealing many treasures and resources.
He shook his head; thinking about this was still too early. For now, forging the Extraordinary Equipment and enhancing his subordinates’ combat strength was the real deal.
Castro, after getting the Extraordinary Armor, became unrivaled; Lide was quite looking forward to seeing what kind of enhancement these fighters with off-the-chart combat strength would gain after getting their Extraordinary Armor.
“Valen, Grote and Kapp have arrived, right? This is Betty; if you have any requirements for the armor and weapons being forged, tell her.”
“Yes, Your Highness.”
Betty followed Valen, and Lide, also curious, led Yisha to see how Valen would proceed.
Then under Valen’s arrangements, Betty, the Valkyrie, went through basic tests of swinging a sword, chopping at wooden stakes, and sprinting.
Only after she had used all her skills in the most basic fight, with two warriors as targets, did Valen call an end to the assessment.
When Betty stopped, people immediately came to help two seemingly tough targets off to heal.
Although Betty had not exerted even 1% of her strength, she still gave two level 5 warriors a hard time.
At this point, Grote and Kapp, having just finished testing, appeared before Lide with excited expressions, especially the level 18 Beastman King Kapp, who was in a state of constant excitement.
He was about to have Extraordinary Equipment, which was simply unbelievable to him.
What kind of life did Beastmen live before??
Poor!
This word was enough to sum it all up.
He, as the king of a twenty-thousand-strong Beastman Tribe, only had a longsword of Perfect Level and armor of Rare Level; he wasn’t even comparable to the captain of some wealthy city on the border.
But now, after taking refuge under a powerful patron, he was immediately enjoying ultra-luxurious treatment, which made this Beastman King, used to the hardship, cry out in delight. Compared to now, what kind of life had he been living before?
If only he had sworn allegiance to His Highness sooner…
“Good day, Your Highness.”
Watching his two dependable generals, Lide nodded with satisfaction.
Level 18 Beastman King Kapp was currently the strongest combat force in Dawn City; if it weren’t for his poor equipment back then, who knows what price they would have had to pay to take him down.
Remembering the scene of Kapp wielding a longsword and wearing ragged armor, yet standing firm against five top-tier fighters, he couldn’t help but smile.
Now he’s mine; how exhilarating.
At that moment, Betty turned slightly and faced Kapp.
Their eyes met.
Betty, holding a greatsword, stiffened slightly, and then her legs pressed down hard, her body coiled like a spring wound to its limit, ready to burst forth with endless power.
Her fighting spirit soared in an instant, her wild eyes brimming with eager anticipation.
This was the first time these past rivals had met after more than half a year.
Seeing Betty, Kapp’s aura surged as his eyes flickered with a cold sharpness, clearly impressed by her previous performance in the Dwarf Valley.
Sparks seemed to fly in the air.
A fighting spirit lingered.
Lide’s mouth twitched slightly, no wonder Mages looked down upon Warriors, viewing them as vulgar and crude, never dignifying them with a direct look.
Were these guys idle?
Polite Mages, even when facing an opponent, only measured themselves through Magic, such a street brawl-like scenario would never happen.
“That’s enough, if you want to fight, go outside. Don’t be a nuisance here.”
Hearing Lide’s rebuke, both parties slowly calmed their auras. Kapp respectfully bowed his head to apologize, then stood silently beside Lide.
Lide’s will was the direction for him as a Temple Knight; there was no chance for disobedience.
But the fighting spirit in Betty’s eyes never faded. Challenging the strong was a trait imprinted in the blood of the Northern people.
Kapp was also one of the strongest opponents she had encountered in her life so strong that even when she used all her cards, she could only tie with him for a while.
Hence, she always wanted to challenge this Beastman who was strong enough for her to sense the hovering presence of Death.
Northern Warrior, Fearless and Dauntless!
“Your Majesty, the test is complete, we will now begin the official forging. In three days’ time, you will receive three sets of Extraordinary Level armor.”
Lide nodded, satisfied, and gave the Dwarf Forging Master a hearty encouragement, promising that if the forged Equipment made him satisfied, he would allow them to drink to their hearts’ content in the city’s tavern for three months without restriction.
Valen smiled so broadly that he could hardly close his mouth – the only tavern in the city belonged to the City Hall’s logistics department, and it was not cheap.
The tavern recently introduced a new brew called “Erguotou,” a supreme liquor designed by Lide himself, which Valen couldn’t get enough of. Unfortunately, the liquor was produced in small quantities. Now with this excuse, wouldn’t he be able to drink as much as he wanted?
After arranging the blacksmith’s work, Lide couldn’t be bothered to stay to watch them forge Equipment. He had seen it a few times and pretty much knew the routine – smithing was truly uninteresting.
Seeing Isa’s yearning gaze, Lide smiled slightly and took the hand of this long-unseen girl to start wandering through the streets of Dawn City.
Yes, it was an unprecedented move.
In the past, he always inspected the situation, observing the city’s development and people’s livelihood from the perspective of a ruler, never experiencing the city he built firsthand as a citizen.
But before doing so, he slightly altered his face.
Otherwise, as the god of the Dawn Sect and master of Dawn City, he would be stopped by countless Believers and residents shouting greetings at every three steps, which felt quite refreshing for the first one or two times but became uninspiring with repetition.
At this time, Betty also followed out, the Northern Land Valkyrie who adored this open and inclusive city.
Even after the strategic expedition to Dwarf Valley, had it not been for Isa still in Green City, she would have liked to stay a bit longer in Dawn City.
As for Kapp and Grot, these two guys, absorbed in their thoughts of Extraordinary Weapons, had already stayed behind to help at the blacksmith shop.
Compared to half a year ago, Dawn City had become much more prosperous, especially after the influx of a large population following the winter, which made the city even more thriving.
The last time Isa and Betty had come mainly for Lide, they hadn’t explored the city much. Now, following Lide, they immediately felt the joy they couldn’t experience in Green City.
The city was clean and tidy, without the stink of sewage or piles of garbage.
The residents smiled, their eyes filled with hope and light, and they were kind and polite to others.
The patrol team was strictly disciplined and loyally diligent; there was no extortion or bullying.
Having lived in the oppressive and hopeless city of Green City for too long, one would fall in love with Dawn City at first sight upon arrival.
The difference was too vast.
“Teacher, this candied haw is really delicious…”
“What is this, Liangpi? Such a strange name…”
“Teacher, why is it called Youtiao? It really smells so good…”
“This soup dumpling actually has soup inside…”
Food in Dawn City was previously very scarce; residents had only one main food staple for a long time – bread.
The City Hall struggled to resolve this issue for a while until Lide, inspired, came up with a brilliant idea.
He brought a variety of simple, easy-to-make, and extremely delicious foods from Earth to Dawn City.
This caused a curious phenomenon in this world of a Medieval European backdrop, where one could actually taste the delicacies exclusive to Huaxia.
How rich is Huaxia’s cuisine? If ordinary people ate three new dishes a day, from birth to death, they could not finish all the dishes.
Lide casually introduced dozens of classic snacks that immediately diversified the food on the streets of Dawn City.
Residents’ lives visibly improved.
Noodles, steamed buns, twisted dough sticks, pancakes, dumplings, baozi, cold noodles, wontons… and so on.
These simple snacks, which were not difficult to make and required simple ingredients, had now become another scenic highlight in Dawn City.
And the two girls beside him could not stop eating.
Originally, he thought Isa would be very happy, but in the end, Lide found that Betty was the happiest.
At that moment, the Northern Royal Family Valkyrie, who had slain a level 19 Molten Demon with two swords and possessed strength that soared through the heavens, was holding over ten kebabs in her left hand and two candied haws on a stick in her right, with her pinky hooked around a paper bag filled with soup dumplings, all while munching on a fried dough stick.
Her pitch-black eyes, which showed no fear even when facing a giant dragon, now sparkled with joy. Furthermore, they roamed around greedily looking for other delicacies.
Her greatsword was carelessly strapped to her back, making her appear the very picture of a food lover.
Lide could only laugh and cry at the sight. Where was the slightly arrogant, combat-power-off-the-charts Valkyrie? The contrast was just too great.
On the other hand, Little Isa’s eating manner was much quieter than Betty’s hearty enjoyment; she nibbled on the candied haws gently, but the smile on her face was equally radiant.
In the end, the three of them strolled from dusk until many shops were about to close, and the two girls ended their city tour reluctantly, though Lide realized they hadn’t even finished exploring one street…
As a level 16 warrior, Betty’s digestive speed was exceptionally fast. The food she consumed soon transformed into pure energy, hence her being the biggest eater. She would stop to try any new snack that she hadn’t had before or that looked even tastier than the last one she tried.
Moreover, many shopkeepers recognized Betty, who had lived in Dawn City for a while, and were exceptionally warm toward her, often giving her a large amount of delicious food for free.
On the other hand, Little Isa wasn’t as fortunate as Betty. With her stomach puffing out slightly under her mage’s robe, she kept stealing glances at Lide and would quickly suck in her belly and bend over to hide it whenever she noticed him looking, pretending nothing had happened.
Lide chuckled at the contrast between the two girls beside him. Today’s food tour was indeed delightful, seeing the city’s vibrant life force from the most grassroots perspective.
The Bloodline was also receiving unimaginable worship at the lowest layers of the city, whether patrolling Bloodline or those in human form. The residents respected them genuinely, not just a facade but heartfelt admiration.
This was quite rare. The happiness in the residents’ eyes and the free-moving silhouettes of the Bloodline on the streets reassured him that his efforts had not been in vain. Sustainable development strategies were indeed a timeless great plan.
He finally felt relaxed.
The high-intensity work over the past half month had kept him on edge, but now the delays brought about by his three-month slumber had been rectified in Dawn City.
So, the pressure on his mind eased as well.
In the following three days, Lide took time off to accompany Isa and Betty, touring every corner of Dawn City—even visiting a pig and horned-lizard breeding farm.
He also used this opportunity to inspect all of the city’s buildings and construction projects.
Overall, while the city had many shortcomings, everything was manageable, and the momentum of Dawn City’s development continued to rise rapidly.
The girls spent the days beaming with smiles, and for Lide, it was the first time in a long while he had enjoyed such relaxed moments with Isa.
Even Betty’s gaze toward Lide softened significantly, losing its previous stiffness.
Over those days, this new food lover became the most popular customer among all the shops in Dawn City.
Anything tasty was welcomed, and Betty’s way of eating made the shopkeepers believe their craft was perfect, gratifying their vanity to a great extent.
—
—
—
“Your Highness, the weapons have been forged…”
But all good things come to an end. On the morning of March 20th, Valen arrived at City Hall, bursting with excitement, unable to hide his internal thrill.
Three sets of Extraordinary Equipment, plus three Extraordinary Weapons—this was indeed a monumental task, which he had completed in just three days.
Valen could almost feel the threshold of the Forging Master Level loosening, giving him hope that, with more time, he could challenge the ultimate pinnacle—the Legendary Blacksmith.
Valen was excited, but upon hearing this, Betty did not show joy; instead, she felt a slight disappointment as she stealthily glanced at Lide sitting on the sofa.
The handsome figure in the black mage’s robe was dazzling.
The forging of the weapons meant they would have to return to Green City…
Returning to Green City meant no more of these unique snacks, no more carefree fun like the past few days…
Isa felt the same, glancing wistfully outside the window. These had been the happiest days of her life because Lide had been by her side.
The young girl wore a pure white semi-hollow fringed long dress made especially for her by the tailor’s shop at Lide’s request, with patterns of pristine white flowers, black calf-leather boots, and long white socks on her feet.
Her flaxen hair hung lightly behind her head, and her delicate face with skin as soft and fair as a baby’s complimented her sparkling red eyes—a goddess stepped right out of an anime world.
Lide sensed something off in the girls’ eyes and shook his head with amusement.
“If you like it, just come more often. My manor will always have rooms prepared for you.”
“Let’s go and see how our weapon forging is doing.”
“This time I will return to Green City with you.”
Hearing Lide’s comforting words, Betty’s mood inexplicably lifted, and she nodded slightly.
Isa looked at Lide with her little head tilted like a kitten, her heart brimming with satisfaction.
The blacksmith shop.
Kapp and Grott had already donned a full set of light silver armor and were holding silver greatswords in their hands.
Grott, after becoming a Bloodline, had grown even taller, reaching a staggering height of 2.3 blades, and Kapp, the Lion-man, was even more outrageous at 2.5 blades.
When Lide saw the two large figures clad in full armor, he felt a sense of height-induced oppression wash over him.
But immediately afterward, the two of them bowed deeply to Lide with their hands on their chests.
“Your Majesty, welcome.”
Lide nodded in satisfaction; the two sets of armor were designed in segments, akin to an enlarged version of fish scale armor, but the defense was significantly enhanced compared to the somewhat thin fish scale armor, allowing for very flexible movement.
The only drawback was their heavy weight, but for a Level 17 and a Level 18 warrior, this weight was nothing to worry about.
He curiously opened the attributes of the two sets of Extraordinary Armor.
“Lion Armor
Quality: Extraordinary★
Traits: Super strong physique (Physical recovery speed increased by 500%, physique increased by 200%)
Solid (Defense increased by 500%, with additional resistance to impact, corrosion, and piercing)
Super Resilience (Immune to Three Circle and lower magic, immune to mind-controlling skills, immune to Three Circle and lower negative states)
Extraordinary Traits: Auto-repair (Enchanted by a special Alchemy Array, capable of absorbing Magic Power to repair the armor), Tough texture (Can use energy to temporarily strengthen the texture of the armor in certain parts of the body, increasing its solidity)
Introduction: Extraordinary armor forged by Dwarf Forging Master Valen Barbaric Hammer, using Mithril and other precious materials.”
“Silver Greatsword
Extraordinary: ★
Traits: Armor-piercing (Destructive against armor, with a chance to sever weapons below Extraordinary Level)
Solid (Possesses the most unyielding blade, able to withstand higher levels of impact)
Sharp (Greatly increased killing power of the blade)
Auto-repair (Can automatically repair damage to the blade)”
“Northern Armor
Quality: Extraordinary★
Traits: Super strong physique, Solid, Super Resilience
Extraordinary Traits: Auto-repair, Tough texture
Introduction: Extraordinary armor forged by Dwarf Forging Master Valen Barbaric Hammer, using Mithril and other precious materials.”
“Silver Greatsword
Extraordinary: ★
Traits: Armor-piercing, Solid, Sharp, Auto-repair
Although the attributes of these two sets of armors were not as good as the Castro armor that had been enhanced with the Power of Faith, they were still quite decent.
However, what struck him as odd was that
The attributes of these two sets of armor and weapons were exactly the same, except for their names.
Curiously, he turned his head and looked at Valen, who was in high spirits, “Valen, why do these two sets of armor have such different designs, yet their attributes are exactly the same?”
Grott was a Northern Warrior; though strong, he still had a human form.
Kapp was different, being a member of the Lion-man Clan with a sturdy lion head that couldn’t possibly be the same as a human’s.
But for two pieces of armor, completely dissimilar in appearance to have the same attributes, this was quite peculiar.
Hearing Lide’s question, a deep sense of pride showed on Valen’s face.
“Your Majesty, this is a new idea that I came up with recently after combining the forging processes of the weapon factory, or rather a new forging method I have just developed.”
Oh? A new forging method?
Lide became interested.
“Tell me about it.”
Valen’s voice gradually became more enthusiastic.
“I’ve thoroughly studied the information you gave me about building factories and came to a very simple conclusion.
No matter how the factory produces, it must be assembled at the end.
The theory of factory-based production has been rapidly developing, and it inspired me greatly.
This time, I experimented with a new idea on these two sets of Extraordinary Weapons. Although the two sets of armor look different, I forged them at the same temperature, using the same materials, and then assembled them in the same way.
In the end, the situation I had imagined really occurred—two sets of armor with identical attributes, no matter how different their appearances.”
At this point, Valen became even more excited, “Your Majesty, the production of Extraordinary Equipment has a chance of failure, but after mastering this skill, we can ensure a 95% success rate in the large-scale, continuous manufacture of Extraordinary Equipment.”
Upon hearing this last sentence, Lide immediately opened his eyes wide.
“Large-scale, continuous manufacturing of Extraordinary Equipment??”
Is this dwarf defying the heavens?
This is even more significant than building a weapon factory.
In addition to excellent materials, the forging of Extraordinary Weapons also requires the blacksmith’s highly skilled forging techniques. Even for a forging master like Valen, the success rate of creating Extraordinary Equipment is only just over sixty percent.
That is to say, there is still more than a thirty percent chance of failure.
If what Valen said could be realized, then the implications would be completely different.
Although the armor forged in this way would have exactly the same attributes and would not have exceptionally good equipment attributes, the word “stable” alone would outweigh everything else.
In mass production, the most important thing often isn’t any special attributes, but simply stability.
“Are you sure??”
Looking at Lide’s excited yet serious gaze, Valen nodded firmly.
“Yes, Your Majesty, I have mastered the technique for mass producing Extraordinary Equipment.
We wouldn’t even need to reach Master Level, just Expert Level blacksmiths could use this method.”
Expert-Level blacksmiths?
Lide frowned.
“How many Expert-Level blacksmiths do we have now?”
“There are a total of 4… excluding myself, three dwarfs and one human.”
Four, that’s a bit few.
Lide shook his head, “How much material do we need to consume to forge a set of armor like this?”
“One set of armor requires raw materials worth thirty thousand Gold Pucks, plus another 40 pounds of Mithril…”
Valen’s voice trailed off with a lack of confidence.
Forty pounds of Mithril, that’s an astronomical figure.
Mithril’s market price is around 4000 to 5000 Gold Pucks per pound, so 40 pounds would be two hundred thousand Gold Pucks at the rate of 5000, plus another thirty thousand for other materials.
A single suit of Extraordinary Armor would cost a mere two hundred and thirty thousand Gold Pucks for materials alone.
The real hidden value is even higher, requiring thousands of Beastmen from the Dwarf Valley to mine for 20 days. The cost of sustaining thousands of Beastmen for those 20 days is also a large sum of money, and is dwarf craftsmanship worthless?
Thus, if one were to sell this suit of Extraordinary Armor, its value would be at least between three hundred to three hundred and fifty thousand Gold Pucks.
However, that’s if it were being sold. Here, the cost is merely thirty thousand Gold Pucks plus the labor of thousands of Beastmen for 20 days.
Completely worth it.
“No worries, Mithril is mined to be used, right? When the next batch of Mithril reserves reach a hundred pounds, you can continue forging equipment for other top combat forces.”
Lide was unconcerned, waving his hand. Utilizing such great effort to seize the Mithril vein was not for the sake of satisfying his vanity, but rather, transforming it into combat power is what needs to be done at this stage.
The situation outside has quietly changed, and Dawn City must now accelerate the improvement of its strength.
“Additionally, if you have other ideas, I’m willing to allow you to experiment with no more than fifty pounds of Mithril every three months.”
Lide spoke with an intense trust, his gaze burning as he looked at Valen, directly giving the Forging Master even greater autonomy.
Fifty pounds of Mithril allowance, that’s a material worth two hundred and fifty thousand Gold Pucks, enough to create ten thousand Alchemy Bombs, easily destroying the Black Wind Tribe of twenty thousand centaurs five times over.
Hearing this, Valen’s excited eyes were almost brimming with tears.
50 pounds of Mithril??!!
By the Forge God above, that’s 50 pounds!
The Barbarian Hammer Tribe’s output hadn’t been that much in three years.
At this moment, the elderly dwarf was deeply moved, as if ready to die for a kindred spirit, looking at Lide with reddened eyes.
“Your Highness, I will not let you down!!”
His tone was firm and laden with unshakeable resolve.
Lide’s lips curled into a radiant smile.
The longest road in this world is always the path of tricks.
This dwarf has probably long forgotten how he initially resisted Dawn City.
After resolving this affair, Lide gestured towards Betty, who was looking at them talk with great interest.
“Valen, what about Betty’s equipment?”
Valen was snapped out of his excitement and hurriedly signaled for others to bring out Betty’s gear from the storage.
A suit of armor appeared in front of Lide, slightly delicate yet flowing with sleek lines of black armor.
Handsome was Lide’s first impression of this ladies’ armor.
The pure black fabric reflected the unique cold luster of metal, while the dark silver patterns on it seemed both ancient and generous. The half-active buckle design made it wearable, and the delicate layout of the wrists and joints provided strength and beauty in abundance.
“Black Ice Armor (Female)
Quality: Extraordinary★★
Traits: Super Speed (Agility and speed increased by 500%, stamina consumption reduced by 50%)
Super Solidity (Defense increased by 500%, extra defensive power against impacts, corrosion, and piercing)
Super Resilience (Immune to Four Circle and below magic, immune to mind and chaos control abilities)
Black Ice Armor (Armor possesses powerful ice attributes, fire resistance increased by 1000%, and within a ten-blade radius attack and reaction speeds decrease by 1% every 10 seconds)
Extraordinary Traits: Auto-repair (Enchanted with a special alchemy array, capable of absorbing magic power to repair the armor), Solid Texture (Can use energy to temporarily strengthen armor’s texture in body parts, increasing solidity)
Introduction: Dwarf Forging Master Valen Barbaric Hammer forged this extraordinary armor from Mithril and other precious materials exclusively for ladies.”
“Black Ice Greatsword
Extraordinary:★★
Traits: Armor Penetration (Can easily break the opponent’s armor, with a chance to cut through weapons below Extraordinary level)
Solidity (Possesses a robust blade that can withstand Legendary Level impacts)
Sharpness (The sword blade’s killing power significantly increased)
Coldness (Every successful attack lowers the target’s attack speed and reaction speed by 1%)
Auto-repair (Can automatically repair the damaged blade)
Lide was somewhat surprised; this set of armor was much stronger than the previous two sets, not just because it had gone from one star to two, but also because it had an additional Black Ice Armor trait.
In a duel, it would surely be an advantage. Despite the diminishing trait not appearing significant, with enough time, the accumulated negative effects would definitively place the enemy at a disadvantage.
Moreover, although the attributes of the longsword were simple, it was still powerful, especially the Coldness trait paired with the armor made it all the more domineering.
Betty fell in love with the armor at first sight, stepping forward and putting it on directly under everyone’s gaze. Only a close-fitting jacket and trousers underneath, otherwise, it wouldn’t fit.
And once she donned the armor, Betty immediately caught Lide’s eye.
“Fearless and striking” was the best description for this wild Female Warrior.
With the black longsword in hand, Betty’s long hair slightly scattered behind her head, and her mixed-race features stood out, so beautiful it was hard to look away.
The black armor clung tightly to her lissome figure, radiating fervor and an innate wildness that provoked a desire for conquest.
“Not bad, not bad at all.”
The only disappointment was… there was absolutely no fullness to it.
Lide shook his head, wondering how he always ended up meeting such wealthy girls…
What’s with all the games being full of baby-faced bombshells??
The image of the owner of the Elvis Tavern in Green City suddenly popped into his mind, that 17th-Level Elf Archer with her surging waves.
The buttons would burst.
This is the right way to open a game…
“Kapp,” Lide reined in his wandering thoughts, forging weapons and equipment was complete, and organizing tasks was next, there was plenty of time to test the power of the experimental weapons, no need to rush it now.
His gaze shifted to the Beastman King.
“Leave immediately and return to Dwarf Valley.
You must be aware of the changes in the outside situation over the past half a year, Craig is now deep in Risier City, and it will be difficult for us to get news from Risier City through other channels in the short term.
You must send someone to investigate what the Beastman is up to in Risier City.”
The highly unusual behavior of the Beastman had been causing Lide unease, especially since he couldn’t contact Craig and Emi after using the Power of Faith.
Kapp, the true master of the Lion Tribe and 18th-Level Beastman King, Lide believed the other party could uncover the information he desired.
“Yes, Your Highness.”
Lide waved his hand and continued, “That’s not all. After you return, make contact with the former Lion Tribe, it would be best if you could take back control of your original tribe to prevent future troubles.
And, the Dwarves from Dwarf Valley have left no trace, be cautious.
The Secret Silver Vein is extremely important to Dawn City, we cannot afford to lose it.”
“As you wish, my master.”
Kapp responded once again.
Having given Kapp his orders, Lide looked towards Grote.
“Stanley has been confirmed not to be returning to Green City to manage the Dark Contract, but if you have any problems, you can contact him immediately.
The Dark Contract is our trump card in Green City, whether it’s purchasing raw materials or gathering intelligence, it has advantages unmatched by other factions.
With the current changes to the greater situation, you must act cautiously, with stability as your primary concern.
Also, you must pay attention to one more thing – the Dark Contract’s branch, Immortal Soul. The Undead from the Lost World have left the Main Plane for now, but they will inevitably return before long.
The strategy Stanley has adopted for them, you must carry it out firmly, and report back to me or Stanley in a timely manner if any issues arise.”
Grote stepped forward and bowed deeply.
“Yes, Your Highness, I will guard the Dark Contract with my life.”
After giving instructions to the two men, Lide looked at Valen, who was eagerly waiting for his share of tasks, and couldn’t help but smile.
This guy also wants to be assigned a couple of tasks?
“Valen, there’s no need for you to handle everything down to the last detail in the weapon factory. Once we open up the market in the Low Hill Ridges, our demand for weapons is going to explode.
During this time, you should recruit more apprentices to prevent production from being unable to keep up when demand increases.”
Valen immediately perked up.
“Yes, Your Highness, I guarantee I will accomplish your orders.”
“Furthermore, during this time, pass the technology for producing Extraordinary Armor to those four Expert-Level Forging Masters. I hope to have at least 20 Forging Masters learn it in the future.
We possess a massive Secret Silver Vein, and we will definitely see more Extraordinary Equipment in the future.”
“Your Highness, the Dwarves will not disappoint you.”
Valen said with confidence, head held high – in forging equipment, no one could outperform the Dwarves.
Lide nodded, having given all his directives.
He turned to look at Little Yisha beside him, gazing up at him with adoration, and he showed a doting smile.
“Let’s go, Yisha, we’re headed back to Green City.”
There was Harrison at City Hall, so there was nothing that needed his attention.
The Crimson Mage Tower seemed stable for now, but due to external changes, it was beginning to become dangerous, and he had to address these issues.
As Dawn City’s most important source of funds, the Crimson Mage Tower could not afford to fail.
The Undead who established an empire in the north, the Death Cemetery that transformed High-level Undead, the severely injured 19th-Level Great Mage Spark, the coast invaded by the Fishman Country with over a dozen harbor cities, the Crimson Mage Tower restrained by the scarcity of Magic raw materials…
As Lide flew out of Dawn City on Castro’s back, he keenly sensed that upon returning to Green City, the situation he would face would differ greatly from before.
