﻿Chapter 296: Chapter 298: First Contact (5600 words) Chapter 296: Chapter 298: First Contact (5600 words) “Master, I am very familiar with the aura on that scroll, I visited it over a thousand years ago…
It seems, that was a place where a Divine had fallen.”
Withered Bone, being an Undead Life, had lived for so long that it was beyond counting.
Even he had forgotten how long he had been alive.
Lide’s eyebrows slightly lifted when he heard this.
“A thousand years ago, a land where a Divine had fallen?”
The land where a Divine had fallen, just saying these words brought an inexplicable force, representing the most powerful beings in this world, excluded by the will of the Main Plane.
A land where even gods could fall was no simple place.
“Was there really a Divine that fell there? What level were you at that time? How did you get in?”
A series of questions plunged Withered Bone into contemplation; the fiery blue Soul Fire within its dragon skull flickered.
After a long while, he spoke, his voice hollow and carrying a peculiar tone.
“Master, in the ancient years beyond measure, I awakened as an Undead Life.
But for a long time after awakening, I was in a daze, the Soul Fire was very weak, and my thoughts were stiff.
I wandered around the world, instinctively searching for the aura of the undead to consume and strengthen my Soul Fire.
I hid in the darkness when the sun was high, and embarked on journeys during the night.
Thus passed the lengthy years, whether it was a hundred years or a thousand, I finally awakened to my own consciousness.
But because of this awakening, I sensed a certain calling, and in my ignorant state, I responded to that call.
Subsequently, I was summoned by a powerful force into that land where the Divine had fallen…”
Speaking up to this point, the blue Soul Fire inside Withered Bone’s skull burned even more intensely, like boiling oil dropped onto a fire.
But the radiance emitted by the Soul Fire was chillingly cold, void of any heat; Lide could even feel the temperature around himself drop by more than ten degrees.
Withered Bone had not yet finished speaking.
“I met the master who had summoned me, an Undead Mage, a powerful Undead Mage.
And the plane I was summoned to was the land where the Divine had fallen!
There, skeletons piled into mountains, black blood flowed like rivers, and resentful spirits covered the sky…”
Lide strangely felt a bit of fear from Withered Bone’s words, igniting his curiosity.
“This plane should be your favorite, why do you fear it?
Isn’t such a thick aura of death suitable for the survival of the undead?”
“Master, it’s different here, completely different…”
The fire of Withered Bone’s soul surged higher, and his tone carried a thicker note of fear.
“In this intense aura of death, there lies a supremely holy power, belonging to the Light God System.
Majestic, holy, and dazzling.
Even the intense power of death could not conceal it.
It was like—Divine.”
Withered Bone’s tone was incredibly solemn.
“Only a Divine could reveal such a dazzling force amid the omnipresent power of death.
And later events also confirmed my thoughts.”
“This land was a bloody battlefield.”
“Death Knight, Ghoul, Ghost, Skeleton Warrior, Zombie, Undead Mage, Ghost Dragon, Bone Dragon… every kind of undead troop present in this space.
And all these undead lives had but one target—a dazzling sky of light.
Inside the sky, thin like crystal, like a giant egg of a Demon Beast, was a Twelve-winged Blazing Angel…”
Lide’s eyes widened sharply. “A Twelve-winged Blazing Angel?!!”
In the legends he had collected about Divines, a Twelve-winged Blazing Angel was a Divine Life, with a combat power equivalent to a lesser Divine Power.
Such beings were amongst the most powerful warriors under the Light God System.
“What happened next? What became of that Blazing Angel?”
Withered Bone shook its head, “I was being controlled by that Undead Mage, preparing to attack, when suddenly a tremendous burst of brilliance lit up the land…
All the undead turned to ash under that brilliance.
Unsurprisingly, I was struck by the Light Power, my Soul Fire severely weakened, putting me directly into a prolonged sleep.”
“As for that Blazing Angel, by the time I awakened again, it had already vanished without a trace.”
As he spoke this, the fire of Withered Bone’s soul finally calmed a bit.
“I have long forgotten how long I slept, perhaps three hundred years, maybe three thousand.”
My consciousness returned once again, not only had the Blazing Angel vanished without a trace, but the entire plane had undergone a massive transformation.
The rivers composed of black blood had dried up, the ghosts that covered the sky had turned into flying ash, and all other forms of undead life had disappeared without a trace.
Only piles of white bones and the dense Power of Death remained.
At this point, the Withered Bone paused for a moment, soothed its emotions, and then continued.
“But in the thick aura of death, the power belonging to the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel still lingered, merged with the Power of Death into an unbelievable yet incredibly real scene.”
“I walked within it for thirty years… finally, I found a shattered spatial rift and barely managed to escape from that land where Divine beings had fallen.
This Bone Dragon was also found within there.
My Soul Fire absorbed Death Aura during that time and also absorbed a small amount of Light Energy, requiring a long time to purify the Soul Fire…”
Hearing this, Lide finally understood the origin of Withered Bone and the secrets of that divine fall site.
Even a Divine being like the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel had appeared.
Death Cemetery seemed quite extraordinary.
“After such a long time, are you sure that the aura on that scroll is from that world?”
“Yes, Master, my soul has slumbered there for countless years, and I am very sensitive to its aura.”
Lide nodded, looking at the gigantic creature before him, and his interest in that plane where the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel had appeared surged immensely.
Originally, Death Cemetery had attracted him for the Death Flower or other high-level Magic Scroll Making Skill, but now, Death Cemetery was obviously not so simple.
The treasures hidden inside might be far richer than he had imagined.
After confirming the information with Withered Bone, Lide did not hesitate any longer and had the Bone Dragon return to the Dimension Space; he then summoned Stanley and two others.
He shared Withered Bone’s information as soon as they met.
After hearing it, Stanley’s eyes filled with shock.
“Your Highness, the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel is the most powerful combat force within the Light God System.
I had not expected such a legendary being to be ambushed by the undead.
It is even highly possible that it fell.
Death Cemetery may contain treasures beyond our imagination.”
Not to mention, just finding a feather from an angel would be a huge gain, that alone would at least be a Legendary Item, and might even contain Divinity.
Of course, if Lide knew Stanley’s thoughts, he would be speechless, thinking all this effort just to pick up a feather??
“Prepare, we’re going to visit Death Cemetery in the north.”
Lide was never one to dawdle.
If it weren’t for Withered Bone, he would need to prepare intensely, but since they had a guide, just blundering through would suffice.
However, before heading out, Lide asked Betty to pause her preparations.
“Betty, after I take everyone and leave, there will be no one to guard the Crimson Mage Tower, and I need you to help me protect it.”
His dark eyes looked directly into Betty’s wild eyes.
“Isa and Vina both need your protection, especially now when Master Spark is seriously injured.”
The unmasked Betty fell silent for a moment, her distinctly contoured face resembling that of a mixed-race, now somewhat reluctantly, before going to war and adventure would be like taking a foodie’s meal away just before they began to eat.
But seeing Lide’s deep gaze, Betty turned her head with a slight reluctance and acknowledged.
“Hmm…”
Lide, seeing this wild Valkyrie act like a little girl, couldn’t help but laugh silently, instinctively reaching out as if he were treating Vina, touching the girl’s long hair.
Betty stiffened, turning her head slightly, her face flushing red as she saw Lide’s action.
Lide also sensed the slightly odd atmosphere but continued petting the soft hair before retracting his hand.
He inexplicably felt like he was teasing his stern female classmate when he was younger, a strange thrill overtaking him.
“Go back, wait for my return.”
Betty looked at Lide’s handsome and charming face with a subtle nod, then, with cheeks flushed, she turned and swiftly left.
The heroic Valkyrie at this moment seemed like she had been caught doing something naughty…
Once Betty left, Lide breathed a sigh of relief.
Getting Betty to return was partly because the Crimson Mage Tower really needed a powerful professional to guard it, especially when Spark was unable to watch over the Crimson Mage Tower.
On the other hand, this mission was extremely dangerous.
Anything related to gods was never simple.
Especially since Withered Bone explicitly stated that it was the battlefield where the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel had once been besieged by the undead.
No one knew what still existed inside.
So this time, he didn’t plan to take too many with him, Stanley, Grote, Withered Bone, Castro, including himself, three Bloodline plus two other life forms would be enough.
Both he, Grote, and Stanley possessed the ‘Rebirth in Blood’ Skill, so even facing great threats, he would be unafraid.
Withered Bone had once slumbered and wandered in that plane, an indispensable guide.
Castro possessed extraordinary armor, and his flying speed had surpassed the speed of sound, allowing him to escape battles he couldn’t win, provided he did not act recklessly.
Only Betty, despite her great strength, lacked many escape skills once trapped, and after death, she could not resurrect.
Thus, Lide promptly sent away this valkyrie of overwhelming combat prowess.
For he had planned for the worst-case scenario when preparing to execute this plan.
“Stanley, arrange the following tasks, have Dawn’s Shadow enter a lurking state, and cease all intelligence-gathering activities.
Grot, send a message to Wales and ask him to look after the Dark Contract for a while; I believe my disciple will be more than happy to comply.
Additionally, inform Dawn City of our actions; Harrison will prepare the necessary contingency plans.”
Lide’s thoughts were calm as he arranged the upcoming tasks without any rash actions.
He was not alone now; he governed a vast force whose every move could impact the fate of countless people.
He was the sole core of Dawn City, anything might go wrong, but not him.
His upcoming expedition to the Death Cemetery to explore the site of a Divine’s fall was fraught with danger; logically, as the most substantial boss, Lide should not risk it.
However, the treasures contained within were too astonishing, and he couldn’t feel at ease without leading the team himself.
Moreover, his indomitable resurrection Talent also gave him the capital to take risks.
And exploring an area filled with mystery was certainly tempting for him.
“Yes, my lord.”
Grot and Stanley answered in unison.
That same night, small bats continuously flew out of the Black Rose Manor.
Various forces under Dawn City also entered into a Level 1 alert state upon receiving Lide’s orders.
Dawn City’s Think Tank had developed dozens of strategic plans for various scenarios such as war, plague, disaster, flood, or foreign invasions.
Among those was a plan for how Dawn City should operate during a period if Lide were to enter a transformational slumber or couldn’t lead Dawn City due to other reasons.
These were the plans Lide had commanded the Think Tank to prepare; always contemplating the worst, the world never lacked threats, and effective preemptive plans were much better than those hastily formed in response to an emergency.
Once Lide’s message spread, everything operated along its intended trajectory, again proving the superiority of the system he had established.
A day later.
As dusk neared.
In a desolate and dilapidated city far from Green City, on the border region, Lide, carried by Castro, slowly descended onto the central square of this city.
Desolate, barren, and in ruins.
These were Lide’s immediate impressions of the city.
The surrounding tall stone buildings had already shattered due to wars or were overgrown with cobwebs due to neglect.
Lonely, miserable.
This city was the large border city of Sorins City in the southern province, bordering the now Undead Empire of the Radiant Empire.
The once-thriving city had turned into a ghost town due to the Undead invasion.
Every resident of the city, regardless of age, gender, or race, had turned into Undead life the moment the city walls were breached.
On the empty streets, not even corpses remained, only in some corners could one find those shattered skeletons.
After releasing his spiritual power and sensing for a while, Lide shook his head.
Indeed, there was no longer any sign of life here.
He turned his head toward the two adventurers, Markli and his brother, a Level 5 caster, who had been thrown to the ground by Castro.
“Markli, have you explored this city, and is there anything special here?”
The two adventurers, with Withered Bone flying in the sky above, Lide in front, and Stanley and Grot blocking the way behind, though no longer bound by chains, still had no ability to resist.
“My lord, no, this is a ghost town.” Markli, now wearing a black robe, still spoke weakly.
Lide frowned slightly, “Then why did you make us detour here?”
“In this city… there is, there’s that pouch…”
“A pouch?”
“Yes, the pouch containing Magic Scroll Making Skill…”
“Such important things, and you just threw it away?”
“My lord, the pouch was too old. We moved into this city for a night immediately after coming through that space rift with the main force.
At that time, we had the members of the adventurer’s guild examine it, and that pouch didn’t seem valuable, just a nearly-rotten pouch.
I thought, if we were to enter that Land of Death again, that pouch might be of help to you.”
Lide looked at Markli, rather surprised; this adventurer was quite meticulous.
“Very well, lead the way properly. If you can find what I am looking for this time, I will allow you all to leave and will also see to it that the Heart-eating Demon no longer holds you accountable.”
After saying this, his tone became very profound as he looked at the two adventurers, “Believe me, I never lie…”
At this moment, Lide’s face did not show the slightest blush.
Stanley, who was behind him, fell into an inexplicable silence upon hearing these words.
My lord, is it really okay for you to say that?
He was reminded once again of Wales screaming about wanting to become Lide’s disciple…
“Thank you, my lord, thank you. I swear on my life that I shall serve you with all my might.”
Currently, Lide still bore the appearance of Lord Ilo, and this adventurer had personally witnessed how Lide made the Heart-eating Demon, his nightmare, kneel.
Now, Lide’s promise was his lifeline.
The weak never have a choice; other than humbly pleasing Lide and begging for his mercy, he had no other option.
“Come with me… that leather pouch is in a small alley just outside the square…”
After twists and turns, it took twenty minutes for the two to retrieve the severely damaged leather bag. The Withered Bone became excited the moment it caught the scent on it.
“Master, it is this scent. It’s stronger than that on the scroll, a mixture of the Power of Death and a faint Light Power.
It’s the Land of God’s Demise!!”
Hiss, the Land of God’s Demise?? Markli and the Spellcaster looked at each other, shock written all over their faces.
What on Earth? That Ancient Ruin was that significant?
At this moment, both of them felt a resurgence of regret; had they known this would happen, why would they have ventured inside?
“Let’s go.”
Lide turned abruptly, not willing to waste any more time.
“Keep leading the way, Markli. Remember, your fates are in your own hands.”
“Yes, my lord.”
Markli was so frightened by the Bone Dragon’s words that he didn’t dare to disobey.
Huff~ Huff~
Moments later, Castro took off, this new ruler having Stanley and Groot sitting behind him, with both his claws holding the two adventurers.
Lide sat on the Withered Bone.
Beside the Withered Bone, a Mage’s Hand was holding the severely damaged leather pouch. It was called a leather pouch, but its material had decayed so significantly that it was unclear what it was originally made from.
However, Lide didn’t intend to delve deeper; the scent on the broken leather pouch was enough to lead the Withered Bone to that Plane.
The group continued flying towards the border.
When the last trace of twilight disappeared across the horizon and moonlight spread across the ground, Lide’s attributes madly increased.
Suddenly, the flying Withered Bone momentarily paused and hovered.
“My lord, we’ve arrived at the Death Cemetery.”
Arrived?
The continually meditating Lide behind the Withered Bone slightly opened his eyes, and instantly, a surprising scene unfolded before him.
Moonlight flowed like water from the night sky, the cold light gently touching the earth, filling the world with a light silver hue.
Not far in front, a clear demarcation line appeared; to the left, the land lit by moonlight, and to the right, a vast black curtain.
The black curtain stood tall like a sheer glacier, towering into invisibility, thick fog swirling within.
Like a sandstorm approaching, the black curtain was devoid of any light, the moonlight seeming to be absorbed upon touching it.
Lide, observing this spectacular scene, was somewhat astonished. The Death Cemetery, just from the name, he originally thought it was merely a cemetery, but this display seemed a bit exaggerated.
At that moment, the distant, towering vertical black curtain suddenly shook.
Several shadows flapped their wings and flew out from behind the curtain.
As those figures exited the curtain, darker than the fog, and instantly stepped into the moonlit area,
Lide, not far from the black curtain, clearly discerned the figures.
Eyes met eyes.
Seeing those five or six figures flapping demon-like flesh wings, Lide showed a hint of surprise in his eyes.
“Bloodline??”
Those figures emerging from the black curtain were not humans or other creatures, but Bloodlines he hadn’t expected.
And they weren’t the Bloodlines under his command; the aura inside them clearly belonged to a different Bloodline clan.
Lide instantly became interested; this was his first encounter with a Bloodline outside the Holy Light Bloodline since he had arrived in Glory.
Spreading his bat wings, he slowly moved towards those several Bloodlines under everyone’s watchful eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 297 - 297 299 Forceful Suppression I Saw an Angel
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 297: Chapter 299: Forceful Suppression, I Saw an Angel (7200 words) Pure Combat Chapter Chapter 297: Chapter 299: Forceful Suppression, I Saw an Angel (7200 words) Pure Combat Chapter PS: From now on, you don’t need to wait for updates; you can look again the next morning. I’ll try to be as early as possible, but sometimes I’m too slow to make changes, sorry~
Also, I want to thank our new alliance hierarchs born in the last two days—”Very Bewildered Jiu, Jiu Yue,” “RuiRui is Taken,” and “Xiao Wang Pays to Read the Official Version.” Thank you all,
I still owe you chapters and now I owe new ones too. I have to become a ruthless typing machine,
>_
——
——
——
——
Main Text
——
——
The black sky was like an abyss that separated the heavens and the earth, and the vampires flapping their bat wings outside the sky curtain seemed like demons crawling out from the depths of the abyss.
Especially since they bore the obvious signs of a fierce battle, these few vampires were infused with a heart-trembling aura.
Lide took off from behind the bone dragon, flapping his wings, his dark and deep pupils measuring these kin with interest. It was his first encounter with any other Bloodline outside of the Holy Light Bloodline.
At this moment, he was quite curious.
These vampires didn’t look much different from each other, with a pair of fleshy bat wings flapping on their backs making a whooshing sound.
Handsome faces, slender figures, sharp tusks in their mouths, and crimson eyes with blood-chilling bloodlight in them.
But unlike the Holy Light Bloodline, the pupils of these other clan vampires were full of cruel murderous intent and the scent of blood.
Moreover, these vampires were exuding enmity, incredibly intense enmity.
Lide hadn’t even approached them when the five vampires’ icy intent to kill was like a knife grazing over his skin.
It seemed to warn him that one more step would face the cruelest of strikes.
Lide’s flying speed paused, his wings now still; he simply floated in mid-air, his gaze intense as he watched the five wary vampires in front of him.
He was considering how to deal with these obviously troublesome kin.
Marse Sari looked at this Bloodline vampire with an air of familiarity yet complete strangeness, his expression gravely solemn.
As the clan leader of the Sari Clan, he had come to this death cemetery in search of some high-level magic materials.
But he hadn’t expected the death cemetery to be extremely dangerous, and most of the over twenty Bloodline members he brought had been lost inside.
The terrible crisis had forced him to exit this mysterious and unknown dark sky curtain.
But unexpectedly, upon leaving, he encountered fellow clan members.
However, Marse Sari wasn’t feeling any closeness; instead, he immediately sensed a huge threat.
Because this unknown Bloodline actually enslaved a terribly imposing bone dragon, and also had an unidentified demon beast clad in armor.
What was more exaggerated was that there were two level 15 Bloodline vampires in the air approaching him.
Marse’s hairs on his back stood up.
Just after losing a large number of hands, to encounter five combatants of level 15 and above directly outside filled him with dread.
He felt he had entered an extremely dangerous state, with crisis looming over him.
“I am Kachar, clan leader of the Holy Light Bloodline, and I mean you no harm.”
Holy Light Bloodline?
Marse frowned slightly. What a strange name; why would the noble Bloodline add the words ‘Holy Light’ in front of it? Those damn and stinking lights should have been swallowed by the night long ago.
Marse glanced subconsciously back at the black sky curtain.
If it came to it, he could only run away.
As for this vampire in front of him who posed a huge threat to him, there was no way he could trust him.
A joke, since when were Bloodlines so kindly and friendly to one another?
If it was him with such great power encountering a Bloodline that came back from a dangerous place, whose strength was far inferior to his own, he would definitely strike without mercy.
Because the other party might carry treasures found from dangerous places.
As for why hunt his own kin… does he need a reason?
As the purest of dark life forms, the Bloodline’s eternal pursuit is interest. As long as there is sufficient interest, it’s all fair game to do anything.
“Clan leader of the Holy Light Bloodline, I am Marse Sari, clan leader of the Sari Clan. Please tell me why you are blocking our path.”
Even though Marse was full of hostility, he could only suppress the malice in his heart. They were at a disadvantage, the ones with lesser strength.
If he dared to act, the one to end miserably would certainly be them.
Lide looked at the several vampires opposite him, their eyes brimming with hostility and caution, squinting slightly.
Interesting.
After pondering for a moment, he shook his head.
It seemed there wasn’t much room for niceties between Bloodline clans. Everyone was just a fox from the same mountain, no tall tales to chat about.
Bloodlines distinguish their clans by their surnames. The Bloodline that Lide was in charge of was publicly known as the Kachar Clan.
Of course, now under his reforms, the name Holy Light Bloodline became more known and accepted, especially with the development of Dawn City and the addition of new Bloodlines; everyone in Dawn City’s Bloodline had an explosive sense of belonging to the Holy Light Bloodline.
The relationship between different Bloodline clans was extremely cold, barely different from that of other dark life forms.
Scenes of interdependence and care like those shown by dwarves and humans are impossible for Bloodlines. It’s rare for two different clan Bloodlines to meet without starting a fight.
That’s why—although Bloodlines have tremendous potential, they have never been able to stir up a storm in the main plane of Glory—the reason is here.
Lack of unity.
Bloodlines are like wolf packs living in the wilderness: fierce, brutal, powerful. But wolf packs from different clans will always be hostile to each other, even fighting over food, their battles often more ferocious than their hunts.
As thoughts flowed through his mind, Lide subtly changed his attitude towards these vampires.
“Marse Sari, you just came out from the death cemetery. I need to know the information you have,” he said.
They all looked somewhat rough, their breaths in disarray, clearly having gone through a fierce battle.
And the vampire at the forefront was a level 16 existence.
Marse Sari
Title: Bloodthirster (After consuming enough blood, power and physical recovery speed increase by 300%, entering a bloodthirsty state, each attack inflicting bleeding, weakened, and lethargy states on the enemy, immune to pain, and immune to mental and instant death abilities below the transcendent level.)
Age: 327
Level: 16
Profession: ??
Talent: ??
Bloodline: Third Generation Sari Clan Bloodline
Introduction: A powerful vampire who revels in devouring blood and slaughter. It’s best not to encounter him in the night.
There are not many attributes visible on the attribute panel, and Lide couldn’t assess the exact strength of his opponent, but reaching Level 16 was indicative of many things.
Upon hearing Lide’s words, Marse’s crimson eyes slightly narrowed, and the bat wings behind him flapped with a whoosh.
“You have no right to command me, Clan Leader of Kachar.”
This guy… has some nerve.
But I like that kind of nerve.
Lide’s eyes slightly narrowed as well, and the aura around him began to slowly rise; the magic power around him gathered rapidly like the tides.
The vampire opposite him wasn’t some kind of benevolent lifeform, but coincidentally, neither was he.
Since both are foxes of the same mountain, there was no need for any so-called benevolence or morality.
Power is justice, an eternal and unchanging truth.
Moreover, he hadn’t yet fought a powerful member of his own race…
Lide’s expression turned colder, causing Marse’s heart to chill instantaneously.
He felt a significant change in Lide’s attitude and, for some unfathomable reason, began to regret the words he had just said; seeming to confront this person appeared to be an incredibly foolish act.
“Command you? I had no such intention, but now, I’ve changed my mind.
Marse Sari,
the Night Goddess says that power is the only and eternal pursuit of life in the darkness.
I’ll give you a chance to fight me one on one; if you win, I’ll let you leave.
But if you fail, you and the members of the Sari Clan will all follow me to explore this Death Cemetery.”
As he spoke, a fervor rose in Lide’s eyes.
Although he knew the Holy Light Bloodline to be very strong, he was unsure of their standing within the Bloodline race.
This Level 16 vampire before him was obviously a good reference.
Level 16 was a bit low, but it would barely suffice.
If Marse knew Lide’s thoughts at that moment, he would certainly spew a mouthful of blood.
A Level 15 challenging a Level 16 and merely using it as a reference for his own combat power, and it still being barely enough? What a joke.
As soon as Lide had finished speaking, Stanley and Grot immediately dispersed, their flapping bat wings subtly cutting off several vampires’ escape routes to the Dark Sky.
At the same time, Withered Bone began high-altitude patrolling, with the pale blue Soul Fire burning fiercely within its skull, those hollow eye sockets watching the vampires.
Castro, clad in Extraordinary Armor, took control of the area below, with a cruise state so fast that no one could escape.
A full encirclement.
Lide’s words were firm commands, not a negotiation with Marse.
He was used to issuing orders.
Whether you listen or not, that’s on you, but my commands must be executed.
“I wonder how you measure up to the Blood Mages or Crimson Hunters, those elite professions exclusive to the Holy Light Bloodline?
Don’t disappoint me.”
Lide muttered to himself, and the aura he emitted suddenly surged. The majestic presence felt like the collapse of mountains and the howl of ocean waves.
Bloodline shackles, unsealed.
The true form of the Bloodline emerged, with dark red and excessively handsome bat wings flapping behind him. His eyes shone like the most brilliant rubies, capable of intoxicating any onlooker of the opposite sex.
His sharp fangs revealed, complemented by a face handsome to the extreme, both bewitching and domineering.
At this moment, Lide’s appearance had broken through the ceiling of handsomeness, so even Withered Bones, who lacked much in the way of human aesthetics, had to admit his beauty.
The Bloodline of the Blood Clan Ancestor activated.
Powerful strength erupted like magma, and with every heartbeat, his body grew stronger.
Under the overwhelming aura of Lide, the air became viscous like mercury.
Facing Lide’s might, Marse’s expression changed dramatically. He felt as though he was being targeted by an Evil Dragon capable of tearing the earth apart, and that in the next second he would be devoured by the irresistible force.
Lide exuded an aura that made Marse’s heart tremble with fear.
“Wait, I…”
Marse had just begun to speak when Lide no longer gave him the chance to continue.
The true form of the Bloodline, with wings flapping, suddenly disappeared from the spot.
Instant Teleportation.
In the blink of an eye, Lide had closed the distance from hundreds of blades away to merely twenty from Marse.
When Lide reappeared before Marse, in his hands he had already conjured two Blazing Fireballs imbued with terrifying energy.
Whoosh whoosh~
The fireballs, trailing long tails of flames, drew a scorching arc across the night sky and arrived in an instant.
Marse’s complexion tightened. Half a second before the two fireballs could strike him, he disappeared from the spot just like Lide had.
But the four Bloodline members behind him hadn’t expected the attack to come so swiftly and didn’t have time to react.
Boom~
A tremendous roar exploded, and the air was swirled up by a wave of intense heat.
The four vampires, barely at level 10, were blown away by the exploding fireballs, blood splattering everywhere, their presence immediately weakened.
Grote and Stanley now moved swiftly forward, and under the full suppression of power, the few vampires had no room to resist and were forcefully subdued by the two Crimson Hunters.
At this moment, Marse, flapping his bat wings, appeared behind Lide just as the fireballs exploded.
The level 16 vampire’s hands shone with a crimson light, and thick Magic Fluctuations stirred around him.
Lide swiftly turned to face Marse thirty blades away, but just as he was about to take his next action, his body suddenly stiffened.
In that instant, he had lost control of his body.
Then the fireball that Lide’s right hand had just conjured was pressed against his face by his own numb and rigid arm.
The scene was extremely eerie, as if Lide, having conjured the fireball, intended to commit suicide.
A spell’s Name suddenly flashed in Lide’s mind—Four Circle Magic, Control Puppet.
But just as the fireball in his hand was about to touch his face, Lide’s eyes abruptly opened wide, and Magic Power surged from him like an inexhaustible source of magic energy.
The sheer force expelled the odd magic power, and he regained control of his body.
Marse, noticing that in less than two seconds Lide had broken free from the control, couldn’t hide the shock in his eyes.
“How is this possible?!! Control Puppet can’t maintain control even for two seconds?!!”
“It’s really quite sudden,” Lide said, a cold arc forming at the corner of his mouth.
Sure enough, a vampire of Level 16 is not to be underestimated; I nearly capsized in the gutter.
He immediately upgraded the threat level of Marse to high-level.
Marse’s shock was but a fleeting moment; the second spell he cast was uninterrupted, allowing no time for Lide to react.
Marse’s body shone with a bright red light, and then Lide suddenly felt the blood in his body congeal, followed by a frenzied boiling sensation, as if it would burst through his pores.
It felt as though he was about to explode.
“Blood Control?” For the first time, Lide experienced the power of Blood Clan Magic, the tearing pain making his ruby-like eyes shine even more brilliantly.
“No, it’s not nearly as powerful as Blood Control; at most, it’s just manipulating the blood.”
“To use the magic of the Bloodline against me? How naive.”
Lide extended his right hand, and under Marse’s shocked gaze, a thick crimson energy emanated from his body, and then he clenched his fist slightly.
Tzila~ The crimson energy dissipated in the air like flames.
The blood within Lide’s body instantly calmed, and the force controlling him was forcibly expelled.
But Marse’s complexion changed drastically; the Level 16 vampire felt an undeniable terror as his blood started to boil in an instant.
However, he didn’t have Lide’s resilience; with a splatter, his boiling blood burst forth, spraying out from his pores in a gruesome bloodbath that bloomed like a flower of blood in the air.
Huff huff~
Just as Lide was about to blast the opponent to pieces, Marse’s body, with a whoosh, transformed into dozens of small bats.
The energy that had controlled his blood also disappeared in that instant, with no way to maintain control.
This method of response was a revelation for Lide, who had relatively little combat experience.
Huff~ In just one second, the swarm of bats coalesced back into the form of Marse.
Clearly, this battle-hardened vampire wasn’t going to be so easily defeated.
Tzila~
The moment Marse’s body recovered, a burst of lightning erupted from his hands.
The crimson lightning energy struck towards Lide at an uncanny angle.
With a strong combat instinct sensing the oncoming crisis, Lide shifted in mid-air, slicing through the air three times with a whoosh.
The crimson lightning ripped through the skies, trailing a scarlet light.
Sensing the pervasive scent of blood in the air, Lide’s mouth formed a sharp arc while he gathered his magic once more.
His body disappeared from its original spot, stepping into the Dimension Space.
Shadow Blade, a specialized skill of the Bloodline.
At that moment, Marse’s vigilance surged, and his body flung backward, his bat wings furiously flapping.
Just as he had moved a little more than ten blades’ distance away, Lide’s body reappeared out of nowhere, and space shattered like a spider’s web.
At that time, a bubbling, magma-like, blazing fireball had already formed in his hands.
Huff huff~
The Magma Fireball, with its velocity of hundreds of blades per second, left Marse with no chance to dodge, as two Four Circle Spells approached bearing a lethal aura of death.
Bang~
The explosion tore through the sky; flames erupted, and in the night, it was as if two small suns had risen, searingly hot and bright, visible from tens of kilometers away.
The center of the explosion looked as if space itself had twisted, the exaggerated temperature making the surroundings seem like they had entered a massive furnace.
But at that moment, Lide felt no joy, for he could sense that the Level 16 vampire had not died.
Gurgle gurgle~
It was like bubbles forming in boiling water; in the center of the explosion, a blood pool over ten blades wide materialized.
The blood pool was extremely peculiar, hazy and veiled in black, as if it wasn’t really existing within the main space.
Seconds after the Magma Fireball explosion, the pool swiftly flowed and shaped itself into a human figure, like a sculpture freshly cast from plasma.
Marse’s figure re-emerged where the blood pool had coalesced.
Pool of Blood could transform into a blood pool that merged with the plane to dodge damage.
A hint of surprise appeared in Lide’s eyes.
This vampire had some tricks up his sleeve. He had never heard of this skill before.
Though his thoughts were active, the Magic Power in his hands did not pause for a moment; in less than a second, two spells formed once again, Fireball Technique and Thunderstorm Skill.
Crackle~
Magic broke through the air. Marse, who had just recovered his true vampire form, immediately sensed the approach of the two spells, causing his expression to change once more.
Why is this bastard able to cast spells so damn fast??!
There was no time for him to ponder, as he gritted his teeth and managed to release a Second Circle Mage Shield within 0.5 seconds.
However, the power of two Third Circle Spells was not something a Second Circle spell could withstand.
Boom~
The first to burst forth was the lightning, with flashes filling the sky like silver snakes tearing apart the heavens.
The Mage Shield shattered instantly; it offered no resistance at all.
The second Third Circle Spell, Fireball Technique, slammed into Marse’s chest.
A muffled explosion sounded, flames erupted, and a vile stench of seared flesh permeated the air.
Yet, Lide did not wait for the outcome; his hands cast spells simultaneously.
Small Fireball Skill flew out at a rate of 0.1 seconds a piece, and these fireballs were even infused with the Power of Crimson by Lide.
Already renowned for his casting speed, the Small Fireball had become even more formidable after Lide reached Level 15, with its casting speed undergoing a qualitative enhancement.
His hands were like dual gatling guns, the dense mass of fireballs drew a scorching line across the sky, forming a chain of nine stars, a chain of a hundred stars.
The sight was extraordinarily spectacular.
Boom boom boom~
Now, with a Small Fireball every 0.1 seconds, and with Dual Casting, twenty Small Fireballs could be released in one second.
Twenty shots per second – the real fireball gatling started up.
Although the Small Fireball Skill itself was not that powerful, after being imbued with the Power of Crimson by Lide, its might increased several folds.
Power of Crimson (Passive: All attacks carry the Power of Crimson, causing armor break, chaos element and corrosive damage, with 30% of damage dealt converted to one’s own life.)
Ratatatata~
If there was a soundtrack, the scene at this moment would be especially sensational.
Small Fireballs erupted on Marse, causing a great commotion.
Endless flames exploded in the air, amidst the fiery red diffused with an alluring crimson, appearing both fierce and bewitching.
Scorching heat, stinging pain—Marse, despite relying on the vampire’s strong regenerative ability and the inherent magic resistance of his talent, barely withstood a wave of damage.
But it was too intense.
He never imagined the opponent’s Bloodline would be so formidable, so unreasonable.
What the hell kind of spell is this??
Why does it last so long??
Marse shielded his head with both hands as a bloody aura enveloped his body, hoping to fend off that lethal assault.
But it was all in vain.
Too frightening—the relentless, fierce attacks were nightmarish.
The damage from the fireballs was secondary; the intense corrosion from the crimson energy made his flesh decay.
He couldn’t resist or defend against it.
Gritting his teeth fiercely.
Whoosh—Marse’s body twisted in an indescribable state, then dissolved like a droplet of water, and reformed into a pool of blood.
The Pool of Blood, the most potent life-saving skill, emerged once more.
Whoosh whoosh whoosh—
The fireballs formed a line, but without a target, the magic was like a Gatling gun firing blanks, with one fireball after another shooting toward the distant sky, trailing a magnificent long line.
Lide frowned upon sensing the disappearance of his target and ceased casting.
Sure enough, that elusive and unattackable pool of blood reappeared before his eyes.
“This skill is way too weird and creepy…”
He was somewhat incredulous, and the magic power in his hands gathered again, with two Four Circle Magic Magma fireballs taking shape in just a couple of breaths.
Whoosh—
Boom—
The fireballs exploded, and the fierce magic energy caused the surrounding light to warp severely.
But still, it had no effect; that pool of blood remained aloft like a veiled imprint in the sky, impervious to any real harm.
Lide’s brows twitched, he waved his hand, and the space before him shattered—Three Circle Magic—Void Walk.
Moments later, he reemerged, unable to sense any presence of the other in the void.
Lide took a deep breath and vanished on the spot like a droplet into the sea, making use of the vampire-specific Talent Skill, Shadow Blade.
But in less than three seconds, Lide reappeared again.
Even within the Dimension Space, he could not detect the presence of that level 16 vampire.
Looking at the bubbling pool of blood in the sky, Lide was truly surprised. What kind of skill was this, that it was truly unattackable and undetectable?
After some thought, he gathered his magic power again, and a Magic Model that he had never used before started to revolve in his mind.
Four Circle Magic—Forbidden Skill, a potent spell capable of suppressing magic, silencing, and preventing mages from casting.
It took Lide a full ten seconds to cast this spell, even with the amplification of all his Talent Specializations.
Whoosh—
As the Magic Model for the Forbidden Skill kicked into gear, the magic power within a thousand-blade radius was locked down.
The magic, which normally flowed like water, instantly froze, and while a caster can swim through water, they certainly can’t walk through ice.
The surrounding Stanley and his companions instantly felt the pressure of being locked down, their originally easygoing expressions turned serious, and even the flight speed of the Withered Bones high above slowed down.
Forbidden Skill does not discriminate between friend and foe.
But the pool of blood still hardly reacted, simply occupying a piece of sky like a crimson ink blot, impervious to attack or further detection.
A full thirty seconds later, just when Lide thought the Forbidden Skill had no effect.
The magic-deprived pool of blood suddenly began to roil intensely, and after several tumultuous boils, it once again assumed Marse’s form.
But at the very moment the level 16 vampire regained his human form, a figure wielding a long blade appeared before him.
Marse saw Lide nearing him, less than three blades away, with an uncontrollable flicker of terror in his eyes.
Just as he thought to act, it was already too late.
Boom—
Splatter—
The long blade swung, and blood sprayed.
When casting, Lide was a relentless barrage of magic bullets, the supreme spellcaster.
In close combat, possessing the Talent Skill Slaughter Hand, which boosted all his Combat Skills to the Extraordinary Level, made him virtually invincible in equal-level encounters.
Bam bam bam—
Lide didn’t intend to kill this level 16 vampire outright.
But he wasn’t going to let him off easy either; under the gaze of all, Marse was mercilessly beaten by him for twenty minutes.
For the first time, this vampire tried the formidable close-combat abilities of the Bloodline.
If it weren’t for Marse relying on the exaggerated regenerative capabilities of the Bloodline, he would have been beaten to death by Lide by now.
When Lide stopped, Marse lay on the ground with broken bones and covered in blood, looking up at him with terror-filled eyes.
At this moment, the life force of the level 16 vampire was as frail as a candle in the wind, on the verge of being extinguished.
Lide unceremoniously sealed the power within him with magic energy.
“Now, I think you won’t have any more questions.”
Marse, feeling the erupting lava-like strength in Lide’s body, coughed up another mouthful of blood.
At this point, his heart was filled with despair. Why was this vampire so strong??
The Bloodline presence this Bloodline revealed was merely level 15. Suddenly, as if something dawned on him, Marse weakly lifted his head, his feeble voice imbued with disbelief.
“Are you, are you possibly a member of the Kachar Clan Bloodline?”
The closer to the first generation Bloodline power the common Bloodline’s is, the stronger they are.
To defeat him at level 15 without much effort, probably only a Bloodline with a purer ancestry.
Lide did not respond to this, as the weak do not have the privilege of choice.
“You no longer have the right to know about this.
Now, answer me, what did you encounter within the Dark Sky that you bear signs of battle?”
Lying on the ground, extremely weak, Marse looked up with a surge of intense fear at the question.
His voice trembled weakly.
“We saw an Angel inside…”

chapters.title: Chapter 298 - 298 300 Exploring the Sinister and Terrifying
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 298: Chapter 300: Exploring the Sinister and Terrifying Land (6000 words) Transitional Chapter Chapter 298: Chapter 300: Exploring the Sinister and Terrifying Land (6000 words) Transitional Chapter “What did you encounter under the Dark Sky, and why are there signs of battle on you?”
Marse’s weak voice trembled.
“We met an angel inside…”
Met an angel??
This shocked Lide.
How could this be possible? Hadn’t that angel disappeared long ago?!!
It had vanished during the era of the Withered Bone attribute, thousands of years ago; had that angel returned now?
Lide took a deep breath, this news was critical, if it were true, then their current plans needed immediate revision.
“Where did you encounter the angel? In the Death Cemetery or some other Dimension Plane?”
Marse spoke faintly, fear unhideable in this Level 16 Vampire’s eyes.
“We encountered a temporary spatial rift that emitted a very peculiar Power of Death.
In search of high-level Magic Materials, we crossed through the spatial rift to another plane, but… it wasn’t long before we faced an angel with twelve wings.
My clan members were mostly slaughtered the moment we encountered the angel.
Had I not retreated swiftly, I would have also become a soul under that angel’s longsword.”
Lide’s heart jolted.
Was that Twelve-winged Blazing Angel really still alive?!!
He sharply turned to look at the Withered Bone, his tone stern.
“Withered Bone, is that Twelve-winged Blazing Angel still alive?”
If it truly still lived, then this exploration was likely doomed from the start.
That was a Divine Monster, weak though it may be, not even a city like Dawn City, lacking even the Transcendent, could contend with it.
Moreover, angels were among the most powerful combatants in the Light God System, always leading the charge even in divine wars.
“Master, that’s impossible.”
Withered Bone shook its massive head, causing the temperature in the air to drop suddenly.
“The Twelve-winged Blazing Angel has long disappeared, and from the aura of the fallen divine location, I fear this angel has been submerged by the Undead.
It might have long turned into a pile of bones.
So many eons have passed, it’s impossible for a light being to have survived inside.”
After pausing for a moment, he added, “Even if there was one, it would be extremely weak, incapable of possessing invincible combat power.
The fact that these vampires could escape from there is the best proof.”
Listen to Withered Bone, Lide fell into deep thought.
Although many of Marse’s vampires, everyone below Level 15, had been killed, there was reason in Withered Bone’s words.
If it were a fully intact Divine Monster, not just these few vampires, even ten or a hundred times their number could not withstand a massacre by a Twelve-winged Blazing Angel.
That had to be a being of at least Level 30, legendary beings paled in comparison in presence of such a creature.
With this key point in mind, Lide felt relieved and made his decision without hesitation.
“Stanley, take them all inside.”
Weakness and retreat were never part of his character.
Risk and reward were always intertwined, lacking even this courage, he could never have led Dawn City to its current heights.
The two guiding adventurers, Markli and that Level 5 Spellcaster, were trembling and speechless at the scene.
A Twelve-winged Blazing Angel had emerged.
What kind of beings had they provoked?
Regret entwined their hearts, as they now tasted the consequences of their greed.
The weak never had the power to choose.
It was so for these two adventurers, and so it was for the five Bloodline members of the Sari Clan forcibly taken into the Death Cemetery by Lide at this moment.
Marse, the Clan Leader of the Sari, had lost all his combat ability and could only let Lide dictate his fate.
Of course, Lide had no extra reaction to this, he was not one of the benevolent.
Whoosh~
As the Withered Bone, with 18 blade-like wings, flapped its wings, moving from the moonlit silvery land into the black curtain of the Dark Sky, the light in the sky dimmed instantly.
Even Lide’s Dark Vision could not see beyond a thousand blades distance at this moment.
It seemed as though the entire world had been draped with a black veil.
Lide sat on Withered Bone’s back, steering this Level 18 Bone Dragon.
After entering the Dark Sky, feeling something, he turned his head to look back.
Through the dark sky, one could faintly see the moonlit land outside, but witnessing this scene under the dark sky felt somewhat dreamlike.
Just a step away, yet worlds apart, outside was a place of light, but unfortunately, his destination was the bottomless abyss.
“Markli, lead the way.
Everyone, prepare for battle. This is the Death Cemetery, hiding Divine Monsters. Do not take it lightly!”
Lide’s chilly tone immediately made the whole team focus and heighten their alertness to the extreme.
No one dared to be negligent about anything here.
After entering the Death Cemetery, under the guidance of two adventurers, they arrived at their first destination.
A spacious abandoned camp.
This place had once been a gathering spot for professionals from various guilds in Green City, where a large number of professionals set out to clear the cursed undead throughout the Death Cemetery.
However, when Green City suddenly ordered the withdrawal of all professionals a month ago, this place was completely abandoned.
Markli’s squad had also entered this Divine’s fallen land during that operation.
Upon arriving at the camp, there wasn’t much rest, as Markli was busy with his spellcaster brother, trying to make sense of a roughly prepared map.
Lide didn’t directly ask Marse, who had just escaped from the Death Cemetery, to guide them.
He couldn’t trust this freshly subdued vampire, and it would be foolish to alter his original plan immediately based on a few words from a captive and follow their lead in such a peril-ridden land of Death.
Thus, the information from Marse was only used as a reference, relying more on himself and the two lower-leveled adventurers who were easier to control.
In such a dangerous place, he needed to maintain enough initiative.
Within the Dark Sky, the light was dim, and the two adventurers couldn’t see far. After coming out of the abandoned camp, it was only when Withered Bone cast two rare spells to enhance their Dark Vision that the adventurers’ exploration got back on track.
Vast, silent.
That was the most direct impression the Death Cemetery gave to Lide, flying low over the land, looking downward.
The grass and trees on the ground had all turned into dry, yellow, withered dead things due to the aura of death. The ground was cracked and hard, no longer able to sustain any life, like the scorched earth of purgatory.
Adding to the horror of the environment were those corpses that were either shriveled or grotesque, or rotting and stinking, lying openly or hidden in dark places.
Apart from some skeletons, those undead that had been eradicated included zombies, ghouls, and even some corpses of professionals killed by the undead, scattered more or less across this land.
Although most had been burned, some dark corners still harbored pale, swollen hands and broken limbs.
All these horrors indicated how cruel encounters had once been in this land.
Where the undead passed, no life persisted.
The intensely rich Power of Death in the air even made Lide, a creature of Dark Life, frown.
This Power of Death, which could directly transform corpses into undead, was constantly eroding him.
Although the dense Power of Death could not affect him significantly for a short period due to his strong power, staying in this environment for a long time would inevitably erode him greatly.
Everyone furrowed their brows and held their breath, except for Withered Bone, a pure Undead Life.
This gigantic beast’s soul was especially vibrant with a ghostly blue color at this moment.
Its body’s aura was rising step by step, the infinite Power of Death making Withered Bone thrive like a fish in water.
This was indeed the final resting place that Undead Life yearned for.
With the landmarks guided by the two adventurers, the group moved forward.
The range of the Death Cemetery far exceeded Lide’s estimation.
It took five Sunshine Hours, and the two adventurers had not yet found the space rift they had marked previously.
However, the only good news was that the evil life he feared might be lurking, or the angel who violently killed the Sari Clan, showed no signs of presence.
This place seemed more like a land of Dead Silence, with no plants, no streams, no undead, nothing at all.
Just when Lide’s resolute heart was becoming impatient, he finally heard the best news since entering the Death Cemetery.
“Sir, it’s this small valley, the space rift is hidden inside!!”
Hearing Markli’s loud shout, Lide immediately perked up, looking down from the sky.
It was a low valley, surrounded by small hills not more than ten blades high and about thirty blades wide.
In the center of the valley was a tree big enough to require five or six people to embrace, but by now, the tree had long since withered and died, its trunk hollowed out in the center, as if eroded.
Seeing the destination, Lide’s mood lifted slightly, as the eerie feeling from flying in the solitary environment was indeed hard to describe.
The group immediately descended.
When Lide stood at the mouth of the valley, he squinted his eyes.
He sensed something different in the air.
The undead aura here was intermixed with traces of Light Energy, although minimal, but not enough to escape Lide’s keen perception.
Withered Bone seemed to have also noticed that strange energy and immediately shouted.
“Master, that energy is from the land where the Divine fell. Death mingled with Light, so unique, I will never forget it in my lifetime.”
At last, he had found it.
Lide let out a slight sigh of relief. Searching for an inconspicuous location amidst such darkness, caused by some negative energy, and in an environment that was desolate and filled with danger and the constant assault of the scent of the undead, was particularly uncomfortable.
With a slight wave of his hand, Lide instructed two adventurers to enter the valley first, and only after confirming there was no danger did he himself step up to the curious, withered, large tree.
Standing on the dry, cracked earth, Lide furrowed his brows.
The tree in front of him was twenty blades tall, standing even higher than the small valley on either side.
Its bark was a dry, hard grey-black, filled with wrinkles. A large piece of bark had already fallen off in front and lay on the ground, revealing a hollow tree heart big enough to easily accommodate three or four adults.
But that was not the key issue. Although there were faint traces of light energy around the tree, the spatial rift, just as the Heart-eating Demon Wales had said, had already closed.
Now, although they had found the route they had originally used, the door was already locked.
“Sir, this is the place. We entered through the spatial rift here originally.”
Seeing Lide’s frowning expression, Markli immediately panicked and hastily explained, “Some spatial rifts are permanent, but some appear temporarily due to unstable spatial forces and disappear once the spatial forces stabilizes…”
Lide waved his hand at this, “Don’t be nervous, you didn’t deceive me.”
After saying this, he turned to look at the Withered Bone standing in the valley, which made the valley look petite by comparison, and transferred two bags that had been taken out from Sorins City by Mage’s Hand to the Withered Bone.
“Withered Bone, can you use the scent from this bag to locate another space?”
Among all those present, only Withered Bone was proficient in space magic. If this level 18 Bone Dragon was at a loss, then he would have to resort to his second option—Marse.
However, the risk of this choice was far greater than entering from here.
These vampires had been directly struck by angels, so entering through Marse might mean facing that angel of unknown power.
He couldn’t judge the angel’s combat abilities based solely on Marse’s word.
Although both he and Withered Bone deduced that even if the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel survived, its strength would be extremely weakened, he was not inclined to entrust his fate to elusive luck without confirmation.
Most importantly, entering through the spatial rift the adventurers had used would allow him to search for the Magic Scroll Making Skill he had been constantly longing for.
Entering through another passage would likely mean missing that location.
Thus, Marse was merely a backup plan, to be used if all else failed.
Withered Bone also used Mage’s Hand to take the severely damaged bag, then placed it on the hollow of its nose and sniffed.
The once formidable figure performing this action inexplicably made Lide feel a sense of dissonance.
Ha…
After sniffing, the giant skull of Withered Bone slightly bowed down, and its hollow eyes stared at the withered big tree, looking it up and down a few times before shaking its head somewhat disappointedly.
“Master, this severely damaged bag has been away from the Divine Fall Land for too long, its power has already dispersed, and the scent is too faint. I cannot use it to perform spatial location.”
Lide raised his eyebrows slightly, the words of Withered Bone weighing heavy on his heart.
If the first step had already failed, then all subsequent plans would need to be immediately revised.
After a silent moment, Lide seemed to remember something and suddenly turned around to look at a few vampires being guarded by Stanley and Groot.
“Do you have anything on you that was brought from the plane where that angel exists?”
Marse, sensing Lide’s determined gaze devoid of any hint of retreat, sighed deeply.
Although he did not know what dangerous object from that extremely perilous plane could catch the eye of this powerful vampire, he was now forcibly pulled into this venture.
Whether this vampire could escape the angel’s pursuit if threatened, he did not know, but with his current severe injuries, escaping was absolutely impossible.
Weighing the pros and cons for a moment, Marse clenched his teeth and took off a ring set with a brilliant blue sapphire from his own finger.
“This ring was brought from that plane, and the lingering aura on it might help you locate that world.”
After saying this, Marse spoke to Lide with a voice that had regained some of its strength,
“Kachar Clan Chief, the Sari Clan has no conflict with you. After you get what you want, could you let us go?”
“It depends on your performance in the coming days.”
Lide did not directly reply to Marse. He took the blue ring, his curiosity piqued by the pained expression on the other’s face.
He opened the attribute panel.
Blue Heart
Quality: Transcendent★
Skill: Magic Condensation (passive) – recovers 40 points of magic power per second while wearing the ring.
Description: This was originally a Legendary Level ring, but due to the passage of time, it has lost its legendary power.
The ring’s attributes were very simple, featuring only one passive skill—Magic Condensation. However, in Lide’s view, its value was much higher than ordinary transcendental equipment.
Because wearing the ring increased the recovery of magic power by 40 points per second.
The two Divine Artifact fragments Lide wore only added 30 points of magic power recovery per second, and although those Divine Fragments had powerful skills not comparable, this was astonishing enough.
Lide gave Marse a deep look, no wonder the man was so pained.
This was indeed excellent equipment for a mage, and not necessarily inferior to legendary equipment.
But because of Marse’s actions, he now regarded this Level 16 vampire more favorably, acknowledging his wisdom in judging the situation.
If Marse had kept the ring hidden and Lide was unable to enter through this space rift, he would have likely had to risk escaping from the position of this Level 16 vampire.
If he encountered that angel again, Lide didn’t know if he would be in danger, but this Level 16 vampire would definitely not escape.
He certainly wouldn’t protect a captive during battle.
Thus, Marse’s seemingly cowardly actions were actually just for self-preservation.
This act of desperate courage reminded Lide of those short-sighted individuals who even at the brink of death wouldn’t let go of a gold brick, and he admired Marse a bit more for it.
“Withered Bone, try this.”
Without further ado, Lide handed the extraordinary-level ring to Withered Bone.
The huge skull of Withered Bone turned and Mage’s Hand brought the ring next to its hollow nostrils to sniff. Moments later, its damaged Dragon Wings flapped vigorously, whoosh~
A raging hurricane erupted in the narrow valley, covering the sky with dust, and fierce airwaves pounded relentlessly on Lide’s Dragon Scale Shield.
Then, under everyone’s watchful eyes, Withered Bone’s massive body charged straight toward the decaying tree.
Just when Lide thought Withered Bone would crash directly into the tree.
Crack~
The sound of shattering glass echoed.
Around the tree, the space was filled with dense, spiderweb-like cracks, and then whoosh~
A cold, mournful wind blew out from the shattered space, and the Power of Death in that moment intensified more than tenfold.
It was like the chilling stench of opening a tomb, pervading the entire valley, making one nauseous.
Due to the spread of the Power of Death, their body surface temperatures rapidly dropped, and the two human adventurers would have turned into undead within three minutes had Lide not cast a spell in time.
But even more shocking was that amidst this dense Power of Death, there was also an indescribable power of light mixed in.
Though its presence was miniscule compared to the dense, mercury-like Power of Death, this bizarre sight was still startling.
No one knew why these originally incompatible powers were now tightly connected.
At this point, everyone knew that they had finally found the entrance.
“Found it?”
A hint of surprise appeared in Lide’s eyes.
But Withered Bone had no time to respond, as the Bone Dragon, with a wingspan of 18 blades, entered another plane through the broken space.
This shattered space rift had turned dark and gloomy, like the gaping maw of an Abyssal Giant Beast, ready to swallow everything in the next second.
This peculiar scene caused Lide to doubt anything within the space rift, where only black mist swirled.
No one would recklessly move forward at this moment.
The atmosphere inexplicably fell silent, leaving only the humming sound of the death wind from the broken plane in one’s ears.
But Withered Bone, which had entered the space rift, seemed to have vanished, remaining silent for a long time.
Lide slightly raised his eyebrows.
The current Withered Bone had not yet been transformed by the Power of Faith and was merely marked by his spiritual imprint. Although he could control its life and death, if this undead life with its bizarre thought processes didn’t care, it could definitely escape.
Despite some worries, Lide did not hurry. Instead, he calmly watched the space emitting the Power of Death.
Having gone through so much training, his mindset and willpower had already become as strong as iron.
One minute, two minutes… until it felt as though a century had passed.
The black fog behind the broken space began to churn.
Suddenly, it formed into a massive black vortex, as if brewing some terrifyingly fearsome life form.
The sky dimmed, and the surrounding atmosphere held only deathly stillness and silence.
A dry wind howled, sounding like the screams of ghosts.
The air was filled with an indescribable scent of decay, like the smell of a house unopened for decades when the doors are finally flung open.
Their skin, blasted by the cold mountain wind carrying the Power of Death, trembled with chill.
At this moment, the black vortex grew even larger, darkening even the surrounding light.
Grotto raised his longsword, his crimson eyes filled with combat fervor. Meanwhile, Stanley began frantically gathering Magic Power in his hands.
The two adventurers standing behind them were almost scared to pee, their legs going weak as they watched this demonic-like scene unfold.
Marse, the Level 16 vampire, unconsciously swallowed his saliva, a mix of nervousness and panic flashing through his blood-red eyes.
The concentration of black fog accelerated, and just as everyone held their breath.
Crack~
A huge black skull emerged from the thick mist.
“Ah!!”
