Especially the intelligence command center and the think tank, these two large advisory agencies were often able to identify gaps and propose excellent plans.
Hence the awe-inspiring scenes that were now unfolding.
“Your Majesty, everyone is prepared.”
Beastman King Kapp, at level 18, stood respectfully behind Lide, reporting. His massive lion’s head was now protected within a solid extraordinary helmet, with only a pair of cold eyes visible.
His tone was deep and solemn.
“Currently, there are a total of twenty thousand beastman warriors stationed in the underworld, ten thousand on the front lines, and another ten thousand within the caves as reinforcements.”
Lide’s deep black eyes continued to gaze into the distance, nodding slightly without speaking.
He was waiting, waiting for the enemy’s arrival.
The tactic being implemented was not complex: lure the cave spiders into attacking by relying on the edge of Grey Stone Fortress to inflict maximum casualties on them.
The initial strategic goal was to cause as much damage to the living forces of the cave spiders as possible, to harvest enough power of death for the land of bone-burying to incubate the bronze eggs.
Of course, this was only the beginning of the plan; his ultimate goal was to seize control of the magic crystal vein.
However, the number of cave spiders occupying half the plane was terrifying, and to rashly attack would be to invite unpredictable consequences.
Dawn City did not yet have the capability to crush the cave spiders nesting within half the plane, especially without knowing how many high-level cave spiders there were.
Therefore, the role of Grey Stone Fortress was to lure the opponent’s high-level combat forces into an attack, thereby allowing the elimination of high-level cave spiders that could pose a significant threat to Dawn City’s forces, in preparation for the next step of Dawn City’s army assaulting the magic crystal vein.
Cave spiders could rapidly breed ordinary spiders en masse, but the combat force above level 15 was not so easily grown.
Grey Stone Fortress’s greatest utility, in Lide’s opinion, lay precisely in this.
But once the plan commenced, Grey Stone Fortress would undoubtedly become a meat grinder; the two forces would clash in the most direct manner possible.
On one side were the primitive and fierce cave spiders, inhabiting half the plane with untold numbers and on the other, the highly developed Dawn City, with its powerful magic scientific research and production capabilities.
Suddenly, Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly.
At the end of his sight appeared a hazy line, like a dust storm sweeping in from afar, enveloping the whole marshland within.
The air carried a nauseating smell that made one’s heart panic.
The cave spiders had arrived.
Moments later, the closer that line approached Grey Stone Fortress, the stronger the stench became, and the expressions of all the soldiers became somber as the hands clutching their swords and shields tensed slowly, their muscles standing out like forged steel.
Particularly striking was a figure in mid-air, a giant beast with the wingspan of 16 blades, clad in steel armor, dancing recklessly before the sandstorm of countless cave spiders.
Castro, the newly born king, the armored giant beast, was playing the key role in this baiting operation.
Hiss~hiss~
Upon entering a thousand-blade distance, the shrill sound like a sharp knife scraping across glass began to roar from the cave spiders’ mouths through the air.
The beastman warriors wearing dwarf armor on the city walls felt a strong pressure facing them, accompanying the chilling sound, everyone finally saw clearly what that gray line was.
Spiders, incredibly huge spiders.
Although these newly-arrived beastman warriors had seen cave spiders captured for introduction before the pre-battle rally, where they were told the weaknesses and how to kill them,
To witness the grand scene of hundreds of thousands of giant spiders running and screaming on the ground was still an innately shocking experience.
At this moment, even previously untested human soldiers felt their hands trembling involuntarily, a natural bodily reaction beyond their control.
Grey Stone Fortress was built on the edge of the underworld against the mountains, with the swampy land in front forming a vast flat area.
When this broad expanse was filled with the frightening cave spiders, the visual impact was enough to shake the soul, even the most resolute warriors would face immense psychological pressure at such a sight.
Especially since everyone was standing high up, having a clear view of this spectacle further intensified the feeling.
The cave spiders, as if maddened, screamed shrilly, rushing at Castro heedlessly.
The distance of a thousand blades flashed by in an instant, and Castro suddenly increased his speed, unleashing a burst of air behind him, and reaching the city wall in a supersonic flight.
Shush~ At the moment he flew over the city wall, the iron giant’s body suddenly turned into a mini bat.
Then, flapping its tiny wings, it flew next to Lide, holding a shattered, withered eggshell with its two sharp little claws.
The egg of the Spider Queen, the cause of the Cave Spiders’ frenzy.
Lide reached out and took the already broken and withered egg of the Spider Queen, glanced at it, and casually threw it behind the city wall.
Its life force had already been devoured by the Bronze Egg; the only purpose these shells served was to enrage the Extraordinary Ghost-faced Spider Queen.
Castro flapped his wings on his shoulder, his tone tinged with excitement.
“Master, I felt the presence of that Extraordinary Spider inside the Spider Nest…”
The way to lure the Cave Spiders was just that simple and brutal; the moment Castro approached the spiders’ nest with the eggshell, the Extraordinary Spider Queen went insane having lost all her eggs.
“Everyone, prepare for battle.”
Lide ignored Castro and looked at the Cave Spiders that had entered within a 500-blade radius of the Grey Stone Fortress, his voice chilly and amplified by Magic Power, ringing through the entire fortress.
“Goblin catapults, fire.”
Stationed at the city gate atop the walls, Lide commanded the most crucial point of the city wall, the frontline against the Cave Spider onslaught.
Following the military order, human soldiers behind the walls operating the goblin trebuchets immediately released the catch, and bowstrings as thick as wrists, stretched to their limit, violently sprung, catapulting Alchemy Bombs with already pulled rings from the launchers.
Bang~ Whoosh~
Carrying the sound of torn air, the Alchemy Bombs traced a high, parabolic arc, flying over the 35-blade-high city walls, drawing a long curve in the sky before crashing down with a whistling sound in the center of the onrushing Cave Spiders.
Bang~ Bang~ Bang~
A volley, and hundreds of Alchemy Bombs detonated.
Boom~ Boom~ Boom~
Like thunder explosions from the ninth heaven, the earth seemed to collapse, and the tremendous sound wave blasted across the wide ground.
Boom~
The first Alchemy Bomb exploded in the densest part of the Cave Spiders, sending sparks in all directions.
Crackle~
Five or six Cave Spiders were directly torn apart by the Alchemy Bombs, with intensely corrosive green mucus flowing out from within their bodies, sizzling as it hit the ground.
And that wasn’t all; whoosh~ the shockwave from the explosion, like an invisible giant hand, directly flung a dozen nearby Cave Spiders into the air, their sharp limbs shredded by the blast as easily as if they were straw.
The green mucus instantly made the damp ground bubble and hiss.
Bang~ Bang~ Bang~
The continuous explosion sounds were like a giant hammer striking ants on the ground, clearing a large area with each blow.
The ferocious, innumerable Cave Spiders that previously seemed unstoppable were now being suppressed.
The scene looked like something from a depiction of an Ancient scene on church frescoes, breathtaking.
But hundreds of Alchemy Bombs were far from enough to destroy the countless Cave Spiders, and those that escaped the blasts became even more frenzied.
Especially after coming close to Grey Stone Fortress and sensing the presence of the Spider Queen’s eggs, they radiated a formidable and terrifying ferocity.
Their green, oily eyes now had a hint of crimson.
Murderous intent spread.
They charged without regard for the cost.
A frenzy of attacks.
In the frontline battlefield, the first Cave Spider reached the walls of Grey Stone Castle. Without hesitation, this creature covered in fur, like a demon that crawled out of hell, began to climb up the wall.
But to the murderous-intent Cave Spider’s surprise, the rough-looking walls of Grey Stone Castle were incredibly slippery, and it simply couldn’t climb up.
Even its fur-covered limbs couldn’t find any purchase.
Lide’s lips curled slightly at the sight, for to prevent spiders from scaling the walls directly, Dawn Mage Tower had spent a huge sum of money to solidify the “Oily Skill,” a Second Circle Magic, on all the walls.
Cave Spiders could climb rock surfaces mainly thanks to the adhesive effect of the velvet on their limbs, and the “Oily Skill” precisely countered this trait.
Bang—the twang of bowstrings echoed in the ears.
Arrow after arrow, carrying the breath of death, pierced through the head of a Level 9 Cave Spider from atop the walls; this spider did not survive three seconds on the wall.
The human archers at this moment had icy cold gazes.
After several expansions, the King’s Blade now boasted a 3,000-strong army, excluding the 2,000 Magic Language Knights.
So when the winter population surged past the 100,000 mark, the King’s Blade’s human army had reached a force of 5,000.
Of these, 1,000 had been trained as archers.
And right now, Gray Stone Fortress, with the capacity for 3,000 people, had 500 archers.
They had become the most indifferent hunters before the enemy breached the walls, hunting down every invading foe.
Wuu wuu—
With the blowing of the cow horn behind them, the Cave Spiders reached the first climax of their assault.
Several, even dozens of them, started stacking up after reaching the walls, trying to pile on top of one another to scale the ramparts.
An uncountable number of Cave Spiders surged like a tidal wave, crazy and ferocious.
The 10 Gray Stone Fortresses, like reefs by the sea, seemed ready to tilt and collapse at any moment under the assault of the stormy waves.
The Beastman Warriors, clad in full-body armor, finally engaged in close combat with these Underworld creatures.
Their long spears mercilessly pierced through the Cave Spiders that had managed to climb the wall; as soon as these Underworld creatures showed their heads, they were met with the fiercest attack.
The immense strength of the stalwart Beastman Warriors easily rent the spiders’ bodies asunder, as effortlessly as killing young chicks; unless a significant number of Cave Spiders could reach the wall at once, they were nothing but fodder for the Beastman Warriors.
And at this moment, the various long-hidden defensive lines finally opened fire.
First were the towers on the walls, those arrows with fierce cold gleams, burst forth as the crossbow strings were drawn taut.
Boom—
Hoo hoo—
The deadly bolts, like the demonic roars, needed no aim for the swarms of Cave Spiders below made easy targets.
Zila—puchi—
Those sharp arrowheads, forged with Fine Gold, tore through the world like the Creation Sword, mercilessly piercing the Cave Spiders in their way.
Nothing could stop the penetrating force of the crossbow bolts.
Seven Cave Spiders in a row were blown apart by a single bolt, the last burrowing so deep into the ground after piercing a spider’s head, the tail was no longer visible.
All 10 Gray Stone Fortresses fired their crossbows nearly simultaneously, thousands of wrist-thick bolts raining down like a volley of launched spears.
Puchi—puchi—
The Cave Spiders, which had already climbed to the bottom of the walls, almost completely blocking off the ground, were instantly shredded by the bolts’ downpour.
Limbs and remains scattered everywhere, green blood flowing into streams.
The dense horde of Cave Spiders was cleared away in an instant.
This volley of crossbow fire killed at least 5,000 Cave Spiders.
Ssss—
But the severe losses did not cause the Cave Spiders to retreat; from behind them, a spine-chilling sound arose, and the previously hesitant Cave Spiders once again went berserk.
Different from the last time, the second wave of attacking Cave Spiders now included a large number of Level 10 Ghost-faced Spiders, and even Lide distinctly felt the presence of uncountably numerous Level 15 Ghost-faced Spiders…
Wuu wuu—
As the urgent horn sounded from within Gray Stone Fortress, and facing the even denser swarm of Cave Spiders, a chill went through every warrior’s heart, for the real war was about to begin…

chapters.title: Chapter 325 - 325 327 Battle of Gray Stone Fortress (Part 2)
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 325: Chapter 327: Battle of Gray Stone Fortress (Part 2) Chapter 325: Chapter 327: Battle of Gray Stone Fortress (Part 2) Level 15… The Ghost-faced Spiders with their heart-chilling aura were now the most bloodthirsty hunters, and the Gray Stone Fortress was their hunted prey.
Of course, the position of prey is never fixed.
After the war at the Gray Stone Fortress broke out, it entered an incredibly tense and heated state.
The sheer number of Cave Spiders, occupying half of the plane, was overwhelming.
Especially after being enraged by the Spider Queen’s eggs, the Cave Spiders launched attacks at all costs, allowing Lide to realize for the first time the power of the human sea tactic.
Especially with the inclusion of High-level Ghost-faced Spiders into the battlefield, the state of the war suddenly became even more brutal.
The endless number of Cave Spiders swarmed like locusts, dense and without end in the dim light, giving everyone a great psychological shock and pressure.
By then, all the firepower of the Gray Stone Fortress was activated once the High-level Cave Spiders joined the battle.
The Crossbows on the towers fired arrow after arrow, like relentless deities. The Fine Gold Crossbow Arrows, with their fatal aura, were the most terrifying blades of death on the battlefield.
Each Crossbow Arrow, as thick as a baby’s wrist, could cause enormous damage to the Cave Spiders in a straight line. Even Level 10 Ghost-faced Spiders hit by a Crossbow Arrow would lose most of their combat power if not killed, and then be annihilated by other firepower in the ensuing battle.
The goblin trebuchets behind the city walls started drawing their bows more frequently, and the horrifying Alchemy Bombs would clear a large area with each explosion.
Meanwhile, the high towers within the fortress, where Mages were stationed, played a huge role.
Once too many Cave Spiders climbed up the walls, Spellcasters would immediately bolster the front line of Beastman Warriors. Terrible magic was the most powerful weapon; each attack brought about miraculous effects.
The presence of Spellcasters greatly relieved the pressure on the defense line.
But war, after all, is war, and never that simple.
While the frontlines were at a fever pitch, a Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider, 4 blades tall and 8 blades long, avoided the main battlefield.
In the dim light, it led 10 Level 15 Ghost-faced Spiders to the farthest right of 10 U-shaped fortresses.
And behind this team of ludicrously leveled Ghost-faced Spiders trailed a full 200 Level 10 Ghost-faced Spiders.
The elite of the elite.
The leading Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider had a ferocious head and a twisted face of death that sent chills down one’s spine.
Its green eyes were like those of a demon, and its mouth, with a sharp tone, let out an extremely piercing shriek, attacking the fortress without any attempt at concealment.
The height of this subsidiary fortress’s wall was 30 blades, its overall structure much smaller than that of the main fortress, and it lacked the dense firepower points of the main fortress.
Therefore, when this group of High-level Ghost-faced Spiders, led by the Level 18’s combat power, attacked, the limited firepower arrangements couldn’t hold the situation.
Moreover, ordinary Alchemy Bombs or Crossbow Arrows couldn’t harm the Ghost-faced Spiders above Level 15. In less than a minute,
Level 10 and 15 Ghost-faced Spiders, along with one Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider, had directly charged to the base of the fortress walls.
Bang, bang~
The human soldiers inside the tower changed complexion as they saw the Ghost-faced Spiders below, obviously larger than the surrounding Cave Spiders.
The previously spaced-out Crossbow Arrows began targeting these distinctly more terrifying spiders, pulling the trigger as a relentless stream of Crossbow Arrows shot from the firing holes atop the tower.
The Crossbow could fire twenty arrows in rapid succession, so there was no need to worry about changing arrows in the short term.
Inside the subsidiary fortress, 300 Crossbows instantly formed an exaggerated rain of arrows.
The baby-arm-thick Crossbow Arrows shot forth like spears thrown by warriors, their arrowheads with four-sided blood grooves reflecting a deadly, cold light.
Thwack—a Crossbow Arrow directly pierced through a Level 10 Ghost-faced Spider, its twisted face of death burst open.
Yet the dense and terrifying hail of arrows couldn’t harm the Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider.
Crack—a single arrow struck the head of a Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider, igniting a spark, but that was all, merely leaving a white mark on its armor.
The bone armor, reflecting a dark luster, seemed to be cast from the hardest steel, impervious even to Fine Gold-crafted arrowheads.
Yet, the provoked Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider flew into a rage.
It let out a shrill screech, and behind it, Level 10 Ghost-faced Spiders along with nearby normal Cave Spiders surged forward with great speed as if given a command.
In a moment, within this section of the city wall, hundreds of giant spiders had gathered, and these spiders did not climb the wall coated in the solidified Oily Skill but began stacking upon one another like building blocks.
What terrified the warriors on the wall was that, despite being under intense fire, these Cave Spiders seemed invincible to death, completely unaffected.
Even their dead bodies could fall at the base of the wall, contributing to the growing pile of blocks.
In less than a minute, these giant spiders had stacked into a pile over twenty blades high.
Upon seeing this, the Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider could no longer contain its restless desire for slaughter. With crossbow bolts raining down, it climbed atop the spider pile, its eight articulated legs slowly bending into the shape of a bow.
Thump—
Its body’s power erupted, and the Ghost-faced Spider leaped up, jumping from the sky onto the top of the wall in a terrifying posture.
The bloodiest encounter began.
The dense throng of Beastman Warriors seemed so insignificant beneath the might of the Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider.
But those Beastman Warriors in solid armor showed not the slightest hint of fear.
Their eyes slowly turned a deep red as they, wielding their sharp long blades, launched themselves toward the Ghost-faced Spider without a moment’s hesitation.
Beastmen never retreat.
Seeing these “ants” not only fail to shrink back but swarm towards it instead completely infuriated the Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider. Its eight limbs swung like lances in a knight’s charge, unstoppable.
Gore—
A Beastman Warrior clad in thick armor was directly pierced through by a limb, and his solid armor did nothing to spare him a second longer.
All eight sharp limbs were the most powerful weapons of slaughter.
The dense Beastman Warriors surrounding it were dealt a devastating blow by the mad onslaught of the Ghost-faced Spider.
But the Beastman Warriors fought on valiantly, undeterred by casualties, aiming to deliver one full-strength slash at the Ghost-faced Spider’s limbs even if they were to die.
Their fighting spirit was strong enough to shake one’s core.
The Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider was not plunged into the one-sided massacre it had imagined but instead bogged down as if in a quagmire.
The Beastman Warriors were clad in Dwarf-crafted heavy armor, specifically refined. Although it couldn’t block the piercing limbs, it significantly hindered the Ghost-faced Spider’s killing rhythm.
Piercing normal armor was like piercing tofu, but piercing the Beastman’s armor was like a spear thrusting through a thick wooden board—it could still penetrate, but it required a significant amount of strength.
Spellcasters on the high platform behind also began offering magical support.
Regrettably, the Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider’s Magic resistance was too high, and the team of spellcasters, without any Level 10 professionals among them, couldn’t inflict any real damage.
Boom—
While the Beastman Warriors were fiercely battling the Ghost-faced Spider, the pile of spiders below grew a few blades taller, and the ten Level 15 Ghost-faced Spiders that had been waiting impatiently also appeared on top of the wall in the same manner.
In the presence of those enormous figures, even the Beastmen, averaging two blades in height, still seemed so diminutive.
With the addition of ten Level 15 Ghost-faced Spiders, the seemingly stable battlefield became perilously unstable in an instant.
The advantage of higher-level combat strength over lower-level troops is not something that can be easily compensated for.
Unfortunately, only three Extraordinary Crossbows, designed to hunt Cave Spiders above Level 15, had been made, and all were placed in the main fortress—secondary fortresses lacked such formidable weapons.
Just as the situation on the battlefield became increasingly dire, nearly leading to a collapse, a series of urgent and rhythmic horn blasts suddenly emanated from the fortress.
The sound waves took only a few seconds to spread across the entire battlefield.
Less than twenty seconds later, a massive roar came from the distance.
That was… the voice of a giant dragon!
At that moment, a Bone Dragon with a wingspan of eighteen blades, whose skull blazed with the blue soul fire, approached, exuding a powerful oppressive force.
Along with the arrival of the Bone Dragon were Castro, reverted to his steel behemoth form, and the Level 15 Crimson Hunter Frey, Level 17 Grot, and Level 18 Beastman King Kapp.
The Hunter Squad, this was the team that Lide assembled with all of his high-end force, and its sole purpose was to hunt down Cave Spider combatants above Level 15.
This plan was also a strategic goal in this war—to inflict as much harm as possible on the Cave Spiders’ high-level combatants.
“Gah gah gah gah gah gah~
Such filthy, foul-smelling, and disgusting spiders, your odor is nauseating.
Allow the great Lord Withered Bones, the Tusk of Dawn City—the Dragon of Destruction—to purify your souls.
I swear to the Death God, to be cleansed by the Dragon Breath will be an honor for you, weak spiders. Are you ready to welcome the arrival of the great Dragon of Destruction…”
Lord Withered Bones’s cackling laughter, when it appeared above the Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider, caused a commotion among the surrounding Cave Spiders.
Dragon Power, the Dragon Power that permeated their souls, made these subterranean monsters unconsciously start to back away.
But the Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider was enraged.
Both Level 18, why do you get to be so domineering?
With a fierce roar, the huge mouth opened skyward towards Withered Bones.
The piercing sound caused a dozen Beastman Warriors’ eardrums to rupture, bleeding profusely, knocking them to the ground in a daze.
Whoosh whoosh~
At that moment, Kapp, who was riding on Withered Bones, narrowed his eyes slightly. The eyes of the lion showed the sharpness of blade edges. After a brief pause, he timed it perfectly, leaping into the air.
His hand wielding the long Extraordinary Battle Blade, he aimed a horizontal slash directly at the Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider.
Jump Cut.
Warrior Skill.
Enhanced by the steep altitude of a hundred blades, this ordinary Warrior Skill’s power increased by more than tenfold.
When the Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider saw this, its huge belly arched up, and its posterior spinnerets violently burst open, spurting out a poisonous web like a bird trap, aimed directly at Kapp in the air.
Clash~
The long blade was like a dragon, flashing a cold light, and the web, oozing with blue slime, was cut through by Kapp’s slash.
But by this time, the Ghost-faced Spider had already reacted, violently moving to the side and avoiding Kapp’s landing spot.
Clang~
Kapp’s long blade struck the wall of the fortress with extreme violence.
The solid wall instantly cracked, spanning several blades’ distance, with rubble flying.
Meanwhile, as the Ghost-faced Spider evacuated to the side, several Beastman Warriors who couldn’t dodge in time were crushed to death. However, Kapp’s arrival greatly boosted the morale of the Beastmen.
This was their king!
More and more Beastman Warriors roared furiously and surged forward, using their lives to severely restrict the Ghost-faced Spider’s movements.
The Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider immediately entered a state of rage, its eight limbs slashing and tearing apart the surrounding Beastman Warriors like a meat grinder gone wild.
Castro’s huge eyes revealed an uncontrollable and chilling murderous intent.
Those were his people!!
He pulled his long knife from the ground, straightened up, and his muscles tightened explosively like a compressed spring, reaching an ultimate point of tension before bursting forth.
Charge!!
Thump~ Thump~ Thump~
With such immense power contained within his body, this Lion-man Warrior who resembled a small giant left footprints that cracked the stone with every step he took on the city wall.
The restrained Level 18 Ghost-faced Spider, far from being cowardly, lashed out with fangs sharper than razors, snapping at Castro like scissors.
Clang~
Charging forward, Castro didn’t dodge in the slightest, his long knife clashing directly with those two sharp tusks.
Sparks flew in all directions.
Castro, with all his furious might, suddenly came to a halt, feeling an irresistible force transmitted through his long knife.
Then the Lion-man warrior was hurled back at an even faster speed, crashing into the city wall and scattering the Beastman Warriors, skidding ten or more feet back, dragging up sparks on the ground.
The extraordinary armor protected his body, but the ground was scraped up, sending up a trail of sparks.
This strike of the Beastman King’s represented a complete defeat.
The force unleashed by the Ghost-faced Spider was clearly far more powerful than one would expect from its smaller stature compared to Castro.
At that moment, the Ghost-faced Spider forcefully broke free, cutting through the circle of Beastmen around it, and lunged straight for Castro who had yet to get up from the ground.
The Ghost-faced Spider could sense the power within Castro, which was stronger than that of an erupting volcano; it had to kill this enemy that posed the greatest threat to it.
But at the same time, reinforcements had arrived. The Withered Bone flying with its wings swept down from the sky, with pale Dragon Breath gathering in its throat.
As it streaked over the city wall, the creature lowered its head, and with a hiss, the Bone Dragon unleashed its breath filled with the essence of death directly at the Ghost-faced Spider.
Yet, the extremely vigilant Ghost-faced Spider didn’t take the direct hit from Withered Bones’ breath, agilely turning to dodge the range of the Dragon Breath.
A suffocating presence of undead death instantly enveloped the entire stretch of the city wall, turning several heavily wounded Beastmen into piles of white bones before they could react.
Castro flipped to his feet, and the intense pain coursing through his body sent the Level 18 Beastman King into a state of uncontrollable rage.
To be thrown around by a Ghost-faced Spider was a disgrace!
With the battle blade held horizontally in his right hand, his eyes turned blood red.
Beastman race talent—Berserk.
Castro’s power surged in an instant, his aura as oppressive as a mountain, his murderous intent almost materialized beside him.
His legs pushed off the ground, and like a fully drawn bow releasing, he struck at the Ghost-faced Spider.
Shame could only be washed away with blood.
—
—
—
PS: I wanted to add more to the story today, but I’ve hit writer’s block, which feels terrible. I have many stories in my mind, but I can’t seem to write them down, endlessly writing and deleting.
That feeling is like needing to urinate without rest, restless, always wanting to resolve it, but without a bathroom in sight, I can only hold it in…

chapters.title: Chapter 326 - 326 328 Prelude to Server Launch (5000 words)
chapters.content:
﻿Chapter 326: Chapter 328: Prelude to Server Launch (5000 words) Chapter 326: Chapter 328: Prelude to Server Launch (5000 words) Within the best hospital room in Shanghai, a very cute nurse bustled into the ward, brimming with excitement.
“Zhou Bo, here’s your lab report, there’s really no problem.”
“It’s truly unbelievable, your cancer really has gone into remission!! God bless~”
The girl was so excited that she was visibly moved, looking at the handsome young man on the bed with genuine joy on her face and eyes sparkling like stars.
“This is simply a medical miracle, your cancer was in the advanced stages, and yet it has completely receded!”
Caught off guard by the nurse’s sudden entrance, Zhou Bo blinked in surprise, instinctively closing the official forum for “Glory” before realizing he hadn’t saved the post he had been halfway through editing…
But he was no longer concerned about that, his attention fully captured by the nurse’s words.
“Thank you, Little Yu, if it weren’t for your care during this time, I doubt I would have recovered so quickly.”
Zhou Bo took a deep breath, unable to hide the surprise in his eyes.
Although he had always felt that ever since he reclassed into the Undead Clan’s hidden profession—Hand of Death in “Glory”—his body had gradually been regaining strength, becoming stronger and no longer frail.
And his spirits were rapidly improving day by day, but the moment he actually held the lab report, his heart couldn’t help but swell with immense joy.
His hands clenched into fists beneath his gray-and-white hospital gown.
“Undead Monarch, Undead Clan… “Glory”…”
“I don’t know what kind of secrets are hidden within, but it’s you who have given me a new life.”
“It’s nothing, I didn’t help much,” the nurse replied with a sweet smile, then hesitated for a moment.
“Zhou Bo, your attending physician will come for a thorough physical examination later. They may ask you some tricky questions, but if you don’t want to answer, you don’t have to…”
Zhou Bo felt warmed by her words, looking at the girl he had been close to for nearly two years, with a slight stir in his heart.
His handsome face showed a hint of nervousness.
“Little Yu, once I’m discharged I…”
“What is it?”
“I… would you let me take you out for dinner… and maybe see a movie?”
After stammering out his invitation, he looked anxiously at the simple and cute girl before him, his right hand unwittingly clenching the bedsheets, Zhou Bo’s heart beating more intensely than ever.
The girl, taken aback by the hopeful eyes before her, subconsciously bit her lip and gave a shy hum in affirmation.
When Zhou Bo heard her agree, the whole world seemed to light up for him.
Just as he was about to speak, a flurry of hurried footsteps approached from outside the ward.
“Where, where?? The terminal cancer patient has really recovered???
You guys aren’t joking, right? He had a critical illness notice three months ago, and now he’s alive?….”
A middle-aged doctor in a white coat with thick glasses rushed into the ward.
Seeing Zhou Bo, who appeared to be in good spirits, it was as if he had seen a lab rat; the gleam in his eyes outshone that from seeing a beauty.
Zhou Bo shuddered internally, “Damn, this guy’s vibe is more terrifying than that of the Demigod Level Undead Monarch??”
The following day.
After a group of cancer specialists skeptically examined him twice from head to toe, they all had to admit, the guy who they thought at most had a few months to live, for whom they had even prepared a morgue bed, was now miraculously cured.
This was simply a miracle in medical history.
Zhou Bo was immediately promoted by the First Hospital as an exemplar, and for a long time hence, he would be showcased to the outside world as a medical miracle, encouraging patients to never give up.
For a time, Zhou Bo became the pillar of faith for many patients.
But Zhou Bo, now returned to normal, naturally knew the real reason behind his recovery, which he preferred not to discuss.
In the hospital ward, Zhou Bo slowly packed his belongings, that he had used over the past two years, into the suitcase that nurse Little Yu had bought for him. With a longing for the future, he turned and left the ward that had so often brought him close to the brink of death.
After completing the discharge procedures, the two approached the hospital’s entrance.
The girl in the nurse’s uniform looked happily at Zhou Bo’s departing figure, but then, as if remembering something, she suddenly appeared a bit disheartened.
Over the course of two years, she had grown accustomed to the boy’s presence, and seeing his smile daily was the warmest sight for her.
It seemed he noticed the girl’s feelings, as Zhou Bo turned around, flashing a brilliant smile.
“Little Yu, don’t think just because I’m discharged from the hospital, you can pretend not to recognize me.”
“Remember our date tomorrow… cough cough, for dinner.”
Only then did the girl snap back to reality, her face showing anticipation mixed with a bit of shyness.
She tried to act nonchalant.
“Nag.”
“You should head back first. You sold your house to pay for the treatment last time; surely you need to find a new place to live.”
As she spoke, she seemed to remember something, and her voice unconsciously lowered,
“If… if you can’t find a place to stay for the time being, there’s a spare room at my house…”
Her voice trailed off more and more, her cheeks coloring with an embarrassed blush.
Beep beep~ At that moment, an inopportunely timed pair of honks interrupted their conversation from the side of the road.
A brand-new Porsche slowly came to a stop on the road before them.
Bang~
The passenger side door opened, and a young, sharp-dressed man quickly got out of the car. Under the girl’s astonished gaze, he approached Zhou Bo and greeted him with respect.
“Mr. Zhou, the car is ready.
The executive meeting at the company is set to start at 4 p.m. today, and the administrative department has already booked the restaurant at Lijiang Five-star Hotel for this evening to welcome you.”
Seeing this, the girl’s mouth hung open foolishly as she stared at Zhou Bo, wanting to say something but not knowing how to start.
Zhou Bo gave the girl a warm smile.
“Little Yu, this is my assistant, Wei Feng.
I acquired a company two months ago and I haven’t had the chance to tell you… I’ll take you to visit this weekend…”
“Oh, what were you saying just now? I didn’t catch it clearly?”
The girl’s cheeks instantly flushed a deep red, and she shook her head vigorously, “I didn’t say anything, you heard wrong.
Go ahead with your business, I still have patients to attend to for their IVs…”
With that, she turned around and quickly walked away with her head down, still somewhat dazed inside.
The girl didn’t understand how the big boy who had sold his house to save her had suddenly become the boss of a large company…
Her thoughts were a mess.
Watching the girl’s retreating figure, Zhou Bo finally remembered what she had said just moments ago, slapping his head sharply.
He glared at the composed young man before him, grinding his teeth.
“Who told you to come so early?”
There’s a spare room at my place… Ah, what exactly did I just miss??
“Mr. Zhou?”
The young assistant looked utterly confused. Was there anything wrong with coming early?
Taking a few deep breaths, Zhou Bo calmed the turmoil in his heart and got into the luxury car.
After the vehicle started, Zhou Bo began to ask questions.
“Little Feng, how many ‘Glory’ gaming pods have we acquired?”
Assistant Wei Feng pondered for a brief moment before responding.
“Mr. Zhou, it seems someone is controlling the release of the gaming pods; we’ve only managed to acquire 500 units.
It appears 500 is the threshold. After we acquired up to 500 last week, no matter where we went to ‘Glory’s’ selling points, we couldn’t purchase any more gaming pods.”
Hearing this, Zhou Bo’s eyes narrowed slightly.
From the day he entered the game, he sensed that Glory was no ordinary venture, due to his sharp instincts as a top player, for his ID was—Knight with the Broken Sword.
As a professional gamer who started playing games crazily since the age of 10, his vision and perception were much sharper than the average person.
After discovering the specialty of “Glory,” he prepared to spare no expense to enlarge his advantage in “Glory.”
Thus, the ability of players to resurrect as Undead became the power that thrilled him the most, and he wanted to organize a team comprised solely of players at his beck and call.
In the Undead Empire, as the meritious person who personally pulled out the Holy Light Sword and released the Undead Monarch sealed for a hundred thousand years, he not only obtained a hidden profession but also became a disciple of the Undead Monarch.
He had immense influence among the natives and was entirely capable of nurturing a powerful team of players.
By then, the reputation of the Knight of the Broken Sword was sure to become eternal among the players.
Zhou Bo had already been pondering the future since his health gradually improved.
Purchasing the company was also part of this idea; everything about this game was worth the effort to him.
Here, buried treasures enough to make everyone’s hearts flutter were hidden.
“The public test for the game is in two days, regardless of whether we can buy more gaming capsules or not, I hope all of you increase your efforts to search. Even if it means paying extra to buy from other players, do not spare any expense.
Little Feng, this game, is not as simple as you think…”
“Yes, Mr. Zhou.”
After giving instructions, Zhou Bo seemed to remember something and curiously asked.
“By the way, last time you mentioned that the club called Crimson Moon contacted us, wanting to obtain the Dark Summoning Skill that summons Bone Dragons from me, how did the negotiation go?”
Wei Feng spoke softly, “Mr. Zhou, last time the other party was willing to offer 500 Second Circle Magic Scrolls in exchange, but we have not agreed yet, we need you to make the final decision.”
Hearing this, a hint of surprise flashed in Zhou Bo’s eyes.
“500 Magic Scrolls??”
In his view, the Dark Summoning Skill capable of summoning Bone Dragons was definitely worth 500 Magic Scrolls, but what surprised him was that someone could produce such a vast number of Magic Scrolls at this point in time.
He was someone who understood the market; according to the information gleaned from “Glory,” except for the southern province of the Nolan Empire where Magic Scrolls seemed more abundant, other areas were scarce.
Being able to come up with so many Magic Scrolls now, the power behind it in “Glory” would definitely not be small.
Zhou Bo’s interest piqued immediately.
“What’s the name of the Crimson Moon’s power in ‘Glory’? Why haven’t I heard any news about them?”
“They were not willing to reveal their specific name.”
“Any other information?”
“According to them, in Green City, the largest city in the southern province of the Nolan Empire, Crimson Moon has established a trade association that has formed ties with several major Nobles.
Thus, anything that can be found on the market, can be traded through them.
And these 500 Magic Scrolls are proof of their strength.
If this transaction goes smoothly, Crimson Moon also hopes to establish a strategic partnership with us in the future and hopes we can trade the specialties of the Undead Empire with them.”
Hearing Wei Feng’s words, Zhou Bo couldn’t help but imagine a massive power in his mind.
Crimson Moon, this name was deeply etched in his memory.
“By the way, Mr. Zhou, here are screenshots from their warehouse. They mentioned during the negotiation that you might be interested after seeing this.”
Wei Feng finished speaking and passed Zhou Bo the mobile phone.
Taking it, Zhou Bo looked at the opened album and took a sharp intake of breath.
“Four Circle Magic Scroll Manufacturing Skill…”
“Extraordinary Level weapons…”
“Thousands of sets of Rare, Perfect Level armor…”
“Tens of thousands of Gold Pucks…”
“…”
Originally, he thought that by becoming a disciple of the Undead Monarch and changing his profession to the hidden Undead profession, he was absolutely at the pinnacle of all players.
But at this moment, looking at the photo on the phone, Zhou Bo’s heart was immediately struck hard.
How is that even possible??
How could anyone acquire such precious treasures and resources in this span of time??
Did the damn Crimson Moon just pry open the treasure vault of the King of Nolan Empire?
That’s just ridiculous.
At the same time, he couldn’t help but feel a profound sense of awe toward the Crimson Moon—a seemingly inconspicuous force, yet possessing resources far beyond his own reach.
This Crimson Moon, so freaking amazing.
At this moment, Zhou Bo probably couldn’t believe that the items displayed were just a batch of materials casually selected by Lide in preparation for the upcoming server opening.
When it comes to real power, Zhou Bo had no idea of the extent of the force Lide currently wielded.
The Crimson Mage Tower, Dark Contract, Dwarf Valley, the dwarf hills, along with the Fishman Tribe they were strategizing to ally with, and the very heart of all influence—Dawn City.
Lide’s domain had grown vast beyond what current players could imagine.
A mastermind was slowly taking shape behind the scenes.
“Mr. Zhou, about the collaboration with Crimson Moon, what do you think?”
After seeing the photos on Wei Feng’s phone, Zhou Bo took a deep breath and spoke resolutely.
“We must collaborate with them, having such a powerful ally within the Human Empire can bring immense benefits to both sides.”
Without Lide knowing, the Dark Summoning Skill, which Zhou Bo so coveted and could summon the Bone Dragon, silently shifted into his possession after a few screenshots surfaced, greatly reducing the time cost he would have spent searching for it.
This marked a solid step toward the birth of the Sea of Bone Dragons.
“During the server opening the day after tomorrow, all professional players in the company must log in on time to create new accounts.
If you can choose the exact birthplace, it must be the Undead Empire.
The Undead Clan will be our focal point for conquest.”
“Yes, Mr. Zhou.”
“Furthermore, regarding…”
Zhou Bo arranged a few tasks in the car, feeling a bit more relaxed, and casually opened the “Glory” official website, scanned the unchanging game information, and then visited the player forum.
The instant he saw those posts, he could feel the jubilant atmosphere in the air.
“HAHAHA, the game is opening in two days!!! My big sculpture is already starving and thirsty. The azaleas on Jasmine Street, did you miss me? BigSword.jpg”
“The game is about to open, let me introduce three places in the Royal Capital of Casano Country that are suitable for big swords. I have personally experienced it—if you have enough Gold Puck, you could even enjoy the marvelous Half-Elf~HalfElf.jpg”
“HAHAHA, looking at all these posts anticipating the public test of the game the day after tomorrow, I couldn’t be happier. A bunch of losers, do you think you’re going to “Glory” to show off? HAHAHA, wait till you have to carry bricks at the dock to fill your belly every day, help unload trucks, or even descend into prostitution, serving over-50-year-old noblewomen, then you’ll understand how exciting this game is. Hang in there, don’t give up, DogHead.jpg”
“Godslayer Guild is recruiting fervently! Here we have adorable cutesy little sisters, rich tycoons who give out red packets at the drop of a hat, and hunky guys with well-defined abs. What are you waiting for, come and sign up~LoliLegs.jpg”
“Latest news, the reward for the game designer’s location, supported by 78,000 players’ funds, has reached 2.35 million RMB, and the number is still rapidly increasing. The most generous tycoon alone contributed 100,000 RMB. Unfortunately, no one knows the location of the “Glory” official website to date; those damn elusive designers are still out of sight, and this reward money remains unclaimed, but tune in at the same time tomorrow for our ongoing report.”
Zhou Bo’s mouth twitched fiercely upon reading the last message.
These nutjob players were unmatched in stirring up trouble.
To protest the inactivity of the official site and the extreme difficulty of “Glory,” a few players initiated a bounty to locate the “Glory” official office.
What started out as a bit of fun spiraled as more and more players, devastated by the native inhabitants of “Glory,” joined in anger.
These deeply aggrieved nutjobs were being outsmarted by the crafty natives over and over.
More and more people joined the reward offer, with some tycoons in their rage promptly dumping 100,000 RMB, just to find an office address… an act that could be called the craziest in history.
Now, aside from the launch of “Glory,” the most attention-grabbing issue was the whereabouts of the game’s developers or operating offices.
Over the past period, this reward of over two million attracted countless players to come searching, sparking a craze outside the gaming community: report the correct address, prove it’s accurate, and you could win over two million RMB—it was like picking up money.
Unfortunately, the “Glory” official site seemed to have vanished into the depths of the Pacific Ocean, as even the most fervent players couldn’t find any trace of it.
And the location of the “Glory” official website became one of the top ten mysteries of “Glory” later on.

chapters.title: Chapter 327 - 327 329 Divine Beings — Divine Monster
chapters.content:
Chapter 327: Chapter 329: Divine Beings — Divine Monster (10,000-Word Mega Chapter) Chapter 327: Chapter 329: Divine Beings — Divine Monster (10,000-Word Mega Chapter) Regarding the question of how the game guild should be established, I believe everyone has understood my meaning.
The Nolan Empire will be the main focus of our conquest in the Crimson Moon.
Our guild’s headquarters will be established in Nuolan Royal City, and all the professional players of Crimson Moon will carry out their missions around it.
Lide Kachar stood within the cavernous conference room, looking down at the more than 600 professional players below.
His tone was grave.
“In the future, this will be the place for you to show your prowess; trust me, you will obtain everything you desire in this game.
I’ve already provided the situation of Nuolan Royal City to the Data Analysis Department. Soon, each of you will receive a copy,
and I hope everyone will gain a deeper understanding of the Nolan Empire.”
“Today is already September 10th, and there are only 30 days left until the server launch. I expect everyone to make adequate preparations in this last month.
One month from now, when the game launches, that will be our moment to shine in Crimson Moon.
Now, you are dismissed.”
Following this concluding statement, Lide Kachar ended the two-hour-long meeting.
He left first with a few senior leaders, leaving behind a group of professional players who were eagerly discussing the contents of the meeting.
Currently, the largest staff in Crimson Moon consists of professional players.
After decades of development, the gaming field has long since transitioned from a profession suitable only for a small group to the hottest profession with the highest annual employment rate.
The key reason is the rapid development of the gaming industry; what was once an industry where only a few top-tier professional players could make a living has now become accessible to the ordinary person whose skills might not be top-notch.
For example, lifestyle professions in virtual games, which require a lot of time, have become a major focus for some professional players.
As an industry grows larger, the division of labor inevitably becomes more refined: combat players, lifestyle players, dungeon raid players, game data collection players… and so on.
This is not surprising.
The hundreds of professional players currently employed by Crimson Moon have already largely met Lide Kachar’s needs for early stages; later on, he plans to use these players as a foundation to further expand the team.
Players’ ability to have no fear of death was indeed an overpowered bug; if used correctly, it would definitely allow for many unexpected achievements.
But all these actions would have to wait for the launch of “Glory.”
As the vice president, Zhao Yue followed Lide Kachar out of the meeting room after it ended.
Today, the voluptuous lady donned a black professional skirt suit, and every move she made was full of a charm that caused hearts to flutter—a seduction unique to mature women, unattainable by younger girls.
At this moment, Zhao Yue’s gaze followed Lide Kachar’s retreating figure, her eyes were filled with complexity.
These past two months were neither long nor short, and she had thought that Lide Kachar would need a substantial amount of time to adapt and might not have been able to enter the work rhythm so quickly.
But his capability was far stronger than she had anticipated.
A leader with immense personal charm.
That was Zhao Yue’s most direct impression of Lide Kachar.
Firm in decision-making, with broad vision, strong capacity for handling affairs, willing to delegate powers, not fearing failure, and daring to admit shortcomings.
These were some of the shining points she found in him.
More importantly, Lide Kachar’s behavior carried a strong personal charm that made it hard for anyone not to be convinced and want to follow in his footsteps.
Working with such an excellent colleague who was hard to fault, even the most demanding person would find it difficult to feel displeased.
Moreover, he was extraordinarily handsome.
With that thought, Zhao Yue’s gaze flitted, and a slight blush surfaced on her charming face.
As someone who had both figure and beauty, as well as education and manners, she was considered a goddess in the eyes of most men and had never lacked suitors.
Among them, many were top-notch elites, with a number of young and wealthy ones in particular.
However, the only one who had ever truly impressed her seemed to be this man of utmost charisma.
Outstanding individuals, irrespective of gender, always drew more attention.
“Mr. Zhao?”
Lide Kachar, as if remembering something, paused in his steps, causing the absentminded Zhao Yue, who was following behind, to nearly bump into him. Thankfully, she managed to stop in time.
Slightly embarrassed, she smoothed the hair by her ears and looked up at the nearly perfect face that could arouse affection in anyone, her cheeks flushed as she spoke.
“Mr. Li, what’s the matter?”
Hearing this somewhat unnatural tone, Lide Kachar’s expression turned curious. He took a long look at Zhao Yue, who was dressed in high heels, black stockings, and a tight skirt; the voluptuous woman before him was as tempting as a ripe peach.
This older sister’s charm was truly unbeatable.
“The newly recruited executives will be joining us in the next couple of days, so I’ll be handing over the company’s management to you all. I’ve recently restructured the company’s system, and there aren’t any major flaws left at this time. As long as we continue to develop according to our established goals, there shouldn’t be too many problems.”
In these past few months, he hadn’t just come to the office for casual visits; he had reformed the existing systems of the Crimson Moon to better align with his preferences.
If it had been him before he stepped into “Glory,” even if placed in his current position, he wouldn’t have been able to make any effective decisions, since managing a company was never his strength.
But after having ruled over a city where every word and action could determine the fates of tens of thousands, managing a company of a mere thousand employees was absolutely a downgrade in complexities.
He could easily control the whole scene.
And the temperament he honed between life and death further unleashed his charm—Lide had truly become the undisputed number one heartthrob of Crimson Moon.
He was the object of discussion among almost every unmarried female employee every day.
“Mr. Li, are you leaving?”
Zhao Yue sensed the underlying implication in Lide’s words and felt an indiscernible twinge of loss in her heart.
“Not exactly leaving, I just have some preparatory work to do, and won’t have much time to manage the company in the short term. However, I will make time to visit the company every few days.”
Lide didn’t notice the real thoughts hidden behind Zhao Yue’s normal composure and said with a light laugh.
He had just realized during the meeting that his body in Glory had been fully reconstructed and was ready to return to the land that was truly his at any moment.
He was somewhat anxious to get back.
Even though only over two months had passed on Earth, more than half a year had gone by in Glory. He had to return and check on the situation in Dawn City.
After receiving Lide’s answer, Zhao Yue took a deep breath and said no more.
“Yes, Mr. Li. I will ensure the company operates according to your plans.”
Lide frowned slightly, sensing the stiffness in Zhao Yue’s tone. He wanted to say something, but Zhao Yue didn’t linger, clicking her high heels as she turned and left under the respectful gazes of the surrounding employees.
This scene left Lide somewhat puzzled—had he said something wrong?
Shaking his head.
Indeed, women are the most incomprehensible creatures in this world.
But my Miss Vena… She’s different.
He found himself missing his little maid.
Without further hesitation, he called his assistant Cheng Lu over, gave some instructions, and then left Crimson Moon.
After Lide left, Cheng Lu sneaked into Zhao Yue’s office with a slightly gossipy expression.
“Cousin…”
Seeing Cheng Lu slink into her office, Zhao Yue glared at her irritably.
“Call me Mr. Zhao here in the company; don’t be disrespectful.”
“Hehe~” Cheng Lu locked the door behind her and suddenly relaxed.
“How is that disrespectful? Even though we are distant relatives, the generational hierarchy stands~”
Zhao Yue closed the file in her hand and looked at her with penetrating eyes, “So, Lide didn’t ask you to handle some things before he left?”
Cheng Lu’s eyes darted around.
“Of course, he did. I’ve already taken care of it, and right now Old Zhou, the driver, is taking Mr. Li back.”
Saying this, she walked up to Zhao Yue, placed her hand on her shoulder, and began massaging, the slightly chubby girl wearing a gossipy smile.
“Cousin, Mr. Li is so handsome. Have you developed any feelings for him during these two months?”
Zhao Yue stiffened and said a little angrily, “What nonsense are you spouting, you little girl?!”
Cheng Lu’s eyes narrowed, sensing something was off with Zhao Yue, and hugged her neck, bending over to look at her from the side.
“Your expression… it’s off, very off. You usually wouldn’t react so strongly. It seems Mr. Li is indeed charming—to attract our lovely beauty in such a short time…”
Zhao Yue huffed coldly, “Cheng Lu, do you want me to tell your mother about you and your boyfriend?”
Cheng Lu’s face drained instantly, and she pleaded in a pathetic tone, “Cousin, you’re scaring me again.”
“Hmph, good to know. Just focus on your work, and once you buy your own place in Shanghai, there’s nothing your mom can do even if she disagrees.”
Cheng Lu finally breathed a sigh of relief, “Alright, I’ll just do as you say.”
But turning back, he still couldn’t let it go, “Still, Mr. Li is so young and wealthy, and moreover, incredibly handsome. Even I almost wavered. Cousin, are you really not moved at all?”
Zhao Yue slowly regained her composure and shook her head.
“Don’t overthink it. Mr. Li and I are just colleagues… work colleagues.”
Cheng Lu looked disappointed, then suddenly turned to gaze at Zhao Yue’s proud figure, stretched taut by her clothing, and suddenly pinched it before giggling and running out of the office.
“Cousin, that’s for scaring me.”
Thunk~
The door closed, and Zhao Yue, not knowing whether to laugh or cry, rubbed her chest, feeling an amazing sensation and blushing slightly.
Suddenly, she remembered Cheng Lu’s words earlier, and looking at the empty office, she found herself lost in thought for a moment…
Handsome… Young and promising…
—
—
—
Having returned to the villa he bought in Fairy Lake Residential Area, Lide Kachar took a comfortable shower.
The expansive villa was currently occupied by him alone, since he would be spending long periods in Glory and, for secrecy’s sake, he hadn’t hired a housekeeper.
Cleaning chores were done by robots, as the level of intelligence in the year 2051 was sufficient for robots to complete some housekeeping tasks.
After checking the house and finding nothing amiss, he lay down in the bedroom on the second floor of the villa and returned to Glory.
The luxurious villa entered a state of silence.
At this moment, Lide Kachar felt himself returning to that empty, desolate, pitch-black space.
However, unlike last time, he could now sense his body and control his limbs.
But when he tried to open his eyes, his eyelids felt as though they were weighed down by heavy iron balls, making him feel exceptionally heavy.
Even with all his might, it took a long, long time to barely open a sliver.
It was months later that he once again saw the world of Glory.
Blood red, a sea of blood red.
His view was filled with the sight of something like fresh blood, not yet coagulated, dripping before his eyes.
Once his eyes were open, a clearer sense of touch transmitted from all parts of his body, and he felt as if something had restrained his limbs.
He couldn’t move.
Lide Kachar gritted his teeth, continued to force his eyes open, and struggled to break free from the bindings.
Finally, after another extended period, crack~
Suddenly, a crisp sound like an eggshell breaking echoed in his ears.
Approaching a tearing sound, Lide Kachar felt as if he had broken some chains, his body tearing apart the restraints around him.
The feeling of being bound vanished instantly.
A surge of powerful strength returned to his body, and at this moment, Lide Kachar finally fully opened his eyes.
Looking around, he found himself lying in a blood pool filled with Magic Blood, and the initially waist-high Magic Blood was now only as high as his knees.
The milky Magic Blood with specks of crimson looked extremely eerie.
Next to him, the crystal-clear remains of a Divine floated.
Taking a deep breath, Lide Kachar stood up. It seemed that what he’d just broken free from was a cocoon formed by the Magic Blood, which had now dissolved back into the blood.
Looking at his naked body, a bitter smile appeared on his face.
He hadn’t expected this bodily reconstruction to cost him so much time.
On Earth, time moved from June 20th to September 10th, a total of 80 days, two and a half months.
But in Glory, it was 240 days, a full eight months.
This adventure had certainly exacted a hefty toll, but fortunately, the gains could make up for the losses.
Drawing a deep breath, he opened his attribute panel and glanced over it.
Lide Kachar
Status: Weak (All attributes decreased by 30%, lasting 30 days)
Race: Bloodline (Ancestor)
Legend Level: 7 (+1) Renowned, with a Legend Level of 8 in the Underworld.
Title: Master of Crimson, Immortal King
Level: Blood Clan Ancestor lv18 (20330/500,000)
Magic Power: 3500/3500
Bloodline: Ancestor Bloodline (Perfect), Evolution Level 30% (Can increase by consuming fresh blood)
Skill: Blood Rebirth (limited) A bat can be left in the Bloodline’s blood pool; after the host dies, it can be reborn in the blood pool, weak for one month after rebirth, cooldown time three months.
Other…
A few minor changes had occurred on the attribute panel. Firstly, a new Weak status appeared behind his status bar, lasting an entire month.
Clearly, it was the penalty of Blood Rebirth.
At the same time, the Evolution Level of his bloodline had increased from the original 15% to 30%.
He now also had twenty thousand Experience Points. Randy, as a fanatic believer system, had rewarded him with 5000, and Frey’s advancement to level 15 had earned 5000 more, apart from the constant one point of experience provided by the Bloodline every month.
The original Bloodline number was 740. November and December provided 1480 points, and based on the hints from the System Space, after January the number of the Bloodline had doubled.
The System Space currently showed a count of 1475 Bloodline, meaning that only five did not perform the initial embracing, while all other Bloodline had initiated their embrace during Lide’s rebirth period.
The first two embracings took place after the Dawn Festival, implying that from January to June, the Experience Points were calculated based on 1475, which added up to 8850 points over six months.
After briefly calculating, Lide couldn’t help but show an intense look of joy on his face.
Experience was secondary. Most importantly, the Bloodline now had a force nearly 1500 strong, a change substantial enough to be called a qualitative transformation.
If Dawn City continued to develop like this for three more years, the number of the Bloodline would break the ten-thousand mark.
A force of ten thousand spellcasters, a power that no one could ignore.
The Bloodline’s explosive soldier mode can only demonstrate its advantages after reaching a certain number.
Of course, the more numerous the Bloodline, the higher the demands on logistics. To expand unrestrainedly, a sufficient population to implement a sustainable development strategy was essential.
Fortunately, Lide had always been very solid on this path.
After emerging from the blood pool, he found clothes from within the System Space and dressed himself.
However, after getting dressed, Lide’s expression subtly tensed.
He noticed something off about the System Space.
The System Space was a space opened within the Dimension Plane and was not of the virtual panel style; all his belongings piled up there—Magic Blood, Alchemy Bombs, change of clothes, and the twelve Spider Queen’s eggs forcibly taken from the Spider Nest.
Plus, that mysterious Bronze Egg.
What was strange to him was that there was an issue with those twelve Spider Queen’s eggs.
They weren’t missing but rather, all of the originally pale gold eggs had cracked open, and due to the passage of time, the egg liquids inside had turned into dry substances.
Conversely, the originally lackluster Bronze Egg, placed beside those Spider Queen’s eggs, now shimmered with a bit of light, as if it had been polished and shined.
Unknown Bronze Egg
Status: In deep slumber
Description: Seems to be the egg of some mighty life form that has devoured a portion of Plane Power during its slumber, but due to the passage of time, it has lost most of its vitality and requires strong Life Force for reactivation.
Although the properties of the Bronze Egg had not changed, Lide immediately identified the culprit.
“This is ridiculous, with so many Star Magic Crystal Stones around, you only absorb the Spider Queen’s eggs…”
His spirit swept through the entire space, finally discovering the sole surviving Spider Egg in a corner away from the Bronze Egg.
“Out of twelve, only one survivor remains…”
Lide couldn’t help feeling a pang of heartache.
The eggs born of extraordinaire spiders, to say nothing else, certainly did not lack potential.
His gaze returned to the Bronze Egg with a somewhat complicated expression.
He felt that this unassuming Bronze Egg had an extraordinary origin, but he had yet to find a way to hatch it.
He considered taking it out for research, but after a moment’s thought, he refrained from further action. For now, it was best to go see the situation in Dawn City first.
He had been away for so long, and he wondered what the state of Dawn City was now.
Turning around, he pushed open the door of the stone hut.
Creak~
As the door opened, the figure of someone filled with excitement appeared within the warmly lit cave by a magic lamp.
“Your Majesty, you have finally awakened.”
Frey, now promoted to Level 15 and having advanced his profession of Crimson Hunter to the second phase, could barely contain the joy on his face.
Eight months, such a long time that it had been difficult for him to remain calm—fortunately, Lide turned out to be alright.
Seeing Frey, Lide also felt a sense of familiarity; after all, it had been over two months since they’d seen each other.
“Frey, how has Dawn City developed these past few months, any changes?”
His greatest concern was that Dawn City had fallen into a developmental stagnation due to his rebirth.
He was the soul of this city, the master of all Holy Light Bloodline beings,
If he were to be in a predicament, then all actions of the Bloodline would be arranged with his safety as the top priority.
That was his worry. The first time when his Bloodline had transformed, the development of Dawn City had significantly slowed; he certainly did not want to see that state repeated.
“Your Majesty, due to your foresight and the arrangements made last time, our development has been entirely normal.”
Even the typically prideful Frey still had excitement on his face that hadn’t faded.
No one had felt more tormented than he in these past months.
He had watched with his own eyes as Lide headed into the Spider Nest, then had sensed Lide’s downfall.
If he hadn’t already known about the talent “Rebirth in Blood,” he might’ve recklessly rushed in to perish alongside those dirty, disgusting, vomit-inducing spiders.
The Holy Light Bloodline never feared death.
“Alright, we can talk about this later, let’s head to City Hall first.”
Lide did not want to discuss further; clearly, the sacred place was not fit for conversation.
Eight months in this world, he wondered how much had changed in Dawn City; upon stepping out of the sacred place, he felt an unusual bout of slight nervousness alongside his strong anticipation.
As Lide stepped out of the sacred place and flew back to City Hall,
All the high-ranking beings received the news.
The king of this city had returned.
Their ruler would once again govern them.
In less than twenty minutes, all the top-ranking officials who were still in Dawn City hurriedly returned to City Hall with great enthusiasm.
City Hall Speaker Harrison, Level 15 Bloodline Frey, Level 18 Beastman King Kapp, the sisters of the Dawn Sect, Nilo and Nicole.
Along with the disfigured former goblin chief Moer, dwarf Forging Master Valen, the principal of Dawn Academy, and the human polymath Horn.
The most powerful high-ranking officials of Dawn City had all arrived.
Stanley was still out running the Dawn’s Shadow project in Green City, Shadow High Priest Emi, and Level 16 Werewolf Craig had no news in Risier City.
Lide looked at the talent-filled scene, feeling very pleased.
This was the team he had built from scratch.
Each one capable and invaluable, standing strong on their own.
And those below, upon seeing Lide safe and sound, were overjoyed in their hearts.
Lide was the single, irreplaceable core of Dawn City; if he were compromised, no one could imagine what the city would become.
The Beastmen would surely claim independence, the Dwarves would likely leave, and even the Humans might no longer heed the Bloodline’s command.
Chaos and internal strife would be the only themes of the city.
Fortunately, none of this had happened, and now, the master of this city had returned.
Everyone could palpably feel the united atmosphere within the room.
“Good day, Your Majesty…”
“Good day, Clan Leader…”
After everyone exchanged greetings, Lide didn’t beat around the bush, moving to the rarely used main seat of the thirty-person long table in the office.
The others took their seats according to rank.
“I have been asleep for eight months; I need to know everything that has happened in Dawn City over the past half year.”
Although Lide had returned, he still felt somewhat estranged from this city to which he had been away for so long. He needed to grasp the current situation in Dawn City.
Three months after Glory Time, the game would enter its public beta. No one could predict what might happen with the arrival of the players.
He must make certain arrangements for this immediately.
While on the whole the players’ strength couldn’t pose much danger to Dawn City, the Broken Sword Knight had made him aware of the power of some high-level players.
Maybe the threat wasn’t significant on the surface, but who knows what clever moves they could pull off in secret.
The idea of mass-producing Bone Dragons was the most typical example, a method that could directly enhance the foundation of the Undead race, not to be underestimated.
“Harrison, you first report the work of the City Hall.”
“Yes, Clan Leader.”
Harrison, the one who was called upon, stood up with a solemn expression and began to report.
“Clan Leader, everything in Dawn City has been normal these past months; according to the contingency plans you left, we didn’t stop development during your slumber.
We have still maintained a strong upward momentum.
First, population.
Last year, in Frost Month, we plundered over 50,000 people from the northern region near Green City, and these people have now been assimilated into Dawn City, becoming part of our strength.
At present, the total population of Dawn City has exceeded 100,000.”
100,000… Upon hearing this number that surpassed his expectations, a hint of joy appeared on Lide’s face.
Population is the foundation of Dawn City’s development. Only with people could the Bloodline prosper, only with people could various industries kick-start.
Dawn City had taken another firm step forward on the basis of becoming a major city.
“Secondly, food.
Aside from the land that has been reserved, all available land on Moonlight Plain has been allotted to the residents.
The winter wheat from the last year was harvested at the end of March this year, and the first spring wheat of this year is expected to be harvested at the end of August.
Right now, our food production is enough for the annual consumption of 200,000 people each season, with a full year’s output able to support a consumption for 400,000 people.
At the moment, food stockpiles are sufficient for a year’s consumption of 200,000 people.”
Harrison paused here to give Lide time to ponder before he continued.
“However, what warrants caution is that, currently, there are over 40,000 people who have not been allotted land.
Half of them are employees of the City Hall and various factories. Around 10,000 are the elderly and children, who don’t have much capacity for labor,
and the last approximately 10,000 are craftsmen, merchants, students, and even priests and the reserve army, etc.”
Lide nodded slightly.
Population is the base of Dawn City, and food is the foundation of the population.
The importance of food is self-evident; agriculture is always the first sector that needs to be assured.
As for those without land, he wasn’t overly concerned; agriculture is the primary sector but not everything, as the secondary sector, industry, also needs a lot of manpower.
Currently, Dawn City was vigorously promoting the development of magical industrialization, which could fully accommodate this surplus population.
“Continue.”
“Thirdly, construction of the new urban area.
The first phase of the new urban area has been completed, and the second phase is being constructed at an accelerated pace, expected to be finished around October, and it is estimated it will accommodate a population of 80,000.”
The new urban area is the only way for Dawn City to expand its scale and is the priority in the short term.
According to Lide’s estimate, the new urban area once fully constructed is expected to accommodate a population of 300,000.
Dawn City will become a true metropolis.
Of course, to truly achieve this goal would still require a long time, and countless human and material resources to invest.
Having ascertained that the basic situation of Dawn City hadn’t changed and was still progressing steadily in a favorable direction, Lide’s expression relaxed considerably.
As long as Dawn City was still developing stably, any other issues weren’t significant; everything was still within controllable limits.
Dawn City was the base of all his powers. As long as the base didn’t fall, even if his other forces met destruction, he could rebuild them in a short time.
After not inquiring any further detailed questions from Harrison, Lide turned his attention to Kapp.
Only then did he begin to inquire about the development of the Underworld; evidently, the priority of Dawn City was much higher than that of the Underworld.
“Kapp, after I fell in battle, was there any disturbance in the Spider Plane? Did you detect the presence of any Extraordinary Spiders?”
Kapp’s massive Lion Tribe head nodded, then shook, speaking in a solemn tone.
“Your Majesty, about thirteen Sunshine Hours after your departure, countless Cave Spiders assaulted the area we were guarding.
The numbers were so overwhelming that we had to abandon the entrance to the Underworld in less than a day due to heavy casualties, and establish our defenses within the caves.
The Cave Spiders’ frenzy lasted a full month before calming down.
Only after receiving support from the logistics units were we able to re-establish our defenses at the entrance to the Underworld and stabilize the regions under our control.”
“During the Cave Spiders’ assault, numerous Level 15 Ghost-faced Spiders appeared, but we did not encounter any Extraordinary ones.”
Lide Kachar breathed a sigh of relief upon hearing this.
Those two Extraordinary spiders truly could not leave the Spider Plane.
His own eggs had been stolen, and he could not believe the enemy would remain indifferent; and had the enemy been able to leave without finding the spider eggs, they would not have strictly guarded the Spider Plane.
With this critical information confirmed, a smile crept onto Lide Kachar’s face.
“What is the current situation in the Underworld, and how much territory do we control? Have there been any new discoveries?”
“Your Majesty, because of the sheer density of the Cave Spiders, we haven’t expanded our area much during this time.
For now, we’ve constructed a military fortress at the entrance that can accommodate 2,000 people.
Our small teams explore the Underworld through infiltration.
Within a 500-kilometer radius of the entrance, we have conducted a thorough investigation.
We’ve also discovered several powerful races and precious ore veins.
Koso, after finding traces of the Thunder Tribe, is now searching for the One-eyed Giant Tribe in the Muddy Marshes.”
Lide Kachar’s brow furrowed slightly, as he was not entirely satisfied with Kapp’s report; the progress in the Underworld seemed too slow.
Now, after more than half a year, they were still only at the preliminary stage of exploration, which made him shake his head.
“Kapp, I’m entrusting you with full responsibility for the Underworld. I need you to expedite the exploration process and clarify the distribution of forces within a thousand kilometers as quickly as possible.
Our main objective is to capture the Spider Nest, where the Magic Crystal Ore veins we need are located, so prepare for a protracted battle.”
After finishing his instructions, Lide Kachar did not wait for Kapp’s response but turned to Harrison.
“Harrison, take note, have the Intelligence Command Center immediately devise no fewer than five plans for seizing the Magic Crystal Stone veins.
Dawn City’s next strategic focus will be on conquering the Magic Crystal Ore veins and developing the Underworld.
Everything else can be postponed for now.”
“Yes, Your Majesty.”
Harrison immediately confirmed.
Having briefly addressed his most pressing concerns, Lide Kachar did not delve further and turned his attention to the others.
“Horn, how’s the progress of the Divine Gifted Holy Armor at the Magic Industry Research Institute?”
The Divine Gifted Holy Armor was a key step in freeing the Bloodline from their shackles. The project had been going on for nearly a year with significant investment of resources and labor.
Eight months prior, the Magic Industry Research Institute had already presented a prototype, and after several months of refinement, Lide Kachar was quite eager to hear good news.
Horn, the head of the Dawn Academy, had a hint of proud smile on his face. “Your Majesty, with the help of a large amount of Thorns Heart juice provided by Lady Nilo,
the development of the Divine Gifted Holy Armor has been refined to the thirteenth version and has reached the mass production stage.
Just give us one more month, and we’ll start mass-producing Divinely Gifted Holy Armors fit for everyone.”
Lide Kachar’s brow smoothed, and his mood improved considerably.
“Good, make sure to prioritize the development; we need the Divine Gifted Holy Armor.”
The Divine Gifted Holy Armor would enable the Bloodline to become immune to Light Attribute powers; such overbearing equipment would undoubtedly bring a significant upgrade to the already nearly 1,500 Bloodline members.
How strong the Bloodline would become without fear of sunlight, no one could know.
“As you wish.”
After Horn’s response, Lide Kachar continued to focus on Harrison.
“Harrison, how are things going with the Crimson Mage Tower and the Dark Contract?”
After getting a rough idea of the situation inside Dawn City, he immediately shifted his attention to the external forces.
Both forces were situated in Green City, whose development environment was good but couldn’t compare to the unrestricted Dawn City.
“Clan Leader, under Miss Vena’s leadership, the Crimson Mage Tower is developing well; it currently supplies us with nearly three hundred thousand Gold Pucks worth of resources every month,” Harrison had a firm grasp on these matters and began his report without hesitation.
“The Dark Contract, under Stanley’s management, has begun a new round of expansion.
The intelligence network structured around the Dark Contract has officially been activated; currently, our intelligence command center acquires a large amount of information daily, providing strong support for our various operations.”
The Crimson Mage Tower, the moneybag,
The Dark Contract, the intelligence network,
Both forces are irreplaceable extensions of Dawn City’s reach and influence.
Lide nodded with satisfaction, his heart completely at ease.
“Very good, Frey, report on the Dwarf Hill Ridges and the Fishman Tribe,” he persisted, continuing to call on his subordinates.
“Yes, Your Majesty,” Frey respectfully stood up, “The free market we’ve established in the Dwarf Hill Ridges has become the largest and most attractive region on the land controlled by the Centaur Tribe.
According to preliminary statistics, over a million centaurs have already visited the free market to trade.
