chapters.content:
Chapter 364: Chapter 366: The Fruitful Results of the Strategy Laid Two Years Ago (6000 words) Chapter 364: Chapter 366: The Fruitful Results of the Strategy Laid Two Years Ago (6000 words) The wind, carrying ice and frost, howled through the sky like the wailing of ghosts.
Snowflakes shrouded the light, turning the entire field of vision into a blanket of white.
As Lide pondered, the figure of Castro suddenly slowed down.
“Master, below us lies the Iron Hoof Tribe…”
His thoughts were interrupted by a voice as thunderous as rolling thunder, and when he looked down sideways, a vast expanse of buildings came into his view.
From high above, the edge was nowhere in sight; the houses, mostly single-storied, didn’t seem low despite that, with snow piling up on the roofs, accumulating like rounded steamed buns.
On the crisscrossing streets, only a sparse number of Centaurs were seen clearing away the snow, with nearly no pedestrians to speak of.
This place was entirely like a human city–except for the lack of walls.
More than a year had passed since his last visit, and the Iron Hoof Tribe had been completely transformed.
After a slight sensing, Lide quickly detected Frey’s presence within this vast stretch of buildings that seemed endless at first glance.
A subtle signal, and the remaining Castros immediately shot towards the center of the city.
This enormous beast, with a wingspan of 16 blades and clad in Extraordinary Armor, filled the snowy sky with a chilling, fearsome aura.
At that moment, the Centaurs below spotted the massive body of Li Castro, causing a huge commotion.
Wuu wuu~
The strident sounds of horns blared, and then the quiet city suddenly erupted into chaos.
In the towering watchtowers, torches were rapidly lit, crossbows readied, and Centaur Warriors, not yet fully equipped in armor, carrying huge helmets emerged from the dwellings and barracks with murderous intent.
Centaurs wielding longbows already had their bows drawn, and arrows gleaming with a cold light aimed at the beast in the sky, as if at any second the shrill whistling of arrows would erupt.
Hundreds of large figures rose from a barracks, their screams akin to demonic whispers–the Magic Language Bats.
But amid all the vigilance, the Centaurs below were astounded to find that after the Magic Language Bats took flight, they did not attack the terrifying beast; instead, they circled around it, escorting it.
Some Centaurs, upon witnessing this scene, seemed to remember something and hurriedly shouted for the others to lower their crossbows.
“It’s the Kachar City Lord, the Hand of Glory of the Iron Hoof Tribe!”
If the title Kachar City Lord was unfamiliar to many Centaurs, Hand of Glory, the shining title that symbolized the strongest warrior of the Centaur tribe, was known to all.
As more and more Centaurs recognized the giant beast in the sky as belonging to the man who had once conquered them, the initial vigilance began to fade, and the drawn crossbows were slowly withdrawn.
Guided by the swarm of Magic Language Bats, Lide landed within their military camp.
By the time he emerged from the multitude of Magic Language Bats, he found the Level 15 tribal chief, Sam Ironhoof, and the second-generation Bloodline Frey, also Level 15, waiting for him at the entrance of the camp.
Upon seeing Lide, the towering Centaur Chieftain, as tall as 3.5 blades and as robust as a great tree, stepped forward, plunging his sturdy long-handled battle axe into the ground, and thumped his chest in salute.
“Good day, honored Hand of Glory, mighty Kachar City Lord, the Iron Hoof Tribe welcomes your arrival…”
“Welcome, Lord Hand of Glory,”
Behind them, a dozen strong Centaurs, each standing 3 blades tall, followed their Chieftain’s lead, thumping their chests; their resonant voices echoed down several streets, attracting the curious gaze of countless Centaurs.
At this moment, Frey, dressed in a black mage’s robe, also elegantly stepped forward. The somewhat proud second-generation Bloodline bowed slightly, “Good day, my lord.”
Lide nodded slightly, his gaze containing a smile as he looked towards Sam, “Chieftain Sam, it’s been many days, it seems the Iron Hoof Tribe has progressed quite well…”
Although in essence, the Iron Hoof Tribe was already a part of Dawn City, with Frey being the true Power Holder, at least outwardly, the Iron Hoof Tribe was still independent; this was similar to the Lion Tribe in Dwarf Valley.
“Kachar City Lord, all of this is thanks to your support…”
Sam presented a very humble attitude, knowing full well the current situation of the Iron Hoof Tribe.
In fact, with Dawn City’s growing influence over the hills, he had long since cast aside any other aspirations.
Once, Dawn City was already more than they could fend off; the incident where the Black Wind Tribe’s twenty thousand Centaur Warriors were carpet-bombed by Alchemy Bombs from Magic Language Bats, and subsequently devoured by Blood Mages controlling tens of thousands of savage bats, still lingered vividly in his mind.
Not to mention the now even better developed Dawn City.
“Chieftain Sam, you are a smart man. Your wise choice has allowed the Iron Hoof Tribe to survive, and it has also won you a tomorrow.
Believe me, as long as you follow in the footsteps of Dawn City, the Iron Hoof Tribe will not only survive, it will grow even stronger.”
Lide’s gaze was like a torch, blazing as he stared at this group of Centaur leaders of the Iron Hoof Tribe, his tone filled with confidence and dominance.
“That is Kachar’s promise to you.”
Sam’s expression was somewhat moved, “Kachar City Lord, the Iron Hoof Tribe will faithfully follow your lead to the death.”
After finishing his words, he turned his head to glance at the crowd, where an old centaur, who bore a striking resemblance to Sam, nodded with a complex expression.
Then Sam took a deep breath as if he had made up his mind. With a somewhat surprised look from Lide, Sam stepped forward and knelt on his front hooves to begin his oath of fealty.
“Oi…pf…nq…Great divine abode that controls death and souls, I am your loyal servant, I am your most devout believer, I am willing to use your power to sign a soul contract with my master…”
A soul contract?
Lide was completely astonished; he had not expected the centaur chieftain to be so resolute.
Seeing this scene, the dozen or so centaurs around Sam, as if they had already discussed it, also knelt down in loyalty.
In just a short moment, Lide felt more than a dozen strands of soul power added to his spiritual sea, and should he wish, he could use that soul power to end the lives of those who had taken the oath at any time.
The number of people one could bind with a soul contract depended on one’s own soul strength; if the strength was insufficient, even binding with a level 1 apprentice would not succeed.
Lide was clearly not someone ordinary people could compare with. After several transformations, it was easy for him to contract hundreds or even thousands of people.
“Rise, Sam; your actions have once again secured a future for you and the Iron Hoof Tribe…”
After speaking, Lide gave a glance to the old centaur in the crowd, his eyes full of admiration. The Iron Hoof Tribe has wise individuals, indeed.
In fact, had Sam not sworn an oath, Lide would have used the power of faith to convert the other party.
The Dwarf Hills were becoming increasingly important, and he could not allow Sam, who had the greatest influence there, to slip out of his control.
“As you wish, my lord…”
After standing up, Sam immediately changed his tone of speech.
With the development of the Iron Hoof Tribe, he had long noticed that the Iron Hoof Tribe stood at a crossroads; its existence was merely at the whim of Lide.
Even thinking from the other’s perspective, if he were in their place, he wouldn’t allow a group of people outside his control to wield such important power; in fact, he had already begun purging and had started replacing everything here with his own people.
Now that Lide had arrived, he even felt it was somewhat late… A true master worthy of following should be one who makes decisions decisively and has a firm will.
Putting himself in others’ shoes, Sam had thought about resistance, but the power displayed by Dawn City was simply beyond the capacity of the Iron Hoof Tribe to resist.
Even most centaurs had gradually accepted their identity as part of Dawn City under its rule, and many were adamantly against going to war with Dawn City.
With their own power weak and internal stability shaky, not to mention the existence of a faction ready to surrender, on one side was a bright and brilliant future, on the other, the abyss of death.
It was only at this juncture that Sam had quietly realized he no longer had a choice.
So when he proposed the idea of loyalty, he unexpectedly received unanimous agreement from all the high-ranking centaurs.
Swearing allegiance to a being who had conquered giant dragons and possessed immense strength did not seem humiliating to the centaurs; being under the protection of the stronger was an instinct for survival.
And only the strong could provide them with a better future.
This seemingly abrupt scene was the result of the strategy Lide had laid out two years ago.
At the time, Dawn City was weak and lacked the capacity to manage a tribe like the Iron Hoof Tribe, so they had adopted an alliance approach to win it over.
But as Dawn City developed rapidly in many aspects, the Iron Hoof Tribe was naturally enveloped by it, and by the time they realized the problem and thought of rebelling, it was already too late.
After the brief and sudden swearing of loyalty, Sam and a group of centaurs followed Lide to the central area’s housing.
Most of the centaurs’ previous buildings were temporary, typically tents made of sewn animal hides.
But after Frey took over the Iron Hoof Tribe, he began building a large number of permanent dwellings, greatly improving the living conditions of the centaurs.
After all, compared to houses that could shelter from wind and rain, animal hide tents were too crude.
It is easy to move from frugality to luxury, but difficult to revert; accustomed to a better life, the centaurs naturally did not want to return to their previous poor living conditions.
Entering the house, a wave of warmth hit them, and the hissing of burning charcoal filled the fireplace, making the air much warmer.
Lide casually surveyed the house; it was constructed of stone and wood. Although it lacked a bit of delicacy and appeared somewhat rough, it was still sturdier than tents and far more practical.
Inside, there were no chairs, but on the thick animal hide carpet, there were neatly arrayed tables.
After entering, the centaurs sat directly on the carpet, with each table marking one spot.
Fortunately, Lide did not mind these details. He sat down on the main spot, which was padded with thick animal hides.
Next to the large-bodied centaurs, both he and Frey appeared rather slender.
But with his strong presence, Lide still firmly controlled the situation.
His profound gaze swept over the group, and the centaurs who made eye contact quickly lowered their heads in submission. Without further formality, Lide dove straight into the matter at hand.
“Sam, report on the current situation of the Iron Hoof Tribe, starting with the population numbers…”
“Yes, Your Highness.”
The Level 15 Chieftain Sam immediately stood up, paid his respects, and then, feeling it was improper to look down on Lide from a standing position, sat back down and began his report earnestly.
“Your Highness, at present, the Iron Hoof Tribe has a population of 87,000 people, which includes 40,000 Heavy Cavalry and 30,000 Archers. The remaining are the elderly and weak who cannot be deployed to the battlefield…”
Sam’s first statement brought Lide a huge surprise; he hadn’t expected the Iron Hoof Tribe to have expanded to such an extent.
If he remembered correctly, the other party was originally just a small tribe with a population of less than 20,000. Now, the population had nearly reached 90,000 and was marching towards 100,000. Their expansion pace was not necessarily slower than that of Dawn City.
“How did these people come to be?” Lide asked curiously.
“Your Highness, through war and annexation.”
Sam spoke of this issue with a hint of excitement, “With the equipment support from Dawn City, the Iron Hoof Tribe encountered no match at the edge of the Dwarf Hills.
Our armored warriors in Heavy Cavalry charged like an unstoppable steel torrent that other tribes’ Centaur Warriors could not withstand, and our Archers’ arrows could easily tear through their Bone Armor and flesh, while their weapons couldn’t even scratch our armor…”
“The area near the barren wastelands has been conquered by us. Apart from a few large tribes, all the smaller ones have been integrated into the Iron Hoof Tribe.
Additionally, as the reputation of the Iron Hoof Tribe has begun to spread, many small tribes have sought to join us voluntarily, which accounts for some of the population…”
Lide nodded, his eyes flickering with contemplation.
“What is the reaction of the other Centaur Tribes to the Iron Hoof Tribe’s expansion? Has there been any movement from Gale City?”
The Dwarf Hills had an unavoidable central point — Gale City — which was the very heart of the Dwarf Hills.
Most of the large Centaur Tribe settlements were concentrated around Gale City, where the land was fertile and could support much larger populations than the fringe areas.
If the Iron Hoof Tribe wished to continue growing, it would inevitably have to confront Gale City.
As a city overseen by a Transcendent being, Gale City’s stance could nearly dictate the direction of the Iron Hoof Tribe’s development.
“Your Highness, there has been no movement from Gale City; we are still too far from them, and the central region is far richer than where we are…
As for the tribes around the Iron Hoof Tribe, they have remained silent about our expansion…”
“Oh? Are they not threatened by the swift expansion of the Iron Hoof Tribe?”
“Your Highness, in truth, outside of facing a common external enemy, there is not much interaction between races. As long as we don’t encroach upon the larger tribes’ territories, they do not concern themselves much with our expansion.”
Sam’s response surprised Lide somewhat; he could understand the distance from Gale City, but were these surrounding Centaur Tribes unaware of the proverb ‘When the lips are gone, the teeth will be cold’?
If the Iron Hoof Tribe grew strong, they might very well be the next target. Were they simply going to stand by and watch?
Lide was somewhat amused; he could not quite grasp the thought processes of these non-human races.
But, this too was a good thing — the Centaurs’ lack of response meant that the Iron Hoof Tribe had more time to develop.
“Mm, very good. The Iron Hoof Tribe should increase its efforts to expand its population.
Employ ‘Distant Diplomacy and Close Conquest’, treat the larger tribes with gifts, and engage in trade to win their support, while continuing plans to annex the smaller tribes.
I hope that the population of the Iron Hoof Tribe can double by the time I visit next…”
Lide’s eyes shone with the eagerness of ambitious enterprise.
“Sam, do you remember the promise I made to you before? In the future, I will build a city for the Iron Hoof Tribe.
And now, I give you a more specific commitment: once the population of the Iron Hoof Tribe reaches two hundred thousand, Dawn City will use all its power to establish Iron Hoof City in this land!
A city that bears the surname of the Iron Hoof Tribe as its name.”
Population, it always came back to population; whatever one wanted to do required a population as a prerequisite.
If there was room for development for the Iron Hoof Tribe, then they should keep on developing until they hit the ceiling.
Lide’s thinking was clear; no matter when, the more power one had in hand, the better.
Let alone the situation now, where there might be a major change at the Divine Ruins in Risier City.
He needed an army potent enough to command.
The Divine Ruins were too valuable, and obtaining even a fraction of its treasures could bring a windfall to Dawn City. Though he had glimpsed the Chaos and Eye of Death, he was not about to be intimidated.
The timid could not savor the richness of crabs.
Moreover, unlike before, the changes in Risier City had now drawn the attention of Sects, adventurers, and factions everywhere.
To employ the power of Bloodline under these circumstances would be suicidal, and those humans might see Bloodline as an enemy.
The power shown by the Iron Hoof Tribe gave him additional plans, and the Centaurs would become another card in his hand.
40,000 Centaur Heavy Cavalry and 30,000 Centaur Archers, these two forces were the ace armies of the Centaur Tribe, and both had established illustrious military records in the Glory Main Plane.
It could be said that possessing such an army meant that as long as the situation in Risier City didn’t spiral out of control, like the emergence of a complete Divine being, then the power in his hands absolutely could not be underestimated, as he would indeed be able to share a part of the spoils.
The arrangements from two years ago had finally borne abundant fruit.
“My lord, the Iron Hoof Tribe will not disappoint you!”
The promise from Lide had Sam almost jumping with excitement.
“We will honor your will with our lives, and within a year, the population of the Iron Hoof Tribe will surely surpass two hundred thousand!”
To build a city was an irresistible temptation for the Iron Hoof Tribe.
Thousands of years ago, the Iron Hoof Tribe had constituted the royal family of Gale City, where they once called the shots, but as the tribe declined, their former glory had long drifted away from them. It was precisely because of this that their obsession was so strong.
To have a city named after their own surname was simply an allure too strong for the Centaurs to resist.
Lide’s eyes were sharp and piercing as he stared intensely at Sam, his tone deep.
“My promise never falls flat.
Shaman, get the Iron Hoof Tribe ready, for there might be a great war looming, and the battlefield will be in Risier City, the city now occupied by the Beastmen.”
Lide’s words caused Sam’s expression to tighten.
“My lord, 70,000 Centaur Warriors of the Iron Hoof Tribe are at your command, ready to fight for you at any moment!
The Iron Hoof Tribe, fears nothing!”
The other Centaurs also showed excitement. As a Strong Battle Race, the Centaurs were violence enthusiasts, and now with the support of high-grade equipment from Dawn City, they were eager to test the sharpness of their battle axes and arrows.
“I will instruct the weapon factories to forge even higher Level equipment for you, and at the same time, you must ensure that all warriors are mentally prepared.
This war may well be more brutal than you can imagine.”
Lide’s dark eyes revealed a complexity that outsiders could not detect, yet he did not elaborate further on matters of the Divine, as this information did not need to be widely known.
After giving a precautionary warning, he changed the subject.
“Sam, Dawn City will establish a complete City Hall system soon, and all subordinate forces must obey the commands of City Hall.
I will also set up a subordinate department of City Hall in the Iron Hoof Tribe–the Department of Municipality.
In the future, you will serve as the head of this department, and Frey as the deputy head, with direct commands from City Hall transmitted to you…”
This matter was actually the true purpose of Lide’s visit to the Iron Hoof Tribe–to establish a unified command system, reclaiming the powers previously delegated to various factions.
In the past he hadn’t imposed this, leading to each internal power fighting independently, but now such a system clearly did not suit the future development of Dawn City.
He had to centralize power back to the City Hall and implement a centralization policy.
In both feudal monarchies and modern societies, centralizing power is essential. The result of dispersing power often leads to internal undermining, with irrational competition forming among the various factions.
With power in City Hall’s hands, they could better regulate the development of all factions, balance and coordinate arrangements, and avoid falling into the vicious cycle of destructive competition.
If this were before his allegiance, such measures would undoubtedly have met with Sam’s objections, but now Sam was more decisive than anyone in agreeing.
“My lord, we will faithfully execute your orders.”
Lide nodded slightly, turning his gaze to Frey, who had been silent all along.
“Frey, is there anything you’d like to say?”
“My lord,” Frey stood up, giving a slight bow, his eyes flickering sharply before he slowly spoke, “The Chief of the Black Wind Tribe, the Level 17 Centaur with the activated Gale Bloodline, Guido, has already secured a foothold by the sea, but currently his rate of development is still far too slow. Should we increase our support for him?”
“Guido?”
Lide nodded slightly; Guido’s initial role in his plan was to attract the attention of Gale City by raising the banner of re-establishing the Centaur Empire, thus sharing the burden of the Iron Hoof Tribe’s development.
But now, his development was clearly slow.
“Notify the Propaganda Department to send a group of propagandists there, and also have the Iron Hoof Tribe cooperate with the Propaganda Department’s efforts. I want to promote Guido as the Centaur Savior!”
A playful glint crossed Lide’s eyes; the half-task style reward he had received in the Underworld before–earning Legend Level for safely escorting 5 Half-Elves back to Black Iron Castle–he had yet to complete.
That is to say, although those 5 Half-Elves returned to Black Iron Castle, because he did not promote his conquest of the giants in the Muddy Swamps, he did not gain Legend Level.
Adding Lord Ilo’s identity into the mix confirmed his suspicion–that as long as others are willing to believe your words, even if you haven’t done that act, you can still gain Legend Level.
He planned to experiment with Guido.
The second Child of Destiny was about to emerge.
Players had already been hoodwinked, but it was uncertain how the Centaurs would react.

chapters.title: Chapter 365 - Chapter 365 Chapter 367 The Half-Elfs Faith Journey in Dawn
chapters.content:
Chapter 365: Chapter 367: The Half-Elf’s Faith Journey in Dawn City (Part 1) (5000 words) Chapter 365: Chapter 367: The Half-Elf’s Faith Journey in Dawn City (Part 1) (5000 words) “Clayson! By order, this is a military command directly issued by the City Lord!
Remember, although you are the most talented among us, you were picked up by Black Iron City! It was Black Iron Castle that nurtured you, without Black Iron Castle you would have been eaten by those filthy monsters long ago, you owe everything to repay Black Iron Castle!”
“If I refuse?!! This isn’t the first time, what I’ve given is more than enough to pay for my life ten times over!!”
“No, you have no right to refuse, your only task now is to go to the Vampire’s city, then cooperate with them to develop bows and arrows, while also spying on their intelligence, bringing back every piece of news about that city.”
Bang~
After a fierce argument, the Half-Elf messenger slammed the door and left.
Clayson Grey Claw, this young Half-Elf clenched his fists tightly, his eyes filled with anger.
“Am I just a tool in your eyes??
I developed the most powerful bows for Black Iron Castle, upgraded the siege crossbows, made the sharpest arrows, boosting the power of Black Iron Castle by at least thirty percent, but in the end, you still don’t trust me??
Just because I’m not a descendant of the Grey Claw Tribe, but someone you picked up from an enemy tribe after the war??”
After a long while, Clayson sighed despondently.
“Fine, if I have to go to the Vampire’s city, let’s go, maybe they didn’t plan on letting me come back alive.
It’s actually funny, if I hadn’t developed such good longbows, maybe I could still live a peaceful life like before…
Damn bastards, to hog this merit for themselves, they actually want to send me to my death at the Vampires’!! Damn it!!”
But no matter how much he complained, a military order was a military order, and Black Iron Castle’s commands could possibly be relaxed for other Half-Elves, but for him, they were exceptionally strict.
Since he was picked up from a tribe annihilated by Black Iron Castle after the war, if not for his outstanding research talent, he might have already been ousted from the army.
Standing up, he slightly adjusted his blue robe, Clayson’s expression was subtly complex.
“These Vampires probably couldn’t produce such a finely luxurious robe, does the Vampire Castle also lead to other cities on the surface?
If not forced, I’d indeed be curious about the surface…
Legend has it the surface has warm sunlight, in the winter you can see snow, there is endless food, the land is fertile, rarely encountering danger…”
After thinking for a moment, Clayson shook his head with a wry smile.
“Maybe, I’m overthinking, those are human cities, but I’m going to a Vampire Castle.
Their city must be built in dark, damp caverns, gloomy without light, with ceilings full of bats, and the surrounding rock walls covered with green moss…”
Thinking of this, the young Half-Elf felt somewhat helpless, for who would willingly go to such a place?
“Master Clayson, everyone is ready…”
Suddenly, a knock on the door interrupted Clayson’s wild thoughts. Taking a deep breath, the young Half-Elf then made up his mind.
“After coming back this time, I will resign from the military, even if I just open a small shop manufacturing crossbows in the city I will no longer serve the so-called Grey Claw Tribe.
You have never considered me one of your own, when it comes to credit you take it yourselves, but when it comes to damned missions like going to the Vampire city, you leave it to me…”
Bang Bang Bang~
“Master Clayson??”
Ee-ya~
Clayson pushed open the door, his gaze calm as he looked at the Half-Elf soldier before him.
“I’m coming, is the team ready?”
The Half-Elf soldier, dressed in black leather armor, carrying a longbow, nodded, “Ready, sir.”
“Hmm, let’s set off.”
“Yes!”
Led by the soldier, Clayson reluctantly turned his head for a last glance at the house he had lived in for over a decade, a small, low room made of Black Iron Stone, which held countless memories.
Perhaps after he returns this time, this house would no longer belong to him, because this place was a military base.
Walking on the dark road, a Magic Lamp was lit at a great distance.
There was no distinction between day and night in the Underworld, the light was always this dim, only the city’s clock could tell the time.
Upon arriving at the gathering location, the presence of three hundred people felt oppressive.
The team leader stepped forward and saluted.
“Lord Clayson!”
“Has everyone arrived?”
“Yes, all three hundred are here. You are to lead everyone to the third military camp to board the Black Beak Giant Eagles, which will transport you to Dawn City.”
Dawn City, upon hearing this name, Clayson couldn’t help but twitch at the corner of his mouth.
A vampire city named Dawn City… By the Half-Body God above, that was the funniest joke he had ever heard.
But in front of his subordinates, he had to remain serious.
Though only twenty-five years old, Clayson had secured the position of deputy captain of the arrow-making department through his exceptional talent.
If it weren’t for the fact that the damn captain had claimed his last bow and arrow design as his own, and even, out of greed for merit, had sent him to a vampire city, he might have been promoted to captain by now.
Thinking of this, Clayson’s expression turned sour as he glanced at the crowd.
“Everyone, let’s move out!”
Although it was an arduous task, Clayson didn’t want others to sense anything was amiss about him.
This group wasn’t actually composed of Black Iron City’s most elite bow and arrow makers; Clayson could recognize many individuals who were unpopular with superiors and were often ostracized within the military.
Shaking his head internally, indeed, those sent to the vampire city were a bunch of unlucky souls.
His mood darkened even further.
Without further thought, he led the team out of the military camp.
But the moment they stepped out of the camp, on the streets outside, a group of people dressed in pure white Priest robes handing out food to begging elderly and weak half-elves caught Clayson’s attention.
He knew who these humans were; they were missionaries from the Dawn Sect who had arrived at Black Iron City yesterday.
Although it was odd that a vampire city had human missionaries, Clayson didn’t pay much attention to these priests.
He held them in contempt–Priests? Were they like those in the half-elf temple in Black Iron City who charged exorbitant fees for healing?
Hehe, such a hypocritical bunch of bloodsuckers, disgusting…
Thus, while he would exclaim, “By the Half-Body God above,” he never believed in the divine; he was firm in his belief that there was no deity in this world worth his devotion except himself.
As the two groups passed each other, unexpectedly, a female missionary from the Dawn Sect gave a gentle smile instead of responding to Clayson’s indifference with coldness.
That warm smile made Clayson feel a bit better.
“If there were more smiles like that in the vampire city, maybe this trip would be worthwhile…”
Clayson thought wishfully, but then shook his head. Meeting such smiles in a vampire city? He must be dreaming.
Perhaps it was because they had come to Black Iron City, this majestic and free city, that they were able to smile like that.
Thinking this made Clayson’s face fill with pride. Although he didn’t approve of the Grey Claw Tribe, Black Iron City was different; it was the city that had nurtured him.
Carrying a mix of emotions, Clayson led his team to the third military camp and boarded the Black Beak Giant Eagles.
He had no longing for the vampire city whatsoever, not in the slightest, and feared that it could be even worse than what the wandering poets had said about Vampire Castle–possibly a disastrous experience.
But, there was no resisting it.
The imaginative young half-elf came back to his senses only after the Black Beak Giant Eagles had flown away from Black Iron City, feeling something as he looked back at the looming Black Iron Castle.
He inexplicably felt that this journey to the legendary dark and bloody vampire city might hold different encounters.
“Could it be that the environment is even worse than imagined? Oh God, spare me…”
—-
—-
—-
After nearly ten Sunshine Hours of flight, the fleet of Black Beak Giant Eagles gradually came to a stop in front of a military fortress.
The scenes that followed struck Clayson as quite strange.
Because he saw Beastmen inside the castle known as Grey Stone Castle–yes, it was surprising enough that vampires had human Priests working for them, now there were Beastmen too??
Those vampires had enslaved so many races??
Though eager to learn some information, under the strict surveillance of the guards, Clayson could not seize the opportunity.
After entering the underground passage from a cave behind the Grey Stone Castle, he entered a gigantic cavern.
Clayson would bet that these Beastmen were intent on hollowing out the mountain, otherwise why would such a massive cavern be excavated.
Then he saw the legendary exclusive mount of vampires, a gigantic bat.
By the Half-Elf god, this was a creature even larger than the Black Beak Giant Eagle. They had said that the human Priests came riding these monsters, but unfortunately he had missed it as he was experimenting with a new type of bowstring material.
But riding it felt quite pleasant.
This young half-elf’s mind was incredibly active, always thinking.
Maybe Lide knew his habits well enough to call him a lively fellow.
Hoo hoo~
Flying inside the cave was particularly thrilling; Clayson felt his heart almost leap out. How could these bizarre giant bats make such rapid, sharp turns unscathed??
If it were a Black Beak Giant Eagle flying in the cave, it would probably crash into the wall during a turn before long–what strange creatures.
It felt like he had been flying for ages…
However, after the initial thrill, Clayson quickly grew bored and sleepy.
Damn, he missed his laboratory. Just this morning he had acquired some new Demon Beast sinew to experiment on; perhaps this unique material could improve his last bowstring…
Just as Clayson was losing all interest, a sudden exclamation came from beside him, followed by an enclosed rock wall appearing in front.
There was no way out!
Clayson’s eyes widened, his doziness instantly vanished as he exclaimed loudly,
“Stop, damn it, there’s no way ahead!!”
But this passage was only a few blade lengths long, and they arrived at the rock wall within a few breaths.
The giant bat beneath Clayson ignored his shouts and continued flapping its wings, crashing towards the uneven rocky cliff.
Just as Clayson’s body stiffened, ready to jump off the Magic Language Bat, another cry of alarm came from ahead–the Magic Language Bat that reached the rock wall first had passed directly through it.
A Space Gate??
Clayson’s face stiffened, feeling suddenly relaxed, then somewhat embarrassed–had his reaction been too extreme, a bit humiliating…
Indeed, after his Magic Language Bat flew through, it didn’t crash into the cliff but arrived in a new place instead.
Clayson felt a chill as he entered a space filled with a gray aura, but before he could react, he had already flown out.
Passed through the Space Gate?
Before Clayson could recover his senses, an intense cold aura hit him face on.
The clothes he wore in the Underworld, which were considered many, felt like he was bathing naked by a clean pool in summer in this cold.
Under the high-speed flight of the Magic Language Bat, he even gulped down a few mouthfuls of cold air, causing Clayson to shiver, his teeth chattering.
But this young Half-Elf could no longer care about anything else; his heart was completely captivated by the scenery before his eyes.
Snowflakes, like white feathers, drifted down from the sky, carrying a cold yet extremely unique sensation, melting quickly when lightly gripped in his hand.
Though slightly dimmed by the snowfall, to Clayson, it was as if his eyes were being illuminated by a Magic Lamp.
Completely different from the Underworld.
Looking into the distance, the view was tremendously expansive; he could even see the sky far, far away.
It was magical.
Clayson felt his soul being cleansed.
Looking down slightly, the earth was already covered in a thick layer of white snow, the whole world blanketed in white.
“Too shocking?? Is this the surface world?”
“I know this stuff falling from the sky must be snow!!”
“Hahaha, it’s so unbelievable that such a thing as snow exists in this world, is it a gift from the Creator God??”
“God of Half-Elves, it’s just so wonderful!!”
The young half-elf, upon witnessing such an unexpected sight, instantly forgot his previous worries, his face filled with joy and smiles.
Moments later, after all the Magic Language Bats had exited through the open Space Gate and the leading vampire had made sure everyone was accounted for, he spoke loudly.
“Friends from Black Iron Castle, welcome to Dawn City. I will take you to the new district of Dawn City, and I hope you leave behind wonderful memories in this great city…”
His voice echoed in the sky, and then the Bloodline, without waiting for others to respond, directed the Magic Language Bats towards another direction.
All the Magic Language Bats followed promptly. At this moment, Clayson came to his senses and took a deep breath as he saw the city covered in ice and snow.
“Dawn City.”
“How, how can this possibly be a Vampire’s city??”
Looking down from the sky, Clayson couldn’t even see the end of the city with its numerous towering buildings, which were no less impressive than the thousand-year heritage of Black Iron Castle and even broader in construction.
With a heart full of shock and disbelief, Clayson’s mouth hung open as he gulped down some cold air before coughing several times to recover.
As they flew over the city, Clayson’s eyes filled with astonishment.
Not only was the city extensive, but shockingly, there were so many humans walking back and forth on the streets.
Is this a joke??
Vampires sending humans to preach was one thing, but in such a large city, few Vampires stood out while humans were everywhere.
Is this really a Vampire’s city???
Carrying a sense of peculiarity, Clayson, guided by the Bloodline leader, slowly descended onto the central square of the city.
Upon their arrival, the residents who were spectating immediately crowded around.
The goblins chatted and laughed with the Dwarves, humans and Beastmen stood shoulder to shoulder, the air filled with a lively atmosphere of gossip and spectacle.
“Damn goblins, you won the bet, guess correctly that we’d land on this square, damn you, why were you right??”
“Hahaha, do you Dwarves have rocks for brains? It was announced around the square, these five Gold Pucks are mine now!!”
“Is this what Half-Elves look like?? Hahaha, just like the painting on the propaganda wall…”
“Tsk tsk, are these guys really from the Underworld? Although their lower halves are different, their upper bodies look pretty capable, what are they here for?”
“Have you not heard? This group of Half-Elves is here to join the Magic Industry Research Institute…”
“Sss, I’m so envious, the Magic Industry Research Institute pays two Gold Pucks a month…”
“Pah, what do you know, three!! My brother’s neighbor’s daughter’s friend is a member of the Magic Industry Research Institute! I know!”
“What, it increased again?!! I must go home and teach my son a lesson, always failing exams, if he doesn’t pass into the High-level College of Dawn Academy to become a member of the Magic Industry Research Institute, I’ll break his legs! Always busy watching how buildings are heated and vegetable greenhouses are constructed, it’s infuriating!”
Clayson, watching the crowd around him buzzing with excitement as if observing rare animals, stood dumbfounded for a moment.
Dwarves, goblins, Beastmen, humans, and even a One-eyed Giant, and what even is a Double-headed Ogre??
How can all these different beings live so harmoniously in one city??
What happened to the so-called Vampire city??
How did it turn out like this??
And what about this Magic Industry Research Institute, the heating…
Right now, he really wanted to turn his head and ask the Bloodline leader if they had come to the wrong place.
And these humans, don’t they see they are an army? Why do they dare to discuss so openly??
Where exactly is this place???
This young Half-Elf felt bewildered amidst the cold wind…

chapters.title: Chapter 366 - Chapter 366 Chapter 368 Half-Elfs Journey of Faith to Dawn
chapters.content:
Chapter 366: Chapter 368: Half-Elf’s Journey of Faith to Dawn City (Part 2) (5400 words) Chapter 366: Chapter 368: Half-Elf’s Journey of Faith to Dawn City (Part 2) (5400 words) After seeing the Dawn City, which was nothing like he had imagined, the young Half-Elf Clayson felt a huge shock.
In his memory, the castles of Vampires were always in dark caves, grim and bloody, but now it seemed that if this city could be described as dark and bloody, then there would be no Good Camp in this world.
This unbelievable city housed every race, and they all lived together in harmony.
By the Half-body God above, this was the most absurd thing he had ever seen in his life.
Vampires were chatting with humans, goblins were betting with Dwarfs, a One-eyed Giant let a child ride on his shoulder, Beastman were laughing as they watched the surrounding crowd…
How had these races blended together?
Wouldn’t they feel danger from each other?
Wouldn’t they fight each other?
This scene, filled with Magic, was something even the wandering poets’ absurd legends had never mentioned.
Unfortunately, Clayson’s many questions clearly went unanswered.
After confirming that all three hundred Half-Elves had arrived, a human warrior in Dwarf Armor stepped forward and led them to their quarters.
Although Clayson was the leader, command had shifted to the surrounding warriors, and he could only follow their arrangements.
But he had no additional thoughts on that, for Clayson felt he didn’t have enough eyes to take it all in. Like the other Half-Elves beside him, his face was filled with surprise as he looked around this bizarre city, finding everything incredibly novel.
Clean and tidy streets without a trace of garbage or stench, a patrol team led by respected and dignified Vampires, the passerby smiling and curious, yet showing no fear that should be present…
These things, ordinary on other days, now seemed enveloped in an incredibly mysterious veil in a city ruled by Vampires.
This city changed his understanding of the surface world and altered his fixed beliefs.
It turns out Vampires weren’t necessarily all evil and bloodthirsty; the humans they ruled could still display such pure smiles.
In Black Iron Castle, the female Priest who preached, that kind of gentle smile, wasn’t rare in this city but could be seen on everyone’s face.
Though it was just a preliminary contact, Clayson inexplicably felt the charm of this city, a charm more attractive than that of Black Iron Castle.
Walking along the street to a residential area, the three hundred Half-Elves were dispersed to various floors.
“Lord Clayson, this is your residence. You can use this house as you like, but please take good care of the key, as losing it will be troublesome.
Also, allow me to show you how to use various things inside…”
Having his own room, Clayson was still somewhat stunned. Looking at the armored human warriors in the house, he couldn’t suppress his curiosity, coughed lightly, and asked,
“Respected sir, is Dawn City always like this?”
Hearing this, the young warrior was momentarily startled and looked at Clayson somewhat puzzled, not understanding what this peculiar Half-Elf wanted to ask.
“Lord Clayson, what do you wish to inquire?”
“On ordinary days, do humans, Beastmen, and goblins in Dawn City all mix and live together like this?”
Clayson’s eyes were filled with doubt, staring intently at the human warrior in front of him, wanting to detect some flaw, yet, to his disappointment, the warrior answered as if it were a matter of course.
“But, don’t they view each other as enemies or even attack each other?”
Clayson was still very puzzled; how could different races get along?
In Black Iron Castle, although it was nominally prohibited for races to fight one another, countless bodies could still be found in the sewers every day…
“Lord Clayson, because our ruler is the great Kachar, we are different.
We are citizens personally ruled by him, the honorable residents of Dawn City. Everyone abides by the rules set by him and everyone loves this city,”
The young human warrior spoke, his tone filled with pride and genuine pride overflowing from his heart.
“Lord Clayson, Dawn City never distinguishes by race, origin, skin color, belief, gender, or age.
Here, we value contributions — that is, what one has contributed to Dawn City.
Those who have contributed to Dawn City are those we respect.”
Otherwise, even if you were a giant dragon, you would still have to queue up behind an ordinary resident.
Mr. Clayson, Dawn City is a Free City, a great city, believe me, what you see is just the tip of the iceberg of Dawn City.
Maybe in less than a month, you will fall in love with this city like I did.”
The human warrior’s words hit Clayson hard like a battering ram, shattering his traditional views.
A city that doesn’t discriminate by race, origin, skin color, belief, gender, or age… Could there really be such a city in this world??
Raised with traditional half-elf culture, Clayson wanted to refute this. In Black Iron Castle, gray dwarves, gnomes, and lizardmen were all considered inferior; half-elves were the superior race.
Yet, having just witnessed those scenes in this city, he found himself unable to voice any objections.
At the same time, a great unease arose inside him.
If Black Iron City were like this, perhaps he wouldn’t have been usurped by his superiors or sent to this city…
The human warrior, seeing that the half-elf hadn’t spoken for a long time, didn’t say more. He believed that after living in Dawn City for a while, he would definitely agree with him, just as he had.
After a moment of silence, the human warrior changed the subject.
“Mr. Clayson, allow me to introduce you to some unique household facilities of Dawn City, otherwise, you might not know how to use them…”
Clayson laughed at the remark; how could an ordinary house have something he couldn’t use?
Just as he was about to retort, he saw something that left him stunned.
A small pipe called ‘running water’ could continuously flow clean, clear stream water, and it was claimed to be from the Eternal Spring, which would flow continuously unless turned off.
Moreover, a switch in a bath could instantly run hot water; the human warrior explained it was still in the experimental stage and not available throughout the city yet, but this was already astounding.
And even more incredible was the so-called central heating. Just by flipping a switch, the room would quickly warm up and shut out the cold.
All these magical alchemical inventions made this ordinary room feel extraordinary to Clayson.
The young half-elf was excited and felt respected; he thought he had been given a superior room specially and was thinking of warmly thanking his host.
But unexpectedly, the human warrior said everyone received this kind of treatment.
By the gods of the half-elves, could such magical alchemical creations be available to all residents of the city??
It was simply unbelievable, such alchemy used for ordinary people, too astonishing…
Suddenly, Clayson felt somewhat numb; it seemed that in this city, anything was normal.
This brought back that unanswered question in his mind… what kind of city is this??
—-
—-
—-
—-
The next day, Clayson got up early. The room had been very warm last night because of the heating, letting him sleep exceptionally peacefully.
This made the half-elf feel strange; usually vigilant, even in Black Iron Castle he was easily awakened, but here he had fallen asleep as soon as he lay down.
Perhaps the happy faces of the city’s residents he saw on the streets made him feel at ease, without the ever-present danger seen in the Underworld…
After last night’s heavy snowfall, warm winter sunlight emerged in the morning. As Clayson pushed open the door of his room, gentle sunlight landed on him, warming him instantly and uplifting the spirits of this half-elf who had never experienced it before.
Standing on the hallway balcony, feeling the somewhat cold railing, he watched the logistics staff clearing the snow on the street, his expression slightly peculiar.
For the first time, he felt that perhaps coming to this city, ruled by vampires, was a fortunate event.
With a smile, the young half-elf turned and headed downstairs. Today, they were going to the place the human warrior had told him about last night–the Magic Industry Research Institute, to jointly develop new crossbows, his main job.
At this moment, Clayson felt strangely eager for what was to come…
Time passed day by day, and half a month went by in the blink of an eye.
Clayson felt deeply attracted to this free city.
Whether in life or in work, everything here was ten times, even a hundred times better than in Black Iron Castle.
At work, the Magic Industry Research Institute had a plentiful supply of Magic Materials for his research, and no matter how absurd his ideas were, no one would mock or look down on them. Even goblins and dwarfs joined in to discuss… This made Clayson exceptionally satisfied.
He felt a respect he had never experienced before…
This respect was not only in the workplace but also in everyday life; the most typical example was whenever he wore the badge of the Magic Industry Research Institute, men and women, old and young, all looked at him with respect as he walked on the streets.
This was a feeling he had never had in Black Iron Castle, where that gloomy city always fostered mutual wariness, and where most people were greedily trying to claim his research results and ideas for themselves; he had never felt happiness in Black Iron Castle… nor had he ever felt so important.
But in Dawn City, it was different; even if he developed some projects with others, as long as there were achievements, they would all receive rewards from the Magic Industry Research Institute.
And no one would embezzle a penny; indeed, the greater his research achievements, the more resources he received, and he was respected even more because of his research results.
Clayson felt this was truly the holy land for development; by comparison, Black Iron Castle was a place even filthy Cave Dwellers would disdain.
And among the Half-Elves who came to Dawn City with him, apart from a few spies sent by Black Iron Castle, most shared almost identical thoughts to his own.
They developed a deep fondness for this tolerant, open, free, and passionate city.
Clayson had also pondered countless times why this city had become so captivating but eventually, all the inquiries pointed to one person, the ruler of the city–Kachar City Lord.
Even more astonishing, the Dawn Sect that had sent human priests to preach in Black Iron Castle was actually worshipping the Kachar City Lord.
In other words, the owner of the city was a deity–The God of Dawn.
Although Clayson had never heard of this deity’s name before, through their doctrines and the actions of the believers, it was undoubtedly a deity from the Light Camp.
But this astonished Clayson even more.
A vampire being a deity of the Light Camp?
Could it really be as the believers and residents said, that vampires are not the dark vampires of legend but are from the Holy Light Bloodline?
The Clan Leader of the Holy Light Bloodline, His Highness Kachar, inherently a God of Dawn with limitless power, had yet forsaken his boundless strength to save the suffering races of the Main Plane…
Although such a narrative was dreamy and hard to accept, the mere existence of the city was incredible, and even more unbelievable was that he had accepted such previously absurd explanations.
Thus, Clayson became highly interested in the Dawn Sect.
After working during the day at the Magic Industry Research Institute, he would often go to the Dawn Church to learn more about this grand Sect.
Before coming to Dawn City, he never believed there was any deity worthy of his belief, not even the Half-body God… but now, he had found a sense of belonging here in spirit.
The teachings of the Dawn Sect and their way of treating the believers resonated deeply with him.
This miraculous Sect never demanded daily prayers from its followers; even the Dawn Priests often said, “Dawn Sect brings a happy life to residents; if prayers occupy your time, then there’s no need for prayer. As long as you devoutly believe in Lord Kachar in your heart, those formal actions are not so important.”
This statement utterly amazed Clayson; it was his first encounter with priests in a temple speaking like this to their followers; the priests in the Demigod temples nearly wanted followers to pray twenty-four hours a day.
The way of conducting affairs was entirely different.
And another point that deeply moved him was that the Dawn Sect did not resent the residents who believed in other Sects; even those who did not believe in the Dawn Sect could enter the church to visit and listen to the priests’ sermons…
A tolerant, open, and free attitude deeply attracted Clayson, and it made him love visiting the church even more…
He liked those stories about Lord Kachar’s establishment of Dawn City, and he enjoyed listening to the Dawn Priests propagate the teachings of truth, goodness, and beauty…
“Clayson? You’re quite early today…”
Having finished work early, Clayson sat in the first row inside the Dawn Church.
Hearing the voice beside him, he turned slightly to see the person and then a sincere smile appeared on his face.
“Lord Patril, good night,” he said, turning his attention to the boy beside Patril holding his hand, “Little Pat, hello…”
“Quickly greet Lord Clayson! Lord Clayson works at the Magic Industry Research Institute…”
Patril patted Little Pat’s shoulder with a full smile.
Little Pat, who was already eight or nine years old, lit up and immediately stepped forward to greet.
“Uncle Clayson, good evening, do you really work at the Magic Industry Research Institute? I’ve heard there are many magical alchemy creations there…”
“Yes, there are many interesting alchemy creations, if you have time next time I can take you to my lab for a visit…”
“Wow~” The little guy got excited instantly, “Thank you, Uncle Clayson, you are the most handsome Half-Elf I’ve ever seen…”
Clayson laughed heartily.
Patril couldn’t help but smile and patted the little guy’s head, “Go play in the backyard, come back when it’s time for the prayer ceremony.”
“Okay, father…”
After Little Pat left, Patril took a seat next to Clayson and said with some emotion, “This little guy is really lucky to have met His Excellency Kachar…”
Clayson was a bit stunned and somewhat puzzled, “Lord Patril, why do you say that?”
Patril gave a bitter smile, “If it weren’t for His Excellency, even if we hadn’t starved to death, we might still be begging for food inside Green City.
Let alone that the little guy can now study magic and knowledge at Dawn Academy that only Nobles can learn, even surviving would be a question…”
Hearing this, Clayson became interested, “Lord Patril, is there a story behind this?”
Patril looked strangely at Clayson, “Don’t you know the origin of Dawn City? It seems that the history of the Church was just covered yesterday…”
“Ah? I…” Clayson touched his nose with some embarrassment, “Yesterday I was experimenting with new Magic Materials and wasn’t there…
But I’ve heard part of the history, were you personally brought back by His Excellency Kachar?”
Patril smiled faintly, his tone deep, and began recalling the winter three years ago.
“It was a winter, and the residents of Eric Town were praying that the Beastmen wouldn’t come, but the Beastmen still arrived…
Then we fled to Green City…
In the end…
Thus, we became the residents of Dawn City, and because of this, we have our current lives.” After speaking, a deep admiration rose in Patril’s eyes.
“His Excellency’s greatness cannot be described with all the words of praise. Lord Clayson, you are fortunate because you can be close to His Excellency’s Glory…”
After Clayson heard how Eric Town was brought back to the uninhabited Dawn City, and how Dawn City had developed to its current state, his expression became very subtle.
“Lord Patril, I truly envy your luck…”
“No, Lord Clayson, if we are talking about envy, it should be reserved for you clever researchers.
His Excellency once said that magic and alchemy are the driving forces behind urban development and progression. I didn’t understand it before, but seeing how Dawn City has improved with your efforts, suddenly I realized, His Excellency is indeed His Excellency, he truly is the wise one.”
Hearing this, the young Half-Elf was both proud and somewhat embarrassed.
“Lord Patril, this is what we should do…”
After finishing his speech, an irrepressible thought arose in his mind, yet he hesitated, wanting to say something but unable to speak.
Seeing his hesitant expression, Patril smiled.
“Lord Clayson, speak your mind freely, this is Dawn City, as long as you don’t blaspheme His Excellency’s Glory or disrupt the harmony of Dawn City, any statement is permissible.”
Clayson, hearing this, took a deep breath and following his inner thoughts, slowly said.
“Lord Patril, I, may I join the Dawn Sect, and become a follower of His Excellency Kachar…”
Patril’s smile gradually brightened, “Clayson, the Dawn Sect welcomes anyone’s faith, I’m glad you made the right choice…”
Hearing this, the pressure on Clayson lifted, and a sincere smile emerged on his face.
He turned to glance at the fresco inside the church, the depiction of Lide descending like a Heavenly God to save the world deeply imprinted in the Half-Elf’s mind.
Unanticipated by everyone, the first Half-Elf Believer quietly came into being.
And this was just the beginning of the external proselytization.
