—
Upon hearing this, Lide smiled and turned his gaze to Nicole, who had been pouting next to him without a chance to speak, “Nicole, your turn.”
After being called upon, the young girl instantly perked up, her large eyes twinkling.
“Yes, Lord Kachar~ Sister, dealing with them is simple. We just have to intimidate the Half-Elves so they wouldn’t dare to take action.
When the time comes, we can send the Divine Monster Asreaga to make a round at Black Iron Castle, making them wary and fearful.”
Lide looked at Nicole approvingly, “Intimidation is indeed a tactic, but to effectively use it, you must also offer incentives alongside the threats.
Using powerful forces to threaten Black Iron Castle may be beneficial to us in the short term, but in the long run, it cannot eliminate the roots of future trouble. Instead, it might provoke resistance from them.
On the other hand, if we lure them with benefits during this time, the outcome would be completely different…”
Lide didn’t continue, his dark eyes encouraging the girl to proceed as he looked at her expectantly.
Nicole’s eyes shone brightly as she looked at Lide, her smile radiant, as she continued the topic.
“For example, we could strengthen our trade cooperation with them, allowing the Half-Elves to reap huge profits from us. Faced with interests, nobody can remain cool-headed. Once they taste the sweet fruits of profit, they might even voluntarily cooperate with our proselytizing.
The specific operation would be to support a few influential Half-Elf factions, making them the biggest beneficiaries, and also help them increase their influence among Half-Elves to counter the dissenters. These people might even eventually become part of our force.”
Nicole’s words greatly pleased Lide. It seemed that his decision to let this young girl gain experience in the City Hall over the past few years was the right one.
“Forfeit small gains to achieve greater ones. This is the basic logic of strategy, and Nicole has done very well.
When the economy of Black Iron Castle is completely tied to us, they will become like the Iron Hoof Tribe, unable to resist the inevitable tide, even if they are reluctant.
At that time, we might even be able to conquer this city without resorting to military force.”
First, pursue economic colonization, then cultivate a large group of pro-self beneficiaries. When the time is ripe for true colonization, the pathfinders can eliminate the opposition for us.
It’s as simple and unadorned as that.
Nicole’s eyes gleamed with admiration, “Your wisdom truly astounds, Your Majesty.”
Harrison and Nicole both nodded in strong agreement.
Lide couldn’t help but smile. Most young men do rather sophomoric things just for such admiration in a girl’s eyes and their words of praise, don’t they?
Thankfully, he was past the age for such folly, but he was still in high spirits.
“Nicole, put the large-scale proselytization in the Underworld on hold for now. We’ll start rolling it out all over in three months.
In these next few months, we have to wage war on Risier City, so we can’t take care of the Underworld.”
After saying this, Lide glanced at Harrison, and the understanding Harrison immediately began to lay out the details about the Divine relic to the two girls.
Eventually, Harrison pondered whether he should just write it down and give a copy to everyone in the upper echelons of Dawn City…
After Harrison finished explaining, Lide continued,
“The Magic Language Bats are inherently despised by the Light Attribute and Nature Sect. If they were to appear, they would likely face a joint siege, so this time, my main goal is to breed a group of Dawn Bats.”
Dawn Bat: Basic Level 10, Mature Body Level 12, Elite Body Level 14, Perfect Body Level 15. Evolution requires the use of a Bronze One-eyed Giant’s Bloodline, 500 points of Power of Faith, and a 30-day evolution period.
This was the breeding method for the Dawn Bat that Lide obtained after cultivating Castro, the Basic King.
Although the Dawn Bat was an advancement from the Magic Language Bat, due to the involvement of Power of Faith and the Bronze One-eyed Giant’s Bloodline during the process, it had already transcended the category of Dark Life.
Fearless of Holy Light and the power of the sun, Dawn Bats could maintain their peak condition even in daylight.
When the Magic Language Bats cannot be deployed, the Dawn Bats are indeed the best choice.
“Majesty, we previously bred about twenty Dawn Bats, which serve as the mounts for the high-ranking officers of the Dawn Wings,” Nicole started, but she did not immediately respond, instead, her eyebrows knitted together slightly.
“Because the consumption of the Power of Faith is too great, we cannot breed them on a large scale.
Now we face the same problem.
Majesty, if we simply want to breed Dawn Bats to replace the Magic Language Bats, I fear the required Power of Faith will be an amount we cannot afford…”
Everyone present was a confidant, and Lide no longer kept them in the dark about the Power of Faith.
But upon hearing these words, he couldn’t help falling silent for a moment.
He had previously planned to breed Dawn Bats, but the biggest problem, as Nicole mentioned, was the consumption of the Power of Faith.
On his attribute panel, he only had 120,000 Power of Faith, with 500 points needed to breed one bat, breeding 100 would require 50,000 points, so he could breed a little over 200 at most.
But a smaller number was better than none, and in the absence of Magic Language Bats, breeding Dawn Bats as substitutes was undoubtedly the best choice.
“Nicole, we need an air force; only with an air force can we maximize the power of alchemical bombs.
Although I’ve arranged for extra preparations in the Alchemy Factory, none can replace the role of an air force.”
The importance of air supremacy had been made clear to him by countless wars on Earth.
And when facing a significant difference in strength between enemies and allies, a powerful air force is absolutely key to victory.
But the identity of the Bloodline must not be exposed; the danger faced after exposure could be ten times greater than not having an air force, so the current choice was also a last resort.
“How much of Castro’s bloodline is stored now?”
Breeding Magic Language Bats also required the bloodline of the Bronze One-eyed Giant, but luckily, when Castro evolved into a Bronze One-eyed Giant, Lide realized his importance and began storing Castro’s blood weekly.
“Enough to create 3,000 Dawn Bats…”
3,000? That was a sufficient number.
“Good. In the next two months, I won’t use the Power of Faith; use all of it in coordination with the Dawn Wings to breed the Dawn Bats.
Now, I gain about 40,000 to 50,000 Power of Faith per month, which may increase as the population of new residents grows, but that’s the amount we have for now.
Including the earnings of the next three months, we can have over 400 Dawn Bats before the war begins.
Although the number can’t compare to the existing 7,000-plus Magic Language Bats, it will barely be enough.”
With an initial level of 10, 400 level-10 flying demon beasts could also be considered a formidable force.
Hearing Lide’s orders, Nicole no longer spoke and promptly acknowledged them.
As a Divine Priest, every interest was considered for Lide, and her suggestions were meant to address any oversight for Lide, nothing else.
Just then, Nicole suddenly seemed to remember something, her eyes lighting up.
“Lord City Lord, intelligence reports say that Black Iron Castle has over a thousand Black Beak Giant Eagles…
If we can’t deploy Magic Language Bats, then can we borrow an army from Black Iron Castle, or rather, hire them to participate in this war?”
The idea was creative.
Lide pondered for a moment before shaking his head.
“It’s uncertain if the half-elves will take part in this war, but these Underground lifeforms cannot be exposed.
Although we currently exclusively enjoy the Underworld, don’t forget, who revealed the presence of a Black Dragon in the swamp, who then stole whose divine artifact?
Since goblins have emerged from the Underworld and been discovered by Risier City, it means there must be other entrances.
Right now, humans are unaware of this, but if they start seriously searching upon realizing the Underworld’s existence, they might find it.
At that time, our exclusive advantage of the Underworld will undoubtedly be gone.”
“Majesty, your wisdom always amazes us…”
Harry responded with a smile.
Nicole, too, nodded in approval, “Yes, it’s a gift from the Creator God…”
Lide felt a mix of amusement and frustration, saying no more, he simply issued his command.
“We have three months until the complete unsealing of the Divine relics. Harrison, you take charge in the City Hall to control the overall picture, monitoring the progress of these tasks.
Nicole, the breeding of the Dawn Bats must not be neglected; you must cultivate enough numbers.”
“Yes, Your Grace!”
Upon receiving the order, Harrison and Neroli responded in unison, while Nicole looked at Lide with a puffed-up expression, “Lord Kachar, what about me??”
Why was she the only one not assigned a task among the three people? Unfair… Hmph.
Hearing these childish words, Lide couldn’t help but smile wryly, what an immature girl.
“Was it you who arranged for the giants to be trained before being put on duty last time?”
“Yes,” Nicole’s dark eyes spun, and she slightly raised her head with a bit of pride.
“After the training, the one-eyed giants and double-headed ogres have become much easier to command.”
“Not bad,” Lide nodded, looking at the instantly-beaming girl and continued.
“But that’s not enough, the battle is about to start, and I need you to devise a set of combat methods suitable for the one-eyed giants and double-headed ogres, and then train them.
It’s best if you could train them to the state of unconditional obedience like human soldiers.
Nicole, it’s a very tough task, are you ready?”
Looking at Lide, who was filled with encouraging and expectant eyes, Nicole was somewhat haughty, “Don’t worry, Lord Kachar, I will train these giants into a qualified and strong army!”
“I’m looking forward to it…”
After assigning the tasks, Lide turned his head and communicated with Neroli about the recent issues with the proselytizing of the Dawn Sect.
Every time there is a massive influx of people, it brings various sect beliefs to Dawn City.
This is the time to test the priests’ ability to handle heretics.
Although supported by the official forces of Dawn City, assimilating believers of other sects often takes a considerable amount of time.
Of course, Neroli is already experienced in this area. After briefly learning some of the latest issues of the Dawn Sect, Lide remembered something very important.
The Dawn Festival is the time for the Bloodline’s first embrace, and now it is January 11.
The number of Bloodline on his attribute panel has surged from 1,358 to 2,708…
Thinking of this, he couldn’t help but turn his head to look at Harrison.
“Harrison, how is the first embrace of the Dawn Festival going?”
“Your Grace, everything is proceeding smoothly. Except for a few humans with significant merits, all others selected for the first embrace came from the army, Dawn Academy, and the Dawn Mage Tower.
Talents and personalities are outstanding, and their levels are all above Level 5.
This time, there were 1,350 people involved in the first embrace. Except for Frey, Emi, Stanley, and a few other Bloodlines who did not undergo the first embrace, all of the Holy Light Bloodline within Dawn City participated in this event.”
Harrison’s expression was somewhat excited; he had watched the Bloodline grow from just over two hundred to now nearly three thousand, in less than four years.
Lide nodded slightly. Before the start of the war with the cave spiders, there were over 1,400 Bloodline,
after the war with the cave spiders, in the nearly a year of prolonged war, although the Holy Light Bloodline held the fortresses and cast spells from the rear, more than a hundred died in battle.
As for the number of Beastman Warriors who died, it exceeded 5,000…
The Magic Crystal Vein was taken back at a bloody price.
War, there’s never any mercy to speak of.
Nor is there any differentiation between justice and injustice, evil and goodness.
Everything is for the prosperity and growth of the race.
If you don’t get stronger, you simply wait for death; there is no third option.
“Well done. After becoming Bloodline, immediately arrange for their profession conversion.
Those with strong abilities can be directly assigned to the military; those still needing to learn must continue their training.
The future of the Bloodline is long; we’re not in a hurry.”
Over 2,700 people also means that now Lide could expect to receive over two thousand basic experience points every month.
That’s more than most players could make in a year from quests at this stage.
Although there’s a long way to go for his 1 million experience points, if the Bloodline continues to develop for another three to five years, the amount of experience they could provide each month would reach tens of thousands.
At that time, it would definitely be a significant number that cannot be ignored, meaning that the more the Bloodline develops, the greater Lide’s benefits.
He was equivalent to being a late-stage Profession, and as long as the Bloodline thrived, he would grow to a chilling level of power.
That was the biggest advantage of being the Ancestor of an Upper Race.
After confirming matters concerning the Bloodline, Lide continued to inquire.
“Has there been any progress with the improvements to the Divine Gifted Holy Armor?”
“No…” Harrison said with a wry smile, shaking his head, “Your Majesty, just manufacturing the Divine Gifted Holy Armor was already very difficult.
Trying to improve it is even more daunting…”
Upon hearing this, the corners of Lide’s mouth twitched, equipment costing 5,000 Gold Pucks each was really too extravagant to play with.
Now, arming nearly three thousand Bloodlines would cost 13.5 million Gold Pucks, where would Dawn City get so much money.
“Keep them working on it, at this price, even bleeding Dawn City dry would not be enough to equip all the Bloodlines.”
“Yes, Your Majesty, I will urge them on…”
After asking the few questions he was most concerned about, Lide let out a slight sigh of relief.
Having been running around all day today, he had finally issued all the tasks.
And this was just the beginning, in the next three months, Dawn City would operate at an unprecedented intensity.
That would be the time to test leadership and control abilities.
“You all have your own tasks, I have other matters to handle.
Do you have any other questions?”
“Your Majesty, we will win the ultimate victory, and the glory will be yours.”
Nilo showed a gentle smile, her gaze steadily on him.
Lide felt the warmth in those golden eyes and his heart grew warm.
His Divine Priest, almost the closest person to him, their souls tightly bound together.
“I am firm in this belief as well. This time will be like the others; I will continue to lead our armies back through the sound of victory.”
Lide’s gaze was deep.
After confirming there were no further questions that required his resolution, he spoke no more.
Amidst Nilo’s and Nicole’s slightly reluctant gazes, he tore through space and entered the Land of Bone-Burying.
Ever since he determined that they would wage war, he had felt an intense sense of urgency that did not allow any relaxation.
With a great battle looming, there was much potential yet to be tapped in the Land of Bone-Burying.
Death Spider Queen could mass-produce Death Spiders…
Land of Corruption could cultivate Death Flowers that enhance soul energy,
Land of Bone-Burying could mass-produce Undead using the Power of Death,
And most crucially–the sealed Twelve-winged Blazing Angel.
Divine relics, Twelve-winged Blazing Angels… it all seemed too coincidental.
Upon entering the Land of Bone-Burying, a feeling of kinship washed over him, and the rich Power of Death around him began surging and swirling as if welcoming his arrival.
His spiritual power spread instantly, and through the soul mark, he gained immediate control over the entire Plane.
Land of Bone-Burying (Undead Plane)
Level: Rare (Next level Rare, upgrade requires 1 million Power of Death)
Power of Death: 428,799
Traits: Capable of growth, Undead Transformation
Special Troops: Frost Giant Dragon (Not activated)
Special Building: Skeleton Altar (Damaged)
Special Area: Land of Corruption (Basic)
Plane Area: Diameter 2000 blades
Anchored Coordinates – Dawn City (A Spatial Gate can be opened within an 800-kilometer radius of Dawn City to enter the Land of Bone-Burying)
Introduction:…
Lide glanced at the attribute panel of the Land of Bone-Burying and had a clear understanding — it had been two months since he transformed the Death Spider Queen, and he had not seriously observed the Land of Bone-Burying during this time.
Two months had seen his Power of Death, which had been reduced to just thirty or forty thousand, soar to over four hundred thousand. Although still some distance away from leveling up, it was enough for him to make a significant recovery.
Setting aside other aspects for the moment, it was undeniable that the Land of Bone-Burying’s role within Dawn City had become increasingly significant.
The ability to open a Spatial Gate at any time meant that Lide wouldn’t exchange it even for a divine artifact; this greatly saved on the transportation time of materials, effectively doubling the production efficiency of Dawn City.
Most notably was the construction of the new urban district. Previously, it involved mining stone from the mountains and transporting it back using Magic Language Bats or giants.
Now, two Spatial Gates could be directly opened: one on the mountain and another at the construction site, allowing direct transportation of materials to the construction site for building.
The efficiency improved far more than just twofold.
It also made possible the transportation of One-eyed Giants to the three thousand blade-height mountains surrounding Dawn City to dig an epic water project.
There was no longer any need for Magic Language Bats — simply direct where to transport and that was it. If undisturbed by the cold, just come down to rest, and once recharged, head back up. The convenience was multiplied countless times over.
For Dawn City at its current stage, Lide even believed to a certain extent that the Land of Bone-Burying’s value in civilian life was completely on a par with, if not exceeding, its military value.
Even if the Land of Bone-Burying could nurture an ultimate life form like the Frost Giant Dragon in the future.
After observing the Land of Bone-Burying’s attribute panel a few times, Lide shifted his attention to the internal environment of the Land of Bone-Burying.
The current Land of Bone-Burying had undergone significant changes since the last time he hatched the Death Spider Queen. Most noticeable were the giant, gray-furred spiders that swarmed the area in the upper left edge.
Covered in terrifying fur, their mouths equipped with dagger-like turtle teeth and eyes gleaming with a greenish glow, they lay dense and silent on the ground, their bodies slightly bent together. At a glance, a quarter area of the Land of Bone-Burying was dominated by these fearsome creatures.
They completely obscured the bone-white ground beneath them, numbering at least ten thousand, sending shivers down the spine of anyone who laid eyes on them.
Undoubtedly, the most conspicuous was the Death Spider Queen, surrounded by countless giant spiders at the center. The abdomen of the Death Spider Queen was five blades long and three blades wide, and its massive mouthparts opened occasionally to drop a glowing green, slime-filled spider egg.
Although it was a scene of his own making, Lide also felt somewhat uneasy.
Death Spider Queen
Level: 14
Special Talent: Spider Queen (can lay eggs to propagate Death Spiders; Death Spider eggs hatch within one month, emerge at Level 5, mature to Level 9, Elites can break through to Level 10, and the highest level they can reach is 14. There’s a very small chance to break through Level 15, feeding on various energy-sufficient decaying plants and bodies.)
Restricted Talent: Rapid Reproduction (Intermediate) (can produce 500 spider eggs per day and increase the hatching rate by 35%; under sufficient energy and food, egg-laying quantity can be increased)
Energy Gathering (Intermediate) (…improves the probability of Elite Spider birth by 10%, 10% chance to give birth to Mutated Death Spider)
Introduction:…
There hadn’t been much change in the Death Spider Queen’s attribute panel. Its birth was the result of Lide using the Power of Death to invade the eggs of an Extraordinary Spider Queen and feeding it the Thorns Holy Fruit to achieve its current attributes.
The saying “one individual is a race” couldn’t be more apt when applied to the Death Spider Queen.
Lide, looking at the Death Spiders lying motionless on the white bone ground, as if hibernating, raised an eyebrow.
The Death Spider Queen produced 500 eggs every day. The eggs took thirty days to hatch. As it had been two months since their birth, the eggs laid in the first month should now have hatched.
After a slight sensing, the number of Death Spiders on the ground was roughly fifteen thousand, fluctuating by no more than 300.
Lide was slightly relieved that these Death Spiders, lying dormant in the Land of Bone-Burying, did not need to feed. As long as no fierce battles occurred, they required very little of the Power of Death to sustain their lives.
Now, these resting Death Spiders, in their reduced state of activity, were minimizing their consumption.
This was another hidden feature of the Land of Bone-Burying — as long as it was an Undead life form, the Power of Death could sustain its life, thus avoiding the awkwardness of having to find food every day after cultivating a troop type.
Logistics had always been the strong point of the Undead life forms, in essence drinking the northwestern wind and producing milk.
Lide smiled slightly, even more satisfied with the Land of Bone-Burying.
Logistics has always been the most significant constraint on an army. For a human army, necessities like clothing, food, shelter, and transport must be secured to maintain adequate combat effectiveness.
In contrast, the Holy Light Bloodline and the Undead have far fewer restrictions. The Bloodline only needs to feed once to sustain a month’s worth of sustenance, and even in intense combat, they could last for one to two weeks.
The Undead are even more overbearing — they require no logistics, simply focusing on amassing troops.
Lide floated in mid-air, casually opening the attribute panel of one of the Death Spiders.
Death Spider
Race: Death Spider
Level: 6
Size: Large creature
Skills: Spitting webs, Death Bite, Spider Venom, Mental Resistance, Sharp Claws and Teeth, High-Speed Sprint.
Bloodline: Death Spider Bloodline (Able to devour the power of death to heal wounds, and attacks carry the power of death, causing wounds to rot.)
Introduction: An ancient predator that likes to hunt with its highly toxic webs.
Not bad, with six skills. Although the added attributes of the skills are quite common, for a demon beast of this level, it’s already outstanding.
However, it seems that the death spider of this level is not much of a help in the upcoming battle.
Lide shook his head, his gaze drifting to other areas in the Land of Bone-Burying.
Although the death spiders were numerous, they only occupied one corner.
The main focus remained on the twelve-tier white bone altar in the center area, where the nearly shattered angel wings were still emitting a faint holy glow.
Lide’s expression was somewhat complex.
The twelve-winged Blazing Angel, ranked seventh among the servants of the Master of Dawn, a terrifying existence of level 30 or above. The scene of resisting the descent of the divine still fresh before his eyes.
What a pity.
It couldn’t be utilized by him.
He opened the attribute panel to glance at the properties of the angel wings.
Twelve-winged Blazing Angel
Status: Transforming, transforming race–Fallen Angel
Transformation time: 13,242 years (Death Power can be used to accelerate the transformation)
Introduction: The seventh-ranking Blazing Angel among the Master of Dawn’s servants. Although she lost most of her power over the long years, she still possesses an unimaginable might currently being eroded by evil forces.
If he remembered correctly, the original transformation time for the twelve-winged Blazing Angel was 13,243 years, and now it was 13,242 years, which means a whole year had passed, and the transformation time decreased by one year…
“I…”
With a helpless face, Lide thought, when would this ever end??
A twelve-winged Blazing Angel of over level 30, could you not play by the rules? By the time the transformation is successful, players might have become gods…
Looking at the 420,000 units of Death Power on his attribute panel, an idea struck him.
Previously, he had been dizzy at the sight of thousands of years of transformation time and had never tested how much Death Power could speed up the transformation process.
Lide stroked his chin and immediately began channeling Death Power towards the twelve-tier white bone altar.
The transformation began.
As he controlled the invasion of Death Power, he immediately sensed the angel wings, with the twelve-winged Blazing Angel sealed by the plane power of the Land of Bone-Burying, yet Lide could still sense that incredibly holy force.
The Holy Light was like rolling magma, ready to burst forth at any moment.
And his input of Death Power was eroding the other at an extremely slow pace.
On the translucent wings, mottled grey traces were spreading.
The only regret was that it was too slow; with the slow pace of erosion that was almost invisible, Lide felt that he really had to wait a millennium.
As the Death Power he was manipulating invaded, the outermost part of the angel wings was eroded by an imperceptible bit…
10,000, 20,000, 50,000, 100,000…
When the Death Power dropped by 100,000, the attribute panel for the twelve-winged Blazing Angel showed a change in the transformation time.
Lide, noticing the change, abruptly opened his eyes and stopped channeling Death Power, looking somewhat expectantly at the attribute panel.
But his expression immediately stiffened.
Because the panel now showed 13,241 years… The time was previously at 13,242 years.
Which meant that he had spent 100,000 units of Death Power just to reduce the transformation time of the twelve-winged Blazing Angel by one year.
By this calculation, did these thirteen thousand or so years need him to expend 1.3 billion units of Death Power??
Lide glanced at his remaining 320,000 Power of Death and his face turned dark.
“Should I say it or not… What the hell kind of Twelve-winged Blazing Angel is this? It’s way too difficult to corrupt.
Can’t you take the initiative yourself? Why does it have to be so troublesome…
1.3 billion Power of Death?? Could killing 10 million Beastmen in the barren wastelands even yield a billion? I’m afraid even if we destroy every city in the entire southern province, we would barely scrape together that much…”
Lide couldn’t help feeling a bit helpless. It seemed that possessing the power of a Twelve-winged Blazing Angel any time soon was a bit too ambitious.
“F*ck it, later I’ll order Asreaga to open twice as many, no, three times as many gates to the Spider Plane. I refuse to believe that slaughtering the entire Spider Plane won’t amass those 1.3 billion Power of Death…”
It might still not be enough…
After a brief calculation, the corner of Lide’s mouth twitched. He could only hope that the spider egg production would speed up; otherwise, who knows what year it would be before the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel could be corrupted.
He then decisively gave up the idea of continuing to input the Power of Death into the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel.
This was like a bottomless sea; trying to fill it up with stones would require an overwhelming amount of resources.
After a brief moment of contemplation, Lide shifted his attention to the Death Spiders.
Relying on other powers to increase combat capabilities in a short period would be quite difficult. Although the Death Spiders themselves were not very strong in combat, upon closer inspection, it seemed there was still some fascinating potential.
He suddenly remembered a common monster from the games he often played.
Self-Destructing Spider.
An explosive weapon that doesn’t care about anything else but crashing into the enemy, and upon nearing them, explodes instantly.
A glint flickered through Lide’s eyes as he started to consider this idea seriously.
The production cost for Death Spiders was extremely cheap. Only a small amount of Power of Death and food were enough, so they could definitely work as a consumable.
Plus, with the Death Spider Queen present, the supply of Death Spiders could be endless, continuously produced.
Another point was that, although the attributes of Death Spiders were passable, they were quite lacking when compared to a regular army, especially the Beastman forces stationed in Risier City. They were not on the same level at all.
Relying solely on the power of the Death Spiders themselves would be but just delivering themselves up for slaughter, one charge from the warwolves was enough to send them all heavenward.
But looking at it from another angle, everything was different.
Using them as carriers by equipping these agile creatures, capable of moving on all terrains, with Alchemy Bombs, and then carrying out suicide attacks on the enemy.
Tsk, tsk, tsk, Lide was rather excited at the thought of the scene where tens of thousands of Death Spiders would rush into the enemy army and explode.
If this idea was feasible, it would be a major weapon in his hand when the air forces of Dawn City couldn’t take off.
Moreover, it wasn’t just for this war. Dawn City could continue to make use of it in the future.
Especially in places like caves–narrow and hard to maneuver in–Self-Destructing Spiders would definitely become everyone’s nightmare…
The more he thought about it, the more Lide felt there was potential in this idea.
Without worrying about how to fit Alchemy Bombs onto the Death Spiders, a more critical issue was that the current daily production of 500 spider eggs was not enough.
After pondering for a moment, Lide directly tore the space apart, and in less than three minutes, when he reappeared, he had three red Thorns Holy Fruits in his hand.
Since the quantity was insufficient, then the solution was to accelerate… There were always more solutions than difficulties.
After he had last fed a Thorns Holy Fruit to the Death Spider Queen, her egg-laying ability had increased from 200 to 500.
Feeding her another Thorns Holy Fruit obviously wouldn’t cause her to undergo a Bloodline Transformation again, but this time, he was aiming for a massive change.
He stepped through in an instant and hovered above the still-egg-laying Death Spider Queen, then with a wave of his hand, three Thorns Holy Fruits fell from nowhere and were fed to her.
The Death Spider Queen, whose stomach was three times bigger than her head, let out a joyful hiss and then swallowed the three Thorns Holy Fruits in one gulp.
In less than 30 seconds, the Level 14 Death Spider Queen’s green eyes began to show a tinge of red, and her abdomen started to spin silk.
Under Lide’s gaze, she wrapped herself in a thick, grey cocoon within a short ten minutes or so.
Then the scene fell into silence.
The Death Spiders that had not been awakened were still sleeping; it was not yet the time for slaughtering swine, so the Land of Bone-Burying seemed very quiet.
Moo~
It wasn’t long before a cow’s moo from behind the White Bone Altar caught Lide’s attention.
That strange Cow Bone Undead?
Lide’s expression was somewhat odd; it was only now that he realized the houses established by the Cow Bone Undead seemed to have been trampled flat by the Death Spiders.
Glancing around the Land of Bone-Burying, he didn’t spot the transformed Cow Bone Undead.
Driven by curiosity, his spiritual power spread out, but in an instant, his face took on a rather amusing expression.
The Cow Bone Undead hadn’t built any surface dwelling, but the jerk had actually dug a huge hole next to the White Bone Altar and constructed an underground room with a living room and a bedroom…
What was more ridiculous was that there was even a white bone bed inside.
The most laughably absurd thing was that there was quite a sizable dining room where the Cow Bone Undead was currently lying down, voraciously gnawing on a spider skull, its short tail wagging rapidly.
The crunching sounds kept coming from underground, which in this environment felt particularly frightening.
That wasn’t all; there was even a more ludicrous scene since the Death Spiders had already taken over the job of transporting the Spider Queen’s eggs; the ordinary undead he had created earlier were now serving this Cow Bone Undead.
These undead had their tasks clearly defined; groups of three or five were searching outside for bones and after finding suitable ones, they would bring them down to the Cow Bone Undead.
The rest of the undead were, at the moment, massaging and pounding the back of the Cow Bone Undead lying on the ground munching on bones… Yes, a back massage, with all the trimmings…
A skeleton enjoying a massage from a bunch of other skeletons; the scene was funny no matter how you looked at it.
“You’re an undead, for goodness’ sake, a massage?? Do you even have a sense of touch??”
Lide was bemused.
After sensing slightly, he was surprised to find that the Cow Bone Undead had actually risen to Level 12, and its aura had become even more daunting than before.
“This damn thing is getting more and more mysterious; I really have no idea how I managed to recruit it in the first place… the other undead are still well-behaved.”
After watching for a while, Lide suddenly realized that he might not be living as comfortably as this Cow Bone Undead… Damn it.
“This guy has a chance to acquire skills by consuming bones; I should go out and collect some Beastman or mercenary corpses to see what kind of undead I can nurture in the end.”
After observing the Cow Bone Undead for a bit, Lide didn’t pay it much more attention.
The Cow Bone Undead wasn’t of much use now; he could continue to raise it, and there was no rush to send it out until it reached Level 15.
Time passed quickly while waiting, and three days later, with a zip–the cocoon wrapped in spider silk from the Death Spider Queen burst open, and she emerged from the grey cocoon.
Lide gazed intently; the Death Spider Queen had grown in size and appeared even more ferocious.
He opened the attribute panel.
Death Spider Queen
Level: Level 14
Special Talent: Spider Queen…
Restricted Talent: Rapid Breeding (Advanced) (can lay 1,000 spider eggs per day and improve the hatching rate by 40%. In the presence of sufficient energy and food, the number of eggs produced can be increased.)
Energy Gathering (Advanced) (increase the chance of Elite Spiders being born by 15%, 15% chance of producing a Mutated Death Spider)
Explanation:…
Not bad, both restricted talents were once again enhanced.
The egg production quantity increased from the original 500 to 1,000, so he could produce 30,000 Death Spiders each month.
With three months left before the war starts, he already had hatched 15,000 Death Spiders, plus the unhatched 15,000, making a total of 30,000.
With 30,000 to be produced each of the remaining three months, but only two batches that could hatch, this equaled 60,000.
This meant that by the time the war began three months later, he would have about 90,000 Death Spiders at his disposal.
Lide was quite satisfied with this number. Although Death Spiders were mass-produced Demon Beasts with combat power lower than that of professionals of the same level, this quantity could cause a qualitative change.
And he didn’t need these Death Spiders to fight head-on with the Beastman army; he planned to transform them into Self-Destructing Spiders.
Once he equipped these Death Spiders with Alchemy Bombs…
Tens of thousands of time bombs that could navigate automatically and charge fearlessly to the enemy to explode, just imagine that scene and power.
It was very fascinating.
“Now, another key point is I must develop an equipment similar to Air Force One’s ordnance armor.
Not only must it allow the Death Spiders to quickly don the equipment, but it must also enable the Death Spiders to easily control the detonation of the Alchemy Bombs…”

Chapter 374: Chapter 376: Various Movements, Game within a Game, Who is the Final Planner? (10,000-Word Mega Chapter) Chapter 374: Chapter 376: Various Movements, Game within a Game, Who is the Final Planner? (10,000-Word Mega Chapter) April 5th, Overcast.
By the Blue Sea Province, adjacent to the southern provinces, a massive mountain range stretching thousands of kilometers.
“Our clansmen, our brothers from the Barbarian Hammer Tribe, have been attacked by those damned Beastmen and Vampires!
Hundreds of brave Dwarves have fallen in battle, countless treasures stolen!
The sins committed by the Beastmen, we Dwarves will take back tenfold from their flesh!!!”
Atop the grand city walls built within the mountains, a Dwarf Clan Leader clad in solid battle armor raised his long-handled war axe, bellowing furiously.
“The Copper Hammer Tribe will deploy our mightiest Dwarf army, and with our war hammers, we will show those damned, filthy, lowly Beastmen–that Dwarves will repay hatred with blood, and tear them to pieces with our war axes!!”
Nalis Copper Hammer, the Copper Hammer Tribe Clan Leader and the lord of this city within the mountains.
Beneath towering city walls, densely packed Dwarf Warriors stood, with goat cavalry atop huge, majestic mountain goats leading the way, flanked by ferocious Dwarf War Cars.
Mountain goats, bearing massive curved horns and powerful in stature, are the mount of choice for Dwarves.
Known for their glory, Dwarf goat cavalry cannot match the charge of the heavily armored Centaur Warriors but possess agility that allows them to traverse rocky walls, making them perfect mounts for Dwarves.
The menacing Dwarf War Cars, pulled by more than three mountain goats each, are driven by groups of three Dwarves with fan-shaped sharp blades at the front, resembling fierce hedgehogs, that become brutal weapons of slaughter when charging into battle.
A weapon of mass destruction.
Moreover, tens of thousands of Dwarf Heavy Infantry, armored as if canned in armor, flowed beneath, with their long-handled war axes and war hammers destined to be the nightmares of all enemies.
This is an army that no one can ignore, with a combat power as respected as their crafted equipment.
“Only through war and blood can the Dwarves’ dishonor be washed away!!!”
The voice of Copper Hammer Tribe Clan Leader, Nalis Copper Hammer, grew ever more vehement.
“And furthermore, within that valley occupied by the Barbarian Hammer Tribe lies our treasure–a Secret Silver Vein!!”
There was a stir among the Dwarves below, a buzz of heated discussions breaking out, eyes lighting up instantly.
Dwarves harbored an insatiable fascination for high-level ore like Mithril.
“It’s a complete vein of Secret Silver!” shouted a Dwarf, also clad in battle armor, standing next to Nalis Copper Hammer.
If the Forging Master Valen were here, he would surely exclaim, for this was none other than Rabiao Hammer, the long-lost Clan Leader of the Barbarian Hammer Tribe, now filled with fiery rage.
“And it’s an extremely rich vein of Mithril; we can even extract tens of pounds of Mithril from the vein each month!!”
The voices soared, causing the Dwarven army below to breathe rapidly… Tens of pounds of Mithril a month?!
By the Forge God above, the Divine must be looking favorably upon them.
Mithril!!!
Rabiao, watching the enormous army of Dwarves below, felt rage nearly erupting from his eyes.
Almost three years had passed since the Barbarian Hammer Tribe was seized!
He would never forget the sight of those damned Beastmen occupying the Barbarian Hammer Tribe and enslaving his people, seizing his ore.
Dwarves will never become damned slaves; a blood debt must be repaid with blood!
Now was the time for vengeance!!!
After over two years of hardships, he found the Copper Hammer Tribe.
The Copper Hammer Tribe had now grown into a large tribe with a population of two hundred thousand.
Upon hearing of the plight of the Barbarian Hammer Tribe, the Copper Hammer Tribe Clan Leader became enraged, not only at the slaughter of Dwarves but outraged that anyone dared rob Dwarves of their Mithril!
By the Forge God above, what a heinous crime! Utterly unforgivable!!
Being a race where every citizen was a soldier, they would now mobilize an army exceeding 80,000.
That damned Beastman Tribe held a mere population of twenty to thirty thousand, and how would a few Vampires matter? Under the Dwarves’ war axes, all would become corpses!
Rabiao Hammer and Nalis Copper Hammer exchanged a glance, the latter shouting furiously.
“Everyone, to arms!
Kill the Beastmen, reclaim our Mithril!”
“For the Dwarves, for the ore!!”
“Roar! For the Dwarves!! For the ore!!”
The furious roars of tens of thousands of Dwarves made the grand city within the mountain tremble.
Rumble~
Turning around, the great army set off.
Their target was the barren wasteland, those damned beasts.
They vowed to reclaim the Secret Silver Vein.
—-
—-
—-
—-
“High Priest, did our God truly guide us to Risier City??”
In the Knight Temple, a temple knight clad in full armor and holding a long sword looked surprised at the High Priest before him–a loyal follower of the Knight God–seemingly in disbelief of what he had just heard.
The High Priest, wearing a luxurious priestly robe and with a hooked nose, was over sixty years old. His eyes narrowed slightly, his gaze as sharp as a cheetah on the hunt.
“Are you doubting the will of the Divine??”
The temple knight was shocked, and cold sweat flowed down his forehead.
“No, not at all, Lord Priest. You believe in my devotion to our God, but… our church in Green City doesn’t have enough manpower, and Risier City is home to hundreds of thousands of Beastmen…
To take something guarded by the Beastmen from within is simply impossible!”
“No, this time it’s not just us,” the High Priest said solemnly, “the temple of the God of Nobles will also cooperate with us. Knights have always been allies with the nobles, this time, we stand together…”
“Odo, you are the most loyal knight to our Lord within the Knight Temple. I hope you understand.
Evil from the past is reviving, and the heavens are changing…
His Lordship was ambushed by those damned followers of the Evil God and has already suffered severe injuries. He has also expended a great deal of Divine Power to divine the future. If we cannot restore to our peak state when evil revives, we will endure unimaginable suffering.
Odo, this is our last chance.
Every branch of the Knight Temple throughout the Nolan Empire will arrive in Green City within a week.
We must obtain the relic inside the Divine Relic at all costs.
There is no turning back now…”
Temple Knight Odo’s expression became solemn when he heard this. He placed his right hand on his chest and knelt on one knee, his knee armor clanking crisply against the ground, his eyes filled with determination.
“Lord Priest, for His Lordship, I will dedicate my life to executing his will.
Humility, honor, sacrifice, valor, mercy, honesty, justice, spirituality–these are the glories of our God, and I will uphold them with my life!”
The High Priest’s face softened slightly upon hearing this.
“Odo, there is no need to worry too much. Our greatest advantage now is that other sects are not yet aware of the true nature of the Divine Relic. They do not believe in the adventurer from the Lost Plane!
That is our biggest chance, calculating without their awareness; their perfunctorily dispatched troops cannot compare to the concentrated power of the Knight Temple!!
And we also have the support of the God of Nobles behind us. You should know who the most honored follower of the God of Nobles in Green City is…”
“Is it that duke?”
“Exactly!”
The High Priest’s enthusiastic tone suddenly turned somewhat sorrowful.
“Unfortunately, if it weren’t for those damned followers of the Evil God who attacked us after His Lordship was wounded a few years ago, our sect’s power would not be reduced to a fraction of what it was. Against the current Beastman army, we wouldn’t be so passive!!
Those evil, filthy, vile lives, once His Lordship restores his Divine Power, will be the day their souls are scorched by holy fire!!!”
After a harsh rebuke, his tone became solemn.
“Odo, send out all our spies to tirelessly gather all information on Risier City.
His Lordship has already sensed that the Evil God within Risier City is about to break his seal soon; this is the last assistance He can give us before His slumber.”
“Our God shall be immortal!!”
—-
—-
—-
—-
“Duke O’Kelly, the evil in Risier City is becoming more intense, and the Holy Light Pearl trembles even from hundreds of kilometers away.
Should we really not make it public?”
A middle-aged priest, his face marked by worry, hesitated as he looked at the figure leaning on the railing, overlooking Green City from the fifth floor. This was the controller of Green City, Duke O’Kelly Nolan, whose surname alone commanded utmost respect.
“As a firm follower of the God of Nobles, I believe I understand more than you do,
Bishop, you don’t need to teach me how to handle matters…”
The middle-aged priest’s demeanor stiffened as he respectfully bowed his head, “Yes, my lord.”
The black, elegant robe accentuated the already tall and imposing figure of Duke O’Kelly; although he had passed the age of fifty, the sparkle in his eyes remained piercing.
The God of Nobles differed greatly from other divine beings. Other divine beings’ priests held a definitely higher status within their sect than believers, especially bishops and priests, because they symbolized the glory of the deity.
But the God of Nobles was different; only nobles could join the Noble God Sect. Within the sect, the higher the title, the more respected the position and the greater the authority to speak. A priest? A priest was nothing but a servant for the nobles.
Thus, although this middle-aged priest wore the badge of a bishop, in front of Duke O’Kelly, he could only listen obediently.
Duke O’Kelly’s blue eyes were as deep as the ocean.
He tilted his head slightly upward, his gaze directed at the night sky shrouded by dark clouds and devoid of any light, his tone deep.
“You know, Bishop, the ally of the God of Nobles, the Knight God, had exhausted his last Divine Power to prophesy…
Darkness envelops the sky, and the earth shatters under the shadows, magma erupts burning farms and villages, plagues and diseases spread unimpeded, and nobles gasp their last breaths…”
The gloomy, low murmurs sounded like the language of death whirling around his ears, causing the bishop behind him to break out in goosebumps.
“My lord…”
“Bishop, you should know!!”
Duke O’Kelly suddenly turned his head, his eyes sharp as unsheathed blades, giving the bishop priest no chance to speak again.
“This is an unprecedented opportunity, God has given us one last warning, and I will spare no expense!”
The previously valiant Duke O’Kelly seemed possessed by a demon as he spoke his next words, which sounded like the ravings of a madman, utterly illogical.
The face that had been so confident and resolute now showed inconceivable hesitation, fear, apprehension, and retreat.
“My family has controlled this city since the day Green City was founded, and no one can take this city away from me…
no one!”
“The distant evil is reviving, and even the God of Nobles can’t protect our safety…”
“Power, only power can allow me, O’Kelly Nolan, to continue to control Green City, to control the Southern Province!”
“Risier City, that birthplace of evil, is our last chance.
No one can snatch this opportunity from my hands!!”
“Green City will forever be under my control!! The Southern Province can only belong to my domain!!”
The final voice emerged like a hoarse, low growl from a beast.
The middle-aged priest watching this scene felt a chill down his spine, his eyes flashing a barely concealable fear.
“My lord, could it be, did you peer into the evil of Risier City through the Holy Light Pearl again last night?? I sensed fear in your eyes.
What exactly is hidden there?
My lord??!”
Having finished speaking, a flow of holy light moved through his hands and then surged into Duke O’Kelly’s body.
Duke O’Kelly, whose expression had been ferocious, gradually calmed under the holy light.
After a full ten minutes, the controller of the Southern Province returned to normal.
“My lord?” The bishop priest, exhausted from the spell, looked at him with a sweaty brow, his tone filled with hesitation, “Are you alright…”
Duke O’Kelly took a deep breath, his blue eyes still filled with uncertainty, a stark contrast to his initial imperious demeanor.
“Bishop, last night, I saw it…”
“Saw it?”
“Yes, I saw that eye, the eye filled with death, destruction, killing, bloodshed – the chaotic Eye of Death… It wanted to pull at my soul, it wanted to devour everything about me…
If it weren’t for the Holy Light Pearl cutting off that aura at the last moment, I might have already become a servant to that evil existence…”
Ss~
The bishop gasped.
“You indeed are favored by His will, to be, to be…”
He couldn’t imagine a duke, blessed with divine grace, still being corroded from hundreds of kilometers away.
Duke O’Kelly suddenly turned, his hands gripping the railing again, which cracked– the solid railing directly shattered by the immense force, remnants flying everywhere.
His tone was full of murderous intent.
“Constrained by other powers, I can’t mobilize all the troops, but I will secretly gather the elite forces from the southern provinces to enter Green City, that evil place, which must be conquered by us!
It wants to enslave me, O’Kelly Nolan, it shall bear my fury.
Bishop, its aura still lingers in my heart, constantly corroding my mind, making me act like a clown.
But as long as I conquer even the land, that evil shall become my servant!”
Hearing this, the bishop knew that Duke O’Kelly had returned, but also felt a bit worried, a mere aura could corrupt a duke with a resolute mind and favored by the divine, the power of that evil god, how strong could it be?
Could it really be as the oracle said, a dying, non-threatening evil god?
A shadow fell over his heart.
“Should we seek Lord Rock’s help? Maybe we need transcendent power…”
“Bishop, transcendent? That evil will devour all power beyond the transcendent, no one can escape…
Inform Lord Rock, let him not go to Risier City, Lord Rock is our ally, I do not wish him to perish in the jaws of evil.”
Duke O’Kelly’s eyes flickered uncertainly.
“Shadows have already enveloped the earth, war is looming…
Even the gods cannot protect us this time, they can barely protect themselves.
This time, in Nolan’s name, we shall go forth without looking back!”
—
—
—
—
April 10, overcast.
The skies of Risier City hadn’t seen the sun since a month ago, the thick clouds like scorched grasslands, pitch-black and desiccated.
More exaggeratedly, the cloud layer gathered like a vortex overhead, bringing a chilling sense of oppression.
Clang clang clang~
The hammer struck the rocks sparking off flecks of fire, the bodies of Beastman laborers, covered in scars, were strenuously excavating the ancient relics that had reached deep underground.
Viewed from the sky, tens of thousands of Beastmen densely packed like ants, the scene was as shocking as legends described.
Shahram Furious Blood Roar, this Beastman Prince, stocky as a stone tower, stood with hands behind his back next to the enormous worksite, watching this breathtaking scene.
“Your Highness, do you feel that aura?
We have reached it. We have touched Him, that intoxicating power!”
Beside the Beastman Prince, the Werewolf Shaman, his pupil-less white eyeballs filled with fanaticism.
“That is a god… that is our starting point for changing everything!”
Shahram’s eyes narrowed slightly, the five octopus-like tendrils on his chin which had turned from flesh-colored to blue, emanating a faint glow, looked both eerie and terrifying.
This Beastman Prince lacked the lion-like mane typical of his kind, his chin only bore the five tendrils symbolizing the Furious Blood Roar family.
That was a millennia-old curse of a bloodline eroded by an evil god, but also the supreme honor of the Beastman.
“Lord Shaman, I have already sensed that rotting, death-filled, and evil aura, this evil god’s power, despite being sealed for millions of years, is still terrifying…”
“Isn’t this what we’ve been striving for? Prince Shahram, only by possessing the power of the Divine can you place the crown of Glory on your head!
I believe, when that moment comes, the entire barren wasteland will cheer for you!”
Upon hearing these words, a hint of cold ferocity flashed in Shahram’s profound eyes, his tone utterly brutal.
“After my coronation as king, the Beastman will no longer hold back. We will reclaim the glory that belongs to the Beastman, and the Nolan Empire will be the first sacrificial lamb under our slaughter.
The decaying Beastman Empire needs my revival!!
I am the King of the Beastman!”
The hundreds of Beastman soldiers at his side heard this domineering tone and instantly knelt on one knee.
“My king, we will follow your steps to the death!”
The Werewolf Shaman, at this moment, pounded his chest with his right hand, his face filled with fervor, “Your Highness, you will surely obtain the power of the Divine!
Everything in the barren wasteland belongs solely to you, the magnificent Shahram Furious Blood Roar–King of the Beastman!”
However, after hearing the flattery, Shahram did not become more excited; instead, his expression returned to calm.
“Where is that vampire who obtained a part of the Evil God’s power? Bring him here…”
“Yes…”
Amber eyes twinkled with an unfathomable glow.
A Beastman Prince with ambitions to revive the ancient glories of the Beastman is hardly an easy adversary.
More than ten minutes later, a figure in a black Mage’s robe, restrained by Magic Prohibition Chains, slowly approached Shahram.
Emi, the Shadow High Priest, a blasphemer, the earliest Level 15 top combatant in Dawn City.
Two years ago, to pillage the goblin clan, Lide had deployed Level 17 Werewolf Craig and Level 15 Emi as insiders in Risier City. After frequent unexpected events, although the goblins were successfully transported out of the city, the two of them had stayed in Risier City.
Now, the scenario from two years ago was repeating; the two were still insiders, and Lide was equally ambitious towards Risier City.
However, Risier City was no longer the city it once was, and Dawn City had also changed.
Upon seeing the Beastman Prince in front of him, Emi’s pupils sharply contracted, and he discreetly turned his head to glance at the distant ruins being excavated, his expression quite subtle.
He could feel the terrifying power gathering beneath the ground; in three days, at most, the seal that was already two-thirds broken could no longer hold back that evil descent.
But he was no longer as uneasy as he had been before.
Because he had just contacted Lide the night before, knowing that hundreds of kilometers away from Risier City, an immensely powerful army was preparing to hunt the Evil God.
“Great Prince Shahram, Emi presents his respectful greetings.”
Emi’s tone was very respectful. As a veteran, deceptions and realities were basic operations, sacrificing his own life and soul for Lide’s strategic objectives was trivial, let alone mere groveling.
Shahram, seeing Emi’s demeanor, nodded slightly, “Vampire, I know you don’t wish to submit to the Beastman, but it doesn’t matter, I don’t need your submission.
Once the seal on the Divine relic is broken, you can complete your mission. Although the strength of a Level 15 vampire is decent, it’s not enough to be of concern to me.
Just complete your task, and I will let you leave.”
His tone was temptingly persuasive, as if his words were bound to happen.
“Your Highness, I will definitely not disappoint you!”
Emi assured loudly, the excitement in his eyes showing no sign of his act.
Sly words, skillful deceit, Level MAX…
Both are foxes of the same hill, none are fools.
“Last time, you said the seal was too strong to detect. Now that it’s nearly broken, can you sense what exists within the altar?”
“Your Highness, that altar is a gateway to this Evil God’s Divine Country. Before stepping into the Divine Country, no one can confirm the presence of Shaman.
To activate the altar, you must dismantle the surrounding seals.
But, you must also prepare, within this Evil God’s Divine Country, there may be terror beyond comprehension…”
Emi sounded very sincere, but it’s just a useful platitude; how dangerous excavating Divine relics could be was already well-prepared for by the Beastman.
But this pleased Shahram quite a bit, “Good, although the divine power you received is very weak, at a critical moment, it might play a bigger role.
Be prepared, the seal will completely open in three days.
Then you will enter with the vanguard troops.”
“Vampire, you are striving for your life, and as long as I get what I want, your life means nothing to me; you can leave at any time.”
“Thank you for your kindness, great Your Highness.”
Emi seemed to be moved to tears.
“Very well, you may leave now.”
Emi had no further chance to observe the Divine relics and was immediately escorted back to the cell by the Beastman Warrior.
Once inside the room, Emi lay on the narrow wooden bed in the dungeon as usual, closed his eyes, and seemed to fall asleep again.
However, at this moment, the Shadow High Priest was preparing to inform Lide, conveying the crucial information that the Divine relics would be unsealed in three days.
But just as he had connected to Lide using the power of the Bloodline and was sending the information, he didn’t have a chance to talk more.
Tap tap–a sudden sound of footsteps came from a distance, echoing hollowly through the dungeon.
The dark and damp underground dungeon seldom saw any light; the sound was somewhat dull and terrifying.
Emi was immediately alert and did not speak another word to Lide, cutting off the connection right away.
Although his body still lay on the bed, his Spiritual Power began to emanate, focusing intently on the source of the sound.
Tap tap–
The footsteps drew nearer, and in the cell with only a shabby bed, Emi waited for the newcomer behind the bars.
Should there be any danger, he would at all costs contact Lide again and pass on the remaining information he had acquired today.
A moment later, a huge wolf’s head appeared outside the iron cage; once Emi sensed the aura, his tensed body relaxed.
The newcomer was a Level 17 Werewolf–Craig.
“Damn vampire, did you just deceive His Highness the prince?”
Craig cursed and then, ears perked and wary, scanned the surroundings a few times; seeing Emi signal that he need not worry, Craig’s expression relaxed and he lowered his voice.
“It was tough finding an excuse to get in here this time. Emi, have you made contact with His Lordship?”
Emi nodded, got up, and approached Craig, eyes alight with excitement.
“Craig, His Lordship has already prepared an army of two hundred thousand men, ready to attack Risier City at any moment!”
Upon hearing this news, a brilliant light flashed in Craig’s eyes, his tone filled with undisguised shock.
“Creator God above, two hundred thousand troops??”
When he and Emi were trapped in Risier City, Dawn City only had a population of twenty to thirty thousand, and the Lion Tribe was also rebuilding; not even twenty thousand troops, let alone two hundred thousand, could have been raised.
In just two short years, the power of Dawn City had expanded to such an extent?! How could he not be shocked?
“Unfortunately, this time it’s a war against the Beastmen, and we can’t employ the Lion Tribe’s army; otherwise, His Lordship could have added another hundred thousand Beastman troops.”
Emi shook his head with some regret.
The Lion Tribe is a Beastman Tribe, and Dawn City’s control over it is still somewhat lacking; having Beastmen attack the Beastman Prince would certainly cause a great rift among the Lion Tribe’s Beastmen, and some might even rebel outright.
Thus, Lide did not involve the Lion Tribe in this war.
This incident was a lesson for Lide; to prevent similar issues in the future, he implemented a core plan–sending all the mid-to-high-ranking Beastman commanders to Dawn City for training.
The training wasn’t just military; it also involved educating and changing their thinking, making them profoundly aware of whom they served.
Moreover, at their graduation ceremony, they must kneel before the statue in Dawn Church and swear allegiance to Lide.
Once the mid-to-high ranks were fully under Lide’s control, even if the lower-ranked Beastmen still had doubts, it wouldn’t affect operations.
“Emi, even so, what His Lordship has accomplished is astonishing enough.”
Craig, his large wolf head also displaying uncontrollable excitement, asked, “How does His Lordship need me to cooperate?”
Emi nodded and smiled, “Just like two years ago, you’ll act as an insider, responsible for assisting His Lordship at the critical moment.
It would be best if you can control one of the city gates, as that will significantly help our army when they enter during the battle.”
“Yes, I understand. I will apply to participate in the defense of the city walls–there should be no problem this time…”
Craig pondered for a moment, his gaze intensifying, “And what about you? Once the Divine relics are unsealed, Shahram will certainly not let you go.
You’ve obtained a portion of the Divine Power and are the focus of everyone’s attention; you cannot escape…”
“Craig, no need to worry, I have already planned my escape route.
“And even if I failed, it wouldn’t matter, for my life had belonged to His Majesty and the Holy Light Bloodline since the day I became a Bloodline.”
“To sacrifice for His Majesty is glorious.”
“All, for the Dawn!”
“For the Dawn…” These firm and vigorous words touched his heart.
Craig fell silent, and after a moment, he nodded solemnly.
“Emi, you’re right, all for the Dawn!
Even if everything is sacrificed, we must complete the mission entrusted by His Majesty. The divine relic in Risier City is too important to us.
It would influence the fate and future of Dawn City, and even if we all die in battle, it would be worth it!”
The two generals behind enemy lines looked at each other, then both smiled simultaneously, reaching an agreement.
Tap tap~
Just then, footsteps from outside interrupted their conversation.
Both of them tensed up instantly. Was someone there?
Craig’s expression changed instantly, a fierce light in his eyes as he pointed at Emi and yelled angrily, “Damn vampire, I warn you!! His Highness Shahram is watching you!
If you dare make any slight move, I’ll twist your head off and feed it to the wolves!”
Emi raised his head, defiantly shouting back.
“Stupid werewolf, I am aware of my situation! I don’t need your threats!
Don’t think I don’t know that your actions today are meant to curry favor with His Highness Shahram.
Hmph, only a fool would make such a move. If you want to win His Highness Shahram’s favor, you should do it in his presence!
Do you think your actions in the dungeon go unnoticed by His Highness? No, those Beastman guards might even report that you intentionally colluded with me. Hahaha, what a fool!”
Tap tap~
The footsteps outside paused upon hearing their angry shouts and argument, then continued.
Moments later, a huge figure in a gray robe appeared before the still arguing pair, their pupil-less white eyes unsettling in the dark environment.
Seeing the figure, Craig’s expression stiffened, and he stopped arguing with Emi, moving forward with a mix of embarrassment and hesitation to greet the newcomer.
“Good day, respected Shaman…”
When the Werewolf Shaman saw Craig, he nodded slightly, his tone indifferent, “Go on out, Craig, showing loyalty to His Highness doesn’t require such foolish actions.
This vampire is important to us. I will check to ensure nothing is amiss…”
Although both were werewolves, their statuses were vastly different.
One was a trusted aide beside the Beastman Prince, a Shaman with tremendous influence; the other was a warrior called up from a poor, desolate tribe, their standings in the Beastman army incomparable.
“But…” Craig seemed reluctant, his eyes harshly glancing at Emi.
“Out!” the Werewolf Shaman’s eyes hardened as he coldly commanded, “Before I lose my temper!”
“Yes, great Shaman…”
Craig’s face was extremely grim as he nodded, then sheepishly left, but his heart relaxed the moment he stepped out of the dungeon – he had almost given himself away.
Had he been exposed just then, although Emi, protected by his divine power, might have been safe, he certainly wouldn’t have survived. Luckily, all was safe.
He hurriedly quickened his steps to leave the dangerous place.
Once Craig had left, Emi also internally breathed a sigh of relief.
Too dangerous. If this Werewolf Shaman had overheard something, it would undoubtedly have a major impact on the plans for Dawn City.
Emi then gathered his spirit and preempted, “Lord Shaman, if you too have come like that foolish werewolf warrior to trouble me, I think you’ll be disappointed. Right now, I only wish to survive; I have no interest in anything else.”
“Vampire, do you think I’m as foolish as that werewolf?”
The Werewolf Shaman’s eyes revealed a hint of mystery, “I am not here for trifles, rather, I wish to make a deal with you.”
“A deal?” Emi showed a trace of confusion, “My life is already under your control, what need is there for a deal?”
These words from the Werewolf Shaman also raised significant alarm in him.
It was too unusual.
What does this Shaman intend to do?
Judging by the other’s appearance, perhaps the Beastman Prince does not know about this matter. This is definitely not an action that should be taken under normal circumstances.
“Vampire, you have already felt the power of my god. Are you still fantasizing about the Beastman occupying my god’s Divine Country after breaking the seal?”
Boom~ Emi’s heart shook, as if struck by thunder from the ninth heaven.
With incredulous eyes, he looked at the Werewolf Shaman standing before him.
Although he had been guessing that this Werewolf Shaman might be incredibly significant, hearing the words “my god” from his mouth still sent chills down his spine.
This Shaman turned out to be a follower of that sealed Evil God!
Is the Beastman Prince aware of this? No, the Beastman Prince definitely does not know! He intends to hunt that Divine Being, so he would never collaborate with a follower of the Evil God.
How should I profit from this? Should I stir up trouble or should I send the message to His Majesty now?
Emi’s thoughts raced rapidly; he only felt a tremendous shadow looming over Risier City.
Even the powerful Beastman Prince was just part of the manipulation by this shadow.
The Werewolf Shaman instantly seemed filled with mystery, unfathomable.
“Lord Shaman, what can I do for you?”
Hearing these submissive words, the Werewolf Shaman’s face revealed a spine-chilling smile, his deathly pale eyes without pupils now enveloped by a gray aura of Extreme Evil.
Terrifying, horrifying.
“What can you do for me? What an understanding vampire…”
“I want all the Beastmen of Risier City to become sacrifices for my god!”
Hiss~
Emi gasped in shock, stepped back three paces, his eyes now completely filled with astonishment.
The Beastmen of Risier City as sacrifices? That’s an army of hundreds of thousands!!
This Werewolf Shaman… his ambition is too great!
Immediately, a sharp alertness shone in his eyes. Why would he share such a high-level secret with me?
“Lord Shaman, although I truly wish to help you, I might be powerless.
Although I have received a portion of that Grand Being’s power, I cannot undo those ancient seals, nor can I remove the Magic Prohibition Chains around me…”
The Werewolf Shaman grinned, “Vampire, do you think that obtaining the power of my god was a stroke of luck?”
Emi’s eyes widened in dismay, incredulously looking at the Werewolf Shaman before him.
“Could it be, could this power…”
“Yes, why did I choose you to touch the altar in the first place?” The Werewolf Shaman’s gaze became even more terrifying, and the gray aura had now covered his face.
“Because, vampire, you are the most extreme form of Dark Life, capable of bearing the Divine Descent of my god!
Over several months, your body has been transformed by the power of my god more than once.
The day the seal breaks will be the time of my god’s descent!”
Damn it!!
This damn bastard wants to use me as a vessel for possession!
Emi’s anger surged, but just as he was about to speak, a blasphemous language from the ancient times echoed in his ear, belonging to an Extremely Evil being, an existence that obliterates everything.
“Plague and death were in the past, plague and death are present, plague and death will always be.”
“He is eternal, He is the past, He exists in the past and He also exists now, He is the master of plague and death, He is the spreader of disease and destruction.
He is eternal, He is also the only one, He will not die, He will live forever, He will also be reborn…”
Emi’s consciousness swayed and then sunk into a deep sleep.
The Werewolf Shaman raised his arms, his body enveloped by a gray aura of Extreme Evil, the blasphemous ancient language echoing like the whispers of the Death God within the dungeon, yet not leaving its confines.
“My god, is about to return…”
“The sky and the earth will crumble under His Divine Power…”
“Everyone shall become His sacrifice!”
