chapters.content:
Chapter 379: Chapter 381: The Battle of the Five Armies, Dawn Descends (Anti-theft Chapter, Please Confirm) Chapter 379: Chapter 381: The Battle of the Five Armies, Dawn Descends (Anti-theft Chapter, Please Confirm) This section of the novel is charged based on 9000 characters, and the word count will be updated to 9200 later. Subscribers will not be affected.
Twenty minutes later, refresh the page, and you can read the latest content.
Around Risier City, whether it was players or natives, everyone felt a chill run down their spine upon witnessing what seemed to be an event of epic proportions that could change the face of Glory.
As the Eye of Death and the chaos opened, the five Divine Artifacts floating beside it began to emit an increasingly intense aura, so much so that everyone could see the true form of the artifacts through their ghostly images.
Terror came hand in hand with temptation.
At this moment, Emi’s consciousness had sunk to the depths and was lost in a boundless power. The moment he stepped onto the black altar, an indescribable titan’s force surged into his body.
Divine power–it was the power of the Divine!
But this did not excite him; rather, a fear beyond words arose in his heart.
His worst fear had come to pass. The ancient Evil God was in a rush to descend, and not even a single Sunshine Hour–let alone half–could be waited for.
An endless torrent of power filled every corner of his body.
The space around him trembled at this instant.
His control over his own body plummeted to an all-time low, and as the Eye of Death opened in the sky, everything changed.
He felt a supremely evil presence occupy his body in that moment, and then he completely lost control of his body, relegating himself to the role of a mere spectator to the actions of this terrifying, foreign invader.
The Evil God had now completely taken over his body!!
“Your Highness, I no longer have the strength to delay for another Sunshine Hour…”
Crack~
At the instant Emi felt the consciousness of the Evil God seizing his body,
a spiderweb-like crack suddenly appeared in the sky below the dense black clouds, as if a mirror had shattered.
Then, within a hundred kilometers around Risier City, everyone could witness a nation in the sky appear.
It was a dominion filled with a deathly stillness; through transparent space, one could clearly see inside–a charred land littered with innumerable precious ores, a mass of precious weapons, Magic Scrolls, armor…
Even the corpses of Divines could be seen there–yes, corpses, with broken arms and headless torsos, as endless gray power entwined above them, with the surrounding space warped and twisted.
That was a power only Divines could possess.
Although this Divine Country was steeped in an appalling atmosphere, everyone who bore witness to this scene fell into madness.
Divine Country!!
This was the Divine Country of that Evil God, and moreover, that Evil God was really dead. No, it had been dead. Even if it was resurrecting right now, without a body, how much of its combat power could remain?
Greed was swallowing every person who beheld this spectacle.
The most terrifying emotion in the world is not fear but inner desire. This is the most extreme existence, unavoidable.
With the appearance of the Divine Country, a blasphemous language from the ancient times echoed in the sky, horrifying, somber, and startling, the speech filled with all the unimaginable evils of the world.
“Plague and Death were in the past; Plague and Death are present today; Plague and Death shall forever be.”
“He is eternal, He is the past, He existed in bygone times, He exists this eve. He is the ruler of Plague and Death, the spreader of disease and destruction.
He is eternal, He is the one, He shall not die, He shall live forever, He shall also be reborn…”
Every tone seemed to explode in the soul, causing everything within hundreds of kilometers to dim under this dreadful might.
Fear was spreading.
Boom~
An even more shocking scene unfolded. Accompanied by the chanting of “Extreme Evil,” the Divine Country imprisoned in the sky began to plummet downward.
The Beastmen in the central area were immediately subjected to an indescribable force, and then the semi-transparent Divine Country crashed into the earth with a tremendous roar.
Boom~
The earth cracked, and the heavens collapsed.
Like a magnitude 12 earthquake, the center of Risier City, where the Black Altar stood, burst open and collapsed.
Dirt splattered, and dust obscured the entire sky.
The Beastman Prince could only lead the surrounding crowd in a frantic evacuation, but when the dust settled slightly,
What they saw next made the surrounding Beastmen’s eyes widen, their breath growing rapid.
No one could describe the feeling of the Divine Country falling from the sky and the earth collapsing at that moment.
It was like a weak child standing in front of a cage containing a ferocious beast. Unintentionally unlocking the chain, the beast smashed open the iron door, baring its gaping, bloodied maw.
The scene was incredibly horrifying and startling, so much so that even language failed to capture the feeling.
A pit a thousand blades wide and two hundred blades deep appeared before the eyes of the Beastmen.
The recent collapse of the earth swallowed tens of thousands of Beastman Warriors near the pit.
Pools of blood were still seeping slowly into the rocks underground.
It was like the Land of Death in the depths of hell.
Under everyone’s gaze, the Black Altar in the center of the pit, connected to the Divine Country, remained intact.
What was even more shocking was that the Vampire, spreading its wings and exuding an aura of “Extreme Evil,” remained suspended in midair.
The “blasphemous language” echoed in the ears of everyone present.
“Plague and death were then, plague and death are now, plague and death shall be eternal…”
It was like hitting the replay button, incessant and unending.
A chilling presence, like a stone pressing against their chests, now enveloped the hearts of every Beastman.
But this was not what everyone was focused on. What the Beastman Prince was staring at was the trace of the Divine Country revealed on the shattered earth,
The massive pit below was directly connected to the core of the Evil God–the Divine Country. Nine immense Space Gates in a circular arrangement guarded the Black Altar, and even then, outsiders could see through the gates a sight of the Divine Country–a land of death and desolation.
The next moment shattered everyone’s imaginations.
The shattered Divine Body within the Divine Country slowly drifted through the Space Gates and finally hovered beside the Vampire.
This eerie scene was displayed in the sky, aligning perfectly beneath the dense black clouds; the chaos and the Eye of Death had vanished, but a mirror image appeared under the thick clouds.
It was so exaggerated that it was visible simultaneously for hundreds of kilometers around.
Now, after word had spread, over 100,000 players near Risier City who witnessed this scene exploded in shock.
They were thrilled to witness such a spectacle at the current stage.
Players were logging off every second to share screenshots– the terrifying and stimulating scene of warfare satisfied those who relished spectacles, and the event even attracted the attention of players across the entire network.
Any development here tugged at the players’ heartstrings because for them, this was undoubtedly a plot mission in “Glory,” possibly allowing players to participate in some historical processes.
But at this moment, no one paid attention to the adventurers swearing in awe beside them; the gaze of the natives was captured by the phantom in the sky.
The shattered Divine Body’s two arms and two legs floated scattered about, while a headless torso drifted slowly.
Although the size of this Divine Body was that of a normal human, the weird curvature of the body, along with the row of fierce spines along its back, still gave away that this Evil God was once far from any life form they knew.
What was truly astonishing was not just the terrifying body, but also the missing head of the ancient Evil God, which piqued everyone’s curiosity. How had this ancient deity fallen? Where was its head?
The Divine Body seemed like an Elemental Plane full of infinite power; each fluctuation sent ripples through the surrounding space, and the thick energy emitted made everyone experience an uncontrollable fervor.
This was the power of a god! The ultimate embodiment of Glory!
They felt it, the dissipating power that intoxicated the soul. If they could possess it… Desire was like the whispers of a demon, devouring everyone’s sanity.
More crucially… these bodies were sealed. Yes, though the consciousness of the ancient Evil God had awakened,
its Divine Body was still bound by ethereal chains inscribed with Ancient Runes, and those almost tangible rune chains were definitely not something that could be undone quickly.
A wildly bold idea arose in the mind of Beastman Prince Shahraram, who was beside the pit.
He was going to slay a god!
Thump, thump~
Thump, thump~
Like wild grass in the spring breeze, this insane thought grew unchecked.
If previously digging up Divine remains to harness the sealed Divine Power was a lateral move, then now it was like drawing a knife for a direct confrontation.
One was picking up what was ready-made, while the other had a price that could be so grim it was indescribable.
But from the moment he came to excavate the Divine ruins, the Beastman Prince had been fully prepared. How could he possibly have just one ace up his sleeve?
“All forces prepare to seize the Divine Body!! Also, send someone immediately to call back the Double-legged Flying Dragons and elite Beastmen of Level 10 and above!!”
“Everyone else, buy time with all your might!”
This order was undeniably ruthless.
To divert forces when other walls were in dire need of support meant that what awaited those Beastmen would be a brutal massacre.
But to Shahraram, this was the best decision; for the ultimate goal, every Beastman Warrior of Risier City could be sacrificed and abandoned without exception.
For the power of the Divine, what did these sacrifices count for?!
“All Beastmen draw your swords, follow me and Bimong to attack!”
With another command, the Beast Bimong, who had not been seen in the battle formation, emerged from the shadows of the street, its terrifying body standing taller than ten men and exuding a chilling aura of brutality.
Its three-bladed claws were Bimong’s most potent weapons, exaggerated enough to tear through city walls with ease!
Its grey-black fur was filled with a visual sense of toughness, and its muscles, more intimidating than those of a giant made of steel, were reminiscent of an enlarged behemoth.
These Golden Life forms, capable of rivaling giant dragons of their same tier, had their strength described in countless tales from ancient times.
Following Bimong were over thirty Warriors riding Wolves, clad in the finest armor and wielding the sharpest long blades, and without exception, their Levels were all above 15.
These were the absolute elite warriors the Beastman Prince had cultivated with great effort and the powers lent by the Beastman Empire.
Their sole purpose was to be sacrificed.
Following these Level 15 warriors was a Minotaur Shaman of Level 19. Unlike the Werewolf Shaman who had mysteriously disappeared, the Minotaur Shaman held a Curse Stick engraved with inexplicably bizarre runes, and the frightened Shaman Army immediately gathered around him.
But even this was not enough. With a determined look in his eyes, Shahraram stretched out his hand, and a rusted iron sword materialized out of thin air.
Despite being covered in rust, the sword exuded an aura eerily similar to that of the Evil God.
That was the power of the Divine…
“The Evil God has not fully resurrected; his body is still sealed.
Now that the enemy can only descend into that Vampire’s body, I will use this weapon imbued with Divine Power to forcefully suppress the enemy. During this gap, we must seize the Divine Body and the Divine Artifacts!!
In the name of the Roaring Fury Blood, attack!!”
The last words were roared out almost as if tearing the cover off a secret.
Wuuu~
Following the Beastman Prince’s command, the Beastman Military Governor behind him immediately blew the war horn, and all Beastman armies began to advance in full force.
But at the moment the Beastmen were about to make their move, under the shocked gaze of all, the Vampire floating above the altar descended to ground level, his blood-red pupils now filled with an endless gray aura.
Emi swung her hands violently, spitting out words of Extreme Evil.
“o…kl…oi… Earth… hearken to my summons!”
The moment the spell was recited in the blasphemous language, the surrounding Magic Power underwent a terrifying turmoil, much like the tide crashing against the beach after a high tide.
Boom, boom~
Under Emi’s control, the earth quaked, and the previously collapsed ground began to rise slowly, like plants rapidly growing in spring.
A thousand blades wide, the hole that was two hundred blades below the surface level evened out with the ground under the watchful eyes of the surrounding crowd, and the deep pit the Beastmen had been digging for nearly two years became flat ground within a dozen breaths.
However, the nine immense Space Gates did not change with the ground, still forming a circular arch protecting the Black Altar.
But after the altar was raised to the surface, an even more covet-worthy sight appeared: five Divine Artifacts emitting chaotic light also floated out from the Space Gates, slowly bobbing up and down beside his body.
At this moment, Emi was like a King seated high on the throne, every move filled with a majesty that stemmed from the very depths of one’s heart.
There was also an extremely permeating sense of fear.
No one could have imagined why a Vampire could carry the descent of a Divine Being, but none of that mattered now, for the things beside him were far more attractive than he was.
Shahraram’s gaze was firmly fixed on the Divine Artifacts and the Divine Body; he wanted them all!
“Attack!!”
Just as all the Beastmen charged up with frenzy and fearlessness, the entire sky plunged into darkness. Then, a hair-raising sound emanated from the nine Space Gates.
Squeak, squeak~
What came next sent chills down the spines of the Beastmen who were halfway through their charge.
Rats, endless and uncountable, no, these weren’t rats; these were Half-rat men possessing rat bodies with human heads.
These bizarre and odd creatures, reeking of foul stench and plague virus, poured out from the Space Gates surrounding the Black Altar like locusts.
Each Space Gate was thirty blades long and twenty blades high, and yet, these plague-bearing Half-rat men squeezed and stacked up to fifteen blades high, making all Beastmen’s hair stand on end.
Mad Rats broke out, like floods bursting from a dam, raging and spilling out from the reservoir.
The reflection in the sky accurately depicted this horrifying spectacle. The surrounding populace within a hundred miles witnessed the collapse of the land, saw Emi command the ground to rise with a wave of her hand, saw the hovering of the Divine Body, and the might of the Divine Artifacts. Now, they also witnessed the shocking scene of the Mad Rats breaking out.
The series of events that transpired delivered a great shock to most people, even slowing their breaths.
Next came an even more chilling sight, as after these Half-rat men emerged from the Space Gates, the blasphemous language lingering in the sky suddenly grew in volume.
“Plague and Death were, Plague and Death are, Plague and Death will forever be…”
It was a phrase of Extreme Evil passed down from ancient times, a life-claiming curse that horrified everyone.
All saw the Half-rat men, upon hearing the spell, expand suddenly. Originally blade-high, in just a few breaths, they grew to 1.7 blades, and some even to 1.8 blades…
The already terrifying Half-rat men transformed into nightmarish beings. Their claws carried deadly bacterium-filled venom, their huge mouths were gateways to plague and Death, every part of their bodies lethal to their enemies.
It was this transformation of the Half-rat men, combined with that ancient blasphemous language, that made it dawn on everyone – this ancient Extreme Evil God must have held dominion over plague and–rats. Yes, these dirty, despicable, trash-like rats, but in the mouth of the Evil God, these beings that everyone wanted to get rid of became the ultimate fear of all–Fierce Rats.
The collision occurred within just a few breaths.
The Beastmen who blew the war horns charged straight at the Fierce Rats, while the emboldened Fierce Rats under the blasphemous language showed not an ounce of fear, their twisted, misshapen human faces shrieking with the most brutal expressions as they leaped forward.
Ssshh~
In the instant of their dual flight collision, blood splattered, and limbs were torn apart.
At this time, the most elite of the Beastman were here–these ferocious warriors, under the leadership of the Beastman Prince, were using their formidable individual strength to relentlessly slaughter the endless swarms of Half-rat men.
Yet the speed at which the Fierce Rats surged out was even more exaggerated than the Undead falling from the sky–there was no end to the slaughter, no extinguishing their numbers.
The thick scent of blood rose like mist, and within moments, corpses covered the ground–the fierce battle had almost instantaneously shocked everyone.
What was even more terrifying was that, after these warriors perished, their souls were pulled out and then devoured by Emi on the Black Altar.
The more gruesome the war, the more terrifying the aura emanating from Emi became.
The situation was beginning to develop in a way no one could predict.
—
—
—
But not even the most terrifying scenes deterred the three armies that had breached the walls of Risier City.
When the reflections under the dark clouds appeared, whether it was humans, Dwarfs, or the Undead who had arrived last, all fell into a state of extreme frenzy.
They saw it, yes, they saw the Divine Body, they saw the Divine Artifacts, they saw the Evil God who had not yet fully regained its power, they saw the hope of obtaining precious treasures.
Duke O’Kelly, within the cavalry camp, had a sharp gaze like that of a hawk–piercing and grabbing attention.
This Duke, who commanded the entire southern province, now had a face as solemn as still water. As the scene in the sky caught his eye, his voice carried a determination that no one could shake, pressing ever forward.
“Blow the horn, full army attack!”
“This time at Green City, failure is not an option!”
The God of Nobles’s senior bishop beside him fell silent, the fist-sized Holy Light Pearl in his hands had turned into pure black by now.
Even cracks had started to appear on it.
“Duke, do we really have no choice?”
Holding onto the last bit of luck, the bishop unwillingly asked once more.
“Your Excellency the bishop… from the moment the war began, no, from the moment His Majesty sensed the revival of evil, we had no more path of retreat.
Victory, or destruction.
No one can stop me from getting what I want, even if it means sacrificing the elite of the entire south!”
The 200,000-strong army was the elite force that Duke O’Kelly had cultivated over many years, with equipment and Level that was undoubtedly top-notch, his pride and joy in the past days.
But this time, before the war even began, he had already regarded this batch of elite forces he had cultivated for years as the dead.
This iron-blooded Duke shared an inexplicable similarity with the Beastman Prince Shahrarm–a similarity of being a hero among men.
“Yes, Duke!”
—
—
—
The northern city wall.
“Damn bastards, why haven’t our Goat Cavalry broken through the Beastman’s defense??
By the Forge God above, I already smell the scent of the Forging Hammer!!”
Nalis Copper Hammer roared furiously, “Hurry up, our ancestors’ Glory is waiting for us right ahead!!”
“Let these beastmen and those filthy rats taste the flavour of the dwarven warhammer!!”
“For the dwarves, charge!!”
“For the dwarves!!”
In an instant, like chickens injected with adrenaline, the dwarves launched another charge, and even more dramatically, the goat cavalry leapt onto the rooftops along the streets inside Risier City, bypassing the dense throngs of beastman warriors below and heading straight for the center.
Cavalry galloping on rooftops, a sight that, apart from the dwarves’ own, could likely not be found anywhere else in Glory.
In contrast to the dwarves’ cunning maneuvers, the undead’s offensive was simpler and more effective.
Bone dragons took advantage of aerial superiority to open a path, with death knights charging directly behind the skeleton warriors. Oftentimes, the skeletons in front hadn’t even entered the battle before they were trampled and shattered by the terrifying death knights,
even the roadblocks made by the beastmen on the streets were directly destroyed by the horrific death knights.
Fearless of pain, fearless of death.
The undead never extinguish.
Due to the lack of an air force to resist the bone dragons, combined with the terror knights’ disregard for costs in their charges, it was the undead army that arrived last which made the fastest progress.
The dwarves, while cunning, had few who actually reached the central area, as many roads in various districts had been destroyed earlier, not even leaving roofs intact, preventing them from taking action.
All three armies pressed forward simultaneously.
And at this critical moment, the beastman prince even diverted a portion of his elite forces elsewhere.
This left the beastman army, already struggling against the three-pronged assault, falling into even swifter defeat. The beastmen might be brave, but without coordinated command, they could only become cannon fodder.
Emi, dressed in a grey mage’s robe, floated above the black altar with her arms outstretched, surrounded by the divine body and the Divine Artifacts.
At that moment, her blood-red pupils were assaulted by a murky energy. Her eyes were devoid of any fluctuation, like a stagnant pool, which made Emi appear more like a soulless puppet.
After the Mad Rat was unleashed, Emi, with arms outspread, suddenly drew them back in, then together with the echoing blasphemous language in the sky, began inscribing inscriptions out of thin air.
Grey energy pulsed out, and the limb-less, headless body floating beside Emi began to shimmer.
The densely packed ancient runes on this broken body could make anyone with a fear of clusters get goosebumps.
Those inscriptions emitted an aura similar to the one used to bind the chaotic Eye of Death, intimidating and chilling to the bone.
Had Lide been there, he would immediately have recognized it as the body containing Divine Status that Emi had spoken of.
With each inscription that Emi drew, another inscription burst on the body.
This unabashed act immediately attracted everyone’s attention; at this moment, Emi became the focal point for millions within a hundred kilometers of Risier City.
Perhaps at this time, she should no longer be called Emi, but rather the Plague and Death God, as this body was nothing more than a temporary vessel for the entity.
The real Emi had long been squeezed into an unseen space of consciousness.
Seeing this, the attacking forces all tightened up.
Everyone could sense that if they failed to obtain what they wanted before the Plague and Death God released the seal on its body,
once the ancient evil god broke free from the sealed body, there would be earth-shattering changes.
They would no longer have the chance to claim what they desired.
The dwarves and humans both descended into ultimate madness upon seeing this; they all had reasons for which they must fight to the death, and while the undead showed no larger movements, just by watching them commit all high-level undead one could feel that they, too, had taken measures.
With every move of the Plague and Death God, the killing became even more frenzied.
The war horns, much like the mournful cries of scavenging crows, continued to echo alongside the blasphemous language over the skies of Risier City.
The Beastman Army began to disintegrate like ice melting in boiling water once their elite troops had been redeployed. With the three armies fighting desperately, it wasn’t long before the Beastman Army crumbled, and the Dwarves could vaguely see the Plague and Death God floating in the air.
At this time, in the core area, the Beastman Prince had fallen into a frenzy.
He had gone berserk.
Under his command, the Level 19 Bimong with the strength of ten blades had become a massive weapon of destruction on the battlefield.
Although the terrifying Fierce Rats surged forth in an onslaught, the epic beast, with its enormous size and formidable defense, rampaged through the Fierce Half-Ratmen with impunity.
However, the Bimong was angered and helpless because it dared not approach the nine Space Gates.
Its instinct warned it of fatal dangers–those were warnings from the soul, and it had to evade.
To hunt down the Divine, to snatch the Divine Artifacts and Divine Body, it had to pass through the gaps between the interweaved Space Gates.
This dilemma put the Bimong in a vicious cycle where it could only vent its anger on the Furious Ratmen.
But the good times didn’t last, as the Beastmen, who had originally suppressed the Fierce Half-Ratmen with their high-level combat strength, began to feel the strain.
A large number of Level 10 High-level Half-Ratmen were mixing in, and as their levels increased, Shahrarm sensed the crisis looming.
A greater change was needed!
The Beastman Prince, strong as a bull, could no longer tolerate the current pace and hurled his rusty iron sword at the Plague and Death God.
As the sword flew halfway, sensing the Evil God’s presence, it burst into a green glow. Then, with an unstoppable force akin to a mountain collapse, it pierced towards the Plague and Death God, who was inscribing inscriptions out of thin air.
With that sword strike, space shattered, and it seemed time itself had come to a halt.
But what shocked Shahrarm was that the iron sword, imbued with the Beast God’s power, failed to suppress the opposing Evil God. Once it entered the Black Altar area, the sword was shaken still in midair by a powerful force.
It merely caused a slight delay in the movements of the Plague and Death God.
But this delay was momentary; the Plague and Death God, after being disturbed, suddenly stopped and turned around. Those gray, lifeless pupils looked at the iron sword erupting with terrifying power and displayed a trace of disdainful mockery.
Its mouth opened wide, and a screech like a demon tearing at a soul spread forth, bursting the infinitely powerful iron sword directly.
Everyone felt a numbness in their souls.
A terrifying surge rose in the air, unleashing boundless might in all directions. The width of the Space Gates, originally thirty blades, suddenly expanded to fifty.
The number of Half-Ratmen pouring out of the Space Gates increased several folds.
And that wasn’t all. After the piercing howls, the bodies of the Half-Ratmen gained in size again, swelling suddenly to the height of two blades, becoming as sturdy as iron towers.
The scene underwent a tremendous reversal.
The real Mad Rat had been unleashed.
The sharp, ear-splitting noise didn’t stop with the Plague and Death God’s resuming of its bodily unsealing movements. It continued to shriek, as if etched into space itself.
Each of the Half-Ratmen became extremely formidable under the power of the screaming and blasphemous language.
The Beastmen, who initially had the advantage, now found themselves in a huge disadvantage. Even with a massive killer weapon like the Bimong, they still couldn’t reverse the absolute disadvantage.
Too many, countless…
The Beastmen originally held a numerical advantage, but now, with nine Space Gates fifty blades wide still spewing out Fierce Half-Ratmen, that advantage became a joke.
And if the Beastmen didn’t change their tactics, they would soon likely be overrun by the released Mad Rats.
The crowds surrounding Risier City fell silent at this spectacle. Is this the power of the Divine?
To enhance tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands of Half-Ratmen of one blade high to two blades tall, directly clashing with ferocious Beastmen–this kind of power was beyond any mortal’s imagination.
“Close in around me as the core!!
Let us relinquish other positions. Those damned humans and the Undead want to plunder the Divine Relics, right?
Then let’s give them the chance!!”
The Beastman Prince, who was originally confident in suppressing the Ancient Evil God with his iron sword, lost all his initial confidence when the weapon’s effectiveness failed.
That iron sword had once been wielded by the Beast God, and countless sacrifices had been offered before coming, so that the Beast God sealed a part of his own power inside it once again.
But now, such a terrifying weapon couldn’t last even a second, and the horror of the Ancient Evil God was beyond his imagination.
However, the temptation of the Divine Artifact and Divine Body kept him clinging to a last slim hope.
At this moment, having paid such a heavy price, if he were not to attain what he desired, his loss would be unbearably great.
Wuu wuu~
Just a few minutes after Shahrarm had ordered to abandon the siege around the Divine Relic, the sound of a human horn echoed not too far away.
The humans, fighting fiercely, finally broke through the Beastmen’s defenses and entered the heart of Risier City.
But what awaited them was neither wine nor flowers nor Divine Artifacts and treasures, but a group of Fierce Half-Ratmen who had crushed the Beastmen.
The might of the Fierce Half-Ratmen dealt a heavy blow to the human army.
But Duke O’Kelly’s will was unshakable and the human warriors, archers, knights, even the Pegasus Cavalry, conducted a siege assault from above this region.
However, the count of Fierce Half-Ratmen was overwhelming, pouring out from the Space Gate continuously like the ceaseless tide.
More absurdly numerous than the Undead, most chilling was that under the enhancement of Divine Power, the formerly frail Half-Ratmen had become incredibly powerful.
The human warriors could only barely hold them off.
“Damn rats!! Taste the giant axe of the Dwarves!!”
With a battle cry, the Dwarf Army riding stout mountain goats came slashing from another direction.
These heavily armored Dwarves, covered in bloodstains, had gone through tough battles, but their faith was unbreakable in their eyes.
Following closely behind the Dwarves were the Undead, another vacant area was taken by these beings who knew neither death nor pain.
In the skies, a ghastly wail sounded as a Bone Dragon with tattered wings cleared the way ahead, with the Death Knights leading countless Undead armies clashing head-on with the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
Fearlessness met ferocious brutality, and the two sides instantly turned into a melee of blood and flesh.
Beastmen, Dwarves, Undead, Humans,
Four armies converged.
Around Risier City for hundreds of kilometers, millions witnessed this epic scene from the reflection in the sky, and as they watched the Beastmen being pressed into a corner by the crazed Half-Ratmen, everyone knew the final battle was commencing.
The core area within ten or more kilometers of Risier City became the ground for this decisive battle.
Victory would be a mythic Godslaying battle, while defeat meant the resurgence of ancient evil… With an Ancient Evil God surviving in the Main Plane, nobody dared to predict what would happen.
Players witnessing this held their breath, frantically capturing screenshots.
Amongst the natives, some started to run in the opposite direction of Risier City, trying to escape the impending disaster, while others charged directly towards the city, hoping to fish in troubled waters amidst the dire danger.
But just then, outside the city where no one was paying attention,
A massive figure was soaring with wings spread wide, all the while cackling madly.
“Ga ga ga~ Damn Beastmen brats, Lord Withered Bones has arrived, ready to be destroyed, are you?!”
“None shall breathe under the Dragon Breath of Lord Withered Bones, I, as the Undying King, shall become eternal…”
“Ga ga ga, do you feel my power? Yes, I am invincible, the invincible Lord Withered Bones…”
Accompanying this chatty Bone Dragon, an immensely large army was advancing swiftly.
The dawn’s army arrived just before the final decisive battle.
The battle of the Five Armies, the ultimate confrontation.

Chapter 380: Chapter 382 (Anti-Theft Section, Do Not Subscribe) The King’s Majestic Presence, With a Single Word the Divine Kneel Chapter 380: Chapter 382 (Anti-Theft Section, Do Not Subscribe) The King’s Majestic Presence, With a Single Word the Divine Kneel “Focus the power around me!
Let other positions be left open, those damn humans and undead want to plunder the Divine artifacts, right?
Then give them the chance!”
After the Iron Sword, which Beastman Prince Shahrarm was originally confident would suppress the Ancient Evil God, had lost its effect, he lost his initial confident stance.
That Iron Sword had been used by the Beast God and had been offered countless sacrifices to reseal some of the Beast God’s power within it.
But now such a terrifying weapon couldn’t even withstand a second, the terror of the Ancient Evil God was beyond his imagination.
Yet, the Divine Artifact and Divine body were tempting him, making him hold on to the last vestige of hope.
At this moment, the price paid was so heavy; if he did not get what he wanted, his losses would be too great to accept.
Whoo-whoo~
Merely a few minutes after Shahrarm ordered the abandonment of the encirclement around the Divine artifact, the human’s horn sounded from a nearby location.
Humans, who fought fiercely, finally broke through the blockade of the Beastmen and entered the core area of Risier City.
However, what awaited them was not wine and flowers, nor was it divine artifacts and jewels, but a group of fierce Half-ratmen who had defeated the Beastmen.
The strength of the fierce Half-ratmen dealt a heavy blow to the human army.
But Duke O’Kelly’s resolve was unshakeable; human warriors, archers, knights, and even the Pegasus Cavalry attacked from above in this area.
Yet the number of fierce Half-ratmen was simply too great, endlessly emerging from the Space Gate, like ceaseless waves.
More astonishing than the undead, and most disheartening was that under the blessing of Divine Power, the originally frail Half-ratmen had grown incredibly strong.
Human warriors could only barely defend.
“Damn rats! Taste the Dwarves’ giant axes!”
With a furious roar, the Dwarf Army mounted on stout goats joined the fray from another front.
These heavily armored Dwarves, covered in bloodstains from a harsh battle, had an unbreakable faith in their eyes.
Following the Dwarves were the Undead, another side of the area blanketed by these beings indifferent to death and pain.
A ghastly howl rose in the sky, a Bone Dragon with tattered Dragon Wings led the way, and behind it, a Death Knight commanded countless undead armies to clash head-on with the fierce Half-ratmen.
Neither party feared death, and the confrontation turned instantly bloody.
Beastmen, Dwarves, undead, humans,
Four armies converged.
Around Risier City, within a hundred kilometers, millions witnessed this epic scene from the reflections in the sky, and seeing the Beastmen overwhelmed by the wild Half-ratmen, everyone knew that the final battle was about to begin.
The core area of Risier City for more than ten kilometers had become the arena of the final showdown.
Victory would be the myth-like battle of slaughtering gods, and defeat, the resurgence of ancient evil… Once a surviving Ancient Evil God appeared on the Main Plane, no one could guarantee what might happen.
Players held their breath upon seeing this scene, frantically taking screenshots.
Among the natives, some began to run in the opposite direction of Risier City, trying to avoid the impending disaster, while others charged straight toward Risier City, seeking to fish in troubled waters amidst extreme danger.
But at this moment, outside the city that no longer held anyone’s attention.
A colossal figure soared, crowing loudly.
“Caw-caw-caw~ Damn beastmen brats, the great Lord Withered Bones is here, are you ready to be obliterated?!”
“No one can breathe under the Dragon Breath of Lord Withered Bones, I am the Undying King, and I shall be eternal…”
“Caw-caw-caw, feel my power! Yes, I am invincible, the invincible Lord Withered Bones…”
Accompanied by this chatty Bone Dragon, an incredibly vast army advanced rapidly below.
Dawn’s army arrived just before the final battle.
The battle of five armies, the battle of culmination.
Whoo-whoo~
The long horn, which sounded from the start of the battle in Risier City, continued to echo through the skies mingled with ancient blasphemous language.
The war horns inevitably link to death and glory, with the defeated dying and the victorious basking in glory.
However, at this moment, the battlefield at the heart of Risier City had become an arena of death with no sight of victory.
This place was watched by the God of Death, reeking of slaughter and flowing with fresh blood.
Crippled warriors shouted in agony, their cries of misery like those of dying wild animals.
To kill or be killed was the only fate of a warrior; life was the cheapest commodity on the battlefield.
There was no mercy in war, no greatness, none of the beauty proclaimed by the world; war was a pure meat grinder.
To earn respect and glory, one had only to survive, to truly survive…
At this time, floating above the Black Altar, Emi–the Plague and Death God–exuded an increasingly terrifying aura.
At the sight of it, everyone felt as if an abyssal giant beast capable of tearing through planes was awakening, and under such majesty, no one could remain calm, making submission an unashamed choice.
The fallen warriors around, their collapsed bodies, and the blood splattered all became a backdrop to this ancient Evil God.
More terrifying was that these dead warriors never found rest; their souls, as if grabbed by a devil reaper, were dragged out of their bodies and then absorbed by the Plague and Death God.
This war had already claimed hundreds of thousands of lives, and that immense power was being absorbed by It.
The bat wings behind the vampire’s body had turned jet black, and their spikes had grown increasingly dreadful.
This bloody battlefield had now become the nourishment for this Evil God, growing stronger.
And darker.
“For the Dwarves!”
“Long live Duke O’Kelly!”
“In the name of Blood Fury Howl!”
“Undead shall never perish!”
But when the temptation was strong enough, there were always those who dared to resist.
Four powerful armies did not give up because the Plague and Death God was growing stronger; instead, their assaults became ever fiercer.
Humans still had over a hundred thousand troops, Dwarves seventy thousand, Undead beyond count, and even the Beastmen, recently besieged by three armies, still had over a hundred thousand left.
The massive battle between hundreds of thousands of troops was a scene worthy of making it into the history books of the Southern Provinces.
This land had also become a butcher’s ground for slaughtering Fierce Half-Ratmen at this moment.
However, the Fierce Half-Ratmen did not consider themselves prey; these servants of Divine beings were more insane than all the armies.
With the blessing of Divine Power, they had transformed from filthy, vile creatures into beings of extreme power.
Tall and strong as a calf, their sharp claws could easily rip through warriors’ armor, their deadly menace evident,
And laden with deadly plagues and pathogens, making them lethally dangerous.
Such transformations turned the usually weak Half-Ratmen into bloodthirsty predators at this moment.
The ground battle was brutal, and the conflict in the sky was equally alarming.
Whoosh, whoosh~
The Double-legged Flying Dragons and Pegasus Cavalry had ceased fighting each other, turning their focus to hunting the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
It wasn’t that these flying beings didn’t want to bypass the army below and attack the Plague and Death God directly, but invariably, approaching within a hundred-blade distance of the Space Gate would envelop them in endless darkness.
As if someone was stripping their souls.
That terrifying experience forced them to abandon the idea of a direct assault on the Plague and Death God, and their bows and arrows were completely ineffective against them.
This left them with no choice but to assist the ground troops in advancing.
“Pegasus Cavalry, form up, dive attack!”
After several assaults, the Sky Cavalry significantly relieved the pressure on the ground forces.
The advantage of air units over ground troops was hard to exploit unless their strength was significantly higher.
The general commanding the Sky Cavalry immediately noticed this and began ordering systematic assaults by the Pegasus Army on the Fierce Half-Ratmen below.
With no enemy Sky Cavalry to interfere, they maximized their advantages.
Composed of 50 Pegasus Knights each, the leading Pegasus Knight gripped a five-blade long Sky Cavalry spear and, upon command, dived in for the attack.
Sweeping downward, high in battle spirit.
The combat of the Pegasus Knights always offered a pleasing sight, the well-trained Sky Cavalry coordinating flawlessly with each assault.
Though the fierce half-ratmen below tried to resist, the vast difference in the reach of their attacks meant that no matter how high the half-ratmen jumped, they couldn’t hurt the sky knights, whose lances, five blades in length, carried them on Pegasus.
The Pegasus knights, in their plunging charges, penetrated the armorless half-ratmen as easily as piercing tofu, and the dense pack of half-ratmen only enhanced this characteristic.
A Pegasus could accelerate up to 200 kilometers per Sunshine Hour, and with formidable momentum in a downward dive, the impact of a charging sky lance was something the fierce half-ratmen could not withstand.
Splurt–blood sprayed, and the sturdy, sharp sky lances, like skewering candied haws, could kill seven or eight half-ratmen in one charge.
The human army, still counting over three thousand sky knights, immediately reduced the pressure on their ground forces thanks to their formidable killing power, and the humans occupying the western frontline swiftly advanced toward the black altar.
Similarly, the Undead and the Beastmen, also possessing flying troops, engaged in dual slaughter that sent chills down the spine with its bloodiness.
The bone dragons were straightforward–their dragon breath was the deadliest weapon, wiping out vast numbers of half-ratmen with each discharge. The corrosion spit and sharp talons of the double-legged flying dragons made the skies their own.
Shrieks, screams, and the fetid stench of blood added to the horror.
The brutality of the battle for Risier City was displayed unabashedly to those gathered within a hundred miles.
Though the witnessing players felt both reverence and adrenaline surge, they lacked the strength to join such a war, or else they would have charged screaming to the front, fighting monsters to level up.
“This Evil God has not yet regained his power! Hope is right before our eyes!”
Duke O’Kelly, mounted on a Pegasus overseeing the battle, saw the achievements of the sky knights and his eyes flashed with excitement, for at that moment, he saw hope, a chance to slay the Evil God and seize his power!
His pondering eyes quickly turned resolute.
Abruptly turning his head, he looked at the several dozen guards around him, Duke O’Kelly’s right hand clenched the hilt of his sword, forcefully drawing the cross longsword.
Clang–
The cross longsword, etched with mysterious patterns, was raised high by Duke O’Kelly, pointing directly at the Plague and Death God.
He roared angrily.
“All forces, charge with me!”
The bishop of the God of Nobles, seeing this, stretched out his hand in disbelief, trying to dissuade him, “Duke O’Kelly, you must not! It’s too dangerous here!
You can’t risk following the troops!
Without you, Green City, no, even the entire southern province will fall into chaos!”
Duke O’Kelly’s gaze hardened, turning to look at the bishop priest, his voice icy.
“Bishop, you follow me!”
The bishop priest was shaken, speechless for a long moment.
Duke O’Kelly was domineering and unbending, not giving him another chance to speak, and at that moment, nobody dared defy the orders of this boss.
“I’ve told you, there’s no turning back now.
The spellcasters still need time before they can cast large magics again, yet the Evil God’s power is quickly recovering. If we don’t stop him now, we all will turn to ashes!
And if we cannot garner enough power this time, even if we survive now, we are merely waiting for death to arrive!
Only by seizing power can we claim the right to breathe after evil resurges.”
Having said this, he turned his head to look at the dozens of soldiers continuously watching him, his tone becoming profoundly rousing.
“My soldiers, my subordinates!”
The tone filled with farewell made the surrounding warriors listen intently, turning their gaze to the one they pledged loyalty to.
“Today could change the fate of Green City, for the ancient Evil God revives before us.
We could flee, turn a blind eye, but our wives, our children, our families, and all that we hold dear lie on this land.
Cowering will cost me everything. The Evil God will not reason with us, and I refuse to believe that all the soldiers of the southern province are cowards and weaklings!
We must fight!”
At that moment, Duke O’Kelly seemed to illuminate with an enormous aura of brilliance, his weighty words struck directly to the core.
“When we sever the head of that Evil God who threatens our families with our longswords, only then will we earn the right to live!
My subordinates, with the southern province and Green City at our back, though the Nolan Empire is vast, we have no escape!
One day we may fail, may die on the battlefield, may lose everything we possess!
But not today!
Break the enemy’s longsword, shatter their shields, behead them!
People of Nolan!
Charge with me!”
With a final roar, Duke O’Kelly spurred his Pegasus fiercely, ascending directly into the sky, leading the charge toward the enemy.
The inspiring words and his leading-by-example actions immediately ignited morale within the Human Army.
“Kill!!!”
The frenzied cries of battle momentarily overshadowed the blasphemous language echoing in the sky and those demonic roars.
High morale brought about a combativeness that feared no death.
Humans have always been creatures easily swayed by their emotions; when they were downtrodden, even a goblin could kill them,
but when their spirits soared, they would dare to charge even at a giant dragon.
Whoo whoo~
The heart-stirring horns sounded.
It seemed to be the signal for a general assault.
Sensing the humans ferociously attacking the Ancient Evil God, the Beastmen and Dwarves also blew their horns for the attack.
The battle might be concluded soon, for they were determined to slay a god!
Under the combined assault of the four armies, the terrifying numbers of Fierce Half-Ratmen began to crumble bit by bit, with those emerging from the space portals unable to keep up with the numbers being slaughtered.
The advantage of the Sky Cavalry was too great; each diving attack cleared a large area, providing the strongest support for the ground troops.
The Plague and Death God, still in the process of unsealing the Divine body, finally sensed the anomaly.
Although the four armies were fierce, they had now enraged this Evil Deity, who had survived from ancient times.
Emi’s body, full of dignity and malevolent aura, abruptly paused, turning slightly as if an emperor was looking down upon lowly slaves.
Seeing the Fierce Half-Ratmen mercilessly slaughtered by the Sky Cavalry, a rare anger flickered in the grey pupils of the vampires.
“I am the God of Plague from days of old, who wields plague and spreads death…
You lowly, pitiful lives, opposing me, you shall be devoured by death and have your souls consumed!”
For the first time, onlookers heard the Evil God speak, and the ancient blasphemous language, filled with indescribable malevolent power, echoed within a hundred li.
This was also the first time the crowd learned the name of this Ancient Evil God–God of Plague from ancient times, wielder of plagues, spreader of death.
Following the God’s words, he abruptly raised his hands high, and then around him, the souls of the dead soldiers began to swell like balloons before popping with a snap.
The souls resembled blue crystal fragments, scattered in every corner of the sky, combining the battlefield’s bloodshed to paint a scene both beautifully and horrifyingly striking.
“ox…ip…eb…lq…” Accompanying this, a few obscure and ancient spells spilled from the mouth of the God of Plague.
Then, an indescribable wave of Magic Power, along with the fragments of souls, began to erupt.
At this moment, whether it was Beastmen, Dwarves, or Humans, they all felt a chill creep over them, as if a great terror was about to descend upon the world.
Just a few breaths after the God of Plague recited the spell, a buzzing noise, like locusts flapping their wings, emitted from the nine Space Gates, distressing to the point of causing one’s ears to ring.
Then a shocking scene unfolded.
From the Space Gates, swarms of Half-Ratmen, denser than locusts, emerged–yes, flying out of the sky.
These disgusting beings were no longer the ground-dwelling Fierce Half-Ratmen but Meat-winged Half-Ratmen, each with meaty wings allowing them to fly.
The backs of these Meat-winged Half-Ratmen were adorned with green, ferocious spines, making them seem like formidable adversaries.
These Meat-winged Half-Ratmen had a wingspan of only 1.5 blades, significantly shorter than the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
But upon emerging from the Space Gates, under the effect of the strange spells and Divine Power, they inflated like balloons.
Giant Meat-winged Half-Ratmen with a wingspan of 3 blades took over the sky.
The scene changed in an instant; the initially dominant Sky Cavalry immediately faced severe trouble.
Meat-winged Half-Ratmen emerged from the space portals at an even more exaggerated pace than the Fierce Half-Ratmen, with over ten thousand flying out of the nine space portals in a very short time.
And it seemed as if, like the Fierce Half-Ratmen, their numbers were nearly infinite.
The ground troops, who were swiftly advancing with the aid of the Sky Cavalry, instantly saw their momentum stalled.
Moreover, this wasn’t all; under everyone’s watchful eyes, the already enhanced Fierce Half-Ratmen’s eyes suddenly turned blood-red, their veins bulged, and their muscles became significantly stronger and harder.
Berserk.
This familiar term surfaced in all the Beastmen’s minds.
But it was the effect of Divine Power, and they were utterly unable to stop it from happening.
With the emergence of the Meat-winged Half-ratmen, the Berserk Half-ratmen once again became ultimate demons.
Originally fierce, the Half-ratmen had now lost their sense of pain due to berserk, with only the thought of slaughter surfacing in their minds.
Thus, even if their chests were pierced or their thighs cut off, these Half-ratmen would bite off a chunk of their enemy’s flesh just like Skeleton Warriors.
In this situation, a once promising scenario suddenly collapsed.
Too many, no one could have imagined that in just a few minutes, more than 50,000 Meat-winged Half-ratmen would fly out of the Space Gate.
And the Berserk Half-ratmen had become as hard as rock, slowly expanding outward even under encirclement from all sides.
This blood-soaked battlefield, spanning several kilometers, had become a Land of Death that no one could bear to witness; the battle was no longer fought on the ground but on a stack of corpses two layers high.
Cruel and bloody.
—-
—-
—-
Half a Sunshine Hour after the arrival of the Meat-winged Half-ratmen, the number of casualties in the four armies had already exceeded half.
The once strongest Beastmen, after a morning of bitter fighting, numbered less than 60,000 and had retreated thousands of blades away from the Black Altar.
Even though Beastman Prince Shahrarm led the charge, and they possessed formidable fighting forces such as Bimong and the Beastman Shaman Army,
the countless, unending swarms of Meat-winged and Berserk Half-ratmen still instilled fear of numeric tactics in them.
Humans felt the same way.
Duke O’Kelly, Level 19, ferocious and unmatched, with deep blue energy burning like flames around him, each dive of the Pegasus King killed hundreds of Meat-winged Half-ratmen; yet, it was still not enough to hold them back.
Too many, far too many.
“Duke! We have less than 80,000 men left! We must retreat!”
Although the war became increasingly fierce, its effects were diminishing as time passed.
The human formation was compressed from a square to a triangle, with only Duke O’Kelly, the tip of the arrow, still holding firm.
Hearing the voice transmitted by magic close to his ear, even the steadfast eyes of Duke O’Kelly couldn’t help but dim.
Too many, far too many.
They were unkillable, and at least one-tenth of the Half-ratmen had leveled up to 10 with the addition of Divine Power.
The enemies they faced in this war were undoubtedly the most difficult foes he had encountered in his lifetime.
Filled with immense reluctance, Duke O’Kelly glanced towards the now invisible Black Altar, then slightly lifted his head.
Now, he could only see the Black Altar, wrapped within endless Half-ratmen, and the God of Plague, a former Evil God, in the sky’s reflection.
The Divine’s floating body was still there, the Divine Artifact’s glow as tempting as ever, seemingly within reach, almost graspable.
Yet, the endless Half-ratmen also told him that the Divine Artifact was as distant as the horizon.
So close to a step that could change fate, yet so powerlessly halted, this sense of powerlessness nearly drove Duke O’Kelly mad.
—-
—-
—-
“Rabiao, can we continue??” Nalis Copper Hammer, after chopping down a Berserk Half-ratman with an axe, looked towards Rabiao Hammer, the still fighting chief of the Barbaric Hammer Tribe, gasping heavily.
Rabiao turned his head, glanced around, the sky covered by Meat-winged Half-ratmen, the land now the domain of the Berserk Half-ratmen.
A bitter and reluctant look appeared in his eyes.
“Nalis Clan Chief, perhaps, it’s time we retreated…”
If there was the slightest possibility, the Dwarves would spare no cost to break through, as obtaining the Forging Hammer was worth the sacrifice of all Dwarves.
But now that hope had been severed.
The power controlled by the God of Plague was beyond what the Dwarves could match now; even though most of his power was sealed, merely letting the Half-ratmen take action had already driven them to despair.
Moreover, this time there were also Beastmen, Humans, and Undead jointly taking action, all powerless in their encirclement.
It wasn’t that the Dwarves weren’t brave enough; it was that the enemy’s strength exceeded everyone’s expectations.
Initially, they presumed that the final battle would face threats from Divine powers, yet they hadn’t anticipated being defeated by the enemy’s enslaved rats.
A strong sense of frustration momentarily dimmed Rabiao’s expression.
“Naris Clan Chief, the war is over now, continuing to fight holds little meaning. We simply cannot breach the half-rat man’s defenses.
Just getting news of the Forging Hammer is already a tremendous gain.
Trust me, once we pass the news to the Dwarf Council, our clansmen will send a much stronger army to reclaim the dwarven treasure!
There is still hope.
Let’s retreat…”
Upon hearing these words, Naris Copper Hammer deeply inhaled, watching the clanspeople around him continuously fall in the fight, their pained cries trembling his heart, and he immediately made a decision.
“Full retreat…”
After Naris’s words fell, it marked the end of their encirclement of the God of Plague, ending in failure nonetheless.
They did not perish at the hands of divine beings; they couldn’t even surpass the opponent’s servants.
Not just the dwarves at this time, but the beastmen were also retreating slowly. Duke O’Keilly, resolute and determined, noticed the intentions of the other two factions and powerlessly watched the dense, meat-winged half-rat men in the sky, ultimately with great reluctance, issued the order to retreat.
They had no way out, but now, moving forward seemed to quicken their demise.
As the three armies’ deaths began to retreat, only the fearless undead seemed still to be resisting firmly, both the undead and the half-rat men possessing innumerable vast numbers, seemingly unstoppable.
But just as the orcs, dwarves, and humans were preparing to retreat, a shocking scene suddenly emerged in the direction of the undead.
Boom!
The earth collapsed.
Countless explosions erupted, like rolling thunder striking the earth, filled with ear-splitting noises.
Naris Copper Hammer and Rabiao Hammer simultaneously looked up at the sky’s reflection and gasped in unison.
Spiders, indescribable in numbers, had now swarmed the southern district of Risier City.
These spiders, ten to a group, would explode upon encountering a formidable opponent, their terrifying power making the earth tremble.
Self-Destructing Spiders.
These bizarre and horrifying spiders came directly from behind the undead; they were not the undead’s backup, but a new army.
Because wherever these spiders went, the undead were the first to be struck down.
Yet the strangest thing was that these explosive spiders seemed not to target the undead but the towering buildings, those uncollapsed obstacles.
This sudden scene immediately caused the eyes of those players and natives watching around Risier City to widen. They had thought the war had almost ended, as it was clear to anyone that the scales of victory had tipped in favor of the God of Plague.
But the sudden appearance of the spiders made them sense something different. What were these suddenly emerging spider forces?
Could they also be the servants of the God of Plague? Otherwise, why would they target the undead?
But, obviously, no one would answer them.
The self-destructing spiders acted on their own, climbing everywhere on walls and rooftops. But if observed carefully, one could see that they moved in a straight line.
Any buildings blocking this line would trigger their self-destruction, smashing the buildings into rubble, once not enough then twice, thrice, until reducing it to flat ground.
The activities of these self-destructing spiders were filled with strangeness, but by now, the other armies could no longer concern themselves with this.
All began slowly retreating, and under the shadow of no hope, continuing to recklessly court death was less wise than preserving the spark of hope.
Yet a more bizarre scene emerged as everyone watched, over 500 flying demon beasts unexpectedly flew out from behind the undead.
These demon beasts, clad in strange thick armor, didn’t directly participate in the battle but flew at nearly a thousand blades of height.
Seeing this, Duke O’Keilly, initially hopeful about a turn in the situation, instantly clouded over.
Flying demon beasts?
His tens of thousands of Pegasus Knight Order were now reduced to fewer than a thousand, and these 500 flying demon beasts plunging down likely wouldn’t even ripple the water.
“Bishop, order the spellcasting army to cancel the large-scale magic,” said Duke O’Keilly, “We’ve lost, it’s time to leave here. Staying further holds no meaning.”
As Duke O’Keilly’s words fell, the bishop beside him, although surviving but covered in blood and heavily injured, hesitated.
“Duke, shouldn’t we wait a moment? Perhaps that newly appeared army…”
“A newly appeared army?” Duke O’Keilly waved his hand, directly interrupting the bishop and gestured at the human army around them, struggling against the half-rat men, his deep eyes full of sorrow, and finally sighed helplessly.
“There’s no chance left, no one can eradicate these damnable half-rat men, nobody.
Their numbers are too many…
We must retreat to Green City, seek assistance from the King, no one can stop this ancient Evil God anymore!”
Saying this, he looked up at the strange flying demon beasts in the sky, then shook his head.
“The new army is too small, even if they had ten times the number, it would not reverse the situation…”
The bishop sighed upon hearing this, feeling completely deflated.
Indeed, even if this newly emerged army were courageous, could they really be as formidable as the combined forces of the Beastmen, the Undead, and the Dwarves?
The answer was obvious.
Just as the human army, under the command of Duke O’Kelly, began to hasten their retreat, the flying Demon Beasts had already reached the central area of Risier City.
The clear reflection beneath the dense clouds vividly displayed this scene.
What were these flying Demon Beasts trying to do? Were they not going to attack?
Duke O’Kelly, catching this scene from the corner of his eye, was struck with confusion, and soon after, he noticed some movement in the armor below the flying Demon Beasts.
Then.
A series of stones fell from underneath.
What???
For a moment, whether it was Duke O’Kelly, the Dwarves or the Beastmen, even the people within hundreds of kilometers around Risier City were astonished by this sight.
Were these flying Demon Beasts flying mid-air just to drop a few stones?
Because of the blurry reflection beneath the clouds, outsiders had difficulty discerning exactly what was being thrown by these Demon Beasts, but according to their appearance, they most likely were stones.
This absurd scene made everyone’s expression rigid.
The war had been fought so fiercely, and this new force had initially attracted some interest with their use of Self-Destructing Spiders.
But now, this almost idiotic tactic made everyone deeply scorn the opposition.
Hoo-hoo~
Those small stones swiftly plummeted under the watchful eyes of the crowd.
At this moment, even Duke O’Kelly couldn’t help but burst out, who were these fools?!
But just as the curse reached his throat, the first stone hit the ground.
Then.
Boom~
It was as if the heavens and earth were torn asunder; an indescribable terror of flames erupted.
Alchemy Bombs exploded upon contact with the ground, the horrendous energy bursting instantaneously, lifting a thirty-blade-high wave of air, blasting shockwaves in all directions.
The low-flying Meat-winged Half-ratmen, delicate as paper, were instantly torn into pieces, blood splattering, limbs shattered.
The situation was even more tragic for the Fierce Half-ratmen on the ground. Even with their strength massively increased after going Berserk, under the terrifying power of the Alchemy Bomb, their bodies were more fragile than tofu.
Within a twenty-blade-radius of the Alchemy Bomb’s impact, all life was crushed into dross.
And that was not all–in the zone from twenty to thirty blades, the Fierce Half-ratmen were literally shaken to death by the dreadful sound waves.
200 Gold Puck Three Circle Alchemy Bombs, exceedingly costly, but their effect was absolutely shocking–the first Alchemy Bomb alone tore apart at least 300 Fierce Half-ratmen and a hundred Meat-winged Half-ratmen.
But this was only the beginning.
Boom~Boom~Boom~
The fully loaded Dawn Wings could carry 20 Alchemy Bombs, with 500 Dawn Wings carrying a total of 10,000 Bombs.
Half of these were Three Circle Alchemy Bombs.
This was the art of explosion.
Not only did Duke O’Kelly and the two Dwarf Clan Leaders witness this epic scene, millions around Risier City saw this extraordinary moment in the sky’s reflection.
Alchemy Bomb carpet bombing.
This was true wiping out; the Dawn Bats carrying the Second Circle and Three Circle Alchemy Bombs–unleashing a bombing force that was more than twice as powerful as when Lide initially attacked the twenty thousand Centaur troops with First Circle Alchemy Bombs.
Tens of thousands of Alchemy Bombs were launched within a few breaths, a power that could be described as earth-shattering.
Terrifying flames skyrocketed tens of blades high, the sound waves visibly distorting the air.
The Fierce Half-ratmen were too densely packed; they had poured continuously out of the Space Gate, achieving a level that several armies could not handle in a short time.
But in front of Alchemy Bombs, all this amounted to nothing.
Alchemy Bombs never reason and despise tactics of mass.
There is no problem that an Alchemy Bomb cannot solve; if there is, then the power is simply not strong enough.
The horrendous blast shredded everything–soil, blood, limbs, along with the explosion piercing through the city, all of it now becoming the dominant chorus over Risier City.
Lide had spent countless resources to forge an air force that revealed its dawn fangs to millions for the first time.
This time, the effect of the alchemical bombs scouring the land was vividly displayed before everyone.
Long after the last alchemical bomb had exploded, the onlooking crowd still hadn’t recovered.
They were still immersed in the shock of the explosion of the alchemy bombs.
This apocalyptic scene would be etched in everyone’s memory forever.
As the smoke cleared mostly, the scene in front of them reappeared.
But upon seeing the aftermath of the bombing, the surrounding armies immediately fell silent.
Limbs and fragments mixed with fresh blood covered the ground, and the stench of singed hair genuinely made one feel nauseous.
Densely packed holes appeared in the area just recently occupied by the fierce Half-Ratmen, where the Half-Ratmen, too numerous to count before, had now diminished to less than a tenth, leaving large patches of emptiness.
The Meat-winged Half-Ratmen in the air fared even worse–they always flew low within 30 blades of height, right in the alchemy bombs’ range,
and these creatures that could layer upon layer in the sky were completely turned to ash, leaving only a pitifully small number remaining.
Duke O’Kelly had widened his eyes since the first alchemy bomb exploded, and by the end, his mouth was unconsciously agape to the utmost extent.
This duke, having fought his entire life, saw such dense and terrifying bombings, and the demon-like roar of the explosions made his spine tingle.
This was a display of technological power, and also a symbol of wealth.
As the ruler of the Southern Province, Duke O’Kelly was thoroughly familiar with the cost of alchemical bombs, so he knew better than anyone else what staggering amount of resources it would take to produce so many bombs with such tremendous power.
Even he could not afford to maintain such a massive army.
At this moment, all that filled the duke’s mind were questions.
To whom did this terrifyingly powerful army belong?
While everyone was still caught in the aftermath of the alchemy bomb explosions, a long horn sound that seemed to reach from ancient times resounded through the skies of Risier City amidst the thick smoke.
Wuu wuu~
Then the ground began to shake, as if some terrifying life form was approaching them.
And that direction was where the Undead were, also precisely where the Self-Destructing Spiders and flying magical creatures carrying alchemy bombs had come from.
Duke O’Kelly and two Dwarf Clan Leaders suddenly turned their heads toward the area of the Undead, their eyes filled with curiosity and surprise.
There’s more??
The Beastmen were directly facing the Undead, so they could observe more clearly.
At this moment, the shock in Beastman Prince Shahrarm’s heart was even greater than anyone else’s, looking at the scorched ground and rising black smoke with disbelief still in his eyes.
Had the more than 300,000 fierce Half-Ratmen been so easily decimated??
His gaze, like everyone else’s, pierced through the smoke left by the exploding alchemy bombs, looking towards where the Undead were.
Waiting for the true nature of this mysterious army.
Thump~thump~
Footsteps??
A few questions flickered through Shahrarm’s eyes.
Why would there be such a strange sound?
Not just the Beastman Prince, everyone around Risier City, numbering millions, was keen to see what this army was and who led it, what race did they belong to?
Thump~thump~
Thump~thump~
The sounds of footsteps did not stop but began to quicken, and the numbers only increased.
Each sound resonated like a siege hammer striking the city walls, extremely dull.
Hoo~
As if to answer everyone’s curiosity, a strong wind gradually dispersed the smoke at that moment.
And the once vague area of the Undead fully emerged.
From the scene that appeared before them, everyone gasped in unison.
Duke O’Kelly’s eyes widened even further, his tone filled with astonishment.
“How is this possible?!!”

Chapter 381: Chapter 383: Seizing the Divine Body, Appearance of the Transcendent (9000 words) Chapter 381: Chapter 383: Seizing the Divine Body, Appearance of the Transcendent (9000 words) “In the name of Ilo, I command you to kneel before me, Ancient God of the past days!”
As Lide’s words echoed across the skies, everyone who witnessed the Divine kneeling was instantly ignited.
This was the scene everyone fantasized about in their daydreams, where a single command amidst thousands of troops brought the enemy leader to kneel in submission.
It was absolutely electrifying!
“Ilo?? Damn, that’s so freaking cool!!”
“Who is Ilo?? How is he so badass??”
“I heard there’s a Dark Contract Guild in Green City, and their leader is called Lord Ilo; I heard it last time I was on a quest…”
“A boss who controls the underground forces of Green City making a God kneel??
Holy shit, this NPC must be a super hidden big boss. Anyone joined the Dark Contract? Should we team up and try next time??”
The discussions among the players peaked right after the God of Plague kneeled, and Lide’s recent actions were just too damn cool.
Coming with a big army and sweeping through the fierce Half-Ratmen, who had not a single military able to contend with them, and then commanding a Divine to kneel at his words.
This series of dominant progress had many players almost losing their pants, hitting right on their points of excitement.
“I bet my life, this guy is currently the strongest NPC known in ‘Glory’. No one else could make a Divine kneel– who could possibly do that??”
“In the name of Ilo, I command you to kneel before me… I’m freaking out; so freaking awesome, ahhhh!!”
Compared to the players’ frenzy, the natives too widened their eyes in disbelief, though not as exaggerated as the players, their inner turmoil was even greater.
“By the goddess above, I bet this is the most glorious day of my life because I have witnessed the brilliance of a Divine, Lord Ilo… praise You!”
“Lord Ilo?? Could it be the leader of the Dark Contract?
By the Thief God, I must have heard wrong; how could the Dark Contract have such a terrifying figure at the helm?!!”
“Have you not heard of Lord Ilo? He is the Dark Tutor of the underground forces in Green City…Lord Ilo once guided the leader of the Demon Heart, the Heart-eating Demon Wales, from level 19 to 20 with just a few words in the western district’s black market!!
Such a mighty being, and you haven’t heard of him??”
“I never imagined Lord Ilo would be as powerful as the legends say, no, he is a hundred times more powerful!!”
Although the natives lacked the exclamations of the players, the admiration revealed in their eyes was even more profound.
With the spread of information from those in the know, the news that Ilo was the leader of Green City’s Dark Contract Guild swiftly spread, revealing the legendary past of Lord Ilo to everyone, only then did they realize, such a great figure was right beside them.
Especially amongst the players, Lide quickly became the one true God in their eyes.
Yet, at this moment, Lide had no mood to attend to these confusions; all his attention was on the God of Plague.
The God of Plague, though it had taken over Emi’s body, Emi was his Bloodline.
What is a characteristic of a Bloodline? Absolute obedience and loyalty.
These were traits etched into the Bloodline and soul.
Realizing this, Lide directly invoked the power of the Bloodline, forcibly making his adversary kneel.
This terrifying being, who knows how many years it had lived, due to insufficient control over Emi’s body, kneeled before Lide amidst the gaze of millions.
But outsiders were unaware of the reasons; they merely saw that Lide’s single command made the God of Plague kneel.
Thus, at this moment, Lide’s image could stand shoulder-to-shoulder with the bright moon– what defines strong and dominant, this was it.
Appearing at the most crucial moment, under the watchful eyes of thousands, dominating the entire scene.
The majesty of a king, none dared overlook.
“New Sun God, you have angered me…” The tone carried an indescribable chill and a savage intent to kill.
The kneeling God of Plague, caught off guard, suffered a setback, but as a god, he regained control of his body by relying on his formidable power and slowly straightened his back.
Those gray eyes, filled with dead silence and void, stared straight at Lide, brimming with coldness.
Lide’s gaze was sharp as he looked directly at the other, showing no weakness.
“Your power hasn’t fully recovered, has it?
Ancient God, I can sense your weakness…”
The indifferent words caused the God of Plague’s expression to change once again.
The comment hit his soft spot. If he had regained his power, he wouldn’t be tolerating provocations from others.
A single Divine Art could annihilate tens of thousands of troops.
But now, he was powerless, his strength largely dissipated over countless prolonged years sealed away, eroded by time.
He was too weak, so weak that a group of despicable mortals dared to provoke him.
Using the altar and the Divine Artifact, he helped the half-rat man go berserk, but the power he currently controlled was negligible.
“Moreover, this altar is your prison, isn’t it? Ancient Deity…”
Lide’s gaze was icy as he had realized something since breaking into this delusional realm. The Power of Faith radiated constantly from him.
He could sense through the Power of Faith that this delusional realm, connected to the Divine Country, was actually a Sealed Land, and all the seals were centered on that black altar.
The God of Plague, after his revival, had never left the altar, which was highly illogical.
Moreover, a deity, a deity who had survived from ancient times, faced with invaders and not striking them down himself but relying on the power of rats, was utterly unreasonable.
The dignity of the powerful is not to be challenged; these are the rules of Glory.
But when others provoke and the provoked are not punished, it can only mean that this so-called powerful one is not strong enough.
Lide’s few words caused the God of Plague’s face to drastically change, noticing this, a cold arc hung on his lips, and the intent to kill began to permeate his eyes.
“Ancient God, I don’t care who you are or how powerful you once were, now, it is no longer your era.”
After these words, he glanced at the unaffected space beside him, perceiving certain presences and immediately his gaze sharpened.
“Give up resistance and accept judgment!”
He hadn’t rambled for so long to be foolish enough to reveal his wit in front of the God of Plague.
He was waiting for the Divine Monster Asreaga to get into position. The one opposite was a genuine deity, who even if not even 1% of his power was restored, was still filled with danger.
Among all his subordinates, only Asreaga could pose a lethal threat to the God of Plague.
For he was a Divine Monster!
Divine Monsters represent the ultimate evil in the world; their prey includes deities, their food is divinity.
Even gods fear powerful Divine Monsters.
Using this legendary mythical being to counter the God of Plague could not have been more suitable.
“The New Sun God is the true ruler of this world. You have all been swept into the dustbin, you lowly ancient deities…”
Lide’s tone remained cold, continuing to provoke the God of Plague with words and distract him.
At this moment, he wasn’t using the Power of Faith to convey his words, and the reflection in the sky did not transmit his sound.
And the God of Plague after seeing Lide, also didn’t let his voice spread out anymore; it seemed Lide, the New Sun God, held great significance to him.
When he regained control of Emi’s body, he slowly stood up, his gray and lifeless eyes instilling fear deep within.
The gray mage robe on his body began to flutter, and the dense, ink-like hideous bat wings behind him made him appear even more terrifying.
The true Evil God.
The comment even harsher than Withered Bone from Lide instantly enraged the already furious God of Plague.
“God of the New Sun, I will peel your soul out and shred it bit by bit!”
“The Destiny Tablet has already been stolen by the rulers of the ancient days, the glory of the old days will revive, and you will all fall…”
Upon hearing this, Lide turned pale, every cell in his body warning him.
Advanced Danger Perception.
It seemed that he had touched upon some unspeakable taboo, some ineffable ancient secret, some mystery that should not exist in this world.
At that moment, Lide even felt that if he continued to listen to this evil deity, he would die.
And that feeling grew stronger and stronger, so intense that his soul was trembling.
This was not a secret he should hear, nor a mystery he should attempt to decipher at his level.
With a forceful suppression of the trembling in his heart, Lide suddenly turned and roared.
“Attack!”
As soon as the words fell, Lide’s body disappeared from the spot and then appeared above the Black Altar.
He rushed toward the ancient deity with the ferocity of a tiger.
Just as the God of Plague thought to resist, Lide immediately used the Bloodline Power within Emi’s body to start transferring the Power of Faith wildly.
When the God of Plague tried to mobilize his power, he suddenly realized that this body was out of his control.
In front of millions of spectators, Lide unimpededly rushed to the God of Plague and stretched out his right hand without hesitation, forcefully placing it on the latter’s forehead.
A surge of pure Holy Power spread out, infused into Emi’s body, directly cutting off the God of Plague’s power with the Power of Faith.
This action immediately triggered a chain reaction, and the blasphemous language that had been echoing in the sky suddenly stopped.
What is happening?
Although there was no sound in the sky’s reflection, Lide’s actions still left the millions around Risier City somewhat astonished.
What is this powerful being, that brought gods to their knees, doing?
Is he trying to kill the other?
Duke O’Kelly also widened his eyes, staring intently at the sky, then suddenly turned his head towards the bishop of the God of Nobles, his face filled with confusion.
“What is Lord Ilo doing??”
The scene inexplicably seemed somewhat bizarre.
The Holy Aura emanating from Lide was so conspicuous under the dense dark clouds.
Amidst the dark environment around, Lide seemed more like a Savior at this moment.
“Your Grace…” the bishop was also slightly taken aback by this scene, and after a moment he smacked his head, extremely excited.
