And equally baffling was why Lord Ilo, who with one phrase could make Divines kneel and burst three Transcendents with one hand, hadn’t appeared in the final moment?
Could it be he went to face an even more terrifying Evil God?
Regardless of how much confusion and mystery remained, everything that occurred today left an unforgettable mark in their hearts.
They too once casually spoke of witnessing a Divine descend upon the world…
After the Ancient Evil God left the Main Plane, the blood-colored cloak covering the sky above Risier City also gradually faded then burst–
Like a bubble directly shattering into energy crystals resembling rubies, slowly falling from the sky.
Under the sunlight, the world shimmered brilliantly, a scene stunning enough to mesmerize anyone.
Lide, sensing that the aura of the God of Plague had completely disappeared, took a deep breath and made Castro, still flapping its wings, stop.
“My lord…” Emi looked hesitantly at Lide, her tone grave.
“We might be in big trouble now…”
Although they successfully snatched the Divine’s head this time, the attitude of the God of Plague suggested an imminent tremendous upheaval.
The information revealed by that Ancient Divine was too much and too heavy.
Dawn City had to prepare in advance.
Lide didn’t immediately respond to Emi; after pondering for a moment, his expression slowly regained determination.
Will as firm as steel.
“I have already sensed the storm coming…”
“But, we fear nothing!”
“Let’s go, back to Dawn City…”
He finished speaking, lowered his head to look at the one-horned head of the Evil God in his hand, its surface densely covered with Ancient Seals exuding an indescribable aura of malevolence.
Though great change was imminent, transcendence was also at hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 384 - Chapter 384: Chapter 386: Aftermath of the Battle, The Elves Stir (9000 words)
chapters.content:
Everyone had not anticipated that the finale of Risier City’s Divine Relic would conclude in such a scenario.
The cape, bloody in appearance, became the last memory point for everyone.
Lord Ilo, the War of Five Armies, the Blood Cloak, Ancient Evil Gods, and so on, became the new legends in the mouths of the minstrels.
But the end of the War of Five Armies was merely the beginning, an unprecedented one.
April 15, three days after the battle for Risier City had ended.
In the core area of Risier City.
At that moment, numerous adventurers and mercenaries were reluctantly searching around the shattered Black Altar, seemingly trying to find some forgotten treasures.
A Level 7 warrior, after searching to no avail for half a day, could not help but sit on the altar cursing in irritation, planning to rest for a while. However, just as he sat down, his eyes suddenly bulged, because he saw the space in front of him distorting.
Then, with a crackling sound like shattering glass, the surrounding space was torn apart.
Countless Fierce Half-Ratmen roared and charged out.
These Fierce Half-Ratmen were even more terrifying and ferocious than before, with frightful barbs growing on their backs, a horn atop their heads, and their sharp teeth and claws even more lethal.
In an instant, the Level 7 warrior was overwhelmed.
These creatures were so numerous they defied count, and with their surge came a gray energy carrying an evil aura.
Nearby, the looting mercenaries and players instantly felt the sharpness of these hellish devils’ claws and fangs.
Risier City fell once again, the impact far more exaggerated than three days prior.
With barbed backs and wings that stretched three blades wide, the Meat-winged Half-ratmen covered the sky, while two-blade tall, vicious, evil Fierce Half-Ratmen took over the land.
Risier City was reclaimed by hundreds of millions of Fierce Half-Ratmen.
This city, which had sealed the Ancient Evil God for millions of years, had completely become a rat’s den.
The Nest of the Evil God.
Even more exaggerated was that the gray evil energy gushing from the altar did not stop at Risier City but began to spread out around it, covering a hundred kilometers in radius before barely coming to a halt.
The area enveloped in gray mist became the Demon Territory, ruled by murderous, cruel, and evil Divine Servants from Risier City.
The screeching of the rats became the only melody of this sky.
This land was thoroughly transformed into a no-man’s land.
And some fearless adventurers and players had again ventured into Risier City, only to discover blasphemous language from the old times echoing once more above the city…
As the starting point, the Divine Relic of Risier City, a terrifying storm was beginning to brew in the Main Plane of Glory.
The Ancient Evil God’s release opened the forbidden cage…everything was changing.
Green City, being most affected, saw notable changes; rumors spread wildly, frightening the citizens into unrest, and many well-established nobles began to move their households away from Risier City, intending to distance themselves from the rat-infested Demon Cave.
This was because the ruler of the southern provinces–Duke O’Kelly, likely had no strength left to protect Green City.
Millions had witnessed Duke O’Kelly’s defeat in Risier City, with tens of thousands of troops lost.
If even the Duke, who commanded such a powerful army, was defeated, what capital did they have to resist the invasion of the Evil God?
For a time, the mood was uneasy.
But what kept many from deciding to leave Green City was another point, the sovereign of the Dark Contract–Lord Ilo.
No one could forget that towering presence above Risier City who made the Divine kneel with just his words, nor could anyone forget the shocking scene where he burst three Extraordinary beings with a single hand.
With such a figure in Risier City, many undoubtedly regained a certain degree of confidence.
Of course, the claim that Lord Ilo is a vampire began to spread widely along with the deeds of Risier City.
But in the end, because the legends of Lord Ilo are so vast, they formed a very interesting situation.
A portion of people firmly believe that Lord Ilo is indeed a vampire, and the massacre above Risier City is merely a cover-up.
Among them, the Heart-eating Demon Wales stands as a representative, a staunch supporter of this argument.
Wales had personally witnessed Lord Ilo, before him, unleashing the power of light through his Bloodline identity, so no rumor or claim could shake his steadfast trust in Lord Ilo.
He even went out of his way to verify the authenticity of the Divine Relic through his own channels, but instead, his adoration for Lord Ilo grew deeper after confirmation.
This Heart-eating Demon, whose aura has quieted, and who at a glance appears no different from an ordinary person, now has one untouchable taboo: no one is allowed to speak ill of Lord Ilo, not even the slightest bit.
And the view of the Heart-eating Demon Wales represents the perspective of the majority of the Underworld population in Green City.
Even if someone came forward with examples to prove that Lord Ilo is a human, they simply couldn’t convince the people of the Underworld in Green City, who instead would believe that Lord Ilo’s disguise was too successful, fooling all these people.
Thus, a miraculous scene emerged in the public opinion arena of Green City.
The people of the Underworld were utterly convinced that Lide was the essence of Dark Life, with humanity being his disguise–just a disguise so successful that it tricked all humans.
But those who had seen Lide wield Holy Light Power to suppress an Evil God were firmly convinced that Lide was human, and that the so-called Dark Life was just a disguise similar to the Life Goddess walking the earth.
These lowly, unwise forces of the Underworld were naturally unaware of the greatness of Lord Ilo’s actions, and both sides firmly believed what they saw was the truth.
The two parties developed a significant divide, yet each was convinced that what they saw and heard was the truth, with the other side merely deceived by Lord Ilo’s facade.
Moreover, everyone felt they had plenty of confidence and evidence, leaving no room to persuade one another.
At the epicenter of this storm, Lide mysteriously became a powerful figure revered by both camps, enjoying worship and admiration from both sides.
It wasn’t that no one doubted him, but because the strength Lide showed was too formidable, no one dared try to verify the truth.
Although the opinions of the natives were divided, they still retained enough sanity, in contrast to the online gamers, who were far crazier than the natives.
In the eyes of most gamers, Lide had undoubtedly become the most formidable existence among NPCs known in Glory, without peer.
Transcendents, Divine beings, they were all just fated to be obliterated or kneel before him.
On the official forum of Glory, thousands of posts about Lide could be refreshingly churned out in a minute.
“The Most Powerful Handsome Man in History–Lord Ilo”
If someone told me yesterday there was someone as handsome as me in this world, I wouldn’t have believed it, until today in Risier City, I saw Ilo burst three Transcendents…
“The God of Risier City–Ilo”
After repeatedly pondering the images of Ilo suppressing everyone, the excitement in my heart can’t calm down for a long time, I’m sorry everyone, I am now a faithful Believer of Ilo, and once I complete this task, I will join the Dark Contract…
“My Love Diary with Husband Ilo”
Today is the third day I’ve known husband Ilo, miss him miss him miss him…
“If my boyfriend were half as handsome as NPC Ilo, I’d never let him out of bed each day”
“‘My Days Living with Ilo’ has officially started serializing, yingyingying, welcome everyone to support, there are many descriptions of good morning and good night scenes”
…
Most posts from the silly gamers were exclamations about Lide’s strength, and some female gamers who coveted his looks filled the forum with screenshots. It’s just that Glory does not allow video recordings, or else by now the videos would be flying everywhere.
Of course, setting aside those silly gamers stirring up excitement, many professional gamers also provided some quite professional analyses.
Among them, the analysis from the player “Broken Sword the Knight,” a notable figure of the Undead Clan, was most popular.
“Reflections on the Divine Relic of Risier City”
Hello everyone, this is the Knight of the Broken Sword. It’s been a long time since I last posted. The Undead Empire has been quite busy lately, and I haven’t had much time to attend to other matters, so I haven’t been able to provide analysis for everyone.
Today I’m posting two gifts as compensation: Bunny Girl Screenshot.jpg and Cat Girl Long Legs.jpg…
The main content of today’s post is to analyze the Divine Relic for everyone.
This matter is too important, and I hope it can raise everyone’s awareness.
Why do I say this? Because when the Evil God broke free in Risier City, I personally heard the phrase “The Old Era has come” from the mouth of the Undead Monarch.
Although I can’t determine exactly what the Old Era is, and my further questions to the Undead Monarch didn’t yield more useful information, I have drawn a conclusion after synthesizing messages from various sources.
The Divine Relic in Risier City should be the starting point of an event.
Or to use gaming terms, it’s the opening of a new expansion pack.
The gods of old will return… That is my judgment.
Those evil beings sealed within the main plane of “Glory” are certainly not solo in their kind.
Everyone may consider, why were those Divine beings sealed? And what will they do after they escape their confinement?
Will they choose to repay evil with kindness, or will they incite war to take revenge on those Divine beings who once betrayed them?
As beings at the pinnacle of “Glory,” Divine beings are the ultimate life forms in this multi-dimensional world.
Once they wage war against each other, how should we, as part of Glory, conduct ourselves?
This is the crux of the matter!
We players have entered “Glory” for too brief a period, and even after half a year of public beta, the top players are still stuck at Level 4, with most people still at Level 3.
We have no choice but to be passively drawn into this conflict.
Of course, this is not only about crisis, but more about opportunities.
I believe everyone knows that Risier City is now a place overrun by Fierce Half-Ratmen. Although the place is fraught with threats, such a dense gathering of monsters is extremely rare in Glory.
I even suspect that this could be an instance specifically created by the official website for players to farm and level up.
These Fierce Half-Ratmen may generally be at Levels 6 or 7, and even Level 10 and above are not uncommon, but with proper strategy, players nearby can use this opportunity to level up quickly.
Therefore, my second inference is that the emergence of the Evil God has, in another sense, opened up a new instance for us. As long as you have the appetite to handle it, you can quickly rise in levels.
This is also a chance for ordinary players to pull away from top players and for top players to become even more elite. It depends on how everyone grasps this opportunity, DogHead.jpg
The turmoil in Risier City is just the beginning, as stated by the Undead Monarch himself. It can be foreseen that not only the Nolan Empire, but more seals will likely break in the future.
And each time will be an opportunity for us.
The Undead Empire is now recruiting a large number of players in preparation for war. If anyone is interested, you can directly contact the WeChat below. A staff member will send you a guide to enter the Undead Empire, and I will personally lead the team to ensure your leveling is safeguarded.
I am the Knight of the Broken Sword, brothers, come and fight me…
It’s undeniable that advanced players have access to information channels beyond what ordinary players can imagine.
Like the Knight of the Broken Sword, who can interact daily with personas like the Undead Monarch, he sometimes has access to even more extensive information than Lide.
So after this post was published, it immediately sparked heated discussion among players.
Of course, most players are interested in the news that more Divine relics will emerge, each eager to show their mettle, clamoring to seize Divine Artifacts and slay gods, as if they can’t wait to pull off a big heist.
The subsequent direction of events also validated the judgment of the Knight of the Broken Sword, or rather, the Undead Monarch.
On April 20, a week after the battle for Risier City, the skies and earth of the Storm Sea Domain suddenly changed color, and an island housing hundreds of thousands of people collapsed with a roar.
Then an Ancient Evil God, with the body of a giant octopus and nine deformed heads, reemerged.
There was no coming of a Savior this time, for the Storm Sea Domain hundreds of miles around was completely massacred by the Ancient Evil God, and many players tasted the flavor of death at the hands of a god.
And with the appearance of this Ancient Evil God came countless Bloodthirsty Octopuses, these creatures surged out from the deep sea densely packed, transforming this sea area into the Land of Death.
The catastrophe of the Storm Sea Domain was termed by players as the Tentacle Catastrophe.
On the same day, at the outer region of the Ancient Forest, a city of the elves was in upheaval, the ground cracked, trees ignited into flames out of thin air, and thick smoke covered the sky.
An Evil God with wings on its back and six eyes on its head crawled out of its seal, and on that day, the six-eyed Evil God became the source of the elves’ terror.
Thousands of elves were devoured by the Evil God, a loss that was close to a catastrophic blow for the always scant elf population.
Finally, only the extraordinarily powerful Elf King from within the Ancient Forest took action to expel that six-eyed Evil God, driving it into the depths of the abyss.
Even so, the shattered elf city remained tainted, and numerous deformed monsters crawled out from the Space Gate, attacking any life they encountered.
When time advanced to April 30th, the entire Glory Main Plane seemed to be engulfed in an indescribable atmosphere.
Since the first Evil God emerged from Risier City, in just this brief half-month, such events had occurred over ten times.
These horrifying deeds directly caused the deaths of millions, sparking the fury of various Light Attribute Sects, who dispatched many Extraordinary Level powers to investigate any place the Evil Gods’ seals might be hidden, seeking to prevent such incidents from happening again.
The various empires were also on high alert, with armies on guard at all times, and Extraordinary Level beings mobilized uniformly.
The Pandora’s Box seemed to have been quietly opened.
—
—
—
April 30th, evening, in the western district of Green City.
On the dimly lit street, only occasionally would a Magic Lamp cast a light as faint as the dying embers of a fire.
On the houses lining the street, colorful stained glass windows were etched with vivid paintings, but the dim light turned these images somewhat bloody and terrifying.
Pointed rooftops with ferocious giant dragon statues seemed particularly sinister at this moment.
In such surroundings, the damp ground and the ancient streets with their hundreds of years of history exuded an ineffable sense of gloom.
Yet within this environment, which could give commoners shivers, there appeared a figure shrouded in a red cloak.
Tap, tap~
The clear sound of leather boots tapping against the ground echoed, and the ivory scholar’s robe she wore highlighted her slender figure strikingly.
The noblewoman’s head was held high like that of a swan, elegant and indifferent, her every move exuding an unmistakably unveiled arrogance.
On the dimly lit street, this highly abnormal scene drew the attention of many.
Members of the Underground Forces loitering on the street exchanged glances, a gleam of lewdness in their eyes, and then a curve of ill-intent formed on their lips as they covertly sized up the woman who, at a glance, appeared to be a noble.
However, there were also many astute individuals who quickly quickened their pace to leave, understanding that a lady walking alone at night, no matter how harmless she may seem, was best approached with caution–this was, after the slums of Green City.
Andabella’s gaze swept around her with indifference, her eternally raised neck broadcasting her upper-crust noble aura to anyone at first glance.
Her gaze swiftly locked onto several hooligans on the street corner who were eyeing her with malicious intent.
She strode forward, and before the few could open their mouths with leering laughter, a terrifying aura erupted from her.
In that instant, it was as if a giant dragon was roaring at the small-time hooligans, their necks feeling as though choked by powerful arms, breathing becoming a luxury at that moment.
“I ask, you answer,”
Andabella’s eyes, sharp as blade’s edge, pierced the onlookers’ gaze, her tone like a master commanding a servant.
But several thieves, barely at level 5, nodded repeatedly, not even considering the idea of rebuffing, all of them had swallowed the lascivious smile from just moments ago.
“Where is the Dark Contract? And where is Lord Ilo?”
This?
The thieves glanced at each other, somewhat panicked, one of them, a tall figure, plucked up his courage to speak.
“Respected lady, the Dark Contract is on the other side of the west district; you need to go through the black market to find it.
As for Lord Ilo, how could beings like us know the whereabouts of such a significant figure…”
Andabella’s brows furrowed slightly.
“How much do you know about the legends surrounding Lord Ilo?”
“Ah? Lord Ilo is the chairman of the Dark Contract, he once…”
After the thief had related all he knew, Andabella couldn’t help feeling disappointed; these were all common knowledge.
“Is that all?”
“Yes, my lord,” the speaking thief swallowed and quickly added, “If you go to the black market to ask Lord Wales, the Heart-eating Demon from the Demon Heart, perhaps you could get more information…”
Andabella nodded slightly at these words, her proud head never lowered in the slightest.
“Thank you, I appreciate your cooperation.”
She turned and left straightaway.
The thieves, who had just narrowly escaped death’s scythe, felt oddly flattered and even thought they had struck it big by being thanked, given the interrogation they’d endured.
Being thanked by such a distinguished noble lady was a first in their lives.
After Andabella’s figure disappeared around the corner of the street, one thief couldn’t help but comment emotionally.
“I have no idea who will end up with such a perfect lady, by the Goddess above, I don’t want to be a thief in my next life…”
The other thieves nodded in agreement.
Later, they didn’t expect that these petty thieves, stimulated by this event, began to work earnestly on improving their abilities and started to learn to read and write, eventually becoming pillars of the Thief Guild.
Moreover, by a stroke of luck, in a chance operation, they made a great contribution to Green City and were rewarded with noble status by Duke O’Kelly, becoming admired nobles and even marrying true noble ladies.
These men became legends in the Green City thieves’ community, with countless thieves born in slums idolizing them.
At this time, Andabella, naturally unaware of future events, was walking towards the street the men had indicated.
“Should I go meet Duke O’Kelly, have people gather information on Lord Ilo first before paying a visit?”
“No, it would be too insincere if it’s not a personal visit.”
“To suppress an Ancient Evil God, he must be formidable…
Perhaps Lord Ilo might understand the Risle Bloodline…”
Andabella walked down the dimly lit streets, her brow tightly furrowed, a hint of her intimidating aura leaking out, causing those with ill-intentions to tremble and no longer dare to peer at her.
But at this moment, the girl’s thoughts were not on these passersby.
“Although I was summoned to Risier City by the power left behind by my ancestors, the force that has fused into my body is too immense, and I simply cannot control it.
The message from my ancestors was to unlock the potential of the bloodline, and once I brought the Risle Bloodline’s glory to light again, I would be able to fully inherit that power.
But all of this is without clue…”
Thinking this, Andabella shook her head, feeling the Blood Cloak fluttering in the wind behind her, her expression subtly changing.
“And who could have thought,” she mused, “that this Legendary Level Blood Cloak I carry on my back is but a replica, made in imitation of our ancestor’s cloak by the Risle Royal Family.”
“And the true Blood Cloak, I fear, is now unknown to all–a genuine Divine Artifact.”
“Regrettably, although I have acquired the true Blood Cloak, I am still unable to control it. Only by awakening the full power of the Risle Bloodline and grasping the ancestral power can I breathe life into the dust-covered Divine Artifact again…”
“But the secrets contained within the Risle Bloodline are too elusive. After more than half a month of research, I have gained nothing…”
“I need help…”
Help?
After the word surfaced in her mind, Andabella’s steps faltered slightly. The image of the man who had saved her from danger, riding atop a steel giant beast, inexplicably appeared in her thoughts.
Thinking of the man who had given her a sense of security for the first time in her life, the corners of her lips instinctively curled upward, and the pride on her face softened a touch.
She had not witnessed the scene where Lide made the God of Plague kneel with a single command. By the time she arrived, Lide had already flown dozens of kilometers away from Risier City.
Therefore, the two had not met, and Castro, the steel giant beast, had not appeared within her sight.
The stories about Lord Ilo reached her ears after she had driven away the God of Plague, tales she heard from outsiders, and his might surprised her.
This was why she desired to seek Lord Ilo’s counsel. As for whether he would pose a danger to her, the power inherited from her ancestors within her body was enough to face any challenge fearlessly.
Even if he were a true Divine being, she was confident she could escape.
Being a girl who acquired the title of polymath in her early twenties, the heights of her ambition were naturally incomprehensible to others.
Therefore, her solo journey to the west district of Green City was somewhat curious but not wholly unfathomable.
“Such intense energy? Are you the descendant of the Risle Royal Family who drove away the Evil God from Risier City?”
But just as Andabella stepped into a small alley, a crisp yet somewhat lazy voice interrupted her stride.
Hm?
Andabella spun around sharply, facing a figure that took her aback.
“An Elf??”
The Level 17 Elf Archer Master, once tormented in the mysterious tavern–Lady Ariel–was now looking at Andabella with evident interest.
“I saw you at Duke O’Kelly’s banquet, City Lord Andabella…”
“I think I’ve seen you as well, Lady Ariel.” Andabella’s brows furrowed slightly, but her expression remained steady.
Elves are purely aligned with nature. As long as their Ancient Forest isn’t harmed, no innocents are indiscriminately killed, and no evil deeds are committed, these proud beings seldom act against outsiders out of disdain.
“Do you seek me for a reason?” But why would this Elf suddenly seek her out??
At the question, Ariel giggled, and the pride not fitting for an Elf on her chest trembled slightly with her laughter.
But Ariel’s next sentence startled Andabella.
“We’ve sensed that power within you, perhaps, we may have a way to help you…”
If it’s too good to be true… Andabella’s expression didn’t change much, but she was already on her guard internally.
“Help me? What would I need to give in return?”
“No, City Lord Andabella, you need not give anything.”
“Then what is your purpose?”
“We have discovered an Ancient Ruin… perhaps, you might be interested.”
“Why invite me?”
“In fact, we were planning to invite Lord Ilo, but we ran into you on the way. It seems to be fate. Is City Lord Andabella also looking for Lord Ilo?”
“You?”
“Yes, we…”
As her words fell, Lady Ariel hesitated for a moment, and then finally waved her hand.
Then the space behind the Elf suddenly shattered, and two figures with such imposing auras that they moved Andabella herself appeared in the alley.
One of them, an Elf Spellcaster in a Mage’s robe, exhibited an aura that undeniably reached the Extraordinary Level, and her stunning beauty brightened the air around her.
The other lady caught Andabella’s attention with several glances.
For this person was not an Elf, and the soul’s aura was almost indistinguishable from a human’s; but that was not the key. The key was her eyes, which were red, as red as fresh blood and rubies.
Moreover, this unknown female Transcendent seemed even more dangerous and lethal to her than the Extraordinary Elf Spellcaster.
Both were Transcendent… Andabella’s thoughts were tumultuous.
Legendaries were too rare, so Transcendents were absolute figures of status no matter where in Glory they were. In Green City, with its population of over a million, there was only Lord Rock in the public eye, his status so revered that it was beyond the comprehension of outsiders.
This time the Elves had dispatched a Transcendent to Green City from the Ancient Forest, which certainly indicated a momentous scheme.
Lady Ariel’s gaze at Andabella was intense.
“City Lord Andabella, perhaps we can visit Lord Ilo together.
Regardless of the outcome, we will share with you the secrets of the Risle Bloodline…”
“You have the secrets of the Risle Bloodline?”
“Miss Andabella, you shouldn’t doubt the Elves’ erudition.”
Andabella glanced at the two Transcendents who had been silent the whole time, her emotions stirred, and in the end, she nodded slightly; she could not refuse the proposal, as the secrets of the Risle Bloodline were too important to her.
“I trust the Elves’ reputation…”
“Then let’s go together…”
That evening, Black Rose Manor welcomed several unexpected guests.
—
—
—
In the City Lord’s Manor of Green City, Duke O’Kelly stood in his study with his hands behind his back, looking at the map of the southern province hanging on the wall, his expression exceedingly grave.
“Your Excellency the Bishop, the Fierce Half-Ratman of Risier City, are they truly beyond extermination? I fear they may become a significant threat to us…”
The Bishop of the God of Nobles had gained his trust since they went through a life-and-death ordeal together half a month ago.
The other’s meticulous and cautious style perfectly complemented Duke O’Kelly’s rough and forceful demeanor, which made O’Kelly appreciate him greatly, leading to assigning him right by his side.
Under normal circumstances, a Bishop of the God of Nobles would naturally hold an exceedingly high status within the Sect and could not be reassigned on a whim.
However, in the Noble God Sect, the great Nobles are the real decision-makers. As the Controller of the southern province, there was no one with higher status than him here, so what was reassigning a bishop?
“Duke, Risier City is not an isolated case.
Recently, reports from all the major empires in the Main Plane of Glory have been coming in; many ancient seals that have existed since time immemorial are being broken by Evil Gods, bringing with them countless monsters along with these Ancient Gods…
No one has yet been able to exterminate these foul beings that crawl out from unknown realms.”
After hearing this, Duke O’Kelly couldn’t help but feel a headache coming on.
After the war at Risier City, his losses were too great so that now he could no longer muster 300,000 elite forces. Yet the vast southern provinces still required his troops for defense, which undoubtedly put him in a dilemma.
“How did the King respond?”
“His Majesty the King will dispatch 100,000 troops to our aid… but the subsequent expenses of this army must be borne by us.”
Duke O’Kelly immediately breathed a sigh of relief.
“Good, send this army to eradicate those damned rats near Risier City.”
After a brief pause, he continued, “Any news from Lord Ilo?”
“No,” the bishop shook his head, “We have contacted the Dark Contract repeatedly, and their response has always been that Lord Ilo has not yet returned.”
“You must personally supervise this matter. When Lord Ilo returns, I want to visit him myself.” Duke O’Kelly’s tone carried a sense of urgency.
The world was clearly changing, and he had to find a new protector for Green City.
The Extraordinary Mage, Rock, while powerful, was too weak to make much of a difference on a battlefield where Ancient Evil Gods were awaking.
By contrast, Ilo, who could crush three Transcendents in one hand, had now become the new prospective Protector of Green City in his heart.
“Yes, Your Grace.”
The bishop immediately nodded and seemed hesitant as if remembering something.
“Your Grace, about the Elves’ request, should we agree to it?”
“Elves?” Duke O’Kelly frowned slightly, turned his head to glance at the bishop, and then questioned,
“Don’t they see the plight of Risier City? What basis do they have for coveting Divine Ruins??”
“Your Grace, the Elves have discovered a broken Plane which may conceal Plane Stones, and also numerous precious ores…”
“No, I’m not interested in those.”
After shaking his head, Duke O’Kelly paused and then slowly added, “I still owe the Elves a small favor. If they decide to proceed with their plan to explore the shattered Plane, after Lord Ilo’s return, when we visit, let’s mention it for them… Maybe Lord Ilo will be interested too. With Lord Ilo’s protection, this matter shouldn’t be too difficult.
“Did the Elves reveal any other information?”
“Your Grace, it seems the Elves are heading there for the Sun Chasing Bow…”
“Is that the Divine Artifact that the Elves have never completed forging?”
“Yes, it appears that the ruin contains Divine Stones capable of forging artifacts, and there’s quite a few of them.”
“That’s irrelevant to us; even if we had those ores, we couldn’t use them. Is there any other information?”
“Well, no… that’s right, there’s also a peculiar human following those Elves, with eyes like rubies…”
“Oh? Not an Elf?”
“No, those eyes are too memorable.”
“Alright, this has nothing to do with us either. If there’s nothing else, you’re dismissed.
“While Elves are mighty, these proud beings are never straightforward. Green City doesn’t have the energy to meddle in their affairs now. What we need to prepare for is the great calamity that’s about to hit our world.”
Duke O’Kelly spoke in a grave tone, his gaze exceedingly solemn.
“Bishop, since His Grace last gave us his decree, no matter how much I pray, there has been no divine oracle, not even the Holy Light Pearl is shrouded in darkness.
I feel the crisis approaching; we don’t have much time…
The power of the Old Era will soon envelop this world, and we will live again in fear under the dominion of Ancient Gods…”

chapters.title: Chapter 385 - Chapter 385: Chapter 387: The Youth Who Lacks Martial Virtue is Torn Apart by the Evil God at the Land of Bone-Burying (6000 words)

Chapter 385: Chapter 387: The Youth Who Lacks Martial Virtue is Torn Apart by the Evil God at the Land of Bone-Burying (6000 words)
May 3rd, Dawn City.
After spring had arrived, the winter wheat’s growth skyrocketed, and now the ears of wheat had begun to take on a golden hue. Farmers on the Moonlight Plain were currently using the latest harvesting tools developed by the blacksmith’s workshop to cut the wheat, their faces beaming with joy as bright as the sunlight.
For most commoners, having land to farm, clothes to wear, and not facing threats to their lives already counted as great fortune.
This city, brimming with hope, experienced joyful changes every day.
In the new district, the newly constructed City Hall had been put into use.
This massive five-story, thirty-blade-high building had become the new landmark of Dawn City.
Now, most of the City Hall departments had moved into the new office building, and to facilitate the control and issuance of orders, Lide had also moved from his old office in the former City Hall.
Standing in his top-floor office, thirty blades high, Lide could see the edge of the new district, and even the farmers harvesting wheat on the Moonlight Plain.
It had been 20 days since the battle for Risier City, but the impact of this war on Dawn City was far from over.
“Harrison, has the Giant Army been retrieved from the island?”
“Sire, they have all been returned.”
Harrison reported respectfully from behind Lide.
After the battle of Risier City, the Centaur Army and the Giant Army retreated separately, with the Magic Language Bats transporting the Giants to the island controlled by the Fishman Tribe once they had withdrawn from the combat.
Meanwhile, the Centaur Army had fallen back to the Dwarf Hills and had temporarily suspended trade with Dawn City.
This was the most cautious course of action, taken to guard against any prying eyes on the Centaur and Giant Armies.
Lide had originally planned to observe for at least three months.
But plans could not keep up with changes; as a great number of Ancient Evil Gods emerged, the attention drawn by the battle for Risier City had been diverted.
Thus, after lying low for half a month and ensuring there was no danger, the Giants began to return to Dawn City.
Only when the entire Giant Army had returned did Lide feel that the war had truly come to an end.
“This time our dispatched Giant Army numbered 1,300, with 130 casualties, all Double-headed Ogres.
The Centaur Army totaled 125,000, with over 8,000 fallen.”
Lide nodded slightly upon hearing Harrison’s report. He had to admit that the army he had spent a vast amount of resources to build was indeed formidable.
While other armies suffered heavy losses or were entirely wiped out, the Centaurs’ casualties were less than 10%, which unequivocally demonstrated their strength.
As for zero casualties, that was merely a fantasy. This was a war where hundreds of thousands clashed; no one could predict what would happen in the next second. The hope of avoiding all deaths was sheer folly.
After his report, Harrison hesitated as if he remembered something, “Sire, we did not discover Lord Asreaga in the direction you mentioned…”
Lide’s brow furrowed. Asreaga had swiftly left Risier City after grabbing the God of Plague’s arm.
He had expected the other party would return to Dawn City, but Asreaga had vanished without a trace.
After concentrating, Lide sensed that the Divine Monster had entered a dormant state, seemingly undergoing some inscrutable metamorphosis.
Lide speculated that perhaps the seal on the God of Plague’s arm had ruptured mid-way, forcing Asreaga to directly absorb the power, resulting in his slumber.
But the Divine Power had concealed Asreaga’s presence, so Lide could not pinpoint his exact location. He could only send out a rough directive and dispatch personnel to search and hopefully discover a trace.
Therefore, they were now facing this situation.
“Continue deploying search teams. The divine arm on Asreaga is too important. Although his power is immeasurably strong, his sensitivity to the outside world must inevitably decline to rock-bottom while he sleeps. If he encounters the forces of the Light Sect, he might not be able to cope.”
“Yes, Sire!” Harrison responded with a stern expression.
Although Lide had delegated the task, he wasn’t overly concerned deep down. After all, the other was a Divine Monster who had survived since ancient times. He most likely had chosen a safe place before he fell asleep.
Dispatching search parties was a precaution. Without locating Asreaga, he could only increase the tolerance for error as much as possible, giving himself more room to maneuver.
Bang~Bang~
Suddenly, a knock at the door interrupted their conversation.
“Come in.”
Lide turned slightly as Emi entered the room.
“Good day, Sire.”
Upon entering, Emi immediately bowed respectfully, her chest tilting forward. The Shadow High Priest, who had returned to Dawn City after two and a half years, appeared excited and seemed quite exhilarated.
“Sire, I have found the way to break the seal of the divine head!”
Yes, it had been a full twenty days since Lide had acquired the divine head and still not broken its seal.
Lide had to acknowledge that his progress in researching the divine head wasn’t as swift as he had imagined.
The ancient seals handed down through the ages were exceedingly robust.
The Ancient Seal, crafted specifically to imprison an Evil God, was not something current magical seals could match.
Even though the seal’s power had significantly diminished over countless years, it was, after all, power meant to bind a god.
Thus, Lide was at an impasse, helplessly stuck for the time being.
There were only three ways to quickly break the seal: the first, naturally, was to find the correct method and unlock it directly.
The second was to tear apart the seal by brute force, where brute force referred to Divine Power level 30 or above.
The third was to use the Power of Faith to erode the seal. As a power only deities could wield, the Power of Faith was doubtlessly the trump card for breaking seals.
In principle, the third option was the best. However, the biggest contradiction lay in the fact that — there wasn’t enough Power of Faith.
Lide tentatively estimated that it would take at least a million units of the Power of Faith to break the seal, which was more than he had accumulated over the years.
So the third idea had to be abandoned. After researching for a couple of weeks without success, Lide, in a fit of anger, handed the problem over to Emi and the Magic Industry Research Institute for joint research.
This back and forth consumed a full 20 days.
“Oh? How should it be done?” Lide had been looking forward to the unsealing for so long that his excitement was indescribable,
His feeling before was much like finding a peerless secret manual in a martial arts novel after much hardship, only to prepare for cultivation and discover that it was written in an alien language that he couldn’t understand at all, which was a real pain in the ass.
A Divine head, this could be a chance to break through as a Transcendent…
Emi’s face was excited, yet her expression was a bit odd.
“Your Majesty, conventional forces are unable to break this seal; indeed, we’ve tried all methods to no avail. However, in the end, we discovered… You might be very surprised to know this method,”
Damn it, what’s this bastard hiding now? Lide gave Emi a fierce glance.
“Spit it out!”
Emi gave a sheepish smile and hurriedly spoke, but her next words made Lide’s eyes widen, and a strange expression appeared on his face.
“Your Majesty, it’s the Cow Bone Undead from the Land of Bone-Burying; it can help us break the seal…”
Looking at Emi’s serious expression, Lide’s face darkened; had he heard wrong? The Cow Bone Undead from the Land of Bone-Burying could help him break the seal on a Divine Body??
What kind of international joke was this? Apart from gnawing on bones, that damned Undead liked to build houses, and lately, it had taken an interest in constructing underground palaces, turning the subsurface of the Land of Bone-Burying into a labyrinth of tunnels.
And this thing could break the seal on a Divine Body? This had to be a joke, right?
Further, the Cow Bone Undead was only Level 14!
“Are you serious??”
At this moment, Lide truly doubted whether this guy’s brain had been kicked in by that cow…
“Yes, Your Majesty.”
Emi’s expression too was a little subtle.
After so much effort, involving the smartest hundreds of Dawn City working day and night for half a month without a solution, the answer was ultimately found on a cow.
This, this seemed a bit embarrassing…
Lide looked at Emi, who spoke with such certainty, and calmed down. Thinking of the Cow Bone Undead’s odd behavior from the day he created it, he felt that it wouldn’t be too inconceivable for that damned Undead cow to pull this off… After all, that creature had never been normal.
“How did the Cow Bone Undead do it? Did it use its Soul Fire to melt the seal, or did it acquire some powerful Skill to destroy it?”
Emi looked embarrassed.
“No, neither… Your Cow Bone Undead is too powerful; it can directly gnaw on the seal…
By the Creator God, it’s simply shocking.
I witnessed the seal on the head of the Divine Body being bitten open by it, those Ancient Runes even being swallowed into its stomach…”
Emi’s explanation became more and more fantastical… but Lide couldn’t shake the feeling that this was definitely something that cow was capable of doing.
“Where is the Cow Bone Undead now?”
“We’ve already taken it to the Magic Industry Research Institute…”
“Let’s go and see for ourselves.”
Not wanting to dawdle, Lide stretched out his hand, opened the Space Gate, and, along with Emi and Harrison who hadn’t had the chance to speak, entered the Magic Industry Research Institute.
To unseal the skull of the God of Plague, during this time Lide allowed Emi, who had previously gained a portion of Divine Power, to utilize the resources of Dawn City.
Since conventional methods were useless, Emi made use of all sorts of strange things, and the Cow Bone Undead was just one of them.
Initially, Emi intended to let the Cow Bone Undead use its Soul Fire to infiltrate and destroy the seal from within, but to everyone’s surprise, the Cow Bone Undead just attacked it with its mouth…
By the time Lide appeared at the entrance of the Magic Industry Research Institute, the newly built industrial zone came into view.
The Magic Industry Research Institute covered an area of over 500 acres, with 30 research buildings, 20 workshops, and production bases, plus a large amount of land waiting for development.
More than 3,000 people lived and worked here daily, including Half-Elfs, goblins, Dwarfs, humans, Bloodlines, and even Beastman, One-eyed Giants, and Double-headed Ogres could be seen everywhere–it was practically a natural multi-race exhibition hall.
“Your Majesty, good day.”
Over a dozen Bloodline guards bowed respectfully upon seeing Lide.
Lide couldn’t be bothered with small talk and had Emi lead the way inside the Magic Industry Research Institute.
Due to the importance of the Magic Industry Research Institute, Lide personally ordered that no one should use the Space Gate of the Land of Bone-Burying to enter, and he made it a point to lead by example and not break his own orders.
After a series of turns, the three of them arrived at the central building that was 20 blades high, amidst respectful greetings.
In the clanking sound of the Magic Elevator, they went straight down to the third basement floor.
Inside a room protected by a Magic Array and Alchemy Traps, Lide saw the skull of the God of Plague that had been gnawed on by the Cow Bone Undead.
The Evil God’s skull was roughly the same size as a normal human head, but what was shocking was that pieces of the chilling Ancient Runes etched upon it were missing as if an ice popsicle had been bitten into, with the teeth marks strikingly clear.
At the moment, the Cow Bone Undead lay listlessly in a slightly empty corner, flicking its cow tail in boredom, seemingly yearning for its underground palace…
Upon seeing Lide, the Cow Bone Undead’s originally lethargic body vibrated suddenly, its head rose quickly, and then with a sudden jolt, it jumped up and lunged towards Lide.
Tap, tap–the sound of cow hooves crisply echoed.
Then, under everyone’s gaze, the Undead cow, a few blades away from Lide, abruptly came to a stop, its forelimbs and head pressed against the floor, and then under the momentum, it slid up right in front of Lide.
“Moo~”
The short tail flailed wildly, emitting a whooshing sound as it cut through the air.
Lide’s mouth involuntarily twitched at this scene.
There are some words I’m not sure if it’s appropriate to speak.
“Your Majesty…” Emi’s eyes sparkled with the glow of discovering a treasure when she saw the Cow Bone Undead.
“After the seal of the Divine Body breaks, could you assign this undead to me? I have many interesting ideas to try…”
The Cow Bone Undead, upon seeing Emi’s bright eyes, shivered as if sensing a huge threat. It quickly stood up, then scurried fearfully behind Lide, lowering its head to his feet, glowering at Emi with a hateful gaze, and emitting a hateful sound from its throat.
Lide couldn’t help but laugh and cry as he nudged the undead that acted like a silly dog with his foot, “Let’s talk about breaking the seal first.”
Emi immediately spoke up, “Your Majesty, after the seal is broken, the aura of the Divine Skull here can’t be concealed by the Magic Array. With the ability of that Evil God, he’ll likely notice our trace…”
Lide waved his hand dismissively, “I’m not that careless.”
Having said that, he waved his hand and directly broke open a Space Gate. Lide stepped into the Land of Bone-Burying with urgency overruling the need to adhere to rules. Just a moment ago, he intended to set an example by following the rules, but now he had to contradict himself.
“Bring that skull in.”
The Cow Bone Undead, upon hearing the order, let out a silly cry, then turned around and, like a dog, carried the grey skull in its mouth straight into the Space Gate. As it left, it glanced at Emi triumphantly, as if to say you have no way to deal with me.
“You go ahead with your tasks; don’t wait for me.”
Lide left behind these instructions and then closed the Space Gate.
That left Emi and Harrison staring at each other in silence.
After entering the Land of Bone-Burying, Lide was cautious to close all the Space Gates he had opened, while using the Power of Death to strengthen the spatial barriers of the Land of Bone-Burying.
Only after all this, did he have time to examine the Evil God’s skull lying on the white bone ground.
The ferocious rat skull remained as hideously ugly as ever, with a single, blade-long unicorn horn on its head that was razor sharp. It was wrapped in densely packed inscriptions that made it even more daunting.
Lide subconsciously opened his attribute panel, and the God of Plague’s skull attributes immediately appeared before his eyes.
Sealed Divine Skull
Quality: Divine-level
Status: Sealed (Damaged)
Explanation: A sealed Divine Skull containing powerful Divine Power. The sealing power has weakened over time due to the passage of time, and the owner of the skull is calling out to it.
A simple attribute, but it made Lide’s brow furrow slightly.
“The God of Plague…indeed never gives up, even if hiding in the bottomless abyss to recover his strength, he still watches this skull closely.
And fortunately, the ancient days he spoke of have not yet come, otherwise he might have directly intervened and snatched it.
But the time left for me isn’t much, either. This world is about to, or is already undergoing, a world-shaking change.
In tumultuous times, only powerful forces can protect everything around.
And Transcendence will be the next stage to aim for…”
After seeing the attributes of the Evil God’s skull, Lide felt an added sense of urgency in his heart.
Throughout the last half-month, the seals of the Evil Gods on the Main Plane of Glory had been breaking one after another, and the deities of ancient days were becoming active, a crisis that was visible.
And there was one thing that he kept in mind, a chilling sentence once spoken by the God of Plague–The Destiny Tablet has been stolen by the deities of ancient days, and the old days will return.
He didn’t quite understand what the Destiny Tablet was, despite all the mythological stories he had frantically collected in this time, which had never mentioned this term.
But he could feel that it was something extremely important to the multi-dimensional world of Glory and the root of all change.
Although Dawn City could now rise up an army of several hundred thousand soldiers, strong as it was, it was not enough in the face of the disaster triggered by the deities.
So, the next goal for Lide would be–to break through Transcendence.
And not just for him, he also needed to enhance the combat capabilities of his subordinates. One Transcendent was far from enough to face the upcoming upheaval.
With the situation so urgent, he no longer had much time to plan anything else.
“Help me bite through the seal…”
Lide reached out and rubbed the Cow Bone Undead’s head, the smooth and hard skull was slightly cool to the touch. The Cow Bone Undead seemed to enjoy Lide’s caresses, wagging its tail even more zealously.
With a tap on the creature’s head, the Cow Bone Undead sensing the command immediately turned around and, taking the skull it found rather tasty, trotted to the center of the area beside the twelve-tiered White Bone Altar and lay down slightly.
Then, under Lide’s peculiar gaze, the undead cow started to gnaw at the terrifyingly pulsating seals like it would a bone it would normally eat.
Crunch~
Crunch~
The seals were directly crunched, the crisp sounds like eating peanuts or biting into crunchy mahua,
Lide watched, his eyelids twitching; young people these days really lack martial virtue…
The Cow Bone Undead not only crunched up the seals, but it also chewed and swallowed the inscriptions directly into its stomach…
“What???”
Lide’s face was full of question marks as he witnessed this scene.
“.What exactly are these seals made of?? It’s one thing to bite through them, but to eat them too?”
He didn’t even know what words to use to describe this eerie scene.
This thing made no sense at all, it had swallowed the seals…
And that wasn’t all, what happened next completely made Lide feel that this cow bone undead was about to ascend to the heavens.
The broken inscriptions were swallowed by the cow bone undead, and under an invisible force, they began to dissolve slowly, just like melting snow.
To make matters even more exaggerated, the dissolved inscriptions began to swirl around the skeleton of the cow bone undead, then as if they were being rewritten by someone, those Ancient Seals started to re-inscribe themselves onto the cow bone undead’s body.
The snowy white skeleton showcased Ancient Runes glowing with a faint blue fluorescence, creating a scene that was unspeakably stunning.
Moo~
Seemingly aware of the changes to its own body, the cow bone undead chewed even more vigorously.
“What in the world have I created??”
Lide’s emotions were at their peak complexity.
This creature was too bizarre, those were seals, and not only did it eat them, it absorbed them???
What the hell is this principle??
Is there no more logic? Don’t think just because you’re a cow you can do whatever you want…
Crack~
As the seals continued to break apart under the cow bone undead’s chewing, the originally rigid and stone-like skull of the God of Plague began to warm up.
Then, an indescribable, untouchable, and unfathomable terrifying aura began to permeate within the Land of Bone-Burying.
The aura was like a fierce beast breaking out of its cage, emitting a low growl ready to select its prey.
To ensure safety, all the Death Spiders were transferred outside, leaving only a few small withered bones inside the Land of Bone-Burying, which were now trembling, their Soul Fires flickering as if they might be extinguished at any moment.
Clearly, these low-level undead that he had created, although lacking intelligence, could also feel that soul-invading terrifying aura.
Lide’s deep, dark eyes held an indescribable gravitas.
He felt it, felt the resurfacing evil power within, calling, yes, calling. The skull was calling out to its soul–the Ancient God of Plague.
Using the Plane Power of the Land of Bone-Burying, Lide could feel a call responding to the Evil God’s skull in the Chaos Void, a call that crossed distances, across countless Planar barriers.
God of Plague.
This Ancient Evil God had sensed its skull…
Lide’s heart chilled, and he forcefully invoked the power of the Land of Bone-Burying to block the other’s sensation.
It was fortunate that the Land of Bone-Burying was anchored in the Main Plane and entirely under Lide’s control, which prevented a major issue.
Yet the mutual calling between the Evil God’s skull and the God of Plague across time and space still put tremendous pressure on Lide.
With a wave of his hand, the surging Power of Death began to tightly envelop the cow bone undead, forming a protective shell like dark clouds, re-establishing another sealing defense line.
Perhaps it was psychological, but Lide distinctly felt that the calling weakened slightly under the isolation of the Power of Death.
“Speed it up!”
Lide’s gaze was sharp, his senses fully extended, constantly sensing every change around him.
If there were any changes, he would immediately summon the Plane Power to suppress the skull, just like the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel.
Not even the God of Dawn could sense the sealed Twelve-winged Blazing Angel, and Lide didn’t believe that the God of Plague was stronger than the God of Dawn.
The only problem was, if he proceeded in this manner, the opportunity to break through to Transcendence would undoubtedly be blocked.
He could only, as with the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel, use a massive amount of Power of Death to transform the Evil God’s skull, so Lide was reluctant to take that step unless absolutely necessary.
The cow bone undead also sensed something was amiss, its short tail no longer wagging, instead standing alert, but the biting in its mouth did not pause for a second.
The cow felt its body growing stronger after chewing this strange skull, which made it very happy.
And as the seals shattered more and more, the inscriptions on the cow bone undead’s body also became numerous and increasingly dense.
At this moment, the cow bone undead had become a skeleton cow emanating faint blue light, possessing an indescribable presence.
Who would have thought a cow would become the key to breaking a Divine seal…
Snap~
With a crisp sound echoing, Lide’s expression changed as the last Sealing Rune was ingested by the cow bone undead, as he had no time to react, an indescribable terrifying power erupted from the Divine skull.
Gray energy gathered on the horn of the Divine skull, then the horn shattered the space of the Land of Bone-Burying, which Lide had reinforced time and again.
It was like a Forbidden Curse compressed a thousand times over and suddenly exploded, with an energy of a volcanic eruption not one ten-thousandth of this power.
In the instant that space shattered, an emanation of Extreme Evil from the torn space surged out–like mountains collapsing and immense tidal waves rolling back to the sky.
It was filled with a darkness and brutality enough to make a Transcendent kneel.
Then, with a hiss–a hand with sinister barbs reached directly through the space cracked open by the Divine skull into the Land of Bone-Burying.
The arm was entwined with gray energy capable of obliterating time and space, and seemed to have countless miniature thunder flashes, heralding the arrival of great terror.
At this moment, Lide’s every hair stood on end, every pore on his body warned him.
Danger!!!
Extreme danger!!!

chapters.title: Chapter 386 - Chapter 386: Chapter 388 Evil God Reappears, Ferocious at Dawn (8400 words)
chapters.content:
Chapter 386: Chapter 388 Evil God Reappears, Ferocious at Dawn (8400 words)
No one could describe how formidable the arm, shrouded in gray energy and extending from the shattered space, was at that instant.
It was an arm capable of collapsing the entire space.
It was the ultimate force of this world, it was Divine.
The Land of Bone-Burying seemed to have been struck, beginning to rumble and tremble, the whole plane shuddering.
It was too powerful, merely an arm, yet it had already exceeded the bearing limit of the Rare Level Land of Bone-Burying.
It seemed that this still frail plane would be shattered by that Evil God who crossed countless spaces and planes.
After the incident in the blink of an eye, Lide forcefully suppressed the fear his body felt towards that divine being, his gaze as firm as iron.
He swung his hand fiercely, immediately calling upon all the Power of Death to reinforce the Bone-Burying Plane, forcefully imprisoning that arm in midair.
Simultaneously, the angel wings on the twelve-layered White Bone Altar had slightly lifted–if that Evil God truly descended, he would stop it at all costs!
The Twelve-winged Blazing Angel was the last resort; once torn apart, he would suffer unbearable losses.
Because once that angel emerged, it would definitely uncover everything he had done, and the opponent wouldn’t be fooled as easily as last time.
“New Sun God, I have already sensed the scent of your soul…
Now, kneel and submit, lift my head high above with both hands and present it to me.
I, shall forgive the sins you once committed, and grant you the power of the Ancient Days…
On the day when the Ancient Days again envelop this world, you shall once again obtain eternal life!”
The ancient blasphemous language echoed through the entire Land of Bone-Burying from the shattered space, the Extreme Evil aura emanating from the spatial rift causing even the Cow Bone Undead’s tail to stand up, and the Soul Fire to tremble.
This Evil God felt even more terrifying to the Cow Bone Undead than a Divine Monster.
Lide stared at the space rift that seemed like the Abyss Mouth, as if it could devour the entire Land of Bone-Burying at any moment.
The evil divine pressure of the God of Plague surged in nearly like a reverse storm surge.
Facing the imposing force of a divine being felt a hundred times more terrifying than being stared at by a giant dragon!
Yet, at this moment, after hearing the threatening words of the God of Plague, Lide’s previously vigilant heart suddenly relaxed.
Although he didn’t reduce the force suppressing that ferocious arm, he was no longer acting at all costs, and he put back the angel wings onto the Twelve-winged White Bone Altar.
Feeling Lide’s change, the Ancient Divine Power was extremely displeased, its majesty surging, and at this moment, Lide felt as if he was standing directly in front of the God of Plague, the opponent watching him with a cold gaze.
At this moment, Lide’s chest felt crushed by a mountain, even simple breathing required a great deal of effort.
But the more the opponent acted this way, the more resolute his gaze became.
Eyes slightly narrowing, he lifted his head to stare directly at the shattered space and that vicious arm flickering with myriad miniature thunders, the blasphemous language once learned from Divine Monster slowly uttered from Lide’s mouth.
“Ancient divine being, the Abyss confines your body, the Main Plane obstructs your soul…”
His mouth curled into a cold arc, his gaze deep.
“You can’t really descend, can you?
What a pitiful creature, as a god surviving from ancient times, unable to conquer even a weak plane.
Before the Ancient Days you speak of descend, you’d better stay holed up in your Abyss Plane and continue being a repulsive, filthy rat–get lost!!”
If Withered Bone were here, he definitely would have cheered wildly at Lide’s defiance, for the opponent was a divine being…
The God of Plague, scorned and mocked by Lide’s indifferent tone, was completely enraged.
Roar~
A piercing roar, like the screams of over a hundred thousand people, tore through the space and caused the Land of Bone-Burying to shake even more violently.
“New Sun God! I will burn your soul for one million years! Ten million years!”
However, after the God of Plague’s roar, the sinister, grey, thunder-enshrouded arm suddenly withdrew from the shattered space rift.
Just as Lide had observed, this ancient Evil God could not descend; all before had been mere intimidation.
Seeing this, Lide’s gaze remained cold.
Had the God of Plague been able to descend, he would not have believed that this being, now his sworn enemy, would be wasting time talking.
After all, he had brazenly seized a skull directly from the other’s grasp–a profound, deep-seated hatred, to say the least.
Moreover, the most crucial point was that the other party was a god!
His actions trampling the dignity of a god would cause outrage not just among ancient Evil Gods but even the kindest of divine spirits.
But the God of Plague was exceedingly verbose,
The more words one uses, the more they reveal their weakness–strong beings do not waste words on the weak.
Thus, after the God of Plague had spoken, Lide determined the state of their condition; even if the Land of Bone-Burying was weak, it was anchored to the Main Plane; the opponent managing to send an arm was already an impressive feat.
The saying ‘villains die from talking too much’ indeed never rang false.
Although the God of Plague could not descend, this was far from over.
His skull was still in the Land of Bone-Burying, a price the God of Plague was willing to pay any cost to reclaim.
Crack~
The originally shattered spatial rift explosively burst open after the withdrawal of the God of Plague’s arm.
Though this ancient Evil God could not descend to the Land of Bone-Burying, he used terrifying divine power to forcibly widen the spatial rift made by the divine skull, turning it into a gate 30 blades long and 10 blades high.
The divine pressure intensified, and Lide circulated the Power of Faith throughout his body, and even began burning the Power of Faith to barely withstand the spine-chilling aura.
As the spatial rift widened, an even more shocking scene unfolded.
A sinister, dim light flickered through the portal stabilized by the God of Plague, then a terrifying grey energy collided with the portal, booming like two mountains crashing, shaking heavens and earth.
Inside the Land of Bone-Burying, a storm surged, and the Cow Bone Undead nearby struggled to stand, their expressions panic-stricken.
When the shaking subsided, Lide regained his senses only to discover behind the broken spatial rift, a land covered in skeletons, mountains of swollen, whitish corpses emitting an immensely horrifying aura–the Land of Death.
As he sensed it briefly, his expression changed.
Was that?
The Divine Country of the God of Plague?!
“New Sun God, my Divine Country is now connected to your weak plane through this spatial portal!
You will no longer escape my watch.
When the ancient days descend, I will personally step through this portal, chop off your head, and extract your soul!”
The tone of the God of Plague carried an undeniable fury and the thrill of impending revenge upon Lide.
Obviously, Lide’s series of actions had made him an eternal enemy of this ancient Evil God.
Although he couldn’t personally descend to the Land of Bone-Burying, he could still feel the connection between this plane and Lide.
The blasphemous language grew ever colder.
“Now, let you taste the fear I bring you day and night, you lowly New Sun God…”
Deep in the bottomless abyss, countless planes away, within an unknown interlayer of planes, the God of Plague, lacking both a head and right arm, was forcibly anchoring his Divine Country to the Land of Bone-Burying.
Even though this anchoring was done through a collapsible space tunnel, he believed it sufficient to deal with this not-so-powerful New Sun God.
The head is the main part of a divine body. Although his divine status was sealed within his body, and he regained the power of plague after reassembling his body, the lack of a head meant his power was reduced by at least thirty percent.
This was absolutely not good news for the God of Plague who wished to establish a foothold in the perilous bottomless abyss.
The bottomless abyss is the most evil and chaotic den of sin in this glorious multi-dimensional plane, filled with evil gods far more powerful than the God of Plague, too many to count on both hands.
Regaining his head was the fastest way to restore his power.
“My servants, occupy and devour this plane! Spare no cost!”
His cold words echoed through the dim Divine Country, and then tens of millions, hundreds of millions, even billions of fierce half-ratmen suddenly looked up and roared!
Following the God of Plague’s ruthless command, countless fierce half-ratmen surged out from a space gate 30 blades wide and 10 blades high.
Their vast numbers exploded forth like a gushing well.
Hiss~
The exclusive hiss of rats became the dominant melody within the Land of Bone-Burying.
Fear spread.
Lide’s expression drastically changed upon seeing this scene.
These fierce half-ratmen, cultivated by the divine power of the God of Plague, represented his power. Once this plane was occupied by the fierce half-ratmen, the power of the God of Plague would begin to erode the Land of Bone-Burying.
By then, the Land of Bone-Burying might no longer belong to him.
Lide instantly felt a tremendous threat, being targeted by a divine being who had survived from the ancient days. It wasn’t a pleasant feeling.
It was like a venomous snake constantly watching him from the shadows.
He felt a strong sense of crisis.
Bloodline shackles, activate.
Watching the fierce half-ratmen surging from the space gate, Lide instantly activated the Ancestor Bloodline.
A terrifying power surged and erupted within his body.
Crack~
Terrifying Silver Dragon Lightning illuminated the murky Land of Bone-Burying.
Four Circle Magic–Thunder God Descent.
Lide stood far from the space gate, alone blocking the fractured spatial rift.
Those fierce half-ratmen that rushed out from the space gate were instantly infused with lightning, their divine servant bodies exploding on impact.
Crack~ Blood and limbs sprayed everywhere, the bone-white ground stained blood-red, the scene unbearably gory and brutal.
In just a few minutes, the ground was significantly elevated by the corpses of the half-ratmen, and the speed of death’s corruption could not keep up with the rate of annihilation caused by the thunder.
In front of the space gate now, true mountains of corpses were piled high.
Lide saw this and thought for a moment, and the ground of white bones collapsed, swallowing the towering mountain of corpses into the underground, and the surface became smooth once again.
This place was truly the Land of Death made from piles of corpses.
“The New Sun God… so weak and pathetic, not even a servant in its own divine country…”
The God of Plague looked upon the scene of the Fierce Half-Ratmen sending themselves to their deaths with utter indifference.
Each Fierce Half-Ratman contained a trace of his power, although weak, the more Fierce Half-Ratmen that died, the heavier his imprint and traces in the opposing plane.
Just wait until the day of the Ancient Evil God’s descent, no matter where the opponent was, he would be able to find him.
Moments later, Lide also realized the intentions of this Ancient Evil God, yet a cold curve formed on his lips.
Thinking of bursting me? You better have the skills!
He slightly manipulated the Power of Death, the gray energy that dispersed into the air due to the Half-Ratmen’s death was instantly devoured, and then on the attribute panel of the Land of Bone-Burying, the amount of the Power of Death slowly started to increase.
Lide’s eyes immediately lit up at this sight.
He suddenly realized, being hunted by the God of Plague seemed to not be such a bad thing…
What was the Land of Bone-Burying most lacking right now? — The Power of Death.
Even if the underworld was desperately killing Cave Spiders, the Power of Death they obtained still couldn’t meet his needs.
Therefore, the Land of Bone-Burying had not yet been upgraded to a Rare level, it hadn’t unlocked the feature to recruit Frost Giants, nor activated the usage of the Twelve-Layer White Bone Altar.
But now the situation seemed to have subtly changed.
Aren’t these Fierce Half-Ratmen a living source of the Power of Death??
And they were delivered right to his doorstep… This Ancient Evil God was simply his lucky star, delivering whatever he was lacking.
The deaths of these Fierce Half-Ratmen in the Land of Bone-Burying, weren’t they all turning into nutrients for its growth??
And most of the Fierce Half-Ratmen were of levels 7 or 8, with level 10s being not uncommon, the Power of Death gained from slaughtering these creatures was much faster than breeding pigs.
After this shift in thought, Lide felt instantly better, and looking at the Space Gate afterwards, it seemed more pleasing than ever.
“Legend says that within five steps of the poison snake, there must be an antidote; could I be this evil god’s nemesis?”
Feeling joyful, Lide got excited, but after about ten minutes, the incessant flow of Fierce Half-Ratmen still made him frown.
Although he could hunt these Half-Ratmen to obtain the Power of Death, there was a significant issue–he couldn’t possibly waste all his time here.
If he were to be dragged here by the God of Plague using Fierce Half-Ratmen, then obtaining even a large amount of the Power of Death would be unacceptable.
The crisis of the Ancient days was about to arrive, he had to quickly advance to Transcendent, and also prepare the subordinate forces of Dawn City for the future.
Now, the Divine Skull that had its seal broken was suppressed by him next to the White Bone Altar using the force of space, the opportunity for a breakthrough was right in front of him.
Lide’s gaze slowly calmed down, and after pondering for a moment, he slightly sensed and realized that the Space Gate’s power could at most allow level 10 Fierce Half-Elves through for a short time, his mind made a decision.
He directly opened the Space Gate, and using the scent of Bloodline found Emi and Harrison.
The two were immediately astonished when they saw the scene inside the Land of Bone-Burying through the Space Gate.
The aura of the evil god was too fierce and terrifying.
It simply wasn’t from this mortal world.
“Harrison, Emi, immediately mobilize the army to come! We have big trouble…” Lide then quickly and briefly explained the current situation to the two.
After listening, Emi and Harrison exchanged looks, both feeling a chill in their hearts.
They never expected the Ancient Evil God’s head would cause so much trouble.
“Yes! Your Majesty!!”
Given the urgency of the situation, they dared not delay and immediately began making arrangements.
Once Lide’s orders were issued, Dawn City sprang into action.
Having just endured the fierce battle at Risier City, the alertness of the Dawn City army had not yet waned. With military orders received, they began to assemble at a stunning speed.
Reservists hit the streets to replace patrol teams, and various weapons and equipment began to be brought out of the warehouses again.
Crossbows, alchemy bombs, powerful bows, high-level armor… Weapons and equipment were nearly endless.
The human armies of the King’s Blade, the Bloodline of the Holy Light Bloodline, and even the Giant Army and Beastmen began to gather.
This war was different from the one at Risier City. Dawn City was facing an invasion by an Ancient Evil God, and the war was happening in the Land of Bone-Burying. Their only enemy was the Ancient Evil God, and there was no need to worry about discovery by the outside world.
Therefore, Lide directly mobilized all military forces.
The command center of the army immediately began drafting battle orders, while the construction department began researching how to build defensive fortifications to counter a significant number of Fierce Half-Ratmen.
It had to be said that Dawn City had changed dramatically from the past; even facing such a sudden urgent battle situation still remained calm and composed. All departments collaborated effectively and, in less than ten minutes, had determined how to deal with the assault of the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
Construction department, army, City Hall, even logistics, weapons factories, etc. all were activated, everything revolving around the defense battle in the Land of Bone-Burying.
One Sunshine Hour, two Sunshine Hours… By the time the fifth Sunshine Hour arrived, Lide felt his spiritual power was like water in a sponge, almost squeezed dry.
He had continuously used Four Circle Magic for five Sunshine Hours, staunchly withstanding the desperate charge of the Fierce Half-Ratmen, providing enough time for the Dawn City army to react.
And the Power of Death on his attribute panel had soared by 200,000, breaking through the 800,000 mark, gaining 40,000 Power of Death per hour.
This terrifying rate of increase made Lide’s eyelids twitch.
If it weren’t for prolonged use of Thunder God Descent which nearly drained his spirit, he might have actually wished to defend a while longer; the feeling of watching the numbers on the attribute panel jump rapidly was just too great.
“Your Majesty, the defensive offense is ready!!”
Just then, Harrison’s voice reached from behind.
Upon hearing the voice, Lide slightly turned his head and after scanning around, he immediately relaxed.
Although it had been only a short five Sunshine Hours, under the mobilization of the entire city’s power in Dawn City, the Land of Bone-Burying had already undergone an earth-shattering transformation.
A ring of gigantic rock fortresses surrounding the Space Gate as the center had formed an encircling defense with no blind spots.
Lide had used the Land of Bone-Burying to open a Space Gate, allowing giants to go to the mountains to mine stone, and then the Blood Clan Spellcasters used magic to smooth the rough edges of the boulders and directly built the walls.
And this wall, which took five Sunshine Hours to construct, was a total of 30 blades high and 5 blades wide.
Thousands of giants, along with over two thousand Blood Clan members, eight thousand Magic Language Bats, and tens of thousands of troops together had miraculously constructed this rock fortress.
It was absolutely stunning.
Most importantly, the circular rock fortress had a radius of 100 blades, completely enclosing the Space Gate.
After the construction department’s design, the 30-blade high rock fortress had nine levels from bottom to top, each allowing archers to stand and shoot through the designated shooting holes in the rock wall.
And at the very top of the rock fortress stood a circle of burly, high-level armored warriors.
Their weapons were gleaming sharp at the moment.
Even in the outer area of the rock fortress, thirty wooden towers that were 10 blades taller than the rock wall had been temporarily but sturdily built, all occupied by Blood Clan Spellcasters.
And a large area behind the rock fortress, aside from logistics personnel, was filled with archers who had already aimed their shooting angles, ready to launch their attacks.
The explosion had already surrounded the Space Gate in a 360-degree, no-dead-angle embrace, ensuring that the Fierce Half-Ratmen would encounter the most brutal shooting as soon as they appeared.
In just a few Sunshine Hours, this magnificent military fortress had risen from the ground, an awe-inspiring sight for anyone.
At the moment of looming danger, Dawn City demonstrated a trembling potential.
This was a city that could truly be called great, a city personally crafted by Lide.
The plan to build a defensive area to kill the Half-Ratmen was selected from 20 different defensive plans and was highly suited to the current army of Dawn City.
The strong bows and sharp arrows were an advantage of Dawn City–an advantage the Fierce Half-Ratmen didn’t have–so maximizing this advantage was undoubtedly the focus of this design.
Clearly, this hedgehog-like fortification had achieved that.
“Be ready, I’m going to withdraw now…”
Lide’s voice carried an inevitable tone of fatigue.
Though the terrifying regenerative ability of the Ancestor Bloodline kept his body in perfect condition, casting spells still consumed spiritual power.
Maintaining the Thunder God Descent, a Four Circle Magic, every second for five consecutive Sunshine Hours demanded a horrifying amount of spiritual power.
Even a Transcendent wouldn’t withstand such continuous drain over five Sunshine Hours; sustaining Four Circle Magic for even one Sunshine Hour was the stuff of myth.
Had he not undergone Divine Baptism and possessed a noble bloodline, he would have been drained dry.
“Your Majesty, we await your command!”
Harrison and Emi stood together on a wooden tower outside the stone city walls, with solemn expressions.
Lide took a deep breath, gazed through the raging thunder and lightning at the Mad Rat Divine Country across the Space Gate, and vanished on the spot with a whoosh.
Without the obstruction of the thunder, the Fierce Half-Ratmen surged out of the Space Gate like a tidal wave.
The scene was enough to make anyone with claustrophobia shiver in horror.
And the Meat-winged Half-rat followed, soaring into the sky at that moment.
The servants of the divine had been released.
But just a second before the Fierce Half-Ratmen could spread.
“Fire!”
A furious shout resulted in the Fierce Half-Ratmen suffering the most severe assault.
Whistling arrows shot out en masse like locusts.
The crossbows, enhanced and innovated by the Half-Elves, were nothing the bodily engrouped Half-Ratmen could withstand.
Blood splattered in that moment, and the bodies of the Fierce Half-Rat people, riddled like hedgehogs, instantaneously carpeted the ground.
In just a dozen breaths, a stack of corpses had piled up several blades high in front of the Space Gate.
This sight was terrifying.
In contrast, the Fierce Half-Ratmen couldn’t do anything against the mountain-like city wall.
The wall, five blades thick, was sturdier than steel. As the Fierce Half-Ratmen charged with a bloodthirsty vigor, they tragically found that they couldn’t match the towering height of such walls.
