May 4th, late at night, a full day had passed since the unsealing of the Evil God’s skull.
Lide had the Cow Bone Undead dig an underground room in the most corner of the Land of Bone-Burying, where he now sat cross-legged at the depth of 100 blades.
Before him lay the skull of the God of Plague.
And on the surface of the Land of Bone-Burying, everything was ready.
To face the upcoming battle, to cope with the possibly furious God of Plague.
Lide had the Space Gate of the Land of Bone-Burying opened in the old quarter of Dawn Square, a wide area that became a military blockade.
Tens of thousands of troops and countless military paraphernalia were neatly arranged, ready to provide support at any moment.
The citizens of Dawn City were also mobilized once again, beginning to produce supplies for the army and provide various logistical supports.
It was the first time all residents faced the war unfolding within Dawn City.
Rather than concealing, the propaganda department opened an observation platform not far from Dawn Square, allowing the citizens to see the inside of the war.
Although they couldn’t see the mountains of corpses and seas of blood inside the defense ring, the roars of the fierce half-ratmen had become a source of nightmares for all residents during this period.
But the war, rather than causing fear among the residents, increased their enthusiasm to repel the foreign enemy; no one could merely stand by and watch.
Underground in the Land of Bone-Burying at this time.
“What a strong power…”
After briefly feeling the skull with a horn in front of him, Lide’s deep eyes shone with a glint.
After a deep breath, he slowly pressed his right hand on the crown of the Divine skull.
But at that instant, a thunderous boom –
As if a thunderous explosion burst in his mind, Lide’s ears even buzzed, and everything around him at that moment became muffled.
Then a sound like the wail of tens of thousands of people before their death arose, the sharp piercing noise also like the mud demons of the deepest abyss screaming tragically towards the sky, spreading terror.
An indescribable dreadful aura pervaded Lide’s heart.
His entire soul felt as if it would be devoured or torn apart by the roaring sound from within the Divine skull.
Then, before Lide could regain his senses, along with that sharp roar, a terrifying force erupted like a volcanic explosion, daunting and chilling.
It was an Extreme Evil power preserved from ancient times, the terror of the Divine power exclusive to the Ancient Evil God.
Fear permeated deep within the Hundred Blade Depths and even spread directly to the surface; the soldiers above felt their hair standing on end, then looked down with horror on their faces,
They felt as if an abyssal giant beast was lurking beneath their feet, possibly ready to devour their souls at any moment.
Lide’s face also turned extremely grim, an indescribable force instantly surged into his body, tearing and torturing his soul.
The dread-inducing Extreme Evil power completely exceeded his expectations; he had anticipated confronting an impact, but never imagined the force would strike so ferociously and overwhelmingly.
“Is this the real power of a Divine??”
Although Lide’s face was somewhat pale, his eyes remained steadfast.
This was just the appetizer.
After withstanding the first wave of impact, he immediately mobilized the byeonglent Power of Faith to envelop his body.
His own power was nearly useless before the Divine power; only the Power of Faith could confront it head-on.
Now, the devouring finally began.
The power erupting from the skull of the God of Plague surged like the ocean waves rolling up towering waters,
flooding into every inch of Lide’s flesh.
The overwhelming force, despite being shielded by the Power of Faith, still caused him an uncontrollable throbbing pain.
But this power was not something Lide wanted to accommodate; his spiritual power began to spread out, his spiritual tendrils slowly delving into the skull of the God of Plague.
After facing the endless pressure of divine beings, he sensed a gray, mercurial substance circulating within his flesh and bones–the essence of Divine Power, a power even more fundamental than Divine Power itself.
This essence constituted the core of beings beyond Level 30 and was their origin.
If magic was the fundamental element of this world, then Divine Power represented the ultimate element of this world.
It was an indescribable substance, possessing a power beyond anything mortals could imagine.
Each drop contained the power to tear through space.
Lide had inadvertently absorbed the divine essence within the remnants of a deity during his transformation in the blood pool and had closely observed the divine essence using his spiritual power afterward.
However, the divine essence from the deity’s remains, whose master had died millions of years ago, was gentle and easily accessible.
But the divine essence within the skull of the Plague God was the complete opposite–resistant and violent. The Plague God’s divine essence did not welcome his exploration.
Moreover, even a slight sense of its presence made Lide feel the cruelty and bloodthirstiness, a power of the Ancient Evil God that could turn any mortal who merely touched it into its servant.
This was a dark divine essence, representing the ultimate evil of this world.
At this moment, every pore in Lide’s body was warning him, suggesting that continuing to contact it would lead to unimaginable dangers.
Advanced Danger Perception.
Lide had never thought that divine essences could have attributes; though he sensed the hidden danger, he did not hesitate and continued his exploration.
After slightly closing his eyes, he attempted to touch the divine essence with the Power of Faith, but the pure white Power of Faith melted instantly like a burnt sponge upon nearing the gray divine essence.
Irreconcilable, the two were incompatible.
This discovery caused a slight frown in Lide.
The Power of Faith was his greatest reliance; if it proved ineffective, then his next steps could not proceed.
Inhaling deeply, he continued his research.
After a lengthy exploration, Lide somewhat realized that the Plague God’s divine essence was too dark, and the powers of light were fundamentally unable to affect it…
But obtaining divine essence was not as difficult as he had imagined. Only dark and evil lives could bear such power–the condition was being able to withstand it.
This realization gave Lide’s expression a subtle nuance.
Had he not been protected by the powers of the Light Attribute when he first touched the Plague God’s skull, he would have been turned into the opponent’s servant by the evil power.
But to truly devour the contained divine essence, one had to be a creature of dark life, a paradoxical method that would leave any being aware of this skull helpless.
Yet this perfectly suited Lide’s characteristics.
With the power of the Holy Light yet being a pure creature of dark life.
In this world, there was only one, and no others.
Whether the Bloodline was suitable for bearing the Plague God’s divine essence could be inferred from the Plague God wanting to use Emi as its body for resurrection.
But now there was another issue Lide had to face–the overwhelming and robust power of the divine essence.
With his Level 19 power attempting to absorb and digest the divine essence that only those above Level 30 could touch, the difficulty was imaginable.
It was even harder than the proverbial snake swallowing an elephant.
Reflecting on this, Lide steadied the tumult within his heart, his eyes resolute and unshakeable as mountains.
Since he had already sat here and made up his mind, he would not leave without breaking through the transcendent limits.
The disaster of bygone days was right before his eyes; others had no way back, and neither did he.
Dawn City must have transcendent forces, and Divine Monster Asreaga was nowhere to be found; he had to stand up and take on this heavy responsibility.
Tens of thousands were looking forward to him.
Looking forward to their master continuing to rule over them, leading them towards glory.
After steadying his emotions, Lide closed his eyes and carefully touched the divine essence within the skull of the Plague God, then began guiding the gray divine essence into his body.
But the divine essence was as viscous as mercury, and even with his terrifying spiritual power as the guide, it was still incredibly difficult.
Lide couldn’t estimate how much time he had consumed, but finally, the first strand of divine essence fused directly into his body from his palm.
Thunder rolled,
and as the divine essence entered his body, a deafening boom resonated in Lide’s ears, as if a Forbidden Curse had exploded inside him, each of his blood vessels swelling from the terrifying force.
Endless power erupted like a collapsing mountain.
Even the tsunamis stirred up by Level 18 fury were not as exaggerated.
At that moment, Lide’s blood vessels simply couldn’t withstand the force washing through them and burst one by one.
His expression twisted unimaginably.
It was too terrifying.
Like countless knives tearing through his body, severing his blood vessels alive.
Agonizing pain surged like a tide, engulfing his nerves and even threatening to strangle his sanity and destroy his will.
The pain of hundreds of blood vessels bursting was indescribable and beyond any words.
It was the pinnacle of suffering that could exist in this world.
Even Lide’s resolute mind showed bulging veins at this moment.
His handsome face twisted with ferocity.
But the strand of divine essence didn’t stop after bursting his blood vessels; it continued as a terrifying energy, destroying all the flesh it passed through.
Even as Lide desperately absorbed the force, it was still too much.
The power of a deity was beyond any mortal’s imagination.
Even though his bloodline was the noble Bloodline of the Ancestor and had undergone a divine baptism, it couldn’t hold up.
Once, he had undergone a divine baptism subtly and while unconscious; he couldn’t comprehend the pain he had encountered.
But now, he watched helplessly, undergoing the Divine Calamity in an absolutely sober state.
The pain was simply indescribable.
It felt like a century had passed before Lide could barely absorb the power emanating from that strand of divinity.
However, the energy required to repair the damage caused by that strand of divinity to his body was even greater than the amount he had absorbed, resulting in a deficit.
It was extremely brutal.
Although he had suffered, the anticipated positive outcome did not materialize; that recent strand of divinity was not even one hundredth of a drop, while there were at least hundreds of drops of divinity within this skull.
This meant that to absorb all this divinity, Lide would have to endure the excruciating pain of his veins bursting all over his body ten thousand times…
Terrifying.
Despite recognizing the difficulty, the pain-hardened Lide’s gaze remained resolute–his mindset, forged over nearly four years, was incomprehensible to outsiders.
Biting his teeth, he continued.
His spiritual power continued to guide, and the second strand of divinity began to surge into his body, instantly expanding a hundredfold and transforming into new strength.
Undoubtedly, Lide, who had just managed to heal his body with his horrific recovery abilities, was once again subjected to catastrophic destruction.
If any outsider saw this scene, they would be dumbfounded. No one had ever dared to channel divinity into their body so brutally and arrogantly. The first time might have been out of ignorance, but the second time the same way?
Even just a minute strand of divinity, which was, after all, the power of a god, was enough to grievously injure a transcendent being.
For an ordinary person, a hundred lives wouldn’t suffice.
Lide’s confidence in doing this came from his exaggerated recovery speed.
As the Ancestor of the Bloodline, once he activated his Bloodline, he could regenerate his body infinitely as long as he still had strength within.
In other words, unless his body was instantly blown to pieces with no remains, even if his heart exploded, he could still recover.
This nearly immortal recovery ability was precisely the confidence that allowed Lide to directly and violently attempt to devour divinity.
But it was like the magic he refined; he too was dancing on the edge of a knife because any mishandling could indeed result in his being blown apart by an unstoppable force.
Yet, fearless, as the king of courting death, there was nothing he dared not do.
The third strand, the fourth strand, the fifth strand…
Lide was like a suicide machine, crazily channeling divinity from the divine skull into his body, and that power kept destroying his body time after time.
Thus, amidst countless destructions and rebuilds, Lide’s body started to become tougher, no longer shattering upon contact with divinity as it did initially; his absorption rate for divinity also began to increase slowly.
And after hundreds of trials, Lide deciphered the proper method amidst the agony.
As long as he didn’t exceed a certain threshold, his body could absorb divinity in the fastest, most perfect way, and the degree of destruction he sustained was within his tolerable range.
At this moment, Lide was treating himself like a robot in an experiment.
But even so, that bone-deep pain still made him long for death.
This was the most grueling torture in the human world and the most mentally tormenting experience.
But all this was voluntarily endured by him.
This was a challenge for Lide.
Had it been forced upon him, it might have been better since there was no choice.
But actively choosing to endure this pain gave a completely different sensation.
Even his body began to resist this act, the muscles in his arms and body starting to tremble involuntarily.
But with an unstoppable, almost death-defying attitude, Lide’s deep eyes remained unbreakable.
Iron will.
A hundred times, a thousand times…
No one knew how much time had passed.
In this dark, underground palace constructed from hundreds of blades of white bones.
He repeated the singular action time and again, channeling divinity into his body, each time suffering the excruciating pain of his entire body being torn apart inch by inch.
He never believed in pie falling from the sky; his current state was earned through bloody battles, just as in the past, and it would continue to be so in the future.
To grow stronger and even more powerful.
The obsession in his heart fueled all his actions.
At this point, no one could imagine how much suffering Lide had undergone, but even more despairing was the uncertainty of how long this suffering would last.
But as long as he hadn’t reached the strength he desired, he wouldn’t stop, because Lide knew this power was not enough, still not enough…
When a boy learns to take responsibility, he is called a man; when a man can carry the fate of tens of thousands on his shoulders, he can be called a leader.
To be born a king is to bear the weight of the crown.

May 15th.
In the dim underground space, where time seemed blurred.
Lide had long forgotten the existence of time, guiding divinity into his body, then frantically absorbing that power amidst being torn apart by his veins and muscles.
This mechanical action was the cruelest punishment in the world, a challenge to anyone’s psyche.
But effort was often met with reward. After an extended period, Lide’s bones slowly began to take on the unique aura of divinity, his blood becoming thicker and more vigorous.
But anomalies often come unexpectedly. After Lide’s body absorbed divine power reaching the first critical point, the whoosh–a description-defying evil aura surfaced in his mind.
A pair of eyes, hollow, emitting an aura of death, those gray eyes.
Tyrannical, murderous, dark, bloodstained… no negative adjective is sufficient to describe the meaning contained in those eyes.
Lide’s body trembled as he saw them, those cold, chilling eyes staring at him.
As if they were right in front of him, he could even see the other’s chest slightly rise and fall with each breath.
The God of Plague.
Those were the eyes of the God of Plague, the Ancient Evil God, watching him from an abyss beyond countless planes.
“You lowly New Sun God… How dare you steal my power?!!”
The blasphemous language of the ancients carried an chilling coldness.
But Lide wasn’t terribly shocked at the moment. From the beginning, he had already expected that this Ancient Evil God would notice after the power within its skull had started to wane.
“I will destroy everything you hold dear…
Burn your soul…
Slaughter your believers…”
The God of Plague was utterly enraged, this time more intensely than ever.
Someone dared to plunder his power right in front of him!!!
He was the ruler of ancient times, a mighty Divine spirit who controlled the power of plague. Before the dawn of the ancient times, someone had dared to provoke him again and again.
This damned blasphemer!
Murderous intent surged in an instant.
In the unknown space within the bottomless abyss, rumbling~
Endless thunder flashed wildly, making several nearby planes wobble due to the fury of the God of Plague.
The power of a Divine spirit was too vast.
The grey energy emitted by the God of Plague spread like a tide from his Divine Country, instantly engulfing several nearby planes and stripping millions of lives of their life force.
This was the wrath of a Divine spirit, more terrifying than the scythe of the Death God.
Everything Lide had done was agitating the sensitive nerves of this Ancient Evil God. If it weren’t for the will of the main plane holding him back, he would have descended to glory without hesitation.
“Destruction!! Death!!!”
Words screamed out by tens of thousands resounded through the sky within the God of Plague’s Divine Country.
The God of Plague’s location was the core of his Divine Country, a bizarre mountain towering like clouds, from which the sounds echoed instantly throughout the entire Plague God Country.
Then, the already frenzied Meat-winged Half-ratmen, irrespective of the costs, rushed toward the already opened Space Gate, running at speeds more than twice their previous pace.
And the chain reaction that ensued…
The defensive ring within the Land of Bone-Burying faced even more ferocious attacks.
The once solid defenses were, in an instant, on the verge of collapse.
The previous Space Gate had spewed out Meat-winged Half-ratmen like water from an ordinary tap, now it was like a high-pressure water cannon.
Although the outlet was the same size, wasn’t the number more than double?
Countless Meat-winged Half-ratmen roared and screamed, carrying boundless fury as they rushed toward the defensive ring.
Their master was commanding them, urging them to kill all enemies, destroy all adversaries, devour everything opposing them.
Slaughter was the only thought in these Meat-winged Half-ratmen’s minds at this moment.
And the sudden increase in Meat-winged Half-ratmen immediately caught the guards, who had been accustomed to the previous numbers, off guard.
There were too many… so densely packed they were beyond description.
Those who avoided the arrows scurried to the base of the rock walls and began to climb up furiously.
Without regard for the cost.
One or two were easy to deal with, fifty were manageable, but when the number climbing the city wall reached hundreds, the once solid defense lines immediately became passive.
Even strong crossbows needed to go through the process of drawing and shooting, there was always a brief pause.
And it was in these brief gaps that these completely crazed Meat-winged Half-ratmen would surge forward.
The 18th level Beastman King Kapp was now back in the Land of Bone-Burying commanding the war; today was his shift.
Seeing the suddenly multiplied numbers of Meat-winged Half-ratmen below, he immediately roared orders.
“Fire!! Archers, shoot at full speed!
Spellcasters, use spells for support immediately!
Warriors on the walls, get ready!”
The roaring command resonated through the Land of Bone-Burying after the spellcasters transmitted it.
Upon receiving the orders, the 30 wooden towers outside the defense ring immediately began to cast spells.
Within moments, whoosh whoosh whoosh~ dozens of fireballs, Thunder Bursts, and lightning balls began to brutally smash into the defense ring.
Boom boom~
Magic exploded, sending flames skyward.
Scores of Meat-winged Half-ratmen were directly devoured by ruthless magic.
Scorched and shattered corpses instantly covered the ground.
But this could not entirely stop the Meat-winged Half-ratmen who had fallen into madness; instead, it further spurred their ferocity.
Like strings of sugar-coated haws, they reached the base of the rock walls and started climbing.
There were too many, it was impossible to snipe them all in time.
“Warriors on the walls, draw your swords and fight!! Don’t let those filthy rats climb up the wall!!”
Beastman King Kapp’s raging voice made the expressions of the warriors at the top of the defense ring stern.
One by one, they fiercely stared at the Fierce Half-Ratmen below who had not been killed by arrows, just waiting for them to show their heads so they could deliver a striking blow.
And after Kapp’s voice fell, the first batch of Fierce Half-Ratmen surged up and faced off against the guard warriors in close combat.
Just as a hideous Fierce Half-Ratman showed its face, a sharp spearhead plunged into its right eye.
With a squelch~ blood splattered, the Fierce Half-Ratman had no time to make a second move and died instantly, falling from the towering city wall and splattering the ground with blood.
But after the death of the first Fierce Half-Ratman, the second one took advantage of this brief moment and furiously sprung forward, climbing straight onto the city wall.
The Beastman Warrior had just withdrawn his long spear and hadn’t reacted yet.
The towering Fierce Half-Ratman, ferocious to the extreme, cared for nothing as it lunged at the Beastman Warrior.
With a thud~ the huge impact made it impossible for the Beastman Warrior to react in time, and he was knocked down, then through the helmet, he saw a foul-smelling big mouth open with sharp tusks like bayonets, tearing directly towards his neck.
Just as the Beastman Warrior thought he was about to die from a neck bite, there was a click~ a crisp sound, then from the corner of his eye, he saw two sharp tusks snap off and fly away.
High-level armor.
At this moment, the Beastman Warrior remembered that his equipment was no longer the beast skins from the barren wilderness but the high-level gear forged under the great Kachar.
The surprise of surviving death instantly filled him with strength.
The killing intent surged, and he directly drew a blade, flashing with a cold gleam, from his thigh; then, with his left hand, he grabbed the head of the Fierce Half-Ratman and swung the blade with his right hand.
With a squelch~
The hot, foul blood splashed over the face of the Beastman Warrior.
Throat cut.
The once incredibly ferocious Fierce Half-Ratman immediately collapsed on the ground, its body cooling rapidly as it lost blood.
All of this happened in the blink of an eye, and by the time the Beastman Warrior stood up again, no more than 5 seconds had passed.
Roar~
The Beastman Warrior let out a furious roar, immediately took up his long spear and covered the gap, continuing to hunt those damned rats.
The fierceness of the Fierce Half-Ratmen was undeniable, and although the guarding warriors were nearly unstoppable, still relying on sheer numbers, more than 500 Fierce Half-Ratmen had breached the city wall in less than a minute.
Like a needle against a spike, only the elite forces of Dawn City were assigned to guard the defense ring at this critical time.
Each warrior wore high-level armor and wielded unstoppable long swords.
These Fierce Half-Ratmen, once they surged onto the city wall, often found themselves facing a steel wall tougher than the 30-blade rock city wall.
What was originally a disoriented army plunged into chaos; after Kapp’s several troop deployments, the overall situation was immediately stabilized.
But this did not make the God of Plague cease. Instead, it grew even angrier, again ordering all the Fierce Half-Ratmen to attack the Land of Bone-Burying.
This was not because the God of Plague was powerless but because this Evil God was waiting. When enough Fierce Half-Ratmen had died, he could use the power of these corpses as an anchor to once again widen the Space Gate, enhancing the force he could send to attack the Land of Bone-Burying.
The country of the God of Plague was an ancient divine country left from the ancient times, several times larger than the southern provinces, with countless Half-Ratmen slaves; to his eyes, such losses were insignificant.
Meanwhile, Lide was still devouring Divine Power.
As he said while devouring the head of the God of Plague, trying to use the divine power inside the Evil God’s head to ascend within the Land of Bone-Burying was like playing with fire,
Because he would always be under the scrutiny of the God of Plague.
But there was no choice, he had to take this risky action.
“Death…”
“Destruction…”
“Devastation…”
“Massacre…”
The deep and powerful blasphemous language of the ancient Evil Gods murmured like a demon, endlessly echoing around Lide’s ears, as if trying to invade his soul.
As more of the Evil God’s Divine Power was absorbed by Lide’s divine body, the influence of the God of Plague on him grew stronger.
The opponent was constantly using blasphemous language to disturb his mind, aiming to shatter his will and resistance.
Unavoidable.
Lide was using the power of the God of Plague to break into a higher realm, and even using it to undergo a transformation of life.
But unlike the divine remnants in the blood pool, the Divine Power in the Evil God’s head had an owner, and the God of Plague could still slightly influence and manipulate this power across countless planes.
This made Lide’s actions fraught with danger, more thrilling than dancing on the edge of a knife.
It was a gamble, a gamble staking the future.
Until the very end, no one could determine the outcome, but Lide had always believed that the Goddess of Luck was favoring him.
As more Divine Power was absorbed and devoured by Lide, he could clearly feel a deeper layer of power in his bloodline transforming.
This transformation was not a simple change but an evolution towards a more perfect version of life.
His blood became more vigorous under the power of divinity, his muscles more elastic and resilient, his bones sturdier, and his soul stronger…
Changes were happening everywhere; his entire being was evolving and transforming from the most basic cellular level.
And with time, Lide could handle more and more Divine Power…
In a corner of the Land of Bone-Burying, the ground where Lide secluded himself now had a very solid small fortress built around it, all guarded by level 10 and above high-level professionals.
From the surface, it seemed there were no problems, but only upon approaching could one faintly sense from the core deep underground, an indescribable aura brewing.
Evil mixed with fresh vitality.
Weird and terrifying.
All the warriors guarding there knew they were protecting their sovereign, guarding the great being who gave them glory and rebirth.
And guarding hope.

May 30th, Land of Bone-Burying.
After nearly a month of frantic work, thousands of giants worked tirelessly in shifts, joined by Blood Clan Spellcasters, human Spellcasters, as well as physically strong Beastmen and Centaurs. Magic Language Bats and finally, the support from the Space Gate at the Land of Bone-Burying.
Emi and Lide reported that the second ring of the two-ring defense system at the Land of Bone-Burying was finally complete.
The first ring of the defense system was centered around the Space Gate, within a radius of 100 blades, a circular defense wall 30 blades high and 5 blades wide was constructed.
The second defense ring was also centered around the Space Gate, within a radius of 500 blades, an 80-blade-high wall that was 12 blades wide was constructed.
Unlike the first ring wall, which was rushed and quite crude in all aspects, the second ring defense system involved the full force of Dawn City and was very well-built.
Not only was there an Alchemy Tower 100 blades high established every 10 blades behind the high wall, but the number of shooting holes reserved in the wall was also so numerous that it could give someone with trypophobia a tingling scalp instantly.
The second defense ring wall combined the advantages of the first ring wall, similarly constructed in a tiered, circular fashion, layer upon layer upwards.
The 80-blade-high wall had a total of 12 layers, each layer having more than 5000 shooting ports.
Along with a defense area 12 blades wide at the very top of the wall, it was truly a nightmare for any enemy.
The wall’s top was entirely manned by Centaurs, whose extensive territories could accommodate these powerful warriors.
While carrying large swords, the Centaurs also handled modified strong two-bladed longbows.
As natural archers, even the most heavily armored Centaur warriors were experts with the bow, no less skilled than humans known for their excellent marksmanship; this was a racial talent that could not be erased.
Thus, assigning Centaurs to guard the highest layer of the wall was an exceptionally good choice.
Even if fierce Half-Ratmen broke through the dense crossbow fire, the Centaurs could instantly pick up the giant battle-axes beside them and deliver a devastating high chop.
This defense was truly watertight.
In the sky, squads made up of Magic Language Bats and Dawn Bats suppressed the Meat-winged Bats.
Dawn City’s main aerial forces had an overwhelming advantage against fierce Half-Ratmen, since they were armored.
Especially the Dawn Bats, whose bellies were equipped with anti-air crossbows that even warriors’ thick shields couldn’t withstand, let alone the small-bodied Meat-winged Half-ratmen.
With layered security, Dawn City turned the terrifying dangers of an Evil God’s invasion into something akin to a tower defense game.
The Space Gate leading to the God of Plague was where monsters spawned in this game, and the towers were the towering alchemy towers behind the walls.
Then, the warriors on the walls, the crossbows, siege crossbows, and other tools were used to hunt down monsters.
Lide was the weak point in the entire tower defense game, should these monsters break through the front defense points and attack the weak spot, the game would ultimately end…
Particularly interesting was that in this tower defense game, slaying monsters also granted great benefits–each slain Fierce Half-Ratman signified an increase in the Power of Death within the Land of Bone-Burying.
Moreover, once the Power of Death increased, it unlocked new buildings and troops–the twelve-layer White Bone Altar and the Frost Giant Dragon.
Unfortunately, Shadow High Priest Emi and Level 18 Beastman King Kapp were unaware of the existence of a tower defense game, and they tried their best to ensure that Lide was not threatened by the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
The attacks from the God of Plague became even more frenzied due to Lide’s accelerated progress in devouring divinity.
On June 10, there was still no movement from Lide beneath the bones.
However, a sudden turn of events on this day sent a chill through Grote, the Child of the North overseeing the battle.
A malevolently dark, evil aura spread out from the Divine Country of the God of Plague, and the space rift that was originally 30 blades long gradually widened to 40 blades, and its height increased from 10 blades to 15 blades.
Merely extending it a short distance, but the entire first ring defense line immediately suffered immense pressure.
Countless Fierce Half-Ratmen, like swarms of locusts, roared frantically as they surged out from the Space Gate; the wooden towers behind the high walls crazily supported with magic, barely alleviating the pressure brought by the tide-like surge of Fierce Half-Ratmen.
Bodies of Fierce Half-Ratmen piled up layer by layer on the ground,
Grote, who had gained the privileges for the Land of Bone-Burying, had already lost count of how many times he had made the ground sink today, but it still wasn’t enough; piles of bodies seven to eight blades high often formed in less than ten minutes.
The scene was both crazy and heart-quivering.
At this moment, the Land of Bone-Burying was truly a hellish existence, where death was as simple as breathing or blinking.
And over a month of slaughter, this land had long transformed into a Land of Corruption where Lide cultivated the Death Flower.
Skeletons had been tainted with blood, and flesh had turned into mud.
It was foreseeable that after the war, this piece of corrupted land would be much higher-grade than those previously made in breeding farms for pigs.
It was fortunate that the Land of Bone-Burying had devoured the souls of the Fierce Half-Ratmen after their death; otherwise, powerful ghosts would certainly have emerged.
Time flowed to June 20, maintaining the slaughter in the Land of Bone-Burying.
The Fierce Half-Ratmen never slowed down their assault, as if the daily casualties in the tens of thousands didn’t exist at all; no one knew how many Half-Ratmen the God of Plague had enslaved.
Lide, situated on the bone-strewn ground, remained silent.
But the warriors stationed nearby increasingly felt a terrifying aura brewing beneath, as if an ancient giant dragon was breaking out of its shell.
The terrifying aura from below spread uncontrolled.
And as Lide’s aura altered, the Fierce Half-Ratmen became even more ferocious.
The God of Plague’s response was–once again widening the Space Gate.
The width of 40 blades was further pulled by the God of Plague to 50 blades, and the height also broke through to 20 blades.
The Space Gate, which originally only accommodated Level 10 Fierce Half-Ratmen, started allowing Level 11 and Level 12 Fierce Half-Ratmen to pass through.
This subjected the already immensely pressured defense walls to an unimaginable impact.
The first ring defense line was about to be breached.

Chapter 390: Chapter 392 (Anti-theft chapter, do not subscribe) Level 23 – Lide Transcendent, Astounding Strategy
This a piracy protection chapter. The main text will replace this chapter in 20 minutes, after which everyone can refresh to continue reading without interruption. The piracy protection chapter charges for 10,000 words, and the upcoming update will be 10,600 words, automatic definitions won’t disadvantage anyone.
—-
—-
—-
—-
Lide sensed something profound.
He could break through now, yes, the power within his body had reached the Extraordinary Level.
At will, he could halt the devouring process this instant and step into the transcendent, turning into an ultimate combatant with immense strength.
But Lide didn’t stop immediately; he felt that he was far from reaching his limit, that his body could still hold more Divine Calamity.
He wanted to become stronger, transcendent was not yet enough…
After settling his mind, Lide chose to continue the devouring.
A person who can endure pain is praiseworthy, but one who knows the pain and willingly endures it deserves admiration.
At this moment, Lide’s actions undoubtedly surpassed what most people understood as the limit.
With every Divine Calamity entering his body, he experienced veins bursting, muscles tearing, and bones shattering… This was the ultimate pain, in the face of which so-called punishments were not worth mentioning.
Yet even so, he remained unshakably firm.
His steely resolve had improved more than tenfold since he first stepped into Glory.
That naive young man had finally grown up.
Now, Lide was truly qualified to be called a leader, a king who had borne the weight of a crown.
“Continue…”
“What doesn’t kill you, ultimately makes you stronger…”
“God of Plague, is this all you’re capable of?”
Lide’s laughter was somewhat hoarse, his complexion ghastly pale but his gaze still unshakable.
In the bottomless abyss beyond the endless planes, the God of Plague, an ancient sovereign on an altar built of bones and gemstones, fell into a rare silence upon sensing Lide’s condition.
This was the first time in countless years that he had seen a New Sun God with such a formidable will.
He knew how terrifying his Divine Calamity was, and the excruciating pain it brought upon the bearer.
He also knew that Lide was resisting solely through his will.
But his blasphemous language’s erosion and temptation were useless, and the slavery characteristic of his evil divinity was ineffective.
At this moment, the mood of this ancient Evil God was extremely complicated.
For the first time, he felt a degree of admiration for a New Sun God he deeply loathed.
Yet, at the same time, his urge to kill grew stronger.
Such a New Sun God must not be allowed to grow.
The world ruled by the ancient days didn’t need such a power.
But the most significant issue was, the God of Plague felt somewhat helpless against this New Sun God.
While he couldn’t descend to the Main Plane, and the other’s will was so firm…
Snapping back to reality, the God of Plague suddenly became enraged. As a sovereign who once ruled countless planes, what right did a new god have to flaunt power before him?
“Hmph, foolish New Sun God! Everything you do today will become the source of your tragedy!!”
After his words fell, he spoke no more.
However, in Lide’s mind, the force of the blasphemous language was tenfold stronger than before.
Endless horror wanted to erode his soul, to devour everything about him.
Darkness rose again.
“This is more like it… Hahaha…”
A nearly crazed smile appeared on Lide’s face as his spiritual power began to recklessly spread into the head of the God of Plague, his gaze arrogant and wild.
“Then, devour everything you possess…”
“Hunter? Prey? Who can truly determine that…”
“Ancient God? Hahaha…”
—-
—-
—-
On July 30, something that terrified the defense forces of the Land of Bone-Burying occurred.
The Space Gate was slowly widening.
This was the fifth expansion.
Emi, Kapp, and Groot, who were supervising the battle from the top of the Alchemy Tower, glanced at each other and saw the gravity in each other’s eyes.
Although they had anticipated this expansion a month ago, when the moment truly arrived, it still left everyone breathless.
The Space Gate widened from 60 blades slowly by an additional 10 blades, reaching 70 blades.
The height, which had not changed before, expanded from 20 blades to 30 blades.
At the moment of the Space Gate’s expansion, all the warriors could clearly sense the terrifying aura from the Divine Country on the other side, an ancient air more horrifying than the evil of demons.
Countless Half-rat men, under this influence, became fierce, powerful, and bloodthirsty.
It was as if the gods were watching over them.
Many resilient warriors inevitably felt a chill run down their spines.
Once the widened Space Gate stabilized.
The scene everyone least wanted to witness occurred.
Level 15.
A Fierce Half-Ratman measuring 2.5 blades in height with sharp tusks and claws as terrifying as razors, came through the Space Gate.
Its back spines were as sharp as daggers, and the tip of its tail resembled a spear; this Level 15 Fierce Half-Ratman was filled with a brutal and bloody aura.
A pure killing machine.
“Target their Level 15 Fierce Half-Ratmen! Ready the heavy crossbows!”
Ultimately, the Magic Industry Research Institute could not develop the Dragon Hunting Crossbows before the great battle arrived, so the responsibility of killing Level 15 Fierce Half-Ratmen was given to the heavy crossbows.
With the original stock plus the frenzied production over the past half-month, over 1000 heavy crossbows were erected on the Second Circle defense walls.
After the command was issued, the heavy crossbows’ chains creaked, and the bowstrings began to slowly expand…
Producing these heavy crossbows had consumed most of the high-level materials from the weapons factory; the cost of each crossbow could only be described as expensive.
The crossbow bolts for the heavy crossbows were as thick as a wrist and forged from fine gold, capable of piercing through walls.
These formidable weapons were Dawn City’s ultimate tool against the Level 15 Fierce Half-Ratmen.
After the first Level 15 Fierce Half-Ratman appeared, it immediately charged toward the city walls, emitting a chilling, deep roar.
Whee, whee, whee~
All the Centaur archers focused their frantic bow-shooting at the very noticeable Level 15 Fierce Half-Ratman.
But this fierce creature showed no fear, and its thick fur acted much like armor, bouncing off arrows as if they were greased.
Moreover, its sprinting speed was significantly higher than that of regular Fierce Half-Ratmen, making it difficult to lock on. Even direct hits from the sparse flying arrows caused only minimal damage.
What was even more terrifying was that this killing machine seemed unbothered by the colossal city wall in front of it, which stood at 80 blades high and was only possible in this magical world.
Once the Fierce Half-Ratman reached the base of the wall, it began climbing using its hands and feet, its sharp claws hooking into the wall like grappling hooks.
It reached the 30-blade high section with a few jumps, above which was a 10-blade wide Oily Skill area.
However, this Level 15 Fierce Half-Ratman didn’t care at all, its sharp claws piercing through the solid walls, forcefully breaking through the Oily Skill, and rapidly ascending past this zone that had stumped countless fierce half-ratmen.
Once past this area, the Level 15 Fierce Half-Ratman climbed unrestrictedly like a dog off its leash.
Ding ling clang~
Arrows fell like raindrops, furiously shot at the Fierce Half-Ratman, hitting the wall with clear sounds, but its thick, bizarre hair was too resistant, bouncing off the arrows, causing barely any damage.
It’s closer, getting closer!!
It had already sensed the presence of humans, the aroma of food.
The fierce half-ratman’s eyes shone green with flecks of blood-red, and murderous intent almost materialized.
Now was the moment!
Beneath the city wall’s top and beyond the range of ten blades was a solidified area treated with Oily Skill, but this level 15 fierce half-ratman leaped over the area in one bound.
It attacked the city wall like a demon escaping its cage.
Several centaur warriors instinctively raised their great axes in a sweeping motion, but they were no match for the level 15 fierce half-ratman.
Cold light flashed, blood exploded.
The centaurs hadn’t even clearly seen their adversary before they felt a chill on their necks, losing consciousness.
Despite wearing high-level armor, it couldn’t stop the sharp forelimbs of the level 15 fierce half-ratman.
This fierce half-ratman was incredibly agile, attacking the dense cluster of centaurs around it.
Unrestrained, it slaughtered in all directions.
The first level 15 fierce half-ratman emerging from the Space Gate tasted blood.
The danger had become increasingly intense.
But just then, a lightning-fast figure streaked across the sky.
Whoo~
The sharp Blade Wings reflected a dazzling light, and its supersonic terrifying speed didn’t even allow the crowd around to blink.
The level 15 fierce half-ratman saw a flash before its eyes and felt intense pain before it could react, instantly losing consciousness.
Looking back at the city wall, there was only a body that had been slashed across the chest, thudding to the ground.
Castro, clad in Extraordinary Armor, had already vanished from atop the wall, and those meat-winged half-ratmen who had escaped the barrage of arrows exploded instantly.
The scene was nothing short of bloody and horrific.
However, the death of the first level 15 fierce half-ratman was not the end but merely the beginning.
Somewhere in a spatial interlayer of the bottomless abyss–Plague God Country.
Outside the Space Gate connecting to the Land of Bone-Burying, a hundred kilometers’ radius was packed with fierce half-ratmen, their black heads tightly pressed against each other, the quantity beyond calculation, enough to explode the mind of anyone with a fear of crowds.
It was terrifying.
No one knew how many half-ratmen had proliferated in this vast god country during the eons the God of Plague had slumbered.
Now, the most grotesquely fearsome level 15 fierce half-ratmen were gathering near the outer side of the Space Gate, their numbers like locusts, countless.
This was the power the Ancient Evil God had accumulated over millions of years; level 15 was the topmost power in the Main Plane, but in a darker plane like the bottomless abyss, this was not a rare entity.
Only the Transcendent were considered the peak.
“Servants of the New Sun God, I, the ruler of the ancient days, bestow upon you death…”
Blasphemous language that seeped into souls emanated from inside the Space Gate, then echoed like the screech of crows over the Land of Bone-Burying.
Hearing this evil speech, the level 15 fierce half-ratmen within the Plague God Country instantaneously fell into madness, surging like a tide with relentless lust for slaughter towards the Space Gate.
Land of Bone-Burying.
Beastman King Kapp’s mane stood on end at this moment.
The eighty-blade wide Space Gate couldn’t be blocked; in two breaths, he saw over a hundred level 15 fierce half-ratmen stepping out of the Space Gate.
Emi and Grot saw this scene and their expressions turned extremely solemn.
Everyone knew the real test had come.
“Heavy crossbows aim at level 15 and above half-ratmen, attack!!
Everyone else, fire at will!!”
The moment Kapp’s roar rang out, whoosh whoosh~
Tens of thousands of crossbow bolts shot out, over a thousand heavy crossbows triggered, arm-sized bolts were the gaze of the Death God, the sword of the God of Justice.
A level 15 fierce half-ratman that had just stepped out of the Space Gate hadn’t even had the chance to react when suddenly, with a splurt, an arm-thick crossbow bolt went straight through its body, forcibly dragging the half-ratman back to the other side of the Space Gate, and with its powerful piercing force, the sharp bolt went through three fierce half-ratmen before stopping.
Blood pooled everywhere.
Yet the smell of blood plunged the fierce half-ratmen into an even deeper frenzy, surging out from the Space Gate at even greater speed.
Thousands of heavy crossbows fired in unison, killing more than half of the level 15 fierce half-ratmen, but still dozens charged to the base of the city wall, where more level 15s emerged from the space gate.
Cap, having given his orders, abruptly turned to Emi, his tone cold.
“Emi, we need to take the field and suppress them. You are in charge of the battlefield now.”
He then turned his head towards Grote, who was seething with killing intent, “Grote, let’s go.”
“No worries, leave it all to me.”
Emi nodded, not delaying or saying more, as the Shadow High Priest was not suited for direct confrontation. Instead, Cap and Grote, two pure warriors, were the true gods of carnage on the battlefield.
Whoosh~ The power of space activated and the towering figures of Cap and Grote instantly appeared atop the lofty city walls.
Meanwhile, a piercing, strange laughter echoed through the Land of Bone-Burying.
“Ga ga ga, has a monster worthy of the great Lord Withered Bones’ attention finally appeared?”
“Oh, rats? Truly a weak and pathetic evil god, to enslave even filthy rats? Tsk tsk tsk, even beggars would despise such creatures. How ludicrous…”
“The inhabitants of Risier City would not allow me to appear, but now, let these lowly, humble, filthy beings taste the Dragon Breath of Lord Withered Bones…”
“I am the eternal Undead, the Dragon of Destruction from Dawn City! Tremble, weep, for you will turn to ash under the light of Lord Withered Bones…”
Woosh woosh~
From outside the second ring of defense walls, an immense Undead Bone Dragon with a wingspan of 18 blades appeared in the sky.
However, even more attention-grabbing than the Bone Dragon’s imposing aura was its incessant chatter, demeaning the God of Plague before it even attacked…
Withered Bones screeched as it dove from the sky, gray-white energy swirling in its throat, releasing a breath imbued with the scent of death, which instantly spewed forth when it was just over ten blades above the ground.
Zzzt~
Several level 15 fierce half-ratmen below couldn’t dodge in time and were directly hit by the dragon breath.
Those who directly faced the dragon breath ended up as nothing but bone scraps after the breath dissipated.
Hundreds of other fierce half-ratmen also died, as the Death Dragon Breath seemed to strip away time itself, instantly aging and decaying the struck lives.
Whoosh~whoosh~ At this moment, Castro, with his Blade Wings, also dove down beside the Withered Bones. The dense crowd of fierce half-ratmen on the ground were easy targets,
The Blade Wings, like reaping wheat, slaughtered hundreds of fierce half-ratmen in a single dive, all cleanly bisected at the waist.
While these high-level combat forces were terrifying and alleviated some of the pressure on the battlefield,
the distant aid did not quench the immediate thirst. Once the number of level 15 fierce half-ratmen emerging from the space gate exceeded 500, the situation rapidly reversed.
The sharp arrows shot by the centaurs could no longer inflict fatal injuries.
Only the heavy crossbows could target these level 15 fierce half-ratmen, but the heavy crossbows’ shooting flaws were significant, making it incredibly difficult to aim effectively at the charging half-ratmen, often resulting in missed shots.
Thus, accompanied by blood and the unique stench of rats, the first wave of level 15 fierce half-ratmen rushed onto the city walls.
The level advantage made even the solid perfect-level armor ineffective in defense; the claws of the level 15 fierce half-ratmen were sharper than daggers and spears.
Blood exploded.
Although centaur warriors were equally ferocious, the difference in strength prevented them from mounting an effective counter, leading to their rapid slaughter.
After several dozen level 15 fierce half-ratmen climbed onto the city walls, they immediately caused massive chaos.
Chaos led to fewer arrows being shot, and with not enough bow pressure, it gave the fierce half-ratmen gaps to storm up the walls, creating a vicious cycle.
“Alchemy bombs! Bombard!”
Just as the pressure on the city walls increased, Emi’s voice timely echoed.
The ready Magic Language Bats immediately began bombing.
Boom boom boom~
The terrifying explosions occurred, and the haughty aura of the fierce half-ratmen was instantly suppressed.
Limbs flew, and dense fierce half-ratmen turned into stacked corpses.
However, alchemy bombs were not unlimited in number. After five rounds of bombing, they had to reluctantly return for resupply.
And in just a few breaths, the fierce half-ratmen surged forth once more.
At this moment, level 18 Beastman King Kapp ignited with blazing golden energy, like a mythic beastman hero reincarnated, his lion-like mane gently fluttering, his battle blade incomparably sharp.
His figure flickered and disappeared, and in the blink of an eye, he appeared atop a section of the city wall occupied by more than a dozen level 15 fierce half-ratmen.
His long blade unsheathed, his fighting spirit unmatched.
A 15th Level Fierce Half-Ratman paused upon seeing Kapp, but then screeched and pounced ferociously, his claws dripping with fresh blood.
Kapp charged forward, swinging his longsword, creating a sound that nearly tore through the space. The 15th Level Fierce Half-Ratman had no time to react, splurt–blood splattered, split into two by the blade.
It was an overwhelming fight, a Beastman King of the 18th Level against a 15th Level Fierce Half-Ratman.
The other fierce half-ratmen, witnessing this scene, rushed forward in a frenzy, giving Kapp no chance to react.
But, as a member of an Upper Race and a former Beastman King, Kapp’s vast combat experience and strength were not something these servants could match.
Blood battled from all sides, his battle blade like a dragon unleashed from its sheath.
One slash per enemy, and within moments only a pile of bodies remained.
Clad in Extraordinary Armor, wielding an Extraordinary Battle Blade, plus the agility provided by spatial force’s instant teleportation, a single man and blade upheld half of the city wall.
To the centaurs below Level 10, the 15th Level Fierce Half-Ratmen were an unsolvable threat, but before Kapp the Beastman King, they were as garbage.
On another front, Grot, once known as the Child of the North, had enhanced his strength significantly after transforming into the Crimson Hunter, a secretive profession within the Bloodline race.
His giant sword, unparalleled in sharpness, swung through the air, leaving behind severed limbs and fragments. The 15th Level Fierce Half-Ratman was ferocious, but under the strikes of this even more ferocious slaughterer, they were mere paper, easily torn apart.
Emi, atop the alchemy tower outside the Second Circle defense walls, witnessed hundreds of 15th Level Fierce Half-Ratmen storming the walls. Although the current residents barely held on, he perceived the threat within.
He abruptly turned to the Blood Clan Spellcaster–a Blood Mage beside him.
“Let all Blood Mages unleash the Bloody Storm.”
Emi’s gaze turned cold, let the slaughter intensify.
Holy Light Bloodline under the Crown’s rule, were we ever weaker than anyone by half?
“Yes!”
A military order was as formidable as a mountain. Within mere moments, Emi’s order reached the alchemy tower behind the Second Circle defense walls.
Over a thousand Blood Mages began casting simultaneously.
Bloody Storm (Consumes 50% of the caster’s blood to summon 100 intangible blood bats composed of magic power and blood to attack enemies. The bats grow, reproduce, and divide as they devour blood, lasting until the blood energy is exhausted).
This was the ultimate move of the Blood Mages.
Unfortunately, apart from a long time ago when it had been used to bomb Black Wind Tribe’s twenty thousand centaurs at Dwarf Hillocks with alchemy bombs, a systematic casting by Blood Mages hadn’t been seen again.
But now, the scene of those slaughter bats sweeping through heaven and earth was about to reemerge.
After about a dozen seconds, an ear-piercing screech of bats rose.
Then, all the warriors within the Land of Bone-Burying saw blood-colored bats flying out from atop the hundreds of blade-high alchemy towers, each bat only the size of a palm but carrying fangs and claws that sent shivers down the spine.
The Slaughter Bats had no physical form, composed purely of blood and magic energy, born solely for killing.
Whoosh–whoosh–
A thousand Blood Mages, each release a hundred blood bats, totaling 100,000.
Within the 500 blade radius of the Second Circle defense walls, 100,000 slaughter bats became a blood-colored glow in the dark space.
The numerous Fierce Half-Ratmen faced immediate, brutal attacks. Some of the Fierce Half-Ratmen opened their mouths to try and bite these blood bats, but the bats simply passed through their teeth and burrowed into their bodies.
Then a chilling scene ensued–after swallowing the blood bats, the Fierce Half-Ratmen’s bodies began to twitch wildly, emitting cries like those of an animal in its death throes.
Then, in just a few breaths, their skin visibly whitened at an observable rate, their fur deflated limply.
Splurt–
Moments later, the blood bat that had entered through the heart of the Fierce Half-Ratman burst out, its size now doubled, and its body darker in hue.
Devouring for growth, the most horrifying trait of the Slaughter Bats.
The Fierce Half-Ratmen relied on their sharp fangs, claws, and the lethal bacteria and plagues they carried for attacking, but these attacks were all futile against the intangible Slaughter Bats.
The Claw would pass right through the body of the Slaughter Bats, and the plagues and bacteria only enhanced the bats’ lethal power.
The, seemingly infinite, Fierce Half-Ratmen were suddenly contained.
This was the Land of Death, where the ground, soaked in months of spilled blood, had permeated the bones; these intangible bats, sustained by blood and magic energy, could devour blood to grow.
Some of the Slaughter Bats dived into the ground, sucking up blood from bodies not yet desiccated.
In the Land of Bone-Burying, it takes a whole day to decompose a body into bones, and these undecomposed bodies immediately became nourishment for the Slaughter Bats.
In less than three minutes, whoosh–thousands of blood bats with a wingspan reaching 3 to 5 blades burst forth from the ground, their presence now incredibly terrifying and potent.
The slaughter bats immediately turned into even more ferocious killing machines, battling fiercely with the fearless fierce half-ratmen.
And the exaggerated number of Level 15 fierce half-ratmen were immediately suppressed by the slaughter bats.
Although the Level 15 fierce half-ratmen had a faint gray energy on their claws that could hurt the bodies of the slaughter bats each time they swung,
due to the feeding of ordinary fierce half-ratmen, the number of slaughter bats had surged to 300,000 within a short period of time, completely covering the sky.
Even though the Level 15 fierce half-ratmen killed wildly, the number of bats was even greater.
And it was the slaughter bats, driven only by a desire for destruction, that made these Level 15 fierce half-ratmen experience the terror of the human wave strategy.
With the appearance of the slaughter bats, a chain reaction started; heavy-duty crossbows also began to play their part, continuously assassinating Level 15 fierce half-ratmen.
Emi, seeing this scene, couldn’t hide his surprise. He hadn’t expected the ultimate move of the Blood Mage to be so effective against the fierce half-ratmen.
The scene, which was on the verge of collapse, was immediately stabilized.
One Sunshine Hour later, the situation began to change drastically, even causing the surrounding warriors to stare in disbelief.
The endless stream of fierce half-ratmen became fodder for the slaughter bats, their numbers increasing and becoming stronger with more fierce half-ratmen.
Eventually, tens of thousands of slaughter bats with a wingspan of 5 blades appeared, and the newly emerged thousands of Level 15 fierce half-ratmen from the Space Gate were wiped out with the coordination of the slaughter bats and heavy-duty crossbows.
In the end, it wasn’t even necessary to draw bows and shoot arrows; just the hundreds of thousands of slaughter bats alone had overwhelmed the fierce half-ratmen.
The final situation turned into Dawn City’s forces pressing down on the servants of the God of Plague in battle.
Kapp then sheathed his sword and returned to Emi’s side, both exchanging glances with subtle expressions, neither had expected such an outcome.
“Kapp, the slaughter bats have already succeeded in their mission; now, we just need to prevent any accidents.”
Kapp looked at the scene where fierce half-ratmen were devoured as soon as they emerged from the Space Gate and nodded slightly, feeling sentimental.
“The race of His Majesty, the Holy Light Bloodline’s power, is truly shocking.”
Emi’s mouth twitched; he hadn’t anticipated the Bloody Storm to be so terrifying, and the strength of the Bloodline had quietly changed his previous views.
“Without the vast number of ordinary fierce half-ratmen and the uncountable corpses underground, it wouldn’t have been possible to sustain such a blood-colored army. Under normal circumstances, such a situation would be very rare.”
“But having said that, there’s indeed a huge potential in the Holy Light Bloodline that could still be explored.”
This terrifying crisis was overcome in such an unexpected way.
Yet, at this time, Lide had still not awakened.
No one knew his condition underground, and everyone could only sense the aura underground growing stronger.
—-
—-
—-
August 16th, the Space Gate underwent its sixth expansion, but the now established slaughter bat swarm was nearly invincible; even the emergence of Level 16 fierce half-ratmen was swallowed by the slaughter bats.
—-
—-
—-
August 30th, the Space Gate was expanded again, and Level 17 fierce half-ratmen appeared from the gate which could cut through hundreds of blades, although it caused some ripples, it eventually returned to calm.
—-
—-
—-
September 10th, four months had passed since Lide’s retreat, and it seemed he had completely disappeared.
The area in Land of Bone-Burying guarded by fortresses, the underground aura was gradually calming down,
and many times, it was already impossible to sense any traces from the ground.
Today, the God of Plague expanded the Space Gate for the eighth time.
After the expansion, which reached 110 blades, Level 18 fierce half-ratmen appeared from the Space Gate.
This time, the battle was not as easy as before.
Even with the support of hundreds of thousands of slaughter bats, the Level 18 fierce half-ratmen still made it to the city walls.
This time, it resulted in the deaths of 3,000 Centaur Warriors, making the scene extremely bloody.
More than 300 Level 18 Fierce Half-Ratmen mixed with a large number of Levels 17, 16, 15 were all slaughtered, which even left the Beastman King Kapp feeling completely exhausted.
Deep scratches appeared on his Extraordinary Armor.
The greater crisis was not this time, but the next.
The second defensive city wall, which was originally thought to be as steady as Mount Tai after the release of the Crimson Hunters, once again faced a huge crisis.
Because, if the ninth Space Gate expansion were to happen, it would definitely bring forth Level 19 Fierce Half-Ratmen.
Level 18 Fierce Half-Ratmen had already been so difficult, what would happen if a batch of over a hundred Level 19 Fierce Half-Ratmen suddenly emerged?
No one could imagine.
Time passed by slowly, and the high echelons of Dawn City grew increasingly uneasy.
The last incident completely disheartened them.
Five days after the eighth expansion of the Space Gate, on September 15th, the Space Gate seemed to have hit the pause button, not a single Fierce Half-Ratman appeared.
This seemed to alleviate the pressure, but everyone was immensely worried.
Because the Crimson Hunters required fresh blood to sustain themselves, without the Fierce Half-Ratmen as a source of food, hundreds of thousands of Crimson Hunters simply could not continue to exist.
In the end, Emi, driven by desperation, ordered these Crimson Hunters to start cannibalizing each other, then the overall number of Crimson Hunters rapidly decreased, visible to the naked eye.
Even so, in no more than three days, this hard-raised Blood-colored Army would completely vanish.
On September 20th, a high military meeting quietly convened at Dawn Square in Dawn City.
They did not meet within the Land of Bone-Burying for fear of being eavesdropped on by the God of Plague.
As the Space Gate of the Land of Bone-Burying had already solidified at Dawn Square, everyone could reach the battlefield at a moment’s notice should any mishap occur.
Beastman King Kapp of level 18, Grot the Child of the North at level 17, Frey the second generation Bloodline at level 15, and Stanley from Green City at level 16 were all present,
along with the Dwarf Forging Master from the Weapon Factory–Valen,
the Goblin Chief from the Alchemy Factory–Moer,
and the President of Dawn Academy–Horn Rieser; these important figures all attended the military meeting.
Shadow High Priest Emi presided.
16-level Bronze One-eyed Giant Koso along with 15-level Castro, and 19-level Withered Bone also attended.
The core agenda of the whole military meeting was–how to handle the ninth Space Gate expansion.
“Although the invasion of Fierce Half-Ratmen has ceased these past few days, everyone should know that this is merely the God of Plague’s tactic to gain time.
It is also to eliminate our Crimson Hunters, although I have already ordered the farms to slaughter pigs to feed the Crimson Hunters, the number has reduced to only one percent of what it was a few days ago, insufficient to sustain a war.”
Emi’s tone was very grave.
“The Space Gate has been expanded by the God of Plague eight times, the next expansion could occur at any moment.
And as His Majesty has not yet awoken, we still need to continue to guard, to buy enough time for His Majesty.”
Emi’s tone carried an unshakeable determination, and all those involved in the discussion wore solemn expressions.
The crisis was imminent; everyone sensed it, felt it.
But they had no way out, nor could they possibly retreat.
His Majesty was right behind them, even if they were all to perish, it was a sacrifice they were willing to make.
“If the next time the Space Gate expands further, along with the diminished effect of the Crimson Hunters, once Level 19 Fierce Half-Ratmen appear, even if there are only 100 of them, augmented by Level 18, 17, 16, and 15 Fierce Half-Ratmen.
We will be unable to cope.”
A harsh reality faced everyone–the enemy of Dawn City was who?–the God of Plague, an Ancient God who had survived from antiquity.
Moreover, the enemy had been recuperating for several months in the Abyss.
The power held in its hands, whether high-end or low-end, completely outclassed Dawn City.
This was undeniable by anyone.
The power of the two was simply not of the same dimension.
Dawn City’s greatest advantage lay in the fact that the Main Plane did not allow overly powerful forces to descend.
But now, the Space Gate in the Land of Bone-Burying had become a weapon in the hands of the God of Plague.
Although the ancient Evil God could not descend himself, his servants could easily attack Dawn City.
No one knew exactly how many Half-rat men this ancient Evil God had enslaved, and although tens of millions of Fierce Half-rat men had died in the Land of Bone-Burying over the past few months, there was still no sign that the enemy was stopping.
Moreover, a combat power, esteemed as top-tier Level 15 across the entire Glory Main Plane, seemed ordinary like gravel before the God of Plague, who could easily dispatch hundreds, even thousands at a time.
Clearly, the power possessed by the God of Plague exceeded their imagination’s limits.
For Dawn City to counter such an existence, they only had the option to utilize their formidable industrial system, there was no other way.
“Is the Alchemy Bomb feasible?”
Goblin Chief Moer, the old goblin whose face had been disfigured, slowly spoke up in the current situation, devoid of his usual extravagant expressions.
Because their opponent was a god.
A goblin facing a god… It was a scene he could not even dream of.
“No, Alchemy Bombs, although powerful, can’t block the enemy indefinitely…”
Emi was the first to give a negative answer; Alchemy Bombs could stop the opponents temporarily, but definitely not for long. How many Alchemy Bombs would it take to eliminate Level 19 Fierce Half-rat men with the Power of Faith?
“But it’s also a method, Moer, choose a location, bury the Alchemy Bombs first, and detonate them when the Fierce Half-rat men emerge. Can you do it?”
“That’s no problem, our latest Alchemy Bombs can be totally controlled,” Moer confidently replied.
“Besides this, the Magic Industry Research Institute’s Dragon Hunting Crossbows need to be produced urgently, we need to manufacture all the heavy-duty crossbows.”
“Also, we need…” Just as Emi was issuing orders in quick succession, suddenly a figure appeared beside them.
A voice filled with certainty and confidence rang out.
“No, no need anymore.”
Everyone simultaneously turned their heads, and upon seeing who the person was, uncontrollable smiles appeared on their faces.
“Your Highness!!!”
The originally tense and even somber atmosphere underwent a huge reversal as soon as Lide appeared.
Although no one knew if Lide had made a breakthrough, the moment he appeared, everyone felt like they had regained their backbone.
The previous low spirit was wiped clean, and morale instantly soared to its peak.
Nothing calmed the heart more before a great battle than the return of the commander.
Some people are natural leaders.
And Lide was undeniably the master of this city, the supreme ruler of everyone.
His every move affected everyone.
“Your Highness, have you made a breakthrough?”
Hearing Emi’s question, everyone perked up their ears.
Just as Lide was about to respond, he suddenly sensed a strong aura of darkness permeating the air.
Turning his head towards the Land of Bone-Burying, a cold curve formed at his lips.
The Space Gate was undergoing disturbances at that moment, with the God of Plague expanding the Space Gate for the ninth time, and this time, his aura was more tyrannical than any previous instances.
“You all have done well recently; I can sense everything inside the Land of Bone-Burying.”
“I came out this time because that Evil God wants to conquer the Land of Bone-Burying in one swoop.”
“Next, we’re facing a war unlike any other…”
“As for making a breakthrough, perhaps I’ve obtained something… beyond your imagination.”
His words ended, and Lide took out a horn that flickered with thunder light, his deep eyes carrying an arrogance no one could fathom.
“I’ve stolen the Divine Position of that Evil God!”
A statement that shocked everyone into speechlessness, all stared wide-eyed and agape at Lide.
Their eyes full of disbelief.
Stealing the Divine Position of the God of Plague???

chapters.title: Chapter 391 - Chapter 391: Chapter 393 Post-Battle Bounty, The Peculiar Divine Artifact (8000 words)
chapters.content:
Chapter 391: Chapter 393 Post-Battle Bounty, The Peculiar Divine Artifact (8000 words)
P.S. I have a modest goal this month–I want our monthly ticket rankings to break into the top 100… cough cough, even though this goal seems a tad unambitious, I would be quite satisfied if we achieved it. If anyone still has some monthly tickets, please quietly cast a few votes. I clasp my hands together in gratitude.
—-
The Space Gate, reinforced with the Divine Power by the God of Plague, was absolutely indestructible in simple terms.
Under normal circumstances, Lide wouldn’t have been able to destroy it.
But clearly, he was not in a normal state at the time.
Because…
Land of Bone-Burying (Undead Plane)
Level: Rare (Next level: Rare, upgrade requires 1,000,000 Power of Death)
Power of Death: 343,253,902
…
Yes, 340 million Power of Death.
God only knows how thrilled he was when he saw this on the attribute panel.
As soon as he saw the Power of Death on his attribute panel, he immediately devised a plan to pull the rug out from under them.
The fierce Half-Ratmen had been pouring out of the Space Gate non-stop for over five months during the war.
Moreover, the fierce Half-Ratmen were mostly Level 8 or 9, with countless at Level 10.
The Power of Death provided by these high-level lives after their demise was more than ten times that of the pigs in a breeding farm.
The core force of the Land of Bone-Burying is the Power of Death. Possessing such ample Power of Death, Lide finally had the confidence to destroy the space channel connecting the two planes.
The God of Plague was not a fool, either. Before executing his plan, he had already spent a massive amount of Divine Power to fortify the space channel, and this Ancient Evil God could sense that Lide did not possess the power to destroy such a solid space channel.
But reality is always cruel. Despite all the God of Plague’s calculations, he could never factor in Lide’s ultimate trump card: the Power of Death.
However, the cost to destroy the Space Gate was not cheap.
Lide originally had 390 million Power of Death on his attribute panel, meaning that it took a full 50 million Power of Death to shatter the Space Gate.
Spending 50 million Power of Death for a Divine Artifact, Lide felt like he had struck it rich to the point of getting a cerebral hemorrhage.
But on the other hand, one could imagine how much the God of Plague had invested.
Yet, the huge plans of this Ancient ruler ultimately came to naught.
Interestingly, it could be said that the God of Plague’s actions had fattened up Lide.
If it weren’t for the opponent constantly sending fierce Half-Ratmen to attack the Land of Bone-Burying, he would not have been able to accumulate over a hundred million Power of Death.
If the God of Plague knew this cruel reality, who knows what he would think; perhaps even spitting out another mouthful of blood could not express the hatred in his heart.
At this moment, within the Land of Bone-Burying, the Divine Artifact–the Crystal Ball exuding a Death Aura–initially opened with Chaos and the Eye of Death, had now quietly closed.
Although the aura it emitted was still too horrific to articulate, it clearly lost its target and seemed somewhat sluggish.
The God of Plague was able to open the Space Gate because of the sudden burst of power from that skull tore space apart, and only after the two corresponded did he anchor the spatial coordinates.
At this moment, the divine essence within that skull had already been devoured by Lide. Now, it had turned into a dried specimen, devoid of any lingering power.
The core of its power–the horn wreathed in arcs of electricity–had become a weapon in Lide’s hands.
Thus, without any internal support, the God of Plague naturally lost its anchor to the Land of Bone-Burying, separated by countless dimensional planes.
Lide had previously felt a great danger, but, at this moment, he sensed it no longer.
The warriors from Dawn City below, upon witnessing this scene, had expressions that were quite a spectacle to behold.
Originally, they thought that with the help of Fierce Half-Ratmen and the Divine Artifact, the God of Plague had made its appearance within the Land of Bone-Burying and a desperate battle was imminent–with many ready to face death in combat.
But in the end, almost comically, they did not face a life and death struggle against the Divine, and now, it seemed Lide had even seized the enemy’s treasured artifact.
The feeling was like ascending from Hell to Heaven.
With this, the incident triggered by the battle of Risier City could be considered tentatively concluded.
Of course, this conclusion meant that the former ruler of yesteryears temporarily could not find Lide. If indeed he managed to discover the whereabouts of Dawn City once more, then the consequences…
“Your Highness, how should we dispose of this Divine Artifact?”
Upon seeing that the situation was under control, Emi spread his bat wings and flew up to Lide’s side, his expression oddly fixated on the gray crystal ball connected by multitude of gray fine lines in the sky.
He had once obtained a portion of the God of Plague’s power and naturally knew the terrifying power contained within this artifact.
But he had not anticipated that it would fall into their hands in such a manner.
If the God of Plague were still present, even if they had obtained it, they could do nothing against the artifact since the enemy had already imprinted it with a spiritual mark.
But now, with the God of Plague lost in an unfathomable abyss, far from the Main Plane, and with the protection of dual forces from the Main Plane and the Land of Bone-Burying blocking the sensing from the other side, the artifact was effectively left without an owner.
It could be said at this moment, the artifact lay on the chopping board like meat, ready for disposal.
Yet Lide did not rush to respond. After carefully sensing the power within the artifact, a slowly blossoming smile appeared on his face.
He had patiently allowed the God of Plague to accumulate its power, and it wasn’t solely for this artifact.
He sought much more.
“Emi, do you sense it?”
Hm? Startled, Emi looked at Lide with confusion, “Your Highness, what do you mean?”
“Sense it with your heart.”
Following Lide’s guidance, Emi immediately focused his attention on the crystal ball, and after a moment, his face revealed an uncontainable surge of elation.
“Your Highness, the divine essence… this, this artifact actually contains such enormous divine essence!!”
His tone was extremely excited, his voice becoming shrill, as Emi struggled to put his overwhelming feelings into words.
Divine essence, he sensed within the crystal ball an essence akin to a tidal wave.
He knew the God of Plague’s artifact required divine essence to control, but the amount transferred was beyond his expectation.
With the collapse of the Space Gate, the Ancient Evil God could no longer sense even its Divine Artifact, so that essence was beyond its control.
Now, the crystal ball, infused with terrifying power, not only became Lide’s possession, but the rich divine essence within it also became his spoils of victory.
Moreover, an important point was that this divine essence was very easy to manipulate, a convenience incomparable to the essence Lide had painstakingly drawn out bit by bit from the God of Plague’s skull.
“Yes, this contains the divine essence of the God of Plague.
Divine Artifacts are not so easily controlled; the power required is immense. That Ancient Evil God spared no expense in its attack against us.
“But now, all this is ours,” Lide said, his smile vibrant as a brilliant starry sky. The strategy just implemented was simple, but the rewards were extraordinarily rich.
After a brief pause, he cast a meaningful glance at Emi.
“Get ready.”
Huh? Emi blinked in confusion at Lide’s gaze but before she could respond, Lide had already flown straight toward the crystal ball.
Even without anyone in control, a Divine Artifact is still a Divine Artifact, its emitted power enough to instill fear in the most resolute of warriors.
Especially the Eye of Chaos and Death within the crystal ball. Though it had closed, the aura it emitted was still filled with darkness and savagery, and one could feel their thoughts being invaded just by drawing a little closer.
That was a higher level of power, not something that could be withstood by sheer will alone.
Lide’s eyes were cold as he stepped closer to the crystal ball.
And sensing the threat, the crystal ball began to emit a grey energy, attempting to repel Lide.
But Lide ignored it, his power surging, rising with an aura filled with darkness.
With a slight wave of the horn in his hand that was wreathed in electrical arcs, a pulse of power nearly identical to that of the God of Plague emanated outward.
The crystal ball, without a master to guide it, immediately sensed the incredibly familiar aura and its resistance began to wane.
Lide seized the moment, his energy growing increasingly terrifying, forcefully dispelling the Artifact’s last thoughts of resistance.
And hundreds of thin grey energy tendrils connecting the Artifact suddenly injected into the crystal ball under Lide’s pressure, then the scene returned to calm.
The tentacle-like energy tendrils disappeared, leaving only the crystal ball suspended in the air.
Lide’s face remained stoic, the opposition was merely a lamb to the slaughter, and all he had to consider was how to consume them.
Right hand turning into a palm, he slowly approached the crystal ball and then, using the origin power obtained from devouring the Evil God’s head, reached out to touch the fearsomely powered crystal ball.
Feeling an outsider drawing near, the crystal ball instinctively repelled, but hindered by the absence of its master’s commands, it could only gradually allow Lide to draw closer.
Whew–the last gap was crossed, Lide’s palm pressed directly against the crystal ball, a cold touch transmitted through,
