After unlocking the shackles of the body, the Golden Ancestor Bloodline will be activated, all attributes increase by 5000% upon activation, and gains the Undying Body trait,
Undying Body: The body will have no vital points, even if the head is chopped off it can still consume Bloodline Power to regrow and recover, current number of times it can recover from fatal damage–5 times, can consume internal blood to maintain this state for a long period.)
Racial Skills: Transform into a bat, bloodsucking recovery.
Passive Skills: Dual Casting, Extraordinary Strength, Extraordinary Physique, Extraordinary Agility, Extraordinary Magic Affinity, Extraordinary Magic Control
Blood Clan Exclusive Magic, can grow:
Blood Control (Extreme)
Bloodsucking Recovery (Perfect)
Bloody Scream (Perfect)
Crimson Mist (Perfect)
Terror’s Arrival (Extreme): Emits the Dignity of Dark Life, enemies will be tested for will every 10 seconds, those whose will is below the threshold will fall into boundless fear, can be actively turned off.
After Lide checked his attribute panel, his blood surged; these attributes had become almost unsolvable in strength.
Moreover, many skills had changed, granting him even more enhancement.
First was the Extraordinary Crimson Power, this powerful passive skill now included the trait of reducing attributes with negative states.
As long as an attack hits the enemy, they would be enveloped in negative states, each able to reduce 10% of attributes, and could stack up to 7 times, reducing up to 70% at most.
Apart from calling this skill perverse, Lide found no other adjective to describe it.
Extraordinary Bloody Storm, this skill had not changed much, but instead of consuming fresh blood to summon, it now consumed 50% Bloodline Power.
The slaughter bats he summoned himself now had 50% of his power; at level 23 Extraordinary, 50% of his power could make many shiver.
It had to be said this skill had become even more terrifying, the only downside maybe was that it consumed quite a lot of Bloodline Power.
Extraordinary Shadow Blade surprised Lide the most.
This skill’s original throat-slitting trait had evolved into Absolute Slaughter, with the first attack from leaving the shadows ignoring any defense below Divine-level and dealing true damage.
This could be described as invincible; many Mage-types who relied on Magic Shields and warriors who depended on armor, now this strike could directly ignore defenses, simply incredible.
Lide Kachar’s current strength was such that with a single swing of his sword even a giant dragon could be cleaved in two. Giving him the power to ignore defenses was an effect that could only be described as exaggerated.
However, the only downside, just like the Bloody Storm, was that each use required consuming 50% of his Bloodline Power.
Although Bloodline Power could be restored by devouring fresh blood, the recovery rate was not fast,
thus the level of consumption meant that this skill, like the Bloody Storm, could not be used frequently. Being able to unleash it three to five times in a single battle was already astonishing, and this was on the contingency that there was enough fresh blood for him to devour.
But even so, Lide regarded this skill as a final move in his heart.
A swing of his sword destroyed all directions.
Next came–Extraordinary Slaughter Hand. It could not be denied that this skill was the most helpful and practical for him.
Several of its traits–Combat Awareness, Combat Skills, and Battlefield Sense–had all risen to Legendary,
and Lide could distinctly feel a significant enhancement in his battle-related attributes, a profound sensation that was indescribable.
It was like a duck learning to swim; once you get it, you really get it. What had seemed as difficult as reaching the heavens became surprisingly simple once you understood.
Moreover, the trait he was most concerned with–Danger Perception had also improved to extraordinary,
This trait had saved him from countless dangers and was definitely a core skill.
The last and most significantly changed skill upon becoming extraordinary was Bloodline Shackles.
Releasing the shackles activated the Golden Ancestor Bloodline–increasing all attributes by 5000% and granting the trait of an Undying Body.
Undying Body: The body would have no critical points; even if the head was severed, it could regrow using Bloodline Power, currently able to recover from fatal damage up to 5 times.
Lide didn’t know how to describe these two traits, they were simply overwhelmingly powerful.
With a 5000% boost in attributes, he just wanted to ask, who else could compete??
Moreover, the Undying Body trait was even more exaggerated. Even with a severed head, he could regrow it using Bloodline Power; though currently, it could only recover from fatal damage 5 times, this essentially granted him five extra lives.
For Lide, already immeasurably powerful, this was the ultimate enhancement.
Wanting to kill him had already been hard enough, but to kill him and still have him not die was beyond monstrous–it was super monstrous.
Furthermore, the most critical aspect was, even if his Bloodline Power was exhausted and he was truly killed, he could still resurrect in the blood pool, and this time, the cooldown period for this blood-bath rebirth talent had been reduced from three months to one month.
Simply incredible.
Lide felt that his transformation into the extraordinary might have been too powerful.
Truly, the extraordinary level was incomparable to level 19.
Moreover, the string of passive skills listed behind the attribute panel made his head spin–Extraordinary Strength, Extraordinary Physique, Extraordinary Agility, Extraordinary Magic Affinity, Extraordinary Magic Control.
All these skills were previously at the peak level.
If he remembered correctly, the pinnacle was already the ceiling for passive skills.
He had never heard of a level above the pinnacle that reached extraordinary.
But now, the Golden Bloodline had further enhanced these powerful passive skills, directly breaking through the ceiling, and enhancing his strength even further.
At this moment, the power surging within Lide’s body like volcanic magma reminded him of the extent of his strength.
“Finally reached the extraordinary level…
Compared to the power flowing within my body now, level 19 was simply like an infant.”
It was no exaggeration that now, Lide Kachar killing those previously near invincible extraordinary spiders from the Spider Plane was as easy as slaughtering a dog.
“The extraordinary Spider Queen of the Spider Plane, it’s time to crush them…”
Lide’s eyes were sharp as blades.
He had not forgotten that particular extraordinary spider that had made him lie in the blood pool for several months.
After checking his own attributes again, Lide’s gaze continued downwards.
It was not just himself that had changed, the Dawn Sect had also undergone no small changes during these few months.
Dawn Sect
The God of Dawn–Lide Kachar (Fake God)
Divine Arts: 1. Soul Assimilation
Divine Position: Bloodline, Blood (Activated, 2%, and when reached 100%, you will completely control these two divine positions)
Doctrine: …
Holy Object: …
Number of Temples Owned: 3
Number of Believers: Zealots 27, Devout Believers 16,249, Believers 92,499, General Believers 33,972
Power of Faith: 533,665 points
Current Convertible Profession–Dawn Priest
Dawn Temple Clergy: Holy Maiden–Nicole
Bishop Priest–Emi Kachar
Dawn Priests: 326 people
Temple Knights: 5 people
Lide glanced at the Dawn Sect’s panel and nodded slightly.
The Dawn Sect now owned three temples: one in the old city district, another in the new city district, and one more in the underworld. These temples all strived to spread the Glory of Lide.
The believers hardly required mention; Dawn City now housed 150,000 humans, the shortest of whom had lived in Dawn City for nearly a year, and the longest nearly four years.
Apart from some elderly who were unwilling to change their decades-long faith, most had become followers of the Dawn Sect.
This also marked the first time Lide saw more devoted believers than general believers.
The number of believers had now reached over 90,000, while general believers had decreased to over 30,000.
Clearly, the war at the Land of Bone-Burying had made most of the residents feel a crisis, and when people encountered a crisis, it was easiest for them to indulge in fantasies, hoping for someone else to save them.
Under such circumstances, the Dawn Sect naturally became the place where residents entrusted their faith.
What delighted Lide the most was the faith power of 533,000 points on the panel; this was indeed an unprecedented fortune.
Although it wasn’t as exaggerated as several billion Power of Death, it also gave him the feeling of having savings.
The Power of Faith was a valuable asset, useful for cultivating Dawn Bats, nurturing Dawn Priests, and even for growing various magic plants.
His unnoticed Dawn Priests had already surpassed 300 people, clearly a credit to his Divine Priest Nicole.
After scanning through and confirming everything was in order, Lide closed the sect’s attribute panel, knowing that the sect was continuing on a stable path, unlikely to undergo significant changes.
He slightly retracted his focus and directed his attention to the last panel.
His alternate identity–Lord Ilo.
Following the battle in Risier City, the changes in this alternate identity panel surprised Lide the most.
Alternate Identity– Ilo, Chairman of the Dark Heart
When using the alternate identity in Green City, gain +30 Legend Level, and acquire the titles Dark Myth and Mythical Mentor.
Dark Myth: You have displayed divine dignity in front of countless individuals, and everyone who witnessed this war believes deeply in your power.
Most people in Green City will regard you as a legendary myth, whether they are from Dark Life or the Light Sect, naturally increasing their favorability towards you to respect.
And it comes with the following traits: 1. When facing beings with a Legend Level 10 points below yours, gain the Dignity Effect; enemies will fear you, and their All Attributes will drop by 30%,
2. Have a high probability of deterring Dark Creatures of lower level than you, making them join your cause,
3. Enjoy a revered reputation among Green City’s nobles and various sects, gaining the right to establish temples and preach in Green City.
Mythical Mentor:
You are a mythical figure who has led countless people to transcend and become extraordinary, with a Legend Level +20, and you have gained the following features.
Guidance: Your words have an enlightening effect on lives stuck in a bottleneck, accelerating their breakthrough.
Attraction: You will attract a large group of professionals stuck in a bottleneck who will see your words as oracles.
Lide’s expression was quite interesting after reading the attributes of his secondary identity.
This identity, Lord Ilo, was incredibly powerful; at level 23, he still couldn’t reach the power that the identity of Ilo should have.
“Told a massive lie that made the whole world dance with me?”
Lide’s smile was radiant.
He inexplicably thought back to where it all began–the president of the Demon Heart, the ogre Wales.
He wondered what kind of expression this little prince of imagination would show when he heard about his accomplishments in Risier City.
He was actually quite looking forward to seeing Wales again next time he visited Green City.
Additionally, this secondary identity of Ilo had another thrilling privilege–establishing a sect and preaching in Green City.
That was just too awesome.
The Dawn Sect, in essence, still belonged to the Fake God Sect. After all, his main deity had just transcended, far from reaching divinity,
so he had not been able to preach abroad because the risk without a true divine presence was indescribable; if exposed, it could endanger the grand scheme he had painstakingly constructed.
It was best to play it safe.
Yet now the situation had changed, the momentum under the identity of Lord Ilo had been established, and a trial could definitely be undertaken.
“If we were to preach externally, the doctrines of the Dawn Sect must be somewhat concealed.”
Lide stroked his chin, recalling his “never give up, strive persistently, unite, be brave, love family and country” divine-level doctrines and couldn’t help but smile wryly–such positive doctrines were indeed a treasure against disharmonic divine beings.
And who could have guessed that this spontaneously formed religion would now shine so brilliantly.
Although the doctrines could no longer be changed, at the end of the day, the final interpretation was in his hands.
He could interpret them however he wanted, without even blushing.
“But maybe I should leave this task to that little girl, Nicole…”
He shook his head and thought no further.
Preaching was something he seldom participated in; after several years of experience, the sisters Nicole and Nilo could handle it far better than he could.
With that, Lide thoroughly reviewed all the changes in his attributes from the recent times.
He had a clear assessment of his strength–within the extraordinary realm, he was unbeatable.
Even if an opponent reached level 24 and touched the legendary, he could suppress them effortlessly.
“Now it’s time to get to work…”
Lide narrowed his eyes slightly, his eyes brimming with chill.
The nearly explosive power within his body made him crave a fight.
“Firstly, the Extraordinary Spider Queen from the Spider Plane; after slaughtering the Spider Queen, it will be the Black Dragon in the Mud Swamp who stole the Divine Artifact.
Once I’ve chained the Black Dragon in the Dawn Square, Dawn City can begin its conquest of the Underworld.
With so many intelligent races in this vast land of the Underworld, wouldn’t it be a waste if they didn’t become believers of the Dawn Sect?”
“And those hidden Ancient Evil Gods, although I don’t know when the Ancient Days will come, just thinking about it makes my unease grow stronger, I must prepare in advance.”
However…after reflecting for a moment, Lide’s expression turned peculiar; he realized something very important–he seemed to have not logged off for half a year.
“I wonder how the Crimson Moon is doing now, and whether those silly players have caused any trouble lately…”
With that thought, Lide couldn’t wait any longer; after sending a magical message to Harrison, he closed his eyes in the office and sat down, then returned to the long-missed Earth.

chapters.title: Chapter 394 - Chapter 394: Chapter 396: The Blood Moon Descends, Gods Will Fall to Mortality (7000 words)
chapters.content:
Chapter 394: Chapter 396: The Blood Moon Descends, Gods Will Fall to Mortality (7000 words)
When Lide opened his eyes again, the off-white color of the ceiling entered his view.
He slightly turned his head and glanced around. Seeing the modern furniture and electronic products in the room, his previously tense nerves instantly relaxed.
The feeling was quite marvelous. Although he had greater power in Glory and had even broken through to the Transcendent level, Earth always gave him an irreplaceable sense of security.
Sitting up, he subconsciously grabbed his cellphone, which he had left on the wireless charger for fear of running out of battery. When he turned on the phone, he was immediately greeted with over 50 missed calls.
A third of them were notifications that he had won various prizes…
The rest were from his assistant, Cheng Lu, and the vice president Zhao Yue, both high-level executives of the Crimson Moon Guild.
Clearly, his disappearance for the past half-year had caused them no small amount of resentment.
However, Lide had already anticipated this and had given instructions beforehand.
As for the Crimson Moon Guild, he had made thorough preparations. He divided the power of the Crimson Moon into two parts.
The decision-making and execution power lay with vice president Zhao Yue and the management team; another department was the Audit Department, tasked with supervising the management team.
The Audit Department was setup by Lide on the fly. Its main function was to remind the management team and prevent them from hollowing out the company, as power must be monitored to operate healthily. Earth didn’t have any Bloodline members who were utterly loyal to him.
He dialed Cheng Lu, his assistant’s number directly.
The moment the call connected, a resentful tone came through.
“Mr. Li, we haven’t been able to reach you for half a year… If it wasn’t for your previous instructions, we really would have called the police.”
Lide smiled slightly, “It’s nothing serious, I just had more important things to deal with. Moreover, I trust you to manage the Crimson Moon.”
Regardless of whether he truly trusted them, the compliment was necessary, “And with your capabilities, managing the Crimson Moon is a breeze.”
“Alright, when will you come to the company? There are still many decisions that need your attention,” said Cheng Lu, feeling rather helpless to be saddled with such an irresponsible boss–it was both relaxing and stressful.
She couldn’t understand how a company worth billions could go without inquiry for half a year.
You could at least call once a month…
“Alright, I’ll be there in two hours.”
After seeing Cheng Lu hang up, Zhao Yue, who had just logged out of the game, raised her eyebrows in her office, “Is Mr. Li finally willing to come to the office?”
Cheng Lu gave a wry smile and nodded, “Mr. Li said he’ll be here in two hours.”
After speaking, she pursed her lips, muttering, “Mr. Zhao, just how many mines does Mr. Li’s family own? He doesn’t care about the company for half a year; wasn’t he afraid that we would run it into the ground?”
Zhao Yue shook her head with a smile. As curious as she was, since the other party was the boss, she had no way to hold him accountable.
Thinking about the man, elegant to the point she found pleasing to the eye, an indescribable emotion surged in her heart.
“Let’s not talk about this. Prepare the work from the past half-year, and let’s report everything to Mr. Li when he arrives.”
“Alright…”
After hanging up, Lide casually set down the phone and stood up to walk towards the bathroom, but after just a few steps, he suddenly felt something was off. Inside his body, it seemed like there was something… Magic Power?
This…
Because that power was so faint, Lide wasn’t quite sure. After all, this was Earth.
He paused in his steps, his eyes slightly narrowed, and began to seriously sense his surroundings.
The air around was still empty, lacking the basic element of Glory–Magic Power–but the weak force inside his body was becoming clearer.
A flicker of contemplation crossed his eyes.
With a somewhat unusual mind-set and even his right hand on his head ready to bear the brunt of Magic Rebound,
He brought his thumb and middle finger close and snapped them–pop! A crisp sound echoed, and then under Lide’s gaze, the air in front of him ignited like a candle being lit.
Then a Small Fireball the size of an apple roared into existence, radiating heat as it formed. The spacious room’s temperature rose substantially in an instant.
“Cast… success??”
Lide’s eyes widened, his face showing undeniable surprise.
He felt the warmth emanating from the Small Fireball, his expression a colorful spectacle.
“Have I really brought back a portion of Magic Power to Earth after my Transcendent breakthrough??”
He extended his right hand, and under the guidance of spiritual power, the Small Fireball began to slowly float towards him, then stayed suspended above his palm.
The orange-yellow fireball came with a mesmerizing aura.
Magic, this was real Magic, and the sensation was too wonderful.
Even though this Small Fireball was as weak as a match compared to the ones he used in Glory, this was damn Earth.
“From the day my body underwent changes, it seems this moment was destined…”
Lide murmured to himself, “The Bloodline’s Bloodline has influenced my Earth body through the soul; I don’t even need to eat anymore. The energy emanating from Glory alone is enough to sustain my bodily functions.
Compared to that, it seems not so extraordinary that I brought back a portion of my casting ability after breaking through to Transcendent.
So, speaking of which, if I can break through to the Legendary level, might I be able to bring back even more powerful forces?”
At this thought, Lide’s eyes suddenly sharpened, and he dispersed the Small Fireball with a flick of his hand.
As the orange-yellow Small Fireball lost its magical support, it slowly faded away until it vanished completely.
He started to ponder more deeply. Casting spells was a positive thing, but what it signified behind the scenes required serious thought.
Did this mean the higher his level in Glory, the more power he could synchronize with on Earth?
What was the underlying principle?
What was the relationship between Earth and Glory?
Why was Glory presented as a game to players?
Countless thoughts flashed through Lide’s mind.
The game Glory had been shrouded in mist from the very beginning, no matter how much he probed, the mist never fully lifted.
Now, it seemed even denser.
“No matter what Glory and Earth eventually evolve into, great strength will always be the best response…”
After taking a deep breath, Lide’s eyes instantly became resolute.
He was no longer the somewhat naive novice from four years ago; now, he was the master of hundreds of thousands, his word deciding the fate of countless individuals.
An absolute superior.
“In Glory, I’ve already acquired a certain ability to protect myself… so next, it should be time to increase my investment in Crimson Moon.”
Dawn City was now taking shape, currently boasting two Transcendents–himself and the Frost Giant Dragon Stran.
Besides them, Emi, who was on the verge of a breakthrough, and the missing Divine Monster, Asreaga–if nothing unexpected happened, once they reemerged, Dawn City would boast an astonishing four Transcendents.
Four Transcendents–what did that signify? In the southern provinces, with tens of millions of people, only Lord Rock of Green City was known to be an Extraordinary Mage in the public eye.
Perhaps there were one or two others hidden in the shadows, but their numbers were certainly pitifully scarce.
Legendary beings often carried great responsibilities and seldom appeared before outsiders, which made Transcendents the ultimate force one could encounter.
Yet now, Dawn City was about to possess four Transcendents, the significance of which was self-evident.
With Dawn City in its initial form, the next step would be to develop the powers on the side of Earth.
What changes the future would bring were unpredictable–who else besides him could weave a Small Fireball?
To face this unknown future, diversifying strategies was undoubtedly the best way to mitigate risks.
After pondering for a moment, Lide no longer hesitated; he took a shower, changed into clean clothes, and went straight downstairs.
Apart from the smart robots, there were no outsiders in the two-billion-dollar villa he lived in.
Two latest-model self-driving cars were parked in the underground garage. Lide got into one, set the destination, and then pulled out his phone to check the latest news about Glory.
But as soon as he opened the official forum, the various posts made his expression quite peculiar.
“Today, I’ll show you the Combat Secret Skill–Iron Charge–I learned at the Warrior Guild”
Lide clicked on the post, and the video began playing automatically: a player wearing a comical mask stood on a balcony, with a huge rusty iron pot fixed to a wooden stake about twenty meters away.
The masked player slightly bent his body, showing a perfectly standard warrior’s starting pose, and then propelled himself with great force, charging forward like an arrow.
The twenty-meter distance was covered in just two breaths.
Clang~
What was shocking was that the huge rusty iron pot was smashed to pieces by the charge, and the masked player accidentally hit the edge of the balcony and cracked the cement rail…
“Folks, hit the like button, and next time I’ll perform a jumping execution…”
After the video ended, Lide’s expression was quite colorful.
He had known that warrior skills from Glory could be used on Earth, but he had not anticipated they would be this effective.
And there were countless similar videos: some using kitchen knives like sabers to split open their neighbors’ heads, only to find their wives dressed scantily coming out…
Some were using pot lids as shields, jumping from the third floor of a building unharmed and standing up, but so excited during the celebration that they accidentally fell into the nearby septic tank…
Some were using brooms as Knight Captain’s lances, charging and piercing through a freshly built cement wall, only to be chased and beaten by dozens of construction workers for three hours…
These players were indeed foolish, but these videos all hinted at one thing–strength.
Yes, despite their ludicrous actions, it was a robust body that allowed them to perform these stunts.
And Lide’s brow furrowed.
Outsiders see the fun, but he felt as if a giant hand was controlling all of this behind the scenes.
He took a deep breath, a depth unnavigable by outsiders lurking in his dark pupils.
“Glory… Earth…”
“Times are changing, huh.”
Murmuring, he quietly closed his eyes, no longer flipping through the always inactive official website.
—-
—-
—-
An hour later.
Crimson Moon.
The top management were somewhat helpless about the fact that their boss hadn’t been to the company in half a year and never bothered to inquire about its affairs. But what can you do when the man is the boss?
So when they heard that Lide was coming, they quickly lined up to welcome him.
The self-driving car stopped in front of the main entrance of Crimson Moon. Seeing this, Deputy CEO Zhao Yue personally stepped forward to open the door. Lide alighted naturally, nodding his head in thanks.
There are only two ways to get out of a car–you open the door yourself, or someone opens it for you. The difference lies in who you are.
About a dozen top managers immediately greeted him in unison.
“Good afternoon, Mr. Li.”
The tidy voices drew many passing employees to look back, and upon seeing Lide’s figure, they were instantly wide-eyed.
Especially the new female employees, their eyes shone; was this the boss? How could someone be this handsome…
“Good afternoon, you’ve worked hard during this time.”
Lide nodded slightly, exchanging pleasantries with the managers with a smile on his face.
What the managers truly thought inside, he did not know, but the smiles on their faces remained as bright as ever.
Each experienced in their own ways, none would create discomfort in Lide’s presence; their external professionalism was well-practiced.
After a round of polite back-and-forth and business flattery, Lide dismissed them and returned to the office with Zhao Yue and his assistant Cheng Lu.
Having not been here for several months, Lide could clearly sense that there were quite a few more people in the company offices.
It seemed that although he had been absent, the development of Crimson Moon had not stalled, which pleased him greatly.
In the office, Lide sat opposite Zhao Yue. While assistant Cheng Lu was brewing a pot of extremely fine Dahongpao tea that cost 12,000 yuan per 500 grams, his gaze fell on Zhao Yue, who was dressed in a classic black and white pencil dress. Her mature and voluptuous allure was incredibly enticing.
“Mr. Zhao, how has Crimson Moon developed during this period? Start with staffing and report everything to me.”
Lide didn’t beat around the bush and went straight to the point.
“Yes, Mr. Li.”
Zhao Yue turned serious when it came to business matters and began her earnest report.
“At present, the total number of people in Crimson Moon has broken through 2,100,
including 1,215 professional gamers.
Data Analysis Department has 627 people,
and Game Commodity Trading Department 210 people,
plus over 100 logistics and administrative staff, making a total of 2,186 people.”
More than 2,000 people?
Lide nodded slightly. For a gaming club, this size was considered medium to large.
“How are we doing with guild formation in Glory?”
Last October, the open beta for “Glory” launched, and now it was September.
Nearly a year had passed, and in other games, one year would already be considered the mid-stage, with many games only lasting one to two years in total.
“Mr. Li, with your support, Crimson Moon has already become one of the top three guilds in the Nolan Empire!”
Zhao Yue’s tone rose with excitement.
Lide, the tycoon, had splurged tens of thousands or even hundreds of thousands of Gold Pucks on Crimson Moon in the game. For players just entering “Glory,” these were astronomical figures.
Even for running a large guild, it was more than enough.
“Currently, the Crimson Moon Guild has a total of 120,000 members, the core of which are our 1,200 professional gamers, followed by 100,000 formal members, with over 10,000 temporary members.”
120,000 players?
Lide raised an eyebrow. The number wasn’t enormous, but it was definitely not a small feat.
Although “Glory” hosted 10 million players, the Main Plane of Glory was so vast that just the population of the Nolan Empire was several hundred million. The addition of 10 million players to the Main Plane was like a drop of water in the ocean; they would be dispersed immediately.
Having recruited tens of thousands of players was likely thanks to the shine of the player’s main city.
“How are we managing and controlling these players recruited in the game now?”
“It’s simple, a contribution system and a well-stocked warehouse.
We’ve established the largest guild warehouse, which contains all kinds of weapons, equipment, Magic Scrolls, Alchemy Potions…
But everything requires contribution points to exchange. The longer they join the guild, the tighter they are bound to us.
We also have improved on many previous systems, made many changes, the core personnel will sign contracts with us, and…”
Zhao Yue seemed quite knowledgeable about this area, speaking eloquently for over half an hour while Lide listened intently.
For Earth, a planet with highly developed information technology, accessing data was not difficult.
For the elite managers on six-figure salaries, designing a system completely suited for Crimson Moon based on past experience wasn’t a challenge.
“Excellent, I trust you have more experience in this area than I do, so go ahead and take the reigns.
All I need is for Crimson Moon to become a force that can be directed at will.”
Lide’s gaze was piercing, and after a brief pause, his tone solemn.
“Mr. Zhao, I believe you can sense the uniqueness of ‘Glory’, especially the point that we can bring power out of this game. This foretells the game’s increasing influence in the future and its growing importance to us.
Crimson Moon has already taken the lead, and no matter what changes occur in the future, as long as we use this advantage to keep developing, we will undoubtedly hold our own in upcoming upheavals.”
“Although the 2,000 members of Crimson Moon aren’t few, it’s not enough. I want to expand to 5,000, to 10,000 members.
These professional players will become the capital for our future growth.
Mr. Zhao, I want Crimson Moon to become the foremost of all guilds.
During this process, whatever help you need, I will provide it.”
Lide’s tone was calm, but the ambition behind his words made Zhao Yue’s breathing slow, her heart thrumming quickly.
To a strong-willed career elite, only the strong are worthy of admiration, and the man before her shone brilliantly.
Wealthy beyond measure, cunning as the sea, elegant in demeanor, handsome in appearance…
Few of the opposite sex could remain unmoved before such a man.
Great people always attract more attention, regardless of gender.
“Mr. Li, I understand. Crimson Moon will reach the heights you expect.”
Zhao Yue took a deep breath, lifted her head slightly, and her tone was unwaveringly firm.
For someone in charge of a company with thousands of employees, her boldness and capability were enough to make many self-proclaimed extraordinary men blush.
“Very well.”
Lide smiled in satisfaction, appreciating the resolute spirit Zhao Yue possessed, which he found similar to his own.
“How far has the collaboration with the Crimson Mage Tower to develop Magic Scrolls progressed?”
If the professional gamers were his blade, then the Data Analysis Department was the craftsmen forging that blade.
Whether it was intelligence collection, data analysis, questing, or boss strategy, they were indispensable.
As Crimson Moon and Dawn City expanded, the role of the Data Analysis Department would only become more crucial.
“At present, we have mastered the production technology of 10 sets of First Circle and Second Circle Magic Scrolls from the Crimson Mage Tower.
And by collaborating with the Supercomputer, we successfully improved four of them, resulting in 12 different types of derivative scrolls…
Now, even if we leave the Crimson Mage Tower, as long as we have spellcasters of sufficient level, we can immediately produce these magic scrolls.”
Lide nodded with satisfaction. The chemical reaction where one plus one equals more than two had clearly taken place, which is exactly what he desired: combining the strengths of both worlds to develop new technologies and magic.
“You’ve done well, but you must ensure absolute secrecy regarding the magic scroll data.
Apart from the normal work deductions and key personnel, no one is allowed to access the data.”
Lide’s gaze became sharp in an instant.
“The production technology of magic scrolls is our core competitive edge. If we lose this data, it will cause us unbearable damage.”
“Don’t worry, the supercomputer where we store the data operates independently and is not connected to the outside network. Without my permission and the key I carry with me, anyone who touches it will immediately trigger an alarm.”
Zhao Yue spoke calmly, yet with absolute confidence.
Seeing this, Lide didn’t say much more. He trusted that Zhao Yue would take the security of this confidential information even more seriously than he would, as he was familiar with her airtight working style.
“How is the Trade Department doing now?”
“The Trade Department has gradually gained ground with the support of the Golden Wheat Commerce in Green City…”
“What are the plans for the next phase of development, currently?”
“Currently…”
Lide began to understand the progress of Crimson Moon’s projects one by one over this period.
Assistant Cheng Lu was helping the two by making tea on the side and also noting down the key points as instructed by Lide.
It took a whole afternoon for Zhao Yue to report half a year’s work of Crimson Moon to Lide.
Lide now had a clearer understanding of the current state of Crimson Moon.
But just as today’s conversation was about to end, he suddenly remembered something.
The Ancient Alchemy Magic Array being constructed over the Magic Crystal Vein.
“Mr. Zhao, you need to prepare a team from the Data Analysis Department. I will take you to a hidden place to study the magic array, just like improving the magic scrolls of the Crimson Mage Tower.”
Although he had transcended to Extraordinary and no longer urgently needed the Ancient Alchemy Magic Array,
It had a very important feature–it could become his temporary Divine Country, transforming other races into Bloodline.
This was of significant meaning to him.
The races under Dawn City were far too numerous and diverse, and these foreign races could not be transformed into Bloodline by the initial embrace.
This created a very awkward point–he could only use the Power of Faith to transform the upper echelons of these foreign races.
Just like with the Iron Hoof Tribe at the moment, he could only control the Iron Hoof Tribe’s army of over a hundred thousand through the Clan Leader, Sam.
The risk of this single-pole operation was undoubtedly high; if anything happened to Sam, the command of this army might not belong to him anymore.
However, if the Ancient Alchemy Magic Array were established, a group of Centaurs could be transformed into Bloodline, and then, using this group as the core, he could take complete control of this army.
The same applied to the Beastmen.
But now the biggest problem was that Dawn City’s knowledge reserve on magic arrays was lacking, resulting in the ridiculously difficult Ancient Alchemy Magic Array not being established for a long time.
He also couldn’t possibly bring others back and forth to the already established Ancient Alchemy Magic Array of the Crimson Mage Tower for transformation.
He didn’t know how big of a commotion the transformation would cause; if it were earth-shattering, then the secrets of the Crimson Mage Tower, which had been so hard to conceal, would be exposed.
He had already thought about involving the Data Analysis Department in improving the magic array last time, but he never really found the time to arrange it.
“A magic array? Mr. Li, that’s more complex than a magic scroll…”
Cheng Lu, who was nearby, spoke up at this moment, with a hint of admiration in her eyes.
“How did you manage to complete so many hidden tasks in Glory? You’re able to access such valuable things at this stage… It’s amazing.”
“When I participated in the internal test, I happened to obtain a Noble identity, and Glory just happens to be a world dominated by Nobles…”
Lide smiled, saying just a little, and left the rest up to her own imagination.
Upon hearing this, Cheng Lu indeed looked enlightened, obviously having filled in the process with her own assumptions.
“Mr. Li, I will form a new group specifically in charge of this matter,” Zhao Yue nodded, also quite intrigued.
As an internal test player, she naturally understood the value of magic arrays. Now that they had the production technology for magic scrolls, once they grasped the magic arrays… as long as the mages of Crimson Moon were trained, wouldn’t they control a source of wealth that would make everyone envious?
At those words, Lide nodded slightly. He only needed to be responsible for arranging things; implementation would naturally be handled by Zhao Yue or other middle management.
His main reasons for coming back this time were actually two things: one was to let the management know that their boss hadn’t run off and was still alive.
The other was to correct any potential deviations in the development direction, ensuring that the next steps for Crimson Moon were in line with his layout–whether recruiting more players or involving them in studying magic arrays, it was all part of his plan.
“Do you have any other matters to report?” Lide picked up the still warm cup of top-quality Da Hong Pao from the table and took a comfortable sip.
“Mr. Li, there is indeed one very important piece of news,” said Zhao Yue as if she suddenly remembered something, her expression turning somewhat solemn.
“Three months ago, one of our professional players inadvertently took on a hidden serial task, which was extremely difficult. We had to employ a team of over a hundred people to complete it.
But the final reward wasn’t any equipment or skills, but a message.
This message was spoken by the NPC who issued the task just before dying, and we are no longer able to verify its authenticity.
However, the content of the message surprised the Data Analysis Department, as it might be a clue to the opening of the next expansion in Glory.”
A message?
Lide became intrigued, “Let’s hear it.”
He hadn’t paid much attention at first, but Zhao Yue’s next words made his eyes widen to their limits.
“The exact words of that message were–When the lands are covered in ice and snow, and the Crimson Moon looms over the world, the shadow of bygone days shall envelop the earth.
At that time, the gods shall fall to mortal realms, the light will no longer shine brightly, the Holy Light will be obscured, and the wickedness of old shall once again rule the world…”

chapters.title: Chapter 395 - Chapter 395: Chapter 397: Order to Prepare for War, Ready to Hunt the Extraordinary Spider Queen
chapters.content:
Chapter 395: Chapter 397: Order to Prepare for War, Ready to Hunt the Extraordinary Spider Queen
The Blood Moon approaches the world, and the gods shall fall to the mortal realm as the ancients rule once more…
Lide’s heart trembled; he had not expected to hear news of the ancient god’s descent from Zhao Yue.
Moreover, the timing was tied to the snow covering the earth.
Recently, with the continuous release of Evil Gods from their seals, a large number of players had begun speculating about this event.
For ordinary players, this wasn’t something that required their attention; it was merely a matter of interest.
However, for the major guilds, being able to catch early signs before the release of the new expansion could enable them to develop response strategies, potentially gaining the upper hand and reaping greater benefits.
He recalled the words of the God of Plague in Risier City and instantly determined that this hard-earned piece of information was highly reliable.
“The Ancient Descent…”
“Is there more useful information about this?”
Seeing Lide’s serious expression, Zhao Yue also looked very grave; she clearly knew the exceptional nature of the news.
“Mr. Lide, the information about the Evil Gods is too high-level; currently, very few players have encountered it, and it will be tough to gather more in a short time.
We have, however, compiled a comprehensive list of player posts on the forum. Starting from the birth of the Evil God in Risier City, up until now, the number of known Evil God releases on the Main Plane has reached thirty-six.
In other words, thirty-six Evil Gods have been revived.
And in regions inaccessible to players, there are likely even more…”
Upon hearing this, Lide’s mouth twitched slightly, feeling somewhat absurd. How could the divine beings of the Main Plane be excluded while so many Evil Gods were sealed within it?
“The Data Analysis Department speculates that these seals might date back to the earliest era of Glory, left at the Creation itself because even the oldest myths going back tens of millions of years don’t mention anything about these ancient Evil Gods.”
Zhao Yue’s explanation was plausible; Lide had also collected absolutely no information on the Ancient Evil Gods.
Logically, such powerful beings should have left some trace. The Light Gods loved to boast about their past deeds; it made no sense for them not to mention them.
This could only mean one thing–either the Ancient Evil Gods existed before the gods were born and were sealed before the gods could record them,
or a powerful force had erased everything regarding the Ancient Evil Gods.
Regardless of which, the information was shocking enough.
“The arrival of the Ancient Evil Gods will cause a great upheaval in ‘Glory.’
You can consider it like a new expansion or a version update.
This is very important; instruct the Data Analysis Department to prioritize gathering information on this topic.”
Lide, with a stern expression, said, “I’ll arrange for an NPC in ‘Glory’ to contact you later, and I’ll set up a contact channel within ‘Glory.’
If there’s an emergency and you can’t contact me from the outside, use that channel to send messages, and I will be informed promptly.”
He spent most of his time immersed in Glory, so trying to contact him by phone was completely pointless.
“Yes, Mr. Lide.”
After discussing some work-related matters with Zhao Yue for a while, Lide no longer felt like staying at the company.
The snow covers the earth, and the ancients return… It was now the end of September, and the Frost Month was only two or three months away.
The snow-covered earth was just around the corner.
Since the public test, the timelines of the two worlds had merged, eliminating any time difference, making time seem to pass ever faster for Lide, fortunate to possess the eternal life of a Bloodline…
After repeatedly instructing Zhao Yue to have the Data Analysis Department intensify their search for information on the Ancient Evil Gods, Lide did not linger and immediately left Crimson Moon.
As he walked out of the company’s doors, his sense of urgency heightened once more.
The Ancient Coming… this signified variables.
And now, Dawn City was still not mentally prepared to face such a colossal change.
He must accelerate his arrangements.
Upon returning home, Lide didn’t hesitate, and directly entered Glory.
Dawn City, less than ten hours after Lide left.
When he opened his eyes, the moon was just rising.
Lide sat in the armchair behind his desk and didn’t rush to get up; instead, he began to think seriously.
Now that he had obtained the critical news that the Ancient might arrive during this crucial Frost Month, it was imperative to make good use of it.
“No matter when changes occur, it’s always right to be prepared now.”
Lide slowly calmed down.
“Someone come.”
Squeak~ the door was pushed open, and two Bloodline guards entered, their expressions respectful as they saluted.
“Your Majesty.”
“Summon Kapu, Stanley, Harrison, and Frey here at the fastest speed.”
“Yes, Your Majesty.”
Sensing the seriousness in Lide’s tone, the guards dared not delay and immediately turned and left.
Twenty minutes later, the four men entered one by one and immediately saluted Lide upon seeing him.
“Good evening, Your Majesty.”
Lide glanced at them and without further ado went straight to the point.
“I have cleared the spatial channel constructed by the God of Plague; Dawn City will not face danger again for a short time.”
“But now, I have received a more important message.” Lide took a deep breath, repeated the words of Zhao Yue, and his expression turned solemn.
“When snow covers the earth and the Blood Moon appears, the Divine will fall to the mortal realm.”
“This message will change the entirety of Glory; we are about to face great trouble.”
Harrison’s brow furrowed tightly, and he spoke with some unease.
“Your Majesty, snow will only cover the ground when we fully enter the Frost Month, which generally occurs at the end of December and the beginning of January.
Currently, there are only three months left until then.
We must make preparations.”
Only three months left… Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly.
“I’ve called you here to prepare for the impending catastrophe.
You have all felt the power of the Ancient Evil God up close. If we truly reach that day, it will unquestionably be the greatest crisis Dawn City has ever encountered.
Leaving aside whether the God of Plague can locate Dawn City when the Ancient days arrive,
if there is chaos outside, our normal trade will inevitably be affected, and it might even cause a complete standstill among various powers.”
The men had already realized the severity of the situation, although the war in the Land of Bone-Burying had concluded with a total victory for Dawn City.
But the power of the God of Plague still made their expressions grave, with the memory of the endless fierce Half-Ratmen lingering in their minds.
“Your Majesty, please give your orders.”
Harrison’s gaze deepened, “The Holy Light Bloodline will always be a sharp blade in Your Majesty’s hand!
We will execute Your will with our lives and souls!”
Lide didn’t dawdle, turning his head to look at the 18th level Beastman King sporting the enormous head of a male lion.
“Kapu, first return to the Underworld to stabilize the situation while also sending additional intelligence agents to gather all information about the Half-Elves and the Underworld, paying special attention to any Transcendent powers.
In times when it’s not suitable to expand in the outer world, an unexplored world will undoubtedly bring us greater benefits.”
Lide paused in his speech, a chilling glint flashing in his eyes, “Also, gather information about the Black Dragon in the Mud Swamp.
Once I slaughter the Extraordinary Spider Queen of the Spider Plane, it will be time to deal with that Black Dragon.”
Having transcended the ordinary, he hadn’t forgotten that the beings that once troubled Dawn City needed to be dealt with, especially the Black Dragon of the Mud Swamp, who still held a Divine Artifact in its grasp.
He had said he would tether the Black Dragon in the plaza of Dawn City, and the time had come to fulfill that boast.
“Yes, Your Majesty!”
Excitement showed on Kapu’s face.
To slay a dragon, and not just any dragon but a genuine Transcendent Black Dragon, was the ultimate glory that all of Glory aspired to, and he couldn’t believe that he would get to be part of it.
“Frey…”
After assigning the tasks, Lide didn’t say much more, turning his gaze to his second-generation Bloodline.
“How is the situation in the Dwarf Hills? Has the Centaur felt external pressure due to the battle at Risier City?”
“Your Majesty, everything is normal in the Dwarf Hills.”
Frey responded respectfully, “Contrary to your concerns, due to the powerful performance of the Iron Hoof Tribe in the battle at Risier City, we have gained even more respect.
Even many Nobles from Green City have already established branches of their trading halls in the free market to facilitate trade with the Iron Hoof Tribe.”
“Indeed, power is the only thing that matters.”
After seeing the strength of the Centaurs, even those humans who had previously looked down on them began to take the initiative to make amends.
Lide nodded slightly, this matter was not so unexpected.
The elite forces of Green City had been buried in Risier City, and even if humans wanted to do something to the Iron Hoof Tribe, they were now powerless.
Moreover, the barren wilderness was a place where not even birds would defecate, so there wasn’t much to covet there. It was likely that these nobles were trading with the Iron Hoof Tribe in order to probe the source of the high-level equipment on the Centaurs.
“How about the Fishman Tribe and King Guido Blackwind of the Gale Empire?”
The Gale Empire… Frey twitched his lips, “My Lord, thanks to the blessing of the Centaur God and the support of the Destiny Hero, the Gale Empire has now amassed an army of 200,000 men.
With our support, his development is thriving day by day.
The Centaurs within Gale City have received news from Guido, but that Extraordinary Centaur has yet to make a move…”
“As for the Fishman Tribe, since they received the Alchemy Bombs, they have now taken control of the entire area near the Lost Coast, and their strength continues to grow day by day.
At the same time, our relationship with them has grown even closer.”
“Good, now let us sell the weapons, equipment, Alchemy Bombs, even Magic Scrolls, and wine from our warehouses, converting everything into Magic Materials, ore, and other essential raw materials for storage.
No one can determine if it will be as safe as now when the Ancient days arrive.
We need to stockpile enough materials to get through this Frost.”
Lide spoke very solemnly, his face filled with gravity.
Frey nodded respectfully, “My Lord, I have already contacted the Fishman Tribe to procure Magic Materials for us with full effort.
I have also signed a one-year supply contract with them to have the Magic Materials prepared in advance; we can receive these goods first, and the missing equipment will be delivered after production in the factory.”
Lide nodded in satisfaction.
“You’ve done very well, continue to stock up boldly. Don’t worry that we cannot produce enough, just go ahead and do it.
The more raw materials we stock now, the more they will serve as ballast when the situation becomes turbulent, they cannot be compared with simple wealth.”
Frey had done an excellent job, so there was no need for further comment.
However, he suddenly remembered something and looked towards Harrison, beginning to inquire.
“What about that Bimong that we captured?”
Since being captured in Risier City, the Bimong, flowing with Golden Bloodline, was still detained in Dawn City.
Initially, due to the lack of Power of Faith, he did not rush to deal with it, and then the incident with the Divine Skull came to pass, leaving him even less time to care for it.
“Bimong is imprisoned in the dungeon, everything is normal at the moment. Shall I bring him over?”
“Keep him locked up for now, I don’t have time to deal with him at the moment. A Level 19 Bimong will not affect the overall situation, let’s talk about it after I handle the matters at hand,” Lide waved his hand dismissively.
Dawn City was no longer what it used to be; he had suppressed the opponent purely out of interest in the Golden Bloodline, otherwise, for an ordinary Level 19, he might not have paid much attention.
Then, shifting the conversation,
“Harrison, I suppose you haven’t completed the task I assigned you a few months ago?”
“My Lord, what are you referring to?” Harrison was a bit puzzled.
“First, establish the agricultural town on Dawn Plain and plant food crops.
Second, research the fully automatic Alchemy Harvester,
Third, develop urban railcars,
Fourth, a city-wide lighting system.”
Lide listed them one by one; these were the tasks he had assigned to Harrison while he was undergoing Divine Devourment.
However, the pressure from the God of Plague was too great, and the entire Dawn City was turning its efforts to manage this war.
Therefore, it was clearly impossible to develop these life facilities during such high-intensity warfare.
Harrison nodded with a wry smile, “Yes, my Lord, the Magic Industry Research Institute and various production workshops are all busy dealing with the Fierce Half-Ratmen, so…”
“That’s alright, it was normal before.
But in the coming months, we need to shift our external focus to the internal needs of Dawn City.
Especially establishing the agricultural town is a priority. The wheat on Moonlight Plain can produce two crops a year, each crop provides a year’s food supply just over 200,000 people, making 400,000 for both crops.
Although this wheat seems abundant, we still need to provide food for the Beastmen and the two thousand giants, which immediately creates a deficit in our food supplies.
Thus, we must plow enough farmland for food production before the sowing season of the winter wheat passes.
You can mobilize all the Spellcasters from the Crimson Mage Tower and any unoccupied Bloodline members to assist in preparing the fields.”
“I need more food.”
Lide spoke about this issue with a grave expression on his face.
Food was the most fundamental lifeline for a city, and although Dawn City no longer lacked food, the increasing population and the arrival of giants had led to a crisis in food supply.
Now that the Ancient Days were about to descend, he had to quickly resolve these issues that could affect the stability of Dawn City.
“I will continue to grant you the authority over the Land of Bone-Burying, allowing you to manipulate the power of space and establish spatial passages in the soon-to-be-established agricultural towns, connecting these towns with Dawn City.”
“At the same time, other aspects of research must also urge the Magic Industry Research Institute to accelerate its progress.
I need to see results as soon as possible.”
Several tasks were issued in succession, putting pressure on Harrison, but the chairman of the City Hall immediately responded without any complaints.
“As you wish, my lord. Before the Dawn Festival arrives, all these tasks you have issued will be completed!”
Hearing this resolute reply, Lide’s face relaxed slightly and after a brief moment of thought, he continued.
“Additionally, this year’s raid for population can be paused if no suitable targets are found.
The addition of nearly 2000 adult giants has greatly alleviated the lack of labor, allowing the population of Dawn City to temporarily meet our needs.
Moreover, we have been at war throughout the year and have not continued to build new districts, lacking areas to settle new populations.
So, delaying for a year is unavoidable.”
There were priorities and emergencies; previously, raiding for population was the most important matter for Dawn City. But with the increase in the population of Dawn City and the strengthening of military power, this matter was no longer so urgent.
Preparing for the imminent Ancient Days was now the top priority.
After organizing the development tasks for Dawn City, Lide turned his gaze to a figure beside him with a fierce scar on his face.
“Stanley.”
“My lord.”
“Now, countless tales about Lord Ilo in Green City have reached their zenith, elevating his reputation to the peak.
As a subordinate force to Lord Ilo, the Dark Contract will definitely become the first choice for many seeking partnerships.
After you return to Green City, immediately divest those excessively dark dealings, retaining only the necessary core assets.
During this process, whether it be nobles or sects extending an olive branch to the Dark Contract, do not refuse any normal collaborations.
The smartest way for a force to avoid destruction is to weave a web and pull everyone around into your chariot.”
Lide’s eyes were piercing, “With your wisdom, I believe you can handle this matter well.”
“Additionally, the Dawn Sect can now tentatively begin preaching to outsiders, and you must also handle the preparatory matters for the preaching this time.
After the Frost Month passes, I will start preaching in Green City.”
“At the same time, you need to secretly send someone to find the person in charge of the Crimson Moon Guild and establish a communication channel with them,
I will write a letter of contact later, which you can take to gain their trust after making contact.”
“Lastly, after you have made contact with the person in charge of the Crimson Moon, some of these adventurers will participate in the research of the Magic Array.
You must bring these people to the Dwarf Valley without exposing your own identity, and also ensure they do not realize the specific location of the Dwarf Valley.”
Lide issued one command after another, not wasting a single word.
Time was of the essence, and he could no longer afford to lay out his plans slowly as before.
“At your command, my lord.”
Stanley responded solemnly, once an Evil God believer and a sinister being who lurked in the shadows.
He naturally understood what kind of turmoil might occur if, as Lide said, the Ancient Days were about to shroud the world and the gods were to become mortal.
Human nature always harbors a dark side.
When the gods who once protected the Main Plane lose the ability to shelter their believers, and when the light no longer shines brightly, the entire social order is at risk of collapsing.
This was an era where divine authority was above royal authority, with major sects playing the role of stabilizing the social order.
If the gods underwent changes, then the entire Glory Main Plane would undergo transformations.
After arranging everyone’s tasks, a chilling glint appeared in Lide’s eyes.
“You each complete your tasks.
I need to make a trip to the Underworld,
It’s time those two Extraordinary Spiders were crushed.”

chapters.title: Chapter 396 - Chapter 396: Chapter 398: Suppressing Two Transcendents with One Hand (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 396: Chapter 398: Suppressing Two Transcendents with One Hand (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)
Dawn City, this massive entity, started to rotate at high speed under Lide’s orders.
What caught people’s attention the most was the intensity of foreign trade, which had increased several times over the previous level.
The hoarding of raw materials was even more extreme.
Not only the Dwarf Hills and the Fishman Tribe, but now also the 17th level Beastman Shaman of the Lion Tribe–Morton Mist, this old Beastman Shaman transformed by the Power of Faith under Lide’s influence, had also started to intensify trade with the Beastmen for Demon Beast furs under the orders of City Hall.
Not to mention the Dark Contract and the Crimson Mage Tower located in the bustling districts.
Finished goods stored within the various forces’ warehouses were being exchanged for raw materials at the fastest rate, and in the Crimson Mage Tower, it was even possible to trade magic scrolls directly for the most Basic raw materials.
Moreover, the price for exchanging raw materials for Magic Scrolls was even more favorable, directly attracting a large number of Nobles.
More and more reports of Evil Gods breaking their seals made people feel changes were impending, and in this chaotic and dangerous world, no one who survived was a fool.
Raw materials might be precious in the future, but not as precious as Magic Scrolls that could be transformed into combat power.
So, the Magic Scrolls produced by the Crimson Mage Tower were snapped up by the big Nobles and commerce associations every day, even more enthusiastically than when the Crimson Mage Tower first started selling Magic Scrolls.
While the various forces were carrying out orders, Lide was not idle.
Underworld.
Magic Crystal Vein.
The original Spider Cave, after more than a year of construction, had now become a Solid underground fortress.
The crisscrossing passages had turned into sleek, level standard roads, and several main arteries were even expanded into Super underground channels 30 blades high and 50 blades wide, with large numbers of Magic Language Bats shuttling back and forth each day, transporting the mined Magic Crystal Stones.
At the same time, every 500 blades down each road, a Solid fortress checkpoint was established, with the Magic Crystal Vein securely guarded within.
Most of the troops mining the ore and defending were Beastmen, who had inherited some of the beastly traits and possessed a weakened version of Dark Vision, allowing them to maintain sufficient combat strength in dim environments.
Moreover, Beastmen were strong and resilient, and as long as they had enough food, they wouldn’t complain about mining ore day after day.
However, Lide had no time to inspect the Magic Crystal Veins, which were quite important for Dawn City.
He was standing in front of the space portal to the Spider Plane, his expression quite nuanced.
Once upon a time, this place was his greatest concern; he feared those two spaces would suddenly widen, allowing the two Extraordinary Spiders to emerge and kill.
The Beastmen alone did not have the capacity to face the Extraordinary.
Fortunately, the situation he worried about had never occurred.
“The force the space portal can accommodate still hasn’t reached the level that would allow the Extraordinary to pass through…”
The current space portal to the Spider Plane was like a hole the size of a fist; it was utterly impossible for a normal adult to squeeze through it.
Lide’s brows furrowed slightly.
“The Space Gate used to protect the Magic Crystal Vein… but now it has become an obstacle.”
The Space Gate stood erect on a huge, flat rock wall, with about 30 space portals, each 3 to 4 blades in diameter. Cave Spiders were still continuously crawling out of them.
He had previously used these portals to farm, to gather the Power of Death.
After a brief consideration, Lide didn’t hesitate much and turned to look at Beastman King Kapp by his side.
“Kapp, you lead your men to stand guard here. I’m about to open the space portal, which may result in a flood of Cave Spiders.”
This underground space, after nearly two years of construction, had a defensive system much stronger than that in the Land of Bone-Burying.
He had no concerns about whether it could withstand the assault of the Cave Spiders.
“Your Highness, don’t worry, nothing can break through our defense line!”
Kapp’s tone was firm, his gaze unshakable.
“Good.”
Lide didn’t mince words, and floated directly in front of the rock wall, his sharp gaze locked on the Space Gates.
Moments later, the Power of Crimson on his body flared up like blazing flames, then under the shocked watch of the surrounding Beastmen, the Cave Spiders that just stepped out of the space portal immediately exploded with a bang~ turning into a green mist of blood.
The scene was very shocking.
Dozens of space portals were continuously producing Cave Spiders, each one bursting as they came out, as if the space portal was setting off fireworks.
Death permeated the air.
Lide’s face was cold and indifferent; such a minor scene didn’t rouse the slightest emotional fluctuation in him.
Energy surged from his body like a tide, eroding towards the spatial channel.
The Land of Bone-Burying, having reached an Extraordinary Level, could now extend over the Magic Crystal Vein. Hence, at this moment, he was able to use the power of the Land of Bone-Burying to shake the Spider Plane.
If it were a plane with a master and in pristine condition, even a weaker one compared to the Land of Bone-Burying would not be so easily eroded.
But the problem was that the Spider Plane had long lost its master, nearly shattered, and part of its Plane Power had also been devoured by the Divine Monster Asreaga, making the already collapsing Spider Plane even more dilapidated.
Now, the rules of the Spider Plane were already deficient, its Plane Power continuously leaking out. It would collapse and shatter within a century.
A century seemed long, but for a plane with a life span of hundreds of millions of years, it was no more than the blink of an eye.
How could an aging, dying plane withstand the erosion from the truly flourishing Land of Bone-Burying?
The surging, overwhelming Plane Power, like high-concentration sulfuric acid, caused the surrounding light to distort in an instant as it invaded the Spider Plane.
That indescribable horror clashed and surged upon the rock walls.
Under that pressure, the surrounding air became extremely dense and viscous like mercury, making it difficult for the Beastman Warriors to breathe.
And at the core, Lide stood as though beneath a Heavenly God, radiant and dazzling, continuing to channel the fearsome power in his hands.
He could clearly feel the resistance the Land of Bone-Burying met as it invaded the Spider Plane–the instinctive rejection of the plane. But without anyone to control it, that rejection was like a thin membrane, easily pierced with a light jab.
The space within dozens of blades’ reach around Lide’s domineering power all turned into twisted, shattered spatial fragments, like sharp knives slashing through the air, instantly annihilating anything that came in contact with these spatial pieces.
The scene seemed as if Lide were prepared to destroy a plane, inadvertently causing hearts to tremble.
Finally, upon reaching a certain threshold, Lide’s eyes flared angrily, and his power began to crush down at tenfold strength.
Crack~ Suddenly, the air sounded like shattering glass.
The entire space displayed spiderweb-like fissures, and then, with a crackling sound, it exploded in an instant, scattering countless fine spatial fragments like crystals.
And in this moment, a space rift a hundred blades wide was revealed, and the rancid-smelling Spider Plane appeared before the eyes of the surrounding Beastman Warriors.
This was Kapp’s first encounter with the Spider Plane, but shock was the only word to describe his reaction upon glimpsing this mysterious plane.
The ground of the Spider Plane was covered in a green, oily mycelium, above which were mountains flying upside down in the sky.
Countless Cave Spiders connected the peaks with their webs, with traces of webs throughout the air.
Enormous, fierce Cave Spiders crawled along the connecting webs between the peaks, one line after another.
This image was like a demon’s lair out of ancient mythologies.
It was daunting, chilling to the bone.
And upon sensing the disturbance in space, especially the scent of an external presence, the Cave Spiders roared furiously and surged madly towards the broken spatial channel.
Seeing this, Lide’s heart stirred slightly. He extended his right hand slightly, and under everyone’s gaze, the Space Gate of the Land of Bone-Burying flung wide open.
Like a gaping abyssal maw, it enveloped this irregularly shaped, hundred-blade-wide space door.
The Beastman army, ready for battle, only saw a flash before their eyes as the torn Space Gate vanished from its original spot.
Now all that was in front of them was the mottled rock wall, scarred by the bombardment of spatial fragments. The spatial channel they had been guarding for over a year was now utterly untraceable.
Under Lide’s control, the Land of Bone-Burying forcibly grafted the original channel that anchored the Spider Plane to the Magic Crystal Vein.
In other words, the Spider Plane’s channel that had anchored the Magic Crystal Vein was now anchoring to the Land of Bone-Burying.
From then on, the Cave Spiders could no longer appear in the Magic Crystal Vein. Through the spatial channel, they could only appear in the Land of Bone-Burying.
This forceful alteration of the anchor point would be impossible if the Spider Plane had an owner, but Lide bullied those two Extraordinary Spiders that didn’t have the ability to control the Spider Plane.
“Kapp, you continue to guard here to prevent any accidents,” Lide left behind this cautionary instruction before his body disappeared on the spot.
Kapp could only smile wryly and nod upon seeing this.
With even the Space Gate gone, Lide was clearly not giving them any chance to prove their worth.
Glancing at the still-confused Beastman Warriors beside him, he could only shake his head and put away his fighting blade.
He knew of Lide’s cautious character… For an accident to occur, that would be too difficult.
—-
—-
—-
Land of Bone-Burying.
After the connection between two planes was established, the stench of the Land of Bone-Burying drew cave spiders like mad, as they swarmed into it to slaughter.
The huge tunnel, hundreds of blades wide, provided a vast path for these gruesome creatures.
Hiss~
The sound of the cave spiders was piercing, like a sharp object scraping across glass, enough to give one goosebumps.
Lide hovered in mid-air, his expression unchanged as he watched the scene of spiders flooding the Land of Bone-Burying like locusts, his gaze fixed on the depths of the Spider Plane.
At the moment space shattered, he sensed the presence of the Extraordinary Spider Queen, that Extraordinary Level Ghost-faced Spider Queen was rushing over at a frenzied speed.
“Filthy vermin, you dare to invade Lord Frost’s territory, you dare to defy the master’s dignity!!”
Just as Lide was about to make a move, a haughty voice came from the sky.
Altan, known as Lord Frost, filled the land with his chilling voice.
Lide didn’t know why this Frost Giant Dragon was named Altan but always liked to call himself Lord Frost… Could one’s surname really be addressed by only half of it?
Below him, the thousands of cave spiders that had poured in tensed up when Altan’s voice echoed, as if overwhelmed by some irresistible pressure,
even shivering and cowering on the spot, too afraid to move. Their previously excited, sharp hisses turned into screams of fear.
Extraordinary Dragon Power, those overwhelmed by it would suffer from negative states like fear and panic, with all attributes decreasing by 40%.
The ultimate combat power of the Undead Clan was not something these cave spiders, of which the majority were Level 8 or 9, with a few at Level 10, could compare to.
The superior advantage of giant dragons, an ultimate life form, over lower life forms was displayed to the fullest.
“Taste the flavor of frost~”
Then, with Lide watching, the Extraordinary Giant Dragon, with wings spanning 26 blades, plunged down in a fierce dive attack.
When he was a hundred blades above the ground, he lowered his head, and a white frosty breath flickered in his bony throat, and then whoosh~ crackle~
Above the expanse of a hundred blades in the sky, a breath of absolute zero capable of freezing space itself gushed downwards.
At that moment, Lide could even sense the space in the Land of Bone-Burying visibly stiffen, as if turned into a block of ice.
Absolute zero, freezing space,
those trembling cave spiders below who dared not move were immediately subjected to a brutal assault.
Crackle~
Upon contact with the frosty dragon breath, those ghastly creatures immediately became encased in white frost, frozen rigid on the spot.
Altan’s Frost Dragon Breath not only reached far, with an attack distance of white blades, but its damage area was also astoundingly wide at 50 blades.
Within this range, all cave spiders turned into ice sculptures, reflecting light.
After just three dive attacks from the Frost Giant Dragon Altan, the group of more than 3000 cave spiders had their souls reaped.
By the time the Extraordinary Frost Giant Dragon took flight again, the ground had become a frost domain, with those gruesome, terrifying cave spiders frozen in place with life-like detail.
The spot now resembled a display of large ice sculptures, except that all these sculptures were made of frozen monsters.
Lide took a deep glance at Altan soaring through the air.
This fellow was indeed Extraordinary. If it had been Withered Bone, he would have to descend to an altitude of 30 blades to use dragon breath.
Not to mention the Extraordinary Level, even Frost Giant Dragons of the same level were a cut above Bone Dragons.
Bone Dragons are transformed from dead giant dragons, and in most cases, they do not reach their combat prowess from before death.
But Frost Giant Dragons were different; these terrifying beings were originally Undead Life, created by the main God of the Undead Clan–God of the Undead, a mighty divine being who once fought the Death God, using a part of the Divine Position to create the ultimate military force.
However, during the Battle of the Ancient Gods, the God of the Undead fell, and the Frost Giant Dragon, a terrifying race he had created, gradually perished until their traces were no longer to be seen, thus being forgotten by the world.
This was a presence that could stand shoulder to shoulder with normal giant dragons and even clash head-on, the ultimate killer of the Undead Clan.
Now, this powerful race would once again reveal its edge in Lide’s hands.
Lide also believed that once he found a few suitable sources of pigs, the race of Frost Giant Dragons would inevitably reappear in swarms, becoming the sharpest blade in his arsenal.
As for the source of piglets, he had one right in front of him at this moment.
His eagerness to conquer the Spider Plane and seek revenge on that Extraordinary Spider that had killed him was one thing, but more importantly–there was no better place for pig farming than the Spider Plane in the short term.
However, before that, he had to eliminate the hidden dangers here–two Extraordinary creatures.
As for whether to subjugate or crush them, that would be decided after he had turned the tables on them.
A cold glint flashed in his eyes.
The power lying dormant within him began to awaken slowly due to his fighting spirit, bubbling through his veins like lava.
After breaking through to the Transcendent level, Lide hadn’t had the time to test his strength. Now, these two Extraordinary Spiders were undoubtedly going to become the whetstone for his blade.
Killing intent surged.
Hiss~
After Altan ascended, a prolonged hissing sound came from the depths of the Spider Plane.
The Cave Spiders, which had been intimidated by the dragon’s power, now surged in spirit as if injected with dragon blood, greatly increasing their resistance to the dragon’s aura; these grotesque creatures then advanced towards the Land of Bone-Burying like a tidal wave once again.
Their ferocious and twisted faces sent chills as if lifting off one’s scalp.
“Have you finally shown up?”
Sensing the terrifying presence within the Spider Plane drawing nearer, Lide narrowed his eyes slightly.
“Altan, clean up all the Cave Spiders entering the Land of Bone-Burying.
But do not enter the Spider Plane… these spiders can only die in the Land of Bone-Burying.”
“As you command, my master… These insignificant vermin shall become icicles in the mouth of the great Lord Frost!”
The arrogant voice echoed, the Transcendent Giant Dragon displaying overwhelming prowess.
Lide’s mouth twitched slightly, too lazy to bother with this creature. He stepped forward, and in the blink of an eye, appeared before the space rift, then leisurely stepped into the Spider Plane.
Leaving the Land of Bone-Burying, the sensation of the heavens and earth revolving around him dissipated, but the aura emanating from him grew even more terrifying.
Level 23, Transcendent, with the golden Ancestor Bloodline.
Any one of these terms could chill someone to the bone.
At this moment, he was the greatest terror of this Plane.
The already unstable space of the Spider Plane rippled like a boulder striking a lake’s surface and even began fracturing with cracks, as Lide entered.
The power within his body was putting unbearable strain on this Plane.
Lide, with an eagle-like gaze, surveyed everything around him.
The Spider Plane’s landscape remained unchanged, mountains floating upside down in the sky with white spider webs, sticky with mucus, forming aerial corridors that connected them.
A string of Cave Spiders hung like candied haws on the web, making a sizzling sound due to the mucus on the webs as they moved, an utterly disgusting sound to hear.
The Plane’s lighting was dim, as if thick clouds had covered the sun, and the air was filled with an indescribable stench of blood. It was the unique smell of spiders, nauseating.
Hiss~
The densely packed Cave Spiders all around had now completely surrounded the intruding Lide, each letting out fierce hisses as they sensed an aura not belonging to them.
In such a terrifying environment, even a veteran soldier with a strong psyche would feel weak in the knees.
Pop~Pop~
Suddenly, a few sounds broke the silence in the air, as if signaling an attack. The Cave Spiders hanging from the web abruptly bent their enormous abdomens, their mouthparts aimed at Lide, and then they began to spew webbing.
Thousands of Cave Spiders spat out their webs simultaneously, creating a spectacle as the cobwebs enveloped Lide like bird catchers, each web laced with a deadly poison that was terribly pungent.
The stench in the air became intolerably pungent in an instant.
But Lide, ignoring the webs that could drown a giant dragon, vanished on the spot with a single step.
A few breaths later, when Lide reappeared, he had already traversed thousands of blades into the Spider Plane, far from the spatial rift encircled by hundreds of thousands of Cave Spiders.
But at the moment of his arrival, a terrifying aura surrounded him.
Lide’s gaze became sharp as a blade’s edge, fiercely turning towards a mountain on his right. It was three hundred blades high, with a large top and small bottom, wrapped in countless webs, and suspended in the sky.
He sensed it, the presence of the Extraordinary Spider Queen.
At that moment, Lide didn’t hesitate in the slightest.
Bloodline shackles, released.
Golden Ancestor bloodline, activated.
Booming thunder~
It was like thunder ripping through the clouds.
Crack~ Crack~ It was just like ancient chains that sealed the heavens and earth swaying within his body, and then, the Power of Crimson, which was like a dragon hiding beneath the water’s surface, erupted with a bang.
Power exploded like a volcano suppressed for eons, the magma it spurted reaching tens of thousands of feet high.
Lide’s body, which had been cleansed and transformed countless times by divine energy, not only did not collapse under this terrifying power, but completely accommodated this indescribable strength.
Heaven and earth were both shocked.
Lide felt that at this moment, he could tear apart the heavens and shatter the rivers with a mere gesture.
