Over the past month, the army of Dawn City had centered on Twilight City and was spreading furiously in all directions, conquering or annihilating many tribes of the Dark Race.
Particularly, the Nagas, personally ordered by Lide, had become the primary target of all the armies’ aggressive hunts, causing the Nagas to be extremely vigilant. Many times their traces had been discovered, only to have them escape.
But now, everything was proceeding too smoothly, which made Anthony feel something was amiss.
“Aimon, tell me exactly how you discovered these Naga traces?”
Upon hearing the question, a young warrior named Aimon next to him spoke, “Yes, sir. Five Sunshine Hours ago, I heard from a few captured dwarves that traces of Nagas had been seen in this thicket. Then I brought people here to verify the traces were from Nagas, and immediately reported back to you…”
“You heard about the Naga traces from captured dwarves? Not from the intelligence department?”
Anthony frowned, his unease growing instantly, “Why didn’t you tell me from the start?”
“Sir, you were busy organizing the army and I didn’t get a chance to report to you in detail. Besides, our intelligence agents also provided us with the same information later.”
Aimon hurriedly explained.
After hearing this, Anthony’s expression eased slightly, but he still felt something was off. Dwarves, although clever, were too physically weak; their individual strength was only comparable to that of the Cave Dwellers.
If the Nagas wanted to deceive them, it would be all too easy.
There was definitely a problem here, Anthony immediately issued a command.
“Retreat from this thicket immediately, have the Magic Language Bats provide support, deploy the Air Force for search.”
Hearing this order, everyone was taken aback, but seeing Anthony’s solemn expression, they immediately responded; as the commander of this army, Anthony’s authority was supremely high, and there was no question of disobedience.
But just as Aimon and a few messengers were preparing to carry out the orders, suddenly a distant scream came.
“Ah!!!”
At that moment, Anthony’s hair stood on end as he sharply turned towards the direction of the scream.
“The right flank of the army is under attack, send out the signal, everyone get ready for battle!”
Aimon’s face turned pale; he immediately put a strange military whistle in his mouth, and moments later a shrill sound traveled several kilometers.
Hearing the whistle, the warriors immediately went on alert, swords drawn, crossbows cocked.
But the situation plunged into chaos no one could have predicted. Just two or three breaths after that scream sounded, constant screams came in from both flanks.
Confronted with the sudden attack, Anthony did not panic and decisively gave another order.
“Let the troops on both flanks gather to the center, form up around me!”
In such a scenario, blindly charging in any direction could suffer severe repercussions. Consolidating strength and then breaking through was the optimal response.
After issuing the second command, the people from both flanks quickly closed in.
“What happened?”
“Lord Anthony, Naga, a lot of Naga, they used magic to disguise themselves, we are surrounded by these Nagas!!”
“Surrounded??” Anthony’s expression turned graver, “Can you determine the approximate strength of the enemy?”
“Not sure, they’re hidden too well; we can’t make out their figures.”
“Aimon, has the distress signal been sent?”
“It has been sent.”
“Good, immediately assemble the formation, archers hold the center, I’ll lead the charge, spellcasters get ready to cast, we’ll break through from the right flank.”
Anthony issued another command; retreating the same way was clearly too risky, as he couldn’t determine how many enemy forces were in ambush.
Instead, it would be better to break out from a flank, managing a breakthrough could mean a chance at life.
Orders were swiftly obeyed, the troops quickly formed up and charged towards the flank.
On the way, Anthony briefly counted the number of people gathered, which was just over 200. This meant that in just over a minute, a third of the warriors had been killed.
This weighed heavily on Anthony’s heart.
The number of Naga exceeded his expectations. If they didn’t handle this situation correctly, these warriors, including himself, might not make it back alive.
But as the commander, Anthony still maintained his usual extraordinary calm.
The intent to kill began to gather in his eyes, his fighting spirit soared.
No matter how many Naga were ambushed, since they dared to come, he dared to kill!
The Cross Longsword in his hand, engraved with blooming irises, sensed Anthony’s fighting spirit. The patterns on it flowed slowly like water, filled with an indescribable mystery.
The Fearless Holy Sword, only a fearless warrior could unleash its greatest power.
Soon, after Anthony ordered a breakthrough, the first collision began.
The air on the right flank was filled with a nauseating stench of blood that hit their noses even before they arrived.
Fear, like a venomous snake, tried to devour the heart of every warrior.
But Anthony, fearless as always, charged forward.
Crack~
After crossing a short bush, like ghosts, dozens of four-armed Naga wielding longswords suddenly appeared.
Their long snake-like bodies, cold gaze, and the dark red spines on their back spelled the terror of their race.
Neither side exchanged any unnecessary words.
“Kill!”
A single word, and blood suddenly flew.
Anthony, holding his sword vertically in front of his chest, rushed directly towards the Naga charging at the front.
The four-armed Naga was terrifyingly frightening, their four longswords swinging in unison. It was daunting enough to make even five men sweat in fear facing them.
But Anthony was without fear, his sharp gaze like a hawk hunting a lamb.
His body, like a spring compressed to the limit, suddenly burst forth with terrifying power in two steps forward, and Anthony could already see the fierce expression on the Naga’s face.
The strength of his arms transferred to the Fearless Holy Sword, and with a flash of cold light.
Anthony’s Longsword cleaved downward, the Naga swung their swords to block,
But, their weapons were not in the same league.
The four longswords were severed as easily as tofu, crack~ The Naga’s face showed a hint of panic, but he was too late to react.
One sword split the Nine Layers of Heaven.
The body split in two.
Blood sprayed several sword-lengths high.
A splashy trail of fresh blood appeared on Anthony’s face.
“For Dawn!”
After slaying a four-armed Naga, Anthony roared aloud.
“Kill!”
The blood clearly boosted the morale. Following Anthony’s roar, the warriors also charged and screamed at the Naga.
A bloody clash unknown to anyone else unfolded in the depths of the obscure bushes.

chapters.title: Chapter 402 - Chapter 402: Chapter 404: Lend Me Your Head for a Blood Sacrifice to My 300 Warriors at Dawn
chapters.content:
Chapter 402: Chapter 404: Lend Me Your Head for a Blood Sacrifice to My 300 Warriors at Dawn
No one could describe just how terrifying it was to battle a four-armed Naga in the dim light.
As an Upper Race, the Nagas possessed a battle strength beyond common imagination. When all four arms slashed their long knives simultaneously, even the thickest shields were no more than foam.
At this moment, Anthony also encountered an unprecedented obstacle.
The Fearless Holy Sword, with its faint glow, became a terrifying blade of slaughter with its unparalleled sharpness.
But it still wasn’t enough.
Even though he was an inheritor of the Heart of Fearlessness and his combat strength seemed invincible when beset by a frenzied siege, the soldiers at his side were not the same.
These warriors, although they were the elite trained by Dawn City, clad in full armor and wielding sharp weapons,
were still reaped like wheat when facing the four-armed Nagas.
The disparity was too great.
Born and bred in a harsh environment, the Nagas, in terms of battle strength or experience, were far stronger than the warriors of Dawn City.
“Kill!”
A young warrior roared and lunged directly at the four-armed Naga attacking from the opposite side, his longsword slashing down fiercely.
Clang~
The sound of metal clashing exploded as the Naga’s two long knives crossed and blocked the deadly attack.
In the narrow green eyes, killer intent was fierce. In the moment of collision, the other two arms did not remain idle–one arm wielding a long knife sliced straight through the young warrior’s abdomen.
Sparks flew.
The high-level armor blocked the fatal blow, and a look of relief appeared on the young warrior’s face. He withdrew his sword for a counterstrike, but as he prepared for a second attack,
Pfft~ the fourth arm, holding a long knife, slashed directly through the armor gap at his neck.
Blood sprayed forth.
In close combat, the advantages of the Upper Race, the four-armed Nagas, were just too great.
Two fists were hard-pressed against four hands, not to mention that Nagas of the same level could still overwhelm human warriors with their crushing battle strength.
It was an innate trait of the Upper Race–the Naga’s bloodline was far stronger than that of humans. Only a higher level or a stronger bloodline could eliminate such disparity.
But reality was always brutal–Dawn City could equip every warrior with high-level armor and weapons, but it was impossible to grant every warrior a bloodline of the Upper Race.
Talent was the most unreasonable thing.
“Rally to me!”
After slaying a Naga, Anthony roared. By now, his armor was stained red with blood, which fell like droplets, with black armor marked by the most lurid and bloodstained traces.
As the sole spearhead of this squad, the warrior wielding the Fearless Holy Sword, he faced the greatest pressure, even having to confront several Nagas’ assaults at once.
Every step forward was taken over the bodies of slain Nagas.
Fortunately, though strong, Anthony was no less a match for anyone.
Each time the Fearless Holy Sword in his hand swung, it was bathed in blood.
Extraordinary combat awareness, formidable combat skills, coupled with an unimaginable Danger Perception.
This inheritor of a Legendary profession was the most Fearless Warrior.
Blood, severed limbs, death–these became the main theme at that moment.
The battle continued.
Dawn City’s troops couldn’t provide support in a short time– they could only rely on themselves.
But there were too many, and the surrounding Nagas only increased, not decreased, as they attempted to break out.
Anthony no longer had the energy to look after the surrounding warriors. When the number of Nagas vastly outnumbered them, everything became uncontrollable.
The number of warriors around him dwindled, fewer and fewer…
Anthony’s breathing grew heavier as well.
Each hard-fought slash of the longsword drained a tremendous amount of strength, from unrivaled dominance at the beginning to a progressively heavier advance.
By the end, Anthony no longer knew how much time had passed; the number of Nagas he had killed was uncountable.
Escape.
That was the only thought.
But as time wore on, his robust body began to exhibit an indescribable weakness, the plentiful strength within him ebbing away.
He was about to collapse.
Yet even so, Anthony’s gaze remained unwavering.
Only those with the courage to face certain death were worthy to wield the Fearless Holy Sword.
No one could stop the charge of a Dawn Warrior, no matter who they were.
But the gap in strength between the two sides was too great.
Was it possible for these three hundred men to break through a trap meticulously laid by the Nagas?
One after another, human warriors were slain by the sharp-bladed four-armed Nagas, and the sound of battle in the air grew ever fainter.
Until at last, only Anthony’s figure remained in the battlefield of bushes and grasses.
Three hundred warriors, none survived…
When Anthony felt that there were no more warriors from Dawn City left alive around him, his eyes were filled with unspeakable sadness and anger.
Kill!
The longsword in his hand became even more ferocious.
The formidable Nagas around him were reaped like wheat by an explosively raging Anthony.
The sharp longsword meant all Nagas could not collide with it a second time, their war knives shattered, their bodies burst.
At that moment, Anthony became the scythe of the Death God, recklessly reaping the lives of the Nagas.
After consecutively slaughtering 57 Nagas, he suddenly stepped on a corpse and staggered.
In that instant, Anthony felt an unspeakably terrifying crisis coming from behind. Just as he thought to dodge, two four-armed Nagas lunged forward from the front, ignoring the edge of the Fearless Holy Sword, and entangled him in the most ferocious way.
Swinging the longsword,
a slash~ two heads rose at the same time, whoosh~ from the darkness, a Naga released the bowstring, the arrow streaking across the sky with fatal momentum.
Thud~
Blood spurted.
Terrifying agony engulfed Anthony,
He had been shot!
The moment this thought arose, the Fearless Warrior forcefully turned his head to look around, only to find himself surrounded by Four-Armed Nagas.
There was no way out.
The warriors who had followed him were nowhere to be seen.
The entire army had been annihilated.
The warriors he led were now forever sleeping in this land.
War was always brutal with no mercy to spare.
Wars fought for survival space made this brutality tenfold, a hundredfold worse.
Rage and sorrow were consuming Anthony’s heart at this moment.
Huff~huff~
But he was too tired; right now Anthony could only feel the heavy breathing that seemed to echo in his ears, layer upon layer,
The shouts and clashing blades around him had faded away, and besides his own breathing, he could only feel his heart pounding…
Is it ending now?
As the Nagas closed in, Anthony’s arm shook uncontrollably as he gripped the Fearless Holy Sword; he could even clearly see the vicious and murderous look in the eyes of the Naga opposite him.
In the face of encirclement by hundreds, even thousands of Nagas, no one here could escape, neither his warriors nor he himself, even while wielding the Fearless Holy Sword…
At this moment, an image of an old man who had been with him all his life–Uncle Jike–flashed in Anthony’s mind, and he remembered the words that had changed his life.
“Anthony, being a soldier is a very painful thing; are you truly prepared?”
“You will witness your comrades die in battle, see your brothers fall as they shield you from the enemy’s weapons,
You might even be ordered to kill some defenseless innocent people, brushing shoulders with death every day; you will be the executioner, the butcher that everyone despises!!
You will live under the shadow of war and death for your entire life, never able to escape.
Are you ready for that?”
Whoosh~
Ptui~
An incredibly sharp arrow pierced through his chest, Anthony’s body lurched forward involuntarily, and the blood in his mouth spewed out uncontrollably.
At this moment, he could no longer feel the pain; exhaustion and weakness had numbed his senses.
Anthony’s lips trembled uncontrollably, his body like a wild grass in a fierce wind, seemingly ready to collapse at any moment, his eyes even seeing double as they looked forward.
“Uncle Jike… I, have no regrets…”
Like a vow, Anthony whispered in his heart at the brink of collapse, then gazed at the Naga in front of him and slowly raised the Fearless Holy Sword, positioning it in front of his chest.
“For Dawn…”
His voice was weak but resolutely firm as it echoed across the bloody battlefield, the fearless aura momentarily causing the surrounding Four-Armed Nagas to pause.
A Warrior’s Requiem.
Return with one’s body.
Anthony let out a final roar and charged straight into the Four-Armed Nagas ahead.
A Dawn Warrior, even in death, would fall on the charge.
Behind him lay the glory of Dawn City, the expectations of everyone.
Fearless and dauntless.
Charge.
Time around him seemed to slow down by thousands of times, as the figure holding the Cross Longsword ignited his own life, unleashing his final strength to charge into the mass of Four-Armed Nagas.
Blood splattered.
When there was no fear left in the heart, no matter how numerous or strong the enemy, no matter how sharp their swords or terrifying their daggers,
They were as nothing.
—-
—-
—-
—-
Upon a small hill far from the battlefield, a few especially intimidating Four-Armed Nagas witnessed the scene with subtle expressions.
The leader, with a crown made of flesh-growths on his head, showed a slight admiration in his narrow eyes upon seeing Anthony not retreat in face of death.
“Unexpectedly, these lowly surface dwellers also possess such courage!
This human warrior has earned my respect, and so I plan… after his death, to personally deliver his body to the Abyss Mouth for consumption, just as this despicable Dark Night Elf.”
After speaking, he turned his head toward the other Nagas, among whom a Dark Night Elf, bound at the hands and covered in scars, was particularly eye-catching.
The captive Dark Night Elf had long, pointed ears and black eyes, with dim, grayish-white skin–a color distinct from that of other elves, well-suited for camouflaging in the Underworld environment.
Her beauty was almost perfect like other elves, only marred by the scars on her body.
“Clan Leader, Lord Austin requires us to conquer the Dark Night Elves’ territory and enslave these wretched lives,
This Dark Night Elf is the daughter of their matriarch; we could use her for greater gains…”
“The mother of the Dark Night Elves?”
The leading Naga with a fleshy crown subconsciously touched a subtle scar on his face, his eyes flashing coldly with murderous intent.
“Damn bastard, one day, we the Black Scale Naga will enslave that despicable race and take everything from them!!”
“Hmph, pitiful Nagas, the Dark Night Elves are blessed by the great Spider Queen; even if you side with that damned Black Dragon, it’s in vain.
The Black Dragon from the Mud Swamp is but a worm in the mud before our exalted Rose. Effortlessly crushed.”
The scar-covered Dark Night Elf displayed a hint of scorn, her tone undiminished by her predicament.
The pride of the Dark Night Elves was not inferior to that of surface elves, only that their love was for slaughter and conspiracy…
Hearing this, the reaction of the Naga with the fleshy crown turned exceedingly cold, his narrow eyes resembling a demon preparing to hunt.
“The power possessed by Lord Austin is beyond the imagination of you lowly beings.
Rose… the Spider Queen might be powerful, but will she answer your call? Can she descend upon us?”
“In the Underworld, only under the reign of Austin can one find an invincible existence!”
Although the darkly famed and mighty Evil God, the master of the Dark Night Elves, the God of Conspiracy–Spider Queen Rose–is deeply feared by the crest-headed Naga,
The fact remains that the Underworld is not an endless abyss, and no matter how powerful Spider Queen Rose is, she cannot truly descend; here, the mighty Black Dragon reigns supreme.
Furthermore, the followers of Spider Queen Rose are numerous, and the common Dark Night Elf tribes have no qualification to earn the attention of such a powerful divine Evil God.
“Hmph, ignorant fools, can you not comprehend the might of Spider Queen?”
The mockery on the Dark Night Elf’s face grew thicker.
The crest-headed Naga did not speak again, but the murderous aura emanating from him multiplied dramatically.
If this Dark Night Elf weren’t of use to him, he would flay her flesh piece by piece and devour her soul!
“Keep her alive and bring her back. I have already arranged everything. As soon as those surface dwellers probe this far, they will inevitably discover the territory of the Dark Night Elves…”
A chill and cruelty flashed in his eyes, “Once the surface dwellers clash with the Dark Night Elves, we will completely eradicate both powers.
When we seize the Tree of Life from the Dark Night Elves, it will be the beginning of Naga rule over the Underworld…
As for Austin, it will become our spearhead to break through the Half-Elf cities, killing their Transcendents…
Everything, will belong to the Naga, the glorious Naga!!”
The bound Dark Night Elf’s complexion changed upon hearing these words; she hadn’t expected that the ultimate goal of these Naga was to instigate calamity, hoping for the powerful force that had suddenly emerged a month ago to collide with the Dark Night Elves, while the Naga reaped the benefits from the shadows,
“No, you will not succeed!!”
“Not succeed?
Believe me, no one can resist the temptation of the Tree of Life!
Not even those surface humans, they would give everything to deal with you even if they knew it was our doing…
Truly, how amusing…”
The tone of the crest-headed Naga was especially chilling, making one shiver.
—-
—-
—-
—-
Anthony was on the brink of being devoured by the Naga, despite the sharpness of the Fearless Holy Sword and his valiance. There comes a time when even the mightiest warrior exhausts his strength, especially a Fearless Warrior with an arrow piercing through his chest.
He couldn’t hold on any longer.
The light in Anthony’s eyes began to fade slowly.
The Secret Technique activated by the sacrifice of his life could no longer sustain him.
Taking a deep breath, Anthony looked around and saw the corpses of at least a hundred Naga at his feet.
His heart regained calmness.
Up to this point in the battle, he had no more yearnings.
His only regret was that he might never see Uncle Jack again,
Nor the girl who was still waiting for his triumphant return.
I’m sorry, Miss Grey.
Blood smeared Anthony’s pale face, and his unfocused eyes carried remorse and reluctance.
I’ve broken my promise…
Next season of revival,
I won’t be able to accompany you to see the hills blooming with irises…
How I wish, I could go see them with you one more time…
From afar, the crest-headed Naga saw that teetering figure, standing strong but on the verge of collapse, and his expression turned cold.
Without the slightest pity or pause, the cold voice of the Naga echoed through the sky.
“Kill that human, then bring his corpse!”
After the order was given, the Naga previously terrified by Anthony’s onslaught rushed forward unrestrained like maniacs, all pouncing toward the figure, flickering like a candle in the wind.
Anthony’s visions were already blurry, and he could only faintly hear the terrifying, strange roars surrounding him.
Whoosh~
As hundreds of Naga surged forward like a tempest, they engulfed the small boat that was Anthony.
An inevitable outcome.
The crest-headed Naga narrowed his eyes at the scene; while he appreciated the human’s bravery, he would not hesitate for a moment.
Besides, but an ant after all, however strong, was just a weak life to be crushed at his whim.
Lifting his head slightly, the murderous intent in his elongated eyes eased a bit, and with a wave of his hand, he instructed his subordinates to pick up the Dark Night Elf and prepare to leave.
A few Naga guards emanating a terrifying aura picked up the bound Dark Night Elf and followed suit.
But just at that moment, an incredibly terrifying fluctuation suddenly came from behind.
The crest-headed Naga’s body shuddered; he felt as if he was being targeted by an ancient giant dragon that had opened its eyes.
Goosebumps rose.
He slowly turned his head and then witnessed an unforgettable, mythological scene.
The ethereal figure of a three-hundred-blade-tall Cross Longsword stood towering in the sky.
The vibrant sword shadows of irises bloomed, like the vigorous growth of plants during the season of revival.
The aura emanating from the longsword shadow was like a plane shattering and collapsing; even Transcendents would blanch at its power.
“What is this?!!!!!”
A shock beyond control flashed in the eyes of the crest-headed Naga.
Could it be that very human he considered nothing more than an ant?
Then,
Puchi~ In the center of the area overwhelmed by the Naga, a dazzling brilliance burst forth, and the Sword Qi tore through heaven and earth.
Annihilation of all things.
The Naga that had just swarmed were like melted snow in the face of the indescribable, terrifying Sword Qi, reduced to fragments.
Within twenty blades’ length, not a single blade of grass remained.
Under the gaze of all the Nagas, a figure, armor shattered, his body covered in knife scars, and even an arrow piercing through his chest, appeared in front of everyone.
But unlike the near-death state he was in before, right now an indescribably formidable power was emanating from his body.
The sword qi, sharp as daggers, swept across, and even solid, thick shields would instantly be ground into dust under its might.
What was even more eye-catching was that the Cross Longsword in his hand was slightly glowing, its form identical to the massive shadow of the Cross Longsword towering three hundred blades tall in the sky.
The human, at this moment, was still closing his eyes.
From afar, the crested Naga’s face revealed an undeniable greed upon witnessing this.
That Longsword, it must be an exceptional weapon, at the very least a piece of Legendary Equipment, and perhaps even– a Divine Artifact.
With this thought, his heart began to pound violently.
“Kill him and seize the Longsword in his hands!”
Just a Low-level human after all; he must have only temporarily triggered the weapon; there’s no way he could truly wield an item of such a high level!!
Thus, this Longsword could only belong to him!
The Naga language echoed through the heavens and the earth; the Nagas who had been in awe moments ago once again surged with murderous intent, their low roars emanating from their throats as they all charged forward together.
But just as the group of Nagas approached within twenty blades’ reach of Anthony, those tightly shut eyes suddenly burst open at that moment.
Light rocketed to the skies.
The image of the Fearless Holy Sword was in his pupils, and where his gaze traveled, it seemed as if space itself was shattering.
And then,
The grand shadow of the three-hundred-blade-long Holy Sword in the cosmos suddenly plunged down towards Anthony.
Zzzt~
As if the sky had collapsed and the earth had sunken, boundless sword qi was distorting the space at that moment.
But when the shadow of the Holy Sword stabbed down, it didn’t harm Anthony at all; instead, like melting snow, it instantly dissolved into a terrifying force and entered his body.
The aura surrounding Anthony steadily ascended.
But this,
Was just the beginning.
When the last light of the Holy Sword’s shadow melted into his body, Anthony began to slightly squint his eyes.
His look was sharp as a blade’s edge.
Staring at the Four-Armed Nagas still rushing forward heedlessly, he straightaway lifted the Fearless Holy Sword in his right hand.
At this moment, the energy within Anthony’s body burst forth like a volcanic eruption, and the very shadow of the Holy Sword he had devoured re-emerged, centering on the Cross Longsword in his hand,
And in the blink of an eye, a three-hundred-blade-long shadow coalesced, with its massive blade pointing outward, and Anthony stood at the very hilt of this Longsword.
The sword qi at this moment overshadowed the heavens and the earth, all stars seemed prostrate at its feet.
The surrounding Nagas’ complexions instantly changed upon seeing this terrifying scene.
But before anyone could react, Anthony’s right hand swung the Fearless Holy Sword.
And then,
There it swept across the ground–the Holy Sword’s shadow, three hundred blades long, thirty blades wide, and twenty blades tall, formed entirely from the sword qi that Tore Space.
It was like a scene from the myths when the War God descended.
Even the most battle-hardened bards would be dumbfounded by such a spectacle.
Seemingly divine,
Anthony’s swinging Longsword was like a stick sweeping ants off the ground; three-blade-tall Nagas appearing as fragile as eggs beneath the shadow of the Holy Sword.
Thud~
Zzzt~
Blood, limbs, grass, and stones.
Wherever the Longsword swept, everything shattered.
The ground collapsed, vegetation flattened, and rocks turned to dust.
The dense positions of the Nagas, upon encountering the Holy Sword’s shadow burst apart into blood mist under the fearsome sword qi.
It was not sharpness that killed the enemy, but rather an indescribable, unspeakable terror brought by the sword qi.
The sword qi shadow in Anthony’s hand was like a galaxy, with this peerless and invincible object traversing the heavens now in his grasp.
With the heavenly Holy Sword in his palm, he swung and extinguished the stars.
Everything around turned to ash, and when Anthony turned for the first time, everything within a radius of three hundred blades around him had been leveled to the ground.
Boulders, shrubs, the earth… shattered and collapsed.
And those thousands of Nagas had now become nothing but a cloud of blood mist.
When Anthony ceased his hand, the scene fell into a deathly silence; their own breathing was the only sound at that moment.
The remaining Nagas’ eyes widened, fixated on the scene, their faces filled with indescribable shock and incredulity.
How could this be possible??!!!
Thousands of mighty Nagas, all slain by a single sword stroke?!!
Had the human been possessed by a deity??
At the heart of countless gazes, Anthony suddenly seemed to sense something, whirling his head around sharply to see the crested Naga hundreds of blades distant.
Their eyes met.
His eyes, swirling with sword qi, were now icy cold.
The crested Naga felt a piercing chill invading his mind, making his scalp tingle.
Then, a phrase from the other caused a cold shiver to run from his back straight to his skull.
“I am the successor of the Heart of Fearlessness; today, by your head, I offer a Blood Sacrifice for my three hundred Dawn Warriors.”
With those words ended,
The three-hundred-blade-long shadow impossibly thrust forth from the void.
As it passed, the world dimmed, and mountains nearly crumbled.
Everywhere the sword shadow traveled, there was nothingness.

chapters.title: Chapter 403 - Chapter 403: Chapter 405: When Players Gain the Power of the Evil God...
chapters.content:
Chapter 403: Chapter 405: When Players Gain the Power of the Evil God…
“Great Twilight Sovereign, I am your most loyal servant, and I offer you rich flesh and blood as a sacrifice, humbly beseeching a sliver of power as a reward.
Praise be to you, ruler of ancient days, eternal Twilight Sovereign…”
In a small town about two hundred kilometers from Green City, a gloomy voice slowly emanated from a cellar corner of a dark, dilapidated manor.
If commoners heard this terrifying intonation, they would undoubtedly fall into madness.
For this was the prayer of Evil God believers, an offering to those malevolent beings lurking in the abyss, the most chilling horror to the bone.
But just outside the cellar, the idle chatter of two bored young men seemed to dispel much of this malicious atmosphere.
“Big Head, do you think it’s true that my girlfriend said she was staying over at her bestie’s house last night?”
The voice made it clear that they were two adventurers from the Lost Plane–those famously known as–silly players.
The player dressed as a Mage couldn’t help but curl his lips disdainfully, “Your girlfriend staying at her bestie’s? Why would you doubt something like that?”
The assassin player seemed hesitant, “But when I called her, she said she was out jogging, her voice was always breathless, and it sounded like a bed or a dresser was rhythmically thumping in the background… And she didn’t want to video chat, why do you think that is?”
The Mage player’s expression stiffened, waving his hand, “You’re overthinking it, when you’re jogging, it’s easy to bump into stuff, right?”
The assassin player furrowed his eyebrows even tighter, “Is that so?”
The Mage player quickly responded, “Of course, why would I lie to you? We’re brothers, aren’t we?”
The assassin player let out a deep sigh, “But her bestie stayed over at my house last night…”
The Mage player’s face froze again, looking at him incredulously, “Say that again?”
The assassin player glanced at him, dismissively saying, “Why would I lie to you, that’s why I’m wondering…”
The Mage player exploded with anger, “Damn it! Isn’t your girlfriend’s bestie my girlfriend’s bestie???”
The assassin player’s expression stiffened, slightly confused, “Really? Didn’t you break up with your girlfriend?”
“Shit, if I don’t beat you to shit today, I’ll kneel and call you Daddy…” The Mage player could never have imagined the fire was going to burn himself.
Leaping to his feet, the magic in his hands began to surge with anger.
“Stop, stop~ Holy shit, we’re all brothers, it doesn’t need to come to this,”
“Brothers my ass, if it wasn’t for me sleeping with your girlfriend last night, I’d be the sucker today!”
“What?? You bastard! You’re the one??!! I knew something was off with you last night!! Damn it, I’m going to kill you today!!”
The two idiots sprang up, roaring and ready to fight, when suddenly from the cellar they were guarding, a figure in black priest’s robes stepped out.
Seeing the two players behaving as if they were fighting to the death, he became extremely angry.
“What the hell are you doing?! Pack up, we’re leaving. Tonight’s ritual is done; just one more sacrifice to that stupid Ancient God and we’ll be rolling in it.”
Still unwilling to back off, they glared at each other.
“Boss, this bastard stole my girlfriend!”
“Boss, he’s the one who started it!!”
“It’s him!!”
“…”
After listening for a while, the priest player curled his lips in displeasure, “What are you bickering about? Over such a trivial matter?
I’ll take you to Heaven on Earth tonight and get each of you three oirans, what more could you want?!”
The two immediately lit up at the mention–three?
After exchanging a glance, they both snorted coldly, retracted their weapons, and said no more.
The priest player, not caring about the details, excitedly announced,
“I’ve already won the trust of the Ancient Evil God. Just one more sacrifice of a thousand people and we can become the spokespeople for this damn kid.”
“A thousand people? Boss, where are we going to find so many people?”
Though the assassin player was still rankled, he held back and asked, “And a mass evil sacrifice will surely alert the churches in the city.
Recently, with the Fierce Half-Ratmen running amok outside Green City, those NPCs are terrifyingly strong. If our identity as Evil God believers is exposed, we’ll definitely be stuck at the Life Goddess’ temple’s resurrection point with no way out.
Damn, these NPCs are pissing me off, blocking the resurrection points like that!!
What a bullshit game, not giving any way out!!”
The more the assassin player spoke, the angrier he got. What kind of game has NPCs block players’ resurrection points to kill them?
But this broken game allowed it, and if the NPCs got feisty, blocking for ten days to half a month was normal.
Last time he tried flirting with a noble NPC and accidentally revealed his Evil God believer identity, he was trapped half a month without leaving the Life Goddess’ temple and almost went crazy with anger.
The priest player chuckled, “Do you remember our last experiment?”
“Our last experiment?” The Mage player’s eyes brightened up at the mention, “Are you talking about the experiment using players as sacrifices?”
“Exactly! We can’t do NPC sacrifices, but using players is possible!!” The priest rubbed his chin, his smile growing increasingly twisted.
“NPCs are tough to deal with, but aren’t players tough too?”
“Boss, what are you planning to do?”
“How? By throwing money around, of course! I might have nothing else, but I’m rich. Just you watch, I’ve already sold twelve properties, and I’m ready to go big on this one!”
“Boss, really? You sold your property?”
“Yeah, I’m holding on to the other hundred or so for now.”
“Damn…”
After discussing for a moment, the priest player suddenly seemed to remember something and asked curiously, “Have you heard of Lord Kachar?”
“Lord Kachar?” Both players were perplexed.
“Is that an NPC? Being addressed with ‘Lord’–could they be Transcendent?”
The priest player shook his head, “No, it’s not an NPC. That Ancient Evil God just asked me about Lord Kachar…
But what do I know about Lord Kachar? Even the Twilight Sovereign ordered me to find traces of Lord Kachar after hearing that.”
Having said that and stroking his chin, he looked pensive, “I asked the other side, and although the Twilight Sovereign didn’t explain why, they seemed quite angry.
I suspect this is another epic Super Quest.
Think about it, the Ancient Evil Gods are about to descend soon.
And these powerful gods are urging me to do this before their descent–what does that tell you? It means this matter is extremely urgent to them, they can’t wait any longer.
Also, the title ‘Lord’ is presumably designated for those above Transcendent.
And judging by the way they asked, I deduce that Lord Kachar must have offended some Ancient Evil God, and they can’t even wait a day to deal with him.
So for our next mission, we must not only carry out the Blood Sacrifice to gain the Ancient Evil God’s power but also seek out information on Lord Kachar.”
Hearing this, the two players lit up, intrigued by the prospect.
“Boss, since you’ve already decided, here’s how we could proceed:
First, spend money to hire players to make sacrifices automatically. To those NPCs, we adventurers from the Lost Plane are all morons, they couldn’t care less what we do.
So, the chances of the NPCs discovering that we’re Evil God believers must be quite slim.
Second, issue paid quests for players to gather information about Lord Kachar, or even post similar messages in the adventurer’s guild. Otherwise, relying solely on ourselves to collect the information, the efficiency will undoubtedly be very low.”
“Hmm, that makes sense, let’s do it that way. I’ll leave these two tasks to you–each of you take one, and let me know how much money you need!”
The priest player nodded in satisfaction.
The two players exchanged a look, sparks flying, then, making sure there were no issues, they both logged off to return to their quarters.
After logging off, both immediately picked up their phones to call their girlfriends…
Meanwhile, far from this small town, in Risier City, in the Dead Silence Land left by the God of Plague, teeming with Fierce Half-Ratmen.
A dozen players cautiously made their way into the city.
The leader was a priest dressed in a long robe, his physique even more robust than that of a normal warrior.
“Guild leader, this is amazing, this mission item actually allows us to enter safely, look, those Fierce Half-Ratmen are right there and not attacking us.”
The leading priest chuckled arrogantly, “What do you know? I paid a hefty price for this top-tier mission item.
It cost me the equivalent of one house.”
“Damn, guild leader, you really went all in this time.”
“Guild leader is the bomb, my eternal god…”
“Guild leader, I don’t want to try anymore, waaaah.”
“Go away, you deadbeat, you’re grossing me out…”
“You guys don’t get it,” the priest guild leader snorted with disdain, “This game is changing the real world. Recently, who knows how many big consortia have been pouring money into it, all for the next big break.
Make no mistake, ‘Glory’ right now is Earth’s biggest opportunity.
As long as we seize a chance, we can make our initial investment back in no time.
Forget a house, even a private jet would be a small matter…”
“Is this the legendary art of bragging?”
“Guild leader is truly insightful, perhaps you are the reincarnation of Zhuge Liang?”
“Guild leader surely has impressive confidence, nothing to argue with…”
“Guild leader, I won’t lock my door tonight…”
As the group shot the breeze, they slowly neared the central area of Risier City.
The current Risier City was far cry from its original bustling appearance.
Gloomy and terrifying would be the best description.
Because of the Ancient Evil God, at this time, Risier City and its surroundings for a hundred miles were all enveloped in dark clouds, and the dense clouds made the light extremely dim.
More crucial was–the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
The space rift that had not closed, and was even growing wider, continued to spew out Fierce Half-Ratmen endlessly.
Added to the continuous emergence of an evil aura, this area had thoroughly become the Land of Dead Silence; no one could break in.
It was rumored that the Extraordinary Mage of Green City–Lord Rock had once paused in the distance of Risier City, but he also did not dare to enter deeply.
Even Transcendents were like this, let alone ordinary people. There was a great horror here that no one knew about.
Ruined walls, shattered streets, decrepit armor, and half-buried skeletons and corpses in the mud…
All of this indicated that this city had once faced a terribly horrifying war.
The deeper these players went towards the city center, the quieter their voices became.
Because on the ruins around them, swarms of Fierce Half-Ratmen were moving about–these servants of the Divine’s terrifying appearance, combined with the gloomy environment, chilled the spines of these players who traveled in groups.
“This damn game isn’t supposed to be a horror game, so why is it so creepy?”
“I’m telling you, there are really ghosts in ‘Glory,’ as well as grudges, and zombies…”
“Fuck, stop scaring people…”
The Priest Guild leader walking in front also felt somewhat chilled. If possible, he really did not want to come to this kind of place.
But thinking of the large investment he had made, he had to at least break even.
He could only brace himself and keep moving forward.
After a full Sunshine Hour, at the central area of Risier City, this once-main battlefield was once again filled with Fierce Half-Ratmen.
The vast numbers were terrifying, with probably more than hundreds of thousands–enough to make anyone with a fear of clusters break out in a cold sweat and grow weak at the knees.
No matter what it was, when a certain number was reached, it would appear extremely unsettling.
At this time, the Priest Guild leader felt even his blood getting cold. A careless move in such a place could lead to a catastrophe…and being killed directly would not matter as much, but it was torturous to be continuously in such a cold and tense environment.
Finally, under the leadership of the Priest Guild leader, a group of players, enduring the chill, made their way through the swarm of Fierce Half-Ratmen and approached the ruined Black Altar.
Behind the Black Altar, Fierce Half-Ratmen were still endlessly crawling out of the spatial rift.
It was like the gaping maw of the abyss, enough to make anyone tremble.
“Guild leader, what do we do next?”
Seeing about a dozen players looking at him intently, the Priest Guild leader bit his teeth; now was not the time to show weakness in front of his subordinates.
He suddenly raised the stone he had been gripping tightly.
Then with a solemn face, he stepped forward, and finally knelt cleanly before the altar, beginning to recite the prayer he had purchased at a high price.
“Mighty Ancient Dominator, eternal God of Plague, your worshipper, your humble servant, offers you the highest greeting, pleading for your gaze…”
After a long prayer was finished, for a long while, all remained quiet.
The Fierce Half-Ratmen were still emerging slowly from the space rift, as if they saw them not.
And the surroundings did not produce the spectacular scene of heaven and earth changing color as imagined by the group of players.
A dozen players saw this scene and looked at each other; the atmosphere turned awkward for a moment.
“Guild leader, were you swindled?”
How could he have been swindled?
The Priest Guild leader was furious, turning his head to glare fiercely at these few guys, and then repeated the prayer again.
But still, all was quiet–no sign of anything happening…
“Impossible!!! I must not have been loud enough!!
Mighty Ancient Dominator, majestic God of Suppression, your worshipper…”
The third time… still useless.
The incredulous Priest Guild leader recited it again, the fourth time, the fifth time… until after the thirtieth time with still no response, he finally despaired.
He violently stood up, then in front of all the players’ gaze, he stomped on the altar and pointed upwards at the sky.
“Fuck your grandma’s Evil God, are you fucking coming out or not?!!!”
After these words fell, it was as if something had been triggered.
Boom–The sky changed color as thunder rumbled in the clouds.
From the spatial channel behind the Dark Altar, a wave of indescribable evil aura suddenly surged out, like the eyes of the abyssal Evil God opening and staring at them.
“Who is calling me…”
Upon hearing these words, the eyes of the group of players widened, then they exchanged looks with each other…the expressions on their faces extremely subtle.
“Fuck, this Evil God is a masochist, huh? Doesn’t show up when called nicely, but comes when cursed…”
“Ha ha ha, what kind of bullshit Evil God, this is killing me…”
“Keep it down, will you? Don’t start trouble blabbering.”
The priest guild master’s face stiffened, a head full of question marks???
But once he snapped out of it, he hurriedly put his feet back down and knelt again with devout sincerity.
He had knelt so many times already; one more wouldn’t hurt. This time, he had to make up for his losses.
“My Lord, I am your loyal believer who has received a token scattered by you…”
After saying that, he raised the stone high, and at that moment, the unremarkable corpse suddenly emitted an indescribable fluctuation of dark energy.
The space around him rippled in waves.
That gray aura of evil felt the stone and instantly grew excited, quickly spreading through the Space Gate; in the blink of an eye, the stone in the priest guild master’s hand disappeared.
“Very well, my loyal believer, I am pleased with your offering!
Step through the Space Gate, and I shall grant you the power to hunt down my enemies…”
Overjoyed at these words, the priest guild master quickly got to his feet and stepped through the Space Gate amid the envious gazes of other players.
A day later.
The player forum was abuzz with excitement.
Because some players had seen someone actually commanding the monstrous servants of the Evil God–the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
And the number they controlled even reached tens of thousands, which was insanely exaggerated!
Moreover, many people recognized the player who controlled the Fierce Half-Ratmen; he was the guild master of a mid-sized guild in Green City.
This discovery caused a huge stir among the players.
Recently, as the Evil God broke free, a large number of monsters appeared.
Most players just treated the minions of the Evil God as targets for killing and leveling up, even as a specially provided leveling dungeon by the game.
But who would have thought that now someone could control these monsters?
Doesn’t this mean that there may be an Evil God Camp hidden in “Glory”?
This discovery made many ambitious players go crazy, going to explore the remnants of the Evil God overnight.
Although most of the players got wiped out by those monsters, believe it or not, a few players gained the favor of the Evil God through shameless efforts.
Although they were only granted a small portion of power, it was enough to crush most players at the current stage; these lucky ones instantly became the top tier players, unrivaled and envied.
This made many players red with envy.
Meanwhile, another event directly pushed the exploration of the Evil God’s remnants to a climax–the player who could command the Fierce Half-Ratmen spoke up.
He claimed that he had become the messenger of the Ancient Evil God–God of Plague, and now any player willing to convert could come to him. If they joined the Ancient Evil God’s Camp, he would reward each person with 100 Fierce Half-Ratmen.
He had only one goal: the archenemy of the Ancient Evil God was none other than Lord Ilo of Green City. Hence, any player joining the Ancient Evil God’s organization must be an enemy of Green City and Lord Ilo.
Furthermore, all players had to gather information about Lord Ilo and report back as soon as they found anything; there would be significant rewards from the Ancient Evil God.
Although Lord Ilo’s scene of crushing three Transcendents in Risier City still remains worshiped to this day, what are players?
Beings who fear neither heaven nor earth, they care not how formidable you are, so many players were tempted.
And the Ancient Evil God isn’t so bad, right? Just sealed away after being overpowered, who knows who might win if the Ancient days return.
The key point is the immediate benefits, an irresistible temptation for fence-sitters.
Just by joining the God of Plague’s camp, you could get 100 Fierce Half-Ratmen; to most players, this was an irresistible lure.
The mainstream player level is currently only Level 4, with only a small portion of elites reaching Level 5, and the top players are at Levels 7 or 8. But the levels of Fierce Half-Ratmen are above 7 or 8.
This would give them power a hundred times stronger than theirs; the temptation is too great.
Whichever way the wind blows, that’s their direction.
Within just a week, an organization called by the forum players as the Ancient Camp emerged out of nowhere, and the number of players who joined was up to tens of thousands.
And everyone was given an unprecedented Epic quest–kill Lord Ilo, the ultimate task.
The subordinate quests–like gathering information on Lord Ilo, learning about his past, etc., also carried rich rewards. With the returns being so abundant, a large number of regular players joined because it was too hard to make it in the Light Camp, and it was more practical to defect.
All of a sudden, the vicinity of Green City became a highly dangerous area, because you never knew when you’d see a player with hundreds of Level 7 or 8 Fierce Half-Ratmen.
Ordinary players had no chance against these players of the Evil God Camp on their own, and for a time, the players from the Evil God Camp surged in status.
They were becoming Green City players’ number one enemy.
A group of players with the ultimate goal of taking down Lord Ilo officially came together, almost like a team ready to push a boss in a dungeon raid.
Along with that, the forum saw numerous paid tasks seeking out Lord Kachar’s whereabouts, and due to the high bounties offered, many players were mobilized.
The area around Green City became chaotic in a way nobody expected.

chapters.title: Chapter 404 - Chapter 404: Chapter 406: Trace of the Black Dragon, The Struggle for Control of the Underworld (7400 words)
chapters.content:
Chapter 404: Chapter 406: Trace of the Black Dragon, The Struggle for Control of the Underworld (7400 words)
Twilight City had been completely integrated into Dawn City’s territory after a month of construction.
Or perhaps, into the hands of the Twilight Sect.
For this was a purely religious city, the sole manager being the Twilight Priest Group of the Twilight Sect, with a Level 18 Half-body Great Mage–Mahari–at its head.
The Twilight Sect’s military arm was named the Twilight Court by Lide, an institution responsible for forceful conquest and overseen by a super Cave Dweller transformed by the Power of Faith–Kedri Sharp Tooth.
With the two utilizing civil and military strategies together, and the additional help of Nicole, Cap, Audis, along with half of Dawn City Hall’s Think Tank,
in just a short month, this former Half-Elf city had all its dwellers–Half-Elves and those captive Dark Races–become believers of the Twilight Sect.
Of course, there were still some stubborn dark life forms, but they had been sent to the mines to labor.
Dealing with these beings from the Evil Camp, Lide took drastic, no-nonsense actions.
Heathens who did not follow the Twilight Sect either mined or met the Death God; an iron-fisted approach effectively deterred the dark life forms prone to evil and slaughter.
Twilight City was developing in the exact direction he had envisioned.
But today, an unexpected event occurred.
“Are you saying it was a conspiracy by this Naga that caused us to lose three hundred warriors?”
The original mansion of the Half-Elf City Lord now belonged to Lide. In the most luxuriously appointed central hall, Anthony, with the Fearless Holy Sword in hand, knelt on one knee, his face filled with guilt and remorse.
And beside Anthony, the figure lying prone and covered with scars was none other than the four-armed Naga leader with a crown of fleshy tumors atop its head.
Lide was unaware of the battle outside Twilight City. By the time the Magic Language Bats arrived to support after spotting a distress signal, all that remained on the scene was Anthony and a few Naga, unconscious on the ground.
The area surrounding the site of the battle, spanning hundreds of feet, had been leveled to the ground.
“Yes, Your Majesty, it is all my fault. I failed to recognize the Naga’s conspiracy in time.”
Seeing Anthony’s remorse, Lide’s brow furrowed but he did not rush to assign blame.
“Detail the entire incident for me.”
“Your Majesty, six Sunshine Hours ago, we discovered traces of the Naga…”
Anthony recounted the whole incident in detail, and after listening, Lide’s frown slightly eased.
Although this incident was inevitably Anthony’s fault as the commander, in such circumstances, any army except his own would likely have been ambushed.
The Naga’s ability to conceal their presence had been apparent when they escaped from the plaza last time.
The power of these Upper Races was not to be underestimated.
It was not surprising to be taken advantage of in this way.
“Later, go down to the military tribunal by yourself to face discipline.”
“Yes, Your Majesty.” Anthony did not offer a single Refutation. The guilt he felt for his fallen brothers was stronger than anyone else’s.
“Is this Dark Night Elf a captive of the Naga?”
Lide didn’t dwell on the matter, turning his gaze to the unconscious Dark Night Elf on the other side.
Their pale skin made these close relatives of the elves appear quite exotic, with curvaceous figures and nearly perfect faces, their beauty on par with that of the Bloodline, only marred by the scars on their bodies.
“Wake the Dark Night Elf.”
After finishing, he waved Anthony off, who was still kneeling on the ground.
“Rise, and when I conquer the Naga, you shall lead the vanguard, avenging our warriors of Dawn City.”
Anthony’s spirit was instantly shaken as he looked up with bloodshot eyes, his tone unwavering.
“Yes, Your Majesty! The blood of Dawn City’s warriors shall not be shed in vain!!”
Lide couldn’t help but fall silent. War was always cruel and bloody, without the slightest hint of romance.
Yet, in the struggle for survival space, there was no talk of giving up.
To give up the struggle was to eliminate oneself actively; if others grew stronger, they would certainly not cast aside their butcher’s knives.
The law of the jungle, survival of the fittest.
If Dawn City wished to continue existing, it had to advance through bloodshed, with no retreat possible.
Upon hearing the command, the two Bloodline members immediately stepped forward and used magic to awaken the Dark Night Elf who was bound and lying on the floor.
“Cough cough…”
After a series of violent coughs, the bound Dark Night Elf slowly opened her eyes.
A moment later, as if realizing something, she abruptly sat up but fell back to the floor due to the restraints throwing off her balance.
After a fierce struggle, she finally accepted her current predicament. With resentment and reluctance, she sat up again, and it was only now that the Dark Night Elf had time to observe her surroundings.
Without a doubt, the extraordinary Lide at the center of everyone’s attention immediately caught her eyes.
Although Lide’s bat wings were not unfurled at the moment, the crimson in his eyes, along with the tusks in his mouth, enabled the Dark Night Elf to recognize his Bloodline identity right away.
Startled, her expression turned very unsightly.
She hadn’t expected the Bloodline to be involved; these surface dwellers appeared terrifyingly powerful.
Her thoughts racing, she took the initiative to speak.
“Respected Bloodline warrior, may I ask what I must offer to gain my freedom?”
In the Underworld, there was no such thing as prisoners being released for nothing, and her question was clever. If Lide stated a price, then she could understand his intentions.
If Lide didn’t state a price, but as long as she followed with her question, she could deduce something.
“What would you pay?” Lide chuckled, a trace of amusement flashing in his eyes.
“What do you have to offer?”
“Respected Bloodline warrior, I can create magic scrolls. I can exchange my Magic Scroll Making Skill for my freedom.”
As the knife to the lamb, the Dark Night Elf was no Elf, lacking any will to resist to the death; her submission was no slower than that of the Cave Dwellers.
“Magic Scroll Making Skill?”
Lide nodded slightly; it was indeed a decent bargaining chip, but now he was not in the mood for such matters, his expression turning slightly colder.
“We’ll discuss that later.
Why did you become a captive of the Naga?”
Upon hearing the chilling tone, the Dark Night Elf felt an overwhelming pressure bearing down on her, as if she was being targeted by a giant dragon capable of shattering the earth.
The transcendent aura was simply too much for the Level 14 Dark Night Elf to resist; her soul itself seemed to tremble.
Without hesitation, she quickly began to speak.
“Bloodline noble, I was searching outside for information on a lost treasure of the Dark Night Elves when I was unfortunately discovered by the Nagas. The squad I led was entirely wiped out, and I too was captured by these Nagas.”
“Lost treasure? What is it?”
Lide was quite curious.
“It’s an Elf divine artifact–the Green Longbow.”
“Did you find it?”
“No, the information was a fake lead deliberately released by the Nagas to lure our tribespeople away.”
“What is the purpose of the Nagas doing this?”
“The Nagas have always wanted to conquer the Underworld, and we Dark Night Elves are their greatest obstacle. So they wanted to capture me for more information and also to lure you…”
“Lure me?”
“Yes, they wanted to create the false impression that we Dark Night Elves had attacked your army and then lure you into invading the territory of the Dark Night Elves.
When both of us are badly injured from the conflict, these Nagas would then finish us all off.”
After hearing this, Lide’s expression became somewhat subtle. He didn’t expect there to be so much behind this situation. It seemed that these Nagas were quite ambitious.
They even wanted to conquer the Underworld, consuming everyone in it.
“Can the Nagas defeat the Half-Elves who have more than one Transcendent?”
“Yes, Bloodline noble…”
The Dark Night Elf’s face revealed a barely perceivable fear, “They have allied with the Black Dragon in the Sludge Swamp.
That Black Dragon possesses a power unmatched by the entire Underworld. If our armies and yours are wiped out by the Nagas, they will enslave other races to attack the Half-Elves’ Liusi City together.”
The Nagas have allied with the Black Dragon??
This news made Lide’s pupils sharply constrict.
He hadn’t expected to encounter news of the Black Dragon here.
He had been relentlessly pursuing information on the Black Dragon for some time.
Whether it was the Twelve Magic Scrolls in the possession of the other party or the Black Dragon itself, Lide held significant interest.
But the most embarrassing thing was that he possessed the Dragon Slaying Skill but could not find the dragon.
The Sludge Swamp was too vast and too dangerous, filled with terrifying toxic mists and Demon Beasts.
The spies he sent suffered many losses, and up to now, they hadn’t even explored one-tenth of the area. He had no idea which year it would be if he were to actually find that Black Dragon.
Could this be considered a gain that required no effort?
“So, is that Black Dragon at the Naga base now?”
“No, Bloodline noble, the Black Dragon has always been in the Sludge Swamp, but the other party has a way to summon it.”
“If the other party can summon the Black Dragon, and the Black Dragon is the most powerful existence in the Underworld, then why hasn’t the Dark Night Elf tribe been overtaken by the Nagas?”
Lide noticed a loophole in the Dark Night Elf’s words, and his gaze turned a bit colder.
Feeling that suddenly terrifying aura, the Dark Night Elf’s body seemed to be crushed under the weight of a mountain.
His heart trembled, and he supported himself on the ground with both hands, his torso bending at this moment.
He spoke with a trembling voice.
“Bloodline noble, I’m not deceiving you, it’s just that my tribe possesses several Dragon Hunting Crossbows capable of hunting Transcendent and even Legendary beings. That’s what has been deterring that Black Dragon from coming forward.
If you attack the territory of the Dark Night Elves, it’s very likely we would use them to hunt you, and then the Nagas and the Black Dragon could profit from the situation…”
Dragon Hunting Crossbows that can hunt the Transcendent? Lide frowned slightly, the oppressive aura eased a little, and the Dark Night Elf could finally catch his breath.
“How many Dragon Hunting Crossbows are there? How powerful are they?”
“This is a secret of our tribe. Although I’m aware of the existence of the Dragon Hunting Crossbows, I can’t know the exact number and location. In the Dark Night Elves, only our Matriarch knows.”
“Do you know where the Naga Tribe is located?”
“Yes!” On this question, the Dark Night Elf instantly became more animated, “Those Nagas are hidden within a veil of mist.”
The next words out of the Dark Night Elf’s mouth made Lide’s eyes widen.
“This group of Nagas is not from the Underworld; they came to the Underworld through a Spatial Gate from the Abyss decades ago…”
This group of Nagas actually came from the Abyss?
This news truly surprised Lide.
“Is the Space Gate that connects to the Abyss still open?”
He asked the most critical point, if the Nagas could continuously summon forces from the Abyss, then he might not be able to handle these Nagas.
Although Dawn City was strong, it wasn’t strong enough to ignore everything.
“That Space Gate has already shattered. Our preceding Matriarch personally witnessed its destruction.”
Good, the Dark Night Elf’s words slightly relieved Lide, the situation hadn’t developed to the worst-case scenario.
“How many members do the Nagas have now?”
“Bloodline noble, I’m not exactly sure of the number, but the estimate should be around 80,000…”
Lide nodded without asking further, and with a wave of his hand,
“Take her down for the Think Tank to interrogate.
Dark Night Elf, you’re a smart person; tell us everything you know, and I’ll let you live.”
A Level 14 Dark Night Elf was not worth him using the Power of Faith to forcibly convert, and besides, Dark Night Elves are followers of Spider Queen Rose, the conspirator God who controls several Abyss Planes with a terrifying power. He didn’t want to rashly compete with the other party for believers.
Although the possibility of being discovered was extremely low, the benefit wasn’t great enough to warrant the risk.
The real prize lay with the unconscious Nagas.
Lide’s gaze turned towards the Naga.
This Naga’s level had reached 17. If he were to convert anyone, it would be this Naga. His primary target had always been the Nagas, the Dark Night Elf was just incidental.
For now, he had no thoughts of enslaving the Dark Night Elves–after all, who could withstand such a terrfying backer?
Once the Bloodline had taken the Dark Night Elf away, Lide ordered the Naga to be awakened.
“Damn surface life, do you know what kind of entity you have provoked??”
Upon discovering that it was bound, the crested Naga had none of the Dark Night Elf’s wits and began to roar in the cold Naga language.
“Lord Austin will destroy everything you have with his fury!!”
Nagas speak a highly obscure language; both Lide and the Bloodline couldn’t understand a word. All they heard was “**&%Y=#@#Y=!”
What the heck is this snake brat saying??
Lide waved his hand dismissively, “Cast a language comprehension spell on him.”
“Yes, Your Majesty.”
After cursing in a rage for a good while, the crested Naga realized that everyone around wore a baffled look, which only fueled his anger as he noticed they couldn’t understand him.
It’s damn irritating to rage and no one understands.
A moment later, a Bloodline hurried over and quickly cast a spell.
Language Comprehension.
It was only then the people around could make sense of the crested Naga’s words.
But understanding them only made them irked. Was this bastard courting death?
“You vampires on the surface!! The Nagas are under the great protection of His Majesty Austin!! Do you wish to taste the wrath of His Majesty Austin?!”
“Release me immediately, or the great Black Dragon His Majesty Austin and the mighty Naga tribe will surely annihilate you all!!”
Lide’s mouth twitched upon hearing this. Was this guy actually saying such things? Was he an idiot?
How did he even survive in the Underworld with such intelligence?
He wouldn’t make it past eighteen years old on the surface either.
Imbeciles are truly everywhere.
Used to dealing with high-intelligence natives, encountering such a fool was quite amusing to him.
He curled his lips mockingly, “Drag him down and beat him for a half Sunshine Hour.”
The crested Naga instantly burned with rage, “You damned bastard, this is a declaration of war against the great Nagas, a provocation to His Majesty Austin’s dignity!!”
Lide waved dismissively, “What are you waiting for? Drag him down and give him a group thrashing for a full Sunshine Hour.”
A few Bloodline finally reacted, “Yes, Your Majesty…”
And so, amidst Anthony’s flabbergasted gaze, the crested Naga was indeed dragged down and received a brutal beating…
Is such a method even possible? That’s a Level 17 Naga… It’s one thing to be tortured for questioning, but a beating? What’s going on??
Lide leisurely sat in the main seat, picked up a cup of tea from the round table, and sipped on the unique red tea of the Underworld.
Forcing a conversion on this foolish Naga would probably consume at least 100,000 Power of Faith…
With the introduction of the Faith Enhancement feature, the Power of Faith had become increasingly precious. Saving a bit where possible was ideal.
The crested Naga put up such fierce resistance that a forced conversion would consume even more Power of Faith.
Let’s not rush into it.
While the Level 17 crested Naga was being thrashed, Lide turned his attention to Anthony.
The bright Level 15 on his attribute panel was particularly conspicuous.
This was Dawn City’s very first human to break through Level 15, and he was one of their own cultivated talents.
Anthony Cleo
Title: Heart of Fearlessness (Fearless, undaunted, able to ignore any level of aura pressure, solidifies a buoyant and indestructible trait, always full of courage as long as not dead. When facing beings stronger than himself, all attributes increase by 1000%)
Level: 15
Profession: The Fearless (Legendary)
Unique Skill: The Fearless (Unaffected by any control skills, fears no adverse environments, the more dangerous the battle, the stronger the combat strength)
Heart of Fearlessness (No fear of life and death, no fear of pain, immune to all mental-class skills, and able to store Fearless Power, which can enhance the power of skills, current storage: 100, cap: 1000)
Inheritance Skills: Sword Intent Cross, Sword Slash Eight Directions, Fierce Sword Energy, Sword Qi Formation, Thousand Swords Release, Thousand Feet Sword Shadow.
Bloodline: Blood of Fearlessness (All Attributes increase by 1000%, affinity with longswords reaches full value, damage with sword weapons increased by 500%)
Evaluation: Inheritor of the ancient profession – Heart of Fearlessness, possesses a fearless heart and dares to draw his sword against Divine beings, only by confronting one’s inner fearlessness can the true power be awakened.
Even after reviewing it several times, Lide still found Anthony’s attributes extraordinary.
It’s actually a Legendary profession, which is quite impressive.
Although Anthony’s profession doesn’t appear to be overpoweringly invincible, the returning Bloodline clearly described his battlefield traces, and Imaging Magic also allowed him to directly witness just how astounding this guy’s burst of power was.
At Level 15, he flipped a Level 17 Naga, along with over a thousand Level 8 and 9 Naga warriors.
These defeated Nagas were an Upper Race, not some weak Cave Spiders.
To assess a profession’s combat strength, it suffices to look at the record and the opponents.
“Anthony, how did you obtain this profession’s inheritance?”
Upon hearing Lide’s question, Anthony looked up with admiring eyes and recounted in earnest the entire process: Meeting Uncle Jike, failing to join the Dawn City military several times, then receiving the Fearless Holy Sword from Uncle Jike, and lastly casting aside all fear to fully activate the inheritance of the Heart of Fearlessness.
After listening, Lide had a subtly expressive face.
He never expected that within Dawn City was hidden such a high-level personage, the last inheritor of the Heart of Fearlessness.
It looked like a thorough investigation of Dawn City would be necessary upon his return.
As a ruler, naturally, his thought process would not mirror that of common folks; he had to ensure Dawn City’s stability.
But of course, he wouldn’t mention this to Anthony.
“Very well, Anthony, your loyalty to Dawn City has earned my recognition.
You said the profession of the Heart of Fearlessness can also be passed down.
Given this, I will create a new legion later. It shall be named the Fearless Army, and you will be the commander.
You can select soldiers from King’s Blade whom you deem capable of inheriting the Heart of Fearlessness to join.
I hope that the Fearless Army will become an absolute trump card of Dawn City.”
Underlings labor physically, intellectuals labor mentally, superiors labor others.
As a superior, he needn’t carry out too many specific tasks; employing talent effectively was sufficient.
Whether it was the words Anthony had just spoken, or his verifiable service record, all indicated the loyalty of this Legendary profession’s recipient to Dawn City.
Under this premise, he also possessed great strength.
So promoting him wasn’t really something special.
Anthony hadn’t expected he could still get promoted after making such a big mistake; his expression was a mix of excitement and guilt.
“Your Highness, I…”
“No need for words. This time you’re only atoning for your crimes with meritorious service. When we attack the Naga Tribe, the Fearless Army will take the lead, and you must be the first to kill into the Naga Tribe.
Only by achieving ultimate victory will you truly qualify to command the Fearless Army. You’re not yet worthy of this army.”
Hearing Lide’s unreserved words, Anthony finally felt somewhat better,
“Yes, Your Highness!!”
Then Lide talked with Anthony about a lot, mostly about the Legendary profession, Inheritance Skill of the Heart of Fearlessness, satisfying his curiosity.
Of course, this profession now also belonged to Dawn City, which made Lide’s mood particularly joyful.
As the master of Dawn City, as long as his soldiers were loyal to him, no matter how strong the profession they obtained, he would ultimately benefit.
A day later, a few footsteps interrupted the conversation between the two.
At this moment, several Bloodline dragged a blood-covered, crested Naga into the hall.
The once bumbling crested Naga was now listless, barely breathing more than he exhaled.
After being beaten up by seven or eight Bloodline for a day, it was impressive he was still alive.
Looking at the crested Naga twitching on the ground from time to time,
Lide’s mouth twitched.
Serves you right…
Without a word, he unleashed his Transcendent power like a level twelve tempest.
The entire hall’s atmosphere suddenly became thick and sluggish as if stuck in mud, and even the surrounding Bloodline, including Anthony, felt a terrifying, formidable pressure descending upon them.
Lide’s gaze was as sharp as a blade’s edge, staring unflinchingly at the crested Naga.
The blasphemous language echoed in the hall, accompanied by an aura resembling the collapse of heaven and earth, shocking to hear.
“Submit, or be destroyed?”
But it seemed Lide didn’t really want an answer; the blasphemous language kept repeating relentlessly.
Submit or be destroyed, this phrase, along with that presence, weighed on the crested Naga’s soul like a heavy stone.
Again and again.
The already dying crested Naga’s life force was rapidly waning. After just three minutes, its body had grown cold, and the heartbeat weak.
It was then that Lide finally took action, stepping forward and placing his right hand on its skull.
The Power of Faith began to pour out wildly.
The crested Naga, whose consciousness was already blurred, wanted to resist, but had no strength left.
As the Power of Faith was rapidly depleted, the Naga’s soul also slowly transformed.
Thirty thousand, fifty thousand… until 100,000 of the Power of Faith was spent, and Lide finally heard the system’s prompt of a successful transformation.
He stood up with some relief and took a deep breath.
Good thing I didn’t force it…
As an Upper Race, the Naga was only at level 17, but the quality of its soul was more than three times stronger than an 18-level Half-Elf Great Mage’s.
Meaning if he had forced it when the Naga was conscious, he may have drained more than 300,000 of the Power of Faith.
The thought of that terrifying number made him somewhat afraid; indeed, a melon forced off its vine is not sweet.
But he wasn’t feeling good now either; he’d barely saved up 200,000 of the Power of Faith in a month, and now it was halved again.
And this time, the conversion was for this numbskull; had it not been for the need to obtain more useful information, he might not have been willing to convert.
The Dark Faith Power had accumulated over 50,000, but that was to be saved for unsealing the Twilight Godhood and wouldn’t be used unless it was a critical moment.
After a full five minutes, the crested Naga finally stood up. Now, healed by the Power of Faith, its injuries were cured.
Upon seeing Lide, the Naga which was previously quite hostile, immediately bowed in submission.
“Master…”
Lide nodded slightly. His heart was still aching for his lost Power of Faith, so he didn’t bother with small talk and went straight to the point, “Where is the Naga Tribe?”
He had long coveted the powerful race of Naga, and if he could enslave this unrivaled, close-combat Upper Race, Dawn City’s strength would certainly receive a significant boost.
Moreover, Twilight City needed Underworld Life to defend it. It didn’t matter if they were Beastman or human; surface life forms couldn’t possibly be stationed underground for long.
And with the Old Day approaching, he needed to pull the Underworld’s forces back to the surface to prevent unknown risks.
Currently, other Dark Races couldn’t meet Lide’s demands, only the Naga had the strength to deter other races.
Dark Night Elves were also an option, but they had the God of Conspiracy, the powerful Divine Power Abyss Dominator–Spider Queen Rose, behind them.
If he enslaved too many Dark Night Elves, there was a real risk of being discovered by that top-tier Evil God of the Abyss, so they were only a secondary option.
The Naga had no Main God, which naturally made them the easier target.
“Master, the Naga Tribe is within a place of mists, extremely dangerous, I must personally lead the way for you to enter…”
The crested Naga spoke respectfully.
Every time Lide saw the scene after a conversion by the Power of Faith, he would marvel at how it was like a bug, on par with the Bloodline’s First Embrace, even possibly stronger.
Although his thoughts were somewhat scattered initially, the next words from the crested Naga made Lide’s eyes narrow.
“Master, the Naga Tribe has recently found a way to reopen the Abyss Gate.
If you wish to conquer the Naga Tribe, you must act quickly.
And the Naga Tribe has also sought asylum with the Black Dragon, Austin…
That Black Dragon from the swamp has already touched the threshold of becoming Legendary, and if the Abyss Gate opens, once the dragon goes to the energy-rich Abyss, it will surely break through to Legendary…”
Break through to Legendary?
Hearing this, a sense of vigilance surged in Lide’s heart.
He was confident to face Transcendent levels, but Legendary was a whole other level. Even with his powerful Ancestor Bloodline, it wasn’t likely he could contend with a Legendary Black Dragon with equal, terrifying talent at level 23.
At that point, who would dominate the Underworld was still uncertain.
Lide immediately felt a sense of urgency.
Before, he had simply wanted to enslave the Naga–that’s why he pursued them. But now, he realized the situation had upgraded to a struggle for control of the Underworld against that Black Dragon.

chapters.title: Chapter 405 - Chapter 405: Chapter 407: The Return of the Two Transcendents, Eve of the Great Battle
chapters.content:
Chapter 405: Chapter 407: The Return of the Two Transcendents, Eve of the Great Battle
Events always unfolded beyond individual control.
The news of the Black Dragon had a significant impact on Lide’s original plan. He had intended to capture Black Iron Castle and use it as a base to steadily promote the Twilight Sect and plunder various magic materials and ores.
But now, the news from the Naga had made him abandon that plan.
If the Naga Tribe succeeded in conspiring with the Black Dragon, it would mean a change of rulership in the Underworld–something he absolutely could not accept.
As the Ancient Days were approaching, and with the addition of players from the outside world, it was no longer suitable for Dawn City to expand its power.
At this moment, the Underworld had become crucial for Dawn City.
Not to mention, he still needed the Dark Race to supply him with the Dark Faith Power. To activate the Twilight Godhood, he was still missing 950,000 points out of the needed one million…
From Lide’s experience, even after activating the Twilight Godhood, controlling its power would definitely require even more Faith Power.
At present, he could only acquire the Dark Faith Power from the Underworld.
Thus, it was a deadlock; the Underworld was an area Lide absolutely couldn’t relinquish.
Besides the Power of Faith, the Underworld was also a vast treasure trove, rich with precious ores and unique magic materials, all waiting to be mined.
Under these circumstances, the Black Dragon seeking to compete with him for dominion over the Underworld was clearly a death wish.
Had his blade grown dull?
Since things had changed, they needed to adapt their plans accordingly.
After inquiring in detail from the Level 17 Naga about the Naga Tribe, Lide hesitated no more and immediately began mobilizing his troops.
Soon, all the decision-makers of Dawn City were assembled in the main hall of the City Lord’s manor.
Beastman King Kapp, Level 18; Half-Body Mage Mahari, Level 18; Fierce Half-Ratman Kedri Sharp Tooth, Level 16; the second generation Bloodline Audis; Heart of Fearlessness successor Anthony, Level 15; and the young girl Nicole.
After everyone had arrived, Lide wasted no time with small talk and went straight to the heart of the matter.
“I’m aware of the news from the Naga Tribe, and now that the situation has changed, we need to alter the plans we initially set.”
