“By the God of Half-Elves, this arrogant fool dares to howl in Liusi City; even dying a million times wouldn’t atone for the offense he has committed!!”
Lide’s arrogant and provocative action had fully ignited the fury of Liusi City.
If curses could kill, Lide would have been slain millions of times over at that moment.
Kakarilo, the 24-level Extraordinary Half-Elf Clan Leader, upon hearing this, was almost driven to frenzy.
That Vampire dared to come here to provoke??!!
He roared furiously at everyone around him.
“Black Beak Giant Eagles, take flight!!
I will personally tear off the flesh of that Vampire! Crush his skull!! Dry out his soul!!”
His voice was piercing, indicating to anyone that the Half-Elf Clan Leader was utterly enraged.
All Black Beak Giant Eagles took to the skies upon the command.
When Kakarilo led tens of thousands of Black Beak Giant Eagles out of Liusi City, he discovered that, indeed, there was only one figure with bat wings unfurled, hovering in the midair.
One man has surrounded a city?!
The rage of all Half-Elves surged even stronger.
How dare he??
How dare he!!!
Lide stood aloof.
His gaze fixed on the terrifying Half-Elves before him.
One man facing an entire city.
Without the slightest trace of fear.
Just as he said, the city had already been surrounded by him alone.

chapters.title: Chapter 408 - Chapter 408: Chapter 410: Hard Clash with the Half-Elf Main City (Part 2) Legendary Half-Elf, Astonishing Secret News (9600 words)
chapters.content:
Chapter 408: Chapter 410: Hard Clash with the Half-Elf Main City (Part 2) Legendary Half-Elf, Astonishing Secret News (9600 words)
Above the skies of Liusi City, on one side, were over ten thousand Black Beak Giant Eagles, among them two Extraordinaries.
On the other side, there was Lide with dark crimson bat wings spread wide.
In the sky, an atmosphere akin to that before a volcanic eruption was spreading and rippling.
Over ten thousand Half-Elves riding on Black Beak Giant Eagles suppressed their inner fury, staring at Lide with eyes full of fierce killing intent and terrifying brutality.
It was unprecedented, a single person, just one person, dared to provoke Liusi City!!
Did this Vampire think the Half-Elves were mere worms in filthy mud? So easily crushed??
Anger was violently stirring, and many Half-Elves had already drawn their longbows, their gazes fixated on Lide as if an arrow from their hands would pierce his throat at the slightest movement.
“Damn Vampire!!!
Who gave you the courage to provoke Liusi City?!!”
Standing beside Kakarilo, the Half-body City Lord, the 21st Level Extraordinary Archer–Derick Eagle Eye couldn’t help but bellow his rage, his voice growing colder.
“How could the great Half-Elves be angered by lowly surface beings?!
The Clan Leader has issued a decree of massacre, and once my army enters the surface, I will make you watch your own city crumble into ruins!!”
A decree of massacre?
Lide just smiled. Thinking of massacring Dawn City? Do you have that ability?
Although the Half-body Clan Leader, Kakarilo, should have been the angriest, he suddenly calmed down, his eyes filled with a depth incomprehensible to outsiders.
“Vampire, whether you occupy Black Iron Castle, or whether you slaughter the 3000 Black Beak Giant Eagles of Liusi City, it’s actually inconsequential…”
“The moment you lead the surface army into the Underworld was destined to spark our war.”
His indifferent words caused Lide to take another look at the Half-body Clan Leader, for their war was not simply a matter of pride.
Lide, as the ruler of Dawn City, carried the fate of hundreds of thousands and had to find a new path for Dawn City before the old days descended.
And Kakarilo, ruler of the Underworld, was just as eager to lead the Half-Elves to a brighter path.
The appearance of the surface army before him signified that they too could travel to the surface, which, for the Half-Elves, was an excellent opportunity.
It was a matter of stance, with no room for compromise.
Only complete annihilation of one side could end this struggle between the surface and the Underworld.
No one would back down; neither Lide nor the Half-Elves could possibly.
To some extent, this moment was destined since the day Koso led a couple of dozen One-eyed Giants appearing in Giant Valley four years ago.
Perhaps this was fate, seemingly ethereal, but already determined.
After Kakarilo calmed down, he started to seriously observe Lide.
With a slight sensing, he could feel that tremble-inducing power emanating from Lide’s being.
Like an Abyssal Giant Beast wearing a mantle of benevolence, once in action, it would shake the heavens and earth.
A foe like none before.
Lide remained silent, but the aura emanating from him started to climb steadily.
They were bound to be enemies, so he couldn’t be bothered with further talk.
He came to eliminate future troubles; Black Dragons and Naga were the formidable foes he would face next, and these Half-Elves trying to stab him now would definitely threaten his rear.
At such a critical moment, he could not tolerate any danger.
Without wasting another word, the Magic Power within him began to race, as the long-dormant force erupted, and an indescribable terror started to spread.
Strong ones never stoop to verbal sparring; only the weak use words to disguise their cowardice.
Hm?
Lide’s dismissive attitude caused the faces of Extraordinary Archers beside Kakarilo to turn red with fury.
“Damn Vampire, daring to be so rampant!”
Although he agreed with Kakarilo’s words, it did not mean Lide could scorn him!!
“Kill!”
With a roar, the arrow already drawn taut in his hand was let loose.
A one-man war against a city officially commenced with that thunderous cry.
Riding atop Black Beak Giant Eagles, the Half-Elves simultaneously pulled their sharp arrows taut at this moment.
Then–
Thwang–
Bowstrings sounded their explosive report.
Merely exchanging a few words, even less than 30 seconds was needed before the battle was underway.
Yet, Lide paid no heed to the rain of arrows that obscured the sky, his gaze intently fixed on the two Extraordinary beings that intrigued him.
With a single step, Lide vanished into thin air just before the arrows could reach, disappearing from his original spot.
Seeing this, the eyes of the onlookers sharpened.
This?!
When Lide’s figure re-emerged, it was amidst a sky filled with thundering lightning.
Four Circle Magic–Thunder God Descent.
With Demon Wings unfurled, he charged into the Black Beak Giant Eagles at a speed that sent shivers down the spine.
With thunder raging around him, he seemed like a mythological being from ancient legends revived, his Extraordinary presence overwhelming, as though billions of tons of ice and snow were collapsing from mountaintops in a crushing torrent.
What was terrifying was that the spell Thunder God Descent, a spell of Four Circle Magic, wasn’t his final move; inside the hundred-blade-wide Thunder Domain, a tornado suddenly began to tear space apart.
And after the Tornado Storm was invoked, the skies turned icy cold as a blizzard of snowflakes howled down.
Ultimate Storm, Ice and Snow Disaster.
Three spells of Four Circle Magic were miraculously unleashed simultaneously in the blink of an eye.
Even more bone-chilling for onlookers was Lide, after having cleared his surroundings of Black Beak Giant Eagles, standing at the center of the storm and thunder with his right hand stretched out and slightly clenched.
Under the shocked gaze of all, these three Four Circle spells were seamlessly merged together.
The scene was simply unbelievable.
Magic that had already been cast could actually merge with each other without rejection or even detonation???
The diameter of the Tornado Storm expanded from fifty blades to a full hundred due to the integration of the Thunder Domain and the Ice and Snow Disaster.
The fast-spinning Tornado Storm flickered with countless blue arcs of thunder, and more astoundingly, it also contained a piercingly cold chill.
Mixed Magic–Thunderstorm Blizzard.
Lide, having previously used Tornado Storm to combine with the Ice and Snow Disaster to handle two Extraordinary Spiders on the Spider Plane, had a new idea. In his spare time, he successfully integrated the fearsome spell Thunder God Descent into the mix.
Not an exaggeration to say, this mixed magic surpassed the power of regular Five Circle Magic, where 1+1+1 totally eclipsed 3, even reaching a multiple-fold increase.
The Thunderstorm Blizzard now painted the entire world a shade of despair, the fearful hurricane mixing with ice and snow, the clouds overhead darkening with an impenetrable blackness.
Tens of thousands of Black Beak Giant Eagles, witnessing this phenomenon, had their expressions twist drastically as they hastily sought to flee in all directions.
Inside Liusi City, hundreds of thousands of Half-Elves, through the magic images cast by the Spellcasters, watched the battle outside the city. The sight of the earth-shattering magic caused many to gasp sharply in unison.
After the three spells merged, Lide had a sudden inspiration and proceeded to do something that shocked the 24th Level Half-Elf Clan Leader and the 21st Level Extraordinary Archer.
A crimson power suddenly ignited around him, and then a terrifying force that practically twisted space itself infused into the mixed spell.
As an indescribable, daunting aura engulfed the world, the thunderous reverberations started to distort, and like a gargantuan hand crazily squeezing, the hundred-blade-wide Thunderstorm Blizzard began to compress.
The hundred-blade distance furiously diminished, ninety blades, eighty blades, sixty blades…
The sky full of energy was being compressed into an incredibly small area with boundless Magic Power coalescing madly.
Under the gaze of hundreds of thousands of Half-Elves, the hundred-blade-wide Thunderstorm Blizzard was compressed by Lide into an energy ball flashing with lightning and holding an extreme cold.
And its size–less than five blades across.
Everyone who witnessed this scene had their eyes filled with indescribable shock.
How could anyone possibly compress such terrifying magic into an object the size of a few blades? Could the vampire before them truly be the self-proclaimed God of Twilight?!!
The scene was so shocking that the Half-Elves above in the sky were dumbfounded, and even failed to interrupt Lide in time.
The Half-body Clan Leader Kakarilo was wide-eyed at the sight, a flicker of fear passed through his heart that he himself was unwilling to admit.
As a transcendent being of Level 24, he had reached the peak of the extraordinary.
But even with his strength, he felt a chilling fear when he saw the energy ball floating in front of Lide, and his spine tingled at this moment.
No one could describe his current state of mind.
Someone among the Half-Elves let out an angry roar, and then they all came to their senses and began to draw their bows again.
Bang~ A dense sound of bowstrings snapped, and arrows capable of easily tearing through a warrior’s armor pierced the sky, exuding an aura more terrifying than the roar of demons.
But the arrows, when they flew to within a few blades’ length of Lide, were twisted away by an indescribable force, and Lide, standing at the center, was left completely unharmed.
Kakarilo’s eyes sharpened; he knew he could wait no longer, as his subordinates had almost no chance of finding a breach in the vampire’s defenses.
He turned his head to glance at Derick Eagle Eye, the Level 21 archer beside him.
“Act now!”
As his words fell, Kakarilo vanished into thin air.
Superdimensional Submarine,
an assassin’s killing move.
No one would have guessed that this Half-body City Lord was actually an Extraordinary assassin.
At the command, Derick Eagle Eye’s eyes sharpened, and he drew his gray bow, carved with the image of a Half-Elf hero, tautly. A deadly Black Feather Arrow was placed on the string with fervor.
Then.
His keen eyes were suffused with a faint green glow, and a terrifying force was transferred to the arrow.
Extraordinary Empowerment, the archer’s strongest killing move, giving the arrow extra energy and lethal power that could easily break through a Mage’s energy shield.
But after the Half-Elves moved, Derick Eagle Eye found the accursed vampire still concentrating on that terrible spell.
A boundless rage surged on top of the trembling fear–how dare he be so presumptuous on the battlefield! He was courting death!
The damned bastard!!!
The power in his hands at this moment increased tenfold, and the luster on the Black Feather Arrow became more and more intense.
When Derick Eagle Eye felt more than half the energy in his body consumed, and even the Black Feather Arrow, forged from Secret Silver Essence Gold, couldn’t withstand that force,
Bang, he released the bowstring.
Whoosh~
Powered by infinite strength, the Black Feather Arrow shot out at an indescribably terrifying speed.
Space was torn apart, and even time seemed to lose its meaning.
Overwhelmed with extreme anger, this Level 21 Extraordinary Archer fired the fiercest arrow of his life.
He knew the moment he released the bowstring that this arrow would surely hit; he even faintly felt that he had touched another level of his profession, and with time, he felt he could achieve an even higher breakthrough.
The power contained in this arrow would mean certain death, not just for a vampire, but even for a giant dragon!
Derick Eagle Eye carried absolute confidence.
Whoosh~
The arrow crossed space, and then before everyone’s eyes, it went through Lide’s magic shield and pierced his heart.
Crackle~
At that moment, blood splattered.
In Liusi City, the moment they saw Lide struck by the arrow, all the Half-Elves went mad with excitement!!
In their eyes, an arrow to the heart, especially one shot by their Extraordinary Archer, meant even if Lide had a thousand lives, he’d surely die!!
“Hahaha, damn Vampire! Even if your magic is powerful, so what? Lord Derick has even hunted giant dragons, let alone a vampire like you?”
“Provoking a lowly life forms like Halflings, it is an honor for you to be killed by Lord Derick!”
“God of the Halfings above, a filthy Vampire dares to call himself the God of Twilight, this is simply unforgivable! This is the punishment of the gods upon you!”
“Heretics and blasphemers should all be hanged…”
A huge smile appeared on Derick Eagle Eye’s face; this vampire was as good as dead.
Because it wasn’t just about piercing the opponent’s heart–that was simple. The arrow wasn’t just for making it fly faster, it had a much greater effect–erosion and explosion.
With his extraordinary power eroding the opponent’s heart, was there any chance of survival?
But in the next second, a scene that made him stiffen occurred before his eyes.
The vampire named Lide just pulled out the arrow as if nothing had happened after it had pierced his heart and casually tossed it aside. The wound that had been blasted by the arrow healed in the blink of an eye.
The excitement in Derick Eagle Eye’s heart instantly solidified as if someone had choked him.
His eyes filled with disbelief.
How could this be possible?
The arrow, containing half his energy, just disappeared?
Not dying from a shot through the heart was one thing, but what about that eroding power?
Lide’s actions had dealt a fatal blow to the confidence of this Level 21 extraordinary archer. Standing there unmoved and being shot, he didn’t feel the slightest pain after the arrow hit him.
What was the point of him being an archer then?
At this moment, inside Liusi City, the Halflings who had just erupted with overwhelming cheers suddenly fell silent, their eyes wide with shock.
“Is, is this… am I seeing things? Did Lord Derick’s arrow hit the vampire’s heart and yet failed to kill him?”
“God of the Halfings above, this must be the vampire’s magical illusion! Impossible! Absolutely impossible!”
“That was Lord Derick’s attack! Even a giant dragon would be badly injured, so how can this vampire show not a single sign of injury, and he is still gathering magic?”
The previously surging morale of the Halflings evaporated without a trace; they widened their eyes and refused to accept what they saw.
Just then, as the Halflings were bitterly disappointed below, the situation suddenly changed.
A shadow with a pale blue blade appeared behind Lide, and as soon as it emerged, the short blade pierced his back.
Thwack–the short blade dug into the bone.
Backstab.
One of the strongest skills of an assassin.
Kakarilo, a Level 24 extraordinary assassin, the Clan Leader of the Half-Elves.
The Halflings inside Liusi City burst into frenzied cheers, and the previously suppressed mood surged up once again.
Kakarilo, after stabbing Lide, still did not show a hint of a smile.
Derick Eagle Eye’s arrow had pierced the heart of the vampire before him and failed to kill him. Although his short blade was smeared with poison that could corrode even the highly immune giant dragons to death, he was still not at ease.
The moment he stabbed into Lide’s body, Kakarilo fiercely pulled out the short blade and then made a motion all too familiar to assassins.
Throat slit.
A killing move in the hands of an extraordinary assassin, not even a giant dragon could escape being seriously injured by this skill.
But at the moment when his short blade was close to Lide’s neck, Lide suddenly twisted his body, those indifferent crimson eyes staring straight into Kakarilo’s eyes.
Crimson Eye: When an enemy gazes into your eyes, they are forced to undergo a willpower test at the Legendary level. Those who fail the will test will fear you, reducing all attributes by 20%.
The moment Kakarilo saw Lide’s eyes, he felt as though his soul was smashed by a giant hammer, and his entire body stiffened.
Then from those crimson eyes, it seemed like countless ghosts emerged, aiming straight for his soul, and at that moment, he saw an unfathomable abyss gazing back at him through Lide’s pupils.
The terrifying soul shock caused his movements to halt for an instant.
Lide’s eyes held a fierce killing intent. The move to compress multiple spells was an idea that came to him after successfully executing Thunderstorm Blizzard,
because he noticed that the fusion of several spells had significant room for improvement, the magic arrangement was quite scattered, and the power was far from reaching its peak.
The thought occurred to him to compress this super blended magic, to make the magic arrangement tighter and increase the power of the spell.
But after taking action, he was restrained because compressing Magic required tremendous strength and unparalleled control over Magic.
Thus, the scene where Magic was condensed on the battlefield, oblivious to others, had occurred.
Only after an arrow pierced his heart did Lide’s attention snap back. He decisively paused the compression, and then he sensed Kachar stabbing him in the back.
“Really, courting death…”
Who gave this Half-Elf the courage to come so close to him?
Lide’s eyes narrowed, the Power of Faith circulated, and the Crimson Eye directly intimidated the Extraordinary assassin.
All this happened within but the blink of an eye.
Without the slightest hesitation, Lide charged forward, his right hand formed a blade, and the Power of Crimson enveloped him as he thrust directly at Kachar’s abdomen.
Puchi~
Kachar was still drowning in boundless fear until the sharp pain in his abdomen jolted him to reality. The drastic change in his complexion revealed his shock as he gritted his teeth and vanished from the spot.
In the instant Kachar disappeared, a Half-Elf appeared where Kachar had been standing.
Looking again, Kachar was already mounted on a Black Beak Giant Eagle hundreds of blades away.
Assassin’s Skill–Forced Replacement.
The Half-Elf clutching the bow, ready to shoot, had a blur in his vision, and then he saw Lide, emanating the Power of Crimson. In that fleeting moment of hanging midair, he saw those crimson eyes and felt a warm wetness–he had literally been scared into wetting himself.
Subsequently, the decoy let out a piercing scream of utmost fear, plummeting to the ground.
This Level 10 Half-Elf had no means of flying, and in full view of everyone, he crashed to the ground, causing a gory spray more than ten blades high.
The heart of the Half-Elves of Liusi City once again went through indescribable turmoil.
Their Clan Leader, after backstabbing that Vampire, had failed to kill him. To make matters worse, the Clan Leader had dragged another Half-Elf into his escape.
Everyone was seething with suppressed rage, but there was nowhere to vent.
Unbearable.
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh~
Arrows continued to rain from the sky in frenzied shooting, leaving the archers in despair as any attack towards Lide was twisted beforehand, sliding off dozens of meters away.
Ineffective attack.
Derick Eagle Eye had finally regained his wits, his gaze turning to the Magic Ball floating in the air.
The compressed mixed Magic was like a bubble shrunk countless times, through which one could see lightning and storms mixed with ice and snow swirling violently.
The surrounding Magic Power was extremely distorted within those violent fluctuations, explaining why the arrows could not reach Lide.
Finding the source of the issue, Derick Eagle Eye fiercely aimed an arrow at the Magic Ball, and whoosh–his arrow, imbued with Extraordinary Power, pierced straight through the Magic Ball.
To his surprise, the Magic Ball wobbled, as if it could collapse.
“Everyone, stop shooting; attack that Magic Ball directly!”
The Half-Elves in the sky immediately set down their longbows and picked up the semi-fixed lance on the Black Beak Giant Eagle.
Then, as if shooting arrows just moments ago, they launched a full-scale assault.
Lide’s wounds had fully recovered by now, and as for the lethal poison on the blade, the Ancestor Bloodline was no joke–the poison was neutralized by his blood, causing zero disturbance.
Seeing the Black Beak Giant Eagles abandoning their crossbows to rush directly at him, the corners of Lide’s mouth slightly curled up.
Really rushing to their deaths, using bows, they stood off at a distance, did they truly think I was compressing three spells just for fun?
His eyes narrowed and, at that moment, his aura surged as an Abyss Demon from ancient times, devouring suns and moons, awakened.
Fear descended upon the world.
With a wave of his hand, under the watchful eye of the Half-Elves, the Super Magic Ball, condensed to its limit and five blades in diameter, ferociously flew towards the charging Black Beak Giant Eagles.
The Eagles were only three or four hundred blades away from him, Lide, and they could close the distance in just a few breaths given the exaggerated speed of the flying troops.
Seeing the Magic Ball take flight, a now fully recovered Level 24 Extraordinary Assassin, Kachar, went pale.
“Scatter!!”
The voice spread crazily with the help of special energy, but it was already too late.
The Magic Ball that had crashed into the flock of Black Beak Giant Eagles exploded with a bang, directly bursting open.
At that moment, the ultimate Thunderstorm Blizzard erupted.
The world lost its color in that instant.
At the epicenter of the Magic Ball’s explosion, space twisted wildly like plasticine under the impact of that force.
Terrifying air waves, like a force 18 storm, shot out from the explosion point in all directions, mixed with the brutally violent energy of thunder and the extreme cold aura,
allowing the power of the Magic Ball’s explosion to be unleashed to its greatest extent at an altitude of over five hundred blades.
Wherever the icy and electric energies passed, a stretch of pure white extended.
Ancient spells containing the breath of extreme cold resulted in the immediate blooming of frost crystals in the wake of the blast, glittering like dazzling ice lotus flowers.
But within this stunning tableau lay a lethal terror.
The Black Beak Giant Eagles could not evade the sweeping force, and the power of Thunder infused into them directly, an energy far too horrifying for beings of level 8 or 9 to withstand.
Their bodies, overfilled with terrible energy, burst into blood mist with a splatter, but in the instant they turned to mist, the intense coldness of the icy powers immediately froze each billow of blood mist into blossoming Death Flowers.
Under the gaze of the Half-Elves from Liusi City, their once prized tens of thousands of Black Beak Giant Eagles burst violently apart with splatters.
The bloody fireworks were so splendid at that moment.
Amidst the crystalline frost in the sky, each bloody bud bloomed atop the ice lotus flowers.
After a few breaths, the terrifying energy dissipated.
At that point, when the Half-Elves of Liusi City looked up at the sky again, everyone gasped in shock.
In the central area where the Magic Ball had exploded, extending two thousand blades outwards, all life within that range had turned into ice crystals.
It was a scene straight out of myth.
After the ice held its shape for a moment, it began to crackle and crash down.
Sizzle…
Bing bang bong…
The Black Beak Giant Eagles on the fringes, which had not exploded from the lightning energy weakening, had also been frozen solid like ice and then plummeted to the ground like meteors.
Bang–they shattered into icy rubble on the ground, with no blood flowing out, for it had all been frozen.
When all the icy debris had crashed down, the whole sky was a vast expanse of white.
The Black Beak Giant Eagles were too densely packed; tens of thousands of them didn’t extend beyond the range of the Magic Ball explosion.
After the explosion, there were only two pale-faced Half-Elves and their ridden Black Beak Giant Eagles remaining; if not for their extraordinary power protecting the eagles beneath them, likely not a single one would have been left now.
Both Half-Elves were no Mages, and faced with a magic explosion of this level, all they could do was protect themselves.
The Half-Elves inside Liusi City, upon witnessing this scene, found their mouths agape, unable to close them.
Tens of thousands of Black Beak Giant Eagles, just gone???
That was several legions!!
Many instinctively exchanged glances, seeing in each other’s eyes both shock and an undeniable fear.
Lide’s supercharged hybrid magic was truly like divine arts.
Whether it was simultaneously releasing three Four Circle Magics or blending three spells into one before compressing and igniting them.
All of it was filled with wonders, no, miracles!!
“Could it be, could that Vampire truly be the God of Twilight?”
An elderly Half-Elf murmured low, but those around who heard these words felt chills run down their spines.
What they had previously mocked as arrogant ramblings echoed in their minds like the tolling of bells at dawn and dusk.
The most unbelievable theory was now raising its head ever so slightly in their hearts.
“No!! Absolutely impossible, the great Half-body God will grant us the power to eradicate all heretics!!”
“Kakarilo Clan Chief hasn’t used his real power yet!”
An enraged Half-body fanatic cried out, causing the surrounding Half-elves to feel ashamed. Then, one after another, they furiously cursed Lide,
as if trying to vent the fear they could not hide through vehement language.
The weak can only use words to cover up their cowardice. At this moment, these Half-elves couldn’t change anything.
Right then, a new change occurred on the battlefield.
After being decimated by Lide’s single blow that eradicated tens of thousands of Black Beak Giant Eagles, Kakarilo, the Half-body Clan Chief who had just failed in his sneak attack and got his abdomen pierced through, had completely calmed down.
It seemed that the previous battle hadn’t enraged him but had instead led him to a state of absolute calm.
What was more astonishing was that the aura of this Level 24 Extraordinary assassin was not intensifying despite the annihilated army of Black Beak Giant Eagles but was instead growing weaker, to the point where one could no longer sense his presence.
Not far away, Derick Eagle Eye, the Level 21 Extraordinary Archer, suddenly had pale blue energy flare up on his body, the momentum completely opposite to that of Kakarilo. It was like an unsheathed sharp blade capable of cutting through steel, with a fierce gleam in his eyes resembling that of a hunting falcon.
The intent to kill surged.
Gritting his teeth, he suddenly drew out seven Black Feather Arrows and pulled back the bow.
Bang~
The moment the bowstring snapped, Kakarot’s figure vanished.
Lide, still immersed in the aftermath of the Magic Ball’s explosion, immediately perceived the incoming threat after the snap of Derick Eagle Eye’s bowstring.
He took a step forward, and his figure disappeared on the spot,
Zzzt~ The black feathers infused with powerful energy shattered the very void where Lide had just been at the instant he vanished.
The moment Lide disappeared, Derick Eagle Eye felt a chilling terror grip him. Danger! He must get away!
He urgently spurred the Black Beak Giant Eagle beneath him to flee backward, but as the eagle turned, splurch~ the blood within the Half-body tamed Demon Beast furiously boiled and then exploded.
Blood and flesh splattered.
Derick Eagle Eye, clad in leather armor, was drenched in blood.
But what was more deadly was the fact that this Extraordinary Archer couldn’t fly.
He plummeted straight down from the sky.
The Half-elves within Dawn City witnessed this scene and let out alarmed gasps.
But at that moment, the plummeting Derick Eagle Eye suddenly stood as if he had landed on firm ground, then calmly stood still in the void.
After Derick Eagle Eye was freed from danger, a hoarse voice suddenly emerged from within Dawn City.
“Vampire, you’ve crossed the line.”
“Dawn City is not something you can shake!”
Though the elderly voice was calm, it carried a strong, undeniable authority.
The Half-elves in Dawn City were touched by this voice, and then many elders immediately went into a frenzy.
“The elder chieftain is not dead yet!”
One sentence awakened many.
“The elder chieftain? Could it be the previous generation chieftain who has been thought dead for over a decade?”
“It is said that the elder chieftain had touched the edge of becoming Legendary, even half-stepped into the Legendary realm. He’s still alive?!!”
Upon hearing that voice, all Half-elves immediately fell into madness. The downtrodden morale from when Lide wiped out tens of thousands of Black Beak Giant Eagles with a single magic attack was swept away.
The elder chieftain would definitely kill that damned Vampire!
When that hoarse voice rang out, Lide reappeared, standing firmly and gazing at a still area in the sky.
Although there was nothing there and he couldn’t sense any aura, his Danger Perception told him that someone was indeed in that void.
Indeed, as if realizing that Lide had detected him,
the next moment that space shattered, and an aged Half-body emerged, bringing with him the recently vanished Kakarilo.
The presence of the old Half-body emitted a sense of danger that was indescribable to Lide, far surpassing the Level 24 Extraordinary assassin beside him.
This old Half-Elf was extremely terrifying.
“Legendary?”
Lide looked at the old Half-Elf and slowly began to speak, his voice at that moment took on a solemnity unimaginable to outsiders.
This old Half-Elf had definitely reached another level, for his aura was not something that Extraordinary Power could compare to.
Even at the peak of Extraordinary Power, it was far from enough.
His heart at this moment was inexplicably clear, no wonder the Black Dragon had cooperated with the Naga, only thinking of conquering the Underworld after breaking through to Legendary.
So the Half-Elves actually had a Legendary seated in power.
His heart was filled with utmost caution; Legendary, this title alone brought indescribable pressure to a person.
The old Half-Elf in a grey cloth robe had cloudy eyes that now slightly opened, looking directly at Lide with a hint of surprise in his tone.
“A vampire from the surface world, I sense an extremely dangerous feeling from you… You are qualified to challenge me.”
Although he had aged to a limit, a Legend was always a Legend; compared to the Extraordinary, he was a living being of a different dimension altogether.
Lide’s gaze at this moment was very serious, but a sense of excitement that others couldn’t imagine was also rising in his heart.
Hard clash with a Legend… The thought once it arose spread wildly like weeds.
Fear? No, such emotion would never exist in him.
What of the Extraordinary, was the Ancestor Bloodline really just for show?!
The aura on his body released recklessly, the long-sealed Bloodline shackles were directly lifted at this moment.
Simultaneously, the Power of Faith operated in conjunction with the Power of Crimson.
At this moment, Lide was like an ancient demon coming into the world, especially the Power of Faith that made his aura rival that of the Divine.
“What a terrifying power… On you, there’s actually the power of Divine…”
The old Half-Elf noticed the surge in Lide’s aura and didn’t rush to attack but instead showed a hint of shock unimaginable to outsiders in his eyes.
Because he felt the power that only Divine could control.
Why could this mere Extraordinary being master such a level of power?!!
“Who are you, exactly?!”
There was actually a touch of fear in the voice of this Legendary-level old Half-Elf.
Hearing this, Lide, who was originally prepared to make a move, frowned.
From the sound of it… did this guy, actually not intend to clash with him?
Moreover, the opponent was cautious of his Power of Faith.
Something stirred in his heart, and he now recalled the information Zhao Yue had once told him. With a thought of giving it a try, the Power of Faith operated wildly, and then he spoke with a solemn voice.
“When ice and snow cover the earth, and the blood moon descends upon the world, the shadows of old are sure to envelop the earth.
And at that time, the gods will fall to the mortal plane; the light will no longer be bright, the Holy Light will be clouded, and the evil of old will rule the world once more…
I am the God of Twilight–Ilo Kachar.”
The old Half-Elf’s eyes widened upon hearing this, showing disbelief and a degree of respect, and then he said something that made Lide’s heart skip a beat.
“You, you’ve actually arrived at the Main Plane ahead of time, this is incredible, no wonder your power is so weak, this must be the price paid for coming here ahead of time…”
Lide sensed something amiss and with the most dignified demeanor spoke lightly, “Who are you? A Legend of the Half-Elves… I can sense a familiar aura from you.”
A familiar aura… Familiar my ass, he had no idea who this old Half-Elf was.
But this old Half-Elf ate it all up and spoke with respect, “Respected God of Twilight, I am a Divine Envoy under the Half-body God–Kaplotz, my God will descend here after the old days come…”
What the heck??
Lide was stunned, he had not expected a casual bluff to yield such astonishing secrets.
The Half-body God was actually going to descend in the Underworld?!
Was this playing too big of a game??

chapters.content:
Chapter 409: Chapter 411: Lide and the Half-Elf’s Gamble, Both Believed the Other Was on the First Level…
“The Half-Elf God will descend…”
Lide looked at the Legendary Half-Elf in front of him with an expression that was quite odd.
Were the minds of these indigenous people so simple now?
They believed whatever they were told without any verification?
“When ice and snow cover the earth, and the blood moon heralds its presence, the shadows of the old days shall engulf the land.
…
The ancient evil will once again rule the world…
The reason the old Half-Elf came to believe that Lide had an impressive background so quickly, apart from the Power of Faith, was almost entirely due to this very sentence.
Months earlier, he had personally heard these words directly from the mouth of the Half-Elf God.
The Half-Elf God had earnestly reminded him that this was a message disseminated by a Main God with Powerful Divine Power, who had paid a tremendous price to see a glimpse of the future.
Therefore, when Lide inadvertently uttered this phrase, it had a more profound impact on the old Half-Elf than outsiders could understand.
And not to mention the Divine Power emanating from Lide, which filled him with immense reverence.
It was a force only a Divine being could wield, and even having broken through to the Legendary Level, he was still far from being able to touch such power.
Yet, here was this Vampire in front of him, who had reached the Transcendent level and could fully control this power. In the old Half-Elf’s heart, if Lide was not a Divine being, could he be Transcendent? Was this some kind of joke?
He, a Legendary, could not control such power, so why could a Transcendent? Hence, Lide had to be a being of even higher Level–a conclusion bolstered by that sentence, which suddenly elevated his stature.
Lide was unaware of so many underlying reasons and did not expect this elder to be as imaginative as the Heart-eating Demon Wales, so he found it quite strange.
But that was not the focus now. The important point was that the Half-Elf God was actually planning to descend into the Underworld.
The implications of this news were manifold.
At the same time, he felt somewhat relieved–fortunate that he had made his way to Liusi City. Otherwise, by the time he had dealt with the Naga and the Black Dragon, he might turn around to find that the Half-Elf God had already come knocking at his door.
By then, the pressure he would face would be extraordinary.
Dawn City did not yet have the power to contend with a Divine being.
As his thoughts flowed, his expression became increasingly indifferent.
He looked down at the old Half-Elf with a lofty gaze.
“Bolots’ Believer, I originally planned to occupy the entire Underworld as a stronghold against the ancient days…”
He turned his head and glanced at Kakarilo and the Extraordinary Archer beside him, who had fallen into complete shock, staring at him incredulously.
“But since you are Believers of Bolots, I can give you a chance. Speak your solution.”
This…
The old Half-Elf, seeing Lide’s expression growing increasingly unkind, had a chill in his heart.
Having subconsciously affirmed that Lide was a supremely powerful being, he felt even smaller inside.
Although he was a Legendary, ostensibly much stronger than a Transcendent, the idea of clashing head-on with a Divine being left him with no confidence at all.
Who knew if this seemingly Transcendent being might suddenly unveil a Divine Artifact and finish him in a second?
And a Divine being who could descend to the Main Plane ahead of time was definitely one of the most powerful. He could not afford to provoke such a being now.
After a brief contemplation, he said with a hint of caution, “Black Iron Castle is yours from this day forward, and the Half-Elves will no longer make any hostile moves against you…”
Upon hearing this, Lide frowned and said unkindly, “Half-Elf, are you provoking me?”
The Power of Faith began to deplete wildly at that moment, his aura surged once more, and the overpowering pressure of the Divine shook the very heavens and earth.
“No, Your Excellency,” the Legendary Half-Elf hastened to say, once again sensing the Divine essence within Lide.
“I have no authority over the ownership of the Underworld. His Excellency Bolots will descend in a few months, and perhaps at that time, you will have better results negotiating with him.”
In light of this, Lide became even less kind: “Half-Elf, you are beseeching me!”
“I…” The Half-Elf faltered.
“The Dark Forest boundary will demarcate the east to Twilight City, while the western region will continue to be under your management. This is the respect I bestow upon the Half-body God of your race,” he declared.
The Dark Forest was the iconic area that separated the Underworld–Lide now held only Black Iron Castle, yet he boldly laid claim to half of the Underworld. Under normal circumstances, the Half-Elves could never tolerate such an occurrence.
However, it was precisely Lide’s lion’s share demand that instilled even greater reverence in this Legendary Half-Elf; it was psychological.
When he regarded Lide as a powerful figure, the actions taken by Lide naturally had to align with the behavior of the strong. If Lide had readily agreed to the terms he’d offered, that would have been truly suspicious.
At this moment, it paradoxically brought the Legendary Half-Elf some peace of mind. Then, under the incredulous gazes of the two Extraordinary beings beside him, he astonishingly nodded in agreement to the preposterous and disrespectful request.
“Your Highness, as you say,” Kakarilo interjected anxiously, eager to speak but was immediately silenced by a stern look from the Legendary Half-Elf.
Ceding half their land was utterly unacceptable, yet the old Half-Elf seemed blind to this fact.
It was because he was not confident in dealing with Lide, whose abilities were unclear–that was the critical reason.
In a few months, Bolots, the Half-body God, would make his descent. The promises made now and whether they would be honored by then were up in the air. Perhaps when the Half-body God arrived, they might immediately go to war with the other party, rendering the verbal agreement the most insignificant of things.
A temporary concession to gain enough maneuvering room was indeed a clever move by the old Half-Elf.
Furthermore, the most crucial aspect was that if, upon the Half-body God’s arrival, they were unwilling to clash with the other party, it would only further attest to the vampire’s great strength.
Thus, this strategic retreat, seemingly a significant loss, was still acceptable in the old Half-Elf’s eyes.
Outsiders saw things differently–Lide had done nothing, yet with a single demand, took away half of the land that rightfully belonged to them. This was outright intolerable.
Yet, with the Legendary Half-Elf present to exert pressure, the other two Extraordinary Half-Elves could do nothing but endure.
Lide narrowed his eyes slightly, himself perceiving the old Half-Elf’s thoughts…but his own intention was not the land; it was to stabilize these Half-Elves. And their actions were to his liking at the moment.
Currently, his greatest enemies were still the Black Dragon and the Naga, but in a few months, they would be the Half-Elves.
He must keep these Half-Elves steady for the next two months. He needed time to find a solution to the Half-body God.
A deep strategic game had been played between the two parties in just a few short sentences, all too subtle for an outsider to notice.
Now that a broad agreement had been reached, subsequent interactions became much simpler. After discussing several inconsequential terms with the old Half-Elf, Lide decisively ended his solo venture into the Half-body Main City.
The gains from this trip were not substantial, yet it had provided invaluable information–the imminent descent of the Half-body God. It also confirmed the words he had heard from Zhao Yue–“Snow shall cover the earth, the days of old shall come, and the gods shall be mortal…”
Another point not to be ignored: he had secured two months to prepare.
After reaching a verbal agreement, Lide left under the resentful gaze of all the Half-Elves in Liusi City.
The entire city fell silent at the sight of Lide leaving unimpeded by the Legendary Half-Elf.
Apart from the two Extraordinary Half-Elves, no one else had heard the old man’s conversation with Lide.
Hence, the Half-Elves of Liusi City couldn’t comprehend why Lide was let go. But due to the old man’s authority, they had to remain silent.
Not until Lide’s figure had vanished did Kakarilo, the Level 24 Extraordinary assassin, contain himself no longer, turning to look indignantly at the old Half-Elf.
“Father, why did you let him go?
Can he truly be Divine? Would a Divine be so weak?” he voiced, filled with frustration.
“Kakarilo…the days of old are coming…” the old Half-Elf’s murky eyes carried a bewildering complexity.
“We cannot afford this risk…”
“Why can’t we take the risk?! Even if he is Divine, since when do Half-Elves need to grovel and appease in such a lowly manner?” Kakarilo said, his face ashen, the corpses of thousands of Black Beak Giant Eagles still encased in ice on the ground, unable to bear submitting under such circumstances.
If the old Half-Elf wasn’t his father, revered and mighty in his heart, he would never have let this matter rest today.
“Because…” the old Half-Elf’s voice grew heavy, “Bolots His Highness has encountered serious trouble. If the land was not ceded to that vampire, even after His Highness’ descent, we would greatly retract our strength.”
He paused, his tone gaining gravity.
“Regardless of whether that vampire is the true God of Twilight or not, I sense danger in him–a lethal danger… The Divine Power within him is not false. It’s intrinsic to him.
Whether he is Divine or a being Extraordinary controlling Divine Power, it shows the significance of that vampire.
I’m not certain I could kill him…even if I did manage to slay him, I would suffer irreversible, grave injuries.”
Kakarilo… “I stepped into the Legendary Level with the help of His Highness’ power, but now His Highness is weakening, and my power has dropped to an unprecedented low point…”
The Legendary Half-Elf finally revealed the truth. It wasn’t that he didn’t want to kill Lide; it was that he could no longer bear the cost of killing Lide.
The terrifying Legendary aura that had just been present dissipated after these words, like shifting from the weight of a mountain to the lightness of cotton candy, not just weakened by a notch.
“Now the most crucial thing is to wait for His Highness to descend. As Half-Elves, we only have Bolots, our single Divine Being.
Only after His Highness descends will the true danger begin. The power of the old days will devour everything, and His Highness must not encounter any mishaps!”
The misery that races without the protection of a Divine Being endure is all too clear to the old Half-Elf.
The Half-Elves occupy the richest veins and lands of the Underworld thanks to the backing of a Divine Being. If their only Divine Being were to encounter trouble, how long could the Half-Elves hold on?
He didn’t dare think about it.
Kakarilo’s heart filled with dread upon hearing such secret news. Bolots, the great Half-body God, was actually, actually weakening??
The enormity of this revelation sent chills down his spine, and the slight dissatisfaction he had felt just a moment ago was now completely forgotten.
The God of the Half-Elves was the greatest Protector to their race; everything else had to take a back seat in His presence.
“Father, I will immediately have the Half-Elves from the other side of the Dark Forest withdraw to Liusi City.”
“No, there’s no need for such haste. Don’t even rush to evacuate. In fact, if that Vampire sends people to take over our city, we need to put up a certain resistance. We must show that we have strong support to confuse that Vampire.”
The old Half-Elf spoke slowly, his eyes becoming increasingly cloudy.
“At the same time, order everyone to immediately manufacture military supplies. We may soon face an unprecedented war…”
In a contest between masters, victory or defeat can hinge on the slightest margin.
Lide believed that his escape this time was due in part to luck, but wasn’t the old Half-Elf thinking the same?
Both opponents had not fully grasped each other’s cards, each believing they were on the last layer, yet neither realized the other was on the next. They both harbored a deep wariness towards each other.
Lide used a message and the Power of Faith to make the old Half-Elf believe he must have a connection with a Divine Being, while his own power had fallen to a low point. Out of wariness, he dared not make a move.
And Lide was equally wary of the Legendary status of the old Half-Elf and the imminent descent of the Half-Elf God. He could only retreat and think of a solution.
This seemingly innocuous encounter had invisible frictions that could change the future landscape and power structure of the Underworld.
Until the final cards were revealed, neither of these old foxes could know if they had gained the upper hand.
—
—
—
After leaving Liusi City, Lide was still deep in thought. Unaware of the extensive information hidden by the Legendary Half-Elf, he felt an urgent dread.
If what the old Half-Elf said was true, and the God of the Half-Elves would descend in a few months, then the situation in the Underworld would definitely not be as he had first envisioned. His footing there was questionable.
Taking a deep breath, he calmed his heart.
Whatever developments happened on the Half-Elves’ side, the most important thing now was to deal with the Black Dragon and the Naga.
It wasn’t that once the Half-Elf God descended, the Black Dragon and Naga issues would go away. If he didn’t eliminate these two major troubles, he might be kicked out of the game before the god’s descent.
Once the Black Dragon entered the Abyss, the trouble would be immense.
A Legendary Level Black Dragon was definitely not comparable to that Legendary Half-Elf. The disparity in combat power was vast.
The disparity was like that between him and those two Extraordinary Half-Elves. He had undergone two Divine Calamities, and his Bloodline and body had reached an Extreme level.
On the battlefield just now, the attacks launched by the two Extraordinary beings allowed him to directly feel the strength of his body.
Especially after unlocking the Bloodline shackles and activating the characteristics of the golden Ancestor Bloodline — the Undying Body, which was terrifying.
Undying Body: No vital points in the entire body, even if the head is chopped off, you can still use the Bloodline Power to regrow and recover. Currently, you can recover from fatal injuries 5 times, and you can sustain this state for an extended period using the blood in your body.
The attacks of the two Extraordinary Half-Elves were fatal to a regular Extraordinary being, but it only used up one recovery from his Undying Body.
And this time it was an accident, entirely because his focus was distracted the first time he compressed magic. On a normal battlefield, the chances of standing still and being a target for the enemy wouldn’t be so easily afforded.
So, all things considered, his solitary venture to Liusi City netted more than the vitally important news of the Half-Elf God’s descent; it also added to his understanding of his combat capabilities.
He now had a clearer sense of his own strength after having directly clashed with the enemy–a summary would be: invincible within the Transcendent realm.
Not to mention he had obliterated tens of thousands of Black Beak Giant Eagles with a single move, if that Legendary Half-Elf had not arrived so swiftly, that Extraordinary Archer would have already been assassinated by him as well.
As for that Level 24 Extraordinary assassin… after piercing through the opponent’s abdomen, a portion of the Power of Crimson had already remained inside.
As long as the opponent didn’t leave immediately, even if they hid within the Dimension Plane, he could easily find them.
“Master…”
Suddenly, a call from behind interrupted Lide’s thoughts. He came back to reality without further consideration and turned to look at Mahari, the Level 18 Half-Elf who was standing on Castro’s back and heaving a sigh of relief.
“Are you alright?”
Lide nodded slightly, “Unharmed.”
Saying this, he moved and flew onto Castro’s back, “The matter is already resolved.”
“Resolved…” Mahari was startled, somewhat surprised, “You mean the Half-Elves won’t be sending troops?”
“Sending troops?” Lide looked at him, smiled.
“Starting today, the Dark Forest marks the boundary, the east belongs to Twilight City.
The west continues to be governed by the Half-Elves.”
“You, you made the Half-Elves cede half of their territory?”
Mahari widened his eyes in shock as he stared at Lide.
A single man ventured alone into the Half-Elf Main City inhabited by hundreds of thousands and even forced them to cede half their land–was this a myth?
The admiration that initially filled this Half-Elf Great Mage’s heart was now bordering on insanity.
“You truly are magnificent…”
“Each took what they needed.”
Lide waved his hand, not particularly concerned with this matter.
With power, the entire Underworld would be his; without power, so-called territorial concession was just empty talk, something the other side could take back at any time.
All this was founded on the basis of power.
His initial objective was simply to prevent the Half-Elves from interfering in his hunt for the Black Dragon.
“Castro, return to Twilight City at once.”
“As you command, Master…”
Although this newly risen monarch’s combat strength could no longer keep up with Lide’s needs, its speed was still unmatched within Dawn City.
The Blade Wings flapped, creating an instantaneous blast in the sky.
Then it vanished on the spot.
When passing by the Dark Forest, the terrifying sigh of the Undead still lingered, but Lide had no mind to ponder these things now. All his thoughts were fixed on how to deal with the Black Dragon and the Half-Elf God.
Twilight City.
For most warriors, Lide had only been away for three or four Sunshine Hours, but they could not imagine that their sovereign’s journey had spared Twilight City from an immense war.
Of course, this war might have merely been postponed.
Since returning from Liusi City, Lide had not left Twilight City for several consecutive days, secluding himself within the City Lord’s manor, with no one knowing what he was scheming.
The terrifying energy fluctuations occasionally emanating from the manor filled people with trepidation; even later the area around the City Lord’s manor within a thousand blades became hollow, as no one dared approach, terrified that they might be torn apart by that frightful power.
Although Lide had secluded himself, on the day of his return, he issued a deadly order that all military needs must be ready within a week, and invading the Naga Tribe was imperative.
This firm command accelerated the already speedy progression of the military’s preparations.
Catapults, Tower Carriages, Alchemy Bombs, goblin bomb trucks, siege crossbow carts… Any siege-related apparatus produced in the factories of Dawn City was immediately transported to Twilight City.
This was the first time Dawn City was making serious preparations for a siege battle, and the preparations Lide made were truly exhaustive to ensure victory in one battle.
In the midst of frantic preparations, time slowly passed… and the aura inside the City Lord’s manor became increasingly intense and terrifying.

chapters.title: Chapter 410 - Chapter 410: Chapter 412: Players' Combat, The Siege of a Player's Main City
chapters.content:
Chapter 410: Chapter 412: Players’ Combat, The Siege of a Player’s Main City
In the southern province, hundreds of kilometers away from Green City, lies the Red Moon Territory.
No one could have imagined that this land, which was once a ruin and where several former lords had died, would now be home to a magnificent city.
Anos City, named after Prince Nolan–Anos Nolan, was also known as the main city for players.
This city, established for just over a year, now boasted towering city walls that only large cities possess.
The solid walls, twenty blades wide, were impervious even to catapults.
Of course, all this was thanks to the players.
These adventurers from the Lost Plane, who could work tirelessly around the clock and possessed limitless stamina, used their boundless energy to frantically haul bricks.
Over 200,000 players labored day and night for an entire year to build the city walls.
Although most buildings inside the city were still low and primitive, this did not hinder the fact that Anos City had become a newly rising metropolis.
But in three days’ time, this city, which already had a permanent population of 300,000 players and 100,000 original residents, would face an unprecedented war.
Because Risier City would be attacked by the Fierce Half-rat men from Risier City.
Yes, the Fierce Half-rat men–those filthy, dreadful servants of the Evil God, carrying deadly germs and plague, would pass by this main city for players in three days’ time.
And behind all this were the players who had sworn allegiance to the Ancient Evil God.
These players called themselves the Ancient Faction and each could easily command hundreds of Fierce Half-rat men.
When the number of players allied with the Ancient Faction exceeded 30,000, the entire area around Risier City and even half of the southern province underwent earth-shattering changes.
Because there were too many, millions of Fierce Half-rat men under the control of the players began to recklessly attack any player who was alone.
Within a short period of time, they had plunged the land into chaos.
Players of the Ancient Faction, relying on the power of the Fierce Half-rat men, bullied the weak, completely infuriating the players who were killed innocently.
The players began to band together, with Anos City–as the main city for players that housed the Destiny Hero, Prince Anos–forming the core resistance against the invasion by the Ancient Faction.
It was all minor skirmishes at first, but a major incident occurred three days ago.
The Crimson Moon, Dark Contract, and Red Dragon’s Fury–three of the top-ranked player guilds in Anos City–activated the powers of the Anos City Player Guilds Alliance, mobilizing more than 250,000 players to jointly eliminate the players of the Ancient Faction.
It was a war that caught the attention of all players, as the Ancient Faction players were too scattered; this time, more than 60% were wiped out. More importantly, the Fierce Half-rat men enslaved by these players were almost completely annihilated.
This war dealt a heavy blow to the arrogance of the Ancient Faction players and sent the players of Anos City into an ecstatic frenzy.
The matter should have ended there, but in the end, something happened that shocked everyone.
The Ancient Evil God of Risier City–the God of Plague had personally ordered the Ancient Faction players to lead the Fierce Half-rat men to conquer Anos City.
After the God of Plague issued the command, the players around Risier City and Anos City all received an epic quest–Plague of Mad Rats.
This quest allowed players to either join the Ancient Faction and lead the Fierce Half-rat men to capture Anos City, or join this free main city for players and target the Ancient Evil God.
Moreover, in this battle, the energy gained by everyone would be tripled due to the gaze of the Ancient Evil God’s will.
This energy was the experience necessary for players to level up.
The news instantly caused a sensation among countless players; this epic quest was seen as a chance to gain experience levels.
Triple the experience was incredibly thrilling.
In just three days, more than a million players gathered in Anos City.
A massive war was about to unfold.
And while players were joining Anos City, the Ancient Faction was not idle. The number of their players exceeded 50,000, which means that the Fierce Half-rat men under the Ancient Faction’s command surpassed 5 million.
Logically, with the ability to lead level 7 or 8 Fierce Half-rat men, many more should have joined the Ancient Faction.
But there was a significant downside to joining the Ancient Faction: once joined, all relations with other factions turned hostile, and one could only be resurrected within the temple of the Ancient Evil God.
And it was impossible to leave the faction for life.
This restriction was too great. Many players had worked hard to raise their favorability in some cities, and now, if they swore allegiance to the Ancient Evil God, they would lose everything.
This was the main reason for the disproportionate number of players joining the Ancient Faction.
And the upcoming siege battle by the Ancient Faction also drew the attention of all the players–not just the players of Glory, but even the mainstream media around the world were reporting on it.
Because the news that “Glory” could improve human bodily functions had spread across the world, Western countries had even united to pressure Huaxia to open up the game.
Huaxia scorned this and did not even bother to respond, which left those old capitalist empires seething with rage and helplessness, for Huaxia had long surpassed its former self, now strong enough to crush those nobodies.
Only a few, still fed by American dog food, touted that technology should be shared by mankind, that Huaxia should not be selfish, and it should open the game for free…
With so many people’s attention focused on it, naturally, the heat was unprecedentedly high. Discussions about the impending war could be seen on various websites.
And on the “Glory” forums, player posts increased explosively, with all sorts of absurd players emerging one after another.
“I’m a netizen from the north, I want to understand which company developed this game, please add me for a detailed chat, there’s compensation.”
“22 reasons why the Ancient Faction will definitely win, first, everyone in the Ancient Faction is handsome! Second, the Ancient Faction has got the goods, and third, the Ancient Faction…”
“Damn, bros, I found an Elf chick in Anos City, this trip wasn’t in vain, I can’t take it anymore, I’m gonna nosebleed, check out my Master Level work~ Sneak shots of the Elf chick’s thighs*jpp, cute green panties*jpg”
“Definitely gotta join Anos City, damn, our main city was breached by the Evil God, where the hell am I supposed to stay overnight now? Are all the people joining the Ancient Faction braindead??”
“Idiotic Anos City players!! The Ancient Evil God is definitely the main character of the next expansion pack, if you don’t take this chance to profit, I want to see how you’re gonna play when Anos City gets flattened!”
“Big bros, cute newbie here begging to be carried, can someone take me to Anos City to hunt rats, I’ll go ‘ying ying ying’ for you”
“I’m a top Level 10 player here, and I’ve found a great grinding spot, if you want to level up to 10 fast like me, private message me, the mentorship fee is only 99, sign up now and you’ll get three out-of-print seeds for free, I prove with the calluses on my hands–guaranteed high quality”
Various ridiculous posts brought lots of fun for many players.
The number of players genuinely arguing between the two factions was relatively small, or it can be said they were drowned in the vast sea, as most players were just joining in for the excitement and to snag some experience.
But some posts from veteran players really opened the eyes of many.
Among them, the most famous was the strong player from the Undead Clan–the Knight of Broken Sword.
This player, who reportedly has broken through to Level 10 with the full support of the Undead Monarch, is definitely the most well-known among the player community.
The Knight of Broken Sword: “Let’s do a brief analysis of the reasons behind the Ancient Evil God’s sudden attack on Anos City.
Since the Undead Empire is right next to the southern province of the Nolan Empire, I hear a lot about this area.
As we all know, the Undead were universally despised pests on the ‘Glory’ main plane before. This time, the Undead Monarch somehow reached an agreement with the surrounding empires and wasn’t besieged.
Combining the current situation, it’s very likely due to the event of the Ancient Evil God’s arrival.
It makes sense that those big shots got the news in advance.
Of course, the main point I’m trying to make is–The power and terror of the Ancient Evil God far exceed our imagination.
If the main plane can put aside the hatred for the Undead to deal with this, just imagine what kind of crisis we’ll be facing.
The Ancient Evil God can easily mobilize millions of troops before his actual arrival, if we judge by appearances, how strong will his actual power be?
Back to the battle for Anos City, based on the information I have, the Ancient Evil God’s gathering forces to attack Anos City is more of a probe.
Yes, a probe with millions of troops, only those mysterious Ancient Evil Gods can do such a thing.
But I’m not surprised about this.
The power that the Ancient Evil God possesses exceeds all our imagination.
As for why they’re probing?
I suppose a big reason is–these Ancient Evil Gods want to assess the high ground of the main plane’s powers.
This is very critical, why? Because if the main plane’s powers are too strong, the Ancient Evil Gods will certainly make extra preparations.
This also suggests that the coming of the Ancient Evil Gods is truly only a matter of time.
Perhaps in other words, the next expansion pack might open tomorrow.
I dare say that this attack on Risier City by the Ancient Evil God will not be the last–it will be the first!
Not only Risier City, but other Evil Gods that have broken their seals and still have servants on the main plane will also dispatch forces to attack nearby cities.
To sum up, this upcoming event with the Ancient Evil Gods is going to be an unprecedented turmoil on the ‘Glory’ main plane.
For those players who haven’t chosen a side, my advice is to wait a bit longer and choose when the time is right.”
It has to be said that the Knight of Broken Sword really had insight, immediately analyzing some profound points.
The majority of players were amazed after reading and the replies instantly broke through ten thousand.
First floor: The boss is the boss, do you need any accessories for your leg?
Second floor: Damn, that’s so badass, even knowing such secrets, I can feel the little deer bumping around in my heart~ Knight of Broken Sword, can I add you on WeChat? I don’t care about gender, I just like brave men.
Third floor: Big boss Broken Sword, is it still possible to join the Undead now? Recently I’ve been with three noble ladies and it’s been too much for me…
Fourth floor: So it’s the Undead without the little ding-dings, I say, Broken Sword, this Name is really too fitting for you.
Fifth floor: So you can wait before choosing a side? I’ve learned something, I’m joining the Ancient Faction…
Sixth floor: …
Most players actually have little interest in the Ancient Faction at this stage, mostly because other factions consider it a mortal enemy, but mostly because life in the Ancient Faction is simply too hard right now.
Though they have the power to command hundreds of Fierce Half-Ratmen, they’ve lost the convenience of big cities, delicious food, warm rooms, and entertainment facilities everywhere… Joining the Ancient Faction, it’s difficult even to form a party for a date.
In a heated discussion atmosphere.
On the third day, the Ancient Faction players drove millions of Fierce Half-Ratmen to surround Anos City.
The sheer number of them was enough to make anyone with a fear of crowds dizzy with discomfort.
Fierce Half-Ratmen, with their sharp claws and teeth, had bodies resembling those of rats and stood around 1.6 blades in height. They carried a filthy, difficult-to-bear stench and their green bean-like eyes flickered with a cold gleam.
They were pure killing machines.
Opposite them, towering atop the 30-blade high walls of Anos City, were players dressed in all sorts of bizarre equipment.
A year had passed, and the players, through their fearless and ridiculous spirits, had undergone a transformative increase in their strength.
Now, the majority of the players were around levels 4 and 5, a few advanced players had reached levels 6 and 7, and the top players had even reached levels 8 and 9.
A select few, like the knights of the Broken Sword, had surpassed level 10.
The overall improvement in the players’ strength had significantly alleviated the once-common scenario of being easily slapped to death by a passing NPC. Only power commanded respect, and at this time, players began to emerge and slowly gain acceptance from the natives.
The roles they played were no longer taken lightly by the high-level natives.
“Prince Anos, this war is feared to be unprecedented in its ferocity…”
As the vice president of the Crimson Moon Guild and also carrying the president’s responsibilities in Lide’s absence, Zhao Yue’s status was no ordinary one.
Moreover, Crimson Moon was the largest guild within Anos City, naturally able to converse with City Lord Prince Anos.
Prince Anos stood atop the city gate wall, gazing at the tide-like surge of Fierce Half-Ratmen advancing towards them, his expression unchanged.
He was no longer the weakling of a year ago, who even his guards could look down upon. Now, he was the lord controlling hundreds of thousands of players in the Undead Army, a grand figure of the Holy Light Bloodline.
Though the scene before him was daunting, it had yet to make his heart flutter with fear.
Furthermore, the conflict between Dawn City and the God of Plague had long been thoroughly reported to him by his intelligence department.
For this day’s arrival, Prince Anos was, in fact, more prepared than anyone else.
“Do not worry, we now have over a million adventurers from the Lost Plane defending the city. No matter how fierce the battle, we can withstand it.”
After saying this, Prince Anos cast a meaningful glance at Zhao Yue, “President Yue, Crimson Moon will be responsible for defending the second segment of the wall, which is at the corner and faces the least pressure.
Additionally, if you cannot sustain the casualties, let me know, and I will send someone to replace you immediately.”
Crimson Moon was a guild Lide had instructed him to look after; Prince Anos dared not neglect it, especially when Zhao Yue appeared to have some special relationship with Lide. He was doing his utmost to look after Crimson Moon.
Zhao Yue nodded slightly. Lide had already told her that Prince Anos had a deep connection with him and that turning to him for anything would be the right choice.
Over the past year, this relationship had indeed provided considerable assistance to Crimson Moon.
With this thought, Zhao Yue couldn’t help but recall the elusive Lide, feeling slightly aggrieved inside–a sense of grievance that this man seemed to take her role of vice president for granted, using her as if she were just another staffer…
Wuu wuu~
While Prince Anos and Zhao Yue were having their casual conversation, a deep horn suddenly echoed from the camp of the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
As the war horn resonated above Anos City, dubbed the Main City of Players, the war at Free City erupted.
For many players, this was their first experience of an event on such an epic scale, where countless Fierce Half-Ratmen were visible beyond a thousand blades, their numbers seemingly endless.
The scene resembled the apocalyptic imagery found in church frescoes, where only the breaking of the abyss could unleash such multitudes of monsters.
The grotesque Fierce Half-Ratmen let out ear-piercing screams like knives scraping glass, sending shivers down one’s spine.
The players on the wall could only see an oppressive, dark mass closing in, the atmosphere tensing to the extreme.
Thick clouds hung in the sky like an inverted mountain pressing against everyone’s heart, adding to the intense psychological impact created by the underground hordes of Fierce Half-Ratmen.
As the Half-Ratmen slowly neared, the exaggerated numbers and horrific visages made many players’ hands tremble.
“Holy shit, is this war? So thrilling! This is even more exciting than sneaking a peek at the neighbors…”
“Quick, support me, my legs are giving out…”
“Kill them! Fire the arrows! What are we waiting for?”
“Here they come, they are getting closer. Do these monsters actually plan to scale the walls barehanded?”
The Fierce Half-Ratmen swarmed in, more densely packed than locusts by a tenfold, a hundredfold. As they approached a certain limit, the catapults behind the walls of Anos City began to stir their chains, and several warriors hoisted the projectiles to the top of the machinery.
When hundreds of catapults were in position, the commander in charge bellowed an order.
“Fire!!”
With an explosive tone, the operators released the catapults, sending the chains whipping wildly.
Whoosh whoosh~
Gigantic stones, propelled by mighty force, flew through the air and over the walls, plummeting down into the thick masses of Fierce Half-Ratmen below with immense inertia.
Pur-chik~
Blood splattered, and limbs and fragments littered the ground.
The scene was extremely bloody.
From the sky above, it looked like humans stomping through a dense horde of ants, the number of Fierce Half-Ratmen was overwhelming, and each boulder thrown caused dozens to explode.
Players on the city walls turned pale at this sight, and some female players even started to retch, hastily retreating.
“Glory” requires players to be at least 18 years old to purchase a gaming pod, but most had never experienced such a spectacle of war.
The usual monster-slaying was bloody enough but still tolerable; however, this kind of gruesome scene with intestines flying everywhere was simply too horrifying and mentally shocking.
But war wouldn’t stop just because some players couldn’t handle it. When the Fierce Half-Ratmen advanced to about 300 blades away from the city walls, under the command of the players, they began their most frenzied charge.
Though the bodies of the Fierce Half-Ratmen were light, their numbers were almost indescribable–as they charged, the ground thundered, even more intensely than a stampede of thousands of horses.
“Quick, give me some arrows, today I’m going to shoot it in the face!!! Let these rats taste my Huang Zhong of Niulanshan’s Eagle-shooting Great Bow!”
“Hahaha, I killed three with one arrow? Isn’t that awesome?”
“So exhilarating, it’s really triple experience. At this rate, it won’t be long until I level up!”
Those bold players on the city walls didn’t panic at the sight, and instead began to use creative methods to harvest experience.
Some wielded longbows, and others had spent a lot of money on crossbows ahead of time, while spellcasters cast area of effect magic…
What’s more exaggerated was that some players had gotten hold of siege crossbows. A few players took positions behind the battlements and the siege crossbows, as thick as an arm, started firing frequently. Every trigger pull took out more than a dozen Fierce Half-Ratmen, and experience points skyrocketed.
Players on the city walls were yelling excitedly, making those behind the walls incredibly envious. Anos City had seen the influx of over a million players, but not even one-tenth could stand on the walls to shoot.
The rest could only take turns.
Those below, seeing others indulging in the experience feast above, naturally felt discontent.
“If only I hadn’t been a step late, I would have been first up there, regretfully… All because that little elf was too clingy…”
“Slow down killing them, leave a few for me–I’m just a bit of experience away from leveling up!!”
“Healer seeking group, healer seeking help, Life Priest, guaranteed full support, preferably there’d be an archer in the squad…”
The chaotic scene left the native soldiers of Anos City dumbfounded.
Their superiors had initially told them to let these adventurers from the Lost Plane go first to deplete the enemy’s living forces before they would join in.
They thought that was just nonsensical–how could these adventurers from the Lost Plane not hide behind in such dangerous combat?
But in reality, they were too naive; not only were these guys not hiding, but they were also angry about not being able to go first.
They truly couldn’t wrap their heads around the thought process of these adventurers from the Lost Plane… Even if they didn’t die, why rush to their deaths?
What good did killing those rats do? It’s not like the corpses of demon beasts could be sold for money, and those bodies carried deadly plagues–whoever touched them died, and there was nothing to loot now anyway…
Roar~
Accompanied by the shrill roar of the Fierce Half-Ratmen, following the exaggerated onslaught of arrows and magical bombardment, the slightly scattered ranks of Fierce Half-Ratmen finally reached the base of the city walls.
Then, under the bizarre gaze of the players, these Half-Ratmen, unarmed with siege equipment, really just bared their claws and began to climb straight up towards the top of the city wall.
But that wasn’t all, after the Fierce Half-Ratmen withstood the attacks at the base of the wall, the sky in the distance suddenly darkened, and then, under the scrutiny of all the players.
Whoosh~ Whoosh~
Countless Flying Half-Ratmen appeared in the sky, flapping their wings.
Instantly, the players who had been laughing and chatting felt immense pressure; there were Fierce Half-Ratmen climbing up the walls from below, and aerial troops capable of flying over the walls from above.
This time, they might not be able to hold on.
The atmosphere began to grow incredibly tense.
While the war for Anos City raged on the surface, deep below in the Underworld within the dense fog zone hundreds of miles from Twilight City.
Magic Language Bats patrolled the sky, their ferocious gaze deterring all invaders. Siege crossbows had been mounted on ground carriages, ready to move and shoot at any time.
The Giant Army, clad in tons of heavy armor, wielding their Wolf Fang Clubs, watched menacingly.
Spellcasters of the Bloodline were grouped in tens, frenetically applying magic shields and various buffing spells on the surrounding troops.
Beastman Warriors let out bestial roars from their throats, Centaurs raised their sharp longbows, and believers of the Twilight Sect looked ahead with devotion to the Divine.
Thousands of Alchemy Bomb Launchers were in position; their Alchemy Bombs only needed the pin to be pulled to be launched.
Facing this powerful army of Dawn was a city with walls 50 blades high, it’s surface covered in dense, sharp barbs like the tusks of a demon–the city of the Naga.
The first battle of the dawn had erupted on the surface, and that city under his secret control was today’s main battleground; the outcome of the war in Anos City would determine the direction of the surface world’s future.
The war for the city of the Naga in the Underworld would also determine the future pattern and dominion of the Underworld.

chapters.title: Chapter 411 - Chapter 411: Chapter 413: Battle of the Naga, Bombs Exploding Until You Cry for Daddy (6800 words)
chapters.content:
Chapter 411: Chapter 413: Battle of the Naga, Bombs Exploding Until You Cry for Daddy (6800 words)
PS: Sorry for the delay. I have just finished editing.
—
—
—
Naga City was built against the mountains, and the enclave of the mountains was the stronghold of the Naga Tribe.
At that moment, the sudden appearance of an army outside the city plunged the entire Naga City into anger.
The Naga Chief, crowned with a tumorous growth, stood in the mid-mountain area inside Naga City, looking down at the entire city and the Dawn Army encircling it from outside.
His narrow eyes harbored cold and deadly intent.
“How dare these despicable surface-dwellers attack the great Naga?? Have their brains been eaten by Brain-Eating Worms?”
“Lowly surface-dwellers, they should all be hanged on the city walls!”
“Chief, please give the command. I will immediately lead the troops and exterminate these surface worms…”
The faces of the Naga elites beside the Chief showed even more intense rage.
It seemed as though they wished their saliva could kill.
How noble were the Naga, who dared so recklessly besiege their city in the Underworld?
