Chapter 416: Chapter 418 (Anti-theft chapter, do not subscribe) Overbearing Dominance, Tearing the Evil God Apart (10,000-word mega chapter)
PS: Everyone, refresh in twenty minutes, this anti-theft exactly 10,000 words. I’ll replace the content in this chapter later. Published at 3:34 in the early morning.
—-
—-
—-
—-
—-
“Damn, is this NPC that handsome?”
“Trampling with iron hooves looks so cool.”
“But that merely relieved the temporary threat, we are still far from being saved.”
Although it was indeed heroic for tens of thousands of centaurs to trample fierce half-ratmen, a harsh reality was that there were as many as a million fierce half-ratmen, so these tens of thousands of centaurs couldn’t cause any fatal damage.
In front of the city wall lay an enormous unbuilt area, sprawling and vast.
After Prince Anos led the Centaurs into this area, these Divine Servants gathered once again along the main road sides, but they were too late to react further as their retreat was cut off by the fierce half-ratmen.
The numerical advantage of the fierce half-ratmen became undoubtedly clear at this moment.
Although the Centaur Army trampled over 100,000 fierce half-ratmen on the main road, upon reaching the vast area in front of the city wall, the centaurs lost their most important asset–their momentum from the charge.
It was like a sharp dagger stuck into thick mud, still sharp but struggling to cut through the surrounding muck.
If this road stretched for a hundred kilometers, then everything ahead could have been crushed by the centaurs, but now the city wall, which originally protected them, became an obstacle that restricted them.
At the loss of their speed, the centaurs faced immense peril.
Especially with the Flying Half-ratmen, swarming like locusts, they covered the sky in a blink.
Within a few breaths, the camera in the official “Glory” livestream couldn’t see Prince Anos’s Centaur Army anymore.
The fierce half-ratmen, dense as ants, roared with a brutal bloodlust as they charged toward the Centaur Army.
Shred these damn centaurs!
The command to kill all life around echoed in their souls, making these fierce half-ratmen fearless of all danger.
They now personified death, brutality, and slaughter.
Although the war had its disturbances, the overall direction didn’t change.
Prince Anos’s sword was extremely sharp, each strike surely taking a life, but as the centaurs were tightly bound by the fierce half-ratmen, without room to gain momentum again, he couldn’t issue another order to charge.
The situation reached a stalemate.
A moment later, Prince Anos decisively issued a command.
“Form a circular military formation with the archers in the center and the Centaur Heavy Armor Warriors as guards!”
Since there was no way to break back through, they decided to be nails firmly hammered into the heart of the fierce half-ratmen, reducing the pressure on their own defenses.
Viewers of the livestream couldn’t help but shake their heads and sigh; it seemed inevitable that Anos City would fall.
The disparity between the strengths of the two sides was too great. Prince Anos’s actions might delay time, but it was just a slow crawl to death.
The live chat was filled with rapid messages.
“This is really the end, I originally thought that in the last moments the Centaur Army might make a difference, but it seems like a futile struggle now.”
“A player’s main city just falling like this? Ah, these monsters of the Ancient factions are simply too many … under such circumstances, only an Extraordinary might save the city.”
“Extraordinary coming? Whoever said that must know nothing. What level of power is that? The entire southern province has only one Extraordinary in Green City, and they must stay to defend it. Why would they come to Anos City?
I say it’s better to run early. That stupid prince is also not smart, still thinking about turning the tables in this situation? As if he could …”
“Right, and even if an Extraordinary could come, it would be useless. Didn’t you see most of the city below is filled with servants of the Ancient Evil God? I don’t believe anything could kill these millions of fierce half-ratmen …”
Viewers were incredibly pessimistic, and even those who still held a glimmer of hope found it hard to imagine any chance of Anos City turning the tables.
The fall of Anos City was imminent.
Outside Anos City, many natives, after viewing the battle situation in Anos City through magic, had very solemn expressions.
Unlike the players, this land was where they had grown up; if Anos City was conquered, did it mean that the other cities would also face the threat of the Ancient Evil God?
For players, losing the main city might hurt for a moment, and they could thrive elsewhere easily, but it was not so simple for the natives; this was their home.
“Duke, the Fierce Half-Ratmen have already conquered most areas of Anos City, only the last Life Goddess temple remains unseized.
Once the last temple falls, those Lost Plane adventurers will lose their place of rebirth, and Anos City will completely fall.”
In the duke’s manor in the center of Green City, Duke O’Kelly was reviewing documents in his study when the God of Nobles’ bishop reported to him with a serious expression about the situation in Anos City.
“Once Anos City falls, as the largest city in the south, Green City will be directly exposed to the military front of Risier City’s Evil God, Duke, we need to prepare early…”
Hearing this, Duke O’Kelly set down the documents in his hands and looked up with a grave expression at the bishop in front of his desk.
“If we send troops now to aid them, could we still help North City achieve victory in the war?”
The bishop shook his head, smiling bitterly, “Duke, whether at the start or now, we were never able to aid Anos City.”
“Oh?” Duke O’Kelly raised an eyebrow, “Having one more city to hold off the Evil God of Risier City might not be a bad thing…”
“That was the case previously, but the situation has changed…” The bishop’s eyes were sharp, “Now you must have a significantly different view on the Lost Plane adventurers, right?”
More than different, it was a huge change.
Duke O’Kelly was swallowed up by thoughts of the city.
Anos City, solely relying on players, had withstood the assault of millions of Fierce Half-Ratmen for several days.
To the noble elites of Green City, this was absolutely heart-stopping.
How long had Anos City been established? Merely a year.
And how long had the Lost Plane adventurers been around? Barely more than a year.
Yet, this city, in existence for a year, with adventurers who appeared just a year ago, had the strength to resist the assault of millions of Divine Servants.
Moreover, the master of Anos City was once considered a royal waste, a prince born to a maid.
What did this represent? It indicated that the adventurers of the Lost Plane were a force with tremendous potential, and now their potential was beginning to be unleashed, no longer merely relying on the ability to resurrect endlessly.
The adventure of the Lost Plane had the power to change the war.
This was the greatest discovery of the nobles of Green City since the battle of Anos City erupted.
In the Main Plane of Glory, power is the only and eternal standard of judgment.
Since the Lost Plane adventurers now possessed considerable power, their treatment could no longer remain as it had been before.
Duke O’Kelly’s eyes carried a hint of awe and wariness, and he nodded solemnly.
“Indeed, in this war the Lost Plane adventurers have played an undeniable role, but how does this relate to whether we support Anos City?”
“Duke, Anos City is referred to as their main city by those adventurers… in other words, they see Anos City as their home.
Moreover, the number of Lost Plane adventurers Anos City has attracted lately has already significantly surpassed the number of adventurers in Green City.
Previously, we considered them a burden and paid no attention, but now, if this continues to develop, the number of adventurers in Anos City will inevitably grow more.
This is a huge impact for Green City, as we also need their strength.”
“But now this sudden upsurge in war has clearly found us a breakthrough. If Anos City is conquered, those adventurers will have nowhere to go.
Then Green City will be their only destination.
Thus, whether we look at it from any perspective of interest, the only way for Green City to gain the maximum benefit is to hold our forces back.”
Duke O’Kelly was naturally no fool, having understood from the words of the bishop that from the beginning, there was an intention to let Anos City destroy itself; if the city was destroyed, it would be more beneficial for Green City.
As the highest ruler overseeing the southern provinces, Duke O’Kelly was not a man of indecision or excessive kindness, as mercy would not hold one’s stance in this position.
“Dispatch troops to monitor near Anos City, meanwhile keep the entire city on alert to prevent the assault of the Evil God’s servants on Green City, and as for Anos City… let it be.”
The bishop nodded, “Duke, you needn’t take it to heart. The war has progressed to such a degree that even if we mobilized the entire city’s strength to assist Anos City, we might still not win. More likely, we would suffer severe losses while Anos City falls.
Moreover, I suspect that the servants of the Ancient Evil God are holding back something, perhaps just waiting for us to make a move.
Anos City is doomed in this war. Not just our army, but even if Lord Rock, an Extraordinary, were to intervene, it would be futile.
At this stage of the battle, no one can save this city that is doomed to fall. No one has that strength.”
Duke O’Kelly sighed slightly upon hearing this, then picked up the document to review it once more.
The strategic location of the Red Moon Territory isn’t important, and neither is Anos City, built atop it. It is at most a city established by a royal castoff.
Furthermore, a highly influential royal member had repeatedly hinted to him not to deploy troops. He had reasons not to send troops and wouldn’t have won even if he did, so he could only remain silent.
“Go now, bring me news immediately, and prepare the contingency plans for after the fall of Anos City…”
“Yes, Duke.”
Although the players displayed astonishing combat strength, and Prince Anos, a noble from Green City whom the royalty greatly despised, was unexpectedly brave,
when news arrived of Prince Anos with his last Centaur Army charging into the Fierce Half-Ratmen only to be overwhelmed by countless Fierce Half-Ratmen, no one had any hope left for this war.
An Extraordinary going there would also be of no help.
—
—
—
“We can’t hold on anymore!! Retreat, retreat to the defensive line behind!! Guild leader, come on, we can’t hold this line!!”
A warrior player, after brutally beheading two Fierce Half-Ratmen, dragged a fellow player and retreated.
At the forefront, the assassin Zhao Yue, now wielding a delicately small crossbow, was furiously shooting the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
Assassins are very skilled with hidden weapons, such as dart shooters and crossbows suitable for assassination.
This area is a secondary sector held by the Crimson Moon. Relying on strong combat and excellent full Dwarf Equipment sets, these players were nailed down firmly here.
But players from several nearby streets had all been killed by the Fierce Half-Ratmen. Although strong, they couldn’t hold out alone and had to retreat to the next street corner, using the prepared defensive positions to snipe at the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
“Everyone retreat to the next defensive position!! I’ll cover our rear!”
Zhao Yue was unequivocal. The crossbow in her hand was one of the perfect tier Equipment made by Lide’s weapons factory, killing these level 7 or 8 Fierce Half-Ratmen with deadly accuracy.
She alone was the core position of a marksman ADC, a very powerful supporting fire point.
As her words fell, the other players began to retreat rapidly, knowing Zhao Yue’s capabilities; they did not hesitate.
After the Crimson Moon players left the line, the Fierce Half-Ratmen surged up like a tide.
Zhao Yue’s expression was cold. Her crossbow, loaded with arrows could shoot thirty rounds, each round at an interval of only 0.3 seconds. Although the range was only about 100 blades, it was the deadliest weapon in this environment.
Whiz Whiz Whiz~
The trigger was furiously pulled, and those charging Fierce Half-Ratmen burst apart directly.
Zhao Yue alone significantly slowed down the assault pace of these Divine Servants. Fortunately, the Flying Half-Ratmen had all gone to hunt the Centaur Army, relieving a great deal of pressure on the players, otherwise she wouldn’t have handled it so easily.
Less than 10 seconds into the intense combat, the arrows in her hands were already spent.
Catching the situation, a neatly made arrow cartridge flashed into her hand, and in less than three seconds, she reloaded, and arrows once again sprayed out.
Zhao Yue’s gaze was cold, appearing irresistibly charming on the battlefield in her leather armor, but unfortunately, no one was around to witness this lethal allure.
After the fifth clip was depleted, Zhao Yue was mildly perturbed as she touched the crossbow in her hand, turning a blind eye to the carnage around.
This was the crossbow given to her by Lide, too bad that heartless capitalist was nowhere to be found now.
Now, facing the destruction of Crimson Moon, he still hadn’t shown up…
A surge of resentment boiled in her heart.
“It’s a pity, Anos City definitely can’t be held this time. Even if Lide were here, faced with this situation, he probably could be of no help.”
“No one could withstand the millions of Fierce Half-Ratmen…”
“It’s so frustrating, has everything we invested this past year been in vain?”
Zhao Yue took a deep breath, their resignation mixed with a hint of unwillingness as they stepped away, their irregular movement maintaining retreat speed while still managing to shoot backwards, their full figure combined with agile movements filled with stunning allure.
When all the players of Crimson Moon had retreated to the next position, many had already lost all hope.
The final street beneath their feet was all that was left before the Life Temple–if the temple fell, the resurrected players would lose their base, and then everything would turn to bubbles.
“It’s over, it’s really over this time, even the Destiny Hero, Prince Anos, is surrounded by the Fierce Half-Ratmen, there’s no hope left for Anos City…”
“Sigh, I always say free stuff shouldn’t be taken. I knew Anos City was in trouble the moment they were giving away land. It must be the game designers intentionally creating a monster siege, just to prevent players from freeloading. Damn these game designers, fuck them…”
“Should we give up? Continuing to fight just means dying one more time…”
“It’s a definite loss, after fighting to this point, not even a Transcendent could save us, unless some Divine being suddenly appears and wipes out all these Fierce Half-Ratmen…”
“Divine being? Haha, are you dreaming?”
Despair permeated every player in Anos City.
At this point, almost no one believed Anos City could still hold.
The fall was inevitable; many players were already considering a strategic retreat…
Fickle hearts, sagging morale.
And in the official livestream of “Glory,” the cunning cameras were focused on the players discussing fervently, their words instantly sending the livestream viewers into an uproar.
“Can’t blame them, holding up to this level is already quite remarkable. If you ask me, they might as well give up; why stubbornly defend this place and waste experience…”
“It’s done, even gods can’t help now…”
“Anos City has fallen, which city will be next? I’m now wondering if it’s worth staying in Green City; at this rate, flattening Green City is just a likely event.”
The chat was overwhelmingly pessimistic, shattering the fantasies of any hopeful players.
The city’s main support, Prince Anos and the Centaurs were trapped at the entrance of the city wall, facing the insane onslaught of hundreds of thousands of Fierce Half-Ratmen, annihilation was only a matter of time.
Moreover, they were cut off from escape.
With morale low and numbers dwindling, the remaining players were clearly overwhelmed by the fearlessly fierce Half-Ratmen.
Subsequent developments also followed everyone’s expectations; Anos City continued to be slowly consumed, eventually leading to players fleeing out of the city, not even the native military governors could stop the rout.
The situation became clearer, the fall of Anos City was no longer suspenseful, especially when the Fierce Half-Ratmen attacked from the rear gates of Anos City, eventually surrounding both the Mage Tower and the Life Goddess Temple, signaling the war was nearing its end.
Under the relentless encroachment of the numerous Fierce Half-Ratmen, the territory controlled by the players was diminishing step by step.
But just as everyone thought the war was over, an anomaly arose.
The dense clouds in the sky plummeted down like collapsing mountains, a frightening aura that seemed like the Abyss Demon God tearing through space and climbing out onto the Main Plane spread everywhere.
Level eighteen storms whipped up tens of millions of tons of seawater crashing into the rocks, thundering mightily.
What was this??
Amidst everyone’s confusion, the rolling clouds coalesced into a vortex, and suddenly a shadow appeared in the sky; then, as if drawn by something, the dark clouds surged downward.
The scene was like a doomsday myth from the mouth of a wandering bard; the entire sky’s black clouds formed a vortex then continuously spiraled downwards, until eventually the massive vortex slowly descended into Anos City.
The viewers in the live room, upon seeing this awe-inspiring event, fell into a death-like silence for a long period, even the chat went quiet for a considerable time.
Only when the black cloud vortex dissipated and peace returned to the world did the online comments explode.
“What was that?? Fuck, why not zoom in?”
“Quick, let’s see!!”
“Did something fall from the sky??”
The official livestream’s camera, seeming to sense the audience’s thoughts, instantly zoomed in and focused on what had descended from the clouds.
When the camera finally focused and everyone saw the being that caused the heavenly anomaly, they all gasped in shock.
“What the hell is that monster??”
“Too terrifying…”
“What a strong presence, look at those fierce half-rat men retreating, and even some are kneeling…”
In the clearing where the Centaur Army was besieged, a monster appeared before everyone’s eyes. It was a towering five-blade tall creature, covered in disgusting tumors, resembling an enlarged version of a fierce half-rat man.
This monster was even uglier than the fierce half-rat men, but the aura it emitted made everyone’s throat tighten.
Transcendent!!
Yes, it was the breath of Transcendence!
At this moment, not only were the players watching the livestream in an uproar, but the natives around Anos City who observed the scene through magic were also terrified.
Many immediately used magic to send the information about the Evil God’s Transcendent back to Green City.
When Duke O’Kelly received this news, his heart was instantly filled with horror.
The thing he feared the most had finally happened.
The evil life in Risier City had shown the combat power he least wanted to see.
Transcendent.
This meant that Green City’s greatest trump card, Lord Rock, an Extraordinary Mage, was no longer confidential, as their opponent now possessed combat power capable of contending with them.
Originally, he could maintain enough calmness within, but now he was truly panicked.
If Anos City were breached, would their next target be Green City?
And who could be sure that the evil forces in Risier City only had one Transcendent Existence, or worse, did they possess even greater power beyond Transcendent??
All of this was cloaked in a fatal veil.
“Bishop, has Lord Ilo sent any messages?”
The reporting bishop shook his head, “Sorry, Lord Ilo has not appeared since the battle of Risier City…”
“Keep a close watch on Anos City, I need to know everything about that evil Transcendent after it appears! Also, find Lord Ilo as soon as possible, Green City needs the protection of a true powerhouse!”
—-
—-
Players using gaming pods and helmets to watch the livestream were nearly scared out of their minds by that five-blade tall Transcendent half-rat man.
The aura it released struck directly at their souls.
Those who hadn’t played “Glory” before experienced for the first time what soul-level suppression felt like.
It was as if someone had their arms around their neck and a rock pressing on their chest, making it extremely difficult for them to breathe.
“Transcendent?? Is this what Transcendent feels like? I was literally scared shitless…”
“Is this really just a game? How can that presence be so real?!”
“I couldn’t even breathe the moment I saw that monster, mom, it’s too terrifying…”
The chat in the livestream was overwhelmed by messages, everyone was extremely shocked by the sudden appearance of the Transcendent.
For many “Glory” players, it was their first close encounter with a Transcendent. The official livestream had brought everything about the Transcendent without any compromise.
Ordinary games use visuals, music, colors, and other external factors to induce fear, but the Transcendent of Glory just by standing there, without any action, made everyone feel weak.
The pressure it emitted wasn’t something a game could simulate; it was the fear that lower-level beings feel when encountering higher-level beings, just like a mouse encountering a cat, naturally feeling terrified.
After the arrival of that Transcendent half-rat man, the aerial half-rat men and the fierce half-rat men originally covering the Centaur Army started to retreat frantically, revealing the Centaur Army in just a few breaths.
Only then could the players clearly see the scene through the livestream.
The Centaur Army formed a circular military formation, with the heavily armored centaurs on the outside and the centaurs wielding bows inside.
Around the perimeter of the formation, the bodies of fierce half-rat men had already piled up seven to eight blades high, the Centaurs even built a wall composed of the bodies of fierce half-rat men.
The terrifying Land of Death.
Of course, the number of Centaurs also dropped from over ten thousand to six thousand under the crazy siege of the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
The casualties were unspeakably heavy.
Now, the armor of Prince Anos, who had led the charge, was nearly shattered, covered densely with marks left by the Fierce Half-Ratmen.
This was an army almost in ruins.
But what was worse, this broken army had encountered an even more powerful enemy–Extraordinary Half-Ratmen.
Prince Anos felt the opponent’s aura, mighty like that of an Abyssal Giant Beast, turned to look at the Centaur Army behind him, and already realized that there was no will left in him to survive.
The opponent had sent an Extraordinary… there was no hope left.
Bitterness overwhelmed his mouth, perhaps he would never return to the Nolan Capital to seek revenge in his lifetime.
“Lowly Centaurs, and that worthless life, I sense a familiar aura upon you… the damned New Sun God!”
Unexpectedly, the Extraordinary Half-Ratman did not immediately start the slaughter, but instead, coldly looked towards Prince Anos.
Ancient blasphemous language resounded through the sky.
“That despicable New Sun God snatched my Divine Artifact in Risier City and his Divine Country… this hatred will never perish, he will become my war trophy!”
Outside Anos City, many natives heard this tone and were instantly in an uproar, as many widened their eyes, watching the scene created by the Spellcasters, stuttering.
“This, this isn’t just Extraordinary, it’s the Evil God from inside Risier City!”
Hiss~
The crowd around gasped when they heard these words.
The Evil God?? That was a thousand times more terrifying than the Extraordinary.
“Are you sure??”
“His tone and the chilling evil speech are exactly like the Evil God from Risier City!! By the Creator God, it is the God of Plague himself who has come this time…”
It didn’t take long for more than one native to confirm from the information spoken by the Extraordinary Half-Ratman that the perpetrator inside Risier City was indeed the God of Plague.
Although it was unclear why he had descended onto a Half-Ratman of only Extraordinary Level, everybody knew that after the arrival of this Evil God, the last spark of Anos City was extinguished.
Many people among the spectators had already begun to prepare to leave this place because once Anos City fell, no one could guarantee that the Evil God would not start a massacre.
The God of Plague looked indifferently at the Centaur Army before him, his eyes intently staring at Prince Anos.
He sensed the Bloodline of Bloodline upon him, an aura that he could never forget, that damned New Sun God!!!
The killing intent began to climb steadily; this body, forged at great cost into a 24th-level Extraordinary, contained immensely terrifying power.
He intended to slaughter these Centaurs alone, then extract the Vampire’s soul for interrogation, to find traces of the New Sun God!
With killing intent surging and gaze as sharp as lightning, the body of the God of Plague, 5 blades tall, like a statue cast from copper water, suddenly erupted.
Within the space of a few blinks, he had crossed a distance of over a hundred blades and, watched by billions of viewers during the live broadcast, this 5-blade-tall monster charged directly into the Centaur Army, initiating a brutally sanguinary massacre.
Although the Centaurs wore Steel Armor forged by Dwarves, in the face of a 24-level Extraordinary, especially one bearing a portion of the soul power of the God of Plague, all their resistance at this moment proved futile.
The claws in the hands of the God of Plague were 1 blade long, and the long spears thrust by the Centaurs were snapped like wild grasses.
The spears that struck him were like poking an iron plate with a wooden stick, utterly incapable of breaching his defense.
The long-suppressed roar of the God of Plague now completely spilled over onto the Centaurs.
His body, like the most ferocious Hulk, rampaged and killed through the Centaur Army, shredding all who dared to block his path.
Blood and limbs flew.
The entire Centaur Army was utterly unable to stop him.
The scene looked like a doomsday mural from a church, shocking and terrifying.
Inside the live stream room, seeing the power of the God of Plague, everyone exploded.
With just a casual swing of his claws, he could tear through the strong Centaurs wearing Steel Armor, so powerful it made one’s scalp tingle.
“Fuck, this is just a pure human-shaped mech!! Who can beat that??”
“With a spear as thick as my wrist, just tearing it apart like that?? That’s insane!!”
“I bet even the Hulk in his normal state couldn’t beat this monster!”
“Anos City has really bad luck, being attacked by so many fierce half-ratmen, and in the end, an Extraordinary Level monster shows up…”
“What Extraordinary? Don’t you know? This monster is the Evil God from inside Risier City, now somehow descended into this monster.”
“There’s such a move? Isn’t Anos City even more screwed now?”
Netizens are watching the excitement, but the players are sighing non-stop; it’s their main city, targeted by an Evil God, and even players not affiliated with Anos City feel stifled and annoyed.
You, as an NPC, being awesome is one thing, but to ruin our only main city in “Glory,” are you even human??
But NPC forces are strong, and there’s nowhere for their frustration to go.
“Damn, these goddamn game planners, they just can’t stand to see us thrive, finally managed to establish a player-friendly main city, and now they simply send a god to destroy it!!”
“Right, I just felt something was off. Why would an Evil God pass by just because we are a few levels up? Definitely those damn game planners are pissed at us and decided to annihilate the player’s main city…”
“Another question, who knows the official website of Glory? Damn them!!”
“Is there anyone who can save this city??”
It could be called a tragic connection between the viewers and players watching the livestream, but for the players in Anos City, only despair could describe their feeling.
When the blasphemous language echoed across the sky, when that Extraordinary aura pressed down on their hearts despite thousands of blades away, the air fell silent.
Everyone was consumed by despair.
Extraordinary… these fierce half-ratmen even had an Extraordinary descent…
Everything was gone.
Zhao Yue stood on top of the ruins of a collapsed building, frantically pulling the trigger of her crossbow. Though her heart held no hope anymore, she still clenched her teeth in a final effort, determined to die on the battlefield!
Since the president of Crimson Moon was not around, she had to take up the responsibility!
Hun Yuan Thunderclap Hand Cheng Kun, the top three leaders of the Dark Contract Guild, also looked bitter as they watched the dwindling number of players emerging from the Life Goddess Temple, a sight of helplessness filling their views.
Players knew it was futile; except for those from their own guild, no one was willing to revive and face death again.
It’s all over, once Anos City falls, the Dark Contract Guild is likely to decline… They had invested so much, and losing everything now, it would be tough to regain such a powerful force as before.
Puchi~
As Hun Yuan was lost in thought, a sharp pain suddenly pierced his chest. Glancing down, he saw the arm of a fierce half-rat man protruding through his torso.
Blood was everywhere.
“Second Brother!!?”
“Fuck!!”
“President!”
Thunderclap Hand and Cheng Kun quickly stepped up, killed the fierce half-rat man in a few moves, but Hun Yuan’s eyes had already lost focus.
In his last moments, with a trace of pain he said, “Damn it, it hurts…
If possible, keep leading the remaining people to hold on till the end, since we can’t retreat anyway…”
As his words fell, Hun Yuan heard the system’s prompt that he would need to wait 8 hours to resurrect, but just a second before he logged out, a voice boomed through the sky like thunder, making him widen his eyes in shock.
“The God of Plague? Who gave you the courage to run wild on my turf?…”
Then, blurred voices of surprise and joy followed from the surrounding people.
“Lord Ilo?!!”
The God of Plague rampaged through the Centaur Army, triggering a bloody massacre.
Just when everyone had lost all hope, suddenly a voice like thunder from the heavens crashed down.
Above Risier City, an indifferent voice echoed continuously.
“God of Plague? Who gave you the courage to run wild on my turf?…”
This?
Upon hearing this, everyone simultaneously looked up. Zhao Yue’s eyes widened as she stared into the sky, her heart shaken, feeling an inexplicably familiar sensation…
The players besieged around the Life Goddess Temple also looked up to where the voice was coming from.
Many exclaimed instinctively.
“Lord Ilo!!”
Yes, Lord Ilo, who had intimidated the Ancient Evil God inside Risier City, appeared at a moment when Anos City was about to fall and seemed almost beyond saving.
The crowd, previously swallowed by despair, felt as though a beam of light had suddenly illuminated their gloomy hearts.
Their hearts filled with indescribable excitement and hope.
At the last moment of Anos City’s fall, that figure appeared like a savior, under the gaze of countless eyes.
In the sky.
Lide wore a pristine white mage’s robe, his features as if crafted by a legendary sculptor with a lifetime of dedication, exquisite and perfect, an elegant aura enveloped in that sacred light adding an indescribable mystery.
His entire being emitted a captivating charm, dazzling and mesmerizing to those who saw him.
The Power of Faith flowed gently from him, a faint holy glow shining like the bright moonlight beneath the dense black clouds.
Lide floated in midair, the pure holy light he emanated starkly contrasted with the surrounding dark and evil aura.
At this moment, he descended in the guise of a savior, and he indeed was the savior.
Especially against the backdrop of the brutal and cruel God of Plague, Lide’s arrival was like a ray of sunlight piercing through an ancient dark sky.
The world became brighter because of his presence.
At this moment, he seemed to represent hope, the faith of everyone.
Just by appearing, Lide had maximized his prominence.
Especially with the contrast of the God of Plague, his image shone even more brilliantly and nobly.
Seeing this, Lide smiled internally. The Dawn Sect would soon preach in the human world, and the higher his reputation now, the more it would facilitate their mission. He had chosen this moment to appear after much deliberation…
At this moment, billions of Earth’s netizens had not yet heard Lide’s voice, but the thunderous sound that filled the sky had them filled with curiosity.
Who is the fool daring to show up under these circumstances?!
The official live broadcast camera swiftly turned, suddenly focusing on the figure suspended in the sky.
Lide, with his charisma, attractiveness, and imposing aura, appeared on the live broadcast screen.
After a moment of silence in the chat, the comments exploded as if going crazy.
“Ahhh~ How can he be so handsome!!!”
“I can’t take it anymore, licking the screen~ slurp~”
“Is this really an NPC? Totally in love…”
“honey, look at him~ If you were even half as handsome as this NPC, you can call me whatever you want every night…”
“My mom walked into the room and asked why I was licking the screen with my tongue…”
“Can’t believe I found an NPC who is half as handsome as me here, truly this game is the most realistic, indeed extraordinary…”
The previously silent female netizens went into a frenzy upon seeing Lide’s near-perfect appearance, the comments were dozens of times more than usual.
The impact on the ladies was simply indescribable.
Just as everyone marveled at Lide’s looks,
The scene changed once again.

Chapter 417: Chapter 419: Title – Savior, The Far from Over Post-War Turbulence (7600 words)
Anos City.
Above the sky, the black clouds swirled like a vortex, exuding an icy and evil aura as if an abyss demon god capable of devouring the world was about to emerge.
The dull rumbling thunder did not stop after the God of Plague had been killed. The bright arcs within the clouds were like bent whips, tearing the cloud cover to shreds.
After the God of Plague was killed, Lide floated in mid-air gently like a feather, his pure white mage robe was dotted with bloodstains like plum blossoms.
Lide, stained with fresh blood, became the sole and eternal image against this dazzling Dark Type backdrop.
Billions of netizens in the official live broadcast room couldn’t help but feel surprised as they witnessed this scene; following the excitement of seeing the God of Plague being instantly killed, they found the calm after the storm even more enchanting.
At that time, Lide didn’t think too much. His lingering immobility in mid-air was merely because he had exhausted all his Bloodline Power with a single strike to kill the God of Plague.
His legs were weak from the exhaustion of his Bloodline Power, like the feeling of getting up at four in the morning after a night of repeated indulgence.
Feeble.
Other than replenishing through the consumption of fresh blood, Bloodline Power could only be restored slowly over a long time.
Killing the Level 24 God of Plague in a single second seemed effortless, but it was definitely not as easy as outsiders perceived.
Only after the weakness caused by the deficit of his Bloodline Power eased slightly did Lide begin to take stock of the situation below.
Anos City was now encased in ice.
29 mixed spells–Extreme Cold Thunderstorms–that were more powerful than level 5 spells directly dealt a devastating blow to the Fierce Half-Ratmen within the city.
Of course, there were quite a few that slipped through the net, but those Fierce Half-Ratmen who were not killed instantly lost their ferocious disregard for death after the God of Plague was vanquished, and began to run toward the outside of the city in a panic.
Within the vast city below, besides ice sculptures, only the Centaur Army at the city gates, which had not been affected by the Magic Fluctuations, remained. However, these centaurs also suffered a tragic hit, their numbers dropping from tens of thousands to less than 4,000, losing over 60%.
The players near the Anos Mage Tower and the Life Goddess temple were also spared from the Extreme Cold Thunderstorms because of Lide’s deliberate control, avoiding complete annihilation.
About ten thousand were left… From millions of players, only about ten thousand survived, a loss of 99%. It was more than just tragic.
Aside from these two areas, the rest of the buildings were draped in solid frost.
Bodies, blood, limbs, broken weapons, collapsed buildings, ice sculptures of the writhing Fierce Half-Ratmen, Death Flowers condensed by the power of extreme cold…
This apocalyptic scene was filled with desolation and an unspeakable eeriness.
The camera in the live broadcast room moved above Lide, and then billions of people saw the scene below from his perspective.
Instantly, they all went wild.
“I have to say, Lord Ilo is just insanely cool. He appeared and solved this big trouble with only two moves; it’s beyond words.”
“A whole city, frozen solid, that’s nuts. If NPCs are all this awesome, what’s even the point for us players…”
“I wonder if we could ever reach that level? I really hope to one day wave my hand and annihilate an entire city!!”
“This is the legendary Savior, appearing at the critical moment, one move to awe the entire field. If I wasn’t a guy, I’d do anything to sleep with him…”
“Cough cough, don’t be so fixated on gender, just because he’s a guy doesn’t mean you don’t stand a chance…”
The aftermath of the battle left players unable to calm down for a long time.
Whether it was freezing an entire city or tearing apart a 6-meter-tall giant monster with bare hands, the name ‘Lord Ilo’ became an indelible symbol in everyone’s hearts.
But just as the camera zoomed out, the livestream for over a billion people was abruptly interrupted.
In the livestream, all that remained was Lide in his blood-stained robe, floating in midair, his profound gaze overlooking the earth.
The engrossed players were stunned, then hurriedly tried to reconnect, only to find the message–The Battle of Anos City concluded, livestream system shut down.
Everyone was left with a face full of question marks.
This was just too damn annoying.
How could it just end when it was getting so exciting???
Netizens were furious, cursing the game developers, calling them inhuman.
Many players immediately went to the official forum to start a furious tirade against the operations and planners of “Glory.”
“Damn game planners, did a dog eat your brain?!! Cutting off the livestream at a time like this??!”
“Which idiotic operator is this! I want to see Lord Ilo!!! I need to see!!!”
“Give me back my livestream!! What’s the big deal with turning it back on? My Lord Ilo vanished… wah wah wah… I can’t handle this blow.”
“Lord Ilo is so cool, I’m in love with this handsome guy… No, I have to go to Anos City, I have to go and have his monkey babies.”
“Draw your swords, Lord Ilo is mine. I hereby declare, this man has caught my eye.”
…
Lide was unaware of the whole livestream incident and, after somewhat recovering, he headed straight above the Centaur Army.
Just as he was about to say something, he suddenly felt an unusual Magic Fluctuation in the surrounding space. With a slight gesture, a powerful wave of Magic Power surged out in all directions.
Those abnormal Magic Fluctuations were instantly subdued under the deliberate disruption of the shock wave, and the surroundings returned to normal.
Outside Anos City at this moment, the Spellcasters who had been using magic to observe the city’s scenes suddenly turned crimson, then spewed out a mouthful of fresh blood, clearly suffering significant injuries.
Unexpectedly, these Spellcasters were not dissatisfied but rather had expressions of relief and gratitude.
“Lord Ilo does not like outsiders spying with magic… Thankfully, thankfully it’s just a minor injury…”
A player beside them looked puzzled at the native Mage, “You’re injured and yet you look like you’ve found a Gold Puck?”
“Ignorant adventurers from the Lost Plane, what do you understand? His Lordship is an eternal Divine, to rashly spy on the Divine is a sin of sacrilege, it is only the magnanimity of the great Lord Ilo that prevented us from being turned into idiots by the backlash of our own Magic Power… Lord Ilo held back…”
After finishing, the Mage’s face was full of admiration, “Truly worthy of Lord Ilo, even us lowly Mages are treated so kindly, a perfect existence…”
The players exchanged glances upon hearing this, lowly Mages? Damn, if you Mages are lowly, then no one in this world can be considered lowly, not even the proud Elves could be as conceited as you…
But then they also felt a touch of envy, this Lord Ilo really was something else, to have them injured and still feeling extremely honored…
Ah, if only they could be that cool, then they’d have whatever beauties they wanted and as many Gold Pucks as they wished… Several players were lost in their fantasies.
Little did they dream that Lord Ilo, whom they were eyeing with envy, was also from Earth, just like them…
Upon seeing Lide descend, the Centaur Army all placed their right fists over their hearts in salute.
“Good day, my Lord!”
This Centaur Army was the Iron Hoof Tribe’s military force, which had once stormed into Risier City under Lide’s command.
Although these rank-and-file warriors weren’t very clear about the true relation between the Iron Hoof Tribe and Lide, they knew it was enough to serve the sovereign they pledged loyalty to.
Prince Anos of Anos City, standing before the centaurs, had his armor not only stained black and red with blood but also nearly shattered. Even his greatsword had several noticeable notches. One could tell at a glance that he had faced a bitter battle.
Upon seeing Lide, Prince Anos promptly dismounted and bowed his head in the most humble gesture.
“My Lord, good day.”
Then he stood up slightly, his expression somewhat bitter, “I’ve let you down, Anos City…”
Lide waved his hand to interrupt Prince Nolan.
“No need for more words. Anos City is not strong enough yet. To hold up against the assault of millions of Divine Servants is already commendable.”
After speaking, he turned his head to look at the devastated city around him, “Your next task is to rebuild Anos City.
The Ancient Evil Gods will descend when snow covers the land.
We don’t have much time left.”
Being attacked by the God of Plague was highly likely. The Ancient Evil Gods’ return wasn’t just about them re-entering this world; they would inevitably contest with the existing powers for living space, perhaps even devour all life on the Main Plane.
Anos City was only three to four hundred kilometers from Risier City, not far for the beings of this world, and with the Ancient players causing trouble, being targeted was not strange at all.
Although the crisis was averted, city construction was the next crucial task.
After pondering for a moment, Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly.
“Anos City needs to continue strengthening its construction, and I will send you 500 One-eyed Giants later.”
500 One-eyed Giants were equivalent to 500 flesh and blood excavators. Their efficiency was bound to satisfy.
“My Lord, Anos City will never face today’s situation again! I guarantee it with my life!” Prince Anos said, filled with gratitude and determination.
Lide just waved his hand without saying much.
This city, newly established for a year, to possess such strength was already remarkable.
What was Dawn City like when it was established for a year? Not to mention facing millions of Divine Servants, even a hundred thousand would be a struggle.
As Lide was discussing the future development of Anos City with Prince Anos, a cautious group of players approached the city walls, emerging from the ice sculptures that had not yet thawed.
The Centaur Army, however, stopped them in their tracks.
“Prince Anos…
“Lord Ilo…”
Hearing the players’ shouts, Lide turned slightly to look at the excited and eager group, which made him secretly amused.
At this moment, these players were probably thinking that they had finally seen the big boss, and were likely scheming to get some benefits from him, ideally a Divine Artifact or two.
“Let them in.”
“Yes, my Lord.”
After receiving the order, the centaurs no longer blocked the players, who were bursting with excitement at the prospect of getting closer.
They were about to meet Lord Ilo, the ultimate being who had frozen the entire city, who had killed over a million Fierce Half-Ratmen.
This was amazing! If they could gain favor with this super boss, they would be set for life. The player known as the ‘Broken Sword Knight’ wouldn’t matter at all.
Every one of them carried the thought of winning favor, their eyes shining with anticipation.
As Zhao Yue drew closer to Lord Ilo, her feelings became increasingly strange.
Despite Lide’s significantly altered appearance, she couldn’t shake the feeling that she had seen Lord Ilo somewhere before.
But how could she forget such a high-level being that she had met, especially one so handsome…
“Great Lord Ilo, the Baby Gold Water Guild offers you our most respectful greetings.”
“Lord Ilo, I am the President of Qiuming Mountain Fast Lane Guild. It is an honor to meet you.”
“Good day, Lord Ilo, I am Zhao Buqun, President of the Five Mountains Sword Sects Guild…”
“I am from the Mountain Climbing Team Guild…”
“I am from the Rat’s Tail Guild…”
The Presidents of these guilds had all commanded players in battle below, so they had survived to the end. Reaching Lide, each one greeted him with shining eyes, their excitement surpassing that of discovering a gold mine.
Lide’s mouth twitched fiercely upon hearing the names of these guilds; Baby Gold Water? Qiuming Mountain Fast Lane? And Zhao Buqun?
What on earth were these ridiculous people thinking? Could they actually get their guild names registered at the Mercenary Guild? How many Gold Pucks did they have to stuff to get their families to accept them??
Ignoring these absurd players trying to curry favor, his gaze turned to Zhao Yue, who was looking at him with a doubtful expression and a furrowed brow.
Seeing this voluptuous sister, Lide felt somewhat guilty inside. After all, he had delegated the huge responsibility of the Crimson Moon Guild to her, which was truly treating her like a tool…
But after thinking for a bit, Lide, the old capitalist, reassured himself. He was training Zhao Yue! If he didn’t trust her, how could he entrust such an important company to her? He was enhancing her abilities, and besides, he was paying her a salary…
Casting aside his slight guilt, he looked towards Zhao Yue with an air of righteousness.
“President Yue, good day…”
Hmm?
This??
The guild leaders around him who were trying to curry favor widened their eyes?
What on earth?
Lord Ilo actually took the initiative to greet someone??
Each and every one of them turned their gazes towards Zhao Yue, clad in assassin leather armor and of extremely voluptuous build, their eyes filled with curiosity.
So this is what you were like, Lord Ilo… Here we thought you were a decent person, it turns out you’re just like us…
If we knew you liked this type, we would have brought our secretaries over…
Zhao Yue was stunned for a moment; she hadn’t expected this super boss to greet her, but after Lide spoke, she felt an even stronger sense of familiarity.
“Good day, Lord Ilo…” Zhao Yue responded with a hint of hesitation, “Please forgive my impertinence, but I can’t shake the feeling that I know you…”
Know him?
The guild leaders around her were instantly intrigued.
Among the twenty-something guild leaders present, only Zhao Yue and another plain-looking middle-aged woman were female guild leaders, and with Zhao Yue’s hotness, she naturally attracted a lot of attention.
There’s something scandalous here… These old LSPs all had faces full of gossip, fantasizing about a hundred and eighty scenarios in their minds…
Lide was also a bit surprised; he hadn’t expected to still be recognized by Zhao Yue even after all his efforts. Were women so unreasonable in this respect??
His thoughts whirred as he spoke slowly.
“Know me? That’s interesting…” Seeing that Lide spoke so casually, Zhao Yue’s doubt somewhat faded, and just as she was about to speak, Lide’s next sentence made her eyes widen.
“The president of your Crimson Moon Guild is currently visiting my temple, and it was he who reported to me the news of Anos City being besieged by the Ancient Evil God.”
Now it dawned on Zhao Yue; she had always felt that Lord Ilo was very familiar, and she finally realized that familiar feeling was Lide.
This Lord Ilo had a strangely similar vibe to that heartless boss…
“Lord Ilo, how is our president doing now?”
Zhao Yue couldn’t help being curious; at this stage, Lide was actually able to contact someone of Lord Ilo’s caliber, no wonder he hadn’t returned to Crimson Moon for a long time.
“He is currently carrying out a mission for me, you needn’t worry, this mission is very important and will take a long time…”
Lide spoke confidently, finding a perfect excuse for his own slacking off.
Seeing Zhao Yue about to speak up again, Lide quickly cut off the older sister; he didn’t want to reveal too much to the meticulous Zhao Yue, as saying too much could lead to trouble.
His expression turned serious.
“The old days are coming, you all go down and prepare. I will establish Dawn Temple in Anos City in the future, we will meet again.”
Zhao Yue still had a lot she wanted to say, but Lide had issued a command to leave and she could only retreat reluctantly.
The other players were even more resentful, having finally got such an opportunity, but before they could finish their words, they were sent away… Sigh, when would they ever be truly qualified to interact with such high-level individuals.
After the players left, Lide relaxed his expression, considering that at their current stage, players could only be left to develop on their own; they would only be useful to him once they grew stronger.
He turned his head again to look at Prince Anos.
“Those fallen adventurers can be given certain rewards, such as contribution points for Anos City or the right to enter certain regulated areas, or you can grant them the right to exchange equipment.
In any case, make sure these adventurers receive some benefits, to more closely bind them with Anos City.”
“Lord, this will cost quite a lot…” Prince Anos hesitated.
“Don’t worry, I will provide support for the missing materials, and besides, Anos City has now reached the scale where it can collect business taxes; in the future, you can keep the taxes collected from adventurer transactions for your own development.”
Initially, in order to develop Anos City and attract players to settle down, the entire city was tax-free. Now that the players had grown wings, it was time to harvest them.
“Yes, Lord…”
As Lide tasked Prince Anos, the last Fierce Half-Ratman silently sneaked out from atop the city walls of Anos City.
When no other creatures existed in Anos City, the system’s prompt sounded.
“Ding~ You have reversed the battle of Anos City and saved a city; in the process, you killed over a million Fierce Half-Ratmen, and under the watchful eyes of countless people, you killed the body of a Level 24 giant Fierce Half-Ratman controlled by the Ancient Evil God.
You have gained 100,000 experience points and acquired the title–Savior.”
“Savior: You have single-handedly slain over a million monsters and always appear at the most dire moments, everyone sees you as the reliance to reverse adverse situations, Legend Level +30.
When you are on the losing side, you will receive the Power of Salvation for 10 minutes. Power of Salvation: All Attributes increase by 2000%, and all friendly soldiers gain the morale boost trait reinforcement.”
Lide showed a hint of surprise upon hearing the system’s prompt.
Savior?
This title was quite impressive.
He would gain the Power of Salvation lasting 10 minutes when at a disadvantage, not only increasing all attributes by 2000%, but also boosting the morale of all soldiers.
Unbelievably strong.
Lide was in a great mood.
Compared to the invaluable title of Savior, those 100,000 experience points didn’t seem like much.
His emotions surged for a while before calming down, and after re-reading the system prompts a few times, Lide’s eyes showed a hint of contemplation.
You had to single-handedly kill over a million monsters and save a city to get this title… That’s no low bar.
If he hadn’t learned to fuse spells while soloing in Half-Elf Main City before, it would’ve been impossible to freeze an entire city.
But regardless of how high the threshold was, he had now reached it.
The next time he came to the rescue, he might not even need to expend those 100,000 Power of Faith to tear apart a Level 24 God of Plague with his bare hands.
Thinking this, Lide felt a bit of regret because killing the God of Plague didn’t drop anything, not even a Divine Artifact or Divine Calamity.
If the God of Plague had known what Lide was thinking at that moment, he would have cursed vehemently. “You’ve stolen my arms, my head, my Divine Position, and even my Divine Artifacts… and you still claim you haven’t gained anything? What the hell?”
After being tricked several times, the God of Plague had learned his lesson and this time only descended with part of his soul power, without bringing any Divine Artifacts or infusing this body with divinity…
The previous encounters with this Ancient Evil God had psychologically scarred Lide, especially that time at the Land of Bone-Burying–when the God of Plague transferred his divinity into the Land of Bone-Burying using a Divine Artifact, aiming for a deadly blow to Lide. In the end, though, Lide managed to cut off the Space Gate, not only causing the God of Plague to lose a massive amount of divinity but also to misplace the Divine Artifact.
The incident nearly shattered the God of Plague’s soul, from which he developed a habit of being cautious and vigilant… If Lide knew the God of Plague’s current state, he would certainly be very pleased and make the other party thank him for it.
Even though he couldn’t plunder anything else from the God of Plague, acquiring the title of Savior was enough to compensate for his losses.
After merrily exiting the attribute panel, Lide, Prince of Anos, watched the surrounding centaurs waiting for his command and raised an eyebrow.
“Gather the corpses of the centaurs and record each of their names.
We will hold a public funeral after the players have resurrected. Our heroes should not be forgotten.”
These words moved the centaurs nearby, as no warrior would not wish to be buried with honor after death, and naturally, centaurs were no exception.
“As you command, my Lord…”
And with the end of the Battle for Anos City, the real storm was just beginning.
Lide couldn’t be said to have become famous overnight because his legend had already been circulating in the martial world before, recognized by both the players on forums and the original inhabitants of Green City.
But this time, Lide became even more prominent, becoming the center of energetic discussions among netizens across the entire Earth without his knowledge.
Most players had only seen pictures of “Glory” online before and had never watched such a direct and impressive live broadcast of “Glory.”
Those who watched the Battle for Anos City using gaming pods and helmets experienced the charm of “Glory” firsthand.
Whether it was the ferocity of the Fierce Half-Ratmen, the variety of tactics employed by the players in resistance, or the vicious assault of the Centaur Army as they charged through the camps, all left a deep impression on them.
Of course, there was only one protagonist of this war–Lord Ilo.
Lord Ilo’s appearance in times of crisis to save everyone and his overwhelming power to freeze an entire city left a deep impression on the netizens.
Added to that his near-perfect looks, he completely ignited the players’ enthusiasm.
Lord Ilo, a name that became known to the entire Earth.
Powerful, mysterious, handsome, charming… it seemed all positive adjectives could be applied to him.
For several consecutive days, “Lord Ilo” related terms occupied the top three spots on all search rankings.
“Lord Ilo is the strongest boss in ‘Glory,'” “The most handsome NPC in history,” “My husband Ilo,” “Twelve little tricks to win over Ilo,” “Secrets I must not tell about Lord Ilo”…
Due to the live broadcast, “Glory” significantly increased in influence, drawing a large number of players who frantically urged the production of “Glory” gaming pods, not satisfied without posting dozens of messages each day.
Especially Ilo’s little fangirls, who were going so crazy that they wished they could strangle the manufacturers of “Glory.” This resulted in the market price of “Glory” gaming pods skyrocketing; the original factory price of 100,000 soared to a market value where no one would sell even for 1,000,000…
Lide was unaware that he had caused such a stir on Earth and that Lord Ilo had become a household name. After resolving the issues in Anos City, he immediately prepared to return to Dawn City.
Although the war in the Underworld had temporarily ceased, there were still many issues that required his strategic decision-making, particularly as the time of the Ancient Descent approached, he felt an increasing sense of urgency.
A crisis was bound to erupt soon, and he needed to prepare more.
However, just as he was about to set off, a sudden report from Prince Anos caught him by surprise.
“Your Highness, the City Lord of Green City, Duke O’Kelly Nolan has come to request an audience…”
Duke O’Kelly Nolan, a member of the Nolan Royal Family, the ruler of the southern province…
Lide’s eyebrows rose; what did this royal noble want with him?
He had met Duke O’Kelly once before, when the Crimson Mage Tower was completed. The Duke had visited to extend his congratulations, courtesy of Lide’s teacher Spark, but their interaction had merely consisted of a nod and polite greetings.
During the battle of Risier City, though Duke O’Kelly had deployed his troops, at the time Lide was preoccupied with resolving the God of Plague issue and didn’t pay much attention to the human armies, nor had he any encounters with them.
Why would Duke O’Kelly come to him now… no, what did he want with Lord Ilo?
After a brief moment of contemplation, his gaze turned towards the attributes of his alternate identity, Ilo,
When using the Ilo identity in Green City, Legend Level +30, granted the titles Dark Myth and Mythical Mentor.
Dark Myth: Most people in Green City regard you as a legendary figure. Regardless of Dark Creatures or the Light Sect, your favorability naturally rises to the level of respect.
And it comes with the following traits: 1. When facing life forms with a Legend Level 10 points below yours, you gain the Dignity Effect; enemies will fear you, and All Attributes will decrease by 30%,
2. A very high chance to intimidate Dark Creatures with a lower Level than you, compelling them to join you,
3. Holding high reputation among the Green City Nobles and various Sects, granting the right to establish a church and proselytize in Green City.
It had to be admitted that his gains from the previous encounter in Risier City were astonishingly large, just the Legend Level associated with Lord Ilo’s identity alone was enough to let him act unbridled in Green City.
“Let Duke O’Kelly in,” he said.
A spark of keenness appeared in Lide’s eyes, and he would take this opportunity to negotiate with the Duke. The Dawn Sect was now at a stage where it could begin to expand outward.
If this ruler of Green City would collaborate with him in establishing a church, then the subsequent proselytizing would undoubtedly be much easier.
As Lide pondered how to deal with this member of the Nolan Royal Family and ruler of the southern province, footsteps approached.
Prince Anos led a nobleman in his 50s, dressed in magnificent armor, into the hall.
But after the two had met, the Duke, a man of eminent repute and lofty position from the south, did something that left Lide utterly astonished.
As Duke O’Kelly approached him, he suddenly brought his right hand to his chest and then knelt on one knee.
The ruler of the south knelt before him, paying respects as if he were the most devout believer in the presence of their god, or as if a humble subject were supplicating before their sovereign.
“Respected Lord Ilo, I, O’Kelly Nolan, extend to you my most respectful greetings…”
Isn’t this Duke O’Kelly the ruler of the south?
Lide suddenly felt somewhat confounded, the clever arguments he had prepared were all choked back.
His expression quite peculiar.
I haven’t even started, and you’re already like this, young man, can’t we follow the procedure in the future…

chapters.content:
Chapter 418: Chapter 420: The Fatty Sheep That Delivers Itself, The Current Development of Dawn City (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)
Watching Duke O’Keilly kneeling on the ground, Lide’s expression was quite subtle.
He did not know how noble this identity as Lord Ilo had become in the eyes of Duke O’Keilly after the battle at Risier City, and the recent battle at Anos City had amplified this sentiment tenfold.
In the eyes of Duke O’Keilly, the Lide standing before him was a True God descended upon the world, possessing endless power.
Facing the increasingly urgent situation, Green City needed such a strong and towering presence for protection. Yearning inwardly for help and adding to that the frighteningly lofty reputation of Lord Ilo, the ruler of the south could not help but act in such a manner.
Although he did not understand the motive behind Duke O’Keilly’s actions, since the other had already knelt, Lide naturally would not be polite.
“O’Keilly, stand.”
“As you command, Lord…”
After O’Keilly stood up, he cautiously assessed Lide, who wore a pure white priest’s robe that bestowed on him an elegant and dignified air. His incredibly handsome visage was of a mere youth in his early twenties.
Most notable was the faint holy light emanating from Lide, making it feel as if the warm sunshine of a winter’s day was shining upon those nearby, comforting and warm.
“O’Keilly, you’ve sought an audience with me. What is your purpose?”
Lide’s tone was calm and indifferent, his gaze upon O’Keilly like that of an adult watching a child…
A middle-aged man in his fifties being observed in such a manner by a younger man who appeared only to be in his twenties made for an incongruous scene.
But neither thought anything amiss, given that Lide was playing the role of a deity, the great God of Dawn–Lord Ilo, who lived for millions of years. Not acting with a bit of divine demeanor would really be too embarrassing.
Hearing Lide’s indifferent query, Duke O’Keilly felt an unexpected sense of privilege.
Having a conversation with such a powerful divine being had never happened before. Although he held a high position within the God of Nobles Sect, he never had the chance to speak face-to-face with a deity.
He quickly spoke up.
“Lord, the Ancient Day is about to descend, and the entire Nolan Empire will face an unprecedented disaster…”
Upon hearing this, Lide felt that something was amiss and interrupted, “O’Keilly, the descent of the Ancient Day is a choice of fate. I cannot change it, and no one else can either…”
Hopefully, this guy wasn’t asking him to prevent the descent of the Ancient Day. That thing was a pitfall, and he certainly didn’t have the capacity for it.
Duke O’Keilly shook his head, his blue eyes filled with hope as he looked at him.
“Lord, I am aware that the Ancient Day’s arrival is unstoppable, and I do not wish for you to halt it.
Rather, it is my desire to plead for your protection over Green City–to protect the millions of residents when the Ancient Day comes…”
Protect Green City?
Upon hearing this, Lide suddenly took interest. He’d been worrying about how to spread the Dawn Sect; it seemed like a pillow had been delivered just as he was dozing off.
Although he was very interested inwardly, his exterior remained impassive, and he even furrowed his brows.
“O’Keilly, you should know that I once lived in Green City for a time.”
Duke O’Keilly nodded. The matter of Lord Ilo being the ruler of the Dark Contract was not a secret, and he had known it for quite some time.
But back then, before the battle of Risier City began, no one imagined that the head of an Underground Force in Green City could be a great deity.
“Do you know why I chose to live in hiding there?”
At this question, Duke O’Keilly’s eyes widened slightly. After pondering for a moment and with a bitter smile, he shook his head; how could he presume to grasp the actions of a deity?
“Lord, please forgive my ignorance. Were you living a mortal life to comprehend higher levels of power?”
A spark lit up in Lide’s eyes; this explanation was good, why hadn’t he thought of that?
He coughed lightly, nodding and then slowly shaking his head.
“There is that reason…” he agreed shamelessly, “but more importantly, I descended to the Main Plane ahead of time because I sensed the coming of the Ancient Day.
However, I suffered considerable damage in the process, and my power is not as invincible as you imagine.
During this time, I have been searching for ways to recover my strength. Conquering Green City’s Underground Force was merely an effort to use them to find the Magic Materials I need…”
Oh, I see, thought Duke O’Keilly, his face lighting up with sudden understanding; he hadn’t expected such a secret.
Recovering his composure, his eyes brightened slightly–Lord Ilo was injured??
Far from being disappointed, his heart grew even more fervent.
The fact that the other party was injured meant he could lend a hand. If Lord Ilo had no desires or needs, what could Green City offer to attract his protection?
Moreover, the ability to freeze an entire city with a mere gesture, instantly killing the God of Plague… If he wasn’t injured, how powerful must he be?
If he could help the other recover, did that not mean that during the upcoming period, Green City would surely gain the protection of a true Divine?
By the Creator God above, he had seen hope.
The excitement in his heart immediately spread to his face, and Duke O’Kelly nearly laughed out loud.
But upon seeing Lide’s slightly furrowed brow, he immediately suppressed the joy in his heart, and his face took on a very solemn expression the next second.
“Lord Ilo, you have severed the power of the Evil God for the civilians of the southern province, and furthermore, you have saved Anos City. This is a great deed worthy of being sung by all life in the Glory Main Plane.
On behalf of the Southern Province and the Nolan Royal Family, I offer our thanks.”
After finishing, he bowed deeply, as if his words were coming from the bottom of his heart, his acting so superb Lide couldn’t help but praise him–old fox indeed; these nobles were no easy marks.
After a session of lofty talk, Duke O’Kelly stood up and, with sincere intent, said to Lide,
“Your Highness, for the sacrifices you’ve made for my subjects, I, O’Kelly Nolan, simply cannot stand by and do nothing.
What do you require to heal your wounds? As long as it’s within my power to find, even if I must use all of Green City’s resources, I shall spare no effort!!”
His tone was filled with determination, as if making a vow.
This Southern Sovereign was prepared to pay dearly in the fight against the approaching Ancient Days, and his words signified he was willing to pay a price beyond imagination.
Of course, Lide was no fool. With a quick thought, he understood Duke O’Kelly’s intentions and felt a tinge of amusement.
A fat sheep had delivered itself to his door–how could such good fortune be true?
He was quite tempted to fleece it thoroughly; Dawn City was in need of everything.
But after a brief consideration, he decided to delay this idea. It didn’t matter when the sheep was slaughtered; he couldn’t drop his dignity now, for he was Lord Ilo.
“O’Kelly, those worldly items are of no use to me. What I desire is something all Divines are vying for…”
Lide’s gaze held a profound meaning as he looked at Duke O’Kelly.
“So, you might as well go back. The descent of the Ancient Days is a catastrophe of fate; no one can escape it. Perhaps Green City might just survive…”
These words struck deep…
No one can escape, but perhaps Green City might survive?
With Lide saying so, how could Duke O’Kelly dare to return?
Duke O’Kelly’s heart skipped a beat as his mind raced–what could be something that all Divines would compete for, something he could not afford to give…
Divine Artifact? No, the other party would not demand a Divine Artifact from him…
Gold Puck? Precious ores? Magic Materials? Some rare Bloodline?…
An epiphany struck Duke O’Kelly like lightning.
He blurted out,
“Believers?!”
Yes, only believers could be something worth fighting over for a Divine, and it was something he couldn’t resolve. After all, Green City had so many Sects, he couldn’t possibly force the Believers to convert, otherwise, he wouldn’t have to wait for the Ancient Days to come before Green City would be wiped out by those enraged Sects.
A look of ‘the child could be taught’ appeared in Lide’s eyes.
Not bad for the Power Holder of the Southern Province; his mind was indeed sharp.
“Since you’ve guessed it, I won’t hide it from you…
The injuries I’ve suffered require the faith of a great number of believers to repair.”
He looked at Duke O’Kelly with a solemn expression, “As a member of the Nolan Royal Family, you must know many secrets about the Divines.
Just as you suspected, believers are the source of Divine Power, which is no exception for me.
I once had a Lost Plane, where all the inhabitants were my believers.”
“But after descending to the Main Plane, due to the Ancient Evil God, I lost communication with that Lost Plane. That’s why I now need new Believers to gain strength.”
With the status and position of Duke O’Kelly, it was absolutely easy to know the arrival of Divine Power, so Lide had nothing to hide.
A flicker of excitement appeared on Duke O’Kelly’s face. The fact that Lide was speaking to him like this meant he had already tentatively recognized him.
After contemplating for a moment, Duke O’Kelly gritted his teeth and said,
“Lord, if it’s about converting Believers from other Sects to worship You, I can’t do that.
But I can build temples and churches for You, dispatch an army to guard them, and have administrative officials preach for You…”
Lide had unexpected demands for Believers, but this request also relieved him because Duke O’Kelly had initially prepared to make a substantial sacrifice.
Compared to this, merely building churches and sending out preachers was entirely acceptable, and it even strangely felt like a direct profit.
Being able to exchange such simple actions for the protection of the Divine would make others green with envy.
Lide, hearing this promise, had a hint of a smile in his eyes and looked at Duke O’Kelly even more amicably.
What a cash cow…
With a perfect expression of hesitation and temptation on his face, he draggingly said, “This doesn’t seem quite right…”
Duke O’Kelly secretly sighed in relief. The other party was indeed tempted.
Without further hesitation, he suddenly turned to look at the doorway, where several knights had not entered the room.
“Kedri, Dal, come in and listen to my command.”
The two tall figures who were called immediately entered the room.
“Duke, your orders, please.”
“Immediately convey my command, instruct the city guard to organize manpower to build the church for Dawn Sect for Lord Ilo!
Do it with the utmost haste, sparing no expense, and if necessary, deploy the Pegasus Knight Order and the Caster Corps!”
The two knights were startled, but seeing Duke O’Kelly’s unquestionable demeanor, they immediately acknowledged and left.
After the two accepted the order and left, Duke O’Kelly then turned to face Lide, apologizing.
“Lord, please forgive my presumption, but from now on, Green City will become the new stronghold of the Dawn Sect…”
Before the battle in Anos City, Lide had dramatically declared himself the God of Dawn, so it was no surprise that it was impossible for Duke O’Kelly’s spies to miss it, hence mentioning the Dawn Sect casually wasn’t a big deal.
Seeing Duke O’Kelly being so sensible, Lide became even more satisfied, practically being offered a sacrifice on a silver platter–was this what they call self-slaughter among the cash cows nowadays?
I like it.
After a brief contemplation, Lide slightly shook his head, speaking with a touch of helplessness,
“O’Kelly… you… sigh, alright, your sincerity has moved me. But I must make it clear to you.
My power is still far from its peak, I haven’t even reached Legendary level.
The reason I was able to kill those Divine Servants was solely relying on Magic and Divine Arts, allowing me to unleash such intense strength. I might not be able to counter the Ancient Evil God as you’ve said…
And for me to return to my peak state, I still need some time, so you should be mentally prepared.”
The more Lide talked like this, the higher his stature rose in Duke O’Kelly’s mind.
Listen to this–even without restoring his Legendary strength, he can freeze a city with Magic and Divine Arts, annihilate millions of Fierce Half-Ratmen.
When he recovers his Legendary strength, could he potentially solo-annihilate the den of the Evil God in Risier City?
Besides, Lord Ilo might have hidden trump cards. Perhaps the power he can unleash is far more terrifying than what he’s currently showing.
Duke O’Kelly, who was wildly imagining, convinced himself in an instant, seeing Lord Ilo before him practically shining in his eyes.
His character is truly noble…
People always believe what they want to believe, and with notable achievements in both battles of Risier City and Anos City, Lide now claims to be merely a level 23 Transcendent, yet no one would believe it.
A joke, isn’t it? How could someone who’s only a level 23 Transcendent crush three Transcendents singlehandedly? Command Divine beings to kneel with a single word? Freeze an entire city with one spell? Slay an Ancient Evil God barehanded?
Deeds always hold more sway than words.
“My Lord, rest assured, Green City will definitely not trouble you during ordinary times. It will only seek your help at the most critical moments…”
Duke O’Kelly hastily made a promise to Lide, and the smile on the face of this Southern Sovereign could not be concealed. In his eyes, Green City was now secured.
With such a solid support, he would no longer have to be as cautious as before when the old days approached.
Having the conversation progress to this point, Lide could only respond with a touch of emotion.
“O’Kelly, your attitude has moved me. I promise that I will come to Green City’s aid in times of crisis.
But I must say this beforehand–if my power has not yet returned to its peak by then, and the enemy is too powerful, I may not be able to protect Green City.
Therefore, besides myself, you should seek as many powerful protectors as possible. The more the strong, the safer Green City will be.”
Duke O’Kelly was deeply moved by these words. In fact, Lide didn’t need to mention it; he wouldn’t have stopped his efforts regardless. The intelligence network of the southern province was in full swing, and Lide was the strongest and most desired target in his plans, but not the last one.
He then assured with a slap on his chest.
“Rest assured! I will do everything in my power to build your churches and spread your teachings so that you can regain your strength as soon as possible.”
With today’s conversation at this point, the outcome was already clear and both parties were very satisfied with the results.
Duke O’Kelly believed he had found a strong backing, and Green City no longer needed to live in fear.
Lide had justifiably allowed the Dawn Sect to become the official Sect of Green City. As for the promise to protect Green City that he had given to Duke O’Kelly… he naturally would take action.
After all, the Dark Contract and the Crimson Mage Tower were still in Green City, and these two forces were like two arms for the Dawn City.
If Green City were to fall, the loss would be unacceptably great for him.
Even if O’Kelly did not speak up, he would involve himself in the defense of Green City at the critical moment, as this was about protecting his own interests, nothing else.
Moreover, he had already stated that he might not be able to defeat the invading enemy–the worst-case scenario was simply not winning… after all, he could resurrect.
Whether he agreed or not, it hardly made a difference, but with this current maneuver, the benefits he obtained were considerable.
Establishing a Sect was just the beginning. The true implicit benefit was that he could enter the upper echelons of Green City openly and legitimately under the name of Lord Ilo.
Green City was the core of the southern province and a stronghold that the Nolan Empire could not overlook.
By infiltrating the upper echelons of Green City, it meant he could mobilize resources and forces a hundred times stronger than working covertly.
For instance, if he wished to purchase a certain rare and precious ore, previously, he would have to pay high prices to buy it from various trading companies.
But if he entered Green City under the name of Lord Ilo, he would merely need to leak this information, and countless Nobles and major trading companies would bend over backwards to find it for him, doing this merely to curry favor with him.
Isn’t it worth it to incur some cost to gain the favor of a Divine being?
This is what power is.
When you are high in the clouds, every person below will make you feel comfortable.
Eventually, all the valuable materials of Green City would be laid before him–Magic Secret Records, Forbidden Curse Scrolls, rare ores, and so on. As long as he needed them, he could easily acquire them.
This invisible benefit was what truly made Lide’s heart bloom with joy.
After confirming the partnership, Lide became much friendlier to Duke O’Kelly, and their conversation grew more intimate.
When it came to such easy pickings, he expressed his great fondness for them, hoping for more and more. He wasn’t afraid of ‘getting fat’–with a hearty appetite, he could swallow any amount.
After more than half a day, Lide found an excuse to end the topic, also agreeing to ascend Green City with Duke O’Kelly in three days.
Duke O’Kelly naturally left, beaming with joy.
Prince Anos, invisible like a ghost until Duke O’Kelly had left, immediately came up to Lide.
“My Lord, I will arrange the construction of the Dawn Sect at once…”
Lide smiled, “What need is there for you to meddle?
Anos City can proceed with the established plans for reconstruction. The establishment of the Church can be delayed. Now, the key is to restore the power of the entire city.”
After speaking, he paused for a moment, pondering before he continued.
