For a divine being, the most lethal threat was the Power of Faith, as this power was the origin power of all divinities, only possessed and fatally wounded by divinities.
If Lide had used Magic Power to erode the altar, it would have been merely a great supplement for him, posing no threat at all.
As Lide infested the Poison Snake Altar with the Power of Faith, his pitch-black pupils began to glow.
He could feel that the seal inside the altar was about to collapse, an alarming power stirring restlessly.
However, unlike the time when the God of Plague broke his seal in Risier City, the Snake Clan God’s power was extremely weak now–at least more than ten times weaker than God of Plague when trapped.
This discovery made Lide, who was originally very wary of the Snake Clan God, feel his heart pounding faster.
A bold idea rose in his mind.
Perhaps, this was an opportunity for a significant feat.
God-killing.
Once this thought took hold, it spread like wildfire.
Root’s firsthand observation confirmed that the long seal had weakened the Snake Clan God’s power to the extreme.
He could still feel the lava-like power sealed within the altar, still raging and surging.
But he now had a sense of control, whereas he felt helpless when facing the God of Plague under similar circumstances before.
Of course, this might be related to his breakthrough to Transcendent, but regardless, the fact that the Snake Clan God’s strength was far below his expectations was settled.
If initially, he only planned to stall for time to let the Main Plane’s will expel this Evil God into the Abyss after breaking the seal, thereby claiming the relic’s treasures,
Now, sensing the weakness of the Snake Clan God, his ambition swelled wildly, his gaze turning colder.
He wanted to kill this sealed Evil God.
Then, the Divine Status and Divine Power of his opponent would become his spoils of war.
And there was a critical point: the Snake Clan God was not an Ancient Evil God. Its power was evil, but it hadn’t the essence of the ancient.
In other words, this was just a sealed Evil God, not one of the past epoch’s Ancient Evil Gods.
This was crucial.
Ancient Evil Gods emerged with the eras, but the Snake Clan God did not.
With this in mind, Lide’s Dark Faith Power surged even more violently.
The aura emitted by the Snake Clan God began to falter under Lide’s relentless onslaught.
On Lide’s attribute panel, his Dark Faith Power was plummeting by thousands of points every few breaths.
If he didn’t possess the Power of Faith, even a Legendary Strongman would face nothing but defeat when facing the Snake Clan God.
But Lide’s strength was of the same Level as the Snake Clan God’s Power of Faith, and his Power of Faith was even stronger than that of the Snake Clan God who had been sealed for countless ages.
One was a weak deity that had declined due to the sealing for innumerable years, while the other was like the morning sun rising in the east.
The two sides were inherently unequal, their forces clashing wildly within the Poison Snake Altar.
“You can’t kill me! You lowly thief, once I break the seal, I will pierce your throat with my fangs, consume your flesh with my venom, corrode your skeleton…”
As the collision intensified, the Snake Clan God became increasingly aware of Lide’s Soul Power and was both shocked and enraged by this man who hadn’t even reached Legendary status!
A Transcendent dared to challenge him, and it even looked like he wanted to devour and kill him!!
How could this be tolerated!
Feeling a profound challenge, the enraged Snake Clan God unleashed all his might to strike, trying to break the seal and at the same time combat Lide’s erosion.
The clash between the two made the earth’s snakes turn their heads towards the altar, emitting a scream so harsh it was like sandpaper being dragged across a wall, causing one’s scalp to tingle.
And the Hellish Profanity echoing through the sky grew even more tumultuous, so much so that the Elves who had already departed from this land changed color dramatically.
Andabella’s eyes, shimmering with a faint silver hue, looked into the distance, the light flickering in them uncertainly.
Her Blood Cloak, which fluttered without wind as the aberration arose, now diffused a faint bloody energy that enveloped all the Elves around her, isolating them from the soul-shaking Undead Profanity.
“Hurry up the preparations, Lord Ilo has already begun to make his move.”
Upon hearing this, several Elves stopped hesitating and started taking action, as they had made enough preparations to explore the divine relics.
If not for the profound suppression of the Abyssal aura on the Elves, they even had confidence in their own power to excavate this site.
Betty, sensing something, stepped forward as the Elves set up around her, her tone tinged with confusion.
“Andabella, do you know Lord Ilo?”
Andabella glanced at the girl beside her and softened her expression slightly, as if thinking of something.
“I don’t know.”
“Don’t know?” Betty looked puzzled. What kind of answer was that? She didn’t even know if she recognized him or not?
“Yes,” Andabella replied, hesitancy flickering in her eyes, “After my Bloodline awakened, I could sense a lot… Lord Ilo’s soul energy feels like a certain friend of mine, but I can’t be certain.”
Betty looked at Andabella thoughtfully and unusually pressed on with a question.
“What was your relation to that friend?”
“Relation…” Andabella appeared a bit lost. Indeed, what was the relation? He had saved her… and that seemed to be all.
“He… saved my life, and also, he took away my clanspeople.”
When the Beastmen had overrun Risier City, Dawn City was in dire need of talents, and many members of the Risier family had been abducted by Lide, which was a major reason Andabella had been searching for him.
Betty fell silent upon hearing this, her eyes filling with doubt, but she did not speak further.
While the two conversed, the collision between Lide and the Snake Clan God became much more intense.
Grey Faith Power and green Divine Power intertwined above the Poison Snake Altar, the space around them materially distorting as if twined like twisted dough.
Though the two seemed evenly matched, the curl of Lide’s lips revealed his growing confidence.
For he sensed that, as the stalemate continued, the Snake Clan God’s power began to decline.
And this was just minutes after it had only begun.
This indicated how much the opponent’s strength had degenerated.
To slay a god… didn’t seem impossible.
This thought surged within him.
Killing intent skyrocketed.
The Snake Clan God also felt the approaching crisis, and an indescribable despair took hold in his heart.
How could a Transcendent push him to such a brink?!
This Vampire was merely Transcendent!!!

chapters.title: Chapter 425 - Chapter 425: Chapter 427: Spatial Fracture, The Disappearance of Lide
chapters.content:
Chapter 425: Chapter 427: Spatial Fracture, The Disappearance of Lide
Within the divine relic, the air was suffused with a suffocating atmosphere.
In the dim environment, the divine pressure weighed on everyone’s heart like a giant rock.
In the central area enveloped by countless poisonous snakes, inside the pitch-black altar, the sealed Snake Clan God had completely fallen into a frenzy.
He sensed a fatal threat on an extraordinary vampire…
This was simply unbearable.
But because the sealing had lasted so long that his power had dissipated too much, it also filled him with fear.
If this continued, he would truly be killed by that damnable vampire.
The thought of being killed by an extraordinary presence nearly drove the Snake Clan God to madness.
“Extraordinary… An extraordinary vampire wants to kill me???”
As his voice, tinged with fury, echoed through the cavernous space, an indescribably terrifying aura suddenly rose from the altar.
The entwined snake reliefs, whose bloody eyes had dimmed, now burst forth with a dazzling crimson light.
“mrgmyd…..nqThmrg…pyndrhmyd…”
An extreme evil and malevolent aura, mixed with the peculiar accent of an exotic realm city state, reverberated through the sky.
The already dim environment of the plane grew even darker. After the evil had gathered to its extreme, a bang–the space above the altar suddenly shattered, unleashing a surge of abyssal aura, vastly different from that of the Snake Clan God.
A god.
Another god!
At a critical moment, the Snake Clan God had actually summoned another Abyss Evil God.
Lord Lide’s face changed at that instant. This bastard actually pulled this trick??
His brows furrowed tightly. Under his perception, the newly emerged malevolent aura swelled like a tide, and to his surprise, it felt somewhat familiar.
Moments later, as if realizing something, his eyes snapped open.
“God of Twilight??!!”
Yes, he sensed it. The new aura that had appeared was almost identical to the aura of the Twilight Godhood in his possession.
Unexpectedly, when the Snake Clan God couldn’t win, he had summoned the God of Twilight…
This caught him off guard.
But he still didn’t let go.
At this point, if he retreated, the seal of the Snake Clan God would immediately collapse, and everything he desired would come to naught.
Moreover, more crucially, even if the God of Twilight was strong, it was sneaking into the Main Plane from another–a feat that, as long as he could withstand the first wave of attacks, the will of the Main Plane would undoubtedly expel.
Not even gods with Powerful Divine Power could contend with the will of the Main Plane; what chance did one with at most Medium Divine Power have to cross borders??
His resolve strengthened in an instant, and far from stopping due to the emergence of the God of Twilight’s aura, he increased the output of his Dark Faith Power.
He intended to completely devour the Snake Clan God.
Sensing Lord Lide’s actions and his murderous intent, the Snake Clan God became both shocked and angry, but he had no choice but to cast spells more rapidly, accelerating the summoning of the God of Twilight.
He believed that once the God of Twilight appeared, upon sensing the twilight aura on Lord Lide, it would kill him at all costs.
That was the chief reason for summoning the God of Twilight at this critical juncture.
Of course, the fact that they were allies before his sealing was also a key point.
At this desperate juncture, the Snake Clan God could no longer bother with the details; summoning the God of Twilight might afford a glimmer of hope. If not summoned, his death was certain.
Crack–
The sound of shattering glass rang above the altar, and then, under Lord Lide’s gaze, space directly fractured.
The surging Divine Power was magnified to the extreme.
The God of Twilight had appeared.
“Who… summoned me…”
Blasphemous words in the language of the abyss emanated from the pitch-black crack, spanning more than a dozen blades in width. At that moment, the malevolent aura nearly solidified, making it nearly impossible for even a level 15 top combatant to endure, let alone a newly level 12 Unicorn.
This was a power from another level entirely.
“God of Twilight… do you remember your ally?” The tone of the Snake Clan God now held a hint of excitement.
“I have discovered a thief who has stolen your power; let us join forces to kill him and retrieve your power!”
After these words were spoken, the shattered spatial rift fell silent for a moment, but almost instantly, with a bang–the rift exploded again.
Zila~
The width of the space directly expanded from more than ten blades to forty or fifty blades, as fragments of space floated up like glass, creating a sight of mesmerizing beauty.
And with it, a black crow formed from soul energy flew out of the spatial passageway.
Divine Power was overwhelming.
After the crow’s arrival, a terrifying presence pressed heavily on Lide’s chest like a massive stone.
“Damn thief!!”
The Soul Crow, which had no physical body, spread its wings and flew, its hollow gaze filling with extreme anger upon seeing Lide.
Yes, it sensed it, its lost Divine Status was in the hands of this damned Vampire.
“So, you are Kachar, Lord?!! When you previously tried to steal my power, I sensed you through my Divine Position, when you were shouting your Name in front of my Believers…
You lowly Vampire, dare you defile my power?!!”
Lide took a deep breath at the enraged tone of the Soul Crow.
Facing two Evil Gods at once, the pressure was almost impossibly intense.
Yet his gaze remained unshakably firm.
He was determined to kill the God of the Snake Clan today, and not even Jesus could stop him.
No matter what kind of dogshit Evil God you are, if you must die, then die you will!
Lide looked up and roared fiercely.
“Asreaga!! Stop him!!”
After a furious shout, beside the Soul Crow, an Ancient Divine Monster appeared, slashing through the air: three blades tall, with a head crowned with twisted horns, eyes filled with brutal bloodlust, and skin marked with blasphemous inscriptions.
Asreaga’s sharp claws were half a blade long; as he swung them, the space around him was cut like paper.
Ruthlessly unmatched.
Zila~
In the blink of an eye, the crow formed from the Divine Energy of the God of Twilight was torn apart by Asreaga.
The Soul Crow had no corpse, but the Extreme Evil power of the Divine Monster could corrode everything, and Asreaga’s oppressive Talent allowed him to devour Negative Energy and grow stronger.
As the Soul Crow shattered, over a third of its Soul Power was devoured by Asreaga.
After the Soul Crow was torn apart, it reformed in the next blink into black energy hundreds of blades away, and its power dimmed significantly upon its reappearance.
“Damn bastard!! Divine Monster!! Why is there a Divine Monster here?!!”
The appearance of Asreaga enraged the God of Twilight, and even the God of the Snake Race, who was being suppressed, was shocked.
Divine Monsters were abominably evil beings that even Divine beings dreaded, possessing a routine ease in god-slaying.
It was beyond their imagination that this Vampire could subjugate even a Divine Monster.
Asreaga didn’t bother conversing with the God of Twilight, but disappeared at the moment the Soul Crow reformed, reappearing beside it in the next second.
At this point, the energy-formed crow could no longer escape.
Despite the God of Twilight’s preparedness, it still couldn’t escape from the hunt of the Divine Monster–spatial Talents were simply too monstrous and powerful.
Zila~
As Asreaga’s claws swiped, his eyes–fused with the Ancient Evil God’s Eye–suddenly emitted a terrifying, bloody radiance.
Ancient Eye: Ancient Intimidation, emitting absolute power capable of daunting beings below the level of Powerful Divine Power.
The Soul Crow, which had intended to scatter and flee again, was immediately overwhelmed by infinite Divine Power, rooted to the spot.
This time, Asreaga didn’t give his opponent a chance to escape, activating a terrifying devouring ability, consuming all the Soul Crow’s power.
If one could see his attribute panel, they’d notice that the Divine Status of this Divine Monster had just increased by 12 points.
“No!!”
A sharp voice filled with immense hatred came from the spatial rift, the God of Twilight feeling as if its heart bled at the loss of the Soul Crow infused with more than ten points of Divine Status.
Divine Status was essential for a Divine being, each drop was incredibly precious.
Despite such a significant loss, the God of Twilight didn’t lose its composure, and watching Lide still ferociously assaulting the Poison Snake Altar, it too became determined.
While Divine Status was precious, it paled in comparison to the Divine Calamity within Lide.
Divine Calamity was fundamental for it: should it reclaim that Divine Stone belonging to it, its power would return to its peak.
After making its decision, and to the surprise of Lide, the shattered spatial rift suddenly burst open, swarming out countless Soul Crows like a plague of locusts.
The already dim environment was now plunged into complete darkness.
Most of these crows were constructed of Divine Power, among them mixed a dozen crows containing even more precious Divine Energy.
Divine Nature was the original source of the gods, whereas Divine Power was something that could be continuously replenished; the two were not the same kind of energy.
The sudden surge of Soul Crows caused immense trouble for Asreaga, a Divine Monster who was strong in everything except for one weakness–he lacked group attack skills.
All of Asreaga’s attacks were targeted at individuals, making him extremely powerful in hunting bosses, but when faced with situations like this, he ran into problems with being overwhelmed.
Although a single swipe of his claws could obliterate a Soul Crow, when the number of opponents reached tens of thousands, individual hunting was clearly insufficient.
For this reason, he could only give up on those ordinary Soul Crows and turned to hunt those imbued with Divine Nature.
There were simply too many Soul Crows to handle.
And unnoticed by anyone, a portion of the Soul Crows headed straight for the area beyond a dozen or so blades’ distance from the Poison Snake Altar upon entering this Plane.
Because they had no physical form, the crows could easily enter the ground below.
At this time, even the Divine Monster’s attention was drawn by the clouds of crows containing Divine Nature, failing to perceive the subtle changes around the altar.
All of Lide’s attention was focused on the aggressive erosion of the Snake Clan God, and although his inner self was constantly alerting him, his Danger Perception was reduced in effectiveness in such an environment, fraught with danger everywhere.
Therefore, he also missed the crows invading the ground nearby.
By the time thousands of Soul Crows poured downward in unison, Lide realized that the God of Twilight must have additional schemes, but by then it was too late.
“Shatter!”
Accompanying the roar from within the spatial rift, the ground around the Poison Snake Altar, over a dozen blades in circumference, instantly exploded.
In this already fragile space of this Plane, it was like cotton set ablaze, and a huge hole burned through.
The space in the area where Lide was located twisted directly, and phantoms of the Abyss Land filled with the stench of sulfur began to emerge around him.
This was inter-dimensional transport.
The God of Twilight evidently intended to transport the entire area into the Abyss.
But the God of Twilight acted too swiftly, and Lide, completely engaged with the Snake Clan God, could not possibly disengage in an instant.
Then, in less than a breath’s time, the God of Twilight used the Soul Crows as an energy source to instantly unleash an extremely terrifying power, transporting the entire Poison Snake Altar and Lide back into the Abyss.
Asreaga only realized the God of Twilight’s plot after the Soul Crows exploded, and it was too late to stop it. He stepped forward, following the transport’s force along with Lide into the Abyss.
When he looked back at that area, the altar that had just stood proudly on the land had vanished without a trace.
After the disappearance of the Poison Snake Altar, the Soul Crows also burst apart, turning into streams of evil energy that dissipated into the air.
At the same time, the incessant Abyssal blasphemous utterances that had been lingering in the air also abruptly stopped.
And the hissing, screaming snakes that covered the twenty-kilometer square of land seemed to have lost their souls all at once, collapsing en masse, silent and motionless.
Looking down from the sky, the center area of the Poison Snake Altar was now nothing but a hole a dozen blades wide and over twenty blades deep.
The Divine Power that had pervaded the space just moments before was gone without a trace.
If not for that hole, no one would believe that there had just been a battle between divine beings here.
The elves, who were urgently preparing in the background, suddenly stopped their actions when the Abyssal blasphemous utterances ceased.
Everyone’s gaze turned towards the direction of the altar, their expressions filled with shock and doubt.
“Why has the Evil God’s aura disappeared?”
Eyes flickering with confusion, Aler, as if recalling something, let out a soft yet far-reaching call.
Moments later, the Unicorn sprinted forward, and with a nimble leap, Aler sat astride and dashed toward the altar.
“Continue with the preparations; I am going to check the situation.”
Feeling a bad premonition rising in her heart, Andabella didn’t delay, her crimson cape unfurling as she floated up and likewise sped towards the altar.
Betty, with a deeply furrowed brow, wanted to follow but unable to fly, continued to wait with a sense of unease.
As Andabella drew closer to the direction of the altar, her anxiety grew heavier. When she arrived at the location and saw the deep pit, her heart lurched, her eyes filled with disbelief.
“The altar… disappeared?!!”
How was this possible?!!
That was the altar that sealed the divine being, how could it just disappear without any disturbances?
Although the recent battle was fierce, the Abyssal blasphemous utterances subdued the noise, and the affected area was very narrow. The start and end were brief; they hadn’t felt much fluctuation.
Upon seeing this scene, Aler was no less shocked, her mind swirling with countless thoughts before she cautiously ventured, “Was it Lord Ilo who took the altar away?”
Andabella shook her head, “No, there are still so many stones of Divine Nature around the altar…
There is no reason for Lord Ilo to do so, who else in the ruins could compete with him for treasures?”
The statement was flawless; if Lord Ilo had the power to easily take away the altar, he had no need to leave, and they were no threat to him.
“Then why…”
“Something must have triggered an ancient magic array, and Lord Ilo, along with the altar, was taken to another plane…”
Andabella’s pale silver eyes swept across the surroundings. “There are several types of evil aura lingering here, likely left by creatures from that plane…”
Upon hearing this, Ailer furrowed her brows and quickly turned her head to glance around before decisively saying,
“No matter where Lord Ilo has gone, I believe that with his strength, there absolutely won’t be a problem. For now, let’s prioritize collecting the Divine Stones from this ruin. Should the altar disappear and the plane collapses directly, everything we’ve done will be in vain, and we won’t be able to report to him upon his return.”
After a moment of contemplation, Andabella nodded. “You have them start excavating the Divine Stones. I’ll scout around.”
Ailer’s actions were all for the sake of the Divine Stones, for the fate of the elves. The disappearance of Lord Ilo held little significance to this Level 17 Elf Archer Master.
The two parties merely had a relationship of cooperation, far from any sort of intimacy, so it was natural for her to remain indifferent.
But Andabella was different. Lord Ilo reminded her so much of the figure who had saved her in Risier City, yet she couldn’t confirm it, so her heart was not as calm as she appeared.
Before long, Andabella spread her cape and began to explore the area, while the other elves and Betty also arrived at the spot.
Upon seeing the altar and Lide gone, Betty displayed an extremely ugly expression.
Her gaze flickered with icy sharpness, fixating intently on Ailer.
“Where is Lord Ilo?”
The tone of this Northern Royal Family member was as cold as the ice and snow of Frost Month, enough to freeze the earth solid.
Even the aura of killing intent on her began to surge at that moment, and her body, wielding a huge sword, was crouched down like a compressed spring, ready to unleash a deadly attack should the response dissatisfy her.
The elves, sensing the killing intent, were somewhat taken aback, not understanding why this girl, who was Andabella’s friend, would act so aggressively.
Ailer’s eyes shifted slightly, and with some hesitation, she said, “Lady Betty, you know Lord Ilo?”
Seeing Betty’s killing intent intensify, she quickly explained, “According to Miss Andabella’s assessment, Lord Ilo must have touched an ancient transmission array and been sent to another plane. And considering how powerful Lord Ilo is, I believe he wouldn’t have any problems…”
Upon hearing Ailer’s words, Betty suddenly recalled that Lide had told them long ago that his Talent allowed him to resurrect within Dawn City, and that they needn’t worry too much if he was in danger.
With this thought, the killing intent in her eyes slightly dissipated, and the Northern Land Valkyrie chose not to elaborate further.
“Continue the excavation. Besides what the elves need, all the Divine Stones must be reserved for Lord Ilo.”
Hearing Betty’s words, Ailer was instantly certain that there must be a murky relationship between Lord Ilo and Betty. But she was too indifferent to speculate further; at this moment, the Divine Stones were here and the future of the elves laid on the ground before her. As long as Betty did not interfere, even if she was Lord Ilo’s lover, it would be of no concern to the elves.
“That is only proper.”
The ensuing clatter of excavation became the only sound within the plane.
Not long after, Andabella, who had gone to explore, returned to the spot. Seeing Betty standing to the side with a cold face, her expression became slightly curious.
But she didn’t ponder it further and turned to look at the elves frantically excavating the Divine Stones.
“I’ve already scouted the area and didn’t find any trace of Lord Ilo. As for that ancient magic array… perhaps it shattered in the moment of transmission. The powers of the ancient era hold too many mysteries, and there’s much I don’t know either.”
The elves were not surprised upon hearing this, or perhaps they no longer cared, for those small silver trinkets beneath the ground were now their treasures.
“Miss Andabella, for the thing you’re looking for, the Exotic Realm City States of Silver Moon Radiance have something that can substitute for it. The Divine Stones we’ve harvested this time should satisfy our needs,” the Red-eyed Lady, donning a black cloak, said at this moment, her red eyes staring straight at Andabella.
“If you’re willing, you may accompany me to the Exotic Realm City States of Silver Moon Radiance.”
However, Andabella did not share the elves’ joyous expressions, appearing hesitant instead.
“Let’s discuss this after we’ve finished excavating the Divine Stones. We should wait for Lord Ilo, he might return before long…”
The elves, along with the Red-eyed Lady, were somewhat surprised upon hearing this. How could these two proud and aloof girls both care so deeply for Lord Ilo? They didn’t seem to have much interaction, did they?
But since Andabella had said so, they didn’t press further and simply buried themselves in continuing the excavation of the Divine Stones.
Silver Moon Radiance City States?
Betty quietly repeated the name to herself a few times before thoughtfully making a mental note.
The purpose of her joining the elves this time was to ascertain the identity of this Red-eyed Lady.
She didn’t directly inquire because she was unable to gauge the attitudes of these people from Isa toward Isa, so she decided to remain silent for now, observing more before making a decision.
Moreover, now that Lide had noticed this lady’s presence, he should be more concerned than she was…
With this thought, Betty’s brows furrowed even more deeply.
Where exactly had Lord Lide gone?

chapters.title: Chapter 426 - Chapter 426: Chapter 428: The Arrival of Old Days, New Players Enter Glory
chapters.content:
In the year 3526 of the Era of Glory, January 1st, on the coldest day of Frost Month, snow covered the earth.
And in the early morning hours, a blood-red crescent moon rose into the sky, its brilliance impossible for even the storm to obscure.
It was as if that moon, hanging over everyone’s head, inaugurated a day that would be recorded in the annals of Glory.
The Ancient Era had arrived.
Before today, before the rise of the blood moon, nobody knew exactly what the Ancient Era entailed; but after the moon rose and the snow covered the land, the residents of the main Plane of Glory experienced for the first time the terror of being dominated by the Ancient Era.
Endless whispers from exotic realm city-states, similar to demonic roars emitting from the deepest abyss, echoed in everyone’s ears–strange, evil, twisted languages.
Humans, Dwarves, Elves, Fishmen, Beastmen, Centaurs…
All intelligent races spent the whole night in the Plane, engulfed by the relentless, evil whispers, and almost seemed to witness a creature with an octopus body and deformed human features breaking into their souls.
Spreading unabated fear, broadcasting that unique–aura of the Ancient Era.
And those deep, low whispers from the abyss continued until nine o’clock the next morning; but the moment those evil whispers ceased, something even more terrifying made most people forget the torturous whispers of the last night.
For the sky of the main Plane of Glory had shattered, yes, shattered.
Just as literally described, with a crisp cracking sound, the entire sky broke apart.
Covered by thick dark clouds, indescribable fissures appeared as if a mirror had been shattered and then haphazardly glued back together.
Then more terrifying was that from those cracks in the sky, surged an aura of the Ancient Era, more horrifying than the abyss itself.
The Ancient Era, representing decay, eternal silence, and destruction.
The utmost evil in the world was corrupting everything, a scene more terrifying than any collision between the bottomless abyss and the main Plane.
A pale gray aura of the Ancient Era poured in from the cracks in the sky, like water seeping from a torn quilt.
It was the darkness preserved from ancient times, enough to make even the most resolute warriors tremble with great horror.
The sky had split.
No one could describe the shock of the residents of the main Plane of Glory; their hearts enveloped by fear, their eyes swallowed by panic.
At this moment, countless believers rushed into churches to pray to their gods, the deities they were loyal to, hoping these grand beings would save the people.
But something even more astonishing happened.
All believers suddenly could not feel the presence of the divine; their gods, whom they had worshipped day and night, prayed to, adored, and yearned for, had vanished.
It was as if these gods had never existed in this world.
Thunderstruck, countless believers felt as if the sky was collapsing at that very moment.
They knelt down, their heads touching the ground, hoping their devotion might reconnect them with their faith, to prove their piety to the divine, to seek safety amidst immense fear.
But still, it was all in vain; the once faint connection each believer felt in their hearts was now completely severed.
Their gods could no longer be sensed.
Panic began to spread uncontrollably.
And as the influence of the vanishing divinities made itself felt, priests and church knights from various Sects began to rapidly regress in Level, their power inevitably plummeting.
Even the believers and priests of powerful divine entities like the Master of Dawn, the Sun Goddess, were not spared; everyone’s power was diminishing…
This harrowing discovery caused the already rampant fear to spread uncontrollably.
An unthinkable notion arose in the minds of believers–had their grand divine beings fallen?
This thought was immediately countered by their own rebuttals.
Impossible!! How could gods possibly fall??
But this blasphemous thought, once it took root, grew wildly like a weed.
If they hadn’t fallen, then why couldn’t they sense the presence of the divinities anymore?
As believers, although the divine rarely reciprocated, prayers always brought them a sense of the divine’s existence, which was why some were so devoted.
But now, this perception was gone…
The governance of Sects was a major stabilizing force in the main Plane of Glory; now disrupted, it immediately caused great chaos.
Countless people succumbed to fear, and lawlessness broke out, with arson, murder, and looting rising in almost every city.
At this moment, Evil God believers were extremely excited; they felt it–the arrival of that evil essence…bloodthirsty, brutal, cruel, the sky at this moment possessed all the darkness they desired.
Numerous Evil God believers began to firmly believe, the apocalypse was upon them, the world was about to be destroyed, and only by turning to the Evil God could one find ultimate salvation.
Though some priests of the Evil God believers, like those from the Light Faction, saw a significant decrease in their casting ability, a considerable number of Evil God believers’ casting power remained unaffected.
The emergence of this matter undoubtedly brought the claim that Doomsday was near to its peak.
Evil God worshippers and believers began to brazenly promote the idea of the apocalypse, even appearing boldly within regions governed by churches that previously could only operate underground and in the shadows.
The madness of the Evil God believers further exacerbated the situation.
But this was not all.
On the third Sunshine Hour after the sky had torn, a voice rang out in everyone’s ears, plunging the Main Plane of Glory into deeper despair.
“My children, the Destiny Tablet that determines the future of Glory has been stolen by the Ancient Evil God.
They ground the Destiny Tablet to dust using the Time Gear, and because the Time Gear is uncontrollable, fragments have scattered across the Multi-dimensional Plane.
The fate of Glory can no longer be predicted, and the darkness of old will envelop the land.
The Glory of the gods will dim, and the Divine will transform into Saints to descend to the mortal realm.
Only by finding the Destiny Tablet again and consolidating the Power of Destiny can the gods qualify to become Divine once more and the Multi-dimensional Plane of Glory be reborn.
I can no longer protect Glory, and after this, I shall fall into slumber, hoping you can awaken me…”
Countless Intelligent Life creatures were filled with tears at this moment.
Everyone felt that presence; it was the Life Goddess, a grand entity respected by all Intelligent Life in this world.
Legends say the Creator God made the world, but it was the Life Goddess who endowed it with life.
She is everyone’s mother, even the most evil Abyss Demons and the dead Undead must maintain enough respect for the Goddess.
Hearing this shocking news, all of Glory trembled.
The Destiny Tablet was stolen by an Evil God, and the goddess would fall into slumber, while the gods would lose their power and have to descend as Saints?
This series of shocks left all of Glory stunned for a long time.
Especially for Believers, if the gods were no longer resplendent, were they still worth worshipping?
Or, might mankind and other life forms have a chance to strive for Divine Status?
Ambitious individuals, Evil God believers, Legendary Strongmen, and Believers of the Gods were all enveloped in a bizarre atmosphere at this moment.
Some were fearful, some panicked, some retreated, but others were excited, agitated, and fanatic.
The gods had fallen, and the stars in the sky would no longer be bright from then on.
Looking up at the sky, the awe-inspiring crack filled the entire world with an indescribable presence.
A catastrophic darkness.
True change had arrived.
—-
—-
—-
The sun seemed to have been shrouded by clouds ever since the sky had shattered.
Duke O’Kelly stood in the backyard of the City Lord’s manor, looking up at the crack in the sky and the Extreme Evil aura emanating from it.
This resolute duke, who had fought all his life, could not help but feel a touch of fear.
It was a fear of the future, a fear of the Life Goddess’s final admonition, and a fear of a near-apocalyptic disaster.
With the Destiny Tablet shattered and the gods fallen, who then could withstand the encroachment of the Ancient Evil God?
He remembered the blasphemous words above Risier City that he could never forget.
I shall return…
The words of the God of Plague now wrapped around his mind like a Magic Curse.
I shall return!
How should the Nolan Empire respond at this time? What about the southern provinces? And what of Green City, his home base?
At that moment, confusion appeared in Duke O’Kelly’s blue eyes.
Tap tap~
The sound of footsteps behind him interrupted Duke O’Kelly’s thoughts. He swiftly turned around to see the bishop, a priest of the God of Nobles, running towards him with a look of fear, his eyebrows furrowing.
“Bishop, you…”
Before he could finish speaking, the bishop knelt down abruptly in front of Duke O’Kelly and looked up at him with endless fear, his voice trembling uncontrollably.
“Duke… Your Lordship, has really descended to the mortal realm? I can no longer sense Your Lordship’s presence, I can’t feel it anymore…”
“My power has diminished to Level 10…”
Fear was devouring the bishop’s heart.
No one could imagine how terrifying the impact was for a devout priest after losing the news of their Divine.
Duke O’Kelly’s face was as still as water, different from other believers, he was the controller of the southern province, holding command over hundreds of thousands of soldiers, so no matter how great the changes in the world, he still had enough confidence.
“Bishop, the Goddess’s words must be true. Our Lord might have already descended to the mortal realm.
But there is nothing to fear, we are all loyal believers of the Lord. Our duty should be to find the Lord and assist Him in returning to the Divine Country.
Fear can’t solve any problem.”
Although his inner turmoil was no less than anyone else’s, Duke O’Kelly still appeared resolute and unshakeable on the surface.
Anyone could give up, except him–he was the support for everyone in the southern province.
Hearing Duke O’Kelly’s words, the bishop’s eyes immediately lit up, “You are right, we must find the Lord and see Him ascend to the Divine Country again!!”
He then urgently added, “Duke, what should we do now?”
Duke O’Kelly shook his head, his face tinged with bitterness.
Though the words were simple, the difficulty of finding the God of Nobles, whose appearance and circumstances were unknown, among countless people was unimaginable.
Even though the main believers of the God of Nobles were concentrated in the Nolan Empire, there was no assurance that He had descended in Green City.
After taking a deep breath, he slowly said,
“I have already sensed the approach of evil. The search for our Lord will undoubtedly take a long time. Now, we need to stabilize the residents of the southern province and Green City.
Has Lord Ilo returned?”
Compared to the elusive God of Nobles, the tangible and reachable Lord Ilo was the true backbone of Green City at the moment.
The bishop shook his head, “Duke, the Elves returned to Green City three days ago and reported that the plane they were exploring had collapsed, and both Lord Ilo and the sealed divine being are missing…
Do you think, could Lord Ilo have been trapped? Or perhaps the Lord simply found an excuse to leave Green City…”
Duke O’Kelly’s brows furrowed, “No, Bishop, Lord Ilo would certainly not leave Green City so easily.
It’s more likely that he’s been entangled by that sealed Evil God…” His tone was mixed with complexity; this was their last reliance.
“What? Why is that?”
“The Dawn Sect is spreading in Green City, and over a hundred thousand believers are a force to be reckoned with.
Moreover, since the ancient days have come, only believers can provide the most direct power to the Divine. Lord Ilo would not leave so easily; he must be trapped somewhere.”
Duke O’Kelly spoke with increasing conviction, his eyes brightening as if he had seen through the fog to the truth of the matter, his tone utterly confident.
This logical explanation also convinced the bishop.
“You are right, we shall wait for Lord Ilo’s return…”
“No, we cannot just wait and do nothing!” Duke O’Kelly’s eyes hardened, showing a hint of murderous intent.
“As the core of the south, Green City must not fall into chaos! Immediately mobilize the military to suppress those Evil God believers and maintain public order.
Also send people to invite all professionals above Level 15 in Green City to the City Lord’s estate to discuss the future. Anyone who does not attend, kill!
Let the Mage Association of Green City and various professional guilds send personnel to assist.
Green City is entering a state of war, prepare everything as for war.
Anyone who disobeys the military order, kill!”
A single command, and bloodshed ascended to the skies.
As the true ruler of this city, Duke O’Kelly was a presence no one dared to overlook.
Even the evil-infested western district, upon this command, immediately hit a pause because the Green City military, exceeding fifty thousand strong, directly massacred seventeen Underground Forces, and those who took advantage of the chaos to murder and plunder were killed en masse.
The dramatic change had just begun, yet the authority of the nobility was still deeply ingrained in everyone’s mind.
And at this moment, no one could contend with Duke O’Kelly.
But as the Life Goddess had said, everything was changing, and the future was uncertain…
—-
—-
—-
The ancient days arrived, and massive changes swept across every piece of land.
The area that underwent the most drastic changes was the region of the Ancient Gods whose seals had been broken.
In Risier City, the Fierce Half-Ratmen began to spread uncontrollably from areas over a hundred kilometers away. In a short time, these dirty, foul-smelling, and cruelly murderous rats could be seen in half of the southern provinces.
Over this land, evil forces began to gather, and the wild Demon Beasts, under the corrosion of the ancient aura, started transforming into pure evil lifeforms.
Suddenly, the occurrence of dark life forms outdoors had increased by dozens of times.
Fallen Gnolls, Corrupted Kobolds, Bloodthirsty Cave Men, Berserk Boarmen…
Most of these life forms commonly seen in the wilderness had now been corrupted by the ancient force, and their power increased multiple times after the fall.
Outside major cities, the level of danger increased tenfold, even a hundredfold.
The sky was shrouded in dark clouds, the bird’s chirping had turned into mournful cries, crops began to wither, lakes became murky, grasslands dried up, and trees withered…
Panic uncontrollably began to spread wildly, with whole villages being slaughtered by suddenly appearing servants of the Evil God, and countless lives were brutally exterminated.
What was more terrifying was that, under such circumstances, no one was capable of going to the villages to ensure the safety of the farmers anymore.
Armies could only rely on solid city walls to defend the major cities, and with the disappearance of the Gods, Priests had lost their deterrent power against the servants of the Ancient Evil God.
The churches, as the main combat force, now resembled a lion without teeth… gradually being phased out.
—-
—-
—-
For the Era of Glory, it was an absolute dark moment, but for Earth today, it was a new day.
January 1, 2052, it’s New Year’s Day.
More than a year after the public beta of Glory, the second public beta took place, counting internal tests as the third game list release.
This time, the number of people who obtained game qualifications was as many as 1.1 billion.
Despite having so many game pods, they were still frantically snatched up by the eager players.
Many players who missed out did not hesitate to pay ten to twenty times the price to buy them at high prices online.
Many resold them and made hundreds of thousands, becoming the fastest way to get rich.
The second public beta of “Glory” is set at nine o’clock at night.
Almost all players who managed to buy game pods lay in their pods early, ready to embrace the arrival of the new world.
But the waiting time is always boring, the forum’s heat began to surge before the game opened, mostly new players excited about the game.
“I’ve been following Glory for over a year, and finally, it’s my turn to play!! Hahaha, Elf sisters, wait for my gracious visit”
“Damn, the officials are definitely doing this on purpose. Today, the Ancient Day comes, and these new players have arrived. This expansion pack is terrifying, I suspect the official site has made a big move. But I’m looking forward to these newcomers entering Glory… hehehe, just in time for the Ancient Day, get ready to be ravaged.”
“I am Swimming Dragon from Beijing nightlife, known as the strongest player over there. After my long undercover work on the forum, I have successfully collected the detailed addresses and list of red-light districts in 127 cities within ‘Glory.’ I wish to invite partners to join me in creating a guide to famous courtesans in the red-light districts, providing real experiences to guide old gentlemen, and also to asses and score each red-light district to prevent everyone from being deceived. At the same time, also planning the market to avoid market price increases, now recruiting ambitious and aspiring people to join this great undertaking”
“I heard this game is quite difficult. I’m from the post-30s, just graduated from university, wondering if there’s any guy who can lead me, if you’re skilled, voice company is available too~black silk thigh photo.jpg”
“I am Long Aotian, today I declare that this game has been conquered by me, don’t ask why I’m so awesome, because bragging doesn’t need to make sense.”
Most of the newcomer players were excited, while only a few who had been following the forum for a long time felt some apprehension.
They knew all too well about the initial situations where players were beaten by natives; now it was their turn to experience being thrashed, *It’s hard to put the feelings in words.*
Of course, the most excited were actually the veteran players.
Although “Glory” previously had 10 million players, they were too scattered across various parts of Glory.
One could hardly see many players in a city, making it difficult to form teams or pick up girls.
Now it was different, the influx of hundreds of millions of players greatly increased the player density, and among them were at least 40 million female players. With Glory’s exaggerated realism, finding a few female players to flirt with might be a real possibility…
Glory greatly improved physical fitness in reality, especially as it was found to aid in losing weight and beauty, which drove many women crazy. If not for the male players being overwhelmingly numerous, they might not have been able to outcompete the female players.
Of course, many players were also waiting to see the fun of new players.
After all, the hardcore nature of Glory had made them taste the bitterness of life.
And amid a heated discussion, the clock struck nine o’clock at night, and the second public beta of Glory officially began.
At this moment, the players lying in the game pods simultaneously appeared in “Glory.”
Not just players from Huaxia, but millions of international players also entered Glory for the first time…

Chapter 427: Chapter 429: The Most Miserable American Player in History (This purely satirical, those who dislike may skip)
ps: This a nonsensical spoof Chapter, which you can skip if you dislike, without affecting the plot.
——
——
——
——
At a military base of the United States Military, a colonel with a cold gaze stared intently at the tall soldier in front of him.
"Henry, as the most elite spy of the United States, I hope that after you enter the game ’Glory’, you will gather more useful information."
"Yes, sir!" the uniformed hulk in front of him responded loudly, his eyes filled with determination.
"Very good," the colonel was quite pleased. "Although you have recorded all the game information over the past month, it is still not enough.
This is an extremely difficult game, and our intelligence department has not yet fully understood it.
View the correct content at
Moreover, there are still large amounts of new information appearing on Huaxia’s networks every day.
This game must be hiding some unspeakable secrets of Huaxia.
So I need you to make connections with some advanced Huaxia players and turn them while gathering information, just in case."
"Yes, sir," Henry’s eyes flashed with immense confidence.
"Sir, I have already mastered all the strategies and skills of this game, and it shall be conquered by our Mountain Peak Country!
We, the United States, are the chosen ones, the race favored by God, and whatever those heretical Huaxia people can do, our great United States can surely do better!"
The colonel nodded in satisfaction, "Very good, you are right, only we are the most excellent race!"
"In addition to you, there are 5,000 elite agents from our Military Intelligence Department entering the game with you, but you may not be able to get help initially because we can’t influence the game’s progress.
I need you to stabilize your footing as soon as possible, it will take some time for the funds to reach you."
Henry responded loudly, "Yes, sir, rest assured, I will handle the funding issue!" His gaze was incredibly resolute; to this elite military agent, what difficulty is there in playing a game?
Moreover, with substantial intelligence support from the Military Intelligence Department, he already had dozens of mature strategies in mind.
Where to be born, what NPCs to meet, what to do—plans had already been made by the military intelligence.
In this situation, it’s like copying answers; how could Henry, as an elite military spy, not be confident?
The colonel was very pleased with Henry’s response.
"Go and prepare..."
Not only was Henry confident, but the colonel’s confidence was even stronger; he firmly believed that with the addition of 5,000 military agents, this so-called absolutely realistic game would be easily conquered...
The public beta of ’Glory’ was a major event watched by the whole world.
Especially true for foreign players, particularly those who had watched the live broadcast of Lide massacring foes in Anos City; they were all eager to enter the game and show off.
Of course, this also included intelligence agents from various countries with special motives.
It couldn’t be helped; ’Glory’ had too much influence, not just because of the game, but more importantly, because of what the game represented.
For instance, the core point— the game could enhance physical fitness in reality—drove top scientists crazy.
But ’Glory’ was too much of a black technology, the hackers of various nations couldn’t even find the server location, let alone break into ’Glory’s anti-theft network to obtain the source code...
Thus, the game slots they had obtained at a huge cost were not going to be wasted easily.
Everyone was ready to strike, sending military forces to participate, all for exploring the secrets of the game.
With different purposes held by various countries, Henry, as an elite agent of the United States, entered ’Glory’ along with hundreds of millions of others.
On January 1, 2052, at 21:00 in the evening, as Henry lay in the gaming pod, darkness fell before his eyes, and when he opened them again, his surroundings had changed.
This was a crumbling Medieval church building, where a quivering Magic Lamp at the decrepit wall corner emitted a faint light, casting the hanging, mottled oil paintings into antiquity.
Henry sat up and began looking around, his blue eyes swiftly turning sharp like those of a hunting falcon.
As an elite agent, although he was absolutely confident about conquering this game, he still restrained his emotions and began to observe carefully after entering the game.
"The intelligence report stated that players are born inside the Temple of the Life Goddess in ’Glory,’ and there are usually priests around. What’s the situation here without a priest?"
Frowning slightly but not dwelling on it, Henry stood up from the altar, straightened his coarse robe, and then walked straight out.
Now his first priority was to find a priest, as he did not know the common language used in ’Glory’; he needed to master the local language to proceed.
Yiya~
The moment the door opened, the blood moon in the sky caused Henry to furrow his brows deeply.
"Indeed, the intelligence department mentioned this morning that a huge change had occurred in ’Glory.’ It is speculated to be due to the second public test where the officials released a new expansion pack—Old Days’ Arrival.
Although ’Glory’s official website had no relevant announcement, considering their secrecy, it seemed to make perfect sense."
Henry’s gaze sharpened as he began to contemplate everything about the game; he seemed like a battle-hardened professional player, displaying elite traits in this deserted place.
Outside the church was a courtyard enclosed by very high walls. Although it looked somewhat dilapidated, it was clean, suggesting frequent activity.
After scanning the surroundings and seeing nothing useful, Henry approached the gate of the courtyard, but just as he was about to push it open,
Bang~
The wooden courtyard door in front of him burst open explosively, splinters flying everywhere.
Then, before Henry could hide, several players burst in.
Seeing Henry, the eyes of these evidently ill-intentioned players lit up.
"Finally, we’ve found a foreign player. Damn, there are way too many Huaxia people; we’re embarrassed to attack them. But this foreigner, we have no qualms. Let’s get to work..."
As an agent specifically targeting Huaxia, Henry, who had studied Mandarin for ten years, naturally understood their words. Startled, he quickly conjured up a feigned amiable smile.
"Hello, dear Huaxia players. Although I am from the United States... I love Huaxia dearly. I adore your cuisine, I adore your culture...
Are you beta players? May I make friends with you? Or perhaps I can offer compensation for you to... help me level up?"
Based on his past experiences, under normal circumstances, Huaxia people would often smile proudly at such flattery; this tactic should have quickly bridged the gap and worked invariably.
But what happened next was beyond his expectation...
"Fuck, this asshole thinks he can trick me? My perception is mage approved; if it wasn’t for my poor control, I would have become a mage by now."
The muscly, pockmarked-faced leader grew furious and roared with a wave of his hand.
"Act fast, today we need to capture 30 foreigners and send them to the Evil God Temple at any cost..."
Upon hearing this, the dimwitted lackey clicked his tongue, "30? Boss, is that really necessary? Isn’t it just because your boyfriend hooked up with an Englishman?..."
"Shut up!!" The pockmarked leader’s face turned green with rage, "What I have with him is love!! These damn Russians deserve to die, capture them to sacrifice to the Evil God!!"
Henry’s face paled. Were these assholes serious??
"Fuck, I am an American! You can’t treat me like this! I can offer you compensation; I have dollars..."
"Hmph, it’s you, an American, that we’re capturing. Take him out..."
Several players rushed forward, and seeing this, Henry grew angry. A top spy of the Military Intelligence Department, who had stolen plenty of major intelligence, and now some idiot players wanted to challenge him?
He promptly assumed a mixed martial arts stance, ready to show these fools what an elite was, what it meant to disrespect an American.
Just as he was about to act, suddenly everything before him blurred, and then a fist as large as a sandbag appeared in front of him.
Puchi~
The next second, the elite spy was knocked down unreasonably.
"he~tu, a newbie without even level 1 dares to pose as a master before me?
Take him back first, the rest of you, continue searching!
Find all the foreign old men lingering around the nearby temples, catch them too if you see them on the streets. Today, grandpa will let them learn the consequences of seducing someone else’s boyfriend!"
From his appearance to being dragged out the door, the spy who possessed a lot of intelligence only had time to glance at the blood moon in the sky...
Eight half-days later.
Swish~
With a gloomy face, Henry respawned above the altar. After regaining consciousness, this military spy quickly glanced at the church to ensure no one was around, then swiftly got up and agilely climbed out the window.
Behind the window was the church’s backyard, and he dared not walk through the front yard, because he didn’t know if those damned Huaxia players were still waiting for him.
Recalling the encounter when he had just been abducted, Henry subconsciously touched his groin, the pain of which still made him shudder...
"Damned bastards, my dick... No, stay calm, let’s handle the important matters first..."
Henry suppressed the fire of revenge in his heart, and after cursing those idiotic players millions of times in his mind, he began to calm down.
There were several things he needed to do now: first, find a Priest to learn the common language and blend into this world.
Second, he could spend money to hire Huaxia players to provide protection, and with money, he could definitely gain a solid footing quickly.
Third, find a safe hideout and stabilize the situation.
After some thought, Henry decided to tackle these tasks simultaneously, which, according to the intelligence from the Military Intelligence Department, was the easiest way to keep the game going.
Even if he could just survive a few days, once the military’s funding arrived in large quantities, he could instantly surge ahead with cash injections.
Although losing the first time hurt, as an elite of the United States Military, Henry quickly adjusted himself.
Having determined his next course of action, he turned to look at the three-bladed High wall in the church’s backyard, sensing the power within his body, he made up his mind.
He could scale it.
He casually threw a stone over the wall to ensure there was no Magic Barrier, then took a few steps forward and hoisted himself up.
Thanks to rigorous training, Henry was naturally no weakling, and even the physical quality of a civilian allowed him to reach the top of the wall in just a few strides.
However, just as he climbed over the wall and a look of pleasure crossed his face, suddenly, Magic Lamps lit up outside the wall, and dozens of guards, who seemed to be lying in wait, all turned their heads toward him in unison.
The scene suddenly turned awkward.
At this moment, Henry wanted to cry.
"Damn bastards!! What are these people doing up this late at night?!"
This was his last thought before hearing the whizzing sound of a crossbow arrow, and then his body heavily fell back down.
days later.
It was now one o’clock in the afternoon.
Revived from the altar, Henry gritted his teeth and stood up, and after seeing no one around from the front door, he quietly slipped out, feeling relieved once he confirmed the yard was secure.
"Those damned players shouldn’t come back again..."
"I can’t scale the back wall either, better to go through the front."
After this thought arose, Henry became much more cautious this time, slightly bending at the waist, then carefully moved forward to peek through the broken gate to check the outside.
But just as he poked his head out, a voice that made him grind his teeth spoke up.
"Oh, I got too tired staying up late last night, just had a nice sleep, and wake up to find a foreigner here, what good luck."
The burly pock-faced player yawned and then looked at Henry with a smile.
"Since I’ve seen ya, come meet our great Devouring God once more..."
Henry’s face turned green as he felt a sharp pain in his groin, immediately turned, and ran. But after just one step, a pain hit the back of his head, and he lost consciousness.
His last and only thought was a Huaxia curse he had learned.
Fuck your grandpa...
days later,
Henry revived from the altar with a cold expression.
After quickly confirming there was no one around, he didn’t rush out this time, but started searching inside the church.
As a professionally trained agent of the United States Military, leveraging cold weapons combat greatly enhanced his combat abilities.
So, he needed to find a suitable weapon.
Unfortunately, there weren’t any good weapons or Equipment here, only a couple of slightly sturdy sticks were found.
With a weapon in hand, he felt a bit more confident inside. Even after dying three times consecutively, this American agent with an unyielding will needed to let others know that you don’t mess with America.
Humph, damn Huaxia people!!
Henry cursed loudly. Then, as he looked at the darkened sky and his lips twitched, his mood instantly soured. This crappy game experience had him killed three times in one day without getting anything done.
This time, he didn’t rush out of the yard. Instead, he climbed out of the window again and returned to the backyard.
He refused to believe that someone had been camping here last night and would be here again tonight.
But just to be safe, Henry cautiously crawled up the ’Three-bladed High’ yard wall, then prepared to poke his head out to observe the surroundings.
The walls were easily scalable for this elite military man, and he quickly climbed toward the top of the wall with minimal noise.
After stabilizing himself in the stone crevices, Henry slowly peeked his head over the wall, wanting to quietly observe the outside.
But just as he poked his head out, a thick wave of magic suddenly flashed across the wall.
Henry shuddered, feeling as if ten thousand llamas had stampeded through his mind.
"There was no magic array here last night, fuck your granddad..."
Splash.
Eight days later.
The resurrected Henry, with a flushed face and trembling hands, lay on the altar.
"I shouldn’t get angry. I’m one of the most elite soldiers trained by the United States. How could I get angry?"
"There’s still a chance, there’s definitely still a chance!"
Shakily standing up, this time Henry abandoned his previous idea of sneaking in and out. It was too dangerous.
He quietly opened the door. The blood moon was still emitting a chilling aura in the sky, but Henry was in no mood to notice it.
Coming into the yard, the gate smashed by a player was still lying shattered on the ground.
Henry crouched down, eyeing the door-less exit of the yard which seemed just a few steps away.
But at this moment, this elite from the United States Military dared not approach, unsure whether the pockmarked lunatic player would suddenly appear.
The two previous experiences of being castrated had left him with severe psychological trauma... The door-less exit seemed like the gaping maw of a demon, ready to devour him at any moment.
Henry gritted his teeth and decided not to take his chances, avoiding the yard’s entrance and instead surveyed around the yard.
The walls facing forward were clearly part of a street; it would be no different from going out through the front door.
However, after circling around, he suddenly discovered a dog hole at the base of the left wall, which clearly led to another street...
Henry sneaked around, crouching in front of the dog hole, his expression torn.
To crawl through or not to crawl through??
"No!! Even if I die, I won’t crawl through a dog hole. I, who have been trained as an elite by the United States army, how could I possibly crawl through a dog hole...!"
Just as he made up his mind, but after glancing at the empty front door, a chill ran down his spine, and he shuddered.
"This is for the United States; this is glory!"
Thinking of the frightening pockmarked player, Henry bit his lip and crawled through the dog hole...
The dog hole was about two blades long. For an elite in the military, crawling through was naturally quick, and within a few moments, his head emerged on the other side.
After poking out his head and confirming that no one was around, he quickly crawled out, dusted off the dirt from his body, and rapidly walked towards the alley outside the street.
Just a few steps later, as he looked back at the church enclosed by high walls, he felt tears streaming down his face.
After more than a day, I had finally escaped from hell.
But just as Henry rejoiced in his newfound freedom, a voice from behind made his face stiffen.
"Yo? How did a foreigner just pop up here? Quick, tie him up, it’ll be dawn soon, the sacrifice must happen quickly."
Slowly turning his head, Henry saw a pockmarked, brawny man along with a few players carrying a knocked-out foreign player appearing in the alley.
Just as he opened his mouth to speak, he only felt a sack-sized fist appear before his eyes, and then the world went dark as he lost consciousness.
This time, as Henry drifted into unconsciousness, his mind was filled with one question— who the hell developed this game??
I curse his granddad!!!

chapters.title: Chapter 428 - 430: Lide Trapped in the Abyss, 1.4 Million Believers (9200 Words)
chapters.content:
Chapter 428: Chapter 430: Lide Trapped in the Abyss, 1.4 Million Believers (9200 Words)
"Damn you pests, if you block the way again I’m going to stuff your heads into the sewer and flush you away! Hurry up, send these Cave Dwellers to Naga City immediately!"
"Under Lord Kachar’s crown, I swear, if he knows you’re dallying like this, he would personally chop off your mud-filled head!"
"Only three hundred Cave Dwellers brought back?? What are you all even doing? I knew I should never have trusted you damned Griffins!
We’re waging a Divine War here, dammit!
Delaying the critical tasks of His Highness, I bet Lord Kapp won’t mind unscrewing your heads one by one and stomping them with his boots, just like squishing worms on the ground!"
In the central square of Twilight City, the furious Beastman Governor cursed at the Twilight City troops escorting the Cave Dwellers.
Divine War, this name alone filled the faces of the troops below with excitement.
Yes, they were waging a Divine War, fighting for the great Lord Kachar, the eternal God of Twilight!
Even though they had yet to see the enemy...
The current military composition of Twilight City was extremely complex, consisting of Bloodlines from Dawn City, Beastmen, Centaurs, Humans, and also the conquered Underworld races like Naga, Half-Elves, Griffins, Kobolds, and others.
All these races, conquered by Lide, had now become followers of the Twilight Sect, and those unbelievers who resisted were mostly sent to labor camps like mines or Microglow Mushroom farms, and those who defied to death had already enriched the soil.
There was no need for mercy toward the evil beings of the Underworld.
On this land, everyone including the neutral Half-Elves could be executed without injustice.
These cruel, blood-thirsty, and brutally dark beings did not deserve any sympathy.
The high command of Dawn City treated them with an iron hand.
And now, these dark races who had become followers of the Twilight Sect were doing something astonishing — capturing Cave Dwellers.
Cave Dwellers, as a weak race of the Underworld, had little value other than for mining, and their flesh was not desirable, making them rarely of interest to any beings other than wild beast hunters.
The actions of Twilight City were undoubtedly surprising.
But at the moment, the warriors below did not care about these details. All they knew was that capturing the Cave Dwellers was an order from the great Lord Kachar.
Despite the perilous environment brimming with hunters, the Cave Dwellers, capable of both living and digging holes, had not only survived but thrived due to their insignificant presence, securing a large population in the Underworld.
When the army of Twilight City received orders to capture Cave Dwellers, within just over a month, more than a million Cave Dwellers had been brought back to Twilight City.
It was an unbelievably startling number.
And it was only then that outsiders realized that such large numbers of Cave Dwellers lived in those desolate areas.
These beings, who often moved on all fours and were highly skilled at digging, could create dazzling labyrinths even out of small hills.
Moreover, once tracks of Cave Dwellers were found, they often numbered in the thousands, with large tribes holding populations of seventy to eighty thousand.
These Cave Dwellers, who survived on Microglow Mushrooms without seeing daylight in their cave dwellings, had developed their own way of living.
"Lord Kapp, this batch of Cave Dwellers totals 70,000 and needs to be immediately sent to Naga City."
The 18-level Half-Elf Great Mage, Mahari Grey Claw, stood beside the Beastman King Kapp, his eyes filled with seriousness.
"His Highness is far in the Abyss, battling the Evil God, and the consumption must be enormous.
Now is the time we need a large number of followers, but the biggest problem is that the surrounding area’s Cave Dwellers have almost been captured by us.
What’s left are either too far away or their dug caves are too deep to capture..."
As Mahari spoke, a flash of sharpness crossed his eyes.
"Lord Kapp, can we make a deal with the Half-Elves from Liusi City to help us capture the Cave Dwellers?"
The Beastman King Kapp, dressed in black battle armor, stared piercingly at those hunched and trembling Cave Dwellers on the square, a hint of chill flashing through his eyes.
"His Highness’s orders must be carried out!
As long as we can obtain more Cave Dwellers, we should spare no expense.
You must immediately represent Twilight City and negotiate with Liusi City; we can exchange the weaponry and equipment of Dawn City for their Cave Dwellers!
There’s no time to waste, set off immediately!"
Mahari was stunned by how decisive Kapp was, but quickly nodded in agreement.
"Yes, Lord Kapp..."
"All for His Majesty!"
After these solemn words were spoken, the 18th Level Half-body Mage silently turned and left. Shortly after, a squadron of Dawn Bats took flight from the military camp, heading towards the Half-body Main City.
The divine war—no one knew how terrifying this war, which existed only in legends, truly was. The higher-ups of Dawn could only do their best to fulfill the orders issued by Lide from the far Abyss.
Kapp took a deep breath after Mahari had left; he hadn’t slept for five consecutive days since he last rested.
At this moment, Twilight City needed him to be the backbone in dealing with it all.
Especially since news had already come from Dawn City that the Ancient Evil God had descended, causing great chaos in the outside world, leaving hardly any resources to support Twilight City.
At this crucial moment, he needed to shoulder it all.
The belief in his heart made the eyes of this Beastman King resolute.
He turned to the guards by his side and immediately issued an order.
"Send word, immediately transport these Cave Dwellers to Naga City!
At the same time, intensify the capture efforts, I need more Cave Dwellers!
Now is the time to show your loyalty to His Majesty!
In the distant Abyss, our ruler is clashing with the foreign Evil Gods, we absolutely must not disappoint His Majesty!"
His voice was filled with gravity and a deadly serious tone, immediately rendering the expressions of the military high command around him extremely somber.
Everyone knew that Lide’s orders must not be taken lightly, as the hundreds of beheaded heads in this period had made this very clear.
Not long after Kapp’s order, tens of thousands of Cave Dwellers were immediately hustled by the army to line up, and the hunting teams that had just returned set out once again towards the city outskirts.
This pattern had continued countless times over the past month.
"Lord Anthony, Lord Kapp has ordered the army to immediately transport the Cave Dwellers to Naga City.
The Magic Language Bats will arrive soon; there can be no delay!"
The commander of the Fearless Legion, Anthony, because his legion was small in number, mainly handled transporting the Cave Dwellers of Twilight City to Naga City.
Upon hearing this, the legendary-job commander immediately nodded in agreement then turned to urge the army behind him to speed up their march.
Most of the Magic Language Bats still needed to be dispatched to search for Cave Dwellers; they couldn’t afford much delay.
Moments later, amidst the frightened gaze of the Cave Dwellers, roars akin to an Abyssal Demon’s began to sound, covering the sky with countless demon bat wings fluttering.
The already dim light momentarily died out completely, a scene like the Abyss had shattered and sin had descended.
The Cave Dwellers below, seeing this scene, immediately trembled with fear overwhelming their eyes.
Only a few thousand soldiers surrounded them, but they faced no trouble managing over seventy thousand Cave Dwellers.
"All Cave Dwellers line up—ten on each Magic Language Bat!"
Upon the command, the soldiers below immediately began loading the terrified Cave Dwellers onto the backs of the Magic Language Bats.
More than 4000 Magic Language Bats carried away half of the Cave Dwellers in the square at once.
After confirming there were no other issues, Commander Anthony immediately mounted a Dawn Bat and led the team towards Naga City.
After the Magic Language Bat swarm had flown away, the skies above Twilight City were calm once again, except for the Cave Dwellers in the square who had witnessed the scene and showed signs of despair.
But their meager combat abilities left these underground beings with no courage to resist.
In the sky, two young warriors followed Anthony forward.
The duo looked at the indifferent Anthony, their eyes filled with undisguised admiration.
One of the warriors, after they had flown out of Twilight City, spoke nervously in a low voice, "Brother Anthony... why does Lord Kachar want to capture these Cave Dwellers?"
Hearing this question, Anthony turned back to look at the two, "Hunter, Henry, as soldiers of Dawn City, you must remember that military secrets must not be probed into."
His icy words startled the two young warriors.
"Yes, Lord Anthony!"
Seeing their nervous expressions, Anthony’s indifferent face softened slightly.
"This is a warning, you must be careful and cautious."
"But this matter is not a secret.
Lord Kachar is engaged in a Divine War in the Abyss, and the Divine War requires a great number of believers to replenish its strength."
"Uncle Kuri is a good friend of mine, and since you are his children, I will be even stricter with you.
Remember, young lads, if you want to survive on the battlefield, there is still much you need to learn."
Anthony finished speaking and then turned his head to look forward, saying no more.
The two young warriors exchanged a glance, slightly moved, and nodded hurriedly in agreement, then dared not speak any further.
But their youthful nature was fickle, and after a moment, they were excitedly looking around from the back of the Magic Language Bat, curious as babies.
Anthony, noticing this scene, had a complex expression... he recalled how naive he had been when he entered the army years ago.
But after several major battles and countless faces falling before him, that innocence could never return.
Despite the vicissitudes, he had no regrets at all.
The hardships he endured were solely for the sake of those smiling faces of Dawn.
All for Dawn.
This had become his sole and eternal belief, for which he would even dare to plunge into the Abyss.
"Your Highness, let Anthony, with the Fearless Holy Sword in hand, guard your glory."
With not a ripple in his heart, Anthony, resolutely setting his gaze on the distant horizon, underwent a subtle change in his aura during this contemplation.
If one were to check his level, one would see that this Legendary profession holder had quietly reached the astonishing Level 18... whereas a few months ago, he was only Level 15.
Legendary profession... seemingly unreasonable.
The two young warriors seemed to have sensed something; their discussion ceased immediately, not daring to utter another word of nonsense.
The subsequent flight was rather dull; with such a massive swarm of Magic Language Bats, coupled with several purgings, no significant threats remained on this route to Naga City.
Anthony leading them was merely a precaution.
Two Sunshine Hours later, the Magic Language Bats passed through the dense poison fog, and the expansive Naga City reappeared before them.
Around thirty kilometers surrounding Naga City, there was no poison fog, seemingly due to the unique geographical environment formed by the towering mountains which deflected the poison fog with air currents, creating a calm environment akin to the eye of a storm.
When the swarm of Magic Language Bats descended onto the vast plains outside Naga City that had once been scoured by Alchemy Bombs from Dawn City.
Anthony did not linger outside but directly drove the Dawn Bat to fly into the city.
At this moment, Naga City had already changed its appearance, and while the scorched earth was still present, there were many new buildings, creating a thriving scene.
What made the city different from before was that the Naga had now been replaced by Cave Dwellers.
It seemed more appropriate to rename Naga City as the City of Cave Dwellers.
When the Dawn Bat descended onto a charred piece of land, Anthony waved his hand to have two young warriors wait there while he, guided by the surrounding soldiers, headed straight for a still-intact Sharp Tooth building.
A Sharp Tooth building was characteristically Naga. After the cleansing of Alchemy Bombs, it was rare to find such a complete structure, and this twenty-plus blade-tall building also served as the office for Naga City.
As soon as the ten guards saw Anthony arrive, they immediately saluted respectfully, not daring to block him even slightly, allowing the powerful commander of the Fearless Army to enter.
"Lord Anthony."
After stepping into the hall, the Super Cave Dweller — Kedri Sharp Tooth, who had been enhanced by Lide with the Power of Faith, immediately stood up to salute.
Observing the king of the Cave Dwellers, Anthony calmly nodded his head.
"Kedri, we have 70,000 new Cave Dwellers, send people immediately to indoctrinate them.
Within three days, these Cave Dwellers must become devout believers of His Majesty!"
Kedri Sharp Tooth nodded, a murderous look evident on his uniquely ugly face.
"Rest assured, Lord, unbelievers have no right to live!"
As a Cave Dweller bestowed with everything by Lide, Kedri Sharp Tooth’s respect for Lide, both in faith and other aspects, had reached an extreme.
He would never forget the day when Lide chose him, transforming him from a weak and insignificant Cave Dweller into a Level 16 king of the Cave Dwellers.
What a magnificent transformation it was.
With Level 16, a rank impossible for ordinary Cave Dwellers to reach, Kedri Sharp Tooth now ruled over the captured millions of Cave Dwellers.
Any Cave Dweller brought in by plunder, upon seeing Kedri Sharp Tooth, would submit without exception.
The intimidation in their bloodline clearly told every Cave Dweller that the one standing before them was their king, a king like no other.
Submission to the strong is the natural instinct of life, let alone for such a weak and vulnerable race as Cave Dwellers, who had been humiliated and instilled from birth with the idea that they were a weak race.
The moment they saw their own race produce such a powerful monarch, submission to him required no extra effort.
And this was why Twilight City had appointed Kedri Sharp Tooth to manage the Cave Dwellers.
Anthony nodded slightly, his expression softening a bit.
"Act immediately, His Majesty still needs a large number of believers.
How is the construction of the prayer chambers built into the mountains progressing?" Cave Dwellers brought to Naga City would be allocated to these prayer chambers.
