The mineral and biological resources within the Abyss, vastly different from those on the main plane and possessing many scarce resources not found on the main plane, would greatly aid Dawn City’s magical technology.
Thus, ruling one or several layers of the Abyss Plane was definitely a maneuver worth attempting.
Moreover, whether attacking the Black Scale Naga Clan, finding a Teleportation Gate back to the main plane, or for the future strength of Dawn City, establishing a new power in the Abyss was imperative.
There were no other options for him to choose unless he decided to give up...
"Oli, how much power does the Kabar Naga Clan currently possess?"
Hearing this inquiry, the previously excited Naga suddenly appeared somewhat embarrassed.
"Your Highness, the Kabar Clan currently has a total of twenty thousand Naga, with an average level of 10, and only myself and another Naga Spellcaster at level 16."
Twenty thousand level 10 Naga, plus two top-tier combatants at level 15, constituted a formidable force in the main plane but seemed rather inconsequential in the Abyss.
Due to its abundant energy, the general level of Abyssal life was above level 10, far exceeding that of the main plane.
In simple terms, the Abyss should be considered an ultimate map in "Glory," likely only accessible in the very late game stages.
Lide nodded slightly without saying much, his gaze turning to his Divine Arts—Faith Enhancement.
As an Upper Race, the Naga had no shortage of potential; he could certainly enhance the power of these Naga.
With over a million believers as support, the current Power of Faith was no longer so strained.
Three Sunshine Hours later, at a vast area of giant rubble with blades over ten feet high, the Naga leader halted his steps.
"Your Majesty, the Kabar Naga Tribe is ahead; loyal believers are waiting for your arrival."
"Very well, let us proceed."
With excitement and exhilaration, the Naga leader, accompanied by over a dozen high-level Naga, led Lide into the rubble-strewn area.
The area was complex, filled with pits and winding paths, with many crevices and passages hosting Naga sentries.
Clearly, the Naga relied on this intricate landscape to fend off invasions from outsiders.
After half a Sunshine Hour, a sturdy—but not necessarily grand—Naga City appeared before Lide.
The city walls, amassed from giant stones over ten blades high and reaching a height of fifty blades, were among the most solid Lide had ever seen.
However, the Naga who built the walls were clever, seamlessly integrating them into the surrounding boulders that are as high as small hills, making them inconspicuous from the sky and difficult to spot.
At that moment, outside the stone city, a vast space was swarming with tens of thousands of Naga.
These Abyssal lives were evidently awaiting Lide’s arrival.
The Naga leader Oli had sent the news of Lide’s arrival back to Naga City ahead of time, setting the stage for this scene.
Lide, indifferent to intervening, decided to use the Kabar Naga as the core to conquer this plane and naturally wanted these Naga to be wholly submissive to him.
Nothing could speed up winning the hearts of the people more than displaying divine power in public.
In the Abyss, power is everything.
Thinking this, Lide held his head high, adopting a proud air as if a deity were descending to the mortal realm and began to slowly levitate into mid-air.
His gaze was as sharp as a hawk eyeing its prey, brilliance exposed in full force.
His primary plane’s pressure began to surge out unrestrained.
In that instant, the entire heavens and earth seemed to darken, as if a calm sea had suddenly erupted into an eighteenth-level storm, changing the colors of the heavens and the earth.
The stars in the sky seemed to encircle beneath Lide’s feet at that moment, the sun and the moon no more than toys in his hands, even the bottomless Abyss trembled thunderously.
The Naga below were instantly overwhelmed in their rationality.
"God of Twilight, the great Your Majesty has truly descended! I sense the air of twilight, praise You from the Abyss!"
"To imagine the God of Twilight in a Bloodline’s body, it’s incredible..."
"So intoxicating, Your Majesty’s presence makes my legs tremble... powerful, dignified, this is my God!!"
"Such a terrifying aura, I dare not look directly at Your Majesty’s face, the divine dignity strikes fear into my soul..."
After sensing the imposing demeanor from the figure floating in mid-air, the Naga were immediately thrown into excitement, agitation, and frenzy.
Before them was a Divine Being—the existence they worshipped, revered, and feared.
"We welcome Your arrival, my God!"
"Your humble believers pray to You..."
"Great God of Twilight..."
At that moment, Lide slowly floated above the Naga, his overwhelming force mercilessly striking out.
The Naga could no longer endure the terrifying aura he emitted, and one by one, they lowered their proud heads in submission. At this moment, these over ten thousand Naga were all Lide’s most humble subjects and believers.
The divine might was as intimidating as a prison.
All the Naga felt as if they were facing a colossal Abyssal Giant Beast, which had now opened its cruel eyes and was coldly observing them.
Each Naga’s heart was tremendously shaken.
This is a Divine Being.
The divine power infused into their souls; no one could escape or resist. At this moment, suspended in mid-air, Lide’s status in the hearts of the Naga soared to an extreme.
Even those Naga with shallow faith saw their belief rapidly intensifying.
Benevolence and majesty are essential in governance.
In dealing with believers, Lide had, over several years of trial, mastered the essence of preaching.
Among the Glory, most Evil Gods used fear and threats to garner the faith of believers.
For instance, Lide’s archenemy—the God of Plague, an Evil God who spread the Power of Faith through plagues, allowed its proliferation, and those who did not worship the God of Plague would be killed by the contagion...
The methods through which Evil Gods gained faith were always filled with bloodshed and violence, having nothing to do with justice or kindness.
The God of Twilight was not actually a traditional Evil God if Lide chose to fully transform him into a neutral Divine entity.
Of course, he would not do so. As a Bloodline, becoming an Evil God was not bad at all; he was originally a major figure of the Dark Type.
Harvesting faith from both the Light Attribute and the Dark Type—why not enjoy the best of both worlds?
"Kabar Naga..."
Lide, hovering in the sky, sensed the Naga below dare not stand upright and directly spoke in the ancient blasphemous language.
Divine Power was magnificent, and the blasphemous language thundered like lightning from the heavens, striking deeply into every Naga’s soul.
"Your devout faith has caught my attention, and your valor has earned my approval.
And my believers shall rise above all races!
From today onward, I shall descend upon the city of the Kabar Naga and grant you mighty power to lead your conquest across the entire Gravel Plane!
All other races will be enslaved by you, my most devout followers!"
These words, full of ambition and arrogance, immediately sent the Naga below into a frenzy.
The great God of Twilight himself leading them to conquer the Gravel Plane?!!
By the Abyss above, it was almost unbelievable.
Yet the desire that rose within them was akin to wild grass in spring, burgeoning uncontrollably, as Lide’s few sentences ignited the entire Naga Tribe’s ambition.
Especially Lide’s statement about enslaving other races plunged these Naga into extreme exhilaration.
To enslave other races signified their superior nobility!
For Abyss Life, enslavement was perfectly normal.
Inaction in the past was due to the Kabar Naga Clan’s weakness, lacking power, but now was different.
The great crowned one said he would support them!
Previously, they had no opportunity, but now, they were to acquire the power to govern other lives.
"Praise you, great God of Twilight!"
"My lord, we swear to spread your glory to death!"
"The Twilight Sect shall be immortal!"
Amidst the chants, Lide’s aura became even more formidable.
Only after sensing a significant rise in the entire Naga Tribe’s level of faith did he lower his form to a reachable height.
The Naga chieftain, Oli Kabar, seeing this, immediately came forward respectfully to guide Lide into the city of the Naga built in the Abyss.
The fanatical gaze of the Naga lining the path shone in their narrow eyes. As he passed by, all bowed with hands clutched at their chests.
With no need for excessive words, the mighty Divine Power and aura of Twilight served as the best pass.
Not until Lide’s figure disappeared did the Naga below dare to lift their heads. Then, in each other’s eyes during mutual glances, they saw excitement and thrill.
The Naga Tribe would become the sovereigns of the Gravel Plane!
The great crowned one would lead them to conquer all races!
Abyss Half-orc, Double-Horned Demon, Enchanting Demon, Undead—all of these would become their slaves!

chapters.title: Chapter 431 - 433: Enchanting Demon, Abyss Melee (9600 words)
chapters.content:
Chapter 431: Chapter 433: Enchanting Demon, Abyss Melee (9600 words)
"Quick, take these corrupted Jackal Wolfs back!! His Majesty requires more followers!!"
"You damned Abyss Worm, if you don’t get out of the way, I will kick your head in!!"
"Those who believe in my god shall gain eternal life!!"
The 270th layer of the bottomless Abyss, the Gravel Plane.
The Naga, nestled in the giant gravel area, expanded wildly for ten continuous days after Lide’s arrival, conquering the surrounding small tribes, corrupted Jackal Wolfs, evil lizardmen, bloodthirsty Kobolds, little devils, inferior demons, Eye Demons, and all other creatures.
The Abyss was chaotic and unstructured; war could break out at any time for no reason at all, and perhaps two tribes would engage in a fight to the death simply because they had overeaten after a hunt...
Under the influence of the will of the Abyss, except for a very few races, most were affected by the chaotic will.
The Naga were one of the few orderly evil lives within the Abyss; at least they could follow rules.
This was the reason why Lide favored the Naga. As for enslaving other races...
To take over the entire Plane, a large workforce is needed. The Kabar Naga Clan numbered barely over twenty thousand; it was impossible to conquer the whole Gravel Plane, let alone control one-tenth of its territory.
Enslaving other races became the only option.
To submit to the strong is a universal rule of Glory, which in the chaotic and unstructured Abyss was pushed to the extreme.
In the Abyss, High-level Demons have absolute rule over lower demons, and similarly, powerful tribes have dominion over weaker tribes.
Under Lide’s will, the habitat of the Naga, renamed as the Giant Gravel Region, saw all weaker races within dozens of kilometers conquered by the Naga’s large army.
After ten days of mad expansion, over 100,000 Abyss Life had been plundered into the city now renamed by Lide as Chaotic City. This was an exaggerating number.
"Your Majesty, our expansion has attracted the attention of the Abyss Half-orcs. Those ugly creatures have been frequently sending Corrosive Wolf Cavalries to scout around us in the past few days."
In the center of Chaotic City, within the most solid Naga structure, the 19th-level Naga leader, Oli Kabar, was respectfully reporting to Lide, who was examining a map at a stone table.
"Right now, 100,000 troops is the extreme we can control. If we continue to expand, it will be difficult to deter those chaotic and evil lives..."
The Naga only had twenty thousand people, including some juveniles; it was no small pressure to forcibly control a force several times greater than theirs.
If it wasn’t for capturing these evil lives in stages, they couldn’t have made so many submit to the Naga.
Upon hearing this, Lide removed his gaze from the crooked map in front of him. The Abyss hardly harbored any cultural talents; this map was produced with significant effort.
"Abyss Half-orcs? No need to pay them any mind. Have you clearly investigated the specifics of the Tempting Demons?"
"The exact number of the Tempting Demons is around 130,000. Since they employ a Ten Thousand People Army system, there are currently 13 legions, which were easy to investigate. Additionally, that recently Transcendent leader of the Tempting Demons has not left their domain in the past few days, making it impossible to gather more accurate data."
A cold light flashed in Lide’s eyes.
One advantage of the Abyss is that defeated demons would submit to higher demons, so he planned to strike at the southern group of Tempting Demons first.
If he could take down this group of Tempting Demons, he could then roll over the Abyss Half-orcs in succession.
Taking them out one by one, connecting the dots, and finally dealing with the Double-Horned Demons at the central position.
As for the undead in the Rotten Land to the north of the Gravel Plane, he had no short-term interest in them, and if there was anything to handle, it would be left until the end.
Those sickening things were hard to profit from even when killed.
In fact, with Lide’s current strength, conquering the Tempting Demons alone wouldn’t be difficult.
But he chose not to confront these forces alone for deeper reasons: the Abyss held too many hidden dangers, going alone could magnify the peril infinitely, and no one could guarantee he wouldn’t capsize in the gutter.
First, I must train the troops. The army under my control now surpasses 100,000, but in essence, they are still a mob with not the slightest sense of cooperation.
War is the best training ground. After several battles, I will be able to more clearly understand the routines of abyssal warfare and develop methods more suited to the style of the Abyssal Army.
The last point, of course, is that I am the God of Twilight, the ultimate big boss, how could it be possible that I need to roll up my sleeves and enter the fray every time? That would truly be beneath my dignity.
Moreover, when the territory expands in the future, could I possibly defend it all by myself? Naturally, I will need the armies of my subordinates to guard the territory. If I do not train these armies now, will I have to act as their nanny every day in the future?
"Prepare for war.
This time, I will personally lead the Naga to conquer the Tempting Demons!"
With just one sentence, Lide had the Naga chiefs excited.
The words may be simple, but they are too domineering; it seems as if with these words spoken, that powerful demon force is destined to be trampled underfoot.
It didn’t take long after Lide’s order was given before the war horn, made from demonic longhorns, sounded throughout Chaotic City.
The captive Evil Races at this moment were all gathered on the open ground in front of the city walls.
The reason they were concentrated here was, one, because Chaotic City couldn’t fit 100,000 people, and on the other hand, it was because of the corpse of the Snake Clan God hanging above the city walls - a Five Circle Magic long body, shaped like an Eight-Armed Snake Demon.
The Divine are ultimately the most powerful beings; even after death, they still emit a chilling aura. The pressure caused by that Divine Power is like a mountain pressing on one’s chest, making the people around struggle even to breathe.
No one can resist such sheer terror; there is only trembling, only fear, only submission.
This is also the fundamental reason why Lide didn’t show up for more than ten days, but the Naga still controlled the situation.
If even Divine beings die at the hands of the master of this city, what right do they have to resist?
It is also because the body of the Snake Clan God is hanging above the city gate that the Naga become more devout every time they enter and exit in these days.
That is a genuine Divine being, and yet it is so publicly hung on the city gate! How shocking it is.
What quickens their heartbeats even more is that the great being who killed the Divine is in Naga City, no, in Chaotic City now.
Listen to this name, Chaotic City, how majestic; it was personally named by His Majesty!
"Abyss above, I just heard the command - our Great Majesty will personally lead us to conquer those lowly Tempting Demons!!"
"Hahaha, I knew this day would come! His Majesty’s order to enslave the surrounding tribes must be in preparation for conquering the Gravel Plane!"
"His Majesty’s Glory will surely spread across the abyss, and those damned heretics, if they don’t submit, then wait to be annihilated by us..."
"The Kabar Naga are the rulers of the Gravel Plane! We will be the only High-level Life!"
Upon hearing the orders to conquer the Tempting Demons, the Naga were nearly driven to madness.
The ambitions of these Upper Races were activated by Lide just ten days before; now, hearing the command, they couldn’t wait to charge at the Tempting Demons and conquer those Abyss Demons.
Ruling other races is the ambition of every Abyss Life - only through this can they showcase their power and noble Bloodline; the Naga are no exception.
Even the weaker Abyss Lives like the Cave Dwellers and fallen dwarves harbor such ambitions.
As the Naga were in heated discussions, the Evil God Races who were newly captured showed various expressions, some frightened and panicked, others lost and confused.
When they saw the corpse of the Divine hanging above the city walls, any will to resist was crushed.
The Divine are dead, what qualification do these weak Lives have to resist?
And what’s more terrifying is that the legendary God of Twilight is actually within this city.
Upon contemplating this horrifying fact, they all unconsciously slowed their breathing, as if afraid of attracting the attention of the terrible being that killed the Divine.
In these days, the Evil Lives that had started following the Twilight Sect are now even more fanatical than the Naga.
They are filled with pride and self-respect; if any of the captives show any disrespect towards Lide, the most fiercely reactive are not the Naga but these new believers of the Twilight Sect.
As the heated discussions continued below, a terrifyingly dreadful presence emanated from within the Chaotic City, a divine power countless times more fearsome than the Divine Body upon the city walls.
All voices were as if strangled, and no one dared to utter another word, plunging the scene into a silence.
Oppression of the soul.
A moment later, over a hundred thousand people simultaneously looked up to the skies.
At that moment, one could see a towering figure radiating with gloomy light, standing across the sky as if from a shattered Star River.
Enveloped by the gloomy light, all anyone could vaguely make out was a pair of spread Demon Wings, but they couldn’t see its face, figure, or even what it was wearing.
Bathed in that divine power, it was mysterious and powerful.
Divine beings need not be overly intimate with their believers; maintaining sufficient mystery and distance is key to enhancing faith.
The more mysterious, the more believers would fill in the blanks with their imagination, deepening their faith in their minds.
Lide was already well aware of this dynamic, and there was no need for him to perform any miracles or anything else to deepen his dignity.
The Divine Body of the Snake Clan God on the city walls was enough to make all evil races below tremble.
Slaying a divine being, such a terrifying achievement, was simply too exaggerated for these lives that hadn’t even reached level 15.
"My believers, when Twilight shrouds the earth, everything shall turn to dust."
The ancient and blasphemous language boomed in the minds of the evil lives below like thunder, causing their souls to shudder in unison.
"From today onward, the Gravel Plane shall become the Twilight Sect’s domain of dominance!
And you, believers of the Twilight Sect, my loyal servants, shall manage this land for me...
My believers will reign supreme above all, and you may enslave and trample those lowly heretic races and Abyss Demons!"
Lide’s domineering words immediately excited the armies below.
They howled and hollered, as if they couldn’t wait to slaughter their enemies on the battlefield and then chain up their captives like dogs to be kept for amusement.
"Kill those Abyss Worms!!"
"Yes, chop off their excrement-filled heads!"
"The Glory of our Sovereign shall be spread by us!"
"Long live the Twilight Sect!!"
The shouts of over a hundred thousand people made the atmosphere incredibly heated.
"Now, every ten thousand shall form a legion, each legion will be divided into ten thousand-man squads, and each squad will be led by 200 Nagas."
"Those who do not believe in the Twilight Sect shall form a separate Vanguard Legion, which will charge ahead during the war with the Enchanting Demons!"
Lide’s voice, filled with endless dignity, resounded through the sky, for these Abyss Lives naturally deserved no kindness; such a thing did not exist on this land.
And his words, like a bucket of cold water poured onto boiling oil, elicited an even greater reaction.
Especially those who had just converted to the Twilight Sect, they felt as if they had found their sense of belonging and confidence, identifying non-believers around them more proactively than even the Nagas.
The recognized Abyss Races couldn’t help but change their expressions and even incite a riot amidst the pushing and shoving commotion.
Chaotic and evil Demons have no rules to speak of, and stimulated, a few inferior demons and little Demons suddenly erupted, killing two Nagas and splashing fresh blood, plunging the scene into even greater Chaos.
With the scent of Death Aura in the air, the sanity of the Abyss Lives began to be consumed, and then they turned to slaughter the people around them.
Although the disturbance happened suddenly, it was after all the Naga’s home turf, and it subsided in just a few minutes.
The cost of this disturbance was thousands more Demon corpses spread across the lower encampment.
Lide witnessed the scene without a hint of fluctuation in his expression, for chaos, disorder, and slaughter were the eternal main themes of the abyss.
The death of these evil lives mattered little; the loss of a thousand would not make a difference. As long as the war was won, they could immediately obtain more troops for reinforcement.
The rules of conduct from the Main Plane did not apply to this land.
Those powerful Demon Lords relied on the continual waging of wars, conquering lands to enslave more demons and thus strengthen themselves.
Many of the Planes in the abyss without any living creatures were mostly due to wars.
However, with the existence of the birthplaces at the bottom of the abyss, countless Abyss Worms hatched daily, growing into new demons, so no matter how fierce the wars in the abyss became, this land of evil never suffered a shortage of life.
And who let those evil races disbelieve in the Twilight Sect? That was simply seeking death.
This, indeed, was the correct way to approach the abyss; those who opposed it were to be killed.
Sure enough, after that scene just now, under the stimulation of fresh blood, those evil lives who still didn’t believe in Lide one by one became nominal believers.
Regardless of the process, at least the outcome was quite good.
After the disturbance was quelled, the Naga leader immediately began arranging to divide the army; Lide had already prepared them for this strategy, so there was no chaos.
Quickly, under the stimulation of fresh blood and Lide’s influence, twelve Ten Thousand People Armies were formed.
Two thousand Nagas were dispersed among the various army corps, acting as the backbone of the army and in command.
The wars of the abyss did not need much preparation; life here was the least valuable. The superiors did not take the armies below seriously, and even the chaotic evil lives did not take themselves seriously.
Conquest! Enslavement! Pillage! One after another, sinister words drove these evil races to gradually lose their minds.
Once the army corps were divided, Lide did not make any further arrangements and directly ordered them to march.
A group of howling and chaotic Abyss Life marched toward the direction of the Enchanting Demons with most of them not even wielding weapons.
But the demons’ tusks and claws were the most suitable tools for reaping souls, scythes of the Death God.
Outside the giant rocky area where the Nagas dwelt,
more than a dozen Three-Bladed High, Five-Bladed Long, with fierce Tusks, Corrosive Wolf Cavalry stood with wide mouths atop a massive boulder, overlooking the distance. Their drool dripped onto the stone, fizzing with corrosion like high-concentration sulfuric acid, pitting dense craters onto the surface.
These terrifying Abyss Predators had on their backs Abyss Half-Orcs with extremely ugly faces, filled with a fierce and murderous air, whose ugly visages were even more off-putting than the Half-Beasts in Earth’s film "The Lord of the Rings."
Upon seeing the gigantic Chaotic City Army emerge from the rocky region, these Corrosive Wolf Cavalry immediately bared their blackened teeth with murderous intent.
"Immediately return and report to the Lord; these damned Nagas have already enslaved the surrounding tribes, and they are heading toward the Enchanting Demons’ territory..."
Abyssal wars never needed reasons; these Corrosive Wolf Cavalry didn’t care why the Nagas were attacking the Enchanting Demons, they were only concerned about what benefits they could get in the war.
Such as, swallowing them whole at the last moment of the struggle!
Abyss Life, though chaotic and disorderly, did not mean lacking brains; they simply preferred a direct and rough approach...
The march of an army of over a hundred thousand was not a quiet affair, but the Nagas had already bloodily cleared the road to the Enchanting Demon, slaying all the demons that could have affected their march.
The territory of the Enchanting Demon was about 300 kilometers away from Chaotic City, and by the demons’ marching speed, it would take two days to arrive.
These robust lives could even march continuously for more than ten days without sleep or rest, and if not for the lack of military discipline, solely relying on force to control these chaotic beings, the demons would absolutely be an excellent choice for soldiers.
Lide floated above in the sky, looking down upon the twelve Ten Thousand People Armies below.
Behind him was the body of the Snake Clan God, which he awkwardly had to bring along as he could not store it in the System Space, for he did not trust leaving it just like that in Chaotic City, especially after what had hung on the city walls...
Moreover, if things went as planned, this Divine Body would also be useful soon.
Since he had decided to take control of the Abyss Plane, he wouldn’t be frugal with his investments; inevitably, he would have to nurture a few Transcendents to garrison, and the body of the Snake Clan God would be the best nourishment.
Although he wanted to keep most of the Divinity of this body for his breakthrough to Legendary, it didn’t prevent him from using a small part of it to cultivate a few powerful subordinates.
The journey was always somewhat tedious, and it wasn’t until Lide caught a three-headed Abyss bird beast to serve as his temporary mount that he managed to keep his emotions in check.
He had left Castro back in Green City when he came to explore the Divine relics, so now he had to make do with what was available.
As the Chaotic Army marched, not a single blade of grass was left living in their wake.
Any solitary evil life forms discovered were immediately conscripted into the Heresy Army, and those who dared resist were beheaded on the spot.
If they were willing to believe in the great Twilight Sect, they might have a chance to join the formal army.
By the next day, the numbers of the Chaotic Army had increased by a few thousand...
The news of the Naga attacking the Enchanting Demons couldn’t be hidden due to the sheer size of the army, and it wasn’t long before all the major powers became aware of it.
Among them, the Abyss Half-orcs and the Double-Horned Demons from the central region of the Gravel Plane had the strongest reactions.
But war was a common occurrence in the Abyss; nobody thought this war was any different from the ones before.
Still, feeling threatened by the massive army of over a hundred thousand, these two forces deployed quite a few spies to monitor the situation.
Lide couldn’t be bothered to even look at this, letting the Naga drive these people away, while the well-hidden demons were ignored altogether.
They needn’t be anxious, he would plow through them one by one.
Although the army did not stop, it wasn’t until the twilight of the next day that they entered the territory of the Enchanting Demons.
Day and night in the Abyss did not depend on the sun and moon; the night sky was still lit, only dimmer than the day. If the brightness of day was 10, then the night would only be 5.
As the God of Twilight, Lide was naturally aware of the day’s cycle of changes, and every time twilight came, he felt his strength increase by a certain extent, similar to how the Bloodline grew stronger in the night.
This moment, it belonged to him.
The territory of the Enchanting Demons was a vast expanse of low-lying scrubland where twisted, aberrant Abyss plants spread like the hair of the dead, sending chills down one’s spine at a glance.
When twelve Chaotic Armies stepped onto the lands of the Enchanting Demons who had already been informed, they had formed a huge formation ready to clash head-on.
But due to the chaos and disorder, the formation appeared messy and, in Lide’s eyes, looking from above in the sky, it seemed even worse than not forming any...
The Enchanting Demons were true Abyss Demons, often described in an exaggerated tone by wandering bards from the Main Plane.
The appearance of these middle-level Demons was filled with magic and horror; approximately two and a half blades tall and slender, but what caused one to break into a cold sweat was the fierce, sharp bone spurs that covered their bodies.
It was even more striking than a hedgehog.
Instead of a humanoid arm at the right, there was a crab-like pincer, the joints of which fit tightly together, capable of easily snapping steel.
The skin under the bone spurs of the Enchanting Demons was grayish-black like soil, and in combination with the spurs and pincer, it presented an intimidating appearance.
What chilled outsiders even more were—the eyes of the Enchanting Demons.
They boasted a pair of eyes even more seductive than those of the Enchanting Demons, and anyone who made eye contact with this demon would be subjected to a burst of energy equivalent to a Three Circle Spell—Abyss Seduction Skill. Those who failed the will check would be seduced by it, turning into lambs for the slaughter.
That’s why they were called Enchanting Demons.
The initial level of an Enchanting Demon was 10, elite level at 14, and the highest level could break through 15, with a rare few Demon Lords surpassing the Transcendent level.
These were the most common middle-level demons in the Abyss.
However, despite being a middle-level demon, their combat effectiveness is not at all poor due to the environment of the Abyss.
"Damn mongrels! Let the mighty Naga send you to meet the Death God!"
"Under his highness’s brilliance, these foolish demons shall be trampled beneath our feet!"
"I want to chop off the heads of these Enchanting Demons and dig out their damned Enchanting Demon Eyes!"
"Kill them!!"
The army, after relentlessly marching for two days and nights, was at its breaking point. Upon encountering the Enchanting Demons, they didn’t even need encouragement; at that moment, their inherent brutality and bloodlust were fully unleashed.
Likewise, the army of Enchanting Demons, which had been waiting outside Thousand Blades for a long while, showed no signs of weakness, their eyes filled with the craziest intent to kill as they gazed at the Chaotic Army.
"Abyss Worms! Daring to provoke the great Enchanting Demons, you’re seeking your own death!"
"It’s been a long time since I’ve tasted Naga flesh, how nostalgic..."
"Let’s go, kill these lowly lives. How could the noble Enchanting Demons be challenged by this Abyssal trash?!"
"Let me devour your brains, I’m hungry..."
When the two sides met, there weren’t even any additional maneuvers; as the war horns sounded, the battle immediately escalated to a climax.
The Enchanting Demons didn’t care why the Chaotic Army was attacking them. They only knew that at this moment they had to tear apart these lowly lives that dared to provoke them!!
Above the sky, Lide observed everything calmly. He did not join the fray but watched the Abyssal battle unfold from the standpoint of an observer.
He wanted to understand firsthand how a battle involving tens of thousands was conducted in the Abyss... He had always been somewhat ignorant of Abyssal warfare, but now he had a live sample before him.
The Chaotic Army roared forth, and the Enchanting Demon Army was unwilling to show weakness either. In mere breaths, the two sides collided.
The Heresy Army, who did not practice the faith of the Twilight Sect, were driven to the very forefront.
On the cruel and bloody battlefield, the Heresy Army served as the first wave of meat shields, with over 8000 heretical creatures colliding directly with the Enchanting Demons.
However, before the two sides even made contact, many of the evil beings who looked directly into the eyes of the Enchanting Demons suddenly stiffened and then turned to slaughter their own forces like madmen.
In an instant, over a thousand were controlled by the Enchanting Demons, creating huge disruptions in the surrounding formations.
Taking advantage of the situation, the Enchanting Demons advanced with their claws, sweeping like the scythes of the Death God, reaping souls. Each swipe meant more of the Chaotic Army fell.
Corrupted Jackal Wolfmen, Evil Lizardmen, bloodthirsty Kobolds—the Chaotic Army, aside from the Nagas, was mostly comprised of these three evil races, totaling over 80,000 beings.
These evil creatures had pitifully low resistance to the Enchanting Demon Eyes of the Enchanting Demons, and in an instant, a large number were wounded or killed.
Puchi, blood and limbs splattered in that moment, the pouring blood soaking the shallow, stunted grass of the Abyss.
The instantaneous skirmish turned white-hot at the moment of collision.
The aura of slaughter on the battlefield consumed the sanity of all engaged in the fight.
The Enchanting Demons were like killing machines, and those Enchanting Demon Eyes were particularly terrifying. Any being that met their gaze was struck as if by lightning, instantly losing the will to resist.
Looking down from the sky, the sheer number of over two hundred thousand army members entwined in combat was breathtaking.
Especially since these armies consisted of diverse races from the Abyss, the scene was like a bard’s tale of infinite blood wars between Abyssal Demons and Hell Demons.
At this moment, Lide still did not intervene. He continued to watch everything as an observer.
Chaos was his overriding impression of this war.
After the battle started, the Nagas, who were originally in command, completely disregarded any strategy and drew their daggers to join the fray, and the other creatures also ignored commands and simply rushed towards the Enchanting Demons.
Even a portion of the minor demons and inferior demons, before they collided with the Enchanting Demons due to an overload of murderous intent, turned on their own ranks and killed without care for friend or foe.
This unprecedented chaotic warfare furrowed Lide’s brows.
But he still did not intervene; he wanted to see just how an Abyssal army’s battle would unfold.
After clashing, the troops below entered a bloodthirsty state, their eyes glowing red with killings, where no rules or tactics existed. The only objective was to behead the enemy, to pierce the enemy’s heart.
A Four-Armed Naga with daggers fashioned from Demon Beast tusks danced through the crowd, and in just a few encounters, slew three or four Enchanting Demons.
After realizing this, a Level 14 Enchanting Demon crushed the skull of a nearby Corrupted Jackal Wolfman with its pincers and then turned towards the Naga who had drawn their attention.
The Enchanting Demon Eyes emitted a malevolent light, attempting to use its powerful Talent to restrain the Naga. However, the Naga was very experienced, tilting its head slightly to avoid direct eye contact with the Enchanting Demon.
The powerful serpentine tail, like a spring compressed to the extreme, began to unleash its ferocity, its form flashing forward like lightning.
Seeing this, the Enchanting Demon swung its iron cast-like giant claw ferociously, its gruesome face revealing a brutal killing intent.
It wanted to crush this Naga riffraff!!
But the constantly active Enchanting Demon Eye was actually the Enchanting Demon’s greatest weapon. Without the coordination of the Enchanting Demon Eye, the fighting capabilities of these kinds of Abyss Demons can only be described as ordinary.
In a flash of lightning, as the two sides closed in, the Enchanting Demon’s claw swung down in an arc, but the agile Naga contorted its body strangely, dodging the giant pincer’s assault.
In that instant, four powerful arms erupted with the force to shatter boulders, and the sharp tusk Dagger, like a bolt of lightning, struck a continuous~ series of blows at the base of the Enchanting Demon’s claw.
Under the massive impact, with a snap~ the Enchanting Demon’s huge pincer actually broke off and crashed to the ground, with fresh blood splattering about.
Pain, like a tidal surge, overwhelmed the Enchanting Demon’s reason, and with an agonized roar from its mouth, but in the next second, the Four-Armed Naga did not give the Demon any more chances.
Pffft~
The Dagger swung again, directly piercing through the neck of the Enchanting Demon, and thick blood spurted out, even causing a strong ripple of magic tide due to the huge Magic Power contained within its blood.
In this skirmish, the Naga prevailed completely.
As an Upper Race, the Naga’s formidable combat power goes without saying, holding no small advantage when facing the Middle-level Demon—the Enchanting Demon.
Although the Naga were strong enough, the same could not be said for other races, such as the Corrupted Jackal Wolfman and the Evil Lizardman, who mainly relied on their sharp teeth and claws for attacks.
But when facing the Enchanting Demon’s large pincers and those deadly Enchanting Demon Eyes, they were often controlled before they could leap forward, then easily had their heads crushed.
Each side had its trump cards, leading to an extraordinarily tense battle situation.
On the chaotic battlefield, there were no ceaseless commands, only the Naga coordinating to some extent among themselves. However, due to the extreme chaos, such levels of cooperation were also very limited in effect.
A battle of more than two hundred thousand was destined not to end in mere minutes. After half a day, the situation on the field remained tense, and it was impossible to tell whether the Enchanting Demons, who could control others, held the advantage or whether the impromptu Chaotic Army did.
Lide, observing the situation, had a good understanding of the battle status of the Abyss—it was even more chaotic than the tales told by wandering bards.
He saw with his own eyes a few Naga, after slaying an Enchanting Demon, casually turning to topple a few Corrupted Jackal Wolfman. He also witnessed the enslaved inferior demons who specialized in killing weaker Kobolds...
The life forms of the Main Plane would have a hard time understanding what’s on the minds of these chaotic and evil beings.
"That Extraordinary Tempting Demon commandant is indeed very patient; it hasn’t appeared for so long... but it’s pointless to drag this out any longer. Everyone here will become my spoils of war... damaging one’s own spoils is not a wise move."
He hesitated no further, floated upward, his eyes carrying a chilling murderous intent as he soared across the sky, directly floating over the battlefield.
The two sides below, in the heat of killing, did not notice Lide in the sky at all. When Demons are agitated, reason becomes nonexistent.
Master of the Divine, Immortal King, Master of Crimson, the descent of fear...
Lide wasted no time in activating all his titles and auras.
In that moment, the heavens and earth changed color, and the stars ceased their spin.
The armies below, engaged in fierce combat, were as if suddenly paused—their bloodlust that had surged to their heads was unceremoniously drenched with hundreds of buckets of ice water, chilling them from head to toe...
Terror, pure terror!
That terrifying presence swept every corner of the world.
This was the pressure of the Divine, the aura of the Divine System Master.
At this moment, Lide was like an ancient wild beast, which ended the era of gods, resurrecting once more, his eyes as fierce as the sun and moon, fixing their gaze upon them.
The remaining hundred thousand evil lives below trembled uncontrollably in both soul and body, an instinctive reaction of their biology, utterly unstoppable.
"Twilight falls, and all things shall turn to ashes...
I am the God of Twilight, holding the Twilight Divine Position, and likewise, I control the fate of you all."
The blasphemous language of ancient times now seemed like boulders crashing down from towering mountains, each word striking the souls of the crowd with a buzzing sound in their ears.
"The Gravel Plane shall become the dwelling place of my believers."
"Kill those who are not my followers!"
The final word "kill" landed with the weight of billions of tons.
It smashed into the minds, causing a thousand waves of shock.
The troops below had not yet recovered their wits when suddenly, from the ranks of the Enchanting Demons, a figure imbued with a mighty aura flew out.
A surge of extraordinary power fluctuated, startlingly, it was none other than the leader of the Extraordinary Tempting Demons.
However, just as Lide thought the opponent was about to resist, that Extraordinary Demon split open with a crackle, blood splattering as its body split like rubber into seven or eight parts, each piece transforming into an Enchanting Demon like the original and fleeing the battlefield without looking back.
That Extraordinary Demon had indeed been scared off by Lide, and it had used a move that was surely a life-saving trump card. It was evident that it would cause great damage to itself, and might even lead to a fall in level.
By the time Lide realized what the leader of the Enchanting Demons had done, those separate figures had already flown far away, and at most he could only pursue three or two of them.
Shaking his head, he could only give up.
Lide looked down at the still panicked and bewildered Enchanting Demons below and twitched the corner of his mouth. Is this the Abyss?
Betraying one’s teammates so decisively?
It was only after the aura of the lord of the Enchanting Demons had completely disappeared that those below realized their boss had been scared to the point of pissing himself and had run away.
The anxiety that was already present in their hearts was instantly devoured by fear, and the will to resist collapsed in that moment.
The Enchanting Demons were not High-level Demons to begin with, and it was a myth to think they could stand against Divine Power.
Under the terrifying pressure as vast as a tempest, the number of Enchanting Demons, totaling some sixty to seventy thousand, each knelt and submitted to the towering figure in the sky.
In the moment of their kneeling, all demons inside sighed with great relief, as if they had just escaped the scythe of the Death God.
Seeing this, the surrounding Nagas and other believers were instantly filled with excitement.
Indeed, as long as one followed the great crown, victory was assured!
Praise the Abyss!
They shouted out one after another.
"The Glory of my God shall become eternal!!"
"Ha ha ha, how could these damned lowly demons withstand the Dignity of our God?"
"We’ve won!! Praise the crown, Your radiance is enough to make the Abyss pale in comparison!!"
"..."
Lide, looking at the excited crowd below, didn’t feel much, as the war, though intense with conflict, was too chaotic of a battle, too Abyssal to watch.
But it was also the first step towards conquering the Gravel Plane.
His gaze shifted toward the distance, where over a dozen Corrosive Wolf Cavalry were observing the battlefield from afar.
A cold murderous light flashed in his eyes.
Abyss Half-orcs... Let’s flatten them today as well. He didn’t have that much time to waste here.
He must take over the entire Gravel Plane at the fastest speed and then capture the teleportation gate owned by the Black Scale Nagas to return to the Main Plane.
Whether it be dispatching the Dawn City troops into the Abyss for a pig-farming plan or plundering the rare minerals of the Abyss, both were excellent choices.

chapters.title: Chapter 432 - 434: The Divine Descending into the Main Plane, The Beginning of Chaos
chapters.content:
Chapter 432: Chapter 434: The Divine Descending into the Main Plane, The Beginning of Chaos
"Duke, three Sunshine Hours ago, Melt Snow City was breached by the Fierce Half-Ratmen from Risier City, leading over one hundred thousand Corrupted Jackal Wolfmen.
All 20,000 people in the city who had not yet been relocated to Green City perished..."
"The road to the Blue Sea Province has been closed since February 1st, but it has not been cleared yet. The main reason is that the 20,000 troops we sent out were attacked by mutated Ancient Monsters en route..."
"Moreover, the followers of the Evil God in Green City have been increasing recently, and despite repeated suppression, we cannot stop the activities of the Evil God believers..."
"What’s even more severe is that the population in the city has now exceeded three million. Although we had food reserves in advance, this winter we need not worry too much.
However, if the power of the Ancient days does not abate, and our fields remain uncultivated, it will be an unprecedented disaster... our food can last at most one year."
Duke O’Kelly stood with his hands behind his back near the now-shut window, looking out over the snowy scape of Green City through the glass. From the highest ninth-floor loft of the City Lord’s manor, he could oversee a third of the city’s district.
The bishop of the God of Nobles was currently reporting the latest news with a worried expression.
From the news he relayed, one could sense that the situation was becoming increasingly dire, sliding towards indescribable decay.
After a long while, Duke O’Kelly’s somewhat hoarse voice finally spoke slowly.
"Has there been any news from the Nolan Capital?"
"No, it’s been three days. All our spellcasters have been unable to contact the Capital using magic.
The effectiveness of spells is extremely poor; even the magic scrolls for sending messages cannot be successfully cast.
We have already sent out doves three times, and it will take at least a few days to receive any news..."
Upon hearing this, Duke O’Kelly’s aged blue eyes sharpened and his expression darkened.
"Tell me some good news, Your Excellency.
It’s already February 3rd, a full month since the sky cracked and the Ancient times descended, and I have never received any good news..."
Speaking thus, the ruler of Green City lifted his head to glance at the sky cracked like a mirror, his expression immensely complex.
The disaster of the Ancient days was too overwhelming...
The bishop showed a wry smile. Good news? Perhaps the biggest piece of good news was that Green City could still hold out for some time.
After pondering for a moment, his eyes brightened.
"Duke, if I must say... the Dawn Sect seems to be doing very well lately, with the number of believers nearing 500,000."
Duke O’Kelly turned slightly and looked at the bishop, somewhat puzzled.
"Lord Ilo has yet to return. Even if the Dawn Sect’s followers reached one million, what difference would it make?"
"Duke, it’s not about the number of believers that matters; rather, it’s that the priests of the Dawn Sect still retain their casting ability...
Over the past month, the Dawn Sect has already cultivated over 500 priests. The Holy Light Power in these priests’ hands has a great restraining effect on those monsters corrupted by the Ancient powers."
Duke O’Kelly’s expression then eased slightly.
"Other sects’ priests are powerless because their divines have disappeared, while Lord Ilo’s followers still possess the power bestowed by Lord Ilo.
However, 500 priests are still insufficient to meet the needs of future wars. Continue to provide them support, I hope the Dawn Sect can cultivate at least 2,000 Dawn Priests..."
The rapid development of the Dawn Sect was inseparable from the strong support of Duke O’Kelly, the ruler of Green City.
At this critical moment, priests with casting ability were a precious resource that Green City desperately needed.
Promoting the Dawn Sect was a win-win situation.
"Also, we must fully investigate Lord Ilo’s whereabouts... Green City, currently only Lord Ilo can shelter us from the storm."
Duke O’Kelly sighed deeply, the duke at the peak of his power felt an inexplicable sense of powerlessness.
After the arrival of the Ancient times, not just the order of the south but the entirety of the Nolan Empire had collapsed.
Over a third of the more than twenty cities in the southern province had fallen, and over half of the remaining cities had their paths to Green City cut off.
Looking around, he suddenly realized that Green City was now like an isolated island, unable to receive any military aid from outside.
Even to the point of pessimism, they could only wait for the sudden appearance of the Ancient Evil God’s onslaught.
If it were only the Evil God’s servants, it would be bearable. Green City had amassed an army of 400,000 by concentrating the power of several cities, and with over 500,000 Independent Professionals, Lide had enough confidence to defend Green City.
But should the power of the Ancient Evil God reach Legendary or even higher levels, the entirety of Green City would be wholeheartedly exposed to the enemy’s slaughter.
In war, high-level combat power acted like a nuclear bomb; having an army of two hundred thousand was no match for a single Big Ivan.
Given such circumstances, it was critical to find a deterrent-level combat strength, and currently, the only person who qualified was the powerful Lord Ilo.
The bishop nodded his head and respectfully replied,
"Duke, seeking Lord Ilo has already been listed as our top priority project. As long as His Eminence appears..."
But just as the bishop had said half of his sentence, a hoarse voice at the door interrupted their conversation.
"There is no need for such efforts. That Lord Ilo is merely a Fake God..."
Hearing this, Duke O’Kelly’s expression darkened dramatically.
He abruptly turned to the doorway.
In an instant, a mysterious figure wearing a grey cloak, his face shrouded in shadow with only a prominent nose visible, appeared inside the room.
The bishop, infuriated, immediately started to rebuke,
"Who is this rascal?! How dare you defame the great Lord Ilo..."
But before he could finish, the cloaked figure suddenly threw back his hood, letting the garment that had enveloped his entire form fall to the ground with a swish.
In that instant, the bishop and the cloaked figure’s eyes met.
After seeing the mysterious figure clearly, the bishop, who was initially furious, stood thunderstruck, his eyes brimming with disbelief.
Then, with legs giving out and a face full of endless joy and terror, he knelt down, his eyes filled with a frenzy unfathomable to others.
"Lord Feilder! Your most devout believer sends you humble greetings!"
Once Duke O’Kelly saw clearly who it was, his eyes widened, unable to recover his senses, his shock no less than the bishop who was already kneeling and worshiping.
Because the man standing before him in a pristine white robe was none other than the God of Nobles—Feilder, the deity whom the entire Nolan nobility revered.
This ancient being, who had lived for millions of years, was now standing before him.
The impact was so strong that Duke O’Kelly had nearly forgotten to pay homage.
Although this was not the first divine being he had seen, having previously encountered Lord Ilo,
Lide gave him a shock of strength, while the God of Nobles struck him with the entry of myth into reality, a completely different concept.
Only after the God of Nobles, Feilder, stepped inside the room did Duke O’Kelly come to his senses and hurriedly suppressed the torrent of emotions within him, stepping forward to bow deeply.
"Duke O’Kelly Nolan greets the God. Your arrival brings glory to the whole Green City..."
Feilder, with his deep amber eyes looking down from above, spoke in an ethereal and indifferent tone,
"Rise, O’Kelly."
"Yes, Your Eminence." O’Kelly stood up, sensing the aura that emanated from him, his gaze flickering slightly. Having worshiped the God of Nobles for decades, he was naturally familiar with his power.
But now, having calmed himself, he realized that the divine aura of the God of Nobles was quite unstable, as if... he had been severely wounded?
This discovery made him somewhat uneasy.
Noticing Duke O’Kelly’s gaze, Feilder’s brow furrowed and he slowly said,
"O’Kelly, I just heard that you were discussing that Lord Ilo?"
This made Duke O’Kelly’s expression hesitant; he didn’t want the other to misunderstand, for discussing another deity in front of one was not a pleasant matter.
"Yes, Your Eminence, Lord Ilo is an exceedingly powerful being, he..."
Duke O’Kelly meant to explain, but as soon as he spoke, the God of Nobles’ expression subtly changed, and the deity unmercifully interrupted him.
"O’Kelly, the so-called Lord Ilo, is nothing but a Fake God, a complete Fake God!"
On the third day of the Ancient Times, the God of Nobles actually descended into Green City.
However, due to the shattering of the Destiny Tablet, his Divine Power had been completely stripped away, his strength not even one ten-thousandth of what it was at his peak.
Thus, for safety, he hid among the refugees to take the opportunity to observe everything in Green City and decide how to proceed.
The scene he observed both delighted and enraged him.
He was delighted that the city’s ruler, Duke O’Kelly, was a believer of his, which meant that if he could gain the support of this City Lord, he could gather believers to restore his power.
But what enraged him was that this believer seemed to have betrayed him, as he was promoting a Dawn Sect he had never heard of.
And the Divine entity of this unfamiliar sect was none other than a previously unheard of Fake God—the Dawn God.
He couldn’t help but hesitate. Would it be safe to approach directly?
If Duke O’Kelly still worshipped him, then the matter would be simple.
But if the other party had already turned to that Fake God, appearing so openly in front of him without power could very well expose him to unimaginable threats.
Slaying gods was a temptation irresistible even to Divine Beings.
Thus, the God of Nobles remained hidden for over a month, and during this time, after he learned that Lord Ilo seemed to have left Green City for a while and had not returned, he finally sneaked into the Lord’s manor.
"I have never heard of the Dawn Sect or the Dawn God among the multitude of gods. That Lord Ilo, in my view, must definitely be a Fake God.
O’Kelly, you have been deceived by that Fake God using some power..."
The God of Nobles’s tone carried a hint of dissatisfaction, as anyone would feel seeing their followers promoting another sect.
Duke O’Kelly, who had been very excited up to this point, now felt as if a bucket of cold water had been poured over him from head to toe, chilling him to the core.
The power of the God of Nobles partially came from his believers, but the main part actually came from the nobility.
The higher the noble title, the more dignified the nobles who worship the God of Nobles and thus, the stronger the divine power he possessed.
Among the myriad Divine beings, the God of Nobles was one of the few whose followers were predominantly not ordinary devotees but a small portion of high-level Nobles.
In this situation, the more highly-ranked the noble, the greater their impact on the God of Nobles was, essentially.
This reasoning is mainly why among high-level Nobles, most did not treat the God of Nobles with absolute reverence, viewing the relationship more as a partnership.
Yes, a partnership. Nobles need Divine entities to justify their rulership as legitimate but to some extent, they also resist divine authority.
Holding imperial power in their hands, Divine authority could constrain them; thus, the nobles’ attitude towards the God of Nobles was always somewhat ambiguous.
And as a member of the Nolan Royal Family and the controller of the southern provinces, Duke O’Kelly’s status within the entire Nolan Empire was surpassed by only a few.
So his attitude towards the God of Nobles did not involve much worship.
However, Duke O’Kelly’s feelings towards Lide were different. He had personally witnessed in Risier City how Lide crushed three Transcendents single-handedly, and he had seen him freeze an entire city and kill over a million Divine Servants with a wave of his hand.
Duke O’Kelly’s respect and admiration for Lide were genuine and deep.
Upon hearing the God of Nobles speak dismissively of Lide, his first reaction was not belief or defense but a surge of anger inside.
It felt like someone you deeply admire and respect was being denigrated and ridiculed by an outsider.
On what grounds?
That was Duke O’Kelly’s first reaction, on what grounds do you accuse Lord Ilo of being a Fake God?
Just as he was about to retort, he looked at the cold eyes of the God of Nobles and forcibly suppressed the dissatisfaction bubbling within him.
After taking a deep breath, he slowly said,
"My Lord, I sense that your aura seems somewhat unstable... Do you need me to have the city guard promote the Noble Sect?"
The words, though bold and righteous, carried a hint of testing, as Duke O’Kelly dared to feel angry also because the God of Noble’s aura was unstable.
If the figure had appeared with a dominant Divine pressure, he would not have dared or been willing to harbor any resentment.
But after the God of Nobles appeared, Duke O’Keilly felt no dangerous aura, a stark contrast to the so-called Fake God Lord Ilo, described by his opponent. That’s why Duke O’Keilly experienced such a range of emotions.
In the end, power was indeed the only source of Glory.
Without power, even a former Divine might not be respected.
The God of Nobles seemed not to realize this yet, interpreting Duke O’Keilly’s lack of objection as an acknowledgment of his mistake.
"O’Keilly, you should immediately shut down those temples of the Fake God and widely spread my faith.
The Ancient corrupted power will soon pose a greater threat around Green City, and I need to recover my strength quickly!"
Duke O’Keilly furrowed his brows at these words, his discomfort intensifying—a feeling amplified by the high-handed tone of the God of Nobles.
And this command didn’t sit well with him, spreading the Noble Sect was fine, but shutting down Lord Ilo’s temples??
Are you joking?
The other was a Divine Arts user who had frozen an entire city. Even if you recover your strength, could you really defeat Lord Ilo?
Indeed, the image of Lide was too substantial and imposing in Duke O’Keilly’s mind.
The God of Nobles, whom he should have been closer to, now felt utterly foreign.
The correct approach for the God of Nobles would have been to establish his dignity upon meeting Duke O’Keilly and then issue commands.
But the God of Nobles overestimated his influence over Duke O’Keilly and underestimated Lide’s grandeur.
And given his current unstable state, establishing dignity would require more strength than he was willing to spend, so he skipped this step altogether.
This led to him issuing overreaching commands without having established his dignity, greatly irritating Duke O’Keilly.
However, as an old noble, Duke O’Keilly was not yet insolent enough to defy the God of Nobles, although his inner respect was nearly worn away, his face still bore a standard noble smile.
"Your Grace, I will follow your command...
You may recover within the city lord’s manor during this time, and I will immediately order the spread of the Noble Sect..."
Before he could finish, the God of Nobles interrupted him, "No, not just the Noble Sect, the Sect of the Knight God must also start preaching..."
"The Knight God? Has he also descended upon Green City?"
Duke O’Keilly was somewhat startled now, so there were three Divine beings in Green City?
He felt both thrilled and anxious—thrilled that the more potent Green City’s forces, the safer it would be, but anxious about how Lord Ilo, upon his return, would treat these two Divines.
He really didn’t want Lide to conflict with these two Divines; even setting aside who would win, whether Green City could even survive was a question...
"Yes, the Knight God has also arrived in Green City and is currently seeking a blasphemer who had desecrated him a few years ago. He has already tracked down the soul of this blasphemer and might show up anytime..."
Duke O’Keilly took a deep breath, sensing that Green City was becoming ever more chaotic with Divines personally stepping in; had the evil Divines also arrived?
"Your Grace, spreading your radiance is my unshirkable duty!"
After saying this, Duke O’Keilly inexplicably thought of Lide; in his heart, there was only one thought—if Lord Ilo were still here, perhaps there would be no need to fear those Ancient Evil Gods.
The duke always harbored a mysterious reverence and trust for Lide, as if Lord Ilo represented everything.
At this moment, the still in the abyss, Lide was unaware that Green City, crucial to him, now hosted Divines descended as saints.
And these two Divines, one way or another, had some ties and hostility towards him...
The changes in Green City were but a trivial reflection on the majestic main plane of Glory.
In the central area of the Ancient Forest, a few days ago, twelve figures cloaked in green capes entered, and the next day, the Elves announced the return of their twelve Divines...
In one of the most powerful human nations in the main plane—the Purple Maple Leaf Empire, the temple of the Sun Goddess within its capital city radiated blinding light as the great Sun Goddess quietly descended.
Furthermore, gods like the War God, the God of Justice, the Forge God, the Master of Dawn... among other powerful Divines, there were rumors of their descension.
The shadow of Ancient evil covering the world, the gods descending as saints, the gradually crumbling order of the kingdom, ambitious hunters of Divines, sinister believers of the Evil God lurking in the shadows, together with the Undead and the Abyss that had not stirred yet...
Numerous forces were now interwoven on the main plane, and the trajectory of the main plane of Glory began moving in an unpredictable direction.

chapters.title: Chapter 433 - 435: The Super Strong Characteristics Brought by 3 Million Believers (7600 words)
chapters.content:
Chapter 433: Chapter 435: The Super Strong Characteristics Brought by 3 Million Believers (7600 words)
"May the Glory of our God endure forever!"
"These damned Half-Beasts should all be hanged on the city walls!"
"Kill!"
"For our God!"
On the 270th level of the Abyss, in the western region of the Gravel Plane.
The roars, screams, and curses of over twenty people mixed together like the crashing waves of a level eighteen storm.
This was the realm of the Abyss Half-Beasts—a region reeking of nauseating sulfur in the thicket of the Abyss.
At this moment, the Naga, chanting the slogan for the God of Twilight and leading the Chaotic Army, including Corrupted Jackal Wolfmen, Evil Lizardmen, Enchanting Demons, and inferior demons, were encircling and slaughtering about seventy to eighty thousand grotesquely deformed Abyss Half-Beasts.
Chaos and slaughter are the eternal themes of the Abyss.
At this time, it was just a week since the Chaotic Army had defeated the Enchanting Demons.
After the lord of the Enchanting Demons had fled, Lide, through the terrifying Majesty of the Divine System Master, had directly subdued the entire Enchanting Demon Army, increasing the Chaotic Army’s numbers to over 180,000.
This was indeed the true way to unleash the Abyss, where on this land of evil, the victors would win everything, be it treasure or armies.
After incorporating the Enchanting Demons, Lide spent a few days organizing his gains and reorganizing the army.
In terms of loot, apart from some poisonous food suitable for Abyssal Life, there was pitifully little else that could catch Lide’s interest for more than a glance.
Had it not been possible to scout for mineral veins in the vast lands, he truly would have had little interest in occupying the Enchanting Demons’ territory.
However, the Enchanting Demon Army, numbering over 70,000—all demons above level 10 whose combat strength was even superior to surface dwellers of the same level—caught his eye.
Unfortunately, in the high-level map of the terrifying Abyss, this army was merely cannon fodder.
After reorganizing the army, Lide did not hesitate; he directly led his forces westward, boldly attacking the Abyss Half-Beasts.
Outsiders could hardly imagine what experiencing constant warfare was like, but the central theme of the Abyss was only slaughter and death.
"These damned Abyss Worms! We can’t hold them back, retreat to the city of the Half-Beasts!"
The Half-Beast Commander, watching the ferocious and invincible Chaotic Army, had his face turn pale and immediately issued the retreat command.
Wuu wuu~
After a burst of brief horn sounds, the already crumbling Abyss Half-Beasts began their total retreat, fleeing towards the rear.
With the advantage gained, the relentless Chaotic Army began furiously attacking the fleeing Half-Beasts.
Ultimately, it was the Half-Beast’s Commander who left behind a Ten Thousand People Army as cannon fodder to block the Chaotic Army’s slaughter.
The battlefield stretched for over ten kilometers; the smell of blood was detectable even tens of kilometers away, attracting numerous evil creatures lurking in the shadows, wanting to scavenge a shattered corpse.
Lide floated mid-air, calmly observing these events unfold. This time, he still did not take action; he needed to assess whether the reorganized Chaotic Army was effective.
The Abyss Half-Beasts were a notch below the Enchanting Demons in terms of individual strength, so the Chaotic Army made much quicker progress against these evil beings.
After the battle with the Enchanting Demons, Lide had already figured out the general pattern of warfare in the Abyss.
And the summary was—there was no pattern.
Yes, it was that simple.
These chaotic and disorderly beings, no matter how strategically positioned before the battle, once the combat began, they would plunge into chaos, completely disregarding commands.
All military formations were as futile as child’s play.
In the end, it would be evident that the outcome of the war relied solely on brute force; whichever side was stronger would emerge victorious.
Fortunately, the enemy behaved in the same way, using only very simple tactics such as flanking or attempting to come from behind, largely engaging in direct confrontation on the battlefield.
Influenced by the will of the Abyss, these chaotic beings could not be precisely commanded like the armies of the Main Plane.
But as the saying goes: each butcher has their own way to slaughter a pig.
Due to the chaotic nature of the Abyss, Lide devised a new tactical system for the Chaotic Army.
First, he reassigned the Naga Tribe, as one of the few orderly evil beings, they could follow commands and cooperate during wars, making them crucial.
Previously, Lide found it wasteful to have the Naga command other demons as they could not truly lead them; instead, the demons would drag the Naga into chaos with them.
So, Lide decided to split the Naga into two armies, each close to ten thousand in number, to form vanguard units.
Whenever faced with tough battles, he would dispatch the Naga.
As an Upper Race corresponding to Upper Demons within the Abyss, their strength was undoubtedly formidable.
Together with the Naga’s coordinated efforts, they completely overpowered the Half-Beasts, who were inferior in strength, in a manner that could be described as devastatingly efficient.
As for the remaining demon troops, Lide also ingeniously gathered the strongest among them to form another legion, which served as the second core placed in the second echelon of the attacking column.
This strategy provided him with three powerful legions.
Although only the Naga were controllable, the demons, despite their chaos, could unleash a power almost comparable to the Naga when grouped together.
The first and second wave of troops that charged into the fray served as cannon fodder, while the third wave would consist of the core demon legion, with the fourth and fifth waves being the Naga, creating a series of waves, each stronger than the last, eventually overwhelming the enemy forces completely.
The attack on the Half-Beast utilized this formation setup; despite the defending Half-Beast Army numbering just under a hundred thousand, collapsing in just one Sunshine Hour was enough to prove the strategy’s effectiveness.
Indeed, these fearless and death-defying demons would make the finest warriors if they were not excessively chaotic, each demon was strong, morale was perpetually high, and they were cruel, bloodthirsty, unafraid of threats, and fearless of death—any army would find them a headache to face.
Fortunately, the rules of Glory are balanced, granting demons strong individual power while simultaneously depriving them of obedience, confining their power to individual might alone.
"Attack!!"
"Kill these despicable Half-Beasts!"
"For Lord Ilo!"
The Chaotic Army below, seeing the Abyss Half-orcs starting to rout, let out excited roars.
Unlike the Enchanting Demons that sallied forth to meet the enemy in full force, the Abyss Half-orcs had only dispatched a third of their forces to engage in battle, with the majority still guarding their city—Half-Beast City.
Lide watched the Chaotic Army push inward, his gaze also drawn toward the massive structure in the distance.
Half-Beast City was built among low shrubs; at that moment, it seemed like a colossal Abyssal Giant Beast menacingly sprawling on the ground, ready to stand up and let out a thunderous roar at any moment.
The huge rocky city walls were uneven on the outside, and within them were embedded numerous black marks.
The entire city wall exuded a foul stench of blood; a closer look would reveal this was from wind-dried bloodstains. To stain such an expansive wall black with blood, how many lives would have to be taken? Perhaps this query could be answered by the piles of white bones stacked several blades high at the base of the wall.
The city walls of the Half-Beast City were purely made of piled stones, rough and uneven with no craftsmanship whatsoever, but when the height of the walls reached 40 blades, they still presented an imposing obstacle like natural rugged terrain.
After being defeated, the half-beasts had retreated into the city, and the Chaotic Army wanted to obliterate them they had to first breach this solid wall.
The nearly frenzied Chaotic Army seemed intent on physically storming the tower, reckless of the consequences.
Fortunately, this action was stopped by a lvl 19 Naga commander, Oli Kabar.
Attacking the walls without siege weapons was completely senseless.
The Abyss Race was proficient in combat but clueless about crafting weapons, except for the Abyss Dwarves—virtually no other race forged weapons.
This resulted in the ground troops appearing somewhat powerless in the face of the city walls.
"Regroup!"
"Heal!"
"Each legion, count your numbers..."
The voice of the Naga commander still echoed, clearly planning to regroup for another assault.
After annihilating tens of thousands of half-beasts who had come out of the city to meet them in battle, the Chaotic Army still had 17 ten thousand men legions left, while at least 200,000 Abyss half-orcs remained in Half-Beast City.
A direct assault could result in extremely heavy casualties.
Over a hundred thousand men under the Naga’s command began to slowly regain some order, lining up disorderly outside the city; from the sky, Lide felt an indescribable sensation.
With just a wave of his hand, those hundred thousand below would sacrifice everything to fight for him.
This feeling of commanding thousands of troops at the flick of his wrist was quite exhilarating.
Lide looked at the Chaotic Army below, which was slowly lining up, just about to make a move, when a very abrupt system notification sound startled him.
"Ding~ Your total number of believers has reached 3 million, activating the Believer System."
"Believer System: Once reaching sufficient levels of faith, you will receive the enhancement of Divine Power. Your believer levels are divided into Fanatical Believers, Devout Believers, Believers, and Casual Believers."
"Casual Believers: May believe in multiple divinities, faith not loyal, can gain a 1% increase in all attributes."
"Believers: Believe only in one deity, with stable faith, can gain a 5% increase in all attributes."
"Devout Believers: Your faith is solid, utterly devout, can gain a 10% increase in all attributes."
"Fanatical Believers: See you as the only one, will defend your glory with their souls and lives, can gain a 20% increase in all attributes."
Lide was slightly stunned; he hadn’t noticed that his total number of believers had reached 3 million?
Subconsciously, he opened his sect panel.
Indeed, at this moment, the total number of believers in both sects had reached 3 million; 820,000 from the Dawn Sect, and a staggering 2.18 million from the Twilight Sect combined just met the requirement.
This believer system activated at 3 million seemed a bit extraordinary... At first glance, the enhancements don’t seem much, but this is a full boost to the entire population?!
million believers, an all-encompassing enhancement... This was too insane.
A slight smile appeared on Lide’s face, just as he was about to look more carefully, the system’s notification sound rang again.
"Ding~ Your total number of believers has reached 3 million, initiating the Priest System, and launching the Sect Spell System."
"Ding~ Your Divine Priest—Niloh, has uploaded 24 sect spells, you can now bestow spells to your priests, which are divine rewards to priests, and can be revoked at any time."
"Priest System includes—Basic Priest, Intermediate Priest, Advanced Priest, Archbishop Priest, White-robed Archbishop, and Red-clothed Archbishop."
"Ding~ You have initiated the Priest System, would you like to upload your spells? Spells uploaded can then be bestowed to your priests."
Waiting for the system notification to quiet down, a thousand thoughts surged in Lide’s mind.
"The total number of believers reaching 3 million not only activated the Believer System but also the Priest System.
Isn’t this a bit exaggerated??"
The previous systems were alright, but fundamentally, it was supported by two Divine Arts.
One could assimilate souls to gather subordinates, and another could use the Power of Faith to enhance the power of subordinates, considered the most core Divine Arts.
But for the lower-level believers, the benefits were not high, at most giving some peace of mind.
Only now did he truly understand the value of a faith sect.
Ignoring that Casual Believers only added 1%, just becoming a Believer and gaining a 5% all-attributes boost was enough to allure anyone.
Not to mention Devout Believers with a 10% increase and Fanatical Believers with a 20%.
Such tangible benefits would definitely elevate his believers to a new level, making proselytizing in the future too convenient.
The initiation of the Priest System signified the formal establishment of sect power; from now on, the sect could completely cultivate its own specialized strength, without needing to assign external forces to guard the sect anymore.
"Ding~ Do you want to upload your spells? Five seconds until auto-cancelation if not selected..."
"Five..."
f r\ee.c(o)(m)
Spell upload?
Lide raised his brows, seeing it as part of the benefits—naturally, there was nothing to hesitate about.
"Confirm last time."
"Ding~ Upload successful."
After the system notification faded, over two thousand points emerged in Lide’s mind; after a brief sensing, he immediately realized.
These over two thousand Spirit Points all belonged to his priests, and if he responded to any of their calls and prayers, he could communicate with the priests through these spiritual connection points.
Priests, as an extension of Divine Power, have always been the most important part of any sect.
His previous Dawn Priest was completely a neutered version, only possessing simple self-healing abilities, unlike other sects’ priests who also had powerful casting abilities.
At this moment, his sect had taken a significant step forward, his position as a deity becoming more formal...
But there was an issue, individually bestowing spells to priests was too cumbersome; how long would it take with thousands of people?
After brief consideration, Lide immediately delegated this authority to his Divine Priest—Niloh.
After sensing the admiration and joy from Niloh, he finally withdrew his focus.
Indeed, training a few capable subordinates was essential...
After Lide heard the system notification, in the Underworld, those of the Dark Race who worshipped the God of Twilight suddenly revealed looks of surprise.
Because they felt a powerful force enveloping them, their strength was instantly augmented.
f r\ee.c(o)(m)
It was a gift from the great Lord of Twilight.
The feeling of being watched by a Divine instantly made these believers feel favored and astonished, and their level of devotion surged upward rapidly.
Many went from being ordinary believers to devoted believers, and the power they gained after becoming devoted believers was even more significant. This led them to believe they were appreciated by the Divine, and their faith increased even further.
In this virtuous cycle, Lide’s panel soon had a large number of devoted believers and fanatical believers. The higher the degree of faith, the more power of faith the believers provided.
This time, the key to activating Lide’s sect trait—the Cave Dwellers—upon realizing their increased strength and that they were being watched by Lide, knelt on the ground almost crazily and began praying with utmost devotion and fervency.
These humble lives had never been valued before, and now they had received a gift from the great Divine, what an honor it was.
The speed of increase in faith among the Cave Dwellers was simply astonishing.
The prayers from Naga City drifted out from the giant caverns and lingered in the sky for a long time.
Not only the Twilight Sect received an enhancement of strength, but the believers of the Dawn Sect experienced the same.
