Because the scale of the Underworld is limited, although it’s far from being fully developed now, with the passage of time, it will inevitably reach the end of its potential.
But the Abyss is different. With a countless number of Planes, the Abyss has infinite potential. As long as he has the ability, Dawn City can achieve even greater room for development.
And within the abyss, there was no need to worry about the rules of the Main Plane; one could develop as they wished.
Moreover, the most reassuring point was that Dawn City was in the Main Plane.
Should he encounter powerful opponents while conquering the abyss in the future, it would be quite difficult for them to break out and pose a significant threat to Dawn City.
Of course, that was the rule now. With the severity of the Ancient Erosion, the rules might change, but no matter what, opening up the abyss as a high-leveled map held immense significance for the future trajectory of Dawn City’s development.
To a large extent, it determined the future development path of Dawn City.
After some consideration, Lide directly sealed the Snake Clan God’s divine body, which he had been carrying with him, in the deepest part of the Land of Bone-Burying.
Unless someone had the power to overturn the entire plane, there was nothing safer than this.
Carrying this corpse around with Mage’s Hand for over two months had truly irritated him.
The Divine Stones that couldn’t be stored in the System Space were also left here.
Having managed his loot, Lide was about to leave the Land of Bone-Burying when a loud roar suddenly attracted his attention.
Moo~
Beside the twelve-layered White Bone Altar, which had been restored to its original state below, appeared a skeletal cow with a height of two blades and a length of 3.5 blades, with two curved horns.
It was that bizarre Cow Bone Undead.
What happened next made Lide’s eyes widen in shock, leaving him speechless.
The Cow Bone Undead seemed to sense his presence and began wagging its short tail frantically. But since Lide was floating mid-air, the undead could not approach.
Then, as if remembering something, the undead bent its limbs slightly, like a cheetah about to pounce on its prey. In an instant, its skeletal body compressed to the extreme, and with a spring-like burst, it launched into the air.
And under Lide’s gaze... the cow actually began to fly.
The cow was flying...
Moo~
It seemed to be the Cow Bone Undead’s first flight; it was unsteady and awkward, leaving one to wonder if it might fall out of the sky the next second.
The ghostly blue Soul Fire surged like waves, and even through its hollow gaze, one could feel the undead’s excitement from its mooing.
Moo~
Upon seeing this scene, a million divine beasts raced through Lide’s mind.
Am I blind... This damn cow can actually fly??
What kind of era is this?? Cows can fly now???
You’re really not letting those warriors who travel on foot live, are you??
This undead is truly reaching for the skies... pfft, it’s already in the sky.
The Cow Bone Undead flew more smoothly as time went on, and moments later, it flew excitedly to Lide’s side.
The cow, as if standing on solid ground, pushed with its hind feet to leap high, landing with its forelegs first, and fiercely lowered its head, rubbing its horned skull against Lide’s feet.
The short cow bone tail wagged like a foxtail grass, rubbing for a while before the body rolled on the ground, exposing its rib-filled belly with hooves pointing to the sky, twisting and turning.
Lide watched the silly cow, unsure whether to laugh or cry.
Eventually, he couldn’t stand it any longer and kicked the cow’s head with his foot, telling it to get up.
The Cow Bone Undead was clever and quickly got the message, springing to its feet and slightly opening its mouth. With Soul Fire shining through its hollow eyes, it eagerly awaited as if expecting him to throw it a couple of bones...
Throwing bones?
Lide’s mouth twitched harshly. It suddenly dawned on him.
This damn cow is always gnawing on bones, just like a dog...
He had previously wondered, and now it seemed clear, gnawing on bones was this stupid cow’s nature.
It was ludicrous – a good cow not behaving like one, instead learning from a dog... Luckily, no one relieved themselves in this place of bone-burying.
After a few glances at the Cow Bone Undead, Lide instinctively opened the cow’s attribute panel, his expression changing instantly upon seeing its level.
This fella... was really shooting for the sky.
Cow Bone Undead
Title: Corpse Eater (Advanced) (A title obtained from devouring a large number of skeletons, increasing the sharpness of teeth by 300%, eating speed by 300%, digestion speed by 300%, with a 5% chance of acquiring the skills of the devoured corpse)
Level: 19
Talent Skills: Devouring Growth (An undead-specific talent that allows one to devour Soul Fires and the Power of Death to strengthen their soul)
Skills: 123... etc
Introduction: This is a strange undead being with very special powers and unlimited potential.
Not only has this guy gone from Basic to Advanced as a Corpse Eater, but his level has also reached 19... That’s Level 19!
Moreover, the soul power in its body is so concentrated that it seems on the verge of breaking through to the Extraordinary Level.
Lide was full of amazement.
How long had the Cow Bone Undead been born?
He had only been in the Land of Bone-Burying for just over three years, and the Cow Bone Undead had been born for barely three years.
In just three short years, this guy had leveled up from Level 1 to 19, averaging six levels per year, a rate of leveling up that was staggering; it had taken him three years to progress from Level 10 to 19.
Lide couldn’t help but take a deep look at the Cow Bone Undead.
Although this guy acted a bit like a simpleton, its potential truly took him by surprise.
After some thought, he spoke with solemnity,
"Since you are the first creature I have created in the Land of Bone-Burying, and life was a gift from me, I shall also bestow upon you a new name."
Upon hearing this, the soul fire of the Cow Bone Undead surged wildly, its pale blue light cooling the surroundings for a moment.
With a sound of excitement and joy, it then flipped over and started rolling in the air.
Lide couldn’t help laughing and crying; he had just started to admire it... this stupid cow, really taking itself for a simpleton, huh??
After a brief moment of contemplation, he declared in a deep voice,
"I, the Divine Main God of the Dawn Pantheon — God of Dawn and Twilight, Overlord of the Land of Bone-Burying, City Lord of Dawn City, and Ancestor of the Bloodline, do hereby bestow upon you the new name — Thanatos Dusk.
You represent death, the end times, and despair."
As the words fell, the Cow Bone Undead rose to its feet, its Soul Fire soaring to the extreme.
Then, from its hollow throat came a cryptic and evil utterance,
"My name—Thanatos Dusk..."
Lide’s eyes widened in astonishment; this simpleton could speak?
But what shocked him even more was that the system prompt followed the Cow Bone Undead’s speech.
"Ding~ In your name as the Divine Main God of the Dawn Pantheon, you have appointed — Thanatos Dusk (Undead) as a Subordinate God. As the first life born in the Land of Bone-Burying, it possesses a special talent, and the will of the plane looks favorably upon it, qualifying it to become a Subordinate God. You have successfully appointed the Subordinate God.
Thanatos Dusk — Divine Positions of Death, the End Times, and Despair; you have spent 500,000 Power of Faith to successfully activate the Divine Position for them."
???!!
Looking at the system prompts, Lide’s head was filled with question marks and exclamation points, his expression extremely vivid.
This works too??
I...
Looking at the Cow Bone Undead in front of him, which, after the system prompt, seemed to exude a sense of holiness, Lide’s eyes flickered uncertainly.
You may not believe it if I tell you, but I just appointed a cow as my Subordinate God, and what’s crazier is, it worked!!
I! I have appointed a cow as my Subordinate God!!!
This should be a good thing, so why do I feel a bit like dying...
Once the Cow Bone Undead, now Thanatos Dusk, a Subordinate God of the Dawn Pantheon with the triple Divine Positions of Death, the End Times, and Despair... is looking at him with hollow but excited eyes.
"Master..."
Lide shuddered at the sound, feeling almost tearfully helpless.
In the future, while others ride ferocious, fierce giant dragons into battle, will he be riding a silly cow that’s good at gnawing on bones? Is there still a path for the good in this world?
What’s more, the three Divine Positions this guy now holds...
The End Times and Despair are controlled by the Lord of Nine-layered Hell—Asmodiers, a dark overlord of myth and legend, hailed just below the Death God and the Life Goddess as the most powerful Evil God.
Even the Sun Goddess, the War God, the God of Power and Justice, and other such supremely powerful deities, have to bow to him.
As for the Divine Position of Death, there’s no need to think about it; Death himself, one of the two eternal beings of Glory along with the Life Goddess, has total control over it, with at least 98% mastery. The rest of the deities who also have the Divine Position of Death share the pitifully small remainder.
This means that for this cow to make a breakthrough in its Divine Positions, it must face the two most powerful beings in Glory—the Lord of Hell and the Death God.
"I really should have kept my mouth shut. Why jabber on when it could have been just a leading cow?"
Lide grumbled about himself with annoyance as his gaze unintentionally swept over the cow bone undead’s body, instinctively opening its attribute panel.
Thanatos Dusk (Fake God)
Title: Corpse Eater, Subordinate God of Dawn (Granted by the Divine Main God of Dawn, received 20 Legend Level points, intimidation against external divinities increased by 200%)
Divine Calamity: 5 points
Divine Position: Death (0.01%), Apocalypse(0.01%), Despair(0.01%)
Level: 19
Skill: ... (omitted)
Description: This is a special undead conferred as a divine being, endowed with exceptionally unique talents, and possesses limitless potential.
At this point, Lide could no longer describe the "Holy shit..." in his heart...
These three Divine Positions had cost him 500,000 Power of Faith and indeed granted the cow 0.01%...
But what’s the use of this thing? If he kept improving it, those two mighty beings might notice it eventually, and then it wouldn’t matter which multi-dimensional plane he fled to.
Which is to say, that Power of Faith was essentially squandered because there’s nowhere to elevate the Divine Position, nor does he dare to.
This was a loss, a big loss.
"But where did those 5 points of divinity come from? Could it be the dried-up skull of the God of Plague left over from my last ascension to Transcendence?
It must be. After getting that shrunken skull, this creature ran underground and never came out."
Lide sighed, "Thanatos in Greek mythology on Earth is the name of the Death God. Naming this dumb cow was just for fun; I didn’t expect it to actually acquire the Divine Position of Death. Could this be fate?"
But he was too lazy to think too much about it and turned his gaze back to the cow bone undead.
"Stay here and wait for me, and I will take you to the Abyss when I return. There, you will have endless bones to gnaw on, and they all belong to powerful demons."
Isn’t it just like raising a dog, pah, a cow? Just feed it bones, that’s all. He’s not lacking anything, especially not bones.
"Master... thank... thank... you... for... your... divine... gift..."
This guy seemed to have just learned how to speak, with a stilted voice, and its language wasn’t the common tongue or the blasphemous language that Lide knew, but rather Undead Profanity, one of the three vilest languages.
After the cow bone undead finished speaking, the faint divine presence that had just been emanating abruptly retracted, then it stood up, lowered its head to rub against his pant leg, and its short tail wagged enthusiastically.
Lide helplessly facepalmed and with a turn, vanished directly within the Land of Bone-Burying.
The newly minted deity—the cow bone undead—stood frozen for quite a while after Lide left. Then it suddenly stood up on two legs, more human-like, scratched its skeletal head, and with the Soul Fire burning fiercely in its eyes, it seemed like the cow was contemplating some major philosophical truth of life...
After leaving the Land of Bone-Burying, Lide’s figure appeared directly in his office in Dawn City.
Warm, clean, neat, and luxuriously elegant, his expression eased a lot at the sight of the familiar surroundings.
Compared to the Abyss, the Main Plane truly was heaven.
At least he didn’t have to endure the perennial whispers of the Abyss, or the stench of sulfur that filled his nostrils at all times.
After scanning the room with a glance, Lide’s attention was immediately captured by the view outside the window.
It was already February 23rd; the coldest time of Frost Month had passed, but the biting cold wind was still harsh, and the ice and snow had only just begun to melt.
Through the glass, he could see the snowy peaks in the distance reflecting a pale light. Snow in Dawn City was cleared daily, so no snow accumulated.
Below the new City Hall was the new district of Moonlight Square, bustling with pedestrians walking back and forth.
The number of humans in Dawn City had exceeded 160,000, and including other races, the total population had surpassed 220,000. Even in the cold weather outside, the city seemed very bustling.
Furthermore, the Space Gate had connected with the Beastman of Dwarf Valley, and the population of the Lion Tribe had already broken through 100,000, which made Dawn City even more lively.
However, the mortal atmosphere below wasn’t what most attracted Lide’s attention. It was the cracks in the sky.
They looked like shattered glass, one after another, striking fear into anyone who saw them.
It was hard to imagine what kind of power could crack the sky.
Moreover, those cracks weren’t physical but a manifestation of rules.
Passersby couldn’t touch those cracks either, but under the influence of the rules, they were displayed without reservation.
"Such a terrifying aura..."
Lide’s deep eyes narrowed slightly, feeling the insignificance in front of that power of the rules.
That was the manifestation of the world’s origin, even divine power couldn’t compare.
The cracks in the sky were like a water bucket splitting apart after being filled to the brim, slowly leaking out an energy that made one’s scalp tingle.
Lide cautiously sensed it and discovered it was extremely similar to the aura found on the God of Plague—the power of the olden days.
The power of the olden days was unlike any current power of glory, not even the evil power of the abyss could compare to the ancient power.
It was an ancient, evil existence with immense corruption and assimilation abilities.
Once tainted with a certain amount of the ancient power, it would irreversibly corrupt one, eventually leading to a complete fall into a creature neither human nor ghost, even more horrifying than an abyss demon.
The inclination of these ancient monsters was—chaos.
Yes, chaos, with the goal of annihilating everything.
The sole desire of these ancient monsters was to shatter this world completely, to return everything to the pre-creation chaos.
This was more terrifying than the demons of the abyss; demons only sought to occupy the main plane and to kill resisting lives, never considering the destruction of the main plane.
In comparison, the attitude of the ancient monsters towards the destruction of everything was simply intolerable even to demons.
The crack in the sky caused the light of bygone days to retreat, the power of the olden days overshadowed everything, and ordinary people could look up to see that heart-thumping trace.
During this time, rumors of the apocalypse on the main plane intensified, and the gradually collapsing order caused chaos to reign.
Seeing this scene, Lide’s expression became extremely solemn, the good mood from leaving the abyss was completely gone.
Because the environment of the main plane might become even worse than the abyss!
After mastering 30% of the Twilight Divine Position, his perception of rules and environment had increased countless times from before.
He could sense that the entire main plane’s rules were gradually moving towards twilight under the influence of the ancient power.
This was an extremely terrifying trend; if the rules entered twilight, then the whole plane would face the danger of collapse.
After taking two deep breaths, his spiritual power spread outwards, he wanted to sense the ancient power further...
With his perception augmented by his divine position, he noticed many things that ordinary people couldn’t see.
The liveliness of magic power in the air was slowly decreasing due to the spread of the ancient power, making casting spells more difficult in the future...
An even more fatal discovery made him gasp— he sensed that the ancient power could corrode and pollute even the air, although very slowly, it was almost irreversible.
Noticing this change, Lide immediately looked out the window at the evergreen plants on Moonlight Square that stood tall in the frost.
But these plants, which should have been standing proudly, were languishing without any vitality, as if crushed by the snow and wind.
Lide took in a sharp breath; he could feel that it wasn’t due to the snow and wind, but the invasion of the ancient power that was reducing the vitality of those plants.
Because the ancient power was still thin, these plants hadn’t died instantly.
But this discovery was enough to send shivers down his spine.
From the small comes the big; if Dawn City was like this, then likely other regions were the same.
As the ruler of a vast power, he naturally wouldn’t see things so superficially.
The implication wasn’t as simple as a few plants withering but a critically fatal point—food.
Yes, the thing inconspicuous in regular times but enough to drive everyone mad when it counted.
Decreasing plant vitality meant inevitably declining food production.
If the ancient power continued to erode, then in a few years, this land could become barren due to the dense ancient power.
What then would all the life on the main plane use to survive??
The implications behind this were deeply horrifying, enough to make all rulers break into cold sweats.
It was like discovering that all of Earth’s plants might become extinct in the coming years, no longer able to bear crops—heralding destruction.
Thinking this, Lide couldn’t help but feel a sense of urgency.
The Bloodline didn’t need ordinary food, but the food source for humans was indeed necessary for humans.
Without food, ordinary humans naturally wouldn’t be able to survive, and the Bloodline would be forced to reduce their numbers due to the decline in the human population.
This absolutely could not be tolerated.
Thinking this, Lide once more looked up at the crack in the sky, this seemingly inconspicuous thing was the most lethal ah.
If the main plane was filled with the dense ancient energy, perhaps in a few decades or a century, the surviving life wouldn’t even be one in a million of the current population.
"No wonder even the Life Goddess has come out to warn all beings... the situation has indeed become severe to a certain extent; the entire main plane might face annihilation.
The coming of the ancient days, so that’s what it means... This is simply more terrifying than the destruction caused by 100 ancient evil gods; it’s about cutting off everyone’s roots."
Lide took a deep breath, glad that he had come back from the abyss in advance. Had he stayed there for a few years, Dawn City might have suffered unbearable losses.
Without further hesitation, he turned and walked out of the office to the area where Harrison was downstairs.
The guards on duty day and night at the door immediately bowed respectfully with their hands on their chests when they saw Lide, their eyes filled with zeal and adoration.
"Good day, Your Highness."
Preoccupied with his concerns, Lide paid them no heed and went straight to Harrison’s office.
Upon seeing Lide enter the room, Harrison’s face lit up with joy. Has Your Highness returned from the Abyss?!
But then, seeing the grave expression on Lide’s face, Harrison was taken aback. What serious matter could have occurred?
He rarely saw such a stern expression on Lide’s face. Even when facing the greatest of difficulties, Lide had always maintained his composure. What was this now?
"Good day, Your Highness, has something grave happened in the Abyss?"
Harrison stepped forward to greet him and asked with a solemn expression and tone.
But seeing Lide shake his head, another thought crossed Harrison’s mind.
"Is it related to the Ancient Emergence?"
Lide looked at his left-hand man, his deep eyes fraught with solemnity.
"Have you sensed the Ancient powers that keep pouring in non-stop through the rifts in the sky?"
"Your Highness, I have sensed them, and the Dawn Mage Tower has already started researching them.
However, the Ancient power we have captured is extremely thin. So far, we’ve only discovered that this power can enhance monsters eroded by the Ancient power, with not much other effect found yet."
Harrison’s words represented Dawn City’s current understanding of the Ancient power.
This force had immediately caught the attention of Dawn City’s upper echelons after the appearance of the sky rifts. To determine the impact of this power on them, research was immediately undertaken.
But no matter how they tested, they couldn’t determine the harm of Ancient power. For now, they’ve only discovered that if the power was concentrated enough, it could transform people into monsters and incidentally, boost the strength of Ancient monsters.
The research indicating that the Ancient power wasn’t very harmful made the higher-ups less vigilant.
Lide’s expression grew even more somber upon hearing this.
If it weren’t for controlling 30% of Twilight Divine Position, he wouldn’t have likely sensed the subtle effects of Ancient power.
Because it was too faint and the process extremely slow, maybe it wouldn’t show any results even after a couple of months.
But it was all the more terrifying because of this. Once outsiders discovered it, it would undoubtedly mean that the situation had solidified, and things would be irreversible.
Lide organized his thoughts and relayed everything he had sensed. He ended with a heavy tone.
"This matter must be included in Dawn City’s highest emergency plans. Let the Think Tank and the Intelligence Command Center project the consequences and propose countermeasures.
This concerns the life and death of Dawn City."
After listening to Lide’s account, Harrison’s expression turned ugly.
The Dawn Mage Tower’s initial research was on the effects of Ancient power on normal life, on spells, and so on.
No one thought that this power was initially targeting plants, eroding, and transforming the Main Plane’s environment.
Had it not been for Lide, they might also have noticed, but by then it could already be too late...
At this critical juncture, discovering it even one day earlier meant one more day to respond.
"Yes, Your Highness, I will immediately get the Think Tank working on solutions!"
Without delay, Harrison ordered the guards at the door to relay this critical news to the Think Tank.
View the correct content at )
After Harrison took care of all this, Lide’s face finally relaxed a bit.
"There’s no need to be overly worried. With the current rate, it will take at least three years for the Ancient power’s erosion to affect our survival.
These three years are our buffer period to store grain for the winter and to seek solutions."
While grave, the matter hadn’t reached a critical level of urgency.
The Think Tank he had personally ordered to be established had grown to over 200 people over the years, all elite talents, and would undoubtedly develop the most perfect solution.
After delegating this task, Lide’s mood lightened somewhat and he shifted the topic to the Abyss.
The issue with the Ancient power needed time to resolve, but the importance of the Abyss was just as critical. Now, it was time to focus on its development.
Then Lide’s next words left Harrison, with a grave expression, utterly stunned and profoundly shaken.
"Harrison, in the past few months I have conquered a dimension in the Abyss and enslaved a Demon Army exceeding 650,000 in number. The strength of these demons is all above level 10, and I have also subjugated 5 Extraordinary-level demons..."
As Lide’s words fell, Harrison felt as though his entire being had descended into dumbfounded shock.
Had he heard correctly?
An army of 650,000 enslaved, not to mention demons all above level 10?
And five Extraordinary as well?!!
At this moment, Harrison felt like he was getting a bit disheveled in the wind.
Forget about the 650,000-strong Demon Army, but what the hell is that about them all being Level 10 and above??
How many above Level 10 does Dawn City have now?
Add the Centaurs, the Beastmen, and the power of the Twilight Sect from the Underworld, do we even count over 5,000 people in total?
And now, suddenly, there are 650,000?!
Can they even play happily anymore...
And five Extraordinary!
That’s Extraordinary level we’re talking about!!
Harrison had a profound experience of how terrifying Extraordinary beings could be when the Bloodline nearly got wiped out by a single spell from an Extraordinary Mage from Green City.
Now, with Lide off to the Abyss for just a few months, in a land where he knew nobody and without any troops from Dawn City, he somehow managed to subdue five Extraordinary in the blink of an eye!
How could this not shock him?
And by such an account, wouldn’t that give Dawn City ten Extraordinaries?
At this thought, Harrison felt utterly suffocated.
Ten Extraordinaries, that Extraordinary Mage of Green City is nothing! We could bury that bastard just with numbers!!
Completely shaken, Harrison found himself speechless for a long time; after a while, he looked at Lide seriously.
"Your Highness, have you gone to the Abyss to inherit the legacy left by the Creator God?
Yes, that must be it; I knew it, you are a descendant of the Creator God..."
Upon hearing this, Lide didn’t know whether to cry or laugh. It was just conquering a Plane and enslaving a few hundred thousand demons, come on, get real.
I haven’t even told you that I casually killed two Evil Gods and stole a Divine Body on the way. Wouldn’t you go insane if you knew that?
He decided to let the guy catch his breath and changed the subject to something else.
"Harrison, I’ve discovered an Ancient Teleportation Array in the Abyss. After the Land of Bone-Burying devoured that array, we can now freely transport within the Abyss.
Now, the Plane of the Abyss I have conquered is still a desolate wasteland; I need enough manpower to start digging.
Also, that Demon Army has only undergone basic restructuring; I need a complete team of officers to go to the Abyss and thoroughly restructure that Demon Army into the blade and tusks of Dawn City within the Abyss."
Watching Lide’s eyes shimmering with cold light, Harrison’s heart skipped a beat, and his voice trembled slightly, "Your Highness, are you planning to?"
Lide’s gaze was calm.
"Invasion of the Abyss! Dawn City shall break new ground on that evil land.
I will turn the Abyss Plane into Dawn City’s pig farm, enslave demons, harvest the Power of Death, and plunder mineral resources..."
Hearing these bland yet world-conqueringly domineering words, Harrison’s blood surged.
At that moment, the Chairman of the City Hall wished he could immediately grab a sword and follow Lide into that nefarious teleported place.
After taking several deep breaths to suppress the excitement in his heart, he was just about to speak when something else seemed to dawn on him, and he hesitantly said.
"Your Highness, there is also something that might interest you about restructuring that Demon Army. Send the officers of the King’s Blade for that, but..."
"Speak."
"Do you remember the mermaid that was brought back from the Fishman Tribe?"
Hearing this, Lide’s gaze sharpened.
That mixed-blood mermaid hiding a secret that could alter the structure of Glory?
He had planned to see this mermaid when he returned to Dawn City a few months ago after his time in Green City, but his descent into the Abyss had left him no time to think about these things.
Now, hearing about her again piqued his curiosity.
"Have you discovered the mermaid’s secret?"
What was the secret that could change the structure of the Main Plane of Glory? He had always been very curious.
With a wry smile, Harrison shook his head, "No, Your Highness, we have not discovered it.
However, that mermaid underwent significant changes after the Ancient descended, seemingly awakening some sort of Bloodline...
Half a month ago, she even sought you out on her own initiative, wanting to meet with you. I asked her why, but she has remained silent, just saying that she’s uncovered that secret."
Lide’s eyes suddenly opened wide.
Uncovered that secret??

chapters.title: Chapter 437 - 439: The Shocking Secret Hidden by the Mixed-Blood Mermaid (10,000-Word Mega - )
chapters.content:
Chapter 437: Chapter 439: The Shocking Secret Hidden by the Mixed-Blood Mermaid (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)
Hearing Harrison’s words, a hint of delight showed on Lide’s face.
He had been concerned about the secret of the half-blood mermaid for not just a day or two, was it finally time for the truth to emerge?
He made a decisive call,
"Bring that mermaid here, I want to question her personally."
The introduction of the system was still before his eyes... the secret that could change the world’s structure, he now held great expectations for this mermaid.
The ancient days had arrived; the catastrophe was already upon them, now the secrets that could change the entire structure of Glory must be related to the ancient days.
Lide had just become aware of deeper secrets associated with the ancient days’ arrival, and acquiring more information about it now would be enormously helpful for Dawn City in facing future risks.
"Yes, Your Highness," Harrison dared not delay and immediately sent someone to carry out the order.
As the guard left, Lide didn’t waste this time of waiting and continued to inquire.
"How has the outside world been since the arrival of the ancient days?"
"It’s not good," Harrison replied with a somber look.
"Monsters corrupted by the power of the ancient days have begun appearing in large numbers. Boosted by the aura of the ancient days, these monsters are incredibly strong, and warriors of the same level find it very difficult to defeat them."
"Furthermore, the appearance of ancient monsters has significantly reduced the livable areas for all races, and the amount of magic scroll materials we’ve been able to purchase has plummeted."
"As for the southern provinces... Green City, which now hosts over three million people, is likely struggling to survive, with just the food issue alone being enough to overwhelm them."
Harrison paused, looking at Lide, signaling him to continue.
"Besides the human world, the territories of other races aren’t faring much better.
Just a month ago, the servants of the God of Plague, the Fierce Half-Ratman, launched an attack nearly ten million strong on the Dwarf Hills. Risier City is not far from the Dwarf Hills and has no natural defenses to rely on.
Under the onslaught of the Fierce Half-Ratman, the centaurs have been progressively defeated, and at this moment, at least half of their territory has been occupied by the Fierce Half-Ratman...
And those filthy rats are still probing around for news about Dawn City."
Lide frowned; he was not surprised that the Rotten Land was attacked by the God of Plague, but he didn’t expect the God of Plague’s vengeance to be so fierce and swift.
"What about the Iron Hoof Tribe?" Others he didn’t care about, but those more than a hundred thousand centaur warriors were a powerful army, and losing them would be a significant loss.
"The Iron Hoof Tribe was relocated to the Dwarf Valley after the onset of the war, and they are now working together with the Lion Tribe to build a city, not suffering much damage.
However, it’s worth mentioning that the one supported by Dawn City, who possesses the Gale Bloodline and has established the Gale Empire, said to be the Child of Destiny, the centaur Guido Blackwind, has, after the arrival of the ancient days, astonishingly won the loyalty of over a million centaurs.
The Gale Empire he initially established has now taken shape and they have become a main force in resisting the ancient monsters.
Currently, it’s this army that is resisting the corrosive attack of the Fierce Half-Ratman in the Dwarf Hills, while the original ruler of the Dwarf Hills—the Transcendent of Gale City—still shows no movement, and the centaurs around Gale City have even retracted their forces, as if they are planning to defend the city."
Lide couldn’t help but laugh silently upon hearing this. Initially, taking in that fellow with the bloodline hailed as a Divine Gift by the centaurs was just a whim, intending to stir things up.
Unexpectedly, due to a fluke, the other party really gained prominence.
Leading over a million centaurs, this was not a small number, and the Main Plane was not the Abyss, this power could already be considered terrifying.
As a strong battle race, the centaurs possessed formidable strength, and once they charged, they would be the nightmare of all enemies.
"Not bad, since he has potential, continue to support him.
I’ll send a Transcendent over to them later to consolidate the army; I need Guido to completely control the Dwarf Hills’ centaurs."
Dawn City had previously assessed the number of centaurs in the Dwarf Hills, determining there were at least six million.
Although he was unsure of the casualties after more than a month of war, there should still be three to four million left.
With such a large number, if they could all convert to the Dawn Sect, wouldn’t that be delightful?
Even if the centaurs’ faith is steadfast, that doesn’t matter, the combat strength of these millions should not be underestimated.
As long as Dawn City could arm them, the Centaur Heavy Armor Warriors and Centaur Archers would definitely become a feared presence.
"Yes, Your Highness, those centaurs receiving your attention is a great honor..."
Harrison spoke unreservedly; the Bloodline was inherently proud, especially now that Dawn City’s Transcendents had reached an astonishing number of ten.
As the speaker for City Hall, his authority was monumental, and he naturally had the right to disregard the Centaur.
Lide nodded, not elaborating much on the topic. He decided on the broad directions, and naturally, the Think Tank and the Intelligence Command Center would fill in the details.
"How has the preaching progressed inside Green City, and what’s the current general situation of the city?"
On the attribute panel of the Dawn Sect, the number of believers had already surpassed 800,000, of which more than 500,000 were contributed by Green City. This made him curious about what exactly had transpired in Green City during this period.
However, Harrison’s next words made his expression stiffen.
"Your Majesty, it seems that a Divine has descended into the Main Plane within Green City..."
Harrison spoke about this topic with extreme caution.
"The Shadow of Dawn plan you established has been in implementation for several years and under Stanley’s control, it has made significant progress.
In the upper echelons of Green City’s nobility, at least 20 high-level nobles have become members of the Holy Light Bloodline.
From the messages transmitted by these spies, the Intelligence Command Center, combining multiple quantitative analyses, has concluded that a Divine, transformed into a Saint, has already appeared."
Whether it was the message Lide received during the Crimson Moon — that Divines would transform into Saints,
Or the warning from the Life Goddess before her slumber about all life across the Multi-dimensional Plane — that the gods had fallen to the mortal realm.
Both pointed unequivocally to one thing — the high and mighty gods, no longer in their former glory, would lose everything and be cast down into the mud.
Although Lide had been mentally prepared, discovering traces of the Divine transformed into a Saint so soon still surprised him.
"Can we confirm which Divine it is in Green City?"
Harrison nodded, "We can roughly infer it’s the God of Nobles."
"The God of Nobles?"
Lide looked thoughtful. The God of Nobles was a deity with weak Divine Power, slightly stronger than the lowest level of Weak Divine Power, but only slightly. Generally, only nobles and commoners aspiring to nobility worshipped this deity.
What he wanted to know most was how much power this descended Divine still possessed.
Although the gods lost most of their power due to the shattering of the Destiny Tablet, to be transformed into a Saint was very mysterious. No one knew exactly what the gold content of this Saint was — was it Transcendent? Legendary? Or Demigod?
Each level naturally required a different approach.
"Can his strength be ascertained?"
"Your Majesty, you overestimate us,"
Harrison showed a bitter smile.
The advent of the Divine in the world was inferred after verifying information from multiple sources.
Those nobles who had become Bloodline members dared not meet the God of Nobles, for who knew if they might be seen through at first glance, after all, that was a Divine.
And even if they did meet, it might not be possible to sense the divine aura due to the vast difference between them.
Lide wasn’t too surprised by this response and had merely asked casually. After all, even he, a fake god, could hide his power, so a genuine Divine would naturally not be easily outclassed.
After a moment of contemplation, he asked the most crucial question.
"What is his attitude towards the Dawn Sect?"
The attitude of the God of Nobles towards the Dawn Sect would determine whether the two would become enemies.
If the other party had a friendly attitude, he wouldn’t want to clash with them at this crucial moment; cultivating and developing was the most important task.
"Your Majesty, it seems that he holds considerable hostility towards us."
But Harrison’s words made Lide’s idea of peacefully coexisting with the other party immediately fall through.
"No matter among the high-level nobles or the lowest commoners, the preaching of the Dawn Sect has been obstructed since the appearance of the God of Nobles. The City Guard has also been subtly restricting our development.
It must be that Divine influencing the City Guard, as your reputation in Green City surely isn’t something others would dare to challenge openly."
Lide’s eyes narrowed. The struggle between Divines was a struggle of faith, and the quantity of believers was finite — one more for you meant one less for me, and everyone wanted to take the biggest slice of the cake.
What irritated him was that, with a population of over three million in Green City, it was clear that the two sides weren’t ready to engage in a loving slaughter of each other yet.
You have your share, why try to snatch from my plate?
The glint of cold light flashed in his eyes, and a chilling intent to kill crept onto his face.
Dare to provoke, no matter if you are the God of Nobles or the God of Foolishness, first let’s see if your teeth are sharp enough.
"Have the intelligence command center fully investigate the movements of the God of Nobles and carefully search to see if other Divines have also descended upon Dawn City.
I need to know more detailed information."
Although Lide was somewhat displeased, he still maintained sufficient composure.
Since one Divine had already appeared, it was not impossible for there to be two, three, or even more.
Divines, though they are the ultimate existence at the pinnacle of Glory, have indescribably strong combat power.
But over the lengthy years, the accumulated number of Divines was actually not small.
Human Divine System, Dwarf God System, Elf God System, Beastman God System, Ocean God System, and so on, even including specific race gods like the Centaur God and the Half-Body God.
Nearly all significant races have their own Divine systems, with the number of Divines in these systems ranging from a few to dozens.
Thus, when all were added up, the number of Divines was actually substantial, it just seemed rare because Glory was vast, and the countless planes of Glory, when averaged out, made it appear exceedingly scarce.
"Your Majesty, Stanley is already working on this, and the Dark Contract is also fully cooperating with the Shadow of Dawn on this plan."
Lide nodded, still relatively confident in Stanley, who had once wanted to colonize and invade Earth; in terms of intelligence, this former follower of the Evil God could certainly rank highly in Dawn City.
But this news still plunged him into deep thought.
"It seems that after resolving the immediate matters, I need to make a trip back to Green City...
No, to be safe, first to break through to Legendary and then go back, lest I get ambushed by some ancient monster that has lived for millions of years."
Lide made his decision immediately; he could not abandon the city of Green City no matter who descended there.
Not to mention the Crimson Mage Tower and the Dark Contract, the several million population of Green City alone was enough to tempt him.
Although having everyone believe in the Dawn Sect was unrealistic, if even half did, the Dawn Sect would benefit significantly, and the Power of Faith would surge as the Dark Faith Power had.
The Power of Faith, as his level of power improved, had become increasingly important; it was a crucial element he must vie for as he reached his peak.
"This time, I will have to clash head-on with a real Divine, blades drawn, only killing will prove whose blade is sharper."
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly; since that God of Nobles was so untenable, he would have to teach him a lesson.
Just then, a knock at the door suddenly interrupted their conversation.
"Your Majesty, Lady Kaslina has been brought here..."
Accompanied by the guard’s report, a delicate and graceful figure stepped into the room.
Lide slightly turned his head, his eyes reflecting the figure of a hybrid mermaid.
The most striking feature was her blue hair floating behind her head, drifting slowly like it was underwater, filled with a sense of lightness.
Her refined face bore eyes the color of the ocean, deep and mysterious, reflecting thousands of enigmas, yet their depths were undisturbed, calm, and indifferent.
Dressed in a white robe, her bare feet as white as scallions without any footwear, but combined with an air of serene and tranquil temperament, she seemed as sacred as a priest devoutly worshipping in a church.
That incredibly unique aura made her unforgettable to all who saw her.
This girl, breathtaking enough to overturn states, now didn’t seem of this world but rather like an angel born of Holy Light or a holy priest praying devoutly under a Divine.
Casilina Abets Storm
This was the mermaid’s full name; she transformed into a human after Dawn, and into a Fishman upon the coming of night.
Even Lide, with his fortitude, was momentarily stunned, but his gaze quickly regained calmness, looking at the mysterious mermaid before him, he spoke softly.
"Kaslina, I heard you wanted to see me?"
The girl’s ocean-blue eyes, undisturbed and coolly glanced at him, her tone so indifferent that no emotion could be discerned.
"Kachar City Lord, the secret you have always wanted to find in me, I now know it."
Lide’s expression sharpened, excitement flickering through his heart, was the mystery finally about to be unveiled?
He waved his hand, dismissing the guards still in the room, until only he, Harrison, and the mermaid were left. Then he pursued the question.
"I’m quite curious how you discovered this secret?"
He said, his interest evident as he looked at the other party.
Over the past few years, the Blood-colored Blade, the strongest assassin, had tirelessly surveilled the other party day and night, with a special analysis team dedicated to scrutinizing everything about Casilina, yet all to no avail.
It was unclear whether the other party had hidden it too well, or if this mermaid had only recently become aware of this secret.
However, now that Casilina had taken the initiative to come to him, he felt as if all his previous efforts had been in vain.
"Bloodline awakening; after the awakening of the bloodline within me, I unsealed the memories that had been sealed deep within my soul."
Casilina’s sea-blue eyes calmly regarded Lide, her tone so neutral it was as if she was an observer, recounting a story about someone else.
"Sealed memories?" Lide’s expression turned grim.
Sealing memories was not a simple act; even with his current abilities he could not achieve it, and even legendary figures might fail, as it involved the sensitive nature of the soul, where a small mishap could mean encountering the Death God.
"Yes, it is a long memory..."
For the first time, a flicker of disturbance crossed Casilina’s eyes, as if she was recalling a distant memory. Then the mermaid’s next words made Lide’s eyes widen in shock.
"Before the Destiny Tablet was stolen, I was guarding it..."
Lide: ?!?!?!
A curse almost escaped his throat.
Was this not a joke?
That was his first thought.
The Destiny Tablet was such an entity that its loss had even caused the celestial divinities to lose their powers and had even caused the eternal Life Goddess to fall into a slumber.
Now, in this insignificant place, this mermaid, who he had accidentally traded back, was claiming she had been in charge of guarding such an origin of glory as the Destiny Tablet...
It was as shocking as if a Stone Age primitive suddenly produced a Star Annihilation Cannon and blew up the sun.
Did it have to be this frightening?
At this moment, Lide was experiencing a tremendous psychological shock.
He subconsciously opened the attribute panel, wanting to check Casilina’s attributes, but now the system could no longer detect any information about her; a series of question marks appeared.
Casilina Abets Storm
???
???
???
Seeing Lide speechless for a long while, Casilina’s expression also shifted slightly, and her tone became a bit somber.
"After the Destiny Tablet was stolen, I knew that the coming of the Ancient Evil was unstoppable, so I sealed the memories and dissipated all my powers, descending preemptively to the Main Plane."
Lide took a deep breath, his gaze fixed on the startling mermaid.
"Lady Casilina, who were you before? And how was the Destiny Tablet lost?"
Anyone who could guard the Destiny Tablet could not be ordinary.
In his view, she had to be at least a divinity with Powerful Divine Power, on the same level as the Sun Goddess, the War God, or the God of Power and Justice.
"Who am I?..." Casilina’s profound gaze stirred faintly, exhibiting rare confusion.
"I do not know my identity. It seems that after the Destiny Tablet was lost, for safety, I erased that part of my memory. Even after unsealing it, I have not recalled that memory."
She had erased her own memory?
Lide’s expression grew even more solemn; what could have happened to compel a formidable entity guarding the Destiny Tablet to firmly seal her own memory, and not only that, but to erase that portion of memory completely before daring to descend to the Main Plane...
"As for the loss of the Destiny Tablet... it was due to a theft by an Ancient Evil God."
"An Evil God’s theft?" Lide frowned slightly. "What kind of Evil God could steal such an important artifact from your hands?"
Kaslina’s face stiffened slightly, and after a moment of hesitation, she revealed a shocking secret.
"The Evil God who stole the Destiny Tablet was an Ancient Dominator, the endpoint of all ancient powers—Asathos.
His might was enough to dim the skies, dull the stars, and make the gods tremble..."
"Asathos..." Lide murmured the unfamiliar name softly.
"Yes, Asathos... Before the Creator God opened the Glory Multi-dimensional Plane, Asathos ruled the Land of Chaos, wielding boundless power.
When the Creator God was creating the Glory Multi-dimensional Plane, he was noticed by that Ancient Dominator, Asathos, who could not tolerate the existence of any world. Asathos attacked the Creator God.
In that unprecedented battle, the Creator God emerged victorious, and Asathos was slain. Recognizing the terrifying nature of the ancients, the Creator God sealed all the Ancient Evil Gods and all their powers..."
Kaslina’s tone trembled slightly as she spoke about that terrifying Ancient Dominator.
"Now, that slain Ancient Dominator has resurrected, seeking to restore the ancient chaos. After stealing the Destiny Tablet, he crushed it using the Time Gear from the heart of the multi-dimensional planes.
The Destiny Tablet was a divine artifact used by the Creator God to hold the Power of Destiny of the Glory Multi-dimensional Plane. With the tablet shattered, the only outcome is the scattering of the Power of Destiny, the extinction of all things, and the world marching toward its end..."
Upon hearing this ancient secret, Lide took a deep breath.
This myth suspiciously resembled the one he had fabricated to deceive the Bloodline...
"Lady Kaslina, do you know how to deal with these Ancient Evil Gods?"
No matter how terrifying those ancient secrets were, they were things of the past. The critical issue now was to address the present crisis.
"The Destiny Tablet," Kaslina’s hair fluttered slightly behind her, her sea-blue eyes showing determination.
"Find the fragments of the Destiny Tablet, reassemble the Power of Destiny, only then can we repair the rifts in the sky, prevent ancient forces from corrupting all, and restore peace to the world."
Lide felt a slight unease hearing this. The familiar turn of the story made him wonder if she was about to say he was the chosen one... and task him with finding the Destiny Tablet?
Thinking this made Lide’s heart ache, but immediately he spoke with a gallant tone.
"Respected Lady Kaslina, how may I be of help? Dawn City will spare no effort within my capabilities to assist you."
Well-spoken, but what was within his capabilities? After all, he was the one who decided those limits... He also wanted to keep the Glory Main Plane stable since it was in his interest.
But the problem was, Dawn City, with its limited resources, would struggle in face of an Ancient Dominator who had contended with the Creator God, not to mention challenging a Legendary.
Kaslina gave Lide a meaningful look, her eyes seemingly piercing into his soul, yet she did not expose his small schemes, her tone regaining its usual cool.
"Kachar City Lord, you would have sought the fragments of the Destiny Tablet without me mentioning it."
"Because each fragment of the Destiny Tablet contains supreme Origin Energy. Even Divinities endowed with Powerful Divine Power could gain immense enhancement by acquiring it.
It is one of the world’s rare treasures...
Moreover, acquiring a fragment of the Destiny Tablet would allow one, within a certain scope, to sweep away ancient powers, restoring all rules to normal, enabling the cultivation of crops, and raising of livestock...
As time passes, the ancient power will permeate the multi-dimensional planes, and this power is unstoppable. Representing destruction and chaos, no one can escape the corruption of ancient power.
In the end, whoever holds a fragment of the Destiny Tablet will have the power to survive.
If you do not seek it, then destruction draws near."
Lide gasped upon hearing this.
The coming of the ancient times was indeed as he had sensed, with the intent to devastate Glory completely.
But upon pondering Kaslina’s words slightly, he realized, this mysterious mermaid’s biggest secret wasn’t that she was a terrifying being guarding the Destiny Tablet, but rather—the fragment of the Destiny Tablet itself.
That was the greatest secret she bore.
Whoever obtained a fragment of the Destiny Tablet could wield power even the Divinities with Powerful Divine Power envied, along with a key point—the fragments could resist the invasion of ancient power and restore all rules.
The significance of this was extraordinary.
No wonder the system had said her hidden secret could change the continent’s dynamics.
At this moment, Lide could still faintly foresee the future scenario of the entire Glory warring over a piece of the Destiny Tablet.
The fragments of the Destiny Tablet represented the key to survival; without this key, annihilation was certain.
Although one was not forced to seek the fragments of the Destiny Tablet and become a cliché hero to save the world, this news was even more troubling.
After taking several deep breaths, Lide managed to suppress the tumult within his heart.
"Lady Kaslina, you must have a way to find the fragments of the Destiny Tablet, otherwise you wouldn’t have sealed your memory and descended to the Main Plane."
Kaslina looked directly into Lide’s eyes, her sea-blue irises deepening, and her unique aura made this mermaid appear sanctified and luminous.
"That’s right, I even know the location of a fragment of the Destiny Tablet right now."
Upon hearing this, Lide’s face lit up with joy, but almost instantly, great caution arose in his heart.
He never believed in the idea of pies falling from the sky and spoke with some hesitation.
"Lady Kaslina, could you please tell me where that fragment of the Destiny Tablet is? Dawn City needs it."
Although Kaslina did not emanate any aura like ordinary people, the feeling in Lide’s heart was as if he stood before an abyssal giant beast with its massive jaws open, extremely dangerous.
Obviously, this mermaid had regained some of her powers while recovering her memories.
Although possibly far from her peak, guarding the Destiny Tablet meant even regaining one percent was enough to make legends tremble.
Thus, Lide completely dismissed any idea of capturing her and converting her with the Power of Faith, as the tables could easily turn.
Upon hearing him, Kaslina’s usually unchanged expression moved subtly, as she stared deeply at Lide.
"Kachar City Lord, as a resident of Dawn City, I believe I am entitled to your protection, perhaps you could ask those who intentionally surround me to leave."
Lide’s mouth twitched, thinking to himself that if he had known her background was so terrifying, he would have never surveilled her day and night.
"Lady Kaslina, please forgive the caution of my subordinates; they will naturally depart soon."
Only then did Kaslina nod in satisfaction.
"The location of that fragment of the Destiny Tablet is in a place you have been before—the Lost Sea."
"The Lost Sea?"
Lide raised an eyebrow; he actually did not enjoy adventures on the sea, preferring the safety of land.
"That’s right, the Blue Star Tribe initially traded me for that octopus containing a part of the Golden Bloodline, aiming to sacrifice it to the demigod-level sea beast of the Lost Sea."
Kaslina mentioned her being sold with calmness, as if it had nothing to do with her.
"Are you saying that the sea beast obtained a fragment of the Destiny Tablet?"
Lide’s mood worsened; the Fishman Tribe had referred to this sacrifice as the Sea God Festival, a name that spoke volumes about the beast’s power.
Now, facing this demigod, the pressure was extraordinarily great.
"Any news of other fragments?"
"After the Destiny Tablet shattered, its Power of Destiny did not dissipate immediately.
Although my bloodline is unique and can sense the aura of the Destiny Tablet, I can only wait until the Power of Destiny fades... Currently, only this piece has been discovered."
Lide nodded thoughtfully, understanding it was better to have some news than none. It’s just a demigod, right? After he got stronger and gathered an army, he would overthrow it.
Slaying a god, he had experience with that.
After a slight pause and with a serious tone, he said,
"Lady Kaslina, although we have had our misunderstandings, I believe that in facing the Ancient Evil God, we stand on the same side.
The fate of Dawn City is now linked with all life in the Main Plane.
As the Lord of Dawn City, I officially invite you to join Dawn City and to establish a tribe centered on you, specifically to investigate the news of the Destiny Tablet fragments.
All for the sake of Dawn!"
Lide’s straightforward words openly invited this foreboding mermaid to join Dawn City.
At this juncture, he needed this mysterious being.
And a critical point—since she shared so much with him, it surely meant that this mermaid held enough fondness for Dawn City; if she had no such feelings, she could have simply left without wasting words.
This tolerant and charming city, is undoubtedly the only paradise in the main plane of Glory, where the assimilation of other races is commonly seen. No matter how powerful it once was, it was only in the past.
After years of experience, Lide had reached another height in his observation of human hearts, so he currently had some confidence.
Upon hearing this, Casilina fell into deep thought, and after a long time, she looked at Lide with unprecedented determination in her gaze and revealed a slight smile, shallow yet stunning enough to amaze.
"For the sake of Dawn City."
Lide, looking at that smile, inexplicably felt it was sacred and inviolable. The mermaid’s temperament was too extraordinary.
His heart relaxed slightly upon hearing this; the slogan "For the sake of Dawn" explained everything.
He was also somewhat satisfied. The slogan, initially designed to unite people’s hearts, had become recognized by everyone with the development of Dawn City.
"For the sake of Dawn" seemed to be merely a slogan, but it also served as a form of identity recognition.
Shouting this phrase within Dawn City meant acknowledging one’s identity as a citizen of Dawn, especially for outsiders.
All full of details, Lide’s smile gradually brightened.
"Lady Casilina, I will have the City Hall establish a department specifically for exploring the Destiny Tablet.
Also, do you have any other news..."
He didn’t finish his sentence, but the implication was clear in his eyes.
Now, Casilina was like a treasure trove. Her joining Dawn City meant a powerful entity had become his subordinate; even if she couldn’t find the fragments of the Destiny Tablet, it was still a huge gain for him.
Casilina shook her head, "Most of my memories have been erased; I don’t have much valuable information.
Moreover, the fragments of the Destiny Tablet are not ordinary and don’t need a separate force for exploration."
Despite Casilina’s words, Lide naturally wouldn’t do so, and had Harrison make good records.
After issuing the orders, another request from Casilina left Lide somewhat dumbfounded.
"I’m very interested in the Magic Industry Research Institute, especially in the recently developed automatic harvesters and seeders... Lord of Kachar, could I perhaps participate in some alchemy research there?"
The image of a guardian of the Destiny Tablet researching agricultural machinery was quite incongruous.
But as it was rare for Casilina to make requests, he naturally had nothing to refuse.
"Of course, it would be an honor for the Magic Industry Research Institute."
Lide then asked Casilina several questions, but most of them only made him feel helpless.
Her memory really was lost too extensively. She knew nothing about where divine artifacts were kept, how to use divine arts, or how to advance to divine positions.
It seemed her sole purpose of descending to the main plane was to retrieve the Destiny Tablet, and all other memories had vanished, which did match her identity as a guardian of the Destiny Tablet.
After several attempts, Lide confirmed Casilina’s words were true and she wasn’t using memory loss as a lie to deceive him.
However, her demeanor seemed too haughty for lies...
But the only thing that upset him today was that after Casilina had pledged her allegiance to him, he still couldn’t see her attribute panel...
Once the impressive mermaid left, Lide then turned his gaze to the silent Harrison beside him.
"Harrison, what do you think of this?"
Harrison showed a bitter smile.
"Your Highness, the ancient arrivals were chaotic enough, now the news about the Destiny Tablet, if leaked, might cause even greater uproar... We need to be well-prepared."
The existing order of Glory was already collapsing, and a new order couldn’t be established in a short term.
The current main plane of Glory was at its most chaotic, and this chaos would only intensify for a lengthy period.
"Within Green City, a divine turned saint, an ancient dominator killed and revived by the Creator God, a mermaid guarding the Destiny Tablet in Dawn City, a demigod-level sea beast possessing a fragment of the Destiny Tablet...
Indeed, it’s a hectic autumn."
Lide shook his head.
"However, no matter how the future changes, enhancing our own strength remains the most critical point.
Now, we still need to focus on Dawn City itself. This chaos will persist for a long time and won’t calm down anytime soon; paying too much attention is pointless."
After pondering for a moment, Lide issued a direct order.

"Harrison, regarding the Destiny Tablet fragment... allocate a part of the think tank to take charge of this matter exclusively and ensure that no information is leaked.
The importance of this matter should be placed at the highest level."
"Remove all the Blood-colored Blade assassins monitoring Kaslina, and designate a separate area for her residence."
"Additionally, have the Intelligence Command Center gather all information regarding the Sea God Festival in the Lost Sea and the sea beast, utilizing the network of the Fishman Tribe for assistance."
After issuing several commands, Harrison immediately responded.
"Yes, Your Majesty."
As the speaker of the City Hall, this second-generation Bloodline naturally understood how important this matter was for Dawn City.
"Dawn City needs to be vigilant but must also not lose its measure—we need to proceed one step at a time."
Lide took a moment to gather his thoughts before his mind turned to the Abyss, and he continued.
"Immediately assemble the officers of the King’s Blade and draw backbone officers from various legions. We need to reorganize the Demon Army of the Abyss immediately. We cannot relax on this matter.
Also, there could be many rare minerals and magic materials in the Abyss; have the Dawn Mage Tower, Alchemy Factory, Weapon Factory, and Dawn Academy jointly form an expedition team. We need to develop the value of the Abyss; it cannot be left untapped and wasted."
Enhancing his own power was the most crucial thing.
He had already occupied the Gravel Plane. Now that he simply needed to develop it to reap the benefits, this matter naturally could not be delayed.
Harrison, somewhat tense from the barrage of information, left with a solemn expression.
Knowing such level of top-secret information and still maintaining composure would indeed be strange.
Lide watched Harrison’s retreating figure, took a deep breath, and felt the impact as well—except he could not show it.
The ruler of Dawn was capable of controlling the fate of millions and had to bear that responsibility.
He needed to immediately reorganize the Chaotic Army of the Gravel Plane and then enter seclusion to break through to legendary; he felt the variables of the future multiplying, and only his own strength was the eternal unchanging truth.
Half a day later, after an urgent mobilization, a group of 2000 officers and a 1000-member expedition team were assembled.
These individuals would be the first force of Dawn City to invade the Abyss.
Once the Demon Army was reorganized, subsequent developments could proceed more freely.
Once everyone had gathered, Lide directly opened a teleportation gate to the Abyss inside the Land of Bone-Burying.
He too returned to the Abyss along with the Dawn Army.
Gravel Plane.
The moment Lide stepped out of the space gate, he was greeted by the salutes of five Extraordinary Demons.
"Good day, Your Majesty."
Naga Leader, Abyss Half-beast Leader, Abyss Butcher, two Double-Horned Demon Lords.
This small, cramped stone building was filled with an aura of terrifying oppressiveness.
Seeing this scene, Lide’s mood slightly improved; after all, the power now possessed by Dawn City was sufficient for self-defense.
"Tear down this building. I’ve brought a group of officers from the Main Plane. You need to cooperate with them on the tasks."
The demons naturally obeyed Lide’s orders, but before proceeding, the Naga Leader spoke up, sparking Lide’s interest.
"Your Majesty, the undead from the Rotten Land in the north sent envoys to seek an audience three Sunshine Hours ago..."
"Oh? What did they say?"
"They want to cooperate with us."
Lide looked at the Naga Leader with interest.
"What kind of cooperation?"
The Naga Leader spoke gravely, "They plan to attack the 269th Plane and want to hire us to go there."

chapters.content:
Chapter 438: Chapter 440: The Lame Undead Main God Fooled, the Plan to Kill a Pig by Borrowing a Knife (8400 words)
"The undead are preparing to attack the 269th Plane and wish to hire us to head there," the Naga leader announced.
Hearing this, Lide raised an eyebrow.
The undead want to strike at the 269th Plane? Do they possess such strength?
Though the 269th Level Gravel Plane was close by, that plane was so barren. And with the undead being a single force, could they truly shake an entire plane?
"Wanting to hire us, can the undead afford such a price?" Lide chuckled, "Ollie, take me to meet the envoys of our neighbors."
Having said that, he turned his head to glance at the two Double-Horned Demon Lords, "You stay here and receive the Dawn Legion."
"Yes, Your Highness."
After giving his instructions, Lide followed the Naga leader and left, leaving behind the four remaining Extraordinary Demons to wait.
Upon entering this den of evil, whispers of Abyssal blasphemy, unconscious and faint yet persistent, began to echo once again.
Any life belonging to the Good Camp would be affected living in such an environment for extended periods, eventually degenerating into a being aligned with the Chaotic Evil Camp.
This was no land of friendship. Lide allowed Dawn’s exploration team into the Abyss, also intending to research how to resolve this issue.
Lide did not pay much attention to the undead in the north of the Gravel Plane’s Corrupted Land.
Moreover, according to the Naga leader, the undead rarely interacted with other forces; this had been the case for decades, even centuries.
In his view, evil beings that huddled in one region, no matter how powerful, couldn’t turn the tide; and with the Gravel Plane being so impoverished, it was unlikely to spawn any beings too powerful.
Therefore, Lide was somewhat curious what these undead, who seldom made contact with the outside world, truly sought from him.
Did they genuinely want to conquer other planes? If so, why hadn’t these undead conquered the Gravel Plane first?
At this time, the territory of the Double-Horned Demons had already stationed the entire Chaotic Army. Beyond the central area, the disordered sight unfolded before them.
Hundreds of thousands of chaotic lives gathered together, creating a scene so chaotic it was unbearable to witness. If not for a few Extraordinary beings and the Naga Law Enforcement Team maintaining order, these demons would likely have started slaying each other at any moment—even though they collectively worshipped Lide.
However, upon seeing Lide, these demons turned obedient and submissive. The Chaotic Army demons all knelt as he passed, their eyes blazing with fervent adoration for Lide, the great God of Twilight.
Lide showed no mercy, releasing his Divine Dignity abundantly; the oppressive might choked the demons, their faces flushed red.
Yet, a glance at the attribute panel showed that not only did Lide’s actions fail to decrease the demons’ loyalty, but their devout faith skyrocketed.
No life revered the strong more than demons. Being ruled by a superior force they couldn’t resist was a great honor.
Lide walked amidst such prostration for seven or eight minutes until the guiding Naga leader stopped in front of a demon building constructed of rubble stones and adorned with twisted symbols.
Without waiting for the Naga leader to report, Lide instantly sensed the unique aura of the undead within the building. Being the owner of an Undead Plane, he was very sensitive to such presences.
He stepped straight through the entrance.
Lide’s Divine oppressiveness did not retract; upon entering the house, it felt like an ancient giant dragon squeezing into a small pond, instantly crushing everything like a collapsing mountain, freezing the souls of every being within.
He saw seven or eight undead before him, the azure Soul Fire burning fiercely within their skeletal skulls, cooling the room despite the flames.
These undead were tall, each over two meters high, and what surprised Lide the most was that they donned Solid Black Armor and wielded greatswords that emanated a chilling aura.
Clearly, these were not the pauper undead he had imagined—they seemed rather significant, and their equipment was not the kind forged by any average smith.
Lide subconsciously opened the attribute panel, glanced over it, and immediately understood.
These special undead were the trump card of the undead forces—Horror Knights.
And their level, astonishingly, all were at Level 15, with the leader even having reached the Transcendent Level.
However, powerful as these Horror Knights were, their Soul Fire still trembled under Lide’s Divine Power as if they could be extinguished at any moment.
The Horror Knight whose level was as high as 20 took a moment to regain composure before respectfully stepping forward and greeting Lide.
"Great God of Twilight, the Dark Sovereign sends his regards to you."
The Dark Sovereign?
Lide’s eyes narrowed. Who was this?
Knowing he was the God of Twilight and still daring to send someone, could it be that the Gravel Plane still concealed some undead overlord?
This was originally the place sealed by the God of Twilight... Could it be that some other undead Evil God was sealed here?
At this thought, Lide’s expression soured. Was he that unlucky? Just occupying an abyssal plane, and there were two gods present...
But on second thought, this seemed like a stroke of luck... If the other party was sealed, just like the God of Twilight, wouldn’t he be in for another windfall?
Interest sparked in his eyes.
"You lowly undead, who gave you the courage to dare hire my legions?"
The blasphemous language of ancient times now mixed with the Power of Faith and thundered out, with dignity magnified tenfold, a hundredfold, like an eighteenth-level explosion that spiraled up into mountains thousands of meters high, earthshaking.
The stars dimmed, and the heavens and earth trembled.
Such a dreadful pressure was certainly not something the newly advanced Transcendent undead could contend with.
The Soul Fire of the Horror Knights, which had previously burned fiercely, now dangled on the brink, like a flickering candle in the wind, possibly extinguished at any moment.
Utterly horrifying.
The once supremely confident Transcendent Horror Knights now felt a fatal danger in their souls by instinct, an uncontestable dignity that infiltrated their essence.
When they spoke again, the tone carried a hint of fear.
"Great being, please forgive our trespasses, we come on behalf of the Dark Sovereign..."
"The Dark Sovereign? Never heard of him. Where is he sealed?"
Not only did Lide not retract his pressure upon hearing this, he intensified it, and his spiritual power also spread out, observing every detail about this Horror Knight.
"Great God of Twilight, my god currently resides in the Undead Plane. The Dark Sovereign is one of the fifteen Monarchs of the Undead Plane, commanding legions of millions, not a sealed god..."
Monarchs of the Undead Plane?
Lide’s gaze sharpened.
The Undead Plane, unlike the Abyss, was composed of countless planes, while the Undead Plane, like the Main Plane, was a vast plane that had existed since the beginning of creation, where only undead life forms thrived.
And the Dark Bosses who ruled over this land of evil were among the fourteen Undead Monarchs.
The God of Bones, once the forger of the Land of Bone-Burying, was one of the top three most powerful Undead Monarchs of the Undead Plane, with extremely terrifying strength.
But the issue was, from time immemorial, there had only been fourteen Monarchs in the Undead Plane. Where did this fifteenth Monarch come from?
He had never heard of this Dark Sovereign, and the Main Plane had never recorded any related information.
"Foolish Horror Knight, there are only fourteen Monarchs in the Undead Plane. Since when did the Dark Monarch become the fifteenth Monarch??"
According to Main Plane legends, every Undead Monarch was extremely powerful, and even those ranking at the top possessed their own Subordinate Gods, and not just any Divine could become an Undead Monarch.
Under the imposing Dignity of the terrifying Main God, the soul fire of the Horror Knight fluttered more and more.
"Great God of Twilight, the Dark Sovereign is a newly ascended Undead Monarch..." Although the voice shook slightly under the pressure, it was filled with confidence.
Lide’s gaze sharpened as he sensed that the Horror Knight was not lying... Could this be true?
Was there really a new Undead Monarch eyeing the Gravel Plane?
His complexion couldn’t help but turn ugly at the thought.
This was many times more terrifying than a sealed Divine.
The enemy this time was overwhelmingly strong.
No, the other party wasn’t an enemy yet.
As Lide’s thoughts whirled, his expression slowly regained composure; if the other party had hostile intentions, they would have directly sent an army instead of a messenger.
For now, it was best to first figure out what this Undead Monarch really wanted before responding.
The Divine Power was slightly retracted, allowing the Horror Knight a moment to catch his breath.
"I sense that you have not lied.
Speak your purpose, Undead."
The Horror Knight, whose soul fire had nearly collapsed under the pressure of the Divine Power, gradually reignited. The Extraordinary Undead then solemnly organized his words before speaking.
"Great God of Twilight, the Undead Plane, due to the millennia of expansion by the other fourteen Grand Dukes, has long run out of new land.
The territory left for my god is too insignificant, unworthy of his Dignity.
My god plans to invade the Abyss and expand his domain."
Lide’s eyelids twitched; this Dark Sovereign’s thoughts coincided almost exactly with his own.
However, while the other wanted an invasion due to a lack of territory in the Undead Plane, he wanted it for the development of Dawn City. The fundamental demands were different, but the goals were remarkably similar.
"Undead, the Dark Sovereign’s thoughts are very similar to mine. What do you want?"
The Horror Knight’s empty eyes stared directly at Lide, and the bluish soul fire within grew even colder.
"Great God of Twilight, we need to use the Abyss Transmission Array that you control...
That Transmission Array was a relic left from the Battle of the Ancient Gods, once used by my god.
Today, we sensed the presence of that Transmission Array and were specially dispatched to come here."
Upon hearing this, Lide couldn’t help feeling somewhat vexed; the other party must have sensed the presence due to the Land of Bone-Burying devouring the Transmission Array and the ensuing energy fluctuation.
But wasn’t this too coincidental, that they just happened to have used it before? It seemed far-fetched...
However, at this moment, there was a problem because the Transmission Array had been devoured by his Land of Bone-Burying; how could he lend it now?
To use the transmission, one must go inside the Land of Bone-Burying and then only can they transfer to other planes...
To transfer within the Land of Bone-Burying...
Transfer...
Lide muttered the word several times, when suddenly a bolt of lightning flashed through his mind.
He had, in that instant, conceived an exceedingly bold and mad idea.
These Undead were intent on conquering other planes, which would inevitably lead to wars against the powers of those planes.
But could these wars be waged within the Land of Bone-Burying??
If so, then his Abyss pig farming scheme could evolve into using another’s knife to slaughter pigs, borrowing the blade of the Undead Monarch to butcher even fatter and larger swine...
Once this idea took root, Lide felt an itch in his heart as if it were being scratched by a cat.
Though it was only a budding thought, if one were to seriously ponder, it was possible to explore just how staggeringly profitable it could be.
Yet, there was an issue. If the Dark Sovereign could become an Undead Monarch, then his minions must be extraordinarily strong. If he were to send Divine Level subordinates, what should Lide do if they discovered something unusual about the Land of Bone-Burying?
Lide’s brow furrowed slightly, but then his eyes brightened.
No, that’s not right, there was a way... It was fully possible to set power level restrictions for passage through the Space Gate. Anything exceeding the Land of Bone-Burying’s capacity to handle could be prevented from passing through, such as if beings above Legendary tried to enter, the Space Gate would collapse... This would circumvent the risk and keep it within controllable limits.
Once those planes were conquered, they could construct their own Transmission Arrays.
Lide believed an Undead Monarch couldn’t lack the capability to build Transmission Arrays; otherwise, he wouldn’t dream of seizing the Abyss Plane.
This would perfectly prevent those powerful subordinates from entering the Land of Bone-Burying.
As for how to turn the Land of Bone-Burying into a battlefield, that was simple too. By opening several Space Gates atop those planes and using treasures or other things to lure those chaotic Demons into the Land of Bone-Burying, it was entirely conceivable to hijack the Dark Sovereign’s armies to execute the Abyss pig farming scheme.
In other words, he would be borrowing the Dark Sovereign’s knife to slaughter the pigs of the Abyss Plane.
He could even switch things around by opening Space Gates on some powerful and resource-rich planes, letting the Dark Sovereign’s army help him slay the native Demons.
Once the job was done and his own forces could handle the aftermath, he’d just send people to take over.
The more Lide pondered, the more he believed this plan was insane, yet its feasibility seemed exceptionally high.
But, leveraging a Monarch Level existence with terrifying power from the Undead Plane was ridiculously risky; if he were to be found out, he might severely crash and burn.
However, if handled with care, the reach of Dawn City could quickly expand within the Abyss.
Before him, this Extraordinary Horror Knight could never imagine that the mere Level 24 God of Twilight was already scheming to utilize the power of a being like the Dark Monarch to grow his own forces.
In fact, anyone who knew of Lide’s thoughts would consider him a madman... This was indeed too crazy.
