And this was not even the full potential of Dawn City. If all were calculated, he could even muster an army of a million... with just the Demon Army accounting for over 65,000.
Even so, the vast army had crammed Twilight City to the bursting point, with troops densely stationed even outside the city.
Level 25 Beastman King Kapp, Level 18 Half-Elf Great Mage, and Level 16 Super Cave Dweller were all fervently watching Lide’s back.
Above the sky, Withered Bone was spreading its wings and flying, with the Frost Giant Dragon Altan trailing behind it like a little lackey.
This haughty, Transcendent Frost Giant Dragon had been subdued by Withered Bone, and when the Level 26 Legendary made a move, Altan, a Level 20 Transcendent, had barely any strength left to resist; he was pitifully weak.
Withered Bone had gained its first little subordinate...
"Sire, according to the intelligence we’ve gathered," reported the intelligence department, "the Half-Elves had started amassing all the military forces of the Underworld several months ago.
By now, over three million Half-Elves have been assembled around the main city, Liusi City, and they have also enslaved over six hundred thousand from other races..."
Is that 3.6 million?
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly.
This was no small number; it seemed the God of Half-Elves was confident in conquering the Underworld.
Unfortunately for them, their foe this time was him.
Even one hundred sheep were no match for a lion.
"How is the army reform?"
"Sire, all the anticipated armies have assembled."
"Order the attack."
"Yes, Sire!"
With the command issued, the great army set out.
On August 13, 3526, in the Era of Glory, over fifty thousand troops from Dawn City began their campaign to conquer the Underworld.
Among them, the Demon Army deployed two hundred thousand troops, the Twilight Legion deployed another two hundred thousand, the Centaur Army one hundred thousand, the Beastman Army fifty thousand, and the King’s Blade in total thirty thousand, including twelve thousand Bomb-carrying Magic Word Bats, four thousand from the Blood Clan Caster Corps... totaling fifty-eight thousand, nearly reaching six hundred thousand.
The crow flies distance between Twilight City and Liusi City was over one thousand kilometers, and since this campaign aimed at conquest and annexation of all territories, they did not use Magic Language Bats to transport forces.
Instead, they pushed forward with commanding authority, subjugating all tribes, cities, and races they encountered along the way—either surrendering as prisoners or being decapitated without exception.
Shortly after departing from Twilight City, to accelerate the advance, Lide ordered the army divided into three cohorts.
He commanded the central forces himself with two hundred thousand from the Demon Army while Withered Bone and Frost Giant Dragon Altan led one hundred thousand Centaur Warriors and thirty thousand from the King’s Blade on the left flank.
Level 25 Beastman King Kapp commanded two hundred thousand from the Twilight Legion and fifty thousand from the Beastman Army on the right flank.
Forces divided into three routes.
With this, the Dawn Army began to reveal its glaring brilliance in the confines of the underground world.
Lide, after years of developing technology in silence and cultivating a complete military-industrial complex, was now leveraging all that had been prepared.
There were bombing squadrons of Magic Bats inducing terror from above, while on the ground, soldiers had armors, weapons, crossbows, and arrows constantly forged by Dwarf Factories... Each army even had Alchemy Bomb Launchers providing continuous fire support at any challenging assault point.
Strongholds vulnerable to alchemy bombs crumbled like froth; the sharp claws of the Underground Races were as if confronting towering mountains and walls when facing Dawn Army’s armors.
Relying on overwhelming equipment superiority, everywhere the Dawn Army went, whether the cities of Half-Elves or the tribes of other Underground Races, all were conquered and flattened.
None could withstand the sweep of the Dawn’s Steel Army after an alchemy bomb bombardment.
A decade of preparation honed a blade sharp enough to sunder the heavens and shatter the earth.
By August 20, the numbers in all three armies had grown significantly due to the vast number of prisoners taken, most notably Lide’s leading Demon Army, which explosively increased from two hundred thousand to four hundred thousand in just a few days.
And under Lide’s divine might, these newly added troops soon became devoted followers, with their blades still pointed towards Liusi City.
By August 25, the Half-Elves, already sensing the disturbances, mobilized a large army to clear the tribes around Liusi City, concurrently forming an army exceeding two million.
On August 30, as the Dawn Army pressed forward to within less than three hundred kilometers of Liusi City, both flanks under Withered Bone’s Legendary Undead Blood Dragon and Kapp, the Beastman King, had been subdued into Dawn’s dominion.
If one were to spread out the map of the Underground World, two-thirds of the territory, excluding the barren wastelands, now belonged to Dawn City.
But everyone knew the war was far from over, as the Half-Elf Army had yet to clash directly with Dawn City.
Indeed, the grand battle unfolded densely in the following days.
On September 2nd, Withered Bone led a large army to attack a Half-Elf city and was ambushed.
Over 400,000 troops rushed out from both the left and right flanks, clashing with the Centaur Army and King’s Blade.
The Centaur Army, concealed by Divine Arts, caught Withered Bone off guard and instantly caused chaos within the ranks.
Just as Withered Bone was about to react, he was abruptly entangled by a Legendary Half-Elf and two Transcendent Half-Elves, leaving him unable to break free.
Frost Giant Dragon Altan tried hard to recover the situation, but it too was quickly restrained by the opposing Transcendent.
Although the real commander of this army was a Bloodline leader, with the two top combat forces engaged and the legion’s sudden attack from below, the army suffered significant losses
Not only did almost 200,000 prisoners gathered over more than ten days perish, but the Centaur Army also lost over 30,000 warriors.
If it weren’t for the ferocity of the Giant Army holding the line, the losses would have been even greater.
At critical moments, 4000 Blood Mages turned the tide dramatically by jointly unleashing their ultimate skill, a "Bloody Storm," which formed hundreds of thousands of slaughtering bats and forcefully broke through the Half-Elf’s battle formation, securing the final victory in this war.
Fearing Lide’s blame upon realizing the heavy losses of his forces, Withered Bone went mad, recklessly withstanding the legendary Half-Elf’s attack and forcibly dealt with a Transcendent to stem further losses.
Ultimately, the Legendary Half-Elf, noticing the frenzied state of Withered Bone and knowing the battle was unwinnable, reluctantly retreated.
Enraged, Withered Bone recklessly pursued the fleeing Half-Elves, leaving only a little more than a hundred thousand alive out of the initial 400,000, marking a horrific loss.
At the same time, Kaplotz also encountered an ambush while passing through a low grass area, facing not only Half-Elves but also mixed forces of over 300,000 from other Underground Races.
The total number of troops exceeded 600,000, an exaggerated count.
However, Kaplotz’s perception of danger far surpassed that of Withered Bone, and he immediately sensed something was wrong and ordered the troops to defend.
As expected, the Half-Elf army launched their assault.
But Kaplotz was a true tribal ruler, having commanded countless battles in his lifetime, incomparable to the chatty Withered Bone.
Leveraging his superior command skills, the Beastman Army and the Twilight Legion coordinated seamlessly, staunchly holding off the Half-Elf army’s charge.
The Half-Elves and the Dawn Army fought fiercely for ten Sunshine Hours and were eventually pierced through by the well-equipped Dawn Army.
In such large-scale warfare, ordinary tactics were no longer effective; it ultimately depended on raw power.
Beneath the heritage of Dawn City, what right did the Half-Elves have to compare their sheer strength with Dawn Army?
After the defeat of the Half-Elf Legion, their enslaved Underground Races were incorporated by the Twilight Legion.
By the end of this war, the strength of the Twilight Legion had inflated to 360,000, and together with the Beastman Army, the total reached an exaggerated 400,000.
The only regret for Kaplotz was that the legendary-level commander among the Half-Elf Legion didn’t engage in battle. Although he sensed the opponent’s presence, the adversary remained hidden in secret corners, thwarting his desire to eliminate a legendary figure.
Upon hearing the news of simultaneous ambushes, Lide was displeased; Kaplotz was fine, but he was furious over Withered Bone’s poor vigilance and sent people to sternly scold that blabbermouth.
Withered Bone was depressed over this, his anger pent up with nowhere to vent...
During these two ambushes, the appearances of two legendary Half-Elves also caught Lide’s attention.
It seemed not only had he cultivated strong forces during this time, but the Half-body God also nurtured several powerful individuals.
With millions of Half-Elf Believers, the resources at their disposal might not be far behind his own.
While leading the Demon Army forward, Lide suddenly discovered that he too had been ambushed.
As he looked at the charging Half-Elf Army from all sides with a puzzled expression, his face was quite a spectacle.
Who gave these fools the courage?
Then, with a wave of his hand, 20 Demon Ten Thousand People Armies surged forward.
These brutal, bloodthirsty demons, handpicked elites of Lide, were all above Level 13...
The Half-Elf Army, initially thinking this was to be an annihilation battle, only realized upon encountering the horrific demons that they couldn’t defeat even one...
Even their Hundred-man Squad Leaders and Thousand-man Commanders were easily killed by ordinary demons.
The terrifying combat strength of the Demon Army made the Half-Elf ambush seem more like delivering food.
"""In just three Sunshine Hours, over 300,000 half-elves were devoured by the Demon Army, and the remaining half-elves collapsed and started to flee in all directions.
Lide, in this battle, also noticed a powerful presence secretly observing everything, but the entity did not take action.
He remained vigilant, pressing forward without seeking out the mysterious figure; after all, what if it was an ambush...
After the battle ended, the casualties of the 200,000-strong Demon Army did not even exceed 5,000. The makeshift army formed from captives didn’t get to partake in the battle until it was time to capture prisoners.
Three battles, three victories. Aside from Withered Bone, who suffered significant losses, the armies led by Lide and Kapp sustained minimal casualties and even expanded significantly due to the number of prisoners captured.
On September 5th, the three great armies continued sweeping through the Underworld, making smaller tribes flee at the mere sight or outright surrender and join the great army.
On September 6th, the relentless half-elves, still not giving up, set up an ambush in a valley, trying to completely wipe out Withered Bone’s troops.
But Withered Bone, who had been berated harshly, remained highly vigilant and immediately sensed the danger, charging into enemy lines alone.
After ascending to Legendary, Withered Bone’s Dragon Breath, now with a range of 200 blades, performed an unprecedented massacre on the ambushing legion as a level 26 Legendary Undead Blood Dragon.
Over 100,000 were devoured by the Dragon Breath. Had two Legendaries not attacked Withered Bone at the last moment, entrapping the frenzied dragon at a great cost, this army might have been utterly decimated.
Although the two Legendaries managed to hold Withered Bone, they found this bizarre undead terribly formidable, being pressed hard even in a two-against-one fight. The idea of slaying Withered Bone fell through, and they were forced to retreat once again.
Unsuccessful in gaining any leverage on Withered Bone’s front, the half-elves did not give up.
The next day, two Legendary half-elves and three Transcendents, without leading an ordinary army, marched straight towards Kapp.
The half-elves had resolved to eliminate at least one Dawn Army.
Upon detecting the enemy’s approach, Kapp immediately sent a distress signal to Lide, facing a fierce battle against two Legendaries and three Transcendents.
This level 25 King of Lions, suffused with Golden Power, wielding his war blade, fought bloodily.
His erupting combat power terrified the half-elves, who didn’t expect this level 25 Legendary to be outrageously strong!
Kapp, with his overwhelming power, forcibly held back the five elite half-elves.
After extended fierce fighting, Kapp finally fell into disadvantage, but by that time, Lide had already arrived.
Lide didn’t even use magic; wielding a sharp war blade and employing the Legendary Level Skill "Shadow Blade," he directly inflicted heavy injuries on a Legendary and killed a Transcendent.
Had the opponents not used an ancient item like the Teleportation Scroll to swiftly leave the battlefield, none might have survived.
After this battle, the half-elves finally abandoned the idea of ambushing the Dawn Army en route and decisively retracted all their forces into the Half-body Main City.
Liusi City, hosting an army of over 2 million, became a city that truly merited the title of Unfallen City.
Built by hollowing out mountains, the city’s strength was indescribable, bolstered by sufficient troops and support from a Divine being.
Indeed, it lived up to the name "Unfallen City."
On September 8th, the Dawn Army showed its battle front, directly breaking through a half-elf city closest to Liusi City. The army was now just 30 kilometers from Liusi City, merely a few Sunshine Hours away.
And here, the three armies also converged.
In less than a month, excluding the frontier zones, the territory of the half-elves was reduced to just Liusi City.
And here, the final battle was to commence.
In this unnamed small city, Kapp, flanked by high-ranking officials, respectfully reported to Lide, who stood atop the city walls, gazing into the distance.
"Sire, all the half-elves and their enslaved armies have already entered Liusi City.
Once we conquer this city, the Underworld will no longer have any forces capable of resisting the Dawn Army!"
The Underworld, though vast, has a much lower density of life due to its harsh living conditions and numerous predators compared to the Main Plane.
The half-elves are undoubtedly the most powerful force in the Underworld, although other tribes do exist besides them.
But from any perspective, none are as formidable as the half-elves.
Once the half-elves are annihilated, other tribes, facing the blades of the Dawn Army, will have only destruction as an option.
Their enemy has always been singular.
Lide turned to look at Kapp, his eyes betraying a hint of chilliness."""
"Not in a hurry, I need an assistant."
"An assistant?" Kapp was slightly startled.
Lide didn’t explain much, and a contemplative look appeared in his eyes.
Moments later, he made a decision.
With a slight wave of his hand, Kapp saw a saber quietly float up beside Lide.
This seemingly unremarkable saber suddenly burst forth with an extremely terrifying aura, as if the soul of an ancient giant beast was sealed within it.
A dark light was activated, shooting from the blade into the sky, and within a few breaths, a magic mirror as tall as two men appeared in the sky.
In the span of a few breaths, the center of the mirror rippled like water.
Then it displayed an image that utterly shocked Kapp.
A terrifying figure stood in a palace of bones, wearing a golden crown, draped in a human skin cloak, and holding a white bone longsword.
The eyes, glowing with a ghostly blue soul fire, stared straight into the magic mirror, and the pressure emanating from his body felt crushing across countless planes, the terrifying aura like a colossal wave smashing down with thousands of tons of sea water.
Kapp even felt his soul nearly collapsing at that moment, as just one look from the other felt like a giant hammer smashing into his spiritual sea.
That was an ancient divine being who had trodden across the Star River.
After scarcely collecting his wits, Kapp’s face was filled with shock.
Such a terrifying being was actually the assistant summoned by His Highness??
Everyone was immensely shocked both by the strength of the figure in the magic mirror and by the fact that Lide could so casually summon such a terrifying entity.
It was too frightening.
"Dawn Main God."
The Dark Sovereign, seeing Lide, flickered the soul fire in his eyes slightly, his tone softening a bit.
"Is there something you need?"
Recently, Lide had helped him conquer ten Abyss planes, and the casualties were not significant, which made the Dark Sovereign think highly of Lide and increased his fondness for him significantly.
This time, facing the Dark Sovereign, Lide did not emit much of an aura, and his tone was much lighter than before.
"Dark Sovereign, do I need a reason to contact a friend?"
Hm?
The Dark Sovereign hesitated for a moment. I was contacted without a specific reason? But it seems right; not every contact must have a purpose.
For a moment, his mind couldn’t grasp the turn of events, unsure of what Lide intended to do.
"Indeed, but I still need to handle those Abyss plane matters and don’t have much time..."
Lide smiled. "No worries, today I primarily wanted to exchange sentiments with you...
Moreover, having known you for so long without offering a gift, today I am going to slay a deity, and I’ve heard that the undead are fond of divine souls. If the Dark Sovereign does not reject a friend’s gift, then this divine soul is presented to you."
A divine soul?
The soul fire in the Dark Sovereign’s empty eye sockets flared up.
Though he was one of the fifteen Undead Monarchs, with immense power in the Undead Plane, the soul of a divine being was still a cherished treasure to him.
Devouring souls allowed the undead to grow; he wanted to ascend to higher levels, which was impossible without powerful souls.
Acquiring a large number of divine souls would definitely be a great help to him.
As beings of Glory at their ultimate life form, the quantity of deities wasn’t small, but hunting them was extremely difficult.
After all, if they couldn’t beat him, they still had countless ways to escape.
Now Lide was offering to gift him a precious divine soul, which further increased the Dark Sovereign’s favorable impression of Lide.
"Dawn Main God, are you speaking the truth?"
Lide caught the stir in the heart of the Dark Sovereign and cracked a slight smile.
"Of course, I am now preparing to attack the main city where the Half-body God resides.
You should know that the gods of the Main Plane have become mundanes, and their power has plummeted to rock bottom."
"Main Plane?" The Dark Sovereign, upon hearing this, looked around briefly for the first time, and after a slight sensing, a hint of surprise appeared in his eyes.
"The rules of the Main Plane oppressively suppress the gods of other planes. If I were to descend, I could not even exist for the span of a breath. Dawn Main God, how have you managed to not be repelled by these rules?"
Lide revealed a bit of sentimentality. "This time, I paid a great price to smuggle myself into the Main Plane, even resorting to using Divine Arts to seal a part of my power just so I could linger a bit longer..."
Hearing this, the Dark Sovereign finally nodded understandingly. Every god has their own unique Divine Arts; sealing one’s own power isn’t too novel.
"This encounter with the Half-body God was an accident. Undead like souls, and Dark Sovereign, you probably are no exception, so I specifically came to hunt that god. I’ll gift his soul to you in advance."
Lide said this with a trace of regret flickering in his eyes.
"I paid a huge price to seal my power this time, fearing that the seal would break open after taking action and get me transported back to the Abyss by the will of the Main Plane.
But even if I fail to achieve my goal this time, as long as it pleases you, Dark Sovereign, I believe the price I’ve paid was not in vain..."
Now his role carried a bit of a flatterer’s tone, and his words also subtly hinted to the Dark Sovereign.
I made such a sacrifice for you...
The soul of the Dark Sovereign flickered slightly, displaying a touch of emotion as he glanced at him.
"Dawn Main God, you indeed are a trustworthy ally.
The rules of the Main Plane are powerful. The task you intend to complete must be significant for such a great sacrifice.
When the time comes, just restrain the Half-body God and leave the rest to me."
Hearing this, Lide smiled inwardly. His hint hadn’t been wasted—it was a success. Dealing with the undead was indeed more straightforward... these creatures were rather direct.
"Since that’s the case, I won’t decline. After all, it’s your soul; better you handle it than I cause any harm. However, I still have a use for his divine body, so, Dark Sovereign, be careful not to destroy it."
The Dark Sovereign nodded. "It should be so." He also needed the divine body, but the soul was more important. Moreover, since Lide had said so, he naturally wouldn’t dispute it, especially since it was a gift from him.
"Once I breach the Half-body Main City and encounter the Half-body God, I will activate this saber. Those deities who descend to the Main Plane and become saints, their power is now at most Legendary..."
The Dark Sovereign was immediately elated upon hearing this. Even if he couldn’t personally descend to the Main Plane, how difficult could it be to handle a Legendary being?
At this moment, the Undead Monarch looked at Lide with increasing fondness. This ally was indeed worthy. He even began thinking about how to repay Lide.
After talking a bit more, Lide actively narrowed the gap with the Dark Sovereign and then cut off the communication.
The goal had been achieved; further chatter was unnecessary.
As the Magic Mirror disappeared, a sense of dread slowly receded from the face of Beastman King Kap. The oppression of the Undead Monarch was not something a 25th level Legendary could withstand.
"Your Majesty... did you really bring the Dark Sovereign as an ally?"
Hearing this incredulous tone, Lide smirked.
"Indeed. The Dark Sovereign can be used by me."
The plan of ’borrowing a knife to kill a pig’ wasn’t just for dealing with ordinary demons. It applied to upper forces as well.
And in this world, how many weapons were sharper than an Undead Monarch at this level?
"Does the Half-body God really require such caution from you?" Kap couldn’t help but express his doubt.
Lide nodded, saying with a profound meaning,
"Although the Half-body God is a deity who has descended to the Main Plane and doesn’t seem very strong, there’s one point we cannot ignore— the allies of the Half-body God."
"Your Majesty, are you suggesting that the Half-body God might unite with other descending gods of the Main Plane to resist our attack?"
A golden glint flashed in Kap’s eyes.
"But who is the ally of the Half-body God?" Have you received any news regarding this matter?"
Lide gazed deeply at the majestic lion and slowly shook his head.
"No, I cannot even confirm whether they have allies..."
"Then why would you?"
Kapp was somewhat puzzled. In his view, the power of a god would inevitably decrease greatly after their descent to the world, and with their strength, taking down a weak god seemed highly probable.
If outsiders were involved, they would have to share the spoils they already had in hand, which would be a waste...
Moreover, since the Dark Sovereign is so powerful, the other party is unreliable...
"Precaution," Lide’s eyes flickered unclearly, "Never underestimate any god, no matter how weak their power might seem.
By involving the Dark Sovereign, we effectively buy ourselves insurance at the cost of the Half-body God’s soul.
The advantage is that we can act boldly, and if there are significant problems, we have sufficient strength to respond.
Another key point is that by cooperating with the Dark Sovereign, we can strengthen our relationship, and given his extraordinary status, we might need him in the future."
Planning for failure before victory, Lide was never one to covet immediate gains; his sights were set further ahead.
This move was guaranteed to be lucrative; even if the Half-body God had no assistants, he had used this opportunity to forge a deeper relationship with the Dark Sovereign. From any perspective, he would not be at a loss.
Moreover, if using the Dark Sovereign’s influence to hunt down gods gave the adversary a taste of victory, then he could act even more brazenly in the future.
It was like having an ace up his sleeve, where he could bring out the Dark Sovereign to bolster his position if he couldn’t handle a fight.
Kapp only saw the possible division of spoils at the first layer, but Lide had already considered drawing the Dark Sovereign in to take the bullet...
—
—
—
"Your Highness, those damned vampires have surrounded Liusi City; I implore you to give the order, let our army go out and crush these execrable blasphemers!!"
Inside the temple of the Half-body God, a group of indignant high-ranking Half-elves glared furiously at the silent, eyes-closed Half-body God atop the high altar.
They had never suffered such a significant defeat. In the past underground world, who could contest the Half-elves for dominion?
But ever since that vampire emerged leading the Twilight Sect, everything had changed.
Were it not for the protection of the great divine, their main city might well have been breached.
This was unbearable!!
Even with the Half-body God present, the army targeting the Twilight Sect had suffered unprecedented losses...
After numerous failed attacks, the resentment among the Half-els’ upper echelons had built up.
Why? Why could the damned God of Twilight act so brazenly? They too had a great deity overseeing them!
Although their military strength couldn’t compare to that of Dawn City and they had faced repeated defeats, every Half-elf still firmly believed that victory in the war would ultimately be theirs.
The radiant glory of Lord Kaplotz would shine upon them eternally; for the glory of their god, they would fearlessly face life and death.
The Half-body God Kaplotz, upon hearing this, slowly opened his eyes. At that moment, his amber eyes emitted a dazzling light.
Sharp as arrows shot from an archer’s bow, the air quieted instantly, and everyone fervently watched their god.
"The God of Twilight has come with his army."
In a tone filled with supremacy and a bird’s-eye view, the once uncontrollably furious Half-elves were suddenly stiffened in their expressions.
The God of Twilight...
Considering that they were battling a god, the anger that had just risen was immediately doused like cold water.
If the underground world could grasp the current state of deities on the surface world, where gods can be slain by mortals, perhaps they wouldn’t have been so timid.
But ultimately, the overwhelming dignity left by the deity had permeated deeply into their souls, instilling a primal fear of gods.
The life of the Underworld was no exception.
Looking down at the quieted half-elves, the Half-Elf God’s eyes flickered, and he spoke slowly.
"The God of Twilight dares to come, which means the War of Gods is destined to begin."
"And this time it’s different from the past..."
"I have prepared a burial place for the God of Twilight... The Underworld can only belong to us half-elves, no one else can interfere!"
With these words, the morale that had just solidified within the room surged immediately.
"Yes, Your Highness, the Underworld can only be a world governed by you! That damned heretic god can only grovel at your feet!"
"Praise you, my god!"
"Kill the God of Twilight, and everything will belong to the half-elves!"
The shouting crowd was incredibly excited.
In their eyes, since the Half-Elf God had spoken, the God of Twilight was surely destined to fall; in their hearts, the Half-Elf God was invincible!
No one could survive under the dignity of the Half-Elf God.
The eyes of the Half-Elf God shimmered, and his gaze held a cold, murderous intent.
"This time, it’s not just us versus the God of Twilight, I have arranged for the allies of the half-elves to come to our aid."
"Allies?" The legendary old half-elf in the front, who had once stood against Lide, lit up.
"Your Highness, could it be the God of Gray Dwarves?"
Although the gray dwarves were close relatives of the dwarves, they belonged to an evil ordered camp, vastly different from the neutral order of the dwarves.
And the only ally the half-elves could truly call were the gray dwarves.
For the God of the Gray Dwarves had always been a good friend of the Half-Elf God, even before they ascended to divinity, the two had known each other.
The Half-Elf God nodded, his face showing a trace of admiration.
"Yes, it is the God of Gray Dwarves. The Gray Dwarves descended in an Underworld of the Main Plane just like me.
But unfortunately, that Underworld mostly collapsed due to the appearance of an Ancient Evil God, and now there isn’t even enough food to sustain his believers.
He will assist us in killing the God of Twilight, and we will establish a trade cooperation with them to provide enough food and territory for his believers."
Hearing this, the half-elves’ eyes brightened, thinking that with two gods against one, their chances of winning looked good.
But the Half-Elf God did not stop there; he gave everyone another big surprise.
"Not only the God of Gray Dwarves, but also the Subordinate God of Smelting and Forging associated with him will join the battle.
Even the fighting power of the God of Smelting does not pale in comparison to the God of Gray Dwarves; he is a rare War God."
"Your Highness, your wisdom is enough to make all gods awe!"
The old half-elf’s eyes were filled with excitement.
Now they had three gods on their side!
Three gods!
Against one God of Twilight, no matter how strong the opponent, they would surely strike a killing blow.
"Go prepare now. Once the war begins, I will use divine arts to drag the God of Twilight into the Divine Country, and then you will conquer his army."
"Your Highness, under your brilliance, I swear with my life, these people will all become our captives! And in the future, they will surely become your believers!"
With the frenzied words of the old half-elf, the higher-ranking half-elves exchanged glances and could see the joy in each other’s eyes.
This wave was definitely stable.
They were already eagerly awaiting the arrival of that damned God of Twilight at their city gates.

chapters.title: Chapter 445 - 447: God of Twilight, You’ve Fallen into Our Ambush, Hahahaha!!
chapters.content:
Chapter 445: Chapter 447: God of Twilight, You’ve Fallen into Our Ambush, Hahahaha!!
September 9th, dry and gloomy.
Underworld, Half-body Main City — Liusi City.
Woo~ Woo~
The war horn’s desolate and deep sound echoed like the roar of a primordial beast, carrying a chilling intent of battle across the field.
When the Dawn Corps set out, the total force numbered 580,000, but after advancing beneath Liusi City, the army’s numbers had not decreased but swelled to 1 million.
Incredible.
The dense army, seen from above, resembled marching ants, covering the entire land.
Everyone’s gaze fixed on the city ahead, lying like a giant beast, their eyes cold and murderous.
Liusi City, built among the mountains, had towering peaks for walls and solid rock faces as shields. Even the highest parts of the outer walls soared over 200 blades high. To attack this city from the front, ground tribes couldn’t even scale the walls.
With shooting holes scattered through the walls and mountain crevices, the Half-body’s forte bows and arrows exposed their cold tips like porcupines. Calling the city a sky chasm would not be an overstatement.
Liusi City had only one wall at the front, with the other three sides enclosed by sky-high peaks, some 700 to 800 blades in height, plus the defending troops, only flying troops could cross.
So, to conquer this city, one had only the frontal approach.
But below the frontal wall was just a road, about a hundred blades wide, leading into the city.
Yet, this path was blocked by a 50-blade-high wall, although this paled in comparison to the surrounding rock walls a hundred blades tall.
Its defense was the most tightly guarded.
"Your Highness, all troops are ready to move. Do we launch the attack?" Kapp stood behind Lide, reporting respectfully, while the other high-ranking officers of the Dawn Army looked at Lide eagerly, awaiting his command.
Only Withered Bone, the Undead Blood Dragon, with his subordinate, the Frost Giant Dragon Altan, soared in midair. This guy’s command authority had been revoked by Lide after the troops assembled.
Indeed, this chatterbox’s performance in command was so terrible that Lide lost the drive to support him. Better to let this guy be a meat shield... talkative types do have their uses.
Lide stood on a raised hillock, his eyes sharply fixed on the distant Half-body Main City, his presence filled with a ruthless intent to kill.
Hearing Kapp’s report, he didn’t hesitate much before issuing the order.
"Follow the plan, attack!"
His tone was even, but laced with immense murderous intent.
This battle represented the final claim over the Underworld. Whoever won would rule this vast stretch of land.
The Half-bodies had absolute confidence, and so did he. He couldn’t believe that any force of equal level could block Dawn’s blade.
Quietly tending the fields and developing for years, he had poured countless efforts. The battle blade he had forged, how could it be easily covered in a single sentence?
The Dawn City of now was no longer the Kachar Castle of merely 200 Bloodline. Its edge was now revealed, formidable enough to make any force of the Main Plane take notice.
At the command, Legendary Beastman King Kapp, Level 25, immediately nodded, a ferocious gleam in his eyes. With a fierce wave of his hand, the signal officers below immediately sounded the horn.
Woo woo woo~
The war horn resounded again, unlike before, this time long and sustained, filled with an air of solemn killing intent.
The commanding officers at the front heard the horn and their faces changed, immediately starting to issue orders.
"The goblin bomb trucks, prepare!"
Click, clack~ Long chains turned, with the sound of links winding up on the winch filling the air.
One after another, goblin bomb trucks, each inscribed with magical symbols, began to emit faint magical fluctuations under the control of the warriors beside them.
The power of the goblin bomb trucks had been amply demonstrated during the last attack on Naga City, and as such, these goblin creations had become a key research project for Dawn City, with the magic symbols painted on them being the most significant improvement.
With the augmentation of magic, not only had their range been significantly boosted, but the weight of the alchemy bombs they could hurl had also greatly increased.
At this moment, it might be more appropriate to call them magic bomb trucks; nonetheless, considering the goblins’ increasingly important status in Dawn City, the name ’goblin bomb truck’ was retained.
The warriors immediately placed the alchemy bombs in a recessed loading area, managing to load five at a time.
The latest-developed bomb truck improved both the bombing distance and shooting accuracy while also increasing the number of alchemy bombs that could be loaded at once.
This setup was perfect for the first wave of bombardment to wash the ground before the enemy could react.
The sharp-eyed half-elves on the walls of Liusi City could clearly see what the Dawn Army was up to.
Although outwardly vigilant of the Dawn Army’s actions, they were somewhat dismissive inside.
With such towering walls as those belonging to Liusi City, there was no way the alchemy bombs, no matter how powerful, could destroy them.
Moreover, the distance between the two sides was seven to eight hundred blades away, and the thought of attacking the city walls, averaging 150 blades in height and reaching up to 200 blades from flat ground, seven to eight hundred blades away, was laughable.
"Those foolish heretics, shielded by the high walls of Liusi City, wouldn’t be able to harm us even with ten million men!"
"Ha ha ha, this is killing me, do these idiots think they can bring down our walls with catapults and those alchemy bombs that are barely larger than my toes?"
"May the great Kaplotz from above, in Your enveloping Glory, those damned cultists have already lost their minds!"
"Come on, damn God of Twilight, I’m standing here on the wall, hurl your alchemy bombs at me!"
"..."
The Dawn Army had used quite a few alchemy bombs while advancing, and the half-elves, not being fools, naturally had obtained this intelligence.
However, most of the Dawn Army’s previous attacks involved air-dropped alchemy bombs, something the half-elves had long been prepared for.
Over 50,000 Black Beak Giant Eagles had already gathered in the sky, and on the ground, the crossbow arrays had been ready for some time, giving no chance for the Magic Language Bats to fly into Liusi City.
Ground-based catapults couldn’t possibly hurl that far, and the sky was absolutely secure. Therefore, at this moment, the half-elves didn’t feel the slightest bit threatened.
As for those who couldn’t reach the wall to bombard it with alchemy bombs... if the Dawn Army really thought that, the half-elves were all the more ready to laugh at the folly.
Using a mountain as their wall, with the thickest width reaching 200 blades, meant that not alchemy bombs, and perhaps not even forbidden curses, could collapse such an exaggerated rock face.
"Fire!"
Accompanying a roar, the warriors who had cranked the winch to its limit suddenly released their hands, and in that moment, magic energy was channeled into the catapult.
Boom~ The tremendous force rebounded, flinging the five alchemy bombs from the thrower with a vengeance.
The alchemy bombs soared high in an arc, then to the half-elves’ astonishment, flew right over the city walls and crashed inside Liusi City.
Those Half-Beasts’ minds went blank at this sight, what in the hell was this thing???
How could it be possible to bomb the backside of walls taller than a hundred blades from a distance of seven to eight hundred blades away, from flat ground?
But no one would be around to answer their doubts.
As the first alchemy bomb fell on a house, the bomb’s firing pin was triggered, and bam~ a deafening noise erupted.
Flames filled the sky like dragon breath, instantly engulfing everything within a radius of more than twenty meters.
Houses were directly ignited by the exaggerated high temperatures, and the half-elves around couldn’t dodge in time and were burned to a crisp.
And this was just the first alchemy bomb.
Boom, boom, boom~ After more than 2000 goblin bomb trucks launched tens of thousands of rounds of ammunition, all the half-elves were forced to recognize a term anew—devastating blow.
Rumble, rumble, rumble~
The explosion of the alchemy bombs was like the divine punishment of world destruction, even the ground trembled.
The half-elves on the city walls swallowed hard, their bows and arrows now pale and feeble against the backdrop of the all-encompassing flames.
This was a degenerate attack, the cruelest form of warfare; the side at the lower dimension had no power to resist whatsoever.
The city walls, the military areas behind them—everything was now covered in fire.
Nightmare descended.
Boom~ Boom~ Boom~
Under such terrifying bombardment, the half-elves couldn’t resist at all; even Level 15 top combatants were instantly swallowed by the artillery fire.
The guard army on the walls, who had just been smirking, now looked as though they’d lost their parents, and many wished they could slap themselves hard for their loose tongues...
But they soon lost that desire as the second wave of alchemy bombs was launched directly over the city walls.
Boom~ Boom~ Boom~
Tall city walls, mighty guard armies, sharp crossbows, solid walls—all of these were their pride.
But under the outrageous cleansing by the alchemy bombs, all were destroyed as easily as paper, and the half-elves, utterly unprepared for the alchemy bombs, had become live targets.
Incendiary bombs, shrapnel, and even poison fog bombs, blinding bombs, and various other alchemy bombs with special capabilities were launched, inflicting even more exaggerated damage to the half-elves’ army with compound damage.
This was a crushing blow of technological superiority; the two sides were not even on the same level.
The tactics used against Naga City were now replicated in Liusi City.
And the most formidable aspect of technology was, even if you knew the strength of your opponent, if you lacked the means to counter, it was in vain; you could only take the hits.
Exaggerated range, terrifying power; the half-elves experienced for the first time just how sharp the blade of Dawn City was.
"Quick, go and find His Majesty!"
"What’s happening? Why is there such chaos at the front line?"
"What’s that noise?"
The supervising half-elf officers in the rear, who had been confident watching whole regions of the wall engulfed in flames, suddenly had very ugly expressions on their faces.
Those damned heretics, why do they possess such powerful weapons??
Wasn’t intelligence saying that these alchemy bombs were scarce and could only be dropped by bats?!
Those damned intelligence officers should be hanged!
"Black Beak Giant Eagles, organize an attack immediately, and destroy those cursed catapults!"
"Mage Group, cast spells!"
"Quick, go ask His Majesty for support..."
The officer corps became a chaotic mess, and after intense clamoring, whoosh—a transparent Magic Shield suddenly rose above the walls of Liusi City, enveloping the whole city within it.
The Half-Elven Spellcasters had begun to act.
Whoosh—
When the Alchemy Bombs below were hurled again, they bounced off like they had hit putty and were flung away. The Alchemy Bombs, which needed a severe impact to detonate, couldn’t be triggered against the Magic Shield.
Then, those Alchemy Bombs failed to achieve their previous effectiveness, falling beneath the city walls and exploding harmlessly. How many Alchemy Bombs would it take to bring down the walls that were several hundreds of blades thick??
Lide observed this scene from the rear with a calm expression, his eyes showing no significant shift.
In the end, this was a world of magic; it wasn’t too surprising that the enemy could resist the attack of Alchemy Bombs if they were prepared.
However... could a single small Magic Shield stop the power amassed by Dawn after so long?
Upon seeing two attacks without effect, the Bombarding Corps’ Commander immediately changed the order.
"Switch to Magic Bombs!"
Whoosh—orders were absolute.
Soldiers immediately took out specially marked boxes next to the ammunition depot, then carried out bright white Magic Bombs from within to replace the already loaded regular Alchemy Bombs.
After thousands upon thousands of training sessions, the soldiers could operate the bomb trucks with their eyes closed. Once the replacement was completed, the Commander, without hesitation, bellowed furiously,
"Fire!"
As the roar echoed, click, click—the magically powered bomb trucks shone brilliantly, then burst forth with immense energy. The launchers, already loaded with significant tension, were once more infused with power.
Boom—the launchers snapped, and the Magic Bombs, making a whooshing sound as they cut through the air, swarmed toward Liusi City like locusts.
The Half-Elven soldiers who’d narrowly survived the artillery barrage had just caught their breath when they witnessed the epic spectacle above their heads.
The dense swarm of Alchemy Bombs should have been repelled by the Magic Shield, but those white Magic Bombs didn’t bounce away upon impact.
Instead, the energy from the Magic Shield activated the Magic Arrays inside the Magic Bombs, then—boom, boom, boom—
The heavens and earth seemed to collapse.
The tens of thousands of Magic Bombs erupted directly on the Magic Shield.
The terrifying shockwaves were like a Category 12 hurricane, sweeping down from the sky.
The skies were filled with flames like oversized fireworks, gorgeous yet bearing a lethal essence—beacons of death.
The originally thick Magic Shield, under such a horrific impact, dwindled quickly like melting snow, its Magic Energy consumed at an extremely exaggerated rate.
Magic Arrays were strong, but they had one fatal—or rather, insurmountable—flaw: to resist external attacks, they could only consume their own Magic Energy.
The impact from the tens of thousands of exploding Magic Bombs directly brought the Magic Array, which once stored terrifying energy, to the brink of collapse.
To offset an equal impact, how much Magic Energy would be needed? It was not just exaggerated.
It was simply indescribable.
In several Mage Towers inside Liusi City, the Magic Arrays providing energy for the Magic Shield, under the watch of the Half-Elven Spellcasters, crackled like short-circuiting wires, bursting with countless sparks.
Then, due to the immense overload, the Magic Circuits overloaded, and boom—the Magic Arrays burst simultaneously like balloons.
Fortunately, because most of the magic energy had been consumed, there was no large explosion; otherwise, the burst of the Magic Array would have certainly devoured everything within a hundred blades’ range.
When the Half-body Mage realized what was happening, it was already too late to do anything; he could only roll and crawl in panic to report to his superiors—heavy with the knowledge that their Magic Array had lasted a mere minute...
Watching the Magic Shield being shattered, Lide’s expression remained calm.
Ever since Dawn City had developed, more resources were available to support the Dawn Mage Tower, weapons factories, and Alchemy Factories, which were scientific research units.
The goblins may have had many shortcomings, but their talent in making Alchemy Bombs was truly exceptional. Lide had previously given them some tips to research different kinds of Alchemy Bombs to deal with various situations, thus strengthening their foundation.
Unexpectedly, the goblins were indeed capable, having developed all kinds of strange Alchemy Bombs.
The Magic Bomb designed to target Magic Shields was one among them. It contained a corresponding Magic Array, which, upon contact with a strong magical force, would activate and set off the explosion.
To prevent accidental detonation of the Magic Bombs, their white shells were made of a material that insulated against magic energy, only connecting the Magic Circuit when the pin was pulled.
These settings made the Magic Bomb a powerful weapon against magical defense measures such as Magic Shields.
Similarly, Dawn City, in its flourishing state, had many more weapons like this. In a safe, affluent environment with abundant resources, the scientific researchers carried many of Lide’s expectations, and their output was indeed satisfying.
"Advance 200 blades forward and continue the bombardment!"
After the Magic Shield was breached, the forward Commander immediately gave the order.
The walls and area behind them had already been bombarded once; continuing the bombardment would have been less effective.
Upon receiving the orders, the Bombarding Corps expertly carried the bomb trucks forward, the posture of their movement showing they were well-trained.
The surrounding army also advanced to cover them, preventing any enemy sneak attacks.
Soon enough, the advancing goblin bomb trucks were launching a new round of bombardment.
It took a moment for the Half-Elves to recover from their daze, and before the high-ranking officers could come up with a counter-plan, an even more ferocious artillery strike descended.
Looking at the flames inside the city, the Half-Elf leaders’ complexions turned as unsightly as if they had swallowed dead rats.
What the hell is going on?? Where’s the Magic Shield? Wasn’t it just activated?
When they looked up, there was no trace of any Magic Shield in the sky, just bare white.
Boom~ Boom~ Boom~
The area behind the walls of Liusi City was a military zone, and advancing 200 blades meant they were now less than 500 blades away from the wall.
The goblin bomb trucks, now fitted with magic devices, had a launch range that had surpassed 1500 blades, meaning everything within 1000 blades behind the walls was within striking distance.
The Half-Elves, just recently overflowing with confidence, for the first time experienced what it meant to feel despair against Dawn City’s army.
The howling black Alchemy Bombs were like the scythe of the Death God; each one hitting the ground caused the earth to tremble.
The sweeping shockwaves and flames became immense, lethal mouths of a demon.
Lide shook his head as he watched the army’s advance.
He found warfare quite dull when technology outclassed the adversary by a level.
It was like an adult fighting a child.
Moreover, the enemy’s aerial forces were tied down by the Magic Language Bats; with air superiority thanks to their airborne crossbows, the Magic Language Bats had a significant advantage over the Black Beak Giant Eagles, deterring the enemy from risking an attack on the bombarding troops below.
"How lonely it is, like the falling snow... Without the presence of top-tier combat power, Dawn City’s army, armed with these Alchemy Bombs, could sweep across half of Glory..."
"Truth only exists within the range of artillery, and this saying, it turns out, is true."
The range of the goblin bomb trucks, after magical modification, was nearly double that of the standard catapults.
What could the Half-Elves use to fight against Dawn City?
The most powerful crossbows of the Half-Elves had a shooting distance of only four to five hundred blades, and their heavy weaponry such as siege engines not more than six to seven hundred blades. Under the exaggerated range of the goblin bomb trucks, such short distances were all easy targets.
Even if there were a few weapons that could reach the bomb trucks, the number of bomb trucks totaled up to 2000—destroying a few dozen, or even a hundred, did nothing significant.
Tucked away underneath mountain fortifications and relying on firing holes for attacks, the Half-Elves did survive in numbers.
But against the forces of Dawn City, their efforts were a drop in the bucket, especially when the Blood Clan Spellcaster team stepped forward to cast spells and shielded the goblin bomb trucks with Magic Shields; the situation became even more embarrassing.
In the end, even Lide couldn’t help but reflect.
"No wonder in those myths and legends left behind, goblins once ruled this world—the lost era was also known as the Alchemy Era.
Although alchemy and Earth’s technology are fundamentally different, the underlying logic still resembles each other."
The Unfallen City, considered by the Half-Elves to be impregnable, lost most of its ability to resist before it even collided with the army of Dawn City.
Technology changes war...
But Lide didn’t take the situation lightly because the better the situation, the more intense the war would become, as the opponents’ ultimate trump card was not some unscalable walls but the ultimate existence in this world—Divine beings.
Even if the Half-Body God had lost much of his power after the fall, such an entity, regardless of his current strength, always warranted caution.
Who knew what kind of trick a god might have up his sleeve? If he could possess so many trump cards, wouldn’t his opponent as well?
The war continued, but the current situation could hardly be called a war anymore; it was a one-sided crushing,
The goblin trebuchets had advanced within three hundred blades of the city walls after several rounds of bombing, and the surrounding army had also closed in.
The Half-Elves probably couldn’t imagine that Dawn City had only shown a portion of their weapons, and their main city, containing all their power, was nearly defenseless.
No one knew how many Half-Elves had died under the bombardment of alchemy bombs, not even the Half-Elves themselves could tally.
They only knew that the prepared defense areas for resisting the enemy were now, aside from a few who escaped, mostly buried in a sea of fire.
A sense of despair began to spread within Liusi City, and those believers who were full of confidence that they could annihilate the intruding enemy were now clueless.
Why, under the protection of a god, were they still beaten so badly?
At this moment, the atmosphere inside the Half-Elf temple was also extremely heavy.
All the Half-Elf high-ranking officials watched the battlefield reflected in the Magic Mirror half-suspended in the air, their expressions stiff, eyes filled with anger and indescribable fear.
That damn God of Twilight, why does he possess such terrifying firepower?
They had thought that the walls of Liusi City would hold for at least a few days, but to their surprise, not even a Sunshine Hour—no, ten minutes—had passed before they were bombarded to the ground...
At this rate, their army might not even come into contact with the enemy before the city fell.
With that thought, the gaze of the Half-Elf high-ranking officials involuntarily turned towards the Half-Elf God seated on the divine altar.
"Your Majesty..."
Seeing this, the Half-Elf God took a deep breath, his face also looking a bit unsightly.
He had calculated everything, yet he had not foreseen how fierce the army of Dawn City would be. He had hoped to ambush them when they could not take down the city walls.
Now the ambush was pointless; if he waited any longer, the whole city would be gone.
He turned his head to look down at the high-ranking Half-Elves eagerly watching him, his tone grim.
"I will lure the God of Twilight into my Divine Country, and when the time comes, you must immediately lead the army to crush his followers!"
"The Underworld can only belong to the Half-Elves!"
Upon hearing the words of the Half-Elf God, morale that had plummeted to rock bottom surged violently as everyone shouted loudly in anger.
"Yes, as long as that damned heretic god is dead, victory in this war will still be ours!"
"Your Majesty, rest assured, the Half-Elf army will surely trample over those damned cultists!"
"Your Glory will guide us to victory..."
Looking at the frenzied crowd below, the Half-Elf God took a deep breath and decided to make his move.
If he waited any longer, the city would be gone.
"Go down and command the troops; the Divine War is about to begin!"
No sooner had the sound of his voice lingered than his figure vanished within the temple.
The leading legendary Half-Elf noticed the disappearance of the Half-Elf God’s presence, and with an excited expression turned his head and glanced at the surrounding Half-Elves, his tone fervent.
"The Divine War led by His Majesty will surely be victorious, that damned God of Twilight won’t possibly escape the siege of the three Divine beings!
Return to the army at once, we will capture the entire legion of the God of Twilight, and they will all become new believers of His Majesty!"
This statement immediately made the already high morale swell even more.
Victory was surely theirs, and everyone held the firmest belief in this.
The God of Twilight? Ha, let’s see if he even survives...
Outside of Liusi City, the advancing Dawn Army suddenly halted its steps.
This was because an extremely terrifying presence was spreading out from the sky at this moment.
It was as if a primordial giant beast that had existed since ancient times had crawled out from the depths of the ocean, its brutal eyes coldly surveying the earth.
Majestic and overwhelming.
The terrifying spiritual pressure spread across the entire sky, making it seem as though the heavens and earth were being trampled underfoot at that moment.
It was the divine pressure of a god, the most primordial breath, and all the armies felt a deadly danger as if their souls would shatter and explode if they took one more step forward.
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly.
The ultimate boss had finally made an appearance.
"God of Twilight... after a million years, why do you attack my main city, kill my followers?"
The voice, tinged with anger, boomed through the sky like rolling thunder and struck down, causing the lower-level warriors in the army below to go weak at the knees, almost kneeling.
The pressure from a divine being was unavoidable; it penetrated the soul.
Lide’s eyes narrowed.
What act are you trying to pull in front of me?
With a single step, his body materialized in midair.
He looked coldly at the amber-glowing sphere in the sky, his tone flat.
"Attack your main city? Kill your followers?..."
"And what if I did?"
The Half-Elf God was startled by his words, and instantly, his blood boiled, his face turning crimson with rage.
"God of Twilight, you are provoking me. Do you want to start a Divine War?!"
"Divine War?" Lide chuckled.
"Do you even qualify?"
I!!!
The Half-Elf God, who had just planned to put on airs and later kill Lide to reap faith, was enraged at this moment.
This damned bastard!!
How dare he! How dare he provoke him so?!
As a divine being, how many years had it been since anyone had dared to treat him this way?!
"You’re seeking your own death!!"
The Half-Elf God roared in rage and then, under the eyes of a million-strong army below, charged directly at Lide.
It seemed that Lide’s provocation had enraged him, as he sought to collide head-on.
Lide’s expression was quite wry. Who knew that there were still those keen on court death these days?
Although the Half-Elf God emitted a powerful aura, Lide had already sensed that while the man appeared strong, he was actually full of bluster and his acting skills weren’t even half as good as Lide’s own.
As an expert in this regard, Lide saw right through the Half-Elf God; his power was, at most, legendary, not even close to a demigod.
No, the rage... it was feigned.
Lide’s eyes sharpened, his thoughts whirling. The Half-Elf God was not a combat deity, so there must be a reason he dared to do this. Should he dodge?
But after glancing at the scimitar slung around his waist, his expression settled back into calm...
Sorry, no matter what scheme you have, this time I’ve borrowed a knife you could never imagine...
All this may seem lengthy, but it happened in the blink of an eye. Just as the Half-Elf God came within striking distance of Lide, the raging fury on his face suddenly changed, a glint of pleasure in his eyes.
"Shatter!"
With a shout, the sky exploded in unison, and the radius around Lide was immediately enveloped by a force. Without even time to blink, the whole world vanished.
Everything whirled.
A few breaths later, Lide appeared in a bleak space.
The ground was made of fleeting illusions and the sky was a dim murkiness; it very much resembled a plane that had just been destroyed.
What made Lide’s expression incredibly rich, however, were the three figures that appeared before him... He had not expected the Half-Elf God to pull such a move, directly dragging him into a plane, and obviously a well-designed trap, plotting three against one...
The Half-Elf God, looking at Lide’s peculiar expression, revealed a cold smile on his face.
"Did you really think I could be provoked by your clumsy taunt?
Ha ha ha, God of Twilight, you’ve been ambushed by us!!"

chapters.title: Chapter 446 - 448: Killing Three Divines, Astonishing Gains
chapters.content:
Chapter 446: Chapter 448: Killing Three Divines, Astonishing Gains
In a space filled with dim and void light.
Lide heard the words of the Half-Elf God, his expression rather odd.
Ambushed?
Do people still shout before ambushing in this day and age? Was his brain kicked by a donkey?
From the corner of his eye, he surveyed the area and saw two dwarves clad in solid armor, wielding war hammers and battle axes.
However, unlike typical dwarves, these two had beards and skin that exhibited an indescribable shade of gray.
Gray Dwarves.
A playful look appeared in Lide’s eyes.
"Half-Elf, is this what you rely on? Two trash Gray Dwarves just like you?"
If Withered Bone were here, he’d surely have screamed in delight; this was real provocation, unlike his long, ineffective rants.
True enough, all three Divine Beings were enraged by Lide’s words.
The Half-Elf God could still bear it, but the two tempestuous Gray Dwarf Divine Beings couldn’t contain their fury.
"Damn God of Twilight, you despicable vampire!! You should be suffocated by goat’s excrement!!"
"How dare you insult the great Gray Dwarves? Believe me, once I catch you, you’ll learn what the most painful punishment in the world is!"
"..."
After the Gray Dwarves spat a few curses, a chilling smile suddenly surfaced on the face of the Half-Elf God.
"God of Twilight, did you think I bantered with you just to hear your inept rage that is on the verge of annihilation?
Ha ha ha ha, this void is my Divine Country, although I can only use less than ten percent of its power now...
But, once the Magic Array inscribed within the Divine Country is activated, even if you regain the power of a Demigod, you will still not escape death today!!"
As he finished speaking, the area around Lide suddenly changed; the wind howled, and lightning flashed.
Silver Dragon Lightning furiously surged around the area, instantly forming a Thunder Cage, isolating the space where Lide stood.
f r\ee.c(o)(m)
At that moment, Lide even saw rules flowing above the lightning, clearly a hidden killer move from the Half-Elf God who had long harbored these plans.
Watching Lide trapped within the Thunder, the Half-Elf God’s face broke into a wildly excited smile.
This detestable vampire, still fell for his trap!
As long as he killed this vampire, he would take over the dominion of the Underworld...
He could then use the resources of the Underworld to fully recover to his peak.
Moreover, if handled properly, he could also invade the surface world after regaining his power, conquering vast territories, using this opportunity to advance to Medium Divine Power, and even evolve into a Powerful Divine Being!!
Thinking of the glorious prospects ahead, the Half-Elf God’s smile grew increasingly maniacal.
Lide, looking at the near hopeless situation onstage, revealed an expression brimming with intrigue.
"Could it be that I can’t escape this space?"
With a Thunder Cage in front and three Divine Beings circling like tigers, it seemed unlikely he could escape.
The Half-Elf God burst into laughter upon hearing this.
"Escape? This is my Divine Country!!
To ensure your certain death, I have sealed off this region; even if you have allies, they absolutely cannot enter from the outside world!!
Right now, even I would struggle to leave, let alone you?!"
"God of Twilight, after your death, your believers, your Divine Status, everything will belong to me!!"
Upon hearing these words, Lide blinked and flashed a brilliant smile.
"In that case, I’m relieved."
Huh?
Seeing Lide’s unusual expression, all three Divine Beings paused, but before they could react, Lide suddenly drew the longsword strapped at his waist and threw it straight out.
"Dark Sovereign, the soul I gift to you has arrived..."
Boom boom boom~
At that moment, the heavens and earth darkened.
The longsword flying in midair struck the Thunder Cage directly, and Silver Dragons danced wildly as the lightning struck the blade.
The longsword, emitting a dark glow, seemed provoked, and a dazzling power erupted from it, like an ancient behemoth tearing through the sky, charging forth.
This force burst forth, creating a massive shockwave.
Splash~
As it swept through, the Thunder Cage, which was condensed from rules, was like a piece of paper in a raging storm, instantly torn apart.
After the shockwave dispersed, the Thunder Cage was directly annihilated, leaving behind only a burnt smell in the air, with no trace left behind.
The Magic Array that the Half-Elf God had placed his hopes on was so easily ripped apart.
While the Divine Beings were still in shock, the light from the longsword erupted once again.
Terrifying energy gathered in the void, forming an imposing phantom wearing a Golden Crown, draped in a human-skin cloak, holding a White Bone Sword, its presence shaking both heaven and earth.
Undead Plane’s fifteenth Monarch—Dark Sovereign.
At this moment, this shadowy space of nothingness trembled in fear...
No one could describe the intensity of the aura when the phantom appeared; it was as if three Divine Spirits stood like children at the foot of a towering mountain, facing the majestic might of the heavens.
The moment the Dark Sovereign appeared, he sensed everything in this void plane.
As an Undead Monarch, his power was terrifying, having long surpassed the limits imaginable in this world; even though his main body was located in numerous planes away, he still maintained an undefeatable stance.
"Dawn Main God... are these the gifts you have brought for me?"
The cold tone of the Dark Sovereign carried a trace of barely detectable surprise; originally, Lide had mentioned only one Divine Spirit, but now three had unexpectedly emerged.
Is this a buy-one-get-two deal? Truly a worthy ally...
"Dark Sovereign, to hunt the souls of these three Divine Spirits, I have spent much effort and paid a considerable price to lure them into the trap.
But since they are gifts for you, all that I have expended is worthwhile.
Feel free to take their souls; just leave their Divine Bodies to me."
Lide’s words were noble and righteous; moved within, the Dark Sovereign felt that he indeed had a worthwhile ally...
Upon hearing this, the three Divine Spirits standing nearby began to tremble.
They sensed the terrifying presence of the Dark Sovereign; though only a phantom, his imposing aura was indescribable.
With their knowledge, they naturally understood that such a terrifying being was beyond their ability to challenge; even in their prime, they had no choice but to flee from such a being.
Not to mention that their current strength was less than five percent of what it had been at their peak...
The previously confident Half-Elf God almost spat out blood when he heard Lide’s words.
Pointing at Lide, his face wore an expression of disbelief mixed with resentment.
"You... you actually plotted against me??!!"
Lide’s mouth twitched, How was I supposed to know you were such a fool, not only trapping yourself in this plane but also dragging two Gray Dwarf Divine Spirits along as reinforcements...
Of course, he would not disclose in front of the Dark Sovereign that all this was the Half-Elf God’s own doing...
At this moment, the Half-Elf God only thought that he had fallen into Lide’s trap, filled with regret and relief that he did not know the truth, or else he might have died from rage.
He thought Lide had deeply plotted from the fifth layer, but his opponent did not move at all, firmly sticking to the first layer...
Lide spoke leisurely, "Dark Sovereign, this is the Half-Elf God’s Divine Country, he might have other last resorts. Act quickly, finish early..."
The Half-Elf God’s complexion stiffened further, his resentment intensifying, but his trickery sped up behind the scenes.
He dared not harbor anger towards the Dark Sovereign and directed all his fury towards Lide.
If he could escape, he swore he would chase Lide, the God of Twilight, to the ends of the earth and sky!!
The most unlucky were the two Gray Dwarf Divine Spirits; all this happened in the span of a few breaths.
They had just finished cursing and were not yet satisfied when they found themselves trapped in a Thunder Cage, like lambs awaiting slaughter, and Lide who had no respect for martial virtue shook them directly, summoning the extremely terrifying existence of the Dark Sovereign.
At that moment, both wished they could slap the Half-Elf God to death.
Didn’t you assure us that the God of Twilight was alone??
Wasn’t it supposed to be foolproof?
Now even a Divine Spirit with Powerful Divine Power has appeared!!
After the olden days had passed, only the terrifying Divine Spirits from the Abyss and the Undead Plane could maintain such formidable Divine Power.
The two Gray Dwarf Divine Spirits despaired upon realizing this; with their current power, facing the Evil Gods from both Land of Extreme Evil, the Abyss, and the Undead, was simply suicidal!
The Dark Sovereign, although only a simple phantom, seemed like an eternal stele suppressing the heavens, frightening everyone deeply.
Those hollow eye sockets eerily glanced at the Half-Elf God, seeming to detect something, as the Undead Profanity echoed throughout the space.
"Thinking of escaping?"
The Half-Elf God’s face changed drastically, and he quickly spoke respectfully.
"Respected Lord of the Undead, I am willing to offer all my wealth to you, just let me leave...
No, I am willing to serve you; you don’t need to lift a finger, I will hunt these two Gray Dwarf Divine Spirits for you right now and offer their souls to you..."
The Half-Elf God was ruthless, betraying his allies without even blinking.
The two Gray Dwarf Divine Spirits, upon hearing this, looked as if they had swallowed dead rats, utterly disgusted.
If they knew any swear words, they’d likely point at the Half-Elf God’s nose and curse... Fuck your damn ancestor, you rat, you not only screwed us over, but you also plan to stab us in the back!
Meanwhile, during the conversation, the space next to the Half-Elf God suddenly shattered; his previously cautious face revealed a trace of madness, and with one step, he vanished from the spot.
The guy actually used that brief moment to escape...
Not far away, the two Gray Dwarf Divine Spirits saw the Half-Elf God open the space and showed a bit of joy, but before they could even blink, the space closed.
Their hearts felt like a roller coaster plummeting from heaven directly into hell.
Their current hatred for the Half-Elf God surpassed even their hatred for Lide... This bastard is too vile.
Running away was one thing, but the fact he did not take them with him, leaving them to die was too cruel!!
Lide frowned, impressed they could still escape?
But just as he was about to speak, the Dark Sovereign’s phantom swiftly drew the White Bone Sword.
At that moment, the sun and moon ceased their paths, the stars dimmed, and even the void around them seemed to stop rotating.
A terrifying pressure, like a mountain high in the sky plummeting down, struck everyone with the most shocking impact.
The Dark Sovereign lightly waved the White Bone Sword toward the empty space ahead, and then a force that seemed undetectable, indescribable, and ineffable overwhelmingly surged forth.
The space before him exploded as if a giant rock had smashed into a cement floor.
Crack~
The sound of the space shattering was crisp to the ear, and the Half-Elf God, who had just disappeared, now spat out blood from his mouth and fell out of the dimension.
This sword had severed countless planes, cutting off the escape route of the Half-Elf who was already fleeing.
The majesty of the Monarch dazzled all onlookers.
The perpetrator, the Dark Sovereign, slowly sheathed his White Bone Sword, as if none of it had ever happened.
But it was this kind of understatement that made the three Divine beings he was watching struggle even to breathe.
Especially the Half-Elf God, now ashen-faced and spitting blood, his heart had been engulfed by despair.
He had just invoked the power of the Divine Country, escaping directly through countless layers of Dimension Space.
Normally, it would be impossible to find him amidst the myriad Dimensional Planes, but even so, the Dark Sovereign had severed his route of escape with a single stroke, making his escape impossible.
Had it been his heyday, he might have had a chance to leave by mobilizing the full power of the Divine Country, but now... he smelled the scent of Death.
"Great Undead Lord, I am willing to offer my soul, I am willing to offer everything..."
Under the pressure of death, the face of the Half-Elf God showed endless terror, and without any hesitation, he got up and knelt on both knees before the Dark Sovereign, bowing down.
The Gray Dwarf God beside him felt an inexplicable sense of relief at this scene—this damned fool deserved to meet Death!!
The Dark Sovereign turned his head to glance at Lide; although it was just a phantom, its deep blue Soul Fire was still dazzling.
"Dawn Main God, I accept your gift..."
After saying this, without waiting for Lide’s response, those empty eyes again intimidated the three Divine beings, evidently ready to make a move.
The Gray Dwarf Gods looked at each other, knowing that this time they might not escape again, but they would not admit defeat!
Surrender meant certain death, but if they could shatter this phantom, they might still have a chance to live.
With gritted teeth, they each raised their battle-axes and hammers, unleashing all their power, causing the space around them to tremble and distort under their Divine Power.
As Divine beings, even though they were only of Legendary rank now, their full might was not to be underestimated.
The two Gray Dwarf Gods, like meteors from shattered stars, charged at the Dark Sovereign with unstoppable force.
"Such...weak and foolish resistance..."
The Undead Profanity at this moment was like a resonating doomsday bell, booming loudly.
Seeing the two attack, the White Bone Sword in the hands of the Dark Sovereign swung out fiercely again.
Crack~
This time even Lide couldn’t sense any energy fluctuations, the two Gray Dwarf Gods, whose desperate stances had warped space,
suddenly stiffened in midair, then all the power they had gathered dispersed, and their bodies fell like kites with cut strings.
But due to the powerful inertia, they skidded dozens of yards across the void ground before stopping.
When Lide sensed their presence again, he found that the souls of the two Gray Dwarf Gods had vanished.
Double kill with one sword.
Lide immediately had a newfound respect for the Dark Sovereign; although this Undead was a bit blunt, its strength was absolutely incredible, instantly killing two gods with a single sword stroke wasn’t just powerful.
Although the two Gray Dwarf Gods had lost most of their power, don’t forget, the Dark Sovereign was also just a phantom appearing on the Main Plane.
The Half-Elf God, still kneeling, sensing all this, felt his blood chill; two Divine beings! He had originally hoped that these two Gray Dwarf Gods would unleash their final trump card and hold off the Dark Sovereign for a while so he could escape again.
But now, that was a pipe dream.
A single sword slaying two gods, how terrifying.
At this moment, the Half-Elf God could only repeat, like his believers, words of surrender and becoming a Subordinate God, humbly praying and bowing.
The Dark Sovereign looked at the kneeling Half-Elf God, took a step forward, and his figure suddenly appeared before him.
Feeling the terrifying pressure approaching, the Half-Elf God shuddered.
"Great Undead Lord, I am willing to become your most loyal servant, willing to become your Undead Subordinate God, I am willing to offer the entire Half-Elf race as nourishment for you, great Undead Lord, your humble servant pleads for your forgiveness..."
Lide felt somewhat emotional upon hearing this.
The Half-Elf God wasn’t very capable, but he was certainly ruthless.
To survive, he could even abandon the race he once protected; this guy had completely lost his bottom line.
But, it must be said, sometimes such people might live longer...
The Dark Sovereign’s empty eyes watched the continuously bowing Half-Elf God, without a ripple in his heart.
"Are you still running?"
"No, not running anymore, great Lord, your glory is enough to dim the Creator God, how could I possibly escape your grasp? I..."
The Half-Elf God raised his head, looking almost madly at the Dark Sovereign, but before he could finish speaking, the ephemeral White Bone Sword in the Dark Sovereign’s hand flashed.
Pfft~
Cut in two.
The Divine Body of the Half-Elf God remained intact, but his soul was severed by this strike... and instantly lost all signs of life.
Seeing this, the Dark Sovereign slightly raised the White Bone Sword, and then a fierce wind erupted.
The souls of the three slain Divine beings, as if pulled by something, flew out from their bodies and were directly absorbed by the White Bone Sword.
If one were to look closely at the blade of the White Bone Sword, they would see three new marks abruptly appear—two Gray Dwarfs and one Half-Elf... and such marks were scattered all over the entire White Bone Sword.
Breaking the norm to become the fifteenth monarch of the Undead Plane, how could this terrifying existence’s journey be simple?
The Divine blood stained on his hands likely exceeded everyone’s imagination.
Lide’s expression became exceedingly complex upon witnessing this scene.
The knife wielded by the Dark Sovereign was unimaginably sharp.
"Dawn Main God, I have already separated their souls from their bodies. Their Divine Statuses are still intact. I’m very satisfied with this gift."
The Dark Sovereign, having completed the task, came over to Lide with a bit of joy.
By seizing the souls of three Divines in a single move and due to their diminished strength, the souls he stripped were even more intact.
He could fully utilize them to cultivate several Divine Monsters as his subordinates; this acquisition was incredibly substantial.
Lide slightly smiled upon seeing this.
The pinnacle of using someone else’s strength to kill was that the other party helped him solve a significant problem and even felt indebted to him.
If it weren’t for the Dark Sovereign, he would have been trapped alone in the God of Half-body God’s Divine Country and encircled by three Divines.
Although he had absolute confidence in his own power, he likely wouldn’t have achieved significant results in the end.
The most likely outcome would have been both sides suffering heavy losses.
Now that the Dark Sovereign had made a move, everything changed.
Now, he had three Divine Bodies in his possession... It was incredibly audacious.
Although the three Divine Bodies had lost their souls, he least cared about souls as he had no means of controlling the souls of the deceased. Instead, the value of the Divine Bodies was more precious to him.
This round, he sat back and watched the show, and even made some profit by owing the Dark Sovereign a favor. It was exhilarating.
The gains were substantial.
"Dark Sovereign, my friend...
This is a testament to our friendship. I will continue to stay on the Main Plane for a while, until I achieve my goal.
If I encounter these Divines descending to the Main Plane in the meantime, I will activate the power in the scimitar with Divine Power. You can prepare to descend when you sense it.
If it is not a battle, my call will be lighter..."
Upon hearing this, the Soul Fire of the Dark Sovereign surged dramatically. This wasn’t over yet? His mood improved even more.
"Good, just call me when you encounter these Divines..."
At this moment, the Undead Monarch’s fondness for Lide skyrocketed. He was incredibly pleased to have made such a reliable ally.
