Lide’s smile was also radiant. This knife was really useful...
But he suddenly seemed to remember something, turned his head to look at the long scimitar in his hand, and couldn’t help but shake his head.
"Dark Sovereign, do you have any other equipment that can carry your power? This scimitar is too conspicuous and not suitable for my identity."
Hearing this, the Dark Sovereign nodded slightly, "Indeed."
Then, with a wave of his hand, that scimitar flew straight to his side.
Under Lide’s watch, the scimitar melted like ice and snow, and the most essential part of the material slowly condensed into a ring engraved with mysterious inscriptions.
After the ring formed, it flew back to Lide’s hand.
"This ring contains my Divine Power. You just need to input power to activate the Divine Power within it, and I will immediately sense it."
Lide took the ring and openly wore it on his hand in front of the Dark Sovereign, showing immense trust.
Upon seeing this, the Dark Sovereign became even more satisfied with Lide.
"Until next time, Dawn Main God."
"Goodbye."
Whoosh~ The Dark Sovereign’s phantom directly dispersed, transforming into energy that all flowed into the ring on Lide’s finger.
Once the Dark Sovereign’s presence had completely disappeared, Lide smiled. With the system, he was well aware of any potential harm from the ring.
Dark Magic Ring
Quality: Special Item
Skill: Summon Undead Monarch (can summon the real body of the Dark Sovereign through the Dark Magic Ring)
Description: A tool gifted by the Dark Sovereign to the Dawn Main God, limited to the Dawn Main God’s use. Attributes cannot be viewed by others; anyone else attempting to activate it will face the wrath of the Dark Sovereign.
Well, it’s a limited item, and if it’s not activated by him, he would face the Dark Sovereign.
Lide was quite pleased with this, seeing it as a lifesaver, being able to summon an Undead Monarch as a hitman at any time; he wouldn’t trade it for a pile of gold.
And if he encounters someone irritating in the future, perhaps he could entice them to activate this Magic Ring and see what their reaction would be when they face the Dark Sovereign.
Delightful.
After reviewing the properties a few times, Lide finally adjusted his mood.
After some contemplation, still with a cautious mindset, he completely isolated the Dark Magic Ring using the Power of Faith. Unless he summoned, the ring on his hand wouldn’t sense any external presence.
While he knew the Dark Sovereign wouldn’t harm him, it still counted as double insurance.
Once he confirmed it was safe, his gaze shifted to the three Divine Bodies and the battle axe and war hammer dropped by the Gray Dwarf on the null land.
These were the greatest gains of the day...

chapters.title: Chapter 447 - 449: Conquering the Underworld, the Only Sovereign
chapters.content:
Chapter 447: Chapter 449: Conquering the Underworld, the Only Sovereign
Three Divine Bodies, two weapons...
Lide looked at the scene with a beaming smile.
Especially the two weapons of the God of Grey Dwarves piqued his interest, could these be the legendary... Divine Artifacts?
He approached with great anticipation, then focused his attention on the weapons.
He opened the attribute panel.
War God’s Hammer
Quality: Legendary★
Skill: ...
Description: A war hammer forged in imitation of a Divine Artifact.
Fierce Axe
Quality: Legendary★
Skill: ...
Description: A giant axe forged as a counterfeit Divine Artifact.
At first glance at the name, Lide thought he had struck gold, but his heart sank when he saw their attributes.
"This is outrageous, for a Divine to wield fake Divine Artifacts, I’m embarrassed for you... No wonder you’re in such a sorry state, pah."
Lide glared harshly at the two figures; they were just Legendary Items, and merely one-star at that—what a waste of his expression.
"Is it that these two don’t own Divine Artifacts, or can’t they bring them down when descending to the Main Plane?"
Though filled with questions, with everyone dead, there was no one to answer them.
"If only I had let the Dark Sovereign interrogate these guys, what a missed opportunity..."
But after the rant, Lide still cheerfully picked up the two weapons from the ground. Though he couldn’t use them himself, they were free loot after all.
In this battle, apart from throwing his sabre, he had just watched; not having to lift a finger and still gaining so much was not bad at all.
After storing the weapons in the System Space, his spiritual power spread out to sense the three Divine Bodies carefully, and after a moment, he nodded with satisfaction.
Indeed, as the Dark Sovereign had said, all three had their Divine Statuses intact.
Though they had lost their power, the core of their Divine Status and Divine Position within a Divine would not disappear, unless the Divine died. Even if their Level dropped to 1, the Divine Status would still exist.
However, the power within the Divine Status was now at an extremely low level, incomparable to their peak.
Lide wasn’t too concerned about this; as long as the Divine Status and Divine Bodies were intact, that was what mattered.
With a wave of his hand, a giant Mage’s Hand appeared, and three of its fingers transformed into chains, binding the Divine Bodies together.
Looking at the scene, Lide smiled in satisfaction.
He had just broken through, and his foundation was not yet stable; he couldn’t absorb more Divine Power to break through again in the short term. But these three Divine Bodies could be used to cultivate top-notch combat power.
These were the bodies of Divines, and the Divine Power they contained could bring an immense boost to any of his subordinates who devoured it.
Lide even had confidence that he could create three new Legendaries... and their Divine Statuses could also cultivate several powerful Subordinate Gods.
The gifts the God of Half-body had given him this time were unbelievably lavish.
With this single effort, his ultimate combat power would increase once more.
With five Legendaries in his hands, wouldn’t he be able to stride across the southern provinces at his leisure?
Crack~
Just as Lide had finished, the space began to tremble slowly, with visible cracks appearing around, clearly about to collapse.
Lide glanced around regretfully; this was a corner of the Half-body God’s Divine Country. If given enough time, perhaps he could’ve invaded the opponent’s Divine Country for more spoils.
But now, with the fall of the Half-body God, this piece of the Divine Country was losing its support and on the brink of collapse—there was no time left.
Shaking his head, he no longer lingered. Even if there were treasures, he couldn’t stay; one must live to spend their earnings, and a Planar collapse was no joke, not even a Demigod could necessarily withstand it.
After scanning the surroundings one last time to ensure no treasures were left behind, his mind settled down.
Seeing the cracks in the void growing larger, he waved his hand, shattering the space in front of him, and his form disappeared from this Plane.
A few breaths after Lide left, the Plane cracked directly, the fragments of space whirling about like a Category 12 hurricane, even the surrounding Dimension Planes were battered and perforated.
---
---
---
Underworld, Liusi City.
The Half-Elf higher-ups watched as Lide’s figure was dragged into the Divine Country by the Half-body God, all showing ecstatic expressions.
It’s done.
That was their first thought.
These Half-Elf higher-ups saw victory in this war the moment Lide disappeared.
Surrounded and killed by three powerful Divines, that damned God of Twilight, no matter how capable, was surely doomed.
"The God of Twilight has been dragged into His Majesty Kaplotz’s Divine Country!! The Half-Elves will be eternal!"
"Praise to you, Our Mighty Excellency!"
"Quick, charge with me!! Those damned heretics and lowly Vampires can only kneel before the Half-Elves..."
The Half-Elves, who had just been bombarded into submission by Alchemy Bombs, suddenly surged with adrenaline, rallying to advance under the urging of their leaders.
However, the front of Liusi City was still covered in cannon fire, and they struggled to find a way out, becoming extremely agitated.
Meanwhile, two Legendaries ascended directly, leading the Black Beak Giant Eagle Air Force to launch a counterattack.
Originally, Liusi City had only one Legendary and two Transcendents, but since the Half-body God’s descent, a significant cost had been spent to nurture a batch of subordinates with formidable power.
One of the current Legendaries was forcefully elevated by the Half-body God.
At this moment, the two Legendary Half-Elves led the charge against Dawn’s forces with utter confidence.
In their eyes, the God of Twilight was destined to die, and without him, how could Dawn’s powerful army outside the city fare?
Moreover, the Half-body God had commanded them to conquer this army! They certainly did not want to disappoint His Majesty...
Once the news of the God of Twilight’s death was sensed by the believers, this army would inevitably collapse on its own.
As for whether the God of Twilight would be killed, they had no doubt whatsoever.
"The enemy is preparing to attack from the air, Dawn Wings prepare!!
Caster Corps prepare!!
Centaur Archers prepare!!"
Looking at the sky darkened by the approaching Black Beak Giant Eagle Army like dark clouds pressing upon the city, the commander of the Dawn Legion immediately issued orders.
The robust centaurs instantly drew their bows, which had been improved more than ten times, and arrows made of Fine Gold and abyssal rare metals glinted with lethal radiance.
Magic Power flashed in the hands of the Bloodline, and one after another, spells began to brew in their hands.
Dawn Knights had already soared upward, and the Magic Crossbows, powered by Magic Power on the backs of the Magic Language Bats, were now unleashing their chilling killing intent.
The 26th Level Legendary Undead Blood Dragon Withered Bone, the 25th Level Legendary Beastman King Kapp, along with the 20th Level Transcendent Frost Giant Dragon Altan, three mighty beings, went straight into the air to meet the enemy.
It is worth mentioning that the Golden Power on Kapp’s body was blazing like flames, lifting his entire being.
After reaching Legendary status, even ground forces like the Beastmen had the means to ascend and engage enemies in the air.
"Attack!!"
With a roar that shook heaven and earth, the dark mass of Black Beak Giant Eagles dove straight toward the ranks of the Dawn Legion.
At this moment, the Half-body Mages within Liusi City became like fire extinguishers, and the Half-body Army burst forth from the front, blazing through the section of the wall in flames, creating a path by force,
The morale of the Half-body Army was unprecedentedly high at this moment.
Everyone firmly believed that launching an attack now was merely about reaping honors, and there was no risk of failure.
The great His Majesty had already guided them toward glory!
The Black Beak Giant Eagles collided first with the Magic Language Bats in the aerial battle.
The sharp claws and beaks of the Black Beak Giant Eagles could easily tear through knights’ armor and warriors’ shields, they were absolute killing machines.
Mounted atop them, the Half-body Sky Cavalry archery skills were exceptional, combining both near and far attacks, their combat power in the air was not to be underestimated.
The only pity was that this time they were facing Dawn Wings, the ace Air Force crafted by Lide.
As the sole anti-air power for Dawn City, Lide’s expenditure for this was by no means small.
This time, the ones meeting the Black Beak Giant Eagles head-on were the Magic Language Knights, a troop specifically designed for aerial combat, each Magic Language Bat carried a human Sky Cavalry on its back, and the fixed Magic Crossbows were their strongest weapons.
Over the years, the Magic Crossbow had undergone at least a hundred improvements, and just recently, it was enchanted with magic inscriptions, upgrading it to an advanced form — the Magic Crossbow.
The Magic Crossbow was not only smaller in size but also had more powerful arrow shots, with significantly increased range and precision.
Moreover, thanks to the enhancement by magic, even the downsized bolt could maintain enough destructive power, this provided it with a larger ammunition capacity.
The current Magic Crossbow could continuously shoot forty bolts, doubling the previous capacity of twenty.
It could also fire at a high speed of two bolts per second, emptying the quiver in merely 20 seconds.
When 5,000 Magic Language Knights simultaneously pulled their triggers in the sky, tens of thousands of crossbow bolts furiously shot out every second, creating a scene as shocking as the myths of legend.
Hoo-hoo~ The whistling of the arrows cut through the air like the scream of a demon, their dense number more terrifying than locusts, covering the entire sky.
The Black Beak Giant Eagles, in order to maintain their flying speed, did not wear protective armor over their vital areas like the Magic Language Bats.
Under the barrage of the Magic Crossbows, although they could dodge some bolts with their superb flying skills, there were far too many to avoid completely.
Spurt—
Blood splattered and feathers scattered.
The first batch of Black Beak Giant Eagles was directly pierced by the arrows, and many bolts passed entirely through their bodies, hitting the second Giant Eagle behind with drops of blood dripping down.
The Black Beak Giant Eagles dropped from the sky like rain, crashing into the ground with a series of dull thuds, feathers and blood mixed with dirt splashing up.
Seeing this scene, the faces of the two leading Half-Elf Legendary figures turned pale.
If they continued their charge like this, half of the Black Beak Giant Eagles would die or be wounded before even getting close.
A Legendary Level aura burst forth from them in an instant, surging with unparalleled, terrifying dignity.
It was as if an 18th-level hurricane had suddenly sprung from nowhere.
The huge presence instantly intimidated the Magic Language Bats, causing significant chaos amongst the Magic Language Knight Corps.
Though the Magic Language Bats were strong, their levels were only between 6 to 9, and there were very few Dawn Bats at Level 10. Facing the Legendary foes more than ten levels higher, they were simply not beings of the same dimension.
They let out terrified roars.
The Black Beak Giant Eagles seized this rare opportunity when the arrows thinned, immediately accelerating their approach.
As both sides were charging toward each other, the flight speed was incredibly fast, and within a few breaths, they collided in the air.
Spurt—
Limbs exploded.
Two Magic Language Bats were even ripped apart by the sharp claws of the Giant Eagles, and conversely, after the close approach, the killing power of the Magic Crossbows was greatly enhanced.
The melee fight between the two sides was unspeakably brutal.
The two riders atop the Black Beak Giant Eagles, who were Half-Elf Legends, mercilessly slaughtered the Magic Language Knights, each attack sweeping away and killing more than a dozen robust Magic Language Bats.
Also, because the Air Forces in the sky were quickly entangled in the battle, the Centaur Archers below could not make much of a mark, as the battlefield was too chaotic and random shots could potentially hurt allies.
Led by the Legendary Half-Elves, the Black Beak Giant Eagles managed to gain an advantage in the moment of collision, causing substantial casualties amongst the Magic Language Bats.
But their fortune was quickly ended as Kapp and Lord Withered Bones finally joined the battlefield.
Lord Withered Bones began to shriek loudly.
"Damn these lowly lives, taste Lord Withered Bones’ Dragon Breath!"
"These disgusting beings feasting on worm excrement, you all should be conquered by Lord Withered Bones..."
"Ga-ga-ga~ Fear, scream, tremble..."
"Foolish Half-Elves, to make an enemy of the great Dragon of Destruction was the most idiotic decision your useless brains could make..."
In an instant, the loud cries of Lord Withered Bones attracted the attention of many Half-Elves, and if it were not for the terrifying Legendary aura that emanated from him, many would have probably swarmed him to severely punish this insolent Bone Dragon.
With Legendary and Transcendent support, the Magic Language Knights’ attacks immediately turned fierce, unleashing the Magic Crossbows in their hands in a relentless barrage, spraying both blood and feathers.
The battle between the two sides heated up in the moment of clashing, with dozens of Black Beak Giant Eagles and Magic Language Bats plummeting from the sky every second.
However, due to the excessively hazardous battle above and frequent attacks from swarms of Black Beak Giant Eagles, the siege engines below were forced to halt firing and began to scatter and relocate.
It was during these brief moments that the enraged Half-body Army, which had been smoldering with fury inside the city, finally burst forth from the city gates in a fierce charge.
Four Transcendent individuals led the front, with the Half-body Army behind them exuding a deadly aura.
The more brutal melee combat was about to begin.
All Half-Elves held steadfast confidence—this war, they must win!
The glory of Kaplotz shone upon them, and the great Half-Elves would rule the entire Underworld!
But just as the Centaur Army in front of the Dawn Army was about to counter-charge, the ferocious Half-body Army suddenly stopped in unison, as if the pause button had been pressed.
Confusion filled the faces that were excited a moment ago, as if they had lost something precious.
Some even threw down their weapons on the battlefield and knelt, tears streaming down their faces, in anticipation of worship.
At this moment, great chaos erupted among the Black Beak Giant Eagles in the sky, with a small portion of the Half-Elves driving a number of the giant eagles to flee amidst such intense combat.
Soon, chaos began to spread through the Half-body Army, and the Black Beak Giant Eagles, once swearing death before surrender, dispersed in a rout.
The ground troops, which had just charged out of the city, madly rushed back.
The rapid change of events left all the commanders of Dawn City somewhat baffled.
What is going on??
Do these Half-Elves have dog brains? Stopping the fight halfway through??
Seeing this scene, Kapp in the sky and Lord Withered Bones sensed the crux of the problem—Lide.
After witnessing the collapse and hasty retreat of two Legendaries, a hint of surprise crossed Kapp’s face.
He turned and roared at the army behind him.
"Charge, all forces! The God of Half-Elves has been slain by our Lord!"
Lord Withered Bones also started screaming, hastily pursuing the retreating Black Beak Giant Eagles.
The collapse of the Half-Elves... such a scene could only occur if the entity they relied on faced calamity. Just now, Lide had been ambushed by the God of Half-Elves.
Others might worry about Lide’s safety, but Kapp had just experienced the Dignity of the Dark Sovereign and, far from worrying, even took a few seconds to silently mourn the God of Half-Elves—someone facing the Dark Sovereign courted death, and no one else was to blame.
After the collapse of the Half-Elves, the aerial forces of Dawn City directly broke the Black Beak Giant Eagles.
The ground forces, even more so, formed a steel tide, counter-attacking through the gateway where the Half-body Army had emerged from the city walls.
Leading the charge were the Centaur Heavy Armor Warriors—heavy-armored Centaurs who were like steel fortresses, utterly unshakable.
Hooves trampled encampments, shattering the ground.
With flames as their backdrop, the army of Dawn City was like the Death Knights come to claim souls in the night, extremely terrifying.
Chaos, unprecedented chaos.
Liusi City, the great city that had stood for countless years, had never before fallen to an invasion.
But today, this city was about to be crushed by an army from the surface.
It was to be conquered by new masters!
Yet this was not the most despairing thing for the Half-Elves, the most despairing thing was... they sensed that His Excellency Kaplotz, the great God of the Half-Elves... had fallen.
Their faith, their reliance, their spiritual pillar, the Divine they had leaned on for support, had just now, lost all signs of life.
There is a special connection between believers and the Divine, and though the Divine may not heed their prayers on ordinary days, believers can still sense the existence of the object of their prayers.
But now, that feeling was empty, gone, and even the deep believers sensed the fear and despair of the God of Half-Elves before his fall, emotions that made these devout believers feel as though they were at the scene themselves.
One believer might still be mistaken, but when they saw their companions beside them showing the same expressions as themselves, they were immediately engulfed by despair.
Fear spread like a plague.
The upper echelons of the Half-Elves were now almost crazily pouring into the Half-Elf temple.
Everyone entered the temple with their last hopes, hoping to see the figure that had always given them peace of mind still present, but every Half-Elf who stepped into the temple was disappointed.
There was nothing, absolutely nothing; the high seat of the Divine was empty, and even the aura of faith within the temple was dissipating...
It’s over... it’s all over now.
All the Half-Elf high-ranking officials looked blankly, their inner helplessness and panic left them not even knowing what to do next.
"Why is this happening? Hadn’t His Excellency arranged for three Dwarf Gods to ambush the God of Twilight?!"
"The aura of His Excellency has scattered... Oh Creator God, this must be fake!!"
"I don’t believe it, I don’t believe that His Excellency has fallen, this must be the despicable trick of the God of Twilight!!"
As these Half-Elves, like frightened chicks, raged with indignant roars, footsteps taptapped, growing closer from a distance.
The only two remaining Legendary Half-Elves entered the temple.
The panic-stricken high-ranking Half-Elves all turned their gazes toward the leading old Half-Elf.
This venerable Legendary had led the Half-Elves for decades without a single mistake.
Now, at the final moment, they placed all their hopes on him.
The old Half-Elf took a deep breath as he faced everyone’s expectant gazes, his wrinkled face calm, but the turmoil inside him was more exaggerated than anyone else’s.
For he clearly felt his own power dissipating, yes, the power of the Legendary was rapidly declining and before long, he was afraid he would fall to the Transcendent level...
All he had was a gift from the God of Half-Elves, and now, with the death of the Half-Elf God, that gift would naturally disappear as well.
But the old Half-Elf knew that everyone could panic, but he could not, for he was now everyone’s hope.
There was no so-called retreat. If they didn’t make an absolute move, the Half-Elves might be destroyed along with the fall of Liusi City.
After steadying his spirit, the old Half-Elf, under the watchful eyes of everyone, walked straight up to the divine seat where the God of Half-Elves used to sit, then turned to face everyone.
Though he tried to hide it, his voice still trembled slightly.
"My people, His Excellency may have encountered a crisis, but we Half-Elves, will never concede like this!!"
This forceful statement stabilized the morale of those nearly on the verge of collapse below.
"The Half-Elves are the finest race and kings of the Underworld! No one can change this fact!
Even though we have been defeated this time, we will eventually reforge the broken sword and reclaim our glory."
Correct content is on .
His tone was resolute and filled with determination and fearlessness.
At this moment, the old Half-Elf has assumed the role of a savior.
"We cannot fall here, nor can we sit idly by and wait for death... We must leave behind the ember of hope, sow the seeds for a future comeback!
Everyone, heed my command!"
The panicked Half-Elves below were immediately subdued by the old Half-Elf’s voice, barely suppressing their fear of losing support, their hearts still despairing but not as hopeless as before.
"Immediately lead your subordinates to break out. Those hidden underground passages will now be used, the more who escape, the more seeds of hope we’ll have.
The Half-Elves will not be extinct,
After you leave, hide in those borderlands.
The Underworld is so vast, not even the God of Twilight with his overwhelming abilities can search every corner.
Just wait for the time, pass on our race, and one day, the Half-Elves will reign over the Underworld again!!"
View the correct content at
The Half-Elf leaders were thoroughly ignited by these words.
They roared like madmen,
"Yes, we absolutely can’t be destroyed, we still have a future!!"
"The Half-Elves will be immortal!!"
"We will return, all of this will be ours again!"
Their tones were filled with hysteria, voices remarkably exaggerated, as if trying to vent their inner panic and unease.
But just then, an indifferent voice made all the Half-Elves as if choked, their roars and outcries forcibly stifled.
"Who gave you the delusion that the Half-Elves have a future?"
The ancient blasphemous language was wicked to the extreme, echoing within the temple with soul-shaking pressure.
Accompanying it was a dreadfully imposing divine dignity.
Like a mountain collapsing from the ninth heaven, shaking all directions, crushing everything beneath.
All the Half-Elves trembled and, filled with boundless fear, turned to face the mysterious existence that appeared in mid-air.
Although the figure was the epitome of handsomeness, to the Half-Elves, he appeared a billion times more terrifying than any demon.
The old Half-Elf standing before the divine throne felt his heart sink, feeling as if he could no longer breathe.
"The God of Twilight... Your Majesty?" His tone was imbued with unavoidable fear, as hoarse as if he had not drunk water for more than ten days in a desert.
Lide looked down from on high with an indifferent expression.
"The Half-Elf God?"
The corner of his mouth curved in a playful arc, and with a wave of his hand, under the watch of all, three lifelike bodies held by the transforming Mage’s Hand were now unveiled to all without cover.
The Mage’s Hand floated slowly to the center of the temple, then dissipated abruptly.
Thud~ Thud~ Thud~
Three muffled sounds in succession, as three divine bodies were tossed onto the ground like dead dogs.
The Half-Elves chilled to the bone upon seeing the bodies on the ground, as among them were two Gray Dwarves divinities, and one exceptionally familiar figure—the Half-Elf God.
Unending fear devoured their hearts.
If sensing the fall of the Half-Elf God they still retained one in ten million chance of luck, thinking it might be an illusion, that the Half-Elf God might return,
But now, all fantasies and unrealistic dreams were shattered.
The bodies lying before their eyes were their eternal faith, the only deity of the Half-Elves, their greatest reliance.
Now, the dream was broken.
Reality was like a vicious slap on the faces of the Half-Elves.
"How is this possible... No, no, it must be fake!! How could the majestic Your Majesty fall?! And the God of Grey Dwarves beside?!
Three gods have fallen here? How could it be true? Damn heretic!!! It must be you deceiving us, it must be you!!
Hahaha, the great god watches over me, he cannot simply die, impossible, impossible..."
A fanatic believer of the Half-Elf God, upon seeing the divine body, couldn’t withstand the shock and descended into chaos, going mad.
But at this moment, no one cared about the crazed believer, many Half-Elves now completely limp on the ground, looking up at Lide in the sky, radiating glorious divine power, unable to muster any will to resist.
Despair had consumed them.
Even the strong-willed old Half-Elf was staggering, the appearance of the Half-Elf God’s divine body shattering the remnants of his will.
His original Legendary realm instantly dropped to Transcendent, and another Legendary by his side similarly followed suit...
Lide’s eyes remained calm.
The celestial authority he exuded was like the sweeping of the Milky Way, pressuring everyone until they couldn’t breathe.
Under successive blows, these high-ranking Half-Elves had completely lost their fighting spirit, sitting numbly and unfocused, staring at the three bodies in the center of the temple.
No one spoke, no one called out, creating an uncannily dead atmosphere.
Seeing this, Lide did not say much else. When the Half-Elf God fell, everything was predetermined.
After a brief contemplation, he flashed in form, appearing directly in front of the divine throne.
The old Half-Elf trembled as Lide approached but dared not make any movement. This devil had just killed the god of his faith... like a thorn in his side.
But Lide had no hesitations, directly seating himself on the divine throne, looking down upon all beings from an even higher position.
"I declare.
From this moment forth, the Half-Elves and Liusi City fall under the rule of the Twilight Sect,
The Underworld, I am the sovereign.
Who agrees, who opposes?"
The Half-Elves below fell silent... All knew the era of the Half-Elves was over.
From today on, the God of Twilight would become the sole ruler of this land."

chapters.title: Chapter 448 - 450: 14 Million Believers, Cat and the God of Joy (8000 Words)
chapters.content:
Chapter 448: Chapter 450: 14 Million Believers, Cat and the God of Joy (8000 Words)
Originally, due to the death of the Half-Elf God, Liusi City had fallen into chaos, and after Lide suppressed the temple, it lost its high-level command.
This main city of the Half-Elves, unseen for hundreds of millions of years, now plunged completely into frenzied turmoil.
The Underground Races, enslaved by the Half-Elves, seized this opportunity to break out of their cages and began to kill and plunder; blood, severed limbs, flames, death, the screams of women, the wails of the elderly, the roars of the wounded warriors... Everything contributed to the city’s descent into twilight and doom.
Dawn City did not play the role of a chaos creator in this chaotic situation; instead, it began suppressing the uprising and restoring order.
After its army entered Liusi City, it first took control of the Underground Races who were taking advantage of the chaos. Those who resisted or disobeyed orders were mercilessly killed.
Heads rolled in profusion, and blood soaked into the floor.
The strong and overbearing style instantly subdued the situation; those who thought of resisting lacked the means to confront the forces of Dawn City. Under the sharp warrior’s swords and solid armors, the turmoil slowly returned to calm.
However, due to the large number of captives, it took a full ten Sunshine Hours for Dawn City’s army to completely control Liusi City.
The more than two million Half-Elves within this city were all taken as captives and guarded in batches.
Eventually, because there were simply too many captives, half of them had to be escorted outside the city for surveillance.
When Dawn City’s army took control of the city, the captured Half-Elves had completely lost the will to resist.
Especially since the Dawn army, with Lide’s nod of approval, took the body of the Half-Elf God from the temple and had Magic Language Bats carry it around the streets several times, immediately making those Half-Elves who were still resentful wilt like frost-bitten eggplants.
With their god killed, what could they possibly muster to resist? And even if they did, what purpose would it serve?
After thoroughly crushing their psyche, these captives became very easy to manage.
By the time the epic battle that determined the fate of the Underworld’s rule had its casualties and gains tallied, it was already the morning of the second day since the war began.
September 10th.
The Half-Elf temple.
Lide, sitting on the divine throne of the Half-Elf God, leisurely sipped wine unique to the Underworld from a Crystal Cup and listened to the reports from the high-level officials of Dawn City below.
"Your Excellency, regarding the total gains from Liusi City, we have worked through day and night to conduct our inventory and have roughly finalized a list of gains. Although there might be small discrepancies due to time constraints, the overall picture will not differ significantly," said Kapp, the Level 25 Legendary Beastman King, who was extremely excited at that moment.
The end of this war signified that the entirety of the Underworld had fallen under Dawn City’s rule.
No other force could compete with Dawn City for dominion over this land anymore.
Dawn City now had a stable background for development, a fact that had exceptional significance at the point in time of the Old Days’ arrival.
Lide glanced around the hall; the smiles on the faces of dozens of Dawn City’s higher-ups were no less than Kapp’s, and he felt quite satisfied internally.
"No worries, there’s still time for more detailed data gathering. For now, just report the overall gains to me," he said.
"Yes, Your Excellency," Kapp immediately unfolded the paper in his hands and began to report earnestly.
"The main gains from this battle are as follows.
First, population.
After capturing Liusi City we took a total of 2.07 million Half-Elves as captives, and another 310,000 from other Underground Races. All these could become new Believers of the Twilight Sect, basking in Your divine light.
And during our advance from Twilight City to Liusi City, the total captives we caught amounted to 650,000.
Combining both, we have a total of 3.03 million captives."
3.03 million?
Lide couldn’t help but feel elated hearing this number.
If these captives all became his Believers, coupled with the already existing older Believers, then the Twilight Sect would soon have more than 9 million followers.
This was an unimaginably vast treasure.
As his power level increased, the importance of the Power of Faith became more pronounced.
Believers capable of generating the Power of Faith were like gold mines that would never run dry, unless the followers died.
This would lay a solid foundation for his future development.
"Second, resources.
Twilight City stored a massive amount of ores, not only high-level ores such as Mithril fine gold, but also foundational ores like iron and copper mines.
Moreover, according to our interrogation, there are two large mithril mines and over a dozen giant iron mines in the Half-Elves’ secret areas, which have not been exploited due to the difficulty of construction.
But with our Alchemy technology, we can completely develop these veins.
These resources will be of great aid to Dawn City, which is in dire need of ore resources."
Two mithril mines?
Lide’s eyes sparkled upon hearing this.
How many risks had Dawn City taken to fight for the Dwarf Valley’s mithril mines?
And now, suddenly, there were two.
Was this a stroke of luck?
Furthermore, the other veins were exactly what Dawn City currently needed.
With the large expansion of Dawn’s army, came increased demand for equipment.
Iron mines, among the basic minerals, were in short supply in Dawn City; finding over a dozen giant veins was like rain in a drought.
The Underworld is indeed the Underworld - encountering so many veins out of the blue, and who knows how many more will be found after further exploration.
Lide was in high spirits.
"Third, food.
To our surprise, in the mountains beside Liusi City, the Half-Elves built more than twenty large warehouses.
These warehouses nearly penetrated the earth, storing an astronomical amount of food, most of which was the belly-filling Microglow Mushrooms. However, preliminary estimates are that they can provide for two million people over three years."
Kapp’s words didn’t stop, and his expression remained excited throughout; all these were treasures, with each one enough to intoxicate people.
"Fourth, the seized weapons and equipment..."
"Fifth, Gold Puck and gemstones..."
"Sixth..."
At last, Kapp listed over ten scattered spoils of war, each one enough to quicken one’s pulse.
The Half-body Main City had gathered the vast majority of the Half-Elves, as well as their wealth, making this war a feast for Lide, leaving him with his belly and bowl full.
After the final tally, just the value of the various gemstones and Gold Pucks amounted to tens of millions of Gold Pucks.
The wealth the Half-Elves had accumulated over tens of thousands of years was now all his war spoils.
In the end, Lide couldn’t help but marvel; indeed, murder and arson bring a golden belt.
Wealth from war was the easiest way to prosperity.
Of course, if one wasn’t careful, it was also easy to lose even one’s undershorts.
The warfare in the Underworld came to a complete end after the spoils had been cleared.
From the appearance of the One-eyed Giants in Giant Valley, killing the exploratory mining team’s blacksmith, to Lide enslaving the One-eyed Giant, learning of the Underworld’s existence, and now, the complete conquest of the Underworld, a full five years had passed.
In these five years, Dawn City had developed from an old castle into a massive force with a million soldiers and the presence of Legendary and Transcendent figures.
The initiator of all this was the man who had gone from slightly green to a true conqueror.
Right when Lide was reflecting on this milestone achievement, the system notification suddenly rang out.
"Ding, you have successfully defeated the original ruler of the Underworld—the Half-Elves—and killed their Divine being, taking over the Half-Elves’ Main City, capturing 99% of the Half-Elves, completely denying them any chance to turn the tables.
You have become the new ruler of the Underworld, and you have acquired a new title—Underground Sovereign.
Underground Sovereign, you rule over a vast Underworld, with your Legend Level increasing by 30, the difficulty in persuading captured prisoners reduced by 70% in the Underworld, your Sect to be widely worshipped by the Unbelievers in the Underworld, making it easier to convert other deities’ Believers during proselytizing.
Furthermore, within the Underworld, your deterring power over the life forms of the Underworld will increase by 1000%, you will gain a 300% All Attributes boost, and there’s a great chance that High-level life forms of the Underworld will pledge allegiance to you."
Was this an unexpected gain?
Lide, upon seeing the system notification, appeared quite pleased.
Another powerful title.
Underground Sovereign—it sounded imposing, and the attributes were outstanding.
He read through it several times, most keen on the features that reduced the difficulty of persuading prisoners and the widespread worship of his Sect by Unbelievers.
In other words, from now on, the difficulty of the Twilight Sect’s proselytizing in the Underworld would dramatically decrease.
This dovetailed perfectly with his focus on Sect development.
It could provide him with tremendous help.
From today onward, the Twilight Sect would be the only Sect in the entire Underworld.
And he would become the sole sovereign of this land.
"Kapp, immediately notify Harrison to dispatch the City Hall management staff down here to establish a new governance system.
Taking this land is not our ultimate goal. Developing its resources and making this land continually provide nourishment for Dawn City is the true purpose of our conquest of the Underworld."
Lide’s gaze swiftly moved away from the attribute panel and looked towards Kapp with a deep and solemn tone.
"Moreover, order the Priests to tirelessly preach to these Underground Races day and night. Once these prisoners become Believers of the Twilight Sect,
We must mobilize troops as quickly as possible to conquer those scattered tribes in the barren lands.
I want you to spread the glory of the Twilight Church throughout the entire Underworld.
There can only be one voice on this land."
A single sentence determined fate.
How the Underworld would develop from now on—Lide had already made his decision.
His plan was simple.
First to assimilate the prisoners, then once they were subdued, to start attacking those small tribes. He wanted all the Underground Races to become Believers of the Twilight Sect and the land to become the complete backyard of Dawn City.
How much support could a stable rear provide for Dawn City? There was no need for elaboration.
"As you wish, Your Majesty!"
After a brief contemplation, Lide suddenly seemed to recall something and said with a furrow in his brow,
"Has it been so long, and have we found any trace of the Black Dragon?"
The Black Dragon of the Underworld, this mysterious entity he had been preoccupied with since the start of the assault on the Underworld, remained elusive even now that he was a Legend.
Seems like he had anticipated the beginning but not the end.
Upon hearing this, Kapp shook his head somewhat awkwardly.
"Your Majesty, we do not know where the Black Dragon is hidden. We have dispatched a large number of personnel into the Mire Swamps without finding any trace of it..."
The Mire Swamps were shrouded in a poisonous mist and vast in area. The difficulty of finding a terrifyingly powerful Black Dragon in such a dangerous place was imaginable.
Lide instinctively turned to look outside the window, where the sight of Withered Bones flying in the sky caught his eyes.
"Immediately send Withered Bones to the Mire Swamps. Perhaps this creature will bring me some surprises."
Previously, he had sent Withered Bones into the Mire Swamps, but at that time, Withered Bones was only Level 19 and too weak, hence too afraid to explore many dangerous areas.
Mire Swamps, though riddled with crises, posed fewer dangers to those at Transcendent Level, and becoming a Legend would mean one could practically strut around without concern.
With Withered Bones venturing there, perhaps there would be sizeable discoveries.
He had once boasted that he would make the Black Dragon a pet tied up in the square of Dawn City; now, it was time to fulfill that boast.
On September 12, Dawn City’s City Hall sent a group of elite officials to the Underworld.
After discussions and inspections, these Elites devised a dual-main-city development strategy with Liusi City and Twilight City as the twin hubs.
Due to its convenient transportation, abundant surrounding mineral veins, and advantageous geographical environment, Liusi City was very suitable for development.
Whereas, due to its proximity to the Magic Crystal Vein and its capacity to quickly connect back to Dawn City through the Land of Bone-Burying, Twilight City was the core point for Dawn City and the Underworld to interconnect and could not be neglected.
With the arrival of officials trained through elite education, the originally chaotic situation was promptly improved, and the Ministry of Civil Affairs, Registry Office, Logistics Department, Propaganda Department, and so on were all restructured.
Everything began to fall into place.
On September 15, the war’s prisoners—Half-Elves and other Underground Races—surrendered en masse due to the restrictions of Lide’s title, Underground Sovereign.
The two Half-Elves who had fallen from Legendary to Level 20 Transcendent also knelt in submission under Lide’s overwhelming power and upon hearing the news of the Half-body God’s death.
And in order to rule the Half-Elves more conveniently, Lide directly assimilated the souls of the Half-Elf elite with the Power of Faith, thus stabilizing their current powers.
In the end, only two Transcendent Half-Elves remained, all the other Transcendents having fallen to Level 19.
But Lide didn’t care much about this; the combat power of the Half-Elves was not strong, and he couldn’t be bothered to elevate their Levels again.
Moreover, in the Underworld, aside from the unseen Black Dragon, Dawn City no longer had any enemies.
Just two Transcendent Half-Elves were enough to suppress the situation.
On September 20th, with the subjugation of the captives, the spread of the Twilight Sect’s teachings accelerated significantly.
Those Half-Elves who had felt Lide’s Divine Power became converts one after another, following the demise of their own deities.
By September 30th, all captives had been absorbed by the Twilight Sect in a mere 20 days, becoming loyal Believers.
And by this time, the number of Twilight Sect Believers on Lide’s attribute panel had exceeded 9 million.
On October 5th, after a brief period of consolidation, the 3 million strong Twilight Sect, under Lide’s command, began a carpet-sweeping campaign through the Underworld with Liusi City and Twilight City as its two main stages.
This time, Lide intended to thoroughly cleanse those hidden small tribes and eradicate any potential threats.
How mighty was the Twilight army? When the Half-Elves, who once ruled, were slain beneath their horses, how could those scattered tribes possibly stand against the great Twilight army?
Wherever the Twilight army went, everything turned to flat ground.
But this campaign was not without its troubles; it encountered several nuisances.
For instance, a Half-Beast tribe hidden among the hills unexpectedly had an army of over 300,000, with a leader who was Transcendent.
A Lizardman variant tribe—Flame Lizardmen—dwelling in caves numbered up to 500,000, with their chief being a single step away from reaching Legendary.
And after thorough searching, more than ten such tribes were discovered.
Some of these, like the Flame Lizardmen tribe, even caused Lide to personally take action to subjugate them.
Although this campaign faced some obstacles, since these tribes fought in isolation and could not unite, the ripples they caused were soon submerged by the Twilight army.
Vast swathes of land were thoroughly branded with the mark of the Twilight Sect.
By October 20th.
Over two-thirds of the land had been completely integrated into the Twilight Sect’s territory, and all hidden tribes had been cleansed. A majority of the Underground Races had become followers of the Twilight Sect.
Those who refused to believe in the Twilight Sect were sent to work in the mines that were already operational.
During this process, Dawn City Hall’s elite team of officials, after surveying maps, holding discussions, and numerous on-site inspections,
eventually decided to establish twelve new cities in the Underworld around the two main cities to better control the Underworld.
On November 2nd.
The military campaign in the Underworld was completed. Aside from the Mire Swamps and several other hazardous areas that the Twilight Sect’s army had not ventured into, all other regions had been scoured by the military.
By the time the Twilight army withdrew to the royal court,
it was calculated that dozens of Underground Races had been captured, totaling over 3.2 million captives.
This was after excluding the population of the Cave Dwellers, for their numbers exceeded 2 million. If included, the total would reach a staggering 5 million.
As the population was too large to conveniently calculate, Lide forcibly ejected the Cave Dwellers to be counted separately.
Afterward, he instructed the Underworld’s City Hall to establish a new household registration system to tally the population of each race one by one.
This census took an entire week, and the data was finalized on November 9.
The Twilight Sect currently ruled over 78 Underground Races, with a total population of 7.2 million, while the separately counted Cave Dwellers numbered 7 million, bringing the total to 14.2 million.
When Lide heard this figure, he was utterly astonished.
million people!!
Such an exaggerated, terrifying number!!
How many people did Dawn City have??
Moreover, except for a few stubborn fools who were still unwilling to convert, most of the population had adopted the faith of the Twilight Sect.
This directly pushed his number of Believers to an unprecedented peak—14 million followers.
Simply astonishing.
Every day, the amount of Power of Faith he received was astronomical, far exceeding what he had obtained in the previous month.
However, he then realized that having such a large population was normal as it came from conquering an Underworld roughly the size of the southern provinces on the surface.
In comparison to such a vast territory, the figure seemed somewhat small.
If it were the surface’s southern provinces, it would be normal for the numbers to be three to five times greater, after all, he ruled all the races of the Underworld.
Among the 14 million population, the number of Cave Dwellers was without a doubt the most shocking to Lide.
No one had paid attention to these creatures with fearsome reproductive capabilities over the eons. The weak and filthy Cave Dwellers, who hid away in the depths of their caves, out of sight from the sun—no one knew or cared to count just how many of them there were.
It was he who recognized that Cave Dwellers were easy to convert, and he didn’t care if accepting these lowly, dirty, and foul-smelling beings as his followers would lower his prestige. Otherwise, the Cave Dwellers might have remained hidden.
Setting aside the fact that the Cave Dwellers were too weak to become warriors, merely considering them as tools for producing Power of Faith was extremely beneficial—after all, they numbered 7 million. Incredible.
Once the census was complete, the cleanup phase of conquering the Underworld could also be considered finished.
What came next was to develop this land teeming with countless ore resources.
Lide had no intention of getting involved with this; he left it to the officials of the City Hall, whose rigorous training assured that their experience would be far more professional than his.
Although the cleanup phase had ended, and the entire Underworld was firmly in his grasp, the only thing that irritated Lide was the still missing Black Dragon.
Even Withered Bone went and found no trace—it was as if such a Black Dragon never existed in this world.
Lide had no choice but to call off Withered Bone’s search, too lazy to continue looking for it. If it couldn’t be found, then so be it—a Black Dragon, could it really turn the heavens upside down?
He would enslave another in the future and chain it up in Dawn City’s square. After all, dragons weren’t extinct, were they? If he really wanted to find one, would it be that hard?
Once his grip on the Underworld was completely secure, Lide didn’t linger any longer, returning to Dawn City with Withered Bone and Kapp.
Conquering the Underworld was just the first step in a journey of a thousand miles; the threat of the Old Days was only just beginning.
——
——
——
Due to the influx of a large population, Dawn City, once a desolate ancient castle, was now extraordinarily prosperous.
The tavern was the favorite place for all residents of Dawn City to relax after a long day.
Because most of the rare wines in Dawn City’s taverns were brewed using techniques passed down by the Kachar City Lord, and because there wasn’t much in the way of leisure activities, in the eyes of many old residents, the tavern was an essential daily destination.
Although the huge city now had more than twenty taverns due to the population explosion,
the most attractive to residents was still Dawn City’s first tavern—Bauhinia Tavern.
Because this tavern was operated by the logistics department of the City Hall, it possessed the largest selection of fine wines and the most lively environment.
At this moment, in the dimly lit but musically enchanting Bauhinia Tavern, everyone’s eyes were on the central area, where a young maiden was gracefully dancing on what had been an ordinary round table for guests to drink at.
The girl was around eighteen or nineteen years old, in the prime of her youth, wearing a pristine white dress, exuding a temperament as elegant as a cat, yet with hints of mystery and pride.
With hands raised high, she moved her hips and waist to the upbeat music, her delicate face filled with joyful smiles.
Giggling, her laugh was as clear as a bell, echoing through the music and into the ears of those around her.
A pair of bare feet, as white as snow, danced lightly on the tabletop, the dark surface contrasting sharply with her pale feet, adding an enticing air to the cheerful dancer.
"Is this the new dancing girl? She’s absolutely sensational. By the gods, I’d bet she’s the most alluring girl I’ve ever seen. I’d give all my wealth to spend a night with her..."
"Fool, don’t think of courting death. That young lady was brought back by the patrolling heroes a week ago..."
"What? Brought back by the patrol?"
"Yes, a week ago the patrol encountered an attack by a group of flying Demon Beasts. Several of them were grievously injured and near death. In the end, while fleeing, they encountered Miss Bast.
The brave and beautiful Miss Bast led some patrol members into a cave and devised a plan to lure those flying Demon Beasts into a confined space, where she personally killed them, saving the patrol members."
"Such a heroic tale, and you didn’t know?"
"So that’s why there have been so many heroes from the patrol visiting the tavern to watch Miss Bast dance recently. I thought it was Miss Bast’s charm that drew them..."
"Now you know. Don’t mess with Miss Bast, or the heroes from the patrol won’t let you off easily..."
Over a dozen musicians played vibrant and rhythmic music, quickly heating up the atmosphere.
Many customers in the tavern, stimulated by the alcohol, began to dance along with the girl standing on the tabletop, who moved her waist with feline agility.
The tavern was instantly filled with joy and fervor, everyone basking in the bliss brought by the delightful young woman.
"Praise be to the Kachar City Lord. Miss Bast is the most beautiful woman I’ve ever seen... It’s such a pleasure to see Miss Bast dance."
"Hahaha, I bet tonight is the most joyful time I’ve had all year..."
"Another round of Gold Ale! Let’s drink till we drop tonight..."
"By the gods, this is just mesmerizing... I would kneel and kiss the back of Miss Bast’s foot..."
Making eye contact with the reveling crowd around her, Bast, the dancing girl standing on the table, revealed a slightly sultry smile, seemingly too mature for her age.
Then with enchanting eyes, she provocatively licked her upper lip with her tongue and then, like a wild cat, licked her wrist, just as fine as jade. The people below, witnessing this scene, were plunged into an even more frenzied mood.
Numerous men, their hormones rising, simultaneously swallowed hard and then gulped down a large bottle of fine wine.
Feeling the increasingly fervent atmosphere around her, the young woman Bast at the center of everyone’s focus let out a coquettish smile and prepared to make her next move when suddenly, from outside, an excited voice could be heard, causing the tavern to fall silent in an instant.
"Hahaha, great news!! Great news!!
Lord Kachar has conquered the Underworld!! The army is now returning from the Underworld!!
He has commanded that tomorrow, at Moonlight Square, medals of honor will be awarded to the troops, and all are welcome to attend the ceremony!!"
The crowd that had been reveling suddenly had its attention captured by these words, and the tavern that had been enveloped in an unusual atmosphere abruptly broke free from that environment of pleasure and joy, becoming frenzied in an instant.
"Hahaha, those damned brats of the Underworld, under the brilliance of our Lord, will surely be conquered!!"
"By the Goddess above, Dawn City shall become an immortal city!"
"For Dawn City!"
"Our Lord is invincible!! Dawn City is also invincible!! Long live!!"
"..."
Then the crowd began to swarm out, all pouring toward the streets outside, and the lively atmosphere that had just been created instantly vanished.
Dawn City had won another victory, a tremendously good piece of news. If one went early now, they might even catch a glimpse of Lord Kachar’s holy countenance.
In just a scant three or four minutes, the tavern that had been bustling with extreme liveliness was now left with only about twenty staff members. The jovial atmosphere from before seemed as if it had never existed.
The girl who stood on the table, graceful and enchanting like a cat, was absolutely dumbfounded by this scene.
In those beautiful amber eyes filled a bit of peculiarity... these bastards, they just up and left so abruptly?
The atmosphere that had taken a week to build up... all ruined...
At the same time, the girl’s heart was filled with boundless curiosity about Kachar City Lord, the legendary figure.
During her time in this strange city, she had heard no shortage of stories about Kachar City Lord.
And everyone, including those doing lowly jobs like washing dishes, feeding horses, or cleaning sewers, praised the Kachar City Lord without cease, with a worship that bordered on madness.
Regrettably, the legendary figure who had built this charismatic city had gone off to battle in the Underworld two months ago, and she had never had the chance to meet him.
Now, hearing the news of Lide’s return, the girl who was like a cat, full of laziness, agility, elegance, and a touch of pride, seemed to think of something interesting, her eyes twinkling.
"Kachar City Lord... giggle, really quite interesting. I never thought I’d see such an intriguing mortal on the Main Plane...
I hope you won’t disappoint me... giggle..."
View the correct content at
With this thought, the girl flipped over, landing nimbly on the ground, then, twisting her slender waist, she walked straight out of the tavern. The surrounding staff greeted the girl with smiles, full of enthusiasm.
As the girl vanished from the tavern, at an unnoticed second-floor corner, a figure cloaked in a dark cape slowly descended the stairs.
What was more surprising was that the surrounding staff seemed completely oblivious to this mysterious person, as if he didn’t exist.
The mysterious cloak-wearer’s face, hidden in the shadows, revealed only a prominent nose and a pair of silver-gray eyes.
Looking at the now empty tavern, he lightly sniffed, as if catching a peculiar scent.
After a moment, his enigmatic eyes revealed a trace of chillness.
"Bast? No, Charis is your God Name, Cat and Joy Goddess...
Hehehe, it is interesting indeed that in this strange city, I’ve encountered this wild cat..."

chapters.title: Chapter 449 - 451: Knight and God of Murder
chapters.content:
Chapter 449: Chapter 451: Knight and God of Murder
The mysterious person cloaked in black watched Bast’s retreating figure in the tavern with a profound gaze, only descending the stairs after she had completely vanished.
Cats are highly sensitive to presence, and had he appeared directly in front of her, she might have noticed.
But now that the wild cat had disappeared, he no longer had any concerns.
The cloaked person, as if entering a desolate land, stepped out of the tavern under the watchful eyes of all.
The surrounding staff appeared oblivious to such a conspicuous figure, seemingly unaware of the cloaked person’s existence, creating a rather eerie scene.
Upon reaching the streets, the eyes of the person in the black cloak, cold as a venomous snake, surveilled everything with a chilling gaze.
Thanks to the city’s electrical system, the night in Dawn City shone as if it were day.
And like the tavern’s employees, the residents who come and went on the streets were oblivious to the cloaked person.
At this moment, two young children, each holding a bread loaf and giggling in their play, ran straight toward the person in the black cloak.
Shockingly, the two kids passed through the cloaked person’s body as though he were air, without encountering any resistance.
The mysterious cloaked person was accustomed to this, his silver-gray eyes unflinching, like a cold-blooded predator indifferently searching for its next quarry.
"Come on, Della, Lord Kachar is inspecting the troops in Moonlight Square. Our heroes are enjoying the celebration, and if we’re early, we might even see His Holiness’s divine visage..."
"Really? Lord Kachar is there today? I thought he wasn’t appearing until tomorrow’s knighthood ceremony."
"Of course, this is what my cousin from the patrol told me!"
Several young people in a hurry passed by the cloaked person, their conversation causing a slight movement in the eyes of this enigmatic being.
"Kachar... His Holiness?
The God of Dawn?
Heh, heh, heh...
That a Fake God could rule such a powerful city is quite surprising to me.
But what right does a Fake God have to occupy this magnificent city?"
The chilly tone that came from beneath the cloak caused an inexplicable chill to rise in the spines of the passersby.
They faintly heard someone whispering nearby, but when they saw nothing, panic crept into their hearts, and they quickly quickened their pace to leave the area.
The cloaked person paid no attention to all this and, after contemplating for a moment, turned and followed the crowd toward Moonlight Square.
He wanted to see Lord Kachar, who the residents regarded as the sun and moon, the master of the city.
At the same time, he wanted to meet his... enemy.
Yes, enemy.
At the thought of this word, a hint of cruelty and excitement shone in the silver-gray eyes of the cloaked person.
That was the excitement of a beast upon sighting its prey.
Half a month ago, in pursuit of blasphemers who had once intruded upon his Divine Country, he had unintentionally entered the city and was deeply astonished by the city’s wonder.
After learning in detail about this city, he made a decision which, in his view, was exceedingly correct—he would become the new ruler of this city.
Such a wondrous city should be ruled by the most powerful being!
A lowly Vampire, living off human blood, was unworthy to be the master of the city.
He, the noble, the great Knight and God of Murder—Stu Yate, would be the new sovereign of the city.
At this thought, the eyes of Stu Yate, the Knight and God of Murder, revealed a hint of intoxication.
Had the Ancient Days not come, he would never have made such a decision, but now, he would plunder everything!
Months ago, before the coming of the Ancient Days, Stu Yate was a stickler for rules, the Knight God who, over millions of years, had barely attained Weak Divine Power, with pitifully few believers.
This all changed after the Ancient Days arrived.
When he descended to the Main Plane, he encountered the God of Murder, whose power had plummeted to the abyss.
Sensing the weakness of the other, he felt a stirring at that moment.
Over countless ages, he had adhered to the rules within his heart, striving to forge and enhance his strength, but his believers dwindled, and he remained the pitiable Weak Divine Power God...
Was all this to carry on?
As the world was on the brink of destruction, was he to continue upholding so-called knightly doctrines?
Perhaps it was the erosion of the Ancient Days’ power, the magnification of his inner darkness, or his unyielding past, but Stu Yate took that step.
Yes, that intoxicating step.
He deceived the God of Murder, whose strength had fallen to less than Transcendent.
Now, the plotting of months would unfold—he would confront his enemy.
And that foolish God of Murder was actually quite trusting of him, for a laughable reason: because this God of the Knight was famously true to his word among the Divines.
Look at that, the God of the Knight who keeps his promises, hahaha, truly a farcical and ridiculous notion.
And then, the most ironic part was that he, the God of the Knight, murdered that God of Murder.
To this day, Stu Yate could never forget the disbelief in the eyes of the God of Murder as his Knight Captain’s Longsword pierced through the heart of the God of Murder.
But, he had never regretted it, even feeling a deep sense of gratitude for his decision back then.
For after he had killed the God of Murder, he plundered his Divine Position and became powerful—the God of both Knight and Murder.
It was precisely because he had stepped out of the confines of his conscience that he obtained a new Divine Position and became even more powerful.
This was a day worthy of being recorded in the annals of history, a conviction Stu Yate held without doubt, for a new Divine had been born.
After personally killing the God of Murder, he had decided not to live as repressed as he had before.
During the time of the ancient calamities, he wanted to hunt more Divines and obtain even greater power.
This time, he would no longer be the rigid and obstinate God of the Knight that others spoke of; he wanted all gods to look up to him!
Ambition is like weeds in spring, once it sprouts, it can never be eradicated.
Having taken this step, Stu Yate knew there was no turning back for him, but he also scorned the very idea of looking back.
This time, his goal would be this city hidden among the mountains, possessing boundless potential.
Stu Yate had a premonition that if he could rule this city, it might be the key step for him to reach the summit in the future.
Such a peculiar premonition allowed him to evade the backlash when the Destiny Tablet shattered, retaining a considerable amount of strength to descend upon the Main Plane.
Stu Yate thus had unshakable faith in his own premonitions.
They were a Talent, a kind of talent unimaginable to others.
"However, before ruling this city, there is that wild cat that interests me...
Charis, the Cat and Joy Goddess...
I wonder what purpose that wild cat has for coming to this city? Merely because she stumbled upon something intriguing and novel?
Or, do you also wish to dominate this city and spread your useless creed of joy?
If that’s the case, perhaps you can become prey before I rule this city. I wonder if the Divine Status of that wild cat is as delectable as that of the God of Murder’s Divine Status...
Hehehehehe..."
The cold smile was like the blizzards of Frost Month, reeking of indescribable brutality.
The once God of the Knight of the Order Good Camp died after he killed the God of Murder, slain by his ambition, now he is the sinister and orderly God of both Knight and Murder, possessing dual Divine Positions among the gods.
Even if he could regain his strength, he was confident of advancing from Weak Divine Power to Medium Divine Power, a desire that hadn’t been fulfilled for millions of years.
"When being dutiful no longer brings me strength, then why not try embracing the darkness?
What a marvelous day..."
Stu Yate took a step and followed the crowd, slowly approaching Moonlight Square, but when he arrived at Moonlight Square, he did not appear openly as he did around the tavern, but instead skillfully utilized the surrounding shadows and buildings to move.
After obtaining the Divine Position of Murder, the once God of the Knight’s way of doing things had changed drastically.
If the God of the Knight was the warrior charging bravely at enemies under the sun, then the God of Murder was now, using underhanded tactics like conspiracy, poison, curse, and all means to kill his enemies at any cost from within the shadows.
At this moment, Stu Yate had absolute patience; he had to fully understand all the news about this city before making a move.
Stu Yate knew very well that now he was the venomous snake in the shadows, his greatest advantage being that no one knew of him; he could use the asymmetry of information to hunt down all the targets on his death list.
The bleak darkness was silently baring its tusks, and the wails of death seemed to begin to hover over the skies of Dawn City...
---
---
---
"Look, over there, those are the Centaurs’ Heavy Cavalry, so majestic!!"
"The Beastman have arrived, that’s the powerful Clan Leader of the Lion Tribe—Lord Cap..."
"That’s Lord Withered Bones..."
To create a triumphant atmosphere, Lide did not have the soldiers return directly through the Space Gate to their respective camps.
Instead, he opened the Space Gate right on Moonlight Square, letting all the residents come to see the soldiers who had fought for them, and allowing all victorious warriors to taste the wonderful sensation of being surrounded and cheered on by the masses.
Lide currently stood in the office of City Hall, looking down from the window edge.
The new City Hall was established right in front of Moonlight Square, with a clear view of all activities below.
This time he didn’t make an appearance, because the spotlight should be on those heroic warriors who had fought valiantly.
f r\ee.c(o)(m)
If he showed up, the residents would only attribute all the glory to him.
Lide’s position in Dawn City had reached the highest it possibly could, and his reputation had long since maxed out; he didn’t need this dispensable honor.
On the contrary, leaving the glory to the soldiers below would have a considerable effect on morale boosting and the cohesion of the army.
Harrison stood by Lide’s side, also looking down at the army below with a tone filled with irrepressible excitement.
"Your Majesty, the Underworld has been completely conquered by us. What should our next step be? Should we make a move on Green City?"
For Harrison, the place he could never forget was the city that once brought calamity to the Bloodline, causing eternal pain to the Bloodline—Green City.
He would never forget how an Extraordinary Mage’s magic nearly wiped out the Bloodline.
So, once Dawn City had gathered sufficient strength, occupying Green City had become his obsession.
The Bloodline had to wash away the past humiliations and discontent, and Green City also had to be incorporated into Dawn City’s territory.
Upon hearing this, Lide didn’t respond immediately. After pondering for a moment, he slowly said.
"Is there any movement from the seal of the Ancient Evil God in Dwarf Valley?"
Harrison was slightly startled, hastily replying.
"Your Majesty, we dispatched our elite Blood-Colored Blade to monitor nearby. In these past two months, the space sealing the Ancient Evil God has expanded significantly, and the Levels of the Ancient Monsters emerging from it are getting higher and higher.
Our troops stationed in Dwarf Valley have been under great pressure, even on the brink of collapse several times...
According to the intelligence command center’s prediction, maybe within the next one or two months, the Ancient Evil God will break through the seal."
After his words fell, the face of this chairman of Dawn City Hall became extremely solemn.
Facing Ancient Monsters that knew neither pain nor fear, flooding in like a tide, and ceaselessly attacking, the warriors in Dwarf Valley were almost exhausted in body and soul over these past few months.
If it weren’t for Dawn City’s powerful support, the city would have already fallen dozens of times.
Yet even with Dawn City’s assistance, Dwarf Valley had almost reached a point of collapse in the last month or two.
Not to mention the increasingly terrifying aura emitted by the Ancient Evil God lately—one could only guess what would happen if it escaped.
Hearing this, Lide’s brows furrowed, his tone getting colder.
"The situation in Green City won’t deteriorate to an irretrievable state; humanity is the foundation of faith, and they won’t slaughter believers indiscriminately.
At most, the God of Nobles will drive the Dawn Sect to collapse, and upon my return to Green City, I can immediately reunite the Sect.
In comparison, the situation in Dwarf Valley is more critical, and we must suppress it.
Moreover, I am very interested in that sealed Ancient Evil God. If we can capture one and study it..."
Back in Risier City, when facing the God of Plague, although Lide managed to seize part of its body, he had no means to study the origin power of the Ancient Evil God and could only hastily consume the origin.
Now, with an Ancient Evil God still sealed before him, the temptation was unquestionably great.
If they truly could capture this Ancient Evil God, the current Dawn City completely had the capacity for a detailed study, becoming fully prepared for any future encounters with other Ancient Evil Gods.
This was Lide’s consideration on a strategic level for the future.
Compared to that, although Green City’s situation seemed dire, it was still manageable as long as the God of Nobles didn’t transform into an Evil God and perform a Blood Sacrifice on the entire city.
After all, the believers of the other party also came from humanity. At this critical time, a large-scale slaughter of humans would be akin to cutting off the direct roots of faith—the God of Nobles wasn’t so foolish, at worst they’d just oppress the Dawn Sect.
One was a matter of face while the other was a matter of substance; face could be reclaimed at any time, but the loss would be great if the substance were lost.
As a pragmatist, Lide’s thoughts were always clear.
Seizing a complete Ancient Evil God for study held much more temptation than killing an ordinary Divine Being, after all, slaying a god wasn’t something rare for him.
"Your Majesty, I will arrange it immediately," Harrison nodded. Once Lide made a decision, he would follow it unconditionally.
Lide nodded, as if he had remembered something, and continued to speak.
"Yes, and have someone summon Valen, Frey, and Stanley back to Dawn City. I want to grant them the power to break through to Legendary."
Three Divine Bodies were still sealed by him in the Land of Bone-Burying, such precious resources held no great significance as mere resources, but turning them into power was more important for Dawn City.
The three people he had named were all key figures in the upper echelons of Dawn City.
Emi, the Dwarf Forging Master, managed the weapons factory and had established considerable merits for Dawn City.
Frey, a second-generation Bloodline, was currently coordinating with the Centaur King Guido Blackwind in the Hills, executing the conquest of the Centaurs.
Stanley, the Vice President of the Dark Contract, was not only the Controller of the intelligence command center but also an executor of the Dark Shadow’s infiltration plan into the human hierarchy, the mastermind behind the colonization of Earth. Most outrageously, he now also controlled a terrifyingly powerful player guild.
Three Divine Bodies could give birth to three Legends, promoting these three individuals would allow them to play even greater roles.
The situation in Dawn City might currently seem optimistic, but what he had to face now was the crisis-ridden Ancient Calamity; the power in his hands was still far from enough.
Because even now, no Ancient Evil God has truly descended upon the Main Plane, only their servants have appeared here.
Lide had also made conjectures about this.
When the crack in the sky’s rules further widened and the energy of the old days on the Main Plane became more intense, maybe he would see a fully manifested Ancient Evil God here—a being much stronger than any common Legendary figure.
That would be when the catastrophe truly arrives.
The current calamities of the old days were nothing more than appetizers.
Thus, an urgent feeling always lingered within him, keeping his nerves taut.
After Harrison left, Lide’s gaze flickered indecisively.
Conquering the Underworld was merely a way to purchase insurance for Dawn City, ensuring an undefeated position in external battles.
After all, having such a stable rear allowed him to develop freely—an advantage that could not be overstated.
But that was not a permanent solution. To securely face the inevitable catastrophe in the future required additional planning on his part.
He had a premonition that the day when an Ancient Evil God would fully arrive on the Main Plane might not be far off.
If he didn’t rush to enhance his strength now, Dawn City might face an even greater crisis.
After observing the scene below the window for a while, Lide suddenly remembered something and stopped watching the celebrating army. He turned and left his office.
He was going to see that half-blood mermaid again, the mysterious being who had once guarded the Destiny Tablet.
He wondered if the other party had regained more memories, as right now, he had many questions he wished to discuss...
Meanwhile, in Moonlight Square, a girl who was looking around amidst the crowded throng drew quite a bit of attention.
Especially from... men.
"Miss Bast, may I treat you to a drink tonight?"
"To think it’s Miss Bast herself; she’s stunning..."
"Is this the new girl from the Bauhinia Tavern? She truly captivates the heart..."
A group of the old men’s eyes shone brightly upon seeing the figure in a white dress with bare, clean feet, each trying to push through to Bast’s side.
But unlike the seductive charm of the tavern, the woman now inciting everyone’s nerves seemed to radiate a hint of coldness that suggested ’keep away from me.’
Her demeanor was elegant yet carried an aloof pride from afar. While still lazy and provocative, that posture made the surrounding people’s hearts turn cold.
It seemed, the tavern’s enchantress had undergone some change...
Bast’s amber eyes scanned the surroundings, and her indifference quieted the heated discussions that had just begun among the crowd.
Many even felt as if they were facing a lofty queen.
Her look of superiority instilled a sense of awe and fear in them.
Disguised as Bast, the Cat and Joy Goddess curled her lips in a disdainful arc.
After glancing at Moonlight Square and not spotting any trace of the legendary Kachar City Lord, she straightened her slender waist and walked away haughtily.
She didn’t even glance at the fervent eyes around her.
In the tavern, she could be uninhibited, enjoying the sight of men boiling with passion and kneeling before her. But outside, she remained an unapproachable Divine.
These lowly humans, do they even have the right to speak to her?
The only disappointment for her today was not having seen the Kachar City Lord...
Having observed Dawn City’s army filled with bloodthirst and a killer aura, she grew increasingly curious about this mysterious City Lord.
What kind of person could build such a miraculous city? Vampires living with humans, Beastmen walking with giants, Dwarfs partnering with goblins... Besides, there were magical alchemy creations with never-ending water, carriages moving along tracks, and a city-wide lighting system that illuminated the night...
The miraculous scenes within Dawn City scratched at her curiosity like a cat.
It’s true what they say: curiosity killed the cat; however, it was unknown if this Cat and Joy Goddess would also fall victim to this old adage.
Bast walked around the crowd and stepped into a dark alley, sniffing to confirm no outsider was present.
The young goddess-looking girl bent her legs slightly and then leaped deftly and gracefully, disappearing atop the rooftops in a cat-like manner.
Not long after Bast had left, a cloaked person—the Knight and God of Murder, Stu Yate, walked into the alley like a ghost.
This evil god who had switched sides searched around with hawk-like gray eyes.
After a moment, as if he had discovered something, his pupils sharply contracted, then stepped forward and bent slightly to pick up a strand of hair that had fallen to the ground from between the cracks of a tile where Bast had just jumped.
After Stu Yate stood up, he brought the strand to his nose for a faint sniff, confirming the scent, and a cold murderous intent flickered in the eyes beneath his cloak.
"To rule this city, let’s start with this wild cat..."

chapters.title: Chapter 450 - 452: Exploring the Beginning of the Ancient Evil God’s Seal
chapters.content:
Chapter 450: Chapter 452: Exploring the Beginning of the Ancient Evil God’s Seal
