"Mm, better to be prepared on all fronts. We can look for desolate ones, ones that have powerful Evil Gods, and we can find several. If her strength is too overwhelming, we will throw her into a Plane with an Abyss Evil God.
If her strength can be suppressed by us, then we will throw her into a desolate Plane and deal with it ourselves..."
"Yes, Your Excellency."
Emi immediately disappeared from the spot, beginning to execute the plan.
Lide also felt a bit more at ease. Such preparations were intricate, but they were also to prevent any accidents.
Although Kaslina had never shown hostility, as the sovereign of Dawn, he had to consider more and could not just happily embrace the other party because they had not shown enmity.
He must possess sufficient strength, even methods to counter the other party, to be at ease.
Only with equal power can there be equal status; this is the unchanging rule of Glory.
Ultimately, in this world, strength is everything.
It was only after Emi returned and inscribed the coordinates of more than a dozen Abyss Planes that Lide returned to Dawn City through the Land of Bone-Burying.
Zhuge lived his life with caution.
Caution had always been his principle of conduct. He would rather do more, even expend extra effort, than to face a crisis with a fatalistic attitude.
---
---
---
Dawn City.
Instead of going to find Kaslina right away, Lide went to the office of Harrison, the City Hall director.
He hadn’t been gone for even two Sunshine Hours to explore the Sealed Land, and even Harrison was quite astonished to see him.
Based on estimates, if Lide spent ten to eight days on this trip, it wouldn’t have been surprising, but now...
"Your Excellency, is everything progressing smoothly?"
Lide nodded calmly, but his next words made the City Council Chairman’s eyes widen in astonishment.
"Everything went smoothly; I have sealed that Ancient Evil God within the Land of Bone-Burying."
Harrison looked at him as if he had seen a ghost, staring shockingly and stammering, "You, you captured the Ancient Evil God?"
This wasn’t a joke, was it?
The intelligence command center had probed so many times; the aura emitted by the other party was terrifying, far beyond Legendary... even by estimates, that Evil God was several times more powerful than Risier City’s God of Plague, perhaps even more.
Such a terrifying existence had been captured in just a short couple of day hours?
He then seemed to realize something and spoke with a sudden understanding.
"It must be that the sealed Ancient Evil God’s power had waned to its nadir, the intelligence command center made a mistake in their exploration..."
Lide smiled, not keeping the suspense any longer, and retold the news about the mysterious sarcophagus and the presence of other Ancient Evil Gods in the Sealed Land. After listening, Harrison’s expression changed.
"Your Majesty, if that is the case, it may be very difficult to keep the Dwarf Valley..."
He instantly saw the crux of the problem. Once the Ancient Evil God descended, the chances of the Dwarf Valley being destroyed were almost certain, given the proximity, and those Ancient Monsters had already caused so many deaths and injuries right beneath the city walls.
"Mm, make arrangements for this, and first move the ordinary Beastmen to Dawn City. Should we indeed face an irresistible enemy, we will relocate at that time.
I am here to inform you of this matter. Now, I must seek out Lady Kaslina to inquire about the sarcophagus..." Lide paused before continuing.
"However, I cannot be certain whether Lady Kaslina will have other thoughts after seeing the sarcophagus and the Angel Wings... If Lady Kaslina harbors any ill intent, you must immediately send troops to control those around her during this period and search her house."
Harrison’s expression turned stern as he respectfully replied.
At the moment, that half-blood Mermaid in Dawn City was in a situation where the visitor was strong and the host weak. The strongest in Dawn City, Lide, could not settle the matter by force, and hence he was quite wary of this Mermaid.
But fortunately, the current relationship between the two parties was still in a controllable honeymoon phase, with no conflicts arising.
After giving his instructions, Lide did not hesitate to step through the Space Gate and arrive at the Magic Industry Research Institute.
Seeing Lide appear before her after only a short daytime, Kaslina gave him a light glance.
But her expression remained unperturbed, as if nothing in this world could capture her interest.
Behind her mermaid mind, her hair seemed to float in the water, making her detached demeanor all the more intense.
She did not seem like someone from this mortal realm.
Every time Lide looked into the mermaid’s deep, sea-blue eyes, he had the illusion that he was in a holy church, seeing a priest devoutly praying, filled with a sense of the sacred.
"Lady Kaslina..."
"Kachar City Lord, the aura of the Tears of Purification has vanished. Have you found the sealed Ancient Evil God?"
A hint of subtle astonishment flickered across Kaslina’s cool expression, interrupting him.
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly as he nodded gravely, "Not only that, but the Ancient Evil God was sealed in a mysterious sarcophagus, which I have transported back here."
Kaslina’s body trembled slightly upon hearing the word ’sarcophagus.’ An urgency emerged in her eyes, which seldom showed much emotion, as she eagerly spoke.
"Is it a sarcophagus bound by chains?
The chains binding the sarcophagus are inscribed with Ancient inscriptions, and the periphery of the sarcophagus is carved with exotic patterns from realm city-states...
Also, there is a deep scratch on the head of the sarcophagus..."
Lide’s pupils dilated abruptly. He had not paid much attention to the appearance of the sarcophagus before, but now he recalled these details instantly.
That Sealed Land was clearly ancient beyond measure - how did this Mermaid know of it?
Moreover, according to the information previously revealed by Kaslina, the Ancient Evil God had been personally sealed by the Creator God. By that account, the sarcophagus clearly dated back to the era of Creation...
Could this mysterious guardian of the Destiny Tablet trace her origins back to the very dawn of Creation long ago?
Thinking this, a shock appeared in Lide’s eyes.
If not for this, how could she know the secrets of the sarcophagus?
If so, then the origin of this Mermaid was far more terrifying than he had imagined...
"Lady Kaslina, how do you know about the sarcophagus?" Despite the surge of emotions within, Lide still pressed down his astonishment and earnestly asked.
But her next statement changed his face dramatically, his eyes filled with disbelief.
"Because I personally sealed that sarcophagus..."

chapters.title: Chapter 453 - 455: The Battle to Conquer the Centaur
chapters.content:
Chapter 453: Chapter 455: The Battle to Conquer the Centaur
"Because, I personally sealed that stone coffin..."
This statement was earth-shattering.
Lide looked at Lady Kaslina in disbelief.
This stone coffin was personally sealed by the mermaid??
Is this not a joke??
Isn’t this going a bit too far?
Waves roared in his heart, and after taking several deep breaths, he managed to suppress the turmoil.
His gaze turned heavy.
"Lady Kaslina, are you serious?"
Lady Kaslina’s profound eyes fixated on Lide, slowly saying,
"The Plane that sealed the stone coffin is the Initial Plane, the first Plane created by the Creator God. However, because the rules of the Initial Plane were incomplete, the Creator God used this Plane as a prison, to seal those powerful Ancient Evil Gods.
By chance, I participated in that sealing. This stone coffin..."
The mermaid’s voice suddenly paused toward the end.
Then she meaningfully looked at Lide.
"Take good care of this stone coffin. When you become a Divine, I will tell you all about it. Right now, you still lack the power to explore the mysteries within."
No wonder there were other Ancient Evil Gods besides the mysterious existence inside the coffin.
The Initial Plane used by the Creator God to seal the Evil Gods—this origin was no small matter. It seemed that moving out of Dwarf Valley had to be carried out.
As for the latter part of her statement, it left Lide thoughtful. Previously, when enquiring about why the Undead Plane and the creatures from the Abyss Evil God hadn’t lost their power, Kaslina had said something similar...
His thoughts whirled rapidly. He wondered how many secrets this mermaid was still hiding.
After steadying his mind, he regained his composure, regardless of what secrets the other party held, strength was the only thing that mattered.
But to become a Divine...
He shook his head. Enthronement wasn’t that easy. Though he had already reached level 28, there was still a long way to go before he could become a Divine.
Thinking back, Kaslina’s reaction had rendered his precautions almost useless...
But that was also not a problem; regardless of whether the other party harbored ill intentions or good, having sufficient counteracting power would never be wrong.
After pondering for a moment, Lide said in a deep voice,
"Lady Kaslina, can the stone coffin not be opened now?"
"If you wish, you can certainly open it, but I advise you to wait a while. Opening the coffin now will not be of much benefit to you..."
Kaslina’s eyes seemed as if they could see through everything, her words laden with profound meaning.
Lide’s eyes flickered, "If I want to open it, how should it be done? Can we only let the other party break through the seal?"
"The Tears of Purification must have already been embedded on the coffin. You just need to isolate the Tears of Purification using Divine Power. Without the Tears of Purification and the sealing chains, the coffin will immediately open."
Kaslina unreservedly laid out the method.
"I understand,"
Lide looked at Kaslina seriously but did not say whether he would open the coffin now.
"Thank you for your advice, Lady Kaslina. I will consider it carefully.
Moreover, please keep me updated about the fragment of the Destiny Tablet. Dawn City needs one piece for protection."
Kaslina’s demeanour also returned to calm, untouched by worldly matters.
"As it should be."
Although the final outcome of this visit differed from what he initially anticipated, overall, he had still achieved his goal.
After chatting with Kaslina for a brief while longer, he turned and left, but Lide’s attitude towards this mermaid had once again changed.
Her background was too astonishing. He would have to dig deeper in the future and establish a better relationship with her.
Even the Dark Sovereign had become his blade; not utilizing higher quality resources available at hand would be too out of character for him.
Once Lide’s figure disappeared from the room, Kaslina’s calm expression slightly changed, and her gaze grew deeper.
"Unexpectedly, a layout from millions of years ago has been dug up by you...
However, the Ancient Days have already dawned, and the old measures have lost their significance. Consider it a gift from me, Lord of Kachar City..."
——
——
——
After returning to his office in the city hall, Lide was still deep in thought. He had never imagined there would be such a connection between the stone coffin and Kaslina.
He hadn’t agreed to become a Divine before opening the stone coffin because of this.
Their thoughts might not align; he was somewhat perplexed about what this mermaid truly wanted.
She claimed to have once guarded the Destiny Tablet, but when the Destiny Tablet was lost, he couldn’t detect any entangled or concerned emotions in her.
Moreover, Kaslina knew that a Demigod Sea Beast in the Lost Sea possessed a fragment of the Destiny Tablet, but he didn’t see her taking action to retrieve it personally, even though she hadn’t regained her demigod power. Nor had she ever mentioned leveraging the power of Dawn City.
From Lide’s perspective, Kaslina’s actions were always a bit bizarre. He didn’t know what her goal was, and that was a crucial reason why he couldn’t fully trust this mermaid.
Too mysterious.
After some thought, Lide had a guard summon Harrison over, as this matter had to be disclosed to him.
Soon, Harrison arrived at the office, and the impact of Lide’s words was even greater on him.
"Lady Kaslina... actually participated in sealing the Ancient Evil God... that’s truly unbelievable..."
The chairman of the City Hall was at a loss for words to describe the shock he felt.
To have taken part in the Creator God sealing an Evil God, how exaggerated was that?
Such feats were seldom matched by Divines even in the myths related in the churches.
"Yes, just keep this in mind, and I will personally handle the rest," said Lide, having recounted the tale and not dwelling further on the issue.
There were still days ahead, and one day he would learn everything about the other party.
His bathtub was very large, harboring a mermaid wouldn’t be a problem...
Moreover, he might not need to wait until the breakthrough to Divinity to open the sarcophagus, because he had an important trump card—the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel.
As long as the angel fell successfully, he would have enough strength to handle the being inside the sarcophagus.
He didn’t believe that an Ancient Evil God sealed for tens of millions of years could still be powerful enough to defeat such a terrifying being like the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel.
"Immediately make arrangements for the aftermath in Dwarf Valley. I don’t want us to be unprepared when the Ancient Evil God arrives."
Abandoning Dwarf Valley wasn’t unthinkable, but the number of Ancient Evil Gods sealed within the Initial Plane was incalculable. The mere appearance of one was enough to shatter the earth to its extreme, so contingencies were a must.
"Yes, Your Majesty," Harrison responded respectfully.
After further communication between the two, Harrison seemed to remember something and spoke solemnly.
"Your Majesty, the Centaur God from the Dwarf Hills has issued the final ultimatum to Guido Blackwind and declared him a rebel.
In about three to five days, they plan to mobilize a vast army to attack Guido’s Gale Empire.
Currently, we only have two Extraordinary Demons stationed there, facing the force of the Centaur God might be challenging..."
The millions of centaurs in the Dwarf Hills were an incredibly rich resource, and Harrison’s covetousness remained.
Lide felt the same way; had it not been for the impending breach of the seal on the Ancient Evil Gods in Dwarf Valley, he might have chosen to take action against the centaurs first.
Now that the opposition had dared to provoke them, it was time to deal with them, especially since the matter of Dwarf Valley had already concluded.
"I remember you mentioned the Centaur God has discovered the location of Dawn City..." Lide watched Harrison intently.
"Yes, Your Majesty.
When Guido attacked Gale City, the Centaur God appeared out of nowhere, not only killing more than a hundred thousand centaurs but also causing us to lose hundreds from the Bloodline."
Harrison’s tone grew colder.
"We discovered traces of High-level Chasing Magic on the Bloodline who managed to escape, therefore we deduce that the Centaur God must know the location of Dawn City..."
The rapid growth of Dawn City was largely due to its superior geographical position.
Hidden deep within the Far Mountain Range, naturally isolated from enemies, it could develop however it wished completely free from external interference.
The benefits gained from this geographical position were beyond imagination.
Although Dawn City had grown, it wasn’t yet powerful enough to be fearless. Exposure might not pose much of a threat in the short term, but over time, the risks would increase.
Not to mention anything else, the God of Plague, one of the Ancient Evil Gods, was still searching the world for traces of Dawn City.
If discovered by them, regardless of how formidable the defenses of Dawn City were, it would inevitably face endless assaults from the God of Plague.
Just seven or eight Ancient Evil Gods being summoned by the enemy would likely result in the imminent fall of Dawn City.
Thinking this, Lide’s eyes grew colder; he had no interest in letting the news of Dawn City leak at this juncture.
"Dwarf Hills, the centaurs... this land, should have belonged to Dawn City long ago."
He made his decision in an instant.
—
—
—
That day, having just returned to Dawn City, Lide ordered his army to assemble.
This time, his target was Dwarf Hills, which he had long deemed ripe for the taking.
On November 6th, the grand army of Dawn assembled, including 10,000 Magic Language Bats, 4,000 Bloodline Blood Mages, along with the Giant Army and the Caster Corps of Dawn.
Meanwhile, Lide also called up the 200,000-strong Demon Army that had been stationed in the Underworld, to join in this campaign against the Dwarf Hills.
Despite the bad reputation of demons in the Main Plane, at this juncture with Ancient Evil already descended, the outside world was no longer in a position to worry about the presence of demons, having their own dangers to fend off.
Guido Blackwind, the puppet leader and King of the Gale Empire, who currently had over 1.2 million centaurs at his command, wasn’t lacking warriors, so Lide felt no need to enlist ordinary soldiers.
On November 7th, Lide activated the Space Gate, allowing the mighty army of Dawn to cross the treacherous Far Mountain Range, and transported them thousands of miles away from Dawn City.
Subsequently, tens of thousands of Magic Language Bats directly airlifted this army to Dwarf Hills.
On November 8th, due to the close proximity now, the Dawn army reached the Dwarf Hills in just one day, carried by the Magic Language Bats.
Upon receiving the news, Guido Blackwind immediately led a 200,000-strong centaur army to come to their aid.
Gale was a word dearly loved by centaurs, second to none.
The main city of the centaurs was called Gale City, their activated Bloodline was called Gale Bloodline, and at this moment, proclaiming that the centaurs were destined to rise, they had established the Gale Empire.
As the King of the Gale Empire, Guido Blackwind, although a puppet raised solely by Lide’s hand, was definitely the Savior among all the Centaurs.
Even now within the Gale Empire, many Centaurs regarded Guido’s position higher than that of the Centaur God and Lide, the God of Dawn.
It was Guido who had sheltered them during times of peril and had led them to annihilate those damned Ancient Monsters, reclaiming their occupied lands for them.
Such martial valor established in battle could not be undone with just a few words.
This was why the Centaur God did not receive their unanimous response. When we were in danger, you abandoned us, and now you want us to return? Are we that cheap?
Of course, there indeed were some Centaurs who were humble. Originally, Guido’s great army numbered 1.5 million, but now only 1.2 million remained, with at least 300,000 having fled...
After meeting Guido, the King of the Gale Empire, Lide did not hesitate at all and took control of the military power directly.
The Gale Empire had already started following the Dawn Sect under Guido’s command.
But now, due to the Centaur God’s descent, many Centaurs had become unsettled during this time, and quite a few had even defected.
This caused some instability in the morale of the entire Centaur army.
After Lide discerned this change, he immediately began reorganizing the troops.
Over the past month, his Power of Faith had accumulated over six million. Lide, initially from Finance University, summoned the high-ranking centaurs and assimilated their souls using the Power of Faith.
He assimilated thousands of Centaurs in one go, and because his grasp of Divine Position had improved, he spent less Power of Faith this time—only five million for these thousands of Centaurs.
These assimilated centaurs, now fiercely loyal to Risier City, immediately solidified the previously wavering military hearts.
Then, quite decisively, he began reorganizing the army using these soul-assimilated Centaurs as the core.
On November 12th, in just three days, Lide forcefully reorganized the 1.2 million-strong Centaur army.
He had the entire army under his grip, and the unstable morale was now stabilized.
On the same day, the Centaur God also began his massive move.
The Centaur army, which had been holed up in Gale City, started mobilizing, their target being the settled Dawn Army in the central part of Dwarf Hills.
November 15th.
Under Lide’s command, the fully reorganized Centaur army began advancing towards Gale City, and at the same moment, the army led by the Centaur God also marched towards them.
Both sides easily scouted each other’s locations.
Amid such a massive battle, ambushes were virtually impossible.
With too many numbers, and the battle line stretched over ten miles, even the fiercest ambush couldn’t easily crush a million-strong army, particularly when the scouts on both sides were not to be underestimated.
The smoke of war had begun to billow over Dwarf Hills, especially as the two armies drew closer...
November 17th.
Lide and the Centaur God stood afar from each other on a plain, 10 kilometers apart.
Both armies had arranged their formations, ready to attack.
Lide commanded the 1.2 million-strong Centaur army, a 200,000-strong Demon Army, along with Space-synced Magic Language Bats, Blood Clan Spellcasters, the Dawn Mage Group, and the Giant Army.
His top combat forces included a Level 26 Undead Blood Dragon Withered Bone, Level 25 Beastman King Kapp, and two Level 21 Extraordinary Double-Horned Demon Lords.
Their overall strength was monstrous. Without the Centaur God, not just sweeping the Dwarf Hills, but all of the southern province would have been easy.
However, the forces of the Centaur God were also formidable, commanding an 1.8 million-strong Centaur army.
But their top combat forces were only two individuals—one being the Centaur God, and the other, the Gale City Lord who had long been rumored to have one foot into the Legendary.
The standoff between the two sides made the air feel as if it had solidified, extremely oppressive, to the point that not even birds dared to fly over this area.
This war, almost epic in scale, was now like an arrow placed on a bowstring, ready to be unleashed.
"Your Majesty, the army is ready. Shall we commence the attack immediately?"
Kapp’s Golden Power burned fiercely like a flame, making his already robust lion’s physique seem like a War God incarnate, formidable and commanding.
Standing behind Withered Bone, Lide’s eyes slightly shifted, his gaze fixed intently on the two especially strong auras in the Centaur formation.
One of those auras made him feel a subtle threat—that must be the Centaur God.
But to his surprise, the Centaur God’s aura was not just strong, but excessively so, giving him a sense of bluster...
After a moment of contemplation, Lide’s eyes gradually sharpened.
Today’s battle would determine the fates.
He had to conquer this land and the Centaurs.
Compared to the Underworld, The Dwarf Hills’ geographical location was trivial. The Underworld could serve as a significant rear for Dawn City, providing a secure development space for Dawn City.
The Dwarf Hills were positioned openly in a chaos-ridden area, full of loopholes, accessible to anyone who might want to strike them.
While Dwarf Hills could be forsaken, the Centaurs had to be won over.
Of course, they still had to win this war before considering others; otherwise, planning how to deal with prisoners only to be defeated would be a mockery.
"Sound the horns, full army attack!" Lide’s stern voice resonated across the skies.
"Kapp, take command of the main army; Withered Bone, come with me to take down the Centaur God..."
As the order was issued.
Wuu wuu~
The deep and piercing sounds of long ox horns echoed, reverberating through the skies above the battlefield.
The previously tense atmosphere among the troops gradually heated up, the faces of the warriors filling with an indescribable, fervent excitement.
The war, had begun.
At the forefront were 300,000 Centaur Heavy Cavalry, always a massive killing machine in charge.
At the moment the horn sounded, the earth underwent a massive tremor.
Lide divided the army into four parts, each consisting of 300,000 soldiers: front, back, left, and right wings, with the center being 200,000 of the Demon Army.
Deploying the entire army into war all at once was not a wise move.
In a battle involving millions of people, it was often only the first three to five hundred thousand soldiers at the forefront engaging in combat, while the armies at the rear couldn’t possibly bypass their own front lines to fight the enemy.
Reserve forces were necessary both to prevent sneak attacks and to allow for flexible coordination.
Following the 300,000-strong army of Centaurs was a 200,000-strong Demon Army that Lide had brought from the Abyss.
With an average level above 13, the Demon Army was undoubtedly the most powerful legion in Dawn City, without a peer.
A combat strength above Level 10 was officer material in the Main Plane, but in the Demon Army, it merely constituted a common soldier.
In the Underworld, the Demon Army had already demonstrated its terrifying combat ability...
The weather in November brought cold winds, and the grass and trees on the land had long turned yellow.
Under the slightly gloomy sky, with millions of soldiers watching, the cold wind was stern.
The charge initiated by hundreds of thousands of soldiers was grotesquely exaggerated and terrifying.
The pebbles on the ground bounced crazily upward due to the earth’s vibrations.
Dust filled the sky, rising thousands of feet high, obscuring the sun.
On the other side, the army of the Centaur God, seeing the Dawn Army charge, hesitated no longer and also sounded the urgent horns.
Boom, boom, boom...
The Centaurs of Gale City were like arrows released from their strings, charging ferociously at the Dawn Army without showing any weakness.
The Centaurs from Gale City were clothed in simple iron armor, with many even wearing leather armor stitched from animal skins and armor made of bones.
Their spears were mostly made of bone, with only a few warriors carrying iron weapons.
By contrast, the Dawn Army was completely different; although they couldn’t quickly produce armor for all centaurs, everyone held a sharp spear forged by Dwarfs.
Bone armor was like mere paper against these spears, let alone regular iron armor.
At the forefront, a lavish force of 150,000 Centaur Heavy Cavalry was completely enveloped in Dwarf Armor.
Their terrifying defense could drive one to despair.
These charging Centaur Heavy Cavalry formed a sheer torrent of steel, crushing the earth beneath them.
With Dawn City as their support, the Dawn Centaurs’ equipment completely overwhelmed that of Gale City.
As the warriors below rapidly approached, and in the sky, Lord Withered Bones also followed the sound of the horn and woefully charged towards the Centaur army.
"Damn brats, are you ready to taste the Death given by the great Lord Withered Bones?"
"Such lowly four-legged beasts..."
"Perish, dying under my invincible Dragon Breath is a supreme honor..."
"Cackles..."
With the speed of Legendary Level, it took just over a dozen breaths to reach the forefront of the Centaur army, while the Dawn Army was still a good distance away.
Lord Withered Bones, completely lacking in moral principles, roared suddenly as a white-gray Undead breath began to spread from its throat.
Upon closing in on the charging Centaur army, it fiercely lowered its head high in the air.
Woo woo~
A gray-white breath mixed with a faint crimson, Death Dragon Breath, swept down irresistibly.
Crackle~
The Centaur army below had no chance to resist; sprayed with Dragon Breath carrying Negative Energy, they instantly dried up and withered.
One by one, they were drained of Life Force, instantly turning into weathered dry corpses, then shredding under inertia.
One second ago, they were bravely charging warriors; the next second, they were reduced to fragments and limbs, an utterly shocking scene.
Upon reaching Legendary Level, Lord Withered Bones’s Dragon Breath range had increased to 200 spears; currently, from a low altitude of 100 spears, its attack spanned a large surrounding circle.
Exhilarated, Lord Withered Bones twisted its head, its gray-white Dragon Breath shooting out like sparked rifles, instantly eroding surrounding Centaurs with an intense Death Energy.
As the spearhead core, the Centaur formation was swiftly cleared, leaving a vast empty space.
Fear spread rapidly...
And the Centaurs from the back, who weren’t hit by the Dragon Breath but stepped into the Death zone, immediately aged rapidly as their Life Force drained away.
One Dragon Breath had created a wide swath of Death territory, such Legendary Being, dreadful indeed.
Standing on the back of Lord Withered Bones, Lide estimated that this one Dragon Breath had devoured at least 3000 Centaurs; the killing effect was alarmingly staggering.
And just as Lord Withered Bones was wreaking havoc, a terrifyingly intense suppressive force suddenly rose from the rear.
Waves surged, rolling up millions of miles of sea water.
Like mountains collapsing, like the earth fracturing.
The entire world dimmed at this moment.
Lord Withered Bones, who brazenly challenged, had finally enraged the hidden Centaur God at the rear.
The ultimate ruler, the God of the Centaurs, was about to take action.

chapters.title: Chapter 454 - 456: Is It Over Already? That’s Boring (Hike up Pants)
chapters.content:
Chapter 454: Chapter 456: Is It Over Already? That’s Boring (Hike up Pants)
"That, that really is our god?..."
"It’s impossible, how could the great Centaur God possibly be defeated by a Fake God?!"
"I don’t believe it, how could this possibly happen?!!"
"It’s all fake, everything is fake!!"
The Centaur Army from Gale City erupted in disbelief barely moments after the collision, their tone filled with despair.
Because above in the sky, everyone clearly saw the deity they believed in and worshipped bound by magic chains and paraded around; they could not even sense any aura from him...
That was the Centaur God, their Protector, suspended mid-air like that!!
How could anyone accept such a scene?!
Accompanying the Centaur God was the lord of Gale City who had ruled them for decades, and even that powerful legend was missing, his fate unknown.
Lide, floating in mid-air, his long magic chains swinging with two prisoners on display, wore an enigmatic expression.
He had not expected the battle to go this smoothly.
Five minutes earlier, he had charged in on Withered Bone, who with a single Dragon Breath had taken out thousands of centaurs, and then the Centaur God could not stand the shock, striking out forcefully.
The Centaur God, soaring into the sky, had an immensely powerful presence, but Lide had not felt too much danger. Only later did he realize that the Centaur God’s strength had barely recovered to level 25, a silver wax gun head.
Not to mention his own legendary level of 28, even Withered Bone, the level 26 Undead Blood Dragon, could suppress the other party.
After realizing this, Lide went all out.
Divine Arts—Twilight Radiance, stripping away the opponent’s life, aging and rotting their soul.
Divine Arts—Twilight’s Approach, making the opponent briefly enter their twilight years.
Those two dishonorable Divine Arts launched a sudden attack, directly striking the Centaur God.
Then he used Legendary Shadow Blade, exploiting the terrifying characteristic of true damage on the first strike for a sneak attack.
A combination of moves left the Centaur God incapacitated and unconscious without so much as a fart; to prevent any accidents, Lide immediately sealed the other’s soul with the Power of Faith, creating the illusion of death.
The lord of Gale City, who had just stepped into the legendary level, was also hampered by his two Divine Arts; still in his geriatric state, he fell into unconsciousness.
The battle seemed so abrupt from start to finish.
Even now, the army below had only just begun to collide, with the Dawn Army taking advantage of their superior equipment to break through like a hot knife through butter.
So when Lide conveyed the news of the Centaur God’s capture to the centaur army below, Gale City’s forces couldn’t believe it or were unwilling to accept the reality...
This was ridiculous; their god couldn’t last even half an hour before being captured after just a few exchanges...
Was this some kind of joke?
The high-level centaurs, after sensing the aura of the Centaur God displayed in mid-air by Mage’s Hand, collapsed completely.
Their strongest support was gone just like that?
What was the point in continuing this war??
In their inner collapse, many high-ranking centaurs didn’t even bother to call out; they just started retreating, clearly not planning to throw away their lives.
Their god had been captured; did they have the right to clash with the opposition?
The opponent still had a Divine presence!!
Without their backbone, facing a deity felt suffocating.
Of course, there were some centaurs with firm beliefs who thought that the captured Centaur God in the sky was nothing but a sham conjured by the accursed Dawn God, deceiving them!
They were certain to shatter their enemies under the glorious radiance and emerge as the ultimate victors!
If everyone thought this way, then the centaur army below might still be troublesome, but there were also many who were terrified.
Some fled backwards and some charged forwards; the chaotic scene nearly led to the collapse of the entire Centaur Army, further causing chaos.
While some high-ranking officers were commanding, once an army of over a million soldiers fell into disarray, it was not something simple commands could restrain.
At that moment, Lide added fuel to the fire, his divine might bearing down like hellfire, the authority of the Dawn Main God striking like a divine punishment from the ninth heaven into everyone’s hearts.
The terrifying pressure made the already anxious centaurs below descend further into panic, their rationality quickly fading as fear took hold in their hearts.
At this moment, Lide’s voice spread in all directions.
"Centaur folk, I am the God of Dawn!
Guido Blackwind, the king of the Gale Empire destined to restore the Centaur Clan’s glory—is My believer."
Lide’s sudden proclamation left the centaurs below in chaos, now blankly looking up at the sky, while the Dawn Army in front also quietly slowed their assault’s pace, giving the centaur army a moment to breathe.
But his next words carried a shocking gravity.
"The reason I lead the attack against you today is that I once promised the Centaur God to protect the Centaur Clan."
The centaurs below were almost at the brink of mental collapse; you’re carrying our deity’s corpse and now you say you promised to protect us??
Was this some kind of joke?
Lide, however, paid no mind to those angry glares and continued.
"This Centaur God that I killed in front of you is not the deity you worshipped...
The true Centaur God fell during the ancient times. Now, the Centaur God you see before you is nothing more than a monster transformed by the Ancient Evil God.
"The Ancient Evil God had stolen all the Divine Power of the Centaur God and replaced him."
The Centaurs below who heard such shocking and outrageous news were all dumbfounded.
Is it really true?
Their god had long since died, and this creature before them was nothing more than a monstrosity transformed by the Ancient Evil God?
An absurd feeling surged through the hearts of the Centaurs, making it impossible for them to believe.
Yet Lide’s firm words made these Centaurs hesitate... These were the words from a Divine mouth, could they really be deceiving them?
Seeing the waver among the Centaurs below, Lide continued to increase his output.
"Centaurs, the race I will protect from now on, wake up.
The Centaur God was once my ally, and the reason I agreed to protect you Centaurs is because I had a very good relationship with him.
But he was murdered by this damned Ancient Evil God before you!! I have avenged him this very moment!!
Centaurs, I am not your enemy.
On the contrary, because of my covenant with the Centaur God, if you are willing to join the Gale Empire, I will protect you just like the former Centaur God from this day forward!"
Lide’s words traveled across the sky and throughout the entire battlefield, and the wills of those Centaurs who had been resolved to fight to the death were dealt a fatal blow.
The Centaur God had already been replaced by the Ancient Evil God... the god they had just regarded as their mortal enemy, the Dawn God, was actually an ally of the Centaur God.
The reason he attacked them was to avenge the god they worshiped, the Centaur God!!
This twisted and bizarre turn of events left the army below at a loss for words, their emotions too complex and intense to describe.
A million questions arose in their hearts, but they did not know what to say.
"It’s impossible, His Majesty can’t be dead... This is definitely fake, no, I don’t believe it!!"
A fervent Believer of the Centaurs nearly went insane at this moment, and without any heed, knelt down to pray, attempting to summon a response from their deity.
"His Majesty had already died... No wonder, no wonder he was so weak that he couldn’t even last a few minutes, it turns out it wasn’t my lord!! This damned Ancient Evil God!!"
Some Centaurs half-believed and half-doubted as they began to curse the divine figure in the sky loudly.
"Great Dawn Sovereign, your Glory will from this day forward eternally illuminate the direction of my advance. Your new Believer salutes you..."
Just as there were die-hard believers, there were some Centaurs who truly became followers of Lide after his speech, although they were a very small minority.
But most of them were still fluctuating between doubt and hesitation.
They felt in their hearts that Lide’s words might be false, but had to admit that the fall of the Centaur God was so rapid that it did not resemble the deity they worshiped.
How powerful had the aura emitted by the Centaur God just been? But he was killed in just a few encounters, such a huge discrepancy made these Centaurs unwilling to believe that he was their race’s Protector.
Instead, they were more inclined to the excuse provided by Lide—that the Centaur God had already been killed.
In the inner turmoil and confusion, these neutral Centaurs also lost their will to resist.
After a round of swindling by Lide, this terrifyingly large army no longer possessed any will to resist.
Seeing this scene, he couldn’t help but smile satisfactorily.
Of all tricks, winning the hearts is the best.
This was war—what schemes could not be employed?
Lide’s seemingly nonsensical and preposterous words had directly stricken the hearts of the Centaurs.
Not only did it hasten the progress of war and greatly reduce his own losses, but it also laid the seeds for conquering captives and future missionary work.
Killing several birds with one stone.
At this moment on the battlefield, the most pitiful was none other than the Centaur God.
The Centaur God was not dead, he hadn’t even passed out; he was just sealed off from his power by the Power of Faith, yet he could still sense the commotion outside.
Right now, the Centaur God was so angry that he seethed with rage, his soul nearly exploding with fury, as he cursed Lide hundreds of thousands of times over in his heart...
Had words been able to kill, Lide would have been crushed to death by hundreds of Planes falling from the heavens at this very moment.
This scoundrel, so despicably vile and dirty!!
How dare he slander him like this!!
But with his power sealed, the Centaur God could not utter a word and could only suppress his anger...
After viewing the uncertainty of the troops below, Lide spoke again.
"Lay down your arms, in the name of the Dawn God I promise you that as long as you do not initiate an attack, my army will not harm a single one of you.
My protected race, believe in me, this is your best choice.
The days of the Ancient are already upon us, those fearsome Evil Gods are devouring the entire world.
The god you worship has already fallen.
If there are no other gods to protect you, the Centaur Clan absolutely cannot survive this great catastrophe.
Centaurs should not perish in disaster, but instead, they should be reborn from it, and return to the glory of once ruling the continent!
The Gale Empire was founded by the Child of Destiny, Guido Blackwind, adhering to the will of the Main Plane—this is your Centaur Empire, also the opening of a new Chapter to restore past Glory.
If you join the Gale Empire, everyone will shed blood for the rise of the Centaurs, rather than die namelessly on this unknown withered grassland.
Cease resistance, join in the struggle for the future of the Centaurs!!"
Conquering hearts, this was the true conquest of hearts.
The enticing words delivered a final blow to the centaurs below.
No centaur wanted to resist anymore...
It must be said that Lide’s speech had a great appeal to the centaurs.
First of all, he was a powerful figure, a killer of the Centaur God—a genuine deity. Power was the only currency in this world.
Therefore, the merit of his words was unquestionable.
Next came the fact that their Centaur God had fallen in battle. Without their pillar of support, the centaurs, like dead dogs, could no longer sense the presence of their deity whose soul was sealed by the Power of Faith.
Regardless of whether the Centaur God’s body was possessed by the Ancient Evil God, it now hung above in the sky.
Lastly, the example laid before them by the Dawn Centaur Army, with their armored vests and weapons in hand, was irresistibly tempting for any centaur.
Moreover, King Guido Blackwind of the Gale Empire had been proclaimed by the centaurs as a savior-like figure.
This indicated that if they pledged allegiance to the enemy, they too would receive favorable treatment.
With all these reasons combined, they seemed to find few justifications to continue resisting, especially since the Centaur God was long dead, and Lide, whom they saw as an enemy, was there to avenge the Centaur God and vowed to protect them—this notion left them defenseless.
Finally, at Lide’s indication, Guido Blackwind was taken up into the sky by Kapp, and the words spoken by this Centaur King brought the war to its ultimate close.
"My fellow clansmen, I am the founder of the Gale Empire, your king—Guido Blackwind, blessed with the great Divine Bloodline of the Centaur God."
Most centaurs did not really care much for Lide, the Dawn Sovereign, after all, they had their own Racial Gods to worship.
But for this king who vowed to rebuild the Centaur Empire and restore its Glory, the centaurs held great affection.
After all, he had truly repelled the Ancient Monsters from Mount Short Hills, a deed not easily forgotten.
"You might have been puzzled as to why I, bearer of the Divine Bloodline, would forsake the great Centaur God and turn to the Dawn Sect...
Because all of this was the late God’s arrangement."
Guido’s words instantly caused an uproar amongst the centaurs.
The late God’s arrangement?!!
The believers couldn’t help looking puzzled. Had their God truly perished?
"Do you remember our legacy? Every centaur that awakens the Gale Bloodline is a blessed Child of Destiny by the Centaur God.
I am no exception!!
Years ago, it was under the deity’s blessing that I awoke the Gale Bloodline.
The God left me with words I would remember for the rest of my life—that he was on the verge of perishing due to the Ancient Evil God’s corruption, and if the centaurs wished to survive the forthcoming cataclysm, they had to seek sanctuary with his ally—the Dawn Sovereign.
After hearing this, unable to bear the thought of our great deity consumed by the Ancient Evil God or our proud race becoming extinct, I established the Gale Empire to seek salvation.
At that time, through the guidance the deity left us, after countless prayers and sacrifices, I managed to establish contact with the grand Dawn Sovereign.
You all know what happened next. While the Ancient Evil God cowered within Gale City, under the radiance of the Dawn Sovereign, I led our armies to repel the Ancient Monsters and reclaimed control of Mount Short Hills!
My people, all of this was orchestrated by the eternal will of our Centaur God!
Establishing the Gale Empire was his last wish!
Could you bear to watch your comrades, loved ones, and offspring consumed by Ancient Monsters, to be slain by the disastrous world?!
Could you bear to witness the centaurs disappear from this world?
Join the Gale Empire, I swear with my soul to you, I will dedicate everything in this life to the rise of the centaurs."
Clang~
After Guido’s words, it was unclear which centaur first dropped their weapon, but then followed a cacophony of clattering, as the entire army of over 1.8 million centaurs laid down their arms and surrendered.
Guido Blackwind’s words were full of persuasion, and not a single centaur could refuse.
Only a few fanatical believers were still praying manically and roaring, refusing to accept that the deity they worshipped had long passed away.
But in the grand scheme of things, those few voices were incapable of stirring any ripples.
And with that, the war ended.
The speed of this conquest over the centaurs caught Lide somewhat off guard.
Damn, I had steeled myself for an all-nighter, and before I could even take off my thermal pants, you tell me it’s all over...
But the end of the war was always a good thing. Not only did it prevent a large number of casualties, but Lide also directly gained control of over 1.8 million centaur warriors.
These captives, along with the original 1.2 million centaurs of the Gale Empire, increased the total number of centaurs under his command to over 3 million.
million!! These were centaurs, a race known for their formidable combat prowess!!
Just give these warriors enough equipment, and they could be transformed into a formidable fighting force instantaneously.
After the war came the time to manage the spoils of victory.
Originally, Lide had planned to make the centaurs a thorn in the side of Mount Short Hills, while also conveniently mining the area’s resources.
But having carried the stone coffin from the Sealed Land and learning that a significant number of Ancient Evil Gods still remained there, he reconsidered.
With the underworld now completely under his control, the expansive lands could accommodate a large population, and it would be better for the centaurs to farm there than to stay in the battlegrounds of Mount Short Hills.
And with the Space Gate, transferring troops was convenient...
In his view, the hill dwarves had value apart from Gale City, and only some meager veins remained; there was nothing else worth taking.
Why then continue to occupy this land?
Looking down at the scene of surrender below, Lide made his decision.
He decided to leave a portion of the centaurs to guard Gale City and send everyone else back to Dawn City.
Upon reflecting, he felt somewhat moved.
Four or five years ago, he had been extremely covetous of the hill dwarves, working painstakingly to win over the Iron Hoof Tribe to open up the market for this territory.
But in just a few short years, everything had undergone tremendous changes.
The land he had once coveted had become nothing but chicken ribs to him, tasteless to eat but wasteful to discard.
On November 20th, after incorporating the surrendering centaur army, the Dawn Army began transporting the centaur forces back to Dawn City.
The City Hall had been prepared early, directly transferring the centaurs underground through the Land of Bone-Burying, and a portion of them were moved to the Gravel Plane of the abyss to aid in its development.
These warriors were put to the best use, with no resources wasted.
At this time, Lide led his troops into the most central city of the hill dwarves—Gale City.
This only main city of the centaurs meant a great deal to them.
It was only by taking this city that he could declare his conquest of the hill dwarves complete.
However, when Lide set foot in this far-famed city, he felt deeply disappointed.
Because the centaurs had been blockaded by humans for too long, the entire city, though spacious, lacked anything of value, filled with a sense of backwardness and primitiveness.
Lide even doubted whether the centaurs had considered living facilities at all when they built the city, perhaps solely focusing on constructing walls for defense.
Messy streets, houses built haphazardly everywhere, sewage drains reeking horribly, ditches full of feces... It was even worse than the slums of Green City.
How could the centaurs have tolerated such an environment?
What rendered him speechless was that the treasure vault of the centaurs contained only a few hundred thousand Gold Pucks, with the rest being miscellaneous foodstuffs; they were so poor that Lide found it pitiable.
After listening to the reports from the personnel below, Lide concluded that Gale City was worthless.
Except for the ten-blade-high walls that could fend off enemies, the city had no industrial facilities, no living facilities—nothing he desired.
Lide decisively recognized this situation; with no value, it was best abandoned entirely.
Then he left without a trace of sentimentality, leading the centaur army away from the city he had just occupied.
Of course, before leaving, he instructed his troops to take everything they could, not sparing a single grain of the food.
On November 26th,
With Frost Month coming to an end, the weather turned even colder.
In nearly a week’s time, all 3 million centaurs were transported back to Dawn City.
And thus, the land of the hill dwarves was completely abandoned by Lide, even with many of its minable veins left untouched.
With mining in the abyss and the Underworld progressing, these two mineral-rich areas could easily compensate for the loss of terrestrial veins, and further development might yield even greater production.
There was no need to waste effort on the hill dwarves.
At this moment, no one expected that this land, occupied by the centaurs for over a hundred thousand years, would experience its first day without them.
On November 27th.
In the City Hall office, Lide sat behind his desk, looking at the files in his hands with a bizarre expression before closing them.
These were the City Hall’s summaries of resources seized from the hill dwarves.
Yet there was nothing in them worthy of his extended attention.
"The hill dwarves ultimately yielded assets worth no more than 200,000 Gold Pucks?"
"The food barely suffices for 500,000 people for a year..."
"These guys are really that broke."
He shook his head with a wry smile.
"But thankfully, the real gains are a population of 3 million, plus a living divine, the Centaur God, and a legendary-level centaur."
"Considering that, the harvest can be deemed barely acceptable."
After some contemplation, Lide had to admit that the centaurs were truly destitute, valuable only in themselves and without a penny to their name.
Fortunately, the Centaur God was a consolation for him, not leaving him empty-handed.
"But what can be done with a living divine? That’s indeed a problem..."
Lide stroked his chin, lost in thought.
He had declared the Centaur God dead when he subdued the centaurs, so now he could only seal the divine’s soul with the Power of Faith,
otherwise, if he were to be unsealed, those believers who still worshiped the Centaur God would immediately sense his presence.
Then all his efforts would have been in vain.
"I wonder if this Centaur God can be subjugated?"
"Having a bona fide divine as an underling doesn’t seem too bad..."

chapters.title: Chapter 455 - 456: The Imprisoned Goddess, Dawn Believers Anxiously Await the Return of the King
chapters.content:
Chapter 455: Chapter 456: The Imprisoned Goddess, Dawn Believers Anxiously Await the Return of the King
Dawn City’s old district, situated near the mountainside, was eerily silent at this moment.
Because this residential building was located in an insignificant fringe area, with neither military facilities nor granaries around, patrols and other people paid it little attention.
Without moonlight and late into the night, Dawn City was still brightly lit, but since this building was unimportant, only a few lampposts lit the surrounding streets.
In the dark environment, these two lampposts not only failed to provide sufficient brightness, but they also made the atmosphere around seem somewhat oppressive.
The sparse breeze blew through the tree branches, making the surrounding environment even colder.
Shortly after a patrol team passed by, a mysterious figure cloaked in a cape used the dim corner to stealthily approach the unremarkable residential building.
The streetlights, filtered through the treetops, cast large patches of light on the ground.
However, the mysterious cloaked individual was like a ghost, casting no shadow even under the light...
What happened next was even more astounding: the cloaked individual, treating the thick walls of the residential building as if they were air, went straight through the walls and deep underground, arriving in a basement deep underground after a short while.
From the excavation marks in the basement, it might have been around for a century; it was definitely not excavated recently.
In fact, the residential building above was built right on top of this basement, completely blocking the entrance.
In other words, this basement was a dead zone, disconnected from the outside world.
Fortunately, a hidden ventilation duct had been left during the initial excavation, preventing the growth of poisonous gases in the basement.
At this moment, in this underground chamber unknown to outsiders, there were large and small wooden storage compartments all around, densely packed with all sorts of peculiar magic materials, as if this place had become a mage’s magic laboratory...
But what surprised them most was at the very back of the basement, where a huge iron cage, half-embedded in the wall filled with magical fluctuations.
Inside this large iron cage, a seventeen or eighteen-year-old girl was bound by inscribed magic iron chains on her hands, feet, and even around her neck.
The magic iron chains were long, and the shackles on her limbs and neck were separate, so the bound girl had some room to move and wasn’t completely restricted.
At that moment, this stunningly beautiful girl appeared listless, her long dress stained with dirt, huddled miserably in the corner of the cage like an abused kitten.
When the mysterious person in the black cloak appeared in the basement, the girl finally seemed to come to life, slowly raising her head, revealing amber eyes that burned with barely concealed fury.
But just as she attempted to move, the inscriptions on the chains lit up, forcibly dispersing the power within her.
Feeling the strange sensation in her body, the girl furrowed her brows, her voice as parched as if she had been thirsty in the desert for half a month.
"You’ve trapped me here for a full half month now, state your purpose, Knight and God of Murder—Stu Yate!"
Her words were filled with uncontrollable rage when she mentioned the name Stu Yate.
The silver-gray eyes beneath Stu Yate’s black cloak shifted slightly.
"Charis... oh, no, you should be called Bast, right? My noble goddess..."
His tone was filled with intense excitement and undeniable pleasure.
"Cat and Goddess of Joy, hehehe... it truly excites me.
Who would have thought that the free, proud Cat Goddess would one day be caged by me..."
The Cat and Goddess of Joy is one of the most capricious deities among the gods, sensual, enchanting, aloof, unpredictable in her actions, fond of pleasure, and liking all things interesting.
Once, Stu Yate had pursued this goddess for a long time, but how could his adherence to the knightly codes possibly appeal to a Cat Goddess who pursued pleasure and fun?
Thus, Bast never even granted Stu Yate a proper glance.
But now, everything was different; the once unattainable goddess was confined in a cage by him, and he could do anything he desired to her.
Whipping the former goddess, ravaging the previously untouchable being... such psychological stimulation almost drove him mad whenever he thought of it.
This was power, wasn’t it?
With power, one could have everything.
If he were still that god of knights on the slate, even if Bast stood before him, he could only secretly anguish.
But he was no longer that powerless god of knights; now, he possessed the power to control fate.
Having captured his former object of pursuit and dragged the high and mighty goddess from her pedestal, the inside of Stu Yate swelled immensely.
Hearing Tu Yate’s unabashed mockery, Bast’s face turned extremely ugly.
As a goddess who once roamed freely, being imprisoned in an iron cage now, the loss of freedom ignited a raging fire within her.
A sense of regret unavoidably rose in her heart; heaven knows how thrilled she had been when she encountered Stu Yate in Dawn City half a month ago.
The cataclysm arrived, she lost her power, and had to hide herself in this post-cataclysm world, cautiously regaining her strength.
Against such a backdrop, when she felt very uneasy inside, she met Stu Yate, who had pursued her before, always polite and very gentlemanly in nature.
Although she had no interest in the protocol-abiding god of knights, she was quite reassured by this deity who had always kept his promises and defended justice in his heart.
Thus, she easily trusted Stu Yate.
But the final outcome... this former god of knights had become a god of knights and murder, and the knightly code he once upheld had become a joke.
"Stu Yate, the position of the god of murder may momentarily obscure the justice in your heart, but I believe the honor of a knight will let you find the lost light...
Come back, abandon the godship of murder; it’s not suitable for you, my once dear friend..."
Bast looked steadfastly at Stu Yate, making one last attempt to persuade.
Stu Yate was momentarily stunned, then this knight, who had once deemed honor as vital as life itself, started laughing wildly as if he heard the funniest joke in the world.
His unrestrained laughter echoed maniacally in the basement, like a patient who had escaped from an asylum...
"Hahahaha... give up?...
Hahahaha... the glory of a knight?"
The laughter lasted for several minutes, until Bast felt a coldness inside, and abruptly, as if someone had grabbed his throat, Stu Yate stopped laughing quite abruptly.
Then he violently threw back the cloak that covered his face, revealing a face marked with gray mysterious inscriptions, the dark aura from the inscriptions added a touch of brutality to his handsome face.
After revealing his true face, Stu Yate quickly stepped forward, his hands slammed on the iron bars of the cage with a resounding clang, veins on the back of his hands bulging, his face filled with violence and anger.
"Give up?! You tell me to give up the godship of murder?!"
His hands fiercely struck the bars of the cage, his tone nearly frantic!
"To give up the powerful strength I now possess and continue being a god of knights who you mock?!"
"Foolish!!"
A loud clanging noise made Bast inside tremble, suddenly she recoiled backward, the chains on her body rubbing against each other with a crisp sound.
Her face displayed an expression of fear, like that of a startled cat.
At this moment, she truly realized that the God of Knights of old was dead... The being before her now was a stranger who held the position of God of Murder.
Watching the goddess’s panicked demeanor in the cage, Stu Yate’s face revealed an indescribable twisted pleasure.
"See, Bast? This is power, the kind of power I’ve never possessed before!
The proud you can now only become a cat I keep in captivity!
All of this is brought by the God of Murder position.
Everything is so wonderful...
Now, I am your master, you have no right to point fingers at me!
Hahahahaha!"
Watching Bast’s alarmed expression, Stu Yate felt both a sense of revenge and a sense of achievement in controlling someone else’s fate, nearly intoxicating the knight and god of murder.
"What in the world do you want to do!"
Bast roared while holding back her inner turmoil.
At this moment, the mad Stu Yate struck fear in her heart, the fear of facing a crazed evil god.
She completely gave up the last illusions in her heart.
This man truly wanted to become an evil god from his heart, not being misled...
Stu Yate suddenly withdrew from the cage, his madness subsiding quickly, his expression returning to calm in a very short time, as if the maniac who had just laughed maniacally had nothing to do with him.
This huge abnormality made Bast in the cage even more terrified.
"What do I want to do? I want you!"
Stu Yate’s silver-gray eyes glinted with a fanatic possessiveness.
Greedy and insane.
"Not only do I want you, but I also want to become the most powerful deity! I aim to be the existence that everyone fears in the catastrophe of the ancient days!"
"You’re dreaming!"
"Dreaming? No, dreams can’t capture something this wonderful.
The ancient days have already dawned, those deities that were once high above are now starting from the same line as us, and some powerful deities are even weaker than us!
The God of Murder previously had medium divine power, but isn’t he now dead by my hand??
As long as I keep murdering deities, I will continue to gain power, after all, the God of Murder position now belongs to me!"
Correct content is on
Stu Yate’s emotions grew more and more excited.
"And don’t you think this city we are in is perfect for being the headquarters on the Main Plane?
As long as I control this city, I can keep luring those deities who descend onto the Main Plane to their deaths!
And you, you are my bait...
The Cat and Joy Goddess, do you realize how tempting you are?
Many of those deities who hear about you, I think the majority will not pass up such an opportunity...
Once I take over this city, I will turn it into a death trap, all those deities will become my prey, without exception..."
Hearing these words, Bast suddenly remembered Stu Yate’s current title... Knight and God of Murder.
Although this idea was quite crude at this moment, if it was really perfected by him, she inexplicably felt that he might truly have the chance to keep hunting other deities.
The position of God of Murder is very special, as long as you murder your enemy with intrigue, you can plunder a part of the enemy’s power, the stronger the murder target, the more power can be plundered.
Many deities in the past have died by the hands of the God of Murder.
"Stu Yate, you will not succeed!
The other deities won’t fall for this, you can’t take over this city...
This magical city is definitely not something you can subvert!"
Stu Yate gave a cold laugh, pulling the cloak up from the back of his head, covering his face again.
"A city built by a fake god... also grants you confidence?
My plan has already begun, Bast.
When I take over this city, I will possess you bit by bit! My... goddess.
Correct content is on )
Hahahahahahahaha..."
Accompanied by a burst of mad laughter, Stu Yate’s figure once again passed through the solid rock walls and disappeared inside the underground.
At this point, Bast was still useful to him, he had no interest in doing... that.
And after tasting the flavor of power, he had already lost much of his interest in the goddess for whom he once desperately yearned.
He visited here more to satisfy his need to show off, having been ignored and looked down upon in the past, and now turning the tables to become the master.
Some things are most beautiful when unattainable, losing interest once obtained.
Long after Stu Yate’s figure disappeared inside the underground, Bast’s face color slightly improved.
But as she turned her head around, glancing at the divine-power-forged iron chains and the chains on her body, she felt an infinite fear in her heart.
A cat yearning for freedom, at this moment, had lost her most precious thing, it seemed no one could save her anymore... Despair was slowly devouring her heart.
---
---
---
After leaving the underground, Stu Yate, dressed in a black cloak, wandered like a ghost through Dawn City.
After a long while, he didn’t hide in some inconspicuous corner but boldly entered a manor owned exclusively by the Bloodline.
Entering the manor’s bedroom, Stu Yate skillfully took off his cloak and placed it in his space storage bag.
Then, with a wave of his hand, he took out an ominously glowing dull mask from the space storage bag.
The mask was thin like human skin, emitting an extremely evil aura.
The knight and God of Murder showed a trace of satisfaction and directly put the mask on his face.
The moment he put on the mask, an indescribable force burst forth.
Stu Yate’s body began to twist and transform at that moment. After a few breaths, the tall knight and the God of Murder had vanished, replaced by a true Vampire with unfolded bat wings and tusks protruding from its mouth.
A real Vampire.
As Stu Yate felt the changes in his body, he walked to the mirror and looked at his reflection, a cold smile forming at the corner of his mouth.
He had made thorough preparations for the takeover of this city.
The mask on his face was a trophy from killing the God of Murder.
Divine Artifact—The Illusion Face.
By killing the target and letting the mask devour its soul, he could transform into the slain victim, and as long as the soul was intact, he could gain most of the victim’s memories through the mask.
This was his confidence!
But that was not all, Stu Yate casually drew a dagger inscribed with mysterious inscriptions from a hidden spot on his waist.
This dagger seemed to imprison countless wronged souls. As soon as it was exposed to the air, the temperature in the room plummeted by more than ten degrees. Its emanating aura was terrifying to the extreme. Merely gazing at the dagger could chill one’s soul with murderous intent.
Godslayer Dagger, another Divine Artifact of the God of Murder—if it could pierce the enemy’s heart, it could directly devour the opponent’s soul, sealing it within the dagger.
These two artifacts had once accompanied the God of Murder in hunting numerous divine beings; now, they would accompany him to the pinnacle!!
Stu Yate’s smile gradually turned maniacal.
Over these months, he had grasped the intricacies of the city. Now, it was time to initiate his plan.
This city required ten times the external force to breach, but they had a fatal flaw—the owner of the city, Kachar City Lord.
He only needed to infiltrate his ranks, cut his throat with the dagger, and consume his soul with the Illusion Face.
Once he killed Kachar City Lord and substituted himself, all glory would belong to him; no one could stop him.
Murderous intent was evident in his now blood-red eyes.
The Vampire might soon learn of their sovereign’s fall, but he had already prepared a countermeasure—before hunting Kachar City Lord, he would find a way to move the Vampires out of Dawn City.
After killing Kachar City Lord, he would immediately control the army of Dawn City. If the Vampires did not obey his command, he could directly order Dawn City’s army to hunt them down.
He could even prevent those vampires from entering Dawn City!
Based on Stu Yate’s understanding of Dawn City’s army, once Kachar City Lord issued an order, the army would definitely carry it out, even if it was to hunt the Vampire!
Could these lowly vampires pose any challenge to him?
Stu Yate was utterly confident in his plan, having made ample preparations.
"This is the charm of conspiracy, truly mesmerizing..."
The knight and God of Murder softly licked the Godslayer Dagger at the tip of his tongue, his gaze intoxicated and deranged.
Step one, understand everything about Dawn City, completed.
Step two, become a member of the Vampire, completed.
Step three, approach Kachar City Lord and murder him, in progress...
---
---
---
Lide looked at the Centaur God lying on the floor, his expression rather peculiar.
He had intended to directly enslave this divine being, but he ultimately found... it was useless.
His invariably successful Divine Art—Soul Assimilation—applied to this being, dissolved instantly like a clay ox entering the sea, stirring not even the slightest ripple.
This was somewhat annoying.
"Should I just kill him???
And having finally caught a living god... wouldn’t it be a waste to kill him like this?"
"And this guy’s soul is also a treasure. Killing him would inevitably dissipate the soul; first, I need to figure out a way to extract his soul..."
While others were troubled by the lack of good opportunities, Lide was troubled by having something too good to handle.
Thud, thud, thud~
As he pondered, there was a knock on the door, and shortly after, Harrison stepped inside the room.
Seeing the unconscious Centaur God on the ground, the City Hall Speaker’s eyelids twitched.
This was his first time seeing a living divine being, and not one of the fake gods ordained by Lide but a real divine being, albeit currently a bit weak. But no matter how weak, it was still a god...
"Your Lordship, how do you plan to deal with this Centaur God?"
Lide shook his head.
"I can’t subdue this guy with Divine Arts; I’m quite troubled indeed, killing him would be too wasteful if I can’t extract his soul..."
"Soul? Your Lordship, Withered Bone is undead..."
"Withered Bone? That idiot!! As an undead, he doesn’t even know how to perform the magic of soul stripping!
Even if he knows, it would still be difficult, a divine being’s soul isn’t easy to extract..."
Finally, Lide helplessly waved his hand, "Let’s seal him for now and deal with him once we find a solution."
Harrison could only respond with a wry smile, having no experience in stripping the soul of a divine being himself.
"And how have the centaurs been arranged?"
The 3 million centaurs were a massive asset; if managed well, they could greatly aid Dawn City.
"They have been settled.
2.8 million have been transported to the Underworld, while the remaining 200,000 were placed in the Abyss Gravel Plane."
Harrison replied, "Your Lordship, the centaurs are being proselytized by priests from the Dawn Sect; within the next half year, they are expected to become our believers."
Lide nodded.
"The 200,000 sent to the Abyss need to be closely monitored. They must be rotated when necessary, otherwise, the rules of the Abyss will corrupt them into evil centaurs..."
Hearing this, Harrison spoke thoughtfully.
"Your Lordship, becoming evil centaurs might not be a bad thing."
Not a bad thing?
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly as he instantly understood the implication of the other’s words.
He pondered for a moment, then nodded.
"Then go ahead and do it. We can afford to sacrifice 200,000 Centaurs."
Mercy does not command troops, righteousness does not manage wealth.
The Centaurs are of the Order Neutral Camp, but if transformed into the Order Evil Camp to gain combat strength, he did not mind letting these Centaurs be transformed.
What he wanted was a strong army, not just freeloaders.
Centaurs aren’t Cave Dwellers; it’s understandable that Cave Dwellers have no combat abilities, but what use are Centaurs without combat abilities?
If they were merely believers, one Centaur ate more than five Cave Dwellers... Was he wasting food for this effort?
"Yes, Lord IIo," Harrison replied before continuing.
"There is another matter to report to you.
Three days ago, Lord Emi developed a new type of plague that greatly enhances human combat abilities, and its side effects are completely controllable, preventing the loss of sanity."
Oh?
Hearing this news, Lide’s eyes immediately lit up.
Lord Emi had been researching plagues since receiving the Plague Divine Position as a reward, nearly a year ago.
Had he finally achieved results now?
"Have tests been arranged? What are the specific effects, and what are the side effects?"
"Tests have been arranged. The plague’s effects are very powerful, capable of enhancing strength and physical quality by up to three times, while the side effects cause the body to mutate, distort, and turn into a horrifying monster.
Because of the powerful side effects, it cannot be applied to our army in the short term."
Harrison seemed slightly regretful; the effects of the plague were very good, but the side effects were quite problematic.
Not many were willing to turn into monstrous beings, neither human nor ghost.
Yet Lide was indifferent, "If Dawn’s army can’t use it, why not experiment with Abyss Demons?
Demons, in pursuit of power, don’t care about their appearance..."
Harrison smiled and said.
"Lord, your idea is somewhat similar to that of the heroic Lord Emi.
Lord Emi has already started experimenting on demons. I just feel it’s a pity that our Bloodline and other armies can’t use it.
After all, that enhancement of physical ability is really good."
Lide nodded, "Good, proceed with the experiment and report back to me once you are sure there are no issues. Then we can promote it on a large scale."
After finishing, he seemed to recall something and looked keenly at Harrison.
"How is Green City doing now?"
During this time, he had been busy dealing with the Ancient Evil God in Dwarf Valley and solving the Centaur issue in the Dwarf Hill, hardly paying attention to the affairs of Green City.
Upon hearing this, Harrison’s face immediately darkened, rage uncontainable in his eyes.
"Lord, that damned God of Nobles has gone mad!
To deal with the Dawn Sect, he has even deployed priests and church knights to take action directly!"
"You despicable heretics! The great God of Nobles is watching over you, and yet you dare to follow the sect of this Fake God?!"
In Green City, on a street in the south district, dozens of church knights wearing the emblem of the God of Nobles were mockingly shoving believers who had come to pray at the Dawn Church.
A crowd had gathered around, pointing and murmuring. Most of them sympathized with the Dawn believers, as they had seen such scenes too often in the past few months.
"No! We are followers of Lord Ilo, and we’re not going anywhere! This is where we belong!"
A devout Dawn believer shouted at a church knight nearby, his face filled with indignation and fury.
These damned bastards had been oppressing the Dawn Sect so brazenly for months!
In the past, the church did not dare to act so recklessly when the Dawn priests were present, but today was a meeting day for the Dawn priests at the Main Church. In so brief a time, the group of church knights had occupied the entrance to the Dawn Church.
"Oh, so you’re followers of a Fake God and you’re upset by it? Ha, these damned heretics, if it weren’t for the mercy of our great Lord, you heretics would have been hanged at the church’s main door long ago!
Lord Ilo? Bah, a fake god, what right does he have to receive worship in Green City!"
This blasphemous speech instantly enraged the Dawn believers.
"How dare you slander Lord Ilo! You are committing blasphemy!"
"This damned blasphemer should be burned at the stake!"
"Kneel and apologize, or today I will show you the consequences of desecrating Lord Ilo!"
Carried away by their rage, the Dawn believers charged at the church knights. Although there were many low-level professionals among the believers, they were no match for the strong church knights.
Despite equal numbers, they were quickly trampled to the ground.
Outside the Dawn Church, there were cries of sorrow.
The passing residents turned pale at the sight, but no one dared to speak; many bowed their heads, suppressing their inner emotions and hurriedly left the scene.
They had seen too much of this in the past few months.
Initially, the nobles had subtly oppressed the Dawn Sect, but over the months, the counterattacks from the Dawn Sect had not troubled them, which only emboldened the arrogant nobles.
Over time, the Noble God Sect had moved to the foreground, becoming executioners and unabashedly preventing the Dawn believers from praying.
Many of the surrounding residents were originally followers of the Dawn Sect, but after such crazed oppression and unable to bear the humiliation anymore, they had to withdraw. They had watched the Dawn Sect decline helplessly.
More importantly, Lord Ilo, who had once driven the entire Green City mad, had disappeared nearly a year ago.
This left most of the Dawn believers in utter despair. Had Lord Ilo truly fallen as the nobles claimed?
The believers still clinging to hope were dwindling by the day; they could not believe, could not accept that their worshipped Divine had fallen. They firmly believed that Lord Ilo would eventually return triumphantly.
Initially, many had held this belief, but as time went on, those who still persevered were fewer and fewer. Perhaps, the Dawn Sect... truly had no hope left.
Lord Ilo could no longer return...
And those vulture-like nobles would completely dominate the city once the Dawn Sect was gone.
Dawn, it seemed, no longer had any light...

Chapter 456: Chapter 457 (Anti-piracy Chapter, do not subscribe) Looking up at the sky, the king returns, unparalleled dominance
PS: This is an anti-theft Chapter, please do not subscribe, as it will not affect anything. In twenty minutes, I will replace the redundant content.
Word count for the anti-theft Chapter (13400) will be replaced by the official Chapter word count (13600)
----
----
----
Even at this moment, the armies below had just begun to clash, with the Dawn Army using their equipment advantage to cut through the enemy like a hot knife through butter.
So when Lide transmitted the news of the Centaur God’s capture to the centaur army below, the troops of Gale City could hardly believe it, or they were unwilling to believe it was true...
It was too absurd; their god couldn’t even last half an hour, captured after only a few exchanges...
Was this some sort of joke?
And those centaur high ranks, after sensing the presence of their Centaur God tied up by Mage’s Hand and paraded midair, simply collapsed.
Was their biggest support just gone like that?
What was the point of continuing this war??
Under the collapse of their inner resolve, many high-ranking centaurs didn’t even signal the others before they started retreating, clearly unwilling to march to their deaths.
Their god had been captured; did they even stand a chance against the opposition who still had a Divine being on their side?
Being enemy to a Divine without any backup crushed them.
Of course, there were also centaurs with firm beliefs who thought that the captured Centaur God in the sky was merely an illusion, a trick by that damned Dawn Sovereign!
Under the protection of their lord, they would surely crush the enemy before them and emerge as the victors!
If everyone thought this way, then perhaps the centaur army below would be more troublesome, but there were many who had lost their courage.
Some fled backwards while some charged forward, creating a chaotic scene that nearly led the entire centaur formation to collapse, further fueling the chaos among all the centaur troops.
Although some high ranks were still commanding, once an army of millions fell into disarray, how could simple commands suppress it?
At this moment, Lide added fuel to the fire, his divine dignity striking every heart like a heavenly punishment from the nine skies.
