The terrifying pressure sent the already uneasy centaurs below into panic, their rationality quickly fading as fear took over their hearts.
And at this moment, Lide’s voice spread throughout the lands.
"Centaurs, I am the Dawn Sovereign!
The destined restorer of the Centaur Empire’s former glory — Guido Blackwind, is my follower."
Lide’s sudden speech left the chaotic centaurs below staring blankly at the sky, while the Dawn Army in front also quietly slowed their onslaught, giving the centaur army a moment to breathe.
His next words, however, carried an air of sensationalism.
"The reason I lead an army to engage you today is that I once promised the Centaur God to protect your race."
The centaurs below were on the verge of a mental breakdown. You’re dragging our god’s corpse, and now you say you had pledged to protect us??
Isn’t this a joke?
But Lide ignored those angry stares and continued.
"This Centaur God that I have slain is not the one you worship..."
"The true Centaur God fell when the Ancient Times had come, and now, this being before you claiming to be the Centaur God is but a monster transformed by an Ancient Evil God.
This Ancient Evil God has stolen all the divine powers of the Centaur God and usurped his place."
The centaurs below were dumbfounded by this earth-shattering news.
Is this true??
Their god had already died, and this one before them was just a monster transformed by the Ancient Evil God?
An absurd feeling surfaced in the hearts of the centaurs, making it hard for them to believe.
But Lide’s firm words made those centaurs hesitate... after all, these were words from a Divine, could they really just be deceiving them?
Seeing the wavering centaurs below, Lide continued to push his narrative.
"Centaurs, my future protected kin, wake up.
The Centaur God was once my ally, and the reason I agreed to protect you was that he and I had a great relationship.
But he was killed by this damned Ancient Evil God before your very eyes!! And now, I have avenged him!!
I am not your enemy, Centaurs.
On the contrary, due to my covenant with the former Centaur God, if you are willing to join the Gale Empire, henceforth, I too will protect you just like the former Centaur God did!"
Lide’s words spread across the battlefield from the sky, delivering a fatal blow to the will of those centaurs who were determined to fight to the death.
The Centaur God had long been replaced by an Ancient Evil God... and the god they had regarded as their mortal enemy, the Dawn Sovereign, turned out to be an ally of their Centaur God.
He had attacked them to avenge their own Centaur God!!
The bizarre twist left the army below indescribably complex, overwhelmed by intricacy.
Countless questions rose in their minds, yet they didn’t know what to say.
"Impossible, our lord could not have died... this is definitely false, no, I do not believe it!!"
A centaur zealot, nearly driven mad, began to pray fervently on his knees, calling for a response from the god he worshipped.
"Our lord had died long ago... no wonder he was so feeble, not enduring even a few minutes. It was not my master!! This damned Ancient Evil God!!"
Some centaurs were half-convinced, beginning to loudly curse at the Centaur God in the sky.
"Great Dawn Sovereign, Your Glory from today onward shall eternally illuminate the path before me. Your new followers salute You..."
Correspondingly, there were in fact some centaurs who truly became Lide’s followers after these words, although they were a very small fraction.
The majority were still halting between doubts and hesitations.
In their hearts, they felt that Lide’s words might be false, but they couldn’t deny that the Centaur God’s defeat was so swift it didn’t seem like the Divine Protector of their faith at all.
How powerful was the aura the Centaur God had just emitted? Yet, he had been killed in just a few encounters, such a huge gap made these centaurs unwilling to believe he was their race’s Protector.
Instead, they were more inclined to the excuse Lide provided them with at this moment—the Centaur God had already been killed.
Amidst the inner turmoil and confusion, these neutral centaurs also lost the will to resist.
With a flip of Lide’s swindle, this terrifyingly numerable army now wholly lacked the spirit to resist.
Witnessing this scene, he couldn’t help but smile in satisfaction.
Among the thirty-six stratagems, capturing one’s heart is supreme.
This is war, what strategy is not permissible?
Lide’s seemingly ridiculous and outrageous speech, however, struck the hearts of the centaurs.
Not only did it accelerate the progress of the war and significantly reduce his own casualties, but it also planted the seeds for conquering prisoners and preaching in the future.
Several birds with one stone.
On the entire battlefield, at this moment, none was more miserable than the Centaur God.
The Centaur God wasn’t dead, he hadn’t even lost consciousness. He was merely isolated from his power by the Power of Faith by Lide, still able to sense the commotion outside.
At this moment, anger was raging in the Centaur God’s heart, his soul nearly bursting with fury, cursing Lide one million and eight hundred thousand times over in his mind...
If words could kill, Lide by now would have been crushed to death by the descent of several hundred Planes.
This bastard, so despicable, shameless, vulgar, dirty!!
To slander him like this!!
But with his power sealed, the Centaur God couldn’t voice any words and could only suffer the indignation silently...
Upon noticing the wavering of the troops below, Lide spoke again.
"Lay down your arms, in the name of the Dawn God, I assure you that as long as you do not attack first, my army will not harm any one of you.
My protected people, trust me, this is your best option.
The days of old have already arrived, those terrifying Evil Gods are devouring the entire world.
The Divine of your belief has now fallen.
Without the protection of another Divine, the Centaur race surely will not survive this great cataclysm.
Centaurs should not perish in the disaster but should be reborn from it and reclaim the glory of once ruling the continent!
The Gale Empire is a nation established by Guido Blackwind, the Child of Destiny, in accordance with the will of the Main Plane; it is your Centaur Empire, and a new Chapter to restore your former Glory.
If you join the Gale Empire, everyone will bleed for the rise of the centaurs, rather than dying meaninglessly on this unknown withered grassland.
Give up resistance, and join the struggle for the future of centaurs!!"
This was the true capturing of hearts.
These enticing words delivered the final blow to the centaurs below.
No more centaurs wanted to resist...
It must be said that Lide’s speech was extremely attractive to the centaurs.
Firstly, he was a strong figure, a true Divine being who had killed the Centaur God, and in this world, power was everything.
Hence, his words were unquestionably credible.
Secondly, the Centaur God had already fallen, and they had lost their backer. Like a dead dog, the Centaur God, whose soul was sealed by the Power of Faith, could no longer be sensed by his followers.
Moreover, whether the body of the Centaur God had been possessed by the Ancient Evil God or not, it was now suspended in the sky.
Finally, the example set by the Dawn Centaur army in front of them, their armor, and weapons in hand, were all profoundly enticing to the centaurs.
Moreover, the King of the Gale Empire, Guido Blackwind, was propagated among the centaurs as a savior-like figure.
This indicated that if they sided with them, they too would receive favorable treatment.
With such reasons compounded, they seemed to lack many grounds for further resistance, especially since the Centaur God was already dead, and their enemy Lide was seeking vengeance for the Centaur God and would also protect them, this reasoning left them defenceless.
In the end, under Lide’s signal, Guido Blackwind was brought into the sky by Kapu, and the words spoken by the Centaur King sealed the fate of the war.
"My people, I am the founder of the Gale Empire, your King—Guido Blackwind, endowed with the Gale Bloodline gifted by the great Centaur God."
For most centaurs, they weren’t particularly moved by Lide, the Dawn God, after all, they had their own Racial Gods.
But for this king, who aspired to rebuild the Centaur Empire and restore the centaur’s Glory, the centaurs held a lot of goodwill.
After all, he genuinely repelled the Ancient Monster’s encroachment on the Dwarf Hills, a merit that can’t be erased with a few words.
"Everyone must be wondering why I, as one blessed with the Divine Bloodline, would leave the great Centaur God and convert to the Dawn Sect...
Because, all of this was arranged by the Lord during his last moments."
Guido’s words immediately caused tumult among the centaurs.
Arrangements in the last moments?!!
The believers couldn’t help but feel bewildered. The Lord, had he truly perished??
"Do you remember our legend? Every centaur who awakens the Gale Bloodline is a Child of Destiny blessed by the Centaur God."
I was no exception!!
A few years ago, under the blessing of our Lord, I awakened the Gale Bloodline.
At that time, our Lord conveyed a message that I would remember for the rest of my life — due to the erosion by an Ancient Evil God, he was on the verge of falling. If the Centaurs wished to survive the upcoming great cataclysm, they could only seek the protection of the Dawn God, our ally.
Correct content is on .
Upon hearing these words, I could not bear to see our Lord consumed by the Ancient Evil God or our great Centaur race to be annihilated, so I established the Gale Empire for our salvation.
At that time, through the guidance left by our Lord, after countless prayers and sacrifices, I finally made contact with the great Dawn God.
You all should know what happened next. The Gale Empire, while that Ancient Evil God holed up in Gale City, basked in the glory of the Dawn God. I led our mighty army to repel the Ancient Monsters and reclaimed control of the Dwarf Hills!
My fellow clansmen, all of this is arranged by our eternal faith — the Centaur God, our Lord!
Establishing the Gale Empire was His will!
Could you really bear to see your comrades, family members, and children devoured by Ancient Monsters or killed by the cataclysmic world?!
Could you really bear to witness the Centaur race disappear from this world?
Join the Gale Empire. I swear to you with my soul, in this life, I will give everything to lead the rise of the Centaurs."
Clang~
As Guido Blackwind’s words fell, it was unknown which Centaur was the first to throw down their weapons. And then, with clanging sounds, the group of more than 1.8 million Centaur warriors all surrendered and laid down their arms.
Guido Blackwind’s words were full of incitement, and no Centaur could refuse.
Only a very few zealots were still frantically praying and roaring at this moment, refusing to believe that the God they worshipped had long since perished.
But in the grand scheme of things, these few individuals could hardly make any waves.
And so the war ended.
The pace at which the Centaurs were conquered was even so fast that Lide was somewhat taken by surprise.
Good grief, I was mentally prepared to fight until daybreak, but before I could even take off my long johns, you’re telling me it’s already over...
But the end of the war is always a good thing. It not only avoided a large number of casualties but also directly granted him more than 1.8 million Centaur warriors.
These surrendered prisoners, together with the original 1.2 million Centaurs of the Gale Empire, brought the total number of Centaurs under his command to over 3 million.
million!! Those are Centaurs, a race with formidable combat strength!!
Just give these warriors enough equipment, and they could immediately form a formidable force.
After the war ended, it was time to arrange for the collection of spoils.
Originally, Lide’s intention was to make the Centaurs a nail anchored in the Dwarf Hills while also conveniently mining the mineral resources of the land.
But as he carried that stone coffin out of the Sealed Land and learned that there were still a significant number of Ancient Evil Gods there, he changed his mind.
The Underworld had already been completely occupied by him, and its vast land could accommodate a large population. The Centaurs in the Dwarf Hills of the four battlefronts would do better to help him cultivate the Underworld.
And with the Space Gate, the transportation of troops was also very convenient...
In his view, the Dwarf Hills at this point, other than Gale City retaining some value, only had some second-rate mineral veins left, with nothing else worth taking.
With that being the case, why bother occupying this land?
Looking down at the surrendering scene below, Lide made a decision.
Except for leaving a part of the Centaurs to guard Gale City, he sent the rest back to Dawn City.
As he thought of this, he also felt somewhat emotional.
Four or five years ago, he was extremely covetous of the Dwarf Hills, going through great lengths to woo the Iron Hoof Tribe in order to open up the market of this land.
But just a few short years later, everything had undergone tremendous changes.
The land he once coveted had become an unsavory spare rib, tasteless to eat but a pity to discard.
On November 20th, after integrating the surrendered Centaurs, the Dawn Army began sending the Centaur forces to Dawn City.
The City Hall had already made preparations and directly transported the Centaurs underground through the Land of Bone-Burying. A portion of the Centaurs was even transferred to the Gravel Plane of the Abyss, to assist in harnessing the Abyss.
These soldiers were all put to the best use, without wasting resources.
Meanwhile, Lide led his troops into the most central city of the Dwarf Hills — Gale City.
This sole main city of the Centaurs held special significance for the Centaurs.
Occupying this city was to declare his conquest of the Dwarf Hills.
But when Lide set foot in this illustrious city, he was deeply disappointed.
Because the Centaurs had been blockaded by humans for far too long, the entire city, apart from being spacious, had nothing else to offer, rife with backwardness and primitive traits.
Lide even suspected that when the Centaurs built this city, they only considered constructing walls for defense against enemies and did not take living facilities into account.
Messy streets, haphazardly built houses, sewers reeking of filth, and ditches filled with feces... This was even worse than the slums of Green City.
How could these Centaurs tolerate such an environment?
Even more speechless to him was that the Centaur treasury only contained a mere tens of thousands of Gold Pucks, with the rest consisting of miscellaneous food, so poor that even Lide felt pity.
After listening to the post-battle personnel cleanup report from below, Lide concluded that Gale City had no value whatsoever.
Aside from the city walls that could defend against enemies, there was no industrial facility, no living amenities, nothing that he desired.
Realizing this, Lide was quite decisive. If there was no value, then it was better to abandon it altogether.
And then he left, without a trace of sentiment, taking the Centaur army and leaving the city he had just occupied.
Of course, before leaving, he had his army empty out the entire city, not leaving a single grain of the food behind.
November 26th
As the Frost Month came to a close, the weather grew colder still.
After nearly a week of transport, three million Centaurs had all been transported back to Dawn City.
Lide had completely abandoned the land of low hills, even leaving many mineable veins untouched.
With the depths of the Abyss and the Underworld being explored, these two rich sources of veins could fully compensate for the loss of the outer veins, perhaps even more so if further developed.
There was simply no need to waste effort on the low hills.
At this moment, no one could have imagined that this land, which had been occupied by the Centaurs for tens of thousands of years, was for the first time welcoming a day without Centaurs.
November 27th.
In the office of the City Hall, Lide sat behind his desk, looking through some documents with a somewhat odd expression on his face before closing them.
It was a summary file of the materials seized from the low hills by the City Hall.
But there was nothing worthy of his further attention.
"Only possessions worth less than two hundred thousand Gold Pucks from the low hills?"
"Food is just enough for five hundred thousand people for one year..."
"These guys really are poor."
He shook his head in silent laughter.
"However, it’s a good thing. The true spoils are the population of three million, as well as the living deity, the Centaur God, plus a Legendary-level Centaur."
"Considering all that, the gains from this exploit can just about be accepted."
After briefly calculating, Lide had to admit that the Centaurs were indeed impoverished. Aside from their own value, they really had nothing else.
Fortunately, there was the Centaur God to provide him some consolation, preventing an endeavor with no profit at all.
"But what can a living deity actually do? That is indeed a question..."
Lide stroked his chin, slipping into deep thought.
Because he had declared the death of the Centaur God when he subdued the Centaurs, he could only use the Power of Faith to seal the deity’s soul for now.
Otherwise, as soon as the seal was broken, those believers who still worshipped the Centaur God would immediately sense his presence.
Then everything he had done would have been for naught.
"I wonder if this Centaur God can be subdued?"
"Having a genuine deity as an underling doesn’t sound too bad..."
---
---
---
In the old district of Dawn City, near the mountain’s edge, a nondescript residential building was particularly quiet at this moment.
Since this residential building was situated in a non-important peripheral area, with neither military facilities nor granaries and treasure vaults nearby, neither patrol teams nor others paid much attention to it.
In the dead of night, Dawn City was still brightly lit, despite the absence of moonlight. However, due to this building’s lack of importance, there were only a few street lamps on the surrounding streets.
In the pitch-dark environment, these two street lamps not only failed to provide sufficient brightness, but also added a somewhat oppressive atmosphere to the surroundings.
An occasional breeze stirred the branches by the streetside, adding an extra chill to the environment.
Shortly after a patrol team passed by the area, a mysterious figure cloaked in a cape took advantage of the dimly lit corner and quietly approached the unimpressive building.
The light from the street lamps filtered through the tree canopies, casting many patches of light on the ground.
Yet that mysterious figure draped in a cloak was like a ghost, with no shadow underneath the light.
Then, a more astounding scene unfolded. The mysterious cloaked figure seemingly disregarded the solid residential building and moved straight through its walls into the underground, reaching an underground chamber hidden deep below after a moment.
Judging by the traces of excavation, this chamber might have been there for a hundred years, certainly not a recent creation.
The residential building above was even built over the chamber, completely blocking the entrance.
In other words, this chamber was now a sealed place, no longer connected to the outside world.
Thankfully, a ventilation duct was left behind during the original excavation, allowing fresh air in and preventing the buildup of toxic gases in the chamber.
At this moment, this underground chamber unknown to others was lined with wooden storage boxes of various sizes, encrusted with strange and peculiar Magic Materials—it seemed to have become a Mage’s magic laboratory...
But what was most astonishing was at the back of the underground chamber, near the wall, where a massive iron cage partially embedded in the magic-imbued wall.
Within this large cage, a girl approximately seventeen or eighteen years old was bound by magic iron chains engraved with inscriptions on her hands, feet, and even around her neck.
The magic iron chains were long, and the locks for each limb and neck were separate, so the girl bound in chains did have some range of movement, preventing her from being entirely immobilized.
At this moment, the strikingly attractive young girl looked distraught, her long dress marked with filthy stains, reminiscent of an abused cat, curled up pitifully in the corner of the cage.
As soon as the figure in the black cloak appeared in the underground chamber, the girl seemed to come to life, slowly lifting her head. Those amber eyes of hers flashed with an uncontrollable fury.
But just as she attempted to act, the inscriptions on the chains lit up instantly, forcibly dispersing the power within her body.
Feeling the abnormality in her body, the girl frowned deeply, her voice as hoarse as if she had been parched in the desert for half a month.
"You’ve trapped me here for a full half month now. State your purpose, Knight and God of Murder—Stu Yate!"
Her voice was laden with an irrepressible anger when she uttered the name Stu Yate.
The silver-grey eyes beneath Stu Yate’s black cloak flickered slightly.
"Charis... oh, no, I should call you Bast, right? My high and mighty goddess..."
His tone carried an intense excitement and an undisguised pleasure.
"Cat and Joy Goddess, haha... indeed, this thrills me.
Who would have thought, the free and proud Cat Goddess would one day be penned in a cage by me..."
The Cat and Joy Goddess is the most capricious god among all divine beings. She’s sensual, charming, aloof, and unpredictable in her actions. She loves pleasure and relishes in all things amusing.
Stu Yate once pursued this goddess for a significant length of time. But how could such an honorable knight, bound by the knightly code, ever make this pleasure-seeking, entertaining Cat Goddess take a fancy to him?
Thus, Stu Yate had never even caught the proper attention of Bast.
But now, everything has changed. The once unattainable goddess is currently imprisoned in his cage, and he can do anything to her he desires.
To whip the former goddess, to ravage the once untouchable... The stimulation of such psychological reveries brought him to the brink of madness.
This is power, isn’t it?
With power, one can possess everything.
If he were still that rigid Knight God, even if Bast stood before him, he could only brood in silence.
But now, he is no longer that impotent Knight God. The current him wields the power to control destinies.
Having captured his former object of pursuit and brought the lofty goddess down from her pedestal, Stu Yate’s heart swelled with extreme egotism.
Hearing Tu Yate’s reckless mockery, Bast’s expression turned horrendously ugly.
Being a goddess who once roamed freely, now caged within iron bars, the sense of lost freedom ignited her raging fury.
At that moment, regret surged through her mind. Only she knew how thrilled she had been to encounter Stu Yate in Dawn City half a month ago.
As the catastrophe arrived, she lost her power and had to hide in this post-cataclysm world, cautiously recovering her strength.
In such a context, when she was feeling deeply uneasy, she met Stu Yate, the same god who had pursued her, always polite and gentlemanly.
Though she had no interest in the rule-abiding Knight God, she felt at ease with this deity who always kept his promises and defended the justice in his heart.
So she easily trusted Stu Yate.
But the end result was... The once Knight God had turned into a hybrid of Knight and God of Murder, and the knight’s code that he had upheld became a joke.
"Stu Yate, although the Plague God Position has temporarily shadowed the justice in your heart, I believe the knight’s honor will guide you back to the lost light...
Come back, abandon the God of Murder position. It doesn’t suit you, my once close friend..."
Bast stared at Stu Yate with determination, resorting to her last chance at persuasion.
Stu Yate paused momentarily, then the former Knight God, who once valued honor above life itself, suddenly began to laugh crazily as if he had heard the funniest joke in the world.
His unrestrained laughter echoed with madness in the basement like that of a patient who had escaped a madhouse...
"Hahahaha... give up?...
Hahaha... the knight’s honor?..."
The laughing continued for several minutes until Bast felt a coldness in her heart. Then abruptly, as though someone had grasped his throat, Stu Yate stopped laughing sharply.
He then furiously flung off his cloak, revealing a face etched with gray, mysterious inscriptions that radiated a dark aura, adding a hint of brutality to his handsome features.
Stu Yate, showing his true face, strode forward and slammed his hands onto the iron cage with such force that the veins on his back stood out, his face brimming with ferocity and rage.
"Give up?! You’re telling me to give up the God of Murder position?!"
His hands smacked the iron cage, his voice almost hysterical!
"To give up the great power I now hold to continue being a Knight God you all mock?!"
"Foolish!!"
Bang! The thunderous crash caused Bast, inside the cage, to tremble and recoil sharply back, the chains on her body clinking crisply together.
Her facial expression was akin to that of a startled cat.
At that moment, she truly realized that the once honorable Knight God was dead... Now before her stood a stranger endowed with the God of Murder position.
Seeing the goddess in turmoil, a perverse pleasure surfaced on Stu Yate’s face.
"Do you see, Bast? This is power, a power I have never before possessed!
You arrogant deity, now only a cat in my keeping!
This is all thanks to the God of Murder position.
Everything is so wonderful...
Now, I am your master; you have no right to judge me!!
Hahahaha!"
Seeing Bast’s panic-stricken expression, Stu Yate was enveloped in both a feeling of revengeful satisfaction and a sense of accomplishment for controlling another’s fate. The god of Knight and Murder was nearly intoxicated.
"What the hell do you want!"
Bast yelled, suppressing the unease in her heart.
The insane Stu Yate instilled a genuine fear in her, akin to the fear one would feel before a crazed evil god.
She completely abandoned her last illusions.
This man truly desired to become an evil god from his core; he was not being corrupted...
Stu Yate suddenly withdrew from the cage’s proximity, his madness instantly dissipating, his expression returning to calm in an exceedingly brief span, as if the maniac who just laughed was unrelated to him.
This abrupt shift exacerbated the fear within the caged Bast.
"What do I want? I want you!"
Stu Yate’s silver-gray eyes shone with fanatical possessiveness.
Greedy and insane.
"Not only do I want you, but I also wish to become the most powerful deity! To emerge from the Ancient Catastrophe as a being that everyone fears!"
"You’re dreaming!"
"Dreaming? No, one cannot dream of something so wonderful.
The old days have come, and those gods who once were lofty now stand on the same starting line as us, some even weaker than us!
Wasn’t the God of Murder of medium Divine Power before, and didn’t he die by my hand?
As long as I can keep murdering gods, then my power will keep on increasing because the Plague God Position now belongs to me!"
Stu Yate’s emotions became even more intense.
"And don’t you think the city we’re in now is the perfect base in the Main Plane?
As long as I control this city, I can keep luring those gods who descend to the Main Plane to their deaths!
And you... you will be my bait...
Cat and Joy Goddess, do you know how strong your allure is?
Most gods who hear of you, I believe, will not miss such an opportunity...
Once I take over this city, I’ll turn it into a death trap, and all gods will become my prey, without exception..."
Hearing these words, Bast recalled the current title that Stu Yate flaunted... Knight and God of Murder.
Although this idea was very crude at the moment, she had an inexplicable feeling that the other party might indeed have the opportunity to keep hunting other gods.
The Plague God Position was very special, as long as you could conspire to kill your enemy, you could plunder part of their power, and the stronger the murder target, the stronger the power taken.
Many gods have died at the hands of the God of Murder in the past.
"Stu Yate, you will not succeed!
The other gods will not be fooled, and you can’t possibly take over this city...
This magical city will definitely not be subverted by you!"
Stu Yate let out a cold laugh, pulled his cloak up from the back of his mind, and covered his face again.
"A city built by a Fake God... gives you confidence?
My plan has already begun, Bast.
When I take over this city, I will possess you bit by bit! My... goddess.
Hahahahaha..."
With a burst of manic laughter, Stu Yate’s figure once again passed through the solid rock walls, disappearing inside the basement.
Bast still had uses for him now, so he temporarily has no interest in... that.
And after tasting the flavor of power, he has lost much interest in the goddess he once desperately pursued.
His visit here was more about satisfying his own need to show off after being ignored and looked down upon, and now, finally being the master.
Some things are only beautiful when unattainable; once attained, they lose their appeal.
Long after Stu Yate’s figure disappeared inside the basement, Bast’s complexion slowly improved.
But as she turned and looked around, seeing the chains forged with Divine Power on her body, she felt an indeterminate fear deep within.
The cat that longed for freedom had, at that moment, lost the most precious thing; it seemed, no one could save her... Despair was slowly devouring her heart.
---
---
---
After leaving the basement, Stu Yate, clad in a black cloak, roamed the city of Dawn like a ghost.
After a long while, he did not hide in some inconspicuous corner but rather boldly entered an estate exclusively belonging to the Bloodline.
Arriving at the estate’s bedroom, Stu Yate skillfully took off his cloak and placed it in his Space Storage Bag.
Then, with a wave of his hand, he took out a dimly glowing, dull mask from the Space Storage Bag.
The mask was as thin as human skin, emanating an extremely evil aura.
The Knight and God of Murder looked satisfied as he donned the mask directly onto his face.
The moment he wore the mask, an indescribable force burst forth.
Stu Yate’s body began to twist and Transform; within a few breaths, the once tall Knight and God of Murder disappeared, replaced by a true Bloodline standing there with outstretched bat wings and showing Tusks.
Stu Yate, while feeling the changes in his body, came in front of a mirror, looking at the reflection with a cold arching at the corner of his mouth.
He had made thorough preparations for his plan to take over this city after.
The mask on his face was a trophy he obtained from killing the God of Murder.
Divine Artifact— Illusion Face.
As long as he killed the other party and allowed the mask to devour their Soul, he could transform into the killed target, and as long as the Soul was intact enough, he could even gain most of the memories of the target through the mask.
This was his assurance!
But that wasn’t all; Stu Yate casually pulled out a Dagger from a hidden part around his waist inscribed with mysterious inscriptions.
The Dagger seemed to imprison countless wronged spirits, and as it was exposed to the air, the temperature in the room dropped by over ten degrees in an instant. The terrifying aura it emitted was extreme. Just staring at the Dagger could make one feel a chilling murderous intent that could freeze one’s Soul.
Godslayer Dagger, another Divine Artifact of the God of Murder, could absorb the enemy’s Soul directly if it could stab into an enemy’s heart and seal it within the dagger.
These two Divine Artifacts had once accompanied the God of Murder in hunting countless gods, and now, they will accompany him towards the pinnacle!!
A gradually mad smile spread across Stu Yate’s face.
In the past few months, he had figured out the pulse of this city, and now, it was time to unfold his plan.
To breach this city from the outside would require at least ten times the strength, but they had a fatal flaw, which was the city’s master—the Kachar City Lord.
He only needed to sneak up to him, use a dagger to sever the man’s throat, and let "Illusion Face" devour his soul.
As long as he could kill him and take his place, all the glory would belong to him, and no one would be able to stop him.
At this moment, the murderous intent was clear in his now blood-red eyes.
The Bloodline race might find out about their ruler’s downfall, but he had already prepared a countermeasure, intending to move the Bloodline away from Dawn City before hunting down the Kachar City Lord.
Once he killed the Kachar City Lord, he would immediately take control of Dawn City’s army, and if the Bloodline did not obey his orders, he could order Dawn City’s forces to hunt them down.
He might even prevent those vampires from entering Dawn City at all!
Given Stu Yate’s knowledge of the Dawn City army, as long as an order was given by the Kachar City Lord, the troops would execute it, even if it meant hunting down the Bloodline!!
Could these lowly vampires pose any difficulty to him?
Stu Yate was utterly confident in his plan, for which he had made ample preparations.
"The charm of conspiracy is indeed fascinating..."
The knight, a follower of the God of Murder, gently licked the Godslayer Dagger in his hand, his gaze intoxicated and disturbed.
The first step, to understand everything about Dawn City, had been completed.
The second step, to become a member of the Bloodline race, had been completed.
The third step, to approach the Kachar City Lord and assassinate him, was in progress...
---
---
---
Lide looked at the Centaur God lying on the floor, his expression somewhat odd.
He had originally intended to enslave this divine being directly, but in the end... it was useless.
His omnipotent Divine Art—Soul Assimilation—when used on the being dissipated instantly like a clay ox into the sea, without causing even a ripple.
This left him quite annoyed.
"Can I only kill him???
And after much effort to capture a living god... wouldn’t it be a waste to just kill him?"
"Besides, this guy’s soul is a treasure, too. If I kill him, the soul would inevitably scatter. I need to find a way to extract his soul first..."
Others might get headaches over not having good things, but Lide was troubled by not knowing how to handle something too valuable.
THUMP THUMP THUMP~
As he was struggling with what to do, there was a knock on the door, and shortly after, Harrison stepped into the room.
Seeing the unconscious Centaur God on the ground, the City Hall Speaker’s eyelids twitched.
It was also his first time seeing a living divine being. This was no pseudo-god ordained by Lide but a genuine god—albeit a weak one at the moment, but even a weakened god was still a god...
"My lord, how do you plan to deal with this Centaur God?"
Lide shook his head.
"I can’t subdue this guy with Divine Arts. I’m having quite the headache. It would be too wasteful to kill him without extracting his soul..."
"Soul? My lord, Withered Bone is undead..."
"Withered Bone? That idiot!! Being an undead and not even knowing the magic to rip away a soul!
And even if he did, it might be hard, for a divine being’s soul is not so easily extracted..."
In the end, Lide waved his hand helplessly, "Forget it, I’ll seal him away for now and deal with him once I find a way."
Hearing this, Harrison could only offer a wry smile without a word. Extracting the soul of a divine being? He had no experience with that either.
"What about the Centaurs? How have they been settled?"
The 3 million Centaurs represented a vast fortune. If handled well, they could greatly aid Dawn City.
"They’ve all been properly settled.
2.8 million of them have been transported to the Underworld, while the other 200,000 have been placed into the Abyss Gravel Plane."
Harrison responded, "My lord, the Dawn Sect priests are proselytizing among these Centaurs. I predict that within the next half-year, they will all become our believers."
Lide nodded.
"Keep a close watch on the 200,000 in the Abyss. Rotate them when necessary, otherwise the rules of the Abyss will corrupt them into evil Centaurs..."
Harrison replied meaningfully, "My lord, becoming evil Centaurs might not be a bad thing."
Not a bad thing?
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly, instantly understanding the implication.
After contemplating for a moment, he nodded.
"Then go ahead and do it. We can afford to lose 200,000 Centaurs."
Compassion is not fit for command of troops, and righteousness is not fit to manage money.
The Centaurs belong to an Order Neutral Camp, but if transforming into the Order Evil Camp could improve their combat effectiveness, he did not mind letting these Centaurs be changed.
He wanted a strong army, not useless eaters.
The Centaurs were not Cave Dwellers; it would be understandable for Cave Dwellers to lack combat strength, but what use would he have for Centaurs without it?
If it was just a believer, one Centaur would eat more than five Cave Dwellers... Would he waste food on that scale?
"Yes, my lord," Harrison replied before continuing.
"There’s another matter to report.
Three days ago, Lord Emi created a new plague that significantly enhances human combat capabilities, and its side effects are completely controllable, preventing the loss of sanity."
Oh?
Hearing this news, Lide’s eyes immediately lit up.
Lord Emi had been researching the plague ever since he received his Plague God Position as a reward, and it had been almost a year.
Had there finally been a result?
"Have tests been arranged? What are the specific effects and side effects?"
"They’ve been arranged. The effects of the plague are very powerful, capable of tripling strength and physical fitness at their peak. However, the side effects cause bodily mutations and distortions, turning one into a monstrous creature.
Due to the severity of the side effects, it cannot be applied to our army in the short term."
Harrison sounded somewhat regretful; the plague had excellent effects, but the side effects were rather a pain.
Not many people would be willing to turn into non-human, non-ghostly monsters.
Lide, however, seemed unconcerned. "If Dawn’s army can’t use it, then why not experiment with Abyss Demons?
Demons, in their pursuit of power, don’t care about appearances..."
Harrison smiled as he said,
"My lord, your thoughts align with those of the heroic Lord Emi.
Lord Emi has already started experimenting on the demons. I just feel it’s a pity that our Bloodline and other armies can’t utilize it.
After all, the effect of enhancing the body is just too good."
Lide nodded, "Fine, proceed with the experiments, and once you’re sure there are no problems, report back to me. Then we can promote it extensively."
When he finished speaking, he seemed to remember something and looked at Harrison with a burning gaze.
"How’s the situation in Green City now?"
He had been busy dealing with the Ancient Evil God in Dwarf Valley and resolving the issue with the centaurs of the dwarven hills, so he hadn’t kept up with the affairs of Green City.
Hearing this, Harrison’s expression immediately darkened, and an uncontrollable anger filled his eyes.
"My lord, that damned God of Nobles has gone insane!
To deal with the Dawn Sect, he even dispatched priests and church knights to take action!!"
"You despicable heretics!! The great God of Nobles is watching you all, and yet you dare to worship the sect of this Fake God?!"
On a street in the southern district of Green City, dozens of church knights, adorned with the Noble God Sect emblem, were mockingly shoving Dawn believers who had come to pray at the Dawn Church.
A large crowd of onlookers had gathered, whispering among themselves. Most were sympathetic toward the Dawn believers, for they had seen such scenes far too often in recent months.
"No! We are the followers of Lord Ilo, we’re not going anywhere! This is where we belong!"
A devout Dawn believer shouted furiously at a nearby sect knight, his face filled with resentment and rage.
These damn bastards had been blatantly oppressing the Dawn Sect for months!
In the past, the Dawn Priests at the church had deterred them from such brazen acts, but today was the day for the Dawn Priests to gather at the Main Church, and in such a short span, these church knights had taken over the entrance of the Dawn Church.
"Ah, so you’re admitting you serve a Fake God, and still not satisfied?? Ha, these damned heretics, if not for our great lord’s mercy, you all would have been hung at the church’s doors already!
Lord Ilo? Pah, a Fake God, with no right to receive worship in Green City!"
These blasphemous words instantly enraged the Dawn believers.
"How dare you defame Lord Ilo!! You are blaspheming!!"
"This damned blasphemer should be burned alive!!"
"Kneel and apologize, or I will show you today the consequences of disrespecting Lord Ilo!"
In a surge of collective outrage, the Dawn believers charged at the church knights. Although there were many Low-level professionals among the believers, they still stood no chance against the robust church knights.
Even with equal numbers, they were quickly subdued and trampled.
Outside the Dawn Church, cries of agony filled the air.
Passersby who witnessed the scene wore ugly expressions, but no one dared speak up. Many lowered their heads, suppressing their emotions, and quickly walked away from the scene.
This sight had become all too familiar over the past few months.
Initially, the Nobles oppressed the Dawn Sect subtly, but as months passed without effective pushback from the Dawn Sect, the Nobles’ arrogance grew.
The Noble God Sect, as time went on, stopped hiding and came to the fore as executioner, brazenly preventing the Dawn believers from praying.
Many nearby residents were once followers of the Dawn Sect, but after such rampant oppression, unable to bear the humiliation, they withdrew. They had watched the decline of the Dawn Sect helplessly.
An even more important point was that Lord Ilo, who had once captivated all of Green City, had been gone for almost a year.
This made the majority of the Dawn believers incredibly despondent. Perhaps, just as the Nobles claimed, had he truly fallen?
Those who remained steadfast in their beliefs longed for his return; they couldn’t accept that the Divine being they worshipped had fallen; they firmly believed that Lord Ilo would eventually make a triumphant return.
At first, many held this sentiment, but as time passed, the number of believers who persisted began to dwindle. Perhaps, the Dawn Sect... truly had no hope.
Perhaps Lord Ilo could never return...
And once the Dawn Sect vanished in decline, those vulture-like Nobles would dominate the city completely.
Dawn seemed to have lost its light...

chapters.title: Chapter 457 - 458: Dominate Green City, Become the Strongest Boss on the Map
chapters.content:
Chapter 457: Chapter 458: Dominate Green City, Become the Strongest Boss on the Map
He was dead.
After months of arrogance and persecuting the Dawn Sect, the God of Nobles was dead.
Under everyone’s gaze, he was blown apart by a single punch.
His death was so swift and unexpected, so devoid of dignity.
The bloody scene caused the crowd below to erupt, unable to stay quiet, as ecstatic shouts reverberated through the air.
And Lide, indifferently floating above in the sky, became an image forever etched in everyone’s memories.
This was the true Divine!
God of Nobles? Nonsense, what was the God of Nobles worth? All the prior bluster, and yet, he was blown apart by a single punch?
The surging crowd saw the devout followers of the Dawn kneeling in madness, their eyes fervently fixed on the figure in the sky.
This was their worshipped Divine, appearing at the last moment, when all hope had been lost.
And he appeared with such overwhelming and almost rebellious dominance, using the life of a Divine as a sacrifice to declare to everyone that the king had returned.
Those residents who had been suppressed and forced out of the Dawn Sect also cheered, their already present faith instantly elevated.
Even those not followers of the Dawn had quietly turned into pan-believers and believers at that moment.
In chaotic times, the mighty are always venerated the most.
And the players were all shocked, their scalps numb, especially the female players, who went mad under the added influence of Lide’s charisma.
His good looks were one thing, but his strength and the aura of an overbearing CEO, or rather, overbearing Divine, was irresistible...
The only ones feeling fear at this moment were the Nobles lurking in the shadows.
Nobody knew how terrifying the psychological impact was when their relied-upon God of Nobles was blown apart by a punch from Lide.
It was a Divine they had worshipped for a million years!
Such an ancient being was the God of Nobles, and yet now he had been killed in an instant.
Not even a fragment of a corpse was left, just a mist of blood.
Their inner excitement had now turned into endless fear.
Some Nobles even felt their hands and feet turn ice-cold; many collapsed on the ground, helplessly and blankly staring at the sky.
Their minds were filled with reluctant acceptance of this reality.
Some resolute Nobles turned and ran. Seeing this, other surrounding Nobles instantly changed expression and hurriedly followed suit.
With the God of Nobles fallen, the entire Green City would inevitably face Lord Ilo’s wrath.
And who could bear the wrath of a being terrifying enough to kill a Divine in an instant?
Acting now might still salvage some of the situation...
These Nobles had fallen from their high positions to a state akin to that of destitute strays in less than a minute.
Lide looked down upon the earth, observing the wildly cheering crowd below. Though his expression was indifferent, his heart was quite delighted.
He had not expected that using his body as a vessel for two Divine Arts, and then employing Shadow Blade and Power of Crimson, would achieve such an exaggerated effect.
One Divine Art was designed to destroy the soul of the opponent, and the other to age their body and soul to senescence,
The Legendary level Shadow Blade, with its first attack ignoring defenses and inflicting true damage, struck the God of Nobles with both Divine Arts during their clash, drastically reducing his body’s strength in a short time,
As they passed by each other, the Power of Crimson infusing into the God of Nobles’ body boiled his blood, inflicting true damage once again.
This sequence of attacks left the God of Nobles unable to respond and thus slain instantly.
If there were a chance to do it over, the God of Nobles would think twice before rashly confronting Lide.
After some thought, Lide surveyed the crowd, observing those who looked at him with intense fervor.
He solemnly declared,
"My followers, the light of Dawn has not been extinguished.
I, have returned."
That single statement made the crowd erupt again, yes, he had returned, and in such a heart-shaking manner.
Some of the devout Dawn followers, tears streaming down their faces, looked up to the sky, so moved that they choked up, unable to speak.
What could be more uplifting than witnessing their worshipped Divine descending from the heavens to save them in a time of crisis? Nothing...
The Dawn Priests were also overjoyed till their faces flushed, especially the young Priest who had earlier confronted the God of Nobles, now nearly frenzied.
He knew that Lord Ilo would return, he just knew!
The light of Dawn would never be extinguished!
Without dwelling much on words, waiting for the cheering to quiet down, Lide began issuing divine decrees.
"From today on, I will take over the governance of Green City."
"During this period, I will enact new laws to protect the life and property safety of common citizens. Anyone who violates these laws will receive divine punishment..."
"My followers, from today onwards, you will once again be enveloped in light; all darkness and crime will be completely removed from your midst."
Hearing this, the residents below burst into cheers of longevity, but the surrounding Nobles who had yet to leave turned pale.
Lord Ilo taking over Green City?
What about them? These nobles?
But no matter how many doubts and questions they harbored in their hearts, at this moment, they didn’t dare to step forward and inquire, nor did they even have the courage to make eye contact with Lide.
The survival rule of the nobles had never been to resist authority; rather, it involved more of pleasing and even integrating into the authority itself.
While many nobles were disheartened by the death of the God of Nobles, some were quite excited, firmly believing that even if Lide ruled over Green City, he could not possibly do without the assistance of the nobles.
At this moment, the nobles firmly controlled everything in Green City, be it the military or civilian life; it was all in their hands...
Lide’s gaze was icy, his presence as bright as the moon overhead, freely exuding the majesty of the ruler of the Divine Dawn system.
This time, he would fully incorporate this city into his realm of rule; this was the true beginning. Killing the God of Nobles was merely an act to establish his authority.
"I will send someone to take over the military of Green City, clean up crime, and manage public order. For the following week, all residents, besides going to their regular jobs, must please stay at home."
His voice, amplified by magic power, reverberated throughout Green City. Under the blessing of divine power, everyone heard this indisputable pronouncement.
The previously confident nobles below suddenly changed their expressions. Taking over the military? What about them? The pride they felt moments ago was instantly trampled into the mud.
A few senior nobles exchanged glances, opened their mouths to say something, yet ultimately, not a word escaped.
No one dared to comment any further; however dissatisfied, they had to suppress it.
Power was the greatest justice. With the God of Nobles killed, who could now stand against Lide?
Not to mention, he had also brought back six formidable Legends...
In a scenario of conquest and defeat, after the God of Nobles was blown away with a punch, the situation in Green City had already been decided.
It was just a matter of how Lide, returning in the posture of a king, wanted to whip Green City, as if disciplining a little maid.
Lide wasn’t overly verbose. After issuing his simple commands, he descended with a few Legends onto the plaza.
Nicole, bound by Magic Prohibition Chains, her priest’s robe stained, her delicate face in utter disarray, appeared as if she had emerged from a refugee camp.
Upon seeing Lide’s arrival, the girl’s nose turned sour, and her eyes instantly reddened.
In the recent battle, Nicole had resisted fiercely, her magic killing at least dozens of enemies. Despite being wounded several times, she showed no fear or retreat. As a White-robed Archbishop, she was sufficiently resolute and stout-hearted, second to none.
But now, seeing the most intimate and trustworthy figure appear, Nicole felt particularly aggrieved inside.
Seeing the girl now so dignified and striking before him, a spoiling smile appeared on Lide’s face.
He had watched this little girl grow up; when she first arrived, lacking nutrition, she was just a frail little thing, only about fifteen or sixteen years old.
Now she was already in her early twenties, and even her beauty had blossomed so strikingly, fascinating and captivating, very much like her sister, Niro.
This gave him a feeling of accomplishment...
"Your Majesty..."
Upon hearing the girl’s aggrieved voice, Lide moved forward two steps and personally removed the Magic Prohibition Chains from Nicole, finally reaching out to ruffle her hair.
"Girl, you did very well. It has been tough for you recently, but leave the rest to me now."
Nicole, feeling an overwhelming sense of security upon hearing these words, nodded vehemently, her eyes red, trying to hold back her tears, yet they flowed down unchecked.
At this moment, Kapp and the other Legends had also removed the chains from others. Aside from a few who died in combat, over a thousand Dawn Priests were liberated.
These loyal followers of the Dawn Sect no longer showed the tragic and desperate expressions they had when captured; their faces now brimmed with excitement and thrill...
After briefly comforting Nicole, Lide wasted no time. The most important task now was to take control of Green City. He looked around at the priests gathered nearby and then at the group of Legends led by Beastman King Kapp.
He directly issued an order.
"Stanley, while we take control of Green City, it is highly likely that some disorders will happen during the transition period. Immediately mobilize the forces of the Dark Contract to stabilize the South District, while also having the Heart-eating Demon, Wales, suppress the chaos.
Moreover, have the nobles grown from the development project of Dawn’s Shadow assist us in taking over the military and fortifications of Green City."
Stanley was immediately responsive, and then he soared into the sky, leaving the central plaza.
Lide had great confidence in Stanley, a former believer of the Evil God, whose wisdom was indeed incomparable to ordinary people.
After issuing this command, his gaze turned to the next second-generation Bloodline—Frey.
Despite bringing only six Legends, he was not alone within Green City.
Lide could mobilize forces that rivalled anyone in Green City.
"Frey, you go immediately to the Crimson Mage Tower and inform Vina and Betty to use all the resources of the Crimson Mage Tower immediately to stabilize the situation with Stanley, and also to assist the nobles from Dawn’s Shadow in taking over the military of Green City.
Moreover, have them send people to Green City Mage Association to coordinate the actions. This task I entrust to you personally."
Due to the Magic Scrolls and various resources supported by Dawn City in the past few years, the Crimson Mage Tower had become a colossal entity.
Its influence could definitely rank within the top three in Green City, even eyeing the top spot.
His little maid Vina had already become a giant figure in Green City, having established a vast network of relations; once mobilized, no one could ignore it.
"Yes, Your Majesty." Frey also followed Stanley’s steps and flew from the plaza.
These plans had actually been prepared before they arrived, on how to take over Green City; the City Hall Think Tank had provided no less than twenty different proposals...
After arranging for the two, Lide’s gaze shifted to the remaining few and continued issuing orders.
"Withered Bone, you patrol the skies above Green City, and immediately stop any disorder you encounter, while coordinating with others’ actions.
Valen, Nata Jifeng, you two go separately to the southern and northern military camps in Green City, maintain order, prohibit the armies from mobilizing, and kill without mercy anyone daring to take advantage of the chaos!"
With Green City’s army stationed in both the southern and northern camps, as long as these two camps were restrained, the situation wouldn’t devolve into chaos.
"Nicole, send out the priests and rally the Dawn believers to help the military stabilize the situation. Don’t let troublemakers cause chaos."
"Kapp and I will go to the city lord’s estate."
"Execute the order immediately."
"Following your command, Your Highness."
Lide’s will was the direction for everyone’s advancement, and after receiving his orders, they all sprang into action at once.
Before the Ancient Evil God’s arrival, a Transcendent was enough to suppress an entire city.
After the arrival, although Divine beings descended, legends were still the supreme beings.
At this moment, with six legendary figures sent out, not just Green City, even the Nolan Capital might lack the strength to resist.
After Lide’s orders were issued, those humans who had been turned into Bloodline began to take over the military control of Green City as planned.
However, the brief power vacuum this created led to various sizes of disturbances erupting in Green City.
Some were due to the military’s reluctance to follow commands, others involved Dark Life and Evil God believers taking advantage of the chaos to kill and pillage.
But these weren’t big issues. Under the suppression of several legendary figures, the vast Green City became as calm as their own estate, quelling the chaos immediately without a fuss.
Moreover, Lide still held the Dark Contract, Demon Heart, and Crimson Mage Tower—three powerful forces, covering both underground and legitimate operatives...
The residents, sensitive from the arrival of the Ancient Day, immediately noticed the changes and started to lock their doors and windows, not venturing out again.
Everyone felt that a change was coming to Green City.
Lide, accompanied by Kapp, went straight to the city lord’s estate, targeting Duke O’Kelly.
At that moment, Duke O’Kelly had just learned that the God of Nobles was destroyed with a single punch. This once-ruler of Green City cleanly disposed of several followers who were surveilling him, regained his personal freedom, and within a very short time, took back control of the city lord’s mansion.
But just as he was about to leave and head to the military camp to take control of the military, he ran into Lide.
Seeing Lide and Beastman King Kapp at his side, Duke O’Kelly’s expression instantly changed, and he hurried forward, placing his hand on his chest in greeting.
"Respected Lord Ilo, welcome back."
After speaking, his heart was incredibly restless.
Even though he had been restricted by the God of Nobles during the persecution of the Dawn Sect, he had ultimately misspoken first and failed to protect the Dawn Sect.
Lide holding him accountable wouldn’t be a problem at all.
Moreover, if even the God of Nobles was killed by the fearsome being before him, what was he? His opponent didn’t need any reason to kill him.
Observing the restless Duke O’Kelly, Lide felt a touch of melancholy; the former ruler of Green City, once only an upward gaze for him, now trembled and fretted before him simply because of his gaze.
What a reversal of the decades.
It was indeed a peculiar feeling.
"No need for such formality, O’Kelly."
"I presume you’ve already heard about the recent events, what are your thoughts now?"
Duke O’Kelly straightened up upon hearing this, his eyes filled with interest as his heart trembled.
This old fox knew it was time to choose.
After taking a few deep breaths, he spoke earnestly.
"Lord Ilo, your power is enough to eclipse the sun and the moon, the death of the God of Nobles is entirely his own fault!"
After stating his position, Duke O’Kelly quickly explained.
"The God of Nobles appeared shortly after you went to explore the Divine relics; he started restricting the Dawn Sect’s preaching right after he appeared.
But I disagreed with his methods, yet he continued relentlessly and even confined me.
For the past half year, I haven’t stepped out of the city lord’s estate..."
After explaining, Duke O’Kelly, seeing that Lide had not spoken, suddenly knelt on one knee in front of him, bowing his proud head under the incredulous gaze of his guards.
With utmost humility, he said,
"My lord, I am willing to become your follower, to help you control Green City, and to spread the glory of Dawn unceasingly, letting your radiance permeate the Main Plane!"
Lide looked deeply at Duke O’Kelly. He truly was a character.
He knew when to advance and when to retreat, understood the times, and could clearly see the situation.
When he decided to conquer Green City, Duke O’Kelly’s fate was already sealed by his hand.
This prestigious ruler of Green City was definitely an obstacle to his control, and if he didn’t cooperate, Lide would definitely remove this hindrance without mercy.
Duke O’Kelly had clearly understood this too, which is why he surrendered so readily after their encounter.
Because whether he surrendered or not, it couldn’t change the overall situation anymore.
Six legends, one Divine, who could contest such power?
In that case, why not join Lide’s camp? If you can’t beat them, join them; there’s no shame in that.
And from the start, he had disagreed with the God of Nobles restricting the Dawn Sect, and having been confined for so long, one could only imagine his resentment.
Of course, the main reason—Lide made an overwhelmingly exalted impression on Duke O’Kelly; in his heart, Lide’s status was even higher than the God of Nobles.
So surrendering to Lide didn’t trigger any resistance in him.
"Very well, O’Kelly, your decision has earned you a future."
"You were able to hold on to your convictions under the persecution of the God of Nobles, which is quite rare. Now, go down with Kapp and coordinate with my subordinates to take charge of the Green City army."
"The saying by the great man that power comes from the barrel of a gun is not at all false."
The army of Green City had to be controlled in his hands before he could do what he wanted to do.
"As you wish, Your Majesty."
November 18th was destined to go down in the annals of Green City.
On this day, Lide returned in the guise of a king, forcefully killed the God of Nobles, and ordered the occupation of the entire Green City.
The whole process of occupation lasted a full three days.
Not because Green City was very large, but because the power transfer was too cumbersome.
Control of the army was the key to controlling everything, but some nobles simply would not believe it and refused to give up their armies, which caused obstacles.
On November 20th, Lide hosted a banquet for all the nobility of Green City who held military power in the City Lord’s mansion.
He relinquished military power over drinks.
That evening, one-third of the nobles gave up and left peacefully.
The other two-thirds of the nobles were all sent to the guillotine.
November 21st.
Dawn City sent a ten thousand-man group of officers to station in Green City, to take over military power and to start restructuring the army.
After the first night of slaughter, the handover went extremely smoothly.
November 25th.
The restructuring of Green City’s army was completely finished, with a final total troop count of 530,000.
Lide firmly controlled Green City.
On the same day, Lide announced the dissolution of the original City Lord’s Civil Servant team, declared the establishment of the Green City Hall, and simultaneously appointed Nicole as the speaker, with Duke O’Kelly from the Crimson Mage Tower, Vina, and second-generation Bloodline Frey as deputy speakers.
Vina was responsible for managing commerce, trade, and the Mage Association.
Duke O’Kelly was responsible for managing public security,
and Frey became the commander-in-chief of the Green City army.
From then on, the situation in Green City was thoroughly stabilized.
November 27th.
The Dawn Sect was established as the only official sect of Green City, all other sects were forbidden to expand, proselytize, or build churches to recruit openly.
The Dawn Sect welcomed its spring.
On November 28th, Lide led a 300,000-strong army to blockade the western district of Green City.
At the same time, six Legendary beings lead troops to suppress the district.
The underground giant of the western district, the Dark Contract, became an insider, cooperating with the army to eradicate the evil in the area.
At the same time, the chairman of the Demon Heart, the Heart-eating Demon Wales, a level-20 Transcendent, knelt and submitted to Lide on sight.
From then on, both underground giants of the western district were brought under Lide’s fold, under the guidance of these two underground giants.
This land, which had harbored evil for thousands of years, was uprooted by Lide.
Evil God believers, demons, minions of Ancient Evil Gods, murderers, gang members, the Fallen, the Dark Race...
All evil life that dared to resist was killed on the spot, those who surrendered were thrown directly into dungeons.
However, during the conquest of the western district, there were some minor troubles, the biggest disturbance being two hidden Extraordinary Lives that were found, one of which had almost reached Legendary Level.
The two Extraordinary Lives momentarily posed a threat to ascend to a higher level...
But no matter how fierce the resistance, under the joint efforts of the six Legendary beings, it was nothing significant, and the two hidden Extraordinary were suppressed on the spot, becoming the shortest-lived Extraordinary in history.
The western district took a full seven days to clean up, and during those seven days, the air over the whole of Green City was thick with the smell of blood.
The city’s sewers had run dry, filled instead with blood...
The piled-up bodies were so numerous that when transported out of the city, they attracted a pack of a thousand wolves that ate for a month and still had not finished a fifth.
December 5th.
The western district was cleaned up by the Green City army, and this land no longer bore its former darkness; light shone into it for the first time in a millennium.
At the same time, the Green City Hall began to implement a household registration reform system, forcibly turning the western district into a transparent world.
However, for some reason, Lide left the underground black market auction site he had once visited, and designated an area where gray market transactions could continue, of course, under military supervision...
He entrusted the marketplace to the Heart-eating Demon Wales as a form of care for this individual who had once been duped by him.
Time shifted to this point, Lide firmly controlled Green City, a giant city with a population of over 4 million.
He became the new ruler of this city.
million residents welcomed their new ruler.
And with this, Lide unknowingly became the strongest boss on the map of Green City and even the Southern Province.
His will would henceforth determine the fate of millions.
Dominating the territory.

chapters.title: Chapter 458 - 459: Post-War Repercussions, The Crack in the Earth’s Sky
chapters.content:
Chapter 458: Chapter 459: Post-War Repercussions, The Crack in the Earth’s Sky
Crimson Mage Tower, third floor.
The dim light from outside streamed through the open window and into the study, casting long shadows from the tall oak bookshelves.
The precious magic books, like maidens awaiting their turn, lay fully exposed to the air.
"Teacher~"
As Lide flipped through the magic books, he heard a voice and slightly turned his head to see a small figure in a long dress, vibrant and adorable, bursting into the study with excitement.
Among the tall oak shelves, the girl seemed like an elf stepping out from the pages, especially her eyes, which sparkled like rubies, stunning anyone who saw them.
Isa quickly approached Lide’s side and then shyly looked up at him, her eyes brimming with dependence and satisfaction.
Seeing the little girl’s eyes, Lide smiled and gently ruffled her hair.
"Didn’t go to the Mage Association today?"
After he had taken over Green City, the local Mage Association was directly handed over to Wina to manage.
As for whether the spellcasters of the Mage Association had any objections... After he used the Power of Faith to elevate his little maid to Transcendent status, those spellcasters wouldn’t dare to utter a peep.
The only higher-level ones were the two 19th-level vice presidents, but that was it.
The former president of the Green City Mage Association was the Transcendent Mage, Rock, who had left Green City a year ago to seek seclusion for breaking through to Legendary.
Besides this guy, who had almost annihilated the Bloodline, nobody else was worthy of a second glance from Lide; all of them combined wouldn’t match up to one of his fingers.
Dominating the map wasn’t a joke. As the highest-level boss on this map, who would dare provoke him?
"I didn’t go..." Isa shook her head, suddenly a bit shy, and said in a low voice, blushing, "I wanted to be with teacher..."
Lide laughed heartily.
Although Isa’s attribute panel indicated she was 20 years old, she had shown no changes at all, both mentally and physically, and still resembled an 11- or 12-year-old girl.
The developmental cycle of the Golden Bloodline seemed to far exceed that of ordinary people.
It is said that elves, with their thousand-year lifespans, only reach adulthood at 200, while giant dragons, a powerful Longevity Species, only mature at 300...
Lide didn’t know exactly what race Isa was, so he had no idea when she would outgrow her childhood.
But these details didn’t matter anymore; he had long since abandoned his initial intention of grooming Isa into a top combat force upon adopting her.
This empathetic and adorable little girl was now the apple of his eye, dearer even than a blood sister.
Although he no longer harbored this thought, Isa hadn’t stopped growing stronger, and half a month ago, she had broken through to become a Transcendent on her own.
A genuine Transcendent.
Seeing Isa now, her eyes curved into crescents, Lide could only sigh at how unfair innate Talent could be.
Even though he had reached level 28, it was only after defeating several Divines and devouring their Divine Bodies and statuses that he attained his current power.
But Isa was different; this girl with the Golden Bloodline had become Transcendent purely through her own Talent...
While Dawn City currently boasted strong power, with numerous Transcendents and even a plethora of Legendries, outside, a Transcendent was still a big shot capable of suppressing an entire city.
At this time, with the Ancient’s arrival, her top combat status hadn’t diminished.
"Well, then sit with teacher and read for a while."
Lide pinched Isa’s delicate little cheek, his expression very relaxed.
It had been a long time since he had quietly read a book in the Crimson Mage Tower like today; these past years had been spent traveling,
battling in the Underworld, conquering the Abyss Plane, breaking through to Legendary, hunting Divines... continuous and incredibly luxurious even to pause for rest.
After the arrival of the Ancient, the shadowy Ancient Dominator was always ready to destroy the world, and for the sake of Dawn City, he had no choice but to stand firm and embrace his responsibilities.
As the Master of Dawn, he reveled in the supreme power brought by ruling millions, but he also had to bear the responsibilities that came with millions of lives.
Heavy indeed is the head that wears the crown.
Thinking of this, Lide felt unexpectedly contemplative. The past years had transformed him dramatically; as Dawn City rapidly grew stronger, had he not also grown to an astonishing extent?
Master of Dawn, the title he bore, now weighed more than ever before.
Isa gently responded and dutifully dragged a stool next to Lide before picking up a magic book and happily started reading.
The girl occasionally stole glances at Lide beside her, then contentedly continued to flip through the book.
Several Sunshine Hours later, thump, thump, thump~ the study door was gently knocked.
"Come in."
After Lide’s words fell, a girl wearing a blue long dress, with golden hair cascading like waves down her back, and a remarkable demeanor, entered the study.
Following the girl was a figure carrying a giant sword, eyes like hunting falcons, and a very wild demeanor.
"Good day, Lord Lide."
Vina approached with a cheerful smile, looking very well-behaved, her blue eyes twinkling like stars as they landed on Lide.
At this moment, this girl, who had become the vice president of Green City Hall, controlling the entire city’s commerce and the Magic Association, reverted to a mere maid’s demeanor.
In front of Lide, this girl always behaved this way, without ever changing.
Even in Vina’s view, everything she possessed outside was less satisfying than serving as a maid by Lide’s side, filled with happiness and achievement.
Northern Land’s Valkyrie Betty, standing behind Vina, felt a ripple through her heart upon seeing Lide, a slight blush on her face, and a brief sparkle of joy that was hard to detect.
However, the taciturn valkyrie did not speak, merely standing quietly carrying the extraordinary longsword that Lide had once ordered forged for her, pretending to be indifferent.
Lide looked at the two enchanting figures in front of his desk, his mood quite pleased.
It must be said that the attractiveness of these two girls was flawless, dazzling wherever they went.
Even he, a picky aesthete, could find no fault with them.
"Have today’s political affairs been managed?"
"Yes, sir," Vina replied with a charming smile, "I have already ordered the nobility and trade unions of Green City to establish a unified Business Alliance.
This alliance will be a subsidiary of the Commercial Department, directly managed by the City Hall.
I will serve as the first president of this alliance.
Establishing the alliance will allow for resource complementation, prevent vicious competition, and improve the production efficiency of major trade associations."
"This is a monopolistic commercial department, which may discourage smaller trade groups during normal times, hindering the healthy development of the city’s commerce and trade.
However, at this time, consolidating the strength of everyone makes it easier to achieve great things, and monopoly is more appropriate."
Lide looked appreciatively at his little maid; Vina’s acumen for commerce was unmatched in all of Dawn City.
"Well done, now is not the time to develop commerce, and I have allowed these trade unions to exist to serve other departments.
Besides the trade unions, how is the Mage Association managed?"
"I have already revised the system of the Mage Association, cutting down many old departments and also establishing many new ones.
The spellcasters closely associated with the Crimson Mage Tower and the White Tower, I have already arranged them to control the crucial positions."
Vina spoke confidently, her demeanor as the business queen of Green City now fully displayed.
"Also, I would like to invite the Dawn Priest to join the Mage Association, not just the Dawn Priest, but all priests and spellcasters who have not lost their power are to be unified under the Mage Association’s management.
The Mage Association should not only include those willing to join; it should manage all the spellcasters of the city, no matter who they are."
Though her words were calm, they carried an indomitable and graceful authority.
If Lide were to support Vina’s idea, the Mage Association would undoubtedly grow into a giant.
All the city’s spellcasters being under the control of the Mage Association would more than double its authority compared to before.
Previously, membership in the Mage Association was voluntary, and even some spellcasters owning Mage Towers were not members of the Mage Association.
"Very well, since I have already entrusted you with managing the Mage Association, go ahead and do it, and if there are problems, I will back you up."
Lide had changed with the times and was not greatly perturbed by this policy that could influence the entire city.
His power had grown so strong that the city’s spellcasters were almost superfluous.
Such was the difference in perspective and vision.
"Lord Lide, I will not disappoint you..."
Vina’s face was flushed, her excitement and joy apparent, clearly delighted by Lord Lide’s trust.
Lord Lide nodded, not continuing the topic, his gaze shifting to the girl standing behind Vina.
"Betty, has there been any word from Andabella yet?"
The last time the Elves, along with the mysterious Red-eyed Lady, Andabella, and Betty had accompanied him to explore the Divine relics,
the God of the Snake Clan had summoned the God of Twilight, dragging him into the Abyss, while the others had returned unharmed to Green City.
Shortly after returning to Green City, the Elves and that mysterious Red-eyed Lady had left with the Divine Stone.
The Red-eyed Lady knew the secrets of Andabella’s bloodline, and Andabella had consequently gone with them.
Now, half a year had gone by with no news.
Lord Lide was so well-informed solely because of Betty’s reports, and it had absolutely nothing to do with the legendary equipment she had promised him...
"No, I’ve tried many methods but haven’t been able to contact them," Betty shook her head.
When Andabella had left initially, she had specifically requested that someone gather information on the Red-eyed Lady, as it pertained to Isa’s origins.
"Storm Sea Domain, Silver Moon Radiance state... When I find the time, I’ll take Isa there."
Lord Lide turned his head to look at Little Yisha, who was staring at him eagerly, and affectionately ruffled her small head.
Regarding the news of the Red-eyed Lady, Betty, with his permission half a month ago, had already informed Isa. Little Isa, being very well-behaved, had comfortingly reassured them not to worry too much.
Her understanding made one’s heart ache.
After a moment of contemplation, Lord Lide spoke with interest.
"Betty, you said last time that the reason for your ascension to the Extraordinary was the bond with Isa?"
Indeed, not only had Isa advanced to become an Extraordinary, but Betty, who had formed a bond with Isa, had also stepped into the realm of the Extraordinary.
At this moment, the title of Valkyrie truly suited her without question.
"Yes," Betty looked at Isa with a tender gaze, "The power of the bond is very strong; I can’t quite understand the exact reason.
Moreover, I can feel that Isa still harbors astonishing potential within her, even though she has broken through the Extraordinary, she has far from unleashed it..."
Lord Lide nodded thoughtfully.
"I’ll note this down."
He had used the Power of Faith to examine their bodies when he learned of their breakthrough to the Extraordinary but found nothing unusual, so he had let it be.
In the future, he would simply take Isa to the Storm Sea Domain and directly inquire the Red-eyed Clan in the Silver Moon Radiance state.
Now, he had the formidable power to act with impunity.
The mysterious Red-eyed Clan had better behave, or else his war blade wouldn’t be merciful...
"Lord Lide, it’s almost evening; do you need me to prepare dinner?" Vina asked softly after their conversation ended.
The fact that Lord Lide was a Bloodline wasn’t a secret within the Crimson Mage Tower anymore, but considering his past non-aversion to human food, Vina always took great care in preparing his meals.
"Of course, arrange a lavish dinner; we’ll dine together."
Lord Lide smiled easily, deciding to relax well these few days in Green City.
Conquering Green City was just the beginning, after all. The cracks seeping ancient powers in the sky constantly reminded him of the crisis looming over his head, the Sword of Damocles ready to strike at any moment.
After digesting the fruits of Green City’s battle, the great war still awaited him...
The God of Plague stationed in Risier City was growing restless, the Ancient Evil God who saw him as a sworn enemy was still searching for news about him everywhere, and his rule over Green City could certainly not be hidden from that dreaded Ancient Evil God. A storm was already on the horizon.
