Watching the still wildly howling Fury Demon, with eyes full of grudges and savageness, even willing to continue fighting, its body suddenly vanished on the spot.
The next second, with a splatter, blood squirted onto his chest as claws pierced the heart.
The extremely Solid Bone Armor of the Fury Demon could not hinder those claws at all.
Divine’s Right Hand, capable of breaking defenses below Powerful Divine Power, was a trait obtained by fusing the right hand of the God of Plague with his own Divine Monster Bloodline Power.
The howling Fury Demon now completely lost the ability to resist, its four arms going limp, collapsing to the ground.
After piercing the Fury Demon’s heart, Asreaga didn’t rush to withdraw it.
The ruthlessness in his eyes became particularly ferocious at that moment.
A terrifying aura exuded from his hand, his claws becoming like a black hole at that point, devouring the Fury Demon’s soul and the power within its body...
As he devoured this power, his aura began to climb.
Divine Monster Talent—Extreme Evil, capable of devouring all Death and negative auras to enhance his own power.
In one year’s time, Asreaga rose from Transcendent to Legendary, and was only a step away from Demigod, thanks to this Talent’s irreplaceable effect.
Thus, for Asreaga, the Abyss was a nightmarishly evil place in the eyes of outsiders, but for him, it was a land of abundance.
Demons were but nourishment to strengthen himself...
In the Main Plane, Asreaga couldn’t find nearly as many prey; even a Transcendent could protect a giant city, govern a province, even if he slaughtered an entire Human Empire, how many prey could he find?
But the Abyss was entirely different, especially deep in the Abyss, where Transcendent and Legendary demons were not commonplace, but their numbers were still incomparable to those in the Main Plane.
In just half a month since his arrival in the Putrefied Swamp, he had already hunted more than 20 Legendary and 30 Transcendent demons... The power accumulated over millions of years in the Abyss was horrifying.
And this was only a small part of his achievements over the year.
This Divine Monster, after falling into the Abyss, with his terrifying spatial Talent, had already hunted across more than ten different planes...
As he depleted the Legendary and Transcendent demons of these planes, he would move to another.
Using the Abyss as nourishment, hunting demons.
This was the true Divine Monster.
Evil yet powerful.
The only exception was the Putrefied Swamp beneath Asreaga’s feet, a plane he had visited no less than ten times.
All of this began when he was swept into the depths of the Abyss by a spatial turbulence and was once attacked by the Lord of Fury at the center of the Putrefied Swamp, who sought to hunt him.
If it hadn’t been for his terrifying spatial Talent slipping him into another plane tainted by an Evil God, avoiding the Lord of Fury’s hunt, he would have been a corpse.
Divine Monsters were not magnanimous beings.
Therefore, Asreaga would return to the Putrefied Swamp periodically to hunt its top combat forces.
In the depths of this Divine Monster’s heart, his gaze was always fixed on the center of the Putrefied Swamp, for one day he would break through and offer the Lord of Fury’s head as a sacrifice to his great father god...
He would ascend to the peak once again in the Abyss, and upon his return, he would surely slaughter the gods!

chapters.title: Chapter 465 - 466: Delicious Food, Fine Wine, and Beautiful Women, Eat Up Vina
chapters.content:
Chapter 465: Chapter 466: Delicious Food, Fine Wine, and Beautiful Women, Eat Up Vina
After Zhao Yue had left the hall, Lide once again found himself deep in thought.
At present, Dawn City had truly dominated the southern provinces. Looking around, there were no more rivals.
Perhaps, in the Sealed Land ahead of Dwarf Valley, an unknown Evil God still existed, but that was a danger for the future, and it still needed time to ferment.
If there were no other Ancient Monsters, he was now truly a lord dominating his realm.
From a castle of 200 people to today’s heights, every time Lide thought about it, he felt a strong sense of achievement.
That feeling was like steadily pursuing a goddess who had seemed unattainable and having her twist and turn beneath him...
After thinking for a moment, Lide shook his head.
Now was not the time to rest on his laurels, although he had dominated the southern provinces, the future was still fraught with crises...
With him in the southern provinces, he had withstood the erosion from the Ancient Evil God’s Descent, but what about the other provinces, the other nations?
How many of those forces could boast a combat power like Frey’s? How much resistance could they mount against the full might of the Ancient Evil God?
If the whole world were to fall, the pressure on Dawn City might become overwhelming...
"The future is a blur; no one knows what tomorrow will bring."
Lide took a deep breath, his eyes gradually hardened with resolve, and his fighting spirit remained undying within.
"As long as I am here, Dawn City will never fall!"
"However, I must change my previous strategies.
Combat power like Frey’s will become increasingly important in future battles.
Ordinary armies, unless they can revive continuously like players, are just lambs to the slaughter when facing supreme combat power.
A single legend could easily destroy tens of thousands, or even hundreds of thousands, of troops..."
"Next, I should focus on cultivating top-tier combat power. One Frey is not enough to satisfy me; the Divine Pantheon of Dawn City should not have just one noteworthy deity..."
"In addition, I must also find a way to enhance my own power, aiming to reach Level 30 Demigod as soon as possible to seek Divine Enthronement..."
After some thought, Lide immediately identified his next objectives.
First, to find fragments of the Destiny Tablet. This was related to the life and death of Dawn City and must be executed immediately.
The known fragment was with a Demigod Sea Beast in the Lost Sea; the location of other fragments remained unknown, but he had already dispatched Zhao Yue to gather information. He believed news of a second fragment would come soon.
Second, to travel to other city-states to hunt down Divine and even Ancient Evil Gods who had not yet regained their full strength.
Training powerful subordinates using the Power of Faith was a good approach and upgrading them to Transcendent or even Legendary wasn’t hard, but reaching higher levels required astronomical resources.
Even with numerous believers, it was impossible to provide enough resources for so many people in Dawn City to enhance their powers.
Thus, hunting Divine to train subordinates seemed the fastest method at present.
Third, his personal power enhancement.
He needed to reach Level 30 Demigod soon in order to seek Divine Enthronement. In a world full of crises like the Ancient World, power was always paramount.
But this was somewhat challenging. He had only recently broken through to Legendary and had not yet reached the peak state of this level. His body still needed time to adapt and buffer, and rushing his enhancement might affect later improvements.
However, this was no hindrance; preparations could be made well in advance.
"Actually, these three tasks can be carried out simultaneously, retrieving the pieces of the Destiny Tablet wouldn’t hinder me from hunting Divines, and hunting Divines is the key to enhancing power..."
"Infinite nesting dolls..."
Lide chuckled.
After sorting out his thoughts, he no longer hesitated and immediately stood up and left.
Having been busy all day, it was time to return to the Crimson Mage Tower for a lavish dinner to satisfy his cravings.
As a Huaxia person with a foodie soul, delicious food was undoubtedly one of the greatest pleasures in life, even if being a Bloodline no longer necessitates the intake of ordinary food, he couldn’t possibly give up on gourmet food.
After stepping out of the mansion, the servant had already prepared a carriage pulled by nine unicorns, and the crowd on the street stepped aside as soon as they saw it, knowing this was reserved for nobility, whom they couldn’t afford to offend.
Sitting in the luxurious carriage, Lide looked through the window at the Green City streetside with a subtle expression.
Armored patrol teams were marching back and forth on the street, imposing and sharp.
The once numb-faced civilians now had a rare color in their eyes; at least in their eyes, Lide saw a glimmer of ignited hope.
Many people were excitedly discussing the events of the day, with the most talked-about being the body of a Divine hung up for display in the central square of Green City.
The term "Lord Ilo" was repeatedly mentioned, causing Lide to chuckle.
It seemed his arrival had indeed given everyone a sense of hope.
That was indeed the case.
Green City had a complex population, and managing it wasn’t as simple as managing Dawn City, which was like drawing on a blank canvas, allowing for free creativity.
Green City was like drawing on a rag that had been painted on countless times; the feeling was completely different.
But after Lide occupied Green City, targeted policies were quickly implemented, sweeping away many of the city’s persistent issues.
Swift action cut through chaos.
The most noticeable change was in the historically evil-ridden Western District.
After military suppression, the Western District of Green City had become a place where residents dared to go out at night.
Although still not as safe as other streets, it was a dramatic change from the situation before where people dared not step outside after dark.
Beyond that, providing food and jobs for beggars, creating a stable environment for residents, suppressing exploitative nobles, taking direct control of various commerce associations, and establishing a new legal framework... all these policies directly revitalized Green City, which was previously lifeless and filled with despair.
Everyone sensed the changes around them.
Of course, there were nobles and vested interest groups, unwilling to be targets, who attempted to fight back, but with military power in hand, their resistance was just a clown show and was quickly suppressed.
In addition, during a previous military decommissioning, many nobles were unwilling to give up power and were subsequently purged by Lide’s command, freeing up large amounts of resources that became nutrition for stabilizing the situation in Green City.
Looking at Lide’s actions since occupying Green City, it was entirely about cutting down nobles and supporting the lower-class residents.
For him, the existence of the nobility had little significance; a professional administrative body like City Hall was far more advanced and useful than the nobles’ previous feudal governance.
Instead, these privileged individuals hindered his policies.
Thus, the nobles of Green City remained under suppression, which was almost miserable compared to their previously exalted lives.
Although harboring discontent internally, faced with a stronger force, those nobles could only keep relinquishing their privileges.
Lide didn’t care about the minor complaints of a few nobles. Frustrations could be held back, and if they didn’t comply, they would all be purged. What he needed was a vast workforce, a larger number of believers.
How few were the nobles? What help could they offer him? Since their value was minimal, why not stand together with the common people...
Of course, some clever nobles chose to directly affiliate themselves with the City Hall, where their exceptional knowledge got them important positions, making them members of Dawn City.
Lord Lide appreciated such people immensely, not only not stopping them but actively absorbing a large number.
As long as they entered the City Hall, there was a supervisory department, and they had to act according to the rules. Taking care of their own families in minor ways was acceptable, but attempting to secure greater benefits would only lead them to the guillotine.
The essence of politics lay in allying with some, uniting others, and suppressing yet another group.
When the choice between opposing him and supporting him was starkly clear, those clever nobles naturally knew how to choose.
And since nobles tended to be the most oppressive towards ordinary people, when these people were restrained, the residents below immediately found breathing room, hence their warm welcome of Lord Lide.
Water can carry a boat but can also capsize it; the grassroots residents were actually quite simple—whomever allowed them to live well would naturally be supported.
Sitting inside his carriage, Lide looked at the glint of hope in the eyes of the surrounding crowd and felt quite satisfied.
Being able to provide his subjects with ample food and clothing was indeed worth his efforts.
Cloppity-clop—the sound of horse hooves clattering crisply on the ground, the wheels of the carriage grinding on the surface with a creaking noise.
After about a Sunshine Hour, the carriage slowly entered into the grand gates of the Crimson Mage Tower.
As Lide disembarked, he found that Vina, Isa, and Betty had already been waiting there.
Seeing the charming figures of the three girls instantly lifted his spirits.
"Teacher..." Isa ran up and grasping Lord Lide’s hand with curved eyes and a delightful smile.
"Lord Lide, dinner is ready. Would you like to freshen up first or start the meal directly?"
Vina asked casually nearby, the adoration in her eyes barely concealed.
This vice-chair of the Green City Hall, managing commerce and the Mage Association, still appeared as his little maid.
Lide gently ruffled Isa’s hair and smiling at Vina, he said,
"Let’s eat first."
Whenever Lide was in the Crimson Mage Tower and Vina was not occupied with urgent matters, she mostly handled these tasks personally.
Little maid was no idle title.
"Great~ I have had prepared your favorite grilled molten rabbit meat and Blue Heart Fruits from the Bia Forest, as well as deepwater swordfish brought from the Blue Sea Province yesterday..."
"These ingredients were rather difficult to get, the Ancient Monsters outside have been a nuisance, destroying many things..."
"I haven’t even found the long-necked snow rabbit that you wanted to eat last time..."
With Isa by his side, Lide listened to Vina introducing today’s dinner beside him, feeling an immense warmth.
It was only within the Crimson Mage Tower that he could put aside external concerns and return to being himself.
Here, although Vina and Isa respected him, they did not look upon him with the unreachability and fear seen in outsiders’ eyes.
As his status and position rose, fewer and fewer people outside dared speak to him this way.
It’s lonely at the top, as the saying somewhat applied.
Betty, silent on the side, watched the harmonious scene between Lide, Vina, and Isa, feeling a touch of envy in her heart...
Entering the Mage Tower, reaching the second-floor dining room, a round table was already filled with a variety of exquisite dishes. Additionally, a constant temperature magic shield was thoughtfully deployed outside to prevent the dishes from getting cold.
Lord Lide looked at Vina with approval—evidently, this too was the girl’s doing.
Of course, he took the head seat, and the three girls also took their seats.
But just as they were about to start eating, Laurent, the president of the Golden Wheat Commerce, suddenly arrived.
"Your Highness, good evening..."
Upon seeing Lide, Laurent’s expression was extremely excited, his tone trembling slightly as he greeted.
His gaze was also particularly fervent at this moment.
Lide gazed at his first subordinate who had joined under the glory, feeling inexplicably emotional inside.
He hadn’t seen Laurent for quite some time, and he had been neglecting the Golden Wheat Commerce that he once cared for deeply.
As he grew stronger, Dawn City gradually reached its pinnacle, and many of his subordinates could no longer keep up with his pace.
"Laurent, haven’t eaten yet, have you? Sit down and join us..."
Upon hearing this, Laurent’s eyes reddened, his face showing immense honor and surprise.
His Highness hadn’t forgotten him!!
But at the same time, there was an undeniable trace of nervousness in his heart.
As the president of the largest commerce under the Crimson Mage Tower, Laurent naturally had a heightened sensitivity to information.
The closeness between Golden Wheat Commerce and the Crimson Mage Tower meant he was privy to much news.
He had previously suspected Lide’s identity, but had never been sure, and now, although Lide had regained his usual appearance, he still wore Lord Ilo’s attire...
The impact of this scene on him was imaginable.
With an undisguisable anxiety, Laurent carefully placed the object he had been holding onto the dining table.
With utmost respect, he said,
"Your Highness, I have already dined, but today I came because I recently purchased some elf wine—Life’s Rhythm—from a noble, and specially came to present it to you."
Vina, hearing this, showed some interest and spoke on behalf of Lide.
"Life’s Rhythm, as legendary, is wine brewed by elves using the Water of Life, and because of its special brewing process, it continuously absorbs surrounding magic power.
The longer it is stored, the richer the magic power it contains, until it eventually transforms into a wine not inferior to the Water of Life.
A bottle of 500-year-old Life’s Rhythm is worth tens of thousands of Gold Pucks, and even three years ago, a 300-year-old bottle was auctioned for a whopping 50,000 Gold Pucks.
Due to its extreme rarity and significant benefits to humans, it is particularly scarce in the market."
Lide, having heard of this famous elf wine, looked with interest at the unassuming Life’s Rhythm and then gestured.
"Help us open the wine."
Given his status, even precious wines seemed mundane to him.
Laurent, seeing that Lide did not ask him to sit down for the meal, felt slightly relieved inside, as dining with Lide put too much pressure on him, more than he could bear.
Standing as a servant was more comforting.
Immediately he briskly turned into a waiter, diligently and respectfully attending to the dinner.
Lide took a sip of the red liquid in the crystal cup and immediately felt a rich wave of magic power spreading within his body, significantly stronger than Magic Blood, and very comforting.
Indeed, worthy of the elf wine, just one sip cost thousands of Gold Pucks.
Delicacies, wine, and beauty—the dinner had everything one could wish for, and Lide was very satisfied, chatting with a few people as they ate.
After a while, Isa’s words caught Lide’s attention.
"Grandpa Spark sent a message this morning that two Evil Gods have appeared at the seal near the Nolan Capital. It seems they are planning to attack Nolan City... Teacher, can we ask Grandpa Spark to come back?"
Spark...
Mentioning his makeshift mentor, Lide felt somewhat helpless.
When he had returned from the abyss to Dawn City, he had sent a message to him, but that slovenly old man was stubborn. No matter what, he refused, insisting on guarding the safety of Nolan Capital...
At that time, Lide had too much on his plate, and since the old man was unwilling, he didn’t force him. After all, he was someone who had been around for decades and had his judgment.
Now hearing Isa mention it again, he couldn’t help but frown.
Things were different from before. When the Ancient Evil God had first descended, the situation was chaotic but not irredeemable.
Now the Ancient Evil God could fully descend onto the Main Plane, and the dangers outside were bound to increase.
If he didn’t take the opportunity to return to Green City before the situation deteriorated to an unacceptable extent, it would only get harder later.
He didn’t believe that the Nolan Capital could be safer than Green City. The Nolan Capital might harbor significant hidden strength, but it was difficult to have the assets to contend with a Medium Divine Power God.
"Yes, I will write another confidential letter to pass to Teacher Spark later. If necessary, I’ll send someone to bring him back."
His makeshift mentor had been generous to him and had never harbored ill intentions. When he had not yet risen to power, he had always shielded the Crimson Mage Tower, so naturally, he couldn’t just ignore him.
Hearing Lide’s agreement, Isa immediately became cheerful, her ruby-like eyes filled with reliance as she looked at him. In the heart of this girl who never seemed to grow up, Lide was definitely the most trustworthy person.
At that moment, Vina seemed to remember something and whispered softly,
"Lord Lide, today we also received a message passed on by Miss Andabella..."
Oh?
Hearing this name, Lide’s expression changed.
He hadn’t forgotten that girl... and her cloak.
He had yet to see the promised equipment.
Although he had reached Legendary status, he had yet to acquire any equipment suitable for him.
Thinking of this, Lide felt somewhat sentimental. He now ruled over tens of millions of people, even had gods under his command, but he didn’t even have a Divine Artifact to show for—a bit embarrassing.
Moreover, those gods he had killed were all broke; he had slain so many gods, and none had a Divine Artifact. It was really infuriating.
"Betty, what did Andabella say?"
Lide turned his gaze toward the Northern Land Valkyrie, who seldom spoke.
This girl had a very close relationship with Andabella. During the last exploration of divine relics, Betty too had gone through Andabella.
This formidable Northern Land Valkyrie, whose presence alone could intimidate most men, bore a wildness forged from countless battles and brushes with death.
But at this moment, this Valkyrie seemed a bit out of character... Betty, looking into Lide’s deep eyes, inexplicably felt uneasy, subconsciously averting her gaze.
"Andabella said that she has resolved her Bloodline issue. She expects to be back in a month. She also asked about your news..."
A month?
Lide nodded.
"You can directly pass the message to her and have her inform the Red-eyed Clan in Silver Moon Radiance about Isa’s news to test their attitude towards Isa."
After finishing these words, he added with a significant tone.
"Also, tell her, isn’t it time she returned the Legendary Equipment she owes me?"
Ah?
Betty looked puzzled upon hearing this, the Legendary Equipment owed?
When did Andabella meet Lord Lide?
Lord Lide saw the girl’s confusion, smiled without explaining, and instead looked forward to seeing the girl’s expression when she heard these words.
The reason for informing the Red-eyed Clan about Isa’s news was also due to changes in the situation.
Initially, when he, the Elf, and the Red-eyed Lady went to the Lost Sea to explore the Divine relics in search of the Divine Stone, he had just entered the Transcendent level.
If their attitude towards Isa was not favorable, or even hostile, it would put significant pressure on the Crimson Mage Tower.
However, times had changed; not only had he reached Legendary status, but he also had the protection of Frey, the terrifying Death Blazing Angel.
Therefore, informing Isa’s kin was not a problem; even if they were Isa’s enemies, he had no fear and would eliminate them all if necessary.
As the Blood Clan Ancestor, a quintessential dark big boss, he was certainly no saint... although the people under his rule saw him as the hope of everyone.
"Okay..." Betty was concise in her reply, still harboring questions inside but choosing not to voice them.
Laurent was quietly listening from the side, not daring to offer any opinions on the discussions and quickly came up to pour more wine when he saw Lord Lide’s cup was empty, acting even more diligently than a waiter.
Even by merely serving from the side, the esteemed president of the Golden Wheat Commerce of Green City felt immense pride.
It was unimaginable that his initial allegiance was to Lord Ilo, who had descended to become a mortal... truly the blessing of ancestors.
No wonder his Lordship had so many far-sighted strategies, managing to develop the Crimson Mage Tower so magnificently in such a short time.
He felt this experience was worth bragging about for a lifetime.
As for the fact that Lord Lide was not originally strong and became stronger later, Laurent had never even considered this possibility; after all, how could someone ascend to the Divine realms from being mortal within just a few years?
That would be a joke.
Thus, Laurent firmly believed he was favored by the gods; how else could he have his success today...
Lord Lide naturally didn’t concern himself with Laurent’s thoughts next to him, his mood was quite pleasant with exquisite food on the table, superb wine in the cup, and an unparalleled beauty by his side.
Not to mention the beauty and food, which were naturally perfect, the Life’s Rhythm in his cup also made him reluctant to let go, with every sip swirling a myriad of flavors across his taste buds and deep into his heart.
Originally, his physical condition meant not even poison could harm him, let alone alcohol, but enjoying a rare relaxation, he did not deliberately counteract the effects of alcohol.
This dinner was extraordinarily delightful, and by the end of it, Laurent brought over Life’s Rhythm, and Lord Lide alone ended up drinking three bottles.
It was only after dinner ended that they realized Lord Lide was drunk.
The three girls had never seen Lord Lide drunk before and found it quite interesting; they then supported him together upstairs back to his room.
At this moment, Laurent naturally wouldn’t be ill-mannered to step forward to help; he stayed back alone in the dining area to clean up.
Looking at several empty bottles, he could only admire them quietly; he had once secretly tried a sip of Life’s Rhythm and ended up sleeping for three days. With 500 years of transformation, Life’s Rhythm had far surpassed the realm of wine and reached a potency greater than Magic Potions.
For Lord Lide to only get drunk after three bottles showed an invincible physical condition.
Third-floor bedroom.
Betty and Vina supported Lide from either side as they helped him into the house, with Isa assisting nearby. With their extraordinary power, any of them could have easily carried Lide back, but they tacitly chose not to use magic.
It seemed like it would be a desecration to do so.
Betty’s face was flushed with a rosy glow. As she helped support him, the inevitable physical contact occurred, those subtle touches made the innocent girl’s heart stir with strange emotions.
Vina felt similarly. The unique scent of the opposite sex emanating from Lide made her heart flutter, and it seemed her legs were almost too shaky to stand.
The two girls exerted quite an effort to guide the now drowsy Lide into the house.
Opposite the library on the third floor was Lide’s bedroom, which was not luxurious but warmly decorated, centered around a huge bed draped with a white velvet comforter.
After placing Lide on the bed, both girls sighed in relief but felt an inexplicable sense of loss and reluctance...
Watching Lide deep asleep in bed, the air in the room grew unusually silent.
As if struck by a thought, Betty and Vina turned to look at each other and in that instant, they both saw the blush on each other’s faces.
A wave of shyness swept over them, and Betty, with her thinner skin, couldn’t help but speak first,
"I, I’ll be heading back first..."
Without waiting for Vina’s response, she quickly turned and left.
Seeing this, Vina couldn’t help but smile, her shyness quietly fading away significantly.
At that moment, Isa was diligently standing by the bed helping Lide take off his shoes, the young girl unaware of the other sisters’ thoughts.
Vina stepped forward to help as well, gently covering Lide with the blanket and watching him sleep with eyes full of tenderness and unhidden adoration.
For this man who had changed her life, Vina never dared to hope for anything. She was content to simply stay by his side.
"Sister Vina, I’m going to go back to sleep..."
After arranging Lide’s shoes neatly, Isa took a satisfied look.
Then, she yawned, showing a bit of sleepiness. The little girl had also had a few sips of Life’s Rhythm and was feeling sleepy.
"Mmm, rest early, you still need to go to the White Tower tomorrow to learn new magic," Vina said with a gentle smile, ruffling the girl’s hair.
This petite, eternally young girl was everyone’s darling at the Crimson Mage Tower.
Ilo nodded but just as she was about to leave, she seemed to remember something, turned around with a flushed face, and timidly approached Lide’s bed.
Under Vina’s gaze, she quickly pecked a kiss on Lide’s cheek, then dashed out of the room, blushing furiously.
Vina’s face was filled with astonishment, soon breaking into suppressed laughter. That little girl...
After the door slammed shut, Vina’s mind relaxed, and it was now just her and Lide in the room.
She looked down at the still deeply sleeping Lide, a blissful smile spreading across her lovely face.
Then, as if remembering something, she looked at Lide’s handsome face, her cheeks gradually flushing once more.
Summoning her courage, the girl timidly sat on the edge of the bed, staring dreamily at the man who had long since become an indelible part of her soul.
After a long time, when Lide shifted slightly in his sleep, it snapped Vina out of her reverie.
Watching the still unawakened figure, Vina pursed her lips, recalling Isa’s actions, which made her cheeks turn even redder.
She pursed her lips again, fighting the shyness in her heart, and boldly leaned down, moving her face closer to the sleeping figure below.
The closer she got to Lide, the stronger that masculine scent became, making Vina’s heart even shyer.
The girl’s heart felt like it was about to jump into her throat, having dared not to kiss him several times before. Finally, seeing his closed eyes, she steeled her heart, closed her eyes as well, and slowly planted a kiss on Lide’s face.
The touch of the kiss brought waves of shyness and happiness almost overflowing from her heart.
With eyes closed, her fluttering eyelashes trembled slightly, then, gathering her courage, the girl opened her eyes, but the sight in the next second nearly made her dizzy.
At that moment, she saw Lide, who had been sleeping deeply, open his eyes...
In that instant, Vina felt like she was suffocating, quickly got up, her shyness almost making her flee, her face reddening like a boiled shrimp.
"Lide, L-Lord Lide, I, I’ll be going back first..."
She stammered out these words and immediately wanted to walk out.
But just as she stood up, a strong force from behind grabbed her arm, her already weak legs failed her, and she fell directly onto the bed, then Vina felt a warm embrace enveloped her, carrying a strong masculine scent.
Lide had relaxed for once today and had a few extra drinks, reassured by being in the Crimson Mage Tower.
He could vaguely sense that two girls had brought him back to his room, a slight heat building in his heart from the physical contact, although luckily he was soon lying on the bed.
As he dozed off, he heard some people talking and then the room slowly quieted down.
But, because the blanket was too thick, the heat did not dissipate and he slept restlessly, hazily sensing a girl’s fragrance wafting over.
Then he woke up, and when he opened his eyes, he saw Vina sneaking a kiss.
He wasn’t some naive boy who could be satisfied with just a kiss, how could he restrain himself in such a situation...
The moment Vina thought to leave, he grabbed his little maid in one swift motion.
Vina was turned around by Lide, their eyes met.
"Lide, Lord Lide..."
The girl, her face flushed, looked at the handsome face so close to hers, feeling shy but also completely at a loss, like a startled deer, wanting to keep distance but reluctant to leave.
Seeing this, Lide’s lips lifted slightly, his gaze tender, completely satisfied with his little maid in every way.
Wrapping his hand around the girl’s waist, he gently tightened his grip, and they pressed together through their clothes.
This gesture spoke louder than a thousand words; the temperature between them soared in a moment.
A heated aura filled the air.
Vina’s heart quivered, then she closed her eyes once again.
Lide saw this and lifted his head to kiss her.
——
That night, the scenery in Green City was breathtaking, even the sudden stormy weather could not diminish its beauty.
The lush grassland was tossed by the intermittent fierce winds, the thirsty stream of winter rejuvenated by the heavy rain, raindrops wetting the grass, decorating the flowers that bloomed even in winter with crystal droplets.
An untrodden path beside the grassland became muddy from the wind and rain, petals blown from the flowers scattered on the path like plum blossoms tinting the snow-covered ground.
The weather was capriciously changing, at times fierce winds prevailed, at other times a gentle drizzle persisted.
When the storm finally ceased, Green City’s lush lawn was completely muddy and chaotic, petals strewn everywhere, and due to the exceedingly cold weather, the clear droplets on the grass were hung with white frost.
A perfect scene of a cold winter night to appreciate.

chapters.title: Chapter 466 - 467: The Undead Stir, Spark Is Confident He Can Thrash Lide
chapters.content:
Chapter 466: Chapter 467: The Undead Stir, Spark Is Confident He Can Thrash Lide
Undead Plane.
This eternal land of dead silence was as ancient as the Abyss, but compared to the fame of the Abyss in the Main Plane, the Undead Plane hardly drew the attention of the ordinary people there.
Because unless there was a reemergence of the undead catastrophe that could destroy the world, the undead rarely had the space to act in the Main Plane—all lives of the good and the Order Camp would eradicate them at all costs.
After all, compared to demons, undead who dug up others’ ancestral graves to resurrect their parents as Skeleton Warriors were obviously more hated.
At this moment, this terrifying place, filled with an aura of deadly silence, welcomed a group of lives from the Main Plane, and these lives were all the famous adventurers from the Lost Plane.
The Broken Sword Knight led hundreds of players into the core area of the Undead Plane, the main city of the undead—City of Sighs.
This undead main city had been established since the dawn of creation, so ancient that it could not be described in terms of time.
This was also the first time players came to such a high-level map, each of them constantly taking stealthy screenshots, their expressions filled with excitement.
All buildings in the City of Sighs were constructed from skeleton white bone, even the city walls were made from countless skeleton remains.
Skeleton streets, Skeleton Mage Towers, Skull Manor... everything was imbued with a unique undead charm.
The buildings here were all imbued with terrifying Undead Magic, indestructible.
However, facing this undead charm, Broken Sword Knight, as a disciple of the ruler of the Undead Empire—the Undead Monarch, was not that excited.
Instead, he was somewhat nervous and apprehensive.
Being summoned to the Undead Plane was something he hadn’t expected, after all, the map here was far from something that players could touch.
Any given skeleton was a high-level undead of Level 15 or 20, how could ordinary players endure that?
Moreover, with his status, he wasn’t qualified to come into contact with this Plane at this stage.
Even though the Undead Empire held great power in the Main Plane and its ruler was called the Undead Monarch, Broken Sword Knight knew that the so-called Undead Monarch...
The ruler of the Undead Empire in the Main Plane was nothing more than a subordinate of one of the fifteen Undead Monarchs, and even just a very ordinary subordinate...
The invasion of the Main Plane and sparking the undead catastrophe was just because he had been cast out.
At the time he received this news, Broken Sword Knight’s expression was very memorable.
His heart was filled with reverence for this legendary resting place of the dead.
Now, they were about to meet the legendary, true Undead Monarch.
As a top player, he immediately utilized his resources to find information about the Undead Plane upon learning he was summoned.
Because there was very little information recorded about the Undead Plane, he had gone to great lengths to find some fragmented records.
Among them, the only piece of valuable information was that there were a total of fourteen Undead Monarchs in the legend of the Undead Plane, who had ruled over this ancient land for millions of years.
But now there appeared a fifteenth monarch, which made Broken Sword Knight quite curious about its meaning.
However, he now lacked the strength to delve into these matters and could only take one step at a time...
After passing through the lengthy skeleton streets of the City of Sighs, under the hollow gaze of numerous high-level undead emanating an extremely terrifying aura,
Broken Sword Knight and his companions arrived in front of an unprecedented grand cathedral in the city center, under the guidance of the guard.
This cathedral, a hundred blades tall, was built entirely out of human skull bones, eerie and hair-raising.
If one hadn’t seen it with their own eyes, no one could imagine such horrific architecture actually existing in the world.
But that wasn’t even the most conspicuous part; the most striking feature was the cathedral’s spire, topped by the enormous twin-horned skull of a beast that spanned dozens of blades in length.
It was difficult to fathom what kind of life form could possess such a gigantic skull.
The enormous skull of the alien beast, along with the walls constructed from other skulls, made this White Bone Cathedral feel utterly macabre to the extreme.
Even more terrifying was the fact that inside the skull burned a ghostly blue Soul Fire, as if the cathedral itself was the divine body of the beast, making the whole cathedral seem alive.
The towering cathedral doors were hollow, resembling the gaping maw of a demon waiting for them to enter.
Even the bravest adventurers couldn’t help but shiver at the sight of such a magnificent and horrifying structure.
The Knight of the Broken Sword, looking at the indifferent Skeleton Knights guarding each side of the cathedral, could only steel himself as he led the group into the Undead Cathedral, where even the ground was made of skulls.
The moment they stepped into the cathedral, all the players felt a shiver run through their bodies, then the space before their eyes twisted, and all sensations were blocked out.
A few breaths later, when the players felt a chill in the air around them and opened their eyes again, they realized they were no longer at the entrance they had walked through.
Surrounded by pitch darkness, they were illuminated by a pale light coming from above, but any attempt to step out of the illuminated area was like encountering an impassable wall.
They also couldn’t discern anything in their surroundings; the light was totally devoured by the darkness.
The Knight of the Broken Sword, seeing such a scene, couldn’t help but feel his scalp tingle; the giant ring of light was like a cage, displaying them for some terrible presence silently observing from the darkness...
Until that unknown fear grew more and more intense, and many players began to feel unsettled.
Suddenly, outside of the light ring, fifteen White Bone Divine Thrones lit up with a ghostly blue gleam.
At that moment, the fifteen hundred blade-tall White Bone Divine Thrones were like sky-reaching steles, and the players inside the ring of light appeared as insignificant as ants in front of the divine thrones.
The Knight of the Broken Sword inside the ring struggled to look up, feeling akin to standing at the foot of a mountain and gazing up at its towering peaks.
This?
Many players were trembling with fear, thinking this was just too exaggerated...
"Respected Undead Monarchs, your humble servants greet you."
The Knight of the Broken Sword was the first to step forward, and after speaking, regardless of the other players’ reactions, he kneeled on one knee facing the central throne, humbly bowing his head.
The surrounding players finally snapped to their senses and began to lower their heads in a show of respect, one by one.
After being battered so extensively over time, players who had risen to such levels were no fools—all those who dared to flout the rules usually ended up dead in terrible ways.
Glory would not coddle them.
Seeing this, the barely discernible figures on the divine thrones, whose appearances were vague, finally spoke, but they were not addressing the players.
"These adventurers from the Lost Plane, they can resurrect indefinitely?"
Another deep voice responded.
"Mmm, but every time they resurrect, they lose a portion of their strength..."
The voice that had spoken first continued.
"I sense a special aura on them...
Their souls are not here, it seems some rules protect them; are those their Plane Rules??"
A hoarse voice spoke, "There are too many Lost Planes; some have been vanished since the Creation. It’s not surprising that some have a few special rules."
"They’re now dead, what died is but a mere body, while their souls remain protected by the rules... Is this the secret to their ability to resurrect?"
A sharp voice, somewhat curious, asked, "How can we break this rule?"
"I can try..."
The Undead Profanity began to echo slowly with a chilling breath, and no one knew which of the Undead Monarchs was speaking, but all players felt a chill run down their spines.
What do these Undead Monarchs want??
Immediately, a scream resounded behind them, and everyone turned around in unison.
A player could be seen engulfed in a ghastly blue energy, his body and flesh decaying bit by bit, looking extremely horrifying.
In just a few breaths, the player turned into a grey liquid, with not even a corpse left behind.
Everyone who saw it felt their scalp tingle...
Fuck, what the hell kind of Undead Monarchs are these, we’re all on the same side, dammit! Have you no sense of martial ethics?!
But clearly, the weak had no right to choose.
"Failed? The rules of this Lost Plane are magical, perhaps we need to find the Plane Stone to glimpse its rules..."
The only consolation for the players was that the Undead Monarch who acted did not succeed.
But before they could breathe a sigh of relief, a second voice sounded.
"Failed? Let me try..."
Seriously, when will this end??
The hundreds of players were about to explode.
If they were to try one by one, a tenth of them would be gone in no time.
Ah!
A horrific scream, and another unlucky one fell to the ground, wailing, then was transformed into a white Skeleton in front of all the players’ eyes.
"Hmm, indeed the rules are magical..."
This comment caused the remaining players to mentally collapse. Did you have to say it?
This was too terrifying; if these Undead indeed found a way to break the resurrection rule, weren’t they at risk of death at any moment?
Many regretted their decision so much it hurt; if they had known this would happen, who would have come here to seek death?
The Knight with the Broken Sword had no choice but to stiffen up and step forward, taking the initiative to speak out.
"Your Highnesses, we are loyal subordinates of the Undead; perhaps maintaining the ability to resurrect could allow us to make more useful contributions to the Undead..."
After hearing this, the Undead Monarchs seated on their thrones ceased their attempts to alternate tries, thinking, after all, who would do their bidding if everyone was killed?
At that moment, a huge, indistinct figure suddenly stood up from the central divine throne.
On top of the high throne, this figure was like a mountain, its fuzzy hollow eyes staring down at the players.
"The power of the Ancient Times has eroded into the Undead Plane, and those beings born from chaos have only one purpose: to destroy all of Glory.
The Undead Plane too is threatened.
Hence, we have unanimously decided to open a channel between the Undead Plane and the Main Plane, sending a great army of the Undead to the Main Plane to collect fragments of the Destiny Tablet.
You adventurers from the Lost Planes will be the main executors of this plan..."
"We are aware of the broad channels of information you possess in the Lost Planes, and we have discovered the essence of your resurrection..."
"Under our nurturing, you will become the spokespeople of the Undead!"
These words quickened the breathing of the players below.
Becoming the spokespeople of the Undead, what an esteemed status that would be?
Even the Knight with the Broken Sword sensed the opportunity right before his eyes.
But as a top-tier player, he still suppressed the excitement in his heart, tentatively inquiring.
"Great Monarch, may I ask, what price must we pay?"
"What price?"
Upon this query, the standing Undead Monarch burst into laughter, the whole space trembling in the chilling laughter that set their hearts quaking.
All the players felt a suffocating pressure coming at them; they couldn’t even breathe.
Countless fearful creatures surged in the darkness around them, while the circle of light that illuminated them rippled, seemingly on the verge of shattering.
"You will come to know..."
The Undead Monarch did not respond directly, those hollow eyes gleaming with an unfathomable mystery.
"Now, I will choose ninety-nine among you to enhance your power, to carry out the great divine decrees..."
The words chilled the heart of the Knight with the Broken Sword; combining the recent actions of the Undead, he was very tempted to refuse.
But regrettably, from the moment they stepped into the cathedral, their fate was no longer in their hands.
Even now, he rather envied the two players that had been slain and resurrected...
As the Knight with the Broken Sword was lost in thought, a dark force descended from the sky with an irresistible grandeur, directly engulfing all the players within the circle of light.
"Ah!!"
After being eroded by the grey energy, all the players felt as though their souls were being torn apart at that moment.
It was as if countless ants were biting their brains, and a million knives were cutting through their bodies...
But such horrifying pain left none unconscious; they were restrained by some force, forced to endure this unprecedented agony.
Accompanied by the madness of screams, time slowly trickled away.
One Sunshine Hour, two Sunshine Hours... No one knew how much time had passed, but to the players, it felt as long as a century.
The Knight with the Broken Sword, though having reached Level 15, didn’t fare much better, feeling only that his soul was being corroded and transformed by a terrifying force...
Finally, after the transformation was complete, all went dark, and he passed out.
Earth.
At this moment, over a hundred players woke up from their game capsules simultaneously, their faces ashen as if they were on death’s doorstep, filled with a lifelessness that was starkly opposed to that of ordinary people.
Many breathed a sigh of relief, grateful to have narrowly escaped disaster.
Some tried to open their game pods to exit, but as they reached out their hands to push the doors, disbelief filled their eyes.
For they discovered that the flesh on their bodies had rotted away into waste, leaving behind only pairs of pallid, fleshless skeletal arms.
More horrifying yet, they could still control their skeletal arms that had turned to bone...
An indescribable terror consumed them.
What on earth had happened?
---
---
---
Whoo-whoo~
As the horn heralded the coming dawn amidst the cold wind, Nolan Imperial City had fallen into a somber mood.
Standing on the towering city walls, soldiers clad in neat armor and armed with powerful bows and crossbows were in full readiness.
Facing the advancing horde of Ancient Monsters in the distance, all warriors’ eyes were sharp as blades.
"These damned worms are coming again!"
A commander, with his helmet hanging at his waist, could not help but spit angrily, cursing viciously.
"I swear to the King! By the end of today, I will have slaughtered a hundred!"
Hearing this, the surrounding warriors also started clamoring.
"Cap, don’t chicken out today, you barely got 60 yesterday, didn’t you?"
"These filthy pieces of trash, it dirties my hands just killing them..."
"For the honor of marrying Her Highness the Princess! I will fight bravely!"
"You’re dreaming of competing with me for the Princess? Draw your sword!"
The wall brimmed with noise in an instant, but curiously, only the soldiers here dared to defy military discipline and shout before the battle, while all others remained vigilant and tense.
Seeing this, the commander put his helmet back on with a vicious smile in his eyes.
Gaining privileges in the army was simple: be strong enough.
This core section of Nolan City’s walls had always been under his command, holding fast against the most terrifying battles without losing an inch. This was the foundation for his defiance of military discipline.
"Prepare for battle, and send those Ancient Monsters back to where they came from!"
A roar later, this hundred-blade length of the wall suddenly fell silent; swords were unsheathed, crossbows were drawn taut, and all eyes stared intently at the approaching tide of Ancient Monsters below.
They were a group of horrifying creatures with bodies like tumors, gaping maws, decaying wings incapable of flight on their backs, and lower bodies that moved by writhing along.
No one could imagine what these Ancient Monsters might have originally been before their corruption, for these beings were revolting enough to make one nauseous.
Boom, boom, boom~
As the Ancient Monsters neared, from the towers behind the walls, magic burst forth, with glimmers lighting up the sky...
Below, the tumor-like creatures were torn apart by cascades of magic, turning into pools of pus and blood...
Morale soared high atop the walls.
"Kill them!"
"Fire!"
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh~
Arrows started flying wildly, and another battle against the onslaught of Ancient Monsters began...
The sounds of magical explosions in the skies now carried deep into Nolan Imperial City.
Within a tower of Nolan Royal Magic Academy, an unkempt old man with a bird’s nest hairdo and a scruffy beard, in disarray, was hooking strange symbols onto a magic pulsating diagram, resembling Ancient Runes or some sort of archaic language.
However, just as he was close to completing the diagram, the sudden loud noise outside caused his hand to tremble, and his final stroke went awry.
After all the effort to end in such a fiasco, the ragged figure felt like crying without tears.
"Damn Ancient bastards!"
In frustration, he threw a punch hard onto the table, bang~ followed by a loud noise, and the disheveled old man’s face turned red in an instant.
Brushing aside the papers, a sturdy iron plate was revealed.
"Who the hell put an iron plate under my desk?!"
Just then, creak, the door was pushed open, and the old man quickly suppressed his pained expression to maintain dignity as he turned to face the figure walking in.
"Professor Spark, are you all right? I just heard your voice from outside..."
A graceful young lady in an opulent court gown stepped into the room with a touch of curiosity.
Hearing this, Spark’s face reddened even more, softly hiding his still trembling hand behind his back as he tried to appear calm.
"Kadi, there’s no need for concern, I was merely irritated at the Ancient Monsters."
Then he quickly changed the subject, "Is it true that the Intelligence Department has found fragments of the Destiny Tablet in the north?"
The noble girl named Kadi nodded slightly.
"Yes, Professor Spark, the news has been confirmed. The King is summoning all Legendary and Transcendent figures to deliberate. I came specifically to inform you."
Spark managed a forced smile through the pain in his hand.
"Kadi, you are Princess of Nolan Royal Family, there was no need for you to come personally..."
"Professor Spark, this matter is of utmost importance. Everyone of Transcendent rank or higher is personally notified by the royal family, and I specifically took on the task of informing you..."
Kadi smiled gracefully and then extended her right hand, passing the item in her hand over to him.
"This is the royal falcon’s envelope; it has just been delivered to the door and I brought it in for you... It should be from Green City."
Instantly, Spark’s eyes lit up, he quickly moved away from his cluttered desk, and approached to take the envelope.
Though he was eager to open it, his face still showed an air of nonchalance.
"Hmph, it must be that good-for-nothing disciple of mine who wrote this letter..."
"Good-for-nothing disciple?"
Kadi curiously said, "Are you talking about the genius Mage who stepped into the Great Mage realm in his twenties? By now, he must be on the brink of reaching the Transcendent, right?
You’re really amazing, to have trained such a powerful disciple..."
Spark felt as comfortable as if he had eaten iced watermelon in summer upon hearing this, but he stubbornly maintained his façade.
"What genius Mage? At his age, he still hasn’t achieved much, hasn’t even reached Transcendent..."
After saying these words, the old man seemed to remember something and chuckled with a sly smile.
Damn Kachar boy, you have no idea what kind of fortune I’ve stumbled upon in Green City this past year!
I’ve already got one foot in the Legendary realm!!
Hahahaha...
Thinking of this made Spark unable to contain his smugness.
This bastard must still be fretting about breaking through to Transcendent, right?
After being knocked down so many times before, now, finally, it’s his turn to rise to the top!
Hahahaha!!
At this moment, Spark was already fantasizing about the shocked expression on Lide’s face when he appeared before him as a half-step Legendary. The thought was enormously satisfying.
You want to surpass your teacher? Haha, you’re dreaming!
Just wait until I enter the Legendary realm, immediately return to Green City, and I will show you who the real genius is!
Kadi watched Spark alternately grind his teeth and then beam with excitement, which made his expression rather peculiar, "Master Spark, are you... running a fever?"
Spark’s face was a study in frustration.
"Kadi, let’s go, the King is waiting for us."
Kadi nodded and looked at the envelope in his hand.
"Aren’t you going to read this letter first? After all, it was sent by your disciple..."
"What’s there to see in this letter? Just leave it here for now..."
Spark said, putting on a front, then indifferently tossed the unopened envelope onto the cluttered desk.
"As you wish, we have prepared a carriage for you."
Seeing this, Kadi didn’t say anything else and turned to leave with Spark.
Exiting the Magic Tower, the two of them boarded separate carriages and set off towards the Imperial Palace.
It seemed the letter in the office had truly been forgotten.
Shortly after Spark left, creak, the door was pushed open, and several apprentices who always helped clean for Spark entered the untidy room with looks of resignation.
This Master Spark is great in every way but just doesn’t care enough about cleanliness...
They started cleaning and soon reached the desk.
One apprentice placed the trash bin next to the desk and then turned to get the broom, while another stepped back subconsciously to make room, not realizing they bumped into the desk.
The unopened envelope was nudged and fell straight into the trash bin.
Neither apprentice saw this happen.
But just a second before the envelope dropped in the trash bin,
Swoosh—suddenly a hand appeared, firmly grabbing the envelope.
The Mage apprentices were startled and quickly paid their respects.
"Master Spark..."
The person who appeared was none other than Spark, who had just left.
Hearing the sound, Spark nodded slightly.
"Right, I forgot something, keep cleaning."
There was nothing of importance in this room; he didn’t mind others tidying up.
After grabbing the envelope, Spark stepped outside, and in an instant, vanished—only to reappear inside the carriage headed towards the Imperial Palace.
Only then did the prideful old man feel at ease to open the envelope.
After reading it several times with relish, he neatly folded the letter and tucked it away.
"Kachar boy, at least you have some conscience...
But how could I possibly go back at this time? I’m only a step away from becoming Legendary.
Besides, I still need to prepare a breakthrough resource for you to attain Transcendence."
He then frowned slightly.
"But what does this guy mean by asking me to watch out for news about the Destiny Tablet shards? Does he want to meddle with them?
Hmm... it can’t be, although the boy’s Talent isn’t as high as mine, he’s very cunning and wouldn’t do something so stupid at this level.
Should I reveal to him the Royal Family’s discovery of the Destiny Tablet shards?"
After thinking it over, Spark decided—although the Royal Family had requested secrecy multiple times, between his disciple and the Royal Family, he unhesitatingly chose his disciple.
Immediately, he took out paper and a quill and began to write vigorously.
After finishing the note, he snapped his fingers, and a majestic hawk with a wingspan of around a blade’s length and a snowy-white body appeared before him.
Judging by the aura emanating from the hawk, it was a Level 10 Demon Beast.
After folding the letter and placing it into a specially made sealable bag under the hawk, Spark snapped his fingers again, sending the hawk soaring high into the sky, far beyond a thousand blades.
After everything was settled, Spark once again smiled contentedly.
"Kachar boy, just wait until the day I ascend to Legendary. I’ll come back and show you who the real genius is!"
"Hahahahaha..."

chapters.title: Chapter 467: The Tyranny of the Land of Bone-Burying, Devouring the Divine Country
chapters.content:
Chapter 467: Chapter 467: The Tyranny of the Land of Bone-Burying, Devouring the Divine Country
Time flew by swiftly, and the corpse of the Ancient God had been hanging in Green City for a full half month now.
During this half-month, the growth rate of the Dawn Sect followers had been astonishing. At this point, of the over four million population in Green City, already more than three million had become Dawn believers.
Although most people’s level of faith was not particularly high, it was enough to illustrate many things.
The original Dawn believers felt proud and shared in the glory during this time.
Their lord had finally returned!
From now on, he would also protect them.
Could followers of other sects see their worshipped divines? Could they be protected?
Without comparison, they would feel no hurt. Compared to those who prayed desperately but received no response, the Dawn Sect, which had a true god presiding over it, seemed so attractive at the moment.
Of course, the speech that Lide delivered after killing the God of Plague also greatly promoted the spread of the Dawn Sect. It wasn’t an exaggeration to say that those words had conquered the hearts of most commoners.
"As long as I draw breath, I will always be your support; you will never walk alone..."
How magnificent these words were.
Who wouldn’t want their worshipped divine to be a powerful and steadfast pillar of strength?
Everyone hopes to receive help from others in their moments of danger, and for many, that is the purpose of worshipping a divine.
Whether it was Lide’s words or the power he displayed, both could win over everyone’s hearts.
Therefore, the sight of a large number of believers changing their faith was not at all surprising.
December 20th, the wind was piercingly cold.
Today, the whole of Green City was bustling with excitement.
Because this was a special day.
The great Lord Ilo was going to remove the largest threat in the southern province before the Dawn Festival arrived—the city of Risier.
This grand city, established by the former imperial royal family, once a magnificent jewel on par with Green City, had now become a dark forbidden land plaguing the south.
There were still three divine artifacts on the God of Plague that hadn’t been found; to Lide, who didn’t even own a decent piece of equipment, the temptation could not be greater.
Moreover, Risier City had become the stronghold of Ancient Monsters, a threat too great to be ignored; without its eradication, Green City could not be at peace.
So flattening Risier City, this gathering place of Ancient Monsters, was a necessary task.
The menace unchecked, no one could rest easy.
"Lide, please be careful."
In front of the Crimson Mage Tower, Vina was meticulously arranging Lide’s black and white spellcaster’s robe, her slender and fair hands gently smoothing out the tiny wrinkles.
Lide looked at the little maid who now completely belonged to him with a tender smile, feeling very satisfied in his heart.
Over the past half-month, Vina had completed her transformation from a girl to a young wife.
The girl who was once slightly green had now taken on the unique charm of a mature woman, every move infused with an enticing air.
"There’s no need to worry; just guard Green City well."
After squeezing her charming and delicate cheeks, Lide turned his gaze towards Isa and Betty.
"Isa, when I return, I’ll take you to the Storm Sea Domain to find your people."
He had always been quite curious about the matters concerning the Red-eyed Clan. What exactly is the Silver Moon Radiance federation? Are they all possessors of the Golden Bloodline?
It seemed that conquering a race that all possessed the Golden Bloodline... might also be quite good.
Isa obediently nodded.
"Mhm, teacher, please be careful..." The little girl was unaware of Lide’s other intentions at this time, just looking at him with eager eyes.
Although in the little girl’s heart, Lide was the most powerful person in the world, she couldn’t help but feel somewhat worried.
Lide smiled faintly, bid a brief farewell, and without any hesitation, he directly boarded the carriage pulled by nine pure white unicorns and headed to the military camp.
After Lide’s carriage disappeared down the street, Vina clasped her hands before her chest and silently prayed for him.
Little Isa, holding Betty’s hand, was visibly downcast.
In the central square of Green City, thanks to its wide terrain, it had become the temporary station for the Pegasus Army and the Dawn Bats.
Upon Lide’s arrival, everyone simultaneously turned their eyes towards him, gazing at their king with respect.
Among the crowd stood Beastman King Kapp, the second-generation Bloodline Frey and Stanley, Duke O’Kelly, and other high-ranking officials—all would be the generals in this campaign against Risier City.
"Good morning, your Lordship!" all the high-ranking officials saluted in unison.
Lide glanced at his generals and wasted no further words, sweeping his hand grandly forth.
"The entire army will march."
With the command given, the Air Force immediately began to take flight.
The other troops had already assembled outside the city.
Over the past half month, the campaign strategy against Risier City had taken form. It was created collectively by the high-intelligence staff in dozens of armies, with every detail considered.
Thus, he didn’t need to worry too much; his personal presence was to cope with any top-tier combat power that might appear in Risier City.
After all, no one could ascertain whether other Evil Gods still existed within Risier City.
The armed forces that would embark on the campaign against Risier City consisted of three parts: firstly, the Air Force, including the Pegasus Army and the Magic Language Bat Army; secondly, the human army from Green City itself, totalling about 600,000, with 400,000 mobilised this time.
The third was the most numerous: the Player Army.
As soon as they heard that they could participate in such a grand war, players from both Anos City and Green City were incredibly excited.
Now, the mainstream level of players was between 7 and 9, with elite players having reached level 10.
If it weren’t for the lack of top-tier combat power, the strength of the players might even surpass Green City’s active armed forces.
Of course, that was theoretically. In reality, players were difficult to command. A small number was manageable, but it became impossible once their numbers reached the hundreds of thousands, let alone over a million.
Bringing them into battle could likely lead to a rout.
These guys are especially brave when there are benefits to be had, but once the wind changes, most of them can’t bear to lose their experience and are very likely to turn tail and run.
As for fighting to the death? Don’t joke, aside from the core members of the major guilds, who would risk their lives?
The higher the level, the more experience is dropped after death, which hurts a lot.
Players are not a monolith; you can’t view them with a collective mindset—they’re a scattered collective formed by countless individuals.
When they go crazy, they can take on anyone without care, but sometimes they’re also terrified of dying...
Of course, at this time, the "Crimson Moon" hadn’t integrated the players from Risier City, so Lide wouldn’t force the players to do anything.
After all, the mission had been issued, and the high rewards were right in front of them, it was up to them to decide.
With and without rewards, the combat power players burst forth is like night and day.
---
---
---
Outside Green City, an exaggeratedly large army like a steel tide, crushed the earth as it marched.
By the end of December, the weather had turned severe, and the sky had begun to sprinkle light snow. Although it wasn’t much, the snow quickly blanketed the soldiers’ armor in a vast expanse of white.
Marching for long periods in winter has always been taboo, but after becoming professionals, their physical attributes would dramatically improve, and the warriors who could become soldiers had already reached Level 5, becoming intermediate professionals.
The weather’s impact on them was no longer so severe; their robust physique allowed them to face the harsh cold indifferently.
Risier City was hundreds of kilometers away from Green City. If it was the air force flying, it would take about two Sunshine Hours to get there.
The ground troops were much slower.
But Lide wasn’t in any rush; he sat comfortably in a warm coach, slowly making his way towards Risier City.
The Green City army, with ten thousand as a legion, advanced in a net-like formation.
Wherever they went, any Ancient Monsters they found were immediately eradicated.
His plan was to conduct a carpet-style cleaning of Ancient Monsters.
Interestingly though, nearly 1.5 million players participated in the attack on Green City—almost four times the number of Green City’s army—so often the Ancient Monsters were cleared by the players before Green City’s forces could encounter them.
To ordinary soldiers, it was better to avoid Ancient Monsters if possible, rather than clash head-on, but to players, these were all experience points—how could they pass them up?
Thus, the scene often played out with players charging at Ancient Monsters with shrieks of excitement while Green City’s troops stood by, enjoying the spectacle.
With such progression, although the pace was slow, wherever the great army passed, the land was left empty, completely swept free of Ancient Monsters.
The objective of eradication was truly achieved.
After the God of Plague had been slain, the Fierce Half-Ratmen began to scatter and flee, causing a widespread scourge in the south.
A large part of them fled back to Risier City.
Lacking a leader, the Ancient Monsters could not organize an effective resistance against the advance of Green City’s army, especially with an army led by Lide.
One day, two days, three days...
It wasn’t until the fifth day that the sweeping army finally caught sight of Risier City on the horizon.
December 26th, heavy snow.
The wind and snow of Frost Month were particularly cold, with the sky blanketed so heavily that one could hardly see the cracks in the sky.
The biting wind, laden with snow, felt like knives scraping against the skin.
Nearly two million strong, the army tightly encircled Risier City amidst the snowstorm.
A steely host.
Morale soaring.
From a bird’s eye view above, one could clearly see the gathering place of Ancient Monsters, encased layer by layer by the army, completely sealed off.
The scene was as awe-inspiring as a mythic epic.
What sparked curiosity, however, was that this city, usually teeming with Ancient Monsters, was now oddly safe; after the army surrounded the city, not a single Fierce Half-Ratman charged out.
It all seemed a bit strange and eerie.
Lide stood on the back of Withered Bones, his sharp gaze fixed on the now dilapidated city, but due to the thick fog formed by the Ancient Power and the covering of ice and snow, it was difficult to see inside.
"Lord, the army is ready, should we attack the city now?"
The second Bloodline warrior, Frey, flapped his wings forward to report; he had been appointed as the highest commander of Green City’s forces, possessing command over Green City’s army.
Of course, when Lide was there, everyone listened to him.
"Issue the order, carry out the plan."
Lide nodded, the mass of troops below was the main force for exterminating Ancient Monsters; he was just there to deal with the enemy divines.
He couldn’t personally attend to everything; what else were these troops for if not to handle such matters?
Woo woo~
As the military horn sounded, the ranks below, already surrounding Risier City, began their assault.
The walls of Risier City were already in ruins, with breaks everywhere that led into the city, eliminating the need for siege towers and other such siege engines.
The first to attack wasn’t Green City’s troops but the dense ranks of the Player Army.
Nearly 1.5 million players swarmed into Risier City like a tidal wave.
These beings capable of resurrection were undoubtedly the best cannon fodder...
"Kill them, brothers, I heard there are Divine Artifacts inside, hurry and grab them!!"
"For the Alliance, for Azeroth!!"
"To the cup of Demacia!!"
The spirit amongst the players was so high that there was no need for outsiders to encourage them excessively; they charged in, hungry as wolves, thirsting like they’d been starved for decades, shouting wildly as they plunged into the fray.
Players thought it was time to reap the benefits; whoever entered first would gain first. There was no reason not to go.
Lide also closely watched the fragmented city-states hidden within the dark mist. The withdrawal of Ancient Monsters’ forces seemed odd no matter how he looked at it.
However, his Legendary Danger Perception didn’t sense much danger, which he found strange.
After the players stormed into Risier City, the Fierce Half-Ratmen that had hidden in the mist finally reemerged.
But unlike the outside world, these Ancient Monsters were significantly stronger at this time, with their overall attributes having increased by at least 30%.
This caused many of the leading players to be killed and sent back to respawn...
Players feared death because they didn’t want to lose experience, but now, with strength in numbers, they didn’t retreat. Instead, they furiously fought their way forward.
"Damn, the Ancient Monsters here give twice as much experience as those outside!! These are all elite monsters!"
"Hahaha, don’t compete with me!"
Soon, the players discovered that although the monsters had become stronger, the experience they gained had increased significantly. Ancient Monsters provided three times the experience of ordinary Demon Beasts, and inside the Ancient Mist, the experience gained was double that of the outside world. That made it six times more.
One slash was overwhelmingly satisfying.
Players with benefits were definitely a headache for everyone, perhaps no less troublesome than Ancient Monsters.
Some warriors who followed the players into the city for exploration were now stunned speechless.
The players were like madmen, who, disregarding death, lunged like voracious wolves at the repulsive Fierce Half-Ratmen.
The number of Fierce Half-Ratmen within Risier City was also unexpectedly small. Although each was strong, there weren’t as many as anticipated.
Before long, under the onslaught of millions of fearless players, the forces pressed on layer by layer. In less than half a day, they reached the center of Risier City—the Black Altar where the God of Plague had once been sealed.
But upon arriving, the players dared not take another step forward.
Because the central area was the Land of Corruption, spanning thousands of blades in diameter.
The ground looked like countless bodies that had decomposed, green bubbles gurgled on the surface, and even the air carried a virulent poison.
free\.c o(m)
Merely getting close and breathing in that poisonous air led players to be poisoned on the spot, with many new arrivals dissolving into pools of corpse water.
The scene was terrifying.
The presence of Ancient Power here was so intense that if the people here were just farmers, not professionals, they would probably be corrupted by Ancient Power within minutes, turned into monstrous beings neither human nor ghost.
The boldest players, seeing the negative statuses on their attribute panels, also lost their nerve and didn’t dare to walk recklessly into the interior.
After Lide received this news, his expression became somewhat odd.
He had prepared so much yet managed to push through easily.
Not to mention the God of Plague, an Ancient Evil God of such level, he hadn’t even seen a single Transcendent. Those Fierce Half-Ratmen had all been piled to death by the players.
"I even had my knife ready... and it was of no use??"
He felt like he was punching cotton.
But without much thought, he mounted Withered Bone and flew directly towards the center of Risier City.
As for Frey, the Death Blazing Angel had been hiding by his side, ready to strike at the first sign of danger.
Moreover, Lide was not afraid of an enemy’s sneak attack. His Talent was exceptionally powerful. Even if he were killed, he could still resurrect.
Withered Bone flew into Risier City, and Lide could distinctly feel the change in the air with the Ancient Power.
If the outside was a light mist, then the inside was like a torrential downpour.
Those decaying, ancient, and daunting powers had long transformed the city into a realm of chaos and barrenness.
He even dared to assert that even if the Ancient Power were to fade, this place would no longer be suitable for humans or other normal living things for thousands of years.
Everything would revert to chaos.
Looking around, he could see that the buildings within the city had become ruins and rubble, while the scattered skeletons told tales of past horrors.
Only the houses that were fortunate enough not to have been destroyed could bear witness that this had once been a glorious city.
"What a detestable Ancient Power... Lord Withered Bones doesn’t like it here..."
Withered Bone exasperatedly blew out a puff of gray-white Death Energy from its nostrils.
Ancient Power fundamentally differed from the Power of the Main Plane; it could not be tolerated by any life exuding Glory.
It was a difference in origins. Once eroded by it, they would fall, even if they were beings representing death and evil like the Undead.
The massive figure with wings spanning twenty-six blades weaved through the thick fog, Power of Crimson blazing like demonic flames on his body, with the flames within the hollow skull emitting a chilling light.
In the dense fog, this Undead Blood Dragon resembled an Ancient Monster more than anything else.
Whooosh~
Quickly, Withered Bone carried Lide to the city center, its immense body slowly descending to the ground, making the surrounding players look on with envy.
"This mount is damn cool..."
Although Withered Bone was a bit talkative, one couldn’t deny its impressive appearance. Otherwise, Lide wouldn’t have recently been using it as his mode of transportation.
Its strength aside, its mere appearance was formidable.
Lide dismounted and landed on the ground, paying no mind to the curious onlookers around him, and headed straight for the corrupt soil at the center.
His spiritual power spread out like the tendrils of an octopus, enveloping a range of hundreds of blades around him.
After a careful sensing, his gaze narrowed slightly.
His expression grew solemn. This place wasn’t simply a Land of Corruption; it was clearly another Plane.
"The God of Plague has actually anchored his Divine Country with the Main Plane. In other words, stepping into this land now, one can directly reach the God of Plague’s Divine Country..."
"This guy is certainly audacious, but it makes sense. With the arrival of Ancient Days, what else can an Ancient Evil God do if not erode the Main Plane?"
After sensing no significant danger, Lide pondered for a moment and then floated up, flying towards the center of the Land of Corruption.
Stepping into this area, Lide felt an extremely odd sensation.
It was as though he was walking at the intersection where two Planes overlapped. One side was the Main Plane and the other, the Divine Country of the God of Plague. The two Planes were overlapping.
Under the watchful eyes of the players outside, Lide’s figure disappeared from sight abruptly shortly after he stepped into the Land of Corruption.
Even Lord Withered Bone was taken aback because he could sense through the soul bond that Lide hadn’t left and was just standing in place.
But from the outside, it was no longer possible to sense his presence, an effect not of a spellcasting, which was very mysterious.
Swoosh~
The instant Lide’s figure vanished, he appeared in a plane filled with a decaying atmosphere.
Looking around, the center of the plane was dominated by a mountain that connected heaven and earth.
Endless lightning erupted at the summit, where from a great distance, one could vaguely see silver dragons dancing amidst the clouds.
The clouds in the sky resembled a greenish venom, and the air was thick with the decay of the Ancient Mist to an extreme degree.
Ordinary people, if they were to breathe even a single breath of this air, would erode into Ancient Monsters.
The land was just like the center of Risier City, a Land of Corruption, filled with energies that life of Glory fiercely repelled.
"Roar~"
At that moment, countless fierce Half-Ratmen, dense as ants on the ground, picked up the scent on Lide that didn’t belong to the Ancient.
These ferocious monsters howled upward at Lide as if they wished to tear him to shreds.
After glancing down, Lide had a slight epiphany; most of those fierce Half-Ratmen who had fled to Risier City had escaped to this Ancient Plane because they still carried too much of the Main Plane’s essence.
"Frey, go see if there are any other Ancient Evil Gods existing within this Divine Country..."
"Following your command, Master..."
After a crisp voice transmitted out, the Level 36 Death Blazing Angel silently disappeared, never having revealed her presence from the beginning to end.
Lide waited until Frey left, then his spiritual power diffused out, spreading all around.
After sensing for a moment, his face showed an irrepressible joy.
Because he had sensed an immensely familiar aura—it was the Land of Bone-Burying.
Is that even possible??
Immediately, with a thought, he extended his right hand and waved.
Crack~
Immediately, cracks appeared in the space in front of Lide, fracturing like a spider web.
