In just a few breaths, infinite power exploded from the cracks, shattering the space in front of him.
In an instant, an irregular spatial rift more than ten blades in length and width appeared before him.
A familiar aura diffused out.
"Eh? Lord?"
Emi, who had been stationed in the Land of Bone-Burying, immediately Instant Teleported upon sensing the aura of a strange world, only to see Lide’s figure instead.
Stepping out of the spatial rift, Emi saw this plane filled with the power of the Ancient and was immediately surprised, "Where is this?"
"This is the Divine Country of the God of Plague."
"No wonder I felt a kinship with this place..."
Having absorbed the power of the God of Plague to break through to Transcendent, Emi even obtained her Divine Position by peeling it off the God of Plague; it wasn’t strange for her to feel a natural kinship with the Divine Country of the God of Plague.
Lide nodded, about to speak, but his expression changed slightly.
He suddenly turned to look at the irregular spatial rift more than ten blades in diameter.
He could sense that the Land of Bone-Burying was using this spatial rift to devour the energies of the Divine Country of the God of Plague...
Although the rift was small and the devoured power was faint, the sensation was very clear.
Strands of Plane Power slowly flowed into the spatial rift and were then absorbed by the Land of Bone-Burying.
The scene was like placing a never-filled wooden barrel into a lake, where the Ancient powers around were repelled by the Land of Bone-Burying, but the foundational power of the Divine Country—the Plane Power—was slowly being devoured.
In a flash of thought, Lide’s expression became somewhat odd.
"The God of Skeleton forged the Land of Bone-Burying and seemed to have also used a similar method to strengthen it once..."
"Normally, a God’s Divine Country couldn’t have its core power devoured so easily.
But... the God of Plague has already been killed by Frey, in other words, this Divine Country is now without an owner, no one will care how excessive the Land of Bone-Burying’s actions are."
With that thought, Lide’s heart raced with excitement.
At its peak, the Land of Bone-Burying spanned thousands of kilometers, not smaller than the southern province.
Though the Land of Bone-Burying had grown to a diameter of 50 kilometers through his nurturing, it was still reduced by countless magnitudes compared to before.
The most direct way to expand the Land of Bone-Burying was to use the Power of Death to elevate its level.
But now the biggest problem was that the Land of Bone-Burying, having reached the Extraordinary Level, needed 1 billion units of Death Energy to advance to Legendary and likely in the hundreds of billions to go further.
These numbers were astronomical, and even if the plan to farm the abyss for Death Energy continued, it would take a very long time.
Previously, there was no choice but to slowly accumulate Death Energy, but now a turning point seemed to have appeared. If the Divine Country of the God of Plague could be devoured, the Land of Bone-Burying would definitely experience transformative growth.
The Divine Country of the God of Plague had existed since the dawn of Creation; no one could possibly know how much power had accumulated over so many years.
At this thought, excitement made Lide’s heart beat faster—he had stumbled upon incredible luck.
The Land of Bone-Burying couldn’t devour just any plane, only a very few with compatible attributes.
Possessing most of the memories since the birth of the Land of Bone-Burying, he knew the difficulty of finding a suitable plane, and it wasn’t an exaggeration to say that it was even less likely than winning the lottery, explaining his extraordinary excitement.
Even the few Divine Artifacts that hadn’t been found combined couldn’t compare to the value of this ownerless plane.
If he handled it properly, he could completely transform the Land of Bone-Burying to a new peak. Perhaps then, he could even refine it into his own Divine Country.
View the correct content at .
"The God of Plague, even in death, has sent me a big gift..."
"Ha ha ha... Good people live a peaceful life."

chapters.title: Chapter 468 - 469: Post-Battle Gains, News from the Nolan Capital
chapters.content:
Chapter 468: Chapter 469: Post-Battle Gains, News from the Nolan Capital
"Emi, the God of Plague has been killed, and now his divine country has become ownerless."
"I just discovered that the Land of Bone-Burying is capable of devouring the power of the Plague God Country to grow, and you should be aware of the significance of this."
Lide’s gaze burned brightly as he looked towards Emi.
"The body of the God of Plague is among the army outside Risier City, and I didn’t bring it in just in case, you should take the body of the God of Plague, which still contains divine status and the remaining Plague God position."
"Next, I plan to let the Land of Bone-Burying devour the Plague God Country to strengthen itself, and if you gain the remaining power of the God of Plague, perhaps it could speed up this process..."
As soon as these words fell, with a wave of his hand, the area he had just stepped into in the divine country rippled like water, directly showing Emi the path to leave.
Upon hearing this, Emi couldn’t help but be shocked. The Land of Bone-Burying could actually devour the divine country of the God of Plague? Was that even possible?
The Land of Bone-Burying could be said to be the engine of Dawn City now, an absolutely indispensable core weapon.
Aware of its crucial importance, he responded crisply.
"Yes, Your Highness!" With no further hesitation, he immediately sprinted toward the direction pointed out by Lide.
When Emi had left, Lide took a deep breath, his expression growing solemn.
It was time to get down to business.
He extended his right hand, and swoosh - the Power of Crimson ignited like gasoline, bursting into flames around his body in an instant.
Legendary Ancestor Bloodline, activate.
Click~
Certain restraints were broken within his body at that moment. An indescribable ferocious power surged through his body, like the dam built atop a high mountain, unable to withstand the raging floodwater, and collapsing, unleashing floodwaters that swept across the land with unstoppable might.
Lide’s presence surged out like an invisible storm, enveloping the surroundings like a category 18 hurricane bearing down.
Below, the Fierce Half-Ratman that had been roaring up at the sky was crushed by the powerful aura, its howling forcibly stifled at that moment, and its voice abruptly ceased.
The dignity infiltrating their souls incited the most primitive fear in these Ancient Monsters.
"Open!!"
The Power of Crimson burst out ferociously, accompanied by his cold shout.
The space rift connecting to the Land of Bone-Burying in front of Lide, now as thin as a sheet of paper, was torn apart by a large hand.
Crack~ Space shattered, with pieces scattering like glass, reflecting gleaming light in the air.
The shards struck out in all directions, creating a terrifying tempest of spatial turbulence.
The Fierce Half-Ratman below was engulfed in the turbulence. These fearsome Ancient Monsters couldn’t even withstand a single breath before being shredded into mincemeat.
The air was thick with the smell of blood.
More shockingly, under Lide’s boundless power, this rift in space had completely blown apart, expanding from just over a dozen blades to 200 blades in diameter.
Swoosh~
After the rift had widened, Lide felt a familiar power directly fortify him, his aura soaring anew.
Upon connecting with the Land of Bone-Burying, the familiar feeling of the entire plane’s power bestowing itself upon him returned.
The terrible power even distorted the light surrounding him.
At this moment, Lide was like a Hell Demon King, descending upon the world, ablaze with crimson flames.
Mighty and dreadful.
Following the several-fold amplification of his power, Lide was in high spirits, about to further widen the rift, but after sensing carefully for a moment, he gave up.
The Plague God Country was now without a master, but it was still a complete plane in its own right.
To open a Space Gate here was equivalent to tearing a hole in the opponent’s rules, and the Plague God Country would automatically repair the wound.
To maintain a Space Gate for a long time required the use of the Power of Death to resist the Plane Power.
A 200-blade wide rift would consume a frightening amount of power every minute. Enlarging it further, the current reserves of the Power of Death would not be able to sustain this level of consumption.
Realizing this, Lide immediately ceased his efforts.
However, he was already greatly satisfied, as the Land of Bone-Burying was now devouring at a rate dozens of times faster than when it measured just over a dozen blades.
He could vividly sense the Land of Bone-Burying gradually filling up.
At this rate, it wouldn’t take half a month for the Land of Bone-Burying to advance to the next level.
The next level was Legendary, requiring 1 billion Power of Death.
In other words, by devouring the power of the Plague God Country, it was equivalent to gaining over sixty million Power of Death each day.
Over sixty million a day... it wasn’t an exaggeration to call this a windfall.
Lide’s smile grew increasingly radiant.
He even sensed through the Land of Bone-Burying that the power contained within the Plague God Country was exceedingly concentrated. If completely devoured, it could even elevate the Land of Bone-Burying to a Divine-level.
That was a hundred billion Power of Death.
If relying solely on the Abyss Pig Farming Plan, one couldn’t even dream of such progress without three to five years.
But what was the current moment? The Ancient Invasion!
The Abyss Pig Farming Plan, though using the authority of the Dark Sovereign and targeting Abyss Demons, could normally last for quite some time without issue.
But under current circumstances, who knew what might change tomorrow?
If the Dark Sovereign gave up on invading the abyss, his pig-slaughtering plan would be directly obstructed.
So, the sooner he upgraded the Land of Bone-Burying, the more leeway he would have.
The Space Gate he opened in the Land of Bone-Burying was hidden in the mist, and outside were the undead and demons, tirelessly slaughtering each other, unaware of the breath in the fog.
After pondering for a while, Lide suddenly saw those ferocious Fierce Half-Ratmen in the distance and his heart stirred. He couldn’t waste such resources.
Kill the pig, kill the pig, whose pig it was made no difference...
The powerful breath on his body instantly retracted, and then from the System Space, he took out a large bottle of Magic Blood. With a flick of his wrist, click—the Magic Blood encased in the glass bottle burst open, whoosh—scattering around like raindrops.
Then he took out another bottle and placed it underground in the Land of Bone-Burying, but this bottle was not shattered, merely the lid was opened.
The Magic Blood was genuine human blood, which, though fermented by divine remains to become a Magic Potion, had an even richer scent.
To Ancient Monsters, this scent was like a bright moon in the darkness, detectable from great distances.
Sure enough, the Fierce Half-Ratmen sensed the scent from afar and started howling as they swarmed in like wolves.
Lide had already concealed his presence at this point, his existence undetectable to the Fierce Half-Ratmen’s level of power.
The Fierce Half-Ratmen, when reaching the front of the space rift that was two hundred blades in diameter, didn’t hesitate at all and burst through it.
Upon entering the Land of Bone-Burying, the Fierce Half-Ratmen instantaneously detected the rich scent of blood.
How could the battlefield of the undead and demons not be bleeding?
These Fierce Half-Ratmen, smelling the blood, went mad and rushed towards the undead and demons.
Ancient Monsters were irreconcilable, natural enemies of life from the Main Plane.
The great battle between the undead and demons turned into a three-way melee.
Nevertheless, the Fierce Half-Ratmen were still much weaker than the undead and demons, so these Ancient Monsters were more like delivering themselves as food.
Seeing this, Lide nodded in satisfaction. He didn’t care who won or who lost; as long as they died in the Land of Bone-Burying, that was enough.
Next, he added a one-way isolation layer in front of the space rift; entering the Land of Bone-Burying from the outside was unobstructed, but trying to leave from inside would be suppressed by the entire Plane’s power, preventing the undead and demons from rushing outside.
After observing for a moment, Lide simply lifted the limitations, allowing the rich scent of blood within the Land of Bone-Burying to pour out into the Plague God Country.
The Fierce Half-Ratmen, smelling an even richer blood scent than the Magic Blood, immediately went mad and rushed headlong into the space rift.
In the distance, the flying Half-Ratmen also smelled the blood and started swarming in like locusts.
Seeing the space rift nearly filled with these Ancient Monsters in a short time, Lide smiled faintly.
This time, it seemed he had taken the plan of killing pigs with a borrowed knife to the extreme.
On one hand, killing Fierce Half-Ratmen to gain the Power of Death, while on the other, devouring the Divine Country to absorb the Plane Power, living like gods...
Exhilarating.
If the God of Plague were to see this scene, it would probably die with an unsettling heart.
There may be no more tragic divine being in the history of Glory than this Ancient Evil God.
Boom!
Right as Lide finished dealing with the Land of Bone-Burying, a thunderous boom came from afar.
He spun around, only to see a mountain peak surrounded by lightning, towering like the clouds in the center of the Plague God Country. Above it, a colossal sword shadow, radiating a lethal aura and tens of thousands of blades in length, rose out of nowhere.
That was... Frey had made her move!
The dark Angel Battle Sword still transformed into a towering sword shadow, pushing away the clouds, with countless lightnings entwining and silver dragons dancing wildly within.
The battle sword shadow seemed as though it had been forged from ten thousand lightnings.
Endless dignity was almost crushing the earth.
Even from such a distance, Lide could feel the terrifying aura emitted by the Angel Battle Sword.
"Is Frey intending to destroy the Plague God Country?"
Just then, the fully formed Angel Battle Sword fiercely slashed towards the mountain peak that reached the clouds.
The scene was unimaginably surreal.
No one could conceive the spectacle of a sword thousands of blades high cleaving a similarly enormous mountain.
Majestic and overwhelming.
At that moment, all the heavens and worlds seemed to be encapsulated in that one sword.
Crack~
With the aura of destroying stars and obliterating the universe, the Angel Battle Sword sliced through, and the billions of tons of mountain crumbled.
The Star River, as though severed by the giant blade, left heaven and earth shocked.
Hundreds, thousands of blades of huge rocks flew up like sand, flinging tens of thousands of blades away, then plummeted down, shaking the earth with the force of a level twelve earthquake.
What came next was even more astonishing.
After the Angel Battle Sword swept through, the mountain peak, touching the sky, was diagonally split by one strike.
The mountain fell, as if struck by a cataclysm, sliding down with an unstoppable momentum.
The mountain was so massive that even as it collapsed, it seemed to do so in slow motion; it was this quality that made it all the more breathtaking.
Boom!
The Plague God Country was trembling at this very moment, making one wonder if the earth would be crushed by the mountain peaks.
The entire process of the mountain’s collapse lasted a full minute, and in the final moment it fell, Lide could even distinctly feel the ground violently shake.
Looking back to where the original mountain stood, all that appeared before his eyes was the slanted, severed form of Headless Mountain.
The might of world-ending destruction.
Lide took several deep breaths.
"So this is the real combat power of a Level 36 Death Blazing Angel? It’s unbelievably mighty...
If the target of its strike had been Green City... by now, Green City would likely be in ruins."
Just as he was about to summon Frey to ask, he suddenly sensed something and sharply turned his head to look at the space rift in the Land of Bone-Burying, his eyes revealing a hint of surprise.
After the mountain was severed, the Land of Bone-Burying’s rate of absorbing the Plague God Country’s power had increased substantially.
According to the current situation, it probably wouldn’t take more than ten days to accumulate enough energy for an upgrade.
It seemed Frey was not acting recklessly after all.
Swoosh~
Moments later, Frey’s figure with twelve black wings unfurled appeared behind Lide.
"Lord, there are no traces of other divines within this divine country."
"No?" Lide turned and gazed at Frey, his eyebrows slightly furrowing. No other divine beings—that meant their initial judgment was wrong.
"Did you find those divine artifacts?"
His main purpose in coming here was to search for divine artifacts. It didn’t matter if there were no divine beings, but not finding the divine artifacts would be quite frustrating.
Frey stretched out a hand and waved it, crack~ the space in front of her shattered, and then a grey-black, shining war hammer appeared in front of Lide.
"Lord, I only found this war hammer. The other two divine artifacts you spoke of seem to have been destroyed by the God of Plague."
"Destroyed?" Lide was slightly taken aback. "Why would he destroy the divine artifacts?"
"To forge a divine body."
Frey’s words dumbfounded him.
"Can divine artifacts be used to forge a divine body?"
"Yes, Lord."
Frey nodded. "Divine artifacts are indeed forged from various special items, containing immense power and divinity. Through some ancient methods, it is possible to absorb the power of divine artifacts to replenish one’s own strength.
Using divine artifacts to forge divine bodies may be rare, but such a method did exist in ancient times, though it has been lost for a long time. I only guessed that the other party used this method from the remnants of the divine artifacts..."
Lide’s mouth twitched. This was just too preposterous—could anything in a magical world be illogical? Divine artifacts and divine bodies being related...
But if he thought about it seriously, it seemed to still trace back to him...
Originally, he had stolen the head and an arm from the God of Plague, clearly wounding the God of Plague deeply, otherwise, he wouldn’t have resorted to such a measure.
Lide couldn’t help but feel a pain in his heart.
What a prodigal act, to have perfectly good divine artifacts and destroy them.
Now, of the three divine artifacts, all that was left was a hammer...
Looking at the unremarkable iron hammer floating in the sky, he couldn’t help but shake his head.
He, the Blood Clan Ancestor, the Lord of Dawn, could not possibly wield a hammer.
Still, he opened the attribute panel with some curiosity.
Forging Hammer
Quality: High-level Divine Artifact
Trait: Able to forge weapons of various levels, the higher the forging skill of the user, the better the forging results.
Description: The divine artifact of the first generation Forge God, it is said that any weapon forged by the Forging Hammer will possess incredible traits.
The attributes were simple, but its origin was extraordinary.
The first generation Forge God... that was a figure who could be traced back to the beginnings of creation.
Lide shook his head, a good item indeed, but it was completely incompatible with him.
With a wave of his hand, he directly grasped the Forging Hammer in hand.
After feeling its weight for a moment, he completely dismissed his last fantasy of the divine artifact.
For him, it was at most an indestructible club, utterly unable to exhibit its special features.
After considering for a moment, Lide’s eyes brightened.
"I can’t use it, but others can. Valen, the dwarf Forging Master, has already obtained the Divine Position of Smelting and Quenching and has even reached Level 25 Legendary.
Isn’t it possible for this guy to forge me some top-tier equipment?
If a divine artifact can’t be forged, surely he can still forge some half-artifacts?"
After a bit of calculation, Lide’s mood instantly improved a bit.
Though this trip did not lead to encounters with other Ancient Evil Gods, thwarting his plan to slaughter a few more divine beings to plunder their strength, and he only obtained one artifact, it still wasn’t a loss.
After all, the Plague God Country left by the God of Plague was enough to make him a fortune, not to mention this extraordinary Forging Hammer as a bonus...
Since there was a profit to be made, he decided to generously overlook the prodigal behavior of the God of Plague.
Then, as if remembering something, Lide looked at Frey with curiosity.
"Frey, why did you need to sever that mountain peak just now? Were the Divine Artifacts hidden within the mountain?"
The move that the Death Blazing Angel had just executed had indeed shocked him.
A sword shadow as tall as ten thousand blades—that was truly an exaggeration.
"Your Majesty, that mountain peak is the core of the Divine Country. Once destroyed, the rules of the Divine Country will descend into Chaos, and perhaps in the midst of that Chaos there might be a chance to find the Plane Stone..."
Destroying the mountain resulted in a disruption of the rules? Lide then understood; no wonder the Land of Bone-Burying’s absorption speed had increased.
"Did you find the Plane Stone?"
"No, the power contained within the Plague God Country is too vast, and I cannot sense the Plane Stone when it is protected by the rules."
Frey shook her head; although she had reached Level 36, the Plague God Country was a complete Plane, and the power it contained was extremely exaggerated.
"However, if you allow me to destroy this Plane, then I am confident I can find it..."
Though the power of the Plague God Country was immense, nobody was mobilizing it, so Frey was absolutely confident she could shatter this Divine Country.
Lide’s mouth twitched at the corner. Destroy this Plane? Wouldn’t that be a huge loss for him?
"This Plane now belongs to us as the spoils of war. The Land of Bone-Burying is growing stronger by absorbing the power of the Plague God Country. Not only should it not be destroyed now, but we must also protect it well."
"I shall follow your orders, Sovereign." Frey replied respectfully and then fell silent.
After transforming from a Twelve-winged Blazing Angel to a Death Blazing Angel, Frey’s personality had changed significantly and now she had become very quiet.
Lide didn’t mind this change. After being eroded by the Power of Death, maintaining the same demeanor would have been a myth.
He turned his head to glance at the Plague God Country. With things having progressed to this extent, the issue with the God of Plague was thoroughly resolved.
From the initial news about an Ancient Evil God being sealed in Risier City to completely killing this Ancient Evil God, more than two years had passed...
This made him somewhat emotional.
Just as he was about to leave the Plague God Country, ripples emerged from the connection to the Main Plane, and then Emi’s figure appeared before him.
This once blasphemer, who now held the transcendent power of the Plague God Position, was carrying the corpse of a Half-rat man as tall as herself.
"Your Majesty, I have retrieved the body of the God of Plague..."
Excitement flickered in Emi’s eyes; he could feel his body’s craving for the power of the God of Plague.
Especially for the Plague God Position, that was power of the same origin.
Lide nodded; he had kept the body of the God of Plague precisely so Emi could attain a greater enhancement, and naturally, he would not be stingy.
He held great expectations for the Plague God Position.
"Well, this Divine Body is now yours to handle.
Frey, go and get Frey and Cap to come in and take over here. The Plague God Country just needs guarding to prevent outsiders from interrupting the Land of Bone-Burying’s absorption. Those Fierce Half-Ratmen don’t need too much attention."
"I’ll return to Dawn City. You will stay here and stand guard in the meantime."
"As you command, Sovereign."
After Lide gave his instructions, he didn’t hesitate, returning to the Land of Bone-Burying through a space rift with Emi.
Emi went straight down to the depths underground upon reaching the Land of Bone-Burying to begin absorbing the Divine Body’s power.
Lide, however, directly appeared at the weapons factory in Dawn City through the Land of Bone-Burying.
Transferring from Risier City thousands of miles away direct to Dawn City, this spatial voyage was indeed a great time-saver.
Looking at the bustling weapons factory with people coming and going, Lide was very pleased.
He had gone through a lot of effort to bring the Dwarfs back to Dawn City. Over the years, although the proportion of Dwarfs in the weapons factory had become very small, their role was absolutely irreplaceable.
He walked into the weapons factory, carrying the Forging Hammer in hand.
A few minutes later, the Dwarf Forging Master Valen was sobbing with the Forging Hammer in hand and refused to let go, ultimately swearing to forge the best Equipment for Lide.
This was a Divine Artifact lost by the Dwarfs for tens of millions of years, their most treasured item. Lide had not expected to retrieve it.
When the other Dwarfs heard the news that the Forging Hammer had been found, they were no better than Valen, and a chorus of wails engulfed the weapons factory.
Lide watched, his mouth twitching uncontrollably. A bunch of Dwarfs with long beards were crying with snot and tears flowing, the scene was truly unsightly. If they were Elves, he might have been willing to watch for a while.
He quickly found an excuse to leave—too eyesore.
As soon as he returned to his office, Harrison, sensing his presence, quickly knocked on the door and entered.
The City Hall Council Chairman’s first words upon seeing Lide shone before him.
"Your Majesty, the Crimson Mage Tower has just sent a message. Your teacher has sent you a letter, saying that shards of the Destiny Tablet have been discovered in Nolan Capital..."
He finished speaking with a somewhat strange expression, hesitating a bit.
"Your teacher also said he’s found three very suitable ladies to become your wives, and he has successfully persuaded two of them already..."
Three... three?!?!
Lide’s face was lined with incredulity.
What was that unkempt old man doing in Nolan Capital all this time?
Finding brides for him, or was that just an excuse for touring the red-light district...

chapters.title: Chapter 469 - 470 Traces of an Unfamiliar Divine in Dawn City
chapters.content:
Chapter 469: Chapter 470 Traces of an Unfamiliar Divine in Dawn City
The message Spark had sent back from the Nolan Capital was somewhat beyond Lide’s expectations.
Of course, it wasn’t about the three ladies Spark had found from who knows where—it was about the fragments of the Destiny Tablet.
He hadn’t expected that just after sending that disheveled old man a message about his quest for the Destiny Tablet fragments, he would immediately receive accurate information in return.
That luck was too good.
He didn’t doubt it, though. This frugal teacher, despite mostly being unreliable—like often enjoying strolls through the red-light district, collecting rather colorful paintings...—was trustworthy in critical moments.
But it must be said that this unexpected news had disrupted his original plan. Regardless, the Destiny Tablet fragments were now the top priority in his list of objectives.
So he quickly rearranged the order of his plans internally.
After a brief moment of thought, Lide looked up at Harrison, about to speak, when suddenly a clear cracking sound came from outside, like the shattering of glass.
Lide felt a surge of apprehension and immediately rose to peer out of the office window, gazing into the distance.
The sky had changed again.
The original fissure in the sky had torn open further, and the ancient air, thicker than before, gushed out like water seeping through a dam, the Old Day force in the air quickly becoming denser.
The sky fissure had expanded again.
Lide’s expression grew grim.
Seeing this, Harrison quickly walked to the window and, upon seeing the expanded crack in the sky, felt a tremor in his spirit. His voice was somewhat hoarse as he said,
"Your Highness, the incursion of the Old Day force is accelerating..."
Lide took a deep breath, the seriousness on his face lingering for a long time.
If the Ancient Evil God could fully descend upon the world, then the pace of the Ancient Invasion was naturally not going to stop there.
But what he hadn’t expected was that the speed at which the fissure widened would be so fast.
After feeling it out for a moment, his gaze shifted towards the somewhat withered plants in the city.
At this rate, by next spring, the wheat yield would undoubtedly be affected, and it might even come to total crop failure...
If such a situation were to occur, it would be an absolute nightmare.
He had over twenty million people under his command who needed to eat... The food stockpiled in the storehouses was roughly enough to last the current population for a year, but what about after that?
If there was a total crop failure this year, what would they do next year?
Food wasn’t something you could plant and eat immediately; it took time. A single season’s failure impacted an entire year.
After pondering for a moment, he turned to look at Harrison, his tone somber.
"Harrison, immediately compile the information on that Sea Beast in the Lost Sea for me.
Next, I will take Frey on a hunt for that Demigod Sea Beast, get the piece of the Destiny Tablet, and then make a trip to the Nolan Capital."
The situation was urgent; there was no time for slow planning.
Information about the Destiny Tablet fragments had been provided early on by Cassilina.
He had also been having Dawn City collect information about that Demigod Sea Beast. It wasn’t that he didn’t want to take Frey straight into the Lost Sea and directly take down that beast.
But that Sea Beast was hidden in a secret Dimension Space, appearing only during the Sea God Festival.
And the Sea God Festival occurred once every ten years, and there were still six or seven years until the next one...
Looking for a Sea Beast concealed within a Dimension Space in the vast sea—wasn’t that like finding a needle in a haystack?
Although Frey was strong, she wasn’t to the extent that she could peer through all the worlds at a glance...
So, he needed support from intelligence.
Harrison immediately nodded in response.
"Your Highness, we have exhausted countless efforts and have yet to find the precise location where that Demigod Sea Beast is hiding.
Even the Mermaids of the Blue Star Tribe only knew that every ten years a powerful life must be sacrificed at a specific place to seek the protection of the Sea God."
Lide frowned, "What’s the solution?" He wasn’t here to listen to non-solutions; there were bound to be challenges, but if they couldn’t find a solution, what was the use of maintaining so many people?
Harrison quickly replied.
"The Intelligence Command Center, in combination with all the collected information, has deduced that the Sea Beast is very likely in a state of dormant transformation. We can hunt a large number of Demon Beasts and use their blood to awaken it, but the number must be very large."
"Blood awakening? What about the precise location?"
"The map has been drawn up; I’ll have someone fetch it for you immediately."
Harrison was wasting words; as soon as his statement concluded, he immediately stepped out of the room to order the guards in the hallway.
"Notify Kertlon immediately to bring us the latest sea chart."
When Harrison stepped back into the room, Lide’s expression was still heavy.
"Harrison, the situation may become increasingly dire. We must find the fragments of the Destiny Tablet, and we can’t afford to delay any longer.
Instruct the Intelligence Command Center and the Think Tank to immediately study the future development directions for Dawn City and methods to counteract the Old Day erosion, and to perfect the plan.
I will retrieve the fragments of the Destiny Tablet."
"As you wish, Your Highness."
Harrison understood the gravity of the situation too, his expression no more relaxed than Lide’s.
After Lide finished speaking, he said no more, turned, and rested his hands on the windowsill, his dark, profound eyes fixed on the ever-widening fissure in the sky.
His gaze flickered with a meaning that was difficult for anyone to fathom.
Although he held a high position, his power was vast, and even a single command could marshal millions of troops to die for him.
But the more so, the more he could feel the crown atop his head was so heavy.
Every bit of authority came with a corresponding responsibility.
As the leader of Dawn, he was everyone’s hope.
He mustn’t just enjoy the power, he also had to shoulder the responsibility that came with it.
And over the years, he had grown from a green rookie to the Dawn Sovereign, and what he learned the most was responsibility.
A man’s maturity often begins with knowing to take on the responsibilities that belong to him...
He wasn’t a savior, he couldn’t save the world, but he wouldn’t sit by and watch Dawn City be eroded by the Ancient Invasion into a desolate ruin.
Because he was, after all, the master of Dawn.
The hope of everyone, the light of all.
With these thoughts, a fighting spirit reignited in Lide’s dark pupils, a fighting spirit that no one could extinguish.
His gaze was as determined as steel, his will unshakable as the mountains.
As long as he still drew breath, Dawn City would never fall.
——
——
——
Bang bang~
The knocking on the door outside brought Lide back to his senses, his aura having undergone a drastic change amidst his thoughts.
He now resembled an unsheathed battle sword, sharp and exposed.
Harrison, who was by his side, only felt an immense authority radiating from Lide, so oppressive that it was almost suffocating.
"Enter."
Creak~
The door was pushed open, and a handsome male Bloodline clad in a black mage’s robe stepped into the room, carrying a rolled-up sea chart in both hands.
The Bloodline who entered had an elegant demeanor, despite holding the sea chart, he still exuded the air of a noble.
"Good day, Your Highness, this is the latest charted sea map."
Lide, with a stern expression, was slightly taken aback when he saw the Bloodline, then his eyes showed a trace of cold sharpness.
This Bloodline... was not ordinary.
He stepped forward, took the map, glanced at a prominent mark to confirm the target he was headed for, and then casually placed it into the System Space.
Then he continued to look at the Bloodline before him, his tone cold.
"Tell me your name."
Hmm?
Upon hearing this, Harrison blinked in surprise, then gave the Bloodline an oddly complex look, his expression subtle.
He had never seen Lide actively inquire about the names of the lower Bloodlines before, what was this today...
The addressed Bloodline appeared a bit startled, then joyfully responded.
"Your Highness, Kertlon Karchar offers you the highest of salutations."
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly, stepped forward again to get closer to the other, and continued.
"Who is your sire?"
Kertlon seemed not to notice this, with reverence, said, "It was Lord Audis who sired me during the last Frost Month."
"Audis?" Lide’s cool face suddenly showed a trace of a smile, "That guy is still managing Twilight City in the Underworld, are you interested in helping him?"
Kertlon stood up straight, with solemnity, said.
"Your Highness, your will is the direction all Bloodlines move towards! I will execute any order unconditionally!"
Lide gave him a thoughtful look.
"Very well, you can go now."
"Yes, Your Highness."
After giving a bow, Kertlon respectfully stepped back and then turned to leave.
Once Kertlon’s figure had vanished from the room, Harrison, somewhat puzzled, looked at Lide.
"Your Highness, what was that about?"
A mere third-generation Bloodline, was it worth Lide’s inquiry?
Moreover, this Kertlon was only level 12, which might have been considered strong before, but in Dawn City, where the Transcendent and Legendary ranks together counted over a dozen, he wasn’t anything extraordinary.
Lide’s questioning surely indicated some unique discovery.
But no matter how Harrison looked at it, this Kertlon was just Kertlon, indistinguishable from any before, which is why he found it quite strange.
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly, his gaze sharp as a blade’s edge.
"There’s something off about that Bloodline’s aura..."
"Off?"
Harrison was startled, then as if remembering something, became full of outrage, "Could it be Kertlon’s identity has been replaced?"
Identity replacement isn’t a fantasy; many magic spells can achieve it, and transformation skill is even a natural talent of some evil races.
Lide shook his head.
"No, Kertlon is not the problem."
"Then what are you suggesting?"
"He has been tainted with a trace of aura, extremely faint..." Lide’s gaze was dark and brooding.
"That’s not the aura of an ordinary life form, more like that of a strange Divine being."
His control over the Twilight Divine Position had reached 40%, making him extremely sensitive to the aura of various things.
The essence of the Twilight Divine Position was to discern the changes in rules, birth, growth, maturity, decay, Death... This was a whole set of rules.
Twilight lies between decay and Death in this cycle...
Therefore, he could sense auras from various lives and things, thus detecting the state they were in.
He had just detected a trace of aura from the Bloodline, although faint, it was tumultuous and raging, something beyond the reach of mortals.
If it weren’t for his improved control over the Twilight Divine Position, he would have found it quite difficult to notice such a faint and highly concealed presence.
"A strange Divine being??" Harrison was startled, and his thoughts began to race frantically.
"Could it be one that slipped in recently, during the transfer of Green City’s residents?" A mass migration was no small matter; chaos was not surprising.
But Lide shook his head.
"That’s unlikely. Frey had already inspected those residents before they were transferred.
That Divine being has definitely not returned to its peak state, it couldn’t have escaped Frey’s check."
Harrison took a deep breath, his expression grave.
"Your Highness, how shall we proceed?"
The thought of a potentially malevolent Divine being hiding by his side made his scalp crawl.
But this was beyond his capacity to deal with.
The methods of a Divine being were manifold – if one really wanted to hide, it would be impossible to find them, even if the whole city were searched.
Besides, Dawn City was no longer the small fortress of 200 people it once was; with a population over three hundred thousand, what kind of enormity would a full search entail?
Moreover, a large-scale probe was more likely to cause chaos and provide the intruder with an opportunity.
"For now, do not disturb Kertlon."
The murderous intent on Lide’s face flashed by, his inner turmoil no less than Harrison’s.
He hadn’t expected someone would be so audacious as to sneak into his stronghold. Were they seeking Death??
Correct content is on .
Dawn City was his foundation; allowing an unknown Divine being to muddle the waters there was absolutely intolerable.
Had he killed too few gods, or had this fellow grown a dozen guts??
"I will handle this matter personally!"
With that, he waved his hand, shattering the space in front of him, stepped forward, and vanished from sight.
Moments later, in the Plague God Country.
Frey abruptly grasped the Angel Battle Sword in her hand and stepped into the Land of Bone-Burying...
This terrifying entity, capable of cleaving mountains with a single strike, was summoned by Lide.
---
---
---
At this moment, the Knight who had undergone a Transformation into a Bloodline and was now the God of Murder – Stu Yate – had no idea that Lide, with the traces he inadvertently left, had detected his presence.
The Evil God, boldly daring, was wandering on the first floor of the City Hall.
The most dangerous place was the safest, a maxim Stu Yate deeply believed.
Furthermore, having obtained the Divine Position of Murder, his ability to hide his aura had significantly improved, and hence he did not believe anyone in the city could detect his presence.
Stu Yate had an absolute confidence in this.
At this moment, the Evil God’s gaze was fixed on Kertlon, who had just come down from the fifth floor, his eyes shining with sharp light.
The opportunity he had long awaited was finally at hand.
Over a month ago, he had willingly volunteered to participate in investigating the Lost Sea, and the location marked on the sea chart he presented to Lide had been firmly etched in his mind.
Stu Yate had keenly sensed the high importance the higher-ups of Dawn City attached to this mission upon hearing it.
He seized this chance to partake in the mission and even set up an excellent trap in the Lost Sea.
Once Lide acted, it would be his turn to bare his Tusks.
After waiting for a long time, the despicable Fake God was finally going to make a move...
This was an exceptional opportunity, even better than his previous plan.
Not only was there a fixed location for an ambush, but it was also far from Dawn City. If he could kill that damned Dawn Sovereign in the Lost Sea and use the Divine Artifact to consume his soul... he would become the new Kachar City Lord.
If orchestrated properly, he could even draw those Bloodlines to the rescue, diverting the sole resistance force of Dawn City.
Once the plan succeeded and he returned to Dawn City as the Kachar City Lord, he could directly control the entire city.
By the time those Bloodlines realized what had happened, he would have command of the army, and they wouldn’t even be able to enter Dawn City.
Although the plan did not seem perfect, Stu Yate had ninety percent confidence in it.
The spoils he obtained from killing the God of Murder were so substantial that it even frightened him.
The Ghost Cloak, which could turn his body into nothingness, allowing him to pass through rocks and walls, ...
He could devour souls and transform into the illusionary face of his victims,
He possessed the Godslayer Dagger that imprisoned souls, and even these were not all.
What really filled him with confidence was another Divine Artifact...
Thinking this, Stu Yate reached into his pocket and touched a palm-sized black stone, his eyes brimming with intoxication.
The High-level Divine Artifact—Sealing Stone.
Once struck by the power activated by the Sealing Stone, one’s abilities would be completely sealed, even Divine beings could not resist.
It was by this artifact that he had sealed the Cat and God of Joy.
Stu Yate had no reason to doubt he would fail.
The Ghost Cloak, Illusion Face, Godslayer Dagger, and the Sealing Stone—how could the unheard-of Fake God resist with this set of Divine Artifacts?
Hehehe...
Such a delightful hunt.
A hint of intoxication flashed across Stu Yate’s eyes.
He could already imagine plunging the dagger into his opponent’s heart and devouring the soul.
From this day forth, he would become the new Kachar City Lord!
Isn’t that interesting?
Holding the Twilight Divine Position had allowed him to taste the joy of scheming against enemies from the shadows.
The greatest strength of this Divine Position was that—as long as the enemy died by his hand, he would gain a power boost.
The stronger the enemies he murdered, the greater the increase in his strength...
The nearly perfect Divine Artifacts in his hands were acquired by the former God of Murder from slaying other Divine beings.
Had the God of Murder not been weakened during the Ancient Invasion to the point of barely stepping into the Transcendent level, lacking the power to utilize these artifacts, even the mightiest would not have posed much of a threat.
But, perhaps this was fate.
Stu Yate laughed maniacally in his heart.
Fate, this time, had favored him—he would be the ultimate winner.
And this was merely the beginning... One day, his name, Stu Yate, would become a glorious and eternal legend.
Tap tap—
He waited for Kertlon to approach.
"Kertlon, I bet His Excellency is very pleased with the map."
Stu Yate restrained his wonderful feeling of controlling everything and approached Kertlon, who had just descended from the fifth-floor office, with a smile.
"The smile on your face has already told me."
Kertlon looked at his old friend, his face beaming with joy.
"Gary, you guessed it right, His Excellency appreciates our work. Tonight at the Bauhinia Tavern, my treat!" Gary was the alias Stu Yate was using while disguised as a Bloodline.
Kertlon then spoke with slight regret.
"It’s a pity that the dancer, Miss Bast from Bauhinia Tavern, has been unaccounted for recently, otherwise, I would definitely have you witness the lady’s dance.
I swear upon the night, no one can resist Miss Bast’s charm..."
Upon hearing this, Stu Yate was momentarily stunned, then his expression turned somewhat strange.
That wild cat’s allure is indeed strong... But pitifully, you won’t ever see her again in your lifetime.
Thinking of Bast, who he had imprisoned, the now-fallen Knight God smiled brilliantly.
"Is that so? That truly is a shame..."
The Cat and Joy Goddess, she is now my pet...
After saying his piece, he shifted the topic, "Kertlon, when does His Excellency wish for us to depart with him?"
"Depart with His Excellency?"
Kertlon looked at Stu Yate curiously, "His Excellency didn’t ask us to follow; do you wish to partake in this operation?"
Stu Yate shrugged and replied with a smile.
"You know, I love the sea."
"Indeed, otherwise, you wouldn’t have volunteered to join us on the last mission. Come, let’s first go to Bauhinia Tavern to have a drink... I bet those fine wines are still there."
Stu Yate politely declined Kertlon’s invitation and calmly walked out the front door of the City Hall.
Surrounded by Bloodline members who continuously greeted him, his expression was one of pure delight.
The sensation of manipulating everything from the shadows intoxicated him.
"After the expedition to the Lost Sea concludes, everything in this city will be mine."
"If not for the perfect takeover of everything in this city, I would have pierced the wretched Fake God’s heart long ago."
"Hehehe... Oh, the anticipation."
"Now, let me return to my pet—the Cat and Joy Goddess."
"This is power, pure power; even the once-proud goddess is but a trinket in my cage..."
"I love all this..."
"Praise the darkness."

chapters.content:
Chapter 470: Chapter 471: The Knight God as the Treasure-Bestowing Boy, Four Divine Artifacts Acquired (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)
Stu Yate looked at the crowd flowing past him, his heart in an excited state. From behind the scenes, he was unperturbed, the feeling of controlling everything fascinated him.
His life as the Knight God seemed exceptionally boring compared to now...
If he had known that falling into darkness would grant him such immense power, perhaps he would have chosen to embrace the darkness before the old days even arrived.
Power was like an aphrodisiac; once tasted, that wonderful flavor made it impossible for his restless heart to ever be calm again.
Winding through several streets, Stu Yate suddenly turned into a hidden alleyway.
A few breaths later, he donned a Ghost Cloak, and the moment it covered his body, he transformed into nothingness, vanishing on the spot to the eyes and perceptions of ordinary people.
The Divine Artifact’s invisibility was not something mortals could see through.
He then slowly removed the Face of Nothingness from his face, and as he did, a surging power swelled within him.
Stu Yate’s eyes, hidden beneath the cloak, narrowed slightly as he comfortably stretched his body.
He then turned and headed for the dungeon where the Cat and Joy Goddess was imprisoned.
Before leaving Dawn City, he intended to reinforce the seal on that cat to prevent any mishaps.
He wouldn’t want the goddess he had desperately longed for and failed to obtain to escape... He hadn’t officially ravaged her yet...
A few minutes later...
On the outskirts of Dawn City, in front of a secluded residential building, the figure of Stu Yate, cloaked in the Ghost Cloak, silently appeared. Then he brazenly passed through the building and slowly drifted into the underground chamber deep beneath the ground.
"Stu Yate..."
Bast, the Cat and Joy Goddess, tightly shackled inside the iron cage, looked at the abruptly appearing Knight and God of Murder with a complex gaze.
The once righteous deity had now become her nightmare – a cat that yearned for freedom was trapped in a small cage, an unimaginable torment.
Hearing the faint voice, Stu Yate slowly pulled the cloak behind him and then revealed his face, carrying a shade of gloom.
His blue eyes fixed on the cat in the cage, and observing her helpless figure, he spoke with a tone filled with sadistic satisfaction.
"My goddess, why are you so pitiful?"
He moved forward a couple of steps, his smile becoming even more chilling.
"Hehehe... Do you know? This city will soon be mine, just like you belong to me now..."
"That Fake God will have his heart pierced by my dagger, and I... I will become the sole ruler here..."
"This will be the starting point for my rise to the peak. I will make all the gods tremble in my cage. Hahahaha..."
"Truly, a wonderful future..."
Upon hearing this, Bast’s face grew even grimmer. If this despicable scoundrel’s scheming were to succeed, then she might truly be without an escape...
She was well aware of the charm and potential of this city. After the chaos of the old days had descended, a stable base of operations was incredibly important.
In the tavern, she had entertained the idea of spreading her faith to restore her strength, but she had never thought to alert the city’s ruler or to rule the city herself.
However, though she didn’t think that way, Stu Yate, with his infinite ambition, wouldn’t think likewise.
"Stu Yate, the calamities of the old days are our common enemy. You should be uniting more forces now. We ought to be allies rather than foes. I am quite adept at gathering intelligence, and I believe if you let me out, I could be of greater assistance to you..."
Although Bast knew the hope was slim, she was still trying her best to grasp at a sliver of chance.
Hearing this, Stu Yate approached the iron chains, looking down upon her with a superior gaze.
"You wish to ally with me?"
His face then took on an expression of extreme satisfaction, his tone laced with a strange intonation.
"Beg me..."
"Proud Cat and Joy Goddess, kneel down, worship your master, lick your master’s shoes for him..."
After saying that, he suddenly lifted his foot and placed his shoe on the iron chain. Clang, the chain made a striking noise, rattling loudly.
Bast’s face went rigid in place, unable to utter a word.
Watching the unpredictable expressions of the Cat and Joy Goddess before him, the perverse pleasure in Stu Yate’s heart nearly drove him insane.
Can’t you see?
This is power. The goddess who once stood high above him, who scorned him, now cowered at his feet and even thought of allying with him.
And if he wished, he could position her in various poses to whip and ravish.
Hahaha...
Is there anything more wonderful in this world than this?
Praise the darkness!
Bast looked at Stu Yate, full of indignation, but then she sighed woefully and curled up in the cage, silent once more.
The weak never have a choice.
Seeing her like this, Stu Yate’s near deranged smile grew more intense; he didn’t care whether she genuinely wanted to swear fealty to him.
He simply reveled in the pleasure of trampling a once high-and-mighty goddess under his feet.
You were once so proud, weren’t you?
You once looked down on me, didn’t you?
Now, aren’t you tied up in a cage, subject to my abuse?
"My little kitty, your master is about to leave to hunt down that damned Fake God.
When I return, I’ll place this iron cage in the square of the city.
I want everyone to know that the proud Cat and Joy Goddess is now my pet.
Hahahaha..."
His deranged laughter echoed through the Underworld; those words made Bast, inside the cage, feel an all-pervading fear for the first time.
To be displayed in the square, to let everyone see her in her current state...
Just the thought of it left her feeling suffocated—this demon!
"Are you the foreign Divine that sneaked into Dawn City?"
At that moment, an indifferent voice rang out in the basement, the tone filled with utter disgust.
"What a nauseating pervert."
"Who gave you the audacity to act so recklessly in Dawn City??"
At this moment, Stu Yate felt his hair stand on end.
There was someone?!
He spun around sharply toward the source of the voice.
He saw a figure in a black and white robe, graceful, with an extraordinarily handsome face, fill his vision.
No one knew how long this mysterious person had been there, nor when he had arrived.
"Kachar City Lord..."
Stu Yate’s voice was incredibly hoarse, the madness that had been in his expression freezing instantly.
Lide looked at this foreign figure, his eyes as cold as millennia-old ice.
A Divine with ill intent had infiltrated Dawn City without notice, which almost made him furious.
Dawn City was his sensitive spot, and to touch it meant death!
His headquarters had nearly been stolen—how could that not infuriate him?
Caught in his conspiracy, Stu Yate quickly regained his composure, and after sensing for a moment, he made a surprising discovery.
The overwhelming encirclement he expected outside the basement had not materialized; it seemed the other party had come alone.
His face quickly regained its calmness, and then he looked somewhat arrogantly at Lide, his tone icy.
"You dare to come alone? That truly surprises me..."
The moment the words fell, a shattered crystal ball suddenly appeared in Stu Yate’s hand, which he then fiercely swung.
Crack~
The crystal ball was smashed to pieces.
A terrifying energy instantly erupted, like a storm that could demolish mountains, immediately sealing the basement. The Magic Power and space around them became mired in the strange energy.
With his plan revealed, Stu Yate’s face took on a crazed appearance.
"Hahaha, a Fake God is a Fake God... Do you know what I just did?"
"The space and Magic Power here have now been completely locked down by me!! Now, do you feel you can’t summon the power from the outside world anymore??"
"Even if you own a Plane, before the energy here is entirely depleted, you can only be like a lamb to the slaughter!!"
"Prepare to welcome Death... esteemed Fake God..."
"Hahaha..."
The reason for Stu Yate’s plan to act only after Lide left Dawn City was twofold.
Firstly, because Lide was very difficult to approach, unpredictable, and impossible to locate.
Secondly, because of the existence of the Land of Bone-Burying, Lide could Instant Teleport to hide within it. Once he entered that world, Stu Yate would have no way to touch Lide. That’s why he had patiently waited before acting.
But unexpectedly, Lide had appeared in this hidden basement.
Although this sudden turn of events had disrupted his plan, it also gave Stu Yate the chance for a one-on-one confrontation with Lide.
Moreover, even if he killed Lide here, no one would find out...
More importantly, although Stu Yate’s power was still far from restored, with several Divine Artifacts in hand, he absolutely refused to believe that a Fake God could escape his hunt!!
A sense of near madness took over him, the joy of being on the cusp of achieving his hard-won goal.
Lide stared at this man with a face full of astonishment... Why did it seem like all the Divines he encountered had brains that didn’t quite work right.
Did he have to say this? If it were him, he would have just taken action and talked later... There was no need to brag just to show how capable one was.
His expression was somewhat mocking as he looked at Stu Yate, who thought he had victory in his grasp.
"Just this?"
Stu Yate smirked coldly as he watched Lide, who showed no fear and even a hint of pity.
At a spot unnoticed by Lide, a palm-sized black stone appeared in Stu Yate’s hand, and Divine Power began to flow into it.
High-level Divine Artifact—Sealing Stone, just ten more seconds and the situation would be secure.
His rambling was all to confuse Lide.
"False God of Dawn City! Whatever you may be hiding, right now, you are just my captive, accept your death...."
Lide’s expression soured upon hearing this, but he was no longer interested in wasting words with a Divine whose strength was far from recovered.
"Freyja, capture him alive..."
The instant his words fell, the space in front of Lide shattered, and the figure of a Level 36 Death Blazing Angel emerged, sword in hand.
Stu Yate, about to launch his sneak attack with the Sealing Stone, felt an overwhelming and terrifying presence bearing down on him.
At the sight of Freyja’s figure, uncontrollable shock showed on his face.
A Twelve-winged Blazing Angel??
How was that possible?!!
But before he could react, the Blazing Angel vanished right before his very eyes.
Immediately after, Stu Yate felt an intense pain in his chest as he—like a baseball struck by a bat—was smashed against the wall.
Crack~ The horrific impact caused the wall to crack extensively.
Stu Yate’s vision blurred, and he nearly passed out.
But, as a Divine, he still possessed a strong will, managing to endure the agony from his body, trying to get up and flee.
Yet, in an instant, that figure reappeared.
Freyja stood emotionlessly in front of Stu Yate, extending her left hand in the air, aiming at the knight and God of Murder smashed against the wall. Infinite Divine Power gushed out like a surging tide.
The powerful Death Blazing Angel gave the Evil God no chance to resist, and directly sealed all his power.
Stu Yate’s body shook, then collapsed weakly to the ground, his eyes filled with despair.
The once arrogant Evil God now seemed unable to beat even a sturdy farmer.
Freyja sheathed her sword and stood aside, having said nothing throughout.
The rapid shift of the situation in the area left Bast, the Cat and Joy Goddess in the cage, utterly dumbfounded.
She hadn’t expected such a heavenly turnaround in just a few breaths.
Who were these two people??
Especially this Twelve-winged Blazing Angel, no, she wasn’t a Blazing Angel; the aura on her was not Divine Power but a powerful Death Energy...
This, this was a Fallen Angel.
By the Creator God above, she had encountered a Twelve-winged Fallen Angel in this narrow underground room!
Bast trembled with confusion and didn’t shift her gaze from Freyja for a long time, until she looked at Lide.
From their actions, it was evident that this man was the true master.
Kachar City Lord... Stu Yate’s words had already revealed the man’s true identity.
But to be protected by a Fallen Twelve-winged Blazing Angel of such a level of combat power, how could he be so simple??
Was he just a City Lord? Or a Fake God that was not worth mentioning??
Why had she never heard of such a legend...
After the fight was resolved, Lide walked up to the cage. At that moment, Stu Yate, now sealed by Divine Power and unable to move like a lump of mud, could only glare at him with eyes full of resentment.
His tone was cold, "Dawn City is also a place you can touch?? Ignorant of death and life."
Stu Yate’s expression turned worse than if he had swallowed a fly, already enveloped and devoured by despair.
"Damn Fake God... how can you possibly have a Twelve-winged Blazing Angel?!"
He had asked around countless times in Dawn City, and the strongest combat force in the city was Lide, who was only Legendary.
Although he had only recovered his Legendary power, at the same level, he was absolutely confident he could hunt down Lide.
But now... a Twelve-winged Blazing Angel had appeared!!
What was this??
It was supposed to be a duel, but you brought help, and the help you brought was so terrifying and powerful, not to mention that his strength hadn’t recovered, even if he were still the Knight God at his peak, he might not be able to defeat this Fallen Twelve-winged Blazing Angel.
Stu Yate looked at Frey with unwillingness in his eyes, but then, as if remembering something, his face showed an unmistakable shock.
"No, I recognize you, you’re the Master of Dawn’s War General — Freyja!!"
"You, you disappeared for tens of thousands of years, haven’t you?!"
Freyja gave him a cold glance, her tone indifferent.
"Master of Dawn? Haha, I once served him, but now, I am the Sharp Blade in the master’s hand, fighting for Dawn."
Having fallen and become the Death Blazing Angel, the former Freyja Dawn was dead, now she was Freyja Dusk, the Death Blazing Angel!
Upon hearing this, Stu Yate trembled, looking at Lide with an unbelieving, shocked gaze.
"You even managed to lead the Master of Dawn’s Angel into falling?!!"
His tone was filled with shock, and at the same time, there was an almost imperceptible hint of jealousy...
This was a Twelve-winged Blazing Angel!
In the entire Light God System, wasn’t every Twelve-winged Blazing Angel a well-known, powerful entity?
Only a Divine Power God could have such a powerful Angel as a subordinate.
Now, a Twelve-winged Blazing Angel, who was many levels above him even at his peak, was supposedly lured into falling by some unknown Fake God acknowledging him as master.
This made Stu Yate’s heart sour as if he had eaten ten thousand lemons.
Why couldn’t he encounter such good fortune??
Why!!
The jealousy in his heart was even more unbearable than the physical pain he suffered!
Life is so unfair, the Creator God is unfair!!
Lide looked at Stu Yate’s resentful and unwilling eyes without much fluctuation in his expression.
He had no fondness for this guy who secretly wanted to deal a heavy blow to Dawn City.
He slightly stretched out his right hand, ready to cast a spell.
However, the surrounding energy couldn’t be mobilized... Remembering the scene where Stu Yate shattered the Crystal Ball, Lide frowned.
"Freyja, break the seal here."
"As you wish, my lord."
Freyja, standing with her sword, had a concentrated look in her eyes. Her Angel Battle Sword burst forth with a dark divine light and the Death Blazing Angel swung her sword towards the ceiling.
In that instant, a brilliant light erupted, as if even the Milky Way was chopped down.
Crack~
A clear sound rang throughout the area, and the forces of Magic Power and space began to move again.
After feeling the restoration for a moment, Lide barely nodded his head, and with a crisp snap of his fingers.
Mage’s Hand appeared.
Swish, swish, swish~
The modified Mage’s Hand began its Transformation.
Noticing something, Stu Yate’s face suddenly turned ashen.
"No, you can’t..."
Before he could finish speaking, Mage’s Hand went forward and began to act, completely ignoring his screams.
Soon, the Knight and God of Murder, this guy who was just full of confidence about ruling over Dawn City, was stripped down to a mere set of underwear.
All his good stuff had been found by the Mage’s Hand.
Lide couldn’t care less to look any more at Stu Yate, who was left with nothing but his underpants, waved his hand, and the space in front of him cracked open, then directly sent this conspiring Evil God to the Land of Bone-Burying.
Watching this scene, Bast inside the iron cage flashed a trace of fear in her eyes.
This Kachar City Lord seemed even more terrifying than Stu Yate...
Lide noticed the strange look in the iron cage, glanced over, then didn’t bother to pay any more attention, turning his gaze to the Divine Artifacts scavenged from Stu Yate.
He never expected that so many Divine Artifacts could be found on a Divine being who liked to play dirty tricks.
"Every Divine being I’ve hunted down before, compared to this guy, they’re all paupers..."
In front of him, there were a total of 4 divine artifacts laid out, a whole four of them!!
Butchering a rich dog felt incredibly satisfying.
From left to right, the first item was a black cloak.
Ghost Cloak
Quality: Divine Artifact
Traits: When worn, it allows the body to become ethereal and immune to all physical damage, freedom to pass through rock walls unhindered, and undetectable to any being with Medium Divine Power or less.
Description: This artifact was forged by the Dwarf God at the devoted request of the God of Murder, but right after receiving the artifact, the God of Murder promptly killed the Dwarf God who made it. In his dying breath, the Dwarf God cursed this artifact—whomever possesses it would be hunted by dwarves for all eternity.
Ghost Cloak, a fitting name indeed.
This is definitely an artifact for peeping, pah, piracy and assassination.
A fine treasure.
The only thing to be wary of is to avoid flaunting it in front of Dwarf Gods, or you might get hammered to death without knowing.
The second item was a dagger.
Godslayer Dagger
Quality: Divine Artifact
Traits: It boasts the sharpest blade that can pierce through the shields of gods endowed with Powerful Divine Power. A life stabbed through the heart by this dagger will have its soul devoured, and the more lives it claims, the stronger the souls it devours, the more powerful it will become.
Description: An exceptionally special artifact, this one was originally a mundane weapon that underwent a transformation after piercing the heart of a Divine and absorbing divine blood and souls, becoming an artifact that even gods fear.
Such potent attributes.
Lide couldn’t help but feel that this dagger was the ultimate equipment for an assassin.
This Evil God truly was a little angel bringing warmth.
The third piece of equipment.
A mask.
Illusion Face
Quality: Divine Artifact
Traits: After devouring the souls of other lives, it can transform into the appearance of the devoured soul’s owner, and the more complete the soul, the more accurate the transformation. After devouring a soul, it can also obtain the memories of the other party.
Description: A very special artifact; born at the dawn of creation, its original owner has long been untraceable, but every assassin lurking in the shadows has wished to possess this artifact.
The fourth item.
Sealing Stone
Quality: High-level Divine Artifact
Traits: Capable of emitting Sealing Light; targets struck by the Sealing Light will have all their powers sealed. The duration of the seal depends on the strength of the target. The more Divine Power input, the stronger the Sealing Light.
Description: An extremely special artifact, believed to be crafted by the Creator God and possessing unimaginable power.
After looking over the attributes of the four divine artifacts, Lide could only sigh.
Easy come, easy go.
He went through so much trouble to get his hands on a single artifact, and it was just a hammer used by a dwarf... really, what a hammer.
Now unexpectedly, without even leaving home, someone had delivered a whole four artifacts to him!
And each one’s attributes were exceptionally impressive.
Although without too many fanciful traits, they were each powerful in their own right.
But the only problem was,
It seemed none were usable by him.
The Sealing Stone was okay, but the other artifacts didn’t align with his fighting style.
"This bastard, couldn’t he have procured some mage-appropriate equipment? I hate it when a dungeon run yields loot for other professions... what a dire husky."
Lide felt both elated and dismayed.
After fiddling with the equipment for a moment, besides the Sealing Stone, he stuffed the rest into the Land of Bone-Burying; these artifacts would wait until he found the right people to bequeath them to.
Divine artifacts contained a special force and couldn’t be kept in System Space.
Having taken care of the loot rather quickly, Lide finally had time to examine the Cat and Joy Goddess — Bast, locked in a cage, bound by her hands, feet, and neck.
With a bit of curiosity, he opened her attribute panel.
Bast
God Name: Charis (Cat and Joy Goddess)
Divine Position: Cat, Wanderer, Joy
Level: 25/34 (Sealed)
Skill: Brief
Introduction: A goddess who loves freedom, wandering and joy, she is now severely injured and her power is extremely weak.
Lide glanced over briefly and was somewhat surprised.
Another divine being??
And her former level was as high as 34.
But then he felt some regret, the Cat and Joy Goddess... Not a combat deity, what’s the use??
With these few lousy divine positions, what can be done besides meowing and being cute??
However, it might be interesting to keep a deity for being cute...
Later on, when showing off, what do you raise? What, a Pegasus, that’s impressive, and what do I raise? Oh, sorry, mine is quite ordinary, just a level 34 divine being, just let her be cute and dance naked...
Bast shuddered slightly under the somewhat strange gaze of Lide, and just as she was about to say something, Lide did not give her the opportunity.
"Frey, pull out the chains."
"Yes, Master."
After receiving the command, Frey immediately stepped forward and grabbed the cage before forcefully pulling.
Bang~ The chains embedded in the wall were brutally pulled out of the masonry, and the rubble behind them burst and scattered around.
Whoosh~
Bast, startled, moved quickly to one side; the chains hit the cage, making a crisp sound.
When the dust settled, the cage had been forcefully yanked out by Frey.
Seeing this, Lide waved his hand, and the space in front of him shattered.
Bast only felt a whirlwind of dizziness, and when she opened her eyes again, she found herself in a cozy room.
The floor was covered with a swan velvet carpet embroidered with bauhinia flowers, surrounded by exquisite sculptures and vivid oil paintings, plus potted green plants by the window, all contributing to a sense of refined elegance.
Where is this?
Bast, still inside the cage not yet released, was full of doubt.
But as if she had been forgotten, ten minutes, twenty minutes, a full Sunshine Hour passed without anyone taking any notice of her.
While Bast was bewildered, click, suddenly a spatial crack appeared in the room.
Lide’s tall figure emerged from the crack and slowly sat down in the armchair behind the desk.
Looking at the pitiable figure that resembled a helpless little kitten, his deep eyes were undisturbed.
"Cat and Joy Goddess, Bast, no, I should call you by your divine name, Charis.
What are you doing invading my city?"
Bast looked at the handsome and elegant Lide, and her nervousness eased slightly; at least she was now facing a deity far more normal than the Knight and God of Murder...
"Respected Kachar City Lord, I harbor no ill will towards you or your city..."
"No ill will? You infiltrated quietly and without notice?" Lide’s gaze was cold.
"Or do you think after staying in the Bauhinia Tavern for a week, I wouldn’t know?"
He had just left, taking Frey with him to investigate Dawn City, but found no other divine beings besides these two.
The sensation Bast caused over two months ago in the Bauhinia Tavern had been reported up by the intelligence headquarters.
Beautiful, dancing so enticingly, and then suddenly disappearing – all of these oddities made it natural for the intelligence headquarters to take note.
Bast, looking into Lide’s intense and penetrating eyes, quickly tried to explain.
"Great Kachar City Lord, I was unintentionally brought back to Dawn City by your soldiers, I didn’t infiltrate deliberately, and I just wanted to find a safe place to recover my strength..."
Lide didn’t seem to buy this explanation and switched the topic.
"How were you captured by the Knight and God of Murder?"
"I didn’t know at the time that the Knight God had fallen into darkness, nor that he had acquired the Divine Position of Murder.
After meeting him in Dawn City by chance, Stu Yate said there was a way to recover strength quickly, I trusted him and didn’t doubt it, soon after, he used a divine artifact to seal all my powers..."
Bast’s voice carried a hint of resentment; being imprisoned for several months had indeed provoked her fury.
Lide frowned at this, dissatisfied with the explanation.
"Do you know anything about the other deities in Dawn City?"
Bast shook her head.
"Besides Stu Yate, I haven’t encountered any other Divine Beings," Lide sighed with some annoyance after his inquiry—it seemed that the Cat and Joy Goddess was nothing but a useless encumbrance.
The Divine Position had no use, nor could it be used to nurture followers. The Divine Body was still valuable, but it seemed like a waste to kill her... after all, she was a living Divine Being, who might be of use in the future.
After thinking for a moment, Lide gestured for the Bloodline outside his door.
"Bring Harrison in."
A few moments later, Harrison briskly walked into the room and upon seeing Bast within the iron chains, his eyes revealed a touch of curiosity.
"Your Highness, is this the unfamiliar Divine Being that left traces on Kertlon?" he asked.
Lide nodded, "No, that Divine Being has already been sealed by me. This one is the Cat and Joy Goddess."
He thought for a while, then took out half a palm-sized Sealing Stone from his chest.
The Power of Faith was injected into it, and moments later, the Sealing Stone burst forth with ghostly light, surging directly at Bast.
When the ghostly light faded, Bast’s face showed utter despair, feeling the indestructible seal solidify once again.
With her current strength, it would probably take a hundred years to break the seal.
"She has been sealed by me. You can take her down for interrogation, or you can study to see if she can be of any use.
Release her shackles, Frey. Her strength can’t even beat a Level 3 warrior now," Lide instructed.
Harrison looked at Bast in the cage with a bizarre expression—it was a living Divine Being, after all.
"Understood, Your Highness."
Bast’s expression shifted unpredictably as Frey completely unsealed her shackles.
The Cat Goddess, her garments tattered and her pale skin exposed in many places, stepped forward to Lide’s desk and said solemnly,
"Respected Kachar City Lord, I am willing to become your subordinate and serve under you."
It was better to submit to the ruler of a city filled with wonders and who had a Fallen Angel at his behest than to be truly taken away for research.
Lide slightly squinted, "Good, then cooperate well with Harrison. He will arrange everything for you, go now."
Bast opened her mouth, as if wanting to say something, but upon seeing Lide’s calm gaze, she sighed resignedly and left the office with Harrison.
After the two departed, Frey appeared beside him, breaking through the space.
Her tone was frigid.
"Your Highness, she only has traces of the Knight God and the God of Murder on her. I didn’t sense any other Divine Being on her..."
"I know," Lide nodded thoughtfully.
"We’re keeping her because we need a target, one that can attract other Divine Beings..."
There’s a saying: a thief cannot be eternally vigilant.
Now that Dawn City was rid of hiding Divine Beings, who knew if other Divine Beings might infiltrate in the future?
Keeping this easily controlled and weak Divine Being, she could certainly attract the attention of those intruders... All in all, the benefits outweighed the disadvantages.
Lide shook his head, having been given a wake-up call.
Though Dawn City was hidden from the world and difficult for outsiders to find, for Divine Beings, discovering and infiltrating it was hard to prevent.
He couldn’t always have Frey stationed in Dawn City, could he?
After a brief pondering, he grew tired of thinking. The simplest solution was to make Dawn City stronger.
If he had more than ten Divine Beings stationed again, then anyone who sneaked in would be wasting their time.
Lide stood up, his dark eyes turning toward the window.
Feeling the increasingly dense aura of ancient times in the air, he took a deep breath and hesitated no longer.
He had to get his hands on the fragments of the Destiny Tablet.
"Frey, come with me to the Lost Sea immediately. Dawn City cannot be delayed."
"Yes, Master."
As Lide’s sharp blade, Frey was ready to strike wherever pointed, without a hint of hesitation.
Lide nodded, calling his guard to inform Harrison of his departure.
But just as the guard stepped out of the office, suddenly, a flapping sound of wings stirred the air.
A mini-armored little bat appeared in front of Lide.
"Master..."
Castro’s voice carried a note of grievance.
As the life created by Lide himself, this Dawn Bat King felt neglected by Lide for some time.
Before, Castro had been Lide’s most beloved mount, thanks to its supersonic flight speed.
But as Lide successively broke through the Transcendent and Legendary levels, Castro’s speed was no longer sufficient, so Lide left the king of the Dawn Bats in Dawn City.
Lide sensed Castro’s slight resentment and reached out to let the little guy land in his palm.
Looking at the miniaturized and endearingly cute Castro, he smiled lightly.
"It’s time to boost your strength a notch..."
He was a person who cherished the past; Castro had been through life and death with him so many times, he naturally couldn’t just abandon it.
He glanced at the attribute panel out of the corner of his eye—the Dawn Sect still had over four million of the Power of Faith.
Although not a lot, it was enough to elevate Castro to the Transcendent level.
Without much ado, he instantly teleported with his longtime favorite mount to the back garden of City Hall.
"Revert to your original form; I grant you the power to break through to the Transcendent."
Upon hearing this, Castro was instantly overjoyed. Its body shot out, and in a few breaths, it grew larger and thicker, transforming into a giant beast with wingspan over ten blades long, clad in solid Extraordinary Armor, resembling a steel monster.
Lide nodded in satisfaction—the armor-clad Castro did indeed look impressive, especially those Blade Wings, which were a great weapon capable of killing countless enemies and even shattering city walls on each dive.
Taking a couple of steps forward, he looked at Castro, whose head was bowed before him, and extended his right hand to rest it on its head.
The sacred Power of Faith began to flow.
The exaggerated strength caused Castro’s aura to gradually climb.
Having assisted many of his subordinates in power enhancement, Lide was well accustomed to such situations.
He calmly channeled the Power of Faith.
Ten minutes, twenty minutes... after one Sunshine Hour.
Accompanied by a roar that reverberated throughout Dawn City,
a Level 20 Transcendent giant beast was born.
Castro, the king of the Dawn Bats,
could once again qualify as a mount for Lide after many years.
Although Level 20 was still not up to Lide’s standards—he considered only Legend grade to be fitting—the Power of Faith was insufficient, so he would have to make do.
Upon this thought, he couldn’t help but smile. What he was now making do with as Transcendent used to be a precious top-tier combat power at Level 15.
Lide turned to give the upgraded Castro, now Transcendent, a few glances. The wingspan of this king of bats had reached 20 blades in length.
Even the Extraordinary Armor, which had once cost a fortune to forge for it, had grown larger with the transformation.
