As Lide’s silhouette flew away from Dawn City, the Ocean God System sensed Lide’s departure.
But these Sea Clan Gods were already assigned tasks, so they showed little reaction to Lide leaving.
After all, their connection wasn’t deep; their joining Dawn City was more because of Casslynne’s sake.
Betty, who was in seclusion comprehending the Divine Position of a Knight, also seemed to sense Lide’s departure, her aura fluctuating briefly before calming down...
The high tower at the center of the Magic Industrial Research Institute.
Casslynne, holding a white cat, seemed to see through the myriad realms, turning her head to stare in the direction of Lide’s departure, her expression subtle.
Carrying destiny, gaining power.
But isn’t destiny also a form of imprisonment?
I’ve grown tired of this imprisonment, I want to break free from the shackles of fate...
I hope you can bring me more surprises, Sovereign of Dawn.
—
—
—
After Lide left Dawn City, he didn’t use the Land of Bone-Burying to teleport thousands of miles away, instead driving Castro to descend to a low altitude, his sharp gaze sweeping across the land like a hunting falcon.
He wanted to see just how chaotic the situation had become.
After flying hundreds of kilometers from Dawn City, an ancient evil aura instantly pervaded the area, the power of corruption from the Chaos Void made the whole world seem like it was facing twilight,
During high-speed flight, not far away, he saw various Ancient Monsters roaming the earth; some lives, just recently corrupted by the Ancient, were still vaguely recognizable.
However, it wasn’t just Ancient Monsters below; occasional appearances of Abyss Demons tainted those decaying airs with the evil of the abyss.
Although the density of demons was not as high as that of Ancient Monsters, seeing demons on the Main Plane still felt profoundly dissonant.
However, under the cold, biting wind and yellowing plants, it did fit quite well with the demons’ background.
Crack~
As Lide skimmed over a frozen river, the space below on the ice suddenly twisted, and then a demon with two long horns emerged out of thin air.
On sensing the aura of the Main Plane, the demon howled and attacked two nearby snow wolves.
And not far away, several Ancient Monsters, already fully corrupted and rotten, appeared...
Instantly, a three-way melee ensued.
Castro was fast, and the scene flashed by in an instant, making Lide somewhat emotional.
That previous scene reflected the current situation of the Main Plane—chaos.
Extreme chaos, where various unrelated lives were now intertwined in battle, far beyond the normal rules of the food chain.
Spanning thousands of miles took just twenty minutes; even not flying at full speed, Castro’s speed was still awe-inspiring, yet Lide had not looked relaxed since leaving Dawn City.
Whether Ancient Monsters or Abyss Demons, both had brought indescribable disasters to this world.
Ancient Monsters and demons had become mainstream, and the normal lives of the Main Plane had become rare.
It was foreseeable that if this continued, the whole Plane would eventually be corrupted and eroded, and then, the world would truly be destroyed.
After observing the thousand miles, Lide drove Castro up into the high skies, having gained a clear understanding of the current situation.
No need to waste any more time, he also began to adjust some of his plans as the situation changed, demanding additional considerations.
Whizz~ Castro’s three times the speed of sound cruise was exaggerated, and in the sky, one could only see a streak before it vanished.
Originally, Lide planned to bypass Green City and head directly to Nolan Capital, but upon sighting Green City, a thought crossed his mind; what was Vina doing now?
Thinking of the little maid he had "consumed," his stern gaze softened.
It had been half a month since he left Green City, and it was uncertain how long this trip to Nolan Capital would take... perhaps, it was time for a farewell.
Immediately upon this thought, Castro, originally set to bypass Green City, slightly turned and sped towards Green City in rapid flight.
Whizz~
The army guarding Green City suddenly became disrupted because an iron beast, flapping Blade Wings, was flying directly toward them.
Before several messengers could sound the alarm, the leader of the Bloodline nearby immediately stopped them.
Didn’t all the Bloodline know that Castro was Lide’s mount? And the bloodline resonance between Lide and them was something outsiders couldn’t understand.
Lide didn’t head to the City Lord’s manor, instead driving Castro across the magnificent, bustling Green City, flying directly to the Crimson Mage Tower.
Upon reaching above the Crimson Mage Tower, the powerful Magic Shield of the tower broke open a huge hole under the shocked gaze of the Mage Apprentices below, and then Lide flew straight in.
Dismounting, he paid no attention to the admiring gazes of the surrounding Mage Apprentices.
He walked straight into the Mage Tower and ascended to the third-floor study.
Stepping in.
Seeing the surprised faces inside the study made Lide smile warmly.
"Lord Lide... "
"Teacher... "
Vina and Isa had not expected Lide to return so suddenly, their hearts nearly leaping out in joy.
Especially for Vina, who was new to love, it felt like her heart was filled with joy.
Although Lide had only been away for about ten days, for a girl who had just tasted the essence of her beloved, it seemed like a century had passed.
At this moment, Vina’s gaze at Lide seemed as if it could drip with water.
Lide looked into Vina’s captivating blue sapphire-like eyes with a tender and indulgent expression.
This was his little maid.
Somewhat proudly in his heart, Vina was now the Deputy City Lord of Green City, wielding great power, with a command that could decide the fate of hundreds of thousands.
Such a dazzling and celebrated existence, referred to as a queen, was merely his maid... and one that he had personally trained.
A nurturing type.
Vina’s golden hair, cascading like ocean waves, fell behind her, lending her an ethereal and striking demeanor.
Upon seeing Lide, the girl’s eyes lit up like stars, brightening the whole world.
"You’re back..." Vina’s voice carried an unmistakable love and tenderness.
Young love is always tender...
Lide, with a smile on his lips, opened his arms and advanced to embrace the girl tightly.
Sniffing the unique fragrance of the girl, his heart instantly calmed.
Though a woman’s arms are not strong, they always offer a haven for her lover to nestle in... a different kind of flavor.
The moment Lide embraced her, Vina’s heart seemed about to leap from her throat.
She felt like the happiest person in the world.
The breath she yearned for day and night surged into her heart, stiffening her body, and then, as if all her strength were drained, she collapsed limply into Lide’s arms.
The constant yearning in her heart fully released in this moment, giving the girl a glow of satisfaction that was incredibly enchanting.
"Teacher..." Little Yisha watched the two embrace tightly, speechless with a blush on her face, slightly embarrassed.
Hearing this childish voice, Vina suddenly snapped back to reality, realizing that Isa was still there, and she blushed uncontrollably.
With a soft cry, she got up with a flushed face, turned her head away, and dared not look at them, as if she were dying of embarrassment.
Lide looked at such a lovely girl, his smile warm and genuine.
His little maid, no matter how stormy it was outside, remained ever the same pure girl in his presence.
Time changed everything, except her attitude towards him.
"Isa, go to the kitchen and have them prepare dinner; teacher will first discuss some matters with Vina, for one Sunshine Hour, no, two Sunshine Hours later, I will come down..."
The innocent Isa, unaware of what was to transpire next, happily nodded and joyfully left the study.
When the door slammed shut and was magically locked,
Vina standing by trembled in her heart as if she sensed something, her shyness almost preventing her from raising her head.
Her breathtakingly beautiful face flushed with red.
Her heart trembled, her body weakened, almost unable to stand.
Lide waved his hand, and the wide-open windows also quietly closed, leaving just the two of them in the study at this instant.
A closed space, with the beloved whom she hadn’t seen for a long time...
A special atmosphere was brewing.
"Lord Lide..."
Vina, seeing that they were undisturbed, allowed her love to surge forth uncontrollably, no longer caring about shyness, and plunged into Lide’s arms with a blushing face.
Lide wrapped his arms around the girl, feeling her surging pride, a smile curving on his lips.
Fouls afoot, that’s a strike...
"Vina, did you miss me?"
Hearing his low whisper near her ear, Vina’s heart trembled, her voice quivering slightly.
"Lord Lide, do you think I’m cursed? Otherwise, why, when I don’t think of you for a moment, does my heart feel blocked, and only when I think of you do I feel like I have a soul, and can breathe easily..."
Hearing that heartfelt voice, Lide’s gaze softened.
Damn it, it’s been too long since I dated, and the girl’s talking love better than I do...
As the girl spoke softly, Lide too was moved, and while embracing, his hand quietly moved along the blue Mage robe to reach the peak.
Ah...
The girl in his arms let out a low call, her heart pounding faster, her entire blood circulation speeding up, her complexion turning flush like a cooked shrimp, completely limply leaning on him, allowing his liberties.
"Lord Lide, Vina misses you so much, thinking of you when waking, during meals, at bedtime, even in dreams, and even while embracing you, your face fills my mind..."
Lide was deeply moved inside, thinking, I’m done for, today this lass might charm me to death...
Slightly lowering his head, looking at the girl whispering with her eyes closed, he hesitated no more and deeply kissed her tender lips.
Vina’s body stiffened for a moment then wrapped around Lide like an octopus.
The air heated up in that moment.
A joyous reunion better than a new marriage.
Subsequently, the study switched to a midnight channel.
There was a poem.
A lone boat falls on the sandy beach,
With a pole but no water, retreat is hard,
Upon meeting a heavy rain, the rivers and lakes overflow,
No effort is needed to go back and forth.
Two Sunshine Hours later.
Lide led Vina downstairs, where the girl, now clad in a blue Mage’s robe, radiated with a brilliance, her entire being exuding an indescribable charm—especially the blend of naivety and allure in her features, which was utterly captivating.
The dining room was already prepared for dinner. Little Yisha was unaware of the tumult Lide had just been through, and happily pulled him to sit down for the meal.
Beside her, Vina felt a bit shy, thankful that Yisha was unaware of the adult matters, allowing the affectionate girl to relax a bit.
During the meal, Lide shared the news that they would soon be heading to Nolan Capital. Vina, who had devoted her whole heart to him, surprisingly made no complaints; instead, she gently admonished him to be cautious and take care of himself.
This moved Lide strangely, as while the girls from Earth were all distinctive and modern, Vina, raised in a feudal society, somehow brought him more comfort.
Thinking about this made him smile. With his current status and position, any partner was within easy reach.
The saying that one never lacks companionship as long as they are sufficient was never false.
But for Lide, things obtained too easily were often uninteresting.
Thus, despite his power, he rarely contemplated these trivial romantic matters, and only now had he truly embraced Vina, the girl who had given him everything.
Indeed, if he really wanted, weren’t all the girls around him excellent? Of course, if he were reckless, it might ultimately turn into—well, even a Dawn Sovereign would end up leaning against the wall to leave...
After dinner, gazing at the charming Vina, Lide suppressed the stirrings in his heart and, after giving some instructions to the two girls, made ready to head to Nolan Capital.
Serious matters were pressing.
"Vina, after I leave, immediately take Yisha to Dawn City. The situation is too chaotic now, and even though you have become Transcendent, you must still be careful not to be careless."
"Yisha, your teacher is going to meet your grandfather Spark. When we return, I’ll take you to the Storm Sea Domain to find your clan..."
Both Vina and Yisha, looking reluctant, obediently nodded their heads.
Lide gently patted the heads of the two girls and, without further hesitation, mounted Castro and soared into the dark night sky.
Only two hopeful girls were left at the entrance of the Crimson Mage Tower.
---
---
---
Nolan Capital.
Inside the prestigious Royal Magic Academy on the Main Plane of Glory, a massive surge of Magic Fluctuation suddenly erupted, as if heaven and earth were collapsing, the sun and moon shattering.
All the students felt an immense pressure, making it hard to even breathe, and some were even so daunted by the terrifying force that they knelt on the ground.
Many high-level professors and teachers turned abruptly, their faces filled with surprise and envy, looking towards the source of the overwhelming presence.
It was Legendary!
"Ha ha ha, I have finally broken through to Legendary!"
As expected, an ecstatic voice echoed in the sky.
The struggling students immediately looked on with envy and admiration.
Legendary, regardless of where one was, this Level represented the pinnacle of combat power.
Before the Ancient Monsters had descended, there were only a handful of Legends in the Nolan Empire; now, they were witnessing the birth of a Legend.
Several students recognized the voice amidst the receding pressure and started an excited discussion.
"That voice seems to be Lord Spark’s!"
"Sss, Lord Spark really is a genius, to have advanced from Transcendent to Legendary in just one year!"
"Haha, our Nolan Capital welcomes another Legendary, those damn Ancient Monsters don’t stand a chance against the Capital now!"
"Genius, such genius indeed demands our admiration!"
With tousled hair and an aura still unsettled from his recent breakthrough, Spark stood laughing crazily atop a Mage Tower within the Academy.
"Haha, Kachar family’s brat, bet you didn’t see this coming!! Just one year and I’ve gone from Transcendent to Legendary!"
"You’re probably still fretting over how to achieve Transcendence!"
"Haha, let this tell you who the real genius is!"
At this moment, remembering his previous humiliating encounters with Lide, Spark felt immensely gratified: Legendary!
What a terrifying Level!
And now, he had achieved it.
Lide probably hadn’t even touched the shadow of Transcendence yet.
Spark was already fantasizing about appearing before Lide, with Lide bowing down in deep respect, yelling "teach me, Master."
Oh, the pleasure, he hadn’t felt this delighted in a long time.
Haha, Kachar family’s pathetic brat, wait to be astounded by your genius teacher!

chapters.title: Chapter 483 - 484: Battle in the Royal Capital, Lide Approaches
chapters.content:
Chapter 483: Chapter 484: Battle in the Royal Capital, Lide Approaches
"Lord Spark, congratulations on reaching Legendary status. His Majesty has invited you to the Royal Palace..."
Not long after Spark had broken through, the news spread, and Princess Kadi approached with grace.
With hair disheveled and his mage’s robe full of wrinkles, the scruffy-looking Spark was sporting a smile even more radiant than a chrysanthemum.
He looked at the rather attractive princess in front of him and laughed loudly,
"Just a breakthrough to Legendary status, pretty ordinary, I’m just a regular person."
But the grin on the old man’s face was far from ordinary; his proud and coy expression was laughably absurd.
He was putting on a bit of a show...
Kadi wasn’t bothered by this, obviously aware of Spark’s unrestrained nature.
She followed his lead with a soft laugh,
"Lord Spark, your talent really makes people envious.
If your genius protege knew that his teacher had advanced from Transcendent to Legendary in just one year, he’d undoubtedly be completely shocked and proud."
In recent times, Spark had often mentioned Lide; Kadi wouldn’t take his words about the ’unpromising student’ at face value—who would mention someone constantly if they weren’t pleased with them?
She knew exactly how to scratch Spark’s itch.
Sure enough, Spark, whose face was already beaming with a wide smile, broke into an even broader grin.
Hahaha, did the Kachar family’s young one hear that?? Not to brag, but compared to my talent, yours is like a speck of crumb on bread... trivial.
Just thinking of Lide’s look of disbelief and admiration upon seeing him made Spark unbearably thrilled.
He was bursting with the desire to show off, even wishing he could immediately return to Green City to show Lide who the real genius was!
"Hahaha, my disciple is also unpolished, can’t really be called a genius, just a little bit behind me, give him a few more years, and perhaps he could catch up to me from a year ago..."
Kadi’s face filled with surprise, then she smiled warmly.
"Lord Spark, breaking through Transcendence in your twenties is also quite genius.
It’s a pity that the Ancient Invasion has occurred, otherwise, your disciples would have surely made a name for themselves far and wide in the Nolan Empire."
Spark’s face showed a hint of pride as he laughed heartily,
"You flatter me, Your Highness. That boy still needs a lot of hard knocks and cultivation, he’s still lacking..."
Kadi couldn’t help but smile and agreed with a few words to the untidy old man, and Spark was satisfied to accompany her to the Imperial Palace.
Minutes later, the royal carriage traveled along the main road, with pedestrians passing by on both sides.
From inside the carriage, Spark looked out the window, his expression turning very somber at the scene before him.
The morale of the patrolling warriors on the street was low, all of them listless, like flowers that hadn’t been watered for half a month, wilted.
Countless residents in ragged clothes, during the cold Frost Month, only had thin clothes for warmth. Beggars were everywhere, their bodies barely covered, huddling together to stay warm, which only added to the destitution...
Spark’s inner joy plunged suddenly, and with complex emotions, he turned to look at Princess Kadi inside the carriage.
"Your Highness, have the commoners around the Royal Capital all been taken in?"
"Not yet..."
Kadi paused at his question, then her eyes showed pain, and her voice also dropped.
"The three cities subordinate to the Royal Capital were breached a week ago, resulting in millions of refugees. The Royal Capital has a limited capacity, and currently, there are still over 300,000 people gathered outside the city."
"Is there a solution?"
"No, our food and other supplies are extremely scarce, and we’re powerless to take in any more refugees.
Once the next wave of Ancient Monsters attacks, I fear these civilians will..."
Kadi sighed sorrowfully, leaving her sentence unfinished, but the meaning was unmistakable.
Should change arise, those disaster-stricken people without shelter will undoubtedly be the first to suffer.
But in the face of such a catastrophic disaster, who can save the world?
The Nolan Capital is already the largest city in the Nolan Empire, yet it can only accommodate over ten million people. With the population around the Royal Capital amounting to a full twenty million, even if a part dies, the remaining portion would still be overwhelming for the Royal Capital to bear.
In the face of world-ending catastrophe, no one can save everyone. The fates of those civilians outside the city walls are already sealed, and when the Ancient Monsters attack again, perhaps we will never see them again...
As a princess, these abandoned people are her subjects, but who can oppose the inevitable collapse, who can defy the heavens?
Lord Spark couldn’t help but fall into silence, ultimately letting out a soft sigh.
The Nolan Capital was already facing a crisis of obliteration from the Ancient Catastrophe, so how could those Nobles possibly spare a thought for a bunch of civilians?
Silence fell in the carriage; neither of them spoke again.
Only the creaking of the carriage wheels remained.
Half a Sunshine Hour later,
The carriage slowly made its way into the Nolan Palace.
Upon entering the Imperial Palace, Spark instantly noticed something different.
The surrounding soldiers were incredibly serious, the guards were several times more numerous than usual—posts every three steps, watch every five.
It seemed something major had happened.
He instantly furrowed his brows, and with an equally serious expression, proceeded to the main hall of the Imperial Palace alongside Kadi.
Moments later, they arrived at a lavishly extravagant palace, its ceiling adorned with all sorts of exquisitely detailed reliefs.
Golden statues of Angels, masterfully hand-painted oil paintings, royal exclusive decorative vessels—every ornate detail sparkling with splendor.
No one doubted the royal family’s heritage, but every time Spark witnessed this sight, he couldn’t help but feel an authentic surge of emotion. If this palace were dismantled and sold, how many nights could someone spend with Elves on Lide’s Lilian Street???
This unkempt old man had a persistence about this matter that most people couldn’t match, even after reaching Legendary status...
After tasting the moment, noticing Kadi’s puzzled look as she turned his way, Spark quickly regained his composure and coughed, hastily striding forward pretending nothing was amiss.
This massive palace was divided into an outer hall and an inner hall, with guards stationed only in the outer hall, while the inner hall was where the Nobles debated affairs.
Passing through the luxurious outer hall and stepping into the more opulent inner hall, he was immediately assaulted by a roar of noise.
Over a hundred splendidly attired Nobles were at that moment engaged in a vociferous debate, squabbling furiously, the scene incredibly chaotic.
"No! We absolutely can’t activate the Destiny Tablet fragments! Once activated, it will surely attract those damned monsters’ attention!"
"Nonsense, you rude bumpkin from Akenerier district, if we don’t activate the Destiny Tablet fragments, are we waiting for a complete crop failure in our Secondary Plane?? Waiting for the breath of the Ancient to turn the entire city’s population into Ancient Monsters??"
"Why can’t we wait a while longer? Wait until the Angel Alliance is formed, and when the Ancient Monsters’ gaze is drawn elsewhere, then use the Destiny Tablet fragments—isn’t that better?! Why must we take such a huge risk to activate them now?!"
"How can you be so sure that the Angel Alliance can attract the attention of all the Ancient Monsters?? Without activating the Destiny Tablet fragments, we’re going to starve millions of civilians to death!!"
"To preserve strength, sacrificing some civilians is not unacceptable..."
"Idiot! Civilians are the foundation of the Empire, without civilians what sort of Noble are you?! Whom will you rule over?!"
From the heated arguments, Spark immediately recognized the reason for the heightened security at the palace.
All of this originated two weeks ago when they found a fragment of the Destiny Tablet in a sealed land.
The Sun Goddess announced to the world that the Destiny Tablet Fragment was the only way to counter the Ancient Invasion.
Thus it sparked a discussion among the Nobles about the Destiny Tablet Fragment.
It was also after sensing the power emanating from the Destiny Tablet Fragment at close range that he experienced a deeper understanding of the rules and made his Legendary breakthrough.
"Lord Spark has arrived!"
Just as Spark was enjoying the sight of the red-faced bickering Nobles, a sudden exclamation of surprise beside him brought the hall’s dispute to an abrupt halt.
Everyone turned their heads in unison to look towards the entrance.
A wave of astonishment and heated discussion then began.
"Rumor has it that Lord Spark was still Transcendent a year ago, and now, in just a short year, he has advanced to become Legendary. It really fills one with envy..."
"It’s said that Lord Spark’s disciple is also a Talent just like him. Indeed, a powerful teacher has a profound influence on his disciples."
"Legendary, including Lord Spark, the Royal Capital now has six Legendary figures stationed here. It’s a pity that the Wind and Snow God and the Hail God left because of the Angel Alliance... Otherwise, our Nolan Capital would never fall."
"So this is what a Legendary looks like? Such an unfettered image, truly befitting of Lord Spark, so captivating..."
At this moment, Spark, who was in disheveled clothing, didn’t show a trace of embarrassment from the compliments around him but instead held his head high with proud arrogance, smiling radiantly and basking in the glory of everyone’s attention.
This old man was blissfully unaware of what shame was, at least until Princess Kadi, unable to bear it any longer, took him by the sleeve and led him through the crowd to the elevated throne, casting a smiling glance at their King.
"Good day, Your Majesty, Spark sends his regards."
Spark looked at the King who was just over fifty, very calmly placed a hand over his chest with minimal formality, displaying the greeting exchanged between Nobles of equal Dignity.
Power was the only criterion; the rules of the Nobles were a joke in the face of absolute power, for rules could not bind the strong.
Having reached the Transcendent Level, one already had powers beyond ordinary people, and upon achieving the Legendary status, even a King had to treat them with respect.
During these tumultuous times, the King, barely Transcendent himself, relied heavily on others, thus he showed extraordinary respect for the strong.
Therefore, Spark’s behavior was completely normal.
"Good day, Lord Spark, the Royal Capital has gained another top Mage, it’s like adding wings to a tiger!"
The King smiled brilliantly, for at this critical moment, any additional power was an extra assurance for survival, the more, the better.
But moments later, the King’s excited expression faltered.
"Regrettably, the two Divine figures of the Royal Capital have left. Otherwise, I wouldn’t be so worried..."
Upon hearing this, the excitement in the hearts of the surrounding Nobles cooled somewhat.
Indeed, with the Divine figures gone, adding another Legendary seemed to hardly compensate for the loss.
View the correct content at )
How infuriating! The Angel Alliance had to be established now of all times...
But fortunately, those two Divine figures were secretly invited to leave back then, before the Angel Alliance had publicly called for the Divines. The Destiny Tablet Fragment was also found after the departure of those two Divine figures. Otherwise, the Nolan Capital might not have been able to retain the Destiny Tablet Fragment.
Having been struck by this blow, the Nobles quickly deflated, and the topic shifted back to the core of this discussion—the Destiny Tablet Fragment.
Currently, the focal point of the dispute was that some Nobles wanted to try activating the Destiny Tablet Fragment, using this Divine Artifact to shield the Royal Capital and buy some breathing space.
Another group of Nobles believed that the risks of activating the Destiny Tablet Fragment were too great, potentially attracting the scrutiny of the Ancient Evil God, which could lead them to face his siege, not protection.
Both sides had valid points, hence the endless debate, and even the King was unable to make a decision.
Spark, of course, had heard about this matter early on, but what concerned him more was that Lide placed great importance on the Destiny Tablet Fragment and had asked him to gather more information.
Although Lide had repeatedly slapped his face with his exaggerated leveling speed, the old man still held Lide in high esteem and paid close attention to any news about the Destiny Tablet Fragment.
After ascending to Legendary status, Lide had an idea.
But just as Spark was about to inquire about the disappearance of the Destiny Tablet fragments, a guard clad in solid armor rushed to the King’s side with a grave expression and whispered into his ear.
Moments later, the King’s face grew uglier, and he suddenly slammed his hand on the armrest, standing up.
"Silence!"
The previously noisy room fell deathly quiet at this roar, and all the nobles turned their heads towards him.
The King swept his gaze around, his face ashen as he said.
"Ten million Ancient Monsters have gathered a hundred miles outside the Royal Capital, and their target is the heart of the Royal Capital.
Furthermore, based on reports from scouts, there are traces of Divine presence among these Ancient Monsters, and their likely target is the Destiny Tablet fragments!"
Hiss~
This explosive news made all the nobles in the hall gasp in unison.
Ten million Ancient Monsters weren’t anything special, but the news of Divine beings following them made their scalps tingle,
especially now that two Divine had left, the situation was terrifying.
"All heed my command, immediately arrange for people to try to activate the Destiny Tablet fragments, and at the same time dispatch an army to prepare for battle!"
The King issued orders without wasting words, his face stern.
"Transcendent and Legendary, please make sure to stay at the Imperial Palace, it can’t be that when the Military Department sends forces to support the city walls, no one can be found."
This exaggerated news made everyone tense.
With a crisis looming, no one argued about whether or not to activate the Destiny Tablet fragments, and the nobles who had just been arguing immediately reached a consensus—attempt to activate the Destiny Tablet fragments.
The reason for the attempt was primarily because no one knew how to use the Destiny Tablet fragments.
Time flowed, and after five Sunshine Hours,
Boom~ Catapults hurled massive stones from behind the walls of the Royal Capital, crashing into the ground and shaking it, tearing the densely packed Ancient Monsters to pieces as if they were made of paper.
On the walls of the Nolan Capital, archers drew their bows and shot in unison, cutting down the Ancient Monsters that had reached the foot of the walls like wheat.
Although the towering walls kept the Ancient Monsters at bay, no one dared to take it lightly, and everyone was extremely nervous, because they could sense that deep within the ranks of the Ancient Monsters, a terrifying Divine Power spread unabated.
The entire world seemed to tremble under the Divine Power.
Numerous Legendary figures stood atop the wall, their expressions extremely solemn as they looked into the distance.
Even one of the Legendary figures felt his hands shaking uncontrollably after sensing that Divine Power, a pressure that reached deep into the soul that no one could escape.
Everyone could feel that there was an extremely terrifying Life within the Ancient Monsters, and that if it acted, it would be earth-shattering.
Even many Legendary figures had tragically prepared themselves to abandon the city.
A full-strength Divine being was something the Royal Capital did not have the power to confront.
They even began to dimly see the sight of this millennia-old capital being destroyed.
Just as everyone’s mood was at its most oppressive, several Legendary figures suddenly revealed a trace of astonishment.
For at that moment, a behemoth clad in Steel Armor had flown directly out from behind the ranks of the Ancient Monsters, and what was even more exaggerated was that the beast in Steel Armor was flying straight towards the area permeated with the Divine presence.

Such a powerful being, daring to confront the Dignity of the Divine?!

chapters.title: Chapter 484 - 485: Spark Finally Meets Lide, Shocked to the Point of Numbness
chapters.content:
Chapter 484: Chapter 485: Spark Finally Meets Lide, Shocked to the Point of Numbness
The steel behemoth that suddenly appeared above the Ancient Monsters caught everyone by surprise.
The Legendary and Transcendent warriors on the city walls all widened their eyes in disbelief.
"What kind of life is that behemoth? It dares to charge at an Ancient Evil God?"
"To withstand such terrifying Divine Power, it’s unbelievable..."
"Has the behemoth been charmed by the Evil God? Why else would it be rushing straight towards the opponent??"
Just as everyone was closely watching, seemingly aware of the steel behemoth’s provocation, amidst the uncountable Ancient Monsters blanketing the earth like locusts, an extreme terror erupted like a mountain collapsing.
The terrible Divine Power was like a gigantic beast towering thousands of feet into the sky, ready to devour the heavens!
In that moment, all light in the heavens and earth was devoured, and darkness became the main melody.
The oppressive force made the air as dense as mercury, everyone felt tingling scalps and tight chests, a tremendous fear struck them.
A God!!
This was a true God.
Without the slightest injury, it descended upon the world in full splendor!!
At this moment, the regular soldiers on the city walls were filled with fear, the strong arms that drew bows uncontrollably quivering.
Even the Transcendent and Legendary warriors, who were High-level combatants, felt that breath of air was extremely lethal and could devour them at any moment.
Divine Power surged mightily, directly covering the entire Royal Capital.
Tens of millions of people at this moment trembled and feared under that Divine Power, and the Imperial Palace at the center of the Royal Capital also sensed that irresistible force.
Suddenly, there was silence.
The King felt a chill down his spine, and his breathing unconsciously stopped.
Once the first wave of impact slightly dissipated, he abruptly stood up from the throne, quickly stepped over to the crowd around the round table in the hall, and furiously shoved aside the sweating Nobles, smacking the table loudly, roaring.
"Activate the Destiny Tablet fragment immediately!! The Ancient Evil God is about to strike!!"
"The Royal Capital’s defensive Magic Array was completely destroyed in the great battle three months ago! No one can counter the power of the Evil God!!"
His voice was filled with an indescribable urgency, obviously, the Divine Power, vast as a myriad of waves, made the King feel a fatal threat.
Without any further action, their only way out was destruction.
The Nobles present instantly turned pale.
Everyone knew that if they allowed the Ancient Evil God to break through, the entire city’s fate would be sealed, with no room for turnaround.
The Destiny Tablet fragment, a Divine Artifact ordained by the Sun Goddess as the only thing capable of countering an Ancient Invasion, now became their sole lifeline.
But what drove the King nearly mad was that even with his forceful orders, there was still no progress.
Because—no one could use the Destiny Tablet fragment.
The fragment of the Destiny Tablet on the black round table was embedded in the stone; one could touch the stone, but direct contact with the fragment itself would result in instantaneous absorption of all power, turning to dust and ash.
The terrifying scene was even more dreadful than a demon possession.
After more than ten Mages collapsed here, the Nobles all felt a chill.
"Your Majesty, the energy of the Destiny Tablet fragment is far too great; we simply can’t control it, let alone activate it. Anyone who directly touches the fragment will be annihilated..."
The King’s face turned very grim, he slammed the round table violently, roaring in fury.
"At any cost, we must activate the fragment!"
"We have no way out..."
He seemed to age a decade after speaking those words.
The weak have never had a choice...
The Nobles looked somber, none daring to speak.
The Mage in the black robe next to the throne took a deep breath, his eyes determined as he stepped towards the round table, speaking solemnly.
"Your Majesty, let me try."
The other Nobles were suddenly brightened upon hearing this; the black-robed Mage had reached Legendary status even before the Ancient Invasion, always a trusted confidant of the King.
It was said that he had reached Level 27; with such a figure taking action, there was definitely hope to activate the Destiny Tablet fragment.
The King’s expression changed again and again; this was his trusted general. If something happened to him, he would have no one left to ensure his safety.
But considering the urgency of the situation, he could only suppress the anxiety in his heart and nodded.
"Be careful."
The black-robed Mage nodded coolly and with all the Nobles watching, he extended his hand to gently touch the Destiny Tablet fragment.
The moment his hand touched the Destiny Tablet fragment, it quivered and suddenly fell still.
The black-robed Mage’s face brightened with joy, and his aura began to surge as if he had received a great enhancement.
This made the surrounding Nobles instantly express extreme joy.
The untouchable Destiny Tablet fragment was finally activated!
The King, upon seeing this, also revealed a smile, his eyes filled with irrepressible excitement.
But just as everyone thought the situation was turning around, it suddenly changed. The Legendary Mage who had just been exuding an expert’s demeanor suddenly began to convulse, and then—bang—exploded on the spot.
Like a burst balloon, a mist of blood rose, splattering the faces of the surrounding crowd.
The Nobles, just recently overjoyed, now had their smiles freeze on their faces.
The scene fell into a deathly silence.
That was a Legend.
Just like that... gone?
Everyone’s eyes filled with confusion and disbelief.
They had originally thought that even if the Legendary Mage under the crown couldn’t activate the Destiny Tablet Fragment, it wouldn’t pose too great a danger.
But reality brutally slapped them across the face, showing them what society really was.
The King’s complexion turned exceedingly ugly, as if he had eaten two hundred pounds of rat droppings.
Just like that... gone?
His Legendary companion of over twenty years, gone in the blink of an eye?
Unspeakable grief filled his heart, but it was of no avail.
And what was worse, if even a Legend couldn’t control the Destiny Tablet Fragment, what were they to do next?
What would they use to confront the Ancient Evil God?!
The King, resolute and weathered by many storms, couldn’t help but fall silent...
The hall sank into a bizarre atmosphere.
A wave of indescribable despair surged over everyone’s hearts.
They had found a Divine Artifact to counter the Ancient Invasion, yet they were unable to use it—could there be anything more despairing?
——
Atop the city walls.
Feeling provoked by the steel behemoth, the Ancient Evil God was seething with rage, having just released its Divine Power.
A gigantic shadow rose up from among the Ancient Monsters, occupying half the sky.
Divine Power grew more terrifying.
"مرگوکشتن"
Accompanied by an endless suppression, a spell of extreme evil echoed.
The sky filled with dark clouds, forming a massive vortex.
Ancient Monsters covered in tumors, dark and swollen, bellowed in unison towards the vortex.
Then, under the watchful eyes of the City Guards, a shadowy figure with back bristling with spikes, four-eyed face, and emitting an endless aura of decay, towered in the sky.
The Ancient Evil God appeared.
But the moment this Evil God materialized, it became blurred, until it was no longer clear to see.
The steel behemoth, having deliberately slowed down a bit, seemed to have found its prey after the birth of the Evil God.
Under the watchful eyes of all, it charged directly toward that dread-inspiring Evil God.
Beneath the surging Divine Power, the normally terrifying steel behemoth appeared exceptionally small, like a solitary leaf in waves capable of ripping apart heaven and earth, exuding a sense of futile resistance.
Inside, Lord Spark felt like he was on a roller coaster, originally shocked that the steel behemoth dared to face Divine Power head-on, and now surprised that it boldly charged in, courting death in the face of such terror.
A nameless despair filled his heart—in the face of such a fearsome Evil God, who could stand against it?
The surrounding Transcendents and Legends felt the same, no one believing the steel behemoth could survive, even anticipating a scene of it spurting blood on the spot.
In the focus of tens of thousands, as the steel behemoth approached the Ancient Evil God, a dazzling and brilliant Sword Qi suddenly rose from its back, visible for a hundred miles.
The Sword Qi slashed toward the sky-shrouding demonic might of the Ancient Evil God with a force that could obliterate the universe and slaughter all realms.
This one strike could cause the heavens to tilt!
Time and space seemed to freeze at that moment, and everyone felt as if time slowed down countless times, millions of residents in the Royal Capital looked up to the sky, catching a glimpse of that Sword Qi streak.
Even the Nobles in the Imperial Palace sensed something and abruptly turned to look out the window at that radiant sword trail.
And under everyone’s gaze, that splendorous Sword Qi, shining like fireworks across the world, spanned the entire sky as if to slay a god.
The Ancient Evil God, carrying boundless Divine Power, sensed the threat the moment the Sword Qi overpowered everything.
Its body burst out with surging Divine Power, dark energy gushing from its hazy figure as if floodgates had opened, a mass of corrupting Dark Power collided head-on with that Sword Qi.
That mass of power, capable of erasing a city of a hundred thousand people.
The ground within a thousand blades crumbled down ten blades deep because of the too-terrifying Divine Power, rumbling as it collapsed.
Tens of thousands of Ancient Monsters were crushed into mincemeat, exploding, blood and gore spread far and wide.
A needle against the wheat.
It seemed to be an ancient collision.
The soldiers inside the Royal Capital had even forgotten to breathe, staring fixedly at this astonishing scene.
Crack~
Moments later, the glow of the sword and the Power of Corruption collided directly.
Against all expectations, the overbearing and world-shattering Power of Corruption was, under that dazzling sword glow,
dissipated like ice under the sun.
A more accurate description would be that the sword glow, resplendent as the blazing sun, cut through the Dark Demon Tide released by the Ancient Evil God with an unbeatable posture.
The blurred shadow, upon witnessing this, was immediately engulfed in rage, utterly disbelieving that its most powerful strike had been shattered, and charged directly towards the sword glow.
Indeed, it sought to destroy the sword glow with its Divine Body, hardened by a hundred refinements.
But an even more astonishing spectacle unfolded.
After annihilating the strike of the Ancient Evil God, the sword glow showed not the slightest sign of weakening and, with an unstoppable burst, pierced right through the body of the Ancient Evil God.
Crack~
The entire heaven and earth seemed to crumble at that moment.
View the correct content at .
After passing through the blurred shadow of the Ancient Evil God, the sword glow remained undimmed, continuing its violent trajectory to the edge of sight. Wherever it passed, space shattered into a primordial state of chaos, taking a long, long time before slowly returning to normal.
Correct content is on )
And before the countless eyes of the Royal Capital, the Ancient Evil God, struck by the sword glow,
was cleaved in two.
The awe-inspiring Divine Power, vast as mountains and seas inverted in the sky, vanished without a trace.
Dead.
The Ancient Evil God, who led millions of ancient forces to attack the Royal Capital, appeared only briefly, its form barely discerned, before it was slain on the spot by a sword glow that appeared out of nowhere.
This unbelievable reversal left the warriors on the city walls breathless, each with eyes wide and mouths agape, unable to recover for a long time.
Their hearts were shaken beyond speech.
How could this be?!!
That was the Ancient Evil God!
It died just like that? And it was instantly killed in full view of everyone!
Who could have unleashed that sword shadow that even the Divine couldn’t withstand?
By the Goddess above, did You intervene personally to punish those Ancient Monsters??
A scene where a Goddess’s sword killed a Divine, a spectacle that could be described as world-shaking and unprecedented.
Even ordinary citizens who had just witnessed the scene knelt on the ground, as if worshiping their own faith.
"By the Goddess above, am I dreaming? Was that Evil God slain just like that??"
"One sword slaying the Divine! How is this possible?! I must be hallucinating..."
"Have we been saved? Is that the reinforcements summoned by His Majesty??"
Not only were the ordinary citizens discussing, but the expressions of the Transcendent and Legendary on the walls also completely lost control, with their inner shock no less than that of the ordinary warriors and citizens.
Lord Spark, witnessing this epic scene, also felt a sincere sense of wonder.
"This is what a transcendent being is, to know such a person would be a life without regrets!"
The unkempt old man’s eyes were filled with worship and reverence, longing in his heart for the entity who had unleashed the sword glow.
Such a character must be incredibly powerful!
After the Ancient Evil God was slain by a sword, the situation changed again.
Below, the Ancient Monsters, lacking the command of the Ancient Evil God, began to scatter.
The steel giant beast flew straight toward the body of the Evil God, now split into two halves, grabbing one half with each of its colossal limbs before turning around and flying towards the Royal Capital.
The City Guards on top of the wall changed color at this sight.
Although the sword shadow from the back of the giant beast had killed the Ancient Evil God, no one knew whether this mysterious being was friend or foe, thus, they were conflicted, feeling both admiration and caution.
But no one dared to raise their weapons against it; one sword had slain a Divine, what terrifying being could this be, and what right did they have to draw a blade against it??
Amidst the complex emotions of the crowd, whoosh~ the giant beast approached the city wall swiftly.
As it drew near, the soldiers could slowly make out what the armored giant beast looked like.
It was a behemoth with wings spanning 20 blades, wrapped in black armor with silver patterns intertwined, its Blade Wings sharp beyond compare, as if they could cleave mountains.
This steel giant beast was magnificent and mighty, its combat prowess beyond doubt.
But even more striking was the body of the Evil God that the giant beast held in its feet.
The Evil God, at least ten blades tall, its body split diagonally in two, with blood from its wounds falling like raindrops.
Although the Evil God was dead, the residual aura it emitted was still chilling.
This was a true Evil God, able to slaughter an entire city with one strike!
Transcendent beings beyond the peak of existence could tell at that point, the sword strike had not only severed the Ancient Evil God’s body, but had also shattered its soul, thus bringing about the slaying of a Divine Being in a single blow, an act truly incredible.
If it had only been the body that was slashed apart, the being would likely have restored itself in an instant.
As the behemoth drew closer, a sharp-eyed soldier spotted a suave and ethereal figure seated on its back, prompting quite the exclamations of surprise.
"Quick, look, there’s someone on the back of that giant beast!! That sword Qi that slew the Divine must have been released by him!"
"This, is this a Divine Being who has returned to its peak state? Truly awe-inspiring..."
"By the goddess above, this must be your envoy sent to save us..."
At this juncture, Lord Spark had not yet seen the person riding on the back of the beast, his emotions still running high, turned his head towards Princess Kadi beside him, and spoke with reverence in his expression.
"Your Highness the Princess, to slay a Divine with a single sword strike, just to behold such a person is our fortune, and if the King were to gain his protection, we would be free from worry."
Kadi nodded in wholehearted agreement.
"Lord Spark, you are right..."
But before she finished speaking, she noticed Lord Spark’s face shifting from anticipation and excitement to disbelief and shock.
It seemed as though he had seen something that could not possibly exist.
Filled with questions, Kadi followed his gaze, only to see the steel behemoth approaching the city wall, with the figure of an unearthly handsome man rising to his feet behind it, casually overlooking the ramparts.
His elegant demeanor made him seem like the bright moon in a dark night, incomparable to the luminescence of anyone else.
He’s way too good-looking...
Staring in amazement, Kadi continued to watch.
Bang~
The steel beast seemed under control as it headed straight for them.
When it got close to the wall, it tossed the Divine Body, now cut in two, onto the ramparts with a slight shake, rolling a few times before coming to a rest in front of them.
Then, the steel creature lightly flapped its wings and stood firmly on the wall’s parapet with its two feet.
By now, Kadi had keenly sensed that the breathtakingly handsome figure on the beast’s back was looking right at her...
Her heart fluttered, what could this mysterious being plan to do? Could it be... A bold idea crossed her mind, and her cheeks immediately flushed.
Moments later, the handsome figure levitated into the air, drifting toward her direction, causing the princess’s heart to race tenfold.
What happened next left her utterly astonished—the awe-inspiring figure approached and then landed right in front of Spark, saluted by placing his hand over his chest, and then addressed him with a form of address that made everyone’s scalp tingle.
"It’s been a long time, Teacher..."
Although the voice was not loud, it reverberated across the expanse of the city walls.
Teacher?? Upon hearing this title, Kadi felt as if struck by lightning, her body rigid, and her mind in a daze.
Lord Spark was actually, actually the mentor to this terrifying existence who had slain the Ancient Evil God??
The sheer contrast nearly shattered her psyche.
Lord Spark, the hidden depths you possess have pained me so... Had we known earlier of your disciple’s might, we need not have lived in such dread.
The warriors on the city walls also froze for a moment, then like cold water hitting boiling oil, they suddenly erupted into commotion.
"Did I hear that correctly?! That unfamiliar Divine Being actually called Lord Spark his teacher??"
"How, how is this possible?? Lord Spark just recently became Legendary, right??"
"He just performed the disciple’s salute to Lord Spark, that’s outrageous..."
At this moment, Lord Spark, looking at the man in front of him, Lide, was not excited but filled with disbelief and shock.
"You little scum from the Kachar family!! You’ve become a god??"
It seemed as though the unkempt old man had taken a fatal blow, staggering backward several steps with a desolate and infuriated expression.
Especially when he saw Kadi looking at both of them with an incredibly surprised expression, it made him feel an unbearable sense of shame and humiliation.
Because he remembered his firm belief today when breaking through to the Legendary level, that he would triumph over Lide...
Recalled how he had boasted in front of Kadi about his exceptional Talent, claiming it would take Lide several years of effort just to reach his level...
Thought back on the gap between himself, having only just become Legendary, and his student who had become a god...
"No, I don’t believe it, I don’t believe it,
With my extraordinary Talent, it only took me one year to break through to Legendary, you, how could you possibly have gone from Level 19 to a Divine Being?!"
"You must be deceiving me, right?"
"I’m the unparalleled genius of Green City, how could I possibly lose to you..."
"Wake up, you’re my disciple..."
"No, I must be hallucinating..."
"As someone with such outstanding Talent as I, it’s impossible to be surpassed by my own disciple, it just can’t be..."
Spark’s stuttering voice, coupled with his disheveled appearance, was rather humorous, and his expression of despondency even caused Lide to let out a wry smile.
This slovenly old man, it’s just unbelievable...

chapters.title: Chapter 485 - 486: Don’t Move, Fragments of the Destiny Tablet Cannot Be Touched by Outsiders!
chapters.content:
Chapter 485: Chapter 486: Don’t Move, Fragments of the Destiny Tablet Cannot Be Touched by Outsiders!
Lide had shouted "Teacher" quite a while ago, yet the people around were still in shock, their eyes brimming with disbelief.
To slay a Divine with a single sword strike—what kind of domineering and powerful figure could this be, and how could he be but a disciple of a Legend?
Moreover, this very Legend had only just achieved breakthrough, still merely Transcendent just a year ago...
It was too incredible to believe.
Princess Kadi, after being stunned for a long time, gradually gathered her wits and, glancing at Spark who muttered to himself, turned her gaze.
Suppressing the shock in her heart, she stepped forward two paces and stood half a step behind Spark, her eyes carrying immense curiosity as she stared at the figure before her, so handsome that her heart trembled.
"Lord Spark, could you introduce this Lord to us?"
Still dazed, Spark was brought back to reality by Princess Kadi’s reminder. He quickly looked around, and catching the incredulous expressions of the surrounding crowd out of the corner of his eye, his spirits, which had taken a hit, instantly soared.
Right, no matter how great this guy is, I’m still his teacher; even if he were a Creator God, he’d still have to show me respect.
Ha ha ha ha, I’m the one who cultivated someone who could slay a Divine God with a single sword strike!
I am the true genius here, after all, how else could I have taken such an exceptionally talented disciple under my wing?
After this change in thought, his downcast expression excitedly lifted.
Slightly raising his head, his expression was like that of a rooster who had won a fight: proud and slightly smug.
Clearing his throat, he feigned nonchalance as he spoke.
"Hehe, this is my direct disciple, the youngest and most talented Great Mage of the Empire—Lide Kachar.
Sorry for startling everyone just now. This is merely my most disappointing disciple, merely capable of killing Evil Gods; not much skill really..."
Hearing this, the surrounding Transcendents and Legends had a "FML" expression.
I mean, what the hell...
This damn guy, what do you mean ’not much skill,’ just able to slay Evil Gods?? Why don’t you go hack one down and let’s see it?
If having no skill means slaying Evil Gods, then having skill must be akin to Creation, right??
And if that’s considered ’no skill,’ what does that make us? Three-year-olds playing with pee and mud??
And you were just scared shitless a moment ago, who are you trying to impress now??
After internally cursing him out, they couldn’t disguise their envy and resentment.
Damn it, how does this bastard manage to train such a strong disciple?! How?? WHY??
Over a dozen Transcendents and a few Legends clenched their teeth in unison and angrily turned to look at their own disciples beside them with faces full of rage.
If you were any good, would we even be putting up with this??
Those disciples, sensing their teachers’ glares, immediately felt a chill down their spines, their faces the epitome of innocence—if we were that good, would we need your teaching?? They became prime examples of being caught in the crossfire while lying down...
With his bird’s nest-like hairdo, Spark, feeling the crowd’s gaze, perked up, lifting his chin pompously as if he wished to look down on people through his nostrils.
His smug demeanor completely replaced the defeated look he wore just moments before.
Upon seeing this, Lide’s mouth twitched fiercely; even after so long, this old guy hadn’t lost his shamelessly unique character, seemingly without any idea what ’saving face’ meant.
He even firmly believed that his own thick skin had been learned from Spark; it had nothing to do with him.
"So this is the Legendary Mage Lord Lide, who entered the realm of a Great Mage at the age of 25, no wonder he’s so powerful..."
"But didn’t they say before that Lord Spark’s disciple was only a Great Mage? How come he can now slay an Evil God with a single sword strike??"
"He’s so cool! If I were as handsome as Lord Lide, I could slay a god too!"
"By the Goddess above, if the one I loved had such a striking appearance, I’d be willing to live twenty years less..."
The voice of Spark resounded in the entire city wall area, heard by tens of thousands, and his shameless remark instantly sparked a fervent uproar.
Especially that the severed Divine Body of Castro still oozing blood before them added an overwhelmingly shocking aura to the scene.
Steel behemoths, the corpse of an Evil God, dimming lights, oppressive black clouds, a city wall scarred with weapon marks, and a supremely handsome Mage lord...
This tableau woven together created an unforgettable picture for the soldiers on the city wall.
"Gentlemen, good day."
Lide Kachar straightened up and nodded solemnly at the legendary and transcendent figures around him, without offering any particular gesture of respect.
In the Royal Capital, not counting his cheap teacher, who was worthy of his salute?
As the ruler of Dawn City, he had long since looked down upon the mortal plane.
To others, although Lide Kachar did not appear arrogant or disdainful of everyone, the captivating brilliance in his eyes still made everyone’s heart tense.
Although he was a disciple of Lord Spark, who would dare to disrespect Lide Kachar and treat him as a junior?
Treating powerful beings with sufficient respect was a rule that had been in place for millions of years; those who did not adhere to it mostly met the Death God.
At that moment, Princess Kadi felt a stir in her heart and stepped forward two paces again, performing an elegant curtsy towards Lide Kachar and spoke in a soft voice.
"Lord Lide, welcome. The Royal Capital shines brighter with your presence."
After finishing the pleasantries, she quickly added another line.
"I am Kadi Nolan, an honorary disciple of Teacher Spark."
Lide Kachar then showed interest in looking at the young lady dressed in luxurious court attire. Nolan? A member of the royal family?
Undoubtedly, the royal family’s appearance was never lacking, and although he was not clear on Kadi’s exact identity, her near-perfect beauty did please his eyes.
He nodded slightly.
"Hello."
After greeting her, he did not pay further attention to her, his gaze turning to Lord Spark, who stood beside him, looking proud as if he were eager to announce to the whole world that he was his disciple.
"Teacher, the Royal Capital is not safe, I have come to take you back to Green City."
What??
Upon hearing Lide’s words, the crowd that had just been very excited suddenly fell silent as if someone had choked them.
Such a powerful entity wasn’t here to defend the Royal Capital??
Their emotions fluctuated wildly between highs and lows.
Kadi’s face fell with disappointment. The handsome and talented mage wasn’t the reinforcement that Teacher Spark had called for??
Spark’s brows furrowed, and as he observed the changing looks of the people around him, his expression became stern.
"Kachar, let’s discuss this matter back in the city."
He neither agreed nor objected, and after speaking, he gestured towards the body of the Ancient Evil God in front of him.
"What do you plan to do with this body of the Evil God?"
Lide Kachar glanced at it. "Leave it be for now."
The worth of a divine body goes without saying, but he was in the Royal Capital to search for the shards of the Destiny Tablet and was not in the mood to care for this corpse.
Waving his hand and pulling out the Divine Status from the divine body, Lide Kachar nodded in satisfaction and continued,
"Teacher, I have come to search for the shards of the Destiny Tablet. Should I find them, I will gift this divine body to His Majesty the King."
If not, then the King could dream on.
Kadi was shocked to hear Lide Kachar’s unreserved words; she hadn’t expected that he would learn about the shards of the Destiny Tablet so quickly and with such a specific purpose.
Green City was miles away from the Royal Capital, now isolated by the Ancient Monsters, and the news channels of the past had long since failed. They even had difficulty communicating with cities a thousand miles from the Royal Capital.
She then turned and glanced at Spark, her eyebrows knotting slightly, clearly connecting Lide Kachar’s knowledge of this news with Spark.
Spark, however, did not pay much attention to these details, stating bluntly,
"Your Highness, please arrange for this body of the Evil God to be transported into the city and kept under guard."
"Kachar family, follow me to meet His Majesty the King..."
At this moment, Spark’s face was no longer carefree; his expression was very serious. Had it not been for his messy hair and wrinkled robe, he might truly have resembled a legendary strongman.
Lide Kachar nodded, not saying much more.
Moments later, Kadi had someone transport the divine body into the city, and Lide Kachar and Spark boarded a carriage heading straight for the Imperial Palace to see the King.
The legendary and transcendent figures on the city wall watched Lide Kachar leave, as if waking from a dream, and hurriedly descended from the wall to board their own carriages to the Imperial Palace.
Lide Kachar, such a majestic character, entered the Royal Capital and even went directly to see the King, the symbolism of which could not be overstated.
If mishandled, they might face a crisis no less severe than the Ancient Evil God’s invasion of the city.
How could a man capable of slaying gods with a single sword be considered ordinary?
Before long, news swiftly spread throughout the entire Royal Capital that the Evil God had been slain and that its body was being transported back to the inner city.
Accompanying this news was word that most people in the Royal Capital had heard of a genius mage named Lide Kachar, who had killed the invading Ancient Evil God with a single sword.
And this genius mage was none other than a disciple of the Magic Tutor under Lord Spark, of the Royal Magic Academy.
As to why a mage would use a sword to kill an Evil God, most people didn’t care—mages, after all, could do anything out of the ordinary, and who could be sure that the sword light wasn’t magic?
With the intentional propaganda of the soldiers, Lide had suddenly become a savior-like figure, vowing to defend the Glory of the Royal Capital to the death and to stand or fall with its residents.
For a moment, the previously subdued morale of the city surged, dispelling the gloom from the departure of the two Divines from the Royal Capital.
Lide was oblivious to these messy affairs, and even if he knew, he couldn’t be bothered to care—the Royal Capital was too far from Dawn City.
The journey of tens of thousands of kilometers would take even a Magic Language Bat flying day and night two days to cover; he had no means of transporting the city’s residents back to Dawn City.
If he couldn’t transport the residents away, then the value of the Royal Capital to him was significantly diminished.
With the formation of the Angel Alliance, future clashes would only become more intense, and the Royal Capital could be destroyed at any moment by catastrophe.
Thus, for a city thousands of miles away, he was powerless to help.
At most, he would take advantage of an opportunity and then leave; there was little need to invest too much effort for a city he couldn’t reach.
Inside the carriage, Spark looked at Lide sitting across from him, his expression returning to that of the smug old man he used to be.
"Kachar family boy, you’ve done well. You haven’t let down my teaching."
Having said this, he stroked his unkempt beard that had been neglected for too long, his face wearing a look of contentment.
Lide couldn’t help but smile wryly. Spark’s time spent teaching him magic probably didn’t even add up to three days; the old man’s skin was indeed thick.
"Is the main reason for your visit the fragment of the Destiny Tablet?"
"Yes, Teacher."
Lide nodded, and after a moment’s contemplation, he informed Spark about the current situation in Green City and some news from Dawn City.
This makeshift mentor had always been generous to him, trustworthy, and now that Dawn City was already in a semi-open state, there wasn’t as much need for secrecy as before.
What was more important was that his strength now allowed him to reveal Dawn City to the outside world.
When Spark finished listening to Lide’s narrative, his expression became extremely lively, even filled with disbelief and shock.
Clearly, the news he had just heard left the Legendary Mage unable to recover his senses for a long time.
"You mean to tell me that you built a city in the Far Mountain Range, and that city now has a population of several hundred thousand..."
"You’ve also formed allies with the Ocean God System, and currently, you have seven Sea Clan Gods under your command..."
"Green City has also fallen under your territory, and Duke O’Kelly has become the Deputy City Lord..."
"You’ve already grasped the mysteries of becoming divine several years ago, and now you are the Dawn God with over ten million believers..."
Although Lide spoke lightly, each piece of news was more explosive than the last, leaving the previously somewhat smug Spark completely stunned, his mind going blank.
It was as absurd and unbelievable as a man who rides a rusty Phoenix brand bicycle to buy groceries every day suddenly telling you that he’s actually the President of the United States, and the bicycle’s brakes are actually a nuclear button.
Had it been earlier, Spark would have scorned Lide’s words, thinking them mere boast.
But the scene of Lide slaying the divine just moments ago was still fresh, and the Evil God’s body was still seeping Divine Blood, which made these absurd statements considerably persuasive.
Power gives the right to speak.
Clearly, Lide now had sufficient right to speak.
"That’s right, so this time I’ve come to take you back with me; Green City is safer.
After the Angel Alliance is established, the wars of the future will be ten to a hundred times more dangerous than now; the Nolan Capital is not the core of the Glory Main Plane, and it will be difficult for the Angel Alliance to protect it.
Once targeted by the Ancient Monsters, it might be besieged by dozens of Evil Gods.
You can imagine that scenario without me needing to describe it further..."
Spark snapped back from the shock, curling his lips slightly.
"Your main target is the Destiny Tablet fragments, picking me up is just incidental..."
Lide smiled slightly and did not argue.
"The Destiny Tablet fragments are of significant importance, not something the Nolan Capital can safeguard.
Once the Angel Alliance and the Ancient Monsters sense the presence of the Destiny Tablet fragments, the very existence of the capital is questionable."
The Nolan Capital has no Divine beings, what can it use to protect the Destiny Tablet fragments? A child with gold wandering through the marketplace often ends with no good outcome.
Spark fell silent.
The oracle of the Sun Goddess stated that the Destiny Tablet fragments are the only power to counter the Ancient Invasion. The nobles of the capital, naturally, would not want to miss out, but Lide’s words left him without the strength to refute.
Possessing them doesn’t mean they belong to them.
The most helpless part for the capital is that they lack the ability to protect the Destiny Tablet fragments.
Moreover, they have tried countless times before, and no one could control this Creation God Artifact. So, for the Nolan Capital, although the Destiny Tablet fragments are invaluable and of extraordinary significance, they are ultimately troubling.
Keeping them will bring mighty enemies seeking to snatch them away, and they are also unable to use them, but giving up would be like sending their own future fate to ruin.
A difficult choice.
"You need to discuss this with the King; the Destiny Tablet fragment is inside the Imperial Palace."
After saying this, Spark gave Lide a deep look.
"But regardless, I hope you refrain from initiating slaughter within the capital... Even if you must kill, please don’t destroy this city."
In Spark’s eyes, someone capable of unleashing that sword strike must have already achieved an extremely high level of power, and once they resort to forceful snatching, no one would be able to stop them.
But the Nolan Capital holds significant meaning for him, and he does not wish to see this main city of humanity destroyed at Lide’s hands.
Lide nodded agreeably.
"I only want the Destiny Tablet fragments, trust me, His Majesty our King, will agree..."
Hearing this, Spark’s eyelid twitched. Dare the King disagree?? What King? Wouldn’t a slash from that sword ensure death?
After some thought, Spark asked with a faintly peculiar expression.
"Kachar, what level are you at now?"
He hadn’t asked before because the shock was too great, but now that he had braced himself, he dared to inquire.
Lide chuckled.
"Level 29."
Level 29?
Spark was startled, not because the level wasn’t high, but because it shouldn’t be possible. To instantly kill an Evil God one would have to be at least Level 31.
"How can Level 29 slay a god with one sword?"
Looking at the thick confusion on Spark’s face, Lide spoke casually.
"That sword wasn’t wielded by me."
"Not you? Then who?" Spark’s eyes widened.
"Just a subordinate, rather unremarkable."
"A subordinate? What level?"
"Level 36 with Medium Divine Power, it was she who struck that blow."
Upon hearing this, the corner of Spark’s mouth twitched violently, and he slapped himself hard before despondently turning his gaze out the window.
I’m a fool, a real fool, why did I bother asking him???
Level 36, Medium Divine Power, merely a subordinate?? Are these even human words???
Unremarkable... Oh, how I wish I were that ’unremarkable’!!!
The Creator God is unfair!!

chapters.title: Chapter 486 - 487: Don’t move, outsiders can’t touch the Destiny Tablet fragments!
chapters.content:
Chapter 486: Chapter 487: Don’t move, outsiders can’t touch the Destiny Tablet fragments!
Lord Spark was distressed and no longer wished to speak to Lide. Alone, he picked at his fingernails while staring out the window, his face wearing an expression of utter despair.
How worthless the mortal world is...
Seeing the old man’s melancholic silence, Lide couldn’t be bothered to speak more, his mind preoccupied with planning their next move.
Once Frey sensed no other divine presences within the city, Lide’s worries had dissipated.
The fragments of the Destiny Tablet couldn’t escape his grasp.
Using the Power of Destiny within him, he had sensed the location of the Destiny Tablet fragments clearly as soon as he had entered the Royal Capital—even if King Nolan had hidden them, it would be futile.
He hoped the king would see the situation clearly; otherwise, he would have to forcibly take the Destiny Tablet fragments and, with tears, plunder the royal family.
After so many years of accumulation, he believed the Nolan Royal Family must possess quite a few valuable items...
The carriage wheels squeaked over the cobblestones, and pedestrians on the streets, upon seeing the mark on the carriage, immediately stepped back with fear, not daring to approach it.
This was a Mage’s carriage; any offense to the occupant could result in facing Death from a casual spell—more frightening than even the Nobles.
The carriage wasn’t moving quickly and only stopped in front of the grand gates of the Imperial Palace about two Sunshine Hours later.
By then, the Nobles of the Royal Capital had all been summoned by the king to the palace hall for a meeting, just half a Sunshine Hour after Lide’s arrival.
The carriage came to a halt, and Spark’s look was still slightly resentful, his expression stubbornly pouting like a child refusing to concede defeat.
I haven’t lost to you; I just haven’t exerted my strength yet... hmph.
After a long while, Spark slowly exhaled a deep breath and said softly, "Kachar, after such a long time, those hypocritical Nobles should have reached a conclusion..."
He had deliberately slowed the carriage to give the Nobles time to discuss how to deal with Lide and establish a united front, to prevent any foolhardy individuals from aggravating Lide and provoking him to flatten the palace with a single sword strike.
After all, Lide had explicitly demanded the fragments of the Destiny Tablet.
It was conceivable that the Nobles might not willingly hand over the Destiny Tablet fragments since it was a Divine Artifact tied to the fate of the Royal Capital.
But now, force superseded all—in the face of absolute power, rules and plots were useless.
Even if some Nobles were foolish, two Sunshine Hours of discussion should have made them aware of their own limitations.
This was Spark’s plan.
Lide felt somewhat moved by these words. Despite the old man’s shabby appearance, barely better than a street beggar with the only advantage being his ability to afford the red-light district, his cunning worldly wisdom was indeed significant.
Their carriage was slow, but the closer it got to the Imperial Palace, the more psychological pressure it exerted on the inhabitants.
The Nobles were more likely to reach the consensus he desired.
Of course, he had a better method—letting Frey barge in and eliminate anyone they wanted, but what could they not obtain?
However, Spark hoped it wouldn’t be too much to ask to try not to engage in a massive slaughter while he could still control the situation; it wouldn’t do to defy this humble request from his makeshift teacher.
They stepped down from the carriage; the Nolan Palace came into view.
The first thing Lide noticed were the towering, solid griffin sculptures standing at either side of the palace gates, each one a dozen blades tall, looking like small mountains.
The Griffin was always the representative squadron of the Nolan Empire’s Air Force; from the founding of the empire, the Griffin Corps had made indelible contributions.
Lide glanced at them and quickly lost interest, continuing to examine other structures in the palace.
Although it was called an Imperial Palace, it felt more like a massive fortress to him, with solid walls, towering spires, and even large siege crossbows mounted within the hidden fortifications on the walls.
Lide looked a few more times and then lost interest; if he had just arrived in Glory, such architecture might have made some impact.
But now, compared to Dawn City, this city was far less spectacular and held little appeal.
"Respected Lord Lide, my father awaits you in the main hall..."
The palace gates had already been flung wide open, and Princess Kadi, with grace and a smiling face, came forward to greet Lide.
Behind the princess stood rows of over a hundred maids, all well-mannered and beautiful, clearly arranged specially to welcome Lide.
Lide glanced at them and was greatly intrigued.
After so long, someone finally understood his preferences. Were they attempting to sway him with beauty? It was not an easy feat.
"Teacher, after you..."
Lide didn’t rush in; instead, he gave Lord Spark the honor of going first.
Spark hesitated for a moment, glancing around him subconsciously.
When he noticed the shock in the eyes of the surrounding crowd, his previously listless expression instantly perked up. He held his head high, huffed with feigned arrogance, and strutted forward with his hands behind his back.
Lide couldn’t help but smirk; this unkempt old man was so easily placated...
He turned his head slightly towards Kadi and nodded courteously, "Thank you for the effort."
He then followed behind Spark into the Imperial Palace.
It was clear that the King had given prior instructions; although there were many curious about him along the way, no one dared to show any disrespect. Even guards standing a hundred steps away had to clutch their chests and bow deeply, the scene reaching a pinnacle of decorum that even the most critical of onlookers could find no fault with.
Lide nodded in approval inwardly, acknowledging that this King was no simple figure.
After entering the Imperial Palace, Lide took a few extra glances at the surrounding architecture.
One had to admit that although the lower-class citizens of this world lived lives as lowly as mud, the high-level nobility indeed had a deeply ingrained culture.
Inside the Imperial Palace, whether it be sculptures and paintings or various ingenious architectural layouts, they could not have been accomplished without significant cultural foundations.
After a short journey, Princess Kadi led Lide and Spark to the main hall where the King held his councils.
Stepping into the grand hall, Lide’s gaze slightly hardened.
At that moment, he saw a luxurious hallway carpeted in red, with hundreds of young girls standing to the side of the carpet holding flowers to welcome him.
Those high-level nobles stood behind the flower-holding girls, their gazes filled with a mixture of vigilance, admiration, and surprise as they watched him.
At this point, Spark was even prouder, holding his head high, his spiky hair not detracting from his unabashed stride onto the red carpet.
Lide smiled softly and also stepped forward.
With his strikingly handsome features and formidable strength, Lide’s appearance immediately caught the eyes of the maids, the noble ladies, and the noble girls hiding behind the crowd.
To sleep with such a man for just one night, how wonderful that would be... this was the heart’s cry of the unsatisfied noblewomen.
He’s so handsome, if only my husband could be so charming, I’d marry him even if it costs all my dowry... this was the desire of the young girls.
Oh Sun Goddess, please grant us such a handsome and powerful man to lead us out of our misery... this was the dream of the maids.
And the nearby nobles were quietly discussing among themselves.
"Is this the disciple of Lord Spark? He really is too handsome. My daughter is fifteen this year, already of marriageable age, I wonder if it’s possible to send her to Lord Lide’s manor to become a concubine..."
A pudgy noblewoman’s eyes sparkled as if she herself longed to take her daughter’s place.
"I actually can’t sense Lord Lide’s aura at all!! Sun Goddess above, I am a Legend, yet what level has this being reached??"
A mage in a white robe spoke, his face a mix of envy and bitterness.
"The aura that the Ancient Evil God emitted just now was unmistakably divine, and now it has been slain by a single sword slash, indicating that Lord Lide possesses power unimaginable to us all.
If we could use a fragment of the Destiny Tablet to keep him in the Capital, we wouldn’t have to live in fear every day..."
Under the gaze of the crowd, guided by Kadi, Lide calmly walked to the endpoint of the red carpet before the throne.
At that moment, the King who should have been sitting on the throne had already stood next to the red carpet, leaving the throne empty as if it was reserved for him, as if Lide was the king about to be crowned.
