At that time, Spark’s mouth was almost twisted in glee, his head held so high that he seemed to be looking down on everyone through his nostrils.
"My father, this is our most honorable guest, Lord Lide..."
Princess Kadi respectfully bowed to the crowned King.
"You’ve done well, my child, you may step down now."
After briefly praising Kadi, the King’s gaze turned to the calmly standing, elegantly poised Lide.
Even with his experience, he couldn’t help but inwardly remark on Lide’s handsomeness...
Mulling over it for a moment, the King, under the stunned watch of everyone, stepped forward, then clutching his chest, bowed deeply with a respectful expression.
"Welcome your arrival, Lord Lide, the Capital shines brighter for it."
A stir went through the crowd, as the King’s actions sent shockwaves through the assembly.
The King represents the dignity of a nation, the highest honor, and is the spiritual pillar for everyone.
But at this moment, this figure symbolizing the face of the Nolan Empire was paying respects to a young man.
What an astonishing scene this was.
While aware of Lide’s heavenly abilities, the scene still left many nobles feeling discontented internally.
But as their fervor cooled, they began to think that the King’s actions might not be inappropriate after all.
The Nolan Empire was no longer the same empire that had been at its zenith before the ancient descent.
In the face of the ancient descent, without top-tier combat capabilities, the Nolan Empire had no right to stand proud before such a terrifying being capable of slaying gods.
Strength was the best credential.
Seeing this, Lide smiled slightly. Far from looking down on the bowing King, he actually appreciated it.
Outsiders only saw the King’s humility, but as the ruler of a nation, bowing his head for the sake of his land and his people behind him wasn’t embarrassing.
Not everyone can easily set aside their seemingly glorious but ultimately empty aura of superiority.
"Good day, Your Majesty."
Lide peacefully accepted a bow from the king, then added a phrase,
"May the Dawn shine upon you."
The king straightened up, his face subtly changing upon hearing these words.
Due to the barriers set by the Ancient Monster, Green City and Nolan Capital had lost most of their communication channels. The capital could not effectively manage Green City; hence, the king had not paid much attention to the news from Green City.
However, when the news of Lide slaying the Divine with a single sword stroke arrived, the king immediately ordered the reorganization of intelligence on Green City.
After all, Green City had been under the rule of the Nolan Empire for a thousand years, and many highly valuable pieces of intelligence had been sent back through special channels by the sleeper agents stationed there.
Combining this with Lide’s formidable combat power, the king had many speculations about Lide’s identity, one of which was scarcely hidden by Lide himself—his alias as the God of Dawn was already becoming apparent...
"Thank you for your blessing, Lord God of Dawn, may your glory shine across the Main Plane."
This statement by the king gave the high-level nobles food for thought, a gleam flashing in their eyes, while the ordinary nobles looked perplexed, unable to grasp the meaning.
What god was the God of Dawn? They had never heard of such a deity...
Spark’s eyelids twitched vigorously as something crossed his mind, but he stood aside like a statue, not speaking.
This sloppy old man sometimes exhibited a full-blown adolescent fantasy; at other times, he was incredibly sharp.
Lide looked meaningfully at the king, neither admitting nor denying, ignoring the conversation and directly stating his purpose as he entered the main hall.
"Your Majesty, I have come to the Royal Capital for the fragment of the Destiny Tablet."
Are we diving into the main topic already?
The king quickly composed himself, realizing the most difficult part was approaching, and immediately responded solemnly,
"The fragment of the Destiny Tablet is indeed in our possession, but it was obtained from a desperate place after immense difficulties and heavy costs. It is very important to us, Lord God of Dawn."
Lide smiled. Bargaining with me? You seem to have forgotten something...
"This is the sole purpose of my visit."
As soon as those words fell, without waiting for the king to respond, the overwhelming Divine Power of the Dawn Main God erupted like the collapse of a colossal mountain, imposing like the collapse of the heavens and the earth.
Lide’s slightly frail figure appeared like an ancient colossal beast capable of devouring the sky and earth, smashing through the void with terrifying and chilling dignity.
The entirety of the hall seemed to be under the cold gaze of the beast’s eyes, which could be compared to the sun and the moon, ready to unleash a deadly attack at any sign of unrest.
The sense of having the grim reaper’s scythe pressed against their throats made the surrounding nobles’ legs tremble unnaturally.
Fear consumed everyone.
The weak never had a choice.
Lide’s deep eyes watched the king, not uttering another word, yet almost driving him to collapse.
Facing the pressure of a Divine, that was an exaggerated stress; if not for the numerous precious items on him, just this Divine Power could have made even the transcendental king collapse to the ground.
A Divine was no longer a mortal; they were beings beyond the rules of this world, possessing endless lifespans.
Though transcendental beings might control a city and be considered rulers in their own right, they were but slightly stronger ants before a Divine.
Looking down upon the mortal realm.
The king instantly grasped the meaning in Lide’s eyes, his face full of bitter struggles. Yet, facing that crushing Divine Power, no matter how unwilling his heart was, he had to bow down.
When Lide struck down the Ancient Evil God with a single sword stroke, the situation was already set; he merely wanted to secure more benefits for the Royal Capital, but now, it seemed that endeavor had failed...
"Yes, Your Excellence, I will immediately have someone bring out the fragment of the Destiny Tablet..."
Upon hearing this, Lide slowly retracted his overwhelming Divine Power, returning to his plain mortal state.
Yet, the nobles inside the room were drenched in cold sweat, looking at Lide with not a hint of doubt or disrespect, even not daring to hold any slander in their hearts.
Though the scene of Lide slaying the Ancient Evil God was earth-shattering, many inside the room had not witnessed it due to the distance, leading to some inherent doubts.
But now, having directly faced that irresistible Divine Power, they immediately recognized the immense power of the person before them.
They became even more well-behaved than schoolchildren scolded by a teacher.
Moments later, over a dozen guards brought in a round table into the hall, on which was the fragment of the Destiny Tablet embedded in a stone.
Lide’s expression changed, his eyes revealing a trace of longing.
He could feel a powerful attraction coming from the fragment of the Destiny Tablet, like a girl in seductive attire swinging her hips from side to side, constantly enticing him to draw his sword...
The surrounding nobles had different expressions upon seeing the fragment of the Destiny Tablet—some clenched their teeth in resentment, some were filled with desire, some were disdainful, and others yearned for it.
Those with resentment in their eyes were mostly relatives and friends of those who had perished after coming into contact with the Destiny Tablet.
Most of those with yearning and desire were motivated by the prophesy of the Sun Goddess, wanting to gain the power of the Destiny Tablet to become savior-like figures.
"Lord God of Dawn, the fragment of the Destiny Tablet has been brought forth for you."
King Nolan looked at the Destiny Tablet fragment with a complex expression. It was just two Sunshine Hours ago that the Legendary, who had followed him for decades, was killed by this fragment, and he was powerless to stop it.
The sense of defeat was indescribable.
Lide glanced at King Nolan, who showed no reluctance, with a subtle expression.
The degree of King Nolan’s compliance greatly exceeded his expectation; he could even sense that King Nolan had absolutely no intention of resistance, which was a major disappointment to him.
This took away his excuse to rob the Imperial Palace. Couldn’t they be a little more ambitious and conspire to slay a god?
If they killed me, wouldn’t they not have to hand over the Destiny Tablet fragment? Why do I always encounter these time-savvy people, aren’t there a few impulsive villains?
After grumbling darkly, Lide, feeling the loss of a national treasury, approached and scrutinized the Destiny Tablet fragment.
This piece of the Destiny Tablet was slightly different from the one obtained in the Lost Sea—the aura of destiny it emitted was stronger, and it was also larger by a third.
Lide observed very carefully and did not act rashly. The nobles nearby, seeing that he made no move for a long time, began to discuss among themselves, widening their eyes.
"Lord Lide seems uncertain about the Destiny Tablet fragment..."
"Hehe, this is a Creation God Artifact! It’s not so easily controlled by anyone."
"Alas, the origins of the Destiny Tablet fragment are too significant. If it were easy to decipher, we wouldn’t have needed to sacrifice so many people."
"Indeed, even the Legendary, who followed His Majesty for decades, couldn’t last two breaths, let alone Lord Lide who is a god slayer—this must be tough..."
"They might have to give up after all, since this is a Creation God Artifact..."
Hearing the surrounding discussions, Spark, who was nearby, frowned with a hint of worry in his eyes.
He had seen for himself the potency of the Destiny Tablet fragment; several Transcendents had died under his watchful eyes from merely touching the fragment.
He had also thought about trying to touch it but sensed a fatal threat; had he really been so foolish, he might have met Death himself by now.
Princess Kadi approached Spark, her face tense with concern.
"Lord Spark, is Lord Lide sure about this? Should we ask him to delay his attempt? After all, this is a Creation God Artifact, I’m worried..."
Spark’s brow furrowed more deeply. He knew the capabilities of Lide, who indeed was powerful, but still at level 29; the true superior existence was the Medium Divine Power God hiding behind him.
Just then, Lide seemed to have finished observing and, under everyone’s gaze, reached directly for the Destiny Tablet fragment.
Seeing this, Spark’s scalp tingled and he shouted loudly.
"Don’t touch it, the Destiny Tablet fragment cannot be touched by outsiders! You..."
He was cut off halfway as Spark’s expression froze. Lide had already casually removed the Destiny Tablet fragment embedded in the stone and was now flippantly playing with it in his hand, to everyone’s astonishment.
"Teacher, is this what you meant by untouchable?" Lide looked at Spark with a smile, casually waving the Destiny Tablet fragment behind him.
The disheveled old man felt his newly risen pride crushed yet again.
Spark looked utterly devastated, wishing he could slap himself twice. Damn it, what was I thinking, what can’t this bastard do?!
The surrounding nobles stared at Lide, who played with the touch-and-die Destiny Tablet fragment as if it were a toy, each expression more spectacular than the last.
That was a Destiny Tablet fragment, not some random trash!
Previously, dozens had touched the fragment only to explode, and now Lide was nonchalantly playing with it.
This immense contradiction nearly drove them mad.
"To actually play with it in his hand, this is too exaggerated..."
"This is a Creation God Artifact; tamed just like that?"
"Why do I feel like all those who touched the Destiny Tablet fragment before died in vain..."
The bewildered Spark had a sudden flash of inspiration amidst the chaos, immediately excited, then he jumped out and pointed at Lide, shouting loudly.
"Hahaha, Kachar, I’ve figured out your true identity!"
Lide looked at the excited Spark with some surprise. Had this guy figured out he was a Bloodline? That shouldn’t be; he had hidden it well.
)
But Spark’s next words made Lide’s mouth twitch harshly.
"There is only one person in this world who can touch a Creation God Artifact, and that is the Creator God! You must be the reincarnation of the Creator God!"
"Hahaha, I, the unparalleled genius of Green City, never thought I’d be defeated by the Creator God in the end. A worthy opponent indeed; I’m not unjustly defeated this time."
"How can we mere mortals compare our talents with the Creator God? Thus, I remain the true genius!"
Lide was about to mock Spark, but instead he found the surrounding nobles wearing enlightened expressions, and even a few Transcendents revealed an ’it all makes sense now’ look...
Lide’s eyes widened in bewilderment.
What the hell? People believe this crap? Are people this easy to fool nowadays??
Saying I’m the Creator God and no one argues? Isn’t anyone using their basic intelligence??

chapters.title: Chapter 487 - 488: Your Subordinate Frey Blocks the Master of Dawn (8200 words)
chapters.content:
Chapter 487: Chapter 488: Your Subordinate Frey Blocks the Master of Dawn (8200 words)
"Under the Crown of the Dawn God, Your Glory is enough to make the sun pale in comparison! May I inquire how You came to control a shard of the Destiny Tablet?"
The King interrupted the discussions of the surrounding crowd and took the initiative to ask Lide.
The reincarnation of the Creator God was certainly a fabrication, but Lide’s ability to control a shard of the Destiny Tablet truly surprised him.
His already high appraisal of Lide in his heart rose significantly.
Annoyed, Lide shot a look at Spark, who wore an expression as if he had already seen through the truth of the matter, before turning his head to look at the increasingly respectful King and spoke indifferently.
"As long as one can bear the Power of Destiny, they can control a shard of the Destiny Tablet..."
"And how can one bear the Power of Destiny?" The King widened his eyes, filled with anticipation as he asked.
Lide’s gaze shifted subtly, subconsciously remembering the Curse of Destiny, but at this moment, he realized that the Spell Katherine had taught him seemed to be restricted and could no longer be taught to others.
He shook his head at that moment.
"I bore the Power of Destiny with the help of an elder possessing infinite might, and I can’t assist you.
Your Majesty, without enough power, do not attempt it.
The Power of Destiny is the origin power of Glory, and even Divine beings with Powerful Divine Power struggle to extricate themselves after coming into contact with it, most likely to be lost in the River of Destiny, perpetually sinking into it..."
Hearing this, the King was both amazed and dismayed—amazed at the profound background of Lide and dismayed that he might not be able to master this formidable power.
The surrounding crowd fell silent upon hearing this, their gazes at Lide carrying a mixture of complex meanings.
Spark quieted down at this point, but his face still wore the expression of someone who had seen through everything.
After a long while, the King took a deep breath and spoke again.
"Under the Crown of the Dawn God, may we earnestly request Your protection over the Royal Capital? We are willing to spread Your faith so that every resident is enveloped in Your radiance."
The King’s words were pleasant, but the essence of his statement was—a transaction, protect me, and I’ll help You disseminate faith.
As the sovereign of a nation, the information he controlled was naturally incomparable to ordinary people; he knew how valuable Believers were to the Divine.
Lide raised an eyebrow, interestedly sizing up the King, appreciating the fellow’s understanding of what he needed.
Tens of millions of people, he was naturally very interested, but this population had already been inundated with various Sects, who knew how often they’d been preached to—a Royal Capital of an empire was naturally valued much more by each Sect than Green City could be.
To find even a casual Believer among these tens of millions would take a significant amount of time, so if it was just preaching, given the distance from Dawn City to the Royal Capital, the effects would likely be limited.
Correct content is on .
So, the King’s condition didn’t hold much attraction for him.
But with that being mentioned, the population of tens of millions seemed irresistible.
Could there be a way to achieve the best of both worlds?
Thinking it over, Lide suddenly realized he had fallen into a cognitive blind spot, overlooking an important point.
Sending Magic Language Bats to transfer the people of the Royal Capital was indeed not feasible, but there were other methods.
For example—Planes.
If the Ocean God System could find the Water Element Plane to transfer the Sea Clan there, could he find a Plane that could accommodate humans?
The power he now possessed defied conventional logic, he had the entire Divine System swearing allegiance to him, finding a Plane shouldn’t be too difficult.
In that case, he could simply transfer the entire population.
As long as it was near Dawn City, he could dispatch the administrative officers from City Hall, confident that it wouldn’t take long for the Dawn Sect to become the mainstream faith of the Royal Capital.
With these thoughts, Lide’s interest in the Royal Capital surged manifold.
Population is the cornerstone of a force; the larger the population, the greater the probability of producing strong beings.
Although the Dawn Divine System had not yet cultivated a bona fide Divine being, they inevitably would in the future, and by preemptively amassing a population, it would be like paving the way for his subordinates’ Divine Enthronement.
This matter was entirely worth pursuing.
If I don’t engulf the Royal Capital, I’ll have to face a strong potential competitor—the Angel Alliance.
Although the Angel Alliance was recently established, once it gets on track, it will inevitably attract a large population, and sustaining many Gods is no easy feat.
If I wait until then, the Royal Capital’s juicy piece might not be available to me.
After pondering for a moment, Lide spoke slowly.
"Your Majesty, I have the ability to ensure the safety of the Royal Capital, but you are too far from Green City.
My Divine Country is already anchored in the Southern Province; I cannot extend my protection across thousands of miles."
Upon hearing this, the King couldn’t help but show a look of disappointment, but Lide’s next words gave him some hope.
"However, just because I cannot come to the Royal Capital does not mean you cannot go to the Southern Province..."
"Please enlighten us, Your Eminence," the King quickly inquired.
Lide smiled and did not directly reveal his thoughts but mentioned another matter.
"Have you ever heard of the Ocean God System?"
The Ocean God System?
The surrounding Nobles were stunned. As the superiors of the Royal Capital, they were of course not ignorant, but what puzzled them was the meaning behind Lide’s words.
"We have indeed heard of it, but what does this have to do with the Ocean God System?"
Lide continued with an indifferent expression.
"Of course, there is a connection. Half a month ago, in order to seek my protection, seven Sea Clan Gods found a suitably habitable Water Element Plane for the Sea Clan and relocated them there.
Now, the spatial coordinates for those Water Element Planes have been anchored in the Southern Province...
All seven Gods of the Ocean God System are currently under my jurisdiction."
These words shocked everyone in the hall.
In order to seek Lide’s help, the Ocean God System was willing to leave the sea and relocate the Sea Clan to another Plane for protection, even with seven Gods of their own...
This explosive news set off a tumultuous wave in the hearts of the Nobles and the King present.
If this news was true, just how powerful was this disciple of Spark before their eyes?!
Could he be a Divine being with Powerful Divine Power, or even one step further??
Next to him, Spark, who had just managed to calm his emotions, now took a sharp breath, feeling his chest tight and head spinning as he watched Lide casually disclose this earth-shaking news.
How could it be? An entire Divine System seeking protection from him??
And even abandoning their life-sustaining ocean at that!!
I...
This scruffy, disheveled old man despondently realized that aside from describing Lide with the reincarnation of the Creator God, he could no longer find any other words...
Otherwise, how could a mere mortal reach level 29 Legendary status in just a few years?!
And to also have subordinates with level 36 Medium Divine Power, even attracting an entire God System with seven Gods to take refuge under him!!
Such a dreamlike scenario practically blinded his "dog eyes."
I’m foolish, truly foolish; I knew this rascal was no ordinary person, so why did I even compete with him?
Feeling like he had wasted decades of his life like a dog, Spark looked at Lide with a face full of regret and indignation, as if all the money he’d saved over ten years in red packets had been snatched away by his mother...
Princess Kadi was also staggered by the news, and it took her a long time to recover. Her beautiful eyes shone with an intense, almost fanatical admiration that she herself did not fully perceive.
"Lide Your Eminence, you mean to say that—if we want to seek your protection, we must do as the Ocean God System did, use the Plane to relocate the entire Royal Capital, then proceed to the Southern Province..."
Lide nodded in approval.
"Of course, despite its solid walls and strong army, the Nolan Capital is nothing but a lamb awaiting slaughter in the face of an Ancient Evil God.
I believe you also know that the Angel Alliance has been formed, and soon Glory will be entering a grand-scale Battle of the Gods.
This is a battle even more terrifying than the twilight of the gods, with the losers facing nothing but annihilation."
His gaze swept across the room, his voice increasing in volume.
"The Nolan Capital is situated slightly below the main location in the Glory Main Plane, not a central area, lacking any significant strategic importance.
Once targeted by the Ancient Evil God, it’s highly probable that the Angel Alliance will not send Divine protection, more likely they will disregard the city altogether.
Thus, the fate of the Nolan Capital has already been sealed, and what you must do now is break free from that fate..."
As for how to break free from fate, that obviously means coming back to Dawn City with me.
He didn’t finish his statement, but the clever ones understood the implication in Lide’s words.
The hall fell into a heavy silence.
The nobles had varying thoughts.
Fools don’t deserve to participate in a meeting of such importance, one that involves the life and death of the entire Royal Capital, so most had to admit there was reason in Lide’s words.
If things continued as they were without any change, his prophecy was very likely to come true.
In a divine war of survival, the destruction of a human city is of no importance.
The King’s complexion changed again and again before he finally sighed in reluctance.
"There are millions of people within the capital, the Divines will not abandon us..."
The Capital’s population is vast, and the number of Divines worshipped even more so, with at least a hundred Divines having churches within the capital.
Humans are the Glory Main Plane’s most populous intelligent race, and consequently, human Divines far outnumber those of other races.
The biggest issue lies in the overabundance of human Divines, whose birth led to factions such as benevolent, neutral, evil, and so on; there isn’t a single Sect that dominates alone.
So, just like the Nolan Capital, worship within the Glory Main Plane is mostly divided among dozens or hundreds of Sects.
Therefore, the King couldn’t believe that these Divines would forsake the millions in the Capital like a piece of fat meat.
Lide smiled, delivering a merciless rebuke.
"If the situation allowed it, naturally the gods would not abandon the Capital. But what is the current timing?
The Angel Alliance has just been established, Holy City is still under construction, and hundreds of millions around the Ancient Forest are still waiting to be settled by the gods. Who has time to care for you?
In other words, for the Nolan Capital to grab the attention of the gods, you’d at least have to wait until Holy City is finished, its neighboring believers settled, and no extra populace is present nearby.
But by that time, how many crises like today’s could the Capital have faced?
Today you were favored by the Goddess of Luck, I saved you.
But what about next time? After I leave, if a stronger Ancient Evil God arrives, will you still be able to resist?"
The icy words were like sharp blades, mercilessly stripping away the King’s last shreds of dignity.
Yes, the gods would be busy building Holy City to face the united Ancient Evil Gods. Who would care about a city that was not in a core area?
By the time the gods remembered them, they would have been destroyed numerous times.
The King wilted like a frostbitten eggplant.
And then, with utmost bitterness, he said,
"O God of Dawn, I beg you to guide us on what we should do."
Lide nodded in satisfaction, his ability to cajole... no... persuade people was clearly making steady progress.
"Since I am willing to mention the matter of the Ocean God System to you, I believe you already have the answer in your heart."
"However, you are unwilling to face it now, unable to make a decision, and find it difficult to abandon the seemingly stable but actually crisis-ridden situation..."
The King opened his mouth as if to say something, but in the end, he sighed in defeat and said no more.
The safety of a kingdom rests upon his shoulders; how could the pressure he bears be so simple?
But the problem is, he really feels bewildered at this moment. The future is fraught with crises; how to survive in a divine battle more terrifying than the twilight of the gods is a choice too difficult, too difficult.
Without power, one cannot control their own destiny.
The surrounding nobles, having heard the dialogue between the two, were greatly moved and eventually looked at each other in silence, falling into silence.
No one spoke again.
Only the King could make the decisions. The matter was too important; no one could take a stand on the spot.
Lide looked around, saw the varying expressions of the nobles, and said no more, leaving them to ponder for themselves.
His assumption was based on the ability to find a corresponding plane. Without it, all this talk was in vain.
"Not only the planes, but up to now, apart from the God of Plague, I have not seen divinities using Divine Countries.
Divine Countries are so powerful, if they could be used, those gods definitely wouldn’t just ignore them.
There must be some problem with this.
I will have to verify this with the Sea Clan Gods; if Divine Countries can be used, evacuating the Nolan Capital wouldn’t be an issue..."
With this thought, Lide hesitated no longer, clenched the fragment of the Destiny Tablet, and gestured to Spark with his hand.
"Teacher, I need some time to control the fragment of the Destiny Tablet..."
Spark had only just managed to adjust his mindset, having just emerged from a state of profound loss and mourning.
Hearing this brought a look of relief to his face, so you’re not invincible after all...
The disheveled old man regained some confidence, nodded, and turned to leave the hall with Lide.
Watching Lide take the fragment of the Destiny Tablet so openly and without hesitation, the surrounding nobles remained silent, no one daring to say more.
It was not until long after his figure had disappeared that the room gradually began to buzz with conversation.
"Alas, I never thought our Royal Capital would face such a horrific crisis. What should we do? Do we really need to flee the Royal Capital as Spark’s disciple suggests?"
"To think that even the Ocean God System needs His Highness Lide’s protection, truly too powerful!"
"To slay a god with a single sword... joining such a powerful figure seems not too hard to accept."
"I wonder if His Highness Lide has any concubines; perhaps we could arrange a marriage with Princess Kadi, this might also increase the Royal Capital’s importance in His Highness Lide’s heart..."
As the nobles were discussing, sudden cries of astonishment came from outside the door, followed by a general entering the hall to report loudly.
"Your Majesty, the Divine Body of the Ancient Evil God has been delivered, please inspect it."
These words made everyone in the room interested. The body of a deity—how precious a treasure could that be?
Slaying a god is always a momentous event at any time; how many years has it been since a divine being has fallen before the coming of the Ancients?
The nobles then got up one after another and followed the King to have a look.
Moments later, at the entrance of the main hall, nobles who emerged had their eyes widened and their faces full of shock.
In front of them, a corpse as large as a hill, with spikes on its back and four eyes on its head, and drenched in blood, lay severed in two on the ground.
If one got closer, they could see that the muscles of this terrifying life form were still twitching, clearly it had been killed not long ago.
Moreover, although it was only a corpse, the aura it emitted still made every person’s skin crawl.
Divine Power like a prison, penetrating the soul, even Legendary Strongmen could not be exempt from this dignity.
This is a god; dominant and unrivaled in life, and still formidable in death.
The King took a few steps forward, drawing near the Divine Body, his eyes revealing an indescribably complex expression.
Words failed to replace the visual shock of the scene.
His heart stirred with towering waves that could not be calmed for a long time.
At this moment, Princess Kadi’s eyes shone brightly, recalling the shocking blow she had witnessed atop the city walls, and the handsome figure in her mind made her heart race even faster.
The surrounding nobles had mixed expressions, but all wore undisguisable shock.
"Is this the true strength of Your Excellency Lide?"
"Perhaps it is our Glory to be protected by Your Excellency Lide..."
"How astonishing..."
Many nobles quietly changed their minds after witnessing the body of the Evil God.
---
---
---
Lide, unaware of the scene in the main hall, sat inside Spark’s carriage, intently sensing the fragments of the Destiny Tablet.
The Power of Destiny within him became more active due to the fragments.
However, since he had not yet absorbed the powers contained within the fragments, the system was unable to detect their attribute and could not determine the sequence number of this piece.
Inside the carriage, Spark looked at Lide, who was half-closing his eyes, with a strange expression. After a long silence, he spoke solemnly.
"Kachar, tell me the truth, are you the reincarnation of the Creator God..."
Lide looked up at the old man with a bird’s nest hairdo, his face lined with frustration. Could this guy not let it go?
With a touch of annoyance, he replied.
"Creator God? Yes, I am a Creator God from another world, traveling to this one..."
Spark’s eyes lit up and he laughed heartily.
"I knew it!!"
Lide: ...
Was this ever going to end? So what if his disciple was more handsome, taller, wealthier, and stronger than him? Besides these qualities, wasn’t everything else quite ordinary?
Was it worth being this upset?
Spark blushed at the fool’s gaze from Lide, quickly changing the subject.
"What secrets does the fragment of the Destiny Tablet hold?"
The Sun Goddess had only conveyed to the outside world that the fragments of the Destiny Tablet could resist the corruption of the Ancient, but she did not reveal much about the fragments.
Thus, most people only knew that the fragments were beneficial, but did not understand why.
Lide did not conceal the truth and recounted the origin of the Destiny Tablet, ending with a sigh.
"If we want to resist the Ancient Invasion, we need to gather all the fragments of the Destiny Tablet, which is not a simple task.
It starts off easy, but as time goes on, the fragments of the Destiny Tablet will inevitably concentrate more and more, and every additional piece gathered will be a fierce battle."
The fragments of the Destiny Tablet will surely concentrate in the hands of a few, and the strength of those who can secure the fragments goes without saying.
To snatch them back from these individuals would be a daunting task, known only to those who have faced life and death.
Similarly, this would become an elimination race, where the fragments of the Destiny Tablet are the tickets to the competition.
To survive, you must get a ticket, or else without it, the elimination will happen automatically, without the need for others to strike.
It was impossible not to fight.
Upon hearing this, Spark’s brows furrowed deeply, and he promptly perceived the risk involved.
"Perhaps it is not necessary to fight to the death; alliances could be formed later, becoming partners to face the enemy together..."
Lide nodded approvingly. Aside from being somewhat dramatic, his cheap teacher was not too shabby.
"That’s why I’m sheltering the Ocean God System."
Speaking of this, Spark was once again in low spirits. His disciple was too formidable, and he, as a genius teacher, could hardly raise his head in front of him.
As they spoke, the carriage slowly came to a stop.
Spark was still deep in thought and did not question Lide further. Lide, enjoying the quiet, did not engage in further chatter.
Both men stepped out of the carriage and entered the Royal Magic Academy.
Inside the academy, in Spark’s exclusive office, Lide settled comfortably on the sofa, clutching the Destiny Tablet fragment in his hand.
"Teacher, I will be obtaining the power from the Destiny Tablet fragment next, which may take some time."
"I’ll guard you..."
"Teacher, you just need to order no outsiders to barge in."
Spark was about to object but then thought of the other’s subordinate being a medium-powered Divine, and instantly lost interest.
He left with a defeated turn.
What was this? As a teacher, to be less than the disciple’s subordinate, it was quite a blow to his confidence.
He began to miss the girls of Jasmine Street; they were gentler and more considerate, with warm and magnificent bosoms...
Once Spark had left, Lide waved his hand and the Twelve-winged Death Blazing Angel hidden in the shadows immediately appeared behind him.
"Frey, you’re responsible for guarding my safety, no one is to enter the room...
If Teacher Spark comes looking for me urgently, you may assist him as appropriate, and follow his orders if need be."
Frey bowed respectfully.
"Sovereign, I will follow your command."
Lide’s order was her direction, so naturally, there would be no objections, even if it meant obeying a mere Legendary Strongman.
After the instructions, Lide hesitated no more and with focused concentration, began directing his Power of Destiny into the fragment of the Destiny Tablet.
Instantly, a jubilant sensation emerged from within the fragment.
The slumbering powers within the Destiny Tablet fragment began to slowly awaken, radiating a closeness towards him, like seeing their own parents.
In just a moment, the dormant powers within the fragment surged into Lide’s body like a flood breaking through a dam.
His body, already transfigured by the Power of Destiny, began to absorb that origin power once more.
Time slipped away.
It was uncertain how long it had been, like a single breath or an entire century.
Lide’s spirit momentarily dazed, and a strand of his spiritual power was once more drawn into the River of Destiny, the ancient secrets of Glory unfolding before his eyes once again.
The second Battle of the Gods, Gods of the Light God System delving into the 600th layer of the abyss...
A Lost Plane collided with the Main Plane, leading to the deaths of hundreds of millions and the fall of more than a dozen Divine Beings...
...
Those past events, buried by time, were once again glimpsed by him.
Those unrecorded histories, once more unveiled...
While Lide leisurely traversed the River of Destiny, the Power of Destiny within him became increasingly condensed. The power output from the fragments of the Destiny Tablet began to slowly diminish, indicating that this act of devouring was nearing its end.
When the Destiny Tablet’s fragments no longer emitted any power, the Force of Destiny contained within Lide’s body reached a new height, but because a strand of his consciousness still spied on past secrets, he unwittingly touched upon some ancient rules.
Suddenly, Lide, still in slumber, felt a chill run down his spine, sensing a lethal breath as if a dagger were pressed against his throat.
His originally dim thoughts were abruptly awakened.
The strand of spiritual power, still swimming in the River of Destiny, took on human form, and now, sensing something, he instinctively looked up at the sky.
A shocking image that he couldn’t possibly describe appeared before his eyes.
In the eternally existing Chaos Void, within the obscure and disorderly primordial realm, a pair of cold eyes that imprinted countless universes now gazed down upon the Multi-dimensional Plane.
Within those eyes, galaxies twisted and myriad worlds collapsed.
The aura they emitted was indescribable, ineffable, untouchable.
This was the most extreme vision of the world.
No one could imagine what kind of terrifying existence the owner of those eyes might be.
Lide’s heart wildly throbbed at this moment.
He could feel that the pair of eyes, looking over the River of Destiny, saw him. Yes, his inconspicuous strand of consciousness had caught the attention of the other.
That existence, which transcended worldly rules, was watching him.
At that moment, Lide felt as transparent as a ghost, unable to hide any secrets.
He smelled the scent of death now, extreme danger, extreme lethality, extreme horror...
He wanted to escape, but even his soul seemed frozen, unable to mobilize his strength.
Between life and death lies great terror.
Crack~
In the few blinks of an eye that those chilling, all-seeing eyes set upon him, a force capable of shattering galaxies grinded down upon him.
The part of the River of Destiny where he was exploded, instantly turning that strand of spiritual power to nothingness.
The next instant, Lide’s eyes flew open, as if a drowning man had surfaced from the water, desperately gasping for breath.
Huff huff~
His forehead was covered with beads of sweat the size of beans, his hands trembling unnaturally.
Too powerful.
Merely being glanced at, he and the surrounding space could not withstand the pressure and were directly annihilated.
Terrifying to the extreme.
Fortunately, it was only a strand of spiritual power drawn into the River of Destiny by the Force of Destiny. Otherwise, he probably would have been completely dead by now. In the face of that unknown, dreadful being, all resistance was as insignificant as ants.
A Name suddenly surged in Lide’s mind.
The ruler of the Ancient Days, the end-point of all ancient powers—Asathos.
Yes, it must be that Ancient ruler never recorded in history.
He had actually seen that fearsome creature in the River of Destiny, a creature that could contend with the Creator God as an Ancient ruler.
It was Lide’s first direct feeling of the terror of a life form on the scale of the Creator God.
That lingering dominance still made his heart tremble even now.
The pressure of the Dawn Main God compared with that gaze overseeing the celestial rivers and the heavens was like that of a small child, utterly insignificant.
"He saw me..."
After a long while, Lide steadied his mind, let out a long breath, and his eyes were incredibly complex.
"I can feel him spying on me, that force that wipes out the void was his doing."
"Overlooking the River of Destiny, what exactly does the ruler of old want to do?"
"The more Power of Destiny I carry, the more I will attract the attention of the Ancient Evil God... Kassandra, I finally understand what that means."
It was clear that the dense Power of Destiny he carried had caught the notice of the ruler of old who had been watching the River of Destiny, and that the other party had directly erased an entire area.
If his Power of Destiny had been as meager as last time, the other party might not have given him a second glance.
"The River of Destiny is a manifestation of the Original Rules of Glory; it is said that the River of Destiny can reflect the fate of all Glory Life, and peeking into the River of Destiny is essentially peeking into the future of Glory.
However, instead of saying the other party has been watching the River of Destiny, it’s more like they have been watching the origin power of Glory.
If the River of Destiny were to be devoured or even controlled by them, then Glory would surely fall completely into their hands."
Lide fell into deep thought, the recent scene in the River of Destiny flashing through his mind.
"No wonder I sensed the presence of ancient times in the River of Destiny just now, it must be the residue of the ruler of old.
Could the widening crack in the sky of the Main Plane also be due to the contamination of the River of Destiny by the ruler of old?"
Various speculations made Lide’s emotions fluctuate.
This time, led to the River of Destiny by the Power of Destiny, although he encountered the ruler of old accidentally, he could also infer deeper secrets based on the very limited information he had.
And he felt a certain level of confidence about how the situation would unfold next.
This scare although unsettling, wasn’t a total loss...
Lide took a deep sigh and his expression slowly returned to calm.
"No matter the situation, what must be faced will be faced.
The ruler of old has noticed me, and from now on, things probably won’t go as smoothly."
Thinking of this, the pressure in his heart suddenly increased.
Being noticed by an enemy’s ultimate boss was not a pleasant feeling.
And according to Kassandra’s information, the more Power of Destiny he carried, the more attention he would draw from the Ancient Evil God, leaving him no possibility of escape.
So, from the moment he started bearing the Power of Destiny, there had been no way back—he was destined to clash with the Ancient Evil God.
"No, from the moment of the Ancient Invasion, I had no way back—to either overthrow those Ancient Monsters and make them wail or let them pin me to the ground and grind all over me..."
After a moment’s pondering, Lide regained his composure.
But just as he was about to take the Destiny Tablet in his hand and look at its attributes.
The door to the room suddenly opened, and Spark rushed in anxiously.
"The brat from the Kachar family, thirteen days have passed, and you’ve finally woken up!!
Quick, follow me outside, the Angel Alliance has sent someone!"
Lide’s eyes narrowed, the Angel Alliance?!
He hadn’t expected those people to take notice of Nolan Capital so quickly; it seems a population of over ten million was indeed enticing.
Just as he thought to ask a question, Spark’s next words changed Lide’s expression.
"The one leading the team is the Master of Dawn, and one of your subordinates has stopped them..."
The Powerful Divine Power of the Master of Dawn?! Frey’s former master??
Frey is stopping him right now??
Upon hearing this, Lide’s scalp tingled.

chapters.title: Chapter 488 - 489: Master of Dawn is also a fool, Lide, firm and unyielding, yielding to softness but not to coercion.
chapters.content:
Chapter 488: Chapter 489: Master of Dawn is also a fool, Lide, firm and unyielding, yielding to softness but not to coercion.
Lide hadn’t expected that during the ten-odd days he was secluded, such a huge matter had arisen.
Master of Dawn.
That was the creator of Frey.
Now, this was a headache.
Before he went into seclusion, he had ordered Frey to protect him, and she must have sensed the arrival of the Master of Dawn and thought that this terrifying divine posed a threat to him, so she took the initiative to confront and block the other party outside the royal capital.
But didn’t Frey’s appearance just expose everything?
Although she had become a Death Blazing Angel, her original master was the Master of Dawn.
Fuck, if the Master of Dawn discovered that his seventh-ranked war general had fallen to become a Death Blazing Angel, then shit would really hit the fan.
With a pained expression on his face, Lide hurriedly asked Spark.
"Teacher, what is the attitude of the Master of Dawn right now?"
He hadn’t told Spark about Frey’s background—otherwise, this old man would probably pack up and flee immediately.
Among the Main Gods of the Light Attribute System, the Master of Dawn was definitely in the top five in terms of combat strength, controlling the dawn, the morning and a part of the Light God Positions.
Ultimate boss.
Fighting such an enemy sent shivers down his spine.
It was also fortunate that the Ancient Invasion had occurred, leaving the gods fallen and the divine having lost most of their power— the Master of Dawn had not yet returned to his peak.
Otherwise, he could only have fled.
For now, only Catharsina, the half-blood mermaid with an incredible background, in Dawn City could suppress the Master of Dawn. Even the Main God of the Ocean God System was like a little brother in front of the Master of Dawn—their combat strengths were absolutely not on the same level.
Spark noticed Lide’s anxiety and said somewhat puzzledly.
"The Master of Dawn seems to be an old acquaintance of your subordinate, and has been continually wanting to take her back.
However, your subordinate is very loyal to you and ignored the Master of Dawn’s words, instead boldly threatening the Master of Dawn and forbidding him from stepping into Nolan Capital."
After speaking, Spark looked at Lide with some suspicion.
"From what the Master of Dawn implies, your subordinate was originally his person. I don’t know why she fell and became an evil being, Kachar, do you know about this?"
Lide’s mouth twitched.
How could I not know?
I am the one who did it...
Damn, now the victim has come knocking, and the fun has just begun.
After thinking for a while, he continued to ask.
"Did they engage in battle? How is the combat strength of the Master of Dawn? Can he defeat Frey?"
Spark shook his head.
"I wasn’t able to perceive their battle, but it seems that after fighting for several Days of Sunshine, neither side could dominate the other."
This made Lide breathe a little easier; thankfully, the Master of Dawn had not returned to his peak state.
But how should this matter be resolved?
Lide couldn’t help but fall into deep thought.
Frey was his biggest reliance; he would not give her up to anyone.
I am the one who skillfully corrupted her; why should I hand her over to you?
If you want to take Frey back, try to take her by force...
The shamelessly thick-skinned Lide’s face had already reached a thickness comparable to city walls.
However, after thinking for a long time, he came up with nothing and decided not to delay any further.
"Teacher, take me to where they are fighting."
Spark looked at Lide, who had a conflicted expression, and hesitated a bit.
"Kachar, that Twelve-winged Blazing Angel, she wouldn’t happen to be the one you lured into falling, would she?"
Lide’s form stiffened, shocked to have been seen through...
Yet, he did not falter but declared confidently,
"No."
Are you joking? Call that temptation? Would I stoop to such primitive tricks?
I was openly overpowering her using the Power of Death to transform her into a Death Blazing Angel.
There’s a fundamental difference, okay?
Spark only abandoned his inner doubts and plans to flee upon seeing Lide’s strong stance.
After descending the stairs, Spark no longer rode the carriage leisurely but cast several spells on himself and started to fly frantically toward the Imperial Palace.
"They are fighting in the Imperial Palace..."
Lide was equally unambiguous, casting spells himself and immediately following Spark.
Two distinct shadows streaked across the sky, and within just a few breaths, they arrived at the entrance to the Imperial Palace.
Princess Kadi, who had been waiting there, instantly relaxed when she saw Lide, her eyes shining brightly. Then, while leading them into the Imperial Palace, she hurriedly briefed Lide on the current situation.
"Your Highness Lide, Lord Spark mentioned that the Twelve-winged Blazing Angel currently obstructing the Master of Dawn is under your command. They are engaged in combat in the skies, and the outcome is yet undetermined.
The Master of Dawn has come to protect the Royal Capital, could your subordinate perhaps allow him to enter?"
Her voice trembled slightly, her face unable to hide her astonishment.
Though she had observed for a long time, the thought of the mighty Master of Dawn from myth battling the handsome young man’s subordinate made her heart quiver.
View the correct content at .
The Master of Dawn required no additional description; the very Divine Title spoke volumes.
Yet such a powerful being was obstructed by a subordinate of a young man.
Such stark contrast stirred waves of emotion in her heart...
Indeed, he was here for the Royal Capital, Lide nodded slightly.
"Have you mentioned the fragments of the Destiny Tablet to the Master of Dawn?"
Princess Kadi shook her head, "No, only the high Nobles are privy to the fragments of the Destiny Tablet, and the Master of Dawn has not yet descended into the Royal Capital."
Lide frowned, weren’t high Nobles enough?
Was this princess too naive? A secret known by two people can’t be guarded, let alone one known by hundreds, how could that still be called a secret?
High Nobles likely had followers of the Master of Dawn among them, who then used temples to relay messages to him—it wasn’t even hard to achieve...
Observing Lide’s inquisitive look, Kadi caught onto the issue with her words and her complexion slightly paled, promptly speaking up.
"Your Highness Lide, I apologize, this isn’t within my control."
Lide waved his hand, now was not the time to ponder this matter; how to confront the upcoming situation was his concern.
Shortly afterward, Princess Kadi led both Lide and Spark into a large garden where many Nobles were currently gazing up, watching the battle.
However, rather than a visible engagement, only thick clouds occasionally leaked bursts of energy, making it impossible to distinguish any figures.
It was almost akin to watching fireworks.
Boom, boom...
The very moment Lide stepped into the garden, the environment suddenly darkened.
A cyan-colored sword shadow spanned the sky, stretches miles in length.
The aura emanating from the sword shadow seemed capable of commanding heaven, perhaps able to destroy a Royal Capital of millions with a single strike.
"Frey, whoever lured you down truly spared no expense, even raising your Level from 34 to 36!
And to bestow upon you three Divine Positions, it really piques my curiosity, who is your current master?"
The Divine Language, filled with sanctity, resonated through the heavens, making those below feel tremendous reverence and aspiration towards its speaker. If not for the absence of a visible figure, there might be several new believers at that moment.
Divine Language...
Lide’s brows furrowed tightly.
The Divine Language had the power to deepen believers’ faith, much like the Abyssal Blasphemy used to corrupt beings into evil lifeforms.
The only difference was that one led people to become followers of Divine, and the other embraced them into darkness—to sum up—both were no good things.
Lide had no particular fondness for such actions because it was akin to casting spirit magic on outsiders; if not brainwashed by the Divine Language over a long period, their faith would gradually diminish.
He had always disdained using such methods to preach; instead, solid preaching could make the believers’ faith more stable and less likely to turn to others.
Though he disdained the Divine Language, its implications gave Lide much to ponder.
So, before her fall, Frey was only at Level 34 and had risen to Level 36 after her fall?
Was this strengthening due to corruption, or did the billion Power of Death elevate her level?
It made sense, after all. If Level 36 with medium divine power ranked seventh under the Master of Dawn, wouldn’t the top five rankers be Level 37 and above?
Even if the Master of Dawn was powerful, it was impossible to have seven subordinates with medium divine power.
Many smaller races, like the Half-Elf, didn’t possess medium divine power; even with the abundant and dense Power of Faith provided by humans, achieving the omnipresence of medium divine power wasn’t feasible.
Furthermore, according to the opposition, Frey only achieved her divine position after her corruption; she did not possess it before...
"Could it be that the Land of Bone-Burying not only transforms other life forms into the undead but also grants them some power?
It seems I need to go try it out..."
As Lide pondered, the scene in the sky changed once more.
Thunder rumbled~
As the Master of Dawn spoke, the giant sword capable of slicing heaven and earth swung down fiercely, cleaving horizontally in front of him.
Where the blade passed, space annihilated, rules shattered, a void of chaos prevailing.
Clearly, the released power exceeded the spatial limits of endurance.
"Shatter!!"
A roar, akin to an ancient giant dragon, echoed as the sword that split the void melted like ice and snow, shattering in the blink of an eye.
The surrounding space stirred a terrifying flow, with a tremendous gust rushing outward.
Even from a great distance, the residents within the Royal Capital felt their skins painfully impacted by the fierce energy.
Just as Frey prepared to strike again, she suddenly sensed Lide’s presence and without hesitation, the Twelve Death Wing Blazing Angel disappeared in mid-air.
Her task was to ensure Lide’s safety, and since Lide had emerged and issued no orders for her to continue the battle.
The Master of Dawn, realizing Frey’s departure, furrowed his brows tightly and turned his gaze from the high reaches of thousands of blades to Lide on the ground.
His expression subtly shifted.
Swish~ Stepping forward, he disappeared into the air.
In the next second, the space before Lide twisted, and from within emerged a figure dressed in a white robe, donning a sacred crown resembling the intertwined sun and moon, holding a grey short wooden staff.
This person, in his early forties, seemed to have descended bathed in holy light, constantly emitting a comfortable pale white glow from behind.
The Master of Dawn.
The surrounding nobles also noticed this extraordinary existence; eyes widened, their faces a mix of excitement at witnessing a legend, anxiety, and even some had already knelt devoutly to worship this divine entity.
Lide, seeing the Master of Dawn, suddenly became extremely alert.
Every cell in his body screamed danger — extreme danger!
This calm, peaceful figure, shrouded in holy light, was like an ancient giant dragon standing before him, concealing power enough to shatter the star river.
Lord Spark and Princess Kadi, with their messy hair, were not faring any better; although the Master of Dawn had restrained his divine might, the inadvertent aura still made them tremble.
This was a life several levels higher than theirs.
Lide forcibly suppressed the tumultuous waves in his heart, his expression calmly unchanged; his dark, deep eyes unflinchingly met the Master of Dawn’s gaze.
His emerging dawn divine might subtly leaked a fraction and was not fully activated, but even this sliver made the originally indifferent Master of Dawn pause, his expression instantly solemn.
His gaze intensely fixed on Lide, with no trace of contempt.
Divine dignity— this was an existence of equal level.
"Strange main god, are you Frey’s new master?"
The Divine Language made the Master of Dawn sparkle with sanctity and light, which upon hearing instantly sparked a strong sense of submission in the crowd, with several guards converting their faith to become followers of the other side on the spot.
Lide’s soul was so resilient that it naturally remained unaffected, and he looked directly at his opponent with a calm demeanor.
"Indeed, destiny chose me for Frey."
As his words fell, a holy aura also emanated from his body, casting a faint glow around him.
Though he lacked the blessing of Divine Language, his appearance alone was no less impressive than that of the Master of Dawn.
Sensing the pure Light Attribute power emanating from Lide, the Master of Dawn furrowed his brows.
Such holy power couldn’t possibly lead Frey to fall from grace, could it be that the instigator wasn’t this unknown deity before him?
"Who tempted her to fall?"
Lide raised an eyebrow, his gaze cold as he stared at the Master of Dawn.
"Are you questioning me?"
We are all Main Gods, what right do you have to prattle before me, Master of Dawn?
Hearing these relentless words, the Master of Dawn felt somewhat displeased, but after considering, he decided not to get angry.
He couldn’t sense Lide’s exact strength, and the intimidating aura Lide emanated carried traces of Moons the divine had died, indicating clearly that this unknown Main God before him was no pushover.
While he hadn’t yet regained his peak combat strength, there was no way he could overpower Lide.
Not to mention that Lide also had a subordinate whose combat power was nearly equal to his own.
Strength was the foundation of an equal conversation, and recognizing Lide’s strength, the Master of Dawn’s expression somewhat softened.
"No, unknown deity, I merely seek the truth.
Frey was originally a War General under me, and I spent a considerable amount of origin power to promote her to a Twelve-winged Blazing Angel.
Tens of thousands of years ago, the ruler of the Undead Plane waged a divine battle against me, and Frey led the Angel Army into battle and was trapped, missing for tens of thousands of years..."
Lide unapologetically interrupted the Master of Dawn.
"Tens of thousands of years? Master of Dawn, unless you can traverse the River of Destiny, no one can know what transpired during that time.
It was only after the Ancient Invasion that I became Frey’s master, when she had already become the Death Blazing Angel."
This was the truth, he only became Frey’s master after she was transformed into a Death Blazing Angel; before her transformation, she was suppressed by him in the Land of Bone-Burying...
Seeing Lide’s forthright expression without any attempt to hide anything, the Master of Dawn fell silent.
A lot had indeed happened during that battle, and too much time had passed.
Even if Frey had fallen, he couldn’t be certain it was the doing of the person before him.
However, regardless of who was responsible for Frey’s fall, he couldn’t simply give up on this Blazing Angel who originally belonged to him.
"Unknown Main God, I think you should be aware that Frey is my subordinate, and I need to regain control over her."
Lide smiled, "Your subordinate? Sorry, but Frey is the Death Blazing Angel I subdued, she has nothing to do with you."
The Master of Dawn’s eyes narrowed slightly.
"What if I insist on having her?"
"You can try."
Lide’s gaze turned instantly cold, and as his words fell, all his titles and skills activated simultaneously, his pressure as the Dawn Main God burst forth unrestrained.
His seemingly slender figure appeared like a primordial beast awakening at that moment, enveloping half the city under his endless intimidating presence.
Even the staunchest warriors would feel their legs go weak under such terrifying pressure, trembling and daring not to speak.
Lide didn’t yield at all, confronting the Master of Dawn with an utterly domineering posture.
Now, openly a Main God, he couldn’t possibly show weakness.
He had to present an unprovokable attitude... This was a zero-sum game, a battle of mental strength, a wager of the heart.
Sensing that overwhelming momentum, the Master of Dawn frowned, especially the subtle but unmistakable threat emanating from the void next to Lide, which heightened his alertness.
He had come today intending to monopolize the Nolan Capital, making this populous city an independent backup against the Angel Alliance, so he hadn’t brought other deities with him.
More critically, he had only recovered to Level 34, and even a full-force attack had only just managed to maintain an unbeaten stance against Frey, thanks largely to the power of several Divine Artifacts he possessed.
With his own combat strength not yet formidable, Lide’s assertiveness made him hesitate.
With just one Frey able to hold him off, plus this mysterious unknown Main God, his chances of winning were incredibly low.
View the correct content at .
Even in victory, the price to pay would be devastating, and at this juncture, engaging in conflict with Lide seemed uneconomical in every sense.
Lide, too, acutely sensed the change in the Master of Dawn and immediately steadied his heart.
Fortunately, the Master of Dawn was a Divine Main God of the Light Attribute System; had it been a Demon Lord from the chaotic evil camp, he might already be brawling with the adversary.
After a brief moment of thought, Lide spoke again.
"Master of Dawn, we are not enemies. Although I have ways to defeat and even kill you, doing so would also inflict considerable injuries upon me..."
The Master of Dawn frowned, his wariness intensifying with those words. The impact of such a statement varied greatly between coming from a mortal and a Main God.
A god who had conquered Frey could hardly be an easy adversary.
Lide watched the other’s expression and continued speaking.
"Following Frey’s submission to me, I expended endless resources to raise her Level to Medium Divine Power.
You should know, having made such a great sacrifice, I would never willingly give her up."
After establishing his stance, he shifted the conversation.
"I’ve heard that the Angel Alliance was just founded and external forces are looking at you with hostility.
I assume you wouldn’t want to establish a powerful enemy at this time for no good reason.
Perhaps we should let this matter go for now. The Ancient Evil Gods are still covetously planning to destroy the whole world; fighting each other now would likely play right into their hands.
The fall of every Main God signifies a loss for the Light Attribute camp.
We can discuss this after we have dealt with the catastrophe left by the ancients..."
Lide began with a forceful threat, then found an excuse not to fight, and finally offered the Master of Dawn a way out—which altogether dissuaded him from starting a war at this moment.
After all, from any perspective, a conflict now was inadvisable.
Indeed, though the hostility in the Master of Dawn’s eyes remained, his posture for battle significantly relaxed.
"Unfamiliar Main God, I have never heard of your existence. Could you tell me your Divine Title?"
Seeing that the other wasn’t continuing to argue about Frey, Lide’s face broke into a smile.
"I am the God of Dawn and Twilight, the Divine Main God of the Dawn Divine System.
Master of Dawn, we currently share a common enemy. If the ancients truly invade successfully, our current conflict will seem utterly ridiculous. With the world on the brink of destruction, what significance would such strife have?"
The best way to resolve internal conflicts is often through an external enemy—an intention clearly aimed to strengthen psychological suggestion.
As expected, Lide’s words sidetracked the Master of Dawn.
He couldn’t help but fall silent.
Given the major backdrop of an ancient invasion, fighting each other to death was meaningless,
but although he understood this reasoning, the fact that Frey had sided with his opponent still immensely irked him, considering she was a Twelve-winged Blazing Angel he had cultivated for countless years.
Nevertheless, he knew he had no way to turn the situation around today, as Frey alone could hold him off, not to mention causing further trouble.
He then changed the topic.
"Dawn Main God, I came today for the Nolan Capital and the fragments of the Destiny Tablet."
"Nolan Capital has been chosen by me and is going to become my chosen nation."
"The Sun Goddess sensed the presence of the Destiny Tablet fragments near Nolan Capital. I have inquired my believers, and the Destiny Tablet fragments are in your possession..."
"We can revisit the matter of Frey later, but the Destiny Tablet fragments pertain to the fate of all Glory, so I urge you to consider the bigger picture and surrender them to me."
Oh, not bad, the young chap is quick to learn, using righteousness to press me.
Lide’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Looks like it is not a case of adversaries not meeting each other.
But you want the Nolan Capital and the Destiny Tablet fragments? Sorry, you’re too late.
"Master of Dawn, Nolan Capital is currently under my protection, you need not worry. With so many other cities on the Main Plane in need of protection, I am sure you won’t miss this one."
"As for the Destiny Tablet fragments, they are under my control and cannot be returned to you..."
The Master of Dawn’s brows rose upon hearing this, his face showing signs of discontent.
"Dawn Main God, the Destiny Tablet is the condensation of the entire Glory’s destiny, possessing the most origin power.
To control the Destiny Tablet, one must gain recognition from the multi-dimensional planes of Glory and also bear the Power of Destiny.
Among the entire Angel Alliance, only the Sun Goddess has borne the Power of Destiny; other main gods cannot control it.
You say you have controlled a piece of the Destiny Tablet? Are you joking?
If you disrupt the overall situation, you will be making enemies with the entire Angel Alliance, all divine beings within the divine systems!
Dawn Main God, you should be able to imagine the consequences."
The Power of Destiny is the most origin force, borne only by the Sun Goddess, the strongest among so many powerful main gods; others don’t even qualify to touch it.
And now, someone suddenly claims to control a piece of the Destiny Tablet—isn’t that ridiculous?
Could it be that so many main gods of the Angel Alliance are inferior to a never-before-heard-of foreign divine being?
But just as the Master of Dawn was about to continue mocking Lide and to pressure him into handing over the piece of Destiny Tablet, his expression froze.
For at that moment, Lide had a piece of the Destiny Tablet in his hand, holding it directly.
More exaggeratedly, the most origin Power of Destiny from Glory started emanating from Lide. He stood right in front of the Master of Dawn, who couldn’t even sense his presence.
All of Lide was shrouded by the Power of Destiny.
Seeing this scene, the heart of the Master of Dawn jolted, his eyes widened in disbelief.
"How is it possible? Without the aid of a Creation God Artifact, how can you control a piece of the Destiny Tablet?
How can you bear the Power of Destiny?!
Impossible, this is absolutely impossible!
That is a power exclusive to the Creator God, how can you possess it?!!"
His voice even carried a sharp edge, startling the nobles secretly observing nearby.
What had happened to make such a towering figure in myths this shocked?
Being able to unsettle a main god as high-ranking as the Master of Dawn sufficiently spoke to the impact of Lide bearing the Power of Destiny.
The shocked expression of the Master of Dawn made Lide fall into contemplation.
With the assistance of Kachar and the system, he had borne the Power of Destiny safely though encountering danger.
Thus, he had never fully understood how difficult it was to bear the Power of Destiny, only knowing that the powerful Divine Power Level Mermaid Main God had failed.
The discomposure of the Master of Dawn at that moment made him rethink, realizing that those who could bear the Power of Destiny were extremely rare.
To the extent that the first reaction of a main god like the Master of Dawn upon seeing someone bearing the Power of Destiny was disbelief.
"It seems the Power of Destiny is more important than I thought, why didn’t Kachar remind me more..."
In a flash of thought, Lide put away the shard of the Destiny Tablet. The other shard was still suppressed in Dawn City and he did not carry it with him.
Only after Lide put away the shard did the Master of Dawn come back to his senses, but his gaze toward Lide changed again, with a hint of jealousy.
Why? Why could he not bear the Power of Destiny when he, the magnificent Master of Dawn, ranked among the top five in the Light God System?
A strange main god, why could he bear it?
Gods are not lives without desires; they are just a group of powerful beings with their desires, and the desire to gain more power is an instinct for all beings.
The Power of Destiny, being the most origin force, was something all knowledgeable divine beings longed to control.
Thus, the Master of Dawn felt aggrieved.
He had almost perished and still had not managed to bear the Power of Destiny; this sudden unknown main god not only stole his subordinate but also controlled the Power of Destiny which he could not.
This intense shock directly broke the Master of Dawn’s defenses.
A sense of unwillingness filled his chest.
"Dawn Main God, how did you gain control of the Destiny Tablet shard?"
Lide raised his eyebrows and smiled.
"Talent."
I...
Master of Dawn choked, unable to vent his frustration.
What does he mean by "Talent"? Is he implying my talent is poor??
I’m the Main God of Powerful Divine Power, not some trashy deity from the streets!
He took a few deep breaths to suppress his turbulent emotions, his eyes burning with passion as he looked at Lide, his voice tinged with desire.
"Dawn Main God, there are three more shards of the Destiny Tablet within the Angel Alliance, which will surely be useful to you.
We could make a deal, tell me how to control the shards of the Destiny Tablet, and I could grant you access to those shards..."
Is this so straightforward?
The real-life version of ’if you can’t beat them, join them’?
After pondering for a moment, Lide decidedly shook his head.
What a joke! Not only is he incapable of teaching the Curse of Destiny, but he wouldn’t even consider such a foolish trade.
The shards of the Destiny Tablet are crucial. How could the Master of Dawn freely give them away? That’s just pie in the sky.
"Master of Dawn, my control over the Power of Destiny was a mere coincidence of fortune, just like magic talent. If you have talent, you have it; if you don’t, no amount of teaching will help."
The Master of Dawn looked even more displeased, but the flames in his eyes eventually died out as he coldly glanced at Lide and decided not to persist.
"Mind your own business, I’ll come back for Frey..."
He turned his head, gazing at the empty space beside him for a moment before tearing through the space and vanishing in front of the Imperial Palace.
After a little while.
"Master, he has left..."
Hearing Frey’s message, Lide shook his head, a look of helplessness on his face.
The Master of Dawn really is a blockhead! Didn’t he believe when I said it was a talent? Can’t he assess his own capabilities?
Do I have a system and so do you??
This is great; now this idiot is just jealous.
Is admitting that you’re a poor student really that hard?
The Angel Alliance will surely learn that he controls the Power of Destiny because of the Master of Dawn, and it’s highly likely that this will lead to more trouble in the future...
Ah, all this because you don’t believe in the existence of talent.
This time, it’s purely the Master of Dawn’s fault and has nothing to do with me—I know nothing about it...
Lide quickly adjusted his mindset after muttering inwardly.
Fortunately, he had already mentally prepared himself before. As long as he didn’t give up on collecting the Destiny Tablet shards, conflict was inevitable.
The Angel Alliance? They’d have to send the Sun Goddess to seduce him, or perhaps the Night Goddess or the Love and Beauty Goddess... Otherwise, forget about it.
Iron-willed Lide doesn’t falter under pressure...
Though the Master of Dawn had left, both Spark and Princess Kadi, who had witnessed the confrontation, were still in a daze.
The Master of Dawn—a terrifying figure in ancient legends, one of the most powerful deities.
Now, such a figure treated Lide as an equal.
And Lide dared to threaten him, even more astonishingly, the Master of Dawn had accepted those threats.
This absurd scene was so fantastical it was hard for them to believe it was real.
They knew Lide was strong, but they had no idea he was this powerful.
To openly defy a deity from myths—how preposterous?
Spark was wide-eyed, struggling to recover from the shock. The poor old man, who had taken great pains to stabilize his mindset over the past several days, was completely overwhelmed by this development.
No more teaching "talented" students after this.
It’s far too disheartening.
That was the Master of Dawn, and he was chased away just like that!
And me, why bother learning magic anymore? I might as well resign myself to a life of mediocrity since, at best, that’s all there is...
Princess Kadi seemed like she was about to cry, her admiration for Lide reaching its peak.
With looks handsome enough to take one’s breath away, an outstandingly elegant demeanor, and power enchanting enough to captivate hearts, was this not the prince charming she had dreamt of?
O Goddess above, you finally heard my prayers, praise be to you...
At this moment, the faces of the surrounding nobles also turned exceptionally vivid.
Their hearts were so shocked by Lide that they could barely speak clearly.
"Master of Dawn... even the Master of Dawn treats Lide as an equal, am I dreaming?"
"We ought to follow such a strong leader!"
"No, I must give my daughter to Lide; even maintaining a normal relationship with such a person could keep our family from falling..."
Surrounded by nobles at the center, the king had also regained his senses, pushed aside those excited nobles, and approached Lide with an expression far more respectful than before.
"O God of Dawn, your radiance is comparable to the bright moon and the fierce sun. The citizens of the Royal Capital need your guidance, please give us your commands."
After the Master of Dawn was driven away by Lide, Nolan Capital could only rely on Lide.
As the king, he was smart—they had no choice but to side with the victor; had Lide been killed by the Master of Dawn, he would have acted the same.
Lide looked deeply at the king.
"Prepare to move out of the Royal Capital, don’t harbor any illusions. The Master of Dawn has appeared, which is not good news. It can be foreseen that the divine battle will soon spread to the Royal Capital, and by then, you may face an onslaught from dozens of Ancient Evil Gods."
The king shivered, immediately understanding the implications of Lide’s words—that the Master of Dawn’s arrival signified that the Angel Alliance was initially formed, and a clash with the Ancient Evil Gods was imminent.
In such a terrifying divine war, the Royal Capital was insignificant.
"Please save the millions of civilians in the Royal Capital..."
Lide glanced around, seeing the hopeful eyes of the crowd, and nodded slightly.
"I will find a safe plane for you to take refuge in."
These millions of people, if they were not consumed, it truly pained his heart. They were all potential believers, after all.
Whoosh whoosh~
While Lide was speaking to the king, a pure white falcon dived quickly towards the ground from the sky above and towards Spark, like a sharp arrow.
Noticing the familiar aura, Spark abruptly woke up and quickly extended his hand to allow the falcon to land on his arm.
Flap flap~
The handsome falcon attracted the curiosity of many nobles; without hesitation, Spark, in front of everyone, took out a secret message from the falcon’s belly and after glancing through it, his expression changed and he immediately turned and went over to Lide.
"Kachar, this is your message..."
The king and the surrounding nobles watched them intently with rather subtle expressions.
Lide’s expression unchanging, took the letter and started reading.
Moments later, his aura suddenly surged, and he turned his head to look at the king, his tone cold.
"Your Majesty, the plane sealing the Ancient Evil God has shattered, I need to return to the southern province..."
The secret message carried several important and very urgent pieces of news.
The first was that the plane sealing the Ancient Evil God in front of Dwarf Valley had shattered, releasing several Ancient Evil Gods who were now wreaking havoc on the barren wastelands.
Moreover, in the past few days, they seemed to have sensed the presence of the fragments of the Destiny Tablet and were heading towards Dawn City.
The deities of the Ocean God System were also unable to handle these Ancient Evil Gods; the opponents seemed quite formidable.
The second piece of news was that the red-eyed race had sent people from the Storm Sea, aiming for Isa and claiming that Isa was their golden descendant, wanting to take her back to the city-state of Silver Moon Radiance, but Vina had intercepted them, requiring his return to resolve the situation.
The last piece was about the Underworld.
The Black Dragon that had long been hidden emerged three days ago, reaching the Divine Level, and possessing a very powerful Divine Artifact that caused major turmoil in the Underworld.
Due to the Ancient Evil Gods, the Ocean God System couldn’t dispatch deities to besiege them, only managing to send two deities to hold them off.

chapters.title: Chapter 489 - 490: When Players Become the Ancient Evil God, Lide Becomes the Prey (9000)
chapters.content:
Chapter 489: Chapter 490: When Players Become the Ancient Evil God, Lide Becomes the Prey (9000)
"The Master of Dawn arrived in the Royal Capital three days earlier."
Green City.
During this time, Green City had enjoyed a rare peace, as the tense atmosphere following the Ancient Arrival had been swept away.
Because the great God of Dawn, Lord Ilo, had become their protector.
The presence of a powerful deity in the city had immeasurably boosted the confidence of its residents.
Moreover, the various pro-citizen policies newly introduced by the City Hall had brought Lide’s support to its peak among the lower-class residents.
With a strong backer above and stable policies below, stabilizing a city was just that simple.
Although the policies aimed at the nobility dissatisfied and even incited resentment among many who had benefited from the old system, they had no choice but to bow their heads before the overwhelming trend.
"Political power grows out of the barrel of a gun," a great man’s words applied in any world.
Although the current trend was irreversible, there were always some high-level nobles discontent with their dwindling privileges.
They resented, they were unwilling to simply hand over the benefits they had usurped.
Dozens of nobles, after the Lady of the Night watched over the land, quietly gathered together.
The place they gathered was located in the most bustling area of South City—Nightingale Street.
This was a notorious red-light district in Green City, where it was said that after dark, three thousand "nightingales" worked, all skilled women.
